8680d78d026f.title: Software architecture
8680d78d026f.sentence: To address these challenges, architects typically provide both technical and business justifications (often related to cost, user satisfaction, and time to market) in a single record of the architectural decision (usually an Architecture Decision Record).

25c7b93518e9.title: Software architecture
25c7b93518e9.sentence: This record can be maintained in an accessible repository, such as a wiki.

d139b6d25074.title: Software architecture
d139b6d25074.sentence: Making architectural decisions involves collecting sufficient relevant information, providing justification for the decision, documenting the decision and its rationale, and communicating it effectively to the appropriate stakeholders.

67f6fd97d8e8.title: Software architecture
67f6fd97d8e8.sentence: - A set of architectural design decisions: software architecture should not be considered merely a set of models or structures, but should include the decisions that lead to these particular structures, and the rationale behind them.

5716d911744e.title: Software architecture
5716d911744e.sentence: - An architect may delay or avoid making architectural decisions due to the fear of choosing incorrectly.

d313b329c1fb.title: Software architecture
d313b329c1fb.sentence: To address this, ongoing and close collaboration with the development team is often necessary, with architectural choices being adjusted based on their feedback.

bcd8fa5f5cf9.title: Software architecture
bcd8fa5f5cf9.sentence: Additionally, decisions are typically made at the "last responsible moment," ensuring there is enough information to justify and validate the decision, while avoiding unnecessary delays that could lead to analysis paralysis and hinder the team's progress.

6224c57a4454.title: Software architecture
6224c57a4454.sentence: - Another anti-pattern can arise when architectural decisions are forgotten, not documented, or not understood, leading to repeated discussions without resolution.

ef9915939b3b.title: Software architecture
ef9915939b3b.sentence: This often occurs when email is used to communicate architectural decisions.

06915d1793ce.title: Software architecture
06915d1793ce.sentence: This ensures there is always a single updated source of truth.

bbe2065cdc06.title: Software architecture
bbe2065cdc06.sentence: There are four core activities in software architecture design.

3994ad67cf24.title: Software architecture
3994ad67cf24.sentence: These core architecture activities are performed iteratively and at different stages of the initial software development life-cycle, as well as over the evolution of a system.

e2a2f4b51a5c.title: Software architecture
e2a2f4b51a5c.sentence: Architectural analysis is the process of understanding the environment in which a proposed system will operate and determining the requirements for the system.

c24c8535c6b3.title: Software architecture
c24c8535c6b3.sentence: The outputs of the analysis activity are those requirements that have a measurable impact on a software system's architecture, called architecturally significant requirements.

feb516d40636.title: Software architecture
feb516d40636.sentence: Architectural synthesis or design is the process of creating an architecture.

86b680ca6f02.title: Software architecture
86b680ca6f02.sentence: Given the architecturally significant requirements determined by the analysis, the current state of the design and the results of any evaluation activities, the design is created and improved.

0e280febadd3.title: Software architecture
0e280febadd3.sentence: Architecture evaluation is the process of determining how well the current design or a portion of it satisfies the requirements derived during analysis.

6f9b6656b731.title: Software architecture
6f9b6656b731.sentence: Some of the available software architecture evaluation techniques include Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method (ATAM) and TARA.

e9618eda9b5a.title: Software architecture
e9618eda9b5a.sentence: Architecture evolution is the process of maintaining and adapting an existing software architecture to meet changes in requirements and environment.

7e02a2ca44a1.title: Software architecture
7e02a2ca44a1.sentence: They include knowledge management and communication, design reasoning and decision-making, and documentation.

c7a51a7ac2e8.title: Software architecture
c7a51a7ac2e8.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture erosion
c7a51a7ac2e8.sentence: Software architecture erosion refers to a gradual gap between the intended and implemented architecture of a software system over time.

a1b3ca2fb6dc.title: Software architecture
a1b3ca2fb6dc.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture erosion
a1b3ca2fb6dc.sentence: Software architecture erosion may occur in each stage of the software development life cycle and has varying impacts on the development speed and the cost of maintenance.

7c818b4bb1d1.title: Software architecture
7c818b4bb1d1.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture erosion
7c818b4bb1d1.sentence: Software architecture erosion occurs due to various reasons, such as architectural violations, the accumulation of technical debt, and knowledge vaporization.

6fe2db186bf9.title: Software architecture
6fe2db186bf9.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture erosion
6fe2db186bf9.sentence: Architecture erosion can decrease software performance, substantially increase evolutionary costs, and degrade software quality.

6b1abaa1042c.title: Software architecture
6b1abaa1042c.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture erosion
6b1abaa1042c.sentence: Besides, the measures used to address architecture erosion contain two main types: preventative and remedial measures.

67cdef09ec08.title: Software architecture
67cdef09ec08.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture erosion
67cdef09ec08.sentence: Preventative measures include enforcing architectural rules, regular code reviews, and automated testing, while remedial measures involve refactoring, redesign, and documentation updates.

9ef219a39b33.title: Software architecture
9ef219a39b33.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture erosion
9ef219a39b33.sentence: For instance, automated architecture conformance checks, static code analysis tools, and refactoring techniques help identify and mitigate erosion early.

e75e9475967e.title: Software architecture
e75e9475967e.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture recovery
e75e9475967e.sentence: Software architecture recovery (or reconstruction, or reverse engineering) includes the methods, techniques, and processes to uncover a software system's architecture from available information, including its implementation and documentation.

b85f4225c75f.title: Software architecture
b85f4225c75f.section: Software architecture topics > Software architecture recovery
b85f4225c75f.sentence: Architecture recovery is often necessary to make informed decisions in the face of obsolete or out-of-date documentation and architecture erosion: implementation and maintenance decisions diverging from the envisioned architecture.

3b6b5aadebf9.title: Software architecture
3b6b5aadebf9.sentence: Requirements engineering entails the elicitation, negotiation, specification, validation, documentation, and management of requirements.

e107a06a9105.title: Software architecture
e107a06a9105.sentence: Requirements engineering and software architecture can be seen as complementary approaches: while software architecture targets the 'solution space' or the 'how', requirements engineering addresses the 'problem space' or the 'what'.

552ee1ea9a6b.title: Requirements engineering
552ee1ea9a6b.sentence: Later development methods, including the Rational Unified Process (RUP) for software, assume that requirements engineering continues through a system's lifetime.

049c4155d253.title: Requirements engineering
049c4155d253.sentence: - Requirements elicitation – Developers and stakeholders meet; the latter are inquired concerning their needs and wants regarding the software product.

edff65abdd3c.title: Requirements engineering
edff65abdd3c.sentence: - Requirements analysis and negotiation – Requirements are identified (including new ones if the development is iterative), and conflicts with stakeholders are solved.

fbc2d36dfe3c.title: Requirements engineering
fbc2d36dfe3c.sentence: - Requirements specification – Requirements are documented in a formal artifact called a Requirements Specification (RS), which will become official only after validation.

ca03477f28d5.title: Requirements engineering
ca03477f28d5.sentence: - Requirements validation – Checking that the documented requirements and models are consistent and meet the stakeholder's needs.

b2588031ca96.title: Requirements engineering
b2588031ca96.sentence: - Requirements management – Managing all the activities related to the requirements since inception, supervising as the system is developed, and even until after it is put into use (e. g., changes, extensions, etc.)

3594fd4b2382.title: Requirements engineering
3594fd4b2382.sentence: In the waterfall model, requirements engineering is presented as the first phase of the software development process.

a785410fc1b7.title: Requirements engineering
a785410fc1b7.sentence: These are sometimes presented as chronological stages although, in practice, there is considerable interleaving of these activities.

49eaad15da55.title: Software architecture
49eaad15da55.sentence: In short, required behavior impacts solution architecture, which in turn may introduce new requirements.

ea308090effd.title: Software architecture
ea308090effd.sentence: Approaches such as the Twin Peaks model aim to exploit the synergistic relation between requirements and architecture.

b8e675978427.title: Software design pattern
b8e675978427.sentence: A software design pattern describes a reusable solution to a commonly needed behavior in software.

7411d6579dfe.title: Software design pattern
7411d6579dfe.sentence: Rather, it is a description of and a template for solving a particular type of problem that can be used in many different contexts, including different programming languages and computing platforms.

ff5c19e15386.title: Software design pattern
ff5c19e15386.sentence: A design pattern is not a rigid structure to be copied directly into source code.

3fab4ff2886f.title: Software design pattern
3fab4ff2886f.sentence: Software architecture patterns operate at a higher level of abstraction than design patterns, solving broader system-level challenges.

0b78baa32b17.title: Software design pattern
0b78baa32b17.sentence: Design patterns can speed up the development process by providing proven development paradigms.

59963651ac7a.title: Software design pattern
59963651ac7a.sentence: Freshly written code can often have hidden, subtle issues that take time to be detected – issues that sometimes can cause major problems down the road.

7acec3743bfa.title: Software design pattern
7acec3743bfa.sentence: Reusing design patterns can help to prevent such issues, and enhance code readability for those familiar with the patterns.

f042b757b6f2.title: Software design pattern
f042b757b6f2.sentence: Design patterns can be organized into groups based on what kind of problem they solve.

ce1371865763.title: Software design pattern
ce1371865763.sentence: Factory method | Define an interface for creating a single object, but let subclasses decide which class to instantiate. Factory Method lets a class defer instantiation to subclasses. | Yes | — N/a

998e9e0cd55d.title: Software design pattern
998e9e0cd55d.sentence: Builder | Separate the construction of a complex object from its representation, allowing the same construction process to create various representations. | Yes | — N/a

88a8045124aa.title: Software design pattern
88a8045124aa.sentence: Adapter, Wrapper, or Translator | Convert the interface of a class into another interface clients expect. An adapter lets classes work together that could not otherwise because of incompatible interfaces. The enterprise integration pattern equivalent is the translator. | Yes

5c36213aa504.title: Software design pattern
5c36213aa504.sentence: Decorator | Attach additional responsibilities to an object dynamically keeping the same interface. Decorators provide a flexible alternative to subclassing for extending functionality. | Yes

0f50a0a0bd0c.title: Software design pattern
0f50a0a0bd0c.sentence: Chain of responsibility | Avoid coupling the sender of a request to its receiver by giving more than one object a chance to handle the request. Chain the receiving objects and pass the request along the chain until an object handles it. | Yes

edbcf810ac64.title: Software design pattern
edbcf810ac64.sentence: Command | Encapsulate a request as an object, thereby allowing for the parameterization of clients with different requests, and the queuing or logging of requests. It also allows for the support of undoable operations. | Yes

9d558f0c7f6f.title: Software design pattern
9d558f0c7f6f.sentence: A concurrency pattern supports concurrent processing.

b035da01312a.title: Software design pattern
b035da01312a.sentence: Some suggest that the need for a design pattern may be a sign that a feature is missing from a programming language.

75385b3b114e.title: Software design pattern
75385b3b114e.sentence: Peter Norvig demonstrates that 16 out of the 23 patterns in the Design Patterns book (which is primarily focused on C++) are simplified or eliminated (via direct language support) in Lisp or Dylan.

965770cc7188.title: Software design pattern
965770cc7188.sentence: Inappropriate use of patterns may unnecessarily increase complexity.

9cdfebb4d3d2.title: Software architecture
9cdfebb4d3d2.sentence: Software architecture pattern is a reusable, proven solution to a recurring problem at the system level, addressing concerns related to the overall structure, component interactions, and quality attributes of the system.

c7396fc8153f.title: Software architecture
c7396fc8153f.sentence: Software architecture style is a high-level structural organization that defines the overall system organization, specifying how components are organized, how they interact, and the constraints on those interactions.

14fb95d5a06d.title: Software architecture
14fb95d5a06d.sentence: Software architecture patterns operate at a higher level of abstraction than software design patterns, solving broader system-level challenges.

742f9f1ac957.title: Software architecture
742f9f1ac957.sentence: Architecture styles typically include a vocabulary of component and connector types, as well as semantic models for interpreting the system's properties.

c0312c259e11.title: Software architecture
c0312c259e11.sentence: These styles represent the most coarse-grained level of system organization.

b1b4b227236f.title: Software architecture
b1b4b227236f.sentence: Examples include Layered Architecture, Microservices, Event-Driven Architecture and hexagonal architecture.

343345ddf280.title: Software architecture
343345ddf280.sentence: While these patterns typically affect system-level concerns, the distinction between architectural patterns and architectural styles can sometimes be blurry.

b2b9568e609c.title: Software architecture
b2b9568e609c.sentence: Common terms for recurring solutions are architectural style, tactic, reference architecture and architectural pattern.

16ee99c4d077.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
16ee99c4d077.sentence: Asking questions about the exact scope of the problem, and clarifying functional requirements early in the interview is essential.

2ba5814cd88c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
2ba5814cd88c.sentence: Usually, requirements are divided into three parts:

30c8692e8925.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
30c8692e8925.sentence: These are the requirements that the end user specifically demands as basic functionalities that the system should offer.

1f694647c45c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
1f694647c45c.sentence: All these functionalities need to be necessarily incorporated into the system as part of the contract.

a41f12c75592.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
a41f12c75592.sentence: - "What are the features that we need to design for this system?"

5ad7c39476b2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
5ad7c39476b2.sentence: - "What are the edge cases we need to consider, if any, in our design?"

fd0cea3f1f02.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
fd0cea3f1f02.sentence: These are the quality constraints that the system must satisfy according to the project contract.

2dde533d5e0b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
2dde533d5e0b.sentence: Ask questions to understand the core features of the system as well as non-functional aspects such as data volume, availability, scale, etc.

cd7c99a8abb6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
cd7c99a8abb6.sentence: These are basically "nice to have" requirements that might be out of the scope of the system.

70693670e4df.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
70693670e4df.sentence: - "Our system should record metrics and analytics"

0abb792953b7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
0abb792953b7.sentence: Follow this 7-step process to do well in a System Design Round

76f07f710d8c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
76f07f710d8c.sentence: In the first step, clarify functional and non-functional requirements.

69d9dd31a521.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
69d9dd31a521.sentence: Next, estimate the capacity of the system.

0a4fa9090bab.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
0a4fa9090bab.sentence: Break down the system into components such as client apps, servers, load balancers, databases, etc.

5389b997d0a6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
5389b997d0a6.sentence: Model the data and choose the right database type for the system.

76db56052eca.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
76db56052eca.sentence: Next, focus on the interfaces to the system.

58a4e71dd8d0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
58a4e71dd8d0.sentence: Address the scalability, performance, and latency aspects of the system by suggesting techniques that will be used.

cd2d22de4299.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
cd2d22de4299.sentence: Lastly, address the reliability and resiliency of the design.

f04e346c9086.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
f04e346c9086.sentence: Focus on attributes like the number of users, traffic, storage/memory needs, and compute and networking requirements.

c2c00adc8e17.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
c2c00adc8e17.sentence: Estimate the scale of the system we're going to design.

2903337492f7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
2903337492f7.sentence: - "What is the desired scale that this system will need to handle?"

39f35e01ae5f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
39f35e01ae5f.sentence: - "What is the read/write ratio of our system?"

87bd4f13f57a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
87bd4f13f57a.sentence: Once we have the estimations, we can start with defining the database schema.

de2e3d56d297.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
de2e3d56d297.sentence: Doing so in the early stages of the interview would help us to understand the data flow which is the core of every system.

41648420c2ef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
41648420c2ef.sentence: In this step, we basically define all the entities and relationships between them.

60dab13ea4be.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
60dab13ea4be.sentence: Once done, focus on the database schema.

8977590fa03e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
8977590fa03e.sentence: Next, we can start designing APIs for the system.

aff03a8e4d60.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
aff03a8e4d60.sentence: These APIs will help us define the expectations from the system explicitly.

1d44b9b87f41.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
1d44b9b87f41.sentence: We don't have to write any code, just a simple interface defining the API requirements such as parameters, functions, classes, types, entities, etc.

1ccf19e08220.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
1ccf19e08220.sentence: It is advised to keep the interface as simple as possible and come back to it later when covering extended requirements.

e0063082d8bf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
e0063082d8bf.sentence: This could be API endpoints or event models exchanged between the various components of the system.

351a37bc1b47.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
351a37bc1b47.sentence: Also, choose a communication approach such as REST, GraphQL, gRPC, or an event-driven

d50ed4c1082c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
d50ed4c1082c.sentence: Start with drawing a simple block diagram that shows these components and their potential interaction with each other.

a56715b63e51.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
a56715b63e51.sentence: Now we have established our data model and API design, it's time to identify system components (such as Load Balancers, API Gateway, etc.) that are needed to solve our problem and draft the first design of our system.

8dfaed8f783b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
8dfaed8f783b.sentence: Once we have a basic diagram, we can start discussing with the interviewer how the system will work from the client's perspective.

e8ffd106eedb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
e8ffd106eedb.sentence: Now it's time to go into detail about the major components of the system we designed.

3bf22dcf07a8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
3bf22dcf07a8.sentence: As always discuss with the interviewer which component may need further improvements.

ad86ae34c1f8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
ad86ae34c1f8.sentence: - "How will we handle a sudden spike in traffic?"

848016bbd7ed.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
848016bbd7ed.sentence: For example, vertical and horizontal scaling, caching, indexing, denormalizing, sharding, replication, CDNs, etc.

8f6fa3649492.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
8f6fa3649492.sentence: Finally, it's time to discuss bottlenecks and approaches to mitigate them.

fc6d468f946a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
fc6d468f946a.sentence: - "Is there any single point of failure?"

41d406acdef2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
41d406acdef2.sentence: - "How can we make our system more robust?"

84433e1f84aa.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::system-design-interviews
84433e1f84aa.sentence: - "How to improve the availability of our cache?"

1257fe32ee35.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-ace-system-design-interviews-like-a-boss.md
1257fe32ee35.sentence: Identify single points of failure and mitigate their impact.

13a5b03b8f70.title: Conway's law
13a5b03b8f70.sentence: Conway's law describes the link between communication structure of organizations and the systems they design.

1ebf13a40134.title: Conway's law
1ebf13a40134.sentence: > [O]rganizations which design systems (in the broad sense used here) are constrained to produce designs which are copies of the communication structures of these organizations.

ea9d0842ecfa.title: Conway's law
ea9d0842ecfa.sentence: The law is based on the reasoning that in order for a product to function, the authors and designers of its component parts must communicate with each other in order to ensure compatibility between the components.

68db1333e8cb.title: Conway's law
68db1333e8cb.sentence: Therefore, the technical structure of a system will reflect the social boundaries of the organizations that produced it, across which communication is more difficult.

21b0a240b863.title: Conway's law
21b0a240b863.sentence: The law is applied primarily in the field of software architecture, though Conway directed it more broadly and its assumptions and conclusions apply to most technical fields.

7852d2eff965.title: Conway's law
7852d2eff965.sentence: The law is, in a strict sense, only about correspondence; it does not state that communication structure is the cause of system structure, merely describes the connection.

3202d6127217.title: Conway's law
3202d6127217.sentence: Different commentators have taken various positions on the direction of causality; that technical design causes the organization to restructure to fit, that the organizational structure dictates the technical design, or both.

3a0698c31fb2.title: Conway's law
3a0698c31fb2.sentence: Opinions also vary on the desirability of the phenomenon; some say that the mirroring pattern is a helpful feature of such systems, while other interpretations say it's an undesirable result of organizational bias.

69e9012d6e1c.title: Conway's law
69e9012d6e1c.sentence: Evidence in support of Conway's law has been published by a team of Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Harvard Business School researchers who, using "the mirroring hypothesis" as an equivalent term for Conway's law, found "strong evidence to support the mirroring hypothesis", and that the "product developed by the loosely-coupled organization is significantly more modular than the product from the tightly-coupled organization".

3bbdc4e70d4b.title: Conway's law
3bbdc4e70d4b.sentence: The authors highlight the impact of "organizational design decisions on the technical structure of the artifacts that these organizations subsequently develop".

39de53dcac59.title: Conway's law
39de53dcac59.sentence: > If the parts of an organization (e.g., teams, departments, or subdivisions) do not closely reflect the essential parts of the product, or if the relationships between organizations do not reflect the relationships between product parts, then the project will be in trouble...

8507be86d87c.title: Conway's law
8507be86d87c.sentence: Therefore: Make sure the organization is compatible with the product architecture.

6c9cf6bb28ec.title: Conway's law
6c9cf6bb28ec.sentence: > The structure of any system designed by an organization is isomorphic to the structure of the organization.

c5f90d9e3c3e.title: Latency (engineering)
c5f90d9e3c3e.sentence: Latency, from a general point of view, is a time delay between the cause and the effect of some physical change in the system being observed.

2c27156dd64e.title: Latency (engineering)
2c27156dd64e.sentence: Latency is physically a consequence of the limited velocity at which any physical interaction can propagate.

a97b5400d377.title: Latency (engineering)
a97b5400d377.sentence: The magnitude of this velocity is always less than or equal to the speed of light.

6cd3ed222914.title: Latency (engineering)
6cd3ed222914.sentence: Therefore, every physical system with any physical separation (distance) between cause and effect will experience some sort of latency, regardless of the nature of the stimulation to which it has been exposed.

7e47735c47db.title: Latency (engineering)
7e47735c47db.sentence: The precise definition of latency depends on the system being observed or the nature of the simulation.

df0493a5ea5c.title: Latency (engineering)
df0493a5ea5c.sentence: In communications, the lower limit of latency is determined by the medium being used to transfer information.

3cdd58f77447.title: Latency (engineering)
3cdd58f77447.sentence: Perceptible latency has a strong effect on user satisfaction and usability in the field of human–machine interaction.

44856d5c5a49.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-5-strategies-to-reduce-latency.md
44856d5c5a49.sentence: For high-scale user-facing systems, high latency is a big loss of revenue.

64e646b9cd91.title: Latency (engineering)
64e646b9cd91.sentence: Networks that exhibit relatively small delays are known as low-latency networks, while their counterparts are known as high-latency networks.

fb2b1d3f519b.title: Latency (engineering)
fb2b1d3f519b.sentence: Any mechanical process encounters limitations modeled by Newtonian physics.

13d7d6266fa0.title: Latency (engineering)
13d7d6266fa0.sentence: Here, it is the time seek time for the actuator arm to be positioned above the appropriate track and then rotational latency for the data encoded on a platter to rotate from its current position to a position under the disk read-and-write head.

cda836d7b9ac.title: Latency (engineering)
cda836d7b9ac.sentence: In the context of computer multitasking, the execution of the process can be postponed if other processes are also executing.

3850a12fd895.title: Latency (engineering)
3850a12fd895.sentence: In addition, the operating system can schedule when to perform the action that the process is commanding.

9ab36c30ffb7.title: Latency (engineering)
9ab36c30ffb7.sentence: The latency is the delay between the events generated by the hardware clock and the actual transitions of voltage from high to low or low to high.

9959df58b06e.title: Bandwidth (computing)
9959df58b06e.sentence: In computing, bandwidth is the maximum rate of data transfer across a given path.

7934bb00c715.title: Bandwidth (computing)
7934bb00c715.sentence: Bandwidth may be characterized as network bandwidth, data bandwidth, or digital bandwidth.

4792c1c6a19d.title: Bandwidth (computing)
4792c1c6a19d.sentence: This definition of bandwidth contrasts with usage in signal processing, wireless communications, modem data transmission, digital communications, and electronics, in which bandwidth is used to refer to the signal bandwidth measured in hertz, meaning the frequency range between the lowest and highest attainable frequencies while meeting a well-defined impairment level in signal power.

64361f3490f4.title: Bandwidth (computing)
64361f3490f4.sentence: The term bandwidth sometimes refers to the net bit rate, peak bit rate, information rate, physical-layer useful bit rate, channel capacity, or maximum throughput of a logical or physical communication path in a digital communication system.

c0540fd9e3c7.title: Bandwidth (computing)
c0540fd9e3c7.sentence: For example, bandwidth tests measure the maximum throughput of a computer network.

9bc0884e8f57.title: Bandwidth (computing)
9bc0884e8f57.sentence: The consumed bandwidth in bit/s corresponds to achieved throughput or goodput, i.e., the average rate of successful data transfer through a communication path.

01f72a7e1c88.title: Bandwidth (computing)
01f72a7e1c88.sentence: For example, a channel with x bit/s may not necessarily transmit data at x rate, since protocols, encryption, and other factors can add appreciable overhead.

08d2ad8a6d91.title: Bandwidth (computing)
08d2ad8a6d91.sentence: For instance, much internet traffic uses the transmission control protocol (TCP), which requires a three-way handshake for each transaction.

a9241cb573c3.title: Bandwidth (computing)
a9241cb573c3.sentence: Although in many modern implementations the protocol is efficient, it does add significant overhead compared to simpler protocols.

3c4ea8669d7e.title: Bandwidth (computing)
3c4ea8669d7e.sentence: Also, data packets may be lost, which further reduces the useful data throughput.

5f91dd3638c9.title: Bandwidth (computing)
5f91dd3638c9.sentence: Useful throughput is less than or equal to the actual channel capacity minus implementation overhead.

f85ce2d678bf.title: Bandwidth (computing)
f85ce2d678bf.sentence: Since bandwidth spikes can skew the measurement, carriers often use the 95th percentile method.

d974b3d920ff.title: Bandwidth (computing)

5a4187f77fdc.title: Bandwidth (computing)

d4cab87184c4.title: Bandwidth (computing)

d2a91a38671b.title: Latency (engineering)
d2a91a38671b.sentence: Network latency in a packet-switched network is measured as either one-way (the time from the source sending a packet to the destination receiving it), or round-trip delay time (the one-way latency from the source to the destination plus the one-way latency from the destination back to the source).

9dfdc4efcb1f.title: Latency (engineering)
9dfdc4efcb1f.sentence: Round-trip latency is more often quoted because it can be measured from a single point.

33341d20a413.title: Latency (engineering)
33341d20a413.sentence: Ping uses the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) echo request which causes the recipient to send the received packet as an immediate response; thus it provides a rough way of measuring round-trip delay time.

b7e6bc816e22.title: Latency (engineering)
b7e6bc816e22.sentence: Ping cannot perform accurate measurements, principally because ICMP is intended only for diagnostic or control purposes, and differs from real communication protocols such as TCP.

9b7b147594ee.title: Latency (engineering)
9b7b147594ee.sentence: Furthermore, routers and internet service providers might apply different traffic shaping policies to different protocols.

a597c5d5fd29.title: Latency (engineering)
a597c5d5fd29.sentence: For more accurate measurements it is better to use specific software, for example: hping, Netperf or Iperf.

75dbee06e874.title: Latency (engineering)
75dbee06e874.sentence: However, in a non-trivial network, a typical packet will be forwarded over multiple links and gateways, each of which will not begin to forward the packet until it has been completely received.

5a9a1b0f1187.title: Latency (engineering)
5a9a1b0f1187.sentence: In such a network, the minimal latency is the sum of the transmission delay of each link, plus the forwarding latency of each gateway.

2fdc14a8af83.title: Latency (engineering)
2fdc14a8af83.sentence: In practice, minimal latency also includes queuing and processing delays.

beefc00f4e27.title: Latency (engineering)
beefc00f4e27.sentence: Queuing delay occurs when a gateway receives multiple packets from different sources heading toward the same destination.

42fc3aade7a0.title: Latency (engineering)
42fc3aade7a0.sentence: Since typically only one packet can be transmitted at a time, some of the packets must queue for transmission, incurring additional delay.

07f2139d8b47.title: Latency (engineering)
07f2139d8b47.sentence: Processing delays are incurred while a gateway determines what to do with a newly received packet.

392afda41e3e.title: Latency (engineering)
392afda41e3e.sentence: The combination of propagation, serialization, queuing, and processing delays often produces a complex and variable network latency profile.

1c913b3f5aaf.title: Latency (engineering)
1c913b3f5aaf.sentence: Bufferbloat can also cause increased latency that is an order of magnitude or more.

c1502ad3c0b1.title: Latency (engineering)
c1502ad3c0b1.sentence: The index of refraction of most fiber optic cables is about 1.5, which means light travels at about two thirds of its vacuum speed in the cable.

2967a4a4f7a0.title: Latency (engineering)
2967a4a4f7a0.sentence: This works out to about 5.0 μs of latency for every kilometer.

24b32a071d27.title: Latency (engineering)
24b32a071d27.sentence: Light in a vacuum takes 3.33 μs to travel one kilometer.

e2fe773e7242.title: Latency (engineering)
e2fe773e7242.sentence: To calculate the latency of a connection, one has to know the distance traveled by the fiber, which is rarely a straight line, since it has to traverse geographic contours and obstacles, such as roads and railway tracks, as well as other rights-of-way.

116e27dacaa6.title: Latency (engineering)
116e27dacaa6.sentence: For distances of greater than 100 kilometers, amplifiers or regenerators are deployed.

6c789c310868.title: Latency (engineering)
6c789c310868.sentence: Latency introduced by these components needs to be taken into account.

4dad52b265ed.title: Latency (engineering)
4dad52b265ed.sentence: Satellites in geostationary orbits are far enough away from Earth that communication latency becomes significant – about a quarter of a second for a trip from one ground-based transmitter to the satellite and back to another ground-based transmitter; close to half a second for two-way communication from one Earth station to another and then back to the first.

11063aaedb44.title: Latency (engineering)
11063aaedb44.sentence: Low Earth orbit is sometimes used to cut this delay (a satellite 400 km up adds about 12 ms), at the expense of more complicated satellite tracking on the ground and requiring more satellites in the satellite constellation to ensure continuous coverage.

c241703aa337.title: Percentile
c241703aa337.sentence: In statistics, a percentile or percentile score, also known as centile (often denoted as Pk or Pk, for a given percentage k), is a score greater than a given percentage of all scores (or data point value) in a sample.

39fb2380e5ff.title: Percentile
39fb2380e5ff.sentence: For example, the 97th percentile (P97) is the value such that 97% of the data points are less than it.

0c12ecc9ea30.title: Percentile
0c12ecc9ea30.sentence: I.e., a score in the k-th percentile would be above approximately k% of all scores in its sample.

bd370f9821a9.title: Percentile
bd370f9821a9.sentence: The 25th percentile (P25) is also known as the first quartile (Q1), the 50th percentile (P50) as the median or second quartile (Q2), and the 75th percentile (P75) as the third quartile (Q3).

65384c38966c.title: Percentile
65384c38966c.sentence: Percentiles are expressed in the same unit of measurement as the input scores, not in percent; for example, if the scores refer to human weight, the corresponding percentiles will be expressed in kilograms or pounds.

4f85f731bff0.title: Percentile
4f85f731bff0.sentence: There is no standard definition of percentile; however, all definitions yield similar results when the number of observations is very large and the probability distribution is continuous.

a376de404d39.title: Percentile
a376de404d39.sentence: Algorithms either return the value of a score that exists in the set of scores (nearest-rank methods) or interpolate between existing scores and are either exclusive or inclusive.

6b8ad2c4d077.title: Percentile
6b8ad2c4d077.sentence: - A percentile calculated using the nearest-rank method will always be a member of the original ordered list.

88dbb940c747.title: Percentile
88dbb940c747.sentence: - Using the nearest-rank method on lists with fewer than 100 distinct values can result in the same value being used for more than one percentile.

2cfd77bfb0c9.title: Percentile
2cfd77bfb0c9.sentence: When Internet service providers bill "burstable" internet bandwidth, the 95th or 98th percentile usually cuts off the top 5% or 2% of bandwidth peaks in each month, and then bills at the nearest rate.

2702c570d8cc.title: Percentile
2702c570d8cc.sentence: In this way, infrequent peaks are ignored, and the customer is charged in a fairer way.

e6665eac8df8.sentence: In distributed systems, cloud computing, and large-scale web services, even a small number of slow requests can make the user experience and system performance much worse.

527f8b9b24ca.sentence: A major problem in system design is managing tail latency, because lowering average latency doesn't always make the worst-case performance better.

f2976a023367.sentence: To lessen its effects, people often use techniques like request hedging, replication, load balancing, and adaptive timeouts.

b7337b301eed.section: Computer hardware and software systems > Tail latency
b7337b301eed.sentence: In latency-sensitive applications like search engines, financial systems, and real-time services, where service-level objectives (SLOs) are often based on high-percentile latencies, it is especially important to understand and improve tail latency.

8395e0c67c7b.sentence: When building a monitoring system from scratch, itâs tempting to design a system based upon the mean of some quantity: the mean latency, the mean CPU usage of your nodes, or the mean fullness of your databases.

4a8ced1f566b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/10-system-design-tradeoffs-you-cannot-ignore.md

54db78e81505.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/10-system-design-tradeoffs-you-cannot-ignore.md
54db78e81505.sentence: Consistency is the assurance of getting the most recent data every single time.

35f713439c29.title: Little's law
35f713439c29.sentence: In mathematical queueing theory, Little's law (also result, theorem, lemma, or formula) is a theorem by John Little which states that the long-term average number of customers (L) in a stationary system is equal to the long-term average effective arrival rate (λ) multiplied by the average time that a customer spends in the system (W).

cabb6d0311c0.title: Little's law
cabb6d0311c0.sentence: The relationship is not influenced by the arrival process distribution, the service distribution, the service order, or practically anything else.

809bff946a1d.title: Little's law
809bff946a1d.sentence: The only requirement is that the system be ergodic.

5a43bb404c04.title: Little's law
5a43bb404c04.sentence: The result applies to any system, and particularly, it applies to systems within systems.

39e801ead3dc.title: Little's law
39e801ead3dc.sentence: For example in a bank branch, the customer line might be one subsystem, and each of the tellers another subsystem, and Little's result could be applied to each one, as well as the whole thing.

ac33fcf26879.title: Little's law
ac33fcf26879.sentence: If the mean number in the system and the throughput are known, the average response time can be found using Little’s Law:

aedfeb6b1531.title: Little's law
aedfeb6b1531.sentence: mean response time = mean number in system / mean throughput

ba5f3f728f2b.title: Little's law
ba5f3f728f2b.sentence: For example: A queue depth meter shows an average of nine jobs waiting to be serviced.

dd8d6b206730.title: Little's law
dd8d6b206730.sentence: Add one for the job being serviced, so there is an average of ten jobs in the system.

37b654aa2bc2.title: Little's law
37b654aa2bc2.sentence: Another meter shows a mean throughput of 50 per second.

2418760c1221.title: Little's law
2418760c1221.sentence: The mean response time is calculated as 0.2 seconds = 10 / 50 per second.

81872cecd3aa.title: Little's law
81872cecd3aa.sentence: Assume customers arrive at the rate of 10 per hour and stay an average of 0.5 hour.

765d4ba94b99.title: Little's law
765d4ba94b99.sentence: This means we should find the average number of customers in the store at any time to be 5.

fade7d93813d.title: Little's law
fade7d93813d.sentence: Now suppose the store is considering doing more advertising to raise the arrival rate to 20 per hour.

3f3b1f35552d.title: Little's law
3f3b1f35552d.sentence: The store must either be prepared to host an average of 10 occupants or must reduce the time each customer spends in the store to 0.25 hour.

ee371d5c277a.title: Little's law
ee371d5c277a.sentence: If the rate at which people enter the store (called the arrival rate) is the rate at which they exit (called the exit rate), the system is stable.

9b5bf49de012.title: Little's law
9b5bf49de012.sentence: By contrast, an arrival rate exceeding an exit rate would represent an unstable system, where the number of waiting customers in the store would gradually increase towards infinity.

7eca5d7644ac.title: Little's law
7eca5d7644ac.sentence: If the arrival rate is much greater than the exit rate, the store will eventually start to overflow, and thus any new arriving customers will simply be rejected (and forced to go somewhere else or try again later) until there is once again free space available in the store.

d3f3b79108a9.title: Little's law
d3f3b79108a9.sentence: This is also the difference between the arrival rate and the effective arrival rate, where the arrival rate roughly corresponds to the rate at which customers arrive at the store, whereas the effective arrival rate corresponds to the rate at which customers enter the store.

f6f1ce799259.title: Little's law
f6f1ce799259.sentence: Software-performance testers have used Little's law to ensure that the observed performance results are not due to bottlenecks imposed by the testing apparatus.

e4fa613bb801.title: Little's law
e4fa613bb801.sentence: To use Little's law on data, formulas must be used to estimate the parameters, as the result does not necessarily directly apply over finite time intervals, due to problems like how to log customers already present at the start of the logging interval and those who have not yet departed when logging stops.

b5720dbeb9d6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
b5720dbeb9d6.sentence: The OSI Model is a logical and conceptual model that defines network communication used by systems open to interconnection and communication with other systems.

ebd6d5ae87bc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
ebd6d5ae87bc.sentence: It's based on the concept of splitting up a communication system into seven abstract layers, each one stacked upon the last.

7c0573e40887.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
7c0573e40887.sentence: The Open System Interconnection (OSI Model) also defines a logical network and effectively describes computer packet transfer by using various layers of protocols.

48a1b93437fc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
48a1b93437fc.sentence: The OSI Model can be seen as a universal language for computer networking.

078bd4bfaa80.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
078bd4bfaa80.section: Why does the OSI model matter?
078bd4bfaa80.sentence: The Open System Interconnection (OSI) model has defined the common terminology used in networking discussions and documentation.

5048aa270479.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
5048aa270479.section: Why does the OSI model matter?
5048aa270479.sentence: This allows us to take a very complex communications process apart and evaluate its components.

01776dba9c31.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
01776dba9c31.section: Why does the OSI model matter?
01776dba9c31.sentence: While this model is not directly implemented in the TCP/IP networks that are most common today, it can still help us do so much more, such as:

e94b5dcea8a0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
e94b5dcea8a0.section: Why does the OSI model matter?
e94b5dcea8a0.sentence: - Make troubleshooting easier and help identify threats across the entire stack.

42c297b1aaa5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
42c297b1aaa5.section: Why does the OSI model matter?
42c297b1aaa5.sentence: - Encourage hardware manufacturers to create networking products that can communicate with each other over the network.

5e2ff32293b9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
5e2ff32293b9.section: Why does the OSI model matter?
5e2ff32293b9.sentence: - Separate a complex function into simpler components.

c25ffaa67cc7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
c25ffaa67cc7.section: Why does the OSI model matter?
c25ffaa67cc7.sentence: - Essential for developing a security-first mindset.

d68bdf5f4edb.title: OSI model
d68bdf5f4edb.sentence: The model describes communications from the physical implementation of transmitting bits across a transmission medium to the highest-level representation of data of a distributed application.

2a28fc491563.title: OSI model
2a28fc491563.sentence: Each layer has well-defined functions and semantics and serves a class of functionality to the layer above it and is served by the layer below it.

907e7b748349.title: OSI model
907e7b748349.sentence: Communication protocols enable an entity in one host to interact with a corresponding entity at the same layer in another host.

a0596305a2ad.title: OSI model
a0596305a2ad.sentence: At each level N, two entities at the communicating devices (layer N peers) exchange protocol data units (PDUs) by means of a layer N protocol.

29098c56d4bf.title: Internet protocol suite
29098c56d4bf.sentence: The internet protocol suite, commonly known as TCP/IP, is a framework for organizing the communication protocols used in the internet and similar computer networks according to functional criteria.

24c52cafc4fb.title: Internet protocol suite
24c52cafc4fb.sentence: From lowest to highest, the layers are the link layer, containing communication methods for data that remains within a single network segment (link); the internet layer, providing internetworking between independent networks; the transport layer, handling host-to-host communication; and the application layer, providing process-to-process data exchange for applications.

7e647557e955.title: Internet protocol suite
7e647557e955.sentence: The internet protocol suite provides end-to-end data communication specifying how data should be packetized, addressed, transmitted, routed, and received.

c108d3030bae.title: Internet protocol suite
c108d3030bae.sentence: The foundational protocols in the suite are the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), the User Datagram Protocol (UDP), and the Internet Protocol (IP).

1f58250de37e.title: Internet protocol suite
1f58250de37e.sentence: The protocols of the link layer operate within the scope of the local network connection to which a host is attached.

c20a451b24d0.title: Internet protocol suite
c20a451b24d0.sentence: The link includes all hosts accessible without traversing a router.

d5f7d2fbe463.title: Internet protocol suite
d5f7d2fbe463.sentence: In principle, TCP/IP is designed to be hardware independent and may be implemented on top of virtually any link-layer technology.

6d58f4e6b3e3.title: Internet protocol suite
6d58f4e6b3e3.sentence: This includes not only hardware implementations but also virtual link layers such as virtual private networks and networking tunnels.

26f926d1bd3a.title: Internet protocol suite
26f926d1bd3a.sentence: This process is called routing and is supported by host addressing and identification using the hierarchical IP addressing system.

5cd644064540.title: Internet protocol suite
5cd644064540.sentence: The internet layer provides an unreliable datagram transmission facility between hosts located on potentially different IP networks by forwarding datagrams to an appropriate next-hop router for further relaying to its destination.

ded4bca6105a.title: Internet protocol suite
ded4bca6105a.sentence: The internet layer does not distinguish between the various transport layer protocols.

94710008b5ef.title: Internet protocol suite
94710008b5ef.sentence: Connectivity at the transport layer can be categorized as either connection-oriented, implemented in TCP, or connectionless, implemented in UDP.

34b7fc6ba7c2.title: Internet protocol suite
34b7fc6ba7c2.sentence: For the purpose of providing process-specific transmission channels for applications, the layer establishes the concept of the network port.

de89fe5ba54b.title: Internet protocol suite
de89fe5ba54b.sentence: The protocols in this layer may provide error control, segmentation, flow control, congestion control, and application addressing (port numbers).

c2e50593283e.title: Internet protocol suite
c2e50593283e.sentence: Examples of application layer protocols include the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), the File Transfer Protocol (FTP), the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), and the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP).

401ab570cb4a.title: Internet protocol suite
401ab570cb4a.sentence: Data coded according to application layer protocols are encapsulated into transport layer protocol units (such as TCP streams or UDP datagrams), which in turn use lower layer protocols to effect actual data transfer.

d3faf301de3e.title: Internet protocol suite
d3faf301de3e.sentence: The TCP/IP model does not consider the specifics of formatting and presenting data and does not define additional layers between the application and transport layers as in the OSI model (presentation and session layers).

6c973a1d1f81.title: Internet protocol suite
6c973a1d1f81.sentence: According to the TCP/IP model, such functions are the realm of libraries and application programming interfaces.

9cc18170951b.title: Internet protocol suite
9cc18170951b.sentence: In general, an application (the highest level of the model) uses a set of protocols to send its data down the layers.

d7b2527392f2.title: Internet protocol suite
d7b2527392f2.sentence: The data is further encapsulated at each level.

72afa33c73e9.title: Internet protocol suite
72afa33c73e9.sentence: Its original expression put the maintenance of state and overall intelligence at the edges, and assumed the internet that connected the edges retained no state and concentrated on speed and simplicity.

415e4176b8af.title: Internet protocol suite
415e4176b8af.sentence: Real-world needs for firewalls, network address translators, web content caches and the like have forced changes in this principle.

f02081ddafaa.title: OSI model
f02081ddafaa.sentence: - The Internet application layer maps to the OSI application layer, presentation layer, and most of the session layer.

ac2d699b7fe7.title: OSI model
ac2d699b7fe7.sentence: - The TCP/IP transport layer maps to the graceful close function of the OSI session layer as well as the OSI transport layer.

a6427efb286a.title: OSI model
a6427efb286a.sentence: - The internet layer performs functions as those in a subset of the OSI network layer.

eee5cee98b33.title: OSI model
eee5cee98b33.sentence: - The link layer corresponds to the OSI data link layer and may include similar functions as the physical layer, as well as some protocols of the OSI's network layer.

30a676da25dd.title: Internet protocol suite
30a676da25dd.section: Comparison of TCP/IP and OSI layering
30a676da25dd.sentence: The three top layers in the OSI model, i.e. the application layer, the presentation layer and the session layer, are not distinguished separately in the TCP/IP model, which only has an application layer above the transport layer.

98d88a0aea56.title: Client–server model
98d88a0aea56.sentence: The client–server model is a form of messaging pattern in a distributed application structure that partitions tasks or workloads between the providers of a resource or service, called servers, and service requesters, called clients.

ab80cdb749ef.title: Client–server model
ab80cdb749ef.sentence: Often clients and servers communicate over a computer network on separate hardware, but both client and server may be on the same device.

1e2f4f790479.title: Client–server model
1e2f4f790479.sentence: Clients, therefore, initiate communication sessions with servers, which await incoming requests.

279d7ac41f50.title: Client–server model
279d7ac41f50.sentence: A client usually does not share its computing resources, but it requests content or service from a server and may share its own content as part of the request.

887de849fc9a.title: Client–server model
887de849fc9a.sentence: Servers are classified by the services they provide.

6ccf8a1b1232.title: Client–server model
6ccf8a1b1232.sentence: For example, a web server serves web pages and a file server serves computer files.

f0bd3bfd7f99.title: Client–server model
f0bd3bfd7f99.sentence: Whether a computer is a client, a server, or both, is determined by the nature of the application that requires the service functions.

1f82c7f96bc3.title: Client–server model
1f82c7f96bc3.sentence: For example, a single computer can run a web server and file server software at the same time to serve different data to clients making different kinds of requests.

dfa48a6c5036.title: Client–server model
dfa48a6c5036.sentence: Clients and servers exchange messages in a request–response messaging pattern.

97a2dabbfb7a.title: Client–server model
97a2dabbfb7a.sentence: The client sends a request, and the server returns a response.

0c147a558465.title: Client–server model
0c147a558465.sentence: Generally, a service is an abstraction of computer resources and a client does not have to be concerned with how the server performs while fulfilling the request and delivering the response.

0cc4c2efd9c7.title: Client–server model
0cc4c2efd9c7.sentence: The client only has to understand the response based on the relevant application protocol, i.e. the content and the formatting of the data for the requested service.

eaa1eb7fecad.title: Client–server model
eaa1eb7fecad.sentence: The language and rules of communication are defined in a communications protocol.

0827a03cbaa9.title: Client–server model
0827a03cbaa9.sentence: To formalize the data exchange even further, the server may implement an application programming interface (API).

d18b85a0377c.title: Client–server model
d18b85a0377c.sentence: The API is an abstraction layer for accessing a service.

41cdcce9c5cd.title: Client–server model
41cdcce9c5cd.sentence: By restricting communication to a specific content format, it facilitates parsing.

50b647d2f0d3.title: Client–server model
50b647d2f0d3.sentence: By abstracting access, it facilitates cross-platform data exchange.

ea2e557e418c.title: Client–server model
ea2e557e418c.sentence: When a bank customer accesses online banking services with a web browser (the client), the client initiates a request to the bank's web server.

136b3c8f725a.title: Client–server model
136b3c8f725a.sentence: The customer's login credentials are compared against a database, and the webserver accesses that database server as a client.

cc05c5851be2.title: Client–server model
cc05c5851be2.sentence: An application server interprets the returned data by applying the bank's business logic and provides the output to the webserver.

94788fc296e3.title: Client–server model
94788fc296e3.sentence: Finally, the webserver returns the result to the client web browser for display.

c7e3770e5c48.title: Client–server model
c7e3770e5c48.sentence: A server may receive requests from many distinct clients in a short period.

c8c44ff2446b.title: Client–server model
c8c44ff2446b.sentence: A computer can only perform a limited number of tasks at any moment, and relies on a scheduling system to prioritize incoming requests from clients to accommodate them.

40e243a9f407.title: Client–server model
40e243a9f407.sentence: To prevent abuse and maximize availability, the server software may limit the availability to clients.

ddcbea3ae80c.title: Client–server model
ddcbea3ae80c.sentence: Denial of service attacks are designed to exploit a server's obligation to process requests by overloading it with excessive request rates.

959c276601e7.title: Client–server model
959c276601e7.sentence: Operations may be performed server-side because they require access to information or functionality that is not available on the client, or because performing such operations on the client side would be slow, unreliable, or insecure.

c81a46e39128.title: Client–server model
c81a46e39128.sentence: Operations may be performed client-side because they require access to information or functionality that is available on the client but not on the server, because the user needs to observe the operations or provide input, or because the server lacks the processing power to perform the operations in a timely manner for all of the clients it serves.

223c4a338e35.title: Client–server model
223c4a338e35.sentence: Additionally, if operations can be performed by the client, without sending data over the network, they may take less time, use less bandwidth, and incur a lesser security risk.

c54030175ad4.title: Client–server model
c54030175ad4.sentence: In the client-server model, the server is often designed to operate as a centralized system that serves many clients.

e00703fb8809.title: Client–server model
e00703fb8809.sentence: The computing power, memory and storage requirements of a server must be scaled appropriately to the expected workload.

87d9a4561652.title: Client–server model
87d9a4561652.sentence: Load-balancing and failover systems are often employed to scale the server beyond a single physical machine.

b8617ab4f9d4.title: Client–server model
b8617ab4f9d4.sentence: In a peer-to-peer network, two or more computers (peers) pool their resources and communicate in a decentralized system.

9d3a0bfb3b1d.title: Client–server model
9d3a0bfb3b1d.sentence: Unlike clients in a client-server or client-queue-client network, peers communicate with each other directly.

8fed35975b42.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
8fed35975b42.sentence: The seven abstraction layers of the OSI model can be defined as follows, from top to bottom:

89412755a2a3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
89412755a2a3.sentence: This is the only layer that directly interacts with data from the user.

95d6fd6acac4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
95d6fd6acac4.sentence: But it should be made clear that client software applications are not part of the application layer, rather the application layer is responsible for the protocols and data manipulation that the software relies on to present meaningful data to the user.

bdf8383c3d67.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
bdf8383c3d67.sentence: Application layer protocols include HTTP as well as SMTP.

4deddf502f5f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
4deddf502f5f.sentence: The presentation layer is also called the Translation layer.

11ab8930cc1d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
11ab8930cc1d.sentence: The functions of the presentation layer are translation, encryption/decryption, and compression.

f08ae5fde212.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
f08ae5fde212.sentence: This is the layer responsible for opening and closing communication between the two devices.

7b14a846ab1e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
7b14a846ab1e.sentence: The session layer ensures that the session stays open long enough to transfer all the data being exchanged, and then promptly closes the session in order to avoid wasting resources.

bf2d4f8efeab.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
bf2d4f8efeab.sentence: The session layer also synchronizes data transfer with checkpoints.

de249c66f5d0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
de249c66f5d0.sentence: The transport layer (also known as layer 4) is responsible for end-to-end communication between the two devices.

22793c8137fb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
22793c8137fb.sentence: This includes taking data from the session layer and breaking it up into chunks called segments before sending it to the Network layer (layer 3).

8b3e7fdccc0d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
8b3e7fdccc0d.sentence: It is also responsible for reassembling the segments on the receiving device into data the session layer can consume.

46e7f034ffc6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
46e7f034ffc6.sentence: The network layer is responsible for facilitating data transfer between two different networks.

8be9cc52a18a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
8be9cc52a18a.sentence: The network layer breaks up segments from the transport layer into smaller units, called packets, on the sender's device, and reassembles these packets on the receiving device.

26714f5bcd12.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
26714f5bcd12.sentence: The network layer also finds the best physical path for the data to reach its destination this is known as routing.

edeb7f112f75.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
edeb7f112f75.sentence: The data link layer is very similar to the network layer, except the data link layer facilitates data transfer between two devices on the same network.

d8b1766e7cb5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
d8b1766e7cb5.sentence: The data link layer takes packets from the network layer and breaks them into smaller pieces called frames.

dfffdff5036f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
dfffdff5036f.sentence: This layer includes the physical equipment involved in the data transfer, such as the cables and switches.

0387e3720322.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
0387e3720322.sentence: This is also the layer where the data gets converted into a bit stream, which is a string of 1s and 0s.

b89e45dfb33c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
b89e45dfb33c.sentence: The physical layer of both devices must also agree on a signal convention so that the 1s can be distinguished from the 0s on both devices.

ab11ceea5b41.title: OSI model
ab11ceea5b41.sentence: The transport layer provides the functional and procedural means of transferring variable-length data sequences from a source host to a destination host from one application to another across a network while maintaining the quality-of-service functions.

332de1d7a384.title: OSI model
332de1d7a384.sentence: Transport protocols may be connection-oriented or connectionless.

dbe0c4177205.title: OSI model
dbe0c4177205.sentence: This may require breaking large protocol data units or long data streams into smaller chunks called "segments", since the network layer imposes a maximum packet size called the maximum transmission unit (MTU), which depends on the maximum packet size imposed by all data link layers on the network path between the two hosts.

31a8a669b6f0.title: OSI model
31a8a669b6f0.sentence: The amount of data in a data segment must be small enough to allow for a network-layer header and a transport-layer header.

cb7a19a0d2b8.title: OSI model
cb7a19a0d2b8.sentence: The process of dividing data into segments is called segmentation; it is an optional function of the transport layer.

e71bbc446996.title: OSI model
e71bbc446996.sentence: Some connection-oriented transport protocols, such as TCP and the OSI connection-oriented transport protocol (COTP), perform segmentation and reassembly of segments on the receiving side; connectionless transport protocols, such as UDP and the OSI connectionless transport protocol (CLTP), usually do not.

de288c71c791.title: OSI model
de288c71c791.sentence: The transport layer also controls the reliability of a given link between a source and destination host through flow control, error control, and acknowledgments of sequence and existence.

d4de77ae7b52.title: OSI model
d4de77ae7b52.sentence: Some protocols are state- and connection-oriented.

58c5aa0f9ba1.title: OSI model
58c5aa0f9ba1.sentence: This means that the transport layer can keep track of the segments and retransmit those that fail delivery through the acknowledgment handshake system.

d72765a19b1b.title: OSI model
d72765a19b1b.sentence: Reliability, however, is not a strict requirement within the transport layer.

8bc3d6297bef.title: OSI model
8bc3d6297bef.sentence: Protocols like UDP, for example, are used in applications that are willing to accept some packet loss, reordering, errors or duplication.

d1b4f4abb73c.title: OSI model
d1b4f4abb73c.sentence: Although not developed under the OSI Reference Model and not strictly conforming to the OSI definition of the transport layer, the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) of the Internet Protocol Suite are commonly categorized as layer 4 protocols within OSI.

7f336b3546f3.title: OSI model
7f336b3546f3.sentence: Transport Layer Security (TLS) does not strictly fit inside the model either.

948841452513.title: OSI model
948841452513.sentence: It contains characteristics of the transport and presentation layers.

cd60b33d2d9e.title: Internet Protocol

0ce5c8c0c8ed.title: Transmission Control Protocol

31f42ac3aeb1.title: Transmission Control Protocol
31f42ac3aeb1.sentence: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is one of the main protocols of the Internet protocol suite, providing reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of octets (bytes) between applications running on hosts communicating via an IP network.

b7918e4dad2e.title: Transmission Control Protocol
b7918e4dad2e.sentence: TCP is connection-oriented, meaning that sender and receiver first need to establish a connection based on agreed parameters; they do this through a three-way handshake procedure.

98f6b5253a6c.title: Transmission Control Protocol
98f6b5253a6c.sentence: TCP is a reliable byte stream delivery service that guarantees that all bytes received will be identical and in the same order as those sent.

e776c4ef11fc.title: Transmission Control Protocol
e776c4ef11fc.sentence: At the lower levels of the protocol stack, due to network congestion, traffic load balancing, or unpredictable network behavior, IP packets may be lost, duplicated, or delivered out of order.

760db7d58ad1.title: Transmission Control Protocol
760db7d58ad1.sentence: TCP detects these problems, requests re-transmission of lost data, rearranges out-of-order data and even helps minimize network congestion to reduce the occurrence of the other problems.

0351b6d0432b.title: Transmission Control Protocol
0351b6d0432b.sentence: At the transport layer, TCP handles all handshaking and transmission details and presents an abstraction of the network connection to the application, typically through a network socket interface.

a96d6beee35d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a96d6beee35d.sentence: Thus, TCP abstracts the application's communication from the underlying networking details.

3e05c99ebd69.title: Transmission Control Protocol
3e05c99ebd69.sentence: Transmission Control Protocol accepts data from a data stream, divides it into chunks, and adds a TCP header, creating a TCP segment.

dc3649aecf3d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
dc3649aecf3d.sentence: The TCP segment is then encapsulated into an Internet Protocol (IP) datagram, and exchanged with peers.

2ac158f3b150.title: Transmission Control Protocol
2ac158f3b150.sentence: The three-way handshake (active open), retransmission, and error detection add to reliability but lengthen latency.

9a50add4371d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
9a50add4371d.sentence: TCP is optimized for accurate delivery rather than timely delivery and can incur relatively long delays (on the order of seconds) while waiting for out-of-order messages or re-transmissions of lost messages.

bc5f3600ee99.title: Transmission Control Protocol
bc5f3600ee99.sentence: Therefore, it is not particularly suitable for real-time applications such as voice over IP.

5955087564dd.title: Transmission Control Protocol
5955087564dd.sentence: Major internet applications such as the World Wide Web, email, remote administration, file transfer and streaming media rely on TCP, which is part of the transport layer of the TCP/IP suite.

bcd54a40a12b.title: Transmission Control Protocol
bcd54a40a12b.sentence: SSL/TLS often runs on top of TCP.

576d823b78fe.title: Transmission Control Protocol
576d823b78fe.sentence: Applications that do not require reliable data stream service may use the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) instead, which provides a connectionless datagram service that prioritizes time over reliability.

377b032a9301.title: Transmission Control Protocol
377b032a9301.sentence: Once the passive open is established, a client may establish a connection by initiating an active open using the three-way (or 3-step) handshake:

72600a21d838.title: Transmission Control Protocol
72600a21d838.sentence: The connection termination phase uses a four-way handshake, with each side of the connection terminating independently.

a8a51807a76e.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a8a51807a76e.sentence: Before a client attempts to connect with a server, the server must first bind to and listen at a port to open it up for connections; this is called a passive open.

565e2f3faab2.title: Transmission Control Protocol
565e2f3faab2.sentence: - SYN: The active open is performed by the client sending a SYN to the server.

3e0c5881deab.title: Transmission Control Protocol
3e0c5881deab.sentence: The client sets the segment's sequence number to a random value x.

4f3e128df1bf.title: Transmission Control Protocol
4f3e128df1bf.sentence: - SYN-ACK: In response, the server replies with a SYN-ACK.

a60e906962f5.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a60e906962f5.sentence: The acknowledgment number is set to one more than the received sequence number, i.e., x + 1, and the sequence number that the server chooses for the packet is another random number, y.

fd4fc55c868c.title: Transmission Control Protocol
fd4fc55c868c.sentence: - ACK: Finally, the client sends an ACK back to the server.

58a79804f0a0.title: Transmission Control Protocol
58a79804f0a0.sentence: The sequence number is set to the received acknowledgment value, i.e., x + 1, and the acknowledgment number is set to one more than the received sequence number, i.e., y + 1.

239fb3ad908c.title: Transmission Control Protocol
239fb3ad908c.sentence: Following the completion of these steps, both the client and server have received acknowledgments and a full-duplex communication is established.

b489d4b42597.title: Transmission Control Protocol
b489d4b42597.sentence: TCP's three-way handshake introduces one RTT of latency during connection establishment before data can be sent.

d42226e04053.title: Transmission Control Protocol
d42226e04053.sentence: For short flows, these delays are very significant.

32e14e9eb648.title: Transmission Control Protocol
32e14e9eb648.sentence: When an endpoint wishes to stop its half of the connection, it transmits a FIN packet, which the other end acknowledges with an ACK.

d6211c86138e.title: Transmission Control Protocol
d6211c86138e.sentence: Therefore, a typical tear-down requires a pair of FIN and ACK segments from each TCP endpoint.

76ab78e40097.title: Transmission Control Protocol
76ab78e40097.sentence: After the side that sent the first FIN has responded with the final ACK, it waits for a timeout before finally closing the connection, during which time the local port is unavailable for new connections; this state lets the TCP client resend the final acknowledgment to the server in case the ACK is lost in transit.

365858b23eb4.title: Transmission Control Protocol
365858b23eb4.sentence: The time duration is implementation-dependent, but some common values are 30 seconds, 1 minute, and 2 minutes.

a5185395449d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a5185395449d.sentence: If the host actively closes a connection while still having unread incoming data available, the host sends the signal RST (losing any received data) instead of FIN.

450c02ca5794.title: Transmission Control Protocol
450c02ca5794.sentence: This assures that a TCP application is aware there was a data loss.

0bc53373225c.sentence: HTTPS extends HTTP and uses encryption for secure communications.

d3f4b03c6653.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-8-popular-network-protocols-in-1-diagram.md

38ac4f04e15d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-8-popular-network-protocols-in-1-diagram.md
38ac4f04e15d.sentence: Applications, like online gaming, stock trading, and messaging apps leverage WebSocket for real-time communication.

c26419847819.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-8-popular-network-protocols-in-1-diagram.md

3028a7de9648.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-8-popular-network-protocols-in-1-diagram.md
3028a7de9648.sentence: FTP is used to transfer computer files between client and server.

52d227c54370.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-8-popular-network-protocols-in-1-diagram.md
52d227c54370.sentence: It has separate connections for the control channel and data channel.

4b38ebb528cd.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-8-popular-network-protocols-in-1-diagram.md
4b38ebb528cd.sentence: Many application-layer protocols build on top of TCP.

a303895988c0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-8-popular-network-protocols-in-1-diagram.md
a303895988c0.sentence: It runs on QUIC, a new transport protocol designed for mobile-heavy internet usage.
