6dc2bcc85881.sentence: It relies on UDP instead of TCP, which enables faster web page responsiveness.

d6d86ffa9887.title: Internet Protocol
d6d86ffa9887.sentence: The Internet Protocol (IP) is the network layer communications protocol in the Internet protocol suite for relaying datagrams across network boundaries.

47b30f1e5540.title: Internet Protocol
47b30f1e5540.sentence: IP has the task of delivering packets from the source host to the destination host solely based on the IP addresses in the packet headers.

fffb2b9125b9.title: Internet Protocol
fffb2b9125b9.sentence: For this purpose, IP defines packet structures that encapsulate the data to be delivered.

407faf4731d3.title: Internet Protocol
407faf4731d3.sentence: It also defines addressing methods that are used to label the datagram with source and destination information.

0bded02ee882.title: Internet Protocol
0bded02ee882.sentence: Each datagram has two components: a header and a payload.

0ee8a8dd2064.title: Internet Protocol
0ee8a8dd2064.sentence: The IP header includes a source IP address, a destination IP address, and other metadata needed to route and deliver the datagram.

61c4e2aba5aa.title: Internet Protocol
61c4e2aba5aa.sentence: The payload is the data that is transported.

0897833383d2.title: Internet Protocol
0897833383d2.sentence: The address space is divided into subnets, involving the designation of network prefixes.

e2bd59ff88d5.title: Internet Protocol
e2bd59ff88d5.sentence: IP addressing entails the assignment of IP addresses and associated parameters to host interfaces.

4b6d7ac46987.title: Internet Protocol
4b6d7ac46987.sentence: IP routing is performed by all hosts, as well as routers, whose main function is to transport packets across network boundaries.

41ad9e36ea6f.title: Internet Protocol
41ad9e36ea6f.sentence: Routers communicate with one another via specially designed routing protocols, either interior gateway protocols or exterior gateway protocols, as needed for the topology of the network.

3d1d9f85c1ec.title: Internet Protocol
3d1d9f85c1ec.sentence: Its routing function enables internetworking, and essentially establishes the Internet.

c20dae27af3f.title: Internet Protocol
c20dae27af3f.sentence: The first major version of IP, Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4), is the dominant protocol of the Internet.

f5304abedccd.title: Internet Protocol
f5304abedccd.sentence: Its successor is Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6), which has been in increasing deployment on the public Internet since around 2006.

bb3b1502b019.title: IP address
bb3b1502b019.sentence: An Internet Protocol address (IP address) is a numerical label, such as 192.168.1.1 or 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334, that is assigned to a device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.

294507cbe531.title: IP address
294507cbe531.sentence: IP addresses serve two main functions: network interface identification, and location addressing.

e2396578cf0f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
e2396578cf0f.sentence: The internet needs a way to differentiate between different computers, routers, and websites.

427ee79910e2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
427ee79910e2.sentence: In essence, IP addresses are the identifier that allows information to be sent between devices on a network.

5dfa89e6c01a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
5dfa89e6c01a.sentence: IP addresses provide a way of doing so and form an essential part of how the internet works.

4767113bc706.title: IP address
4767113bc706.sentence: The IP address space is managed globally by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) and the five regional Internet registries (RIRs).

cd3d2c990c00.title: IP address
cd3d2c990c00.sentence: IANA assigns blocks of IP addresses to the RIRs, which are responsible for distributing them to local Internet registries in their region, such as internet service providers (ISPs) and large institutions.

e90fb47f6f00.title: IP address
e90fb47f6f00.sentence: An IPv4 address has a size of 32 bits, which limits the address space to 4294967296 (232) addresses.

6c0f907820db.title: IP address
6c0f907820db.sentence: Of this number, some addresses are reserved for special purposes such as private networks (≈18 million addresses) and multicast addressing (≈270 million addresses).

e7054a91011b.title: IP address
e7054a91011b.sentence: IPv4 addresses are usually represented in dot-decimal notation, consisting of four decimal numbers, each ranging from 0 to 255, separated by dots, e.g., 192.0.2.1.

ad46a7047337.title: IP address
ad46a7047337.sentence: Each part represents a group of 8 bits (an octet) of the address.

eb3acaa573f3.title: IP address
eb3acaa573f3.sentence: A host may use geolocation to deduce the geographic position of its communicating peer.

a35eb3d001ca.title: IP address
a35eb3d001ca.sentence: This is typically done by retrieving geolocation info about the IP address of the other node from a database.

9161620733d2.title: User Datagram Protocol
9161620733d2.sentence: In computer networking, the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is one of the core communication protocols of the Internet protocol suite used to send messages (transported as datagrams in packets) to other hosts on an Internet Protocol (IP) network.

a8bc340cf764.title: User Datagram Protocol
a8bc340cf764.sentence: UDP is a connectionless protocol, meaning that messages are sent without performing a handshake or otherwise establishing a shared connection, and each host is not expected to keep track of what it has sent.

574497121dcf.title: User Datagram Protocol
574497121dcf.sentence: Within an IP network, UDP does not require prior communication to set up communication channels or data paths.

683244eca270.title: User Datagram Protocol
683244eca270.sentence: UDP provides checksums for data integrity, and port numbers for addressing different functions at the source and destination of the datagram.

ce4dc471892f.title: User Datagram Protocol
ce4dc471892f.sentence: It does not make any guarantee of successful delivery, indicate the original ordering, or detect duplication, thus exposing the user's program to any unreliability of the underlying network.

645e50a93fd2.title: User Datagram Protocol
645e50a93fd2.sentence: It also provides no feedback to the sender.

3daab7a311ab.title: User Datagram Protocol
3daab7a311ab.sentence: If transmission reliability is desired, it must be implemented in the user's application.

89fcb5e36829.title: User Datagram Protocol
89fcb5e36829.sentence: If using UDP, the end-user applications must provide any necessary handshaking, such as real-time confirmation that the message has been received.

ff7a1a72fee9.title: User Datagram Protocol
ff7a1a72fee9.sentence: A UDP datagram consists of a datagram header followed by a data section (the payload data for the application).

9851197b9706.title: User Datagram Protocol
9851197b9706.sentence: The UDP datagram header consists of 4 fields, each of which is 2 bytes (16 bits):

95e63c95d721.title: User Datagram Protocol
95e63c95d721.sentence: This field is optional in IPv4, and mandatory in most cases in IPv6.

1eb3db041459.title: User Datagram Protocol
1eb3db041459.sentence: The field size sets a theoretical limit of 65,535 bytes (8-byte header + 65,527 bytes of data) for a UDP datagram.

a60842fcbdf2.title: User Datagram Protocol
a60842fcbdf2.sentence: However, the actual limit for the data length, which is imposed by the underlying IPv4 protocol, is 65,507 bytes (65,535 bytes − 8-byte UDP header − 20-byte IP header).

5ce0046756d9.title: User Datagram Protocol
5ce0046756d9.sentence: - Broadcasts – being connectionless, UDP can broadcast - sent packets can be addressed to be receivable by all devices on the subnet.

9777b2153077.title: User Datagram Protocol
9777b2153077.sentence: - Multicast – a multicast mode of operation is supported whereby a single datagram packet can be automatically routed without duplication to a group of subscribers.

5a62177e25c0.title: Transmission Control Protocol
5a62177e25c0.sentence: Port numbers are used to identify different services and to allow multiple connections between hosts.

1d0d2d6b261e.title: Transmission Control Protocol
1d0d2d6b261e.sentence: A TCP connection is identified by a four-tuple of the source address, source port, destination address, and destination port.

7ce87c292ec6.title: Transmission Control Protocol
7ce87c292ec6.sentence: TCP uses 16-bit port numbers, providing 65,536 possible values for each of the source and destination ports.

550aabc3a098.title: Transmission Control Protocol
550aabc3a098.sentence: Port numbers are categorized into three basic categories: well-known, registered, and dynamic or private.

185200b1fa09.title: Transmission Control Protocol
185200b1fa09.sentence: The well-known ports are assigned by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) and are typically used by system-level processes.

57a8390826e8.title: Transmission Control Protocol
57a8390826e8.sentence: Some examples include: FTP (20 and 21), SSH (22), Telnet (23), SMTP (25), HTTP over SSL/TLS (443), and HTTP (80).

2271ab3bea94.title: Transmission Control Protocol
2271ab3bea94.sentence: Registered ports (1024–49151) may be assigned to specific services by third-party developers, but some operating systems also allocate ephemeral client ports from this range.

aedbcf2b257c.title: Transmission Control Protocol
aedbcf2b257c.sentence: Dynamic or private ports (49152–65535) are not associated with any registered services and are commonly used exclusively as ephemeral ports for temporary client connections.

d60531161283.title: Transmission Control Protocol
d60531161283.sentence: Network Address Translation (NAT) typically uses dynamic port numbers on the public-facing side to disambiguate the flow of traffic that is passing between a public network and a private subnetwork, thereby allowing many IP addresses (and their ports) on the subnet to be serviced by a single public-facing address.

39df8b9273b3.title: Transmission Control Protocol
39df8b9273b3.sentence: The dependency of connection identity on addresses means that TCP connections are bound to a single network path; TCP cannot use other routes that multihomed hosts have available, and connections break if an endpoint's address changes.

98d94d2fe26f.title: User Datagram Protocol
98d94d2fe26f.sentence: An application binds a socket to its endpoint of data transmission, which is a combination of an IP address and a port.

cc64036461ec.title: User Datagram Protocol
cc64036461ec.sentence: In this way, UDP provides application multiplexing.

0f0592c58af9.title: User Datagram Protocol
0f0592c58af9.sentence: Port numbers 0 through 1023 are used for common, well-known services.

5cd1f68e2a89.title: User Datagram Protocol
5cd1f68e2a89.sentence: Port 0 is reserved, but is a permissible source port value if the sending process does not expect messages in response.

0b5f4417acb8.title: User Datagram Protocol
0b5f4417acb8.sentence: On Unix-like operating systems, using one of these ports requires superuser operating permission.

71b73a5035cb.title: Network socket
71b73a5035cb.sentence: A network socket is a software structure within a network node of a computer network that serves as an endpoint for sending and receiving data across the network.

82254ffac0fd.title: Network socket
82254ffac0fd.sentence: In this context, a socket is externally identified to other hosts by its socket address, which is the 3-tuple of transport protocol, IP address, and port number.

11bab80ed2bd.title: Network socket
11bab80ed2bd.sentence: The structure and properties of a socket are defined by an application programming interface (API) for the networking architecture.

d0b8f52ce142.title: Network socket
d0b8f52ce142.sentence: Sockets are created only during the lifetime of a process of an application running in the node.

1134b0dcafac.title: Network socket
1134b0dcafac.sentence: The application programming interface (API) for the network protocol stack creates a handle for each socket created by an application, commonly referred to as a socket descriptor.

ab3377a606f6.title: Network socket
ab3377a606f6.sentence: In Unix-like operating systems, this descriptor is a type of file descriptor.

6917225ab6f4.title: Network socket
6917225ab6f4.sentence: In the standard Internet protocols TCP and UDP, a socket address is the combination of an IP address and a port number, much like one end of a telephone connection is the combination of a phone number and a particular extension.

8a04ecc5e487.title: Network socket
8a04ecc5e487.sentence: Based on this address, Internet sockets deliver incoming data packets to the appropriate application process.

f7f930a359dc.title: Network socket
f7f930a359dc.sentence: An application can communicate with a remote process by exchanging data with TCP/IP by knowing the combination of protocol type, IP address, and port number.

9f3e0f80a114.title: Network socket
9f3e0f80a114.sentence: The operating system forwards the payload of incoming IP packets to the corresponding application by extracting the socket address information from the IP and transport protocol headers and stripping the headers from the application data.

347ecd1f2fba.title: Network socket
347ecd1f2fba.sentence: The application programming interface (API) that programs use to communicate with the protocol stack, using network sockets, is called a socket API.

a87b5ef1b8b5.title: Network socket
a87b5ef1b8b5.sentence: Internet socket APIs are usually based on the Berkeley sockets standard.

dfee1274249c.title: Network socket
dfee1274249c.sentence: A stream socket provides a sequenced and unique flow of error-free data without record boundaries, with well-defined mechanisms for creating and destroying connections and reporting errors.

580cf23d0427.title: Network socket
580cf23d0427.sentence: A stream socket transmits data reliably, in order, and with out-of-band capabilities.

39a9d0b418a6.title: Network socket
39a9d0b418a6.sentence: On the Internet, stream sockets are typically implemented using TCP so that applications can run across any network using TCP/IP protocol.

db56590239dc.title: Network socket
db56590239dc.sentence: Connectionless sockets, which use User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

0805ff016b6a.title: Network socket
0805ff016b6a.sentence: Each packet sent or received on a datagram socket is individually addressed and routed.

0f9ad6c5f79a.title: Network socket
0f9ad6c5f79a.sentence: Order and reliability are not guaranteed with datagram sockets, so multiple packets sent from one machine or process to another may arrive in any order or might not arrive at all.

312367609c96.title: Network socket
312367609c96.sentence: Allow direct sending and receiving of IP packets without any protocol-specific transport layer formatting.

65c487e9e6d8.title: Network socket
65c487e9e6d8.sentence: With other types of sockets, the payload is automatically encapsulated according to the chosen transport layer protocol (e.g. TCP, UDP), and the socket user is unaware of the existence of protocol headers that are broadcast with the payload.

ff578a2912e2.title: Network socket
ff578a2912e2.sentence: When reading from a raw socket, the headers are usually included.

32dd2166a538.title: Network socket
32dd2166a538.section: Socket states in the client-server model
32dd2166a538.sentence: Computer processes that provide application services are referred to as servers, and create sockets on startup that are in the listening state.

90fc0554db7b.title: Network socket
90fc0554db7b.section: Socket states in the client-server model
90fc0554db7b.sentence: These sockets are waiting for initiatives from client programs.

0e8fdec43d13.title: Network socket
0e8fdec43d13.section: Socket states in the client-server model
0e8fdec43d13.sentence: A TCP server may serve several clients concurrently by creating a unique dedicated socket for each client connection in a new child process or processing thread for each client.

a76c0c46803c.title: Network socket
a76c0c46803c.section: Socket states in the client-server model
a76c0c46803c.sentence: A server may create several concurrently established TCP sockets with the same local port number and local IP address, each mapped to its own server-child process, serving its own client process.

f8beaa26e0e0.title: Network socket
f8beaa26e0e0.section: Socket states in the client-server model
f8beaa26e0e0.sentence: They are treated as different sockets by the operating system since the remote socket address (the client IP address or port number) is different; i.e., since they have different socket pair tuples.

cc1cb505e98a.title: Network socket
cc1cb505e98a.sentence: Local and remote sockets communicating over TCP are called socket pairs.

ba63a706108f.title: Network socket
ba63a706108f.sentence: Each socket pair is described by a unique 4-tuple consisting of source and destination IP addresses and port numbers, i.e. of local and remote socket addresses.

852338dba02a.title: Network socket
852338dba02a.section: Socket states in the client-server model
852338dba02a.sentence: UDP sockets do not have an established state, because the protocol is connectionless.

22da90abba95.title: Network socket
22da90abba95.section: Socket states in the client-server model
22da90abba95.sentence: A UDP server process handles incoming datagrams from all remote clients sequentially through the same socket.

c048e6139508.title: Network socket
c048e6139508.section: Socket states in the client-server model
c048e6139508.sentence: UDP sockets are not identified by the remote address, but only by the local address, although each message has an associated remote address that can be retrieved from each datagram with the networking application programming interface (API).

de96688c8f4a.title: Network socket
de96688c8f4a.sentence: However, stateful network firewalls, network address translators, and proxy servers keep track of active socket pairs.

42a9fa324fbf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
42a9fa324fbf.sentence: The transition from Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) to Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) is primarily driven by the need for more internet addresses, alongside the desire to streamline certain aspects of network management.

aa32b60697ce.title: IP address
aa32b60697ce.sentence: IPv4 addresses are defined as a 32-bit number, which later became too small to provide enough addresses as the internet grew, leading to IPv4 address exhaustion over the 2010s.

eab6d6fa6df7.title: IP address
eab6d6fa6df7.sentence: Its designated successor, IPv6, uses 128 bits for the IP address, giving it a larger address space.

0c1766f39656.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
0c1766f39656.sentence: IPv4 uses a 32-bit address format, which is typically displayed as four decimal numbers separated by dots (e.g., 192.168.0.12).

f7c1b3bcb546.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
f7c1b3bcb546.sentence: The 32-bit format allows for approximately 4.3 billion unique addresses, a number that is rapidly proving insufficient due to the explosion of internet-connected devices.

07b6137dca3c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
07b6137dca3c.sentence: In contrast, IPv6 utilizes a 128-bit address format, represented by eight groups of four hexadecimal digits separated by colons (e.g., 50B3:F200:0211:AB00:0123:4321:6571:B000).

5ff4622cea9b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
5ff4622cea9b.sentence: This expansion allows for approximately much more addresses, ensuring the internet's growth can continue unabated.

27dc675c025e.title: IP address
27dc675c025e.sentence: By the early 1990s, the rapid exhaustion of IPv4 address space available for assignment to Internet service providers and end-user organizations prompted the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) to explore new technologies to expand addressing capability on the Internet.

0d2fcf4a1836.title: IP address
0d2fcf4a1836.sentence: The result was a redesign of the Internet Protocol, which eventually became known as Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) in 1995.

f9ca1b60ce50.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
f9ca1b60ce50.sentence: The IPv4 header is more complex and includes fields such as the header length, service type, total length, identification, flags, fragment offset, time to live (TTL), protocol, header checksum, source and destination IP addresses, and options.

72eb91db1c5b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
72eb91db1c5b.sentence: IPv6 headers are designed to be simpler and more efficient.

22a4fa76cc4e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
22a4fa76cc4e.sentence: The fixed header size is 40 bytes and includes less frequently used fields in optional extension headers.

41c7786a9cea.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
41c7786a9cea.sentence: This simplification helps improve packet processing speeds.

f71680a6c095.title: IP address
f71680a6c095.sentence: Today, these two versions of the Internet Protocol are in simultaneous use.

134170ed6069.title: IP address
134170ed6069.sentence: Among other technical changes, each version defines the format of addresses differently.

b59a8a0ce330.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
b59a8a0ce330.sentence: - Dual Stack: This technique involves running IPv4 and IPv6 simultaneously on the same network devices.

ee157852b586.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
ee157852b586.sentence: It allows seamless communication in both protocols, depending on the destination address availability and compatibility.

7929c4891e39.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
7929c4891e39.sentence: The dual stack is considered one of the best approaches for the smooth transition from IPv4 to IPv6.

a8c953250cb3.title: IP address
a8c953250cb3.sentence: In IPv6, the address size was increased from 32 bits in IPv4 to 128 bits, thus providing up to 2128 (approximately 3.403×10^38) addresses.

1bc70405467c.title: IP address
1bc70405467c.sentence: This is deemed sufficient for the foreseeable future.

10067465e4b9.title: IP address
10067465e4b9.sentence: The intent of the new design was not to provide just a sufficient quantity of addresses, but also to redesign routing in the Internet by allowing more efficient aggregation of subnetwork routing prefixes.

efdb2802c6b8.title: IP address
efdb2802c6b8.sentence: This resulted in slower growth of routing tables in routers.

ce73062cfa16.title: User Datagram Protocol
ce73062cfa16.sentence: Transmission Control Protocol is a connection-oriented protocol and requires handshaking to set up end-to-end communications.

cbf4ddcf1330.title: User Datagram Protocol
cbf4ddcf1330.sentence: User Datagram Protocol is a simpler message-based connectionless protocol.

6c60647fa126.title: User Datagram Protocol
6c60647fa126.sentence: Once a connection is set up, user data may be sent bidirectionally over the connection.

7ebe9b8ece0d.title: User Datagram Protocol
7ebe9b8ece0d.sentence: - Reliable – TCP manages message acknowledgment, retransmission and timeouts.

15cb56554bfc.title: User Datagram Protocol
15cb56554bfc.sentence: If data gets lost along the way, it will be resent.

f728d435d3ac.title: User Datagram Protocol
f728d435d3ac.sentence: In TCP, there is either no missing data or, in case of multiple timeouts, the connection is dropped.

c1d36add6f48.title: User Datagram Protocol
c1d36add6f48.sentence: - Ordered – If two messages are sent over a connection in sequence, the first message will reach the receiving application first.

e5e8807e3266.title: User Datagram Protocol
e5e8807e3266.sentence: When data segments arrive in the wrong order, TCP buffers the out-of-order data until all data can be properly reordered and delivered to the application.

92743fa111cd.title: User Datagram Protocol
92743fa111cd.sentence: - Streaming – Data is read as a byte stream; no distinguishing indications are transmitted to signal message (segment) boundaries.

47413d138296.title: User Datagram Protocol
47413d138296.sentence: - Heavyweight – TCP requires three packets to set up a socket connection before any user data can be sent.

19fec1a1d40e.title: User Datagram Protocol
19fec1a1d40e.sentence: TCP handles reliability and congestion control.

a02ef2a0dd02.title: User Datagram Protocol
a02ef2a0dd02.sentence: Connectionless protocols do not set up a dedicated end-to-end connection.

22afcf404af9.title: User Datagram Protocol
22afcf404af9.sentence: Communication is achieved by transmitting information in one direction from source to destination without verifying the readiness or state of the receiver.

50f5bf588473.title: User Datagram Protocol
50f5bf588473.sentence: - Unreliable – When a UDP message is sent, it cannot be known if it will reach its destination; it could get lost along the way.

feff2700d612.title: User Datagram Protocol
feff2700d612.sentence: There is no concept of acknowledgment, retransmission, or timeout.

98ef212dc501.title: User Datagram Protocol
98ef212dc501.sentence: - Not ordered – If two messages are sent to the same recipient, the order in which they arrive cannot be guaranteed.

91476688b164.title: User Datagram Protocol
91476688b164.sentence: - Lightweight – There is no ordering of messages, no tracking connections, etc. It is a very simple transport layer designed on top of IP.

2d8a0fa4ccc7.title: User Datagram Protocol
2d8a0fa4ccc7.sentence: - Datagrams – Packets are sent individually and are checked for integrity on arrival.

cb9d92ee5418.title: User Datagram Protocol
cb9d92ee5418.sentence: Packets have definite boundaries, which are honored upon receipt; a read operation at the receiver socket will yield an entire message as it was originally sent.

324ff08363e6.title: User Datagram Protocol
324ff08363e6.sentence: - No congestion control – UDP itself does not avoid congestion.

b1f2cd49bd32.title: User Datagram Protocol
b1f2cd49bd32.sentence: Congestion control measures must be implemented at the application level or in the network.

03edb1121a7f.title: User Datagram Protocol
03edb1121a7f.sentence: Time-sensitive applications often use UDP because dropping packets is preferable to waiting for packets delayed due to retransmission; having such delays may not be an option in a real-time system.

57d5973cf7e7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-4-most-popular-use-cases-for-udp.md
57d5973cf7e7.sentence: Many VoIP and video conferencing applications leverage UDP due to its lower overhead and ability to tolerate packet loss.

7229f2a17578.title: User Datagram Protocol
7229f2a17578.sentence: - It is transaction-oriented, suitable for simple query-response protocols such as the Domain Name System or the Network Time Protocol.

9b0920cc8a06.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-4-most-popular-use-cases-for-udp.md
9b0920cc8a06.sentence: Real-time communication benefits from UDP's reduced latency compared to TCP.

98f459078200.title: User Datagram Protocol
98f459078200.sentence: Streaming media, real-time multiplayer games and voice over IP (VoIP) are typical applications that leverage UDP.

34c26291665b.title: User Datagram Protocol
34c26291665b.sentence: In these particular applications, loss of packets is not usually a fatal problem.

7c86307323ba.title: User Datagram Protocol
7c86307323ba.sentence: In VoIP, for example, latency and jitter are the primary concerns.

388d9f383627.title: User Datagram Protocol
388d9f383627.sentence: Real-time video and audio streaming protocols are designed to handle the occasional lost packets, so only slight degradation in quality occurs, compared to the large delays that would occur if lost packets were retransmitted.

549e25dec997.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-4-most-popular-use-cases-for-udp.md
549e25dec997.sentence: DNS (Domain Name Service) queries typically use UDP for their fast and lightweight nature.

1bf9a4f02830.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-4-most-popular-use-cases-for-udp.md
1bf9a4f02830.sentence: Although DNS can also use TCP for large responses or zone transfers, most queries are handled via UDP.

bf47fcec7e47.title: User Datagram Protocol
bf47fcec7e47.sentence: - It is stateless, suitable for very large numbers of clients, such as in streaming media applications like IPTV.

5f7157114423.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-4-most-popular-use-cases-for-udp.md
5f7157114423.sentence: In low-latency trading, UDP is utilized for efficient market data delivery to multiple recipients simultaneously.

bead8ba7d2b2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-4-most-popular-use-cases-for-udp.md
bead8ba7d2b2.sentence: UDP is often used in IoT devices for communications, sending small packets of data between devices.

e6db2b8bd82f.title: User Datagram Protocol
e6db2b8bd82f.sentence: QUIC is a transport protocol built on top of UDP.

27745a06f39a.title: User Datagram Protocol
27745a06f39a.sentence: QUIC provides a reliable and secure connection.

013f347e43a4.title: User Datagram Protocol
013f347e43a4.sentence: HTTP/3 uses QUIC as opposed to earlier versions of HTTPS which use a combination of TCP and TLS to ensure reliability and security respectively.

623695e440a3.title: User Datagram Protocol
623695e440a3.sentence: This means that HTTP/3 uses a single handshake to set up a connection, rather than having two separate handshakes for TCP and TLS, meaning the overall time to establish a connection is reduced.

a67aa4ad0879.title: Internet Protocol
a67aa4ad0879.sentence: As a consequence of this design, the Internet Protocol only provides best-effort delivery and its service is characterized as unreliable.

494b88dbd674.title: Internet Protocol
494b88dbd674.sentence: In network architectural parlance, it is a connectionless protocol, in contrast to connection-oriented communication.

c73b3aa8ef49.title: Internet Protocol
c73b3aa8ef49.sentence: The upper layer protocols of the Internet protocol suite are responsible for resolving reliability issues.

bed768eb3612.title: Internet Protocol
bed768eb3612.sentence: The design of the Internet protocol suite adheres to the end-to-end principle, a concept adapted from the CYCLADES project.

f3f2d1859f31.title: Internet Protocol
f3f2d1859f31.sentence: Under the end-to-end principle, the network infrastructure is considered inherently unreliable at any single network element or transmission medium and is dynamic in terms of the availability of links and nodes.

92bcb999308b.title: Internet Protocol
92bcb999308b.sentence: For the benefit of reducing network complexity, the intelligence in the network is located in the end nodes.

93172bb6396e.title: Internet Protocol
93172bb6396e.sentence: Various fault conditions may occur, such as data corruption, packet loss and duplication.

a9175638818d.title: Internet Protocol
a9175638818d.sentence: All fault conditions in the network must be detected and compensated for by the participating end nodes.

44beea6d7e6d.title: Internet Protocol
44beea6d7e6d.sentence: Because routing is dynamic, meaning every packet is treated independently, and because the network maintains no state based on the path of prior packets, different packets may be routed to the same destination via different paths, resulting in out-of-order delivery to the receiver.

54b7eec69e29.title: Internet Protocol
54b7eec69e29.sentence: For example, a host may buffer network data to ensure correct ordering before the data is delivered to an application.

8166f13bb2e3.title: Internet Protocol
8166f13bb2e3.sentence: IPv4 provides safeguards to ensure that the header of an IP packet is error-free.

ffefb1149850.title: Internet Protocol
ffefb1149850.sentence: A routing node discards packets that fail a header checksum test.

e447e1ca5e90.title: Internet Protocol
e447e1ca5e90.sentence: Although the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) provides notification of errors, a routing node is not required to notify either end node of errors.

d8b9211f6dc3.title: Internet Protocol
d8b9211f6dc3.sentence: IPv6, by contrast, operates without header checksums, since current link layer technology is assumed to provide sufficient error detection.

96320f6c55fc.title: Transmission Control Protocol
96320f6c55fc.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
96320f6c55fc.sentence: TCP uses a sequence number to identify each byte of data.

edbee49f30a7.title: Transmission Control Protocol
edbee49f30a7.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
edbee49f30a7.sentence: Acknowledgments (ACKs) are sent with a sequence number by the receiver of data to tell the sender that data has been received up to the specified byte.

3149215765e8.title: Transmission Control Protocol
3149215765e8.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
3149215765e8.sentence: Reliability is achieved by the sender detecting lost data and retransmitting it.

5fb5a0725494.title: Transmission Control Protocol
5fb5a0725494.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
5fb5a0725494.sentence: The sequence number identifies the order of the bytes sent from each computer so that the data can be reconstructed in order, regardless of any out-of-order delivery that may occur.

7f300a163bef.title: Transmission Control Protocol
7f300a163bef.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
7f300a163bef.sentence: The sequence number of the first byte is chosen by the transmitter for the first packet, which is flagged SYN.

cdd8f1d5da63.title: Transmission Control Protocol
cdd8f1d5da63.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Error detection
cdd8f1d5da63.sentence: Sequence numbers allow receivers to discard duplicate packets and properly sequence out-of-order packets.

df3a56f8c19d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
df3a56f8c19d.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Error detection
df3a56f8c19d.sentence: Acknowledgments allow senders to determine when to retransmit lost packets.

f72ff55f300a.title: Transmission Control Protocol
f72ff55f300a.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
f72ff55f300a.sentence: ACKs do not imply that the data has been delivered to the application; they merely signify that it is now the receiver's responsibility to deliver the data.

70c263b50c45.title: Transmission Control Protocol
70c263b50c45.sentence: Since packet transfer by many networks is not reliable, TCP achieves this using a technique known as positive acknowledgment with re-transmission.

817c2f4874e7.title: Transmission Control Protocol
817c2f4874e7.sentence: The sender keeps a record of each packet it sends and maintains a timer from when the packet was sent.

2492aaf082e8.title: Transmission Control Protocol
2492aaf082e8.sentence: The sender re-transmits a packet if the timer expires before receiving the acknowledgment.

307d0f7a2acc.title: Transmission Control Protocol
307d0f7a2acc.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
307d0f7a2acc.sentence: TCP uses two primary techniques to identify loss.

b9d0a392e247.title: Transmission Control Protocol
b9d0a392e247.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
b9d0a392e247.sentence: Retransmission timeout (RTO) and duplicate cumulative acknowledgments (DupAcks).

774c238fa946.title: Transmission Control Protocol
774c238fa946.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission > Duplicate-ACK-based retransmission
774c238fa946.sentence: If a single segment (say segment number 100) in a stream is lost, then the receiver cannot acknowledge packets above that segment number (100) because it uses cumulative ACKs.

be9ba9f9b35c.title: Transmission Control Protocol
be9ba9f9b35c.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission > Duplicate-ACK-based retransmission
be9ba9f9b35c.sentence: Hence, the receiver acknowledges packet 99 again upon receipt of another data packet.

cbc107c8bddf.title: Transmission Control Protocol
cbc107c8bddf.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission > Duplicate-ACK-based retransmission
cbc107c8bddf.sentence: This duplicate acknowledgement is used as a signal for packet loss.

bad2494515f3.title: Transmission Control Protocol
bad2494515f3.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission > Duplicate-ACK-based retransmission
bad2494515f3.sentence: That is, if the sender receives three duplicate acknowledgments, it retransmits the last unacknowledged packet.

775a304c2494.title: Transmission Control Protocol
775a304c2494.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission > Duplicate-ACK-based retransmission
775a304c2494.sentence: A threshold of three is used because the network may reorder segments, causing duplicate acknowledgements.

4bb6bc9808b3.title: Transmission Control Protocol
4bb6bc9808b3.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission > Timeout-based retransmission
4bb6bc9808b3.sentence: When a sender transmits a segment, it initializes a timer with a conservative estimate of the arrival time of the acknowledgment.

cc0056ec50a2.title: Transmission Control Protocol
cc0056ec50a2.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission > Timeout-based retransmission
cc0056ec50a2.sentence: The segment is retransmitted if the timer expires, with a new timeout threshold of twice the previous value, resulting in exponential backoff behavior.

7c8e932efd3d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
7c8e932efd3d.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
7c8e932efd3d.sentence: TCP uses an end-to-end flow control protocol to avoid having the sender send data too fast for the TCP receiver to receive and process it reliably.

21b96793ba23.title: Transmission Control Protocol
21b96793ba23.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
21b96793ba23.sentence: Having a mechanism for flow control is essential in an environment where machines of diverse network speeds communicate.

a5902c1ef168.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a5902c1ef168.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
a5902c1ef168.sentence: For example, if a PC sends data to a smartphone that is slowly processing received data, the smartphone must be able to regulate the data flow so as not to be overwhelmed.

2fed72e97817.title: Transmission Control Protocol
2fed72e97817.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
2fed72e97817.sentence: TCP uses a sliding window flow control protocol.

afdb4c02e2a2.title: Transmission Control Protocol
afdb4c02e2a2.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
afdb4c02e2a2.sentence: In each TCP segment, the receiver specifies in the receive window field the amount of additionally received data (in bytes) that it is willing to buffer for the connection.

20e43182b0fa.title: Transmission Control Protocol
20e43182b0fa.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
20e43182b0fa.sentence: The sending host can send only up to that amount of data before it must wait for an acknowledgment and receive window update from the receiving host.

03d99f569fc8.title: Transmission Control Protocol
03d99f569fc8.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
03d99f569fc8.sentence: When a receiver advertises a window size of 0, the sender stops sending data and starts its persist timer.

55c542694eaf.title: Transmission Control Protocol
55c542694eaf.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
55c542694eaf.sentence: The persist timer is used to protect TCP from a deadlock situation that could arise if a subsequent window size update from the receiver is lost, and the sender cannot send more data until receiving a new window size update from the receiver.

201bea5983db.title: Transmission Control Protocol
201bea5983db.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
201bea5983db.sentence: When the persist timer expires, the TCP sender attempts recovery by sending a small packet so that the receiver responds by sending another acknowledgment containing the new window size.

a84d5e864d7f.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a84d5e864d7f.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
a84d5e864d7f.sentence: If a receiver is processing incoming data in small increments, it may repeatedly advertise a small receive window.

3cba116e33d5.title: Transmission Control Protocol
3cba116e33d5.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Flow control
3cba116e33d5.sentence: This is referred to as the silly window syndrome, since it is inefficient to send only a few bytes of data in a TCP segment, given the relatively large overhead of the TCP header.

bbb8a762db93.title: Transmission Control Protocol
bbb8a762db93.sentence: A 16-bit TCP window size field controls the flow of data, and its value is limited to 65,535 bytes.

a026d2167b3b.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a026d2167b3b.sentence: The TCP window scale option, as defined in RFC 1323, is an option used to increase the maximum window size to 1 gigabyte.

b4ed89656e08.title: Transmission Control Protocol
b4ed89656e08.sentence: For more efficient use of high-bandwidth networks, a larger TCP window size may be used.

f3b6948a0c0c.title: Transmission Control Protocol
f3b6948a0c0c.sentence: The window scale option is used only during the TCP 3-way handshake.

f8fb777f038d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
f8fb777f038d.sentence: Both sides must send the option in their SYN segments to enable window scaling in either direction.

beba3bb72fa2.title: Transmission Control Protocol
beba3bb72fa2.sentence: The window scale value can be set from 0 (no shift) to 14 for each direction independently.

970880d282bc.title: Internet Protocol
970880d282bc.sentence: There are four principal addressing methods in the Internet Protocol:

16e5922febb1.title: Internet Protocol
16e5922febb1.sentence: - Unicast delivers a message to a single specific node using a one-to-one association between a sender and destination: each destination address uniquely identifies a single receiver endpoint.

9e1ae3f8144f.title: Internet Protocol
9e1ae3f8144f.sentence: - Broadcast delivers a message to all nodes in the network using a one-to-all association; a single datagram (or packet) from one sender is routed to all of the possibly multiple endpoints associated with the broadcast address.

77b43d2c790f.title: Internet Protocol
77b43d2c790f.sentence: - Multicast delivers a message to a group of nodes that have expressed interest in receiving the message using a one-to-many-of-many or many-to-many-of-many association; datagrams are routed simultaneously in a single transmission to many recipients.

796a8b217790.title: Internet Protocol
796a8b217790.sentence: - Anycast delivers a message to any one out of a group of nodes, typically the one nearest to the source using a one-to-one-of-many association where datagrams are routed to any single member of a group of potential receivers that are all identified by the same destination address.

35bde30ad31c.title: Internet Protocol
35bde30ad31c.sentence: The network automatically replicates datagrams as needed to reach all the recipients within the scope of the broadcast, which is generally an entire network subnet.

4ad7ad152208.title: Internet Protocol
4ad7ad152208.sentence: Multicast differs from broadcast in that the destination address designates a subset, not necessarily all, of the accessible nodes.

7243de6527f0.title: Internet Protocol
7243de6527f0.sentence: The routing algorithm selects the single receiver from the group based on which is the nearest according to some distance or cost measure.

c7cd56636605.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/unicast-vs-broadcast-vs-multicast-vs-anycast.md
c7cd56636605.sentence: Used in protocols such as HTTP, FTP, and SMTP.

3a3383d83264.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/unicast-vs-broadcast-vs-multicast-vs-anycast.md
3a3383d83264.sentence: Used in Address Resolution Protocol, DHCP, and NTP

eca17c9b55d9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/unicast-vs-broadcast-vs-multicast-vs-anycast.md
eca17c9b55d9.sentence: However, it doesn’t mean that every receiver gets the message.

a1459422ce5a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/unicast-vs-broadcast-vs-multicast-vs-anycast.md
a1459422ce5a.sentence: Used in IPTV and video conference applications.

9db0fecbc0a1.sentence: Used in DNS querying and CDNs.

312a1cd6c1aa.title: IP address
312a1cd6c1aa.sentence: Sending the same data to multiple unicast addresses requires the sender to send all the data many times over, once for each recipient.

22362577a4e3.title: IP address
22362577a4e3.sentence: In either case, the sender sends a single datagram from its unicast address to the multicast group address, and the intermediary routers take care of making copies and sending them to all interested receivers (those that have joined the corresponding multicast group).

d961a75fe78b.title: Internet Protocol
d961a75fe78b.sentence: One of the technical constraints is the size of data packets possible on a given link.

d8585bb0592a.title: Internet Protocol
d8585bb0592a.sentence: Facilities exist to examine the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size of the local link and Path MTU Discovery can be used for the entire intended path to the destination.

a242f3b34edf.title: Internet Protocol
a242f3b34edf.sentence: The IPv4 internetworking layer automatically fragments a datagram into smaller units for transmission when the link MTU is exceeded.

3e232497c4b1.title: Internet Protocol
3e232497c4b1.sentence: IP provides reordering of fragments received out of order.

930aacd75a42.title: Internet Protocol
930aacd75a42.sentence: An IPv6 network does not perform fragmentation in network elements, but requires end hosts and higher-layer protocols to avoid exceeding the path MTU.

a4f8ead4ae7c.title: Internet Protocol
a4f8ead4ae7c.sentence: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is an example of a protocol that adjusts its segment size to be smaller than the MTU.

2a942b239ae7.title: Internet Protocol
2a942b239ae7.sentence: The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) and ICMP disregard MTU size, thereby forcing IP to fragment oversized datagrams.

5fa6aee22f95.title: Transmission Control Protocol
5fa6aee22f95.sentence: The maximum segment size (MSS) is the largest amount of data, specified in bytes, that TCP is willing to receive in a single segment.

586d9caacfb4.title: Transmission Control Protocol
586d9caacfb4.sentence: For best performance, the MSS should be set small enough to avoid IP fragmentation, which can lead to packet loss and excessive retransmissions.

ac23e12bf647.title: OSI model
ac23e12bf647.sentence: For example, for data being transferred across Ethernet, the MTU is 1500 bytes, the minimum size of a TCP header is 20 bytes, and the minimum size of an IPv4 header is 20 bytes, so the maximum segment size is 1500−(20+20) bytes, or 1460 bytes.

256265b0aebe.title: OSI model
256265b0aebe.sentence: If the message is too large to be transmitted from one node to another on the data link layer between those nodes, the network may implement message delivery by splitting the message into several fragments at one node, sending the fragments independently, and reassembling the fragments at another node.

5572538af28d.title: Maximum transmission unit
5572538af28d.sentence: A larger MTU brings greater efficiency because each network packet carries more user data while protocol overheads, such as headers or underlying per-packet delays, remain fixed; the resulting higher efficiency means an improvement in bulk protocol throughput.

8444be302cce.title: Maximum transmission unit
8444be302cce.sentence: A larger MTU also requires processing of fewer packets for the same amount of data.

b84aac426e01.title: Maximum transmission unit
b84aac426e01.sentence: Large packets occupy a link for more time than a smaller packet, causing greater delays to subsequent packets, and increasing network delay and delay variation.

f0d6106177d6.title: Maximum transmission unit
f0d6106177d6.sentence: Their greater payload makes retransmissions of larger packets take longer.

5a20de5419f7.title: Maximum transmission unit
5a20de5419f7.sentence: All fragments of a packet must arrive for the packet to be considered received.

5e206bc073ab.title: Maximum transmission unit
5e206bc073ab.sentence: If the network drops any fragment, the entire packet is lost.

7977c5ca6ed6.title: Maximum transmission unit
7977c5ca6ed6.sentence: The addition is small, but each packet now has to be sent in two fragments, the second of which carries very little payload.

d7e3ef14c16d.title: Maximum transmission unit
d7e3ef14c16d.sentence: The same amount of payload is being moved, but every intermediate router has to forward twice as many packets.

8ef3bd10373a.title: TCP congestion control
8ef3bd10373a.sentence: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) uses one of several congestion control algorithms that include various aspects of an additive increase/multiplicative decrease (AIMD) scheme, along with other schemes including slow start and a congestion window (CWND), to achieve congestion avoidance.

455ec5f8fc52.title: Transmission Control Protocol
455ec5f8fc52.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Congestion control
455ec5f8fc52.sentence: Modern implementations of TCP contain four intertwined algorithms: slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery.

81a6bb7db442.title: Transmission Control Protocol
81a6bb7db442.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Congestion control
81a6bb7db442.sentence: These mechanisms control the rate of data entering the network, keeping the data flow below a rate that would trigger collapse.

0da88f360641.title: Transmission Control Protocol
0da88f360641.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Congestion control
0da88f360641.sentence: TCP uses a number of mechanisms to achieve high performance and avoid congestive collapse, a gridlock situation where network performance is severely degraded.

6f2be8961b5b.title: TCP congestion control
6f2be8961b5b.sentence: To avoid congestive collapse, TCP uses a multi-faceted congestion-control strategy.

936880cef16a.title: TCP congestion control
936880cef16a.sentence: Per the end-to-end principle, congestion control is largely a function of internet hosts, not the network itself.

32f1fb310fad.title: Transmission Control Protocol
32f1fb310fad.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Congestion control
32f1fb310fad.sentence: Acknowledgments for data sent, or the lack of acknowledgments, are used by senders to infer network conditions between the TCP sender and receiver.

7f670123c72d.title: Transmission Control Protocol
7f670123c72d.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Congestion control
7f670123c72d.sentence: Coupled with timers, TCP senders and receivers can alter the behavior of the flow of data.

e0d54c09cb1a.title: Transmission Control Protocol
e0d54c09cb1a.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Congestion control
e0d54c09cb1a.sentence: In addition, senders employ a retransmission timeout (RTO) that is based on the estimated round-trip time (RTT) between the sender and receiver, as well as the variance in this round-trip time.

c2b0bd101b32.title: TCP congestion control
c2b0bd101b32.sentence: For each connection, TCP maintains a CWND, limiting the total number of unacknowledged packets that may be in transit end-to-end.

d42f744a1b30.title: TCP congestion control
d42f744a1b30.sentence: The congestion window is maintained by the sender and is a means of preventing a link between the sender and the receiver from becoming overloaded with too much traffic.

822cdc8eef53.title: TCP congestion control
822cdc8eef53.sentence: This should not be confused with the sliding window maintained by the sender, which exists to prevent the receiver from becoming overloaded.

d5f8107b49e0.title: TCP congestion control
d5f8107b49e0.sentence: A sender can send data less than its own congestion window and the receive window.

1ac870eeb6ab.title: TCP congestion control
1ac870eeb6ab.sentence: AIMD combines linear growth of the congestion window with an exponential reduction when congestion occurs.

69275ecdcbfc.title: TCP congestion control
69275ecdcbfc.sentence: Multiple flows using AIMD congestion control will eventually converge to use equal amounts of a contended link.

271d77d8bc9b.title: TCP congestion control
271d77d8bc9b.sentence: Slow start begins initially with a congestion window size (CWND) of 1, 2, 4 or 10 MSS.

6e763a1f8c95.title: TCP congestion control
6e763a1f8c95.sentence: The value for the congestion window size can be increased by 1 MSS with each acknowledgment (ACK) received, effectively doubling the window size each RTT.

5b20746649b7.title: TCP congestion control
5b20746649b7.sentence: The transmission rate will be increased by the slow-start algorithm until either a packet loss is detected, the receiver's advertised window (rwnd) becomes the limiting factor, or slow start threshold (ssthresh) is reached, which is used to determine whether the slow start or congestion avoidance algorithm is used, a value set to limit slow start.

99347a3e6ae8.title: TCP congestion control
99347a3e6ae8.sentence: If the CWND reaches ssthresh, TCP switches to the congestion avoidance algorithm.

665c6c6dc2a4.title: TCP congestion control
665c6c6dc2a4.sentence: It should be increased by up to 1 MSS for each RTT.

2158cb9ff765.title: TCP congestion control
2158cb9ff765.sentence: When a loss occurs, retransmission is sent, half of the current CWND is saved as ssthresh and slow start begins again from its initial CWND.

f83bbc1ca0b6.title: TCP congestion control
f83bbc1ca0b6.sentence: When a sender receives three duplicate acknowledgments, it can be reasonably confident that the segment carrying the data that followed the last in-order byte specified in the acknowledgment was lost.

0ab0835c7854.title: TCP congestion control
0ab0835c7854.sentence: A sender with fast retransmit will then retransmit this packet immediately without waiting for its timeout.

e97fc9b7bf4f.title: TCP congestion control
e97fc9b7bf4f.sentence: A fast retransmit is sent, half of the current CWND is saved as ssthresh and as the new value for CWND, thus skipping slow start and going directly to the congestion avoidance algorithm.

488369a5e905.title: TCP congestion control
488369a5e905.sentence: The overall algorithm here is called fast recovery.

d758be341f37.title: Transmission Control Protocol
d758be341f37.sentence: TCP was originally designed for wired networks where packet loss is considered to be the result of network congestion and the congestion window size is reduced dramatically as a precaution.

855268ade977.title: Transmission Control Protocol
855268ade977.sentence: However, wireless links are known to experience sporadic and usually temporary losses due to fading, shadowing, handover, interference, and other radio effects that are not strictly congestion.

f888ebccda62.title: Transmission Control Protocol
f888ebccda62.sentence: This causes the radio link to be underused.

05f5c792f8cc.title: TCP congestion control
05f5c792f8cc.sentence: Thus, slow start can perform poorly in situations with poor reception, such as wireless networks.

2a373b912a5a.title: TCP congestion control
2a373b912a5a.sentence: The slow start protocol also performs badly for short-lived connections.

22a55f8c98cd.title: TCP congestion control
22a55f8c98cd.sentence: To avoid this problem, modern browsers either open multiple connections simultaneously or reuse one connection for all files requested from a particular web server.

c0659c0102ff.title: Address Resolution Protocol
c0659c0102ff.sentence: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is a communication protocol for discovering the link layer address, such as a MAC address, associated with an internet layer address, typically an IPv4 address.

76af778f2afc.title: Address Resolution Protocol
76af778f2afc.sentence: ARP enables a host to send, for example, an IPv4 packet to another node in the local network by providing a protocol to get the MAC address associated with an IP address.

bc2f1f65132d.title: Address Resolution Protocol
bc2f1f65132d.sentence: The host broadcasts a request containing the target node's IP address, and the node with that IP address replies with its MAC address.

9da6759b54fb.title: Address Resolution Protocol
9da6759b54fb.sentence: The Address Resolution Protocol is a request–response protocol.

969388f828e6.title: Address Resolution Protocol
969388f828e6.sentence: Its messages are directly encapsulated by a link-layer protocol.

cb9865c39493.title: Address Resolution Protocol
cb9865c39493.sentence: It is communicated within the boundaries of a single subnetwork and is never routed.

542d8d687f7a.title: Address Resolution Protocol
542d8d687f7a.sentence: Before sending the packet to B, A broadcasts an ARP request message – addressed with the broadcast MAC address FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF and requesting response from the node with IP address 192.168.0.55.

a80454053da8.title: Address Resolution Protocol
a80454053da8.sentence: All nodes of the network receive the message, but only B replies since it has the requested IP address.

78d77aa9f70a.title: Address Resolution Protocol
78d77aa9f70a.sentence: B responds with an ARP response message containing its MAC addresses which A receives.

7f62acf814b5.title: Address Resolution Protocol
7f62acf814b5.sentence: A sends the data packet on the link addressed with B's MAC address.

e0390bca24ab.title: Address Resolution Protocol
e0390bca24ab.sentence: Typically, a network node maintains a lookup cache that associates IP and MAC addresses.

ad6ababf1c41.title: Address Resolution Protocol
ad6ababf1c41.sentence: In this example, if A had the lookup cached, then it would not need to broadcast the ARP request.

45d42d3f3e75.title: Address Resolution Protocol
45d42d3f3e75.sentence: Also, when B received the request, it could cache the lookup to A so that if B needs to send a packet to A later, it does not need to use ARP to look up its MAC address.

a16772cd32aa.title: Address Resolution Protocol
a16772cd32aa.sentence: Before beginning to use an IPv4 address (whether received from manual configuration, DHCP, or some other means), a host implementing this specification must test to see if the address is already in use, by broadcasting ARP probe packets.

09814d287ead.title: Address Resolution Protocol
09814d287ead.sentence: This is useful for updating other hosts' mappings of a hardware address when the sender's IP address or MAC address changes.

9ec793a5c153.title: Address Resolution Protocol
9ec793a5c153.sentence: An ARP announcement is not intended to solicit a reply; instead, it updates any cached entries in the ARP tables of other hosts that receive the packet.

2f79a4f951ce.title: Address Resolution Protocol
2f79a4f951ce.sentence: Because ARP does not provide methods for authenticating ARP replies on a network, ARP replies can come from systems other than the one with the required Layer 2 address.

042769b45fd4.title: Address Resolution Protocol
042769b45fd4.sentence: By contrast, in ARP spoofing the answering system, or spoofer, replies to a request for another system's address with the aim of intercepting data bound for that system.

0d28b87a8cd3.title: Address Resolution Protocol
0d28b87a8cd3.sentence: A malicious user may use ARP spoofing to perform a man-in-the-middle or denial-of-service attack on other users on the network.

894f15714df8.title: Address Resolution Protocol
894f15714df8.sentence: An ARP proxy is a system that answers the ARP request on behalf of another system for which it will forward traffic, normally as a part of the network's design, such as for a dial-up internet service.

40d47d903cee.title: Address Resolution Protocol
40d47d903cee.sentence: In Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) networks, the functionality of ARP is provided by the Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP).

3c94ff775aca.title: Address Resolution Protocol
3c94ff775aca.sentence: ARP's placement within the Internet protocol suite and the OSI model may be a matter of confusion or even of dispute.

6bae4afdbb9d.title: Address Resolution Protocol
6bae4afdbb9d.sentence: RFC 826 places it into the link layer and characterizes it as a tool to inquire about the "higher level layer", such as the Internet layer.

0fac5147f174.title: Address Resolution Protocol
0fac5147f174.sentence: RFC 1122 also discusses ARP in its link layer section.

f40af793a44f.title: Address Resolution Protocol
f40af793a44f.sentence: Richard Stevens places ARP in the OSI's data link layer while newer editions associate it with the network layer or introduce an intermediate OSI layer 2.5.

0b7e92801613.title: Transmission Control Protocol
0b7e92801613.sentence: As TCP provides applications with the abstraction of a reliable byte stream, it can suffer from head-of-line blocking: if packets are reordered or lost and need to be retransmitted (and thus are reordered), data from sequentially later parts of the stream may be received before sequentially earlier parts of the stream; however, the later data cannot typically be used until the earlier data has been received, incurring network latency.

ce10d1392073.title: Transmission Control Protocol
ce10d1392073.sentence: The application cannot normally access the packets coming after a lost packet until the retransmitted copy of the lost packet is received.

97304568df96.title: Transmission Control Protocol
97304568df96.sentence: If multiple independent higher-level messages are encapsulated and multiplexed onto a single TCP connection, then head-of-line blocking can cause processing of a fully received message that was sent later to wait for delivery of a message that was sent earlier.

29af3143039f.title: Transmission Control Protocol
29af3143039f.sentence: Web browsers attempt to mitigate head-of-line blocking by opening multiple parallel connections.

f6f351e2da1b.title: Transmission Control Protocol
f6f351e2da1b.sentence: This incurs the cost of connection establishment repeatedly, as well as multiplying the resources needed to track those connections at the endpoints.

7339c2d2334e.title: Transmission Control Protocol
7339c2d2334e.sentence: Parallel connections also have congestion control operating independently of each other, rather than being able to pool information together and respond more promptly to observed network conditions; TCP's aggressive initial sending patterns can cause congestion if multiple parallel connections are opened; and the per-connection fairness model leads to a monopolization of resources by applications that take this approach.

7853c3c18bd0.title: QUIC
7853c3c18bd0.sentence: QUIC (/kwɪk/) is a general-purpose transport layer network protocol initially designed by Jim Roskind at Google.

663247910b20.title: QUIC
663247910b20.sentence: It does this by establishing a number of multiplexed connections between two endpoints using User Datagram Protocol (UDP), and it is designed to obsolete TCP at the transport layer for many applications.

9603339e36ac.title: QUIC
9603339e36ac.sentence: Based on | IP, normally layered with UDP

e05e2d8384f7.title: QUIC
e05e2d8384f7.sentence: As most HTTP connections will demand TLS, QUIC makes the exchange of setup keys and listing of supported protocols part of the initial handshake process.

2e12704807e8.title: QUIC
2e12704807e8.sentence: In most implementations, TCP will see any error on a connection as a blocking operation, stopping further transfers until the error is resolved or the connection is considered failed.

306260fc2527.title: QUIC
306260fc2527.sentence: If a single connection is being used to send multiple streams of data, as is the case in the HTTP/2 protocol, all of these streams are blocked although only one of them might have a problem.

83431807a18b.title: QUIC
83431807a18b.sentence: This phenomenon is known as head-of-line blocking.

ac2d30de8cab.title: QUIC
ac2d30de8cab.sentence: The second change is to use UDP rather than TCP as its basis, which does not include loss recovery.

124c5dc8b45e.title: QUIC
124c5dc8b45e.sentence: Instead, each QUIC stream is separately flow-controlled, and lost data is retransmitted at the level of QUIC, not UDP.

3fd77a5ca2cc.title: QUIC
3fd77a5ca2cc.sentence: This means that if an error occurs in one stream, like the favicon example above, the protocol stack can continue servicing other streams independently.

8204ea17e103.title: QUIC
8204ea17e103.sentence: This eliminates the need to set up an unencrypted pipe and then negotiate the security protocol as separate steps.

1fc24d6d3825.title: QUIC
1fc24d6d3825.sentence: In the context of supporting encrypted HTTP traffic, QUIC serves a role similar to that of TCP, but with reduced latency during connection setup and more efficient loss recovery when multiple HTTP streams are multiplexed over a single connection.

db28af615796.title: QUIC
db28af615796.sentence: For instance, the packets are encrypted individually, so that they do not result in the encrypted data waiting for partial packets.

4b87bf442c06.title: QUIC
4b87bf442c06.sentence: This is not generally possible under TCP, where the encryption records are in a bytestream and the protocol stack is unaware of higher-layer boundaries within this stream.

8a21155507bd.title: QUIC
8a21155507bd.sentence: Another goal of the QUIC system was to improve performance during network-switching events, like what happens when a user of a mobile device moves from a local Wi-Fi hotspot to a mobile network.

672677d32795.title: QUIC
672677d32795.sentence: When this occurs on TCP, a lengthy process starts where every existing connection times out one-by-one and is then re-established on demand.

c524aabdc891.title: QUIC
c524aabdc891.sentence: To solve this problem, QUIC includes a connection identifier to uniquely identify the connection to the server regardless of source.

f2832c399304.title: QUIC
f2832c399304.sentence: This allows the connection to be re-established simply by sending a packet, which always contains this ID, as the original connection ID will still be valid even if the user's IP address changes.

fc649474613b.title: QUIC
fc649474613b.sentence: QUIC can be implemented in the application space, as opposed to being in the operating system kernel.

5e5b0eef37fe.title: QUIC
5e5b0eef37fe.sentence: This organization allows future changes to be made more easily as it does not require changes to the kernel for updates.

5d50aa32db27.title: QUIC
5d50aa32db27.sentence: It also moves congestion control algorithms into the user space at both endpoints, rather than the kernel space, which is claimed to allow these algorithms to improve more rapidly.

d0629a908e90.title: QUIC
d0629a908e90.sentence: One concern about the move from TCP to UDP is that TCP is widely adopted and many of the "middleboxes" in the Internet infrastructure are tuned for TCP and rate-limit or even block UDP.

d4648e52eb77.title: QUIC
d4648e52eb77.sentence: This led to the use of a system for rapid fallback to TCP; Chromium's network stack starts both a QUIC and a conventional TCP connection at the same time, which allows it to fall back with negligible latency.

9742ab47a0d4.title: QUIC
9742ab47a0d4.sentence: QUIC has been specifically designed to be deployable and evolvable and to have anti-ossification properties; it is the first IETF transport protocol to deliberately minimise its wire image for these ends.

0701b5a5805e.title: QUIC
0701b5a5805e.sentence: In May 2021, the IETF standardized QUIC in RFC 9000, supported by RFC 8999, 9001 and 9002.

2bc8cf8d471d.title: QUIC
2bc8cf8d471d.sentence: In contrast, the IETF QUIC protocol has been redeveloped as a general-purpose transport protocol that uses standard TLS 1.3 for its cryptographic handshake and incorporates a modular packet and connection design intended for broader interoperability.

8b84d9f72f4b.title: QUIC
8b84d9f72f4b.sentence: QUIC was developed with HTTP in mind, and HTTP/3 was its first application.

05870a8871df.title: QUIC
05870a8871df.sentence: DNS-over-QUIC is an application of QUIC to name resolution, providing security for data transferred between resolvers similar to DNS-over-TLS.

6dea4e4ef0fb.title: QUIC
6dea4e4ef0fb.sentence: Another application is SMB over QUIC, which, according to Microsoft, can offer an "SMB VPN" without affecting the user experience.

4f6de1fba160.title: IP address
4f6de1fba160.sentence: A public IP address is a globally routable unicast IP address, meaning that the address is not an address reserved for use in private networks, such as those reserved by RFC 1918, or the various IPv6 address formats of local scope or site-local scope, for example, for link-local addressing.

9e80c7775586.title: IP address
9e80c7775586.sentence: Public IP addresses may be used for communication between hosts on the global Internet.

826ffd553ec2.title: IP address
826ffd553ec2.sentence: Some addresses are reserved for private networks and are not globally unique.

fa70f7f84081.title: IP address
fa70f7f84081.sentence: In a home situation, a public IP address is the IP address assigned to the home's network by the ISP.

649c2b8fd41b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
649c2b8fd41b.sentence: A public IP address is an address where one primary address is associated with your whole network.

a2fbf22de02c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
a2fbf22de02c.sentence: In this type of IP address, each of the connected devices has the same IP address.

1a413af37299.title: IP address
1a413af37299.sentence: Three non-overlapping ranges of IPv4 addresses for private networks are reserved.

edc331ee1fe3.title: IP address
edc331ee1fe3.sentence: These addresses are not routed on the Internet, and thus their use need not be coordinated with an IP address registry.

9fe089b6af73.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
9fe089b6af73.sentence: A private IP address is a unique IP number assigned to every device that connects to your internet network, which includes devices like computers, tablets, and smartphones, which are used in your household.

703acd04db46.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
703acd04db46.sentence: Example: IP addresses generated by your home router for your devices.

cbf91874b265.title: IP address
cbf91874b265.sentence: Today, such private networks are widely used and typically connect to the Internet with network address translation (NAT), when needed.

478f26e51b14.title: IP address
478f26e51b14.sentence: However, it was found that this was not always necessary as private networks developed and public address space needed to be conserved.

68778bd55b35.title: Network address translation
68778bd55b35.sentence: Network address translation (NAT) is a method of mapping an IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets while they are in transit across a traffic routing device.

d1d105a2778c.title: Network address translation
d1d105a2778c.sentence: One Internet-routable IP address of a NAT gateway can be used for an entire private network.

dad736a33ae0.title: IP address
dad736a33ae0.sentence: The NAT device maps different IP addresses on the private network to different TCP or UDP port numbers on the public network.

3af4a8b91abb.title: Network address translation
3af4a8b91abb.sentence: Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) uses 32-bit addresses, capable of uniquely addressing about 4.3 billion devices on the network.

db6bbcedc021.title: Network address translation
db6bbcedc021.sentence: It is a popular and essential tool in conserving global address space in the face of IPv4 address exhaustion.

bfc6135f05b9.title: Network address translation
bfc6135f05b9.sentence: The simplest type of NAT provides a one-to-one translation of IP addresses (RFC 1631).

75c51f728fe2.title: Network address translation
75c51f728fe2.sentence: In this type of NAT, only the IP addresses, IP header checksum, and any higher-level checksums that include the IP address are changed.

e40c9d1eed71.title: Network address translation
e40c9d1eed71.sentence: Most network address translators map multiple private hosts to one publicly exposed IP address.

6a22a373d63e.title: Network address translation
6a22a373d63e.sentence: This is the most common type of NAT and has become synonymous with the term NAT in common usage.

1ad4e97b3468.title: Network address translation
1ad4e97b3468.sentence: The network has a router having network interfaces on both the private and the public networks.

f3523dcd76c3.title: Network address translation
f3523dcd76c3.sentence: The public address is typically assigned by an Internet service provider.

b562a36bd452.title: Network address translation
b562a36bd452.sentence: As traffic passes from the private network to the Internet, NAT translates the source address in each packet from a private address to the router's public address.

e7dc26c1f964.title: Network address translation
e7dc26c1f964.sentence: The NAT facility tracks each active connection.

47c20f818674.title: Network address translation
47c20f818674.sentence: When the router receives inbound traffic from the Internet, it uses the connection tracking data obtained during the outbound phase to determine to which private address it should forward the reply.

eed8135d5da4.title: Network address translation
eed8135d5da4.sentence: For these protocols, the port numbers are changed so that the combination of IP address (within the IP header) and port number (within the Transport Layer header) on the returned packet can be unambiguously mapped to the corresponding private network destination.

21aa417f8d3b.title: Network address translation
21aa417f8d3b.sentence: RFC 2663 uses the term network address and port translation (NAPT) for this type of NAT.

2b7273e0c19e.title: Network address translation
2b7273e0c19e.sentence: Other names include port address translation (PAT), IP masquerading, NAT overload, and many-to-one NAT.

6fe9f369c256.title: Network address translation
6fe9f369c256.sentence: The NAT device then makes an entry in a translation table containing the internal IP address, original source port, and the translated source port.

2dd19cc86e19.title: Network address translation
2dd19cc86e19.sentence: Upon receiving a packet from the external network, the NAT device searches the translation table based on the destination port in the packet header.

7bfc17e156e1.title: Network address translation
7bfc17e156e1.sentence: If a match is found, the destination IP address and port number are replaced with the values found in the table and the packet is forwarded to the inside network.

f93cd17f6f82.title: Network address translation
f93cd17f6f82.sentence: Otherwise, if the destination port number of the incoming packet is not found in the translation table, the packet is dropped or rejected because the PAT device doesn't know where to send it.

1783edb63bd0.title: Network address translation
1783edb63bd0.sentence: This method allows communication through the router only when the conversation originates in the private network, since the initial originating transmission establishes the required information in the translation tables.

82825ccd9d86.title: Network address translation
82825ccd9d86.sentence: Because the internal addresses are all disguised behind one publicly accessible address, it is impossible for external hosts to directly initiate a connection to a particular internal host.

fdcb986b3758.title: Network address translation
fdcb986b3758.sentence: DNAT is commonly used to publish a service located in a private network on a publicly accessible IP address.

a998a0016986.title: Network address translation
a998a0016986.sentence: This use of DNAT is also called port forwarding, or DMZ when used on an entire server, which becomes exposed to the WAN, becoming analogous to an undefended military demilitarized zone (DMZ).

8001027f5ebc.title: Network address translation
8001027f5ebc.sentence: Hosts behind NAT-enabled routers do not have end-to-end connectivity and cannot participate in some internet protocols.

e9645d13241e.title: Network address translation
e9645d13241e.sentence: Some application layer protocols, such as File Transfer Protocol (FTP) and Session Initiation Protocol (SIP), send explicit network addresses within their application data.

240edba44d1e.title: Network address translation
240edba44d1e.sentence: Some protocols can accommodate one instance of NAT between participating hosts ("passive mode" FTP, for example), sometimes with the assistance of an application-level gateway (see § Applications affected by NAT), but fail when both systems are separated from the internet by NAT.

5ac54a753614.title: Network address translation
5ac54a753614.sentence: Applications such as VOIP, videoconferencing, and other peer-to-peer applications must use NAT traversal techniques to function.

ea670b395f67.title: Network address translation
ea670b395f67.sentence: The use of NAT also complicates tunneling protocols such as IPsec because NAT modifies values in the headers, which interfere with the integrity checks done by IPsec and other tunneling protocols.

8418a3e4278d.title: Network address translation
8418a3e4278d.sentence: Network address translation is not commonly used in IPv6 because one of the design goals of IPv6 is to restore end-to-end network connectivity.

02b856b41f0a.title: Network address translation
02b856b41f0a.sentence: The large addressing space of IPv6 obviates the need to conserve addresses and every device can be given a unique globally routable address.

e402e897d311.title: IP address
e402e897d311.sentence: Persistent configuration is also known as using a static IP address.

bb5802aa3d11.title: IP address
bb5802aa3d11.sentence: In contrast, when a computer's IP address is assigned each time it restarts, this is known as using a dynamic IP address.

dcfe10c712ed.title: IP address
dcfe10c712ed.sentence: Dynamic IP addresses are assigned by the network.

dc14b334366b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
dc14b334366b.sentence: A static IP address does not change and is one that was manually created, as opposed to having been assigned.

0b5ccbfb88d2.title: IP address
0b5ccbfb88d2.sentence: Computers and equipment used for the network infrastructure, such as routers and mail servers, are typically configured with static addressing.

8d275fc4596b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
8d275fc4596b.sentence: These addresses are usually more expensive but are more reliable.

cfaa406505ac.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::ip
cfaa406505ac.sentence: Example: They are usually used for important things like reliable geo-location services, remote access, server hosting, etc.

5521957f920f.title: IP address
5521957f920f.sentence: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is the most frequently used technology for assigning addresses.

2db62d629b1e.title: IP address
2db62d629b1e.sentence: It avoids the administrative burden of assigning specific static addresses to each device on a network.

98ab6be7430d.title: IP address
