98ab6be7430d.sentence: It also allows devices to share the limited address space on a network if only some of them are online at a particular time.

fafa17ae5de5.title: IP address
fafa17ae5de5.sentence: The address assigned with DHCP is associated with a lease and usually has an expiration period.

4f48d13dd526.title: IP address
4f48d13dd526.sentence: If the lease is not renewed by the host before expiry, the address may be assigned to another device.

a51c007f8a9e.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
a51c007f8a9e.sentence: The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is a network management protocol used on Internet Protocol (IP) networks for automatically assigning IP addresses and other communication parameters to devices connected to the network using a client–server architecture.

fe663edf4131.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
fe663edf4131.sentence: The technology eliminates the need for individually configuring network devices manually, and consists of two network components, a centrally installed network DHCP server and client instances of the protocol stack on each computer or device.

54885e377ff8.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
54885e377ff8.sentence: The DHCP server manages a pool of IP addresses and information about client configuration parameters such as default gateway, domain name, the name servers, and time servers.

b1b03b7385cc.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
b1b03b7385cc.sentence: Many routers and residential gateways have DHCP server capability.

3219c5cc4dc8.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
3219c5cc4dc8.sentence: The DHCP employs a connectionless service model, using the User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

06a33a90c335.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
06a33a90c335.sentence: The server listens on UDP port number 67, and the client listens on UDP port number 68.

9ccae7b9c026.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
9ccae7b9c026.sentence: When a computer or other device connects to a network, the DHCP client software sends a DHCP broadcast query requesting the necessary information.

773e2d1e02bc.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
773e2d1e02bc.sentence: Depending on implementation, the DHCP server may have three methods of allocating IP addresses:

c71cec58ed3c.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
c71cec58ed3c.sentence: A network administrator reserves a range of IP addresses for DHCP, and each DHCP client on the LAN is configured to request an IP address from the DHCP server during network initialization.

b28b90e73b2a.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
b28b90e73b2a.sentence: The request-and-grant process uses a lease concept with a controllable time period, allowing the DHCP server to reclaim and then reallocate IP addresses that are not renewed.

d8a01d168660.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
d8a01d168660.sentence: The DHCP server permanently assigns an IP address to a requesting client from a range defined by an administrator.

3ac7a870c344.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
3ac7a870c344.sentence: An administrator maps a unique identifier (a client id or MAC address) for each client to an IP address, which is offered to the requesting client.

f8b614afd8f9.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
f8b614afd8f9.sentence: In this case, a DHCP client that has not yet acquired an IP address cannot communicate directly with a DHCP server not on the same subnet, as the client's broadcast can only be received on its own subnet.

6298342437b4.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
6298342437b4.sentence: The DHCP client broadcasts on the local link; the relay agent receives the broadcast and transmits it to one or more DHCP servers using unicast.

a53e535d9e36.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
a53e535d9e36.sentence: The IP addresses of the DHCP servers are manually configured in the relay agent.

c40a2844cc23.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
c40a2844cc23.sentence: The DHCP server uses the GIADDR-value to determine the subnet, and subsequently the corresponding address pool, from which to allocate an IP address.

1416988334ab.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
1416988334ab.sentence: On large networks that consist of multiple links, a single DHCP server may service the entire network when aided by DHCP relay agents located on the interconnecting routers.

f3c2aa17ce84.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
f3c2aa17ce84.sentence: The base DHCP does not include any mechanism for authentication.

c09556363890.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
c09556363890.sentence: Because the client has no way to validate the identity of a DHCP server, unauthorized DHCP servers (commonly called "rogue DHCP") can be operated on networks, providing incorrect information to DHCP clients.

fbe428919d71.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
fbe428919d71.sentence: This can serve either as a denial-of-service attack, preventing the client from gaining access to network connectivity, or as a man-in-the-middle attack.

aede40f8bedc.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
aede40f8bedc.sentence: Because the DHCP server provides the DHCP client with server IP addresses, such as the IP address of one or more DNS servers, an attacker can convince a DHCP client to do its DNS lookups through its own DNS server, and can therefore provide its own answers to DNS queries from the client.

05b534695c0a.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
05b534695c0a.sentence: This also allows DHCP clients to exhaust the DHCP server's store of IP addresses—by presenting new credentials each time it asks for an address, the client can consume all the available IP addresses on a particular network link, preventing other DHCP clients from getting service.

7c0d659fa646.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
7c0d659fa646.sentence: The Relay Agent Information Option protocol extension (usually referred to in the industry by its actual number as Option 82) allows network operators to attach tags to DHCP messages as these messages arrive on the network operator's trusted network.

2b32b9549f7a.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
2b32b9549f7a.sentence: This tag is then used as an authorization token to control the client's access to network resources.

f35b0dafb6c2.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
f35b0dafb6c2.sentence: Another extension, Authentication for DHCP Messages (RFC 3118), provides a mechanism for authenticating DHCP messages.

f179ad925850.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
f179ad925850.sentence: As of 2002, this extension had not seen widespread adoption because of the problems of managing keys for large numbers of DHCP clients.

a35dbb762c61.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
a35dbb762c61.sentence: This fact, combined with the introduction of 802.1X, slowed the deployment and take-rate of authenticated DHCP, and it has never been widely deployed.

402f68955c63.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
402f68955c63.sentence: The challenges of key management and processing delays due to hash computation have been deemed too heavy a price to pay for the perceived benefits.

ff0b3b72a4b1.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
ff0b3b72a4b1.sentence: The IPv6 version of the protocol is designated as DHCPv6.

88c547721b17.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
88c547721b17.sentence: The details of the protocol for IPv4 and IPv6 differ sufficiently that they may be considered separate protocols.

7e4e8a276b7a.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
7e4e8a276b7a.sentence: For the IPv6 operation, devices may alternatively use stateless address autoconfiguration.

820f993ea39a.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
820f993ea39a.sentence: DHCP operations fall into four phases: server discovery, IP lease offer, IP lease request, and IP lease acknowledgement.

fd2e1af30a5d.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
fd2e1af30a5d.sentence: DHCP clients are allocated leases that last for some period of time.

8a50247c1cfe.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
8a50247c1cfe.sentence: The DHCP client broadcasts a DHCPDISCOVER message on the network subnet using the destination address 255.255.255.255 (limited broadcast) or the specific subnet broadcast address (directed broadcast).

d5a0ab07cd52.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
d5a0ab07cd52.sentence: A DHCP client may also request an IP address in the DHCPDISCOVER, which the server may take into account when selecting an address to offer.

174ea6d0a542.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
174ea6d0a542.sentence: When a DHCP server receives a DHCPDISCOVER message from a client, which is an IP address lease request, the DHCP server reserves an IP address for the client and makes a lease offer by sending a DHCPOFFER message to the client.

08937b0d5d6d.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
08937b0d5d6d.sentence: This message may contain the client's Client ID (Option 61, containing a unique value, traditionally a MAC address), the IP address that the server is offering, the subnet mask, the lease duration, and the IP address of the DHCP server making the offer.

6703d731e2fe.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
6703d731e2fe.sentence: In response to the DHCP offer, the client replies with a DHCPREQUEST message, broadcast to the server, requesting the offered address.

3a9651477ee4.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
3a9651477ee4.sentence: A client can receive DHCP offers from multiple servers, but it will accept only one DHCP offer.

ac46bd2bb07d.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
ac46bd2bb07d.sentence: The client must send the server identification option in the DHCPREQUEST message, indicating the server whose offer the client has selected.

3dca5920c7d6.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
3dca5920c7d6.sentence: When other DHCP servers receive this message, they withdraw any offers that they have made to the client and return their offered IP address to the pool of available addresses.

2528d890b9f5.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
2528d890b9f5.sentence: When the DHCP server receives the DHCPREQUEST message from the client, the configuration process enters its final phase.

1528093e1726.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
1528093e1726.sentence: The acknowledgement phase involves sending a DHCPACK packet to the client.

82dbe3b45954.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
82dbe3b45954.sentence: This packet includes the lease duration and any other configuration information that the client might have requested.

97f904d4a422.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
97f904d4a422.sentence: At this point, the IP configuration process is completed.

40b58c841b9c.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
40b58c841b9c.section: Operation > Selecting and configuring IP addresses
40b58c841b9c.sentence: Before claiming an IP address, the client should probe the newly received address (e.g. with ARP), in order to find if there is another host present in the network with the proposed IP address.

133aa6bb6e56.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
133aa6bb6e56.section: Operation > Selecting and configuring IP addresses
133aa6bb6e56.sentence: If there is no reply, this address does not conflict with that of another host, so it is free to be used.

0e2aca51dbcf.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
0e2aca51dbcf.section: Operation > Selecting and configuring IP addresses
0e2aca51dbcf.sentence: When the server is reusing an IP address from its pool, it may first check (using ping) to see if it is not taken already.

24cc53fc3650.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
24cc53fc3650.section: Operation > Selecting and configuring IP addresses
24cc53fc3650.sentence: This may happen if a host is configured manually with an IP address that lies within the DHCP scope.

56fcd65c7999.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
56fcd65c7999.sentence: Clients begin to attempt to renew their leases once half the lease interval has expired.

0ed4a1e4fa53.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
0ed4a1e4fa53.sentence: They do this by sending a unicast DHCPREQUEST message to the DHCP server that granted the original lease.

0316bd418343.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
0316bd418343.sentence: If the DHCP server is unreachable for an extended period of time, the DHCP client will attempt to rebind, by broadcasting its DHCPREQUEST rather than unicasting it.

ea0e9c208a8e.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
ea0e9c208a8e.sentence: Because it is broadcast, the DHCPREQUEST message will reach all available DHCP servers.

c83790449428.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
c83790449428.sentence: When the lease expires, the client must stop using the IP address granted to it in its lease.

7e881f2b87a2.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
7e881f2b87a2.sentence: At that time it will restart the DHCP process from the beginning by broadcasting a DHCPDISCOVER message.

f37b7f938ca2.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
f37b7f938ca2.sentence: However, since its IP address has changed, any ongoing connections will be broken.

a5df68a8d915.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
a5df68a8d915.sentence: The client sends a request to the DHCP server to release the DHCP information and the client deactivates its IP address.

89e3ed71fd46.title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
89e3ed71fd46.sentence: As client devices usually do not know when users may unplug them from the network, the protocol does not mandate the sending of DHCP Release.

56c11ca068ce.title: IP address
56c11ca068ce.sentence: IP networks may be divided into subnetworks in both IPv4 and IPv6.

2105eb635742.title: IP address
2105eb635742.sentence: For this purpose, an IP address is recognized as consisting of two parts: the network prefix in the high-order bits and the remaining bits called the rest field, host identifier, or interface identifier (IPv6), used for host numbering within a network.

cc979c09f96a.title: IP address
cc979c09f96a.sentence: The subnet mask or CIDR notation determines how the IP address is divided into network and host parts.

75277a46adb9.title: IP address
75277a46adb9.sentence: The term subnet mask is only used within IPv4.

1e3ad4a8bf9b.title: IP address
1e3ad4a8bf9b.sentence: Both IP versions, however, use the CIDR concept and notation.

a233e80992bc.title: IP address
a233e80992bc.sentence: In this, the IP address is followed by a slash and the number (in decimal) of bits used for the network part, also called the routing prefix.

2f3306e859f7.title: IP address
2f3306e859f7.sentence: For example, an IPv4 address and its subnet mask may be 192.0.2.1 and 255.255.255.0, respectively.

06b3b957b032.title: IP address
06b3b957b032.sentence: The CIDR notation for the same IP address and subnet is 192.0.2.1/24, because the first 24 bits of the IP address indicate the network and subnet.

c145385aa649.title: rfc>9293
c145385aa649.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.1. Retransmission Timeout
c145385aa649.sentence: Because of the variability of the networks that compose an internetwork system and the wide range of uses of TCP connections, the retransmission timeout (RTO) must be dynamically determined.

8153bcd6df7d.title: rfc>9293
8153bcd6df7d.sentence: Because segments may be lost due to errors (checksum test failure) or network congestion, TCP uses retransmission to ensure delivery of every segment.

5c94dd881f7d.title: rfc>9293
5c94dd881f7d.sentence: Duplicate segments may arrive due to network or TCP retransmission.

977785b9a517.title: rfc>9293
977785b9a517.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.1. Retransmission Timeout
977785b9a517.sentence: The RTO MUST be computed according to the algorithm in, including Karn's algorithm for taking RTT samples (MUST-18).

332251cf0510.title: rfc>9293
332251cf0510.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.1. Retransmission Timeout
332251cf0510.sentence: This was then replaced by the algorithm described in RFC 1122, which was subsequently updated in RFC 2988 and then again in RFC 6298.

9b063b595723.title: rfc>9293
9b063b595723.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.2. TCP Congestion Control
9b063b595723.sentence: RFC 1122 required implementation of Van Jacobson's congestion control algorithms slow start and congestion avoidance together with exponential backoff for successive RTO values for the same segment.

33eb8a1d1294.title: rfc>9293
33eb8a1d1294.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.2. TCP Congestion Control
33eb8a1d1294.sentence: RFC 6298 describes exponential backoff of RTO values, including keeping the backed-off value until a subsequent segment with new data has been sent and acknowledged without retransmission.

792d4598baad.title: rfc>9293
792d4598baad.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.2. TCP Congestion Control
792d4598baad.sentence: A TCP endpoint MUST implement the basic congestion control algorithms slow start, congestion avoidance, and exponential backoff of RTO to avoid creating congestion collapse conditions (MUST-19).

9cd8482df32d.title: rfc>9293
9cd8482df32d.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.2. TCP Congestion Control
9cd8482df32d.sentence: An endpoint MAY implement such alternative algorithms provided that the algorithms are conformant with the TCP specifications from the IETF Standards Track as described in RFC 2914, RFC 5033, and RFC 8961 (MAY-18).

d3d87e2af80f.title: rfc>9293
d3d87e2af80f.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
d3d87e2af80f.sentence: Excessive retransmission of the same segment by a TCP endpoint indicates some failure of the remote host or the internetwork path.

ed4a52b6fb31.title: rfc>9293
ed4a52b6fb31.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
ed4a52b6fb31.sentence: (a) There are two thresholds R1 and R2 measuring the amount of retransmission that has occurred for the same segment.

76cf6a535b92.title: rfc>9293
76cf6a535b92.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
76cf6a535b92.sentence: (b) When the number of transmissions of the same segment reaches or exceeds threshold R1, pass negative advice (see Section 3.3.1.4 of ) to the IP layer, to trigger dead-gateway diagnosis.

5e24d99aaca6.title: rfc>9293
5e24d99aaca6.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
5e24d99aaca6.sentence: (c) When the number of transmissions of the same segment reaches a threshold R2 greater than R1, close the connection.

0e2ce59495c5.title: rfc>9293
0e2ce59495c5.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
0e2ce59495c5.sentence: The value of R1 SHOULD correspond to at least 3 retransmissions, at the current RTO (SHLD-10).

939941519387.title: rfc>9293
939941519387.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
939941519387.sentence: The value of R2 SHOULD correspond to at least 100 seconds (SHLD-11).

8180cbe955c0.title: rfc>9293
8180cbe955c0.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
8180cbe955c0.sentence: (e) TCP implementations SHOULD inform the application of the delivery problem (unless such information has been disabled by the application; see the "Asynchronous Reports" section (Section 3.9.1.8)), when R1 is reached and before R2 (SHLD-9).

49964984f96a.title: rfc>9293
49964984f96a.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
49964984f96a.sentence: (d) An application MUST (MUST-21) be able to set the value for R2 for a particular connection.

d9cb49d16ec2.title: rfc>9293
d9cb49d16ec2.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
d9cb49d16ec2.sentence: For example, an interactive application might set R2 to "infinity", giving the user control over when to disconnect.

cacacb3cce2e.title: rfc>9293
cacacb3cce2e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
cacacb3cce2e.sentence: An attempt to open a TCP connection could fail with excessive retransmissions of the SYN segment or by receipt of a RST segment or an ICMP Port Unreachable.

d24757f90421.title: rfc>9293
d24757f90421.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.3. TCP Connection Failures
d24757f90421.sentence: In particular, R2 for a SYN segment MUST be set large enough to provide retransmission of the segment for at least 3 minutes (MUST-23).

a96872f1f55e.title: rfc>9293
a96872f1f55e.sentence: The term "segmentation" refers to the activity TCP performs when ingesting a stream of bytes from a sending application and packetizing that stream of bytes into TCP segments.

4d0750baa554.title: rfc>9293
4d0750baa554.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.2. Path MTU Discovery
4d0750baa554.sentence: The TCP MSS Option specifies an upper bound for the size of packets that can be received (see ).

7dbcb4aa8e10.title: rfc>9293
7dbcb4aa8e10.sentence: Individual TCP segments often do not correspond one-for-one to individual send (or socket write) calls from the application.

4830a6327ded.title: rfc>9293
4830a6327ded.sentence: Applications may perform writes at the granularity of messages in the upper-layer protocol, but TCP guarantees no correlation between the boundaries of TCP segments sent and received and the boundaries of the read or write buffers of user application data.

1bb9466bf2bc.title: rfc>9293
1bb9466bf2bc.sentence: - Reducing the number of packets in flight within the network.

abd56cc37543.title: rfc>9293
abd56cc37543.sentence: - Increasing processing efficiency and potential performance by enabling a smaller number of interrupts and inter-layer interactions.

943a59a719d7.title: rfc>9293
943a59a719d7.sentence: - Limiting the overhead of TCP headers.

c1d5ac397256.title: rfc>9293
c1d5ac397256.sentence: Note that the performance benefits of sending larger segments may decrease as the size increases, and there may be boundaries where advantages are reversed.

c9c118c9ef7b.title: rfc>9293
c9c118c9ef7b.sentence: - Avoiding sending a TCP segment that would result in an IP datagram larger than the smallest MTU along an IP network path because this results in either packet loss or packet fragmentation.

bb34f1de345c.title: rfc>9293
bb34f1de345c.sentence: Making matters worse, some firewalls or middleboxes may drop fragmented packets or ICMP messages related to fragmentation.

93850b5f2379.title: rfc>9293
93850b5f2379.sentence: - Preventing delays to the application data stream, especially when TCP is waiting on the application to generate more data, or when the application is waiting on an event or input from its peer in order to generate more data.

7b4e2a159454.title: rfc>9293
7b4e2a159454.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
7b4e2a159454.sentence: TCP endpoints MUST implement both sending and receiving the MSS Option (MUST-14).

107ddc7f2ee4.title: rfc>9293
107ddc7f2ee4.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
107ddc7f2ee4.sentence: TCP implementations SHOULD send an MSS Option in every SYN segment when its receive MSS differs from the default 536 for IPv4 or 1220 for IPv6 (SHLD-5), and MAY send it always (MAY-3).

fe22e51cc76e.title: rfc>9293
fe22e51cc76e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
fe22e51cc76e.sentence: If an MSS Option is not received at connection setup, TCP implementations MUST assume a default send MSS of 536 (576 - 40) for IPv4 or 1220 (1280 - 60) for IPv6 (MUST-15).

37be0dfbc5b3.title: rfc>9293
37be0dfbc5b3.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
37be0dfbc5b3.sentence: The maximum size of a segment that a TCP endpoint really sends, the "effective send MSS", MUST be the smaller (MUST-16) of the send MSS (that reflects the available reassembly buffer size at the remote host, the EMTU_R ) and the largest transmission size permitted by the IP layer (EMTU_S ):

04e27d6163c9.title: rfc>9293
04e27d6163c9.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
04e27d6163c9.sentence: - TCPhdrsize is the size of the fixed TCP header and any options.

342c4383ea30.title: rfc>9293
342c4383ea30.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
342c4383ea30.sentence: - IPoptionsize is the size of any IPv4 options or IPv6 extension headers associated with a TCP connection.

259bb6456986.title: rfc>9293
259bb6456986.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
259bb6456986.sentence: The MSS value to be sent in an MSS Option should be equal to the effective MTU minus the fixed IP and TCP headers.

22e6e94840d0.title: rfc>9293
22e6e94840d0.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.7. Segmentation > 3.7.1. Maximum Segment Size Option
22e6e94840d0.sentence: When TCP is used in a situation where either the IP or TCP headers are not fixed, the sender must reduce the amount of TCP data in any given packet by the number of octets used by the IP and TCP options.

61034116e1df.title: Transmission Control Protocol
61034116e1df.sentence: Normally, TCP waits for 200 ms for a full packet of data to send (Nagle's Algorithm tries to group small messages into a single packet).

4fda81073b63.title: Transmission Control Protocol
4fda81073b63.sentence: This wait creates small but potentially serious delays if repeated constantly during a file transfer.

8194a602b1b4.title: Transmission Control Protocol
8194a602b1b4.sentence: In the case of Telnet, each user keystroke is echoed back by the server before the user can see it on the screen.

866525e6fc48.title: Transmission Control Protocol
866525e6fc48.sentence: This delay would become very annoying.

d7aacda6f3b3.title: Transmission Control Protocol
d7aacda6f3b3.sentence: Setting the socket option TCP_NODELAY overrides the default 200 ms send delay.

ce1b1d7517b2.title: Transmission Control Protocol
ce1b1d7517b2.sentence: Application programs use this socket option to force output to be sent after writing a character or line of characters.

44c568d350e3.title: rfc>9293
44c568d350e3.sentence: A fundamental notion in the design is that every octet of data sent over a TCP connection has a sequence number.

8284b21a6c36.title: rfc>9293
8284b21a6c36.sentence: Since every octet is sequenced, each of them can be acknowledged.

11b82ed2ec24.title: rfc>9293
11b82ed2ec24.sentence: This mechanism allows for straightforward duplicate detection in the presence of retransmission.

3552e272643f.title: rfc>9293
3552e272643f.sentence: The acknowledgment mechanism employed is cumulative so that an acknowledgment of sequence number X indicates that all octets up to but not including X have been received.

5afe4c7829b1.title: rfc>9293
5afe4c7829b1.sentence: It is essential to remember that the actual sequence number space is finite, though large.

1b30419a7d54.title: rfc>9293
1b30419a7d54.sentence: Since the space is finite, all arithmetic dealing with sequence numbers must be performed modulo 2^32.

aeb79470f713.title: rfc>9293
aeb79470f713.sentence: The SYN and FIN are the only controls requiring this protection, and these controls are used only at connection opening and closing.

9542da4a52d0.title: rfc>9293
9542da4a52d0.sentence: This is achieved by implicitly including some control flags in the sequence space so they can be retransmitted and acknowledged without confusion (i.e., one and only one copy of the control will be acted upon).

23b6e07b9807.title: rfc>9293
23b6e07b9807.sentence: For sequence number purposes, the SYN is considered to occur before the first actual data octet of the segment in which it occurs, while the FIN is considered to occur after the last actual data octet in a segment in which it occurs.

975673b4faef.title: rfc>9293
975673b4faef.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection

9851339e25ec.title: rfc>9293
9851339e25ec.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
9851339e25ec.sentence: New instances of a connection will be referred to as incarnations of the connection.

5df286350e3d.title: rfc>9293
5df286350e3d.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
5df286350e3d.sentence: The problem that arises from this is -- "how does the TCP implementation identify duplicate segments from previous incarnations of the connection?" This problem becomes apparent if the connection is being opened and closed in quick succession, or if the connection breaks with loss of memory and is then reestablished.

530dc3f581f1.title: rfc>9293
530dc3f581f1.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
530dc3f581f1.sentence: To support this, the TIME-WAIT state limits the rate of connection reuse, while the initial sequence number selection described below further protects against ambiguity about which incarnation of a connection an incoming packet corresponds to.

c71ba6485aa6.title: rfc>9293
c71ba6485aa6.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
c71ba6485aa6.sentence: When new connections are created, an initial sequence number (ISN) generator is employed that selects a new 32-bit ISN.

779216fcb721.title: rfc>9293
779216fcb721.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
779216fcb721.sentence: This clock is a 32-bit counter that typically increments at least once every roughly 4 microseconds, although it is neither assumed to be realtime nor precise, and need not persist across reboots.

38e032774f47.title: rfc>9293
38e032774f47.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
38e032774f47.sentence: The clock component is intended to ensure that with a Maximum Segment Lifetime (MSL), generated ISNs will be unique since it cycles approximately every 4.55 hours, which is much longer than the MSL.

900716aad99a.title: rfc>9293
900716aad99a.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
900716aad99a.sentence: A TCP implementation MUST use the above type of "clock" for clock-driven selection of initial sequence numbers (MUST-8), and SHOULD generate its initial sequence numbers with the expression:

0e62b4bd1d82.title: rfc>9293
0e62b4bd1d82.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
0e62b4bd1d82.sentence: where M is the 4 microsecond timer, and F() is a pseudorandom function (PRF) of the connection's identifying parameters ("localip, localport, remoteip, remoteport") and a secret key ("secretkey") (SHLD-1).

91f9228447be.title: rfc>9293
91f9228447be.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
91f9228447be.sentence: F() MUST NOT be computable from the outside (MUST-9), or an attacker could still guess at sequence numbers from the ISN used for some other connection.

0494689780fb.title: rfc>9293
0494689780fb.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
0494689780fb.sentence: There are security issues that result if an off-path attacker is able to predict or guess ISN values.

4c7230e6a31b.title: rfc>9293
4c7230e6a31b.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.3. The TCP Quiet Time Concept
4c7230e6a31b.sentence: At 2 megabits/sec., it takes 4.5 hours to use up 2^32 octets of sequence space.

721cf0789a8f.title: rfc>9293
721cf0789a8f.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.3. The TCP Quiet Time Concept
721cf0789a8f.sentence: At 100 megabits/sec., the cycle time is 5.4 minutes, which may be a little short but still within reason.

a1c46ab0face.title: rfc>9293
a1c46ab0face.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.3. The TCP Quiet Time Concept
a1c46ab0face.sentence: At 1 Gbps, the cycle time is 34 seconds, only 3 seconds at 10 Gbps, and around a third of a second at 100 Gbps.

6a7a5b237733.title: rfc>9293
6a7a5b237733.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.3. The TCP Quiet Time Concept
6a7a5b237733.sentence: In these higher-performance cases, TCP Timestamp Options and Protection Against Wrapped Sequences (PAWS) provide the needed capability to detect and discard old duplicates.

48c023121941.title: rfc>9293
48c023121941.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
48c023121941.sentence: Please note that for modern networks that support high data rates where the connection might start and quickly advance sequence numbers to overlap within the MSL, it is recommended to implement the Timestamp Option as mentioned later in Section 3.4.3.

840242b65373.title: Transmission Control Protocol
840242b65373.sentence: To alleviate this issue TCP employs the selective acknowledgment (SACK) option, defined in 1996 in RFC 2018, which allows the receiver to acknowledge discontinuous blocks of packets that were received correctly, in addition to the sequence number immediately following the last sequence number of the last contiguous byte received successively, as in the basic TCP acknowledgment.

5b1d0f03f7ab.title: Transmission Control Protocol
5b1d0f03f7ab.sentence: Relying purely on the cumulative acknowledgment scheme employed by the original TCP can lead to inefficiencies when packets are lost.

fb3992be10f2.title: Transmission Control Protocol
fb3992be10f2.sentence: For example, suppose bytes with sequence number 1,000 to 10,999 are sent in 10 different TCP segments of equal size, and the second segment (sequence numbers 2,000 to 2,999) is lost during transmission.

8157b711eb8b.title: Transmission Control Protocol
8157b711eb8b.sentence: In a pure cumulative acknowledgment protocol, the receiver can only send a cumulative ACK value of 2,000 (the sequence number immediately following the last sequence number of the received data) and cannot say that it received bytes 3,000 to 10,999 successfully.

d3d675721060.title: Transmission Control Protocol
d3d675721060.sentence: Thus the sender may then have to resend all data starting with sequence number 2,000.

845636f26eb5.title: Transmission Control Protocol
845636f26eb5.sentence: In the example above, the receiver would send an ACK segment with a cumulative ACK value of 2,000 and a SACK option header with sequence numbers 3,000 and 11,000.

638ff1fd8687.title: Transmission Control Protocol
638ff1fd8687.sentence: The sender would accordingly retransmit only the second segment with sequence numbers 2,000 to 2,999.

7eb2f0026562.title: Transmission Control Protocol
7eb2f0026562.sentence: The SACK option is not mandatory and comes into operation only if both parties support it.

1ee1a6110458.title: Transmission Control Protocol
1ee1a6110458.sentence: This is negotiated when a connection is established.

b07d063a5e0c.title: Transmission Control Protocol
b07d063a5e0c.sentence: The use of SACK has become widespread—all popular TCP stacks support it.

acc06f9808c0.title: Transmission Control Protocol
acc06f9808c0.sentence: An important factor in the improvement is that selective acknowledgment can more often avoid going into slow start after a loss and can hence better use available bandwidth.

a16c24482821.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a16c24482821.sentence: However, TCP can only selectively acknowledge a maximum of three blocks of sequence numbers.

e734e67c1b18.title: rfc>9293
e734e67c1b18.sentence: The "three-way handshake" is the procedure used to establish a connection.

1a3d5c208fe7.title: rfc>9293
1a3d5c208fe7.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
1a3d5c208fe7.sentence: This is done in an exchange of connection-establishing segments carrying a control bit called "SYN" (for synchronize) and the initial sequence numbers.

f35037a43451.title: rfc>9293
f35037a43451.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
f35037a43451.sentence: The synchronization requires each side to send its own initial sequence number and to receive a confirmation of it in acknowledgment from the remote TCP peer.

04a8aa0cae8b.title: rfc>9293
04a8aa0cae8b.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
04a8aa0cae8b.sentence: Each side must also receive the remote peer's initial sequence number and send a confirming acknowledgment.

4b2f3c8d9f2e.title: rfc>9293
4b2f3c8d9f2e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
4b2f3c8d9f2e.sentence: Because steps 2 and 3 can be combined in a single message this is called the three-way (or three message) handshake (3WHS).

cf9f8adc26f3.title: rfc>9293
cf9f8adc26f3.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
cf9f8adc26f3.sentence: A 3WHS is necessary because sequence numbers are not tied to a global clock in the network, and TCP implementations may have different mechanisms for picking the ISNs.

4438ee45eadf.title: rfc>9293
4438ee45eadf.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.1. Initial Sequence Number Selection
4438ee45eadf.sentence: The receiver of the first SYN has no way of knowing whether the segment was an old one or not, unless it remembers the last sequence number used on the connection (which is not always possible), and so it must ask the sender to verify this SYN.

48e4980d9d82.title: rfc>9293
48e4980d9d82.sentence: The principal reason for the three-way handshake is to prevent old duplicate connection initiations from causing confusion.

73a799f4c6f0.title: rfc>9293
73a799f4c6f0.sentence: In line 2 of Figure 6, TCP Peer A begins by sending a SYN segment indicating that it will use sequence numbers starting with sequence number 100.

6efdf67f82aa.title: rfc>9293
6efdf67f82aa.sentence: In line 3, TCP Peer B sends a SYN and acknowledges the SYN it received from TCP Peer A. Note that the acknowledgment field indicates TCP Peer B is now expecting to hear sequence 101, acknowledging the SYN that occupied sequence 100.

ebe03a993162.title: rfc>9293
ebe03a993162.sentence: Note that the sequence number of the segment in line 5 is the same as in line 4 because the ACK does not occupy sequence number space (if it did, we would wind up ACKing ACKs!).

e9f1c2633a90.title: rfc>9293
e9f1c2633a90.sentence: At line 3, an old duplicate SYN arrives at TCP Peer B. TCP Peer B cannot tell that this is an old duplicate, so it responds normally (line 4).

e9ceb24a2f92.title: rfc>9293
e9ceb24a2f92.sentence: TCP Peer A detects that the ACK field is incorrect and returns a RST (reset) with its SEQ field selected to make the segment believable.

8a412709611a.title: rfc>9293
8a412709611a.sentence: TCP Peer B, on receiving the RST, returns to the LISTEN state.

86c4534b5c49.title: rfc>9293
86c4534b5c49.sentence: When the original SYN finally arrives at line 6, the synchronization proceeds normally.

96ecff03ff21.title: rfc>9293
96ecff03ff21.sentence: The procedure also works if two TCP peers simultaneously initiate the procedure.

f4838fa4fc92.title: rfc>9293
f4838fa4fc92.sentence: When simultaneous open occurs, each TCP peer receives a SYN segment that carries no acknowledgment after it has sent a SYN.

52d9f1a3b701.title: rfc>9293
52d9f1a3b701.sentence: A TCP implementation MUST support simultaneous open attempts (MUST-10).

f7e6cd4e43e6.title: rfc>9293
f7e6cd4e43e6.sentence: Although these examples do not show connection synchronization using data-carrying segments, this is perfectly legitimate, so long as the receiving TCP endpoint doesn't deliver the data to the user until it is clear the data is valid (e.g., the data is buffered at the receiver until the connection reaches the ESTABLISHED state, given that the three-way handshake reduces the possibility of false connections).

193a4864bb3e.title: rfc>9293
193a4864bb3e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
193a4864bb3e.sentence: A connection progresses through a series of states during its lifetime.

b96e03bfd271.title: rfc>9293
b96e03bfd271.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
b96e03bfd271.sentence: A TCP connection progresses from one state to another in response to events.

b90d69a27961.title: rfc>9293
b90d69a27961.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
b90d69a27961.sentence: The events are the user calls, OPEN, SEND, RECEIVE, CLOSE, ABORT, and STATUS; the incoming segments, particularly those containing the SYN, ACK, RST, and FIN flags; and timeouts.

0184e8716522.title: rfc>9293
0184e8716522.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
0184e8716522.sentence: The states are: LISTEN, SYN-SENT, SYN-RECEIVED, ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT, and the fictional state CLOSED.

4f456cb4c7ef.title: rfc>9293
4f456cb4c7ef.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
4f456cb4c7ef.sentence: CLOSED is fictional because it represents the state when there is no TCB, and therefore, no connection.

c77eff143f07.title: rfc>9293
c77eff143f07.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
c77eff143f07.sentence: The OPEN call specifies whether connection establishment is to be actively pursued, or to be passively waited for.

44cb75e1648c.title: rfc>9293
44cb75e1648c.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
44cb75e1648c.sentence: A passive OPEN request means that the process wants to accept incoming connection requests, in contrast to an active OPEN attempting to initiate a connection.

51994c2f6423.title: rfc>9293
51994c2f6423.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
51994c2f6423.sentence: LISTEN - represents waiting for a connection request from any remote TCP peer and port.

50c2cd261f95.title: rfc>9293
50c2cd261f95.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
50c2cd261f95.sentence: SYN-SENT - represents waiting for a matching connection request after having sent a connection request.

eceaa4e84934.title: rfc>9293
eceaa4e84934.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
eceaa4e84934.sentence: SYN-RECEIVED - represents waiting for a confirming connection request acknowledgment after having both received and sent a connection request.

920074015048.title: rfc>9293
920074015048.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
920074015048.sentence: ESTABLISHED - represents an open connection, data received can be delivered to the user.

fe9121f93565.title: rfc>9293
fe9121f93565.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
fe9121f93565.sentence: The normal state for the data transfer phase of the connection.

d932302010cf.title: rfc>9293
d932302010cf.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
d932302010cf.sentence: FIN-WAIT-1 - represents waiting for a connection termination request from the remote TCP peer, or an acknowledgment of the connection termination request previously sent.

d608afba8c78.title: rfc>9293
d608afba8c78.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
d608afba8c78.sentence: FIN-WAIT-2 - represents waiting for a connection termination request from the remote TCP peer.

28313f8e8f3e.title: rfc>9293
28313f8e8f3e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
28313f8e8f3e.sentence: CLOSE-WAIT - represents waiting for a connection termination request from the local user.

d6edb432342d.title: rfc>9293
d6edb432342d.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
d6edb432342d.sentence: CLOSING - represents waiting for a connection termination request acknowledgment from the remote TCP peer.

51cde8ce55b1.title: rfc>9293
51cde8ce55b1.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
51cde8ce55b1.sentence: LAST-ACK - represents waiting for an acknowledgment of the connection termination request previously sent to the remote TCP peer (this termination request sent to the remote TCP peer already included an acknowledgment of the termination request sent from the remote TCP peer).

760a9fa8c6cc.title: rfc>9293
760a9fa8c6cc.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
760a9fa8c6cc.sentence: TIME-WAIT - represents waiting for enough time to pass to be sure the remote TCP peer received the acknowledgment of its connection termination request and to avoid new connections being impacted by delayed segments from previous connections.

3cc87f722c17.title: rfc>9293
3cc87f722c17.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
3cc87f722c17.sentence: Note 3: A RST can be sent from any state with a corresponding transition to TIME-WAIT (see for rationale).

afc8004773c5.title: rfc>9293
afc8004773c5.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
afc8004773c5.sentence: Similarly, receipt of a RST from any state results in a transition to LISTEN or CLOSED, though this is also omitted from the diagram for legibility.

4f3800a68178.title: rfc>9293
4f3800a68178.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.3. TCP Terminology Overview > 3.3.2. State Machine Overview
4f3800a68178.sentence: NOTA BENE: This diagram is only a summary and must not be taken as the total specification.

132eef947ac0.title: Transmission Control Protocol
132eef947ac0.sentence: TCP may be attacked in a variety of ways.

ac8bbf295174.title: Transmission Control Protocol
ac8bbf295174.sentence: However, there are vulnerabilities in TCP, including denial of service, connection hijacking, TCP veto, and reset attack.

14e52737c01a.title: Transmission Control Protocol
14e52737c01a.sentence: By using a spoofed IP address and repeatedly sending purposely assembled SYN packets, followed by many ACK packets, attackers can cause the server to consume large amounts of resources keeping track of the bogus connections.

8f90d2e757ee.title: Transmission Control Protocol
8f90d2e757ee.sentence: This is known as a SYN flood attack.

8956d4fa2184.title: Transmission Control Protocol
8956d4fa2184.sentence: Proposed solutions to this problem include SYN cookies and cryptographic puzzles, though SYN cookies come with their own set of vulnerabilities.

371425a08637.title: Transmission Control Protocol
371425a08637.sentence: An attacker who is able to eavesdrop on a TCP session and redirect packets can hijack a TCP connection.

051936c0dbc1.title: Transmission Control Protocol
051936c0dbc1.sentence: To do so, the attacker learns the sequence number from the ongoing communication and forges a false segment that looks like the next segment in the stream.

a12abd991e9b.title: Transmission Control Protocol
a12abd991e9b.section: Protocol operation > Data transfer > Reliable transmission
a12abd991e9b.sentence: This number can be arbitrary, and should, in fact, be unpredictable to defend against TCP sequence prediction attacks.

d230630072d5.title: OSI model
d230630072d5.sentence: The network layer provides the functional and procedural means of transferring packets from one node to another connected in "different networks".

1f552bd144f3.title: OSI model
1f552bd144f3.sentence: A network is a medium to which many nodes can be connected, on which every node has an address and which permits nodes connected to it to transfer messages to other nodes connected to it by merely providing the content of a message and the address of the destination node and letting the network find the way to deliver the message to the destination node, possibly routing it through intermediate nodes.

29c139988212.title: OSI model
29c139988212.sentence: Message delivery at the network layer is not necessarily guaranteed to be reliable; a network layer protocol may provide reliable message delivery, but it does not need to do so.

dee63cf80b8b.title: OSI model
dee63cf80b8b.sentence: It may, but does not need to, report delivery errors.

a4680db54367.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::osi-model
a4680db54367.sentence: If the two devices communicating are on the same network, then the network layer is unnecessary.

0baa430e7356.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
0baa430e7356.sentence: The Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) is a supporting protocol in the Internet protocol suite.

c0423bf0dfdd.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
c0423bf0dfdd.sentence: It is used by network devices, including routers, to send error messages and operational information indicating success or failure when communicating with another IP address.

76e39a264f48.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
76e39a264f48.sentence: For example, an error is indicated when a requested service is not available or that a host or router could not be reached.

7863c198dbbd.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
7863c198dbbd.sentence: ICMP errors are directed to the source IP address of the originating packet.

cb42406e6253.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
cb42406e6253.sentence: ICMP differs from transport protocols such as TCP and UDP in that it is not typically used to exchange data between systems, nor is it regularly employed by end-user network applications (with the exception of some diagnostic tools like ping and traceroute).

3642983f40d7.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
3642983f40d7.sentence: There is no port number associated with an ICMP packet, as these numbers are associated with protocols in the transport layer above, such as TCP and UDP.

8378761ebd1d.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
8378761ebd1d.sentence: ICMP is a network-layer protocol; this makes it a layer 3 protocol in the seven-layer OSI model.

1e1beb6c0975.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
1e1beb6c0975.sentence: ICMP uses the basic support of IP as if it were a higher-level protocol; however, ICMP is actually an integral part of IP.

877e68639086.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
877e68639086.sentence: The ICMP packet is encapsulated in an IPv4 packet.

ad966092c09b.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
ad966092c09b.sentence: The ICMP header starts after the IPv4 header and is identified by its protocol number, 1.

2f9a39636cce.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
2f9a39636cce.sentence: A separate Internet Control Message Protocol (called ICMPv6) is used with IPv6.

996d28d8ec4c.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
996d28d8ec4c.sentence: All ICMP packets have an eight-byte header and a variable-sized data section.

1c3b0e4094fc.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
1c3b0e4094fc.sentence: Control messages are identified by the value in the type field.

e9f1631815dd.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
e9f1631815dd.sentence: The code field gives additional context information for the message.

b393cf63a9c3.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
b393cf63a9c3.sentence: ICMP error messages contain a data section that includes a copy of the entire IPv4 header, plus at least the first eight bytes of data from the IPv4 packet that caused the error message.

997485e35924.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
997485e35924.sentence: This data is used by the host to match the message to the appropriate process.

49d7f9e35b64.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
49d7f9e35b64.sentence: For example, every device (such as an intermediate router) forwarding an IP datagram first decrements the time to live (TTL) field in the IP header by one.

fe3d4925849a.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
fe3d4925849a.sentence: If the resulting TTL is 0, the packet is discarded and an ICMP time exceeded message is sent to the datagram's source address.

97e9a2aacdbe.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
97e9a2aacdbe.sentence: Time Exceeded is generated by a gateway to inform the source of a discarded datagram due to the time to live field reaching zero.

cec73083f9ce.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
cec73083f9ce.sentence: The related ping utility is implemented using the ICMP echo request and echo reply messages.

2542063496f7.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
2542063496f7.sentence: The traceroute command can be implemented by transmitting IP datagrams with specially set IP TTL header fields, and looking for ICMP time exceeded in transit and destination unreachable messages generated in response.

ac2091828f45.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
ac2091828f45.sentence: Time exceeded messages are used by the traceroute utility to identify gateways on the path between two hosts.

38565d39d3b5.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
38565d39d3b5.sentence: Destination unreachable is generated by the host or its inbound gateway to inform the client that the destination is unreachable for some reason.

51d58d07db0c.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
51d58d07db0c.sentence: Reasons for this message may include: the physical connection to the host does not exist (distance is infinite); the indicated protocol or port is not active; the data must be fragmented but the 'don't fragment' flag is on.

600c2edeb82b.title: Maximum transmission unit
600c2edeb82b.sentence: Any device along the path whose MTU is smaller than the packet will drop such packets and send back an ICMP Destination Unreachable (Datagram Too Big) message which indicates its MTU.

671dda29d9a4.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
671dda29d9a4.sentence: ICMP Redirect is a mechanism for routers to convey routing information to hosts.

56b6b15a2079.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
56b6b15a2079.sentence: If a host tries to send data through a router (R1) and R1 sends the data to another router (R2) and a direct path from the host to R2 is available (that is, the host and R2 are on the same subnetwork), then R1 will send a redirect message to inform the host that the best route for the destination is via R2.

c54725fca55f.title: Internet Control Message Protocol
c54725fca55f.sentence: The host should then change its route information and send packets for that destination directly to R2.

a279a4408156.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
a279a4408156.sentence: TCP has built-in systems to check for errors and to guarantee data will be delivered in the order it was sent, making it the perfect protocol for transferring information like still images, data files, and web pages.

fcd331e9c696.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
fcd331e9c696.sentence: We should use UDP over TCP when we need the lowest latency and late data is worse than the loss of data.

c8e2c1c4e559.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
c8e2c1c4e559.sentence: But while TCP is instinctively reliable, its feedback mechanisms also result in a larger overhead, translating to greater use of the available bandwidth on the network.

2635ee11d735.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
2635ee11d735.sentence: With UDP, there is no overhead for opening a connection, maintaining a connection, or terminating a connection.

71c8cfbcf751.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
71c8cfbcf751.sentence: Data is continuously sent to the recipient, whether or not they receive it.

3e3617c333ed.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
3e3617c333ed.sentence: A key difference between TCP and UDP is speed, as TCP is comparatively slower than UDP.

f94c9c34ae0a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
f94c9c34ae0a.sentence: Overall, UDP is a much faster, simpler, and more efficient protocol, however, retransmission of lost data packets is only possible with TCP.

0c0dfbac983f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
0c0dfbac983f.sentence: It is largely preferred for real-time communications like broadcast or multicast network transmission.

18a29270ba24.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::tcp-and-udp
18a29270ba24.sentence: Use cases | HTTPS, HTTP, SMTP, POP, FTP, etc | Video streaming, DNS, VoIP, etc

e1f3daeb39a2.title: Network address translation
e1f3daeb39a2.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
e1f3daeb39a2.sentence: NAT traversal problems arise when peers behind different NATs try to communicate.

18343eea68be.title: Network address translation
18343eea68be.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
18343eea68be.sentence: One way to solve this problem is to use port forwarding.

760cb140e1e0.title: Network address translation
760cb140e1e0.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
760cb140e1e0.sentence: Another way is to use various NAT traversal techniques.

5c9ce4191673.title: Network address translation
5c9ce4191673.sentence: Some applications that use IP address information may need to determine the external address of a network address translator.

5381e5a7515e.title: Network address translation
5381e5a7515e.sentence: Furthermore, it may be necessary to examine and categorize the type of mapping in use, for example, when it is desired to set up a direct communication path between two clients, both of which are behind separate NAT gateways.

c043d499cc9d.title: Network address translation
c043d499cc9d.sentence: For this purpose, RFC 3489 specified the protocol Simple Traversal of UDP over NATs (STUN) in 2003.

566c84b9f4ab.title: Network address translation
566c84b9f4ab.sentence: It classified NAT implementations as full-cone NAT, (address) restricted-cone NAT, port-restricted cone NAT or symmetric NAT, and proposed a methodology for testing a device accordingly.

d59faa2002a1.title: Network address translation
d59faa2002a1.sentence: However, these procedures have since been deprecated from standards status, as the methods are inadequate to correctly assess many devices.

b394f1619b24.title: Network address translation
b394f1619b24.section: Methods of translation > NAT mapping vs NAT filtering
b394f1619b24.sentence: RFC 4787 distinguishes between NAT mapping and NAT filtering.

cdcd66728c67.title: Network address translation
cdcd66728c67.section: Methods of translation > NAT mapping vs NAT filtering
cdcd66728c67.sentence: It defines endpoint-independent mapping, address-dependent mapping and address- and port-dependent mapping, explains that these three possible choices do not relate to the security of the NAT as security is determined by the filtering behavior and then specifies "A NAT MUST have an 'Endpoint-Independent Mapping' behavior."

1de98ee23cdc.title: Network address translation
1de98ee23cdc.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
1de98ee23cdc.sentence: The most popular technique for TCP NAT traversal is TCP hole punching.

87a7c6bf7f04.title: Network address translation
87a7c6bf7f04.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
87a7c6bf7f04.sentence: TCP hole punching requires the NAT to follow the port preservation design for TCP.

3871530a9388.title: Network address translation
3871530a9388.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
3871530a9388.sentence: NAT port preservation for outgoing TCP connections is crucial for TCP NAT traversal because, under TCP, one port can only be used for one communication at a time.

5903f94da59a.title: Network address translation
5903f94da59a.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
5903f94da59a.sentence: On the other hand, for UDP, NATs do not need port preservation.

df84899beccd.title: Network address translation
df84899beccd.section: Type of NAT and NAT traversal, role of port preservation for TCP
df84899beccd.sentence: Indeed, multiple UDP communications (each with a distinct endpoint) can occur on the same source port, and applications usually reuse the same UDP socket to send packets to distinct hosts.

5d247aed15ab.title: rfc>9293
5d247aed15ab.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.3. Delayed Acknowledgments -- When to Send an ACK Segment
5d247aed15ab.sentence: A host that is receiving a stream of TCP data segments can increase efficiency in both the network and the hosts by sending fewer than one ACK (acknowledgment) segment per data segment received; this is known as a "delayed ACK".

b9d648dc76bb.title: rfc>9293
b9d648dc76bb.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.3. Delayed Acknowledgments -- When to Send an ACK Segment
b9d648dc76bb.sentence: A TCP endpoint SHOULD implement a delayed ACK (SHLD-18), but an ACK should not be excessively delayed; in particular, the delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds (MUST-40).

999468e395cf.title: rfc>9293
999468e395cf.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.3. Delayed Acknowledgments -- When to Send an ACK Segment
999468e395cf.sentence: An ACK SHOULD be generated for at least every second full-sized segment or 2*RMSS bytes of new data (where RMSS is the MSS specified by the TCP endpoint receiving the segments to be acknowledged, or the default value if not specified) (SHLD-19).

5709f40bdcfc.title: rfc>9293
5709f40bdcfc.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.3. Delayed Acknowledgments -- When to Send an ACK Segment
5709f40bdcfc.sentence: Excessive delays on ACKs can disturb the round-trip timing and packet "clocking" algorithms.

40c84d395829.title: rfc>9293
40c84d395829.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.3. Delayed Acknowledgments -- When to Send an ACK Segment
40c84d395829.sentence: More complete discussion of delayed ACK behavior is in Section 4.2 of RFC 5681, including recommendations to immediately acknowledge out-of-order segments, segments above a gap in sequence space, or segments that fill all or part of a gap, in order to accelerate loss recovery.

e5037ac08f60.title: rfc>9293
e5037ac08f60.section: Appendix A. Other Implementation Notes > A.3. Nagle Modification
e5037ac08f60.sentence: In common operating systems, both the Nagle algorithm and delayed acknowledgments are implemented and enabled by default.

c8e3a52a88c2.title: rfc>9293
c8e3a52a88c2.section: Appendix A. Other Implementation Notes > A.3. Nagle Modification
c8e3a52a88c2.sentence: TCP is used by many applications that have a request-response style of communication, where the combination of the Nagle algorithm and delayed acknowledgments can result in poor application performance.

ecc38d1d8fe0.title: rfc>9293
ecc38d1d8fe0.section: Appendix A. Other Implementation Notes > A.3. Nagle Modification
ecc38d1d8fe0.sentence: Additionally, many applications simply disable Nagle since this is generally supported by a socket option.

54de133f7abd.title: rfc>9293
54de133f7abd.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance
54de133f7abd.sentence: The "Silly Window Syndrome" (SWS) is a stable pattern of small incremental window movements resulting in extremely poor TCP performance.

d0ab7d88cac4.title: rfc>9293
d0ab7d88cac4.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
d0ab7d88cac4.sentence: A TCP implementation MUST include a SWS avoidance algorithm in the sender (MUST-38).

63bff2c9fa63.title: rfc>9293
63bff2c9fa63.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.2. Receiver's Algorithm -- When to Send a Window Update
63bff2c9fa63.sentence: A TCP implementation MUST include a SWS avoidance algorithm in the receiver (MUST-39).

a935808d89d8.title: rfc>9293
a935808d89d8.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance
a935808d89d8.sentence: The Nagle algorithm discourages sending tiny segments when the data to be sent increases in small increments, while the SWS avoidance algorithm discourages small segments resulting from the right window edge advancing in small increments.

d622d713061d.title: rfc>9293
d622d713061d.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.2. Receiver's Algorithm -- When to Send a Window Update
d622d713061d.sentence: The solution to receiver SWS is to avoid advancing the right window edge RCV.NXT+RCV.WND in small increments, even if data is received from the network in small segments.

74c3da019d73.title: rfc>9293
74c3da019d73.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.2. Receiver's Algorithm -- When to Send a Window Update
74c3da019d73.sentence: The suggested SWS avoidance algorithm for the receiver is to keep RCV.NXT+RCV.WND fixed until the reduction satisfies:

212c408242b6.title: rfc>9293
212c408242b6.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.2. Receiver's Algorithm -- When to Send a Window Update
212c408242b6.sentence: where Fr is a fraction whose recommended value is 1/2, and Eff.snd.MSS is the effective send MSS for the connection (see Section 3.7.1).

738ea6c560b9.title: rfc>9293
738ea6c560b9.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data

4fae5ecea078.title: rfc>9293
4fae5ecea078.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
4fae5ecea078.sentence: [SND.NXT = SND.UNA and] PUSHed and D <= U

27ee4b770ca8.title: rfc>9293
27ee4b770ca8.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data

1500990bdcc8.title: rfc>9293
1500990bdcc8.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
1500990bdcc8.sentence: - or if the override timeout occurs.

ce82d425f3d5.title: rfc>9293
ce82d425f3d5.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
ce82d425f3d5.sentence: Here Fs is a fraction whose recommended value is 1/2.

d4b0eae46928.title: rfc>9293
d4b0eae46928.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
d4b0eae46928.sentence: The sender's SWS avoidance algorithm is more difficult than the receiver's because the sender does not know (directly) the receiver's total buffer space (RCV.BUFF).

6cef094f05af.title: rfc>9293
6cef094f05af.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
6cef094f05af.sentence: An approach that has been found to work well is for the sender to calculate Max(SND.WND), which is the maximum send window it has seen so far on the connection, and to use this value as an estimate of RCV.BUFF.

e3e0c59d1f94.title: rfc>9293
e3e0c59d1f94.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
e3e0c59d1f94.sentence: To avoid a resulting deadlock, it is necessary to have a timeout to force transmission of data, overriding the SWS avoidance algorithm.

35f5e537987a.title: rfc>9293
35f5e537987a.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.2. Silly Window Syndrome Avoidance > 3.8.6.2.1. Sender's Algorithm -- When to Send Data
35f5e537987a.sentence: The override timeout should be in the range 0.1 - 1.0 seconds.

c7f82ef32cf0.title: rfc>9293
c7f82ef32cf0.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
c7f82ef32cf0.sentence: Since the two directions of a TCP connection are closed independently, it is possible for a connection to be "half closed", i.e., closed in only one direction, and a host is permitted to continue sending data in the open direction on a half-closed connection.

c111c01004f6.title: rfc>9293
c111c01004f6.sentence: CLOSE is an operation meaning "I have no more data to send." The notion of closing a full-duplex connection is subject to ambiguous interpretation, of course, since it may not be obvious how to treat the receiving side of the connection.

d6b16f9ca91b.title: rfc>9293
d6b16f9ca91b.sentence: We have chosen to treat CLOSE in a simplex fashion.

05d3fa504828.title: rfc>9293
05d3fa504828.sentence: The user who CLOSEs may continue to RECEIVE until the TCP receiver is told that the remote peer has CLOSED also.

51d5c5fb58fe.title: rfc>9293
51d5c5fb58fe.sentence: Note that a TCP endpoint receiving a FIN will ACK but not send its own FIN until its user has CLOSED the connection also.

e98c09fa1c30.title: rfc>9293
e98c09fa1c30.sentence: A TCP implementation will reliably deliver all buffers SENT before the connection was CLOSED so a user who expects no data in return need only wait to hear the connection was CLOSED successfully to know that all their data was received at the destination TCP endpoint.

0dcfd78854dc.title: rfc>9293
0dcfd78854dc.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
0dcfd78854dc.sentence: The normal TCP close sequence delivers buffered data reliably in both directions.

6f7c27cccc81.title: rfc>9293
6f7c27cccc81.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
6f7c27cccc81.sentence: A host MAY implement a "half-duplex" TCP close sequence, so that an application that has called CLOSE cannot continue to read data from the connection (MAY-1).

9d1f3f81e26b.title: rfc>9293
9d1f3f81e26b.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
9d1f3f81e26b.sentence: If such a host issues a CLOSE call while received data is still pending in the TCP connection, or if new data is received after CLOSE is called, its TCP implementation SHOULD send a RST to show that data was lost (SHLD-3).

8904a43cb0cd.title: rfc>9293
8904a43cb0cd.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
8904a43cb0cd.sentence: A TCP connection is said to be "idle" if for some long amount of time there have been no incoming segments received and there is no new or unacknowledged data to be sent.

02e27a538483.title: rfc>9293
02e27a538483.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
02e27a538483.sentence: To confirm that an idle connection is still active, these implementations send a probe segment designed to elicit a response from the TCP peer.

1293a20b58c3.title: rfc>9293
1293a20b58c3.sentence: TCP is connection oriented, though it does not inherently include a liveness detection capability.

823a69acdc9b.title: rfc>9293
823a69acdc9b.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
823a69acdc9b.sentence: Implementers MAY include "keep-alives" in their TCP implementations (MAY-5), although this practice is not universally accepted.

61568c955f4e.title: rfc>9293
61568c955f4e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
61568c955f4e.sentence: Such a segment generally contains SEG.SEQ = SND.NXT-1 and may or may not contain one garbage octet of data.

0a5011df89c5.title: rfc>9293
0a5011df89c5.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
0a5011df89c5.sentence: If keep-alives are included, the application MUST be able to turn them on or off for each TCP connection (MUST-24), and they MUST default to off (MUST-25).

3bb87d45458c.title: rfc>9293
3bb87d45458c.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
3bb87d45458c.sentence: Keep-alive packets MUST only be sent when no sent data is outstanding, and no data or acknowledgment packets have been received for the connection within an interval (MUST-26).

94286ce3ca3a.title: rfc>9293
94286ce3ca3a.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
94286ce3ca3a.sentence: This interval MUST be configurable (MUST-27) and MUST default to no less than two hours (MUST-28).

071be1b0ddc4.title: rfc>9293
071be1b0ddc4.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
071be1b0ddc4.sentence: It is extremely important to remember that ACK segments that contain no data are not reliably transmitted by TCP.

6eab8710b870.title: rfc>9293
6eab8710b870.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.4. TCP Keep-Alives
6eab8710b870.sentence: Consequently, if a keep-alive mechanism is implemented it MUST NOT interpret failure to respond to any specific probe as a dead connection (MUST-29).

c24a170c8161.title: rfc>9293
c24a170c8161.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.2. Reset Generation
c24a170c8161.sentence: As a general rule, reset (RST) is sent whenever a segment arrives that apparently is not intended for the current connection.

5ed9638c590c.title: rfc>9293
5ed9638c590c.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.3. Reset Processing
5ed9638c590c.sentence: The receiver of a RST first validates it, then changes state.

3409612a25aa.title: rfc>9293
3409612a25aa.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.2. Reset Generation
3409612a25aa.sentence: A reset must not be sent if it is not clear that this is the case.

fea179d7161d.title: rfc>9293
fea179d7161d.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.2. Reset Generation
fea179d7161d.sentence: A SYN segment that does not match an existing connection is rejected by this means.

5880fd2f7f42.title: rfc>9293
5880fd2f7f42.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.3. Reset Processing
5880fd2f7f42.sentence: In all states except SYN-SENT, all reset (RST) segments are validated by checking their SEQ fields.

db18bcc49f56.title: rfc>9293
db18bcc49f56.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.3. Reset Processing
db18bcc49f56.sentence: A reset is valid if its sequence number is in the window.

b9bb4eb4308d.title: rfc>9293
b9bb4eb4308d.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.3. Reset Processing
b9bb4eb4308d.sentence: In the SYN-SENT state (a RST received in response to an initial SYN), the RST is acceptable if the ACK field acknowledges the SYN.

e0190c5a0139.title: rfc>9293
e0190c5a0139.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.3. Reset Processing
e0190c5a0139.sentence: If the receiver was in the LISTEN state, it ignores it.

c482968c8102.title: rfc>9293
c482968c8102.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.3. Reset Processing
c482968c8102.sentence: If the receiver was in SYN-RECEIVED state and had previously been in the LISTEN state, then the receiver returns to the LISTEN state; otherwise, the receiver aborts the connection and goes to the CLOSED state.

5aacc851d34d.title: rfc>9293
5aacc851d34d.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.3. Reset Processing
5aacc851d34d.sentence: If the receiver was in any other state, it aborts the connection and advises the user and goes to the CLOSED state.

1efe5b7f0f60.title: rfc>9293
1efe5b7f0f60.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.1. Half-Open Connections and Other Anomalies
1efe5b7f0f60.sentence: An established connection is said to be "half-open" if one of the TCP peers has closed or aborted the connection at its end without the knowledge of the other, or if the two ends of the connection have become desynchronized owing to a failure or reboot that resulted in loss of memory.

ad8689fb4b2e.title: rfc>9293
ad8689fb4b2e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.1. Half-Open Connections and Other Anomalies
ad8689fb4b2e.sentence: Such connections will automatically become reset if an attempt is made to send data in either direction.

47284b6027a6.title: rfc>9293
47284b6027a6.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.1. Half-Open Connections and Other Anomalies
47284b6027a6.sentence: If at site A the connection no longer exists, then an attempt by the user at site B to send any data on it will result in the site B TCP endpoint receiving a reset control message.

4bf53fe86522.title: rfc>9293
4bf53fe86522.sentence: A TCP header follows the IP headers, supplying information specific to TCP.

da0db73aa373.title: rfc>9293
da0db73aa373.sentence: A TCP header, followed by any user data in the segment, is formatted as follows, using the style from:

1f9b76c2f3e4.title: rfc>9293
1f9b76c2f3e4.sentence: If SYN is set, the sequence number is the initial sequence number (ISN) and the first data octet is ISN+1.

08319a2a52e8.title: rfc>9293
08319a2a52e8.sentence: Once a connection is established, this is always sent.

a6059b6dd756.title: rfc>9293
a6059b6dd756.sentence: The currently assigned control bits are CWR, ECE, URG, ACK, PSH, RST, SYN, and FIN.

efc580aef154.title: rfc>9293
efc580aef154.sentence: The number of 32-bit words in the TCP header.
