68b348120eb1.title: rfc>9293
68b348120eb1.sentence: The TCP header (even one including options) is an integer multiple of 32 bits long.

affc2a4c3712.title: rfc>9293
affc2a4c3712.sentence: The number of data octets beginning with the one indicated in the acknowledgment field that the sender of this segment is willing to accept.

47057d1f96ab.title: rfc>9293
47057d1f96ab.sentence: The value is shifted when the window scaling extension is used.

c3f832a792dd.title: rfc>9293
c3f832a792dd.sentence: The TCP checksum is never optional.

418c2044a766.title: rfc>9293
418c2044a766.sentence: The sender MUST generate it (MUST-2) and the receiver MUST check it (MUST-3).

3b42bb646b95.title: rfc>9293
3b42bb646b95.sentence: The checksum also covers a pseudo-header (Figure 2) conceptually prefixed to the TCP header.

4b8a95d0d3de.title: rfc>9293
4b8a95d0d3de.sentence: Including the pseudo-header in the checksum gives the TCP connection protection against misrouted segments.

1aa0b8b593c0.title: rfc>9293
1aa0b8b593c0.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
1aa0b8b593c0.sentence: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in the TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL (Maximum Segment Lifetime) (MUST-13).

90ca768462b5.title: rfc>9293
90ca768462b5.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.4. Sequence Numbers > 3.4.2. Knowing When to Keep Quiet
90ca768462b5.sentence: For this specification the MSL is taken to be 2 minutes.

c695c51bb207.title: rfc>9293
c695c51bb207.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
c695c51bb207.sentence: However, it MAY accept a new SYN from the remote TCP endpoint to reopen the connection directly from TIME-WAIT state (MAY-2), if it:

d3e07230a5d9.title: rfc>9293
d3e07230a5d9.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
d3e07230a5d9.sentence: When the TCP Timestamp Options are available, an improved algorithm is described in in order to support higher connection establishment rates.

8cc19e96b022.title: rfc>9293
8cc19e96b022.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.6. Closing a Connection > 3.6.1. Half-Closed Connections
8cc19e96b022.sentence: This algorithm for reducing TIME-WAIT is a Best Current Practice that SHOULD be implemented since Timestamp Options are commonly used, and using them to reduce TIME-WAIT provides benefits for busy Internet servers (SHLD-4).

225345219101.title: rfc>9293
225345219101.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.5. Establishing a Connection > 3.5.2. Reset Generation
225345219101.sentence: The side of a connection issuing a reset should enter the TIME-WAIT state, as this generally helps to reduce the load on busy servers for reasons described in.

858118f26325.title: rfc>9293
858118f26325.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.1. Zero-Window Probing
858118f26325.sentence: The sending TCP peer must regularly transmit at least one octet of new data (if available), or retransmit to the receiving TCP peer even if the send window is zero, in order to "probe" the window.

c4875755e0b1.title: rfc>9293
c4875755e0b1.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.1. Zero-Window Probing
c4875755e0b1.sentence: This retransmission is essential to guarantee that when either TCP peer has a zero window the reopening of the window will be reliably reported to the other.

81e83794f9e2.title: rfc>9293
81e83794f9e2.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.1. Zero-Window Probing
81e83794f9e2.sentence: This is referred to as Zero-Window Probing (ZWP) in other documents.

9e09ba53f160.title: rfc>9293
9e09ba53f160.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.1. Zero-Window Probing
9e09ba53f160.sentence: The transmitting host SHOULD send the first zero-window probe when a zero window has existed for the retransmission timeout period (SHLD-29) (Section 3.8.1), and SHOULD increase exponentially the interval between successive probes (SHLD-30).

114ce35c9c2c.title: rfc>9293
114ce35c9c2c.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.1. Zero-Window Probing
114ce35c9c2c.sentence: A TCP implementation MAY keep its offered receive window closed indefinitely (MAY-8).

48cf20d1f450.title: rfc>9293
48cf20d1f450.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.1. Zero-Window Probing
48cf20d1f450.sentence: As long as the receiving TCP peer continues to send acknowledgments in response to the probe segments, the sending TCP peer MUST allow the connection to stay open (MUST-37).

e3167c0c4ab8.title: rfc>9293
e3167c0c4ab8.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window > 3.8.6.1. Zero-Window Probing
e3167c0c4ab8.sentence: This enables TCP to function in scenarios such as the "printer ran out of paper" situation described in Section 4.2.2.17 of.

cf0207374d26.title: rfc>9293
cf0207374d26.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window
cf0207374d26.sentence: A TCP receiver SHOULD NOT shrink the window, i.e., move the right window edge to the left (SHLD-14).

1292bdebe08a.title: rfc>9293
1292bdebe08a.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window
1292bdebe08a.sentence: However, a sending TCP peer MUST be robust against window shrinking, which may cause the "usable window" (see Section 3.8.6.2.1) to become negative (MUST-34).

3ef44cbe193e.title: rfc>9293
3ef44cbe193e.section: 3. Functional Specification > 3.8. Data Communication > 3.8.6. Managing the Window
3ef44cbe193e.sentence: If the window shrinks to zero, the TCP implementation MUST probe it in the standard way (described below) (MUST-35).

d826105c2370.title: Maximum transmission unit
d826105c2370.sentence: Path MTU Discovery is a technique for determining the path MTU between two IP hosts, defined for both IPv4 and IPv6.

9b24d7751ec1.title: Maximum transmission unit
9b24d7751ec1.sentence: The Internet Protocol defines the path MTU of an Internet transmission path as the smallest MTU supported by any of the hops on the path between a source and destination.

09ebc17a0768.title: Maximum transmission unit
09ebc17a0768.sentence: Put another way, the path MTU is the largest packet size that can traverse this path without suffering fragmentation.

26ba1b5f8bac.title: Maximum transmission unit
26ba1b5f8bac.sentence: It works by sending packets with the DF (don't fragment) option in the IP header set.

50fa179bc419.title: Maximum transmission unit
50fa179bc419.sentence: This information allows the source host to reduce its assumed path MTU appropriately.

09775a175cb1.title: Maximum transmission unit
09775a175cb1.sentence: The process repeats until the MTU becomes small enough to traverse the entire path without fragmentation.

afa21ba44a4d.title: Maximum transmission unit
afa21ba44a4d.sentence: Unfortunately, increasing numbers of networks drop ICMP traffic (for example, to prevent denial-of-service attacks), which prevents path MTU discovery from working.

ea1124971711.title: Maximum transmission unit
ea1124971711.sentence: Packetization Layer Path MTU Discovery is a Path MTU Discovery technique which responds more robustly to ICMP filtering.

a92fb0e5cc31.title: Maximum transmission unit
a92fb0e5cc31.sentence: In an IP network, the path from the source address to the destination address may change in response to various events (load-balancing, congestion, outages, etc.) and this could result in the path MTU changing (sometimes repeatedly) during a transmission, which may introduce further packet drops before the host finds a new reliable MTU.

2abb151d7d81.title: Maximum transmission unit
2abb151d7d81.sentence: A connection with mismatched MTU may work for low-volume data but fail as soon as a host sends a large block of data.

e22e885fe314.title: Maximum transmission unit
e22e885fe314.sentence: A failure of Path MTU Discovery carries the possible result of making some sites behind badly configured firewalls unreachable.

94296f6ff0dd.title: Maximum transmission unit
94296f6ff0dd.sentence: One can possibly work around this, depending on which part of the network one controls; for example, one can change the MSS (maximum segment size) in the initial packet that sets up the TCP connection at one's firewall.

33c08bc747a2.title: TCP congestion control
33c08bc747a2.sentence: There are several variations and versions of the algorithm implemented in protocol stacks of operating systems of computers that connect to the Internet.

e1c049106260.title: TCP congestion control
e1c049106260.sentence: While both consider retransmission timeout (RTO) and duplicate ACKs as packet loss events, the behavior of Tahoe and Reno differ primarily in how they react to duplicate ACKs:

ac1a967135e7.title: TCP congestion control
ac1a967135e7.sentence: - Tahoe: if three duplicate ACKs are received (i.e., four ACKs acknowledging the same packet, which are not piggybacked on data and do not change the receiver's advertised window), Tahoe performs a fast retransmit, sets the slow start threshold to half of the current congestion window, reduces the congestion window to 1 MSS, and resets to slow start state.

2e94d131f7c3.title: TCP congestion control
2e94d131f7c3.sentence: - Reno: if three duplicate ACKs are received, Reno will perform a fast retransmit and skip the slow start phase by instead halving the congestion window (instead of setting it to 1 MSS like Tahoe), setting the ssthresh equal to the new congestion window, and enter a phase called fast recovery.

11052b7bd9f0.title: TCP congestion control
11052b7bd9f0.sentence: In both Tahoe and Reno, if an ACK times out (RTO timeout), slow start is used, and both algorithms reduce the congestion window to 1 MSS.

2528af5834bf.title: TCP congestion control
2528af5834bf.sentence: CUBIC is a less aggressive and more systematic derivative of BIC, in which the window is a cubic function of time since the last congestion event, with the inflection point set to the window prior to the event.

9eb53c11b11a.title: TCP congestion control
9eb53c11b11a.sentence: CUBIC is used by default in Linux kernels since version 2.6.19.

d1406d29572d.title: TCP congestion control
d1406d29572d.sentence: For instance, when a CUBIC flow (which is the default TCP implementation in Linux, Android, and MacOS) coexists with a BBR flow in the network, the BBR flow can dominate the CUBIC flow and get the whole link bandwidth from it (see figure 18 in).

85fcdc43870c.title: TCP congestion control
85fcdc43870c.sentence: While most CCAs are loss-based, in that they rely on packet loss to detect congestion and lower rates of transmission, BBR, like TCP Vegas, is model-based.

30b058b9a5a0.title: TCP congestion control
30b058b9a5a0.sentence: Bottleneck Bandwidth and Round-trip propagation time (BBR) is a CCA developed at Google in 2016.

3a6222459c7d.title: TCP congestion control
3a6222459c7d.sentence: The algorithm uses the maximum bandwidth and round-trip time at which the network delivered the most recent flight of outbound data packets to build a model of the network.

3d04fbf304a7.title: TCP congestion control
3d04fbf304a7.sentence: BBR version 1 (BBRv1) fairness to non-BBR streams is disputed.

f8973dd91ee5.title: TCP congestion control
f8973dd91ee5.sentence: This consist of three primary categories: black box, grey box, and green box.

2ba9c3abb0fd.title: TCP congestion control
2ba9c3abb0fd.sentence: They operate only on the binary feedback received upon congestion and do not assume any knowledge concerning the state of the networks which they manage.

d012be0d6a42.title: TCP congestion control
d012be0d6a42.sentence: Grey box algorithms use time-based measurements, such as RTT variation and rate of packet arrival, in order to obtain measurements and estimations of bandwidth, flow contention, and other knowledge of network conditions.

9a8c02d52f91.title: TCP congestion control
9a8c02d52f91.sentence: Green box algorithms offer bimodal methods of congestion control that measure the fair share of total bandwidth that should be allocated for each flow, at any point, during the system's execution.

8466996744b8.title: Domain Name System
8466996744b8.sentence: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a hierarchical and distributed name service that provides a naming system for computers, services, and other resources on the Internet or other Internet Protocol (IP) networks.

da4cac553d31.title: Domain Name System
da4cac553d31.sentence: Most prominently, it translates readily memorized domain names to the numerical IP addresses needed for locating and identifying computer services and devices with the underlying network protocols.

abc7a267b8c6.title: Domain Name System
abc7a267b8c6.sentence: An often-used analogy to explain the DNS is that it serves as the phone book for the Internet by translating human-friendly computer hostnames into IP addresses.

71933ab7f306.title: Domain Name System
71933ab7f306.sentence: For example, the hostname www.example.com within the domain name example.com translates to the addresses 93.184.216.34 (IPv4) and 2606:2800:220:1:248:1893:25c8:1946 (IPv6).

b030f7747853.title: Domain Name System
b030f7747853.sentence: The Domain Name System delegates the responsibility of assigning domain names and mapping those names to Internet resources by designating authoritative name servers for each domain.

a2d2fb907016.title: Domain Name System
a2d2fb907016.sentence: Network administrators may delegate authority over subdomains of their allocated name space to other name servers.

08e0d682b4a2.title: Domain Name System
08e0d682b4a2.sentence: This mechanism provides distributed and fault-tolerant service and was designed to avoid a single large central database.

2091dd3005b4.title: Domain Name System
2091dd3005b4.sentence: The DNS can be quickly and transparently updated, allowing a service's location on the network to change without affecting the end users, who continue to use the same hostname.

4502659b393e.title: Scalability
4502659b393e.sentence: - The distributed nature of the Domain Name System (DNS) allows it to work efficiently, serving billions of hosts on the worldwide Internet.

b0ebabbf3052.title: Domain Name System
b0ebabbf3052.sentence: A DNS name server is a server that stores the DNS records for a domain; a DNS name server responds with answers to queries against its database.

055243e6f534.title: Domain Name System
055243e6f534.sentence: The DNS database is conventionally stored in a structured text file, the zone file, but other database systems are common.

830038d766bd.title: Domain Name System
830038d766bd.sentence: The Domain Name System originally used the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) as transport over IP.

c1829f561e00.title: Domain Name System
c1829f561e00.sentence: Reliability, security, and privacy concerns spawned the use of the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) as well as numerous other protocol developments.

8c025117480f.title: Domain Name System
8c025117480f.sentence: Although not intended to be a general-purpose database, DNS has been expanded over time to store records for other types of data for either automatic lookups, such as DNSSEC records, or for human queries such as responsible person (RP) records.

e7984011e6f8.title: Domain Name System
e7984011e6f8.sentence: As a general-purpose database, the DNS has also been used in combating unsolicited email (spam) by storing blocklists.

55fdf3576f32.title: Domain Name System
55fdf3576f32.sentence: The DNS reflects the structure of administrative responsibility on the Internet.

80ecdba06e4f.title: Domain Name System
80ecdba06e4f.sentence: Each subdomain is a zone of administrative autonomy delegated to a manager.

a5563279f221.title: Anycast
a5563279f221.sentence: Anycast is a network addressing and routing methodology in which a single IP address is shared by devices (generally servers) in multiple locations.

6f7d97e76d40.title: Anycast
6f7d97e76d40.sentence: Routers direct packets addressed to this destination to the location nearest the sender, using their normal decision-making algorithms, typically the lowest number of BGP network hops.

dd76744eb8d5.title: Anycast
dd76744eb8d5.sentence: Anycast is implemented in the Internet via Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), where multiple hosts (usually in different geographic areas) are given the same anycast IP address and they all announce it to their BGP table.

3185077cf7ff.title: Anycast
3185077cf7ff.sentence: Routers consider these to be alternative routes to the same destination, even though they are actually routes to different destinations with the same address.

d8a0b49206c2.title: Anycast
d8a0b49206c2.sentence: Routers will often select the path with fewer hops, which leads to the one closer to the client as being selected (often faster).

07190dfdaaf2.title: Anycast
07190dfdaaf2.sentence: It doesn't always happen, as some routers will choose other metrics (least congested, cheapest).

825490dde55b.title: Anycast
825490dde55b.sentence: Anycast is supported explicitly in the IPv6 addressing architecture.

b7a692a6490f.title: Anycast
b7a692a6490f.sentence: The method used in IPv4 of advertising multiple routes in BGP to multiply-assigned unicast addresses also still works in IPv6, and can be used to route packets to the nearest of several geographically dispersed hosts with the same address.

1a4e56e93d48.title: Anycast
1a4e56e93d48.sentence: This approach, which does not depend on anycast-aware routers, has the same use cases together with the same problems and limitations as in IPv4.

6f8f66ba0c9c.title: Anycast
6f8f66ba0c9c.sentence: All Internet root nameservers are implemented as clusters of hosts using anycast addressing.

457497a95e4b.title: Anycast
457497a95e4b.sentence: Many commercial DNS providers have switched to an IP anycast environment to increase query performance and redundancy, and to implement load balancing.

fd2462573f84.title: Anycast
fd2462573f84.sentence: Anycast routing is widely used by content delivery networks such as web and name servers, to bring their content closer to end users.

416b47ad5ca1.title: Anycast
416b47ad5ca1.sentence: Content delivery networks may use anycast for actual HTTP connections to their distribution centers, or for DNS.

8625a40e896c.title: Anycast
8625a40e896c.sentence: Early objections to the deployment of anycast routing centered on the perceived conflict between long-lived TCP connections and the volatility of the Internet's routed topology.

bebd01266c89.title: Anycast
bebd01266c89.sentence: In concept, a long-lived connection, such as an FTP file transfer (which can take hours to complete for large files) might be re-routed to a different anycast instance in mid-connection due to changes in network topology or routing, with the result that the server changes mid-connection, and the new server is not aware of the connection and does not possess the TCP connection state of the previous anycast instance.

b1eba22d88ff.title: Anycast
b1eba22d88ff.sentence: In practice, such problems were not observed, and these objections dissipated by the early 2000s.

78cea4d53192.title: Anycast
78cea4d53192.sentence: Measurements of long-term anycast flows revealed very few failures due to mid-connection instance switches, far fewer (less than 0.017% or "less than one flow per ten thousand per hour of duration" according to various sources) than were attributed to other causes of failure.

b994e980f227.title: Anycast
b994e980f227.sentence: Because most HTTP connections to such networks request static content such as images and style sheets, they are generally short-lived and stateless across subsequent TCP sessions.

b7ca9eb078ea.title: Anycast
b7ca9eb078ea.sentence: The general stability of routes and statelessness of connections makes anycast suitable for this application, even though it uses TCP.

7667d4096985.title: Anycast
7667d4096985.sentence: Anycast is normally highly reliable, as it can provide automatic failover without adding complexity or new potential points of failure.

9a00bde9c2f4.title: Anycast
9a00bde9c2f4.sentence: Anycast applications typically feature external "heartbeat" monitoring of the server's function, and withdraw the route announcement if the server fails.

2c18f9a8993b.title: Anycast
2c18f9a8993b.sentence: "Heartbeat" functionality is important because, if the announcement continues for a failed server, the server will act as a "black hole" for nearby clients; this is the most serious mode of failure for an anycast system.

8530d296f75c.title: Anycast
8530d296f75c.sentence: Even in this event, this kind of failure will only cause a total failure for clients that are closer to this server than any other, and will not cause a global failure.

68bb4133a8a7.title: Anycast
68bb4133a8a7.sentence: However, even the automation necessary to implement "heartbeat" routing withdrawal can itself add a potential point of failure, as seen in the 2021 Facebook outage.

c6478ff78ce4.title: Anycast
c6478ff78ce4.sentence: Anycast methodologies on the Internet may be exploited to distribute DDoS attacks and reduce their effectiveness: As traffic is routed to the closest node, a process over which the attacker has no control, the DDoS traffic flow will be distributed amongst the closest nodes.

fea4796baf24.title: Anycast
fea4796baf24.sentence: The effectiveness of this technique depends upon maintaining the secrecy of any unicast addresses associated with anycast service nodes, however, since an attacker in possession of the unicast addresses of individual nodes can attack them from any location, bypassing anycast addressing methods.

ca4a8d26fc9f.title: Anycast
ca4a8d26fc9f.sentence: Anycast allows any operator whose routing information is accepted by an intermediate router to hijack any packets intended for the anycast address.

45f95fee78fa.title: Anycast
45f95fee78fa.sentence: As with conventional IP routing, careful filtering of who is and is not allowed to propagate route announcements is crucial to prevent man-in-the-middle or blackhole attacks.

69ff3d281892.title: Domain Name System
69ff3d281892.sentence: From the time of its origin in 1983 the DNS has used the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) for transport over IP.

9dfaf2c97a70.title: Domain Name System
9dfaf2c97a70.sentence: Its limitations have motivated numerous protocol developments for reliability, security, privacy, and other criteria, in the following decades.

72b6483db520.title: Domain Name System
72b6483db520.section: Transport protocols > Classic DNS: DNS over UDP and TCP port 53 (Do53)
72b6483db520.sentence: UDP reserves port number 53 for servers listening to queries.

6bc307b59159.title: Domain Name System
6bc307b59159.section: Transport protocols > Classic DNS: DNS over UDP and TCP port 53 (Do53)
6bc307b59159.sentence: Such a query consists of a clear-text request sent in a single UDP packet from the client, responded to with a clear-text reply sent in a single UDP packet from the server.

b27c8f5ce879.title: Domain Name System
b27c8f5ce879.section: Transport protocols > Classic DNS: DNS over UDP and TCP port 53 (Do53)
b27c8f5ce879.sentence: When the length of the answer exceeds 512 bytes and both client and server support Extension Mechanisms for DNS (EDNS), larger UDP packets may be used.

aa3718ee5bff.title: Domain Name System
aa3718ee5bff.section: Transport protocols > Classic DNS: DNS over UDP and TCP port 53 (Do53)
aa3718ee5bff.sentence: Use of DNS over UDP is limited by, among other things, its lack of transport-layer encryption, authentication, reliable delivery, and message length.

6e8dafc39512.title: Domain Name System
6e8dafc39512.section: Transport protocols > Classic DNS: DNS over UDP and TCP port 53 (Do53)
6e8dafc39512.sentence: In 1989, RFC 1123 specified optional Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport for DNS queries, replies and, particularly, zone transfers.

1324955ab42e.title: Domain Name System
1324955ab42e.section: Transport protocols > Classic DNS: DNS over UDP and TCP port 53 (Do53)
1324955ab42e.sentence: Via fragmentation of long replies, TCP allows longer responses, reliable delivery, and re-use of long-lived connections between clients and servers.

5d41c168b3cd.title: Transmission Control Protocol
5d41c168b3cd.sentence: For embedded systems, network booting, and servers that serve simple requests from huge numbers of clients (e.g. DNS servers) the complexity of TCP can be a problem.

3078d13942d5.title: Domain Name System
3078d13942d5.sentence: DNS over TLS emerged as an IETF standard for encrypted DNS in 2016, utilizing Transport Layer Security (TLS) to protect the entire connection, rather than just the DNS payload.

82ad27d19772.title: Domain Name System
82ad27d19772.sentence: DoT servers listen on TCP port 853.

5324dcf4a5bd.title: Domain Name System
5324dcf4a5bd.sentence: RFC 7858 specifies that opportunistic encryption and authenticated encryption may be supported, but did not make either server or client authentication mandatory.

e0dd283d245c.title: Domain Name System
e0dd283d245c.sentence: DNS over HTTPS was developed as a competing standard for DNS query transport in 2018, tunneling DNS query data over HTTPS, which transports HTTP over TLS.

f8fc689e5d1d.title: Domain Name System
f8fc689e5d1d.sentence: DoH was promoted as a more web-friendly alternative to DNS since, like DNSCrypt, it uses TCP port 443, and thus looks similar to web traffic, though they are easily differentiable in practice without proper padding.

cc76ea009e48.title: Domain Name System
cc76ea009e48.sentence: RFC 9250, published in 2022 by the Internet Engineering Task Force, describes DNS over QUIC.

d5e8e4e06d60.title: Domain Name System
d5e8e4e06d60.sentence: It has "privacy properties similar to DNS over TLS (DoT) [...], and latency characteristics similar to classic DNS over UDP".

c4dec3659a9c.title: Domain Name System
c4dec3659a9c.sentence: This method is not the same as DNS over HTTP/3.

ba93ae13dbae.title: Domain Name System
ba93ae13dbae.sentence: The DNSCrypt protocol, which was developed in 2011 outside the IETF standards framework, introduced DNS encryption on the downstream side of recursive resolvers, wherein clients encrypt query payloads using servers' public keys, which are published in the DNS (rather than relying upon third-party certificate authorities) and which may in turn be protected by DNSSEC signatures.

5fa014d867b3.title: Domain Name System
5fa014d867b3.sentence: DNSCrypt uses either TCP port 443, the same port as HTTPS encrypted web traffic, or UDP port 443.

bf9518f7b810.title: Domain Name System
bf9518f7b810.sentence: The domain name space consists of a tree data structure.

724b6107bc2e.title: Domain Name System
724b6107bc2e.sentence: The domain name itself consists of the label, concatenated with the name of its parent node on the right, separated by a dot.

d4bbf1aafed0.title: Domain Name System
d4bbf1aafed0.sentence: Each node or leaf in the tree has a label and zero or more resource records (RR), which hold information associated with the domain name.

5cd814eac332.title: Domain Name System
5cd814eac332.sentence: The rightmost label conveys the top-level domain (TLD); for example, the domain name www.example.com belongs to the TLD com.

6a0b6499fbee.title: Domain Name System
6a0b6499fbee.sentence: The hierarchy of domains descends from right to left; each label to the left specifies a subdivision, or subdomain of the domain to the right.

bcee18b0220e.title: Domain Name System
bcee18b0220e.sentence: For example, the label example specifies a subdomain of the com domain, and www is a subdomain of example.com.

eaeaa8b2a8d4.title: Domain Name System
eaeaa8b2a8d4.sentence: This tree of subdivisions may have up to 127 levels.

f49a0a6eb18f.title: Domain Name System
f49a0a6eb18f.sentence: The tree subdivides into zones beginning at the root zone.

2349c473f002.title: Domain Name System
2349c473f002.sentence: A DNS zone may consist of as many domains and subdomains as the zone manager chooses.

c04f0fa0610a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
c04f0fa0610a.sentence: There are several types of TLD names.

c8ac81119f8d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
c8ac81119f8d.sentence: For example, generic TLD (.com,.org), country code TLD (.us), test TLD (.test).

dd12d946a32d.title: Domain Name System
dd12d946a32d.sentence: A label may contain zero to 63 characters, because the length is only allowed to take 6 bits.

d8dd4e29f030.title: Domain Name System
d8dd4e29f030.sentence: The null label of length zero is reserved for the root zone.

484fb215f3ef.title: Domain Name System
484fb215f3ef.sentence: The full domain name may not exceed the length of 253 characters in its textual representation (or 254 with the trailing dot).

ed5bf270e836.title: Domain Name System
ed5bf270e836.sentence: This rule is known as the LDH rule (letters, digits, hyphen).

e685368bb89f.title: Domain Name System
e685368bb89f.sentence: The characters allowed in labels are a subset of the ASCII character set, consisting of characters a through z, A through Z, digits 0 through 9, and hyphen.

1288e0b33787.title: Domain Name System
1288e0b33787.sentence: Labels may not start or end with a hyphen.

b63ea8f119a7.title: Domain Name System
b63ea8f119a7.sentence: Domain names are interpreted in a case-independent manner.

8ef7b159c084.title: Domain Name System
8ef7b159c084.sentence: The limited set of ASCII characters permitted in the DNS prevented the representation of names and words of many languages in their native alphabets or scripts.

7feb5dcf9e20.title: Domain Name System
7feb5dcf9e20.sentence: To make this possible, ICANN approved the Internationalizing Domain Names in Applications (IDNA) system, by which user applications, such as web browsers, map Unicode strings into the valid DNS character set using Punycode.

d40767510104.title: Top-level domain
d40767510104.sentence: A top-level domain (TLD) is one of the domains at the highest level in the hierarchical Domain Name System of the Internet after the root domain.

622e91e32671.title: Top-level domain
622e91e32671.sentence: For all domains in lower levels, it is the last part of the domain name, that is, the last non-empty label of a fully qualified domain name.

4fe274d2c488.title: Top-level domain
4fe274d2c488.sentence: For example, in the domain name www.example.com, the top-level domain is.com.

e0c75ff31cc7.title: Top-level domain
e0c75ff31cc7.sentence: The top-level domain names are installed in the root zone of the name space.

8e6528562932.title: Top-level domain
8e6528562932.sentence: Responsibility for management of most top-level domains is delegated to specific organizations by the ICANN, an Internet multi-stakeholder community, which operates the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA), and is in charge of maintaining the DNS root zone.

3b0d01c6a1ba.title: Top-level domain
3b0d01c6a1ba.sentence: As of 2015, IANA distinguishes the following groups of top-level domains:

ef070c8866c2.title: Top-level domain
ef070c8866c2.sentence: - Infrastructure top-level domain (ARPA): This group consists of one domain, the Address and Routing Parameter Area.

59b36ec5f30c.title: Top-level domain
59b36ec5f30c.sentence: - Generic top-level domains (gTLD): Top-level domains with three or more characters

9c76f1b17b06.title: Top-level domain
9c76f1b17b06.sentence: - Generic restricted top-level domains (grTLD): These domains are managed under official ICANN-accredited registrars.

9453ad8b1ba0.title: Top-level domain
9453ad8b1ba0.sentence: - Sponsored top-level domains (sTLD): These domains are proposed and sponsored by private agencies or organizations that establish and enforce rules restricting the eligibility to use the TLD.

b5863f6a1d51.title: Top-level domain
b5863f6a1d51.sentence: - country-code top-level domains (ccTLD): Two-letter domains established for countries or territories.

31d586636008.title: Top-level domain
31d586636008.sentence: - Internationalized country code top-level domains (IDN ccTLD): ccTLDs in non-Latin character sets (e.g., Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, or Chinese).

f638009542e2.title: Top-level domain
f638009542e2.sentence: With some historical exceptions, the code for any territory is the same as its two-letter ISO 3166 code.

c99599632b96.title: Top-level domain
c99599632b96.sentence: Since 2009, countries with non–Latin-based scripts may apply for internationalized country code top-level domain names, which are displayed in end-user applications in their language-native script or alphabet but use a Punycode-translated ASCII domain name in the Domain Name System.

77d1a8e56960.title: Top-level domain
77d1a8e56960.sentence: The domain.arpa was the first Internet top-level domain.

afe7da10eaf3.title: Top-level domain
afe7da10eaf3.sentence: It was intended to be used only temporarily, aiding in the transition of traditional ARPANET host names to the domain name system.

e3c53b112550.title: Top-level domain
e3c53b112550.sentence: However, after it had been used for reverse DNS lookup, it was found impractical to retire it, and is used today exclusively for Internet infrastructure purposes such as in-addr.arpa for IPv4 and ip6.arpa for IPv6 reverse DNS resolution, uri.arpa and urn.arpa for the Dynamic Delegation Discovery System, and e164.arpa for telephone number mapping based on NAPTR DNS records.

0e87db7f44f6.title: Top-level domain
0e87db7f44f6.sentence: A set of domain names is reserved by the Internet Engineering Task Force as special-use domain names.

b49d8c36cce3.title: Top-level domain
b49d8c36cce3.sentence: These reserved names should not be used in production networks that utilize the global domain name system.

fb155a572339.title: Top-level domain
fb155a572339.sentence: .invalid | RFC 6761 | use in invalid domain names

ff0bc0fb2e88.title: Top-level domain
ff0bc0fb2e88.sentence: .localhost | RFC 6761 | avoiding conflict with the traditional use of localhost as a hostname

b86cb6bc3995.title: Top-level domain
b86cb6bc3995.sentence: .local | RFC 6762 | link-local host names that can be resolved via the multicast DNS name resolution protocol

00f03eb56ab9.title: Top-level domain
00f03eb56ab9.sentence: .onion | RFC 7686 | self-authenticating names of Tor onion services

a0299bb49bc9.title: Top-level domain
a0299bb49bc9.sentence: ICANN rejected several proposed domains to include.home and.corp due to conflicts regarding gTLDs that are in use in internal networks.

fcac02583dc2.title: Top-level domain
fcac02583dc2.sentence: For example, programmers may have used custom local domains such as foo.bar or test.dev, which would both collide with the creation of gTLDs.bar in 2014 and.dev in 2019.

cc9bc12eacd2.title: Top-level domain
cc9bc12eacd2.sentence: Due to the structure of DNS, each node in the tree has its own collection of records, and since top-level domains are nodes in DNS, they have records of their own.

6a9a436e2bfc.title: Top-level domain
6a9a436e2bfc.sentence: Dotless domains are top-level domains that take advantage of that fact and implement A, AAAA or MX DNS records to serve webpages or allow incoming email directly on a TLD – for example, a webpage hosted on http://example/ or an email address user@example.

a1eb3993f321.title: Top-level domain
a1eb3993f321.sentence: ICANN and IAB have spoken out against the practice, classifying it as a security risk among other concerns.

d1a39d35c338.title: Time to live
d1a39d35c338.sentence: Time to live (TTL) or hop limit is a mechanism which limits the lifespan or lifetime of data in a computer or network.

22c4f2679eee.title: Time to live
22c4f2679eee.sentence: TTL may be implemented as a counter or timestamp attached to or embedded in the data.

96975bdc6d8b.title: Time to live
96975bdc6d8b.sentence: Once the prescribed event count or timespan has elapsed, data is discarded or revalidated.

70da593d5c84.title: Time to live
70da593d5c84.sentence: In computer networking, TTL prevents a data packet from circulating indefinitely.

c9f6a86a262a.title: Time to live
c9f6a86a262a.sentence: In computing applications, TTL is commonly used to improve the performance and manage the caching of data.

cb11b64e3d98.title: Time to live
cb11b64e3d98.sentence: Under the Internet Protocol, TTL is an 8-bit field.

77fcb8a24db3.title: Time to live
77fcb8a24db3.sentence: The maximum TTL value is 255, the maximum value of a single octet.

dae91c748c1a.title: Time to live
dae91c748c1a.sentence: The TTL field is set by the sender of the datagram, and reduced by every router on the route to its destination.

8f94eccec3bb.title: Time to live
8f94eccec3bb.sentence: If the TTL field reaches zero before the datagram arrives at its destination, then the datagram is discarded and an Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) error datagram (11 - Time Exceeded) is sent back to the sender.

d383a2411b16.title: Time to live
d383a2411b16.sentence: The purpose of the TTL field is to avoid a situation in which an undeliverable datagram keeps circulating on an Internet system, and such a system eventually becoming swamped by such "immortals".

8c55faab9654.title: Time to live
8c55faab9654.sentence: In theory, under IPv4, time to live is measured in seconds, although every host that passes the datagram must reduce the TTL by at least one unit.

33600b79ae94.title: Time to live
33600b79ae94.sentence: In practice, the TTL field is reduced by one on every hop.

06fc7897c6de.title: Time to live
06fc7897c6de.sentence: To reflect this practice, the field is renamed hop limit in IPv6.

64203301e12a.title: Time to live
64203301e12a.sentence: TTLs also occur in the Domain Name System (DNS), where they are set by an authoritative name server for a particular resource record.

971c54ee860c.title: Time to live
971c54ee860c.sentence: When a caching (recursive) nameserver queries the authoritative nameserver for a resource record, it will cache that record for the time (in seconds) specified by the TTL.

3e947bae2aa4.title: Time to live
3e947bae2aa4.sentence: Time to live may also be expressed as the date and time on which a record expires.

85531da58982.title: Time to live
85531da58982.sentence: The Expires: header in HTTP responses, the Cache-Control: max-age header field in both requests and responses and the expires field in HTTP cookies express time-to-live in this way.

fe00c1debd7b.title: Domain Name System
fe00c1debd7b.sentence: The Domain Name System specifies a database of information elements for network resources.

ee90e2d26983.title: Domain Name System
ee90e2d26983.sentence: Each record has a type (name and number), an expiration time (time to live), a class, and type-specific data.

9f32065136df.title: Domain Name System
9f32065136df.sentence: When sent over an Internet Protocol network, all records (answer, authority, and additional sections) use the common format specified in RFC 1035:

b5efccc34172.title: Domain Name System
b5efccc34172.sentence: NAME | Name of the node to which this record pertains | Variable

d72483290ca5.title: Domain Name System
d72483290ca5.sentence: TYPE | Type of RR in numeric form (e.g., 15 for MX RRs) | 2

3d965d652c55.title: Domain Name System
3d965d652c55.sentence: TTL | Count of seconds that the RR stays valid (The maximum is 2 31 −1, which is about 68 years) | 4

d0e736cc6084.title: Domain Name System
d0e736cc6084.sentence: RDLENGTH | Length of RDATA field (specified in octets) | 2

f67b817a8c17.title: Domain Name System
f67b817a8c17.sentence: RDATA | Additional RR-specific data | Variable, as per RDLENGTH

e4ae2d28cbcc.title: Domain Name System
e4ae2d28cbcc.sentence: It indicates the format of the data and it gives a hint of its intended use.

9dae47e566db.title: Domain Name System
9dae47e566db.sentence: RDATA is data of type-specific relevance, such as the IP address for address records, or the priority and hostname for MX records.

025f8a834a0c.title: Domain Name System
025f8a834a0c.sentence: CLASS of a record is set to IN (for Internet) for common DNS records involving Internet hostnames, servers, or IP addresses.

50cebeadcc2f.title: Domain Name System
50cebeadcc2f.sentence: Each class is an independent name space with potentially different delegations of DNS zones.

6f8555812da1.title: Domain Name System
6f8555812da1.sentence: Resource records of the same type are described as a resource record set (RRset), having no special ordering.

8b6ddd873ad3.title: Domain Name System
8b6ddd873ad3.sentence: DNS resolvers return the entire set upon query, but servers may implement round-robin ordering to achieve load balancing.

27c705e92757.title: Domain Name System
27c705e92757.sentence: The domain name system supports wildcard DNS records which specify names that start with the asterisk label, *, e.g., *.example.

4d2bbd919920.title: Domain Name System
4d2bbd919920.sentence: DNS records belonging to wildcard domain names specify rules for generating resource records within a single DNS zone by substituting whole labels with matching components of the query name, including any specified descendants.

4c738610c9ca.title: Domain Name System
4c738610c9ca.sentence: The right to use a domain name is delegated by domain name registrars which are accredited by the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) or other organizations such as OpenNIC, that are charged with overseeing the name and number systems of the Internet.

9587af3f2cf7.title: Domain Name System
9587af3f2cf7.sentence: In addition to ICANN, each top-level domain (TLD) is maintained and serviced technically by an administrative organization, operating a registry.

dc87f7233d51.title: Domain Name System
dc87f7233d51.sentence: A registrant is a person or organization who asked for domain registration.

38c51366288e.title: Domain Name System
38c51366288e.sentence: The registrants (users of a domain name) are customers of the registrar, in some cases through additional subcontracting of resellers.

eb26dea795f8.title: Domain Name System
eb26dea795f8.sentence: A registry is responsible for operating the database of names within its authoritative zone, although the term is most often used for TLDs.

bab92d23d5de.title: Domain Name System
bab92d23d5de.sentence: The registry receives registration information from each domain name registrar, which is authorized (accredited) to assign names in the corresponding zone and publishes the information using the WHOIS protocol.

3346ae39999e.title: Domain Name System
3346ae39999e.sentence: The TLD registries, such as for the domains COM, NET, and ORG use a registry-registrar model consisting of many domain name registrars.

b712aba3bd2c.title: Domain Name System
b712aba3bd2c.sentence: In this method of management, the registry only manages the domain name database and the relationship with the registrars.

88d08d6614e7.title: Domain Name System
88d08d6614e7.sentence: From about 2001, most generic top-level domain (gTLD) registries have adopted this so-called thick registry approach, i.e. keeping the WHOIS data in central registries instead of registrar databases.

33524f730b8c.title: Domain Name System
33524f730b8c.sentence: For TLDs on COM and NET, a thin registry model is used.

37e4fccb81bd.title: Domain Name System
37e4fccb81bd.sentence: The domain registry (GoDaddy, BigRock and PDR, VeriSign, etc.) holds basic WHOIS data (i.e., registrar and name servers, etc.).

34a0219a9bca.title: Domain Name System
34a0219a9bca.sentence: The Stanford Research Institute (now SRI International) maintained a text file named HOSTS.TXT that mapped host names to the numerical addresses of computers on the ARPANET.

f9ac2b86c7c3.title: Domain Name System
f9ac2b86c7c3.sentence: By the early 1980s, maintaining a single, centralized host table had become slow and unwieldy and the emerging network required an automated naming system to address technical and personnel issues.

1199ad581780.title: rfc>1034
1199ad581780.section: 2. INTRODUCTION > 2.1. The history of domain names
1199ad581780.sentence: - Host name to address mappings were maintained by the Network Information Center (NIC) in a single file (HOSTS.TXT) which was FTPed by all hosts [RFC-952, RFC-953].

c08edbfecda1.title: rfc>1034
c08edbfecda1.section: 2. INTRODUCTION > 2.1. The history of domain names
c08edbfecda1.sentence: bandwidth consumed in distributing a new version by this scheme is proportional to the square of the number of hosts in the network, and even when multiple levels of FTP are used, the outgoing FTP load on the NIC host is considerable.

e88f29d94db8.title: rfc>1034
e88f29d94db8.section: 2. INTRODUCTION > 2.1. The history of domain names
e88f29d94db8.sentence: Local organizations were administering their own names and addresses, but had to wait for the NIC to change HOSTS.TXT to make changes visible to the Internet at large.

cd03f4f12bd8.title: rfc>1034
cd03f4f12bd8.section: 2. INTRODUCTION > 2.1. The history of domain names
cd03f4f12bd8.sentence: Organizations also wanted some local structure on the name space.

fe355d5648f7.title: Domain Name System
fe355d5648f7.sentence: Mockapetris instead created the Domain Name System in 1983 while at the USC Information Sciences Institute.

c02f0ee26cb6.title: Domain Name System
c02f0ee26cb6.sentence: In November 1987, RFC 1034 and RFC 1035 superseded the 1983 DNS specifications.

0a055682b681.title: Domain Name System
0a055682b681.sentence: The Internet Engineering Task Force published the original specifications in RFC 882 and RFC 883 in November 1983.

6cbb4847c9a7.title: Domain Name System
6cbb4847c9a7.sentence: The most common types of records stored in the DNS database are for start of authority (SOA), IP addresses (A and AAAA), SMTP mail exchangers (MX), name servers (NS), pointers for reverse DNS lookups (PTR), and domain name aliases (CNAME).

0eb8e57bede8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
0eb8e57bede8.sentence: Here are the 8 most commonly used DNS Record Types.

e9b3054d6ca1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
e9b3054d6ca1.sentence: Maps a domain name to an IPv4 address.

9ba812c89406.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
9ba812c89406.sentence: It is one of the most essential records for translating human-readable domain names into IP addresses.

abe820cf2f8a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
abe820cf2f8a.sentence: Similar to an A record but maps a domain name to an IPv6 address.

75cfba382596.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
75cfba382596.sentence: They are used for websites and services that support the IPv6 protocol.

b58726f9b070.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
b58726f9b070.sentence: Used to alias one domain name to another.

2d9c113db754.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
2d9c113db754.sentence: Often used for subdomains, pointing them to the main domain while keeping the actual domain name hidden.

470cbff46f79.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
470cbff46f79.sentence: - CNAME (Canonical Name record): Forwards one domain or subdomain to another domain, does NOT provide an IP address.

87d6cf5b5e16.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
87d6cf5b5e16.sentence: Directs email traffic to the correct mail server.

55704a8830ba.title: Domain Name System
55704a8830ba.sentence: For instance, mail transfer agents use DNS to find the best mail server to deliver e-mail: An MX record provides a mapping between a domain and a mail exchanger; this can provide an additional layer of fault tolerance and load distribution.

b84353fc71ec.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
b84353fc71ec.sentence: Specifies the authoritative DNS servers for the domain.

7883a1404e37.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
7883a1404e37.sentence: These records help direct queries to the correct DNS servers for further lookups.

be0c7d47c252.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
be0c7d47c252.sentence: Provides reverse DNS lookup, mapping an IP address back to a domain name.

220c62d850e3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
220c62d850e3.sentence: It is commonly used in verifying the authenticity of a server.

4e1c7057bc82.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
4e1c7057bc82.sentence: SRV record specifies a host and port for specific services such as VoIP.

6c9c854aef2c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
6c9c854aef2c.sentence: They are used in conjunction with A records.

415015d77674.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
415015d77674.sentence: Allows the administrator to add human-readable text to the DNS records.

a72eda0d95da.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
a72eda0d95da.sentence: It is used to include verification records, like SPF, for email security.

384fa5ed1d7f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
384fa5ed1d7f.sentence: - SOA (Start of Authority): Stores admin information about a domain.

6e9164e44767.title: Domain Name System
6e9164e44767.sentence: A reverse DNS lookup is a query of the DNS for domain names when the IP address is known.

bc0341980690.title: Domain Name System
bc0341980690.sentence: The DNS stores IP addresses in the form of domain names as specially formatted names in pointer (PTR) records within the infrastructure TLD arpa.

d09d9314f487.title: Domain Name System
d09d9314f487.sentence: For IPv4, the domain is in-addr.arpa.

09db1d5a4eb6.title: Domain Name System
09db1d5a4eb6.sentence: For IPv6, the reverse lookup domain is ip6.arpa.

2ab07c8a5a02.title: Domain Name System
2ab07c8a5a02.sentence: The IP address is represented as a name in reverse-ordered octet representation for IPv4, and reverse-ordered nibble representation for IPv6.

c85f29b3c793.title: Domain Name System
c85f29b3c793.sentence: For example, assuming the IPv4 address 208.80.152.2 is assigned to Wikimedia, it is represented as a DNS name in reverse order: 2.152.80.208.in-addr.arpa.

22823878d183.title: Domain Name System
22823878d183.sentence: When performing a reverse lookup, the DNS client converts the address into these formats before querying the name for a PTR record following the delegation chain as for any DNS query.

2c48004f6eaa.title: Domain Name System
2c48004f6eaa.sentence: Multiple domain names may be associated with an IP address.

ad0179a87ab8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
ad0179a87ab8.sentence: If the server does not have a PTR record, it cannot resolve a reverse lookup.

48374da8d4bd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
48374da8d4bd.sentence: Reverse lookups are commonly used by email servers.

327e0fbb1b3a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
327e0fbb1b3a.sentence: Email servers check and see if an email message came from a valid server before bringing it onto their network.

f0e0b9286406.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
f0e0b9286406.sentence: Many email servers will reject messages from any server that does not support reverse lookups or from a server that is highly unlikely to be legitimate.

6a78257a0a82.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
6a78257a0a82.sentence: Note: Reverse DNS lookups are not universally adopted as they are not critical to the normal function of the internet.

c66bf4d57a4e.title: rfc>1034
c66bf4d57a4e.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.2. Inverse queries (Optional)
c66bf4d57a4e.sentence: Inverse queries are NOT an acceptable method for mapping host addresses to host names; use the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain instead.

60ed1af6a8e5.title: rfc>1034
60ed1af6a8e5.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
60ed1af6a8e5.sentence: The domain system provides such a feature using the canonical name (CNAME) RR.

440ddeeeea73.title: rfc>1034
440ddeeeea73.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
440ddeeeea73.sentence: A CNAME RR identifies its owner name as an alias, and specifies the corresponding canonical name in the RDATA section of the RR.

3be40d3a1e03.title: rfc>1034
3be40d3a1e03.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
3be40d3a1e03.sentence: In existing systems, hosts and other resources often have several names that identify the same resource.

6eb6f864d069.title: rfc>1034
6eb6f864d069.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
6eb6f864d069.sentence: Most of these systems have a notion that one of the equivalent set of names is the canonical or primary name and all others are aliases.

a961616aae3e.title: rfc>1034
a961616aae3e.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
a961616aae3e.sentence: If a CNAME RR is present at a node, no other data should be present; this ensures that the data for a canonical name and its aliases cannot be different.

8b1a0d9bbbc2.title: rfc>1034
8b1a0d9bbbc2.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
8b1a0d9bbbc2.sentence: This rule also insures that a cached CNAME can be used without checking with an authoritative server for other RR types.

ee6a768079e6.title: rfc>1034
ee6a768079e6.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
ee6a768079e6.sentence: When a name server fails to find a desired RR in the resource set associated with the domain name, it checks to see if the resource set consists of a CNAME record with a matching class.

910786ecdfae.title: rfc>1034
910786ecdfae.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
910786ecdfae.sentence: If so, the name server includes the CNAME record in the response and restarts the query at the domain name specified in the data field of the CNAME record.

7842caad5229.title: rfc>1034
7842caad5229.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
7842caad5229.sentence: The one exception to this rule is that queries which match the CNAME type are not restarted.

07dd7bf6fa1a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
07dd7bf6fa1a.sentence: The authoritative nameserver contains information specific to the domain name it serves (e.g. google.com) and it can provide a recursive resolver with the IP address of that server found in the DNS A record, or if the domain has a CNAME record (alias) it will provide the recursive resolver with an alias domain, at which point the recursive resolver will have to perform a whole new DNS lookup to procure a record from an authoritative nameserver (often an A record containing an IP address).

ecebc1712afc.title: rfc>1034
ecebc1712afc.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
ecebc1712afc.sentence: Domain names in RRs which point at another name should always point at the primary name and not the alias.

ddcc63aff035.title: rfc>1034
ddcc63aff035.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
ddcc63aff035.sentence: This avoids extra indirections in accessing information.

e07436619563.title: rfc>1034
e07436619563.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.6. Resource Records > 3.6.2. Aliases and canonical names
e07436619563.sentence: Of course, by the robustness principle, domain software should not fail when presented with CNAME chains or loops; CNAME chains should be followed and CNAME loops signalled as an error.

943b9b1eee34.title: List of DNS record types
943b9b1eee34.sentence: This is an overview of resource records (RRs) permissible in zone files of the Domain Name System (DNS).

a1fe10b36fc3.title: List of DNS record types
a1fe10b36fc3.sentence: DNAME | 39 | RFC 6672 | Delegation name record | Alias for a name and all its subnames, unlike CNAME, which is an alias for only the exact name. Like a CNAME record, the DNS lookup will continue by retrying the lookup with the new name.

ce36dc088e0d.title: List of DNS record types
ce36dc088e0d.sentence: ALIAS / ANAME / apex CNAME / CNAME flattening / top-level redirection | - | draft-ietf-dnsop-aname-04 | Alias similar to DNAME | An ANAME, ALIAS, apex CNAME, CNAME flattening, or sometimes also top-level redirection record is a pseudo record type and a commonly used but not RFC-standardized record type. Its implementation varies. It serves as an alternative to CNAMEs especially for the bare domain name and where such records should co-exist with others. It causes the DNS software vendor to synthetically generate A and AAAA records similar to the ones of the ANAME-records destination. If the destination changes these synthetic A and AAAA records change automatically as well. The actual mechanisms used are often considered proprietary.

c5a833d3fd5c.title: List of DNS record types
c5a833d3fd5c.sentence: TXT | 16 | RFC 1035 | Text record | Originally for arbitrary human-readable text in a DNS record. Since the early 1990s, however, this record more often carries machine-readable data, such as specified by RFC 1464, opportunistic encryption, Sender Policy Framework, DKIM, DMARC, DNS-SD, etc.

27f904e330d2.title: List of DNS record types
27f904e330d2.sentence: SRV | 33 | RFC 2782 | Service locator | Generalized service location record, used for newer protocols instead of creating protocol-specific records such as MX

f3af3e84bd61.title: List of DNS record types
f3af3e84bd61.sentence: SVCB | 64 | RFC 9460 | Service Binding | This resource record provides metadata and other information that can help clients connect to the host. The HTTPS record is a specialised SVCB record to help when establishing HTTPS connections. The more general SVCB record can provide other information such as supported protocols, alternative endpoints, and some types of aliasing not supported by CNAME records.

3b6fe4bfcadc.title: List of DNS record types
3b6fe4bfcadc.sentence: HTTPS | 65 | RFC 9460 | HTTPS Binding | A specialised type of SVCB record. Provides connection information required to establish a secure connection via HTTPS, which would ordinarily be obtained and negotiated during connection to the host. Obtaining the information from the DNS server instead of negotiating it with the host allows for more secure connections (e.g. by using Encrypted Client Hello) and lower latency when the connection to the host is first established.

a8a5c8282b44.title: List of DNS record types
a8a5c8282b44.sentence: CAA | 257 | RFC 8659 | Certification Authority Authorization | DNS Certification Authority Authorization, constraining acceptable CAs for a host/domain

b926d0e4648b.title: List of DNS record types
b926d0e4648b.sentence: TLSA | 52 | RFC 6698 | TLSA certificate association | A record for DANE. RFC 6698 defines "The TLSA DNS resource record is used to associate a TLS server certificate or public key with the domain name where the record is found, thus forming a 'TLSA certificate association'".

8a522b2ebd10.title: List of DNS record types
8a522b2ebd10.sentence: SSHFP | 44 | RFC 4255 | SSH Public Key Fingerprint | Resource record for publishing SSH public host key fingerprints in the DNS, in order to aid in verifying the authenticity of the host. RFC 6594 defines ECC SSH keys and SHA-256 hashes. See the IANA SSHFP RR parameters registry for details.

1bc11eaca127.title: List of DNS record types
1bc11eaca127.sentence: RRSIG | 46 | RFC 4034 | DNSSEC signature | Signature for a DNSSEC-secured record set. Uses the same format as the SIG record.

3546565fbeb3.title: List of DNS record types
3546565fbeb3.sentence: DNSKEY | 48 | RFC 4034 | DNS Key record | The key record used in DNSSEC. Uses the same format as the KEY record.

e7104529bbff.title: List of DNS record types
e7104529bbff.sentence: DS | 43 | RFC 4034 | Delegation signer | The record used to identify the DNSSEC signing key of a delegated zone

abd1f6681695.title: List of DNS record types
abd1f6681695.sentence: NSEC | 47 | RFC 4034 | Next Secure record | Part of DNSSEC—used to prove a name does not exist. Uses the same format as the (obsolete) NXT record.

dc41ef6b1f3f.title: List of DNS record types
dc41ef6b1f3f.sentence: NSEC3 | 50 | RFC 5155 | Next Secure record version 3 | An extension to DNSSEC that allows proof of nonexistence for a name without permitting zonewalking

67e30b750458.title: List of DNS record types
67e30b750458.sentence: AXFR | 252 | RFC 1035 | Authoritative Zone Transfer | Transfers entire zone file from the primary name server to secondary name servers

27a3492f6783.title: List of DNS record types
27a3492f6783.sentence: IXFR | 251 | RFC 1996 | Incremental Zone Transfer | Requests a zone transfer of the given zone but only differences from a previous serial number. This request may be ignored and a full (AXFR) sent in response if the authoritative server is unable to fulfill the request due to configuration or lack of required deltas.

c2f87910d1d3.title: List of DNS record types
c2f87910d1d3.sentence: * | 255 | RFC 1035 | All cached records | Returns all records of all types known to the name server. If the name server does not have any information on the name, the request will be forwarded on. The records returned may not be complete. For example, if there is both an A and an MX for a name, but the name server has only the A record cached, only the A record will be returned. Usually referred to as ANY (e.g., in dig, Windows nslookup, and Wireshark). In 2019, RFC 8482 standards-track publication led many DNS providers, including Cloudflare, to provide only minimal responses to "ANY" queries, instead of enumerating records.

f0354b43011f.title: List of DNS record types
f0354b43011f.sentence: OPT | 41 | RFC 6891 | Option | This is a pseudo-record type needed to support EDNS.

9d5a290e34e5.title: List of DNS record types
9d5a290e34e5.sentence: MD | 3 | RFC 883 | RFC 973 | Mail destination (MD) and mail forwarder (MF) records: MAILA is not an actual record type, but a query type which returns MF and/or MD records. RFC 973 replaced these records with the MX record.

9ba9cc171aa0.title: List of DNS record types
9ba9cc171aa0.sentence: WKS | 11 | RFC 883 RFC 1035 | Declared as "not to be relied upon" by RFC 1123 (more in RFC 1127 ). | Record to describe well-known services supported by a host. Not used in practice. The current recommendation and practice is to determine whether a service is supported on an IP address by trying to connect to it. SMTP is even prohibited from using WKS records in MX processing.

4ed273f22d98.title: List of DNS record types
4ed273f22d98.sentence: HINFO | 13 | RFC 8482 RFC 1035 | Placeholder record, or host information | Repurposed to be used while responding to ANY queries. Originally defined as "Host information", intended to inform about host's operating system and hardware. RFC 8482 did not obsolete this conventional meaning for explicit HINFO queries, but rather considers it rarely used.

cd255abf627f.title: rfc>1034
cd255abf627f.sentence: The DNS has three major components:

137019767ac6.title: rfc>1034
137019767ac6.sentence: - The DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS, which are specifications for a tree structured name space and data associated with the names.

70cf52dad419.title: rfc>1034
70cf52dad419.sentence: - NAME SERVERS are server programs which hold information about the domain tree's structure and set information.

bf268bfa4469.title: rfc>1034
bf268bfa4469.sentence: - RESOLVERS are programs that extract information from name servers in response to client requests.

8200e70c2a0b.title: rfc>1034
8200e70c2a0b.sentence: A name server may cache structure or set information about any part of the domain tree, but in general a particular name server has complete information about a subset of the domain space, and pointers to other name servers that can be used to lead to information from any part of the domain tree.

3acdb7f6cd8d.title: rfc>1034
3acdb7f6cd8d.sentence: Name servers know the parts of the domain tree for which they have complete information; a name server is said to be an AUTHORITY for these parts of the name space.

6ea585327613.title: rfc>1034
6ea585327613.sentence: Authoritative information is organized into units called ZONEs, and these zones can be automatically distributed to the name servers which provide redundant service for the data in a zone.

6133443d477d.title: rfc>1034
6133443d477d.sentence: Resolvers must be able to access at least one name server and use that name server's information to answer a query directly, or pursue the query using referrals to other name servers.

46ec1386d187.title: rfc>1034
46ec1386d187.sentence: A resolver will typically be a system routine that is directly accessible to user programs; hence no protocol is necessary between the resolver and the user program.

8fae07827887.title: rfc>1034
8fae07827887.sentence: - From the user's point of view, the domain system is accessed through a simple procedure or OS call to a local resolver.

04e5d73634fe.title: rfc>1034
04e5d73634fe.sentence: The domain space consists of a single tree and the user can request information from any section of the tree.

9ac8b83c2294.title: rfc>1034
9ac8b83c2294.sentence: - From the resolver's point of view, the domain system is composed of an unknown number of name servers.

ebfd900901ed.title: rfc>1034
ebfd900901ed.sentence: - From a name server's point of view, the domain system consists of separate sets of local information called zones.

c7c0e6b41fb7.title: rfc>1034
c7c0e6b41fb7.sentence: The name server must periodically refresh its zones from master copies in local files or foreign name servers.

ac7416ca65d5.title: rfc>1034
ac7416ca65d5.sentence: The name server must concurrently process queries that arrive from resolvers.

9e73adba1d6d.title: rfc>1034
9e73adba1d6d.sentence: In the interests of performance, implementations may couple these functions.

993569c1abe6.title: rfc>1034
993569c1abe6.sentence: For example, a resolver on the same machine as a name server might share a database consisting of the the zones managed by the name server and the cache managed by the resolver.

09537b310d8b.title: rfc>1034
09537b310d8b.sentence: - The primary goal is a consistent name space which will be used for referring to resources.

60964996bccd.title: rfc>1034
60964996bccd.sentence: - The sheer size of the database and frequency of updates suggest that it must be maintained in a distributed manner, with local caching to improve performance.

3c53214e3bae.title: rfc>1034
3c53214e3bae.sentence: - The costs of implementing such a facility dictate that it be generally useful, and not restricted to a single application.

6a369ba8c131.title: rfc>1034
6a369ba8c131.sentence: In order to avoid the problems caused by ad hoc encodings, names should not be required to contain network identifiers, addresses, routes, or similar information as part of the name.

e9438dea43de.title: rfc>1034
e9438dea43de.sentence: attempt to collect a consistent copy of the entire database will become more and more expensive and difficult, and hence should be avoided.

5515c7256f98.title: rfc>1034
5515c7256f98.sentence: The same principle holds for the structure of the name space, and in particular mechanisms for creating and deleting names; these should also be distributed.

53cb675c0546.title: rfc>1034
53cb675c0546.sentence: - Where there tradeoffs between the cost of acquiring data, the speed of updates, and the accuracy of caches, the source of the data should control the tradeoff.

ccf7e4d5c093.title: rfc>1034
ccf7e4d5c093.sentence: All data associated with a name is tagged with a type, and queries can be limited to a single type.

94acb71dcc12.title: rfc>1034
94acb71dcc12.sentence: - Because we want the name space to be useful in dissimilar networks and applications, we provide the ability to use the same name space with different protocol families or management.

937fcddb6a82.title: rfc>1034
937fcddb6a82.sentence: The DNS tags all data with a class as well as the type, so that we can allow parallel use of different formats for data of type address.

232de2395e68.title: rfc>1034
232de2395e68.sentence: - We want name server transactions to be independent of the communications system that carries them.

e4b59d0aa013.title: rfc>1034
e4b59d0aa013.sentence: Some systems may wish to use datagrams for queries and responses, and only establish virtual circuits for transactions that need the reliability (e.g., database updates, long transactions); other systems will use virtual circuits exclusively.

9680032c75ae.title: rfc>1034
9680032c75ae.sentence: - The system should be useful across a wide spectrum of host capabilities.

8b9f25255877.title: rfc>1034
8b9f25255877.sentence: Both personal computers and large timeshared hosts should be able to use the system, though perhaps in different ways.

72cdc42495e7.title: Domain name registrar
72cdc42495e7.sentence: A domain name registrar is a company, person, or office that manages the reservation of Internet domain names.

7a02edca9bd8.title: Domain name registrar
7a02edca9bd8.sentence: A domain name registrar must be accredited by a generic top-level domain (gTLD) registry or a country code top-level domain (ccTLD) registry.

2130ad2da0c8.title: Domain name registrar
2130ad2da0c8.sentence: Domain registration information and accreditation is maintained by the domain name registries, which contract with domain registrars to provide registration services to the public.

02cf86872531.title: Domain name registrar
02cf86872531.sentence: Only the designated registrar may modify or delete information about domain names in a central registry database.

ae2819992ab6.title: Domain name registrar
ae2819992ab6.sentence: Registration of a domain name establishes a set of name server records in the DNS servers of the parent domain, indicating the IP addresses of DNS servers that are authoritative for the domain.

07133fc6343f.title: Domain name registrar
07133fc6343f.sentence: Registrars require the specification of usually at least two name servers.

4f82efe129fb.title: Domain name registrar
4f82efe129fb.sentence: Registration of a domain does not automatically imply the provision of DNS services for the registered domain.

ad2344e7458f.title: Domain name registrar
ad2344e7458f.sentence: Most registrars do offer DNS hosting as an optional free service for domains registered through them.

a56c7f8b63e8.title: Domain name registrar
a56c7f8b63e8.sentence: This involves a registrar processing public key data and creating DS records for addition into the parent zone.

0edf1e498f48.title: Domain name registrar
0edf1e498f48.sentence: All new GTLD registries and registrars must support DNSSEC.

9b20693b93dc.title: Domain name registrar
9b20693b93dc.sentence: A domain name transfer is the process of changing the designated registrar of a domain name.

bf26a52bc497.title: Domain name registrar
bf26a52bc497.sentence: ICANN has defined a Policy on Transfer of Registrations between Registrars.

647df6f09722.title: Domain name registrar
647df6f09722.sentence: - The end user verifies that the WHOIS or Registration Data Access Protocol (RDAP) admin contact info is correct, particularly the email address; obtains the authentication code (EPP transfer code) from the old registrar, and removes any domain lock that has been placed on the registration.

0c96a5840506.title: Domain name registrar
0c96a5840506.sentence: - The gaining Registrar must obtain express authorization from either the Registered Name Holder or the Administrative Contact.

ff00db9555e7.title: Domain name registrar
ff00db9555e7.sentence: The new registrar starts electronically the transfer of the domain with the help of the authentication code (auth code).

73b3802b386a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
73b3802b386a.sentence: A subdomain is an additional part of our main domain name.

5802b2de89ff.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
5802b2de89ff.sentence: It is commonly used to logically separate a website into sections.

7577ccf5d59b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
7577ccf5d59b.sentence: We can create multiple subdomains or child domains on the main domain.

49dcac434896.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
49dcac434896.sentence: For example, blog.example.com where blog is the subdomain, example is the primary domain and.com is the top-level domain (TLD).

bce7f23d59a2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
bce7f23d59a2.sentence: Similar examples can be support.example.com or careers.example.com.

e7403a89331f.title: Domain Name System
e7403a89331f.sentence: Assuming the resolver has no cached records to accelerate the process, the resolution process starts with a query to one of the root servers.

b30526844108.title: Domain Name System
b30526844108.sentence: The resolver now queries the servers referred to, and iteratively repeats this process until it receives an authoritative answer.

e7bd8a9ca02a.title: Domain Name System
e7bd8a9ca02a.sentence: In typical operation, the root servers do not answer directly, but respond with a referral to more authoritative servers, e.g., a query for "www.wikipedia.org" is referred to the org servers.

6abf09d536f9.title: Domain Name System
6abf09d536f9.sentence: Domain name resolvers determine the domain name servers responsible for the domain name in question by a sequence of queries starting with the right-most (top-level) domain label.

e6d15892e012.title: Domain Name System
e6d15892e012.sentence: For proper operation of its domain name resolver, a network host is configured with an initial cache (hints) of the known addresses of the root name servers.

0c2447dcb0a9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
0c2447dcb0a9.sentence: There are 3 basic levels of DNS servers:

889c9eaa0c03.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
889c9eaa0c03.sentence: It stores the IP addresses of Top Level Domain (TLD) name servers.

eb4d9309ba51.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
eb4d9309ba51.sentence: It stores the IP addresses of authoritative name servers.

94e5f5ef6850.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
94e5f5ef6850.sentence: It provides actual answers to the DNS query.

20787cead661.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
20787cead661.sentence: - google.com is typed into the browser, and the browser sends the domain name to the DNS resolver.

96046746284e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
96046746284e.sentence: - The resolver queries a DNS root name server.

be56cad47847.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
be56cad47847.sentence: - The root server responds to the resolver with the address of a TLD DNS server.

e872b16ce80b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
e872b16ce80b.sentence: - The resolver then makes a request to the.com TLD.

4284f001381f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
4284f001381f.sentence: - The TLD server responds with the IP address of the domain’s name server, google.com (authoritative name server).

81094375d7fb.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
81094375d7fb.sentence: - The DNS resolver sends a query to the domain’s nameserver.

fe4799742052.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md

6d1d9c95d4e4.title: Domain Name System
6d1d9c95d4e4.sentence: A common approach to reduce the query load on DNS servers is to cache the results of name resolution locally or on intermediary resolver hosts.

ca828c55955c.title: Domain Name System
ca828c55955c.sentence: Each DNS query result comes with a time to live (TTL), which indicates how long the information remains valid before it needs to be discarded or refreshed.

71db4d0b5daf.title: Domain Name System

ad24eb318c1c.sentence: When it hits zero, the record is deleted or purged from the cache.

c3fd130fbaba.sentence: The key functionality of the DNS exploited here is that different users can simultaneously receive different translations for the same domain name, a key point of divergence from a traditional phone-book view of the DNS.

c0ae6a965f53.title: Domain Name System
c0ae6a965f53.sentence: An important and ubiquitous function of the DNS is its central role in distributed Internet services such as cloud services and content delivery networks.

4ce6004ee569.title: Domain Name System
4ce6004ee569.sentence: When a user accesses a distributed Internet service using a URL, the domain name of the URL is translated to the IP address of a server that is proximal to the user.

fae8cb8722c6.title: Domain Name System
fae8cb8722c6.sentence: This process of using the DNS to assign proximal servers to users is key to providing faster and more reliable responses on the Internet and is widely used by most major Internet services.

780190ecfabf.title: Domain Name System
780190ecfabf.sentence: Multiple hostnames may correspond to a single IP address, which is useful in virtual hosting, in which many web sites are served from a single host.
