935cdcae0068.sentence: The Host header field distinguishes between various DNS names sharing a single IP address, allowing name-based virtual hosting.

93058dabf211.title: Domain Name System
93058dabf211.sentence: Originally, security concerns were not major design considerations for DNS software or any software for deployment on the early Internet, as the network was not open for participation by the general public.

81015a91df1a.title: Domain Name System
81015a91df1a.sentence: DNS responses traditionally do not have a cryptographic signature, leading to many attack possibilities; the Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) modify DNS to add support for cryptographically signed responses.

f861af4a2bfb.title: Domain Name System
f861af4a2bfb.sentence: One such issue is DNS cache poisoning, in which data is distributed to caching resolvers under the pretense of being an authoritative origin server, thereby polluting the data store with potentially false information and long expiration times (time-to-live).

a2f014245320.title: Domain Name System
a2f014245320.sentence: Subsequently, legitimate application requests may be redirected to network hosts operated with malicious intent.

ebc6f993beec.sentence: Other extensions, such as TSIG, add support for cryptographic authentication between trusted peers and are commonly used to authorize zone transfer or dynamic update operations.

7f6c625a3f2b.title: Domain Name System
7f6c625a3f2b.sentence: DNS can also "leak" from otherwise secure or private connections, if attention is not paid to their configuration, and at times DNS has been used to bypass firewalls by malicious persons, and exfiltrate data, since it is often seen as innocuous.

1ce8cdc3b7c1.title: Domain Name System
1ce8cdc3b7c1.sentence: This technique involves the use of DNS TXT records to send commands to infected systems.

d0867e15595a.title: Domain Name System
d0867e15595a.sentence: This form of malware communication is stealthy, as DNS requests are usually allowed through firewalls, and because DNS traffic is often seen as benign, these communications can bypass many network security defenses.

0424a06bff1f.sentence: For example, paypal.com and paypa1.com are different names, yet users may be unable to distinguish them in a graphical user interface depending on the user's chosen typeface.

3ebd333b3276.title: Domain Name System
3ebd333b3276.sentence: This problem, known as the IDN homograph attack, is acute in systems that support internationalized domain names, as many character codes in ISO 10646 may appear identical on typical computer screens.

6bfb6e475b50.sentence: This vulnerability is occasionally exploited in phishing.

3fb36f0a7212.title: Domain Name System
3fb36f0a7212.sentence: DNS resolvers are classified by a variety of query methods, such as recursive, non-recursive, and iterative.

a9b0ef2892af.title: Domain Name System
a9b0ef2892af.sentence: In a recursive query, a DNS resolver queries a single DNS server, which may in turn query other DNS servers on behalf of the requester.

d6c5846d754c.title: Domain Name System
d6c5846d754c.sentence: The iterative query procedure is a process in which a DNS resolver queries a chain of one or more DNS servers.

6b2338a702ab.title: Domain Name System
6b2338a702ab.sentence: A resolution process may use a combination of these methods.

c0104f93dbc8.title: Domain Name System
c0104f93dbc8.sentence: A recursive query is one for which the DNS server answers the query completely by querying other name servers as needed.

42718bafce0f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
42718bafce0f.sentence: In a recursive query, a DNS client requires that a DNS server (typically a DNS recursive resolver) will respond to the client with either the requested resource record or an error message if the resolver can't find the record.

b32f79005ce0.title: Domain Name System
b32f79005ce0.sentence: For example, a simple stub resolver running on a home router typically makes a recursive query to the DNS server run by the user's ISP.

3e5fea9082e4.title: Domain Name System
3e5fea9082e4.sentence: Each server refers the client to the next server in the chain, until the current server can fully resolve the request.

7c85446f6492.title: Domain Name System
7c85446f6492.sentence: For example, a possible resolution of www.example.com would query a global root server, then a "com" server, and finally an "example.com" server.

24a6b101b1c5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
24a6b101b1c5.sentence: The DNS client must then repeat the query directly against the DNS server it was referred.

3992627cdcd5.title: Domain Name System
3992627cdcd5.sentence: In a non-recursive query, a DNS resolver queries a DNS server that provides a record either for which the server is authoritative, or it provides a partial result without querying other servers.

eb5b9bd5d7ea.title: Domain Name System
eb5b9bd5d7ea.sentence: In case of a caching DNS resolver, the non-recursive query of its local DNS cache delivers a result and reduces the load on upstream DNS servers by caching DNS resource records for a period of time after an initial response from upstream DNS servers.

010a18d46c38.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns

a327eda1d53e.sentence: In both cases, there is no need for additional rounds of queries (like in recursive or iterative queries).

04cf515e97ee.sentence: In typical operation, a client issues a recursive query to a caching recursive DNS server, which subsequently issues non-recursive queries to determine the answer and send a single answer back to the client.

3aeb16fb3d2e.title: Domain Name System
3aeb16fb3d2e.sentence: The resolver, or another DNS server acting recursively on behalf of the resolver, negotiates use of recursive service using bits in the query headers.

9235e6a381fe.title: rfc>1034
9235e6a381fe.sentence: The two general approaches to dealing with this problem are "recursive", in which the first server pursues the query for the client at another server, and "iterative", in which the server refers the client to another server and lets the client pursue the query.

1f933117e1b1.title: rfc>1034
1f933117e1b1.sentence: Both approaches have advantages and disadvantages, but the iterative approach is preferred for the datagram style of access.

2e7e1a8afc31.title: rfc>1034
2e7e1a8afc31.sentence: The domain system requires implementation of the iterative approach, but allows the recursive approach as an option.

cdb724ecd9ad.title: Domain Name System

d7089b18b105.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
d7089b18b105.sentence: The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) is a suite of extension specifications by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) for securing data exchanged in the Domain Name System (DNS) in Internet Protocol (IP) networks.

37cd266429e0.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
37cd266429e0.sentence: The protocol provides cryptographic authentication of data, authenticated denial of existence, and data integrity, but not availability or confidentiality.

359280593fed.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
359280593fed.sentence: The original design of the Domain Name System did not include any security features.

be2d07f0dadc.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
be2d07f0dadc.sentence: It was conceived only as a scalable distributed system.

f9c9ae91223a.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
f9c9ae91223a.sentence: The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) attempt to add security, while maintaining backward compatibility.

032d46804b0e.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
032d46804b0e.sentence: DNSSEC was designed to protect applications using DNS from accepting forged or manipulated DNS data, such as that created by DNS cache poisoning.

33cb6dcff83a.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
33cb6dcff83a.sentence: DNSSEC does not provide confidentiality of data; in particular, all DNSSEC responses are authenticated but not encrypted.

b3950ac1d484.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
b3950ac1d484.sentence: All answers from DNSSEC protected zones are digitally signed.

2dde91c57b8a.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
2dde91c57b8a.sentence: By checking the digital signature, a DNS resolver is able to check if the information is identical (i.e. unmodified and complete) to the information published by the zone owner and served on an authoritative DNS server.

bc190dc48ca9.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
bc190dc48ca9.sentence: While protecting IP addresses is the immediate concern for many users, DNSSEC can protect any data published in the DNS, including text records (TXT) and mail exchange records (MX), and can be used to bootstrap other security systems that publish references to cryptographic certificates stored in the DNS such as Certificate Records (CERT records, RFC 4398), SSH fingerprints (SSHFP, RFC 4255), IPsec public keys (IPSECKEY, RFC 4025), TLS Trust Anchors (TLSA, RFC 6698), or Encrypted Client Hello (SVCB/HTTPS records for ECH).

c9c4fce050bd.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c9c4fce050bd.sentence: DNSSEC works by digitally signing records for DNS lookup using public-key cryptography.

8e1fbebc3bde.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
8e1fbebc3bde.sentence: When DNSSEC is used, each answer to a DNS lookup contains an RRSIG DNS record, in addition to the record type that was requested.

22c7ea6dd04c.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
22c7ea6dd04c.sentence: The RRSIG record is a digital signature of the answer DNS resource record set.

d4f87ac33368.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
d4f87ac33368.sentence: The digital signature is verified by locating the correct public key found in a DNSKEY record.

3247bb37bde1.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
3247bb37bde1.sentence: The DS record is placed in the parent zone along with the delegating NS records.

8df9ac7fcf8d.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
8df9ac7fcf8d.sentence: References a DNSKEY record in the sub-delegated zone.

403d1b77e180.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
403d1b77e180.sentence: The NSEC and NSEC3 records are used to provide cryptographic evidence of the non-existence of any Resource Record (RR).

cea9d6208278.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
cea9d6208278.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
cea9d6208278.sentence: - The process starts when a security-aware resolver sets the "DO" ("DNSSEC OK") flag bit in a DNS query.

2c1347d0719f.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
2c1347d0719f.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
2c1347d0719f.sentence: Since the DO bit is in the extended flag bits defined by Extension Mechanisms for DNS (EDNS), RFC 6891, all DNSSEC transactions must support EDNS.

33ef207caa76.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
33ef207caa76.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
33ef207caa76.sentence: EDNS support is also needed to allow for the much larger packet sizes that DNSSEC transactions require.

2c6546d61063.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
2c6546d61063.sentence: DNSSEC does not protect against DoS attacks directly, though it indirectly provides some benefit (because signature checking allows the use of potentially untrustworthy parties).

d31597e82e56.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
d31597e82e56.sentence: DNSSEC cannot protect against false assumptions; it can only authenticate that the data is truly from or not available from the domain owner.

4174b0c55568.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
4174b0c55568.sentence: Other standards (not DNSSEC) are used to secure bulk data (such as a DNS zone transfer) sent between DNS servers.

d5830aee4f1b.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
d5830aee4f1b.sentence: It is widely believed that securing the DNS is critically important for securing the Internet as a whole, but deployment of DNSSEC specifically has been hampered (As of 22 January 2010^) by several difficulties:

63676bfce698.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
63676bfce698.sentence: - The need to design a backward-compatible standard that can scale to the size of the Internet

a00eee7a016d.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
a00eee7a016d.sentence: - Deployment of DNSSEC implementations across a wide variety of DNS servers and resolvers (clients)

c498532f80d1.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c498532f80d1.sentence: - Disagreement among implementers over who should own the top-level domain root keys

813b68c5acd7.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
813b68c5acd7.sentence: - Overcoming the perceived complexity of DNSSEC and DNSSEC deployment

0cbc991ffd0e.title: Round-robin DNS
0cbc991ffd0e.sentence: Round-robin DNS is a technique of load distribution, load balancing, or fault-tolerance provisioning multiple, redundant Internet Protocol service hosts, e.g., Web server, FTP servers, by managing the Domain Name System's (DNS) responses to address requests from client computers according to an appropriate statistical model.

afe43c925352.title: Round-robin DNS
afe43c925352.sentence: In its simplest implementation, round-robin DNS works by responding to DNS requests not only with a single potential IP address, but with a list of potential IP addresses corresponding to several servers that host identical services.

10ff413e5cf4.title: Round-robin DNS
10ff413e5cf4.sentence: The DNS server will be set up so that domain name has multiple A records, one for each IP address.

5a6f5492c1a9.title: Round-robin DNS
5a6f5492c1a9.sentence: With each DNS response, the IP address sequence in the list is permuted.

374698036e00.title: Round-robin DNS
374698036e00.sentence: Traditionally, IP clients initially attempt connections with the first address returned from a DNS query, so that on different connection attempts, clients would receive service from different providers, thus distributing the overall load among servers.

5b92faf132f3.title: Round-robin DNS
5b92faf132f3.sentence: Some resolvers attempt to re-order the list to give priority to numerically "closer" networks.

8f326239bcfa.title: Round-robin DNS
8f326239bcfa.sentence: This behaviour was standardized in RFC 3484 during the definition of IPv6.

5aaed1c3d717.title: Round-robin DNS
5aaed1c3d717.sentence: When applied to IPv4, a bug in Windows Vista caused issues and defeated round-robin load-balancing.

e3b5f70c0f23.title: Round-robin DNS
e3b5f70c0f23.sentence: Although easy to implement, round-robin DNS has a number of drawbacks, such as those arising from record caching in the DNS hierarchy itself, as well as client-side address caching and reuse, the combination of which can be difficult to manage.

299658b861c1.title: Round-robin DNS
299658b861c1.sentence: Round-robin DNS should not solely be relied upon for service availability.

e94a10ece54f.title: Round-robin DNS
e94a10ece54f.sentence: If a service at one of the addresses in the list fails, the DNS will continue to hand out that address and clients will still attempt to reach the inoperable service.

fc2e7889e3de.title: Round-robin DNS
fc2e7889e3de.sentence: Some desktop clients do try alternate addresses after a connection timeout of up to 30 seconds.

3d5a33492de4.title: Round-robin DNS
3d5a33492de4.sentence: Round-robin DNS may not be the best choice for load balancing on its own, since it merely alternates the order of the address records each time a name server is queried.

9848829274c9.title: Round-robin DNS
9848829274c9.sentence: Because it does not take transaction time, server load, and network congestion into consideration, it works best for services with a large number of uniformly distributed connections to servers of equivalent capacity.

5562a0cad00d.title: Round-robin DNS
5562a0cad00d.sentence: Otherwise, it just does load distribution.

be2b3c596b9c.title: Round-robin DNS
be2b3c596b9c.sentence: For example, modified DNS servers (such as lbnamed) can routinely poll mirrored servers for availability and load factor.

e98f674a2c48.title: Round-robin DNS
e98f674a2c48.sentence: If a server does not reply as required, the server can be temporarily removed from the DNS pool, until it reports that it is once again operating within specs.

0c49e43c6f1b.title: DNS spoofing
0c49e43c6f1b.sentence: DNS spoofing, also referred to as DNS cache poisoning, is a form of computer security hacking in which corrupt Domain Name System data is introduced into the DNS resolver's cache, causing the name server to return an incorrect result record, e.g. an IP address.

fe4e3c6314f1.title: DNS spoofing
fe4e3c6314f1.sentence: This results in traffic being diverted to any computer that the attacker chooses.

228008b8991f.title: DNS spoofing
228008b8991f.section: Overview of the Domain Name System
228008b8991f.sentence: When a DNS server has received a false translation and caches it for performance optimization, it is considered poisoned, and it supplies the false data to clients.

cf38e741bca0.title: DNS spoofing
cf38e741bca0.section: Overview of the Domain Name System
cf38e741bca0.sentence: If a DNS server is poisoned, it may return an incorrect IP address, diverting traffic to another computer (often an attacker's).

58bcb016c8fd.title: DNS spoofing
58bcb016c8fd.section: Overview of the Domain Name System
58bcb016c8fd.sentence: This means if it receives another request for the same translation, it can reply without needing to ask any other servers, until that cache expires.

01c292309d17.title: DNS spoofing
01c292309d17.sentence: Poisoning attacks on a single DNS server can affect the users serviced directly by the compromised server or those serviced indirectly by its downstream server(s) if applicable.

2d757c5d1cb5.title: DNS spoofing
2d757c5d1cb5.sentence: To perform a cache poisoning attack, the attacker exploits flaws in the DNS software.

126cd03a6b32.title: DNS spoofing
126cd03a6b32.sentence: This attack can be used to redirect users from a website to another site of the attacker's choosing.

04be3f84234f.title: DNS spoofing
04be3f84234f.sentence: This technique can also be used for phishing attacks, where a fake version of a genuine website is created to gather personal details such as bank and credit/debit card details.

0a8b06ea11cc.title: DNS spoofing
0a8b06ea11cc.sentence: The vulnerability of systems to DNS cache poisoning goes beyond its immediate effects as it can open users up to further risks such as phishing, malware injections, denial of service, and website hijacking due to system vulnerabilities.

d01fd1e62218.title: DNS spoofing
d01fd1e62218.section: Variants > Redirect the target domain's name server
d01fd1e62218.sentence: The first variant of DNS cache poisoning involves redirecting the name server of the attacker's domain to the name server of the target domain, then assigning that name server an IP address specified by the attacker.

dfcf80a095ed.title: DNS spoofing
dfcf80a095ed.section: Variants > Redirect the target domain's name server
dfcf80a095ed.sentence: A vulnerable server would cache the additional A-record (IP address) for ns.target.example, allowing the attacker to resolve queries to the entire target.example domain.

3fcdd304d67f.title: DNS spoofing
3fcdd304d67f.sentence: Many cache poisoning attacks against DNS servers can be prevented by being less trusting of the information passed to them by other DNS servers, and ignoring any DNS records passed back that are not directly relevant to the query.

9ba8dfd77df2.title: DNS spoofing
9ba8dfd77df2.sentence: Source port randomization for DNS requests, combined with the use of cryptographically secure random numbers for selecting both the source port and the 16-bit cryptographic nonce, can greatly reduce the probability of successful DNS race attacks.

316b557d2af5.title: DNS spoofing
316b557d2af5.sentence: However, when routers, firewalls, proxies, and other gateway devices perform network address translation (NAT), or more specifically, port address translation (PAT), they may rewrite source ports in order to track connection state.

bb52815cf339.title: DNS spoofing
bb52815cf339.sentence: When modifying source ports, PAT devices may remove source port randomness implemented by nameservers and stub resolvers.

f23705f91178.title: DNS spoofing
f23705f91178.sentence: Secure DNS (DNSSEC) uses cryptographic digital signatures signed with a trusted public key certificate to determine the authenticity of data.

651e82d5748c.title: DNS spoofing
651e82d5748c.sentence: DNSSEC can counter cache poisoning attacks.

0536b7d01253.title: DNS spoofing
0536b7d01253.sentence: This kind of attack can be mitigated at the transport layer or application layer by performing end-to-end validation once a connection is established.

8e59075fceca.title: DNS spoofing
8e59075fceca.sentence: A common example of this is the use of Transport Layer Security and digital signatures.

b9de45905af3.title: DNS spoofing
b9de45905af3.sentence: For example, by using HTTPS (the secure version of HTTP), users may check whether the server's digital certificate is valid and belongs to a website's expected owner.

0c4fc83bf6fc.title: Domain Name System
0c4fc83bf6fc.sentence: Originally designed as a public, hierarchical, distributed and heavily cached database, the DNS protocol has no confidentiality controls.

d9ea07bef3d5.title: Domain Name System
d9ea07bef3d5.sentence: User queries and nameserver responses are sent unencrypted, enabling network packet sniffing, DNS hijacking, DNS cache poisoning and man-in-the-middle attacks.

ca4f394c77bb.title: Domain Name System
ca4f394c77bb.sentence: - VPNs, which move DNS resolution to the VPN operator and hide user traffic from the local ISP.

026e5223fc10.title: Domain Name System
026e5223fc10.sentence: - Tor, which replaces traditional DNS resolution with anonymous.onion domains, hiding both name resolution and user traffic behind onion routing counter-surveillance.

efddc6fca5cf.title: Domain Name System
efddc6fca5cf.sentence: - Proxies and public DNS servers, which move the actual DNS resolution to a trusted third-party provider.

7f8f2cc65d5c.title: Domain Name System
7f8f2cc65d5c.sentence: - Some public DNS servers may support security extensions such as DNS over HTTPS, DNS over TLS and DNSCrypt.

ac1ca0f151be.title: Domain Name System
ac1ca0f151be.sentence: Solutions preventing DNS inspection by the local network operator have been criticized for thwarting corporate network security policies and Internet censorship.

ad8075c30087.title: Domain Name System
ad8075c30087.sentence: Public DNS servers are also criticized for contributing to the centralization of the Internet by placing control over DNS resolution in the hands of the few large companies which can afford to run public resolvers.

3810a3abb7f0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
3810a3abb7f0.sentence: A root server accepts a recursive resolver's query which includes a domain name, and the root nameserver responds by directing the recursive resolver to a TLD nameserver, based on the extension of that domain (.com,.net,.org, etc.).

e54752a6a8e2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
e54752a6a8e2.sentence: A TLD nameserver maintains information for all the domain names that share a common domain extension, such as.com,.net, or whatever comes after the last dot in a URL.

c27ed07972d7.title: Root name server
c27ed07972d7.sentence: It directly answers requests for records in the root zone and answers other requests by returning a list of the authoritative name servers for the appropriate top-level domain (TLD).

0daa30648a5c.title: Root name server
0daa30648a5c.sentence: The root zone file is a small (about 2 MB) data set at the apex of the Domain Name System, and its publication is the primary purpose of root name servers.

1753834efa28.title: Root name server
1753834efa28.sentence: The contents of the root zone file is a list of names and numeric IP addresses of the root domain authoritative DNS servers for all top-level domains (TLDs) such as com, org, edu, and the country code top-level domains (it also includes that info for root domain, the dot).

a2f253c3a263.title: Root name server
a2f253c3a263.sentence: The root name server, using its root zone file, answers with a referral to the authoritative servers for the appropriate TLD or with an indication that no such TLD exists.

bbcdf1a7a801.title: Root name server
bbcdf1a7a801.sentence: A combination of limits in the DNS and certain protocols, namely the practical size of unfragmented User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packets, resulted in a decision to limit the number of root servers to thirteen server addresses.

2ef94022a015.title: Root name server
2ef94022a015.sentence: The choice of 13 name servers was made because of limitations in the original DNS specification, which specifies a maximum packet size of 512 bytes when using the User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

784548ae85c6.title: Root name server
784548ae85c6.sentence: The addition of IPv6 addresses for the root name servers requires more than 512 bytes, which is facilitated by the EDNS0 extension to the DNS standard.

89692bbb1f7e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
89692bbb1f7e.sentence: There are 13 DNS root nameservers known to every recursive resolver.

eb8181e717d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
eb8181e717d4.sentence: Note that while there are 13 root nameservers, that doesn't mean that there are only 13 machines in the root nameserver system.

6b1f8a1215fb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
6b1f8a1215fb.sentence: There are 13 types of root nameservers, but there are multiple copies of each one all over the world, which use Anycast routing to provide speedy responses.

3d4556a37dac.title: Root name server
3d4556a37dac.sentence: Although 13 root name servers are specified, this does not mean that there are only 13 physical servers; each operator uses redundant computer equipment so that it can continue providing reliable service even if server hardware or software fails.

1efa0dae3899.title: Root name server
1efa0dae3899.sentence: Additionally, all operate in multiple geographical locations using a routing technique called anycast addressing, providing increased performance and even more fault tolerance.

3cce14804eac.title: Root name server
3cce14804eac.sentence: However, enabled by the use of anycast addressing, the actual number of root server instances—1954—is much larger, as of December 5, 2025.

3eff0313bbfa.title: Domain Name System
3eff0313bbfa.sentence: The hints are updated periodically by an administrator by retrieving a dataset from a reliable source.

9fff11b859f1.title: Root name server
9fff11b859f1.sentence: Resolvers use a small 3 KB root.hints file published by Internic to bootstrap this initial list of root server addresses; in other words, root.hints is necessary in order to break the circular dependency of needing to know the addresses of a root name server to lookup the same address.

c97771d65db0.title: Root name server
c97771d65db0.sentence: In practice, most of this information does not change very often over a period of hours, and therefore it is cached by intermediate name servers or by a name cache built into the user's application.

418fefca49ce.title: Root name server
418fefca49ce.sentence: DNS lookups to the root name servers may therefore be relatively infrequent.

df212f07e620.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
df212f07e620.sentence: The IANA breaks up the TLD servers into two main groups:

521ba96f5625.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
521ba96f5625.sentence: - Generic top-level domains: These are domains like.com,.org,.net,.edu, and.gov.

b21d2ad3e9b5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
b21d2ad3e9b5.sentence: - Country code top-level domains: These include any domains that are specific to a country or state.

92d19c041879.title: rfc>1034
92d19c041879.sentence: One option for implementing a resolver is to move the resolution function out of the local machine and into a name server which supports recursive queries.

3307bb9b498e.title: rfc>1034
3307bb9b498e.sentence: All that the remaining stub needs is a list of name server addresses that will perform the recursive requests.

a8d4428f9b23.title: rfc>1034
a8d4428f9b23.sentence: This can provide an easy method of providing domain service in a PC which lacks the resources to perform the resolver function, or can centralize the cache for a whole local network or organization.

ac3ffabaf2fd.title: rfc>1034
ac3ffabaf2fd.sentence: This type of resolver presumably needs the information in a configuration file, since it probably lacks the sophistication to locate it in the domain database.

cd229c142882.title: rfc>1034
cd229c142882.sentence: The user also needs to verify that the listed servers will perform the recursive service; a name server is free to refuse to perform recursive services for any or all clients.

7440570b7634.title: rfc>1034
7440570b7634.sentence: This type of service suffers from some drawbacks.

1bdc75de191e.title: rfc>1034
1bdc75de191e.sentence: Since the recursive requests may take an arbitrary amount of time to perform, the stub may have difficulty optimizing retransmission intervals to deal with both lost UDP packets and dead servers; the name server can be easily overloaded by too zealous a stub if it interprets retransmissions as new requests.

6119ff949522.title: Domain Name System
6119ff949522.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
6119ff949522.sentence: An authoritative name server is a name server that only gives answers to DNS queries from data that have been configured by an original source, for example, the domain administrator or by dynamic DNS methods, in contrast to answers obtained via a query to another name server that only maintains a cache of data.

d30cf25a704a.title: Domain Name System
d30cf25a704a.sentence: Each domain has at least one authoritative DNS server that publishes information about that domain and the name servers of any domains subordinate to it.

ad978834b94c.title: Domain Name System
ad978834b94c.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
ad978834b94c.sentence: An authoritative name server can either be a primary server or a secondary server.

36b255b950f9.title: Domain Name System
36b255b950f9.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
36b255b950f9.sentence: A primary server is a server that stores the original copies of all zone records.

53d42aa946de.title: Domain Name System
53d42aa946de.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
53d42aa946de.sentence: A secondary server uses a special automatic updating mechanism in the DNS protocol in communication with its primary to maintain an identical copy of the primary records.

f3f79d129956.title: Domain Name System
f3f79d129956.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
f3f79d129956.sentence: Every DNS zone must be assigned a set of authoritative name servers.

016f70548ef8.title: Domain Name System
016f70548ef8.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
016f70548ef8.sentence: This set of servers is stored in the parent domain zone with name server (NS) records.

3fc945939030.title: rfc>1034
3fc945939030.sentence: By administrative fiat, we require every zone to be available on at least two servers, and many zones have more redundancy than that.

d3cf370332d3.title: rfc>1034
d3cf370332d3.sentence: A given zone will be available from several name servers to insure its availability in spite of host or communication link failure.

b10546415bb1.title: Domain Name System
b10546415bb1.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
b10546415bb1.sentence: An authoritative server indicates its status of supplying definitive answers, deemed authoritative, by setting a protocol flag, called the "Authoritative Answer" (AA) bit in its responses.

a38630b1c477.title: Domain Name System
a38630b1c477.section: Structure > Name servers > Authoritative name server
a38630b1c477.sentence: When a name server is designated as the authoritative server for a domain name for which it does not have authoritative data, it presents a type of error called a "lame delegation" or "lame response".

f08032846715.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
f08032846715.sentence: The authoritative nameserver is usually the resolver's last step in the journey for an IP address.

43b24ca7efa6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
43b24ca7efa6.sentence: If it cannot find the domain, returns the NXDOMAIN message.

00287e25d9ab.title: Domain Name System
00287e25d9ab.sentence: Dynamic DNS updates use the UPDATE DNS opcode to add or remove resource records dynamically from a zone database maintained on an authoritative DNS server.

f873eb0be4fa.title: Domain Name System
f873eb0be4fa.sentence: This facility is useful to register network clients into the DNS when they boot or become otherwise available on the network.

cf9f9430645c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
cf9f9430645c.sentence: You can register authoritative name servers with domain name registrar such as GoDaddy, Namecheap, etc.

1e3a0a576eff.title: Domain Name System
1e3a0a576eff.sentence: The mechanism by which responsibility for different parts of the DNS name space is assigned to different name servers is called delegation.

3be32c7c4e5b.title: Domain Name System
3be32c7c4e5b.sentence: Administrative responsibility for any zone may be divided by creating additional zones.

d41d53677dc5.title: Domain Name System
d41d53677dc5.sentence: Authority over the new zone is said to be delegated to a designated name server.

6339fa1020bc.title: Domain Name System
6339fa1020bc.sentence: The parent zone ceases to be authoritative for the new zone.

fd6b9f6c4458.title: Domain Name System
fd6b9f6c4458.sentence: Every public network domain under the TLDs is delegated, by having an NS record in the parent domain pointing to the DNS names of the name servers for the delegated (or child) domain.

25f406a9cd3e.title: Domain Name System
25f406a9cd3e.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
25f406a9cd3e.sentence: Name servers in delegations are identified by name, rather than by IP address.

7a1ec4273899.title: Domain Name System
7a1ec4273899.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
7a1ec4273899.sentence: This means that a resolving name server must issue another DNS request to discover the IP address of the server to which it has been referred.

698982ccd250.title: Domain Name System
698982ccd250.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
698982ccd250.sentence: If the name given in the delegation is a subdomain of the domain for which the delegation is being provided, there is a circular dependency.

bb390121755c.title: Domain Name System
bb390121755c.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
bb390121755c.sentence: In this case, the name server providing the delegation must also provide one or more IP addresses for the authoritative name server mentioned in the delegation.

be2d659f2520.title: Domain Name System
be2d659f2520.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records

02a028667aa3.title: Domain Name System
02a028667aa3.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
02a028667aa3.sentence: A glue record is a combination of the name server and IP address.

33bfa10ffea3.title: Domain Name System
33bfa10ffea3.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
33bfa10ffea3.sentence: The delegating name server provides this glue in the form of records in the additional section of the DNS response, and provides the delegation in the authority section of the response.

c8dd886c689a.title: Domain Name System
c8dd886c689a.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
c8dd886c689a.sentence: For example, if the authoritative name server for example.org is ns1.example.org, a computer trying to resolve www.example.org first resolves ns1.example.org.

d3edd0bc97db.title: Domain Name System
d3edd0bc97db.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
d3edd0bc97db.sentence: As ns1 is contained in example.org, this requires resolving example.org first, which presents a circular dependency.

260e7522cd09.title: Domain Name System
260e7522cd09.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
260e7522cd09.sentence: To break the dependency, the name server for the top level domain org includes glue along with the delegation for example.org.

de9dc3370542.title: Domain Name System
de9dc3370542.section: Operation > Circular dependencies and glue records
de9dc3370542.sentence: The glue records are address records that provide IP addresses for ns1.example.org.

eff242b44a46.title: rfc>1034
eff242b44a46.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones
eff242b44a46.sentence: Within a class, "cuts" in the name space can be made between any two adjacent nodes.

af7191dde271.title: rfc>1034
af7191dde271.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones
af7191dde271.sentence: After all cuts are made, each group of connected name space is a separate zone.

0d4ede646603.title: rfc>1034
0d4ede646603.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones
0d4ede646603.sentence: The zone is said to be authoritative for all names in the connected region.

1f87fd238bc6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
1f87fd238bc6.sentence: A DNS zone is a distinct part of the domain namespace which is delegated to a legal entity like a person, organization, or company, who is responsible for maintaining the DNS zone.

67b61e6e881c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::domain-name-system-dns
67b61e6e881c.sentence: A DNS zone is also an administrative function, allowing for granular control of DNS components, such as authoritative name servers.

5357db07df87.title: rfc>1034
5357db07df87.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones
5357db07df87.sentence: Once an organization controls its own zone it can unilaterally change the data in the zone, grow new tree sections connected to the zone, delete existing nodes, or delegate new subzones under its zone.

0b21dde46efa.title: rfc>1034
0b21dde46efa.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones
0b21dde46efa.sentence: If the organization has substructure, it may want to make further internal partitions to achieve nested delegations of name space control.

c676d2ab9ba5.title: rfc>1034
c676d2ab9ba5.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
c676d2ab9ba5.sentence: The data that describes a zone has four major parts:

704ae127a704.title: rfc>1034
704ae127a704.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
704ae127a704.sentence: - Authoritative data for all nodes within the zone.

99679486e349.title: rfc>1034
99679486e349.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
99679486e349.sentence: - Data that defines the top node of the zone (can be thought of as part of the authoritative data).

c1502cbe1db0.title: rfc>1034
c1502cbe1db0.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
c1502cbe1db0.sentence: - Data that describes delegated subzones, i.e., cuts around the bottom of the zone.

d02064dbf27d.title: rfc>1034
d02064dbf27d.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
d02064dbf27d.sentence: - Data that allows access to name servers for subzones (sometimes called "glue" data).

7a9202e200cc.title: rfc>1034
7a9202e200cc.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
7a9202e200cc.sentence: All of this data is expressed in the form of RRs, so a zone can be completely described in terms of a set of RRs.

e4a7cf69d7ef.title: rfc>1034
e4a7cf69d7ef.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
e4a7cf69d7ef.sentence: These RRs are of two types: name server RRs that list, one per RR, all of the servers for the zone, and a single SOA RR that describes zone management parameters.

347ce22701bd.title: rfc>1034
347ce22701bd.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
347ce22701bd.sentence: The RRs that describe cuts around the bottom of the zone are NS RRs that name the servers for the subzones.

95387d971ec6.title: rfc>1034
95387d971ec6.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
95387d971ec6.sentence: Since the cuts are between nodes, these RRs are NOT part of the authoritative data of the zone, and should be exactly the same as the corresponding RRs in the top node of the subzone.

3b2517252c3e.title: rfc>1034
3b2517252c3e.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
3b2517252c3e.sentence: The NS RRs that name the servers for subzones are often not enough for this task since they name the servers, but do not give their addresses.

cb3b75a9fab1.title: rfc>1034
cb3b75a9fab1.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
cb3b75a9fab1.sentence: To fix this problem, a zone contains "glue" RRs which are not part of the authoritative data, and are address RRs for the servers.

1730de59fe0e.title: rfc>1034
1730de59fe0e.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.1. Technical considerations
1730de59fe0e.sentence: These RRs are only necessary if the name server's name is "below" the cut, and are only used as part of a referral response.

0340b09627e5.title: rfc>1034
0340b09627e5.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.2. Administrative considerations
0340b09627e5.sentence: When some organization wants to control its own domain, the first step is to identify the proper parent zone, and get the parent zone's owners to agree to the delegation of control.

79d6cfc7ef30.title: rfc>1034
79d6cfc7ef30.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.2. Administrative considerations
79d6cfc7ef30.sentence: Once the proper name for the new subzone is selected, the new owners should be required to demonstrate redundant name server support.

1610836ca58b.title: rfc>1034
1610836ca58b.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.2. Administrative considerations
1610836ca58b.sentence: As the last installation step, the delegation NS RRs and glue RRs necessary to make the delegation effective should be added to the parent zone.

c12f6a515968.title: rfc>1034
c12f6a515968.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.2. Administrative considerations
c12f6a515968.sentence: Note that there is no requirement that the servers for a zone reside in a host which has a name in that domain.

4f54cec1d3b8.title: rfc>1034
4f54cec1d3b8.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.2. Administrative considerations
4f54cec1d3b8.sentence: In many cases, a zone will be more accessible to the internet at large if its servers are widely distributed rather than being within the physical facilities controlled by the same organization that manages the zone.

c2f66f79409e.title: rfc>1034
c2f66f79409e.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.2. Administrative considerations
c2f66f79409e.sentence: For example, in the current DNS, one of the name servers for the United Kingdom, or UK domain, is found in the US.

7e4a9b8b6d78.title: rfc>1034
7e4a9b8b6d78.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.2. How the database is divided into zones > 4.2.2. Administrative considerations
7e4a9b8b6d78.sentence: This allows US hosts to get UK data without using limited transatlantic bandwidth.

78af013b7409.title: rfc>1034
78af013b7409.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
78af013b7409.sentence: Part of the job of a zone administrator is to maintain the zones at all of the name servers which are authoritative for the zone.

825ff7e4df7f.title: rfc>1034
825ff7e4df7f.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
825ff7e4df7f.sentence: When the inevitable changes are made, they must be distributed to all of the name servers.

6ccd5f630eaf.title: rfc>1034
6ccd5f630eaf.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
6ccd5f630eaf.sentence: While this distribution can be accomplished using FTP or some other ad hoc procedure, the preferred method is the zone transfer part of the DNS protocol.

40a4c4b1ede6.title: rfc>1034
40a4c4b1ede6.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
40a4c4b1ede6.sentence: The general model of automatic zone transfer or refreshing is that one of the name servers is the master or primary for the zone.

2f33438a0673.title: rfc>1034
2f33438a0673.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
2f33438a0673.sentence: Changes are coordinated at the primary, typically by editing a master file for the zone.

9d3f0ca22211.title: rfc>1034
9d3f0ca22211.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
9d3f0ca22211.sentence: After editing, the administrator signals the master server to load the new zone.

838a6c9abec2.title: rfc>1034
838a6c9abec2.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
838a6c9abec2.sentence: The other non-master or secondary servers for the zone periodically check for changes (at a selectable interval) and obtain new zone copies when changes have been made.

6e766432271e.title: rfc>1034
6e766432271e.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
6e766432271e.sentence: To detect changes, secondaries just check the SERIAL field of the SOA for the zone.

9998290e4c1d.title: rfc>1034
9998290e4c1d.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
9998290e4c1d.sentence: In addition to whatever other changes are made, the SERIAL field in the SOA of the zone is always advanced whenever any change is made to the zone.

f0315f9ac4c2.title: rfc>1034
f0315f9ac4c2.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
f0315f9ac4c2.sentence: The advancing can be a simple increment, or could be based on the write date and time of the master file, etc. The purpose is to make it possible to determine which of two copies of a zone is more recent by comparing serial numbers.

78f97191a155.title: rfc>1034
78f97191a155.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
78f97191a155.sentence: The parameters are called REFRESH, RETRY, and EXPIRE.

86d80df5e998.title: rfc>1034
86d80df5e998.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
86d80df5e998.sentence: Whenever a new zone is loaded in a secondary, the secondary waits REFRESH seconds before checking with the primary for a new serial.

e35ec4b2ccb3.title: rfc>1034
e35ec4b2ccb3.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
e35ec4b2ccb3.sentence: If this check cannot be completed, new checks are started every RETRY seconds.

396b064a75a2.title: rfc>1034
396b064a75a2.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
396b064a75a2.sentence: If the secondary finds it impossible to perform a serial check for the EXPIRE interval, it must assume that its copy of the zone is obsolete an discard it.

77bc1a25f9fd.title: rfc>1034
77bc1a25f9fd.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
77bc1a25f9fd.sentence: The check is a simple query to the primary for the SOA RR of the zone.

c8a6370b551f.title: rfc>1034
c8a6370b551f.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
c8a6370b551f.sentence: If the serial field in the secondary's zone copy is equal to the serial returned by the primary, then no changes have occurred, and the REFRESH interval wait is restarted.

02bde289b3ea.title: rfc>1034
02bde289b3ea.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
02bde289b3ea.sentence: When the poll shows that the zone has changed, then the secondary server must request a zone transfer via an AXFR request for the zone.

eaa3cdafed46.title: rfc>1034
eaa3cdafed46.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
eaa3cdafed46.sentence: The AXFR may cause an error, such as refused, but normally is answered by a sequence of response messages.

cd4047716e34.title: rfc>1034
cd4047716e34.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
cd4047716e34.sentence: Intermediate messages carry all of the other RRs from the zone, including both authoritative and non-authoritative RRs.

cff21ac1911a.title: rfc>1034
cff21ac1911a.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
cff21ac1911a.sentence: The stream of messages allows the secondary to construct a copy of the zone.

68a258edc558.title: rfc>1034
68a258edc558.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
68a258edc558.sentence: Because accuracy is essential, TCP or some other reliable protocol must be used for AXFR requests.

f8e952c4dbbf.title: rfc>1034
f8e952c4dbbf.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
f8e952c4dbbf.sentence: Each secondary server is required to perform the following operations against the master, but may also optionally perform these operations against other secondary servers.

fca131b080cc.title: rfc>1034
fca131b080cc.section: 4. NAME SERVERS > 4.3. Name server internals > 4.3.5. Zone maintenance and transfers
fca131b080cc.sentence: This strategy can improve the transfer process when the primary is unavailable due to host downtime or network problems, or when a secondary server has better network access to an "intermediate" secondary than to the primary.

011926814196.title: rfc>1034
011926814196.sentence: - Access to information is more critical than instantaneous updates or guarantees of consistency.

f3ac3a367525.title: rfc>1034
f3ac3a367525.sentence: Hence the update process allows updates to percolate out through the users of the domain system rather than guaranteeing that all copies are simultaneously updated.

09c412497a73.title: rfc>1034
09c412497a73.sentence: The general model is that copies are distributed with timeouts for refreshing.

8676b063d817.title: rfc>1034
8676b063d817.sentence: When updates are unavailable due to network or host failure, the usual course is to believe old information while continuing efforts to update it.

e94910366304.title: rfc>1034
e94910366304.sentence: The distributor sets the timeout value and the recipient of the distribution is responsible for performing the refresh.

1af3e819f07e.title: rfc>1034
1af3e819f07e.sentence: In special situations, very short intervals can be specified, or the owner can prohibit copies.

fc47c053be3f.title: rfc>1034
fc47c053be3f.sentence: - Most of the data in the system will change very slowly (e.g., mailbox bindings, host addresses), but that the system should be able to deal with subsets that change more rapidly (on the order of seconds or minutes).

a7f63728e732.title: rfc>1034
a7f63728e732.sentence: Each organization that has responsibility for a particular set of domains will provide redundant name servers, either on the organization's own hosts or other hosts that the organization arranges to use.

74c90e6dd572.title: rfc>1034
74c90e6dd572.sentence: The domain system assumes that all data originates in master files scattered through the hosts that use the domain system.

02e197e6a530.title: rfc>1034
02e197e6a530.sentence: These master files are updated by local system administrators.

d012256005cd.title: rfc>1034
d012256005cd.sentence: Master files are text files that are read by a local name server, and hence become available through the name servers to users of the domain system.

91644176ce2d.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
91644176ce2d.section: Operation > Trust anchors and authentication chains
91644176ce2d.sentence: An authentication chain is a series of linked DS and DNSKEY records, starting with a trust anchor to the authoritative name server for the domain in question.

4275fb6d91da.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
4275fb6d91da.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
4275fb6d91da.sentence: Using the chain of trust model, a Delegation Signer (DS) record in a parent domain (DNS zone) can be used to verify a DNSKEY record in a subdomain, which can then contain other DS records to verify further subdomains.

9537fb9d3c65.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
9537fb9d3c65.section: Operation > Trust anchors and authentication chains
9537fb9d3c65.sentence: To be able to prove that a DNS answer is correct, one needs to know at least one key or DS record that is correct from sources other than the DNS.

c83c2262118b.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c83c2262118b.section: Operation > Trust anchors and authentication chains
c83c2262118b.sentence: These starting points are known as trust anchors and are typically obtained with the operating system or via some other trusted source.

6065ee13a0f5.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
6065ee13a0f5.section: Operation > Trust anchors and authentication chains
6065ee13a0f5.sentence: Without a complete authentication chain, an answer to a DNS lookup cannot be securely authenticated.

954d8f65b52a.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
954d8f65b52a.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
954d8f65b52a.sentence: Ideally, the security-aware resolver would start with verifying the DS and DNSKEY records at the DNS root.

2655c0c21b50.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
2655c0c21b50.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
2655c0c21b50.sentence: Then it would use the DS records for the "com" top-level domain found at the root to verify the DNSKEY records in the "com" zone.

d5129233fce9.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
d5129233fce9.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
d5129233fce9.sentence: From there, it would see if there is a DS record for the "example.com" subdomain in the "com" zone, and if there were, it would then use the DS record to verify a DNSKEY record found in the "example.com" zone.

864ccc152d07.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
864ccc152d07.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
864ccc152d07.sentence: Finally, it would verify the RRSIG record found in the answer for the A records for "www.example.com".

e224c84b5360.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
e224c84b5360.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
e224c84b5360.sentence: If there is a DS record for "example.com", but no RRSIG record in the reply, something is wrong and maybe a man in the middle attack is going on, stripping the DNSSEC information and modifying the A records.

84bb02ca5b2a.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
84bb02ca5b2a.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
84bb02ca5b2a.sentence: Or, it could be a broken security-oblivious name server along the way that stripped the DO flag bit from the query or the RRSIG record from the answer.

5afacd470e2b.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
5afacd470e2b.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
5afacd470e2b.sentence: Or, it could be a configuration error.

d8ff23d6e791.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
d8ff23d6e791.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Recursive name servers
d8ff23d6e791.sentence: Finally, it may be that the "example.com" zone implements DNSSEC, but either the "com" zone or the root zone do not, creating an "island of security" which needs to be validated in some other way.

a827c3140865.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
a827c3140865.section: Deployment > Deployment at the DNS root
a827c3140865.sentence: Since the chain of trust must be traced back to a trusted root without interruption in order to validate, trust anchors must still be configured for secure zones if any of the zones above them are not secure.

079f855abae8.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
079f855abae8.section: Deployment > Deployment at the DNS root
079f855abae8.sentence: DNSSEC was first deployed at the root level on July 15, 2010.

02deb7c5e477.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
02deb7c5e477.section: Deployment > Deployment at the DNS root
02deb7c5e477.sentence: This is expected to greatly simplify the deployment of DNSSEC resolvers, since the root trust anchor can be used to validate any DNSSEC zone that has a complete chain of trust from the root.

c7708b1d284e.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c7708b1d284e.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Stub resolvers
c7708b1d284e.sentence: Stub resolvers are "minimal DNS resolvers that use recursive query mode to offload most of the work of DNS resolution to a recursive name server." A stub resolver will simply forward a request to a recursive name server, and use the Authenticated Data (AD) bit in the response as a "hint to find out whether the recursive name server was able to validate signatures for all of the data in the Answer and Authority sections of the response." Microsoft Windows uses a stub resolver, and Windows Server 2008 R2 and Windows 7 in particular use a non-validating but AD-bit-aware stub resolver.

a74fdb3e9591.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
a74fdb3e9591.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Stub resolvers
a74fdb3e9591.sentence: A validating stub resolver can also potentially perform its own signature validation by setting the Checking Disabled (CD) bit in its query messages.

2f4460a83054.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
2f4460a83054.section: Operation > The lookup procedure > Stub resolvers
2f4460a83054.sentence: A validating stub resolver uses the CD bit to perform its own recursive authentication.

385d33027529.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
385d33027529.sentence: Cryptographically proving the absence of a domain requires signing the response to every query for a non-existent domain.

a88ef35a931e.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
a88ef35a931e.sentence: DNS resolvers use NSEC records to verify the non-existence of a record name and type as part of DNSSEC validation.

cb36ef37b69e.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
cb36ef37b69e.sentence: However, DNSSEC was designed around using offline computers to sign records so that zone-signing-keys could be kept in cold storage.

bd8aa6f944ee.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
bd8aa6f944ee.sentence: This represents a problem when trying to authenticate responses to queries for non-existent domains since it is impossible to pre-generate a response to every possible hostname query.

c25a7d5f6852.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c25a7d5f6852.sentence: The initial solution was to create NSEC records for every pair of domains in a zone.

092a7e844395.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
092a7e844395.sentence: Thus if a client queried for a record at the non-existent k.example.com, the server would respond with an NSEC record stating that nothing exists between a.example.com and z.example.com.

e36c8ef5c1b5.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
e36c8ef5c1b5.sentence: However, this leaks more information about the zone than traditional unauthenticated NXDOMAIN errors because it exposes the existence of real domains.

9fba4693074d.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
9fba4693074d.section: Authenticating NXDOMAIN responses and NSEC > Preventing domain walking
9fba4693074d.sentence: The NSEC3 records (RFC 5155) were created as an alternative which hashes the name instead of listing them directly.

ae45e3fb9739.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
ae45e3fb9739.section: Authenticating NXDOMAIN responses and NSEC > Preventing domain walking
ae45e3fb9739.sentence: Over time, advancements in hashing using GPUs and dedicated hardware meant that NSEC3 responses could be cheaply brute forced using offline dictionary attacks.

19988c067b0b.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
19988c067b0b.section: Authenticating NXDOMAIN responses and NSEC > Preventing domain walking
19988c067b0b.sentence: NSEC5 has been proposed to allow authoritative servers to sign NSEC responses without having to keep a private key that can be used to modify the zone.

41f1f34222dc.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
41f1f34222dc.section: Authenticating NXDOMAIN responses and NSEC > Preventing domain walking
41f1f34222dc.sentence: Due to the messy evolution of the protocol and a desire to preserve backwards compatibility, online DNSSEC signing servers return a "white lie" instead of authenticating a denial of existence directly.

20eb21674817.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
20eb21674817.section: Authenticating NXDOMAIN responses and NSEC > Preventing domain walking
20eb21674817.sentence: The technique outlined in RFC 4470 returns a NSEC record in which the pairs of domains lexically surround the requested domain.

c7bc5feb85d4.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c7bc5feb85d4.section: Authenticating NXDOMAIN responses and NSEC > Preventing domain walking
c7bc5feb85d4.sentence: For example, request for k.example.com would thus result in an NSEC record proving that nothing exists between the (fictitious) domains j.example.com and l.example.com.

c98e7cf0f9da.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c98e7cf0f9da.sentence: DNSSEC involves many different keys, stored both in DNSKEY records, and from other sources to form trust anchors.

fe7737bc4711.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
fe7737bc4711.sentence: Keys in DNSKEY records can be used for two different things and typically different DNSKEY records are used for each.

4c9a12cf51c2.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
4c9a12cf51c2.sentence: First, there are key signing keys (KSK) which are used to sign other DNSKEY records containing zone signing keys (ZSK), which are used to sign other records.

566e43bc87f4.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
566e43bc87f4.sentence: Since the ZSKs are under complete control and use by one particular DNS zone, they can be switched more easily and more often.

5c8c07ecf28e.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
5c8c07ecf28e.sentence: As a result, ZSKs can be much shorter than KSKs and still offer the same level of protection while reducing the size of the RRSIG/DNSKEY records.

a54de0777a0b.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
a54de0777a0b.sentence: When a new KSK is created, the DS record must be transferred to the parent zone and published there.

9bce48806551.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
9bce48806551.sentence: The DS records use a message digest of the KSK instead of the complete key in order to keep the size of the records small.

d398632a4529.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
d398632a4529.sentence: This is helpful for zones such as the.com domain, which are very large.

4ffd9b7fa249.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
4ffd9b7fa249.sentence: In order to allow for replacement keys, a key rollover scheme is required.

a4c42dc8bc8d.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
a4c42dc8bc8d.sentence: Typically, this involves first rolling out new keys in new DNSKEY records, in addition to the existing old keys.

c9a6c276bf5a.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
c9a6c276bf5a.sentence: Then, when it is safe to assume that the time to live values have caused the caching of old keys to have passed, these new keys can be used.

95ef81ef2f11.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
95ef81ef2f11.sentence: Finally, when it is safe to assume that the caching of records using the old keys have expired, the old DNSKEY records can be deleted.

4b29c6a03380.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
4b29c6a03380.sentence: To limit replay attacks, there are not only the normal DNS TTL values for caching purposes, but additional timestamps in RRSIG records to limit the validity of a signature.

5741044b428c.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
5741044b428c.sentence: Unlike TTL values which are relative to when the records were sent, the timestamps are absolute.

de8e48316a43.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
de8e48316a43.sentence: This means that all security-aware DNS resolvers must have clocks that are fairly closely in sync, say to within a few minutes.

389b924fd102.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
389b924fd102.sentence: These timestamps imply that a zone must regularly be re-signed and re-distributed to secondary servers, or the signatures will be rejected by validating resolvers.

798a5a23a188.title: Split-horizon DNS
798a5a23a188.sentence: In computer networking, split-horizon DNS (also known as split-view DNS, split-brain DNS, or split DNS, or Mirage) is the facility of a Domain Name System (DNS) implementation to provide different sets of DNS information, usually selected by the source address of the DNS request.

794b0b74f445.title: Split-horizon DNS
794b0b74f445.sentence: Split-horizon DNS can provide a mechanism for security and privacy management by logical or physical separation of DNS information for network-internal access (within an administrative domain, e.g., company) and access from an unsecure, public network (e.g. the Internet).

7566f52c6825.title: Split-horizon DNS
7566f52c6825.sentence: This facility can provide a mechanism for security and privacy management by logical or physical separation of DNS information for network-internal access (within an administrative domain, e.g., company) and access from an unsecure, public network (e.g. the Internet).

839d72ce6b9b.title: Split-horizon DNS
839d72ce6b9b.sentence: One common use case for split-horizon DNS is when a server has both a private IP address on a local area network (not reachable from most of the Internet) and a public address, i.e. an address reachable across the Internet in general.

09e40eccb48e.title: Split-horizon DNS
09e40eccb48e.sentence: By using split-horizon DNS the same name can lead to either the private IP address or the public one, depending on which client sends the query.

90ac9f97c6de.title: Split-horizon DNS
90ac9f97c6de.sentence: This allows for critical local client machines to access a server directly through the local network, without the need to pass through a router.

4e8050c5f143.title: Split-horizon DNS
4e8050c5f143.sentence: Passing through fewer network devices improves the network latency.

e42ed782cb81.title: Split-horizon DNS
e42ed782cb81.sentence: Hardware-based implementations run distinct DNS server devices for the desired access granularity within the networks involved.

029690bd3b66.title: Split-horizon DNS
029690bd3b66.sentence: Software solutions use either multiple DNS server processes on the same hardware or special server software with the built-in capability of discriminating access to DNS zone records.

e1f830de9721.title: Split-horizon DNS
e1f830de9721.sentence: The latter is a common feature of many server software implementations of the DNS protocol (cf. Comparison of DNS server software) and is sometimes the implied meaning of the term split-horizon DNS, since all other forms of implementation can be achieved with any DNS server software.

07549425ef39.title: Split-horizon DNS
07549425ef39.sentence: Split-horizon DNS is designed to provide different authoritative answers to an identical query and DNSSEC is used to ensure veracity of data returned by the DNS.

b8b6d54400e7.title: Split-horizon DNS
b8b6d54400e7.sentence: These apparently conflicting goals create the potential for confusion or false security alerts in poorly constructed networks.

31f8550317b0.title: Split-horizon DNS
31f8550317b0.sentence: Research has produced recommendations to properly combine these two DNS features.

a4c79c822041.title: Domain Name System
a4c79c822041.sentence: The DNS protocol uses two types of DNS messages, queries and responses; both have the same format.

a6f8eed7870e.title: Domain Name System
a6f8eed7870e.sentence: Each message consists of a header and four sections: question, answer, authority, and an additional space.

1f1af4befbc0.title: Domain Name System
1f1af4befbc0.sentence: The header section consists of the following fields: Identification, Flags, Number of questions, Number of answers, Number of authority resource records (RRs), and Number of additional RRs.

9ba80e6aaf36.title: Domain Name System
9ba80e6aaf36.sentence: Each field is 16 bits long, and appears in the order given.

d8d50910c920.title: Domain Name System
d8d50910c920.sentence: The identification field is used to match responses with queries.

e2d1fb5a72d5.title: Domain Name System
e2d1fb5a72d5.sentence: Indicates if the message is a query (0) or a reply (1).

3336c59459d6.title: Domain Name System
3336c59459d6.sentence: Authoritative Answer, in a response, indicates if the DNS server is authoritative for the queried hostname.

3a24a478bb2c.title: Domain Name System
3a24a478bb2c.sentence: TrunCation, indicates that this message was truncated due to excessive length.

40f02b059a4e.title: Domain Name System
40f02b059a4e.sentence: Recursion Desired, indicates if the client means a recursive query.

74bd801b84f6.title: Domain Name System
74bd801b84f6.sentence: Recursion Available, in a response, indicates if the replying DNS server supports recursion.

008ff6d4228e.title: Domain Name System
008ff6d4228e.sentence: Response code, can be NOERROR (0), FORMERR (1, Format error), SERVFAIL (2), NXDOMAIN (3, Nonexistent domain), etc.

f1ccadbb48f4.title: Domain Name System
f1ccadbb48f4.sentence: The question section has a simpler format than the resource record format used in the other sections.

a4b5f00548d1.title: Domain Name System
a4b5f00548d1.sentence: Each question record (there is usually just one in the section) contains the following fields:

5b9efc868502.title: Domain Name System
5b9efc868502.sentence: The domain name is broken into discrete labels which are concatenated; each label is prefixed by the length of that label.

57038b13157d.title: Domain Name System
57038b13157d.sentence: It means that the name ends with octet 0, since it represents the length of the null label (which represents the root).

b64142fc871f.title: rfc>1034
b64142fc871f.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.1. Standard queries
b64142fc871f.sentence: A standard query specifies a target domain name (QNAME), query type (QTYPE), and query class (QCLASS) and asks for RRs which match.

fdc509f6b6de.title: rfc>1034
fdc509f6b6de.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.1. Standard queries
fdc509f6b6de.sentence: This type of query makes up such a vast majority of DNS queries that we use the term "query" to mean standard query unless otherwise specified.

4519e8067bf7.title: rfc>1034
4519e8067bf7.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries
4519e8067bf7.sentence: In the Internet, queries are carried in UDP datagrams or over TCP connections.

cc4e8308007c.title: rfc>1034
cc4e8308007c.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.1. Standard queries
cc4e8308007c.sentence: In addition to relevant records, the name server may return RRs that point toward a name server that has the desired information or RRs that are expected to be useful in interpreting the relevant RRs.

f7d48e8a8531.title: rfc>1034
f7d48e8a8531.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.1. Standard queries
f7d48e8a8531.sentence: For example, a name server that doesn't have the requested information may know a name server that does; a name server that returns a domain name in a relevant RR may also return the RR that binds that domain name to an address.

697b3facc99e.title: rfc>1034
697b3facc99e.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.1. Standard queries
697b3facc99e.sentence: For example, a mailer tying to send mail to Mockapetris@ISI.EDU might ask the resolver for mail information about ISI.EDU, resulting in a query for QNAME=ISI.EDU, QTYPE=MX, QCLASS=IN.

f19cfb60f5cc.title: rfc>1034
f19cfb60f5cc.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.1. Standard queries
f19cfb60f5cc.sentence: Because the server assumes that if the requester wants mail exchange information, it will probably want the addresses of the mail exchanges soon afterward.

735cf389eeb5.title: rfc>1034
735cf389eeb5.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.2. Inverse queries (Optional)
735cf389eeb5.sentence: Name servers may also support inverse queries that map a particular resource to a domain name or domain names that have that resource.

8c35e0845f47.title: rfc>1034
8c35e0845f47.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.2. Inverse queries (Optional)
8c35e0845f47.sentence: Inverse queries are primarily useful for debugging and database maintenance activities.

23f0de339bde.title: rfc>1034
23f0de339bde.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.2. Inverse queries (Optional)
23f0de339bde.sentence: The domain system cannot guarantee the completeness or uniqueness of inverse queries because the domain system is organized by domain name rather than by host address or any other resource type.

78734c14ed6c.title: rfc>1034
78734c14ed6c.section: 3. DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS > 3.7. Queries > 3.7.2. Inverse queries (Optional)
78734c14ed6c.sentence: Therefore, the RRs returned in inverse queries should never be cached.

a90f9146aa44.title: rfc>1034
a90f9146aa44.sentence: The top level algorithm has four steps:

3c7b7710bd9d.title: rfc>1034
3c7b7710bd9d.sentence: - See if the answer is in local information, and if so return it to the client.

6e57d40518bd.title: rfc>1034
6e57d40518bd.sentence: - Find the best servers to ask.

e4a78adf4d65.title: rfc>1034
e4a78adf4d65.sentence: - Send them queries until one returns a response.

873fe4d1e463.title: rfc>1034
873fe4d1e463.sentence: a. if the response answers the question or contains a name error, cache the data as well as returning it back to the client.

ccb95b34cab9.title: rfc>1034
ccb95b34cab9.sentence: b. if the response contains a better delegation to other servers, cache the delegation information, and go to step 2.

aa63d7e6e449.title: rfc>1034
aa63d7e6e449.sentence: c. if the response shows a CNAME and that is not the answer itself, cache the CNAME, change the SNAME to the canonical name in the CNAME RR and go to step 1.

34e1b7825d16.title: rfc>1034
34e1b7825d16.sentence: d. if the response shows a servers failure or other bizarre contents, delete the server from the SLIST and go back to step 3.

7233d5737a30.title: rfc>1034
7233d5737a30.sentence: The general strategy is to look for locally-available name server RRs, starting at SNAME, then the parent domain name of SNAME, the grandparent, and so on toward the root.

d28ba13da96e.title: rfc>1034
d28ba13da96e.sentence: Thus if SNAME were Mockapetris.ISI.EDU, this step would look for NS RRs for Mockapetris.ISI.EDU, then ISI.EDU, then EDU, and then.

09cf86a4b4c3.title: rfc>1034
09cf86a4b4c3.sentence: If the search for NS RRs fails, then the resolver initializes SLIST from the safety belt SBELT.

872a83c067f5.title: rfc>1034
872a83c067f5.sentence: Although there are special situations, the usual choice is two of the root servers and two of the servers for the host's domain.

75de2661b516.title: rfc>1034
75de2661b516.sentence: authoritative data is always used in preference to cached data when both are present.

d661a8453b59.title: rfc>1034
d661a8453b59.sentence: - Bound the amount of work (packets sent, parallel processes started) so that a request can't get into an infinite loop or start off a chain reaction of requests or queries with other implementations EVEN IF SOMEONE HAS INCORRECTLY CONFIGURED SOME DATA.

0ec0fdf30c75.title: rfc>1034
0ec0fdf30c75.sentence: The resolver should be highly paranoid in its parsing of responses.

9f776af38edc.title: HTTP
9f776af38edc.sentence: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is an application layer protocol in the Internet protocol suite for distributed, collaborative, hypermedia information systems.

461792ec655d.title: HTTP
461792ec655d.sentence: HTTP is the foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web, where hypertext documents include hyperlinks to other resources that the user can easily access, for example by a mouse click or by tapping the screen in a web browser.

e1b722fb8eff.title: rfc>9110
e1b722fb8eff.sentence: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is a stateless application-level protocol for distributed, collaborative, hypertext information systems.

1cb2561bc273.title: HTTP
1cb2561bc273.sentence: HTTP is a request–response protocol in the client–server model.

01aacd51c4ed.title: HTTP
01aacd51c4ed.sentence: A transaction starts with a client submitting a request to the server, the server attempts to satisfy the request and returns a response to the client that describes the disposition of the request and optionally contains a requested resource such as an HTML document or other content.

ee3c48a4ff83.title: HTTP
ee3c48a4ff83.sentence: In a common scenario, a web browser acts as the client, and a web server, hosting one or more websites, is the server.

dc99606e7334.title: HTTP
dc99606e7334.sentence: A web browser is an example of a user agent (UA).

fa5d13e10795.title: HTTP
fa5d13e10795.sentence: Other types of user agent include the indexing software used by search providers (web crawlers), voice browsers, mobile apps, and other software that accesses, consumes, or displays web content.

250bcb191554.title: HTTP
250bcb191554.sentence: As a stateless protocol, HTTP does not require the web server to retain information or status about each user for the duration of multiple requests.

184481cafdbf.title: HTTP
