184481cafdbf.sentence: HTTP is a stateless application-level protocol and it requires a reliable network transport connection to exchange data between client and server.

99a08411265e.title: HTTP
99a08411265e.sentence: HTTP presumes an underlying and reliable transport layer protocol.

68727e0a742b.title: HTTP
68727e0a742b.sentence: The standard choice of the underlying protocol prior to HTTP/3 is Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).

8b5b92087c88.title: HTTP
8b5b92087c88.sentence: In HTTP implementations, TCP/IP connections are used using well-known ports (typically port 80 if the connection is unencrypted or port 443 if the connection is encrypted, see also List of TCP and UDP port numbers).

5719617cdd6d.title: HTTP
5719617cdd6d.sentence: A web resource is located by a uniform resource locator (URL), using the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) schemes http and https.

434a37913ff0.title: HTTP
434a37913ff0.sentence: HTTP is designed to permit intermediate network elements to improve or enable communications between clients and servers.

89ba3d48acba.title: HTTP
89ba3d48acba.sentence: High-traffic websites often benefit from web cache servers that deliver content on behalf of upstream servers to improve response time.

6372a2c30848.title: HTTP
6372a2c30848.sentence: Web browsers cache previously accessed web resources and reuse them, whenever possible, to reduce network traffic.

873106839a20.title: HTTP
873106839a20.sentence: HTTP proxy servers at private network boundaries can facilitate communication for clients without a globally routable address, by relaying messages with external servers.

6d571cb9bdee.title: HTTP
6d571cb9bdee.sentence: To allow intermediate HTTP nodes (proxy servers, web caches, etc.) to accomplish their functions, some of the HTTP headers (found in HTTP requests/responses) are managed hop-by-hop whereas other HTTP headers are managed end-to-end (managed only by the source client and by the target web server).

afd8d237eb80.title: rfc>9110
afd8d237eb80.sentence: This document describes the overall architecture of HTTP, establishes common terminology, and defines aspects of the protocol that are shared by all versions.

0c1ee2e86aad.title: rfc>9110
0c1ee2e86aad.sentence: Because the semantics of HTTP are not versioned, these extension points are persistent; the version of the protocol in use does not affect their semantics.

36cbeab3ed38.title: Public-key cryptography
36cbeab3ed38.sentence: Public-key cryptography, or asymmetric cryptography, is the field of cryptographic systems that use pairs of related keys.

fb0c1c159fc2.title: Public-key cryptography
fb0c1c159fc2.sentence: Each key pair consists of a public key and a corresponding private key.

5c97fbe5141d.title: Public-key cryptography
5c97fbe5141d.sentence: Security of public-key cryptography depends on keeping the private key secret; the public key can be openly distributed without compromising security.

ce22b8ec4119.title: Public-key cryptography
ce22b8ec4119.sentence: Key pairs are generated with algorithms based on mathematical problems termed one-way functions.

2059913b3c8a.title: Public-key cryptography
2059913b3c8a.sentence: Before the mid-1970s, all cipher systems used symmetric key algorithms, in which the same cryptographic key is used with the underlying algorithm by both the sender and the recipient, who must both keep the key secret.

6082075e4f95.title: Public-key cryptography
6082075e4f95.sentence: Of necessity, the key in every such system had to be exchanged between the communicating parties in some secure way prior to any use of the system – for instance, via a secure channel.

a203f535a459.title: Public-key cryptography
a203f535a459.sentence: In particular, if messages are meant to be secure from other users, a separate key is required for each possible pair of users.

e9f8043aba80.title: Public-key cryptography
e9f8043aba80.sentence: By contrast, in a public-key cryptosystem, the public keys can be disseminated widely and openly, and only the corresponding private keys need be kept secret.

602312db57bc.title: Public-key cryptography
602312db57bc.sentence: - In a public-key encryption system, anyone with a public key can encrypt a message, yielding a ciphertext, but only those who know the corresponding private key can decrypt the ciphertext to obtain the original message.For example, a journalist can publish the public key of an encryption key pair on a website so that sources can send secret messages to the news organization in ciphertext.

05e7ec2d526d.title: Public-key cryptography
05e7ec2d526d.sentence: Public-key encryption on its own also does not tell the recipient anything about who sent a message—it just conceals the content of the message.

4518d4b51773.title: Public-key cryptography
4518d4b51773.sentence: - In a digital signature system, a sender can use a private key together with a message to create a signature.

f45f86449ca5.title: Public-key cryptography
f45f86449ca5.sentence: Anyone with the corresponding public key can verify whether the signature matches the message, but a forger who does not know the private key cannot generate any message/signature pair that will pass verification with the public key.For example, a software publisher can create a signature key pair and include the public key in software installed on computers.

745cc7423560.title: Public-key cryptography
745cc7423560.sentence: Later, the publisher can distribute an update to the software signed using the private key, and any computer receiving an update can confirm it is genuine by verifying the signature using the public key.

d80c64915100.title: Public-key cryptography
d80c64915100.sentence: As long as the software publisher keeps the private key secret, even if a forger can distribute malicious updates to computers, they cannot convince the computers that any malicious updates are genuine.

3200d502fccc.title: Public-key cryptography
3200d502fccc.sentence: Because asymmetric key algorithms are nearly always much more computationally intensive than symmetric ones, it is common to use a public/private asymmetric key-exchange algorithm to encrypt and exchange a symmetric key, which is then used by symmetric-key cryptography to transmit data using the now-shared symmetric key.

a55ed06bc8fb.title: Public-key cryptography
a55ed06bc8fb.sentence: PGP, SSH, and the SSL/TLS family of schemes use this procedure; they are thus called hybrid cryptosystems.

a5a1b54b6f88.title: Public-key cryptography
a5a1b54b6f88.sentence: The initial asymmetric cryptography-based key exchange to share a server-generated symmetric key from the server to client has the advantage of not requiring that a symmetric key be pre-shared manually, such as on printed paper or discs transported by a courier, while providing the higher data throughput of symmetric key cryptography over asymmetric key cryptography for the remainder of the shared connection.

6d579aedf3e4.title: Public-key cryptography
6d579aedf3e4.sentence: Compared to symmetric cryptography, public-key cryptography can be too slow for many purposes, so these protocols often combine symmetric cryptography with public-key cryptography in hybrid cryptosystems.

ff017cf7685b.title: Public-key cryptography
ff017cf7685b.sentence: One important issue is confidence or proof that a particular public key is authentic, i.e., that it is correct and belongs to the person or entity claimed, and has not been tampered with or replaced by some (perhaps malicious) third party.

397486f98ce1.title: Public-key cryptography
397486f98ce1.sentence: Another potential security vulnerability in using asymmetric keys is the possibility of a "man-in-the-middle" attack, in which the communication of public keys is intercepted by a third party (the "man in the middle") and then modified to provide different public keys instead.

3063d16f39eb.title: Public-key cryptography
3063d16f39eb.sentence: Encrypted messages and responses must, in all instances, be intercepted, decrypted, and re-encrypted by the attacker using the correct public keys for the different communication segments so as to avoid suspicion.

da7063006e9a.title: Public-key cryptography
da7063006e9a.sentence: - A public key infrastructure (PKI), in which one or more third parties, known as certificate authorities, certify ownership of key pairs.

a0c3a900caa1.title: Public-key cryptography
a0c3a900caa1.sentence: - A web of trust decentralizes authentication by using individual endorsements of links between a user and their public key.

89dc2cf0d272.title: Public-key cryptography
89dc2cf0d272.sentence: PGP uses this approach, in addition to lookup in the domain name system (DNS).

b1003badda85.title: Public-key cryptography
b1003badda85.sentence: An attacker who could subvert one of those certificate authorities into issuing a certificate for a bogus public key could then mount a "man-in-the-middle" attack as easily as if the certificate scheme were not used at all.

99966c159fe8.title: Public-key cryptography
99966c159fe8.sentence: Aside from poor choice of an asymmetric key algorithm (there are few that are widely regarded as satisfactory) or too short a key length, the chief security risk is that the private key of a pair becomes known.

0eaca006e095.title: Public-key cryptography
0eaca006e095.sentence: All security of messages, authentication, etc., encrypted with this private key will then be lost.

3ef74764db9e.title: Public-key cryptography
3ef74764db9e.sentence: This is commonly mitigated (such as in recent TLS schemes) by using forward secrecy capable schemes that generate an ephemeral set of keys during the communication, which must also be known for the communication to be compromised.

774324187038.title: Public-key cryptography
774324187038.sentence: With the advent of quantum computing, many asymmetric key algorithms are considered vulnerable to attacks, and new quantum-resistant schemes are being developed to overcome the problem.

42e54d4c2c7d.title: HTTP
42e54d4c2c7d.sentence: At the highest level, a message consists of a header followed by a body.

4b71ca25be9f.title: HTTP
4b71ca25be9f.sentence: A body is optional or, in other words, can be blank.

aec243eff60d.title: HTTP
aec243eff60d.sentence: A request is sent by a client to a server.

a55f3427eeac.title: HTTP
a55f3427eeac.sentence: A response is sent to the client by the server.

c392bce569fd.title: HTTP
c392bce569fd.sentence: The start line includes a method name, a request URI and the protocol version with a single space between each field.

230255b064ad.title: HTTP
230255b064ad.sentence: The following request start line specifies method GET, URI /customer/123 and protocol version HTTP/1.1:

e71ea042db7c.title: HTTP
e71ea042db7c.sentence: The start line of a response consists of the protocol version, a status code and optionally a reason phrase with fields separated by a single space character.

b015e32c9687.title: HTTP
b015e32c9687.sentence: The following response start line specifies protocol version HTTP/1.1, status code 400 and reason phrase Bad Request.

e7938ae6b205.title: HTTP
e7938ae6b205.sentence: A header field represents metadata about the containing message.

e2d2423bd61b.title: HTTP
e2d2423bd61b.sentence: A header field line is formatted as a name-value pair with a colon separator.

75c8446b0074.title: HTTP
75c8446b0074.sentence: Generally, the information of a header field is used by software and not shown to the user.

da964ee526e5.title: HTTP
da964ee526e5.sentence: Unlike a method name that must match exactly (case-sensitive), a header field name is matched ignoring case although often shown with each word capitalized.

48cdbc8038cc.title: HTTP
48cdbc8038cc.sentence: In the HTTP/1.1 protocol, all header fields except Host are optional.

d00f19a4aec1.title: HTTP
d00f19a4aec1.sentence: A body consists of data in any format; not limited to ASCII.

2bc3df39b9d8.title: HTTP
2bc3df39b9d8.sentence: The format must match that specified by the Content-Type header field if the message contains one.

c13660c9a3b5.title: HTTP
c13660c9a3b5.sentence: The standards do not limit the size of a header field or the number of fields in a message.

5e847f7bc1d7.title: HTTP
5e847f7bc1d7.sentence: However, most servers, clients, and proxy software impose limits for practical and security reasons.

8feaadc9ab34.title: HTTP
8feaadc9ab34.sentence: Later versions, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, use a binary protocol, where headers are encoded in a single HEADERS and zero or more CONTINUATION frames using HPACK (HTTP/2) or QPACK (HTTP/3), which both provide efficient header compression.

5f34e8f0e54c.title: HTTP
5f34e8f0e54c.sentence: The request or response line from HTTP/1 has also been replaced by several pseudo-header fields, each beginning with a colon (:).

3ed661acde40.title: HTTP
3ed661acde40.sentence: In HTTP/1.1, a keep-alive-mechanism was officially introduced so that a connection could be reused for more than one request/response.

ab0f55aa8197.title: HTTP
ab0f55aa8197.sentence: In HTTP/0.9, the TCP/IP connection is always closed after server response has been sent, so it is never persistent.

803207f88357.title: HTTP
803207f88357.sentence: In HTTP/1.0, the TCP/IP connection should always be closed by server after a response has been sent.

2446d796fcfb.title: HTTP
2446d796fcfb.sentence: In HTTP/1.0, a separate TCP connection to the same server is made for every resource request.

65d463add7a2.title: HTTP
65d463add7a2.sentence: In HTTP/1.1, instead a TCP connection can be reused to make multiple resource requests (i.e. of HTML pages, frames, images, scripts, stylesheets, etc.).

2d605dbb22db.title: HTTP
2d605dbb22db.sentence: Such persistent connections reduce request latency perceptibly because the client does not need to re-negotiate the TCP 3-Way-Handshake connection after the first request has been sent.

06ce82ec437d.title: HTTP
06ce82ec437d.sentence: Another positive side effect is that, in general, the connection becomes faster with time due to TCP's slow-start-mechanism.

4d41497dae5e.title: HTTP
4d41497dae5e.sentence: HTTP/1.1 communications therefore experience less latency as the establishment of TCP connections presents considerable overhead, especially under high traffic conditions.

566c2c4e58eb.title: HTTP
566c2c4e58eb.sentence: HTTP/1.1 added also HTTP pipelining in order to further reduce lag time when using persistent connections by allowing clients to send multiple requests before waiting for each response.

b4df75b21e15.title: HTTP
b4df75b21e15.sentence: This optimization was never considered really safe because a few web servers and many proxy servers, specially transparent proxy servers placed in Internet / Intranets between clients and servers, did not handle pipelined requests properly (they served only the first request discarding the others, they closed the connection because they saw more data after the first request or some proxies even returned responses out of order etc.).

4b416be80963.title: HTTP
4b416be80963.sentence: After many years of struggling with the problems introduced by enabling pipelining, this feature was first disabled and then removed from most browsers.

a91022bfd327.title: HTTP
a91022bfd327.sentence: HTTP/2 extended the usage of persistent connections by multiplexing many concurrent requests/responses through a single TCP/IP connection.

26016f2d719e.title: HTTP
26016f2d719e.sentence: HTTP/3 does not use TCP/IP connections but QUIC + UDP.

2f133031b99e.title: HTTP
2f133031b99e.section: Technology > Data exchange > Request and response messages through connections
2f133031b99e.sentence: At any time and for many reasons, either the client or server can close the connection.

56f0105fb464.title: HTTP
56f0105fb464.section: Technology > Data exchange > Request and response messages through connections
56f0105fb464.sentence: Closing a connection is usually advertised by one or more HTTP headers in the last request or response.

db5a13e3862c.title: HTTP
db5a13e3862c.sentence: A request identifies a method (sometimes informally called verb) to classify the desired action to be performed on a resource.

78b18a81ae21.title: rfc>9110
78b18a81ae21.sentence: The request method token is the primary source of request semantics; it indicates the purpose for which the client has made this request and what is expected by the client as a successful result.

178f9bda56c9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
178f9bda56c9.sentence: - HTTP GET This retrieves a resource from the server.

b38713d9b21a.title: rfc>9110
b38713d9b21a.sentence: The GET method requests transfer of a current selected representation for the target resource.

e05e19350aa8.title: rfc>9110
e05e19350aa8.sentence: GET is the primary mechanism of information retrieval and the focus of almost all performance optimizations.

d01cf4f1b767.title: HTTP
d01cf4f1b767.sentence: The server should only retrieve data; not modify state.

3549c0683399.title: HTTP
3549c0683399.sentence: For retrieving without making changes, GET is preferred over POST, as it can be addressed through a URL.

8e0eea65913f.title: HTTP
8e0eea65913f.sentence: This enables bookmarking and sharing and makes GET responses eligible for caching, which can save bandwidth.

75e5243f045d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
75e5243f045d.sentence: - HTTP HEAD The HEAD method asks for a response identical to a GET request but without the response body.

1177317f4e84.title: rfc>9110
1177317f4e84.sentence: The HEAD method is identical to GET except that the server MUST NOT send content in the response.

9487c1e60050.title: rfc>9110
9487c1e60050.sentence: HEAD is used to obtain metadata about the selected representation without transferring its representation data, often for the sake of testing hypertext links or finding recent modifications.

6fe4757cc44a.title: HTTP
6fe4757cc44a.sentence: Uses include checking whether a page is available via the status code and getting the size of a file via header field Content-Length.

24db161274a8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
24db161274a8.sentence: - HTTP POST This is used to create new resources.

43a5ae695fee.title: rfc>9110
43a5ae695fee.sentence: The POST method requests that the target resource process the representation enclosed in the request according to the resource's own specific semantics.

b89879539e05.title: rfc>9110
b89879539e05.sentence: For example, POST is used for the following functions (among others):

ce4d9e63390a.title: rfc>9110
ce4d9e63390a.sentence: If one or more resources has been created on the origin server as a result of successfully processing a POST request, the origin server SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response containing a Location header field that provides an identifier for the primary resource created (Section 10.2.2) and a representation that describes the status of the request while referring to the new resource(s).

00bb84ebb2b4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
00bb84ebb2b4.sentence: - HTTP PUT This updates or Creates a resource.

48488271d58a.title: rfc>9110
48488271d58a.sentence: The PUT method requests that the state of the target resource be created or replaced with the state defined by the representation enclosed in the request message content.

5ac76ea9c700.title: HTTP
5ac76ea9c700.sentence: A distinction from POST is that the client specifies the target location on the server.

3546b2fca962.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
3546b2fca962.sentence: Multiple identical requests will update the same resource.

6bc2cbb585cf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
6bc2cbb585cf.sentence: - HTTP DELETE This is used to delete a resource.

1b697b3dd374.title: rfc>9110
1b697b3dd374.sentence: The DELETE method requests that the origin server remove the association between the target resource and its current functionality.

f4aa417b549c.title: rfc>9110
f4aa417b549c.sentence: In effect, this method is similar to the "rm" command in UNIX: it expresses a deletion operation on the URI mapping of the origin server rather than an expectation that the previously associated information be deleted.

5cc18cad2ccd.title: rfc>9110
5cc18cad2ccd.sentence: Relatively few resources allow the DELETE method -- its primary use is for remote authoring environments, where the user has some direction regarding its effect.

3a5ebb15386c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
3a5ebb15386c.sentence: - HTTP PATCH The PATCH method applies partial modifications to a resource.

75c42f539824.title: HTTP
75c42f539824.sentence: The request is to modify a resource according to its partial state in the request.

10821716a291.title: HTTP
10821716a291.sentence: Compared to PUT, this can save bandwidth by sending only part of a resource's representation instead of all of it.

875782d99dba.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
875782d99dba.sentence: - HTTP CONNECT The CONNECT method establishes a tunnel to the server identified by the target resource.

ad7d74733dc5.title: rfc>9110
ad7d74733dc5.sentence: The CONNECT method requests that the recipient establish a tunnel to the destination origin server identified by the request target and, if successful, thereafter restrict its behavior to blind forwarding of data, in both directions, until the tunnel is closed.

aa2a6a244d24.title: rfc>9110
aa2a6a244d24.sentence: Tunnels are commonly used to create an end-to-end virtual connection, through one or more proxies, which can then be secured using TLS (Transport Layer Security, ).

c74fec2409ac.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
c74fec2409ac.sentence: - HTTP OPTIONS This describes the communication options for the target resource.

d62088d99a04.title: rfc>9110
d62088d99a04.sentence: The OPTIONS method requests information about the communication options available for the target resource, at either the origin server or an intervening intermediary.

a2ac023d723c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
a2ac023d723c.sentence: - HTTP TRACE This performs a message loop-back test along the path to the target resource.

e8360f2bdf9f.title: rfc>9110
e8360f2bdf9f.sentence: The TRACE method requests a remote, application-level loop-back of the request message.

8806571e5d65.title: rfc>9110
8806571e5d65.sentence: TRACE allows the client to see what is being received at the other end of the request chain and use that data for testing or diagnostic information.

25f1b3839c72.title: rfc>9110
25f1b3839c72.sentence: All general-purpose servers MUST support the methods GET and HEAD.

95decbad6197.title: rfc>9110
95decbad6197.sentence: The method token is case-sensitive because it might be used as a gateway to object-based systems with case-sensitive method names.

43eb5b32c61f.title: rfc>9110
43eb5b32c61f.sentence: An origin server that receives a request method that is unrecognized or not implemented SHOULD respond with the 501 (Not Implemented) status code.

7d8779ee37d8.title: rfc>9110
7d8779ee37d8.sentence: An origin server that receives a request method that is recognized and implemented, but not allowed for the target resource, SHOULD respond with the 405 (Method Not Allowed) status code.

54092b01b145.title: rfc>9110
54092b01b145.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.3. Methods and Caching
54092b01b145.sentence: This specification defines caching semantics for GET, HEAD, and POST, although the overwhelming majority of cache implementations only support GET and HEAD.

cb25eddebac0.title: rfc>9110
cb25eddebac0.sentence: Responses to POST requests are only cacheable when they include explicit freshness information (see Section 4.2.1 of ) and a Content-Location header field that has the same value as the POST's target URI (Section 8.7).

c5618aee6af5.title: rfc>9110
c5618aee6af5.sentence: Responses to the PUT method are not cacheable.

60980211e618.title: rfc>9110
60980211e618.sentence: Responses to the DELETE method are not cacheable.

c8c5fb766818.title: rfc>9110
c8c5fb766818.sentence: If a successful PUT request passes through a cache that has one or more stored responses for the target URI, those stored responses will be invalidated (see Section 4.4 of ).

10b92e147fbe.title: rfc>9110
10b92e147fbe.section: 3. Terminology and Core Concepts > 3.3. Connections, Clients, and Servers
10b92e147fbe.sentence: HTTP is defined as a stateless protocol, meaning that each request message's semantics can be understood in isolation, and that the relationship between connections and messages on them has no impact on the interpretation of those messages.

5cbf7ae40737.title: HTTP
5cbf7ae40737.sentence: If a web application needs an application session, it implements it via HTTP cookies, hidden variables in a web form or another mechanism.

f841a28d50fd.title: rfc>9110
f841a28d50fd.section: 3. Terminology and Core Concepts > 3.3. Connections, Clients, and Servers
f841a28d50fd.sentence: Many implementations depend on HTTP's stateless design in order to reuse proxied connections or dynamically load balance requests across multiple servers.

ee1f8aea7367.title: rfc>9110
ee1f8aea7367.section: 3. Terminology and Core Concepts > 3.3. Connections, Clients, and Servers
ee1f8aea7367.sentence: As a result, a server MUST NOT assume that two requests on the same connection are from the same user agent unless the connection is secured and specific to that agent.

60e60146bdba.title: HTTP
60e60146bdba.sentence: Typically, to start a session, an interactive login is performed, and to end a session, a logout is requested by the user.

bef4c66a7636.title: HTTP
bef4c66a7636.sentence: These operations use a custom authentication mechanism, not HTTP authentication.

bb427fb17627.title: HTTP cookie
bb427fb17627.sentence: An HTTP cookie (also called web cookie, Internet cookie, browser cookie, or simply cookie) is a small block of data created by a web server while a user is browsing a website and placed on the user's computer or other device by the user's web browser.

59797b81ef62.title: HTTP cookie
59797b81ef62.sentence: The browser then sends them back to the server with every request, introducing states (memory of previous events) into otherwise stateless HTTP transactions.

0e852a9a9c3a.title: HTTP cookie
0e852a9a9c3a.sentence: Cookies are set using the Set-Cookie header field, sent in an HTTP response from the web server.

2eaa1d3b16ca.title: HTTP cookie
2eaa1d3b16ca.sentence: This header field instructs the web browser to store the cookie and send it back in future requests to the server (the browser will ignore this header field if it does not support cookies or has disabled cookies).

cac832978c7b.title: HTTP cookie
cac832978c7b.sentence: Cookies are arbitrary pieces of data, usually chosen and first sent by the web server, and stored on the client computer by the web browser.

ae1d132d5058.title: HTTP cookie
ae1d132d5058.sentence: Attributes store information such as the cookie's expiration, domain, and flags (such as Secure and HttpOnly).

e60d5a1f87a5.title: HTTP cookie
e60d5a1f87a5.sentence: Browsers do not include cookie attributes in requests to the server—they only send the cookie's name and value.

776f405165f9.title: HTTP cookie
776f405165f9.sentence: Cookie attributes are used by browsers to determine when to delete a cookie, block a cookie or whether to send a cookie to the server.

4370afae853e.title: HTTP cookie
4370afae853e.sentence: A session cookie (also known as an in-memory cookie, transient cookie or non-persistent cookie) exists only in temporary memory while the user navigates a website.

f454509f30c9.title: HTTP cookie
f454509f30c9.sentence: Session cookies expire or are deleted when the user closes the web browser.

62ed6029d137.title: HTTP cookie
62ed6029d137.sentence: A persistent cookie expires at a specific date or after a specific length of time.

926dc76982bf.title: HTTP cookie
926dc76982bf.sentence: Persistent cookies are also used for reasons such as keeping users logged into their accounts on websites, to avoid re-entering login credentials at every visit.

2cb37aa96d1b.title: HTTP cookie
2cb37aa96d1b.sentence: The first, theme, is considered to be a session cookie since it does not have an Expires or Max-Age attribute.

ad9125e3b4c3.title: HTTP cookie
ad9125e3b4c3.section: Implementation > Cookie attributes > Expires and Max-Age
ad9125e3b4c3.sentence: The Expires attribute defines a specific date and time for when the browser should delete the cookie.

3fb1845e4373.title: HTTP cookie
3fb1845e4373.section: Implementation > Cookie attributes > Expires and Max-Age
3fb1845e4373.sentence: Alternatively, the Max-Age attribute can be used to set the cookie's expiration as an interval of seconds in the future, relative to the time the browser received the cookie.

1afc7ae37e80.title: HTTP cookie
1afc7ae37e80.sentence: To remove a cookie, the server must include a Set-Cookie header field with an expiration date in the past.

5a4c003dc283.title: HTTP cookie
5a4c003dc283.section: Implementation > Cookie attributes > Domain and Path
5a4c003dc283.sentence: The Domain and Path attributes define the scope of the cookie.

89ffa0f84417.title: HTTP cookie
89ffa0f84417.section: Implementation > Cookie attributes > Domain and Path
89ffa0f84417.sentence: For security reasons, cookies can only be set on the current resource's top domain and its subdomains, and not for another domain and its subdomains.

41f4a993c2a0.title: HTTP cookie
41f4a993c2a0.section: Implementation > Cookie attributes > Domain and Path
41f4a993c2a0.sentence: If a cookie's Domain and Path attributes are not specified by the server, they default to the domain and path of the resource that was requested.

c07721ed1ab8.title: HTTP cookie
c07721ed1ab8.section: Implementation > Cookie attributes > Domain and Path
c07721ed1ab8.sentence: In the former case, the cookie will only be sent for requests to foo.com, also known as a host-only cookie.

54b7946b6c5b.title: HTTP cookie
54b7946b6c5b.section: Implementation > Cookie attributes > Domain and Path
54b7946b6c5b.sentence: In the latter case, all subdomains are also included (for example, docs.foo.com).

8dc4ece256c1.title: HTTP cookie
8dc4ece256c1.sentence: To keep track of which user is assigned to which shopping cart, the server sends a cookie to the client that contains a unique session identifier (typically, a long string of random letters and numbers).

5d00eb1a3c73.title: HTTP cookie
5d00eb1a3c73.sentence: Today, however, the contents of a user's shopping cart are usually stored in a database on the server, rather than in a cookie on the client.

9c40961a4510.title: HTTP cookie
9c40961a4510.sentence: Because session cookies only contain a unique session identifier, this makes the amount of personal information that a website can save about each user virtually limitless—the website is not limited to restrictions concerning how large a cookie can be.

53dd55105298.title: HTTP cookie
53dd55105298.sentence: Session cookies also help to improve page load times, since the amount of information in a session cookie is small and requires little bandwidth.

897b0ee8beff.title: HTTP cookie
897b0ee8beff.sentence: Because cookies are sent to the server with every request the client makes, that session identifier will be sent back to the server every time the user visits a new page on the website, which lets the server know which shopping cart to display to the user.

82ac3fea9479.title: HTTP cookie
82ac3fea9479.sentence: Authentication cookies are commonly used by web servers to authenticate that a user is logged in, and with which account they are logged in.

9e48706a14df.title: HTTP cookie
9e48706a14df.sentence: Without the cookie, users would need to authenticate themselves by logging in on each page containing sensitive information that they wish to access.

39f19574fea8.title: HTTP cookie
39f19574fea8.sentence: When the user visits a website's login page, the web server typically sends the client a cookie containing a unique session identifier.

cb3f6841b044.title: HTTP cookie
cb3f6841b044.sentence: When the user successfully logs in, the server remembers that that particular session identifier has been authenticated and grants the user access to its services.

45258d2d0062.title: HTTP cookie
45258d2d0062.sentence: A third-party cookie, belongs to a domain different from the one shown in the address bar.

f477d68b13c0.title: HTTP cookie
f477d68b13c0.sentence: This sort of cookie typically appears when web pages feature content from external websites, such as banner advertisements.

9ace61392d24.title: HTTP cookie
9ace61392d24.sentence: This opens up the potential for tracking the user's browsing history and is used by advertisers to serve relevant advertisements to each user.

e7dfa6e5b9a9.title: HTTP cookie
e7dfa6e5b9a9.sentence: The advertiser can then use these cookies to build up a browsing history of the user across all the websites that have ads from this advertiser, through the use of the HTTP referer header field.

26ffe4755503.title: HTTP
26ffe4755503.sentence: The status code is a three-digit, decimal, integer value that represents the disposition of the server's attempt to satisfy the client's request.

d101307fb0f1.title: rfc>9110
d101307fb0f1.sentence: The status code of a response is a three-digit integer code that describes the result of the request and the semantics of the response, including whether the request was successful and what content is enclosed (if any).

33ffdcccc273.title: rfc>9110
33ffdcccc273.sentence: All valid status codes are within the range of 100 to 599, inclusive.

2716d3551b62.title: rfc>9110
2716d3551b62.sentence: The first digit of the status code defines the class of response.

e2240b1f7cbd.title: rfc>9110
e2240b1f7cbd.sentence: The last two digits do not have any categorization role.

1f2d49e6491b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/http-status-code-you-should-know.md
1f2d49e6491b.sentence: The response codes for HTTP are divided into five categories:

716ddff46766.title: rfc>9110
716ddff46766.sentence: - 1xx (Informational): The request was received, continuing process

e151e0186351.title: rfc>9110
e151e0186351.sentence: - 2xx (Successful): The request was successfully received, understood, and accepted

6de6bc7ccfad.title: rfc>9110
6de6bc7ccfad.sentence: - 3xx (Redirection): Further action needs to be taken in order to complete the request

01fdcb0c92b6.title: rfc>9110
01fdcb0c92b6.sentence: - 4xx (Client Error): The request contains bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled

aecca15da5d7.title: rfc>9110
aecca15da5d7.sentence: - 5xx (Server Error): The server failed to fulfill an apparently valid request

4b49ff0b0a55.title: rfc>9110
4b49ff0b0a55.sentence: However, a client MUST understand the class of any status code, as indicated by the first digit, and treat an unrecognized status code as being equivalent to the x00 status code of that class.

98bfa3425ce2.title: rfc>9110
98bfa3425ce2.sentence: For example, if a client receives an unrecognized status code of 471, it can see from the first digit that there was something wrong with its request and treat the response as if it had received a 400 (Bad Request) status code.

50ddff54bb46.title: HTTP
50ddff54bb46.sentence: A client may not understand each status code that a server reports but it must understand the class as indicated by the first digit and treat an unrecognized code as equivalent to the x00 code of that class.

706c12d7998b.title: rfc>9110
706c12d7998b.sentence: A client that receives a response with an invalid status code SHOULD process the response as if it had a 5xx (Server Error) status code.

12616a7b2983.title: rfc>9110
12616a7b2983.sentence: A single request can have multiple associated responses: zero or more "interim" (non-final) responses with status codes in the "informational" (1xx) range, followed by exactly one "final" response with a status code in one of the other ranges.

e05e622d7d6a.title: HTTP
e05e622d7d6a.sentence: Generally, a client handles a response primarily based on the status code and secondarily on response header fields.

be893f8345c0.title: rfc>9110
be893f8345c0.sentence: The response message will usually contain a representation that explains the status.

0f1ac0fdbac8.title: rfc>9110
0f1ac0fdbac8.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.1. Overview of Status Codes
0f1ac0fdbac8.sentence: All such status codes ought to be registered within the "Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Status Code Registry", as described in Section 16.2.

484ff3967afd.title: rfc>9110
484ff3967afd.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.1. Overview of Status Codes
484ff3967afd.sentence: The reason phrases listed here are only recommendations -- they can be replaced by local equivalents or left out altogether without affecting the protocol.

9f2ccc3780bf.title: HTTP
9f2ccc3780bf.sentence: The standard also allows the user agent to attempt to interpret the reason phrase, though this might be unwise since the standard explicitly specifies that status codes are machine-readable and reason phrases are human-readable.

443b7ab4c749.title: rfc>9110
443b7ab4c749.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.1. Overview of Status Codes
443b7ab4c749.sentence: Responses with status codes that are defined as heuristically cacheable (e.g., 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, and 501 in this specification) can be reused by a cache with heuristic expiration unless otherwise indicated by the method definition or explicit cache controls; all other status codes are not heuristically cacheable.

f5ba65c7ba75.title: rfc>9110
f5ba65c7ba75.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
f5ba65c7ba75.sentence: A request method is considered "idempotent" if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request.

479911800a27.title: HTTP
479911800a27.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
479911800a27.sentence: A request method is idempotent if multiple identical requests with that method have the same effect as a single such request.

9fdb927e8cd7.title: rfc>9110
9fdb927e8cd7.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
9fdb927e8cd7.sentence: Of the request methods defined by this specification, PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent.

27f95355068a.title: HTTP
27f95355068a.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
27f95355068a.sentence: The methods PUT and DELETE, and safe methods are defined as idempotent.

d75bc154cf7f.title: HTTP
d75bc154cf7f.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
d75bc154cf7f.sentence: In contrast, the methods POST, CONNECT, and PATCH are not necessarily idempotent, and therefore sending an identical POST request multiple times may further modify the state of the server or have further effects, such as sending multiple emails.

8d0d7a9c1662.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
8d0d7a9c1662.sentence: It is not idempotent, making two identical POST will duplicate the resource creation.

6a680d34f73c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
6a680d34f73c.sentence: Multiple identical requests return the same result.

f25e2a930889.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-9-http-request-methods.md
f25e2a930889.sentence: Multiple identical requests will delete the same resource.

f192309d2604.title: HTTP
f192309d2604.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
f192309d2604.sentence: A website might, for instance, set up a PUT endpoint to modify a user's recorded email address.

335019ab440e.title: HTTP
335019ab440e.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
335019ab440e.sentence: If this endpoint is configured correctly, any requests which ask to change a user's email address to the same email address which is already recorded—e.g. duplicate requests following a successful request—will have no effect.

685210af813c.title: HTTP
685210af813c.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
685210af813c.sentence: Similarly, a request to DELETE a certain user will have no effect if that user has already been deleted.

bafe37be1d7a.title: rfc>9110
bafe37be1d7a.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
bafe37be1d7a.sentence: Like the definition of safe, the idempotent property only applies to what has been requested by the user; a server is free to log each request separately, retain a revision control history, or implement other non-idempotent side effects for each idempotent request.

d08f38c397c5.title: rfc>9110
d08f38c397c5.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
d08f38c397c5.sentence: Idempotent methods are distinguished because the request can be repeated automatically if a communication failure occurs before the client is able to read the server's response.

d37bbd2d2662.title: rfc>9110
d37bbd2d2662.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
d37bbd2d2662.sentence: For example, if a client sends a PUT request and the underlying connection is closed before any response is received, then the client can establish a new connection and retry the idempotent request.

244cc819662e.title: rfc>9110
244cc819662e.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
244cc819662e.sentence: It knows that repeating the request will have the same intended effect, even if the original request succeeded, though the response might differ.

854be00bd2fc.title: rfc>9110
854be00bd2fc.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
854be00bd2fc.sentence: A client SHOULD NOT automatically retry a request with a non-idempotent method unless it has some means to know that the request semantics are actually idempotent, regardless of the method, or some means to detect that the original request was never applied.

878742ecaf60.title: rfc>9110
878742ecaf60.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
878742ecaf60.sentence: A proxy MUST NOT automatically retry non-idempotent requests.

2dbdf3a199e7.title: rfc>9110
2dbdf3a199e7.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
2dbdf3a199e7.sentence: A client SHOULD NOT automatically retry a failed automatic retry.

b79d52e3f67d.title: rfc>9110
b79d52e3f67d.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
b79d52e3f67d.sentence: Some clients take a riskier approach and attempt to guess when an automatic retry is possible.

a1a1650d82e2.title: rfc>9110
a1a1650d82e2.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.2. Idempotent Methods
a1a1650d82e2.sentence: For example, a client might automatically retry a POST request if the underlying transport connection closed before any part of a response is received, particularly if an idle persistent connection was used.

756725d49cb2.title: HTTP
756725d49cb2.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
756725d49cb2.sentence: A user might, for example, inadvertently send multiple POST requests by clicking a button again if they were not given clear feedback that the first click was being processed.

3d45bebc2785.title: HTTP
3d45bebc2785.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
3d45bebc2785.sentence: While web browsers may show alert dialog boxes to warn users in some cases where reloading a page may re-submit a POST request, it is generally up to the web application to handle cases where a POST request should not be submitted more than once.

ed1db4248950.title: HTTP
ed1db4248950.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
ed1db4248950.sentence: Note that whether or not a method is idempotent is not enforced by the protocol or web server.

bcb4f73b6b71.title: HTTP
bcb4f73b6b71.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
bcb4f73b6b71.sentence: It is perfectly possible to write a web application in which (for example) a database insert or other non-idempotent action is triggered by a GET or other request.

245f3d40fef3.title: HTTP
245f3d40fef3.section: Message format > Request > Method > Idempotent method
245f3d40fef3.sentence: To do so against recommendations, however, may result in undesirable consequences, if a user agent assumes that repeating the same request is safe when it is not.

3d9b11ed6994.title: rfc>9110
3d9b11ed6994.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
3d9b11ed6994.sentence: Request methods are considered "safe" if their defined semantics are essentially read-only; i.e., the client does not request, and does not expect, any state change on the origin server as a result of applying a safe method to a target resource.

a850ae55c8d6.title: HTTP
a850ae55c8d6.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
a850ae55c8d6.sentence: A request method is safe if a request with that method has no intended effect on the server.

1b69889dd4f7.title: HTTP
1b69889dd4f7.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
1b69889dd4f7.sentence: In other words, safe methods are intended to be read-only.

e0902d2c1ce4.title: rfc>9110
e0902d2c1ce4.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
e0902d2c1ce4.sentence: Of the request methods defined by this specification, the GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE methods are defined to be safe.

cfcae70f2147.title: HTTP
cfcae70f2147.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
cfcae70f2147.sentence: The methods GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, and QUERY are defined as safe.

1e6c152b8bce.title: HTTP
1e6c152b8bce.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
1e6c152b8bce.sentence: In contrast, the methods POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, and PATCH are not safe.

44e86bdef60e.title: rfc>9110
44e86bdef60e.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
44e86bdef60e.sentence: The purpose of distinguishing between safe and unsafe methods is to allow automated retrieval processes (spiders) and cache performance optimization (pre-fetching) to work without fear of causing harm.

6d850336d276.title: rfc>9110
6d850336d276.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
6d850336d276.sentence: In addition, it allows a user agent to apply appropriate constraints on the automated use of unsafe methods when processing potentially untrusted content.

1efa3c7ab137.title: rfc>9110
1efa3c7ab137.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
1efa3c7ab137.sentence: A user agent SHOULD distinguish between safe and unsafe methods when presenting potential actions to a user, such that the user can be made aware of an unsafe action before it is requested.

2caed80bfeba.title: rfc>9110
2caed80bfeba.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
2caed80bfeba.sentence: Likewise, reasonable use of a safe method is not expected to cause any harm, loss of property, or unusual burden on the origin server.

34cadd85e393.title: rfc>9110
34cadd85e393.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
34cadd85e393.sentence: This definition of safe methods does not prevent an implementation from including behavior that is potentially harmful, that is not entirely read-only, or that causes side effects while invoking a safe method.

83d8c06fd97f.title: rfc>9110
83d8c06fd97f.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
83d8c06fd97f.sentence: What is important, however, is that the client did not request that additional behavior and cannot be held accountable for it.

3a5f68f61b05.title: rfc>9110
3a5f68f61b05.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
3a5f68f61b05.sentence: For example, most servers append request information to access log files at the completion of every response, regardless of the method, and that is considered safe even though the log storage might become full and cause the server to fail.

e621b028405a.title: rfc>9110
e621b028405a.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
e621b028405a.sentence: Likewise, a safe request initiated by selecting an advertisement on the Web will often have the side effect of charging an advertising account.

377c8d457363.title: HTTP
377c8d457363.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
377c8d457363.sentence: Safe methods can still have side effects not seen by the client, such as appending request information to a log file or charging an advertising account.

9a9bc76e1ee1.title: rfc>9110
9a9bc76e1ee1.sentence: A resource cannot treat a request in a manner inconsistent with the semantics of the method of the request.

b36d89da5418.title: rfc>9110
b36d89da5418.sentence: For example, though the URI of a resource might imply semantics that are not safe, a client can expect the resource to avoid actions that are unsafe when processing a request with a safe method (see Section 9.2.1).

ab14e4a271ee.title: rfc>9110
ab14e4a271ee.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
ab14e4a271ee.sentence: When a resource is constructed such that parameters within the target URI have the effect of selecting an action, it is the resource owner's responsibility to ensure that the action is consistent with the request method semantics.

6afaa9fb8911.title: rfc>9110
6afaa9fb8911.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
6afaa9fb8911.sentence: For example, it is common for Web-based content editing software to use actions within query parameters, such as "page?do=delete".

15ee4f438c24.title: rfc>9110
15ee4f438c24.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
15ee4f438c24.sentence: If the purpose of such a resource is to perform an unsafe action, then the resource owner MUST disable or disallow that action when it is accessed using a safe request method.

870d5a7b7b31.title: rfc>9110
870d5a7b7b31.section: 9. Methods > 9.2. Common Method Properties > 9.2.1. Safe Methods
870d5a7b7b31.sentence: Failure to do so will result in unfortunate side effects when automated processes perform a GET on every URI reference for the sake of link maintenance, pre-fetching, building a search index, etc.

b6cfb46ae55b.title: HTTP
b6cfb46ae55b.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
b6cfb46ae55b.sentence: Despite the prescribed safety of GET requests, in practice their handling by the server is not technically limited in any way.

c813ef51148c.title: HTTP
c813ef51148c.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
c813ef51148c.sentence: Careless or deliberately irregular programming can allow GET requests to cause non-trivial changes on the server.

cb3ed559a0c3.title: HTTP
cb3ed559a0c3.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
cb3ed559a0c3.sentence: This is discouraged because of the problems which can occur when web caching, search engines, and other automated agents make unintended changes on the server.

42d7bd25ff07.title: HTTP
42d7bd25ff07.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
42d7bd25ff07.sentence: For example, a website might allow deletion of a resource through a URL such as https://example.com/article/1234/delete, which, if arbitrarily fetched, even using GET, would simply delete the article.

7dfa0c162259.title: HTTP
7dfa0c162259.section: Message format > Request > Method > Safe method
7dfa0c162259.sentence: A properly coded website would require a DELETE or POST method for this action, which non-malicious bots would not make.

1df35483ce3e.sentence: To prepare a web server to accept HTTPS connections, the administrator must create a public key certificate for the web server.

e0cf83d43895.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
e0cf83d43895.sentence: Symmetric-key algorithms are algorithms for cryptography that use the same cryptographic keys for both the encryption of plaintext and the decryption of ciphertext.

963b5d659d49.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
963b5d659d49.sentence: The keys, in practice, represent a shared secret between two or more parties that can be used to maintain a private information link.

ce3c130f0eb7.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
ce3c130f0eb7.sentence: The requirement that both parties have access to the secret key is one of the main drawbacks of symmetric-key encryption, in comparison to asymmetric-key encryption (also known as public-key encryption).

8e43ecc0d289.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
8e43ecc0d289.sentence: Symmetric-key algorithms require both the sender and the recipient of a message to have the same secret key.

01c66eb6ef01.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
01c66eb6ef01.sentence: However, symmetric-key encryption algorithms are usually better for bulk encryption.

cfab54733b9f.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
cfab54733b9f.sentence: With the exception of the one-time pad they have a smaller key size, which means less storage space and faster transmission.

d87569e5d342.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
d87569e5d342.sentence: Due to this, asymmetric-key encryption is often used to exchange the secret key for symmetric-key encryption.

4a4ceb2c5ad4.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
4a4ceb2c5ad4.sentence: Nearly all modern cryptographic systems still use symmetric-key algorithms internally to encrypt the bulk of the messages, but they eliminate the need for a physically secure channel by using Diffie–Hellman key exchange or some other public-key protocol to securely come to agreement on a fresh new secret key for each session/conversation (forward secrecy).

dbf4e9d86e82.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
dbf4e9d86e82.sentence: All early cryptographic systems required either the sender or the recipient to somehow receive a copy of that secret key over a physically secure channel.

ae5886be4905.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
ae5886be4905.sentence: Symmetric-key encryption can use either stream ciphers or block ciphers.

4df0b571a76e.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
4df0b571a76e.sentence: Stream ciphers encrypt the digits (typically bytes), or letters (in substitution ciphers) of a message one at a time.

51bd2e60d148.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
51bd2e60d148.sentence: Block ciphers take a number of bits and encrypt them in a single unit, padding the plaintext to achieve a multiple of the block size.

c5dbad0a077c.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
c5dbad0a077c.sentence: The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm, approved by NIST in December 2001, uses 128-bit blocks.

71397afc4735.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
71397afc4735.sentence: Examples of popular symmetric-key algorithms include Twofish, Serpent, AES (Rijndael), Camellia, Salsa20, ChaCha20, Blowfish, CAST5, Kuznyechik, RC4, DES, 3DES, Skipjack, Safer, and IDEA.

23d1a44254df.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
23d1a44254df.sentence: Encrypting a message does not guarantee that it will remain unchanged while encrypted.

312f839a963e.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
312f839a963e.sentence: Hence, often a message authentication code is added to a ciphertext to ensure that changes to the ciphertext will be noted by the receiver.

54e9ad23899f.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
54e9ad23899f.sentence: Message authentication codes can be constructed from an AEAD cipher (e.g. AES-GCM).

17b82694ec0f.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
17b82694ec0f.sentence: Quantum computers would exponentially increase the speed at which these ciphers can be decoded; notably, Grover's algorithm would take the square-root of the time traditionally required for a brute-force attack, although these vulnerabilities can be compensated for by doubling key length.

c0d8beb20c5b.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
c0d8beb20c5b.sentence: By contrast, it would still take a quantum computer the same amount of time to decode a 256 bit AES cipher as it would a conventional computer to decode a 128 bit AES cipher.

1e07b88ef3e1.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
1e07b88ef3e1.sentence: For this reason, AES-256 is believed to be "quantum resistant".

e2fc51c4a8ef.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
e2fc51c4a8ef.sentence: When used with asymmetric ciphers for key transfer, pseudorandom key generators are nearly always used to generate the symmetric cipher session keys.

ccb989a40a78.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
ccb989a40a78.sentence: However, lack of randomness in those generators or in their initialization vectors is disastrous and has led to cryptanalytic breaks in the past.

00363ffd793e.title: Symmetric-key algorithm
00363ffd793e.sentence: Therefore, it is essential that an implementation use a source of high entropy for its initialization.

97364e35ad24.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
97364e35ad24.sentence: Diffie–Hellman (DH) key exchange is a mathematical method of securely generating a symmetric cryptographic key over a public channel.

6c2efba07a64.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
6c2efba07a64.sentence: By contrast, the Diffie–Hellman key exchange method allows two parties that have no prior knowledge of each other to jointly establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel.

486e157ec0be.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
486e157ec0be.sentence: This key can then be used to encrypt subsequent communications using a symmetric-key cipher.

4bfa5a1926be.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
4bfa5a1926be.sentence: Traditionally, secure encrypted communication between two parties required that they first exchange keys by some secure physical means, such as paper key lists transported by a trusted courier.

344e03f2d53a.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
344e03f2d53a.sentence: - Alice and Bob publicly agree to use a modulus p = 23 and base g = 5 (which is a primitive root modulo 23).

897eed586256.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
897eed586256.sentence: - Alice chooses a secret integer a = 4, then sends Bob A = ga mod p

acab540c10b0.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
acab540c10b0.sentence: - Bob chooses a secret integer b = 3, then sends Alice B = gb mod p

188003110adb.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
188003110adb.sentence: - Alice computes s = Ba mod p

1455a593c3d5.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
1455a593c3d5.sentence: - Bob computes s = Ab mod p

3f36c81859da.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
3f36c81859da.sentence: - Alice and Bob now share a secret (the number 18).

5da82c5d4b75.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
5da82c5d4b75.sentence: Only a and b are kept secret.

7b7fdcc68de1.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
7b7fdcc68de1.sentence: All the other values – p, g, ga mod p, and gb mod p – are sent in the clear.

79481a9dc8f4.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
79481a9dc8f4.sentence: The eavesdropper has to solve the Diffie–Hellman problem to obtain gab.

4954c509475a.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
4954c509475a.sentence: This is currently considered difficult for groups whose order is large enough.

2ce760b9a23d.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
2ce760b9a23d.sentence: The simplest and the original implementation, later formalized as Finite Field Diffie–Hellman in RFC 7919, of the protocol uses the multiplicative group of integers modulo p, where p is prime, and g is a primitive root modulo p. To guard against potential vulnerabilities, it is recommended to use prime numbers of at least 2048 bits in length.

f19f1a5a1078.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
f19f1a5a1078.sentence: Although Diffie–Hellman key exchange itself is a non-authenticated key-agreement protocol, it provides the basis for a variety of authenticated protocols, and is used to provide forward secrecy in Transport Layer Security's ephemeral modes (referred to as EDH or DHE depending on the cipher suite).

9c1c62a0c779.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
9c1c62a0c779.sentence: When Alice and Bob share a password, they may use a password-authenticated key agreement (PK) form of Diffie–Hellman to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

afb692477a16.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
afb692477a16.sentence: A pre-shared public key also prevents man-in-the-middle attacks.

a54a79b01694.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
a54a79b01694.sentence: Protocols that achieve forward secrecy generate new key pairs for each session and discard them at the end of the session.

b6f44c5cf6e7.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
b6f44c5cf6e7.sentence: The Diffie–Hellman key exchange is a frequent choice for such protocols, because of its fast key generation.

dac099326016.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
dac099326016.sentence: Forward secrecy results from the use of ephemeral keys: the private keys are discarded once key agreement is complete, making them safe from later compromise.

3a908e7d79d5.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
3a908e7d79d5.sentence: Ephemeral keys are practical because it is computationally cheap to create public-private key pairs suitable for use with Diffie-Hellman exchange.

108c456b49bf.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange

108c456b49bf.sentence: It turns out that much Internet traffic uses one of a handful of groups that are of order 1024 bits or less.

fb315323df65.sentence: By precomputing the first three steps of the number field sieve for the most common groups, an attacker need only carry out the last step, which is much less computationally expensive than the first three steps, to obtain a specific logarithm.

5d5234dc48fe.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
5d5234dc48fe.section: Security and practical considerations > Practical attacks on Internet traffic
5d5234dc48fe.sentence: The Logjam attack used this vulnerability to compromise a variety of Internet services that allowed the use of groups whose order was a 512-bit prime number, so called export grade.

98e52107a1f6.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange

98e52107a1f6.sentence: A CVE released in 2021 (CVE-2002-20001) disclosed a denial-of-service attack (DoS) against the protocol variants using ephemeral keys, called D(HE)at attack.

7174e2e6ef3c.section: Security and practical considerations > Denial-of-service attack
7174e2e6ef3c.sentence: The attack exploits that the Diffie–Hellman key exchange allows attackers to send arbitrary numbers that are actually not public keys, triggering expensive modular exponentiation calculations on the victim's side.

693139220d66.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange
693139220d66.section: Security and practical considerations > Security against quantum computers
693139220d66.sentence: Quantum computers can break public-key cryptographic schemes, such as RSA, finite-field DH and elliptic-curve DH key-exchange protocols, using Shor's algorithm for solving the factoring problem, the discrete logarithm problem, and the period-finding problem.

c78bfc4b0669.title: Diffie–Hellman key exchange

c78bfc4b0669.sentence: A post-quantum variant of Diffie-Hellman algorithm was proposed in 2023, and relies on a combination of the quantum-resistant CRYSTALS-Kyber protocol, as well as the old elliptic curve X25519 protocol.

d19050ea139b.sentence: Browsers other than Firefox generally use the operating system's facilities to decide which certificate authorities are trusted.

314bfeb06b4f.sentence: This is indicated with a set of trust bits in a root certificate storage system.

edae711ca98a.sentence: A public-key certificate is typically requested from a PKI using a CSR, which needs to be transferred using a secure certificate enrollment protocol such as CMP, EST, or ACME.

04f29fb7be61.sentence: The parties involved in the enrollment process must verify the authenticity, integrity, and authorization of the CSR, for which the certificate issuer bears the main responsibility.

fb7908aa4092.sentence: A self-signed certificate is a certificate with a subject that matches its issuer, and a signature that can be verified by its own public key.

99cbb73e8c9d.sentence: Internet-facing servers, such as public Web servers, must obtain their certificates from a trusted, public certificate authority (CA).

eb54bbb0b522.title: Certificate authority
eb54bbb0b522.sentence: In cryptography, a certificate authority or certification authority (CA) is an entity that stores, signs, and issues digital certificates.

e2e5c05137b2.title: Certificate authority
e2e5c05137b2.sentence: A CA acts as a trusted third party—trusted both by the subject (owner) of the certificate and by the party relying upon the certificate.

9accdd149799.title: Certificate authority
9accdd149799.sentence: If the CA can be subverted, then the security of the entire system is lost, potentially subverting all the entities that trust the compromised CA.

ed646839f815.title: Certificate authority
ed646839f815.sentence: A CA's obligation in such schemes is to verify an applicant's credentials, so that users and relying parties can trust the information in the issued certificate.

277098bbccff.title: Certificate authority
277098bbccff.sentence: The certificate is also a confirmation or validation by the CA that the public key contained in the certificate belongs to the person, organization, server or other entity noted in the certificate.

39d9134bcede.title: Certificate authority
39d9134bcede.sentence: Usually, client software—for example, browsers—include a set of trusted CA certificates.

5b59a841cf6d.title: Certificate authority
5b59a841cf6d.section: Implementation weakness of the trusted third party scheme
5b59a841cf6d.sentence: The critical weakness in the way that the current X.509 scheme is implemented is that any CA trusted by a particular party can then issue certificates for any domain they choose.

16f99694cd04.title: Certificate authority
16f99694cd04.section: Implementation weakness of the trusted third party scheme
16f99694cd04.sentence: Such certificates will be accepted as valid by the trusting party whether they are legitimate and authorized or not.

b4144ce7ce0b.title: Certificate authority

b4144ce7ce0b.sentence: As all major web browsers are distributed to their end-users pre-configured with a list of trusted CAs that numbers in the dozens this means that any one of these pre-approved trusted CAs can issue a valid certificate for any domain whatsoever.

60ba831a1c6e.title: Certificate authority
60ba831a1c6e.sentence: An attacker who steals a certificate authority's private keys is able to forge certificates as if they were CA, without needed ongoing access to the CA's systems.

8a3a91530111.title: Certificate authority
8a3a91530111.sentence: Key theft is therefore one of the main risks certificate authorities defend against.

66b58cdb5c9a.title: Certificate authority
66b58cdb5c9a.sentence: Publicly trusted CAs almost always store their keys on a hardware security module (HSM), which allows them to sign certificates with a key, but generally prevent extraction of that key with both physical and software controls.

03e75073a0bd.title: Certificate authority
03e75073a0bd.sentence: CAs typically take the further precaution of keeping the key for their long-term root certificates in an HSM that is kept offline, except when it is needed to sign shorter-lived intermediate certificates.

3293b644733e.title: Certificate authority
3293b644733e.sentence: The intermediate certificates, stored in an online HSM, can do the day-to-day work of signing end-entity certificates and keeping revocation information up to date.

031aede9d9d2.title: Certificate authority
031aede9d9d2.sentence: The CA/Browser Forum publishes the Baseline Requirements, a list of policies and technical requirements for CAs to follow.

201dfc6fbb3f.title: Certificate authority
201dfc6fbb3f.sentence: These are a requirement for inclusion in the certificate stores of Firefox and Safari.

181e7908dc64.title: Certificate authority
181e7908dc64.sentence: 1st July 2012 | 60 Months | v1.0 of the Baseline Requirements. §9.4

45b6a8b66d76.title: Man-in-the-middle attack
45b6a8b66d76.sentence: It has been widely superseded by Certificate Transparency (CT), which mandates that all TLS certificates be logged in publicly auditable records to detect fraudulent or unauthorized certificates in real time.

81059dd9185f.title: Man-in-the-middle attack
81059dd9185f.sentence: While HTTP Public Key Pinning (HPKP) was originally designed to prevent MITM attacks involving compromised certificate authorities, it has been deprecated by major browsers due to its high risk of accidental site bricking.

2cacf354c53d.title: Certificate authority
2cacf354c53d.sentence: Commercial CAs charge money to issue certificates, and their customers anticipate the CA's certificate to be contained within the majority of web browsers, so that safe connections to the certified servers work efficiently out-of-the-box.

dbb214ab199c.title: Certificate authority
dbb214ab199c.sentence: The quantity of web browsers, other devices, and applications which trust a particular certificate authority is referred to as ubiquity.

4ba79429c5cf.title: Certificate authority
4ba79429c5cf.sentence: In addition to commercial CAs, some non-profits issue publicly-trusted digital certificates without charge, for example Let's Encrypt.

8ed01ffcc936.title: Certificate authority
8ed01ffcc936.sentence: Some large cloud computing and web hosting companies are also publicly-trusted CAs and issue certificates to services hosted on their infrastructure, for example IBM Cloud, Amazon Web Services, Cloudflare, and Google Cloud Platform.

fd3096428711.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
fd3096428711.sentence: An encryption method is presented with the novel property that publicly revealing an encryption key does not thereby reveal the corresponding decryption key.

0725783ccbd1.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
0725783ccbd1.sentence: This has two important consequences: (1) Couriers or other secure means are not needed to transmit keys, since a message can be enciphered using an encryption key publicly revealed by the intented recipient.

7590bef42acd.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
7590bef42acd.sentence: (2) A message can be “signed” using a privately held decryption key.

da48b27ef794.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
da48b27ef794.sentence: Only he can decipher the message, since only he knows the corresponding decryption key.

578e8ae379a8.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
578e8ae379a8.sentence: Anyone can verify this signature using the corresponding publicly revealed encryption key.

581e87577629.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
581e87577629.sentence: Signatures cannot be forged, and a signer cannot later deny the validity of his signature.

bb2693032873.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
bb2693032873.sentence: A message is encrypted by representing it as a number M, raising M to a publicly specified power e, and then taking the remainder when the result is divided by the publicly specified product, n, of two large secret primer numbers p and q.

15c7eec7b102.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
15c7eec7b102.sentence: Decryption is similar; only a different, secret, power d is used, where e * d ≡ 1(mod (p - 1) * (q - 1)).

0c07c0915ea3.title: paper>10.1145/359340.359342
0c07c0915ea3.sentence: The security of the system rests in part on the difficulty of factoring the published divisor, n.

fecfe023d1e0.title: HTTP
fecfe023d1e0.sentence: HTTP provides a general framework for access control and authentication, via an extensible set of challenge–response authentication schemes, which can be used by a server to challenge a client request and by a client to provide authentication information.

1680fc15c038.title: rfc>9110
1680fc15c038.sentence: HTTP provides a general framework for access control and authentication, via an extensible set of challenge-response authentication schemes, which can be used by a server to challenge a client request and by a client to provide authentication information.

0cc59495fcd5.title: HTTP
0cc59495fcd5.sentence: HTTP provides multiple authentication schemes such as basic access authentication and digest access authentication which operate via a challenge–response mechanism whereby the server identifies and issues a challenge before serving the requested content.

960d1fc9ff03.title: rfc>9110
960d1fc9ff03.sentence: For example, the "basic" and "digest" authentication schemes are defined by and, respectively.

c2279f56e3f1.title: rfc>9110
c2279f56e3f1.sentence: New and existing authentication schemes are specified independently and ought to be registered within the "Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Authentication Scheme Registry".

cffa8b31c49b.title: rfc>9110
cffa8b31c49b.sentence: A 401 (Unauthorized) response message is used by an origin server to challenge the authorization of a user agent, including a WWW-Authenticate header field containing at least one challenge applicable to the requested resource.

5e953b27f52f.title: rfc>9110
5e953b27f52f.sentence: The server generating a 401 response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field (Section 11.6.1) containing at least one challenge applicable to the target resource.

c229b2d4afcd.title: rfc>9110
c229b2d4afcd.sentence: A user agent that wishes to authenticate itself with an origin server -- usually, but not necessarily, after receiving a 401 (Unauthorized) -- can do so by including an Authorization header field with the request.

4289a7b705fe.title: rfc>9110
4289a7b705fe.sentence: A server that receives valid credentials that are not adequate to gain access ought to respond with the 403 (Forbidden) status code (Section 15.5.4).

c4de51d60d9e.title: rfc>9110
c4de51d60d9e.section: 11. HTTP Authentication > 11.5. Establishing a Protection Space (Realm)
c4de51d60d9e.sentence: A "protection space" is defined by the origin (see Section 4.3.1) of the server being accessed, in combination with the realm value if present.

a497d3da8f51.title: rfc>9110
a497d3da8f51.section: 11. HTTP Authentication > 11.5. Establishing a Protection Space (Realm)
a497d3da8f51.sentence: These realms allow the protected resources on a server to be partitioned into a set of protection spaces, each with its own authentication scheme and/or authorization database.

1269910bed18.title: rfc>9110
1269910bed18.section: 11. HTTP Authentication > 11.5. Establishing a Protection Space (Realm)
1269910bed18.sentence: The protection space determines the domain over which credentials can be automatically applied.

a801658dfda4.title: rfc>9110
a801658dfda4.section: 11. HTTP Authentication > 11.5. Establishing a Protection Space (Realm)
a801658dfda4.sentence: If a prior request has been authorized, the user agent MAY reuse the same credentials for all other requests within that protection space for a period of time determined by the authentication scheme, parameters, and/or user preferences (such as a configurable inactivity timeout).

d1b84cedc3e0.title: HTTP
d1b84cedc3e0.sentence: The HTTP authentication specification includes realms that provide an arbitrary, implementation-specific construct for further dividing resources common to a given root URI.

4172ba065853.title: HTTP
4172ba065853.sentence: This in effect allows the server to define separate authentication scopes under one root URI.

ccaef563fbc3.title: rfc>9110
ccaef563fbc3.sentence: The 4xx (Client Error) class of status code indicates that the client seems to have erred.

ae1ff0076781.title: rfc>9110
ae1ff0076781.sentence: Except when responding to a HEAD request, the server SHOULD send a representation containing an explanation of the error situation, and whether it is a temporary or permanent condition.

b81441af9109.title: rfc>9110
b81441af9109.sentence: These status codes are applicable to any request method.

86e1268167eb.title: rfc>9110
86e1268167eb.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.1. 400 Bad Request
86e1268167eb.sentence: The 400 (Bad Request) status code indicates that the server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing, or deceptive request routing).

fed277e717f1.title: rfc>9110
fed277e717f1.sentence: The 401 (Unauthorized) status code indicates that the request has not been applied because it lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource.

0410a7ad223e.title: rfc>9110
0410a7ad223e.sentence: The 403 (Forbidden) status code indicates that the server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it.

2ffcfe70bf24.title: rfc>9110
2ffcfe70bf24.sentence: If authentication credentials were provided in the request, the server considers them insufficient to grant access.

4e97e9fd3c11.title: rfc>9110
4e97e9fd3c11.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.5. 404 Not Found
4e97e9fd3c11.sentence: The 404 (Not Found) status code indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists.

408598a35b64.title: rfc>9110
408598a35b64.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.5. 404 Not Found
408598a35b64.sentence: A 404 status code does not indicate whether this lack of representation is temporary or permanent; the 410 (Gone) status code is preferred over 404 if the origin server knows, presumably through some configurable means, that the condition is likely to be permanent.

2b838d564646.title: rfc>9110
2b838d564646.sentence: The 410 (Gone) status code indicates that access to the target resource is no longer available at the origin server and that this condition is likely to be permanent.

96e601a811d4.title: rfc>9110
96e601a811d4.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.6. 405 Method Not Allowed
96e601a811d4.sentence: The 405 (Method Not Allowed) status code indicates that the method received in the request-line is known by the origin server but not supported by the target resource.

68de362cfe22.title: rfc>9110
68de362cfe22.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.6. 405 Method Not Allowed
68de362cfe22.sentence: The origin server MUST generate an Allow header field in a 405 response containing a list of the target resource's currently supported methods.

56e09178b006.title: rfc>9110
56e09178b006.sentence: The 409 (Conflict) status code indicates that the request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource.

67d9f2b55608.title: rfc>9110
67d9f2b55608.sentence: This code is used in situations where the user might be able to resolve the conflict and resubmit the request.

acc01eb7a35c.title: rfc>9110
acc01eb7a35c.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.13. 412 Precondition Failed
acc01eb7a35c.sentence: The 412 (Precondition Failed) status code indicates that one or more conditions given in the request header fields evaluated to false when tested on the server (Section 13).

e1c91b26620d.title: rfc>9110
e1c91b26620d.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.13. 412 Precondition Failed
e1c91b26620d.sentence: This response status code allows the client to place preconditions on the current resource state (its current representations and metadata) and, thus, prevent the request method from being applied if the target resource is in an unexpected state.

4fc9ca8ab339.title: rfc>9110
4fc9ca8ab339.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.14. 413 Content Too Large
