618908219205.sentence: Because this mechanism does not require storing all outstanding tickets, it may be easier to implement in distributed systems with high rates of resumption and 0-RTT, at the cost of potentially weaker anti-replay defense because of the difficulty of reliably storing and retrieving the received ClientHello messages.

7b61c3eec455.title: rfc>8446
7b61c3eec455.sentence: In this case, the best anti-replay protection is provided by having a single storage zone be authoritative for a given ticket and refusing 0-RTT for that ticket in any other zone.

e96829e1f3e0.title: rfc>8446
e96829e1f3e0.sentence: Because the ClientHello indicates the time at which the client sent it, it is possible to efficiently determine whether a ClientHello was likely sent reasonably recently and only accept 0-RTT for such a ClientHello, otherwise falling back to a 1-RTT handshake.

ef419ef04e61.title: rfc>8446
ef419ef04e61.sentence: In order to implement this mechanism, a server needs to store the time that the server generated the session ticket, offset by an estimate of the round-trip time between client and server.

71da9ca49f65.title: rfc>8446
71da9ca49f65.sentence: The server can determine the client's view of the age of the ticket by subtracting the ticket's "ticket_age_add" value from the "obfuscated_ticket_age" parameter in the client's "pre_shared_key" extension.

33d197bded32.title: rfc>8446
33d197bded32.sentence: When a new ClientHello is received, the expected_arrival_time is then compared against the current server wall clock time and if they differ by more than a certain amount, 0-RTT is rejected, though the 1-RTT handshake can be allowed to complete.

02159239dc2e.title: rfc>9110
02159239dc2e.sentence: A conditional request is an HTTP request with one or more request header fields that indicate a precondition to be tested before applying the request method to the target resource.

f3e39f8fbe30.title: rfc>9110
f3e39f8fbe30.sentence: Conditional GET requests are the most efficient mechanism for HTTP cache updates.

63e495802c92.title: rfc>9110
63e495802c92.sentence: Conditionals can also be applied to state-changing methods, such as PUT and DELETE, to prevent the "lost update" problem: one client accidentally overwriting the work of another client that has been acting in parallel.

772381f19132.title: rfc>9110
772381f19132.sentence: Each precondition defined below consists of a comparison between a set of validators obtained from prior representations of the target resource to the current state of validators for the selected representation (Section 8.8).

1e1f801d2e2e.title: rfc>9110
1e1f801d2e2e.sentence: Hence, these preconditions evaluate whether the state of the target resource has changed since a given state known by the client.

2bed032fdd86.title: HTTP
2bed032fdd86.section: Technology > Data exchange > Content retrieval optimizations
2bed032fdd86.sentence: HTTP/1.0 added headers to manage resources cached by a client in order to allow conditional GET requests.

dbae23149491.title: HTTP
dbae23149491.section: Technology > Data exchange > Content retrieval optimizations
dbae23149491.sentence: - A server must return the entire content of the requested resource only if its last modified time is not known by the client or if it changed since the last full response to a GET request.

ba7eb8e8bfdd.title: rfc>9110
ba7eb8e8bfdd.sentence: If-None-Match is primarily used in conditional GET requests to enable efficient updates of cached information with a minimum amount of transaction overhead.

48fa639791d4.title: rfc>9110
48fa639791d4.sentence: When a client desires to update one or more stored responses that have entity tags, the client SHOULD generate an If-None-Match header field containing a list of those entity tags when making a GET request; this allows recipient servers to send a 304 (Not Modified) response to indicate when one of those stored responses matches the selected representation.

6cc45e54fbad.title: rfc>9110
6cc45e54fbad.sentence: An origin server that evaluates an If-None-Match condition MUST NOT perform the requested method if the condition evaluates to false; instead, the origin server MUST respond with either a) the 304 (Not Modified) status code if the request method is GET or HEAD or b) the 412 (Precondition Failed) status code for all other request methods.

74a6846426a4.title: rfc>9110
74a6846426a4.sentence: The "If-Modified-Since" header field makes a GET or HEAD request method conditional on the selected representation's modification date being more recent than the date provided in the field value.

458d24814102.title: rfc>9110
458d24814102.sentence: Transfer of the selected representation's data is avoided if that data has not changed.

087bdf3a1ed1.title: rfc>9110
087bdf3a1ed1.sentence: A recipient MUST ignore If-Modified-Since if the request contains an If-None-Match header field; the condition in If-None-Match is considered to be a more accurate replacement for the condition in If-Modified-Since, and the two are only combined for the sake of interoperating with older intermediaries that might not implement If-None-Match.

b0c0869d4065.title: rfc>9110
b0c0869d4065.sentence: When used for cache updates, a cache will typically use the value of the cached message's Last-Modified header field to generate the field value of If-Modified-Since.

a2b039b3e1d2.title: rfc>9110
a2b039b3e1d2.sentence: The "If-Match" header field makes the request method conditional on the recipient origin server either having at least one current representation of the target resource, when the field value is "*", or having a current representation of the target resource that has an entity tag matching a member of the list of entity tags provided in the field value.

75ad7b74b30a.title: rfc>9110
75ad7b74b30a.sentence: An origin server MUST use the strong comparison function when comparing entity tags for If-Match (Section 8.8.3.2), since the client intends this precondition to prevent the method from being applied if there have been any changes to the representation data.

52fe1e884662.title: rfc>9110
52fe1e884662.sentence: If-Match is most often used with state-changing methods (e.g., POST, PUT, DELETE) to prevent accidental overwrites when multiple user agents might be acting in parallel on the same resource (i.e., to prevent the "lost update" problem).

caac178c7ede.title: rfc>9110
caac178c7ede.sentence: Instead, the origin server MAY indicate that the conditional request failed by responding with a 412 (Precondition Failed) status code.

e5c39fdcdbed.title: rfc>9110
e5c39fdcdbed.sentence: An origin server that evaluates an If-Match condition MUST NOT perform the requested method if the condition evaluates to false.

9578b37a1cdc.title: rfc>9110
9578b37a1cdc.sentence: If-None-Match can also be used with a value of "*" to prevent an unsafe request method (e.g., PUT) from inadvertently modifying an existing representation of the target resource when the client believes that the resource does not have a current representation (Section 9.2.1).

c73bb1165fb6.title: rfc>9110
c73bb1165fb6.sentence: This is a variation on the "lost update" problem that might arise if more than one client attempts to create an initial representation for the target resource.

57fe8698c0dc.title: rfc>9110
57fe8698c0dc.section: 13. Conditional Requests > 13.2. Evaluation of Preconditions > 13.2.2. Precedence of Preconditions
57fe8698c0dc.sentence: A recipient cache or origin server MUST evaluate the request preconditions defined by this specification in the following order:

d8816e1875ce.title: rfc>9110
d8816e1875ce.section: 13. Conditional Requests > 13.2. Evaluation of Preconditions > 13.2.2. Precedence of Preconditions
d8816e1875ce.sentence: - When recipient is the origin server and If-Match is present, evaluate the If-Match precondition:

b224d31b2ada.title: rfc>9110
b224d31b2ada.section: 13. Conditional Requests > 13.2. Evaluation of Preconditions > 13.2.2. Precedence of Preconditions
b224d31b2ada.sentence: - When recipient is the origin server, If-Match is not present, and If-Unmodified-Since is present, evaluate the If-Unmodified-Since precondition:

52323071e476.title: rfc>9110
52323071e476.section: 13. Conditional Requests > 13.2. Evaluation of Preconditions > 13.2.2. Precedence of Preconditions
52323071e476.sentence: - When If-None-Match is present, evaluate the If-None-Match precondition:

747ec4853d38.title: rfc>9110
747ec4853d38.section: 13. Conditional Requests > 13.2. Evaluation of Preconditions > 13.2.2. Precedence of Preconditions
747ec4853d38.sentence: - When the method is GET or HEAD, If-None-Match is not present, and If-Modified-Since is present, evaluate the If-Modified-Since precondition:

954b577d273d.title: rfc>9110
954b577d273d.section: 13. Conditional Requests > 13.2. Evaluation of Preconditions > 13.2.2. Precedence of Preconditions
954b577d273d.sentence: - When the method is GET and both Range and If-Range are present, evaluate the If-Range precondition:

cc7cbf9da3e7.title: rfc>9110
cc7cbf9da3e7.sentence: The "Range" header field on a GET request modifies the method semantics to request transfer of only one or more subranges of the selected representation data (Section 8.1), rather than the entire selected representation.

1668ec9fedcd.title: rfc>9110
1668ec9fedcd.sentence: When a client has stored a partial representation, it is desirable to request the remainder of that representation in a subsequent request rather than transfer the entire representation.

46bfacd35dd2.title: rfc>9110
46bfacd35dd2.sentence: Clients often encounter interrupted data transfers as a result of canceled requests or dropped connections.

d2d7bb72bda0.title: rfc>9110
d2d7bb72bda0.sentence: Likewise, devices with limited local storage might benefit from being able to request only a subset of a larger representation, such as a single page of a very large document, or the dimensions of an embedded image.

143ee0d75b51.title: HTTP
143ee0d75b51.section: Technology > Data exchange > Content retrieval optimizations
143ee0d75b51.sentence: - Byte range serving allows a client to request portions (ranges of bytes) of a resource.

51ec53ba64ae.title: HTTP
51ec53ba64ae.section: Technology > Data exchange > Content retrieval optimizations
51ec53ba64ae.sentence: This is useful to resume an interrupted download (when a file is very large), when only a part of a content has to be shown or dynamically added to the already visible part by a browser (i.e. only the first or the following n comments of a web page) in order to spare time, bandwidth and system resources, etc.

f13d42142849.title: rfc>9110
f13d42142849.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.3. Successful 2xx > 15.3.7. 206 Partial Content > 15.3.7.1. Single Part
f13d42142849.sentence: If a single part is being transferred, the server generating the 206 response MUST generate a Content-Range header field, describing what range of the selected representation is enclosed, and a content consisting of the range.

a276c4892486.title: rfc>9110
a276c4892486.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.3. Successful 2xx > 15.3.7. 206 Partial Content > 15.3.7.2. Multiple Parts
a276c4892486.sentence: If multiple parts are being transferred, the server generating the 206 response MUST generate "multipart/byteranges" content, as defined in Section 14.6, and a Content-Type header field containing the "multipart/byteranges" media type and its required boundary parameter.

fa451c12a361.title: rfc>9110
fa451c12a361.section: 15. Status Codes > 15.5. Client Error 4xx > 15.5.17. 416 Range Not Satisfiable
fa451c12a361.sentence: The 416 (Range Not Satisfiable) status code indicates that the set of ranges in the request's Range header field (Section 14.2) has been rejected either because none of the requested ranges are satisfiable or because the client has requested an excessive number of small or overlapping ranges (a potential denial of service attack).

64a7499ff434.title: rfc>9110
64a7499ff434.sentence: The "Accept-Ranges" field in a response indicates whether an upstream server supports range requests for the target resource.

929b209b7873.title: rfc>9110
929b209b7873.sentence: A client MAY generate range requests regardless of having received an Accept-Ranges field.

9f09e6b3386b.title: rfc>9110
9f09e6b3386b.sentence: Conversely, a client MUST NOT assume that receiving an Accept-Ranges field means that future range requests will return partial responses.

b654cb6345b7.title: rfc>9110
b654cb6345b7.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields
b654cb6345b7.sentence: Resource metadata is referred to as a "validator" if it can be used within a precondition (Section 13.1) to make a conditional request (Section 13).

b9f7b15b0658.title: rfc>9110
b9f7b15b0658.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields
b9f7b15b0658.sentence: This specification defines two forms of metadata that are commonly used to observe resource state and test for preconditions: modification dates (Section 8.8.2) and opaque entity tags (Section 8.8.3).

29bf75969b3a.title: rfc>9110
29bf75969b3a.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.3. ETag
29bf75969b3a.sentence: The "ETag" field in a response provides the current entity tag for the selected representation, as determined at the conclusion of handling the request.

f6b7dd07d018.title: rfc>9110
f6b7dd07d018.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.3. ETag
f6b7dd07d018.sentence: An entity tag is an opaque validator for differentiating between multiple representations of the same resource, regardless of whether those multiple representations are due to resource state changes over time, content negotiation resulting in multiple representations being valid at the same time, or both.

48c844ff3e03.title: rfc>9110
48c844ff3e03.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.3. ETag
48c844ff3e03.sentence: An entity tag consists of an opaque quoted string, possibly prefixed by a weakness indicator.

d9b6293d5bc6.title: rfc>9110
d9b6293d5bc6.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.3. ETag
d9b6293d5bc6.sentence: An entity tag can be more reliable for validation than a modification date in situations where it is inconvenient to store modification dates, where the one-second resolution of HTTP-date values is not sufficient, or where modification dates are not consistently maintained.

47c17258a9c3.title: rfc>9110
47c17258a9c3.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.1. Weak versus Strong
47c17258a9c3.sentence: A "strong validator" is representation metadata that changes value whenever a change occurs to the representation data that would be observable in the content of a 200 (OK) response to GET.

e00a0e1a3c35.title: rfc>9110
e00a0e1a3c35.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.1. Weak versus Strong
e00a0e1a3c35.sentence: A strong validator is unique across all versions of all representations associated with a particular resource over time.

f0e0b12133ad.title: rfc>9110
f0e0b12133ad.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.1. Weak versus Strong
f0e0b12133ad.sentence: Weak validators are easy to generate but are far less useful for comparisons.

c28ac96018b7.title: rfc>9110
c28ac96018b7.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.1. Weak versus Strong
c28ac96018b7.sentence: Strong validators are ideal for comparisons but can be very difficult (and occasionally impossible) to generate efficiently.

29c8a9606017.title: rfc>9110
29c8a9606017.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields > 8.8.3. ETag
29c8a9606017.sentence: An entity tag can be either a weak or strong validator, with strong being the default.

5b51d0cab905.title: rfc>9110
5b51d0cab905.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields
5b51d0cab905.sentence: In a successful response to a state-changing request, validator fields describe the new representation that has replaced the prior selected representation as a result of processing the request.

642c1f835fe2.title: rfc>9110
642c1f835fe2.section: 8. Representation Data and Metadata > 8.8. Validator Fields
642c1f835fe2.sentence: For example, an ETag field in a 201 (Created) response communicates the entity tag of the newly created resource's representation, so that the entity tag can be used as a validator in later conditional requests to prevent the "lost update" problem.

3ae837023b08.title: rfc>9111
3ae837023b08.sentence: When a cache has one or more stored responses for a requested URI, but cannot serve any of them (e.g., because they are not fresh, or one cannot be chosen; see Section 4.1), it can use the conditional request mechanism (Section 13 of ) in the forwarded request to give the next inbound server an opportunity to choose a valid stored response to use, updating the stored metadata in the process, or to replace the stored response(s) with a new response.

77ea93edb53a.title: rfc>9111
77ea93edb53a.sentence: This process is known as "validating" or "revalidating" the stored response.

9a0423fbc145.title: rfc>9111
9a0423fbc145.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.1. Sending a Validation Request
9a0423fbc145.sentence: When generating a conditional request for validation, a cache either starts with a request it is attempting to satisfy or -- if it is initiating the request independently -- synthesizes a request using a stored response by copying the method, target URI, and request header fields identified by the Vary header field (Section 4.1).

4254d5e4b977.title: rfc>9111
4254d5e4b977.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.1. Sending a Validation Request
4254d5e4b977.sentence: These contain validator metadata sourced from a stored response(s) that has the same URI.

49bab0b76fc0.title: rfc>9111
49bab0b76fc0.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.1. Sending a Validation Request
49bab0b76fc0.sentence: One such validator is the timestamp given in a Last-Modified header field (Section 8.8.2 of ), which can be used in an If-Modified-Since header field for response validation, or in an If-Unmodified-Since or If-Range header field for representation selection (i.e., the client is referring specifically to a previously obtained representation with that timestamp).

2c41595380c8.title: rfc>9111
2c41595380c8.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.1. Sending a Validation Request
2c41595380c8.sentence: Another validator is the entity tag given in an ETag field (Section 8.8.3 of ).

e83a6de2ace4.title: rfc>9111
e83a6de2ace4.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.1. Sending a Validation Request
e83a6de2ace4.sentence: One or more entity tags, indicating one or more stored responses, can be used in an If-None-Match header field for response validation, or in an If-Match or If-Range header field for representation selection (i.e., the client is referring specifically to one or more previously obtained representations with the listed entity tags).

95bf706f57d3.title: rfc>9111
95bf706f57d3.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.1. Sending a Validation Request
95bf706f57d3.sentence: - MUST send the relevant entity tags (using If-Match, If-None-Match, or If-Range) if the entity tags were provided in the stored response(s) being validated.

723b85e5ff43.title: rfc>9111
723b85e5ff43.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.1. Sending a Validation Request
723b85e5ff43.sentence: - SHOULD send the Last-Modified value (using If-Modified-Since) if the request is not for a subrange, a single stored response is being validated, and that response contains a Last-Modified value.

14de0c811ae4.title: rfc>9111
14de0c811ae4.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.3. Handling a Validation Response
14de0c811ae4.sentence: - A 304 (Not Modified) response status code indicates that the stored response can be updated and reused; see Section 4.3.4.

6657767a9095.title: rfc>9111
6657767a9095.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.4. Freshening Stored Responses upon Validation
6657767a9095.sentence: When a cache receives a 304 (Not Modified) response, it needs to identify stored responses that are suitable for updating with the new information provided, and then do so.

8a5161f7c629.title: rfc>9111
8a5161f7c629.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.3. Handling a Validation Response
8a5161f7c629.sentence: - A full response (i.e., one containing content) indicates that none of the stored responses nominated in the conditional request are suitable.

b426758d8940.title: rfc>9111
b426758d8940.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.3. Handling a Validation Response
b426758d8940.sentence: Instead, the cache MUST use the full response to satisfy the request.

7b6e1b5a194c.title: rfc>9111
7b6e1b5a194c.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.3. Handling a Validation Response
7b6e1b5a194c.sentence: The cache MAY store such a full response, subject to its constraints (see Section 3).

0a6c10ac7c06.title: rfc>9111
0a6c10ac7c06.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.3. Handling a Validation Response
0a6c10ac7c06.sentence: - However, if a cache receives a 5xx (Server Error) response while attempting to validate a response, it can either forward this response to the requesting client or act as if the server failed to respond.

b87ad36d8917.title: rfc>9111
b87ad36d8917.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.3. Handling a Validation Response
b87ad36d8917.sentence: In the latter case, the cache can send a previously stored response, subject to its constraints on doing so (see Section 4.2.4), or retry the validation request.

949bc69241f5.title: rfc>9111
949bc69241f5.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.4. Freshening Stored Responses upon Validation
949bc69241f5.sentence: - If the new response contains one or more "strong validators" (see Section 8.8.1 of ), then each of those strong validators identifies a selected representation for update.

f1a7664ec430.title: rfc>9111
f1a7664ec430.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.4. Freshening Stored Responses upon Validation
f1a7664ec430.sentence: - If the new response contains no strong validators but does contain one or more "weak validators", and those validators correspond to one of the initial set's stored responses, then the most recent of those matching stored responses is identified for update.

5f926df29caf.title: rfc>9111
5f926df29caf.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.4. Freshening Stored Responses upon Validation
5f926df29caf.sentence: For each stored response identified, the cache MUST update its header fields with the header fields provided in the 304 (Not Modified) response, as per Section 3.2.

36fbb2840348.title: rfc>9111
36fbb2840348.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.5. Freshening Responses with HEAD
36fbb2840348.sentence: This property of HEAD responses can be used to invalidate or update a cached GET response if the more efficient conditional GET request mechanism is not available (due to no validators being present in the stored response) or if transmission of the content is not desired even if it has changed.

624e82ae896a.title: rfc>9111
624e82ae896a.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.5. Freshening Responses with HEAD
624e82ae896a.sentence: When a cache makes an inbound HEAD request for a target URI and receives a 200 (OK) response, the cache SHOULD update or invalidate each of its stored GET responses that could have been chosen for that request (see Section 4.1).

582a61c8efc2.title: rfc>9111
582a61c8efc2.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.2. Handling a Received Validation Request
582a61c8efc2.sentence: Each client in the request chain may have its own cache, so it is common for a cache at an intermediary to receive conditional requests from other (outbound) caches.

01c763d51767.title: rfc>9111
01c763d51767.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.3. Validation > 4.3.2. Handling a Received Validation Request
01c763d51767.sentence: In summary, the If-Match and If-Unmodified-Since conditional header fields are not applicable to a cache, and If-None-Match takes precedence over If-Modified-Since.

e10d204f5fee.title: rfc>9111
e10d204f5fee.sentence: This section defines cache response directives.

636e670048fc.title: rfc>9111
636e670048fc.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.1. max-age
636e670048fc.sentence: The max-age response directive indicates that the response is to be considered stale after its age is greater than the specified number of seconds.

2a9ad813e411.title: rfc>9111
2a9ad813e411.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.10. s-maxage
2a9ad813e411.sentence: The s-maxage directive incorporates the semantics of the proxy-revalidate response directive (Section 5.2.2.8) for a shared cache.

303a47e48495.title: rfc>9111
303a47e48495.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.4. no-cache
303a47e48495.sentence: The no-cache response directive, in its unqualified form (without an argument), indicates that the response MUST NOT be used to satisfy any other request without forwarding it for validation and receiving a successful response; see Section 4.3.

1efb1d2a4721.title: rfc>9111
1efb1d2a4721.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.4. no-cache
1efb1d2a4721.sentence: This allows an origin server to prevent a cache from using the response to satisfy a request without contacting it, even by caches that have been configured to send stale responses.

db56bb6581bd.title: rfc>9111
db56bb6581bd.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.5. no-store
db56bb6581bd.sentence: The no-store response directive indicates that a cache MUST NOT store any part of either the immediate request or the response and MUST NOT use the response to satisfy any other request.

7b7dda40bfe7.title: rfc>9111
7b7dda40bfe7.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.1. Request Directives > 5.2.1.5. no-store
7b7dda40bfe7.sentence: This directive is not a reliable or sufficient mechanism for ensuring privacy.

0a0be1ba7375.title: rfc>9111
0a0be1ba7375.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.1. Request Directives > 5.2.1.5. no-store
0a0be1ba7375.sentence: In particular, malicious or compromised caches might not recognize or obey this directive, and communications networks might be vulnerable to eavesdropping.

061bc45595a8.title: rfc>9111
061bc45595a8.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.7. private
061bc45595a8.sentence: | *Note:* This usage of the word "private" only controls where | the response can be stored; it cannot ensure the privacy of the | message content. Also, the qualified form of the directive is | often handled by caches as if an unqualified private directive | was received; that is, the special handling for the qualified | form is not widely implemented.

384497332044.title: rfc>9111
384497332044.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.9. public
384497332044.sentence: The public response directive indicates that a cache MAY store the response even if it would otherwise be prohibited, subject to the constraints defined in Section 3.

c5ca3e770e8c.title: rfc>9111
c5ca3e770e8c.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.9. public
c5ca3e770e8c.sentence: In other words, public explicitly marks the response as cacheable.

4b6f28e5238b.title: rfc>9111
4b6f28e5238b.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.9. public
4b6f28e5238b.sentence: For example, public permits a shared cache to reuse a response to a request containing an Authorization header field (Section 3.5).

7f2d409f5278.title: rfc>9111
7f2d409f5278.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.9. public
7f2d409f5278.sentence: Note that it is unnecessary to add the public directive to a response that is already cacheable according to Section 3.

edd647072999.title: rfc>9111
edd647072999.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.2. must-revalidate
edd647072999.sentence: The must-revalidate response directive indicates that once the response has become stale, a cache MUST NOT reuse that response to satisfy another request until it has been successfully validated by the origin, as defined by Section 4.3.

5e3cbb293139.title: rfc>9111
5e3cbb293139.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.2. must-revalidate
5e3cbb293139.sentence: In all circumstances, a cache MUST NOT ignore the must-revalidate directive; in particular, if a cache is disconnected, the cache MUST generate an error response rather than reuse the stale response.

bbe9eec963ff.title: rfc>9111
bbe9eec963ff.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.2. must-revalidate
bbe9eec963ff.sentence: The generated status code SHOULD be 504 (Gateway Timeout) unless another error status code is more applicable.

c8d5547c11b1.title: rfc>9111
c8d5547c11b1.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.2. must-revalidate
c8d5547c11b1.sentence: The must-revalidate directive ought to be used by servers if and only if failure to validate a request could cause incorrect operation, such as a silently unexecuted financial transaction.

1622ce9c2d1a.title: rfc>9111
1622ce9c2d1a.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.8. proxy-revalidate
1622ce9c2d1a.sentence: The proxy-revalidate response directive indicates that once the response has become stale, a shared cache MUST NOT reuse that response to satisfy another request until it has been successfully validated by the origin, as defined by Section 4.3.

0e858b4162ec.title: rfc>9111
0e858b4162ec.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.8. proxy-revalidate
0e858b4162ec.sentence: This is analogous to must-revalidate (Section 5.2.2.2), except that proxy-revalidate does not apply to private caches.

f0eed6fcebd3.title: rfc>9111
f0eed6fcebd3.section: 5. Field Definitions > 5.2. Cache-Control > 5.2.2. Response Directives > 5.2.2.6. no-transform
f0eed6fcebd3.sentence: The no-transform response directive indicates that an intermediary (regardless of whether it implements a cache) MUST NOT transform the content, as defined in Section 7.7 of.

f1df885d567e.title: rfc>9111
f1df885d567e.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
f1df885d567e.sentence: "Invalidate" means that the cache will either remove all stored responses whose target URI matches the given URI or mark them as "invalid" and in need of a mandatory validation before they can be sent in response to a subsequent request.

7741f8bd3fbb.title: rfc>9111
7741f8bd3fbb.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
7741f8bd3fbb.sentence: Because unsafe request methods (Section 9.2.1 of ) such as PUT, POST, or DELETE have the potential for changing state on the origin server, intervening caches are required to invalidate stored responses to keep their contents up to date.

2bc5752ad10f.title: rfc>9111
2bc5752ad10f.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
2bc5752ad10f.sentence: A cache MUST invalidate the target URI (Section 7.1 of ) when it receives a non-error status code in response to an unsafe request method (including methods whose safety is unknown).

4c37d4f5ec58.title: rfc>9111
4c37d4f5ec58.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
4c37d4f5ec58.sentence: A "non-error response" is one with a 2xx (Successful) or 3xx (Redirection) status code.

1e55bd0a80e4.title: rfc>9111
1e55bd0a80e4.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
1e55bd0a80e4.sentence: A cache MAY invalidate other URIs when it receives a non-error status code in response to an unsafe request method (including methods whose safety is unknown).

9c8c7aa248b9.title: rfc>9111
9c8c7aa248b9.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
9c8c7aa248b9.sentence: In particular, the URI(s) in the Location and Content-Location response header fields (if present) are candidates for invalidation; other URIs might be discovered through mechanisms not specified in this document.

26e36ba22a61.title: rfc>9111
26e36ba22a61.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
26e36ba22a61.sentence: However, a cache MUST NOT trigger an invalidation under these conditions if the origin (Section 4.3.1 of ) of the URI to be invalidated differs from that of the target URI (Section 7.1 of ).

2b63e61766ed.title: rfc>9111
2b63e61766ed.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses

1b0b587f37c8.title: rfc>9111
1b0b587f37c8.section: 4. Constructing Responses from Caches > 4.4. Invalidating Stored Responses
1b0b587f37c8.sentence: Note that this does not guarantee that all appropriate responses are invalidated globally; a state-changing request would only invalidate responses in the caches it travels through.

6725ae743017.title: rfc>9111
6725ae743017.sentence: A cache MUST NOT store a response to a request unless:

785a95ff8195.title: rfc>9111
785a95ff8195.sentence: When presented with a request, a cache MUST NOT reuse a stored response unless:

593f8c07a0d1.title: rfc>9111
593f8c07a0d1.sentence: - the request method is understood by the cache;

af7652ef524b.title: rfc>9111
af7652ef524b.sentence: - the response status code is final (see Section 15 of );

5689a7354512.title: rfc>9111
5689a7354512.sentence: - the no-store cache directive is not present in the response (see Section 5.2.2.5);

6595e2bca6c6.title: rfc>9111
6595e2bca6c6.sentence: - if the cache is shared: the private response directive is either not present or allows a shared cache to store a modified response; see Section 5.2.2.7);

dea781ea7106.title: rfc>9111
dea781ea7106.sentence: - the presented target URI (Section 7.1 of ) and that of the stored response match, and

6fb54b25c7c2.title: rfc>9111
6fb54b25c7c2.sentence: - the request method associated with the stored response allows it to be used for the presented request, and

1ab8be3061fc.title: rfc>9111
1ab8be3061fc.sentence: - request header fields nominated by the stored response (if any) match those presented (see Section 4.1), and

c2cead11714f.title: rfc>9111
c2cead11714f.sentence: - the stored response does not contain the no-cache directive (Section 5.2.2.4), unless it is successfully validated (Section 4.3), and

be8970672acd.title: rfc>9111
be8970672acd.sentence: - the stored response is one of the following:

153d32cf0303.title: rfc>9111
153d32cf0303.sentence: - allowed to be served stale (see Section 4.2.4), or

9a3c75cd08ae.title: rfc>9111
9a3c75cd08ae.section: 3. Storing Responses in Caches > 3.5. Storing Responses to Authenticated Requests
9a3c75cd08ae.sentence: In this specification, the following response directives have such an effect: must-revalidate (Section 5.2.2.2), public (Section 5.2.2.9), and s-maxage (Section 5.2.2.10).

60284d7bd53a.title: Hash function
60284d7bd53a.sentence: A hash function is any function that can be used to map data of arbitrary size to fixed-size values, though there are some hash functions that support variable-length output.

413b30991e22.title: Hash function
413b30991e22.sentence: The values returned by a hash function are called hash values, hash codes, (hash/message) digests, or simply hashes.

b205e60e091c.title: Hash function
b205e60e091c.sentence: The values are usually used to index a fixed-size table called a hash table.

6fa2b401a72e.title: Hash function
6fa2b401a72e.sentence: Hash functions and their associated hash tables are used in data storage and retrieval applications to access data in a small and nearly constant time per retrieval.

4327e6d62e72.title: Hash function
4327e6d62e72.sentence: They require an amount of storage space only fractionally greater than the total space required for the data or records themselves.

88cd7dd78980.title: Hash function
88cd7dd78980.sentence: Unlike lists or trees, it provides near-constant access time.

ad5d66d3e12d.title: Hash function
ad5d66d3e12d.sentence: It also uses much less storage than trying to store all possible keys directly, especially when keys are large or variable in length.

32ce33f5c2b5.title: Hash function
32ce33f5c2b5.sentence: A hash function may be considered to perform three functions:

16285f0c4b54.title: Hash function
16285f0c4b54.sentence: - Convert variable-length keys into fixed-length (usually machine-word-length or less) values, by folding them by words or other units using a parity-preserving operator like ADD or XOR,

0515c8d119f1.title: Hash function
0515c8d119f1.sentence: - Scramble the bits of the key so that the resulting values are uniformly distributed over the keyspace, and

41fb6d2abfe2.title: Hash function
41fb6d2abfe2.sentence: - Map the key values into ones less than or equal to the size of the table.

9976ac9e1345.title: Hash function
9976ac9e1345.sentence: A good hash function satisfies two basic properties: it should be very fast to compute, and it should minimize duplication of output values (collisions).

b5a9cd55fd83.title: Hash function
b5a9cd55fd83.sentence: A good hash function should map the expected inputs as evenly as possible over its output range.

babe03ab32bd.title: Hash function
babe03ab32bd.sentence: That is, every hash value in the output range should be generated with roughly the same probability.

f7ed99766930.title: Hash function
f7ed99766930.sentence: The reason for this requirement is that the cost of hashing-based methods goes up sharply as the number of collisions — pairs of inputs that are mapped to the same hash value — increases.

af962c432a7b.title: Hash function
af962c432a7b.sentence: This criterion only requires the value to be uniformly distributed, not random in any sense.

90c5a747bbd8.title: Hash function
90c5a747bbd8.sentence: A hash procedure must be deterministic—for a given input value, it must always generate the same hash value.

923e9d973464.title: Hash function
923e9d973464.sentence: In other words, it must be a function of the data to be hashed, in the mathematical sense of the term.

5862ebbfe278.title: Hash function
5862ebbfe278.sentence: This requirement excludes hash functions that depend on external variable parameters, such as pseudo-random number generators or the time of day.

34c50bca6630.title: Hash function
34c50bca6630.sentence: Use of hash functions relies on statistical properties of key and function interaction: worst-case behavior is intolerably bad but rare, and average-case behavior can be nearly optimal (minimal collision).

007e45ff1356.title: Hash function
007e45ff1356.sentence: High table loading factors, pathological key sets, and poorly designed hash functions can result in access times approaching linear in the number of items in the table.

b9f557068071.title: Hash function
b9f557068071.sentence: A common solution is to compute a fixed hash function with a very large range (say, 0 to 232 − 1), divide the result by n, and use the division's remainder.

29da1652072b.title: Hash function
29da1652072b.section: Properties > Variable range with minimal movement (dynamic hash function)
29da1652072b.sentence: A hash function that will relocate the minimum number of records when the table is resized is desirable.

214bce1e3231.title: Hash function
214bce1e3231.section: Properties > Variable range with minimal movement (dynamic hash function)
214bce1e3231.sentence: A hash function with minimal movement is especially useful in distributed hash tables.

0421eac160bb.title: Hash function
0421eac160bb.sentence: Hash functions are also used to build caches for large data sets stored in slow media.

ee2e0d66b5ed.title: Hash function
ee2e0d66b5ed.sentence: A cache is generally simpler than a hashed search table, since any collision can be resolved by discarding or writing back the older of the two colliding items.

22b81312fd84.title: Hash function
22b81312fd84.sentence: Hash functions are an essential ingredient of the Bloom filter, a space-efficient probabilistic data structure that is used to test whether an element is a member of a set.

5648acc5d729.title: Hash function
5648acc5d729.sentence: Hash tables may use non-cryptographic hash functions, while cryptographic hash functions are used in cybersecurity to secure sensitive data such as passwords.

d3d390aceb6f.title: Hash function
d3d390aceb6f.sentence: - Integrity checking: Identical hash values for different files imply equality, providing a reliable means to detect file modifications.

5e4bebc0bd89.title: Hash function
5e4bebc0bd89.sentence: - Message authentication codes (MACs): Through the integration of a confidential key with the input data, hash functions can generate MACs ensuring the genuineness of the data, such as in HMACs.

601c4bc45ef2.title: Hash function
601c4bc45ef2.sentence: - Password storage: The password's hash value does not expose any password details, emphasizing the importance of securely storing hashed passwords on the server.

ad81115fee5f.title: Hash function
ad81115fee5f.sentence: - Signatures: Message hashes are signed rather than the whole message.

611faedd9006.title: Base64
611faedd9006.sentence: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding that uses 64 printable characters to represent each 6-bit segment of a sequence of byte values.

0b8f355a686a.title: Base64
0b8f355a686a.sentence: As for all binary-to-text encodings, Base64 encoding enables transmitting binary data on a communication channel that only supports text.

fe9472aef503.title: Base64
fe9472aef503.section: Examples > Encoding when no padding needed
fe9472aef503.sentence: Each input sequence of 6 bits (which can encode 26 = 64 values) is mapped to a Base64 alphabet letter.

4b12435815d6.title: Base64
4b12435815d6.section: Examples > Encoding when no padding needed
4b12435815d6.sentence: Therefore, Base64 encoding results in four characters for each three input bytes.

d08b86ce7681.title: Base64
d08b86ce7681.sentence: When comparing the original data to the resulting encoded data, Base64 encoding increases the size by 33% plus about 3% additional if inserting line breaks for typical line length.

ec9c60b4d6ac.title: Base64
ec9c60b4d6ac.section: Examples > Encoding with one padding character
ec9c60b4d6ac.sentence: If the input consists of a number of bytes that is 2 more than a multiple of 3 (e.g. 'M', 'a'), then the last 2 bytes (16 bits) are encoded in 3 Base64 digits (18 bits).

1dfd6d6b311a.title: Base64
1dfd6d6b311a.section: Examples > Encoding with two padding characters
1dfd6d6b311a.sentence: If the input consists of a number of bytes that is 1 more than a multiple of 3 (e.g. 'M'), then the last 8 bits are represented in 2 Base64 digits (12 bits).

250666dc395c.title: Base64
250666dc395c.section: Examples > Encoding with one padding character
250666dc395c.sentence: The two least significant bits of the last content-bearing 6-bit block are treated as zero for encoding and discarded for decoding (along with the trailing = padding character).

29c36c0ff518.title: Base64
29c36c0ff518.sentence: When decoding, each sequence of four encoded characters is converted to three output bytes, but with a single padding character the final 4 characters decode to only two bytes, or with two padding characters, the final 4 characters decode to a single byte.

cfa349ba968a.title: Base64
cfa349ba968a.sentence: Use of the padding character in encoded text is not essential for decoding.

2d01cac02ef7.title: Base64
2d01cac02ef7.sentence: The number of missing bytes can be inferred from the length of the encoded text.

4e6954edadd7.title: Base64
4e6954edadd7.sentence: Notably, when concatenating Base64 encoded strings, then use of padding characters is required during encoding to avoid ambiguity when decoding.

972ee6873467.title: Base64
972ee6873467.sentence: Typically, an encoding uses A–Z, a–z, and 0–9 for the first 62 values.

fe66d0c204de.title: Base64
fe66d0c204de.sentence: Many variants use + and / for the last two.

1f14854aa303.title: Base64
1f14854aa303.sentence: The most commonly used alphabet is that described by RFC 4648 and most variations only differ in the last two letters used.

2205ba1df553.title: Base64
2205ba1df553.sentence: The RFC also specifies a second Base64 encoding that it calls Base 64 Encoding with URL and Filename Safe Alphabet that is intended for representing relatively long identifying information.

f0afa7067799.title: Base64
f0afa7067799.sentence: For example, a database persistence framework for Java objects might use Base64 encoding to encode a relatively large unique id (generally 128-bit UUIDs) as a string for use as an HTTP parameter in an HTTP form or an HTTP GET URL.

88722a24e4c6.title: JSON Web Token
88722a24e4c6.sentence: The Base64url Encoding is similar to base64, but uses different non-alphanumeric characters and omits padding.

3b63fcba6872.title: Base64
3b63fcba6872.sentence: Base64 encoding is prevalent on the World Wide Web where it is often used to embed binary data such as a digital image in text such as HTML and CSS.

6d50fe7e19b0.title: Base64
6d50fe7e19b0.sentence: To embed binary data in an XML file, using a syntax similar to <data encoding="base64">...</data> e.g. favicons in Firefox's exported bookmarks.html.

46b4a2f9b076.title: Base64
46b4a2f9b076.sentence: Base64 is widely used for sending e-mail attachments, because SMTP – in its original form – was designed to transport 7-bit ASCII characters only.

590c8b7b2733.title: Base64
590c8b7b2733.sentence: Encoding an attachment as Base64 before sending, and then decoding when received, assures older SMTP servers correctly transmit messages with attached binary information.

00f4dc5f34d5.title: Base64
00f4dc5f34d5.sentence: MIME does not specify a fixed length for Base64-encoded lines, but it does specify a maximum line length of 76 characters.

d075d8df661a.title: Base64
d075d8df661a.sentence: Unix stores password hashes computed with crypt in the /etc/passwd file using an encoding called B64. crypt's alphabet puts the punctuation. and / before the alphanumeric characters. crypt uses the alphabet "./0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" without padding.

4c7463c02640.title: Bcrypt
4c7463c02640.sentence: The base-64 encoding in bcrypt uses the table./ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789, which differs from RFC 4648 Base64 encoding.

4035d865fadd.title: Bcrypt
4035d865fadd.sentence: As such, the encoding is not compatible with the more common RFC 4648 Base64 encoding.

107e209ae0ed.title: Hash collision
107e209ae0ed.sentence: In computer science, a hash collision or hash clash is when two distinct pieces of data in a hash table share the same hash value.

b96bbaea79c8.title: Hash collision
b96bbaea79c8.sentence: Hash is typically used as a many-to-one function, with the number of potential inputs (size of input domain) much larger that the number of potential output values ("range"), making collisions inevitable ("pigeonhole principle").

33b11f622c6a.title: Hash collision
33b11f622c6a.sentence: When there is a set of n objects, if n is greater than |R|, which in this case R is the set of the hash values, a hash collision is guaranteed to occur.

77f20d264a86.title: Hash collision
77f20d264a86.sentence: Another reason hash collisions are likely at some point in time stems from the idea of the birthday paradox in mathematics.

9b1b3920f2fe.title: Hash collision
9b1b3920f2fe.sentence: This idea has led to what has been called the birthday attack.

a3b3dec92d1f.title: Hash collision
a3b3dec92d1f.sentence: The premise of this attack is that it is difficult to find a birthday that specifically matches your birthday or a specific birthday, but the probability of finding a set of any two people with matching birthdays increases the probability greatly.

8b650fb146de.title: Hash collision
8b650fb146de.sentence: Bad actors can use this approach to make it simpler for them to find hash values that collide with any other hash value – rather than searching for a specific value.

e3dfd2b26a49.title: Hash collision
e3dfd2b26a49.sentence: A collision violates the assumptions of integrity algorithms, so CHFs are designed to make finding a practical collision computationally infeasible (so-called collision resistance).

5a18ffbde973.title: Hash collision
5a18ffbde973.sentence: The typical uses of non-cryptographic hash functions (NCHFs) – like bloom filters, hash tables, count sketches – are less sensitive to collisions, so NCHFs require just the uniform distribution and avalanche properties.

976b7a6edc7b.title: Hash collision
976b7a6edc7b.sentence: Still, collision resistance is an additional feature that is useful against hash flooding attacks; simple NCHFs, like the cyclic redundancy check (CRC), have essentially no collision resistance and thus cannot be used with an input open to manipulation by an attacker.

44506a458e0b.title: Hash collision
44506a458e0b.sentence: Since hash collisions are inevitable, hash tables have mechanisms of dealing with them, known as collision resolutions.

74c2738255e7.title: Hash collision
74c2738255e7.sentence: Two of the most common strategies are open addressing and separate chaining.

61d4030affbc.title: Hash collision
61d4030affbc.sentence: Cells in the hash table are assigned one of three states in this method – occupied, empty, or deleted.

2ec943019412.title: Hash collision
2ec943019412.sentence: If a hash collision occurs, the table will be probed to move the record to an alternate cell that is stated as empty.

59b5a4fcbd4b.title: Hash collision
59b5a4fcbd4b.sentence: Some types of probing are linear probing, double hashing, and quadratic probing.

7b4ab37b618f.title: Hash collision
7b4ab37b618f.sentence: This strategy allows more than one record to be "chained" to the cells of a hash table.

ebbd06f74d5c.title: Hash collision
ebbd06f74d5c.sentence: If two records are being directed to the same cell, both would go into that cell as a linked list.

14bc1ab2188d.title: Hash collision
14bc1ab2188d.sentence: Keeping track of so many lists is difficult and can cause whatever tool that is being used to become very slow.

4d4d721f5f77.title: Hash collision
4d4d721f5f77.sentence: The impact of collisions depends on the application.

1dc509a84fe4.title: Hash collision
1dc509a84fe4.sentence: When hash functions and fingerprints are used to identify similar data, such as homologous DNA sequences or similar audio files, the functions are designed so as to maximize the probability of collision between distinct but similar data, using techniques like locality-sensitive hashing.

8c02b73a3242.title: Hash collision
8c02b73a3242.sentence: Checksums, on the other hand, are designed to minimize the probability of collisions between similar inputs, without regard for collisions between very different inputs.

a781e364d96b.title: Bloom filter
a781e364d96b.sentence: In computing, a Bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic data structure, conceived by Burton Howard Bloom in 1970, that is used to test whether an element is a member of a set.

e5a49f493159.title: Bloom filter
e5a49f493159.sentence: False positive matches are possible, but false negatives are not – in other words, a query returns either "possibly in set" or "definitely not in set".

98f99a136e80.title: Bloom filter
98f99a136e80.sentence: An empty Bloom filter is a bit array of m bits, all set to 0.

805e1ef30522.title: Bloom filter
805e1ef30522.sentence: It is equipped with k different hash functions, which map set elements to one of the m possible array positions.

d72490a091c4.title: Bloom filter
d72490a091c4.sentence: To add an element, feed it to each of the k hash functions to get k array positions.

11a91cdd9e0e.title: Bloom filter
11a91cdd9e0e.sentence: Set the bits at all these positions to 1.

d70c51287b8d.title: Bloom filter
d70c51287b8d.sentence: To test whether an element is in the set, feed it to each of the k hash functions to get k array positions.

ce3202ed13b3.title: Bloom filter
ce3202ed13b3.sentence: If any of the bits at these positions is 0, the element is definitely not in the set; if it were, then all the bits would have been set to 1 when it was inserted.

588185527186.title: Bloom filter
588185527186.sentence: If all are 1, then either the element is in the set, or the bits have by chance been set to 1 during the insertion of other elements, resulting in a false positive.

6ca5f01ba4e7.title: Bloom filter
6ca5f01ba4e7.sentence: Elements can be added to the set, but not removed (though this can be addressed with the counting Bloom filter variant); the more items added, the larger the probability of false positives.

8581ec4a43d7.title: Bloom filter
8581ec4a43d7.sentence: However, the false positive rate increases steadily as elements are added until all bits in the filter are set to 1, at which point all queries yield a positive result.

fed1a1b0d201.title: Bloom filter
fed1a1b0d201.sentence: Removing an element from this simple Bloom filter is impossible because there is no way to tell which of the k bits it maps to should be cleared.

a086e5781da5.title: Bloom filter
a086e5781da5.sentence: Since the simple algorithm provides no way to determine whether any other elements have been added that affect the bits for the element to be removed, clearing any of the bits would introduce the possibility of false negatives.

a5aa6f3cc57b.title: Bloom filter
a5aa6f3cc57b.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
a5aa6f3cc57b.sentence: In a counting filter, the array positions (buckets) are extended from being a single bit to being a multibit counter.

faccf29e1eff.title: Bloom filter
faccf29e1eff.sentence: A Bloom filter with a 1% error and an optimal value of k, in contrast, requires only about 9.6 bits per element, regardless of the size of the elements.

09dcf7f6835e.title: Bloom filter
09dcf7f6835e.sentence: However, Bloom filters do not store the data items at all, and a separate solution must be provided for the actual storage.

e22fed0d1559.title: Bloom filter
e22fed0d1559.sentence: - Google Bigtable, Apache HBase, Apache Cassandra, ScyllaDB and PostgreSQL use Bloom filters to reduce the disk lookups for non-existent rows or columns.

c754e211490f.title: Bloom filter
c754e211490f.sentence: Avoiding costly disk lookups considerably increases the performance of a database query operation.

e1f839b4a53e.title: Log-structured merge-tree
e1f839b4a53e.sentence: To make the search faster, LSM trees often use a bloom filter for each on-disk component.

4fa83b2472f9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-can-cache-systems-go-wrong.md
4fa83b2472f9.sentence: - Use a bloom filter to check the key existence first, and if the key doesn’t exist, we can avoid hitting the database.

9390098970ec.title: paper>10.1145/362686.362692
9390098970ec.sentence: The paradigm problem considered is that of testing a series of messages one-by-one for membership in a given set of messages.

784b776074e5.title: paper>10.1145/362686.362692
784b776074e5.sentence: The computational factors considered are the size of the hash area (space), the time required to identify a message as a nonmember of the given set (reject time), and an allowable error frequency.

b2b4cfa182d2.title: paper>10.1145/362686.362692
b2b4cfa182d2.sentence: Analysis of the paradigm problem demonstrates that allowing a small number of test messages to be falsely identified as members of the given set will permit a much smaller hash area to be used without increasing reject time.

6eb8a34f13ac.title: paper>10.1145/362686.362692
6eb8a34f13ac.sentence: The reduction in space is accomplished by exploiting the possibility that a small fraction of errors of commission may be tolerable in some applications, in particular, applications in which a large amount of data is involved and a core resident hash area is consequently not feasible using conventional methods.

0eeb37715d8e.title: paper>10.1145/362686.362692
0eeb37715d8e.sentence: In such applications, it is envisaged that overall performance could be improved by using a smaller core resident hash area in conjunction with the new methods and, when necessary, by using some secondary and perhaps time-consuming test to “catch” the small fraction of errors associated with the new methods.

8e4c6e63e1a3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
8e4c6e63e1a3.sentence: A quadtree is a tree data structure in which each internal node has exactly four children.

9266b510aeb5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
9266b510aeb5.sentence: They are often used to partition a two-dimensional space by recursively subdividing it into four quadrants or regions.

2071d8afda90.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
2071d8afda90.sentence: Each child or leaf node stores spatial information.

1dea4d160c1a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
1dea4d160c1a.sentence: Quadtrees are the two-dimensional analog of Octrees which are used to partition three-dimensional space.

f478bd74a809.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
f478bd74a809.section: Quadtrees > Why do we need Quadtrees?
f478bd74a809.sentence: While in theory using latitude and longitude we can determine things such as how close points are to each other using euclidean distance, for practical use cases it is simply not scalable because of its CPU-intensive nature with large data sets.

465db211d156.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
465db211d156.section: Quadtrees > Why do we need Quadtrees?
465db211d156.sentence: Quadtrees enable us to search points within a two-dimensional range efficiently, where those points are defined as latitude/longitude coordinates or as cartesian (x, y) coordinates.

705db56841c9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
705db56841c9.section: Quadtrees > Why do we need Quadtrees?
705db56841c9.sentence: Additionally, we can save further computation by only subdividing a node after a certain threshold.

b644179f12cf.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
b644179f12cf.section: Quadtrees > Why do we need Quadtrees?
b644179f12cf.sentence: And with the application of mapping algorithms such as the Hilbert curve, we can easily improve range query performance.

49335ccba369.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
49335ccba369.sentence: - Location-based services like Google Maps, Uber, etc.

09c397322290.title: Quadtree
09c397322290.sentence: The data associated with a leaf cell varies by application, but the leaf cell represents a "unit of interesting spatial information".

b58ae19772c7.title: Quadtree
b58ae19772c7.sentence: The subdivided regions may be square or rectangular, or may have arbitrary shapes.

1ed2b2419104.title: Quadtree
1ed2b2419104.sentence: - Efficient collision detection in two dimensions

698a5b4780eb.title: Quadtree
698a5b4780eb.sentence: - Solution of multidimensional fields (computational fluid dynamics, electromagnetism)

1ad3b6c90f59.title: Quadtree
1ad3b6c90f59.sentence: Quadtrees, particularly the region quadtree, have lent themselves well to image processing applications.

387a7c74b220.title: Quadtree
387a7c74b220.section: Image processing using quadtrees > Image union / intersection
387a7c74b220.sentence: One of the advantages of using quadtrees for image manipulation is that the set operations of union and intersection can be done simply and quickly.

8b3259b60b5d.title: MD5
8b3259b60b5d.sentence: The MD5 message-digest algorithm is a widely used hash function producing a 128-bit hash value.

2913ccfbef62.title: MD5
2913ccfbef62.sentence: The 128-bit (16-byte) MD5 hashes (also termed message digests) are typically represented as a sequence of 32 hexadecimal digits.

0b419ba694eb.title: MD5
0b419ba694eb.sentence: MD5 processes a variable-length message into a fixed-length output of 128 bits.

9d5d8992935d.title: MD5
9d5d8992935d.sentence: The input message is broken up into chunks of 512-bit blocks (sixteen 32-bit words); the message is always padded even if its original length is divisible by 512 (see RFC 1321, section 3.1).

f5085b950159.title: MD5
f5085b950159.sentence: Even a small change in the message will (with overwhelming probability) result in a mostly different hash, due to the avalanche effect.

50dd132c26cc.title: MD5
50dd132c26cc.sentence: In 2004 it was shown that MD5 is not collision-resistant.

88cec95f1685.title: MD5
88cec95f1685.sentence: As such, MD5 is not suitable for applications like SSL certificates or digital signatures that rely on this property for digital security.

502159b7400e.title: MD5
502159b7400e.sentence: A collision attack exists that can find collisions within seconds on a computer with a 2.6 GHz Pentium 4 processor (complexity of 224.1).

b942ed7de015.title: MD5
b942ed7de015.sentence: On 31 December 2008, the CMU Software Engineering Institute concluded that MD5 was essentially "cryptographically broken and unsuitable for further use".

4082f46765e2.title: MD5
4082f46765e2.sentence: MD5 digests have been widely used in the software world to provide some assurance that a transferred file has arrived intact.

2e9a5547d664.title: MD5
2e9a5547d664.sentence: As it is easy to generate MD5 collisions, it is possible for the person who created the file to create a second file with the same checksum, so this technique cannot protect against some forms of malicious tampering.

7cdde7c04c17.title: MD5
7cdde7c04c17.sentence: In some cases, the checksum cannot be trusted (for example, if it was obtained over the same channel as the downloaded file), in which case MD5 can only provide error-checking functionality: it will recognize a corrupt or incomplete download, which becomes more likely when downloading larger files.

4d69bbbcb38c.title: MD5
4d69bbbcb38c.sentence: Historically, MD5 has been used to store a one-way hash of a password, often with key stretching.

3b3b6a0af8d7.title: MD5
3b3b6a0af8d7.sentence: NIST does not include MD5 in their list of recommended hashes for password storage.

aab2e80aabd1.title: K-d tree
aab2e80aabd1.sentence: In computer science, a k-d tree (short for k-dimensional tree) is a space-partitioning data structure for organizing points in a k-dimensional space.

aa661ce77566.title: K-d tree
aa661ce77566.sentence: The k-d tree is a binary tree in which every node is a k-dimensional point.

91e5bdb52482.title: K-d tree
91e5bdb52482.sentence: Every non-leaf node can be thought of as implicitly generating a splitting hyperplane that divides the space into two parts, known as half-spaces.

1f5763683b2b.title: K-d tree
1f5763683b2b.sentence: Points to the left of this hyperplane are represented by the left subtree of that node and points to the right of the hyperplane are represented by the right subtree.

a4fe00e46417.title: K-d tree
a4fe00e46417.sentence: The hyperplane direction is chosen in the following way: every node in the tree is associated with one of the k dimensions, with the hyperplane perpendicular to that dimension's axis.

d27c44203d88.title: K-d tree
d27c44203d88.sentence: So, for example, if for a particular split the "x" axis is chosen, all points in the subtree with a smaller "x" value than the node will appear in the left subtree and all points with a larger "x" value will be in the right subtree.

46c9711d5218.title: K-d tree
46c9711d5218.sentence: - As one moves down the tree, one cycles through the axes used to select the splitting planes.

33f46aea4fc4.title: K-d tree
33f46aea4fc4.sentence: - Points are inserted by selecting the median of the points being put into the subtree, with respect to their coordinates in the axis being used to create the splitting plane.

bbde8dfb44a8.title: K-d tree
bbde8dfb44a8.sentence: This method leads to a balanced k-d tree, in which each leaf node is approximately the same distance from the root.

ef975966ee07.title: K-d tree
ef975966ee07.sentence: - Inserting a new point into a balanced k-d tree takes O(log n) time.

b6951379dd6d.title: K-d tree
b6951379dd6d.sentence: - Removing a point from a balanced k-d tree takes O(log n) time.

29b32ca547a9.title: K-d tree
29b32ca547a9.section: Operations on k-d trees > Adding elements
29b32ca547a9.sentence: Adding points in this manner can cause the tree to become unbalanced, leading to decreased tree performance.

12c9e505f53f.title: K-d tree
12c9e505f53f.sentence: Balancing a k-d tree requires care because k-d trees are sorted in multiple dimensions, so the tree-rotation technique cannot be used to balance them as this may break the invariant.

869d60c0a0e4.title: K-d tree
869d60c0a0e4.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
869d60c0a0e4.sentence: The nearest neighbor search (NN) algorithm aims to find the point in the tree that is nearest to a given input point.

36b72f16f145.title: K-d tree
36b72f16f145.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
36b72f16f145.sentence: - Starting with the root node, the algorithm moves down the tree recursively, in the same way that it would if the search point were being inserted (i.e. it goes left or right depending on whether the point is lesser than or greater than the current node in the split dimension).

7d3f3a8bd8e9.title: K-d tree
7d3f3a8bd8e9.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
7d3f3a8bd8e9.sentence: - Once the algorithm reaches a leaf node, it checks the node point and if the distance is better than the "current best", that node point is saved as the "current best".

5f80e50aae65.title: K-d tree
5f80e50aae65.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
5f80e50aae65.sentence: - The algorithm unwinds the recursion of the tree, performing the following steps at each node:

813021cf0623.title: K-d tree
813021cf0623.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
813021cf0623.sentence: - If the current node is closer than the current best, then it becomes the current best.

c35544c16de1.title: K-d tree
c35544c16de1.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
c35544c16de1.sentence: - The algorithm checks whether there could be any points on the other side of the splitting plane that are closer to the search point than the current best.

ba20816a83ed.title: K-d tree
ba20816a83ed.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
ba20816a83ed.sentence: In concept, this is done by intersecting the splitting hyperplane with a hypersphere around the search point that has a radius equal to the current nearest distance.

c901fea71a4c.title: K-d tree
c901fea71a4c.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
c901fea71a4c.sentence: - If the hypersphere crosses the plane, there could be nearer points on the other side of the plane, so the algorithm must move down the other branch of the tree from the current node looking for closer points, following the same recursive process as the entire search.

95d4c8158b71.title: K-d tree
95d4c8158b71.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
95d4c8158b71.sentence: - If the hypersphere doesn't intersect the splitting plane, then the algorithm continues walking up the tree, and the entire branch on the other side of that node is eliminated.

dc0fdd472c3b.title: K-d tree
dc0fdd472c3b.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
dc0fdd472c3b.sentence: It can provide the k nearest neighbors to a point by maintaining k current bests instead of just one.

a9430a8cfba6.title: K-d tree
a9430a8cfba6.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
a9430a8cfba6.sentence: A branch is only eliminated when k points have been found and the branch cannot have points closer than any of the k current bests.

ad51ebfcbd23.title: K-d tree
ad51ebfcbd23.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
ad51ebfcbd23.sentence: For example, approximate nearest neighbor searching can be achieved by simply setting an upper bound on the number of points to examine in the tree or by interrupting the search process based upon a real time clock (which may be more appropriate in hardware implementations).

d70d87cea447.title: K-d tree
d70d87cea447.section: Operations on k-d trees > Nearest neighbor search
d70d87cea447.sentence: Approximate nearest neighbor is useful in real-time applications such as robotics due to the significant speed increase gained by not searching for the best point exhaustively.

1afb3aa1dd8a.title: K-d tree
1afb3aa1dd8a.section: Operations on k-d trees > Range search
1afb3aa1dd8a.sentence: For example, if a tree is storing values corresponding to income and age, then a range search might be something like looking for all members of the tree which have an age between 20 and 50 years and an income between 50,000 and 80,000.

7794be56a2bc.title: K-d tree
7794be56a2bc.section: Operations on k-d trees > Range search
7794be56a2bc.sentence: Since k-d trees divide the range of a domain in half at each level of the tree, they are useful for performing range searches.

59434c4be8cf.title: K-d tree
59434c4be8cf.section: Degradation in performance with high-dimensional data
59434c4be8cf.sentence: In low-dimensional spaces, the nearest point is an O(log⁡(n)) operation on average, in the case of randomly distributed points, although analysis in general is tricky.

f28ae34bf589.title: K-d tree
f28ae34bf589.section: Degradation in performance with high-dimensional data
f28ae34bf589.sentence: In high-dimensional spaces, the curse of dimensionality causes the algorithm to need to visit many more branches than in lower-dimensional spaces.

62f04d3b46a2.title: K-d tree
62f04d3b46a2.section: Degradation in performance with high-dimensional data
62f04d3b46a2.sentence: Otherwise, when k-d trees are used with high-dimensional data, most of the points in the tree will be evaluated and the efficiency is no better than exhaustive search, and, if a good-enough fast answer is required, approximate nearest-neighbour methods should be used instead.

2e04e301cd66.title: Trie
2e04e301cd66.sentence: In computer science, a trie (/ˈtraɪ/, /ˈtriː/ ⓘ), also known as a digital tree or prefix tree, is a specialized search tree data structure used to store and retrieve strings from a dictionary or set.

5d73030b07c6.title: Trie
5d73030b07c6.sentence: Unlike a binary search tree, nodes in a trie do not store their associated key.

bd22d2bcfef3.title: Trie
bd22d2bcfef3.sentence: Instead, each node's position within the trie determines its associated key, with the connections between nodes defined by individual characters rather than the entire key.

74f27656187f.title: Trie
74f27656187f.sentence: Every child node shares a common prefix with its parent node, and the root node represents the empty string.

064d2979600d.title: Trie
064d2979600d.sentence: Searching for a value in a trie is guided by the characters in the search string key, as each node in the trie contains a corresponding link to each possible character in the given string.

64589f044ddd.title: Trie
64589f044ddd.sentence: A null link during the search indicates the inexistence of the key.

c7494e7fdf5a.title: Trie
c7494e7fdf5a.sentence: The search operation takes O(m) time, where m is the size of the string parameter key.

82f0d040ffd3.title: Trie
82f0d040ffd3.sentence: Insertion into a trie is guided by using the character sets as indexes to the children array until the last character of the string key is reached.

5849ce811809.title: Trie
5849ce811809.sentence: If null links are encountered before reaching the last character of the string key, new nodes are created.

6cc11a294fc3.title: Trie
6cc11a294fc3.sentence: The input value is assigned to the value of the last node traversed, which is the node that corresponds to the key.

2eee0713e1c7.title: Trie
2eee0713e1c7.sentence: Deletion of a key–value pair from a trie involves finding the node corresponding to the key, setting its value to null, and recursively removing nodes that have no children.

92b847473a2c.title: Trie
92b847473a2c.section: Replacing other data structures > Replacement for hash tables
92b847473a2c.sentence: - Searching for a node with an associated key of size m has the complexity of O(m), whereas an imperfect hash function may have numerous colliding keys, and the worst-case lookup speed of such a table would be O(N), where N denotes the total number of nodes within the table.

33f0ff6248d9.title: Trie
33f0ff6248d9.section: Replacing other data structures > Replacement for hash tables
33f0ff6248d9.sentence: - Tries do not need a hash function for the operation, unlike a hash table; there are also no collisions of different keys in a trie.

b0f8b8b44eff.title: Trie
b0f8b8b44eff.section: Replacing other data structures > Replacement for hash tables
b0f8b8b44eff.sentence: - Within a trie, keys can be efficiently sorted lexicographically.

449cc6729283.title: Trie
449cc6729283.section: Replacing other data structures > Replacement for hash tables
449cc6729283.sentence: However, tries are less efficient than a hash table when the data is directly accessed on a secondary storage device such as a hard disk drive that has higher random access time than the main memory.

18f0e3128cfb.title: Trie
18f0e3128cfb.sentence: Each node contains as many links as the number of characters in the applicable alphabet (although tries tend to have a substantial number of null links).

c969877b6f61.title: Trie
c969877b6f61.sentence: In some cases, the alphabet used is simply that of the character encoding—resulting in, for example, a size of 128 in the case of ASCII.

316fb469e1d5.title: Trie
316fb469e1d5.sentence: Using a vector of pointers for representing a trie consumes enormous space; however, memory space can be reduced at the expense of running time if a singly linked list is used for each node vector, as most entries of the vector contains nil.

ac12e33a8322.title: Trie
ac12e33a8322.sentence: Another technique includes storing a vector of 256 ASCII pointers as a bitmap of 256 bits representing ASCII alphabet, which reduces the size of individual nodes dramatically.

61691a4bc92d.title: Trie
61691a4bc92d.sentence: This can reduce memory usage by a factor of eight; but lookups need to visit twice as many nodes in the worst case.

c17906acf23e.title: Trie
c17906acf23e.sentence: Radix tree, also known as a compressed trie, is a space-optimized variant of a trie in which any node with only one child gets merged with its parent; elimination of branches of the nodes with a single child results in better metrics in both space and time.

8b72f01dc24b.title: Trie
8b72f01dc24b.sentence: This works best when the trie remains static and set of keys stored are very sparse within their representation space.

f817f5b0465f.title: Trie
f817f5b0465f.sentence: Tries are particularly effective for tasks such as autocomplete, spell checking, and IP routing, offering advantages over hash tables due to their prefix-based organization and lack of hash collisions.

7c9923340eba.title: Trie
7c9923340eba.sentence: Trie data structures are commonly used in predictive text or autocomplete dictionaries, and approximate matching algorithms.

226b49914963.title: Trie
226b49914963.sentence: Tries enable faster searches, occupy less space, especially when the set contains large number of short strings, thus used in spell checking, hyphenation applications and longest prefix match algorithms.

596ff6c68865.title: Trie
596ff6c68865.sentence: Compressed variants of tries, such as databases for managing Forwarding Information Base (FIB), are used in storing IP address prefixes within routers and bridges for prefix-based lookup to resolve mask-based operations in IP routing.

18a214f778fb.title: Trie
18a214f778fb.sentence: A specialized kind of trie called a compressed trie, is used in web search engines for storing the indexes - a collection of all searchable words.

601f9f238690.title: Trie
601f9f238690.sentence: Each terminal node is associated with a list of URLs—called occurrence list—to pages that match the keyword.

28c5c403a5df.title: Z-order curve
28c5c403a5df.sentence: In mathematical analysis and computer science, functions which are Z-order, Lebesgue curve, Morton space-filling curve, Morton order or Morton code map multidimensional data to one dimension while preserving locality of the data points (two points close together in multidimensions with high probability lie also close together in Morton order).

18a762fa3156.title: Z-order curve
18a762fa3156.sentence: The z-value of a point in multidimensions is simply calculated by bit interleaving the binary representations of its coordinate values.

8916ca343def.title: Z-order curve
8916ca343def.sentence: Two-dimensional Z-values are also known as quadkey values; see Tiled web map.

1bcd9aa69cb3.title: Z-order curve
1bcd9aa69cb3.sentence: Connecting the z-values in their numerical order produces the recursively Z-shaped curve.

838fb356ac4a.title: Z-order curve
838fb356ac4a.sentence: Once the data are sorted by bit interleaving, any one-dimensional data structure can be used, such as simple one dimensional arrays, binary search trees, B-trees, skip lists or (with low significant bits truncated) hash tables.

0c8fb156626d.title: Z-order curve
0c8fb156626d.sentence: The resulting ordering can equivalently be described as the order one would get from a depth-first traversal of a quadtree or octree.

d4b912a1a473.title: Z-order curve
d4b912a1a473.sentence: The Z-ordering can be used to efficiently build a Compressed quadtree (or octree in 3D) for a set of points.

bb6b18803bcf.title: Z-order curve
bb6b18803bcf.sentence: The basic idea is to sort the input set according to Z-order.

a14150c03f22.title: Z-order curve
a14150c03f22.sentence: Once the points are in sorted order, two properties make it easy to build a quadtree: The first is that the points contained in a square of the quadtree form a contiguous interval in the sorted order.

2297fbcd8bbe.title: Z-order curve
2297fbcd8bbe.sentence: However, when querying a multidimensional search range in these data, using binary search is not really efficient: It is necessary for calculating, from a point encountered in the data structure, the next possible Z-value which is in the multidimensional search range, called BIGMIN.

d9b651550652.title: Z-order curve
