d9b651550652.section: Use with one-dimensional data structures for range searching
d9b651550652.sentence: To speed up the search, one would calculate the next Z-value which is in the search range, called BIGMIN (36 in the example) and only search in the interval between BIGMIN and MAX (bold values), thus skipping most of the hatched area.

48644fa642b9.title: Z-order curve
48644fa642b9.section: Use with one-dimensional data structures for range searching
48644fa642b9.sentence: Searching in decreasing direction is analogous with LITMAX which is the highest Z-value in the query range lower than F. The BIGMIN problem has first been stated and its solution shown in Tropf and Herzog.

b3ca26e69634.title: Z-order curve
b3ca26e69634.section: Use with one-dimensional data structures for range searching
b3ca26e69634.sentence: As the approach does not depend on the one dimensional data structure chosen, there is still free choice of structuring the data, so well known methods such as balanced trees can be used to cope with dynamic data, and keeping the tree balance when inserting or deleting takes O(log n) time.

8579dd781a25.title: Z-order curve
8579dd781a25.section: Use with one-dimensional data structures for range searching
8579dd781a25.sentence: The Free choice makes it easier to incorporate the method into existing databases.

e2bba74927ab.title: Z-order curve
e2bba74927ab.section: Use with one-dimensional data structures for range searching
e2bba74927ab.sentence: This is in contrast for example to R-trees where special considerations are necessary.

e86d18b4db45.title: Z-order curve
e86d18b4db45.section: Use with one-dimensional data structures for range searching
e86d18b4db45.sentence: Z-order is one of the few multidimensional access methods that has found its way into commercial database systems.

309cd9f37ed0.title: Z-order curve
309cd9f37ed0.sentence: As an alternative, the Hilbert curve has been suggested as it has a better order-preserving behaviour, and, in fact, was used in an optimized index, the S2-geometry.

439b160da0f5.title: Address geocoding
439b160da0f5.sentence: - Geohash, a public domain system based on the Morton Z-order curve.

269009b69862.title: Z-order curve
269009b69862.sentence: Some GPUs store texture maps in Z-order to increase spatial locality of reference during texture mapped rasterization.

47cd3c022497.title: Z-order curve
47cd3c022497.sentence: This allows cache lines to represent rectangular tiles, increasing the probability that nearby accesses are in the cache.

62e29cfd35e3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
62e29cfd35e3.sentence: Geohashing is a geocoding method used to encode geographic coordinates such as latitude and longitude into short alphanumeric strings.

d2a6cce8d432.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
d2a6cce8d432.sentence: Geohash is a hierarchical spatial index that uses Base-32 alphabet encoding, the first character in a geohash identifies the initial location as one of the 32 cells.

890293bb67b5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
890293bb67b5.sentence: This cell will also contain 32 cells.

e76a66f7c652.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
e76a66f7c652.sentence: This means that to represent a point, the world is recursively divided into smaller and smaller cells with each additional bit until the desired precision is attained.

f38a646021e7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
f38a646021e7.sentence: The precision factor also determines the size of the cell.

2caf3f05ce4e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
2caf3f05ce4e.sentence: Geohashing guarantees that points are spatially closer if their Geohashes share a longer prefix which means the more characters in the string, the more precise the location.

a476757358ef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
a476757358ef.sentence: For example, geohashes 9q8yy9mf and 9q8yy9vx are spatially closer as they share the prefix 9q8yy9.

fe3414f4224f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
fe3414f4224f.sentence: - It is a simple way to represent and store a location in a database.

0a0245058a6a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
0a0245058a6a.sentence: - We can efficiently find the nearest neighbors of a point through very simple string comparisons and efficient searching of indexes.

2e87b0e61d3b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::geohashing-and-quadtrees
2e87b0e61d3b.sentence: Geohashing can also be used to provide a degree of anonymity as we don't need to expose the exact location of the user because depending on the length of the geohash we just know they are somewhere within an area.

7aa5ebd24d0a.title: Geohash
7aa5ebd24d0a.sentence: It is a hierarchical spatial data structure which subdivides space into buckets of grid shape, which is one of the many applications of what is known as a Z-order curve, and generally space-filling curves.

d48b7b28dfe0.title: Geohash
d48b7b28dfe0.sentence: Geohashes offer properties like arbitrary precision and the possibility of gradually removing characters from the end of the code to reduce its size (and gradually lose precision).

06d5ca0d72a8.title: Geohash
06d5ca0d72a8.sentence: First, data indexed by geohash will have all points for a given rectangular area in contiguous slices (the number of slices depends on the precision required and the presence of geohash "fault lines").

19cab811ac6f.title: Geohash
19cab811ac6f.sentence: This is especially useful in database systems where queries on a single index are much easier or faster than multiple-index queries.

7c2aca64536f.title: Geohash
7c2aca64536f.sentence: Second, this index structure can be used for a quick-and-dirty proximity search: the closest points are often among the closest geohashes.

3724a4b0579c.title: Hilbert curve
3724a4b0579c.sentence: The Hilbert curve (also known as the Hilbert space-filling curve) is a continuous fractal space-filling curve first described by the German mathematician David Hilbert in 1891, as a variant of the space-filling Peano curves discovered by Giuseppe Peano in 1890.

8be468150d62.title: Hilbert curve
8be468150d62.sentence: Both the true Hilbert curve and its discrete approximations are useful because they give a mapping between 1D and 2D space that preserves locality fairly well.

4fc586608525.title: Hilbert curve
4fc586608525.sentence: This means that two data points which are close to each other in one-dimensional space are also close to each other after folding.

bc9d4f86e98f.title: Hilbert curve
bc9d4f86e98f.sentence: Because of this locality property, the Hilbert curve is widely used in computer science.

18c9defae1a7.title: Hilbert curve
18c9defae1a7.sentence: The locality property of the Hilbert curve has also been used to design algorithms for exploring regions with mobile robots and indexing geospatial location data.

814b4cf90f36.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
814b4cf90f36.sentence: And with the application of mapping algorithms such as the Hilbert curve, we can perform efficient range queries to find nearby drivers for the customer.

2a2ba86e5374.title: Hilbert curve
2a2ba86e5374.sentence: For multidimensional databases, Hilbert order has been proposed to be used instead of Z order because it has better locality-preserving behavior.

12507545f35e.title: Hilbert curve
12507545f35e.sentence: For example, Hilbert curves have been used to compress and accelerate R-tree indexes (see Hilbert R-tree).

029791dab9b4.title: Hilbert curve
029791dab9b4.sentence: The linear distance of any point along the curve can be converted to coordinates in n dimensions for a given n, and vice versa, using any of several standard mathematical techniques such as Skilling's method.

44f609247a79.title: Hilbert curve
44f609247a79.sentence: It is possible to implement Hilbert curves efficiently even when the data space does not form a square.

651dfea9b06a.title: Hash function
651dfea9b06a.sentence: Fuzzy hashing, also known as similarity hashing, is a technique for detecting data that is similar, but not exactly the same, as other data.

bad359c6db56.title: Hash function
bad359c6db56.sentence: This is in contrast to cryptographic hash functions, which are designed to have significantly different hashes for even minor differences.

b945e5ee6d1e.title: Hash function
b945e5ee6d1e.sentence: Perceptual hashing is the use of a fingerprinting algorithm that produces a snippet, hash, or fingerprint of various forms of multimedia.

b0dee247a95c.title: Hash function
b0dee247a95c.sentence: A perceptual hash is a type of locality-sensitive hash, which is analogous if features of the multimedia are similar.

4e2ee285a9d3.title: Hash function
4e2ee285a9d3.sentence: Perceptual hash functions are widely used in finding cases of online copyright infringement as well as in digital forensics because of the ability to have a correlation between hashes so similar data can be found (for instance with a differing watermark).

cbd0f0137bec.title: Hash function
cbd0f0137bec.sentence: Fuzzy hashing has been used to identify malware and has potential for other applications, like data loss prevention and detecting multiple versions of code.

eba782047604.title: Hash function
eba782047604.sentence: When the data values are long (or variable-length) character strings—such as personal names, web page addresses, or mail messages—their distribution is usually very uneven, with complicated dependencies.

a3ff2f89e2ec.title: Hash function
a3ff2f89e2ec.sentence: The paradigmatic example of folding by characters is to add up the integer values of all the characters in the string.

ceef377a3fb2.title: Hash function
ceef377a3fb2.sentence: For example, text in any natural language has highly non-uniform distributions of characters, and character pairs, characteristic of the language.

e2dbed41a2de.title: Hash function
e2dbed41a2de.sentence: A better idea is to multiply the hash total by a constant, typically a sizable prime number, before adding in the next character, ignoring overflow.

d0c6b01f59dd.title: Hash function
d0c6b01f59dd.sentence: The final operation would be a modulo, mask, or other function to reduce the word value to an index the size of the table.

4c6ca969adb5.title: Hash function
4c6ca969adb5.sentence: The weakness of this procedure is that information may cluster in the upper or lower bits of the bytes; this clustering will remain in the hashed result and cause more collisions than a proper randomizing hash.

8f456f50b4ba.title: Hash function
8f456f50b4ba.sentence: ASCII byte codes, for example, have an upper bit of 0, and printable strings do not use the last byte code or most of the first 32 byte codes, so the information, which uses the remaining byte codes, is clustered in the remaining bits in an unobvious manner.

b492d973a94c.title: Hash function
b492d973a94c.section: Hashing variable-length data > Middle and ends
b492d973a94c.sentence: Simplistic hash functions may add the first and last n characters of a string along with the length, or form a word-size hash from the middle 4 characters of a string.

74c2451161ce.title: Hash function
74c2451161ce.section: Hashing variable-length data > Middle and ends
74c2451161ce.sentence: This saves iterating over the (potentially long) string, but hash functions that do not hash on all characters of a string can readily become linear due to redundancies, clustering, or other pathologies in the key set.

f122fc4729dc.title: Hash function
f122fc4729dc.sentence: In some applications, such as substring search, one can compute a hash function h for every k-character substring of a given n-character string by advancing a window of width k characters along the string, where k is a fixed integer, and n > k.

267c17773da2.title: Hash function
267c17773da2.sentence: The straightforward solution, which is to extract such a substring at every character position in the text and compute h separately, requires a number of operations proportional to k·n.

0c4b847db7b6.title: Hash function
0c4b847db7b6.sentence: However, with the proper choice of h, one can use the technique of rolling hash to compute all those hashes with an effort proportional to mk + n where m is the number of occurrences of the substring.

d3d9b42ee27b.title: Hash function
d3d9b42ee27b.sentence: The most familiar algorithm of this type is Rabin-Karp with best and average case performance O(n+mk) and worst case O(n·k) (in all fairness, the worst case here is gravely pathological: both the text string and substring are composed of a repeated single character, such as t="AAAAAAAAAAA", and s="AAA").

a767220d9141.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md

11559b18d933.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md

ac4c60a227b9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md

971009e0a0f2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md

d9381cbe0177.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
d9381cbe0177.sentence: The first bit is unused to ensure positive IDs.

d1dd6a8c0be1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
d1dd6a8c0be1.sentence: This generator doesn’t need to talk to an ID generator via the network, so is fast and scalable.

e0031c33cca1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
e0031c33cca1.sentence: For example, data center ID can be added to the “MachineID” component to guarantee global uniqueness.

c83b6009b058.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
c83b6009b058.sentence: Most database products offer auto-increment identity columns.

e8dd25206bbb.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
e8dd25206bbb.sentence: Since this is supported in the database, we can leverage its transaction management to handle concurrent visits to the ID generator.

6a71379405f6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
6a71379405f6.sentence: This guarantees uniqueness in one table.

9734677dbed0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
9734677dbed0.sentence: However, this involves network communications and may expose sensitive business data to the outside.

dac738176037.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
dac738176037.sentence: For example, if we use this as a user ID, our business competitors will have a rough idea of the total number of users registered on our website.

e10de6e7a7af.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
e10de6e7a7af.sentence: An alternative approach is to retrieve IDs from the database in batches and cache them in the ID servers, each ID server handling a segment of IDs.

2c23a1e1152e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-5-unique-id-generators-in-distributed-systems.md
2c23a1e1152e.sentence: This greatly saves the I/O pressure on the database.

ab4f41cc60de.title: Universally unique identifier
ab4f41cc60de.sentence: A universally unique identifier (UUID) is a 128-bit number used to identify information in computer systems.

23ac9d5ddce1.title: Universally unique identifier
23ac9d5ddce1.sentence: Their uniqueness does not depend on a central registration authority or coordination between the parties generating them, unlike most other numbering schemes.

211da196270a.title: Universally unique identifier
211da196270a.sentence: The term globally unique identifier (GUID) is also used, typically in software created by Microsoft.

c0443fe82b56.title: Universally unique identifier
c0443fe82b56.sentence: Most used is the 8-4-4-4-12 format, a string of 32 hexadecimal digits with four hyphens, xxxxxxxx-xxxx-vxxx-wxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx.

2f8c91f9dbd1.title: Universally unique identifier
2f8c91f9dbd1.sentence: Thus, anyone can create large numbers of UUIDs and use them as identifiers with near certainty that they do not duplicate UUIDs that have been, or will be, created by others, with the only coordination required to achieve uniqueness being conformance with the UUID standards.

d5d8cef4fdef.title: Universally unique identifier
d5d8cef4fdef.sentence: Information labeled with UUIDs by independent parties can therefore coexist in the same databases or channels, with a negligible probability of duplication.

860dcd8d26a1.title: Universally unique identifier
860dcd8d26a1.sentence: While the probability that a UUID will be duplicated is not zero, it is close enough to zero to be negligible.

076b72b2e644.title: Universally unique identifier
076b72b2e644.sentence: Thus, the probability to find a duplicate within 103 trillion properly-generated version-4 UUIDs is one in a billion.

ba8e5e67145b.title: Universally unique identifier
ba8e5e67145b.sentence: In the case of many standard version-1, -2, or -6 UUIDs using unique MAC addresses and/or timestamps, collisions can occur only as a result of deliberate construction or error, such as manufacturing problems, skewed clocks, or software bugs.

751bc6d3b70d.title: Universally unique identifier
751bc6d3b70d.sentence: Duplicate UUIDs can also occur due to error with the UUID versions generated using processes such as random number generation or hashing.

fad88d0141e7.title: Universally unique identifier
fad88d0141e7.sentence: It is important, for example, to have a high-entropy source of randomness when generating version-4 UUIDs.

6b4d2c777852.title: Universally unique identifier
6b4d2c777852.sentence: The meaning of the bits is determined by the variant, of which three are defined.

8d9d968412e5.title: Universally unique identifier
8d9d968412e5.sentence: Of these, the most common is variant 1, with the other variants being for backwards compatibility with previous formats or for future definition.

9302199aebd7.title: Universally unique identifier
9302199aebd7.sentence: Variants 1 and 2 have "versions", which further define the interpretation of the UUID.

2e6d646def71.title: Universally unique identifier
2e6d646def71.sentence: UUIDs are commonly used as a unique key in database tables.

a659fbc730eb.title: Universally unique identifier
a659fbc730eb.sentence: The random nature of standard UUIDs of versions 3, 4, and 5, and the ordering of the fields within standard versions 1 and 2 may create problems with database locality or performance when UUIDs are used as primary keys.

23701075dece.title: Universally unique identifier
23701075dece.sentence: By reordering and encoding version-1 and -2 UUIDs so that the timestamp comes first, insertion performance loss can be averted.

bb47203cfd0d.title: Universally unique identifier
bb47203cfd0d.sentence: This is the rationale for variant 1 (DCE) versions 6 and 7, standardized in RFC 9562.

69804b08de90.title: rfc>9562
69804b08de90.sentence: The UUID format is 16 octets (128 bits) in size; the variant bits in conjunction with the version bits described in the next sections determine finer structure.

ff38479d3105.title: rfc>9562
ff38479d3105.sentence: The variant field determines the layout of the UUID.

5781df888e60.title: rfc>9562
5781df888e60.sentence: That is, the interpretation of all other bits in the UUID depends on the setting of the bits in the variant field.

74b639176df2.title: rfc>9562
74b639176df2.sentence: The variant field consists of a variable number of the most significant bits of octet 8 of the UUID.

397c39d69157.title: rfc>9562
397c39d69157.sentence: The version number is in the most significant 4 bits of octet 6 (bits 48 through 51 of the UUID).

bd1d87d38732.title: Snowflake ID
bd1d87d38732.sentence: Snowflake IDs, or snowflakes, are a form of unique identifier used in distributed computing.

5ebdc739c63b.title: Snowflake ID
5ebdc739c63b.sentence: - The next 41 bits encode a timestamp, representing milliseconds since the chosen epoch.

06340de4cc6e.title: Snowflake ID
06340de4cc6e.sentence: - The next 10 bits represent a machine ID, preventing clashes.

28850a309063.title: Snowflake ID
28850a309063.sentence: - The next 12 more bits represent a per-machine sequence number, to allow creation of multiple snowflakes in the same millisecond.

2baab3247cec.title: Snowflake ID
2baab3247cec.sentence: The format was created by Twitter (now X) and is used for the IDs of tweets.

7afbe3e14c0d.title: Snowflake ID
7afbe3e14c0d.sentence: The format has been adopted by other companies, including Discord, Fluxer and Instagram.

6fc91b79e534.title: Snowflake ID
6fc91b79e534.sentence: Only 63 bits are variable, so that a non-negative number can be processed readily as a 64-bit signed integer; the final number is generally serialized textually as a decimal number.

6d90e65766f3.title: Snowflake ID
6d90e65766f3.sentence: Snowflakes are sortable by time, because they are based on the time they were created.

36b75c7fa939.title: Snowflake ID
36b75c7fa939.sentence: Additionally, the time a snowflake was created can be calculated from the snowflake.

844c1ce2ad17.title: Snowflake ID
844c1ce2ad17.sentence: This can be used to get snowflakes (and their associated objects) that were created before or after a particular date.

7ab807d61c25.title: Snowflake ID
7ab807d61c25.sentence: - The 10-bit machine ID field can be further split into sub-fields by a given implementation.

9491522661ad.title: Snowflake ID
9491522661ad.sentence: For example, the archived version of the original Twitter snowflake library in Scala splits it into a 5-bit data center ID and a 5-bit worker ID.

cff5c96a61cf.title: Snowflake ID
cff5c96a61cf.sentence: - Instagram uses a modified version of the format, with 41 bits for a timestamp, 13 bits for a shard ID, and 10 bits for a sequence number.

44d2c7b6d115.title: Universally unique identifier
44d2c7b6d115.sentence: The OSF DCE and Microsoft COM/DCOM variants (1 & 2, respectively) have versions, indicated by the value of the high four bits of the seventh byte of the UUID.

2637787e0b91.title: rfc>9562
2637787e0b91.sentence: UUIDv1 is a time-based UUID featuring a 60-bit timestamp represented by Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) as a count of 100-nanosecond intervals since 00:00:00.00, 15 October 1582 (the date of Gregorian reform to the Christian calendar).

ef6e5cdc01f0.title: rfc>9562
ef6e5cdc01f0.sentence: UUIDv1 also features a clock sequence field that is used to help avoid duplicates that could arise when the clock is set backwards in time or if the Node ID changes.

c0b2f033c799.title: Universally unique identifier
c0b2f033c799.section: Format > Versions > Versions 1 and 6 (date–time and node ID)
c0b2f033c799.sentence: Version 1 concatenates a 48-bit node ID with a 60-bit timestamp.

68729372bea3.title: Universally unique identifier
68729372bea3.section: Format > Versions > Versions 1 and 6 (date–time and node ID)
68729372bea3.sentence: The node ID is usually the MAC address of a network interface controller (NIC) on the system generating the UUID.

49597a8a6d24.title: Universally unique identifier
49597a8a6d24.section: Format > Versions > Versions 1 and 6 (date–time and node ID)
49597a8a6d24.sentence: The timestamp is the number of 100-nanosecond intervals since midnight 15 October 1582 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), the date on which the Gregorian calendar was first adopted.

b0d3ccc69d16.title: rfc>9562
b0d3ccc69d16.sentence: UUIDv3 is meant for generating UUIDs from names that are drawn from, and unique within, some namespace as per Section 6.5.

22447ef6b836.title: rfc>9562
22447ef6b836.sentence: UUIDv3 values are created by computing an MD5 hash over a given Namespace ID value (Section 6.6) concatenated with the desired name value after both have been converted to a canonical sequence of octets, as defined by the standards or conventions of its namespace, in network byte order.

333582b26e83.title: rfc>9562
333582b26e83.sentence: UUIDv5 values are created by computing an SHA-1 hash [FIPS180-4] over a given Namespace ID value (Section 6.6) concatenated with the desired name value after both have been converted to a canonical sequence of octets, as defined by the standards or conventions of its namespace, in network byte order.

e97c17268988.title: Universally unique identifier
e97c17268988.sentence: Version-3 and version-5 UUIDs are generated by hashing a namespace identifier and name.

7d9575a15267.title: Universally unique identifier
7d9575a15267.sentence: The namespace identifier is itself a UUID.

a1a9e74876fa.title: Universally unique identifier
a1a9e74876fa.sentence: Version 3 uses MD5 as the hashing algorithm, and version 5 uses SHA-1.

0e345c0056b4.title: Universally unique identifier
0e345c0056b4.sentence: This is useful when systems need to determine a UUID based on a set of other names or identifiers without reference to a central registry.

dae4b2843512.title: rfc>9562
dae4b2843512.sentence: UUIDv4 is meant for generating UUIDs from truly random or pseudorandom numbers.

de2d465629a9.title: rfc>9562
de2d465629a9.sentence: Alternatively, an implementation MAY choose to randomly generate the exact required number of bits for random_a, random_b, and random_c (122 bits total) and then concatenate the version and variant in the required position.

9ba30e771f25.title: Universally unique identifier
9ba30e771f25.sentence: As in other UUIDs, four bits are used to indicate version 4, and two or three bits to indicate the variant (102 or 1102 for variants 1 and 2 respectively).

17d6658255c5.title: Universally unique identifier
17d6658255c5.sentence: Thus, for variant 1 (that is, most UUIDs) a random version-4 UUID will have six predetermined variant and version bits, leaving 122 bits for the randomly generated part, for a total of 2122, or 5.3×10^36 (5.3 undecillion) possible version-4, variant-1 UUIDs.

5d17e2ed52fe.title: rfc>9562
5d17e2ed52fe.sentence: UUIDv6 is a field-compatible version of UUIDv1 (Section 5.1), reordered for improved DB locality.

caf397225163.title: rfc>9562
caf397225163.sentence: Instead of splitting the timestamp into the low, mid, and high sections from UUIDv1, UUIDv6 changes this sequence so timestamp bytes are stored from most to least significant.

ff483411f386.title: rfc>9562
ff483411f386.sentence: Systems that do not involve legacy UUIDv1 SHOULD use UUIDv7 (Section 5.7) instead.

6d6529c061f3.title: rfc>9562
6d6529c061f3.sentence: UUIDv7 features a time-ordered value field derived from the widely implemented and well-known Unix Epoch timestamp source, the number of milliseconds since midnight 1 Jan 1970 UTC, leap seconds excluded.

b4c82b1add1e.title: rfc>9562
b4c82b1add1e.sentence: UUIDv7 values are created by allocating a Unix timestamp in milliseconds in the most significant 48 bits and filling the remaining 74 bits, excluding the required version and variant bits, with random bits for each new UUIDv7 generated to provide uniqueness as per Section 6.9.

9bfa2869e45d.title: rfc>9562
9bfa2869e45d.sentence: Alternatively, implementations MAY fill the 74 bits, jointly, with a combination of the following subfields, in this order from the most significant bits to the least, to guarantee additional monotonicity within a millisecond:

ce8d3894d668.title: rfc>9562
ce8d3894d668.sentence: Implementations SHOULD utilize UUIDv7 instead of UUIDv1 and UUIDv6 if possible.

09b0b35bc1ae.title: Universally unique identifier
09b0b35bc1ae.sentence: Version-7 UUIDs are intended as monotonically ascending, creation-time-ordered, lexically sortable keys in large databases and distributed systems, contributing to locality and performance.

219a87831ea9.title: Universally unique identifier
219a87831ea9.sentence: With version 7 as database keys, "new" records are inserted at the logical end of the key sequence, and records which are close in time are near each other in the key sequence.

3901920618e7.title: Universally unique identifier
3901920618e7.sentence: This contrasts with the random version 4, which when used as database keys, are evenly and randomly dispersed across the key sequence, even when the underlying records are close in time, negatively affecting performance in many types of databases.

640a1b9945ee.title: rfc>9562
640a1b9945ee.sentence: UUIDv8 provides a format for experimental or vendor-specific use cases.

ceeca434625a.title: rfc>9562
ceeca434625a.sentence: The only explicitly defined bits are those of the version and variant fields, leaving 122 bits for implementation-specific UUIDs.

d477343bccf6.title: rfc>9562
d477343bccf6.sentence: UUIDv8's uniqueness will be implementation specific and MUST NOT be assumed.

945b0ce176ad.title: Universally unique identifier
945b0ce176ad.sentence: In essence, version 8 UUIDs are 128 bit integers with 122 opaque bits generated by any desired method, plus 4 version bits (binary 1000), and 2 variant bits (binary 10).

03e624b79fda.title: Universally unique identifier
03e624b79fda.sentence: Version 8 UUIDs are unspecified except for the variant and version, effectively allocating one-sixteenth of the UUID variant 1 identifier space for private, experimental, non-standard, or vendor-specific identifiers.

ceebcc89ba65.title: Universally unique identifier
ceebcc89ba65.sentence: Versions 1, 2, 6, and 7 are based on, and expose, the time when the UUID was generated, which often corresponds to the creation of a record, or an historical event.

bdd4a4d18e73.title: Universally unique identifier
bdd4a4d18e73.sentence: It may be possible to determine from time-based monotonically-ascending UUIDs when a system went live, or what objects in a system are new or recently updated.

4febff8b8231.title: Universally unique identifier
4febff8b8231.sentence: If the identified objects represent product orders or user sign-ups, for example, it may be possible to determine user growth or sales volume over time from the UUIDs.

f3c5216f94d8.title: rfc>9562
f3c5216f94d8.sentence: Timestamps embedded in the UUID do pose a very small attack surface.

97ec5ce9d052.title: rfc>9562
97ec5ce9d052.sentence: The minimum requirements for generating UUIDs of each version are described in this document.

b2af7a55960d.title: rfc>9562
b2af7a55960d.sentence: Everything else is an implementation detail, and it is up to the implementer to decide what is appropriate for a given implementation.

98ac880746ff.title: rfc>9562
98ac880746ff.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.13. DBMS and Database Considerations
98ac880746ff.sentence: For many applications, such as databases, storing UUIDs as text is unnecessarily verbose, requiring 288 bits to represent 128-bit UUID values.

9199043f55a9.title: rfc>9562
9199043f55a9.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.13. DBMS and Database Considerations
9199043f55a9.sentence: Thus, where feasible, UUIDs SHOULD be stored within database applications as the underlying 128-bit binary value.

ff423152841b.title: rfc>9562
ff423152841b.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.13. DBMS and Database Considerations
ff423152841b.sentence: - Storing in binary form requires less space and may result in faster data access.

bcfe8f3a74af.title: rfc>9562
bcfe8f3a74af.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.13. DBMS and Database Considerations
bcfe8f3a74af.sentence: - Storing as text requires more space but may require less translation if the resulting text form is to be used after retrieval, which may make it simpler to implement.

dea7b4e5224e.title: rfc>9562
dea7b4e5224e.sentence: UUIDv6 and UUIDv7 are designed so that implementations that require sorting (e.g., database indexes) sort as opaque raw bytes without the need for parsing or introspection.

913dd3e2f26e.title: rfc>9562
913dd3e2f26e.sentence: Time-ordered monotonic UUIDs benefit from greater database-index locality because the new values are near each other in the index.

aab8a8a08054.title: rfc>9562
aab8a8a08054.sentence: The real-world differences in this approach of index locality versus random data inserts can be one order of magnitude or more.

4d441c3501bc.title: rfc>9562
4d441c3501bc.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.13. DBMS and Database Considerations
4d441c3501bc.sentence: Designers of database schema are cautioned against using name-based UUIDs (see Sections 5.3 and 5.5) as primary keys in tables.

ddeedccb665a.title: rfc>9562
ddeedccb665a.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.13. DBMS and Database Considerations
ddeedccb665a.sentence: The subsequent change of the identifier, used as a "name" input for name-based UUIDs, can invalidate a given database structure.

a8a5f0c42db2.title: rfc>9562
a8a5f0c42db2.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.13. DBMS and Database Considerations
a8a5f0c42db2.sentence: The general advice is to avoid name-based UUID natural keys and, instead, to utilize time-based UUID surrogate keys based on the aforementioned problems detailed in this section.

9bbf2496c4f2.title: rfc>9562
9bbf2496c4f2.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.2. Monotonicity and Counters
9bbf2496c4f2.sentence: Normally, time-based UUIDs from this document will be monotonic due to an embedded timestamp; however, implementations can guarantee additional monotonicity via the concepts covered in this section.

597b436eaaf5.title: rfc>9562
597b436eaaf5.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.2. Monotonicity and Counters
597b436eaaf5.sentence: Take care to ensure UUIDs generated in batches are also monotonic.

1b84662cddf8.title: rfc>9562
1b84662cddf8.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.2. Monotonicity and Counters
1b84662cddf8.sentence: Fixed Bit-Length Dedicated Counter (Method 1): Some implementations allocate a specific number of bits in the UUID layout to the sole purpose of tallying the total number of UUIDs created during a given UUID timestamp tick.

1bffab15dc2e.title: rfc>9562
1bffab15dc2e.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.2. Monotonicity and Counters
1bffab15dc2e.sentence: Monotonic Random (Method 2): With this method, the random data is extended to also function as a counter.

0ef0afb54ed7.title: rfc>9562
0ef0afb54ed7.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.2. Monotonicity and Counters
0ef0afb54ed7.sentence: Replace Leftmost Random Bits with Increased Clock Precision (Method 3): For UUIDv7, which has millisecond timestamp precision, it is possible to use additional clock precision available on the system to substitute for up to 12 random bits immediately following the timestamp.

800f7110dcd9.title: rfc>9562
800f7110dcd9.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.4. Distributed UUID Generation
800f7110dcd9.sentence: While UUIDs already feature sufficient entropy to ensure that the chances of collision are low, as the total number of UUID generating nodes increases, so does the likelihood of a collision.

eb19bf7b6f8c.title: rfc>9562
eb19bf7b6f8c.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.4. Distributed UUID Generation
eb19bf7b6f8c.sentence: Node IDs: With this method, a pseudorandom Node ID value is placed within the UUID layout.

79e815da939a.title: rfc>9562
79e815da939a.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.4. Distributed UUID Generation
79e815da939a.sentence: Implementations that choose to leverage an embedded node id SHOULD utilize UUIDv8.

f5fe99a5fed7.title: rfc>9562
f5fe99a5fed7.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.4. Distributed UUID Generation
f5fe99a5fed7.sentence: As applications scale, the communication with the central registry could become a bottleneck and impact UUID generation in a negative way.

0bd0519f078d.title: rfc>9562
0bd0519f078d.section: 6. UUID Best Practices > 6.4. Distributed UUID Generation
0bd0519f078d.sentence: Shared knowledge schemes with central/global registries are outside the scope of this specification and are NOT RECOMMENDED.

7dbd2d184051.title: rfc>9562
7dbd2d184051.sentence: Implementations SHOULD utilize a cryptographically secure pseudorandom number generator (CSPRNG) to provide values that are both difficult to predict ("unguessable") and have a low likelihood of collision ("unique").

e0936b9b0416.title: rfc>9562
e0936b9b0416.sentence: Take care to ensure the CSPRNG state is properly reseeded upon state changes, such as process forks, to ensure proper CSPRNG operation.

56f4bb714fce.title: rfc>9562
56f4bb714fce.sentence: Implementations SHOULD NOT assume that UUIDs are hard to guess.

a43c20af81b8.title: rfc>9562
a43c20af81b8.sentence: For example, they MUST NOT be used as security capabilities (identifiers whose mere possession grants access).

6517f264e42d.title: rfc>9562
6517f264e42d.sentence: If UUIDs are required for use with any security operation within an application context in any shape or form, then UUIDv4 (Section 5.4) SHOULD be utilized.

f1062afcbfa8.title: rfc>9562
f1062afcbfa8.sentence: Implementations should weigh the consequences of UUID collisions within their application and when deciding between UUID versions that use entropy (randomness) versus the other components such as those in Sections 6.1 and 6.2.

b79b93aad320.title: rfc>9562
b79b93aad320.sentence: Low Impact: A UUID collision generated a duplicate log entry, which results in incorrect statistics derived from the data.

aac0201cd288.title: rfc>9562
aac0201cd288.sentence: Collisions must be avoided: failure is unacceptable.

ac0f06816342.title: rfc>9562
ac0f06816342.sentence: Applications dealing with this type of scenario must employ as much collision resistance as possible within the given application context.

6abd6849379f.title: rfc>9562
6abd6849379f.sentence: As general guidance, avoiding parsing UUID values unnecessarily is recommended; instead, treat UUIDs as opaquely as possible.

07142b63239e.title: Count–min sketch
07142b63239e.sentence: In computing, the count–min sketch (CM sketch) is a probabilistic data structure that serves as a frequency table of events in a stream of data.

fdddeeceecbc.title: Count–min sketch
fdddeeceecbc.sentence: It uses hash functions to map events to frequencies, but unlike a hash table uses only sub-linear space, at the expense of overcounting some events due to collisions.

13278689851f.title: Count–min sketch
13278689851f.sentence: The actual sketch data structure is a two-dimensional array of w columns and d rows.

098859d5593f.title: Count–min sketch
098859d5593f.sentence: Associated with each of the d rows is a separate hash function; the hash functions must be pairwise independent.

0678affcecdc.title: Count–min sketch
0678affcecdc.sentence: The parameters w and d are fixed when the sketch is created, and determine the time and space needs and the probability of error when the sketch is queried for a frequency or inner product.

c1a852f9b1b9.title: Count–min sketch
c1a852f9b1b9.sentence: When a new event of type i arrives we update as follows: for each row j of the table, apply the corresponding hash function to obtain a column index k = hj(i).

4157ff676824.title: Count–min sketch
4157ff676824.sentence: Then increment the value in row j, column k by one.

659d61d0c8b3.title: Count–min sketch
659d61d0c8b3.sentence: The estimated count is given by the least value in the table for i, namely âi=minjcount[j,hj(i)], where count is the table.

856c296b13a0.title: Count–min sketch
856c296b13a0.sentence: Obviously, for each i, one has ai≤âi, where ai is the true frequency with which i occurred in the stream.

e8c241cee10f.title: Count–min sketch
e8c241cee10f.sentence: Additionally, this estimate has the guarantee that âi≤ai+εN with probability 1−δ, where N=∑i∈𝒰ai is the stream size, i.e. the total number of items seen by the sketch.

58396d19a4b5.title: Count–min sketch
58396d19a4b5.sentence: The parameters w and d can be chosen by setting w = ⌈e/ε⌉ and d = ⌈ln 1/δ⌉, where the error in answering a query is within an additive factor of ε with probability 1 − δ (see below), and e is Euler's number.

f1dee039f134.title: Count–min sketch
f1dee039f134.sentence: Like the count sketch, the Count–min sketch is a linear sketch.

2b5e97d8815c.title: Count–min sketch
2b5e97d8815c.sentence: That is, given two streams, constructing a sketch on each stream and summing the sketches yields the same result as concatenating the streams and constructing a sketch on the concatenated streams.

0fd3668e392f.title: Count–min sketch
0fd3668e392f.sentence: This makes the sketch mergeable and appropriate for use in distributed settings in addition to streaming ones.

67cba5fa327b.title: Count–min sketch
67cba5fa327b.sentence: One potential problem with the usual min estimator for count–min sketches is that they are biased estimators of the true frequency of events: they may overestimate, but never underestimate the true count in a point query.

03a701e3dd9e.title: Count–min sketch
03a701e3dd9e.sentence: Furthermore, while the min estimator works well when the distribution is highly skewed, other sketches such as the Count sketch based on means are more accurate when the distribution is not sufficiently skewed.

0daf2c59bc58.title: Count–min sketch
0daf2c59bc58.sentence: Conservative updating changes the update, but not the query algorithms.

b35de66d377a.title: Count–min sketch
b35de66d377a.sentence: Count–min sketch is an alternative to count sketch and AMS sketch and can be considered an implementation of a counting Bloom filter (Fan et al., 1998) or multistage-filter.

ad8a49c3d623.title: Count–min sketch
ad8a49c3d623.sentence: However, they are used differently and therefore sized differently: a count–min sketch typically has a sublinear number of cells, related to the desired approximation quality of the sketch, while a counting Bloom filter is more typically sized to match the number of elements in the set.

db25519f2dc1.title: Merkle tree
db25519f2dc1.sentence: In cryptography and computer science, a hash tree or Merkle tree is a tree in which every "leaf" node is labelled with the cryptographic hash of a data block, and every node that is not a leaf (called a branch, inner node, or inode) is labelled with the cryptographic hash of the labels of its child nodes.

50f45dd1fe60.title: Merkle tree
50f45dd1fe60.sentence: A hash tree allows efficient and secure verification of the contents of a large data structure.

2818f856b8e8.title: Merkle tree
2818f856b8e8.sentence: Demonstrating that a leaf node is a part of a given binary hash tree requires computing a number of hashes proportional to the logarithm of the number of leaf nodes in the tree.

3c6f124ff824.title: Merkle tree
3c6f124ff824.sentence: Conversely, in a hash list, the number is proportional to the number of leaf nodes itself.

240ccb80d5ba.title: Merkle tree
240ccb80d5ba.sentence: In the top of a hash tree there is a top hash (or root hash or master hash).

eee4b3a030e5.title: Merkle tree
eee4b3a030e5.sentence: Before downloading a file on a P2P network, in most cases the top hash is acquired from a trusted source, for instance a friend or a web site that is known to have good recommendations of files to download.

c7413ca97fff.title: Merkle tree
c7413ca97fff.sentence: When the top hash is available, the hash tree can be received from any non-trusted source, like any peer in the P2P network.

e4b2d0482658.title: Merkle tree
e4b2d0482658.sentence: Then, the received hash tree is checked against the trusted top hash, and if the hash tree is damaged or fake, another hash tree from another source will be tried until the program finds one that matches the top hash.

e8127843f564.title: Merkle tree
e8127843f564.sentence: The main difference from a hash list is that one branch of the hash tree can be downloaded at a time and the integrity of each branch can be checked immediately, even though the whole tree is not available yet.

4312e4f3f4fc.title: Merkle tree
4312e4f3f4fc.sentence: This can be an advantage since it is efficient to split files up in very small data blocks so that only small blocks have to be re-downloaded if they get damaged.

c25e15cf4481.title: Merkle tree
c25e15cf4481.sentence: Most hash tree implementations are binary (two child nodes under each node) but they can just as well use many more child nodes under each node.

7e70136abca4.title: Merkle tree
7e70136abca4.sentence: Usually, a cryptographic hash function such as SHA-2 is used for the hashing.

4b840437afe7.title: Merkle tree
4b840437afe7.sentence: If the hash tree only needs to protect against unintentional damage, non-cryptographic checksums such as CRCs can be used.

ce4d54d64ad0.title: Merkle tree
ce4d54d64ad0.sentence: They can help ensure that data blocks received from other peers in a peer-to-peer network are received undamaged and unaltered, and even to check that the other peers do not lie and send fake blocks.

648f66dd0b6f.title: Merkle tree
648f66dd0b6f.sentence: - ZFS file system (to counter data degradation);

adcf4380f637.title: Merkle tree
adcf4380f637.sentence: - Git and Mercurial distributed revision control systems (although, strictly speaking, they use directed acyclic graphs, not trees);

dc8e49c4aeb3.title: Merkle tree
dc8e49c4aeb3.sentence: - the Bitcoin and Ethereum peer-to-peer networks;

575a4662f943.title: Merkle tree
575a4662f943.sentence: - a number of NoSQL systems such as Apache Cassandra, Riak, and Dynamo.

ab9a3799279e.title: Merkle tree
ab9a3799279e.sentence: The Merkle hash root does not indicate the tree depth, enabling a second-preimage attack in which an attacker creates a document other than the original that has the same Merkle hash root.

a6c07d2f26ee.title: Merkle tree
a6c07d2f26ee.sentence: One simple fix is defined in Certificate Transparency: when computing leaf node hashes, a 0x00 byte is prepended to the hash data, while 0x01 is prepended when computing internal node hashes.

c6b3942bae0a.title: HyperLogLog
c6b3942bae0a.sentence: HyperLogLog is an algorithm for the count-distinct problem, approximating the number of distinct elements in a multiset.

56028d6b06b4.title: HyperLogLog
56028d6b06b4.sentence: Probabilistic cardinality estimators, such as the HyperLogLog algorithm, use significantly less memory than this, but can only approximate the cardinality.

c00f1dd1c0da.title: paper>10.46298/dmtcs.3545
c00f1dd1c0da.sentence: This extended abstract describes and analyses a near-optimal probabilistic algorithm, HYPERLOGLOG, dedicated to estimating the number of \emphdistinct elements (the cardinality) of very large data ensembles.

57061785b177.title: HyperLogLog
57061785b177.sentence: Calculating the exact cardinality of the distinct elements of a multiset requires an amount of memory proportional to the cardinality, which is impractical for very large data sets.

954c43f2e0e8.title: paper>10.46298/dmtcs.3545
954c43f2e0e8.sentence: Using an auxiliary memory of m units (typically, "short bytes''), HYPERLOGLOG performs a single pass over the data and produces an estimate of the cardinality such that the relative accuracy (the standard error) is typically about $1.04/\sqrt{m}$.

a354ec7d7d7b.title: HyperLogLog
a354ec7d7d7b.sentence: The HyperLogLog algorithm is able to estimate cardinalities of > 10^9 with a typical accuracy (standard error) of 2%, using 1.5 kB of memory.

b5ddf89c87d1.title: paper>10.46298/dmtcs.3545
b5ddf89c87d1.sentence: For instance, the new algorithm makes it possible to estimate cardinalities well beyond $10^9$ with a typical accuracy of 2% while using a memory of only 1.5 kilobytes.

a2f87e612e03.title: paper>10.46298/dmtcs.3545
a2f87e612e03.sentence: This improves on the best previously known cardinality estimator, LOGLOG, whose accuracy can be matched by consuming only 64% of the original memory.

ba39b85d2071.title: HyperLogLog
ba39b85d2071.sentence: The basis of the HyperLogLog algorithm is the observation that the cardinality of a multiset of uniformly distributed random numbers can be estimated by calculating the maximum number of leading zeros in the binary representation of each number in the set.

3b2afba93ab5.title: HyperLogLog
3b2afba93ab5.sentence: If the maximum number of leading zeros observed is n, an estimate for the number of distinct elements in the set is 2n.

a9daa41b0418.title: HyperLogLog
a9daa41b0418.sentence: In the HyperLogLog algorithm, a hash function is applied to each element in the original multiset to obtain a multiset of uniformly distributed random numbers with the same cardinality as the original multiset.

0cc2b20c5084.title: HyperLogLog
0cc2b20c5084.sentence: The simple estimate of cardinality obtained using the algorithm above has the disadvantage of a large variance.

cb627ac94cb0.title: HyperLogLog
cb627ac94cb0.sentence: In the HyperLogLog algorithm, the variance is minimised by splitting the multiset into numerous subsets, calculating the maximum number of leading zeros in the numbers in each of these subsets, and using a harmonic mean to combine these estimates for each subset into an estimate of the cardinality of the whole set.

dfd9a92e994f.title: HyperLogLog
dfd9a92e994f.sentence: The data of the HyperLogLog is stored in an array M of m counters (or "registers") that are initialized to 0.

c639f9312855.title: HyperLogLog
c639f9312855.sentence: The add operation consists of computing the hash of the input data v with a hash function h, getting the first b bits (where b is log2(m)), and adding 1 to them to obtain the address of the register to modify (assuming 1-based indexing).

f7b9ffdf9e81.title: HyperLogLog
f7b9ffdf9e81.sentence: With the remaining bits as w, compute ρ(w) which returns the position of the leftmost 1, where leftmost position is 1 (in other words: number of leading zeros plus 1).

e071237063b4.title: HyperLogLog
e071237063b4.sentence: The new value of the register will be the maximum between the current value of the register and ρ(w).

1fa99367a9be.title: HyperLogLog
1fa99367a9be.sentence: The HyperLogLog has three main operations: add to add a new element to the set, count to obtain the cardinality of the set and merge to obtain the union of two sets.

4ede8b554a4b.title: HyperLogLog
4ede8b554a4b.sentence: The count algorithm consists in computing the harmonic mean of the m registers, and using a constant to derive an estimate E of the count:

6f3841448ac0.title: HyperLogLog
6f3841448ac0.sentence: The merge operation for two HLLs (ℎ𝑙𝑙1,ℎ𝑙𝑙2) consists in obtaining the maximum for each pair of registers j:1..m

6d74a5578764.title: HyperLogLog
6d74a5578764.sentence: As this size is fixed, we can consider the running time for the add operation to be O(1).

6e7ff5f55d5e.title: HyperLogLog
6e7ff5f55d5e.sentence: The count and merge operations depend on the number of registers m and have a theoretical cost of O(m).

051af50ef533.title: paper>10.46298/dmtcs.3545
051af50ef533.sentence: The algorithm parallelizes optimally and adapts to the sliding window model.

987f9aa9d622.title: HyperLogLog
987f9aa9d622.sentence: The HyperLogLog technique, though, is biased for small cardinalities below a threshold of 52m.

edd06a8a7acc.title: HyperLogLog
edd06a8a7acc.sentence: The original paper proposes using a different algorithm for small cardinalities known as Linear Counting.

466d9d2b77e7.title: HyperLogLog
466d9d2b77e7.sentence: The HyperLogLog++ algorithm proposes several improvements in the HyperLogLog algorithm to reduce memory requirements and increase accuracy in some ranges of cardinalities:

c59e840b2ce6.title: HyperLogLog
c59e840b2ce6.sentence: - 64-bit hash function is used instead of the 32 bits used in the original paper.

72aedb73dc21.title: HyperLogLog
72aedb73dc21.sentence: An empirical bias correction is proposed to mitigate the problem.

ea05de7785b4.title: HyperLogLog
ea05de7785b4.sentence: - A sparse representation of the registers is proposed to reduce memory requirements for small cardinalities, which can be later transformed to a dense representation if the cardinality grows.

223b657265e5.title: Bloom filter
223b657265e5.sentence: To prevent caching one-hit-wonders, a Bloom filter is used to keep track of all URLs that are accessed by users.

3d07632e27e8.title: Bloom filter
3d07632e27e8.sentence: A web object is cached only when it has been accessed at least once before, i.e., the object is cached on its second request.

9cf352b4a490.title: Bloom filter
9cf352b4a490.sentence: Nearly three-quarters of the URLs accessed from a typical web cache are "one-hit-wonders" that are accessed by users only once and never again.

9d6646c72f1e.title: Bloom filter
9d6646c72f1e.sentence: It is clearly wasteful of disk resources to store one-hit-wonders in a web cache, since they will never be accessed again.

57b4b7dcfed1.title: Bloom filter
57b4b7dcfed1.sentence: The use of a Bloom filter in this fashion significantly reduces the disk write workload, since most one-hit-wonders are not written to the disk cache.

c4b35b7bb995.title: Bloom filter
c4b35b7bb995.sentence: Further, filtering out the one-hit-wonders also saves cache space on disk, increasing the cache hit rates.

c27b3b2a91fd.title: Bloom filter
c27b3b2a91fd.sentence: - The servers of Akamai Technologies, a content delivery provider, use Bloom filters to prevent "one-hit-wonders" from being stored in its disk caches.

1d9b0b0d019c.title: Bloom filter
1d9b0b0d019c.sentence: Using a Bloom filter to detect the second request for a web object and caching that object only on its second request prevents one-hit wonders from entering the disk cache, significantly reducing disk workload and increasing disk cache hit rates.

c96c12d568e5.title: Bloom filter
c96c12d568e5.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
c96c12d568e5.sentence: Counting filters provide a way to implement a delete operation on a Bloom filter without recreating the filter afresh.

aef02a0ad86e.title: Bloom filter
aef02a0ad86e.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
aef02a0ad86e.sentence: In fact, regular Bloom filters can be considered as counting filters with a bucket size of one bit.

0e622c5f647e.title: Bloom filter
0e622c5f647e.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
0e622c5f647e.sentence: The insert operation is extended to increment the value of the buckets, and the lookup operation checks that each of the required buckets is non-zero.

d02964edf3c6.title: Bloom filter
d02964edf3c6.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
d02964edf3c6.sentence: The delete operation then consists of decrementing the value of each of the respective buckets.

9d6c787c4d0d.title: Bloom filter
9d6c787c4d0d.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
9d6c787c4d0d.sentence: The size of counters is usually 3 or 4 bits.

8ab29d940a17.title: Bloom filter
8ab29d940a17.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
8ab29d940a17.sentence: Hence counting Bloom filters use 3 to 4 times more space than static Bloom filters.

db2540ec7b1f.title: Bloom filter
db2540ec7b1f.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
db2540ec7b1f.sentence: Arithmetic overflow of the buckets is a problem and the buckets should be sufficiently large to make this case rare.

a4a0ac1a1aa3.title: Bloom filter
a4a0ac1a1aa3.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
a4a0ac1a1aa3.sentence: Because the counting Bloom filter table cannot be expanded, the maximal number of keys to be stored simultaneously in the filter must be known in advance.

b8093d4ea559.title: Bloom filter
b8093d4ea559.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
b8093d4ea559.sentence: Once the designed capacity of the table is exceeded, the false positive rate will grow rapidly as more keys are inserted.

617242220257.title: Bloom filter
617242220257.section: Extensions and applications > Counting Bloom filters
617242220257.sentence: Another issue with counting filters is limited scalability.

6cd3ed9e8f2c.title: Bloom filter
6cd3ed9e8f2c.sentence: Many alternatives to Bloom filters, including quotient filters and cuckoo filters, are based on the idea of hashing keys to random (log⁡n+log⁡ϵ−1)-bit fingerprints, and then storing those fingerprints in a compact hash table.

64c8077afbea.title: Bloom filter
64c8077afbea.sentence: Another alternative to classic Bloom filter is the cuckoo filter, based on space-efficient variants of cuckoo hashing.

0c9942ea6723.title: Bloom filter
0c9942ea6723.sentence: Classic Bloom filters use 1.44log2(1/ε) bits of space per inserted key, where ε is the false positive rate of the Bloom filter.

21e2985b3da5.title: Bloom filter
21e2985b3da5.sentence: However, the space that is strictly necessary for any data structure playing the same role as a Bloom filter is only log2(1/ε) per key.

3e178069b9bc.title: Bloom filter
3e178069b9bc.sentence: Hence Bloom filters use 44% more space than an equivalent optimal data structure.

6e0760b1437f.title: Bloom filter
6e0760b1437f.sentence: In this case, a hash table is constructed, holding neither keys nor values, but short fingerprints (small hashes) of the keys.

644c5b969c19.title: Bloom filter
644c5b969c19.sentence: If looking up the key finds a matching fingerprint, then key is probably in the set.

72aca3a16ad4.title: Bloom filter
72aca3a16ad4.sentence: Cuckoo filters support deletions and have better locality of reference than Bloom filters.

ed948cf78e5c.title: Bloom filter
ed948cf78e5c.sentence: Advantages of the quotient filter, when compared to the Bloom filter, include its locality of reference and the ability to support deletions.

26aef9b638f6.title: Bloom filter
26aef9b638f6.sentence: Graf & Lemire (2020) describes an approach called an xor filter, where they store fingerprints in a particular type of perfect hash table, producing a filter which is more memory efficient (1.23log2(1/ε) bits per key) and faster than Bloom or cuckoo filters.

75817f1f752b.title: Bloom filter
75817f1f752b.sentence: (The time saving comes from the fact that a lookup requires exactly three memory accesses, which can all execute in parallel.) However, filter creation is more complex than Bloom and cuckoo filters, and it is not possible to modify the set after creation.

82e0844ba13c.title: Quadtree
82e0844ba13c.sentence: Quadtrees may be classified according to the type of data they represent, including areas, points, lines and curves.

20c56c1ded9f.title: Quadtree
20c56c1ded9f.sentence: Quadtrees may also be classified by whether the shape of the tree is independent of the order in which data is processed.

9d7a6cc6af85.title: Quadtree
9d7a6cc6af85.sentence: The region quadtree represents a partition of space in two dimensions by decomposing the region into four equal quadrants, subquadrants, and so on with each leaf node containing data corresponding to a specific subregion.

0db98193383a.title: Quadtree
0db98193383a.sentence: Each node in the tree either has exactly four children, or has no children (a leaf node).

47eab860dfa3.title: Quadtree
47eab860dfa3.sentence: The height of quadtrees that follow this decomposition strategy (i.e. subdividing subquadrants as long as there is interesting data in the subquadrant for which more refinement is desired) is sensitive to and dependent on the spatial distribution of interesting areas in the space being decomposed.

c8363f57c92f.title: Quadtree
c8363f57c92f.sentence: The point quadtree is an adaptation of a binary tree used to represent two-dimensional point data.

ce5ca9c261e2.title: Quadtree
ce5ca9c261e2.sentence: It shares the features of all quadtrees but is a true tree as the center of a subdivision is always on a point.

5e6542fa8fbf.title: Quadtree
5e6542fa8fbf.section: Types > Point quadtree > Node structure for a point quadtree
5e6542fa8fbf.sentence: A node of a point quadtree is similar to a node of a binary tree, with the major difference being that it has four pointers (one for each quadrant) instead of two ("left" and "right") as in an ordinary binary tree.

c4f2e341c98e.title: Quadtree
c4f2e341c98e.sentence: It is often very efficient in comparing two-dimensional, ordered data points, usually operating in O(log n) time.

205931abf9dd.title: Quadtree
205931abf9dd.sentence: Point quadtrees are worth mentioning for completeness, but they have been surpassed by k-d trees as tools for generalized binary search.

6461c68e86fa.title: Quadtree
6461c68e86fa.sentence: Point-region (PR) quadtrees are very similar to region quadtrees.

ee69ab225332.title: Quadtree
ee69ab225332.sentence: In a region quadtree, a uniform value is stored that applies to the entire area of the cell of a leaf.

9a42a87e85bd.title: Quadtree
9a42a87e85bd.sentence: The cells of a PR quadtree, however, store a list of points that exist within the cell of a leaf.

090922bdf5eb.title: Quadtree
090922bdf5eb.sentence: Like the point quadtree, the PR quadtree may also have a linear height when given a "bad" set.

e3c6580577cf.title: Quadtree
e3c6580577cf.sentence: Edge quadtrees (much like PM quadtrees) are used to store lines rather than points.

227a72208294.title: Quadtree
227a72208294.sentence: The polygonal map quadtree (or PM Quadtree) is a variation of quadtree which is used to store collections of polygons that may be degenerate (meaning that they have isolated vertices or edges).

182ce48e1c55.title: Quadtree
182ce48e1c55.sentence: If we were to store every node corresponding to a subdivided cell, we may end up storing a lot of empty nodes.

e01dd9317205.title: Quadtree
e01dd9317205.sentence: We can cut down on the size of such sparse trees by only storing subtrees whose leaves have interesting data (i.e. "important subtrees").

c24a488f02fe.title: Geohash
c24a488f02fe.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
c24a488f02fe.sentence: Geohashes can be used to find points in proximity to each other based on a common prefix.

6ebe54c916c2.title: Geohash
6ebe54c916c2.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
6ebe54c916c2.sentence: However, edge case locations close to each other but on opposite sides of the 180 degree meridian will result in Geohash codes with no common prefix (different longitudes for near physical locations).

ee3fee733a0d.title: Geohash
ee3fee733a0d.sentence: Geohashing guarantees that the longer a shared prefix between two geohashes is, the spatially closer they are together.

cc72468ef672.title: Geohash
cc72468ef672.sentence: The reverse of this is not guaranteed, as two points can be very close but have a short or no shared prefix.

be5b11ae0a45.title: Geohash
be5b11ae0a45.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
be5b11ae0a45.sentence: However, two points with a long common prefix will be close by.

4b10a513ac99.title: Geohash
4b10a513ac99.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
4b10a513ac99.sentence: Points close to the North and South poles will have very different geohashes (different longitudes for near physical locations).

c8cd3e7b76c2.title: Geohash
c8cd3e7b76c2.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
c8cd3e7b76c2.sentence: Two close locations on either side of the Equator (or Greenwich meridian) will not have a long common prefix since they belong to different 'halves' of the world.

4f44c03376e6.title: Geohash
4f44c03376e6.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
4f44c03376e6.sentence: In order to do a proximity search, one could compute the southwest corner (low geohash with low latitude and longitude) and northeast corner (high geohash with high latitude and longitude) of a bounding box and search for geohashes between those two.

a1773b8d3c03.title: Geohash
a1773b8d3c03.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
a1773b8d3c03.sentence: This search will retrieve all points in the z-order curve between the two corners, which can be far too many points.

bdd56035b477.title: Geohash
bdd56035b477.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Edge cases
bdd56035b477.sentence: This method also breaks down at the 180 meridians and the poles.

399e433bcad1.title: Geohash
399e433bcad1.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Non-linearity
399e433bcad1.sentence: Since a geohash (in this implementation) is based on coordinates of longitude and latitude the distance between two geohashes reflects the distance in latitude/longitude coordinates between two points, which does not translate to actual distance, see Haversine formula.

4bb416268594.title: Geohash
4bb416268594.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Non-linearity
4bb416268594.sentence: Note that these limitations are not due to geohashing, and not due to latitude-longitude coordinates, but due to the difficulty of mapping coordinates on a sphere (non linear and with wrapping of values, similar to modulo arithmetic) to two dimensional coordinates and the difficulty of exploring a two dimensional space uniformly.

7f9cb6635f53.title: Geohash
7f9cb6635f53.section: Limitations when used for deciding proximity > Non-linearity
7f9cb6635f53.sentence: Despite those issues, there are possible workarounds, and the algorithm has been successfully used in Elasticsearch, MongoDB, HBase, Redis, and Accumulo to implement proximity searches.

558256fd3d44.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
558256fd3d44.sentence: Load balancing lets us distribute incoming network traffic across multiple resources ensuring high availability and reliability by sending requests only to resources that are online.

f7e8889371c5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
f7e8889371c5.sentence: Modern high-traffic websites must serve hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of concurrent requests from users or clients.

e017c04c5fc5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
e017c04c5fc5.sentence: To cost-effectively scale to meet these high volumes, modern computing best practice generally requires adding more servers.

9c0f1e1f9808.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
9c0f1e1f9808.sentence: A load balancer can sit in front of the servers and route client requests across all servers capable of fulfilling those requests in a manner that maximizes speed and capacity utilization.

83f0acf8ecd6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
83f0acf8ecd6.sentence: This ensures that no single server is overworked, which could degrade performance.

4dede61ce584.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
4dede61ce584.sentence: If a single server goes down, the load balancer redirects traffic to the remaining online servers.

406092bd5d61.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
406092bd5d61.sentence: When a new server is added to the server group, the load balancer automatically starts sending requests to it.

34c14c8fb30a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/key-use-cases-for-load-balancers.md
34c14c8fb30a.sentence: - Scalability Load balancers facilitate horizontal scaling by effectively managing increased traffic.

3eb668d51d85.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/key-use-cases-for-load-balancers.md
3eb668d51d85.sentence: Additional servers can be easily added to the pool, and the load balancer will distribute traffic across all servers.

8e7ec0cc0f6c.title: Load balancing (computing)
8e7ec0cc0f6c.sentence: In addition to efficient problem solving through parallel computations, load balancing algorithms are widely used in HTTP request management where a site with a large audience must be able to handle a large number of requests per second.

258867f9b312.title: Load balancing (computing)
258867f9b312.sentence: One of the most commonly used applications of load balancing is to provide a single Internet service from multiple servers, sometimes known as a server farm.

692817f390e4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/key-use-cases-for-load-balancers.md
692817f390e4.sentence: - Traffic Distribution Load balancers evenly distribute incoming traffic among multiple servers, preventing any single server from becoming overwhelmed.

67fd9f8903f4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/key-use-cases-for-load-balancers.md
67fd9f8903f4.sentence: - High Availability Load balancers enhance system availability by rerouting traffic away from failed or unhealthy servers to healthy ones.

77172054c9df.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/key-use-cases-for-load-balancers.md
77172054c9df.sentence: - SSL Termination Load balancers can offload SSL/TLS encryption and decryption tasks from backend servers, reducing their workload and improving overall performance.

2def90eb6214.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/key-use-cases-for-load-balancers.md
2def90eb6214.sentence: - Session Persistence For applications that require maintaining a user's session on a specific server, load balancers can ensure that subsequent requests from a user are sent to the same server.

51ed6fc8e07c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/key-use-cases-for-load-balancers.md
51ed6fc8e07c.sentence: - Health Monitoring Load balancers continuously monitor the health and performance of servers, removing failed or unhealthy servers from the pool to maintain optimal performance.

cfc2045c4c17.title: Load balancing (computing)
cfc2045c4c17.sentence: A load-balancing algorithm always tries to answer a specific problem.

709844ffa0b5.title: Load balancing (computing)
709844ffa0b5.sentence: Among other things, the nature of the tasks, the algorithmic complexity, the hardware architecture on which the algorithms will run as well as required error tolerance, must be taken into account.

9b669f44acb3.title: Load balancing (computing)
9b669f44acb3.sentence: Therefore compromise must be found to best meet application-specific requirements.

2e74a35ac491.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
2e74a35ac491.sentence: DNS load balancing is the practice of configuring a domain in the Domain Name System (DNS) such that client requests to the domain are distributed across a group of server machines.

55c9bcdf6d6a.title: Load balancing (computing)
55c9bcdf6d6a.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > Round-robin DNS
55c9bcdf6d6a.sentence: Round-robin DNS is an alternate method of load balancing that does not require a dedicated software or hardware node.

7b4bb570339c.title: Load balancing (computing)
7b4bb570339c.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > Round-robin DNS
7b4bb570339c.sentence: In this technique, multiple IP addresses are associated with a single domain name; clients are given IP in a round-robin fashion.

0b7f0b5d7906.title: Load balancing (computing)
0b7f0b5d7906.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > Round-robin DNS
0b7f0b5d7906.sentence: IP is assigned to clients with a short expiration so the client is more likely to use a different IP the next time they access the Internet service being requested.

1e846d3a77b2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
1e846d3a77b2.sentence: Unfortunately, DNS load balancing has inherent problems limiting its reliability and efficiency.

6a1aa2f484f1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
6a1aa2f484f1.sentence: Most significantly, DNS does not check for server and network outages, or errors.

ecb187795e91.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
ecb187795e91.sentence: It always returns the same set of IP addresses for a domain even if servers are down or inaccessible.

3cf606500757.title: Load balancing (computing)
3cf606500757.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > DNS delegation
3cf606500757.sentence: Another more effective technique for load-balancing using DNS is to delegate www.example.org as a sub-domain whose zone is served by each of the same servers that are serving the website.

ea3f4073341b.title: Load balancing (computing)
ea3f4073341b.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > DNS delegation
ea3f4073341b.sentence: However, the zone file for www.example.org on each server is different such that each server resolves its own IP Address as the A-record.

a539b97bf671.title: Load balancing (computing)
a539b97bf671.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > DNS delegation
a539b97bf671.sentence: This way, when a server is down, its DNS will not respond and the web service does not receive any traffic.

7cbd7f70a804.title: Load balancing (computing)
7cbd7f70a804.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > DNS delegation
7cbd7f70a804.sentence: Furthermore, the quickest DNS response to the resolver is nearly always the one from the network's closest server, ensuring geo-sensitive load-balancing.

c96f7dc950ab.title: Load balancing (computing)
c96f7dc950ab.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > DNS delegation
c96f7dc950ab.sentence: This technique works particularly well where individual servers are spread geographically on the Internet.

a4f171fa2a3c.title: Load balancing (computing)
a4f171fa2a3c.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > DNS delegation
a4f171fa2a3c.sentence: A short TTL on the A-record helps to ensure traffic is quickly diverted when a server goes down.

42b39fb81ec8.title: Load balancing (computing)
42b39fb81ec8.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > DNS delegation
42b39fb81ec8.sentence: Consideration must be given to the possibility that this technique may cause individual clients to switch between individual servers in mid-session.

a02a8c66f732.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
a02a8c66f732.sentence: The simplest solution is to return multiple A or AAAA records in the DNS reply and let the client pick an IP address arbitrarily.

0ac004377631.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
0ac004377631.sentence: The first problem is that it provides very little control over the client behavior: records are selected randomly, and each will attract a roughly equal amount of traffic.

5a4abfdf63ae.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
5a4abfdf63ae.sentence: In theory, we could use SRV records to specify record weights and priorities, but SRV records have not yet been adopted for HTTP.

a5c5975795ce.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
a5c5975795ce.sentence: Recursive resolution of IP addresses is problematic, as the IP address seen by the authoritative nameserver does not belong to a user; instead, itâs the recursive resolverâs.

1b355ce728cc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
1b355ce728cc.sentence: This is a serious limitation, because it only allows reply optimization for the shortest distance between resolver and the nameserver.

d836de4009c6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
d836de4009c6.sentence: A possible solution is to use the EDNS0 extension proposed in [Con15], which includes information about the clientâs subnet in the DNS query sent by a recursive resolver.

41936299adf2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
41936299adf2.sentence: We can mitigate this scenario by using an anycast address for authoritative nameservers and leverage the fact that DNS queries will flow to the closest address.

a52c7d943dc2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
a52c7d943dc2.sentence: A further improvement builds a map of all networks and their approximate physical locations, and serves DNS replies based on that mapping.

cec346af17b4.title: Load balancing (computing)
cec346af17b4.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > Server-side load balancers > Scheduling algorithms
cec346af17b4.sentence: Numerous scheduling algorithms, also called load-balancing methods, are used by load balancers to determine which back-end server to send a request to.

93245c6e2588.title: Load balancing (computing)
93245c6e2588.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > Server-side load balancers > Scheduling algorithms
93245c6e2588.sentence: Simple algorithms include random choice, round robin, or least connections.

0b09413b5f9b.title: Load balancing (computing)
0b09413b5f9b.section: Use cases > Internet-based services > Server-side load balancers > Scheduling algorithms
0b09413b5f9b.sentence: More sophisticated load balancers may take additional factors into account, such as a server's reported load, least response times, up/down status (determined by a monitoring poll of some kind), a number of active connections, geographic location, capabilities, or how much traffic it has recently been assigned.

d2006c70ec83.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-load-balancing-algorithms.md
d2006c70ec83.sentence: - Round robin The client requests are sent to different service instances in sequential order.

e9fe63064197.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-load-balancing-algorithms.md
e9fe63064197.sentence: - Hash This algorithm applies a hash function on the incoming requests’ IP or URL.

8340a6800efe.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-load-balancing-algorithms.md

c3da46771738.title: Load balancing (computing)

6ddf4dddf137.title: Load balancing (computing)
6ddf4dddf137.sentence: This can be much less expensive and more flexible than failover approaches where every single live component is paired with a single backup component that takes over in the event of a failure (dual modular redundancy).

f75a7cfae7db.title: Load balancing (computing)

537bca86d195.title: Load balancing (computing)

cdeabd71b41b.title: Proxy server

31a056b05e14.sentence: Depending on the workload, processing the encryption and authentication requirements of a TLS request can become a major part of the demand on the Web Server's CPU; as the demand increases, users will see slower response times, as the TLS overhead is distributed among Web servers.

d8775c6c6391.sentence: One clear benefit to TLS offloading in the balancer is that it enables it to do balancing or content switching based on data in the HTTPS request.

ba773da1fd89.title: Load balancing (computing)

1a54296ba346.sentence: The fundamental feature of a load balancer is to be able to distribute incoming requests over a number of backend servers in the cluster according to a scheduling algorithm.

737a671020e7.sentence: This is sometimes used as a simple way to account for some servers having more capacity than others, though it may not always work as desired.

15a684a20bd0.title: Load balancing (computing)

15a684a20bd0.sentence: When the number of available servers drops below a certain number, or the load gets too high, standby servers can be brought online.

6a9ed3b8f5c7.sentence: Load balancers can provide features such as SYN cookies and delayed-binding (the back-end servers don't see the client until it finishes its TCP handshake) to mitigate SYN flood attacks and generally offload work from the servers to a more efficient platform.

9ccd3e90c388.sentence: The larger the response and the further away the client is, the more this feature can improve response times.

7650ae286e58.sentence: The trade-off is that this feature puts additional CPU demand on the load balancer and could be done by web servers instead.
