7478bbc54914.sentence: The load balancer can buffer responses from the server and spoon-feed the data out to slow clients, allowing the webserver to free a thread for other tasks faster than it would if it had to send the entire request to the client directly.

682450e06e2b.title: Proxy server
682450e06e2b.sentence: In computer networking, a proxy server is an intermediary server application between a client requesting a resource and the server then providing that resource.

b00c50326f57.title: Proxy server
b00c50326f57.sentence: Instead of connecting directly to a server that can fulfil a request for a resource, such as a file or web page, the client directs the request to the proxy server, which evaluates the request and performs the required network transactions.

fd1ba2fd4a8d.title: Proxy server
fd1ba2fd4a8d.sentence: This serves as a method to control the complexity of the request or provide additional benefits such as load balancing, privacy or security.

a46214f0ff53.title: Proxy server
a46214f0ff53.sentence: Proxies were devised to add structure and encapsulation to distributed systems.

4b6d5ec59105.title: Proxy server
4b6d5ec59105.sentence: A proxy server may reside on the user's local computer, or at any point between the user's computer and the destination servers.

9a992e1c9443.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::proxy
9a992e1c9443.sentence: Typically, proxies are used to filter requests, log requests, or sometimes transform requests (by adding/removing headers, encrypting/decrypting, or compression).

8c836a1da264.title: Proxy server
8c836a1da264.sentence: A proxy server that passes unmodified requests and responses is usually called a gateway or sometimes a tunneling proxy.

14e4462d52dc.title: Proxy server

14e4462d52dc.sentence: The request from the client is the same as a regular HTTP request except the full URL is passed, instead of just the path.

236ab6519320.title: Proxy server

236ab6519320.sentence: This request is sent to the proxy server, the proxy makes the request specified, and returns the response.

1528df478e50.title: Proxy server
1528df478e50.sentence: - Forwarding headers: Some proxies append HTTP headers to disclose client or proxy information that would otherwise be lost when a request is forwarded.

480c794908d9.title: Proxy server
480c794908d9.sentence: Historically this has often been done with non-standard fields such as X-Forwarded-For, while the standardised Forwarded field provides a defined syntax for similar information.

aca7b98886e6.title: Proxy server
aca7b98886e6.sentence: Such headers are deployment-dependent and should not be treated as inherently trustworthy, since they may be absent, modified, or contain values added by multiple proxies.

3bea9e576e29.sentence: The proxy concept refers to a layer-7 application in the OSI reference model.

9b3cdc0126c0.title: Proxy server
9b3cdc0126c0.section: Implementations of proxies > Comparison to network address translators
9b3cdc0126c0.sentence: Because NAT operates at layer 3, it is less resource-intensive than the layer-7 proxy, but also less flexible.

45f7c4674315.sentence: A forward proxy, often called a proxy, proxy server, or web proxy is a server that sits in front of a group of client machines.

6ee5cd4b4da5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::proxy
6ee5cd4b4da5.sentence: When those computers make requests to sites and services on the internet, the proxy server intercepts those requests and then communicates with web servers on behalf of those clients, like a middleman.

94fc1b6f247c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::proxy
94fc1b6f247c.sentence: A simplified way to sum it up would be to say that a forward proxy sits in front of a client and ensures that no origin server ever communicates directly with that specific client.

ad5689ca525c.title: Proxy server
ad5689ca525c.section: Types > Reverse proxies > Forward proxy vs. reverse proxy
ad5689ca525c.sentence: This means it can regulate traffic according to preset policies, convert and mask client IP addresses, enforce security protocols, and block unknown traffic.

51a4a24d29a8.title: Proxy server
51a4a24d29a8.section: Types > Reverse proxies > Forward proxy vs. reverse proxy
51a4a24d29a8.sentence: A forward proxy enhances security and policy enforcement within an internal network.

00818e91f29e.sentence: A content-filtering web proxy server provides administrative control over the content that may be relayed in one or both directions through the proxy.

35ed01dca733.sentence: It also usually produces logs, either to give detailed information about the URLs accessed by specific users or to monitor bandwidth usage statistics.

f50806879237.sentence: An open proxy is a forwarding proxy server that is accessible by any Internet user.

27c9c796f39f.sentence: - Anonymous proxy: This server reveals its identity as a proxy server but does not disclose the originating IP address of the client.

158b1e50d52d.sentence: Web filtering proxies are not able to peer inside secure sockets HTTP transactions, assuming the chain-of-trust of SSL/TLS (Transport Layer Security) has not been tampered with.

335d1290cfdb.title: Reverse proxy
335d1290cfdb.sentence: In computer networks, a reverse proxy or surrogate server is a proxy server that appears to any client to be an ordinary web server, but in reality merely acts as an intermediary that forwards the client's requests to one or more ordinary web servers.

659734bcba37.title: Proxy server
659734bcba37.sentence: Reverse proxies send requests to one or more ordinary servers that handle the request.

328dcbe57fe7.title: Proxy server
328dcbe57fe7.sentence: The response from the original server is returned as if it came directly from the proxy server, leaving the client with no knowledge of the original server.

6dfbade61083.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::proxy
6dfbade61083.sentence: On the other hand, a reverse proxy sits in front of an origin server and ensures that no client ever communicates directly with that origin server.

12806f4a141e.title: Reverse proxy
12806f4a141e.sentence: An important advantage of doing so is that the web servers can be hidden behind a firewall (often a Web application firewall) on a company-internal network, and only the reverse proxy needs to be directly exposed to the Internet.

e0eb0dff6cf8.title: Reverse proxy
e0eb0dff6cf8.sentence: Reverse proxies differ from forward proxies, which are used when the client is restricted to a private, internal network and asks a forward proxy to retrieve resources from the public Internet.

f5c8e0fada67.title: Proxy server
f5c8e0fada67.section: Types > Reverse proxies > Forward proxy vs. reverse proxy
f5c8e0fada67.sentence: A reverse proxy, instead of protecting the client, is used to protect the servers.

37a8c131a955.title: Reverse proxy
37a8c131a955.sentence: Reverse proxies can inspect HTTP headers, which, for example, allows them to present a single IP address to the Internet while relaying requests to different internal servers based on the URL of the HTTP request.

a90656bd39b0.title: Reverse proxy
a90656bd39b0.sentence: A reverse proxy can distribute the load from incoming requests to several servers, with each server supporting its own application area.

843e9ea3c70c.title: Reverse proxy
843e9ea3c70c.sentence: In the case of reverse proxying web servers, the reverse proxy may have to rewrite the URL in each incoming request in order to match the relevant internal location of the requested resource.

488e00969dd2.title: Proxy server

127ee2d5069e.title: Reverse proxy
127ee2d5069e.sentence: A reverse proxy can optimize content by compressing it in order to speed up loading times.

559aaad49f79.title: Reverse proxy
559aaad49f79.sentence: Reverse proxies can keep a cache of static content, which further reduces the load on these internal servers and the internal network.

686fec1b1425.title: Reverse proxy
686fec1b1425.sentence: A reverse proxy can reduce load on its origin servers by caching static content and dynamic content, known as web acceleration.

9b61d7a83653.title: Reverse proxy
9b61d7a83653.sentence: Proxy caches of this sort can often satisfy a considerable number of website requests, greatly reducing the load on the origin server(s).

b37ffef60017.title: Reverse proxy
b37ffef60017.sentence: In a technique named "spoon-feeding", a dynamically generated page can be produced in its entirety and served to the reverse proxy, which can feed the page to the client as the connection allows.

d9b526cfb04d.title: Reverse proxy
d9b526cfb04d.sentence: The program that generates the page need not remain open, thus releasing server resources during the possibly extended time the client requires to complete the transfer.

6b4c9ca6cbe2.title: Proxy server
6b4c9ca6cbe2.sentence: - Spoon feeding: reduces resource usage caused by slow clients on the web servers by caching the content the web server sent and slowly "spoon feeding" it to the client.

c216ac3d1a18.title: Reverse proxy
c216ac3d1a18.sentence: Application firewall features can protect against common web-based attacks, like a denial-of-service attack (DoS) or distributed denial-of-service attacks (DDoS).

25b60a7f74be.title: Reverse proxy

816bf8b41097.title: Proxy server

bbccfc8cbc7c.title: HAProxy

047e0a7c8a37.title: HAProxy

531d1dbe5fc8.title: HAProxy

8a225bb9bd69.title: HAProxy
8a225bb9bd69.sentence: 64-core ARM servers were shown to reach 2 million requests per second and 100 Gbit/s.

77b3a81d39ef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway
77b3a81d39ef.sentence: It is a single entry point into a system that encapsulates the internal system architecture and provides an API that is tailored to each client.

f71667037a8e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/api-gateway-101.md
f71667037a8e.sentence: An API gateway is a server that acts as an API front-end, receiving API requests, enforcing throttling and security policies, passing requests to the back-end service, and then returning the appropriate result to the client.

7a0e62d7be57.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway
7a0e62d7be57.section: Why do we need an API Gateway?
7a0e62d7be57.sentence: The granularity of APIs provided by microservices is often different than what a client needs.

0afc47a48245.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway
0afc47a48245.section: Why do we need an API Gateway?
0afc47a48245.sentence: Microservices typically provide fine-grained APIs, which means that clients need to interact with multiple services.

c7209b9a9033.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway
c7209b9a9033.section: Why do we need an API Gateway?
c7209b9a9033.sentence: Hence, an API gateway can provide a single entry point for all clients with some additional features and better management.

5629a3527089.title: Proxy server
5629a3527089.sentence: A caching proxy server accelerates service requests by retrieving the content saved from a previous request made by the same client or even other clients.

d2650eb51eb6.title: Proxy server
d2650eb51eb6.sentence: Caching proxies were the first kind of proxy server.

9152fd6b1352.title: Proxy server
9152fd6b1352.sentence: Web proxies are commonly used to cache web pages from a web server.

b3f3728effc1.title: Proxy server
b3f3728effc1.sentence: Caching proxies keep local copies of frequently requested resources, allowing large organizations to significantly reduce their upstream bandwidth usage and costs, while significantly increasing performance.

08da61e8510e.title: Proxy server
08da61e8510e.sentence: Most ISPs and large businesses have a caching proxy.

90b1580c041d.title: Proxy server
90b1580c041d.sentence: Poorly implemented caching proxies can cause problems, such as an inability to use user authentication.

692b8b64b7ff.title: Proxy server
692b8b64b7ff.sentence: A proxy that is designed to mitigate specific link-related issues or degradation is a Performance Enhancing Proxy (PEPs).

88ecb4200ce8.title: Proxy server
88ecb4200ce8.sentence: These are typically used to improve TCP performance in the presence of high round-trip times or high packet loss (such as wireless or mobile phone networks); or highly asymmetric links featuring very different upload and download rates.

1338a5ac04dd.title: Proxy server
1338a5ac04dd.sentence: PEPs can make more efficient use of the network, for example, by merging TCP ACKs (acknowledgements) or compressing data sent at the application layer.

c3f4a105da64.title: Nginx
c3f4a105da64.sentence: nginx (pronounced "engine x" /ˌɛndʒɪnˈɛks/ EN-jin-EKS, stylized as NGINX) is a web server that can also be used as a reverse proxy, load balancer, mail proxy and HTTP cache.

e31c4306c3ec.title: Nginx
e31c4306c3ec.sentence: nginx may be configured to serve static web content or to act as a proxy server.

8ac18c1a4fef.title: Nginx
8ac18c1a4fef.sentence: nginx can be deployed to also serve dynamic content on the network using FastCGI, SCGI handlers for scripts, WSGI application servers or Phusion Passenger modules, and can serve as a software load balancer.

d3e5ed2343f2.title: Nginx
d3e5ed2343f2.sentence: nginx uses an asynchronous event-driven approach, rather than threads, to handle requests.nginx's modular event-driven architecture can provide predictable performance under high loads.

e5385677e4b6.title: Nginx
e5385677e4b6.section: Features > HTTP proxy and Web server features

4f9b87448f9b.title: Nginx

4f9b87448f9b.sentence: - Load balancing with in-band health checks

bb23ff318ef5.title: Nginx

bb23ff318ef5.sentence: - TLS/SSL with SNI and OCSP stapling support, via OpenSSL

c0bd357eba23.title: Nginx

c0bd357eba23.sentence: - Name- and IP address-based virtual servers

0c33ff441b6e.title: Nginx

0c33ff441b6e.sentence: - Automatic issuance and renewal of TLS certificates using the ACME protocol

b8f0a09c5e95.title: Nginx
b8f0a09c5e95.section: Features > HTTP proxy and Web server features

290ea74e9f24.title: Nginx

290ea74e9f24.sentence: - WebSockets since 1.3.13, including acting as a reverse proxy and load balancing of WebSocket applications

7210e767ea8b.title: Nginx

7210e767ea8b.sentence: - HTTP/2 protocol support, including as an upstream/backend protocol via the "ngx_http_proxy_module" since version 1.29.4

ebecb69860fa.title: Nginx
ebecb69860fa.section: Features > HTTP proxy and Web server features

b4ca4eedf9fd.title: Nginx

aa412be70dbe.title: Nginx
aa412be70dbe.sentence: While nginx initially outperformed, Apache has offered similar performance since version 2.4.

e17944aea3cc.title: Nginx
e17944aea3cc.sentence: This former performance boost came at a cost of decreased flexibility, such as the ability to override system-wide access settings on a per-file basis (Apache accomplishes this with an.htaccess file, while nginx has no such feature built in).

a2a569eec619.title: Nginx

3e1e9b969f4d.title: Nginx

a36ff26b3a5b.title: Proxy server
a36ff26b3a5b.sentence: An intercepting proxy redirects or filters client traffic without being explicitly selected by the client.

d81752a199c6.title: Proxy server
d81752a199c6.sentence: It is therefore often deployed without requiring browser or application proxy settings, and clients may be unaware that their traffic is passing through a proxy.

d72fdb9747e5.title: Proxy server
d72fdb9747e5.sentence: In HTTP terminology, an interception proxy differs from a conventional HTTP proxy because it is not chosen by the user agent; instead, it is placed in the network path and filters or redirects outgoing traffic, commonly TCP port 80 traffic.

c96c9ccc58b3.title: Proxy server
c96c9ccc58b3.sentence: In deployment contexts, interception proxies are also commonly called transparent proxies, but this usage should be distinguished from older HTTP terminology, where a "transparent proxy" meant a proxy that did not modify requests or responses beyond what was required for proxy authentication and identification.

3def2a4728a4.title: Proxy server
3def2a4728a4.section: Implementations of proxies > Transparent proxy > Purpose
3def2a4728a4.sentence: Intercepting proxies are commonly used in businesses to enforce acceptable use policies and to ease administrative overheads since no client browser configuration is required.

4d56d1ab3467.title: Proxy server
4d56d1ab3467.section: Implementations of proxies > Transparent proxy > Purpose
4d56d1ab3467.sentence: Intercepting proxies are also commonly used by ISPs in some countries to save upstream bandwidth and improve customer response times by caching.

77cb7dd73294.title: Proxy server
77cb7dd73294.section: Implementations of proxies > Transparent proxy > Issues
77cb7dd73294.sentence: First, the original destination IP and port must somehow be communicated to the proxy.

d7e0663202f2.title: Proxy server
d7e0663202f2.section: Implementations of proxies > Transparent proxy > Issues
d7e0663202f2.sentence: Intercepting also creates problems for HTTP authentication, especially connection-oriented authentication such as NTLM, as the client browser believes it is talking to a server rather than a proxy.

d56787abbf73.title: Proxy server
d56787abbf73.section: Implementations of proxies > Transparent proxy > Issues
d56787abbf73.sentence: Finally, intercepting connections can cause problems for HTTP caches, as some requests and responses become uncacheable by a shared cache.

88af3046d030.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::proxy
88af3046d030.sentence: Introducing reverse proxy results in increased complexity.

8b85c7991bc5.title: Reverse proxy
8b85c7991bc5.sentence: A reverse proxy is a single point of failure for the back-end services it fronts: an outage caused by misconfiguration, a denial-of-service attack, or a software fault can make every frontend service unreachable to outside clients, even when the back-end services themselves remain healthy.

1c9d9676a6e7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::proxy
1c9d9676a6e7.sentence: A single reverse proxy is a single point of failure, configuring multiple reverse proxies (i.e. a failover) further increases complexity.

1d09b0f88521.title: Reverse proxy
1d09b0f88521.sentence: Giving the reverse proxy of a third party access to private keys (for caching or optimizing content) places the entire triad of confidentiality, integrity and availability in the hands of the third party who operates the proxy.

1862ca8dfceb.title: Reverse proxy
1862ca8dfceb.sentence: A reverse proxy is capable of tracking IP addresses of requests that are relayed through it as well as reading and/or modifying any non-encrypted traffic.

ced7046e1380.title: Reverse proxy
ced7046e1380.sentence: However, this implies that anyone who has compromised the server could do so as well.

0850edb72369.title: Reverse proxy
0850edb72369.sentence: Applications that were developed for the internal use of a company are not typically hardened to public standards and are not necessarily designed to withstand all hacking attempts.

2b35be4a2f33.title: Reverse proxy
2b35be4a2f33.sentence: When an organization allows external access to such internal applications via a reverse proxy, they might unintentionally increase their own attack surface and invite hackers.

eec89b41b1a8.sentence: In the Backend For Frontend (BFF) pattern, we create separate backend services to be consumed by specific frontend applications or interfaces.

ae4b9688ce92.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway

1823028e143e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway

5c6d31c5a56c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway
5c6d31c5a56c.sentence: To solve this issue, the frontend should have some logic to reformat the data, and therefore, we can use BFF to shift some of this logic to the intermediate layer.

f0523459c2d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway

0934c4dbe88a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::api-gateway

c3dff918dddc.title: API management
c3dff918dddc.sentence: API management is the process of creating and publishing web application programming interfaces (APIs), enforcing their usage policies, controlling access, nurturing the subscriber community, collecting and analyzing usage statistics, and reporting on performance.

92757f76bf20.title: API management
92757f76bf20.sentence: API management components provide mechanisms and tools to support developer and subscriber communities.

0ee057621c3e.title: API management
0ee057621c3e.sentence: While solutions vary, components that provide the following functions are typically found in API management products:

6d15ad606ada.title: API management
6d15ad606ada.sentence: A server that acts as an API front-end receives API requests, enforces throttling and security policies, passes requests to the back-end service and then passes the response back to the requester.

21f21daaf9b6.title: API management
21f21daaf9b6.sentence: A gateway often includes a transformation engine to orchestrate and modify the requests and responses on the fly.

e31573730642.title: API management
e31573730642.sentence: A gateway can also provide functions such as collecting analytics data and providing caching.

b62d02ba1cfb.title: API management
b62d02ba1cfb.sentence: The gateway can provide the functionality to support authentication, authorization, security, audit and regulatory compliance.

1767af18d944.title: API management
1767af18d944.sentence: A collection of tools that API providers use to define APIs, for instance using the OpenAPI or RAML specifications, generate API documentation, govern API usage through access and usage policies for APIs, test and debug the execution of API, including security testing and automated generation of tests and test suites, deploy APIs into production, staging, and quality assurance environments, and coordinate the overall API lifecycle.

f9fabd3db793.title: API management
f9fabd3db793.sentence: A community site, typically branded by an API provider, that can encapsulate for API users in a single convenient source information and functionality including documentation, tutorials, sample code, software development kits, an interactive API console and sandbox to trial APIs, the ability to subscribe to the APIs and manage subscription keys such as OAuth2 Client ID and Client Secret, and obtain support from the API provider and user and community.

b05e0cd631cf.title: API management
b05e0cd631cf.sentence: Functionality to monitor API usage and load (overall hits, completed transactions, number of data objects returned, amount of compute time and other internal resources consumed, the volume of data transferred).

30a2985e6f2c.title: API management
30a2985e6f2c.sentence: This can include real-time API monitoring with alerts being raised directly or via a higher-level network management system, for instance, if the load on an API has become too great, as well as functionality to analyze historical data, such as transaction logs, to detect usage trends.

50be1e17be5a.title: API management
50be1e17be5a.sentence: The API provider can use the information gathered by the reporting and analytics functionality to optimize the API offering within an organization's overall continuous improvement process and define software Service-Level Agreements for APIs.

dd26eb2a751e.title: API management
dd26eb2a751e.sentence: This functionality can include support for setting up pricing rules based on usage, load and functionality, issuing invoices, and collecting payments, including multiple types of credit card payments.

07f80e08ed02.title: Cache (computing)
07f80e08ed02.sentence: In computing, a cache (/kæʃ/ ⓘ KASH) is a hardware or software component that stores data so that future requests for that data can be served faster; the data stored in a cache might be the result of an earlier computation or a copy of data stored elsewhere.

54cc9fc9ef14.title: Cache (computing)
54cc9fc9ef14.sentence: A cache hit occurs when the requested data can be found in a cache, while a cache miss occurs when it cannot.

72369445c5a0.title: Cache (computing)
72369445c5a0.sentence: Cache hits are served by reading data from the cache, which is faster than recomputing a result or reading from a slower data store; thus, the more requests that can be served from the cache, the faster the system performs.

1e29de3025f0.title: Cache (computing)
1e29de3025f0.sentence: A cache is made up of a pool of entries.

18967e4f6ec0.title: Cache (computing)
18967e4f6ec0.sentence: Each entry has associated data, which is a copy of the same data in some backing store.

7626c0ecb740.title: Cache (computing)
7626c0ecb740.sentence: Each entry also has a tag, which specifies the identity of the data in the backing store of which the entry is a copy.

924b76ed7e84.title: Cache (computing)
924b76ed7e84.sentence: When the cache client (a CPU, web browser, operating system) needs to access data presumed to exist in the backing store, it first checks the cache.

cd7fc4f1c42b.title: Cache (computing)
cd7fc4f1c42b.sentence: If an entry can be found with a tag matching that of the desired data, the data in the entry is used instead.

a10fbce0321f.title: Cache (computing)
a10fbce0321f.sentence: This requires a more expensive access of data from the backing store.

9f34a364b705.title: Cache (computing)
9f34a364b705.sentence: Once the requested data is retrieved, it is typically copied into the cache, ready for the next access.

14c3f81aa29d.title: Cache (computing)
14c3f81aa29d.sentence: To be cost-effective, caches must be relatively small.

9366deed51a1.title: Cache (computing)
9366deed51a1.sentence: Nevertheless, caches are effective in many areas of computing because typical computer applications access data with a high degree of locality of reference.

faf53eb37030.title: Cache (computing)
faf53eb37030.sentence: In memory design, there is an inherent trade-off between capacity and speed because larger capacity implies larger size and thus greater physical distances for signals to travel, causing propagation delays.

f476f996400b.title: Cache (computing)
f476f996400b.sentence: There is also a tradeoff between high-performance technologies such as SRAM and cheaper, easily mass-produced commodities such as DRAM, flash, or hard disks.

02ceda96ebd2.title: Cache (computing)
02ceda96ebd2.sentence: The use of a cache also allows for higher throughput from the underlying resource by assembling multiple fine-grained transfers into larger, more efficient requests.

21a285b7ce98.title: Cache (computing)
21a285b7ce98.sentence: Central processing units (CPUs), solid-state drives (SSDs) and hard disk drives (HDDs) frequently include hardware-based cache, while web browsers and web servers commonly rely on software caching.

45bcc623537f.title: Locality of reference
45bcc623537f.sentence: In computer science, locality of reference, also known as the principle of locality, is the tendency of a processor to access the same set of memory locations repetitively over a short period of time.

15e21bc1e4c9.title: Cache (computing)
15e21bc1e4c9.sentence: Such access patterns exhibit temporal locality, where data that has been recently requested is requested again, and spatial locality, where data is requested that is stored near data that has already been requested.

64bacdb7cc80.title: Locality of reference
64bacdb7cc80.sentence: There are two basic types of reference locality – temporal and spatial locality.

32743e66a90c.title: Locality of reference
32743e66a90c.sentence: Temporal locality refers to the reuse of specific data and/or resources within a relatively small time duration.

71d61f746a1a.title: Locality of reference
71d61f746a1a.sentence: Spatial locality (also termed data locality) refers to the use of data elements within relatively close storage locations.

becd04869a17.title: Locality of reference
becd04869a17.sentence: Sequential locality, a special case of spatial locality, occurs when data elements are arranged and accessed linearly, such as traversing the elements in a one-dimensional array.

94072b81460d.title: Locality of reference
94072b81460d.sentence: - Temporal locality: If at one point a particular memory location is referenced, then it is likely that the same location will be referenced again in the near future.

17abb09d72a1.title: Locality of reference
17abb09d72a1.sentence: In this case it is common to make efforts to store a copy of the referenced data in faster memory storage, to reduce the latency of subsequent references.

5dfb6e8a978c.title: Locality of reference
5dfb6e8a978c.sentence: Systems which exhibit strong locality of reference are good candidates for performance optimization through the use of techniques such as the caching, prefetching for memory and advanced branch predictors of a processor core.

470226df1513.title: Cache (computing)
470226df1513.sentence: This is mitigated by reading large chunks into the cache, in the hope that subsequent reads will be from nearby locations and can be read from the cache.

cd02131ef5fd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::caching
cd02131ef5fd.sentence: Caches take advantage of the locality of reference principle "recently requested data is likely to be requested again".

4f7ad67a9da5.title: Locality of reference
4f7ad67a9da5.section: Spatial and temporal locality usage > Hierarchical memory
4f7ad67a9da5.sentence: Data elements in a cache do not necessarily correspond to data elements that are spatially close in the main memory; however, data elements are brought into cache one cache line at a time.

3b51e218cd15.title: Locality of reference
3b51e218cd15.section: Spatial and temporal locality usage > Hierarchical memory
3b51e218cd15.sentence: This means that spatial locality is again important: if one element is referenced, a few neighboring elements will also be brought into cache.

a8c54cc0ddac.title: Locality of reference
a8c54cc0ddac.sentence: Poor locality of reference results in cache thrashing and cache pollution and to avoid it, data elements with poor locality can be bypassed from cache.

386768d5337d.title: Locality of reference
386768d5337d.sentence: In programming languages such as C, matrices are stored in memory using row-major order, meaning that sequential access to contiguous elements improves cache utilization and reduces cache misses.

32a8f4ab84db.title: Locality of reference
32a8f4ab84db.sentence: However, as matrix dimensions increase, the access pattern becomes a critical factor, since non-sequential traversals generate significantly more cache misses and RAM accesses, reducing overall computational efficiency.

91282ad69722.title: CPU cache
91282ad69722.sentence: A CPU cache is a hardware cache used by the central processing unit (CPU) of a computer to reduce the average cost (time or energy) to access data from the main memory.

4e2b5fbbe99d.title: CPU cache
4e2b5fbbe99d.sentence: A cache is a smaller, faster memory, located closer to a processor core, which stores copies of the data from frequently used main memory locations, avoiding the need to always refer to main memory which may be tens to hundreds of times slower to access.

c6d8187bf60a.title: CPU cache
c6d8187bf60a.sentence: Cache memory is typically implemented with static random-access memory (SRAM), which requires multiple transistors to store a single bit.

c06fef790a28.title: CPU cache
c06fef790a28.sentence: This makes it expensive in terms of the area it takes up, and in modern CPUs the cache is typically the largest part by chip area.

73737f425030.title: CPU cache
73737f425030.sentence: Data is transferred between memory and cache in blocks of fixed size, called cache lines or cache blocks.

0a92e80bf47b.title: CPU cache
0a92e80bf47b.sentence: The cache entry will include the copied data as well as the requested memory location (called a tag).

e37ea88fd21a.title: CPU cache
e37ea88fd21a.sentence: If the processor finds that the memory location is in the cache, a cache hit has occurred.

7b287a07deed.title: CPU cache
7b287a07deed.sentence: However, if the processor does not find the memory location in the cache, a cache miss has occurred.

d6e544df6411.title: CPU cache
d6e544df6411.sentence: For a cache miss, the cache allocates a new entry and copies data from main memory, then the request is fulfilled from the contents of the cache.

962b46f575e4.title: CPU cache
962b46f575e4.section: Cache hierarchy in a modern processor > Multi-level caches
962b46f575e4.sentence: Larger caches have better hit rates but longer latency.

d2bd190c9ec3.title: CPU cache
d2bd190c9ec3.section: Cache hierarchy in a modern processor > Multi-level caches
d2bd190c9ec3.sentence: To address this tradeoff, many computers use multiple levels of cache, with small fast caches backed up by larger, slower caches.

f0b7855498ab.title: CPU cache
f0b7855498ab.section: Cache hierarchy in a modern processor > Multi-level caches
f0b7855498ab.sentence: Multi-level caches generally operate by checking the fastest but smallest cache, level 1 (L1), first; if it hits, the processor proceeds at high speed.

3fb78586bb1a.title: CPU cache
3fb78586bb1a.section: Cache hierarchy in a modern processor > Multi-level caches
3fb78586bb1a.sentence: If that cache misses, the slower but larger next level cache, level 2 (L2), is checked, and so on, before accessing external memory.

327713859ff0.title: CPU cache
327713859ff0.sentence: L3 caches are generally shared among multiple CPU cores.

fe90c8a3fd60.title: CPU cache
fe90c8a3fd60.sentence: If the placement policy is free to choose any entry in the cache to hold the copy, the cache is called fully associative.

965330066069.title: CPU cache
965330066069.sentence: At the other extreme, if each entry in the main memory can go in just one place in the cache, the cache is direct-mapped.

c2f454befcea.title: CPU cache
c2f454befcea.sentence: Many caches implement a compromise in which each entry in the main memory can go to any one of N places in the cache, and are described as N-way set associative.

01238dad6939.title: CPU cache
01238dad6939.sentence: Checking more places takes more power and chip area, and potentially more time.

a8a9833981d4.title: CPU cache
a8a9833981d4.sentence: On the other hand, caches with more associativity suffer fewer misses (see conflict misses), so that the CPU wastes less time reading from the slow main memory.

1e3ffca0f8f5.title: CPU cache
1e3ffca0f8f5.sentence: The general guideline is that doubling the associativity, from direct mapped to two-way, or from two-way to four-way, has about the same effect on raising the hit rate as doubling the cache size.

eb29e20d0956.title: CPU cache
eb29e20d0956.sentence: However, increasing associativity more than four does not improve hit rate as much, and are generally done for other reasons (see virtual aliasing).

b274dc1e0355.title: Cache replacement policies
b274dc1e0355.sentence: The hit ratio of a cache describes how often a searched-for item is found.

e497254dcf5b.title: Cache (computing)
e497254dcf5b.sentence: The percentage of accesses that result in cache hits is known as the hit rate or hit ratio of the cache.

cb0e6bc045d5.title: Cache replacement policies
cb0e6bc045d5.sentence: A cache has two primary figures of merit: latency and hit ratio.

7e984b2be94a.title: Cache replacement policies
7e984b2be94a.sentence: The latency of a cache describes how long after requesting a desired item the cache can return that item when there is a hit.

540b29cfa518.title: Cache replacement policies
540b29cfa518.sentence: Hit-rate measurements are typically performed on benchmark applications, and the hit ratio varies by application.

ced9e82d4d18.title: Cache replacement policies
ced9e82d4d18.sentence: Video and audio streaming applications often have a hit ratio near zero, because each bit of data in the stream is read once (a compulsory miss), used, and then never read or written again.

20367c12415b.title: Cache replacement policies
20367c12415b.sentence: Many cache algorithms (particularly LRU) allow streaming data to fill the cache, pushing out information which will soon be used again (cache pollution).

4e85e96ec010.title: Cache replacement policies
4e85e96ec010.sentence: More efficient replacement strategies track more usage information to improve the hit rate for a given cache size.

23a54be4b2e7.title: Cache replacement policies
23a54be4b2e7.sentence: Faster replacement strategies typically track less usage information—or, with a direct-mapped cache, no information—to reduce the time required to update the information.

801b1965724e.title: Cache replacement policies
801b1965724e.sentence: Each replacement strategy is a compromise between hit rate and latency.

eaa18fdcb153.title: Cache replacement policies
eaa18fdcb153.sentence: In computing, cache replacement policies (also known as cache replacement algorithms or cache algorithms) are optimizing instructions or algorithms which a computer program or hardware-maintained structure can utilize to manage a cache of information.

e69e75e77d8d.title: Cache replacement policies
e69e75e77d8d.sentence: When the cache is full, the algorithm must choose which items to discard to make room for new data.

4b53a13112fe.title: Cache replacement policies
4b53a13112fe.sentence: Caching improves performance by keeping recent or often-used data items in memory locations which are faster, or computationally cheaper to access, than normal memory stores.

20c47c4ce5e7.title: Cache (computing)
20c47c4ce5e7.sentence: During a cache miss, some other previously existing cache entry is typically removed in order to make room for the newly retrieved data.

bc6b4a93cac0.title: Cache (computing)
bc6b4a93cac0.sentence: The heuristic used to select the entry to replace is known as the replacement policy.

0479f06813d6.title: Cache (computing)
0479f06813d6.sentence: One popular replacement policy, least recently used (LRU), replaces the oldest entry, the entry that was accessed less recently than any other entry.

2c6129280c3b.title: Cache (computing)
2c6129280c3b.sentence: More sophisticated caching algorithms also take into account the frequency of use of entries.

0f76b0079693.title: Cache replacement policies
0f76b0079693.sentence: Other factors may be size, length of time to obtain, and expiration.

9cde731cbcdc.title: Cache replacement policies
9cde731cbcdc.sentence: Depending on cache size, no further caching algorithm to discard items may be needed.

2242545d0eb7.title: Cache (computing)
2242545d0eb7.sentence: Cache writes must eventually be propagated to the backing store.

9a1edd2d43be.title: Cache (computing)
9a1edd2d43be.sentence: The timing for this is governed by the write policy.

373ecf35deca.title: Cache (computing)
373ecf35deca.sentence: Consequently, a decision needs to be made for write misses: whether or not to load the data into the cache.

cd87891a641b.title: Cache (computing)
cd87891a641b.sentence: - Write-through: Writes are performed synchronously to both the cache and the backing store.

397691ef3998.title: Cache (computing)
397691ef3998.sentence: - Write-back: Initially, writing is done only to the cache.

542f3969d753.title: Cache (computing)
542f3969d753.sentence: The write to the backing store is postponed until the modified content is about to be replaced by another cache block.

fe08c1f04aca.title: Cache (computing)
fe08c1f04aca.sentence: A write-back cache is more complex to implement since it needs to track which of its locations have been written over and mark them as dirty for later writing to the backing store.

38e52a4fa987.title: Cache (computing)
38e52a4fa987.sentence: The data in these locations are written back to the backing store only when they are evicted from the cache, a process referred to as a lazy write.

60ebcb70f585.title: Cache (computing)
60ebcb70f585.sentence: For this reason, a read miss in a write-back cache may require two memory accesses to the backing store: one to write back the dirty data, and one to retrieve the requested data.

6ad31c45cc45.title: Cache (computing)
6ad31c45cc45.sentence: - Write allocate (also called fetch on write): Data at the missed-write location is loaded to cache, followed by a write-hit operation.

136f0fe432fe.title: Cache (computing)
136f0fe432fe.sentence: - No-write allocate (also called write-no-allocate or write around): Data at the missed-write location is not loaded to cache, and is written directly to the backing store.

8a1f8e86b1e6.title: Cache (computing)
8a1f8e86b1e6.sentence: In this approach, data is loaded into the cache on read misses only.

79be6db51a4a.title: Cache (computing)
79be6db51a4a.sentence: - A write-back cache typically employs write allocate, anticipating that subsequent writes or reads to the same location will benefit from having the data already in the cache.

67d412fd8d26.title: Cache (computing)
67d412fd8d26.sentence: - A write-through cache uses no-write allocate.

66e3b29fddf6.title: Cache (computing)
66e3b29fddf6.sentence: Here, subsequent writes have no advantage, since they still need to be written directly to the backing store.

9710339a87ec.title: Cache (computing)
9710339a87ec.sentence: Write-through operation is common when operating over unreliable networks, because of the enormous complexity of the coherency protocol required between multiple write-back caches when communication is unreliable.

9cfac1701ef3.title: Cache (computing)
9cfac1701ef3.sentence: Entities other than the cache may change the data in the backing store, in which case the copy in the cache may become out-of-date or stale.

fb4c8626ccac.title: Cache (computing)
fb4c8626ccac.sentence: Alternatively, when the client updates the data in the cache, copies of that data in other caches will become stale.

0a47781dd15b.title: Cache replacement policies
0a47781dd15b.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > Least frequently used (LFU)
0a47781dd15b.sentence: The LFU algorithm counts how often an item is needed; those used less often are discarded first.

eb287f9cea8f.title: Cache replacement policies
eb287f9cea8f.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > Least frequently used (LFU)
eb287f9cea8f.sentence: This is similar to LRU, except that how many times a block was accessed is stored instead of how recently.

19d441524158.title: Cache replacement policies
19d441524158.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > Least frequently used (LFU)
19d441524158.sentence: While running an access sequence, the block which was used the fewest times will be removed from the cache.

8fde091595ce.title: Cache replacement policies
8fde091595ce.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > LFU with dynamic aging (LFUDA)
8fde091595ce.sentence: If an object was frequently accessed in the past and becomes unpopular, it will remain in the cache for a long time (preventing newly- or less-popular objects from replacing it).

11cf672fbf1a.title: Cache replacement policies
11cf672fbf1a.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > LFU with dynamic aging (LFUDA)
11cf672fbf1a.sentence: A variant, LFU with dynamic aging (LFUDA), uses dynamic aging to accommodate shifts in a set of popular objects; it adds a cache-age factor to the reference count when a new object is added to the cache or an existing object is re-referenced.

cbff2f18ed2d.title: Cache replacement policies
cbff2f18ed2d.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > LFU with dynamic aging (LFUDA)
cbff2f18ed2d.sentence: Dynamic aging reduces the number of such objects, making them eligible for replacement, and LFUDA reduces cache pollution caused by LFU when a cache is small.

9abbedb36880.title: Cache replacement policies
9abbedb36880.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > Least frequent recently used (LFRU)
9abbedb36880.sentence: The least frequent recently used (LFRU) algorithm combines the benefits of LFU and LRU.

519dd6fb9f4a.title: Cache replacement policies
519dd6fb9f4a.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > Least frequent recently used (LFRU)
519dd6fb9f4a.sentence: In LFRU, the cache is divided into two partitions: privileged and unprivileged.

f0e7116715cb.title: Cache replacement policies
f0e7116715cb.section: Policies > Simple frequency-based policies > Least frequent recently used (LFRU)
f0e7116715cb.sentence: The privileged partition is protected; if content is popular, it is pushed into the privileged partition.

80d1728e7a00.title: Cache replacement policies
80d1728e7a00.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Least Recently Used (LRU)
80d1728e7a00.sentence: Discards least recently used items first.

3b7338961cb7.title: Cache replacement policies
3b7338961cb7.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Least Recently Used (LRU)
3b7338961cb7.sentence: This algorithm requires keeping track of what was used and when, which is cumbersome.

abcc5701b50a.title: Cache replacement policies
abcc5701b50a.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Least Recently Used (LRU)
abcc5701b50a.sentence: It requires "age bits" for cache lines, and tracks the least recently used cache line based on these age bits.

4f2164a3079e.title: Cache replacement policies
4f2164a3079e.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Least Recently Used (LRU)
4f2164a3079e.sentence: When a cache line is used, the age of the other cache lines changes.

41593f5b6f78.title: Cache replacement policies
41593f5b6f78.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Least Recently Used (LRU)
41593f5b6f78.sentence: LRU is a family of caching algorithms, that includes 2Q by Theodore Johnson and Dennis Shasha and LRU/K by Pat O'Neil, Betty O'Neil and Gerhard Weikum.

1770cebd7f9d.title: Cache replacement policies
1770cebd7f9d.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > LRU approximations > Pseudo-LRU (PLRU)
1770cebd7f9d.sentence: For CPU caches with large associativity (generally > four ways), the implementation cost of LRU becomes prohibitive.

70f571d68b85.title: Cache replacement policies
70f571d68b85.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > LRU approximations > Pseudo-LRU (PLRU)
70f571d68b85.sentence: In many CPU caches, an algorithm that almost always discards one of the least recently used items is sufficient; many CPU designers choose a PLRU algorithm, which only needs one bit per cache item to work.

28dc5769a562.title: Cache replacement policies
28dc5769a562.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > LRU approximations > Clock-Pro
28dc5769a562.sentence: The LRU algorithm cannot be implemented in the critical path of computer systems, such as operating systems, due to its high overhead; Clock, an approximation of LRU, is commonly used instead.

06c0252445a8.sentence: Least Recently Used (LRU) can be a good policy for our system.

abb8c0274be7.title: Cache coherence
abb8c0274be7.sentence: In computer architecture, cache coherence is the uniformity of shared resource data that is stored in multiple local caches.

7306fd8d734b.title: Cache coherence
7306fd8d734b.sentence: In a cache coherent system, if multiple clients have a cached copy of the same region of a shared memory resource, all copies are the same.

3d0a500db3dc.title: Cache coherence
3d0a500db3dc.sentence: Without cache coherence, a change made to the region by one client may not be seen by others, and errors can result when the data used by different clients is mismatched.

d70da7e2e8f9.title: Cache coherence
d70da7e2e8f9.sentence: Changes to the data in any cache must be propagated to other copies (of that cache line) in the peer caches.

5985ce9858d1.title: Cache coherence
5985ce9858d1.sentence: - Writes to the same location must be sequenced.

0fe4ae0e86ba.title: Cache coherence
0fe4ae0e86ba.sentence: In other words, if location X received two different values A and B, in this order, from any two processors, the processors can never read location X as B and then read it as A. The location X must be seen with values A and B in that order.

a81119919f85.title: Cache coherence
a81119919f85.sentence: The two most common mechanisms of ensuring coherency are snooping and directory-based, each having their own benefits and drawbacks.

3c80ed284682.title: Cache coherence
3c80ed284682.sentence: Snooping based protocols tend to be faster, if enough bandwidth is available, since all transactions are a request/response seen by all processors.

614a5697e155.title: Cache coherence
614a5697e155.sentence: The drawback is that snooping isn't scalable.

b173aaa394ae.title: Cache coherence
b173aaa394ae.sentence: Directories, on the other hand, tend to have longer latency (with a 3 hop request-forward-respond) but use much less bandwidth since messages are point to point and not broadcast.

a84fb81ac156.title: Cache coherence
a84fb81ac156.sentence: For this reason, many of the larger systems (>64 processors) use this type of cache coherence.

560594434335.title: Cache coherence
560594434335.sentence: In a directory-based system, the data being shared is placed in a common directory that maintains the coherence between caches.

18782fb20d6e.title: Cache coherence
18782fb20d6e.sentence: If the design states that a write to a cached copy by any processor requires other processors to discard or invalidate their cached copies, then it is a write-invalidate protocol.

847b1a88cf65.title: Cache coherence
847b1a88cf65.sentence: If the protocol design states that whenever any copy of the shared data is changed, all the other copies must be "updated" to reflect the change, then it is a write-update protocol.

51411a646002.title: Cache coherence
51411a646002.sentence: When a write operation is observed to a location that a cache has a copy of, the cache controller invalidates its own copy of the snooped memory location, which forces a read from main memory of the new value on its next access.

c2c0e16621b8.title: Cache coherence
c2c0e16621b8.sentence: When a write operation is observed to a location that a cache has a copy of, the cache controller updates its own copy of the snooped memory location with the new data.

332eb19c3eb7.title: Page cache
332eb19c3eb7.sentence: In computing, a page cache, sometimes also called disk cache, is a transparent cache for the pages originating from a secondary storage device such as a hard disk drive (HDD) or a solid-state drive (SSD).

d7c5606d7c34.title: Page cache
d7c5606d7c34.sentence: The operating system keeps a page cache in otherwise unused portions of the main memory (RAM), resulting in quicker access to the contents of cached pages and overall performance improvements.

95293a589591.title: Page cache
95293a589591.sentence: A page cache is implemented in kernels with the paging memory management, and is mostly transparent to applications.

9d8dff6cde34.title: Page cache
9d8dff6cde34.sentence: Usually, all physical memory not directly allocated to applications is used by the operating system for the page cache.

fe4821027379.title: Page cache
fe4821027379.sentence: Since the memory would otherwise be idle and is easily reclaimed when applications request it, there is generally no associated performance penalty and the operating system might even report such memory as "free" or "available".

69a34fbe8c4e.title: Page cache
69a34fbe8c4e.sentence: When compared to main memory, hard disk drive read/writes are slow and random accesses require expensive disk seeks; as a result, larger amounts of main memory bring performance improvements as more data can be cached in memory.

81d246b4b498.title: Page cache
81d246b4b498.sentence: Pages in the main memory that have been modified during writing data to disk are marked as "dirty" and have to be flushed to disk before they can be freed.

901bbcb212a3.title: Page cache
901bbcb212a3.sentence: When a file write occurs, the cached page for the particular block is looked up.

b61f0b7f9d5e.title: Page cache
b61f0b7f9d5e.sentence: If it is already found in the page cache, the write is done to that page in the main memory.

4908c03150b5.title: Page cache
4908c03150b5.sentence: Pages in the page cache modified after being brought in are called dirty pages.

0a98127a7a6d.title: Page cache
0a98127a7a6d.sentence: Since non-dirty pages in the page cache have identical copies in secondary storage (e.g. hard disk drive or solid-state drive), discarding and reusing their space is much quicker than paging out application memory, and is often preferred over flushing the dirty pages into secondary storage and reusing their space.

e9aaf0e1dc2d.title: Page cache
e9aaf0e1dc2d.sentence: Executable binaries, such as applications and libraries, are also typically accessed through page cache and mapped to individual process spaces using virtual memory (this is done through the mmap system call on Unix-like operating systems).

860c8ea55e25.title: Page cache
860c8ea55e25.sentence: This not only means that the binary files are shared between separate processes, but also that unused parts of binaries will be flushed out of main memory eventually, leading to memory conservation.

2e1856b73afb.title: Cache (computing)
2e1856b73afb.sentence: A cache's sole purpose is to reduce accesses to the underlying slower storage.

aca8577acbbe.title: Cache (computing)
aca8577acbbe.sentence: Fundamentally, caching realizes a performance increase for transfers of data that is being repeatedly transferred.

ea3a2254e9ee.title: Cache (computing)
ea3a2254e9ee.sentence: Buffering, on the other hand, reduces the number of transfers for otherwise novel data amongst communicating processes, which amortizes the overhead involved for several small transfers over fewer, larger transfers.

2782b33a00c5.title: Cache (computing)
2782b33a00c5.sentence: It also provides an intermediary for communicating processes that are incapable of direct transfers amongst each other, or ensures a minimum data size or representation required by at least one of the communicating processes involved in a transfer.

c512bc022757.title: Cache (computing)
c512bc022757.sentence: Also, a whole buffer of data is usually transferred sequentially (for example, to hard disk), so buffering itself sometimes increases transfer performance or reduces the variation or jitter of the transfer's latency as opposed to caching, where the intent is to reduce the latency.

e5f62b88da1a.title: Cache (computing)
e5f62b88da1a.sentence: These benefits are present even if the buffered data are written to the buffer once and read from the buffer once.

44bc6a73cec4.title: Cache (computing)
44bc6a73cec4.sentence: Contrary to strict buffering, a caching process must adhere to a potentially distributed cache coherency protocol in order to maintain consistency between the cache's intermediate storage and the location where the data resides.

208eac66ad55.title: Cache (computing)
208eac66ad55.sentence: Caching almost always involves some form of buffering, while strict buffering does not necessarily involve caching.

e52882985984.title: Cache (computing)
e52882985984.sentence: Caches with a prefetch input queue or more general anticipatory paging policy go further—they not only read the data requested, but guess that the next chunk or two of data will soon be required, and so prefetch that data into the cache ahead of time.

1817ffc07b78.title: Cache (computing)
1817ffc07b78.sentence: On a cache read miss, caches with a demand paging policy read the minimum amount from the backing store.

339fa6d42b7d.title: Cache (computing)
339fa6d42b7d.sentence: A typical demand-paging virtual memory implementation reads one page of virtual memory (often 4 KB) from disk into the disk cache in RAM.

060fdec2b590.title: Cache (computing)
060fdec2b590.sentence: Anticipatory paging is especially helpful when the backing store has a long latency to read the first chunk and much shorter times to sequentially read the next few chunks, such as disk storage and DRAM.

fa7ffcc0a734.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-5-caching-strategies.md
fa7ffcc0a734.sentence: When we introduce a cache into the architecture, synchronization between the cache and the database becomes inevitable.

b386309404f1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-5-caching-strategies.md
b386309404f1.sentence: Let’s look at 5 common strategies for how we keep the data in sync.

dde138d9c6b7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-5-caching-strategies.md
dde138d9c6b7.sentence: The caching strategies are often used in combination.

7f0f87b6c9e1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-5-caching-strategies.md
7f0f87b6c9e1.sentence: For example, write-around is often used together with cache-aside to make sure the cache is up-to-date.

38011e4cceef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::caching
38011e4cceef.sentence: Data is written into the cache and the corresponding database simultaneously.

835b579c8041.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::caching
835b579c8041.sentence: Pro: Fast retrieval, complete data consistency between cache and storage.

6606d59df289.title: Memcached
6606d59df289.sentence: In computing, Memcached (pronounced either /mɛmkæʃˈdiː/ mem-cash-DEE ["dee/d" being for daemon], or /ˈmɛmkæʃt/ MEM-cashed) is a general-purpose distributed memory-caching system.

9b6f57131557.title: Memcached
9b6f57131557.sentence: It is often used to speed up dynamic database-driven websites by caching data and objects in RAM to reduce the number of times an external data source (such as a database or API) must be read.

4ecb14ce0e5e.title: Memcached
4ecb14ce0e5e.sentence: Memcached's APIs provide a large hash table distributed across multiple machines.

ef7e31148601.title: Memcached
ef7e31148601.sentence: When the table is full, subsequent inserts cause older data to be purged in least recently used (LRU) order.

e860b578adc6.title: Memcached
e860b578adc6.sentence: The system uses a client–server architecture.

a6eb3391edf0.title: Memcached
a6eb3391edf0.sentence: The servers maintain a key–value associative array; the clients populate this array and query it by key.

82408792e83c.title: Memcached
82408792e83c.sentence: Keys are up to 250 bytes long and values can be at most 1 megabyte in size.

ba6198c54616.title: Memcached
ba6198c54616.sentence: Each client knows all servers; the servers do not communicate with each other.

750ddab81021.title: Memcached
750ddab81021.sentence: If a client wishes to set or read the value corresponding to a certain key, the client's library first computes a hash of the key to determine which server to use.

bf60e7deca9c.title: Memcached
bf60e7deca9c.sentence: This gives a simple form of sharding and scalable shared-nothing architecture across the servers.

b08a1632ed97.title: Memcached
b08a1632ed97.sentence: The servers keep the values in RAM (and, starting in 1.6.0, in auxiliary cache on disk using an external storage server option); if a server runs out of available memory or disk, it discards the oldest values.

42e5404bea66.title: Memcached
42e5404bea66.sentence: Therefore, clients must treat Memcached as a transitory cache; they cannot assume that data stored in Memcached is still there when they need it.

d21a770d92d2.title: Memcached
d21a770d92d2.sentence: Memcached can be equally valuable for situations where either the number of requests for content is high, or the cost of generating a particular piece of content is high.

f560bfabf0ad.title: Memcached
f560bfabf0ad.sentence: The client would first check whether a Memcached value with the unique key "userrow:userid" exists, where userid is some number.

2344657c4893.title: Memcached
2344657c4893.sentence: If the result does not exist, it would select from the database as usual, and set the unique key using the Memcached API add function call.

cad3858ef242.title: Memcached
cad3858ef242.sentence: However, if only this API call were modified, the server would end up fetching incorrect data following any database update actions: the Memcached "view" of the data would become out of date.

6bdff3f03edc.title: Memcached

82913f236a9a.title: Memcached

4f7d9e141836.title: Memcached
4f7d9e141836.sentence: Similar action would need to be taken when database records were deleted, to maintain either a correct or an incomplete cache.

5fe523880d47.title: Memcached
5fe523880d47.sentence: For efficient simplicity, all Memcached operations are treated equally.

c0c8432c369f.title: Memcached
c0c8432c369f.sentence: Clients with a valid need for access to low-security entries within the cache gain access to all entries within the cache, even when these are higher-security and that client has no justifiable need for them.

c2019d5b3263.title: Memoization
c2019d5b3263.sentence: In computing, memoization or memoisation is an optimization technique used primarily to speed up computer programs.

15e0c256eb48.title: Memoization
15e0c256eb48.sentence: It works by storing the results of expensive calls to pure functions, so that these results can be returned quickly when the same inputs occur again.

83c0e3dcd559.title: Cache (computing)
83c0e3dcd559.sentence: Memoization is an optimization technique that stores the results of resource-consuming function calls within a lookup table, allowing subsequent calls to reuse the stored results and avoid repeated computation.

72721dd52128.title: Memoization
72721dd52128.sentence: It is a type of caching, normally implemented using a hash table.

1e5e43b86ddd.title: Memoization
1e5e43b86ddd.sentence: A memoized function, when called with a given set of inputs for the first time, stores the inputs along with the computed results.

7e3ac6c7f334.title: Memoization
7e3ac6c7f334.sentence: Upon subsequent calls with remembered inputs, the function returns the remembered results rather than recomputing them, thus eliminating the cost of a recomputation.

1c9fbfba7915.title: Memoization
1c9fbfba7915.sentence: The set of remembered associations may be a fixed-size set controlled by a replacement algorithm or a fixed set, depending on the nature of the function and its use.

ad250d331b2e.title: Memoization
ad250d331b2e.sentence: A function can only be memoized if it is referentially transparent; that is, only if calling the function has exactly the same effect as replacing that function call with its return value.

2dd72891e163.title: Memoization
2dd72891e163.sentence: (Special case exceptions to this restriction exist, however.) While related to lookup tables, since memoization often uses such tables in its implementation, memoization populates its cache of results transparently on the fly, rather than needing them to be supplied in advance.

736427df98a2.title: Memoization
736427df98a2.sentence: It is a typical example of a space–time tradeoff, where the runtime of a program is reduced by increasing its memory usage.

d9c18d5ee8d5.title: Memoization
d9c18d5ee8d5.sentence: Memoized functions are optimized for speed in exchange for a higher use of computer memory space.

41997a64bcb3.title: Cache (computing)
41997a64bcb3.sentence: It is related to the dynamic programming algorithm design methodology, which can also be thought of as a means of caching.

25d1687e0d68.title: Cache replacement policies
25d1687e0d68.sentence: The most efficient caching algorithm would be to discard information which would not be needed for the longest time; this is known as Bélády's optimal algorithm, optimal replacement policy, or the clairvoyant algorithm.

7bbf9de10db9.title: Cache replacement policies
7bbf9de10db9.sentence: Bélády's algorithm is the optimal cache replacement policy, but it requires knowledge of the future to evict lines that will be reused farthest in the future.

5a988fc97dfb.title: Cache replacement policies
5a988fc97dfb.sentence: Since it is generally impossible to predict how far in the future information will be needed, this is unfeasible in practice.

125ca2f6ccb1.title: Cache replacement policies

6565dea62e07.title: Cache replacement policies

397b74d240d2.sentence: A number of replacement policies have been proposed which attempt to predict future reuse distances from past access patterns, allowing them to approximate the optimal replacement policy.

d5dc6ecb4027.title: Cache replacement policies
d5dc6ecb4027.sentence: Some of the best-performing cache replacement policies attempt to imitate Bélády's algorithm.

3626ed81dfc4.sentence: With this algorithm, the cache behaves like a FIFO queue; it evicts blocks in the order in which they were added, regardless of how often or how many times they were accessed before.

916ba6480783.title: Cache replacement policies

916ba6480783.sentence: The cache evicts the block added most recently first, regardless of how often or how many times it was accessed before.

a6c4ddd65620.title: Cache replacement policies
a6c4ddd65620.sentence: Random replacement selects an item and discards it to make space when necessary.

97578e1be1e0.title: Cache replacement policies
97578e1be1e0.section: Policies > Simple queue-based policies > Last in first out (LIFO) or First in last out (FILO)
97578e1be1e0.sentence: The cache behaves like a stack, and unlike a FIFO queue.

fac7591771af.sentence: This algorithm does not require keeping any access history.

4db1276e2cdf.sentence: It has been used in ARM processors due to its simplicity, and it allows efficient stochastic simulation.

8da82f4b91c0.sentence: Unlike LRU, MRU discards the most recently used items first.

Researchers presenting at the 22nd VLDB conference noted that for random access patterns and repeated scans over large datasets (also known as cyclic access patterns), MRU cache algorithms have more hits than LRU due to their tendency to retain older data.

9e837c111c68.title: Cache replacement policies
9e837c111c68.sentence: Therefore, SIEVE does not update the global data structure at cache hits and delays the update till eviction time; meanwhile, it quickly evicts newly inserted objects because cache workloads tend to show high one-hit-wonder ratios, and most of the new objects are not worthwhile to be kept in the cache.

88b20839d04a.sentence: SIEVE uses a single FIFO queue and uses a moving hand to select objects to evict.

a586d79f9e4f.title: Cache replacement policies
a586d79f9e4f.sentence: Compared to existing algorithms, which mostly build on LRU (least-recently used), S3-FIFO only uses three FIFO queues: a small queue occupying 10% of cache space, a main queue that uses 90% of the cache space, and a ghost queue that only stores object metadata.

22bfd3af1d78.title: Cache replacement policies
22bfd3af1d78.sentence: The small queue is used to filter out one-hit-wonders (objects that are only accessed once in a short time window); the main queue is used to store popular objects and uses reinsertion to keep them in the cache; and the ghost queue is used to catch potentially-popular objects that are evicted from the small queue.

3856bd48eaa1.title: Cache replacement policies
3856bd48eaa1.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Segmented LRU (SLRU)
3856bd48eaa1.sentence: An SLRU cache is divided into two segments: probationary and protected.

1db1f2aaa4b7.title: Cache replacement policies

05218939ac76.title: Cache replacement policies
05218939ac76.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Segmented LRU (SLRU)
05218939ac76.sentence: Hits are removed from where they reside and added to the most-recently accessed end of the protected segment; lines in the protected segment have been accessed at least twice.

867a4b4c3627.title: Cache replacement policies
867a4b4c3627.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Segmented LRU (SLRU)
867a4b4c3627.sentence: The protected segment is finite; migration of a line from the probationary segment to the protected segment may force the migration of the LRU line in the protected segment to the most-recently used end of the probationary segment, giving this line another chance to be accessed before being replaced.

cfab532c4fc7.title: Cache replacement policies
cfab532c4fc7.section: Policies > Simple recency-based policies > Segmented LRU (SLRU)
cfab532c4fc7.sentence: When data must be discarded from the cache, lines are obtained from the LRU end of the probationary segment.

18d7ed0107dc.title: Cache replacement policies

18d7ed0107dc.sentence: Adaptive replacement cache (ARC) constantly balances between LRU and LFU to improve the combined result.

22c7b7160b1c.title: Cache replacement policies
22c7b7160b1c.section: Policies > Other policies > Adaptive replacement cache
22c7b7160b1c.sentence: It improves SLRU by using information about recently evicted cache items to adjust the size of the protected and probationary segments to make the best use of available cache space.

5257a3361db6.title: Adaptive replacement cache
5257a3361db6.sentence: Adaptive Replacement Cache (ARC) is a page replacement algorithm with better performance than LRU (least recently used).

567d8957785c.title: Adaptive replacement cache
567d8957785c.sentence: This is accomplished by keeping track of both frequently used and recently used pages plus a recent eviction history for both.

8eda4d7bf4f7.title: Adaptive replacement cache
8eda4d7bf4f7.sentence: Basic LRU maintains an ordered list (the cache directory) of resource entries in the cache, with the sort order based on the time of most recent access.

ffa20fd4f368.title: Adaptive replacement cache
ffa20fd4f368.sentence: ARC improves the basic LRU strategy by splitting the cache directory into two lists, T1 and T2, for recently and frequently referenced entries.

64e9aa918c55.title: Adaptive replacement cache
64e9aa918c55.sentence: - T2, for frequent entries, referenced at least twice.

012fab7d65f9.title: Adaptive replacement cache
012fab7d65f9.sentence: - Any entry in L1 that gets referenced once more, gets another chance, and enters L2, just to the right of the central! marker.

c4dc2f4401e4.title: Adaptive replacement cache
c4dc2f4401e4.sentence: In turn, each of these is extended with a ghost list (B1 or B2), which is attached to the bottom of the two lists.

3d32a94c90bf.title: Adaptive replacement cache
3d32a94c90bf.sentence: These ghost lists act as scorecards by keeping track of the history of recently evicted cache entries, and the algorithm uses ghost hits to adapt to recent change in resource usage.

ee1ee12d3e57.title: Adaptive replacement cache

c8ba7cc7c260.title: Cache stampede
c8ba7cc7c260.sentence: A cache stampede is a type of cascading failure that can occur when massively parallel computing systems with caching mechanisms come under a very high load.

622b2e4a5200.title: Cache stampede
622b2e4a5200.sentence: This behaviour is sometimes also called dog-piling.

61d0ae879e5f.title: Cache stampede
61d0ae879e5f.sentence: Under particularly high load to a single URL, the system remains responsive as long as the resource remains cached, with requests being handled by accessing the cached copy.

fcb948ffd531.title: Cache stampede
fcb948ffd531.sentence: This minimizes the expensive rendering operation.

d8ac05e43950.title: Cache stampede
d8ac05e43950.sentence: However, under very heavy load, when the cached version of that page expires, there may be sufficient concurrency in the server farm that multiple threads of execution will all attempt to render the content of that page simultaneously.

07f3bc3219a3.title: Cache stampede
07f3bc3219a3.sentence: Systematically, none of the concurrent servers know that the others are doing the same rendering at the same time.

4de690f51e52.title: Cache stampede
4de690f51e52.sentence: If sufficiently high load is present, this may by itself be enough to bring about congestion collapse of the system via exhausting shared resources.

6bec829c8202.title: Cache stampede
6bec829c8202.sentence: Congestion collapse results in preventing the page from ever being completely re-rendered and re-cached, as every attempt to do so times out.

7cb3a558eeaf.title: Cache stampede
7cb3a558eeaf.sentence: Thus, cache stampede reduces the cache hit rate to zero and keeps the system continuously in congestion collapse as it attempts to regenerate the resource for as long as the load remains very heavy.

c3c6446a6f63.title: Cache stampede
c3c6446a6f63.sentence: To give a concrete example, assume the page in consideration takes 3 seconds to render and we have a traffic of 10 requests per second.

172e2c441eec.title: Cache stampede
172e2c441eec.sentence: Then, when the cached page expires, we have 30 processes simultaneously recomputing the rendering of the page and updating the cache with the rendered page.

7fe42c23415d.title: Cache stampede

275562fc796a.title: Cache stampede
275562fc796a.sentence: If the function recompute_value() takes a long time and the key is accessed frequently, many processes will simultaneously call recompute_value() upon expiration of the cache value.

6c49ebd1e630.title: Cache stampede
6c49ebd1e630.sentence: In typical web applications, the function recompute_value() may query a database, access other services, or perform some complicated operation (which is why this particular computation is being cached in the first place).

853babcc5d0c.title: Cache stampede
853babcc5d0c.sentence: When the request rate is high, the database (or any other shared resource) will suffer from an overload of requests/queries, which may in turn cause a system collapse.

6c6e71d84ae8.title: Cache stampede
6c6e71d84ae8.sentence: Several approaches have been proposed to mitigate cache stampedes (also known as dogpile prevention).

a18db23dd5d4.title: Cache stampede

4a41839c09f8.title: Cache stampede

0dea756cf0cc.title: Cache stampede
0dea756cf0cc.sentence: This solution moves the recomputation of the cache value from the processes needing it to an external process.

e9e8eb7e812d.title: Cache stampede
e9e8eb7e812d.section: Cache stampede mitigation > Probabilistic early expiration
e9e8eb7e812d.sentence: With this approach, each process may recompute the cache value before its expiration by making an independent probabilistic decision, where the probability of performing the early recomputation increases as we get closer to the expiration of the value.

0cf51fc30214.title: Cache stampede
0cf51fc30214.sentence: There are different implementation options for the case when the lock is not acquired:

13ae345af03f.title: Cache stampede
13ae345af03f.sentence: - Return a "not-found" and have the client handle the absence of the value properly

76f2995bff6f.title: Cache stampede
76f2995bff6f.sentence: - Keep a stale item in the cache to be used while the new value is recomputed

f2f9b2de21b6.title: Cache stampede
f2f9b2de21b6.sentence: If implemented properly, locking can prevent stampedes altogether, but requires an extra write for the locking mechanism.

98c1a16e25dc.title: Cache stampede
98c1a16e25dc.sentence: Apart from doubling the number of writes, the main drawback is a correct implementation of the locking mechanism which also takes care of edge cases including failure of the process acquiring the lock, tuning of a time-to-live for the lock, race-conditions, and so on.

b1f12990a25d.title: Cache stampede
b1f12990a25d.sentence: The recomputation of the external process can be triggered in different ways:

c4c8bf1b7a81.title: Cache stampede
c4c8bf1b7a81.sentence: - When the cache value approaches its expiration

080dae7ecbd5.title: Cache stampede
080dae7ecbd5.sentence: - When a process needing the value encounters a cache miss

bb12c925c534.title: Cache stampede
bb12c925c534.sentence: This approach requires one more moving part - the external process - that needs to be maintained and monitored.

34413f0cba82.title: Cache stampede
