60043744dec4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::caching
60043744dec4.sentence: It's important to note that a cache should not be used as permanent data storage.

be8d1d33e6e9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::caching
be8d1d33e6e9.sentence: They are almost always implemented in volatile memory because it is faster, and thus should be considered transient.

1baf0b392ff2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::caching
1baf0b392ff2.sentence: - Caching isn't helpful when it takes just as long to access the cache as it does to access the primary data store.

fa5d973b26f0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::caching
fa5d973b26f0.sentence: - Caching isn't helpful when the data changes frequently, as the cached version gets out of sync, and the primary data store must be accessed every time.

71172995aa6e.title: Redis
71172995aa6e.sentence: Persistence in Redis can be achieved through two different methods: snapshotting, where the dataset is asynchronously transferred from memory to disk at regular intervals as a binary dump, using the Redis RDB Dump File Format; or journaling, where a record of each operation that modifies the dataset is added to an append-only file (AOF) in a background process.

62e78ae918de.title: Redis
62e78ae918de.sentence: Redis typically holds the whole dataset in memory.

8a885860cca3.title: Redis
8a885860cca3.sentence: Redis can rewrite the append-only file in the background to avoid an indefinite growth of the journal.

263fde1e53f3.title: Redis
263fde1e53f3.sentence: Journaling was introduced in version 1.1 and is generally considered the safer approach.

d04c35a860fe.title: Redis
d04c35a860fe.sentence: By default, Redis writes data to a file system at least every two seconds, with more or less robust options available if needed.

996d4e54f476.title: Redis
996d4e54f476.sentence: In the case of a complete system failure on default settings, only a few seconds of data will be lost.

4364bf8c98f7.title: Redis
4364bf8c98f7.sentence: The Redis implementation uses the fork system call to duplicate the process holding the data.

b3b65790b5c1.title: Redis
b3b65790b5c1.sentence: This allows the parent process to continue serving clients while the child process persists the in-memory data to disk.

4c1cea39640f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/memcached-vs-redis.md
4c1cea39640f.sentence: Popular interview question - what are the differences between Redis and Memcached?

37dcda34db28.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/memcached-vs-redis.md
37dcda34db28.sentence: The advantages of data structures make Redis a good choice for:

c7728676362f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/memcached-vs-redis.md
c7728676362f.sentence: For example, login status, membership status.

8243856c3ffd.title: Redis
8243856c3ffd.sentence: Redis supports a number of data types including Strings, JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) documents, Hashes (a collection of fields, each field is a name-value string pair), lists, sets, vector sets, and more.

b2d3a7d11da0.title: Cache invalidation
b2d3a7d11da0.sentence: There are three specific methods to invalidate a cache, but not all caching proxies support these methods.

eb9fe97ab8eb.title: Cache invalidation
eb9fe97ab8eb.sentence: Removes content from caching proxy immediately.

0faf04b4ac7f.title: Cache invalidation
0faf04b4ac7f.sentence: This method removes all variants of the cached content.

15d7b39f6149.title: Cache invalidation
15d7b39f6149.sentence: When the client requests the data again, it is fetched from the application and stored in the caching proxy.

1af28af277eb.title: Cache invalidation
1af28af277eb.sentence: Fetches requested content from the application, even if cached content is available.

034e6c334582.title: Cache invalidation
034e6c334582.sentence: The content previously stored in the cache is replaced with a new version from the application.

c2363f7d060c.title: Cache invalidation
c2363f7d060c.sentence: This method affects only one variant of the cached content.

25dd196bf756.title: Cache invalidation
25dd196bf756.sentence: A reference to the cached content is added to a blacklist (or ban list).

8dffb7e6a44a.title: Cache invalidation
8dffb7e6a44a.sentence: Client requests are then checked against this blacklist, and if a request matches, new content is fetched from the application, returned to the client, and added to the cache.

a0aa218f501e.title: Cache invalidation
a0aa218f501e.sentence: This method, unlike purge, does not immediately remove cached content from the caching proxy.

b6ddd32eaa3f.title: Cache invalidation
b6ddd32eaa3f.sentence: Instead, the cached content is updated after a client requests that specific information.

6adbf7695605.title: Thundering herd problem
6adbf7695605.sentence: The thundering herd problem is a performance-degrading phenomenon in computer science and computer networking that occurs when a large number of processes or threads are simultaneously awakened, however, only one process is able to respond to the event or access the new resource, causing most other processes to fail and go back to sleep.

f7d41aeb8b96.title: Thundering herd problem
f7d41aeb8b96.sentence: This unnecessary awakening consumes CPU and other system resources, potentially reducing overall performance and slowing the process that succeeds.

a5df2c9a751f.title: Thundering herd problem
a5df2c9a751f.sentence: When the thundering herd problem occurs while attempting to access a cache, it is often referred to as a cache stampede.

30d088f07ab0.title: Thundering herd problem
30d088f07ab0.sentence: The Linux kernel serializes responses for requests to a single file descriptor, so only one thread or process is woken up.

5bc758b26117.title: Thundering herd problem
5bc758b26117.sentence: For epoll() in version 4.5 of the Linux kernel, the EPOLLEXCLUSIVE flag was added.

4fd2e389dae3.title: Thundering herd problem
4fd2e389dae3.sentence: Thus several epoll sets (different threads or different processes) may wait on the same resource and only one set will be woken up.

07b141449146.title: Thundering herd problem
07b141449146.sentence: Similarly in Microsoft Windows, I/O completion ports can mitigate the thundering herd problem, as they can be configured such that only one of the threads waiting on the completion port is woken up when an event occurs.

3e8b228b62d7.title: Thundering herd problem
3e8b228b62d7.sentence: In systems that rely on a backoff mechanism (e.g. exponential backoff), the clients will retry failed calls by waiting a specific amount of time between consecutive retries.

6b922d5319a7.title: Thundering herd problem
6b922d5319a7.sentence: In order to avoid the thundering herd problem, jitter can be purposefully introduced in order to break the synchronization across the clients, thereby avoiding collisions.

f31a3086d495.title: Thundering herd problem
f31a3086d495.sentence: In this approach, randomness is added to the wait intervals between retries, so that clients are no longer synchronized.

bf8093eb9e40.title: Cache (computing)
bf8093eb9e40.section: In-network cache > Information-centric networking > Weather forecast
bf8093eb9e40.sentence: An optimization by edge servers to truncate the GPS coordinates to fewer decimal places meant that the cached results from a nearby query would be used.

cb8e60c014b3.title: Cache (computing)
cb8e60c014b3.section: In-network cache > Information-centric networking > Weather forecast
cb8e60c014b3.sentence: In 2011, the use of smartphones with weather forecasting options was overly taxing AccuWeather servers; two requests from the same area would generate separate requests.

a619c8e9ed8e.title: Cache (computing)
a619c8e9ed8e.section: In-network cache > Information-centric networking > Weather forecast
a619c8e9ed8e.sentence: The number of to-the-server lookups per day dropped by half.

a3d010e232b2.title: Content delivery network
a3d010e232b2.sentence: CDNs provide high availability and performance by distributing content geographically closer to end users, and arose in the late 1990s to alleviate the performance bottlenecks of the Internet as it was becoming a critical medium.

a6477da2a746.title: Content delivery network
a6477da2a746.sentence: Since then, CDNs have grown to serve a large portion of Internet content, including text, graphics and scripts, downloadable objects (media files, software, and documents), applications (e-commerce, portals), live streaming media, on-demand streaming media, and social media services.

5182b920373a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
5182b920373a.sentence: Generally, static files such as HTML/CSS/JS, photos, and videos are served from CDN.

cd16885543dc.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-cdn-content-delivery-network.md
cd16885543dc.sentence: A CDN refers to geographically distributed servers (also called edge servers) that provide fast delivery of static and dynamic content.

fa25081bcab6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-cdn-content-delivery-network.md
fa25081bcab6.sentence: With CDN, users don’t need to retrieve content (music, video, files, pictures, etc.) from the origin server.

3614d5c2f276.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-cdn-content-delivery-network.md
3614d5c2f276.sentence: Instead, the content is cached at CDN nodes around the globe, and users can retrieve the content from nearby CDN nodes.

9e787c233630.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
9e787c233630.sentence: Serving content from CDNs can significantly improve performance as users receive content from data centers close to them and our servers do not have to serve requests that the CDN fulfills.

87ad4dab9deb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
87ad4dab9deb.sentence: For example, when someone in the UK requests our website which might be hosted in the USA, they will be served from the closest edge location such as the London edge location.

370e8ee68f33.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
370e8ee68f33.sentence: This is much quicker than having the visitor make a complete request to the origin server which will increase the latency.

2833dea226db.title: Content delivery network
2833dea226db.sentence: Benefits include reducing bandwidth costs, improving page load times, and increasing the global availability of content.

ed65ffa1f336.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
ed65ffa1f336.sentence: Content Delivery Network (CDN) increases content availability and redundancy while reducing bandwidth costs and improving security.

8b73248abd91.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-cdn-content-delivery-network.md
8b73248abd91.sentence: - Improving website security, especially protecting against DDoS (Distributed Denial-of-Service) attack

b01577204fc8.title: Content delivery network
b01577204fc8.sentence: Content owners such as media companies and e-commerce vendors pay CDN operators to deliver their content to their end users.

905a9a06e082.title: Content delivery network
905a9a06e082.sentence: In turn, a CDN pays Internet service providers (ISPs), carriers, and network operators for hosting its servers in their data centers.

731763eb3816.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
731763eb3816.sentence: - Extra charges: It can be expensive to use a CDN, especially for high-traffic services.

12c9d7af9174.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
12c9d7af9174.sentence: - Restrictions: Some organizations and countries have blocked the domains or IP addresses of popular CDNs.

1c3943b26833.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
1c3943b26833.sentence: - Location: If most of our audience is located in a country where the CDN has no servers, the data on our website may have to travel further than without using any CDN.

09f98f1cf618.title: Peer-to-peer
09f98f1cf618.sentence: Peer-to-peer (P2P) computing or networking is a distributed computing or networking architecture in which participants share part of their own resources, such as processing power, storage, or network capacity.

be871be457b4.title: Peer-to-peer
be871be457b4.sentence: These resources are made directly available to other peers without reliance on intermediary entities, and participants act as both resource provider and resource requesters.

c184f373944f.title: Peer-to-peer
c184f373944f.sentence: In contrast, the traditional client–server model assigns resource provider and requester roles to different participants, with centralized servers acting as providers and clients acting as requesters.

245d18455978.title: Peer-to-peer
245d18455978.sentence: Peer-to-peer networks generally implement some form of virtual overlay network on top of the physical network topology, where the nodes in the overlay form a subset of the nodes in the physical network.

0d479aaa52ee.title: Peer-to-peer
0d479aaa52ee.sentence: Data is still exchanged directly over the underlying TCP/IP network, but at the application layer peers can communicate with each other directly, via the logical overlay links (each of which corresponds to a path through the underlying physical network).

afceea0f8fc0.title: Peer-to-peer
afceea0f8fc0.sentence: Overlays are used for indexing and peer discovery, and make the P2P system independent from the physical network topology.

91b89cbdcfc8.title: Peer-to-peer
91b89cbdcfc8.sentence: Based on how the nodes are linked to each other within the overlay network, and how resources are indexed and located, we can classify networks as unstructured or structured (or as a hybrid between the two).

9ef050ffcecb.title: Peer-to-peer
9ef050ffcecb.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Unstructured networks
9ef050ffcecb.sentence: Unstructured peer-to-peer networks do not impose a particular structure on the overlay network by design, but rather are formed by nodes that randomly form connections to each other.

9a2c5440263e.title: Peer-to-peer
9a2c5440263e.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Unstructured networks
9a2c5440263e.sentence: (Gnutella, Gossip, and Kazaa are examples of unstructured P2P protocols).

cc2f6dc1de2e.title: Peer-to-peer
cc2f6dc1de2e.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Unstructured networks
cc2f6dc1de2e.sentence: Because there is no structure globally imposed upon them, unstructured networks are easy to build and allow for localized optimizations to different regions of the overlay.

fcfe6abfde58.title: Peer-to-peer
fcfe6abfde58.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Unstructured networks
fcfe6abfde58.sentence: Also, because the role of all peers in the network is the same, unstructured networks are highly robust in the face of high rates of "churn"—that is, when large numbers of peers are frequently joining and leaving the network.

90ded78a2f04.title: Peer-to-peer
90ded78a2f04.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Structured networks
90ded78a2f04.sentence: In structured peer-to-peer networks the overlay is organized into a specific topology, and the protocol ensures that any node can efficiently search the network for a file/resource, even if the resource is extremely rare.

31af50d204c1.title: Peer-to-peer
31af50d204c1.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Structured networks
31af50d204c1.sentence: The most common type of structured P2P networks implement a distributed hash table (DHT), in which a variant of consistent hashing is used to assign ownership of each file to a particular peer.

96b57838842e.title: Peer-to-peer
96b57838842e.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Structured networks
96b57838842e.sentence: This enables peers to search for resources on the network using a hash table: that is, (key, value) pairs are stored in the DHT, and any participating node can efficiently retrieve the value associated with a given key.

db19d6c64273.title: Peer-to-peer
db19d6c64273.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Hybrid models
db19d6c64273.sentence: Hybrid models are a combination of peer-to-peer and client–server models.

3969ce6be9fd.title: Peer-to-peer
3969ce6be9fd.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Hybrid models
3969ce6be9fd.sentence: A common hybrid model is to have a central server that helps peers find each other.

522ff04ec7a9.title: Peer-to-peer
522ff04ec7a9.section: Architecture > Routing and resource discovery > Hybrid models
522ff04ec7a9.sentence: There are a variety of hybrid models, all of which make trade-offs between the centralized functionality provided by a structured server/client network and the node equality afforded by the pure peer-to-peer unstructured networks.

16e9f2f8a4e2.title: Peer-to-peer
16e9f2f8a4e2.section: Architecture > Resilient and scalable computer networks
16e9f2f8a4e2.sentence: The decentralized nature of P2P networks increases robustness because it removes the single point of failure that can be inherent in a client–server based system.

fbeaee6489ea.title: Peer-to-peer
fbeaee6489ea.section: Architecture > Resilient and scalable computer networks
fbeaee6489ea.sentence: As nodes arrive and demand on the system increases, the total capacity of the system also increases, and the likelihood of failure decreases.

b86c605e6cd3.title: Peer-to-peer
b86c605e6cd3.sentence: This means that unlike client–server systems, the content-serving capacity of peer-to-peer networks can actually increase as more users begin to access the content (especially with protocols such as BitTorrent that require users to share, refer a performance measurement study).

a0f7e9e0aa31.title: Peer-to-peer
a0f7e9e0aa31.sentence: This property is one of the major advantages of using P2P networks because it makes the setup and running costs very small for the original content distributor.

077c56693057.title: Peer-to-peer
077c56693057.sentence: What makes this particularly dangerous for P2P software, however, is that peer-to-peer applications act as servers as well as clients, meaning that they can be more vulnerable to remote exploits.

f83d1a6c826b.title: Peer-to-peer
f83d1a6c826b.section: Architecture > Security and trust > Routing attacks
f83d1a6c826b.sentence: Since each node plays a role in routing traffic through the network, malicious users can perform a variety of "routing attacks", or denial of service attacks.

415dd2a41e4a.title: Peer-to-peer
415dd2a41e4a.section: Architecture > Security and trust > Routing attacks
415dd2a41e4a.sentence: Examples of common routing attacks include "incorrect lookup routing" whereby malicious nodes deliberately forward requests incorrectly or return false results, "incorrect routing updates" where malicious nodes corrupt the routing tables of neighboring nodes by sending them false information, and "incorrect routing network partition" where when new nodes are joining they bootstrap via a malicious node, which places the new node in a partition of the network that is populated by other malicious nodes.

6b8098b9aed8.title: Peer-to-peer
6b8098b9aed8.section: Social implications > Incentivizing resource sharing and cooperation
6b8098b9aed8.sentence: Cooperation among a community of participants is key to the continued success of P2P systems aimed at casual human users; these reach their full potential only when large numbers of nodes contribute resources.

aec1546ade8d.title: Peer-to-peer
aec1546ade8d.section: Social implications > Incentivizing resource sharing and cooperation
aec1546ade8d.sentence: But in current practice, P2P networks often contain large numbers of users who utilize resources shared by other nodes, but who do not share anything themselves (often referred to as the "freeloader problem").

42a4635a281b.title: Peer-to-peer
42a4635a281b.section: Social implications > Incentivizing resource sharing and cooperation
42a4635a281b.sentence: Freeloading can have a profound impact on the network and in some cases can cause the community to collapse.

6112c1ef6df8.title: Denial-of-service attack
6112c1ef6df8.sentence: In computing, a denial-of-service attack (DoS attack /dɒs/ doss) is a cyberattack in which the perpetrator seeks to make a machine or network resource unavailable to its intended users by temporarily or indefinitely disrupting services of a host connected to a network.

34ee936855f7.title: Denial-of-service attack
34ee936855f7.sentence: In a distributed denial-of-service attack (DDoS attack /ˈdiː.dɒs/ DEE-doss), the incoming traffic flooding the victim originates from many different sources.

2d9cfe54bbf7.title: Denial-of-service attack
2d9cfe54bbf7.sentence: Denial of service is typically accomplished by flooding the targeted machine or resource with superfluous requests in an attempt to overload systems and prevent some or all legitimate requests from being fulfilled.

fa40bd9d90de.title: Denial-of-service attack
fa40bd9d90de.sentence: There are two general forms of DoS attacks: those that crash services and those that flood services.

dc0b2809452b.title: Denial-of-service attack
dc0b2809452b.sentence: More sophisticated strategies are required to mitigate this type of attack; simply attempting to block a single source is insufficient.

efa2248dc1fa.title: Denial-of-service attack
efa2248dc1fa.sentence: A DDoS attack uses more than one unique IP address or machine, often from thousands of hosts infected with malware.

c5bba6c6b90e.title: Denial-of-service attack
c5bba6c6b90e.section: Types > Application layer attacks > Method of attack
c5bba6c6b90e.sentence: A common way of achieving this today is via distributed denial-of-service, employing a botnet.

4de8134c5ec8.title: Denial-of-service attack
4de8134c5ec8.sentence: Some common examples of DDoS attacks are UDP flooding, SYN flooding and DNS amplification.

3969c72f8fd5.title: Denial-of-service attack
3969c72f8fd5.sentence: A SYN flood occurs when a host sends a flood of TCP/SYN packets, often with a forged sender address.

61b5d9bdd48d.title: Denial-of-service attack
61b5d9bdd48d.sentence: Each of these packets is handled like a connection request, causing the server to spawn a half-open connection, send back a TCP/SYN-ACK packet, and wait for a packet in response from the sender address.

ef6a1ea052ae.title: Denial-of-service attack
ef6a1ea052ae.sentence: These half-open connections exhaust the available connections the server can make, keeping it from responding to legitimate requests until after the attack ends.

d3bfa8de5121.title: Denial-of-service attack
d3bfa8de5121.sentence: A distributed denial-of-service attack may involve sending forged requests of some type to a very large number of computers that will reply to the requests.

4749956f0ac3.title: Denial-of-service attack
4749956f0ac3.sentence: Using Internet Protocol address spoofing, the source address is set to that of the targeted victim, which means all the replies will go to (and flood) the target.

93d97176f25e.title: Denial-of-service attack
93d97176f25e.sentence: Amplification attacks are used to magnify the bandwidth that is sent to a victim.

7b8f0fe5d4c2.title: Denial-of-service attack
7b8f0fe5d4c2.sentence: An application layer DDoS attack (sometimes referred to as layer 7 DDoS attack) is a form of DDoS attack where attackers target application-layer processes.

61ab35d71354.title: Denial-of-service attack
61ab35d71354.sentence: The attack over-exercises specific functions or features of a website with the intention to disable those functions or features.

a841ee5aa9d3.title: Denial-of-service attack
a841ee5aa9d3.section: Types > Application layer attacks > Method of attack
a841ee5aa9d3.sentence: It requires fewer resources than network layer attacks but often accompanies them.

a28f628ff063.title: Denial-of-service attack
a28f628ff063.section: Types > Application layer attacks > Method of attack
a28f628ff063.sentence: An attack may be disguised to look like legitimate traffic, except it targets specific application packets or functions.

6f5d73037fa3.title: Denial-of-service attack
6f5d73037fa3.section: Types > Application layer attacks > Method of attack
6f5d73037fa3.sentence: The attack on the application layer can disrupt services such as the retrieval of information or search functions on a website.

6dc157bc226e.title: Denial-of-service attack
6dc157bc226e.sentence: A yo-yo attack is a specific type of DoS/DDoS aimed at cloud-hosted applications which use autoscaling.

0b01c358dc43.title: Denial-of-service attack
0b01c358dc43.sentence: During the attack, an attacker repeatedly changes between sending a lot of traffic (which causes a scale-up) and stopping the burst (causing a scale-down as a result).

4a6682d4b3c9.title: Denial-of-service attack
4a6682d4b3c9.sentence: Defensive responses to denial-of-service attacks typically involve the use of a combination of attack detection, traffic classification and response tools, aiming to block traffic the tools identify as illegitimate and allow traffic that they identify as legitimate.

a1eb58782bd3.title: Denial-of-service attack
a1eb58782bd3.sentence: All traffic destined to the victim is diverted to pass through a cleaning center or a scrubbing center via various methods such as: changing the victim IP address in the DNS system, tunneling methods (GRE/VRF, MPLS, SDN), proxies, digital cross connects, or even direct circuits.

530f58735021.title: Denial-of-service attack
530f58735021.sentence: The cleaning center separates bad traffic (DDoS and also other common internet attacks) and only passes good legitimate traffic to the victim server.

f4fbe466334d.title: Denial-of-service attack
f4fbe466334d.sentence: DDoS attacks can overwhelm any type of hardware firewall, and passing malicious traffic through large and mature networks becomes more and more effective and economically sustainable against DDoS.

c0e9219a2051.title: Denial-of-service attack
c0e9219a2051.sentence: An unintentional denial-of-service can occur when a system ends up denied, not due to a deliberate attack by a single individual or group of individuals, but simply due to a sudden enormous spike in popularity.

370746214c3f.title: Denial-of-service attack
370746214c3f.sentence: This can happen when an extremely popular website posts a prominent link to a second, less well-prepared site, for example, as part of a news story.

cfc04ff9bcfe.title: Denial-of-service attack
cfc04ff9bcfe.sentence: The result is that a significant proportion of the primary site's regular users – potentially hundreds of thousands of people – click that link in the space of a few hours, having the same effect on the target website as a DDoS attack.

d455031ecea8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
d455031ecea8.sentence: In a CDN, the origin server contains the original versions of the content while the edge servers are numerous and distributed across various locations around the world.

3f85a51924a8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-are-content-delivery-networks-cdn-so-popular.md
3f85a51924a8.sentence: - Origin Server: This is the primary source of content.

5373271f6ce0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-are-content-delivery-networks-cdn-so-popular.md
5373271f6ce0.sentence: - Edge Servers: They cache and server content to the users and are distributed across the world.

d6b1cb231ad0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
d6b1cb231ad0.sentence: To minimize the distance between the visitors and the website's server, a CDN stores a cached version of its content in multiple geographical locations known as edge locations.

ef5f11903c50.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
ef5f11903c50.sentence: Each edge location contains several caching servers responsible for content delivery to visitors within its proximity.

99daa4b6a363.title: Content delivery network
99daa4b6a363.sentence: Most CDN providers will provide their services over a varying, defined set of PoPs, depending on the coverage desired, such as the United States, Asia-Pacific, International or Global, etc. These sets of PoPs can be called "edges", "edge nodes", "edge servers", or "edge networks" as they would be the closest edge of CDN assets to the end user.

0ee2a4ab18ea.sentence: This means that, unlike client–server systems, the content-centric networks can actually perform better as more users begin to access the content (especially with protocols such as Bittorrent that require users to share).

fc65cb581593.title: Content delivery network
fc65cb581593.sentence: If content owners are not satisfied with the options or costs of a commercial CDN service, they can create their own CDN.

7f8deccfb6a4.title: Content delivery network
7f8deccfb6a4.sentence: This is called a private CDN.

0ab7fe00a42a.title: Content delivery network
0ab7fe00a42a.sentence: A private CDN consists of PoPs (points of presence) that are only serving content for their owner.

03f49d496ab1.title: Content delivery network
03f49d496ab1.sentence: These PoPs can be caching servers, reverse proxies or application delivery controllers.

4420fd0415f9.title: Content delivery network
4420fd0415f9.sentence: It can be as simple as two caching servers, or large enough to serve petabytes of content.

3fe3428dca35.title: Content delivery network

87e2355fbd8f.title: Content delivery network
87e2355fbd8f.sentence: Large content distribution networks may even build and set up their own private network to distribute copies of content across cache locations.

dbe8510e0991.title: Content delivery network
dbe8510e0991.sentence: Such private networks are usually used in conjunction with public networks as a backup option in case the capacity of the private network is not enough or there is a failure which leads to capacity reduction.

107a902ab10b.title: Content delivery network
107a902ab10b.section: CDN trends > Emergence of telco CDNs
107a902ab10b.sentence: To address this, telecommunications service providers have begun to launch their own content delivery networks as a means to lessen the demands on the network backbone and reduce infrastructure investments.

78bba50f7a9a.title: Content delivery network
78bba50f7a9a.sentence: Because they own the networks over which video content is transmitted, telco CDNs have advantages over traditional CDNs.

7d371fbc816c.title: Content delivery network
7d371fbc816c.section: CDN trends > Emergence of telco CDNs
7d371fbc816c.sentence: The rapid growth of streaming video traffic required large capital expenditures by broadband providers in order to meet new demand and retain subscribers by delivering a sufficient quality of experience.

2bb69af0148c.title: Content delivery network
2bb69af0148c.sentence: They own the last mile and can deliver content closer to the end-user because it can be cached deep in their networks.

195f54706b2b.title: Content delivery network
195f54706b2b.sentence: This deep caching minimizes the distance that video data travels over the general Internet and delivers it more quickly and reliably.

e0dd26fc0ec1.title: Content delivery network
e0dd26fc0ec1.sentence: Telco CDNs also have a built-in cost advantage since traditional CDNs must lease bandwidth from them and build the operator's margin into their own cost model.

7b67758ac37c.title: Content delivery network
7b67758ac37c.sentence: In addition, by operating their own content delivery infrastructure, telco operators have better control over the utilization of their resources.

7847da2ee53c.title: Content delivery network
7847da2ee53c.sentence: Content management operations performed by CDNs are usually applied without (or with very limited) information about the network (e.g., topology, utilization, etc.) of the telco operators with which they interact or have business relationships.

bb7581f8caa4.title: Content delivery network
bb7581f8caa4.sentence: In contrast, the deployment of telco-CDNs allows operators to implement their own content management operations, which enables them to have better control over the utilization of their resources and, as such, provide better quality of service and experience to their end users.

ee39f6264980.title: Content delivery network
ee39f6264980.sentence: Virtualization technologies are being used to deploy virtual CDNs (vCDNs) (also known as a software-defined CDN or sd-CDN) to reduce content provider costs, and at the same time, increase elasticity and decrease service delay.

0418d17aa37b.title: Content delivery network
0418d17aa37b.sentence: With vCDNs, it is possible to avoid traditional CDN limitations, such as performance, reliability, and availability, since virtual caches are deployed dynamically (as virtual machines or containers) in physical servers distributed across the provider's geographical coverage.

65f08bfb5316.title: Content delivery network
65f08bfb5316.sentence: As the virtual cache placement is based on both the content type and server or end-user geographic location, the vCDNs have a significant impact on service delivery and network congestion.

5f658626f474.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-are-content-delivery-networks-cdn-so-popular.md
5f658626f474.sentence: - The edge server checks its local cache for the content.

70e8c3b9ec9f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-are-content-delivery-networks-cdn-so-popular.md

6a63e4168ef5.sentence: If found, the edge server serves the content to the user.

a05e32d65598.sentence: - If not found, the edge server forwards the request to the origin server.

c7ad267bca9b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
c7ad267bca9b.sentence: Once the static assets are cached on all the CDN servers for a particular location, all subsequent website visitor requests for static assets will be delivered from these edge servers instead of the origin, thus reducing the origin load and improving scalability.

0ee7be3543fa.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming

3b1b32af059e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
3b1b32af059e.sentence: Sites with a small amount of traffic or sites with content that isn't often updated work well with push CDNs.

a8bb2d179e0a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn
a8bb2d179e0a.sentence: Contrary to the Push CDN, this requires less maintenance because cache updates on CDN nodes are performed based on requests from the client to the origin server.

ab7080fa8e46.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::content-delivery-network-cdn

9f2537f5498e.title: Edge computing
9f2537f5498e.sentence: Edge computing is a distributed computing model that brings computation and data storage closer to the sources of data.

82a40d05a107.title: Edge computing
82a40d05a107.sentence: More broadly, it refers to any design that pushes computation physically closer to a user, so as to reduce the latency compared to when an application runs on a centralized data center.

0f8660f961c5.title: Edge computing
0f8660f961c5.sentence: Edge computing involves running computer programs that deliver quick responses close to where requests are made.

49831da5c695.title: Edge computing
49831da5c695.sentence: A CDN uses nodes located at the network edge, close to users, to prefetch and cache web content.

b9040feda356.title: Edge computing
b9040feda356.sentence: These edge nodes can also perform content customization, such as displaying location-relevant advertising.

3ba6bf55613f.title: Edge computing

a855b9604fc1.title: Edge computing
a855b9604fc1.sentence: In the early 2000s, these systems expanded their scope to hosting other applications, leading to early edge computing services.

3504259e152d.title: Edge computing
3504259e152d.sentence: These services could do things like find dealers, manage shopping carts, gather real-time data, and place ads.

2450ccb0067f.title: Edge computing
2450ccb0067f.sentence: The increase in IoT devices at the edge of the network is producing a massive amount of data — storing and using all that data in cloud data centers pushes network bandwidth requirements to the limit.

150c51147ab5.title: Edge computing
150c51147ab5.sentence: Despite the improvements in network technology, data centers cannot guarantee acceptable transfer rates and response times, which often is a critical requirement for many applications.

065c6dc5f16a.title: Edge computing
065c6dc5f16a.sentence: Edge computing brings analytical computational resources close to the end users and therefore can increase the responsiveness and throughput of applications.

eda62f169d54.title: Edge computing
eda62f169d54.sentence: Avoiding transmission over the internet results in significant bandwidth savings and therefore increases efficiency.

5c94d641d724.title: Edge computing
5c94d641d724.sentence: If the recognition is performed locally, it is possible to send the recognized text to the cloud rather than audio recordings, significantly reducing the amount of required bandwidth.

6c8a5831a80a.title: Edge computing
6c8a5831a80a.sentence: Management of failovers is crucial in order to keep a service alive.

c7d59ea7d700.title: Edge computing

63745f5e7828.title: Edge computing
63745f5e7828.sentence: As an example, an edge computing device, such as a voice assistant, may continue to provide service to local users even during cloud service or internet outages.

fb7e2c9c0a22.title: Edge computing

04bcbc644b00.title: Edge computing

f5617db56dea.title: Edge computing
f5617db56dea.sentence: Edge nodes may also be resource-constrained devices, limiting the choice in terms of security methods.

ccd43d37c266.title: Edge computing
ccd43d37c266.sentence: On the other hand, by keeping and processing data at the edge, it is possible to increase privacy by minimizing the transmission of sensitive information to the cloud.

e6132a5e2a79.title: Subresource Integrity
e6132a5e2a79.sentence: Specifically, it validates assets served by a third party, such as a content delivery network (CDN).

c15302c72132.title: Subresource Integrity
c15302c72132.sentence: This ensures these assets have not been compromised for hostile purposes.

39fcb495b1df.title: Subresource Integrity
39fcb495b1df.sentence: To use SRI, a website author wishing to include a resource from a third party can specify a cryptographic hash of the resource in addition to the location of the resource.

be4b75e4dcf5.title: Subresource Integrity
be4b75e4dcf5.sentence: Browsers fetching the resource can then compare the hash provided by the website author with the hash computed from the resource.

65aad332b877.title: Subresource Integrity
65aad332b877.sentence: If the hashes don't match, the resource is discarded.

e8eb366bf895.title: Subresource Integrity
e8eb366bf895.sentence: An integrity value may contain more than one space-separated hash expression.

120e22abab77.title: Subresource Integrity
120e22abab77.sentence: Each expression combines a hash algorithm name with a Base64-encoded digest; when several recognized algorithms are supplied, the user agent validates the response using the strongest algorithm in the list.

f85dc79cd35a.title: Subresource Integrity
f85dc79cd35a.sentence: Subresource Integrity can be used with JavaScript files and linked stylesheets.

ea482fad2f60.title: Subresource Integrity
ea482fad2f60.sentence: When a resource is loaded from a different origin, integrity verification requires Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS), with the server permitting access through the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.

2cac248be863.title: Subresource Integrity
2cac248be863.sentence: The crossorigin attribute enables the browser to request such resources in CORS mode.

b62dd655181f.title: Content delivery network
b62dd655181f.sentence: CDNs serving JavaScript have also been targeted as a way to inject malicious content into pages using them.

479e38aaac08.title: Content delivery network
479e38aaac08.sentence: As such these services are being pointed out as potential privacy intrusions for behavioral targeting and solutions are being created to restore single-origin serving and caching of resources.

c3d4f41c61fa.title: Content delivery network
c3d4f41c61fa.sentence: CDN vendors may cross over into other industries like security, DDoS protection and web application firewalls (WAF), and WAN optimization.

b13a7ad05bd1.title: Content delivery network
b13a7ad05bd1.sentence: Subresource Integrity mechanism was created in response to ensure that the page loads a script whose content is known and constrained to a hash referenced by the website author.

be5ee7c004af.title: Content delivery network
be5ee7c004af.sentence: CDN providers profit either from direct fees paid by content providers using their network, or profit from the user analytics and tracking data collected as their scripts are being loaded onto customers' websites inside their browser origin.

eec7715fab39.title: Content delivery network
eec7715fab39.sentence: In particular, a website using a CDN may violate the EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

5c3426af8aad.title: Content delivery network
5c3426af8aad.sentence: For example, in 2021 a German court forbade the use of a CDN on a university website, because this caused the transmission of the user's IP address to the CDN, which violated the GDPR.

a0a83f07c97b.title: Database
a0a83f07c97b.sentence: In computing, a database is an organized collection of data or a type of data store based on the use of a database management system (DBMS), the software that interacts with end users, applications, and the database itself to capture and analyze the data.

786a39eb6b7c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
786a39eb6b7c.sentence: A database is an organized collection of structured information, or data, typically stored electronically in a computer system.

0c7c11873c4b.title: Database
0c7c11873c4b.sentence: The sum total of the database, the DBMS and the associated applications can be referred to as a database system.

bb5a4a821203.title: Database
bb5a4a821203.sentence: Often the term "database" is also used loosely to refer to any of the DBMS, the database system or an application associated with the database.

a5ce15787850.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
a5ce15787850.sentence: Together, the data and the DBMS, along with the applications that are associated with them, are referred to as a database system, often shortened to just database.

541ca49a00e9.title: Database
541ca49a00e9.sentence: Databases are used to support internal operations of organizations and to underpin online interactions with customers and suppliers (see Enterprise software).

19144e7c6be6.title: Database
19144e7c6be6.sentence: Examples include computerized library systems, flight reservation systems, computerized parts inventory systems, and many content management systems that store websites as collections of webpages in a database.

933c793b0855.title: Database
933c793b0855.sentence: One way to classify databases involves the type of their contents, for example: bibliographic, document-text, statistical, or multimedia objects.

1eb659d64827.title: Database
1eb659d64827.sentence: Another way is by their application area, for example: accounting, music compositions, movies, banking, manufacturing, or insurance.

60164277576c.title: Database
60164277576c.sentence: A third way is by some technical aspect, such as the database structure or interface type.

4ffdb2211244.title: Database
4ffdb2211244.sentence: - An in-memory database is a database that primarily resides in main memory, but is typically backed-up by non-volatile computer data storage.

c15d60c92769.title: Database
c15d60c92769.sentence: Main memory databases are faster than disk databases, and so are often used where response time is critical, such as in telecommunications network equipment.

e5ea664e7541.title: Database
e5ea664e7541.sentence: - A distributed database is one in which both the data and the DBMS span multiple computers.

94c87c565f48.title: Database
94c87c565f48.sentence: A common example is storing materialized views, which consist of frequently needed external views or query results.

bbad7fd18e05.title: Database
bbad7fd18e05.sentence: Storing such views saves the expensive computing them each time they are needed.

8f2cd6f44d2f.title: Database
8f2cd6f44d2f.sentence: Occasionally a database employs storage redundancy by database objects replication (with one or more copies) to increase data availability (both to improve performance of simultaneous multiple end-user accesses to the same database object, and to provide resiliency in a case of partial failure of a distributed database).

7f4b32df0220.title: Database
7f4b32df0220.sentence: Sometimes it is desired to bring a database back to a previous state (for many reasons, e.g., cases when the database is found corrupted due to a software error, or if it has been updated with erroneous data).

3a6e09d6c8f6.title: Database
3a6e09d6c8f6.sentence: To achieve this, a backup operation is done occasionally or continuously, where each desired database state (i.e., the values of its data and their embedding in database's data structures) is kept within dedicated backup files (many techniques exist to do this effectively).

6c4af33283eb.title: Relational database
6c4af33283eb.sentence: A relational database (RDB) is a database based on the relational model of data, as proposed by E. F. Codd in 1970.

35055a2b17dc.title: Relational database
35055a2b17dc.sentence: A Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) is a type of database management system that stores data in a structured format using rows and columns.

130a8f17bfb7.title: Relational database
130a8f17bfb7.sentence: A relational model organizes data into one or more tables (or "relations") of columns and rows, with a unique key identifying each row.

cdb7af799b5d.title: Relational database
cdb7af799b5d.sentence: Many relational database systems are equipped with the option of using SQL (Structured Query Language) for querying and updating the database.

a092ec527862.title: Relational database
a092ec527862.sentence: Generally, each table/relation represents one "entity type" (such as customer or product).

c3fb2bd2e92e.title: Relational database
c3fb2bd2e92e.sentence: The rows represent instances of that type of entity (such as "Lee" or "chair") and the columns represent values attributed to that instance (such as address or price).

e01751dee797.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
e01751dee797.sentence: It supports data integrity and avoids redundancy through the use of keys and normalization.

03c7b5f2a97c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
03c7b5f2a97c.sentence: It efficiently handles many-to-many relationships and supports complex queries and transactions.

058f8e9db0a4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
058f8e9db0a4.sentence: The relational model's strength lies in its flexibility and the simplicity of its query language, SQL (Structured Query Language), making it the most widely used data model for traditional database systems.

88e7be999f04.title: Relational database
88e7be999f04.sentence: In order for a database management system (DBMS) to operate efficiently and accurately, it must use ACID transactions.

2a24e173d4c9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
2a24e173d4c9.sentence: In order to maintain consistency before and after a transaction relational databases follow ACID properties.

2a3f04dbea03.title: Relational database
2a3f04dbea03.sentence: One well-known definition of what constitutes a relational database system is composed of Codd's 12 rules.

0b942714cfa0.title: Relational database
0b942714cfa0.sentence: However, no commercial implementations of the relational model conform to all of Codd's rules, so the term has gradually come to describe a broader class of database systems, which at a minimum:

f2094dce9e96.title: Relational database
f2094dce9e96.sentence: A relational database has become the predominant type of database.

5a8b7efe9d1e.title: Relational database
5a8b7efe9d1e.sentence: Most databases in widespread use today are based on this model.

e0c99398c0b4.title: Relational database
e0c99398c0b4.sentence: Relational databases have often replaced legacy hierarchical databases and network databases, because RDBMS were easier to implement and administer.

85a6e6e8e512.title: Relational database
85a6e6e8e512.sentence: However, due to the expanse of technologies, such as horizontal scaling of computer clusters, NoSQL databases have recently become popular as an alternative to RDBMS databases.

3a087194c71d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
3a087194c71d.sentence: Let's look at some advantages of using relational databases:

6a674975c2c0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
6a674975c2c0.sentence: Below are the disadvantages of relational databases:

c0579e85d457.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
c0579e85d457.sentence: - Difficult to scale due to poor horizontal scalability

dc22fd97cfe5.title: NoSQL
dc22fd97cfe5.sentence: NoSQL (a colloquial title that became formal, meaning "not only SQL" or "non-relational") refers to a type of database design that stores and retrieves data differently from the traditional table-based structure of relational databases.

491b2cf5540c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
491b2cf5540c.sentence: NoSQL is a broad category that includes any database that doesn't use SQL as its primary data access language.

7685a1553605.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
7685a1553605.sentence: These types of databases are also sometimes referred to as non-relational databases.

33b164ab36e3.title: NoSQL
33b164ab36e3.sentence: Unlike relational databases, which organize data into rows and columns like a spreadsheet, NoSQL databases use a single data structure—such as key–value pairs, wide columns, graphs, or documents—to hold information.

cb54542fd949.title: NoSQL
cb54542fd949.sentence: Since this non-relational design does not require a fixed schema, it scales easily to manage large, often unstructured datasets.

d5992ecc18eb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
d5992ecc18eb.sentence: Unlike in relational databases, data in a NoSQL database doesn't have to conform to a pre-defined schema.

0893d3c66a21.title: NoSQL
0893d3c66a21.sentence: NoSQL systems are sometimes called "Not only SQL" because they can support SQL-like query languages or work alongside SQL databases in polyglot-persistent setups, where multiple database types are combined.

4a4f54ecef91.title: NoSQL
4a4f54ecef91.sentence: NoSQL databases are popular in big data and real-time web applications due to their simple design, ability to scale across clusters of machines (called horizontal scaling), and precise control over data availability.

683ca86d3cb6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
683ca86d3cb6.sentence: On the other hand, NoSQL databases are horizontally scalable, meaning we can add more servers easily to our NoSQL database infrastructure to handle large traffic.

90fbe8f53c1e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
90fbe8f53c1e.sentence: Any cheap commodity hardware or cloud instances can host NoSQL databases, thus making it a lot more cost-effective than vertical scaling.

24a0ba2fb4b1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
24a0ba2fb4b1.sentence: A lot of NoSQL technologies also distribute data across servers automatically.

b1befdd0744d.title: NoSQL
b1befdd0744d.sentence: However, many NoSQL systems prioritize speed and availability over strict consistency (per the CAP theorem), using eventual consistency—where updates reach all nodes eventually, typically within milliseconds, but may cause brief delays in accessing the latest data, known as stale reads.

d118ae464504.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
d118ae464504.sentence: NoSQL databases follow BASE consistency model.

800b161c3fe2.title: Database
800b161c3fe2.sentence: For that reason, many NoSQL databases are using what is called eventual consistency to provide both availability and partition tolerance guarantees with a reduced level of data consistency.

0e184e23325e.title: NoSQL
0e184e23325e.sentence: While most lack full ACID transaction support, some, like MongoDB, include it as a key feature.

90e40dfd026c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
90e40dfd026c.sentence: Most of the NoSQL solutions sacrifice ACID compliance for performance and scalability.

78ae98c0e8b3.title: NoSQL
78ae98c0e8b3.sentence: Barriers to wider NoSQL adoption include their use of low-level query languages instead of SQL, inability to perform ad hoc joins across tables, lack of standardized interfaces, and significant investments already made in relational databases.

d65e4a556041.title: NoSQL
d65e4a556041.sentence: There are various ways to classify NoSQL databases, with different categories and subcategories, some of which overlap.

119391513168.title: NoSQL
119391513168.sentence: What follows is a non-exhaustive classification by data model, with examples:

05db3770fa6f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
05db3770fa6f.sentence: A time-series database is a database optimized for time-stamped, or time series, data.

682bb2198587.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
682bb2198587.sentence: Multi-model databases combine different database models (i.e. relational, graph, key-value, document, etc.) into a single, integrated backend.

b2a83ed76e09.title: Database
b2a83ed76e09.sentence: NewSQL is a class of modern relational databases that aims to provide the same scalable performance of NoSQL systems for online transaction processing (read-write) workloads while still using SQL and maintaining the ACID guarantees of a traditional database system.

c5a8b6d7ebf6.title: Graph database
c5a8b6d7ebf6.sentence: A graph database (GDB) is a database that uses graph structures for semantic queries with nodes, edges, and properties to represent and store data.

b5a4dbbd804f.title: Graph database
b5a4dbbd804f.sentence: Based on graph theory, graph databases store data in a way that reflects how it is conceptually understood, using nodes to represent entities and edges to represent the relationships between them.

82df0ed8e976.title: Graph database
82df0ed8e976.sentence: Relationships are first-class citizens in a graph database and can be labeled, directed, and given properties.

aa14706be57b.title: Graph database
aa14706be57b.sentence: The graph relates the data items in the store to a collection of nodes and edges, the edges representing the relationships between the nodes.

32fd9cdbd8fc.title: Graph database
32fd9cdbd8fc.sentence: The relationships allow data in the store to be linked together directly and, in many cases, retrieved with one operation.

e4074fefd55a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
e4074fefd55a.sentence: The relationships allow data in the store to be linked together directly and, in many cases, retrieved with one operation.

99161c57fbc6.title: Graph database
99161c57fbc6.sentence: Graph databases typically implement index-free adjacency, in which nodes store direct references to other nodes in the database, as opposed to a relational database, which uses a single global database index.

6a4962fe3fdb.title: Graph database
6a4962fe3fdb.sentence: Direct references are likened to a "micro-index", and typically allow O(1) access-times when querying to adjacent nodes, whereas querying an index is typically O(log(n)) with n being the size of the index, meaning that query times are proportional to the how much of the graph is queried rather than the size of the graph.

de6536c2d87f.title: Graph database
de6536c2d87f.sentence: A labeled-property graph model is represented by a set of nodes, relationships, properties, and labels.

e8984ae4f675.title: Graph database
e8984ae4f675.sentence: Both nodes of data and their relationships are named and can store properties represented by key–value pairs.

035ddcc2e68a.title: Graph database
035ddcc2e68a.sentence: The edges representing the relationships have two qualities: they always have a start node and an end node, and are directed; making the graph a directed graph.

c7fc390c8b79.title: Graph database
c7fc390c8b79.sentence: In an RDF graph model, each addition of information is represented with a separate node.

78dba5263916.title: Graph database
78dba5263916.sentence: An RDF graph notation or a statement is represented by: a node for the subject, a node for the object, and an arc for the predicate.

85d67893959c.title: Graph database
85d67893959c.sentence: Graph databases are a powerful tool for graph-like queries.

bf3bf2ec4969.title: Graph database
bf3bf2ec4969.sentence: For example, computing the shortest path between two nodes in the graph.

d31d67c18506.title: Graph database
d31d67c18506.sentence: Other graph-like queries can be performed over a graph database in a natural way (for example graph's diameter computations or community detection).

13be513ea6b8.title: Graph database
13be513ea6b8.sentence: Graphs are flexible, meaning it allows the user to insert new data into the existing graph without loss of application functionality.

b2110fe378be.title: Graph database
b2110fe378be.sentence: There is no need for the designer of the database to plan out extensive details of the database's future use cases.

a2b125d11ac8.title: Graph database
a2b125d11ac8.sentence: Although relationships can be analyzed with the relational model, complex queries performing many join operations on many different attributes over several tables are required.

c8ba5ba8744a.title: Graph database
c8ba5ba8744a.sentence: This can eliminate the costly join operations.

3698a6310910.title: Graph database
3698a6310910.sentence: The true value of the graph approach becomes evident when one performs searches that are more than one level deep.

3218c80fd8b4.title: Graph database
3218c80fd8b4.sentence: The relative advantage of graph retrieval grows with the complexity of a query.

13b29ccd728c.title: Graph database
13b29ccd728c.sentence: They can scale more naturally to large datasets as they do not typically need join operations, which can often be expensive.

8fd8177f44d9.title: Graph database
8fd8177f44d9.sentence: Relational databases are very well suited to flat data layouts, where relationships between data are only one or two levels deep.

d93266e54d8c.title: Graph database
d93266e54d8c.sentence: Conversely, relational database management systems are typically faster at performing the same operation on large numbers of data elements, permitting the manipulation of the data in its natural structure.

6f1502fca7ab.title: Graph database
6f1502fca7ab.sentence: Despite the graph databases' advantages and recent popularity over relational databases, it is recommended the graph model itself should not be the sole reason to replace an existing relational database.

d070bf9f77e1.title: Graph database
d070bf9f77e1.sentence: A graph database may become relevant if there is an evidence for performance improvement by orders of magnitude and lower latency.

13aed6eb215c.title: NoSQL
13aed6eb215c.sentence: Graph databases are designed for data whose relations are well represented as a graph consisting of elements connected by a finite number of relations.

7e02fe93eae8.title: NoSQL
7e02fe93eae8.sentence: Examples of data include social relations, public transport links, road maps, network topologies, etc.

58161fbfb3f0.title: Graph database
58161fbfb3f0.sentence: They are especially well suited to social networking systems, where the "friends" relationship is essentially unbounded.

9c1a1a9977cc.title: Graph database
9c1a1a9977cc.sentence: As of 2021, no graph query language has been universally adopted in the same way as SQL was for relational databases.

d31f18a635d2.title: Graph database
d31f18a635d2.sentence: Early standardization efforts led to multi-vendor query languages like Gremlin, SPARQL, and Cypher.

3a056a9028d6.title: Graph database
3a056a9028d6.sentence: GQL is intended to be a declarative database query language, like SQL.

553f72c699ec.title: Document-oriented database
553f72c699ec.sentence: A document-oriented database, or document store, is a computer program and data storage system designed for storing, retrieving, and managing document-oriented information, also known as semi-structured data.

6998a82b92b3.title: Database
6998a82b92b3.sentence: - A document-oriented database is designed for storing, retrieving, and managing document-oriented, or semi structured, information.

9200096d0cb7.title: Database
9200096d0cb7.sentence: Document-oriented databases are one of the main categories of NoSQL databases.

0c701d5ca7ed.title: Document-oriented database
0c701d5ca7ed.sentence: Although implementations vary in their specific definitions, document-oriented databases generally treat documents as self-contained units that encapsulate and encode data in a standardized format.

41ef2ff6642b.title: Document-oriented database
41ef2ff6642b.sentence: Common encoding formats include XML, YAML, JSON, as well as binary representations such as BSON.

b04038b82e3a.title: Document-oriented database
b04038b82e3a.sentence: Documents in a document store are equivalent to the programming concept of an object.

247527373dcd.title: NoSQL
247527373dcd.sentence: While the details of this definition differ among document-oriented databases, they all assume that documents encapsulate and encode data (or information) in some standard formats or encodings.

7075e8e2605d.title: NoSQL
7075e8e2605d.sentence: Encodings in use include XML, YAML, and JSON and binary forms like BSON.

9fcffdab365d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/types-of-databases.md
9fcffdab365d.sentence: - Document DB: A document database is a kind of database that stores information in a format similar to JSON.

d976e16e34f6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/types-of-databases.md
d976e16e34f6.sentence: It's different from traditional databases and is made for working with documents instead of tables.

067f06bf4364.title: Document-oriented database
067f06bf4364.sentence: They are not required to adhere to a fixed schema, and documents within the same collection may contain different fields or structures.

e653915ebc28.title: Document-oriented database
e653915ebc28.sentence: Unlike relational databases, in which each record contains the same fields and unused fields are left empty, document-oriented databases do not require uniform fields across documents.

f4651f060762.title: Document-oriented database
f4651f060762.sentence: This design allows new information to be added to some documents without affecting the structure of others.

1e6008520a6e.title: NoSQL
1e6008520a6e.sentence: Compared to relational databases, collections could be considered analogous to tables and documents analogous to records.

5e1a1bf9d001.title: NoSQL
5e1a1bf9d001.sentence: But they are different – every record in a table has the same sequence of fields, while documents in a collection may have fields that are completely different.

19e6e6c9be1a.title: Document-oriented database
19e6e6c9be1a.sentence: Documents in a document-oriented database are addressed via a unique identifier.

dbc9b5689d9e.title: Document-oriented database
dbc9b5689d9e.sentence: This identifier, often a string, URI, or path, can be used to retrieve the document from the database.

9315ef7e11c5.title: Document-oriented database
9315ef7e11c5.sentence: Most document stores maintain an index on the key to optimize retrieval, and in some implementations the key is required when creating or inserting a new document.

50125edcd3e4.title: NoSQL
50125edcd3e4.sentence: Documents are addressed in the database via a unique key that represents that document.

1dce19a18cb8.title: Document-oriented database
1dce19a18cb8.sentence: In addition to key-based access, document-oriented databases typically provide an API or query language that enables retrieval based on document content or associated metadata.

cb1f7372a25e.title: Document-oriented database
cb1f7372a25e.sentence: For example, a query may return all documents with a specific field matching a given value.

773248f1fbd2.title: Document-oriented database
773248f1fbd2.sentence: The available query features, indexing options, and performance characteristics vary across implementations.

f56512c352c5.title: NoSQL
f56512c352c5.sentence: Another defining characteristic of a document-oriented database is an API or query language to retrieve documents based on their contents.

0783cb07ded1.title: Document-oriented database
0783cb07ded1.sentence: Updates may involve replacing the entire document or modifying individual elements or fields within the document.

7e54beaba9b2.title: Document-oriented database
7e54beaba9b2.sentence: In key-value stores, data is treated as opaque by the database, whereas document-oriented systems exploit the internal structure of documents to extract metadata and optimize storage and queries.

90cb767d06ef.title: Document-oriented database
90cb767d06ef.sentence: By contrast, document-oriented databases can classify and interpret document content.

bd7c16b114da.title: Document-oriented database
bd7c16b114da.sentence: This enables queries that distinguish between types of data––for example, retrieving all phone numbers containing "555" without also matching a postal code such as "55555."

116271d6b946.title: Document-oriented database
116271d6b946.section: Relationship to other databases > Relationship to key-value stores
116271d6b946.sentence: For users who do not require advanced query, retrieval, or update capabilities, the distinction between document-oriented databases and key-value stores may be minimal.

86c5dac58424.title: Document-oriented database
86c5dac58424.sentence: Relational databases store data in predefined tables, often requiring an object to be split across multiple tables.

942eb5c78377.title: Document-oriented database
942eb5c78377.sentence: In contrast, document databases store all information for a given object in a single document, with each document potentially having a unique structure.

ee04ed3e0ba8.title: Document-oriented database
ee04ed3e0ba8.sentence: This design eliminates the need for object-relational mapping when loading data into the database.

65117a05b366.title: Document-oriented database
65117a05b366.section: Relationship to other databases > Relationship to relational databases
65117a05b366.sentence: In contrast, a document-oriented database stores all data related to an object within a single document, and stored in the database as a single entry.

2f839c915da0.title: Document-oriented database
2f839c915da0.section: Relationship to other databases > Relationship to relational databases
2f839c915da0.sentence: The document is retrieved using a unique key, and all related information is returned together, without needing to look up multiple tables.

ed09c86ba3ef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
ed09c86ba3ef.sentence: They are general-purpose databases that serve a variety of use cases for both transactional and analytical applications.

f6bae94985df.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
f6bae94985df.sentence: Elasticsearch is a distributed, free and open search and analytics engine for all types of data, including textual, numerical, geospatial, structured, and unstructured.

007f61530afc.title: Elasticsearch
007f61530afc.sentence: It is based on Apache Lucene and provides a distributed, multitenant-capable full-text search engine with an HTTP web interface and schema-free JSON documents.

e14e8ed31e6e.title: Elasticsearch
e14e8ed31e6e.sentence: Elasticsearch is built on Apache Lucene and exposes Lucene's capabilities through a JSON and Java API.

252ab6686e93.title: Elasticsearch
252ab6686e93.sentence: Documents are stored in indices, which are divided into primary shards; each shard may have zero or more replicas distributed across cluster nodes.

8fe4cc86cb5f.title: Elasticsearch
8fe4cc86cb5f.sentence: Routing and rebalancing are handled automatically.

f82d5639b212.title: Elasticsearch
f82d5639b212.sentence: Elasticsearch is distributed and uses JSON documents stored in indices divided into shards, each of which may have replicas distributed across cluster nodes.

aea1d08e75b4.title: Elasticsearch
aea1d08e75b4.sentence: Once an index has been created, the number of primary shards cannot be changed.

53bdb0791c7e.title: Elasticsearch
53bdb0791c7e.sentence: It supports full-text search, faceted search, real-time search, and multitenancy.

2f55e79deded.title: Elasticsearch
2f55e79deded.sentence: The engine supports faceted search and percolation, a form of prospective search in which stored queries are matched against incoming documents rather than the reverse.

c59602875a34.title: Elasticsearch
c59602875a34.sentence: Real-time GET requests make Elasticsearch usable as a NoSQL datastore, though it does not support distributed transactions.

a3d13445dd2d.title: Spatial database
a3d13445dd2d.sentence: - Elasticsearch is a document-based database system that supports two types of geo data: geo_point fields which support lat/lon pairs, and geo_shape fields, which support points, lines, circles, polygons, multi-polygons, etc.

9bbe40a2dd4d.title: Key–value database
9bbe40a2dd4d.sentence: A key-value database, or key-value store, is a data storage paradigm designed for storing, retrieving, and managing associative arrays, a data structure more commonly known today as a dictionary.

d65c59d82780.title: Key–value database
d65c59d82780.sentence: These records are stored and retrieved using a key that uniquely identifies the record, and is used to find the data within the database.

921729a2ee33.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
921729a2ee33.sentence: One of the simplest types of NoSQL databases, key-value databases save data as a group of key-value pairs made up of two data items each.

52f353b53c13.title: NoSQL
52f353b53c13.sentence: Key–value (KV) stores use the associative array (also called a map or dictionary) as their fundamental data model.

44af77a84866.title: NoSQL
44af77a84866.sentence: In this model, data is represented as a collection of key–value pairs, such that each possible key appears at most once in the collection.

accb65460982.title: NoSQL
accb65460982.sentence: The key–value model is one of the simplest non-trivial data models, and richer data models are often implemented as an extension of it.

ea44826ccc9b.title: Key–value database
ea44826ccc9b.sentence: In contrast, key-value systems treat the value as opaque to the database itself, and typically support only simple operations such as storing, retrieving, updating, and deleting a value by its key.

5639bb32954e.title: Key–value database
5639bb32954e.sentence: Opaqueness is what distinguishes key–value DBMSs from document databases.

8582eb645112.title: Key–value database
8582eb645112.sentence: A document DBMS can interpret the structure of a record, whereas a key–value DBMS treats each value as an opaque object that can only be retrieved in its entirety by its associated key, rather than querying by and retrieving individual fields.

e6457f062f6c.title: Key–value database
e6457f062f6c.sentence: This offers considerable flexibility and makes such systems well suited to low-latency, high-throughput workloads dominated by direct key lookups, but less suitable for applications that require complex queries or explicit relationships among records.

91dbaa3c15b5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
91dbaa3c15b5.sentence: - Highly scalable for high volumes of traffic

f329a9e6ca40.title: Key–value database
f329a9e6ca40.sentence: A lack of standardization, limited transaction support, and relatively simple query interfaces long restricted many key-value systems to specialized uses, but the rapid move to cloud computing after 2010 helped drive renewed interest in them as part of the broader NoSQL movement.

27957d257246.title: Key–value database
27957d257246.sentence: Their scalability and availability made them attractive for cloud data management, although limited transaction support, low-level query interfaces, and the lack of standardization remained obstacles to wider adoption.

dcb6475755e2.title: NoSQL
dcb6475755e2.sentence: The key–value model can be extended to a discretely ordered model that maintains keys in lexicographic order.

67db43d459b1.title: NoSQL
67db43d459b1.sentence: This extension is computationally powerful, in that it can efficiently retrieve selective key ranges.

02c35450bf15.title: NoSQL
02c35450bf15.sentence: Some databases support ordering of keys.

a639797b33f7.title: Key–value database
a639797b33f7.sentence: For example, Oracle NoSQL Database organizes records using composite keys with "major" and "minor" components, an arrangement that Oracle compares to a directory-path structure in a file system.

3d84ca03133c.title: Key–value database
3d84ca03133c.sentence: Some key–value DBMSs do support complex value types; for example, Redis supports lists.

a594f831731d.title: Key–value database
a594f831731d.sentence: Key–value systems span a wide consistency spectrum, from eventually consistent designs to strongly consistent or serializable ones, and some allow the consistency level to be configured as part of the trade-off against latency and availability.

2588128c5b85.title: NoSQL
2588128c5b85.sentence: Key–value stores can use consistency models ranging from eventual consistency to serializability.

ac9400b4bd98.title: Key–value database
ac9400b4bd98.sentence: Some maintain data in memory (RAM), while others employ solid-state drives or rotating disks.

d473296ff2a2.title: NoSQL
d473296ff2a2.sentence: There are various hardware implementations, and some users store data in memory (RAM), while others on solid-state drives (SSD) or rotating disks (aka hard disk drive (HDD)).

cc3cef9951cd.title: Key–value database
cc3cef9951cd.sentence: Other examples include in-memory systems such as Memcached and Redis, and persistent systems such as Berkeley DB, Riak, and Voldemort.

4a837459d663.title: Key–value database
4a837459d663.sentence: A more recent example is RocksDB, a persistent key–value storage engine developed at Facebook and designed for large-scale applications.

81541418c275.title: Database
81541418c275.sentence: Connolly and Begg define database management system (DBMS) as a "software system that enables users to define, create, maintain and control access to the database." Examples of DBMS include MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle Database, and Microsoft Access.

1fcddea31e86.title: Database
1fcddea31e86.sentence: The DBMS additionally encompasses the core facilities provided to administer the database.

094212cd9386.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
094212cd9386.sentence: A DBMS serves as an interface between the database and its end-users or programs, allowing users to retrieve, update, and manage how the information is organized and optimized.

33cfc0e98bbe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
33cfc0e98bbe.sentence: A DBMS also facilitates oversight and control of databases, enabling a variety of administrative operations such as performance monitoring, tuning, and backup and recovery.

0625ffb2b05e.title: Database
0625ffb2b05e.sentence: The core functionality is the storage, retrieval and update of data.

45d878a5895e.title: Database
45d878a5895e.sentence: The functionality provided by a DBMS can vary enormously.

4be197355a8a.title: Database
4be197355a8a.sentence: Codd proposed the following functions and services a fully-fledged general purpose DBMS should provide:

43389867c629.title: Database
43389867c629.sentence: - User accessible catalog or data dictionary describing the metadata

688886c6fe16.title: Database
688886c6fe16.sentence: - Facilities for recovering the database should it become damaged

5e9a2edb508b.title: Database
5e9a2edb508b.sentence: - Support for authorization of access and update of data

bca76de430fe.title: Database
bca76de430fe.sentence: - Enforcing constraints to ensure data in the database abides by certain rules

a4dca35da2b5.title: Database
a4dca35da2b5.sentence: The core part of the DBMS interacting between the database and the application interface sometimes referred to as the database engine.

47ab36420844.title: Database
47ab36420844.sentence: A general-purpose DBMS will provide public application programming interfaces (API) and optionally a processor for database languages such as SQL to allow applications to be written to interact with and manipulate the database.

a321ddb54f6a.title: Database
a321ddb54f6a.sentence: A special purpose DBMS may use a private API and be specifically customized and linked to a single application.

04d4d1d2236f.title: Database
04d4d1d2236f.sentence: The DBMS acronym is sometimes extended to indicate the underlying database model, with RDBMS for the relational, OODBMS for the object (oriented) and ORDBMS for the object–relational model.

c2e2d2d3fb04.title: Database
c2e2d2d3fb04.sentence: Other extensions can indicate some other characteristics, such as DDBMS for a distributed database management systems.

de1a09407b8b.title: Database
de1a09407b8b.sentence: The client–server architecture was a development where the application resided on a client desktop and the database on a server allowing the processing to be distributed.

be4a7882b676.title: Database
be4a7882b676.sentence: This evolved into a multitier architecture incorporating application servers and web servers with the end user interface via a web browser with the database only directly connected to the adjacent tier.

686ffdb06b54.title: Database transaction
686ffdb06b54.sentence: A database transaction symbolizes a unit of work, performed within a database management system (or similar system) against a database, that is treated in a coherent and reliable way independent of other transactions.

26350fee09d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
26350fee09d4.sentence: A transaction is a series of database operations that are considered to be a "single unit of work".

13f546df7d12.title: Database transaction
13f546df7d12.sentence: Transactions in a database environment have two main purposes:

6febdec1e7e0.title: Database transaction
6febdec1e7e0.sentence: - To provide reliable units of work that allow correct recovery from failures and keep a database consistent even in cases of system failure.

63ae1807da63.title: Database transaction
63ae1807da63.sentence: - To provide isolation between programs accessing a database concurrently.

a0eb017915c8.title: Database transaction
