a0eb017915c8.sentence: If this isolation is not provided, the programs' outcomes are possibly erroneous.

026c697e15b8.title: Database transaction
026c697e15b8.sentence: One example is a transfer from one bank account to another: the complete transaction requires subtracting the amount to be transferred from one account and adding that same amount to the other.

064f942300f5.title: Database transaction
064f942300f5.sentence: A database transaction, by definition, must be atomic (it must either be complete in its entirety or have no effect whatsoever), consistent (it must conform to existing constraints in the database), isolated (it must not affect other transactions) and durable (it must get written to persistent storage).

395ffd257b5b.title: Database transaction
395ffd257b5b.sentence: Database practitioners often refer to these properties of database transactions using the acronym ACID.

8297d50ab35b.title: Database transaction
8297d50ab35b.sentence: A transactional database is a DBMS that provides the ACID properties for a bracketed set of database operations (begin-commit).

ef974fb10a33.title: Database transaction
ef974fb10a33.sentence: Transactions ensure that the database is always in a consistent state, even in the event of concurrent updates and failures.

99e1e7f88ccf.title: Database
99e1e7f88ccf.sentence: Each transaction has well defined boundaries in terms of which program/code executions are included in that transaction (determined by the transaction's programmer via special transaction commands).

efdca6d86314.title: Database transaction
efdca6d86314.sentence: Database systems implement distributed transactions as transactions accessing data over multiple nodes.

e4d47295c84f.title: Database transaction
e4d47295c84f.sentence: A distributed transaction enforces the ACID properties over multiple nodes, and might include systems such as databases, storage managers, file systems, messaging systems, and other data managers.

2564f35b5ff8.title: Database transaction
2564f35b5ff8.sentence: In a distributed transaction there is typically an entity coordinating all the process to ensure that all parts of the transaction are applied to all relevant systems.

e7a618cf3883.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
e7a618cf3883.sentence: Not all databases choose to support ACID transactions, usually because they are prioritizing other optimizations that are hard or theoretically impossible to implement together.

325290c48d91.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
325290c48d91.sentence: Usually, relational databases support ACID transactions, and non-relational databases don't (there are exceptions).

c9d0c6aac6cf.title: ACID
c9d0c6aac6cf.sentence: In computer science, ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability) is a set of properties of database transactions intended to guarantee data validity despite errors, power failures, and other mishaps.

51eca88aefc3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
51eca88aefc3.sentence: The term ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

57806cade7e4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
57806cade7e4.sentence: ACID properties are used for maintaining data integrity during transaction processing.

0228c07f099f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
0228c07f099f.sentence: The writes in a transaction are executed all at once and cannot be broken into smaller parts.

49973c058e75.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
49973c058e75.sentence: If there are faults when executing the transaction, the writes in the transaction are rolled back.

aa2dcce0c128.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
aa2dcce0c128.sentence: All operations in a transaction succeed or every operation is rolled back.

94466da3b8d4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
94466da3b8d4.sentence: Unlike “consistency” in CAP theorem, which means every read receives the most recent write or an error, here consistency means preserving database invariants.

10a4a52d14fc.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
10a4a52d14fc.sentence: Any data written by a transaction must be valid according to all defined rules and maintain the database in a good state.

082202c9cfd7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
082202c9cfd7.sentence: On the completion of a transaction, the database is structurally sound.

e73b72fdfcaa.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
e73b72fdfcaa.sentence: When there are concurrent writes from two different transactions, the two transactions are isolated from each other.

1d73ddc132e8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
1d73ddc132e8.sentence: Transactions do not contend with one another.

e659e9b19bb5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
e659e9b19bb5.sentence: Contentious access to data is moderated by the database so that transactions appear to run sequentially.

3c6443151520.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
3c6443151520.sentence: The most strict isolation is “serializability”, where each transaction acts like it is the only transaction running in the database.

ab512764c6b8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
ab512764c6b8.sentence: Data is persisted after a transaction is committed even in a system failure.

ca5175baaa56.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
ca5175baaa56.sentence: Once the transaction has been completed and the writes and updates have been written to the disk, it will remain in the system even if a system failure occurs.

03d302941b84.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
03d302941b84.sentence: In a distributed system, this means the data is replicated to some other nodes.

735a5427260b.title: ACID
735a5427260b.sentence: There are two popular families of techniques: write-ahead logging and shadow paging.

c855f5386f7b.title: ACID
c855f5386f7b.sentence: In write ahead logging, durability is guaranteed by writing the prospective change to a persistent log before changing the database.

950475a2e45f.title: ACID
950475a2e45f.sentence: That allows the database to return to a consistent state in the event of a crash.

841739b74f43.title: ACID
841739b74f43.sentence: In shadowing, updates are applied to a partial copy of the database, and the new copy is activated when the transaction commits.

1f7124b97007.title: ACID
1f7124b97007.sentence: Guaranteeing ACID properties in a distributed transaction across a distributed database, where no single node is responsible for all data affecting a transaction, presents additional complications.

75aa74432666.title: ACID
75aa74432666.sentence: Network connections might fail, or one node might successfully complete its part of the transaction and then be required to roll back its changes because of a failure on another node.

96c035276f87.title: ACID
96c035276f87.sentence: The two-phase commit protocol (not to be confused with two-phase locking) provides atomicity for distributed transactions to ensure that each participant in the transaction agrees on whether the transaction should be committed or not.

95ea0d12b50d.title: ACID
95ea0d12b50d.sentence: Briefly, in the first phase, one node (the coordinator) interrogates the other nodes (the participants), and only when all reply that they are prepared does the coordinator, in the second phase, formalize the transaction.

ece6de327a5a.title: Database
ece6de327a5a.sentence: A database model is a type of data model that determines the logical structure of a database and fundamentally determines in which manner data can be stored, organized, and manipulated.

994f8e62dad8.title: Database
994f8e62dad8.sentence: The most popular example of a database model is the relational model (or the SQL approximation of relational), which uses a table-based format.

8f0b282c1e43.title: Database
8f0b282c1e43.sentence: Common logical data models for databases include:

c52be64526ac.title: Database
c52be64526ac.sentence: An object–relational database combines the two related structures.

0eafe909478a.title: Database
0eafe909478a.sentence: Specialized models are optimized for particular types of data:

8e64f01043a8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
8e64f01043a8.sentence: - Flat Model The flat data model is one of the simplest forms of database models.

f844aa30effa.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
f844aa30effa.sentence: It organizes data into a single table where each row represents a record and each column represents an attribute.

f6245fb6b88a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
f6245fb6b88a.sentence: This model is similar to a spreadsheet and is straightforward to understand and implement.

c09832d2307b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
c09832d2307b.sentence: However, it lacks the ability to efficiently handle complex relationships between data entities.

09844672749b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
09844672749b.sentence: - Hierarchical Model The hierarchical data model organizes data into a tree-like structure, where each record has a single parent but can have multiple children.

d4888ac87c04.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
d4888ac87c04.sentence: This model is efficient for scenarios with a clear "parent-child" relationship among data entities.

ae6d8bb2543a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
ae6d8bb2543a.sentence: However, it struggles with many-to-many relationships and can become complex and rigid.

4e42bb552e7d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
4e42bb552e7d.sentence: - Network Model The network data model allows each record to have multiple parents and children, forming a graph structure that can represent complex relationships between data entities.

94755fb2f05c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
94755fb2f05c.sentence: This model overcomes some of the hierarchical model's limitations by efficiently handling many-to-many relationships.

5c26b03d9a42.title: Isolation (database systems)
5c26b03d9a42.sentence: In database systems, isolation is one of the ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) transaction properties.

e1f49477a8d0.title: Isolation (database systems)
e1f49477a8d0.sentence: It determines how transaction integrity is visible to other users and systems.

df91a099827e.title: Isolation (database systems)
df91a099827e.sentence: A lower isolation level increases the ability of many users to access the same data at the same time, but also increases the number of concurrency effects (such as dirty reads or lost updates) users might encounter.

ccb680cf95df.title: Isolation (database systems)
ccb680cf95df.sentence: Conversely, a higher isolation level reduces the types of concurrency effects that users may encounter, but requires more system resources and increases the chances that one transaction will block another.

35681e175090.title: Isolation (database systems)
35681e175090.sentence: Of the four ACID properties in a DBMS (Database Management System), the isolation property is the one most often relaxed.

b86f9d785b9f.title: Isolation (database systems)
b86f9d785b9f.sentence: When attempting to maintain the highest level of isolation, a DBMS usually acquires locks on data which may result in a loss of concurrency, or implements multiversion concurrency control.

cf46644c54b5.title: Isolation (database systems)
cf46644c54b5.sentence: For many database applications, the majority of database transactions can be constructed to avoid requiring high isolation levels (e.g. SERIALIZABLE level), thus reducing the locking overhead for the system.

f606c5a01c23.title: Isolation (database systems)
f606c5a01c23.sentence: The programmer must carefully analyze database access code to ensure that any relaxation of isolation does not cause software bugs that are difficult to find.

f862e0ca9b4b.title: Isolation (database systems)
f862e0ca9b4b.sentence: Conversely, if higher isolation levels are used, the possibility of deadlock is increased, which also requires careful analysis and programming techniques to avoid.

6bb59d5e9ee2.title: Isolation (database systems)
6bb59d5e9ee2.sentence: Isolation is typically enforced at the database level.

b362516a778d.title: Isolation (database systems)
b362516a778d.sentence: However, various client-side systems can also be used.

e11e2cfc5296.title: Isolation (database systems)
e11e2cfc5296.sentence: A transaction manager can provide global isolation and atomicity.

b6181f12fad6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-are-database-isolation-levels.md
b6181f12fad6.sentence: Database isolation allows a transaction to execute as if there are no other concurrently running transactions.

b44d82c0dfed.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-acid-mean.md
b44d82c0dfed.sentence: However, this is hard to implement in reality, so we often adopt loser isolation level.

6d666d8dade6.title: Relational database
6d666d8dade6.sentence: Therefore, most physical implementations have a unique primary key (PK) for each row in a table.

9066d52f0181.title: Relational database
9066d52f0181.sentence: Rows in a table can be linked to rows in other tables by adding a column for the unique key of the linked row (such columns are known as foreign keys).

645f6d4f33a9.title: Relational database
645f6d4f33a9.sentence: Each row in a table has its own unique key.

a343e22e3e4d.title: Relational database
a343e22e3e4d.sentence: When a new row is written to the table, a new unique value for the primary key is generated; this is the key that the system uses primarily for accessing the table.

83ca50d2f1f3.title: Relational database
83ca50d2f1f3.sentence: System performance is optimized for PKs.

b577092ba385.title: Relational database
b577092ba385.sentence: While natural attributes (attributes used to describe the data being entered) are sometimes good primary keys, surrogate keys are often used instead.

daa5f634d6f6.title: Relational database
daa5f634d6f6.sentence: A surrogate key is an artificial attribute assigned to an object which uniquely identifies it (for instance, in a table of information about students at a school they might all be assigned a student ID in order to differentiate them).

373928509092.title: Relational database
373928509092.sentence: The surrogate key has no intrinsic (inherent) meaning, but rather is useful through its ability to uniquely identify a tuple.

1ed636e37753.title: Relational database
1ed636e37753.sentence: Other, more natural keys may also be identified and defined as alternate keys (AK).

f10d2ee13112.title: Relational database
f10d2ee13112.sentence: Often several columns are needed to form an AK (this is one reason why a single integer column is usually made the PK).

40c19af261ec.title: Relational database
40c19af261ec.sentence: A composite key is a key made up of two or more attributes within a table that (together) uniquely identify a record.

229ac3dea7b2.title: Relational database
229ac3dea7b2.sentence: When a PK migrates to another table, it becomes a foreign key (FK) in the other table.

a1961c9587a6.title: Relational database
a1961c9587a6.sentence: Foreign keys need not have unique values in the referencing relation.

4b3da8cdcab0.title: Relational database
4b3da8cdcab0.sentence: A foreign key can be used to cross-reference tables, and it effectively uses the values of attributes in the referenced relation to restrict the domain of one or more attributes in the referencing relation.

007fc8b364bf.title: Relational database
007fc8b364bf.sentence: Foreign key refers to a field in a relational table that matches the primary key column of another table.

1ea5c839431b.title: Relational database
1ea5c839431b.sentence: When each cell can contain only one value and the PK migrates into a regular entity table, this design pattern can represent either a one-to-one or one-to-many relationship.

5a6c43b4fb76.title: Relational database
5a6c43b4fb76.sentence: Most relational database designs resolve many-to-many relationships by creating an additional table that contains the PKs from both of the other entity tables – the relationship becomes an entity; the resolution table is then named appropriately and the two FKs are combined to form a PK.

6f54c6205ecf.title: Wide-column store
6f54c6205ecf.sentence: A wide-column store (or extensible record store) is a type of NoSQL database.

51af548c59f6.title: Wide-column store
51af548c59f6.sentence: It uses tables, rows, and columns, but unlike a relational database, the names and format of the columns can vary from row to row in the same table.

f34c9d42748a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
f34c9d42748a.sentence: Data is stored in column families, rather than in rows and columns.

3f374a233e99.title: Wide-column store
3f374a233e99.sentence: A wide-column store can be interpreted as a two-dimensional key–value store.

134d6c5b7014.title: Wide-column store
134d6c5b7014.sentence: A wide-column store is a 2-level structure where each value is identified by 2 keys: the first key acts as a row identifier and the second acts as a column identifier.

55fc243e9c03.title: Wide-column store
55fc243e9c03.sentence: Columns are grouped together into column-families, which are physically stored together on disk.

f691cff96aaf.title: Wide-column store
f691cff96aaf.sentence: The top-level structure of a wide-column store is called a keyspace, and column families are contained within this structure.

fc94b98d508e.title: Wide-column store
fc94b98d508e.sentence: A row is made up of a set of keys and values, which may span several column families, a column family is often likened to a table in a relational database.

868c285a9ca2.title: Wide-column store
868c285a9ca2.sentence: A wide-column database may also have supercolumns, which contain a map to other columns, this creating a nest column.

13119754b1ec.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
13119754b1ec.sentence: Wide column databases, also known as wide column stores, are schema-agnostic.

23a045478d2c.title: Wide-column store
23a045478d2c.sentence: The name column-store historically referred to databases like C-Store, which was a column-oriented relational database.

0b41cad14d8f.title: Wide-column store
0b41cad14d8f.sentence: It eventually came to refer to Bigtable, Apache Cassandra, and similar systems, which also store groups of columns ("column families") together, but ditch the relational model.

023aed373fb4.title: Wide-column store
023aed373fb4.sentence: Google's Bigtable is one of the prototypical examples of a wide-column store.

4140b1585594.title: Wide-column store
4140b1585594.sentence: Besides being denormalized, a wide-column database's structure is not as fixed as relational database, allowing dynamically adding columns, as well as allowing rows to have varying columns.

d7bc65341d7e.title: Wide-column store
d7bc65341d7e.sentence: Compared to a document databases, wide-column databases divide each record into column families that the database recognizes as separate units.

0bc9f771569c.title: Wide-column store
0bc9f771569c.sentence: This additional structure allows the database to organize into a two-dimensional structure, whereas document databases generally treat the entire document as the unit of storage and optimization despite allowing queries and partial retrievals of individual fields.

3d99f08c8e30.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
3d99f08c8e30.sentence: - Highly scalable, can handle petabytes of data

74072a94fe29.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::nosql-databases
74072a94fe29.sentence: - Ideal for real-time big data applications

fda120abed2d.title: Online transaction processing
fda120abed2d.sentence: Online transaction processing (OLTP) is a type of database system used in transaction-oriented applications, such as many operational systems.

d56d6c9f0532.title: Online transaction processing
d56d6c9f0532.sentence: The term online refers to the expectation that these systems respond to user requests and process them in real time.

f7d0268d90be.title: Online transaction processing
f7d0268d90be.sentence: OLTP is typically contrasted with online analytical processing (OLAP), which is generally characterized by much more complex queries and is executed in smaller volumes, for the purpose of business intelligence or reporting rather than processing transactions.

fe95a29e88af.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/types-of-databases.md
fe95a29e88af.sentence: Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) is a technology optimized for reporting and analysis purposes.

b6985445a637.title: Online transaction processing
b6985445a637.sentence: Examples of OLTP systems include order entry, retail sales, and financial transaction systems.

d0fe40e793a6.title: Online transaction processing
d0fe40e793a6.sentence: An automated teller machine (ATM) is an example of a commercial transaction-processing application.

c4b4005c19cf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
c4b4005c19cf.sentence: - OLTP: For transactional systems requiring strong consistency

442c5de06f5f.title: Database
442c5de06f5f.sentence: They typically process relatively high volumes of updates using transactions.

373c62221785.title: Online transaction processing
373c62221785.sentence: Online transaction processing applications typically have high throughput and are insert- or update-intensive in database management.

2760b3e218e5.title: Online transaction processing
2760b3e218e5.sentence: These applications are used concurrently by hundreds of users.

eb5dc2928959.title: Online transaction processing
eb5dc2928959.sentence: The key goals of OLTP applications are availability, speed, concurrency, and recoverability (durability).

ecf39d70a4d8.title: Online transaction processing
ecf39d70a4d8.sentence: Online transaction processing is concerned with concurrency and atomicity.

cb468440f746.title: Online transaction processing
cb468440f746.sentence: Concurrency control ensures that two users accessing the same data in a database system cannot modify it simultaneously; one user must wait until the other has finished processing before making changes.

f4b8b79e6e0a.title: Online transaction processing
f4b8b79e6e0a.sentence: Atomicity ensures that all steps in a transaction are completed successfully as a group; if any step fails, all other steps must also fail.

4f05bc156a80.title: Online analytical processing
4f05bc156a80.sentence: In computing, online analytical processing (OLAP) (/ˈoʊlæp/), is an approach to quickly answer multi-dimensional analytical (MDA) queries.

47de12d238a1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
47de12d238a1.sentence: - OLAP: Optimized for complex queries and data analysis

986fab3023a9.title: Online transaction processing
986fab3023a9.sentence: Whereas OLTP systems handle all kinds of queries (read, insert, update, and delete), OLAP is generally optimized for read-only operations and may not support other types of queries.

1fa29c5df059.title: Online analytical processing
1fa29c5df059.sentence: Whereas OLAP systems are mostly optimized for read, OLTP has to process all kinds of queries (read, insert, update and delete).

0f14af8a7abc.title: Data warehouse
0f14af8a7abc.sentence: OLTP databases contain detailed and current data.

a96cdefd7faf.title: Data warehouse
a96cdefd7faf.sentence: The schema used to store transactional databases is the entity model (usually 3NF).

5bdfc2e8225e.title: Data warehouse
5bdfc2e8225e.sentence: Normalization is the norm for data modeling techniques in this system.

864a4ffe5258.title: Data warehouse
864a4ffe5258.sentence: OLAP databases store aggregated, historical data in multi-dimensional schemas (usually star schemas).

703dcb96da55.title: Data warehouse
703dcb96da55.sentence: Because of these differences in access, operational databases (loosely, OLTP) benefit from the use of a row-oriented database management system (DBMS), whereas analytics databases (loosely, OLAP) benefit from the use of a column-oriented DBMS.

e5fcd599acaf.title: Data warehouse
e5fcd599acaf.sentence: Data warehouses are optimized for analytic access patterns, which usually involve selecting specific fields rather than all fields as is common in operational databases.

253a3ed8d5d8.title: Data warehouse
253a3ed8d5d8.sentence: For OLTP systems, performance is the number of transactions per second.

c3798ddcef09.title: Data warehouse
c3798ddcef09.sentence: Online analytical processing (OLAP) is characterized by a low rate of transactions and complex queries that involve aggregations.

890fe7e7e925.title: Data warehouse
890fe7e7e925.sentence: Response time is an effective performance measure of OLAP systems.

d8f07d0900b0.title: Data warehouse
d8f07d0900b0.sentence: In computing, a data warehouse (DW or DWH), also known as an enterprise data warehouse (EDW), is a system used for reporting and data analysis and is a core component of business intelligence.

f1348054f634.title: Data warehouse
f1348054f634.sentence: Data warehouses are central repositories of data integrated from disparate sources.

72d8c9c3d9ab.title: Data warehouse
72d8c9c3d9ab.sentence: They are intended to be used by analysts and managers to help make organizational decisions.

a19a5c990c30.title: Data warehouse
a19a5c990c30.sentence: They store current and historical data organized in a way that is optimized for data analysis, generation of reports, and developing insights across the integrated data.

c3ec636e4939.title: Data warehouse
c3ec636e4939.sentence: The data stored in the warehouse is uploaded from operational systems (such as marketing or sales).

f27a95078e41.title: Data warehouse
f27a95078e41.sentence: The data may pass through an operational data store and may require data cleansing for additional operations to ensure data quality before it is used in the data warehouse for reporting.

640576c2cd66.title: Data warehouse
640576c2cd66.sentence: The two main workflows for building a data warehouse system are extract, transform, load (ETL) and extract, load, transform (ELT).

a02b42784242.title: Data warehouse
a02b42784242.sentence: Operational databases are optimized for the preservation of data integrity and speed of recording of business transactions through use of database normalization and an entity–relationship model.

3cb383dc09ef.title: Data warehouse
3cb383dc09ef.sentence: Fully normalized database designs often result in information from a business transaction being stored in dozens to hundreds of tables.

eb3810eeeb9f.title: Data warehouse
eb3810eeeb9f.sentence: The databases have very fast insert/update performance because only a small amount of data in those tables is affected by each transaction.

dad804cc6d94.title: Data warehouse
dad804cc6d94.sentence: To improve performance, older data are periodically purged.

58b74e97d621.title: Data warehouse
58b74e97d621.sentence: Operational systems maintain a snapshot of the business, while warehouses maintain historic data through ETL processes that periodically migrate data from the operational systems to the warehouse.

1ed10b12b4ca.title: Data warehouse
1ed10b12b4ca.sentence: - Mitigate the problem of isolation-level lock contention in transaction processing systems caused by long-running analysis queries in transaction processing databases.

83c39378e213.title: Data warehouse
83c39378e213.sentence: - Maintain data history, even if the source transaction systems do not.

fe6ee743c649.title: Data warehouse
fe6ee743c649.sentence: - Integrate data from multiple sources into a single database and data model.

8cd07a524171.title: Data warehouse
8cd07a524171.sentence: A data warehouse maintains a copy of information from the source transaction systems.

0fa9090d0198.title: Data warehouse
0fa9090d0198.sentence: There are basic features that define the data in the data warehouse that include subject orientation, data integration, time-variant, nonvolatile data, and data granularity.

7d50853a2d90.title: Data warehouse
7d50853a2d90.sentence: While operational systems reflect current values as they support day-to-day operations, data warehouse data represents a long time horizon (up to 10 years) which means it stores mostly historical data.

5da8e5416185.title: Data warehouse
5da8e5416185.sentence: The data in the data warehouse is read-only, which means it cannot be updated, created, or deleted (unless there is a regulatory or statutory obligation to do so).

4e65f4289a33.title: Data warehouse
4e65f4289a33.section: Data organization > Dimensional versus normalized approach for storage of data
4e65f4289a33.sentence: The two most important approaches to store data in a warehouse are dimensional and normalized.

b447ca062a1c.title: Data warehouse
b447ca062a1c.section: Data organization > Dimensional versus normalized approach for storage of data
b447ca062a1c.sentence: The dimensional approach uses a star schema as proposed by Ralph Kimball.

def0607841d1.title: Data warehouse
def0607841d1.section: Data organization > Dimensional versus normalized approach for storage of data
def0607841d1.sentence: The normalized approach, also called the third normal form (3NF) is an entity-relational normalized model proposed by Bill Inmon.

955e2a2ee1cf.title: Data warehouse
955e2a2ee1cf.section: Data organization > Dimensional versus normalized approach for storage of data > Dimensional approach
955e2a2ee1cf.sentence: In a dimensional approach, transaction data is partitioned into "facts", which are usually numeric transaction data, and "dimensions", which are the reference information that gives context to the facts.

f3c29b3acdbe.title: Data warehouse
f3c29b3acdbe.section: Data organization > Dimensional versus normalized approach for storage of data > Dimensional approach
f3c29b3acdbe.sentence: This dimensional approach makes data easier to understand and speeds up data retrieval.

95daf837285f.title: Data warehouse
95daf837285f.section: Data organization > Dimensional versus normalized approach for storage of data > Normalized approach
95daf837285f.sentence: In the normalized approach, the data in the warehouse are stored following, to a degree, database normalization rules.

de27d54164f9.title: Data warehouse
de27d54164f9.section: Data organization > Dimensional versus normalized approach for storage of data > Normalized approach
de27d54164f9.sentence: Normalized relational database tables are grouped into subject areas (for example, customers, products and finance).

5d8d9369f9e0.title: Data warehouse
5d8d9369f9e0.sentence: A data mart is a simple data warehouse focused on a single subject or functional area.

55c9440a7586.title: Data warehouse
55c9440a7586.sentence: Data marts are often built and controlled by a single department in an organization.

b2c8291038c9.title: Data warehouse
b2c8291038c9.sentence: In the bottom-up approach, data marts are first created to provide reporting and analytical capabilities for specific business processes.

b3872418e8ae.title: Data warehouse
b3872418e8ae.sentence: These data marts can then be integrated to create a comprehensive data warehouse.

ec285a74262e.title: Data warehouse
ec285a74262e.sentence: The top-down approach is designed using a normalized enterprise data model.

2e4ecb112ad6.title: Data warehouse
2e4ecb112ad6.sentence: Dimensional data marts containing data needed for specific business processes or specific departments are created from the data warehouse.

59f2ebc243ff.title: Data warehouse
59f2ebc243ff.sentence: A Data lake is a centralized repository that stores large volume of data in raw format that is processed at the run time.

7ca3dd843647.title: Data warehouse
7ca3dd843647.sentence: It can collect data from multiple sources such as APIs, Files, databases, sensors, websites, etc. Unlike data warehouses, data lakes stores data is structured, semi-structured and unstructured format that makes them usable for machine learning and big data processing.

8ec4862138ab.title: Star schema
8ec4862138ab.sentence: In computing, the star schema or star model is the simplest style of data mart schema and is the approach most widely used to develop data warehouses and dimensional data marts.

df797096f032.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
df797096f032.sentence: It features a central fact table that contains measurable, quantitative data, surrounded by dimension tables that contain descriptive attributes related to the fact data.

be481697713d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
be481697713d.sentence: - Snowflake Model The snowflake model is a variation of the star schema where the dimension tables are normalized into multiple related tables, reducing redundancy and improving data integrity.

b90d1b54da69.title: Star schema
b90d1b54da69.sentence: The star schema consists of one or more fact tables referencing any number of dimension tables.

4b03d1aef8b5.title: Star schema
4b03d1aef8b5.sentence: The star schema gets its name from the physical model's resemblance to a star shape with a fact table at its center and the dimension tables surrounding it representing the star's points.

304191b741b1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
304191b741b1.sentence: - Star Schema The star schema is a specialized data model used in data warehousing for OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) applications.

a90c82210b88.title: Star schema
a90c82210b88.sentence: The star schema separates business process data into facts, which hold the measurable, quantitative data about a business, and dimensions which are descriptive attributes related to fact data.

bf2ccc91a3cf.title: Star schema
bf2ccc91a3cf.sentence: Examples of fact data include sales price, sale quantity, time, distance, speed and weight measurements.

34df1cdb1a91.title: Star schema
34df1cdb1a91.sentence: Related dimension attribute examples include product models, product colors, product sizes, geographic locations, and salesperson names.

8d99de77c0ff.title: Star schema
8d99de77c0ff.sentence: Fact tables record measurements or metrics for a specific event.

4ef9ecb0b4d1.title: Star schema
4ef9ecb0b4d1.sentence: Fact tables generally consist of numeric values, and foreign keys to dimensional data where descriptive information is kept.

8f05315cad82.title: Star schema
8f05315cad82.sentence: Fact tables are designed to a low level of uniform detail (referred to as "granularity" or "grain"), meaning facts can record events at a very atomic level.

39e24d44328a.title: Star schema
39e24d44328a.sentence: This can result in the accumulation of a large number of records in a fact table over time.

417dfdad295c.title: Star schema
417dfdad295c.sentence: Fact tables are defined as one of three types:

6dc9e1506be2.title: Star schema
6dc9e1506be2.sentence: Dimension tables usually have a relatively small number of records compared to fact tables, but each record may have a very large number of attributes to describe the fact data.

1f5743504517.title: Star schema
1f5743504517.sentence: - Time dimension tables describe time at the lowest level of time granularity for which events are recorded in the star schema

097fad8e7283.title: Star schema
097fad8e7283.sentence: - Geography dimension tables describe location data, such as country, state, or city

62f958a27f50.title: Star schema
62f958a27f50.sentence: - Employee dimension tables describe employees, such as sales people

11416ffdee07.title: Star schema
11416ffdee07.sentence: - Range dimension tables describe ranges of time, dollar values or other measurable quantities to simplify reporting

9211c3b19b6d.title: Star schema
9211c3b19b6d.sentence: Dimension tables are generally assigned a surrogate primary key, usually a single-column integer data type, mapped to the combination of dimension attributes that form the natural key.

e23116bfeccf.title: Star schema
e23116bfeccf.sentence: Star schemas are denormalized, meaning the typical rules of normalization applied to transactional relational databases are relaxed during star-schema design and implementation.

ca201edb6655.title: Star schema
ca201edb6655.sentence: - Simpler queries – star-schema join-logic is generally simpler than the join logic required to retrieve data from a highly normalized transactional schema.

f6d2bf75061c.title: Star schema
f6d2bf75061c.sentence: - Simplified business reporting logic – when compared to highly normalized schemas, the star schema simplifies common business reporting logic, such as period-over-period and as-of reporting.

ef63fdf3add5.title: Star schema
ef63fdf3add5.sentence: - Query performance gains – star schemas can provide performance enhancements for read-only reporting applications when compared to highly normalized schemas.

1afe1565f4db.title: Star schema
1afe1565f4db.sentence: - Fast aggregations – the simpler queries against a star schema can result in improved performance for aggregation operations.

545c73a2c101.title: Star schema
545c73a2c101.sentence: - Feeding cubes – star schemas are used by all OLAP systems to build proprietary OLAP cubes efficiently; in fact, most major OLAP systems provide a ROLAP mode of operation which can use a star schema directly as a source without building a proprietary cube structure.

c200cf253122.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
c200cf253122.sentence: This model is optimized for query performance in analytical applications, offering simplicity and fast data retrieval by minimizing the number of joins needed for queries.

1232ea1e1ca5.title: Star schema
1232ea1e1ca5.section: Benefits > Use and comparison with the snowflake schema
1232ea1e1ca5.sentence: By contrast, a snowflake schema normalizes dimension hierarchies into multiple linked tables.

0f3be8bcdb10.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
0f3be8bcdb10.sentence: This results in a structure that resembles a snowflake.

e79fcd8d2ce6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-database-models.md
e79fcd8d2ce6.sentence: While the snowflake model can lead to more complex queries due to the increased number of joins, it offers benefits in terms of storage efficiency and can be advantageous in scenarios where dimension tables are large or frequently updated.

4818c964b458.title: Star schema
4818c964b458.section: Benefits > Use and comparison with the snowflake schema
4818c964b458.sentence: Kimball recommends avoiding snowflaking unless there is a clear need (for example, extremely large dimensions) because it adds complexity for users and can hurt query performance.

da4016c4927f.title: Star schema
da4016c4927f.sentence: Analytic queries over a star schema usually join one large fact table with a handful of relatively small dimensions; many DBMSs implement ‘‘star-join’’ optimizations for this pattern.

533f6cbb931b.title: Star schema
533f6cbb931b.sentence: Fact_Sales is the fact table and there are three dimension tables Dim_Date, Dim_Store and Dim_Product.

68bb0e04cc17.title: Star schema
68bb0e04cc17.sentence: Having dimensions of only a few attributes, while simpler to maintain, results in queries with many table joins and makes the star schema less easy to use.

36037e7fb857.title: Online analytical processing
36037e7fb857.sentence: OLAP is part of the broader category of business intelligence, which also encompasses relational databases, report writing and data mining.

f3203905f1f0.title: Online analytical processing
f3203905f1f0.sentence: OLAP tools enable users to analyse multidimensional data interactively from multiple perspectives.

cb349f071aa3.title: Online analytical processing
cb349f071aa3.sentence: Typical applications of OLAP include business reporting for sales, marketing, management reporting, business process management (BPM), budgeting and forecasting, financial reporting and similar areas, with new applications emerging, such as agriculture.

b9d7b47bab83.title: Online analytical processing
b9d7b47bab83.sentence: At the core of any OLAP system is an OLAP cube (also called a 'multidimensional cube' or a hypercube).

f0e71e66b996.title: Online analytical processing
f0e71e66b996.sentence: It consists of numeric facts called measures that are categorized by dimensions.

cdc95d2560da.title: Online analytical processing
cdc95d2560da.sentence: The measures are placed at the intersections of the hypercube, which is spanned by the dimensions as a vector space.

061459948d27.title: Online analytical processing
061459948d27.sentence: The usual interface to manipulate an OLAP cube is a matrix interface, like Pivot tables in a spreadsheet program, which performs projection operations along the dimensions, such as aggregation or averaging.

16dab1af2974.title: Online analytical processing
16dab1af2974.sentence: The cube metadata is typically created from a star schema or snowflake schema or fact constellation of tables in a relational database.

bd978830ce0f.title: Online analytical processing
bd978830ce0f.sentence: Measures are derived from the records in the fact table and dimensions are derived from the dimension tables.

e3537b78719f.title: Online analytical processing
e3537b78719f.sentence: OLAP consists of three basic analytical operations: consolidation (roll-up), drill-down, and slicing and dicing.

d1ef274dec2d.title: Online analytical processing
d1ef274dec2d.sentence: Consolidation involves the aggregation of data that can be accumulated and computed in one or more dimensions.

e7a0c4c86580.title: Online analytical processing
e7a0c4c86580.sentence: For example, all sales offices are rolled up to the sales department or sales division to anticipate sales trends.

b90ee246e9bd.title: Online analytical processing
b90ee246e9bd.sentence: By contrast, the drill-down is a technique that allows users to navigate through the details.

4f8b0f94468e.title: Online analytical processing
4f8b0f94468e.sentence: For instance, users can view the sales by individual products that make up a region's sales.

ec9fd3c5b1c1.title: Online analytical processing
ec9fd3c5b1c1.sentence: Slicing and dicing is a feature whereby users can take out (slicing) a specific set of data of the OLAP cube and view (dicing) the slices from different viewpoints.

1d063432a4a4.title: Online analytical processing
1d063432a4a4.sentence: The most important mechanism in OLAP which allows it to achieve such performance is the use of aggregations.

dd46811f2804.title: Online analytical processing
dd46811f2804.sentence: Aggregations are built from the fact table by changing the granularity on specific dimensions and aggregating up data along these dimensions, using an aggregate function (or aggregation function).

0548ff096975.title: Online analytical processing
0548ff096975.sentence: It has been claimed that for complex queries OLAP cubes can produce an answer in around 0.1% of the time required for the same query on OLTP relational data.

b15388d9b5e3.title: Online analytical processing
b15388d9b5e3.sentence: The number of possible aggregations is determined by every possible combination of dimension granularities.

1cf40e75821d.title: Online analytical processing
1cf40e75821d.sentence: Because usually there are many aggregations that can be calculated, often only a predetermined number are fully calculated; the remainder are solved on demand.

90a70c2ea93a.title: Online analytical processing
90a70c2ea93a.sentence: The problem of deciding which aggregations (views) to calculate is known as the view selection problem.

e3497f0d5e39.title: Online analytical processing
e3497f0d5e39.sentence: Functions that can be decomposed in this way are called decomposable aggregation functions, and include COUNT, MAX, MIN, and SUM, which can be computed for each cell and then directly aggregated; these are known as self-decomposable aggregation functions.

278323b5897a.title: Online analytical processing
278323b5897a.sentence: In other cases, the aggregate function can be computed by computing auxiliary numbers for cells, aggregating these auxiliary numbers, and finally computing the overall number at the end; examples include AVERAGE (tracking sum and count, dividing at the end) and RANGE (tracking max and min, subtracting at the end).

9fce2f5fccb0.title: Online analytical processing
9fce2f5fccb0.sentence: In other cases, the aggregate function cannot be computed without analyzing the entire set at once, though in some cases approximations can be computed; examples include DISTINCT COUNT, MEDIAN, and MODE; for example, the median of a set is not the median of medians of subsets.

b9ef00262f0b.title: Online analytical processing
b9ef00262f0b.sentence: These latter are difficult to implement efficiently in OLAP, as they require computing the aggregate function on the base data, either computing them online (slow) or precomputing them for possible rollouts (large space).

38d2f56e77e0.title: Connection pool
38d2f56e77e0.sentence: In software engineering, a connection pool is a cache of reusable database connections managed by the client or middleware.

db6b8ebbc068.title: Connection pool
db6b8ebbc068.sentence: It reduces the overhead of opening and closing connections, improving performance and scalability in database applications.

13f40e15c643.title: Connection pool
13f40e15c643.sentence: SQL databases typically use stateful, binary protocols that maintain session-specific information, such as transaction states and prepared statements, necessitating optimized connection pooling to minimize the overhead of repeatedly establishing connections.

77a0c44fe575.title: Connection pool
77a0c44fe575.sentence: Conversely, many mainstream NoSQL databases, like Azure Cosmos DB and Amazon DynamoDB, utilize stateless, HTTP-based protocols that handle each request independently.

b182861fe340.title: Connection pool
b182861fe340.sentence: This architecture often reduces the need for traditional connection pooling, though reusing established connections can still offer performance benefits in high-throughput scenarios by avoiding the overhead of connection creation.

eb84159029e3.title: Connection pool
eb84159029e3.section: Connection pooling efficiency > Connection limits and overprovisioning
eb84159029e3.sentence: When connection pool configurations exceed these limits, issues such as rejected connections, throttling, or degraded performance can occur.

94025b01fd2b.title: Connection pool
94025b01fd2b.section: Connection pooling efficiency > Connection limits and overprovisioning
94025b01fd2b.sentence: Depending on how database limits are applied, overprovisioned connection pools can create significant resource contention as the server struggles to manage excessive simultaneous connections.

a087349bf6fb.title: Connection pool
a087349bf6fb.section: Connection pooling efficiency > Connection limits and overprovisioning
a087349bf6fb.sentence: Over-provisioned pools can overwhelm server resources, causing increased latency and degraded system performance.

0436b075c8ab.title: Connection pool
0436b075c8ab.section: Connection pooling efficiency > Connection limits and overprovisioning
0436b075c8ab.sentence: To optimize database connectivity, connection pool configurations should be carefully aligned with the database's capacity and the application's specific workload, ensuring efficient connection reuse without overburdening the database server and maintaining a balance between connection availability and resource utilization.

3294644eb505.title: Connection pool
3294644eb505.section: Connection pooling efficiency > Connection limits and overprovisioning
3294644eb505.sentence: Idle connections may encounter issues due to network conditions, such as NAT timeouts or dropped connections, or database state changes, such as session invalidation or transaction timeouts, potentially triggering reconnection processes that introduce additional overhead and performance penalties.

e758ccfd4d68.title: Connection pool
e758ccfd4d68.sentence: Token-based authentication mechanisms, such as Azure AD authentication, may affect connection pooling due to token expiration.

c7b70b0e8007.title: Connection pool
c7b70b0e8007.sentence: Expired tokens can invalidate connections within the pool, interrupting reuse.

8aee1dd5ee33.title: Connection pool
8aee1dd5ee33.sentence: - Function-as-a-Service (FaaS): AWS Lambda creates new database connections per invocation, which can cause connection storms under high concurrency if unmanaged.

8343dee62c51.title: Connection pool
8343dee62c51.sentence: Solutions like Amazon RDS Proxy help pool connections efficiently.

008d644bf45b.title: Connection pool
008d644bf45b.sentence: - Containerized Environments: Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) containers maintain open database connections for their lifecycle.

e142153281be.title: Connection pool
e142153281be.sentence: - Virtual Machine-Based Environments: AWS EC2 instances scale connection demand with the number of instances.

2f0e0846d740.title: Connection pool
2f0e0846d740.sentence: Without connection pooling mechanisms (e.g., HikariCP, pgbouncer), idle or excessive connections can strain database resources.

ec3c331d685f.title: Connection pool
ec3c331d685f.sentence: Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and SQL Server on virtual machines rely on client-side connection pooling implemented by libraries such as ADO.NET and JDBC.

d2348fad88b8.title: Connection pool
d2348fad88b8.sentence: The database engine does not manage pooling, as it is entirely handled at the client level.

1763ee46f40e.title: Connection pool
1763ee46f40e.sentence: In Azure Cosmos DB, connection pooling is managed at the SDK level rather than by the database service itself.

f3b037ee7e72.title: gh>donnemartin/system-design-primer/solutions/system_design/web_crawler/README.md
f3b037ee7e72.sentence: - The Crawler Service can improve performance and reduce memory usage by keeping many open connections at a time, referred to as connection pooling

9c3727c93c4b.title: Database
9c3727c93c4b.sentence: Database languages are special-purpose languages, which allow one or more of the following tasks, sometimes distinguished as sublanguages:

0e9f6d80cd03.title: Database
0e9f6d80cd03.sentence: Database languages are specific to a particular data model.

d871e331a8e2.title: Database
d871e331a8e2.sentence: - Data control language (DCL) – controls access to data;

57fc9e4612d9.title: Database
57fc9e4612d9.sentence: - Data definition language (DDL) – defines data types such as creating, altering, or dropping tables and the relationships among them;

0b8d5ce1105e.title: Database
0b8d5ce1105e.sentence: - Data manipulation language (DML) – performs tasks such as inserting, updating, or deleting data occurrences;

973db6235a47.title: Database
973db6235a47.sentence: - Data query language (DQL) – allows searching for information and computing derived information.

0aa16d5e0742.title: Database
0aa16d5e0742.sentence: - SQL combines the roles of data definition, data manipulation, and query in a single language.

8d975ed17e80.title: Database
8d975ed17e80.sentence: The standards have been regularly enhanced since and are supported (with varying degrees of conformance) by all mainstream commercial relational DBMSs.

834b6a91d944.title: Database
834b6a91d944.sentence: A database language may also incorporate features like:

27f374c09d41.title: Database
27f374c09d41.sentence: - DBMS-specific configuration and storage engine management

1664566a8c11.title: Database
1664566a8c11.sentence: - Computations to modify query results, like counting, summing, averaging, sorting, grouping, and cross-referencing

b8e93e35a7da.title: Database
b8e93e35a7da.sentence: - Constraint enforcement (e.g. in an automotive database, only allowing one engine type per car)

2f4be6d3bcbc.title: Database
2f4be6d3bcbc.sentence: - Application programming interface version of the query language, for programmer convenience

2ec5e4159b0e.title: SQL
2ec5e4159b0e.sentence: Structured Query Language (SQL) (pronounced /ˌɛsˌkjuˈɛl/ S-Q-L; or alternatively as /ˈsiːkwəl/ ⓘ "sequel") is a domain-specific language used to manage data, especially in a relational database management system (RDBMS).

5c8bb7ec0d21.title: SQL
5c8bb7ec0d21.sentence: It is particularly useful in handling structured data, i.e., data incorporating relations among entities and variables.

cb324b31db91.title: SQL
cb324b31db91.sentence: SQL is designed for a specific purpose: to query data contained in a relational database.

5a3485cab18b.title: SQL
5a3485cab18b.sentence: SQL is a set-based, declarative programming language, not an imperative programming language like C or BASIC.

d988cc3e30ab.title: SQL
d988cc3e30ab.sentence: However, extensions to Standard SQL add procedural programming language functionality, such as control-of-flow constructs.

75c75ca895c7.title: SQL
75c75ca895c7.sentence: Introduced in the 1970s, SQL offered two main advantages over older read–write APIs such as ISAM or VSAM.

a88eb0b560d0.title: SQL
a88eb0b560d0.sentence: Firstly, it introduced the concept of accessing many records with one single command.

8bdbd125914f.title: SQL
8bdbd125914f.sentence: Secondly, it eliminates the need to specify how to reach a record, i.e., with or without an index.

afc626659ca1.title: SQL
afc626659ca1.sentence: Originally based upon relational algebra and tuple relational calculus, SQL consists of many types of statements, which may be informally classed as sublanguages, commonly: data query language (DQL), data definition language (DDL), data control language (DCL), and data manipulation language (DML).

d8f69e5e41c2.title: SQL
d8f69e5e41c2.sentence: The scope of SQL includes data query, data manipulation (insert, update, and delete), data definition (schema creation and modification), and data access control.

f538d553408c.title: SQL
f538d553408c.sentence: SQL was one of the first commercial languages to use Edgar F. Codd's relational model.

85110cd76328.title: SQL
85110cd76328.sentence: SQL became a standard of the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) in 1986 and of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in 1987.

16c4a24bf765.title: SQL
16c4a24bf765.sentence: Despite not entirely adhering to the relational model as described by Codd, SQL became the most widely used database language.

fdb73ef38787.title: SQL
fdb73ef38787.sentence: Despite the existence of standards, virtually no implementations in existence adhere to it fully, and most SQL code requires at least some changes before being ported to different database systems.

38266febcf7e.title: SQL
38266febcf7e.section: Interoperability and standardization > Reasons for incompatibility
38266febcf7e.sentence: - The complexity and size of the SQL standard means that most implementers do not support the entire standard.

3c469c39c73a.title: SQL
3c469c39c73a.section: Interoperability and standardization > Reasons for incompatibility
3c469c39c73a.sentence: - The SQL standard does not specify the database behavior in some important areas (e.g., indices, file storage), leaving implementations to decide how to behave.

442f58d01d46.title: SQL
442f58d01d46.sentence: In particular, date and time syntax, string concatenation, NULLs, and comparison case sensitivity vary from vendor to vendor.

005ee44b53d4.title: SQL
005ee44b53d4.sentence: SQL deviates in several ways from its theoretical foundation, the relational model and its tuple calculus.

c2948dcec2b1.title: SQL
c2948dcec2b1.sentence: In that model, a table is a set of tuples, while in SQL, tables and query results are lists of rows; the same row may occur multiple times, and the order of rows can be employed in queries (e.g., in the LIMIT clause).

b7eb6d651bed.title: SQL
b7eb6d651bed.sentence: This is usually avoided by declaring a primary key, or a unique constraint, with one or more columns that uniquely identify a row in the table.

5ea5e74fdbcf.title: SQL
5ea5e74fdbcf.sentence: The Null marker indicates the absence of a value, and is distinct from a value of 0 for an integer column or an empty string for a text column.

cb0d56364bf0.title: SQL
cb0d56364bf0.sentence: The concept of Nulls enforces the 3-valued-logic in SQL, which is a concrete implementation of the general 3-valued logic.

5ad43ffef9ac.title: SQL
5ad43ffef9ac.sentence: - Predicates, which specify conditions that can be evaluated to SQL three-valued logic (3VL) (true/false/unknown) or Boolean truth values and are used to limit the effects of statements and queries, or to change program flow.

dbb734fa5cb6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
dbb734fa5cb6.sentence: In the world of databases, there are two main types of solutions, SQL (relational) and NoSQL (non-relational) databases.

e749a504d0d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
e749a504d0d4.sentence: Both of them differ in the way they were built, the kind of information they store, and how they store it.

6d4d6ab31103.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
6d4d6ab31103.sentence: Relational databases are structured and have predefined schemas while non-relational databases are unstructured, distributed, and have a dynamic schema.

f320a465e7c2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
f320a465e7c2.sentence: SQL stores data in tables, where each row represents an entity and each column represents a data point about that entity.

7e1516d0befd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
7e1516d0befd.sentence: NoSQL databases have different data storage models such as key-value, graph, document, etc.

2509f0637a8d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
2509f0637a8d.sentence: In SQL, each record conforms to a fixed schema, meaning the columns must be decided and chosen before data entry and each row must have data for each column.

fbaec699a556.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
fbaec699a556.sentence: The schema can be altered later, but it involves modifying the database using migrations.

e6d893ae19b9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
e6d893ae19b9.sentence: Whereas in NoSQL, schemas are dynamic.

0257b2d0bd4f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
0257b2d0bd4f.sentence: Fields can be added on the fly, and each record (or equivalent) doesn't have to contain data for each field.

da154bdc558e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
da154bdc558e.sentence: SQL databases use SQL (structured query language) for defining and manipulating the data, which is very powerful.

b866f692fa1f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
b866f692fa1f.sentence: In a NoSQL database, queries are focused on a collection of documents.

f6791a5ce254.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
f6791a5ce254.sentence: Different databases have different syntax for querying.

43cad66c0f4d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
43cad66c0f4d.sentence: In most common situations, SQL databases are vertically scalable, which can get very expensive.

99745202df47.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
99745202df47.sentence: It is possible to scale a relational database across multiple servers, but this is a challenging and time-consuming process.

affd13bfba7c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
affd13bfba7c.sentence: The vast majority of relational databases are ACID compliant.

375c08dd71c3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
375c08dd71c3.sentence: So, when it comes to data reliability and a safe guarantee of performing transactions, SQL databases are still the better bet.

b469b81f5ad1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
b469b81f5ad1.sentence: - Lookups by index are very fast

5272ba52e214.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-vs-nosql-databases
5272ba52e214.sentence: As always we should always pick the technology that fits the requirements better.

d5d01c0fda66.title: Spatial database
d5d01c0fda66.sentence: A spatial database is a general-purpose database (usually a relational database) that has been enhanced to include spatial data that represents objects defined in a geometric space, along with tools for querying and analyzing such data.

b42441a62ee5.title: Spatial database
b42441a62ee5.sentence: Most spatial databases allow the representation of simple geometric objects such as points, lines and polygons.

38f7b6efdb0c.title: Spatial database
38f7b6efdb0c.sentence: The datatypes in most spatial databases are based on the OGC Simple Features specification for representing geometric primitives.

299aa7bd80ab.title: Spatial database
299aa7bd80ab.sentence: The core functionality added by a spatial extension to a database is one or more spatial datatypes, which allow for the storage of spatial data as attribute values in a table.

7bd266a56a64.title: Spatial database
7bd266a56a64.sentence: Because all geographic locations must be specified according to a spatial reference system, spatial databases must also allow for the tracking and transformation of coordinate systems.

4025ec22c7fb.title: Spatial database
4025ec22c7fb.sentence: The second major functionality extension in a spatial database is the addition of spatial capabilities to the query language (e.g., SQL); these give the spatial database the same query, analysis, and manipulation operations that are available in traditional GIS software.

d907460e7343.title: Spatial database
d907460e7343.sentence: In most relational database management systems, this functionality is implemented as a set of new functions that can be used in SQL SELECT statements.

1f0d5940641f.title: Spatial database
1f0d5940641f.sentence: Several types of operations are specified by the Open Geospatial Consortium standard:

e739728a055b.title: Spatial database
e739728a055b.sentence: - Measurement: Computes line length, polygon area, the distance between geometries, etc.

aeb82383c1cb.title: Spatial database
aeb82383c1cb.sentence: - Geoprocessing: Modify existing features to create new ones, for example by creating a buffer around them, intersecting features, etc.

637080767673.title: Spatial database
637080767673.sentence: - Predicates: Allows true/false queries about spatial relationships between geometries.

ebb7e882909b.title: Spatial database
ebb7e882909b.sentence: - Geometry Constructors: Creates new geometries, usually by specifying the vertices (points or nodes) which define the shape.

92430a09c0a1.title: Spatial database
92430a09c0a1.sentence: - Observer Functions: Queries that return specific information about a feature, such as the location of the center of a circle.

7a1f9f3e2620.title: Spatial database
7a1f9f3e2620.sentence: Thus, a spatial join between a points layer of cities and a polygon layer of countries could be performed in a spatially-extended SQL statement as:

e6b1c040ccab.title: Spatial database
e6b1c040ccab.sentence: SELECT * FROM cities, countries WHERE ST_Contains(countries.shape, cities.shape)

0b1316773fad.title: Spatial database
0b1316773fad.sentence: Examples include "do two polygons overlap?" or 'is there a residence located within a mile of the area we are planning to build the landfill?' (see DE-9IM)

2cf0f5503534.title: Spatial database
2cf0f5503534.sentence: Database systems use indices to quickly look up values by sorting data values in a linear (e.g. alphabetical) order; however, this way of indexing data is not optimal for spatial queries in two- or three-dimensional space.

3ae623a1635b.title: Spatial database
3ae623a1635b.sentence: Instead, spatial databases use a spatial index designed specifically for multi-dimensional ordering.

e3461b16dc57.title: Spatial database
e3461b16dc57.sentence: A spatial index is used by a spatial database to optimize spatial queries, implementing spatial access methods.

c8c78c5970b7.title: Spatial database
c8c78c5970b7.sentence: - R-tree: Typically the preferred method for indexing spatial data.

fc08a442ff6f.title: Spatial database
fc08a442ff6f.sentence: Objects (shapes, lines and points) are grouped using the minimum bounding rectangle (MBR).

629dc07ef1cf.title: Spatial database
629dc07ef1cf.sentence: Objects are added to an MBR within the index that will lead to the smallest increase in its size.

d4f8707edea4.title: Spatial database
d4f8707edea4.sentence: Almost all current relational and object-relational database management systems now have spatial extensions, and some GIS software vendors have developed their own spatial extensions to database management systems.

4e360cee8539.title: Spatial database
4e360cee8539.sentence: Some databases support only simplified or modified sets of these operations, especially in cases of NoSQL systems like MongoDB and CouchDB.

36fc88d1544b.title: Web mapping
36fc88d1544b.sentence: They are necessary whenever a web mapping application has to deal with dynamic data (that changes frequently) or with huge amount of geographic data.

493941b6d12b.title: Online analytical processing
493941b6d12b.sentence: OLAP systems have been traditionally categorized using the following taxonomy.

b5450c9d405d.title: Online analytical processing
b5450c9d405d.sentence: MOLAP (multi-dimensional online analytical processing) is the classic form of OLAP and is sometimes referred to as just OLAP.

097b536a1d8a.title: Online analytical processing
097b536a1d8a.sentence: ROLAP works directly with relational databases and does not require pre-computation.

44f65d73c1e0.title: Online analytical processing
44f65d73c1e0.sentence: MOLAP stores this data in an optimized multi-dimensional array storage, rather than in a relational database.

14841fd8452d.title: Online analytical processing
14841fd8452d.sentence: Some MOLAP tools require the pre-computation and storage of derived data, such as consolidations – the operation known as processing.

a645ae8aec19.title: Online analytical processing
a645ae8aec19.sentence: Such MOLAP tools generally utilize a pre-calculated data set referred to as a data cube.

6df472639580.title: Online analytical processing
6df472639580.sentence: The base data and the dimension tables are stored as relational tables and new tables are created to hold the aggregated information.

5cf2507f968d.title: Online analytical processing
5cf2507f968d.sentence: It depends on a specialized schema design.

43deda24a1cb.title: Online analytical processing
43deda24a1cb.section: Types > Relational OLAP (ROLAP) > Advantages of ROLAP
43deda24a1cb.sentence: - ROLAP is considered to be more scalable in handling large data volumes, especially models with dimensions with very high cardinality (i.e., millions of members).

0719729f0849.title: Online analytical processing
0719729f0849.section: Types > Relational OLAP (ROLAP) > Advantages of ROLAP
0719729f0849.sentence: - The data are stored in a standard relational database and can be accessed by any SQL reporting tool (the tool does not have to be an OLAP tool).

68289e572c0a.title: Online analytical processing
68289e572c0a.section: Types > Relational OLAP (ROLAP) > Disadvantages of ROLAP
68289e572c0a.sentence: - There is a consensus in the industry that ROLAP tools have slower performance than MOLAP tools.

b21aa154c3ac.title: Online analytical processing
b21aa154c3ac.section: Types > Relational OLAP (ROLAP) > Disadvantages of ROLAP
b21aa154c3ac.sentence: - The loading of aggregate tables must be managed by custom ETL code.

995f4acf9d51.title: Online analytical processing
995f4acf9d51.sentence: - MOLAP generally delivers better performance due to specialized indexing and storage optimizations.

dd5c8403b308.title: Online analytical processing
dd5c8403b308.sentence: MOLAP also needs less storage space compared to ROLAP because the specialized storage typically includes compression techniques.

61f6567222cd.title: Online analytical processing
61f6567222cd.sentence: - Some MOLAP implementations are prone to database explosion, a phenomenon causing vast amounts of storage space to be used by MOLAP databases when certain common conditions are met: high number of dimensions, pre-calculated results and sparse multidimensional data.

491594a29984.title: Online analytical processing
491594a29984.sentence: The undesirable trade-off between additional ETL cost and slow query performance has ensured that most commercial OLAP tools now use a "Hybrid OLAP" (HOLAP) approach, which allows the model designer to decide which portion of the data will be stored in MOLAP and which portion in ROLAP.

bcef4f1cfd2c.title: Online analytical processing
bcef4f1cfd2c.sentence: HOLAP addresses the shortcomings of MOLAP and ROLAP by combining the capabilities of both approaches.

6dac142a9e4a.title: Online analytical processing
6dac142a9e4a.sentence: In this mode HOLAP stores aggregations in MOLAP for fast query performance, and detailed data in ROLAP to optimize time of cube processing.

b297faa84ef5.title: Online analytical processing
b297faa84ef5.sentence: In this mode HOLAP stores some slice of data, usually the more recent one (i.e. sliced by Time dimension) in MOLAP for fast query performance, and older data in ROLAP.

e38deaf49dbe.title: NoSQL
e38deaf49dbe.section: Query optimization and indexing in NoSQL databases
e38deaf49dbe.sentence: Different NoSQL databases, such as DynamoDB, MongoDB, Cassandra, Couchbase, HBase, and Redis, exhibit varying behaviors when querying non-indexed fields.

5b2087c86023.title: NoSQL
5b2087c86023.section: Query optimization and indexing in NoSQL databases
5b2087c86023.sentence: However, modern NoSQL databases often incorporate advanced features to optimize query performance.

2248c82fcd60.title: NoSQL
2248c82fcd60.section: Query optimization and indexing in NoSQL databases
2248c82fcd60.sentence: Many perform full-table or collection scans for such queries, applying filtering operations after retrieving data.

e95d73603b76.title: NoSQL
e95d73603b76.section: Query optimization and indexing in NoSQL databases
e95d73603b76.sentence: For example, MongoDB supports compound indexes and query-optimization strategies, Cassandra offers secondary indexes and materialized views, and Redis employs custom indexing mechanisms tailored to specific use cases.

2acb8d4c31e2.title: NoSQL
2acb8d4c31e2.section: Query optimization and indexing in NoSQL databases
2acb8d4c31e2.sentence: Systems like Elasticsearch use inverted indexes for efficient text-based searches, but they can still require full scans for non-indexed fields.

a865bcf6c134.title: NoSQL
a865bcf6c134.section: Query optimization and indexing in NoSQL databases
a865bcf6c134.sentence: This behavior reflects the design focus of many NoSQL systems on scalability and efficient key-based operations rather than optimized querying for arbitrary fields.

0e77b315eec5.title: NoSQL
0e77b315eec5.section: Query optimization and indexing in NoSQL databases
0e77b315eec5.sentence: Consequently, while these databases excel at basic CRUD operations and key-based lookups, their suitability for complex queries involving joins or non-indexed filtering varies depending on the database type—document, key–value, wide-column, or graph—and the specific implementation.

7d28c1701b51.title: Relational database
7d28c1701b51.sentence: Constraints restrict the data that can be stored in relations.

2d6e9566ce01.title: Relational database
2d6e9566ce01.sentence: These are usually defined using expressions that result in a Boolean value, indicating whether or not the data satisfies the constraint.

75ea246ce9b1.title: Relational database
75ea246ce9b1.sentence: Constraints can apply to single attributes, to a tuple (restricting combinations of attributes) or to an entire relation.

6d5bd14b6523.title: Relational database
6d5bd14b6523.sentence: A domain describes the set of possible values for a given attribute, and can be considered a constraint on the value of the attribute.

f21b62ce43db.title: Relational database
f21b62ce43db.sentence: The character string "ABC", for instance, is not in the integer domain, but the integer value 123 is.

b87520765d80.title: Relational database
b87520765d80.sentence: Constraints are often used to make it possible to further restrict the domain of an attribute.

2f6050626371.title: Relational database
2f6050626371.sentence: For instance, a constraint can restrict a given integer attribute to values between 1 and 10.

6f5cd9931111.title: Relational database
6f5cd9931111.sentence: Constraints provide one method of implementing business rules in the database and support subsequent data use within the application layer.

4910e615d604.title: Relational database
4910e615d604.sentence: SQL implements constraint functionality in the form of check constraints.

907aa63cfaef.title: Relational database
907aa63cfaef.sentence: The two principal rules for the relational model are known as entity integrity and referential integrity.

ac4d0dba56b2.title: Relational database
ac4d0dba56b2.sentence: Queries made against the relational database, and the derived relvars in the database are expressed in a relational calculus or a relational algebra.

e4375466acbd.title: Relational database
e4375466acbd.sentence: In his original relational algebra, Codd introduced eight relational operators in two groups of four operators each.

97282eaec0a7.title: Relational database
97282eaec0a7.sentence: - The union operator (∪) combines the tuples of two relations and removes all duplicate tuples from the result.

909ee274c441.title: Relational database
909ee274c441.sentence: The relational union operator is equivalent to the SQL UNION operator.

fc3977e22b52.title: Relational database
fc3977e22b52.sentence: - The intersection operator (∩) produces the set of tuples that two relations share in common.

d262a798b4f7.title: Relational database
d262a798b4f7.sentence: Intersection is implemented in SQL in the form of the INTERSECT operator.

8d37fc825cc6.title: Relational database
8d37fc825cc6.sentence: - The set difference operator (-) acts on two relations and produces the set of tuples from the first relation that do not exist in the second relation.

6f2a6216e85d.title: Relational database
6f2a6216e85d.sentence: Difference is implemented in SQL in the form of the EXCEPT or MINUS operator.

a16f8e49c578.title: Relational database
a16f8e49c578.sentence: - The cartesian product (×) of two relations is a join that is not restricted by any criteria, resulting in every tuple of the first relation being matched with every tuple of the second relation.

90c92ad2ab35.title: Relational database
90c92ad2ab35.sentence: The cartesian product is implemented in SQL as the Cross join operator.

2468d3113da3.title: Relational database
2468d3113da3.sentence: - The selection, or restriction, operation (σ) retrieves tuples from a relation, limiting the results to only those that meet a specific criterion, i.e. a subset in terms of set theory.

9b016fec79fc.title: Relational database
9b016fec79fc.sentence: The SQL equivalent of selection is the SELECT query statement with a WHERE clause.

6c867b75d7a6.title: Relational database
6c867b75d7a6.sentence: - The projection operation (π) extracts only the specified attributes from a tuple or set of tuples.

16f543075ae4.title: Relational database
16f543075ae4.sentence: - The join operation defined for relational databases is often referred to as a natural join (⋈).

9eb8b40551f6.title: Relational database
9eb8b40551f6.sentence: In this type of join, two relations are connected by their common attributes.

b2a953f5f65e.title: Relational database
b2a953f5f65e.sentence: - The relational division (÷) operation is a slightly more complex operation and essentially involves using the tuples of one relation (the dividend) to partition a second relation (the divisor).

4829f321458b.title: Relational database
4829f321458b.sentence: In SQL, an INNER JOIN prevents a cartesian product from occurring when there are two tables in a query.

ad5874cc2b32.title: Relational database
ad5874cc2b32.sentence: Thus, for N tables in an SQL query, there must be N−1 INNER JOINS to prevent a cartesian product.

6b542659ed16.title: NoSQL
6b542659ed16.sentence: Since most NoSQL databases lack ability for joins in queries, the database schema generally needs to be designed differently.

89b8683d6f51.title: NoSQL
89b8683d6f51.sentence: There are three main techniques for handling relational data in a NoSQL database.

45b2d706ff5b.title: Database
45b2d706ff5b.sentence: NoSQL databases are often very fast, do not require fixed table schemas, avoid join operations by storing denormalized data, and are designed to scale horizontally.

d68ace9979c8.title: NoSQL
d68ace9979c8.sentence: Instead of retrieving all the data with one query, it is common to do several queries to get the desired data.

91e493172940.title: NoSQL
91e493172940.sentence: NoSQL queries are often faster than traditional SQL queries, so the cost of additional queries may be acceptable.

c9770b30dacc.title: NoSQL
c9770b30dacc.sentence: If an excessive number of queries would be necessary, one of the other two approaches is more appropriate.

924fc14b4208.title: NoSQL
924fc14b4208.section: Handling relational data > Caching, replication and non-normalized data
924fc14b4208.sentence: Instead of only storing foreign keys, it is common to store actual foreign values along with the model's data.

cd477d7dfb06.title: NoSQL
cd477d7dfb06.section: Handling relational data > Caching, replication and non-normalized data
cd477d7dfb06.sentence: For example, each blog comment might include the username in addition to a user id, thus providing easy access to the username without requiring another lookup.

14aa627a1e88.title: NoSQL
14aa627a1e88.section: Handling relational data > Caching, replication and non-normalized data
14aa627a1e88.sentence: When a username changes, however, this will now need to be changed in many places in the database.

f57c31e596fe.title: NoSQL
f57c31e596fe.section: Handling relational data > Caching, replication and non-normalized data
f57c31e596fe.sentence: Thus this approach works better when reads are much more common than writes.

f6247fbf273d.title: NoSQL
f6247fbf273d.sentence: With document databases like MongoDB it is common to put more data in a smaller number of collections.

c5d92a132d2d.title: NoSQL
c5d92a132d2d.sentence: For example, in a blogging application, one might choose to store comments within the blog post document, so that with a single retrieval one gets all the comments.

c772c83fc23c.title: NoSQL
