c772c83fc23c.sentence: Thus in this approach a single document contains all the data needed for a specific task.

c425bfc6fcc7.title: Relational database
c425bfc6fcc7.sentence: A stored procedure is executable code that is associated with, and generally stored in, the database.

73402a841f25.title: Relational database
73402a841f25.sentence: Stored procedures usually collect and customize common operations, like inserting a tuple into a relation, gathering statistical information about usage patterns, or encapsulating complex business logic and calculations.

f2a223bb9811.title: Relational database
f2a223bb9811.sentence: Often procedures can be used to greatly reduce the amount of information transferred within and outside of a system.

0af946b2dba9.title: Relational database
0af946b2dba9.sentence: For increased security, the system design may grant access to only the stored procedures and not directly to the tables.

cc960cadd84c.title: Relational database
cc960cadd84c.sentence: Frequently they are used as an application programming interface (API) for security or simplicity.

8104331fff07.title: Relational database
8104331fff07.sentence: Stored procedures are not part of the relational database model, but all commercial implementations include them.

42426b42fddd.title: Relational database
42426b42fddd.sentence: Implementations of stored procedures on SQL RDBMS's often allow developers to take advantage of procedural extensions (often vendor-specific) to the standard declarative SQL syntax.

3cc5b548deb1.title: Relational database
3cc5b548deb1.sentence: Other relations do not store data, but are computed by applying relational operations to other relations.

285f344c77b7.title: Relational database
285f344c77b7.sentence: In implementations these are called "views" or "queries".

da8ca166586a.title: Relational database
da8ca166586a.sentence: Relations that store data are called "base relations", and in implementations are called "tables".

c0eb5fc6594c.title: Relational database
c0eb5fc6594c.sentence: These relations are sometimes called "derived relations".

1973b7ccfe5b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
1973b7ccfe5b.sentence: A materialized view is a pre-computed data set derived from a query specification and stored for later use.

de3ab99af20e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
de3ab99af20e.sentence: Because the data is pre-computed, querying a materialized view is faster than executing a query against the base table of the view.

c87806e0134d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
c87806e0134d.sentence: This performance difference can be significant when a query is run frequently or is sufficiently complex.

65e7229ec7d1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
65e7229ec7d1.sentence: It also enables data subsetting and improves the performance of complex queries that run on large data sets which reduces network loads.

88f72c4c732d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
88f72c4c732d.sentence: There are other uses of materialized views, but they are mostly used for performance and replication.

4702cc8baa72.title: Vector database
4702cc8baa72.sentence: A vector database, vector store or vector search engine is a database that stores and retrieves embeddings of data in vector space.

bfc8f40af8e8.title: Vector database
bfc8f40af8e8.sentence: Vector embeddings are mathematical representations of data in a high-dimensional space.

17db912d8054.title: Vector database
17db912d8054.sentence: In this space, each dimension corresponds to a feature of the data, with the number of dimensions ranging from a few hundred to tens of thousands, depending on the complexity of the data being represented.

0ada56568a1d.title: Vector database
0ada56568a1d.sentence: These feature vectors may be computed from the raw data using machine learning methods such as feature extraction algorithms, word embeddings or deep learning networks.

a3b20658dbf6.title: Vector database
a3b20658dbf6.sentence: Words, phrases, or entire documents, as well as images, audio, and other types of data, can all be vectorized.

ea4444c3563b.title: Vector database
ea4444c3563b.sentence: The goal is that semantically similar data items receive feature vectors close to each other.

7e5b7bffb44e.title: Vector database
7e5b7bffb44e.sentence: Vector databases typically implement approximate nearest neighbor algorithms so users can search for records semantically similar to a given input, unlike traditional databases which primarily look up records by exact match.

e48ea60bc2c2.title: Vector database
e48ea60bc2c2.sentence: Use-cases for vector databases include similarity search, semantic search, multi-modal search, recommendations engines, object detection, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

208f795d10fd.title: Vector database
208f795d10fd.sentence: Common techniques for similarity search on high-dimensional vectors include:

7f15d462c608.title: Vector database
7f15d462c608.sentence: These techniques may also be combined in vector search systems.

898e9262a7cd.title: Vector database
898e9262a7cd.sentence: In recent benchmarks, HNSW-based implementations have been among the best performers.

f4bcc7b367b5.title: Vector database
f4bcc7b367b5.sentence: Text documents describing the domain of interest are collected, and for each document or document section, a feature vector (known as an "embedding") is computed, typically using a deep learning network, and stored in a vector database along with a link to the document.

f62e64f1ef79.title: Vector database
f62e64f1ef79.sentence: Given a user prompt, the feature vector of the prompt is computed, and the database is queried to retrieve the most relevant documents.

b5e9fd06c4e5.title: Vector database
b5e9fd06c4e5.sentence: These are then automatically added into the context window of the large language model, and the large language model proceeds to create a response to the prompt given this context.

87b010cc97f1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
87b010cc97f1.sentence: - Full-Text Search: Fast, flexible text search capabilities

7d22451536e0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
7d22451536e0.sentence: - Document Stores: JSON-like document storage and querying

2a89c61f964d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
2a89c61f964d.sentence: - Key-Value Stores: High-speed, simple data models

d0f7c7a4f6e7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
d0f7c7a4f6e7.sentence: - Graph Databases: Managing highly connected data

35d6507302fd.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
35d6507302fd.sentence: - Embeddings: Efficient storage and retrieval of vector representations

4fd37e416716.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-database.md
4fd37e416716.sentence: - Geospatial: Specialized for location-based data and queries

41363a1ce2ef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
41363a1ce2ef.sentence: While choosing a database we need to keep the properties of both the models and the requirements of our application in mind.

765beeb64734.title: Polyglot persistence
765beeb64734.sentence: Polyglot persistence is using multiple data storage technologies within a single system, in order to meet varying data storage needs.

c84ac4b45515.title: Polyglot persistence
c84ac4b45515.sentence: Complex applications combine different types of problems, so picking the right language for each job may be more productive than trying to solve all aspects of the problem using a single language.

0d82d6d6cbeb.title: Polyglot persistence
0d82d6d6cbeb.sentence: This same concept can be applied to databases, that an application can communicate with different databases, using each for what it is best at to achieve an end goal, hence the term polyglot persistence.

38a372164965.title: Polyglot persistence
38a372164965.sentence: Since there are numerous databases available to solve different problems, using a single database to satisfy all of a program's requirements can result in a non-performant, "jack of all trades, master of none" solution.

22efce8a12e1.title: Polyglot persistence
22efce8a12e1.sentence: Thus different problems are solved by different database systems, all within the same application.

43020734a1d5.title: Polyglot persistence
43020734a1d5.sentence: Relational databases, for example, are good at enforcing relationships that exist between various data tables.

2e4480d932b8.title: Polyglot persistence
2e4480d932b8.sentence: To discover a relationship or to find data from different tables that belong to the same object, an SQL join operation can be used.

ddab2cb31308.title: Polyglot persistence
ddab2cb31308.sentence: This might work when the data is smaller in size, but becomes problematic when the data involved grows larger.

d7fb608cb43f.title: Polyglot persistence
d7fb608cb43f.sentence: A graph database might solve the problem of relationships in case of Big Data, but it might not solve the problem of database transactions, which may be provided better by relational database management systems.

6b877bf09ab8.title: Polyglot persistence
6b877bf09ab8.sentence: Instead, a NoSQL document database might be used to store unstructured data for that particular part of the problem.

e15d10ebc36c.title: Polyglot persistence
e15d10ebc36c.sentence: Martin Fowler writes in one of his articles, "One of the interesting consequences of this is that we are gearing up for a shift to polyglot persistence where any decent sized enterprise will have a variety of different data storage technologies for different kinds of data.

2e6920343c82.title: Polyglot persistence
2e6920343c82.sentence: There will still be large amounts of it managed in relational stores, but increasingly we'll be first asking how we want to manipulate the data and only then figuring out what technology is the best bet for it."

5723aae0ca09.title: Multi-model database
5723aae0ca09.sentence: A multi-model database is most directly a response to the "polyglot persistence" approach of knitting together multiple database products, each handing a different model, to achieve a multi-model capability as described by Martin Fowler.

0057027c555a.title: Multi-model database
0057027c555a.sentence: This strategy has two major disadvantages: it leads to a significant increase in operational complexity, and there is no support for maintaining data consistency across the separate data stores, so multi-model databases have begun to fill in this gap.

72c6a7d0c1f9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
72c6a7d0c1f9.sentence: BASE properties are much looser than ACID guarantees, but there isn't a direct one-for-one mapping between the two consistency models.

dfba34acacae.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
dfba34acacae.sentence: In the NoSQL database world, ACID transactions are less common as some databases have loosened the requirements for immediate consistency, data freshness, and accuracy in order to gain other benefits, like scale and resilience.

c5993bfa9f3b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
c5993bfa9f3b.sentence: The database appears to work most of the time.

798f6b82d8bc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
798f6b82d8bc.sentence: Stores don't have to be write-consistent, nor do different replicas have to be mutually consistent all the time.

dff94c687aa7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
dff94c687aa7.sentence: The data might not be consistent immediately but eventually, it becomes consistent.

843ed2422001.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
843ed2422001.sentence: Reads in the system are still possible even though they may not give the correct response due to inconsistency.

f18073e35d33.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
f18073e35d33.sentence: With the increasing amount of data and high availability requirements, the approach to database design has also changed dramatically.

c8d7265641f9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
c8d7265641f9.sentence: To increase the ability to scale and at the same time be highly available, we move the logic from the database to separate servers.

b256a1e13b0c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
b256a1e13b0c.sentence: In this way, the database becomes more independent and focused on the actual process of storing data.

9e796b6604a5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
9e796b6604a5.sentence: There's no right answer to whether our application needs an ACID or a BASE consistency model.

e87ecd5edca6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
e87ecd5edca6.sentence: Both the models have been designed to satisfy different requirements.

659127e67f78.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
659127e67f78.sentence: A fully ACID database is the perfect fit for use cases where data reliability and consistency are essential.

91f79783c340.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
91f79783c340.sentence: Given BASE's loose consistency, developers need to be more knowledgeable and rigorous about consistent data if they choose a BASE store for their application.

90ebc2d9641d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
90ebc2d9641d.sentence: It's essential to be familiar with the BASE behavior of the chosen database and work within those constraints.

97f9827284d0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::acid-and-base-consistency-models
97f9827284d0.sentence: On the other hand, planning around BASE limitations can sometimes be a major disadvantage when compared to the simplicity of ACID transactions.

836dc1c85a6a.title: CAP theorem
836dc1c85a6a.sentence: Database systems designed with traditional ACID guarantees in mind such as RDBMS choose consistency over availability, whereas systems designed around the BASE philosophy, common in the NoSQL movement for example, choose availability over consistency, but MongoDB and Redis resolve network partitions by maintaining consistency while compromising on availability.

ac365f9e8343.title: ACID
ac365f9e8343.sentence: ACID databases prioritize consistency over availability — the whole transaction fails if an error occurs in any step within the transaction; in contrast, BASE databases prioritize availability over consistency: instead of failing the transaction, users can access inconsistent data temporarily: data consistency is achieved, but not immediately.

15b3bbfdc3c3.title: ACID
15b3bbfdc3c3.sentence: A database either leans towards ACID or BASE, but it cannot be both (according to CAP theorem).

b027572ad3d8.title: ACID
b027572ad3d8.sentence: However, some NoSQL databases might exhibit certain ACID traits.

a2c67d60a411.title: ACID
a2c67d60a411.sentence: For example, SQL databases (like MySQL, PostgreSQL, AWS RedShift) are structured over the ACID model, while NoSQL databases (like DynamoDB or ElasticSearch) use the BASE architecture.

4aabbd44db06.title: Time series database
4aabbd44db06.sentence: A time series database (TSDB) is a software system optimized for handling time series data—a sequence of data points indexed in chronological order.

5d575e214ff3.title: Time series database
5d575e214ff3.sentence: Early iterations of these databases were primarily associated with industrial applications, where they functioned as data historians to efficiently record measurements from physical sensors; however, modern implementations now span a much wider range of uses.

58720eccc57d.title: Time series database
58720eccc57d.sentence: Common application areas include industrial automation monitoring, operational data historians, infrastructure and application performance monitoring (APM), IoT telemetry, smart energy grid management, financial market tick data tracking, and scientific experimental measurements.

c41128faeed4.title: Time series database
c41128faeed4.sentence: Compared to general-purpose datasets, time series datasets are highly uniform and scale rapidly, typically consisting of sequential timestamps mapped to specific metric values.

9ce63b5dbad2.title: Time series database
9ce63b5dbad2.sentence: Because individual entries rarely feature complex, cross-table relational dependencies, TSDBs do not require the overhead of traditional relational constraints.

cd3502c0f3f4.title: Time series database
cd3502c0f3f4.sentence: Furthermore, because these workloads seldom demand indefinite data retention, TSDBs can drastically reduce storage footprints and accelerate queries relative to general-purpose databases.

8af519436a82.title: Time series database
8af519436a82.sentence: Due to the high ingestion rates and sequential nature of this data, TSDB repositories heavily utilize specialized compression algorithms to manage storage efficiently.

f16ee6d7a1d8.title: Time series database
f16ee6d7a1d8.sentence: For example, the sequential uniformity of temporal data allows specialized compression algorithms—such as delta encoding or Gorilla compression—to achieve significantly higher data density than standard compression techniques.

a2f29f4e4fe1.title: Time series database
a2f29f4e4fe1.sentence: Additionally, while general-purpose systems are optimized for persistent data retention, TSDBs natively automate data lifecycle management by downsampling or dropping entire historical data partitions in bulk.

8497829ee441.title: Time series database
8497829ee441.sentence: Finally, specialized temporal indexing strategies further isolate time windows to maximize query performance.

056f7a0c95e2.title: Time series database
056f7a0c95e2.sentence: Time series databases are commonly designed for append-only workloads, where massive volumes of sequential observations or discrete events are continuously ingested alongside corresponding timestamps.

f23480bc6e16.title: Time series database
f23480bc6e16.sentence: In these environments, data streams are typically generated at extreme velocities and high volumes.

d199c3742cfe.title: Time series database
d199c3742cfe.sentence: Primary design paradigms focus on maximizing write throughput, ensuring low-latency range queries, utilizing highly efficient data compression, and natively supporting multi-window temporal aggregations or automated downsampling.

a4c8ebaeb491.title: Time series database
a4c8ebaeb491.sentence: To facilitate multidimensional indexing, many implementations organize data using a schema composed of key-value tags, device IDs, or other metadata.

389e4b8e5b47.title: Time series database
389e4b8e5b47.sentence: This metadata structure allows applications to isolate and query telemetry based simultaneously on specific time intervals and source attributes.

a60a17e9d2d9.title: Isolation (database systems)
a60a17e9d2d9.sentence: Concurrency control comprises the underlying mechanisms in a DBMS which handle isolation and guarantee related correctness.

061764c25519.title: Isolation (database systems)
061764c25519.sentence: It is heavily used by the database and storage engines both to guarantee the correct execution of concurrent transactions, and (via different mechanisms) the correctness of other DBMS processes.

47786f6017ce.title: Isolation (database systems)
47786f6017ce.sentence: The transaction-related mechanisms typically constrain the database data access operations' timing (transaction schedules) to certain orders characterized as the serializability and recoverability schedule properties.

b9b96b990006.title: Isolation (database systems)
b9b96b990006.sentence: Constraining database access operation execution typically means reduced performance (measured by rates of execution), and thus concurrency control mechanisms are typically designed to provide the best performance possible under the constraints.

7019be5b59ab.title: Isolation (database systems)
7019be5b59ab.sentence: Often, when possible without harming correctness, the serializability property is compromised for better performance.

94c88e4c82c5.title: Isolation (database systems)
94c88e4c82c5.sentence: However, recoverability cannot be compromised, since such typically results in a database integrity violation.

6ef058097fbb.title: Isolation (database systems)
6ef058097fbb.sentence: Two-phase locking is the most common transaction concurrency control method in DBMSs, used to provide both serializability and recoverability for correctness.

e486b6cb13eb.title: Isolation (database systems)
e486b6cb13eb.sentence: In order to access a database object a transaction first needs to acquire a lock for this object.

087254c57fe9.title: Isolation (database systems)
087254c57fe9.sentence: Depending on the access operation type (e.g., reading or writing an object) and on the lock type, acquiring the lock may be blocked and postponed, if another transaction is holding a lock for that object.

0b3dfe9b87e5.title: ACID
0b3dfe9b87e5.sentence: Many databases rely upon locking to provide ACID capabilities.

e719896c0827.title: ACID
e719896c0827.sentence: Locking means that the transaction marks the data that it accesses so that the DBMS knows not to allow other transactions to modify it until the first transaction succeeds or fails.

114f296568cc.title: ACID
114f296568cc.sentence: The lock must always be acquired before processing data, including data that is read but not modified.

7352b22f52f1.title: ACID
7352b22f52f1.sentence: Non-trivial transactions typically require a large number of locks, resulting in substantial overhead as well as blocking other transactions.

01f98f7ee5e1.title: Data warehouse
01f98f7ee5e1.sentence: The typical extract, transform, load (ETL)-based data warehouse uses staging, data integration, and access layers to house its key functions.

ecd4580a2668.title: Data warehouse
ecd4580a2668.sentence: In this approach, data gets extracted from heterogeneous source systems and are then directly loaded into the data warehouse, before any transformation occurs.

774835c1dd90.title: Data warehouse
774835c1dd90.sentence: The staging layer or staging database stores raw data extracted from each of the disparate source data systems.

45be9da7a92c.title: Data warehouse
45be9da7a92c.sentence: The integration layer integrates disparate data sets by transforming the data from the staging layer, often storing this transformed data in an operational data store (ODS) database.

f6d4231fb76c.title: Data warehouse
f6d4231fb76c.sentence: The integrated data are then moved to yet another database, often called the data warehouse database, where the data is arranged into hierarchical groups, often called dimensions, and into facts and aggregate facts.

ce2056044552.title: Data warehouse
ce2056044552.sentence: The access layer helps users retrieve data.

2835009fd2d1.title: Batch processing
2835009fd2d1.sentence: The extract, transform, load (ETL) step in populating data warehouses is inherently a batch process in most implementations.

c94aacd63425.title: Data warehouse
c94aacd63425.sentence: ELT-based data warehousing gets rid of a separate ETL tool for data transformation.

b27b881c2646.title: Data warehouse
b27b881c2646.sentence: Instead, it maintains a staging area inside the data warehouse itself.

d8fb8f703e9e.title: Data warehouse
d8fb8f703e9e.sentence: All necessary transformations are then handled inside the data warehouse itself.

2bec9d1e5e94.title: Data warehouse
2bec9d1e5e94.sentence: Finally, the manipulated data gets loaded into target tables in the same data warehouse.

e6cb198c296b.title: Multi-model database
e6cb198c296b.sentence: In the field of database design, a multi-model database is a database management system designed to support multiple data models against a single, integrated backend.

e7fc3ba11549.title: Multi-model database
e7fc3ba11549.sentence: In contrast, most database management systems are organized around a single data model that determines how data can be organized, stored, and manipulated.

895bb859fba0.title: Multi-model database
895bb859fba0.sentence: Document, graph, relational, and key–value models are examples of data models that may be supported by a multi-model database.

e4d129af5405.title: Multi-model database
e4d129af5405.sentence: A multi-model database is a database that can store, index and query data in more than one model.

2db227c9ca69.title: Multi-model database
2db227c9ca69.sentence: Multi-model databases are intended to offer the data modeling advantages of polyglot persistence, without its disadvantages.

722b976c0c70.title: Multi-model database
722b976c0c70.sentence: Operational complexity, in particular, is reduced through the use of a single data store.

594a0e4dbfcc.title: Multi-model database
594a0e4dbfcc.sentence: They pointed out that the advantages of multi-model databases over single-model databases are as follows:

3bc86cb98f05.title: Multi-model database
3bc86cb98f05.sentence: - they are able to ingest a variety of data formats such as CSV (including Graph, Relational), JSON into storage without any additional efforts.

4cb4887fc5ee.title: Multi-model database
4cb4887fc5ee.sentence: - they can employ a unified query language such as AQL, Orient SQL, SQL/XML, SQL/JSON to retrieve correlated multi-model data, such as graph-JSON-key/value, XML-relational, and JSON-relational in a single platform.

a9c5b5320525.title: Multi-model database
a9c5b5320525.sentence: - they are able to support multi-model ACID transactions in the stand-alone mode.

97c955bdb781.title: Multi-model database
97c955bdb781.sentence: The main difference between the available multi-model databases is related to their architectures.

d8255b3c72c7.title: Multi-model database
d8255b3c72c7.sentence: Multi-model databases can support different models either within the engine or via different layers on top of the engine.

0010691a9881.title: Multi-model database
0010691a9881.sentence: Some products may provide an engine which supports documents and graphs while others provide layers on top of a key-key store.

1b2dc2804641.title: Multi-model database
1b2dc2804641.sentence: With a layered architecture, each data model is provided via its own component.

f38a795283af.title: NewSQL
f38a795283af.sentence: NewSQL is a class of relational database management systems that seek to provide the scalability of NoSQL systems for online transaction processing (OLTP) workloads while maintaining the ACID guarantees of a traditional database system.

2541abce49be.title: NewSQL
2541abce49be.sentence: Many enterprise systems that handle high-profile data (e.g., financial and order processing systems) are too large for conventional relational databases, but have transactional and consistency requirements that are not practical for NoSQL systems.

e77fe3556ee3.title: NewSQL
e77fe3556ee3.sentence: The only options previously available for these organizations were to either purchase more powerful computers or to develop custom middleware that distributes requests over conventional DBMS.

a4ee78f19359.title: NewSQL
a4ee78f19359.sentence: Both approaches feature high infrastructure costs and/or development costs.

c5380592f286.title: NewSQL
c5380592f286.sentence: NewSQL systems attempt to reconcile the conflicts.

40a8d50a626a.title: NewSQL
40a8d50a626a.sentence: The two common distinguishing features of NewSQL database solutions are that they support online scalability of NoSQL databases and the relational data model (including ACID consistency) using SQL as their primary interface.

07c6c9e82000.title: NewSQL
07c6c9e82000.sentence: Typical applications are characterized by heavy OLTP transaction volumes.

c746da878605.title: NewSQL
c746da878605.sentence: - touch small amounts of data per transaction

12e39149585a.title: NewSQL
12e39149585a.sentence: - have a small number of forms (a small number of queries with different arguments).

25be43e62be9.title: NewSQL
25be43e62be9.sentence: However, some support hybrid transactional/analytical processing (HTAP) applications.

b653f040cec0.title: NewSQL
b653f040cec0.sentence: NewSQL systems can be loosely grouped into three categories:

5c0c75a7977d.title: NewSQL
5c0c75a7977d.sentence: Some systems employ a cluster of shared-nothing nodes, in which each node manages a subset of the data.

10fa40ff0a2e.title: NewSQL
10fa40ff0a2e.sentence: The second category are optimized storage engines for SQL.

ab8fe725a490.title: NewSQL
ab8fe725a490.sentence: These systems provide the same programming interface as SQL, but scale better than built-in engines.

b58e9cfa1edd.title: NewSQL
b58e9cfa1edd.sentence: These systems automatically split databases across multiple nodes using Raft or Paxos consensus algorithm.

ca8ff74cbbba.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
ca8ff74cbbba.sentence: The N+1 query problem happens when the data access layer executes N additional SQL statements to fetch the same data that could have been retrieved when executing the primary SQL query.

cca438bec0bd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
cca438bec0bd.sentence: The larger the value of N, the more queries will be executed, the larger the performance impact.

d2ee1ec3eb6a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sql-databases
d2ee1ec3eb6a.sentence: This is commonly seen in GraphQL and ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) tools and can be addressed by optimizing the SQL query or using a dataloader that batches consecutive requests and makes a single data request under the hood.

3085c74b294a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
3085c74b294a.sentence: A transaction in a database can be in one of the following states:

77ee883898bc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
77ee883898bc.sentence: This is the initial state of every transaction.

7b77f3ed42c0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
7b77f3ed42c0.sentence: In this state, the transaction is being executed.

d25d3f755fd8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
d25d3f755fd8.sentence: When a transaction executes its final operation, it is said to be in a partially committed state.

dc9ff1d5680c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
dc9ff1d5680c.sentence: If a transaction executes all its operations successfully, it is said to be committed.

3b20dddf16c3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
3b20dddf16c3.sentence: All its effects are now permanently established on the database system.

1df44d05cf75.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
1df44d05cf75.sentence: The transaction is said to be in a failed state if any of the checks made by the database recovery system fails.

d036a4870441.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
d036a4870441.sentence: A failed transaction can no longer proceed further.

91e5a3702c85.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
91e5a3702c85.sentence: If any of the checks fail and the transaction has reached a failed state, then the recovery manager rolls back all its write operations on the database to bring the database back to its original state where it was prior to the execution of the transaction.

d7f3b91d4b6c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
d7f3b91d4b6c.sentence: Transactions in this state are aborted.

4b20d3f3bd34.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
4b20d3f3bd34.sentence: The database recovery module can select one of the two operations after a transaction aborts:

2447c76af166.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::transactions
2447c76af166.sentence: If there isn't any roll-back or the transaction comes from the committed state, then the system is consistent and ready for a new transaction and the old transaction is terminated.

205758e1a545.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
205758e1a545.sentence: The role of a schema is to define the shape of a data structure, and specify what kinds of data can go where.

ab55050aae8a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
ab55050aae8a.sentence: Schemas can be strictly enforced across the entire database, loosely enforced on part of the database, or they might not exist at all.

985c21a9ba77.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
985c21a9ba77.sentence: Each table contains various columns just like in a spreadsheet.

700367fba4e5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
700367fba4e5.sentence: A table can have as meager as two columns and upwards of a hundred or more columns, depending upon the kind of information being put in the table.

347e0931c147.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
347e0931c147.sentence: A column contains a set of data values of a particular type, one value for each row of the database.

deb2bac5f6ba.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
deb2bac5f6ba.sentence: A column may contain text values, numbers, enums, timestamps, etc.

8616425fa9b9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
8616425fa9b9.sentence: Data in a table is recorded in rows.

796646507146.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::databases-and-dbms
796646507146.sentence: There can be thousands or millions of rows in a table having any particular information.

7cd83ccf89da.title: Multiversion concurrency control
7cd83ccf89da.sentence: Multiversion concurrency control (MCC or MVCC) is a non-locking concurrency control method commonly used by database management systems to provide concurrent access to the database and in programming languages to implement transactional memory.

51555d591f5c.title: Multiversion concurrency control
51555d591f5c.sentence: MVCC aims at solving the problem by keeping multiple copies of each data item.

5acef5779bac.title: Multiversion concurrency control
5acef5779bac.sentence: The simplest way is to make all readers wait until the writer is done, which is known as a read-write lock.

16750ebae1e7.title: Multiversion concurrency control
16750ebae1e7.sentence: Locks are known to create contention especially between long read transactions and update transactions.

023bc4a5baee.title: Multiversion concurrency control
023bc4a5baee.sentence: When an MVCC database needs to update a piece of data, it will not overwrite the original data item with new data, but instead creates a newer version of the data item.

2c55a435e79e.title: Multiversion concurrency control
2c55a435e79e.sentence: In this way, each user connected to the database sees a snapshot of the database at a particular instant in time.

5828855b3360.title: Multiversion concurrency control
5828855b3360.sentence: Any changes made by a writer will not be seen by other users of the database until the changes have been completed (or, in database terms: until the transaction has been committed.)

4d3d0916952f.title: Multiversion concurrency control
4d3d0916952f.sentence: The version that each transaction sees depends on the isolation level implemented.

9c22af7e4531.title: Multiversion concurrency control
9c22af7e4531.sentence: The most common isolation level implemented with MVCC is snapshot isolation.

c2e532fb1735.title: Multiversion concurrency control
c2e532fb1735.sentence: With snapshot isolation, a transaction observes a state of the data as of when the transaction started.

61651808c566.title: Multiversion concurrency control
61651808c566.sentence: Read transactions under MVCC typically use a timestamp or transaction ID to determine what state of the DB to read, and read these versions of the data.

79c5d30441f2.title: Multiversion concurrency control
79c5d30441f2.sentence: Read and write transactions are thus isolated from each other without any need for locking.

5b2728812bd0.title: ACID
5b2728812bd0.sentence: This allows readers to operate without acquiring locks, i.e., writing transactions do not block reading transactions, and readers do not block writers.

ede99691bb16.title: Multiversion concurrency control
ede99691bb16.sentence: However, despite locks being unnecessary, they are used by some MVCC databases such as Oracle.

ef02cc047bbd.title: Multiversion concurrency control
ef02cc047bbd.sentence: Each version of object P has both a Read Timestamp (RTS) and a Write Timestamp (WTS) which lets a particular transaction Ti read the most recent version of the object which precedes the transaction's Read Timestamp RTS(Ti).

127f604dadcf.title: Multiversion concurrency control
127f604dadcf.sentence: To restate; every object (P) has a Timestamp (TS), however if transaction Ti wants to Write to an object, and the transaction has a Timestamp (TS) that is earlier than the object's current Read Timestamp, TS(Ti) < RTS(P), then the transaction is aborted and restarted.

2783ca6114ce.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-are-database-isolation-levels.md
2783ca6114ce.sentence: There are two hidden columns for each row: transaction_id and roll_pointer.

b043637377e9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-are-database-isolation-levels.md
b043637377e9.sentence: Now transaction A modifies the balance to 200, a new row of the log is created, and the roll_pointer points to the old row.

da0ae09b994d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-are-database-isolation-levels.md
da0ae09b994d.sentence: When transaction A starts, a new Read View with transaction_id=201 is created.

3659970203d2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-are-database-isolation-levels.md
3659970203d2.sentence: Transaction B finds that transaction_id 201 is not committed, it reads the next committed record(transaction_id=200).

925c7797a874.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-are-database-isolation-levels.md
925c7797a874.sentence: Even when transaction A commits, transaction B still reads data based on the Read View created when transaction B starts.

b0aeb0dc679d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-are-database-isolation-levels.md
b0aeb0dc679d.sentence: So transaction B always reads the data with balance=100.

2e36c7851de8.title: Multiversion concurrency control
2e36c7851de8.sentence: MVCC introduces the challenge of how to remove versions that become obsolete and will never be read.

feb82b4066bc.title: Multiversion concurrency control
feb82b4066bc.sentence: In some cases, a process to periodically sweep through and delete the obsolete versions is implemented.

21a9796f0c43.title: Multiversion concurrency control
21a9796f0c43.sentence: PostgreSQL can use this approach with its VACUUM FREEZE process.

d2e05a3effef.title: Multiversion concurrency control
d2e05a3effef.sentence: Other databases split the storage blocks into two parts: the data part and an undo log.

893a0f631c29.title: Multiversion concurrency control
893a0f631c29.sentence: The main inherent limitation of this latter approach is that when there are update-intensive workloads, the undo log part runs out of space and then transactions are aborted as they cannot be given their snapshot.

367a0596fea8.title: Multiversion concurrency control
367a0596fea8.sentence: The drawback to this system is the cost of storing multiple versions of objects in the database.

a0bbaa3a17d5.title: Multiversion concurrency control
a0bbaa3a17d5.sentence: On the other hand, reads are never blocked, which can be important for workloads mostly involving reading values from the database.

54f126b0309d.title: Two-phase locking
54f126b0309d.sentence: In databases and transaction processing, two-phase locking (2PL) is a pessimistic concurrency control method that guarantees conflict-serializability.

45b1f5f76f13.title: Two-phase locking
45b1f5f76f13.sentence: The two phase locking rules can be summarized as: each transaction must never acquire a lock after it has released a lock.

84e34301a95d.title: Two-phase locking
84e34301a95d.sentence: The protocol uses locks, applied by a transaction to data, which may block (interpreted as signals to stop) other transactions from accessing the same data during the transaction's life.

82f475a50d11.title: Two-phase locking
82f475a50d11.sentence: By the 2PL protocol, locks are applied and removed in two phases:

c73c0dfc733b.title: Two-phase locking
c73c0dfc733b.sentence: - Expanding phase (aka Growing phase): locks are acquired and no locks are released (the number of locks can only increase).

1daceabf75fb.title: Two-phase locking
1daceabf75fb.sentence: - Shrinking phase (aka Contracting phase): locks are released and no locks are acquired.

612fa9a0f1d4.title: Two-phase locking
612fa9a0f1d4.sentence: The serializability property is guaranteed for a schedule with transactions that obey this rule.

3bd08d3501e8.title: Two-phase locking
3bd08d3501e8.sentence: Two types of locks are used by the basic protocol: Shared and Exclusive locks.

98ba83a505fc.title: Two-phase locking
98ba83a505fc.sentence: For 2PL, the only used data-access locks are read-locks (shared locks) and write-locks (exclusive locks).

b9c3048f5248.title: Two-phase locking
b9c3048f5248.sentence: - A transaction is allowed to read an object if and only if it is holding a read-lock or write-lock on that object.

79a34f1945bb.title: Two-phase locking
79a34f1945bb.sentence: - A transaction is allowed to write an object if and only if it is holding a write-lock on that object.

3ded08ee89da.title: Two-phase locking
3ded08ee89da.sentence: - A schedule (i.e., a set of transactions) is allowed to hold multiple locks on the same object simultaneously if and only if none of those locks are write-locks.

c3de8f6c63b5.title: Two-phase locking
c3de8f6c63b5.sentence: If a disallowed lock attempts on being held simultaneously, it will be blocked.

ad129b2c7ff2.title: Two-phase locking
ad129b2c7ff2.sentence: Using locks that block processes, 2PL, S2PL, and SS2PL may be subject to deadlocks that result from the mutual blocking of two or more transactions.

fc0116631fba.title: Two-phase locking
fc0116631fba.sentence: To comply with the strict two-phase locking (S2PL) protocol, a transaction needs to comply with 2PL, and release its write (exclusive) locks only after the transaction has ended (i.e., either committed or aborted).

9f34a66e1183.title: Two-phase locking
9f34a66e1183.sentence: Unlike 2PL, S2PL provides strictness (a special case of cascade-less recoverability).

ec5f91742067.title: Two-phase locking
ec5f91742067.sentence: To comply with strong strict two-phase locking (SS2PL), a transaction's read and write locks are released only after that transaction has ended (i.e., either committed or aborted).

2bdfdb4a7b2d.title: Two-phase locking
2bdfdb4a7b2d.sentence: A transaction obeying SS2PL has only a phase 1 and lacks a phase 2 until the transaction has completed.

4e5a81c88cd1.title: Distributed transaction
4e5a81c88cd1.sentence: In practice most commercial database systems use strong strict two-phase locking (SS2PL) for concurrency control, which ensures global serializability, if all the participating databases employ it.

f28ed0f19e88.title: Two-phase locking
f28ed0f19e88.sentence: Conservative two-phase locking (C2PL) differs from 2PL in that transactions obtain all the locks they need before the actual execution begins.

193a1c899a52.title: Two-phase locking
193a1c899a52.sentence: This is to ensure that a transaction that already holds some locks will not block waiting for other locks.

d72f4579dc6c.title: Two-phase locking
d72f4579dc6c.sentence: In cases of heavy lock contention, C2PL reduces the time locks are held on average, relative to 2PL and Strict 2PL, because transactions that hold locks are never blocked.

2d9049ff4232.title: Two-phase locking
2d9049ff4232.sentence: In light lock contention, C2PL holds more locks than is necessary, because it is difficult to predict which locks will be needed in the future, thus leading to higher overhead.

f76cdfc16968.title: Two-phase locking
f76cdfc16968.sentence: Furthermore, each transaction needs to declare its read and write set (the data items that will be read/written), which is not always possible.

34d2128e2081.title: Two-phase locking
34d2128e2081.sentence: Because of these limitations, C2PL is not used very frequently.

c552d8949d44.title: Two-phase commit protocol
c552d8949d44.sentence: The two-phase commit (2PC) protocol should not be confused with the two-phase locking (2PL) protocol, a concurrency control protocol.

2136a7ccfa7d.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
2136a7ccfa7d.sentence: In PostgreSQL, you can request any of the four standard transaction isolation levels, but internally only three distinct isolation levels are implemented, i.e., PostgreSQL's Read Uncommitted mode behaves like Read Committed.

4c17844b9394.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
4c17844b9394.sentence: This is because it is the only sensible way to map the standard isolation levels to PostgreSQL's multiversion concurrency control architecture.

6fae302d5c26.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
6fae302d5c26.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
6fae302d5c26.sentence: Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL.

b4b34bcdd36f.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
b4b34bcdd36f.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
b4b34bcdd36f.sentence: When a transaction uses this isolation level, a SELECT query (without a FOR UPDATE/SHARE clause) sees only data committed before the query began; it never sees either uncommitted data or changes committed by concurrent transactions during the query's execution.

1398b7fc79ee.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
1398b7fc79ee.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
1398b7fc79ee.sentence: Also note that two successive SELECT commands can see different data, even though they are within a single transaction, if other transactions commit changes after the first SELECT starts and before the second SELECT starts.

d5b7c37418ff.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
d5b7c37418ff.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
d5b7c37418ff.sentence: In this case, the would-be updater will wait for the first updating transaction to commit or roll back (if it is still in progress).

45f99d7d4200.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
45f99d7d4200.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
45f99d7d4200.sentence: If the first updater commits, the second updater will ignore the row if the first updater deleted it, otherwise it will attempt to apply its operation to the updated version of the row.

3eaf99184a81.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
3eaf99184a81.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
3eaf99184a81.sentence: The search condition of the command (the WHERE clause) is re-evaluated to see if the updated version of the row still matches the search condition.

8c3ea860c3ef.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
8c3ea860c3ef.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
8c3ea860c3ef.sentence: Because each command is affecting only a predetermined row, letting it see the updated version of the row does not create any troublesome inconsistency.

8293deabb47a.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
8293deabb47a.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
8293deabb47a.sentence: This behavior makes Read Committed mode unsuitable for commands that involve complex search conditions; however, it is just right for simpler cases.

b3dbb03c6c9c.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
b3dbb03c6c9c.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
b3dbb03c6c9c.sentence: Because of the above rules, it is possible for an updating command to see an inconsistent snapshot: it can see the effects of concurrent updating commands on the same rows it is trying to update, but it does not see effects of those commands on other rows in the database.

7855332c61f1.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
7855332c61f1.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.1. Read Committed Isolation Level #
7855332c61f1.sentence: The partial transaction isolation provided by Read Committed mode is adequate for many applications, and this mode is fast and simple to use; however, it is not sufficient for all cases.

41946c15ae59.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
41946c15ae59.section: 13.2. Transaction Isolation # > 13.2.2. Repeatable Read Isolation Level #

1ff1e7baab94.title: Snapshot isolation
1ff1e7baab94.sentence: In databases, and transaction processing (transaction management), snapshot isolation is a guarantee that all reads made in a transaction will see a consistent snapshot of the database (in practice it reads the last committed values that existed at the time it started), and the transaction itself will successfully commit only if no updates it has made conflict with any concurrent updates made since that snapshot.

999e7bab109c.title: Snapshot isolation
999e7bab109c.sentence: A transaction executing under snapshot isolation appears to operate on a personal snapshot of the database, taken at the start of the transaction.

3b4e077cd003.title: Snapshot isolation
3b4e077cd003.sentence: When the transaction concludes, it will successfully commit only if the values updated by the transaction have not been changed externally since the snapshot was taken.

8d1880cf4ce3.title: Snapshot isolation

9ab9f9a61283.title: Snapshot isolation
9ab9f9a61283.sentence: In practice snapshot isolation is implemented within multiversion concurrency control (MVCC), where generational values of each data item (versions) are maintained: MVCC is a common way to increase concurrency and performance by generating a new version of a database object each time the object is written, and allowing transactions' read operations of several last relevant versions (of each object).

5e33a3ec2aaa.title: Snapshot isolation
5e33a3ec2aaa.sentence: Some systems built using multiversion concurrency control (MVCC) may support (only) snapshot isolation to allow transactions to proceed without worrying about concurrent operations, and more importantly without needing to re-verify all read operations when the transaction finally commits.

ff220824cad5.title: Snapshot isolation
ff220824cad5.sentence: The only information that must be stored during the transaction is a list of updates made, which can be scanned for conflicts fairly easily before being committed.

6c5ddbb83036.title: Snapshot isolation
6c5ddbb83036.sentence: Snapshot isolation has been adopted by several major database management systems, such as InterBase, Firebird, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Anywhere, MongoDB and Microsoft SQL Server (2005 and later).

e8c150152c77.title: Snapshot isolation
e8c150152c77.sentence: The main reason for its adoption is that it allows better performance than serializability, yet still avoids most of the concurrency anomalies that serializability avoids (but not all).

e6bba10a2c37.title: Snapshot isolation
e6bba10a2c37.sentence: Snapshot isolation has been used to criticize the ANSI SQL-92 standard's definition of isolation levels, as it exhibits none of the "anomalies" that the SQL standard prohibited, yet is not serializable (the anomaly-free isolation level defined by ANSI).

f4caa1577b4a.title: Snapshot isolation

f5af2a071cb1.title: Snapshot isolation
f5af2a071cb1.sentence: Snapshot isolation is called "serializable" mode in Oracle and PostgreSQL versions prior to 9.1, which may cause confusion with the "real serializability" mode.

8829470babee.title: Snapshot isolation
8829470babee.sentence: In spite of its distinction from serializability, snapshot isolation is sometimes referred to as serializable by Oracle.

c554d0a004a9.title: Snapshot isolation
c554d0a004a9.sentence: There are arguments both for and against this decision; what is clear is that users must be aware of the distinction to avoid possible undesired anomalous behavior in their database system logic.

ed5dd0d08de4.sentence: ANSI SQL-92 [MS, ANSI] defines Isolation Levels in terms of phenomena: Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, and Phantoms.

f61c09a6f1fb.title: paper>10.1145/568271.223785
f61c09a6f1fb.sentence: This paper shows that these phenomena and the ANSI SQL definitions fail to properly characterize several popular isolation levels, including the standard locking implementations of the levels covered.

3183264e6f50.sentence: This level is different from Read Committed in that a query in a repeatable read transaction sees a snapshot as of the start of the first non-transaction-control statement in the transaction, not as of the start of the current statement within the transaction.

4cd6274c539f.title: Isolation (database systems)
4cd6274c539f.sentence: Most DBMSs offer a number of transaction isolation levels, which control the degree of locking that occurs when selecting data.

6d4200c4aa15.title: Isolation (database systems)
6d4200c4aa15.sentence: A serializable execution is defined to be an execution of the operations of concurrently executing SQL-transactions that produces the same effect as some serial execution of those same SQL-transactions.

d114a4a91088.title: Isolation (database systems)
d114a4a91088.sentence: A serial execution is one in which each SQL-transaction executes to completion before the next SQL-transaction begins.

702eed981a16.title: Isolation (database systems)
702eed981a16.sentence: With a lock-based concurrency control DBMS implementation, serializability requires read and write locks (acquired on selected data) to be released at the end of the transaction.

dcbfaa08d3a0.title: Isolation (database systems)
dcbfaa08d3a0.sentence: Also range-locks must be acquired when a SELECT query uses a ranged WHERE clause, especially to avoid the phantom reads phenomenon.

44336198827e.title: Isolation (database systems)
44336198827e.sentence: When using non-lock based concurrency control, no locks are acquired; however, if the system detects a write collision among several concurrent transactions, only one of them is allowed to commit.

25832263b762.title: Isolation (database systems)
25832263b762.sentence: In this isolation level, a lock-based concurrency control DBMS implementation keeps read and write locks (acquired on selected data) until the end of the transaction.

9992374cd098.title: Isolation (database systems)

8e623e3ed147.title: Isolation (database systems)

8574d5bcf9bd.title: Isolation (database systems)

20449bcc78ec.title: Isolation (database systems)

cf2c67fefc24.title: Isolation (database systems)
cf2c67fefc24.sentence: Since each isolation level is stronger than those below, in that no higher isolation level allows an action forbidden by a lower one, the standard permits a DBMS to run a transaction at an isolation level stronger than that requested (e.g., a "Read committed" transaction may actually be performed at a "Repeatable read" isolation level).

dd0d6a5312f4.title: Isolation (database systems)

110c604e9839.title: Isolation (database systems)
110c604e9839.sentence: The ANSI/ISO standard SQL 92 refers to three different read phenomena when a transaction retrieves data that another transaction might have updated.

3d4a3e0de739.title: Isolation (database systems)
3d4a3e0de739.sentence: A dirty read (aka uncommitted dependency) occurs when a transaction retrieves a row that has been updated by another transaction that is not yet committed.

58d7e2ba8d2c.title: Isolation (database systems)
58d7e2ba8d2c.sentence: Now if transaction 2 rolls back its update (already retrieved by transaction 1) or performs other updates, then the view of the row may be wrong in transaction 1.

8785ed478f9f.title: Isolation (database systems)
8785ed478f9f.sentence: A non-repeatable read occurs when a transaction retrieves a row twice and that row is updated by another transaction that is committed in between.

c2b74537cd1a.title: Isolation (database systems)
c2b74537cd1a.sentence: A phantom read occurs when a transaction retrieves a set of rows twice and new rows are inserted into or removed from that set by another transaction that is committed in between.

405221159ebe.title: Isolation (database systems)
405221159ebe.sentence: At the READ UNCOMMITTED isolation level, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the updated row: this is a dirty read.

88bfa772b1c7.title: Isolation (database systems)
88bfa772b1c7.sentence: At the READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, and SERIALIZABLE isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the initial row.

586f75b53ddb.title: Isolation (database systems)
586f75b53ddb.sentence: At the READ UNCOMMITTED and READ COMMITTED isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the updated row: this is a non-repeatable read.

b6105dd58106.title: Isolation (database systems)
b6105dd58106.sentence: At the REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the initial row.

289cce744919.title: Isolation (database systems)
289cce744919.sentence: At the READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, and REPEATABLE READ isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the new set of rows that includes the inserted row: this is a phantom read.

c1bbae8fb366.title: Isolation (database systems)
c1bbae8fb366.sentence: At the SERIALIZABLE isolation level, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the initial set of rows.

7bbbbdbb921c.title: Isolation (database systems)
7bbbbdbb921c.sentence: Write skew is a phenomenon where two writes are allowed to the same column(s) in a table by two different writers (who have previously read the columns they are updating), resulting in the column having data that is a mix of the two transactions.

151693a83aa3.title: Isolation (database systems)
151693a83aa3.sentence: Anomaly serializable is not the same as serializable.

1d7c2d7451aa.title: Isolation (database systems)
1d7c2d7451aa.sentence: That is, it is necessary, but not sufficient that a serializable schedule should be free of all three phenomena types.

d0a5e85e207c.sentence: The result of successfully committing a group of transactions is inconsistent with all possible orderings of running those transactions one at a time.
