47137641db02.sentence: As mentioned above, this is specifically allowed by the standard, which only describes the minimum protections each isolation level must provide.

a5146e7e9fbe.title: Snapshot isolation
a5146e7e9fbe.sentence: In a write skew anomaly, two transactions (T1 and T2) concurrently read an overlapping data set (e.g. values V1 and V2), concurrently make disjoint updates (e.g. T1 updates V1, T2 updates V2), and finally concurrently commit, neither having seen the update performed by the other.

b2c3fc4e3bb6.title: Snapshot isolation
b2c3fc4e3bb6.sentence: Were the system serializable, such an anomaly would be impossible, as either T1 or T2 would have to occur "first", and be visible to the other.

b285bb7dae07.title: Snapshot isolation
b285bb7dae07.sentence: The bank will allow either V1 or V2 to run a deficit, provided the total held in both is never negative (i.e. V1 + V2 ≥ 0).

05803aa24d5b.title: Snapshot isolation
05803aa24d5b.sentence: Phil initiates two transactions concurrently, T1 withdrawing $200 from V1, and T2 withdrawing $200 from V2.

a28f265f4db0.title: Snapshot isolation
a28f265f4db0.sentence: If the database is under snapshot isolation(MVCC), however, T1 and T2 operate on private snapshots of the database: each deducts $200 from an account, and then verifies that the new total is zero, using the other account value that held when the snapshot was taken.

d7151ebb0345.title: Snapshot isolation
d7151ebb0345.sentence: Since neither update conflicts, both commit successfully, leaving V1 = V2 = −$100, and V1 + V2 = −$200.

d58badedeb1a.title: Snapshot isolation
d58badedeb1a.sentence: Potential inconsistency problems arising from write skew anomalies can be fixed by adding (otherwise unnecessary) updates to the transactions in order to enforce the serializability property.

5cc5eed7ceab.title: Snapshot isolation
5cc5eed7ceab.sentence: Add a special conflict table, which both transactions update in order to create a direct write–write conflict.

317b17509c68.title: Snapshot isolation
317b17509c68.sentence: Have one transaction "update" a read-only location (replacing a value with the same value) in order to create a direct write–write conflict (or use an equivalent promotion, e.g. Oracle's SELECT FOR UPDATE).

af416effc0ac.title: Snapshot isolation
af416effc0ac.sentence: For instance, T2 could set V1 = V1, creating an artificial write–write conflict with T1 and, again, preventing the two from succeeding concurrently.

4fa49890060e.title: Snapshot isolation
4fa49890060e.sentence: However, this approach violates the normal form.

121901366811.title: Snapshot isolation
121901366811.sentence: This solution may not always be possible.

d4c979cf9f9b.title: Snapshot isolation
d4c979cf9f9b.sentence: In general, therefore, snapshot isolation puts some of the problem of maintaining non-trivial constraints onto the user, who may not appreciate either the potential pitfalls or the possible solutions.

be9afa4b903d.title: Snapshot isolation
be9afa4b903d.sentence: In 2008, Cahill et al. showed that write-skew anomalies could be prevented by detecting and aborting "dangerous" triplets of concurrent transactions.

e4ee623894b0.title: Snapshot isolation
e4ee623894b0.sentence: This implementation of serializability is well-suited to multiversion concurrency control databases, and has been adopted in PostgreSQL 9.1, where it is known as Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI).

0d1588f8912f.title: Snapshot isolation
0d1588f8912f.sentence: When used consistently, this eliminates the need for the above workarounds.

f9966560ca18.title: Snapshot isolation
f9966560ca18.sentence: The downside over snapshot isolation is an increase in aborted transactions.

a79ec9e49c52.title: Database normalization
a79ec9e49c52.sentence: Database normalization is the process of structuring a relational database in accordance with a series of normal forms to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity.

3973f30ead9c.title: Database normalization
3973f30ead9c.sentence: Normalization entails organizing the columns (attributes) and tables (relations) of a database to ensure that their dependencies are properly enforced by database integrity constraints.

3270eab71131.title: Database normalization
3270eab71131.sentence: It is accomplished by applying some formal rules either by a process of synthesis (creating a new database design) or decomposition (improving an existing database design).

1df109479518.title: Database normalization
1df109479518.sentence: It was first proposed by British computer scientist Edgar F. Codd as part of his relational model.

83737aba88fb.title: Database
83737aba88fb.sentence: The goal of normalization is to ensure that each elementary "fact" is only recorded in one place, so that insertions, updates, and deletions automatically maintain consistency.

a4e3c082aa38.title: Database normalization
a4e3c082aa38.section: Objectives > Minimize redesign when extending the database structure
a4e3c082aa38.sentence: A fully normalized database can be extended to accommodate new types of data with minimal changes to its existing structure.

1f30f71c37b4.title: Database normalization
1f30f71c37b4.section: Objectives > Minimize redesign when extending the database structure
1f30f71c37b4.sentence: As a result, applications interacting with the database are minimally affected.

7a358e66d234.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
7a358e66d234.sentence: Normalization is the process of organizing data in a database.

018d94cee6c1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
018d94cee6c1.section: Normalization > Why do we need normalization?
018d94cee6c1.sentence: The goal of normalization is to eliminate redundant data and ensure data is consistent.

373d8cdb25fe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
373d8cdb25fe.sentence: Indexes are well known when it comes to databases, they are used to improve the speed of data retrieval operations on the data store.

b28325e7e36a.title: Database index
b28325e7e36a.sentence: Indexes are used to quickly locate data without having to search every row in a database table every time said table is accessed.

8696ea884269.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
8696ea884269.sentence: Indexes are used to quickly locate data without having to examine every row in a database table.

596420927382.title: Database index
596420927382.sentence: Indexes can be created using one or more columns of a database table, providing the basis for both rapid random lookups and efficient access of ordered records.

a20777b2703a.title: Database index
a20777b2703a.sentence: An index is a copy of selected columns of data, from a table, that is designed to enable very efficient search.

d216a6eb1e66.title: Database index
d216a6eb1e66.sentence: An index normally includes a "key" or direct link to the original row of data from which it was copied, to allow the complete row to be retrieved efficiently.

50a3cb56c406.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
50a3cb56c406.sentence: An index is a data structure that can be perceived as a table of contents that points us to the location where actual data lives.

df7e11cb30c2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
df7e11cb30c2.sentence: So when we create an index on a column of a table, we store that column and a pointer to the whole row in the index.

585ad3568adb.title: Database index
585ad3568adb.sentence: This means that the number of operations in the average case is O(N) or linear time.

44674dc07cac.title: Database index
44674dc07cac.sentence: Most database software includes indexing technology that enables sub-linear time lookup to improve performance, as linear search is inefficient for large databases.

f37d2ab48278.title: Database index
f37d2ab48278.sentence: Many index designs exhibit logarithmic (O(log(N))) lookup performance and in some applications it is possible to achieve flat (O(1)) performance.

0e9c12b85b00.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
0e9c12b85b00.sentence: An index makes the trade-offs of increased storage overhead, and slower writes (since we not only have to write the data but also have to update the index) for the benefit of faster reads.

2df34c9a1c41.title: Database index
2df34c9a1c41.sentence: There are complex design trade-offs involving lookup performance, index size, and index-update performance.

ed99186b338f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
ed99186b338f.sentence: Indexes are also used to create different views of the same data.

f6c57866c5d0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
f6c57866c5d0.sentence: For large data sets, this is an excellent way to specify different filters or sorting schemes without resorting to creating multiple additional copies of the data.

80479054ab65.title: Database index
80479054ab65.sentence: Some databases extend the power of indexing by letting developers create indexes on column values that have been transformed by functions or expressions.

ffd2bfcdb45f.title: Database index
ffd2bfcdb45f.sentence: For example, an index could be created on upper(last_name), which would only store the upper-case versions of the last_name field in the index.

ac65dcdf0eb3.title: Database index
ac65dcdf0eb3.sentence: Another option sometimes supported is the use of partial index, where index entries are created only for those records that satisfy some conditional expression.

81e20279e29b.title: Database index
81e20279e29b.sentence: An index is typically being accessed concurrently by several transactions and processes, and thus needs concurrency control.

850700d36abc.title: Database index
850700d36abc.sentence: While in principle indexes can utilize the common database concurrency control methods, specialized concurrency control methods for indexes exist, which are applied in conjunction with the common methods for a substantial performance gain.

510d8e06c9da.title: Hash table
510d8e06c9da.sentence: In computer science, a hash table is a data structure that implements an associative array, also called a dictionary or simply map; an associative array is an abstract data type that maps keys to values.

5d2ee65844ef.title: Hash table
5d2ee65844ef.sentence: A hash table uses a hash function to compute an index, also called a hash code, into an array of buckets or slots, from which the desired value can be found.

0b3e7e810bde.title: Hash table
0b3e7e810bde.sentence: During lookup, the key is hashed and the resulting hash indicates where the corresponding value is stored.

cd11392ca340.title: Hash table
cd11392ca340.sentence: In a well-dimensioned hash table, the average time complexity for each lookup is independent of the number of elements stored in the table.

373647dbb897.title: Hash table
373647dbb897.sentence: Time complexity in big O notation Operation Average Worst case Search Θ(1) O(n) Insert Θ(1) O(n) Delete Θ(1) O(n) Space complexity Space Θ(n) O(n)

c600649afc85.title: Hash table
c600649afc85.sentence: Under reasonable assumptions, hash tables have better time complexity bounds on search, delete, and insert operations in comparison to self-balancing binary search trees.

3b7b805a089b.title: Hash table
3b7b805a089b.sentence: Most hash table designs employ an imperfect hash function.

06415d843f78.title: Hash table
06415d843f78.sentence: Hash collisions, where the hash function generates the same index for more than one key, therefore typically must be accommodated in some way.

c8decfcc0e47.title: Hash table
c8decfcc0e47.sentence: Common strategies to handle hash collisions include separate chaining, which stores multiple elements in the same slot using linked lists, and open addressing, which searches for the next available slot according to a probing sequence.

4d09eaf01f3f.title: Hash table
4d09eaf01f3f.section: Hash function > Choosing a hash function
4d09eaf01f3f.sentence: Uniform distribution of the hash values is a fundamental requirement of a hash function.

08611e682b40.title: Hash table
08611e682b40.section: Hash function > Choosing a hash function
08611e682b40.sentence: A non-uniform distribution increases the number of collisions and the cost of resolving them.

5b4cdf7841ad.title: Hash table
5b4cdf7841ad.sentence: The efficiency of a hash table depends on the load factor (α), defined as the ratio of the number of stored elements to the number of available slots, with lower load factors generally yielding faster operations.

86dad5613d60.title: Hash table
86dad5613d60.sentence: The performance of the hash table deteriorates in relation to the load factor α.

d60eee786280.title: Hash table
d60eee786280.sentence: The implementation of a hash table typically ensures that the load factor α remains below a certain constant, αmax.

f2f9cffb05e2.title: Hash table
f2f9cffb05e2.sentence: Therefore, a common approach is to resize or "rehash" the hash table whenever the load factor α reaches αmax.

788721cf72f9.title: Hash table
788721cf72f9.sentence: The items cannot simply be copied over into the same indices since the hash function depends on the table size.

d7680d0e92da.title: Hash table
d7680d0e92da.section: Dynamic resizing > Resizing by moving all entries
d7680d0e92da.sentence: Generally, a new hash table with a size double that of the original hash table gets allocated privately and every item in the original hash table gets moved to the newly allocated one by computing the hash values of the items followed by the insertion operation.

cd8fe9c7726a.title: Hash table
cd8fe9c7726a.section: Dynamic resizing > Resizing by moving all entries
cd8fe9c7726a.sentence: Rehashing is simple, but computationally expensive.

884ed8b80df7.title: Hash table
884ed8b80df7.section: Dynamic resizing > Alternatives to all-at-once rehashing
884ed8b80df7.sentence: Some hash table implementations, notably in real-time systems, cannot pay the price of enlarging the hash table all at once, because it may interrupt time-critical operations.

cc73001c6d87.title: Hash table
cc73001c6d87.sentence: Hashing is an example of a space–time tradeoff.

f8a4cbbac9c4.title: Hash table
f8a4cbbac9c4.sentence: In many situations, hash tables turn out to be on average more efficient than search trees or any other table lookup structure.

1a2f90137ef7.title: Hash table
1a2f90137ef7.sentence: For this reason, they are widely used in many kinds of computer software, particularly for associative arrays, database indexing, caches, and sets.

fb1bfe45215d.title: Hash table
fb1bfe45215d.sentence: Hash tables may also be used as disk-based data structures and database indices (such as in dbm) although B-trees are more popular in these applications.

d305770d726e.title: Hash table
d305770d726e.sentence: Hash tables can be used to implement caches, auxiliary data tables that are used to speed up the access to data that is primarily stored in slower media.

e675f2392f0e.title: Hash table
e675f2392f0e.sentence: Many programming languages provide built-in hash table structures, such as Python’s dictionaries, Java’s HashMap, C++’s unordered_map, and Go maps, which abstract the complexity of hashing from the programmer.

ecc1361df4eb.title: B-tree
ecc1361df4eb.sentence: In computer science, a B-tree is a self-balancing tree data structure that maintains sorted data and allows searches, sequential access, insertions, and deletions in logarithmic time.

ec67188c1681.title: B-tree
ec67188c1681.sentence: The B-tree generalizes the binary search tree, allowing nodes to have more than two children.

92b7ef46d1ce.title: B-tree
92b7ef46d1ce.sentence: By allowing more children under one node than a regular self-balancing binary search tree, the B-tree reduces the height of the tree and puts the data in fewer separate blocks.

bbd97f65ad23.title: B-tree
bbd97f65ad23.sentence: This is especially important for trees stored in secondary storage (e.g., disk drives), as these systems have relatively high latency and work with relatively large blocks of data, hence the B-tree's use in databases and file systems.

f229fd4d07da.title: B-tree
f229fd4d07da.sentence: This remains a major advantage when the tree is stored in memory, as modern computer systems rely heavily on CPU caches.

feb76df8aac7.title: B-tree
feb76df8aac7.sentence: In addition to its use in databases, the B-tree (or § Variants) is also used in filesystems to allow quick random access to an arbitrary block in a particular file.

d27c04d49608.title: B-tree
d27c04d49608.sentence: - Every node has at most m children.

676946fc22cf.title: B-tree
676946fc22cf.sentence: - Every node, except for the root and the leaves, has at least ⌈m/2⌉ children.

955188d8502e.title: B-tree
955188d8502e.sentence: - All leaves appear on the same level.

57279358eb5f.title: B-tree
57279358eb5f.sentence: - A non-leaf node with k children contains k−1 keys.

deee084d0569.title: B-tree
deee084d0569.sentence: The keys of each non-leaf node act as separation values that divide its subtrees.

c27f521db7f9.title: B-tree
c27f521db7f9.sentence: Starting at the root, the tree is recursively traversed from top to bottom.

6ad4f20e9d34.title: B-tree
6ad4f20e9d34.sentence: At each level, the search reduces its field of view to the child pointer (subtree) whose range includes the search value.

821b44ce2987.title: B-tree
821b44ce2987.sentence: Binary search is typically (but not necessarily) used within nodes to find the separation values and child tree of interest.

e041975bff74.title: B-tree
e041975bff74.sentence: Space complexity Space O (n) Time complexity Function Amortized Worst case Search O (log ⁡ n) O (log ⁡ n) Insert O (log ⁡ n) O (log ⁡ n) Delete O (log ⁡ n) O (log ⁡ n)

590f9f72e0db.title: B-tree
590f9f72e0db.section: Informal description > Comparison to other trees
590f9f72e0db.sentence: Because a range of child nodes is permitted, B-trees do not need re-balancing as frequently as other self-balancing search trees, but may waste some space since nodes are not entirely full.

498bb86658bc.title: B-tree
498bb86658bc.sentence: Bayer and McCreight (1972), Comer (1979), and others define the order of a B-tree as the minimum number of keys in a non-root node.

b6db312c03b4.title: B-tree
b6db312c03b4.sentence: Knuth (1998) avoids the problem by defining the order to be the maximum number of children (which is one more than the maximum number of keys).

927f0fb82ba0.title: B-tree
927f0fb82ba0.sentence: Bayer and McCreight's paper Organization and maintenance of large ordered indices was first circulated in July 1970 and later published in Acta Informatica.

3f692dbf24f5.title: Write-ahead logging
3f692dbf24f5.sentence: In computer science, write-ahead logging (WAL) is a family of techniques for providing atomicity and durability (two of the ACID properties) in database systems.

043ba0169ebb.title: Write-ahead logging
043ba0169ebb.sentence: A write ahead log is an append-only auxiliary disk-resident structure used for crash and transaction recovery.

6cabfcfd08a9.title: Write-ahead logging
6cabfcfd08a9.sentence: The changes are first recorded in the log, which must be written to stable storage, before the changes are written to the database.

cc7d9ebd5bf4.title: Write-ahead logging
cc7d9ebd5bf4.sentence: Every operation that modifies the database state has to be logged on disk before the contents on the associated pages can be modified

dc60eb358859.title: Write-ahead logging
dc60eb358859.sentence: - Allow the page cache to buffer updates to disk-resident pages while ensuring durability semantics in the larger context of a database system.

1237444a2f95.title: Write-ahead logging
1237444a2f95.sentence: If a write-ahead log is used, the program can check this log and compare what it was supposed to be doing when it unexpectedly lost power to what was actually done.

c602307fc24f.title: Write-ahead logging
c602307fc24f.sentence: Upon restart, that program might need to know whether the operation it was performing succeeded, succeeded partially, or failed.

a03b11e4d274.title: Write-ahead logging
a03b11e4d274.sentence: On the basis of this comparison, the program could decide to undo what it had started, complete what it had started, or keep things as they are.

e76672f22cb4.title: Write-ahead logging
e76672f22cb4.sentence: Usually both redo and undo information is stored in the log.

77f0a0c9fde9.title: Write-ahead logging
77f0a0c9fde9.sentence: After a certain number of operations, the program should perform a checkpoint, writing all the changes specified in the WAL to the database and clearing the log.

ef4b0bb42c06.title: Write-ahead logging
ef4b0bb42c06.sentence: WAL allows updates of a database to be done in-place.

42f41e3a53f9.title: Write-ahead logging
42f41e3a53f9.sentence: The main advantage of doing updates in-place is that it reduces the need to modify indexes and block lists.

9ef644aa1508.title: Write-ahead logging
9ef644aa1508.sentence: Another way to implement atomic updates is with shadow paging, which is not in-place.

1c86c823c1ce.title: Write-ahead logging
1c86c823c1ce.sentence: Modern file systems typically use a variant of WAL for at least file system metadata; this is called journaling.

e5b6942905e3.title: paper>10.1145/128765.128770
e5b6942905e3.sentence: ARIES is applicable not only to database management systems but also to persistent object-oriented languages, recoverable file systems and transaction-based operating systems.

1ae07c137adb.title: paper>10.1145/128765.128770
1ae07c137adb.sentence: ARIES has been implemented, to varying degrees, in IBM's OS/2 TM Extended Edition Database Manager, DB2, Workstation Data Save Facility/VM, Starburst and QuickSilver, and in the University of Wisconsin's EXODUS and Gamma database machine.

47617d086181.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
47617d086181.sentence: Briefly, WAL's central concept is that changes to data files (where tables and indexes reside) must be written only after those changes have been logged, that is, after WAL records describing the changes have been flushed to permanent storage.

ab0c67a8479b.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
ab0c67a8479b.sentence: If we follow this procedure, we do not need to flush data pages to disk on every transaction commit, because we know that in the event of a crash we will be able to recover the database using the log: any changes that have not been applied to the data pages can be redone from the WAL records.

b91799b43a40.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
b91799b43a40.sentence: (This is roll-forward recovery, also known as REDO.)

1c72cb011394.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
1c72cb011394.sentence: Using WAL results in a significantly reduced number of disk writes, because only the WAL file needs to be flushed to disk to guarantee that a transaction is committed, rather than every data file changed by the transaction.

8bdf2607cc39.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
8bdf2607cc39.sentence: The WAL file is written sequentially, and so the cost of syncing the WAL is much less than the cost of flushing the data pages.

4647c715b0f8.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
4647c715b0f8.sentence: Furthermore, when the server is processing many small concurrent transactions, one fsync of the WAL file may suffice to commit many transactions.

fb6f33d3fb7a.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
fb6f33d3fb7a.sentence: WAL also makes it possible to support on-line backup and point-in-time recovery, as described in Section 25.3.

8b18f6b85875.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
8b18f6b85875.sentence: By archiving the WAL data we can support reverting to any time instant covered by the available WAL data: we simply install a prior physical backup of the database, and replay the WAL just as far as the desired time.

9915a7b6f3d5.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-intro.html
9915a7b6f3d5.sentence: What's more, the physical backup doesn't have to be an instantaneous snapshot of the database state — if it is made over some period of time, then replaying the WAL for that period will fix any internal inconsistencies.

5692058adc56.title: Database
5692058adc56.sentence: Putting data into permanent storage is generally the responsibility of the database engine a.k.a.

62752016dd56.title: Database
62752016dd56.sentence: Various low-level database storage structures are used by the storage engine to serialize the data model so it can be written to the medium of choice.

5ee5d7210948.title: Database
5ee5d7210948.sentence: Techniques such as indexing may be used to improve performance.

8a9274cc88e7.title: Database
8a9274cc88e7.sentence: Data typically reside in the storage in structures that look completely different from the way the data look at the conceptual and external levels, but in ways that attempt to optimize (the best possible) these levels' reconstruction when needed by users and programs, as well as for computing additional types of needed information from the data (e.g., when querying the database).

83dfa491877e.title: Database
83dfa491877e.sentence: Though typically accessed by a DBMS through the underlying operating system (and often using the operating systems' file systems as intermediates for storage layout), storage properties and configuration settings are extremely important for the efficient operation of the DBMS, and thus are closely maintained by database administrators.

2aea1fbf6873.title: Database
2aea1fbf6873.sentence: Conventional storage is row-oriented, but there are also column-oriented and correlation databases.

ee82b2af8dad.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/b-tree-vs.md
ee82b2af8dad.sentence: B-Tree is the most widely used indexing data structure in almost all relational databases.

558a8701189c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/b-tree-vs.md
558a8701189c.sentence: LSM-Tree (Log-Structured Merge Tree) is widely used by many NoSQL databases, such as Cassandra, LevelDB, and RocksDB.

4009b995d50f.title: Inverted index
4009b995d50f.sentence: In information science, an inverted index (also referred to as a postings list, postings file, or inverted file) is a database index storing a mapping from content, such as words or numbers, to its locations in a table, or in a document or a set of documents (named in contrast to a forward index, which maps from documents to content).

83fd54f73c70.title: Inverted index
83fd54f73c70.sentence: The purpose of an inverted index is to allow fast full-text searches, at a cost of increased processing when a document is added to the database.

73d865c10647.title: Inverted index
73d865c10647.sentence: It is the most popular data structure used in document retrieval systems, used on a large scale for example in search engines.

4f7982b7e850.title: Inverted index
4f7982b7e850.sentence: The inverted index data structure is a central component of a typical search engine indexing algorithm.

0dc6706c9d06.title: Inverted index
0dc6706c9d06.sentence: Once a forward index is developed, which stores lists of words per document, it is next inverted to develop an inverted index.

0447704a71d5.title: Inverted index
0447704a71d5.sentence: Instead of listing the words per document in the forward index, the inverted index data structure is developed which lists the documents per word.

24b6ea38088e.title: Inverted index
24b6ea38088e.sentence: Querying the forward index would require sequential iteration through each document and to each word to verify a matching document.

e8d6983f61fa.title: Inverted index
e8d6983f61fa.sentence: The time, memory, and processing resources to perform such a query are not always technically realistic.

45bf1fb22d91.title: Inverted index
45bf1fb22d91.sentence: With the inverted index created, the query can be resolved by jumping to the word ID (via random access) in the inverted index.

a64efd595683.title: Inverted index
a64efd595683.sentence: There are two main variants of inverted indexes: A record-level inverted index (or inverted file index or just inverted file) contains a list of references to documents for each word.

53ae3e4e4611.title: Inverted index
53ae3e4e4611.sentence: A word-level inverted index (or full inverted index or inverted list) additionally contains the positions of each word within a document.

890aaa1a3a44.title: Inverted index
890aaa1a3a44.sentence: The latter form offers more functionality (like phrase searches), but needs more processing power and space to be created.

11a552178a3a.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
11a552178a3a.sentence: GIN indexes are “inverted indexes” which are appropriate for data values that contain multiple component values, such as arrays.

5c50371676d7.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
5c50371676d7.sentence: An inverted index contains a separate entry for each component value, and can efficiently handle queries that test for the presence of specific component values.

c1d510fc747a.title: Search engine indexing
c1d510fc747a.sentence: Many search engines incorporate an inverted index when evaluating a search query to quickly locate documents containing the words in a query and then rank these documents by relevance.

34bcc8c6cbb6.title: Search engine indexing
34bcc8c6cbb6.sentence: Because the inverted index stores a list of the documents containing each word, the search engine can use direct access to find the documents associated with each word in the query in order to retrieve the matching documents quickly.

4efebd55480d.title: Search engine indexing
4efebd55480d.sentence: This index can only determine whether a word exists within a particular document, since it stores no information regarding the frequency and position of the word; it is therefore considered to be a Boolean index.

83e173cdf0b5.title: Search engine indexing
83e173cdf0b5.sentence: Such an index determines which documents match a query but does not rank matched documents.

40cf1915744c.title: Search engine indexing
40cf1915744c.sentence: In some designs the index includes additional information such as the frequency of each word in each document or the positions of a word in each document.

277cc186c0c2.title: Search engine indexing
277cc186c0c2.sentence: Position information enables the search algorithm to identify word proximity to support searching for phrases; frequency can be used to help in ranking the relevance of documents to the query.

73cd741b5266.title: Search engine indexing
73cd741b5266.section: Indexing > Inverted indices > Implementation of Phrase Search Using an Inverted Index
73cd741b5266.sentence: For phrase searching, a specialized form of an inverted index called a positional index is used.

79e20ccaaba8.title: Search engine indexing
79e20ccaaba8.section: Indexing > Inverted indices > Implementation of Phrase Search Using an Inverted Index
79e20ccaaba8.sentence: A positional index not only stores the ID of the document containing the token but also the exact position(s) of the token within the document in the postings list.

9dfab8b789bc.title: Search engine indexing
9dfab8b789bc.section: Indexing > Inverted indices > Implementation of Phrase Search Using an Inverted Index
9dfab8b789bc.sentence: The occurrences of the phrase specified in the query are retrieved by navigating these postings list and identifying the indexes at which the desired terms occur in the expected order (the same as the order in the phrase).

c5c12f52cfdf.title: Search engine indexing
c5c12f52cfdf.section: Indexing > Inverted indices > Implementation of Phrase Search Using an Inverted Index
c5c12f52cfdf.sentence: The postings lists can be navigated using a binary search in order to minimize the time complexity of this procedure.

5a72ee7d265f.title: R-tree
5a72ee7d265f.sentence: R-trees are tree data structures used for spatial access methods, i.e., for indexing multi-dimensional information such as geographical coordinates, rectangles or polygons.

38a81258cbe3.title: R-tree
38a81258cbe3.sentence: The key idea of the data structure is to group nearby objects and represent them with their minimum bounding rectangle in the next higher level of the tree; the "R" in R-tree is for rectangle.

39d210231f06.title: R-tree
39d210231f06.sentence: Since all objects lie within this bounding rectangle, a query that does not intersect the bounding rectangle also cannot intersect any of the contained objects.

053fea1fe231.title: R-tree
053fea1fe231.sentence: Similar to the B-tree, the R-tree is also a balanced search tree (so all leaf nodes are at the same depth), organizes the data in pages, and is designed for storage on disk (as used in databases).

1fc7963f15ca.title: R-tree
1fc7963f15ca.sentence: Each page can contain a maximum number of entries, often denoted as M. It also guarantees a minimum fill (except for the root node), however best performance has been experienced with a minimum fill of 30%–40% of the maximum number of entries (B-trees guarantee 50% page fill, and B*-trees even 66%).

31cb32288a9c.title: R-tree
31cb32288a9c.sentence: For every rectangle in a node, it has to be decided if it overlaps the search rectangle or not.

7cac3c0a6c85.title: R-tree
7cac3c0a6c85.sentence: If yes, the corresponding child node has to be searched also.

427f04558fac.title: R-tree
427f04558fac.sentence: In this way, most of the nodes in the tree are never read during a search.

d52eff68f8f1.title: R-tree
d52eff68f8f1.sentence: In this structure, the internal nodes serve as an initial filter by quickly excluding regions of space that do not intersect the query, while the leaf nodes provide a refined, precise evaluation by storing the actual spatial objects.

b3c5d3a54faa.title: R-tree
b3c5d3a54faa.sentence: A common real-world usage for an R-tree might be to store spatial objects such as restaurant locations or the polygons that typical maps are made of: streets, buildings, outlines of lakes, coastlines, etc. and then find answers quickly to queries such as "Find all museums within 2 km of my current location", "retrieve all road segments within 2 km of my location" (to display them in a navigation system) or "find the nearest gas station" (although not taking roads into account).

5d09a6db3f2c.title: R-tree
5d09a6db3f2c.sentence: Until the queue is empty or the desired number of results have been returned the search continues by processing the nearest entry in the queue.

0f492d79d342.title: R-tree
0f492d79d342.sentence: Tree nodes are expanded and their children reinserted.

13ad9b5a9f25.title: R-tree
13ad9b5a9f25.sentence: At each step, all rectangles in the current directory node are examined, and a candidate is chosen using a heuristic such as choosing the rectangle which requires least enlargement.

f35525e24093.title: R-tree
f35525e24093.sentence: If the leaf node is full, it must be split before the insertion is made.

deff41b323fc.title: R-tree
deff41b323fc.sentence: Again, since an exhaustive search is too expensive, a heuristic is employed to split the node into two.

b070d46b8c0d.title: R-tree
b070d46b8c0d.section: Algorithm > Insertion > Splitting an overflowing node
b070d46b8c0d.sentence: In the classic R-tree, Guttman proposed two such heuristics, called QuadraticSplit and LinearSplit.

5b6719220297.title: R-tree
5b6719220297.sentence: Adding the newly created node to the previous level, this level can again overflow, and these overflows can propagate up to the root node; when this node also overflows, a new root node is created and the tree has increased in height.

a9fc00f34bf5.title: R-tree
a9fc00f34bf5.sentence: The key difficulty of R-tree is to build an efficient tree that on one hand is balanced (so the leaf nodes are at the same height) on the other hand the rectangles do not cover too much empty space and do not overlap too much (so that during search, fewer subtrees need to be processed).

7a26647ab828.title: R-tree
7a26647ab828.sentence: R-trees do not guarantee good worst-case performance, but generally perform well with real-world data.

871e45f22431.title: R-tree
871e45f22431.section: Algorithm > Insertion > Choosing the insertion subtree
871e45f22431.sentence: The decreased overlap of rectangles in the R*-tree is one of the key benefits over the traditional R-tree.

cd298579c795.title: R-tree
cd298579c795.section: Algorithm > Insertion > Splitting an overflowing node
cd298579c795.sentence: In addition to having a more advanced splitting heuristic, the R*-tree also tries to avoid splitting a node by reinserting some of the node members, which is similar to the way a B-tree balances overflowing nodes.

619ab804a8c8.title: R-tree
619ab804a8c8.section: Algorithm > Insertion > Splitting an overflowing node
619ab804a8c8.sentence: This was shown to also reduce overlap and thus increase tree performance.

df7dcbcd87b3.title: R-tree
df7dcbcd87b3.sentence: Most of the research and improvements for R-trees aims at improving the way the tree is built and can be grouped into two objectives: building an efficient tree from scratch (known as bulk-loading) and performing changes on an existing tree (insertion and deletion).

31afdb710f5e.title: R-tree
31afdb710f5e.sentence: - Sort-Tile-Recursive (STR): Another variation of Nearest-X, that estimates the total number of leaves required as l=⌈number of objects/capacity⌉, the required split factor in each dimension to achieve this as s=⌈l1/d⌉, then repeatedly splits each dimensions successively into s equal sized partitions using 1-dimensional sorting.

58a26d06213c.title: R-tree
58a26d06213c.sentence: Instead, the page will be dissolved and all its children (which may be subtrees, not only leaf objects) will be reinserted.

448b1d4aa853.title: Database normalization
448b1d4aa853.sentence: When an attempt is made to modify (update, insert into, or delete from) a relation, the following undesirable side effects may arise in relations that have not been sufficiently normalized:

2e763ac47d86.title: Database normalization
2e763ac47d86.sentence: > To free the collection of relations from undesirable insertion, update and deletion dependencies.

16c96e0bcd6d.title: Database normalization
16c96e0bcd6d.sentence: To reduce the need for restructuring the collection of relations, as new types of data are introduced, and thus increase the life span of application programs.

7f4763582e6c.title: Database normalization
7f4763582e6c.sentence: There are circumstances in which certain facts cannot be recorded at all.

0784b9f18f36.title: Database normalization
0784b9f18f36.sentence: Therefore, the details of any faculty member who teaches at least one course can be recorded, but a newly hired faculty member who has not yet been assigned to teach any courses cannot be recorded, except by setting the Course Code to null.

e51f8b467555.title: Database normalization
e51f8b467555.sentence: The same information can be expressed on multiple rows; therefore updates to the relation may result in logical inconsistencies.

61b11c6a333c.title: Database normalization
61b11c6a333c.sentence: For example, each record in an "Employees' Skills" relation might contain an Employee ID, Employee Address, and Skill; thus a change of address for a particular employee may need to be applied to multiple records (one for each skill).

28f5f1dff343.title: Database normalization
28f5f1dff343.sentence: If the update is only partially successful – the employee's address is updated on some records but not others – then the relation is left in an inconsistent state.

fe325b97639e.title: Database normalization
fe325b97639e.sentence: Under certain circumstances, the deletion of data representing certain facts necessitates the deletion of data representing completely different facts.

356e8e483a4c.title: Database normalization
356e8e483a4c.sentence: The "Faculty and Their Courses" relation described in the previous example suffers from this type of anomaly, for if a faculty member temporarily ceases to be assigned to any courses, the last of the records on which that faculty member appears must be deleted, effectively also deleting the faculty member, unless the Course Code field is set to null.

05e608627725.title: Database normalization
05e608627725.sentence: Most 3NF relations are free of insertion, updation, and deletion anomalies.

84c7aeb7d050.title: B-tree
84c7aeb7d050.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
84c7aeb7d050.sentence: A B-tree index creates a multi-level tree structure that breaks a database down into fixed-size blocks or pages.

e2dd8b2c0074.title: B-tree
e2dd8b2c0074.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
e2dd8b2c0074.sentence: Each level of this tree can be used to link those pages via an address location, allowing one page (known as a node, or internal page) to refer to another with leaf pages at the lowest level.

c3fbc7e24db6.title: B-tree
c3fbc7e24db6.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
c3fbc7e24db6.sentence: This blocking is the core idea behind the creation of the B-tree, where disk blocks form a hierarchy of levels to make up the index.

1f4ad7abc88a.title: B-tree
1f4ad7abc88a.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
1f4ad7abc88a.sentence: Most pages in this structure will be leaf pages which refer to specific table rows.

f9d912d5df95.title: B-tree
f9d912d5df95.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
f9d912d5df95.sentence: Because each node (or internal page) can have more than two children, a B-tree index will usually have a shorter height (the distance from the root to the farthest leaf) than a Binary Search Tree.

8b6fde1b28c6.title: B-tree
8b6fde1b28c6.section: B-tree usage in databases > Sorted file search time
8b6fde1b28c6.sentence: The time required to read a record on a disk drive far exceeds the time needed to compare keys once the record is available due to seek time and rotational delay.

c5d2ee02a82f.title: B-tree
c5d2ee02a82f.section: B-tree usage in databases > Sorted file search time
c5d2ee02a82f.sentence: For simplicity, assume reading from disk takes about 10 milliseconds.

5d0bcb4cd7a3.title: B-tree
5d0bcb4cd7a3.section: B-tree usage in databases > Sorted file search time
5d0bcb4cd7a3.sentence: The time required to locate one record out of a million in the example above would be 20 disk reads, each taking 10 milliseconds, which equals 0.2 seconds.

1b34b84b2206.title: B-tree
1b34b84b2206.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
1b34b84b2206.sentence: That can be improved by creating an auxiliary index that contains the first record in each disk block (sometimes called a sparse index).

a2bf259d3148.title: B-tree
a2bf259d3148.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
a2bf259d3148.sentence: This auxiliary index would be 1% of the size of the original database, but it can be searched quickly.

c0c99a5f1dd8.title: B-tree
c0c99a5f1dd8.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
c0c99a5f1dd8.sentence: Finding an entry in the auxiliary index would tell us which block to search in the main database; after searching the auxiliary index, we would have to search only that one block of the main database—at a cost of one more disk read.

72c67c6de8fa.title: B-tree
72c67c6de8fa.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
72c67c6de8fa.sentence: That would create an aux-aux index that would need only 100 entries and would fit in one disk block.

6d1ad20139bd.title: B-tree
6d1ad20139bd.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
6d1ad20139bd.sentence: Instead of reading 14 disk blocks to find the desired record, we only need to read 3 blocks.

802fea1cf7b8.title: B-tree
802fea1cf7b8.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
802fea1cf7b8.sentence: Instead of 150 milliseconds, we need only 30 milliseconds to get the record.

0496b1617d27.title: B-tree
0496b1617d27.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
0496b1617d27.sentence: Reading and searching the first (and only) block of the aux-aux index, which is the root of the tree, identifies the relevant block in aux-index in the level below.

3f6bd987bc53.title: B-tree
3f6bd987bc53.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
3f6bd987bc53.sentence: Reading and searching that aux-index block identifies the relevant block to read until the final level, known as the leaf level, identifies a record in the main database.

00f760e1a33a.title: B-tree
00f760e1a33a.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
00f760e1a33a.sentence: The auxiliary indices have turned the search problem from a binary search requiring roughly log2 N disk reads to one requiring only logb N disk reads where b is the blocking factor (the number of entries per block: b = 100 entries per block in our example; log100 1,000,000 = 3 reads).

118555a11e51.title: B-tree
118555a11e51.section: B-tree usage in databases > Usage in databases
118555a11e51.sentence: - keeps keys in sorted order for sequential traversing

682dad0abedf.title: B-tree
682dad0abedf.section: B-tree usage in databases > Usage in databases
682dad0abedf.sentence: - uses a hierarchical index to minimize the number of disk reads

cd4cfdba4d89.title: B-tree
cd4cfdba4d89.section: B-tree usage in databases > Usage in databases
cd4cfdba4d89.sentence: - uses partially full blocks to speed up insertions and deletions

83be3991d809.title: B-tree
83be3991d809.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
83be3991d809.sentence: The B-tree remains the standard index implementation in almost all relational databases, and many nonrelational databases use it as well.

d86fc697e99e.title: B-tree
d86fc697e99e.section: B-tree usage in databases > Index performance
d86fc697e99e.sentence: In practice, if the main database is being frequently searched, the aux-aux index and much of the aux index may reside in a disk cache, so they would not incur a disk read.

9f05f288a556.title: B-tree
9f05f288a556.sentence: The general class includes variations such as the B+ tree, the B* tree and the B*+ tree.

08d3dfe13b31.title: B-tree
08d3dfe13b31.sentence: - In the B+ tree, the internal nodes do not store any pointers to records; thus all pointers to records are stored in the leaf nodes.

815202523ce8.title: B-tree
815202523ce8.sentence: - The B* tree balances more neighboring internal nodes to keep the internal nodes more densely packed.

03d24f8e89cb.title: B+ tree
03d24f8e89cb.sentence: A B+ tree can be viewed as a B-tree in which each node contains only keys (not key–value pairs), and to which an additional level is added at the bottom with linked leaves.

745d5d39edef.title: B+ tree
745d5d39edef.sentence: A B+ tree consists of a root, internal nodes, and leaves.

26d4f3799b75.title: B+ tree
26d4f3799b75.sentence: - All leaf nodes have the same number of ancestors (i.e., they are all at the same depth).

c2c077dc36b2.title: B-tree
c2c077dc36b2.sentence: Because B+ tree internal nodes have fewer pointers, each node can hold more keys, causing the tree to be shallower and thus faster to search.

ade7eb9c47b5.title: B+ tree
ade7eb9c47b5.sentence: This is primarily because unlike binary search trees, B+ trees have very high fanout (number of pointers to child nodes in a node, typically on the order of 100 or more), which reduces the number of I/O operations required to find an element in the tree.

b38c370a7199.title: B+ tree
b38c370a7199.sentence: This means that starting from the root, we are looking for the leaf which may contain the value k.

7c1bb108b987.title: B+ tree
7c1bb108b987.sentence: Because we only traverse one branch of all the children at each rung of the tree, we achieve O(log⁡N) runtime, where N is the total number of keys stored in the leaves of the B+ tree.

df9aa604e022.title: B+ tree
df9aa604e022.sentence: The leaves (the bottom-most index blocks) of the B+ tree are often linked to one another in a linked list; this makes range queries or an (ordered) iteration through the blocks simpler and more efficient (though the aforementioned upper bound can be achieved even without this addition).

dc9905cf157c.title: B+ tree
dc9905cf157c.sentence: This illustrates one of the significant advantages of a B+tree over a B-tree; in a B-tree, since not all keys are present in the leaves, such an ordered linked list cannot be constructed.

baa834b328e4.title: B-tree
baa834b328e4.sentence: In addition, a leaf node may include a pointer to the next leaf node to speed up sequential access.

e839a2c4647d.title: B+ tree
e839a2c4647d.sentence: However, it is quite expensive, because each entry requires us to start from the root and go down to the appropriate leaf page.

853178b5716b.title: B+ tree
853178b5716b.sentence: An efficient alternative is to use bulk-loading.

1674270902b8.title: B+ tree
1674270902b8.sentence: - The first step is to sort the data entries according to a search key in ascending order.

1c64874c7bbc.title: B+ tree
1c64874c7bbc.sentence: Relational database management systems such as IBM Db2, Informix, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle 8, Sybase ASE, and SQLite support this type of tree for table indices, though each such system implements the basic B+ tree structure with variations and extensions.

b33fd9a7e6c7.title: B+ tree
b33fd9a7e6c7.sentence: NTFS uses B+ trees for directory and security-related metadata indexing.

461589537e88.title: B+ tree
461589537e88.sentence: The ReiserFS, NSS, XFS, JFS, ReFS, and BFS filesystems all use this type of tree for metadata indexing; BFS also uses B+ trees for storing directories.

621111983b3a.title: paper>10.1145/356770.356776
621111983b3a.sentence: B-trees have become, de facto, a standard for file organization.File indexes of users, dedicated database systems, and general-purpose access methods have all been proposed and nnplemented using B-trees This paper reviews B-trees and shows why they have been so successful It discusses the major variations of the B-tree, especially the B+-tree, contrasting the relatwe merits and costs of each implementatmn.It illustrates a general purpose access method whmh uses a B-tree.

a58550b595f3.title: B-tree
a58550b595f3.sentence: This variant ensures non-root nodes are at least 2/3 full instead of 1/2.

a59179f35506.title: B-tree
a59179f35506.sentence: As the most costly part of the operation of inserting the node in a B-tree is splitting the node, B*-trees are created to postpone the splitting operation as long as they can.

652124def392.title: B-tree
652124def392.sentence: To maintain this, instead of immediately splitting up a node when it gets full, its keys are shared with a node next to it.

bb3f6ea70a1d.title: B-tree
bb3f6ea70a1d.sentence: This spill operation is less costly to do than split because it requires only shifting the keys between existing nodes, not allocating memory for a new one.

c140da76fa43.title: Database index
c140da76fa43.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Clustered
c140da76fa43.sentence: Clustering alters the data block into a certain distinct order to match the index, resulting in the row data being stored in order.

b29fbbb356d6.title: Database index
b29fbbb356d6.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Non-clustered
b29fbbb356d6.sentence: The non-clustered index tree contains the index keys in sorted order, with the leaf level of the index containing the pointer to the record (page and the row number in the data page in page-organized engines; row offset in file-organized engines).

1e750a4e0abb.title: Database index
1e750a4e0abb.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Clustered
1e750a4e0abb.sentence: Therefore, only one clustered index can be created on a given database table.

e09bf8efd7af.title: Database index
e09bf8efd7af.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Clustered
e09bf8efd7af.sentence: Clustered indexes can greatly increase overall speed of retrieval, but usually only where the data is accessed sequentially in the same or reverse order of the clustered index, or when a range of items is selected.

36bd213c3909.title: Database index
36bd213c3909.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Clustered
36bd213c3909.sentence: Since the physical records are in this sort order on disk, the next row item in the sequence is immediately before or after the last one, and so fewer data block reads are required.

ddb09409984b.title: Database index
ddb09409984b.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Non-clustered
ddb09409984b.sentence: - The physical order of the rows is not the same as the index order.

9a69a08c3cbb.title: Database index
9a69a08c3cbb.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Non-clustered
9a69a08c3cbb.sentence: There can be more than one non-clustered index on a database table.

5116cdb20c0a.title: Database index
5116cdb20c0a.section: Index architecture and indexing methods > Non-clustered
5116cdb20c0a.sentence: - The indexed columns are typically non-primary key columns used in JOIN, WHERE, and ORDER BY clauses.

9d58ee7c195a.title: Database index
9d58ee7c195a.sentence: In Microsoft SQL Server, the leaf node of the clustered index corresponds to the actual data, not simply a pointer to data that resides elsewhere, as is the case with a non-clustered index.

ef99ef99e458.title: Log-structured merge-tree
ef99ef99e458.sentence: In computer science, the log-structured merge-tree (also known as LSM tree, or LSMT) is a data structure with performance characteristics that make it attractive for providing indexed access to files with high insert volume, such as transactional log data.

e757e9ac98aa.title: Log-structured merge-tree
e757e9ac98aa.sentence: LSM trees, like other search trees, maintain key-value pairs.

152ca29ccec0.title: Log-structured merge-tree
152ca29ccec0.sentence: LSM trees maintain data in two or more separate structures, each of which is optimized for its respective underlying storage medium; data is synchronized between the two structures efficiently, in batches.

2d3a1afde553.title: Log-structured merge-tree
2d3a1afde553.sentence: As described by Patrick O'Neil, a two-level LSM tree comprises two tree-like structures, called C0 and C1.

47a3545a1991.title: Log-structured merge-tree
47a3545a1991.sentence: C0 is smaller and entirely resident in memory, whereas C1 is resident on disk.

cb2b392f6c59.title: Log-structured merge-tree
cb2b392f6c59.sentence: New records are inserted into the memory-resident C0 component.

41c76ca0e0a8.title: Log-structured merge-tree
41c76ca0e0a8.sentence: If the insertion causes the C0 component to exceed a certain size threshold, a contiguous segment of entries is removed from C0 and merged into C1 on disk.

ae2f11fdf4ac.title: Log-structured merge-tree
ae2f11fdf4ac.sentence: The performance characteristics of LSM trees stem from the fact that each component is tuned to the characteristics of its underlying storage medium, and that data is efficiently migrated across media in rolling batches, using an algorithm reminiscent of merge sort.

72fe74a97f81.title: Log-structured merge-tree
72fe74a97f81.sentence: Such tuning involves writing data in a sequential manner as opposed to as a series of separate random access requests.

c7b51e9521c9.title: Log-structured merge-tree
c7b51e9521c9.sentence: This optimization reduces total seek time in hard-disk drives (HDDs) and latency in solid-state drives (SSDs).

089296061f60.title: Log-structured merge-tree
089296061f60.sentence: Most LSM trees used in practice employ multiple levels.

e6df7eb4952b.title: Log-structured merge-tree
e6df7eb4952b.sentence: Level 0 is kept in main memory, and might be represented using a tree.

2b5429db9ddf.title: Log-structured merge-tree
2b5429db9ddf.sentence: The on-disk data is organized into sorted runs of data.

b2e7df276b63.title: Log-structured merge-tree
b2e7df276b63.sentence: Each run contains data sorted by the index key.

6c98b9518760.title: Log-structured merge-tree
6c98b9518760.sentence: To perform a query on a particular key to get its associated value, one must search in the Level 0 tree and also each run.

3808dcbe7da0.title: Log-structured merge-tree
3808dcbe7da0.sentence: In order to keep down the cost of queries, the system must avoid a situation where there are too many runs.

15f994068b38.title: Log-structured merge-tree
15f994068b38.sentence: LSM-tree was originally designed for write-intensive workloads.

574886c70965.title: Log-structured merge-tree
574886c70965.sentence: As increasingly more read and write workloads co-exist under an LSM-tree storage structure, read data accesses can experience high latency and low throughput due to frequent invalidations of cached data in buffer caches by LSM-tree compaction operations.

9b88f5e2cf93.title: Apache Cassandra
9b88f5e2cf93.sentence: Cassandra uses a Log Structured Merge Tree (LSM tree) index to optimize write throughput, in contrast to the B-tree indexes used by most databases.

72cdc6bacc9f.title: Denormalization
72cdc6bacc9f.sentence: Denormalization is a strategy used on a previously-normalized database to increase performance.

9465a81c9c50.title: Denormalization
9465a81c9c50.sentence: In computing, denormalization is the process of trying to improve the read performance of a database, at the expense of losing some write performance, by adding redundant copies of data or by grouping data.

8c028a23bc51.title: Denormalization
8c028a23bc51.sentence: It is often motivated by performance or scalability in relational database software needing to carry out very large numbers of read operations.

8f3aaef4b7b8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
8f3aaef4b7b8.sentence: It attempts to improve read performance at the expense of some write performance.

3db47cabe74a.title: Denormalization
3db47cabe74a.sentence: If these relations are stored physically as separate disk files, completing a database query that draws information from several relations (a join operation) can be slow.

5c33b3c92f98.title: Denormalization
5c33b3c92f98.sentence: If many relations are joined, it may be prohibitively slow.

e6041833aa5e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
e6041833aa5e.sentence: Once data becomes distributed with techniques such as federation and sharding, managing joins across the network further increases complexity.

0f0fc6bcd536.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
0f0fc6bcd536.sentence: Denormalization might circumvent the need for such complex joins.

2a2816caa403.title: Denormalization
2a2816caa403.sentence: There are two strategies for dealing with this by denormalization:

16bb118da55b.title: Denormalization
16bb118da55b.sentence: - "DBMS support": The database management system stores redundant copies in the background, which are kept consistent by the DBMS software

ca55730de4df.title: Denormalization
ca55730de4df.sentence: - "DBA implementation": The database administrator (or designer) design around the problem by denormalizing the logical data design

9f4bbc5a9d52.title: Denormalization
9f4bbc5a9d52.sentence: This method is often implemented in SQL as indexed views (Microsoft SQL Server) or materialized views (Oracle, PostgreSQL).

3f899a26ed51.title: Denormalization
3f899a26ed51.sentence: With this approach, database administrators can keep the logical design normalized, but allow the database management system (DBMS) to store additional redundant information on disk to optimize query response.

5e8091371514.title: Denormalization
5e8091371514.sentence: In this case it is the DBMS software's responsibility to ensure that any redundant copies are kept consistent.

a8ebdeec3200.title: Denormalization
a8ebdeec3200.sentence: With care this can achieve a similar improvement in query response, but at a cost — it is now the database designer's responsibility to ensure that the denormalized database does not become inconsistent.

01c22151e115.title: Denormalization
01c22151e115.sentence: This is done by creating rules in the database called constraints, that specify how the redundant copies of information must be kept synchronized, which may easily make the de-normalization procedure pointless.

14e9bad4d553.title: Denormalization
14e9bad4d553.sentence: Moreover, constraints introduce a trade-off, speeding up reads (SELECT in SQL) while slowing down writes (INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE).

2e94de128066.title: Denormalization
2e94de128066.sentence: This means a denormalized database under heavy write load may offer worse performance than its functionally equivalent normalized counterpart.

948843ce7d7a.title: Denormalization
948843ce7d7a.sentence: Denormalization differs from the unnormalized form in that denormalization benefits can only be fully realized on a data model that is otherwise normalized.

12e0c653549c.title: Denormalization
12e0c653549c.sentence: A denormalized data model is not the same as a data model that has not been normalized, and denormalization should only take place after a satisfactory level of normalization has taken place and that any required constraints and/or rules have been created to deal with the inherent anomalies in the design.

6e94ec9ce39e.title: Denormalization
6e94ec9ce39e.sentence: For example, all the relations are in third normal form and any relations with join dependencies and multi-valued dependencies are handled appropriately.

b13d6646d087.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
b13d6646d087.sentence: Note: Denormalization does not mean reversing normalization.

9437d507bad2.title: Denormalization
9437d507bad2.sentence: - "Storing" the count of the "many" elements in a one-to-many relationship as an attribute of the "one" relation

bd6e240f7124.title: Denormalization
bd6e240f7124.sentence: - Adding attributes to a relation from another relation with which it will be joined

3692faac027a.title: Denormalization
3692faac027a.sentence: - Star schemas, which are also known as fact-dimension models and have been extended to snowflake schemas

3151faa58d55.title: Denormalization
3151faa58d55.sentence: With the exception of truly enormous systems, increased storage requirements is considered a relatively small problem in the 2020s.

2d9fc090320b.title: Hash table
2d9fc090320b.sentence: Hence the second part of the algorithm is collision resolution.

e58964410fb1.title: Hash table
e58964410fb1.sentence: The two common methods for collision resolution are separate chaining and open addressing.

721a95097d9c.title: Hash table
721a95097d9c.sentence: In separate chaining, the process involves building a linked list of key–value pairs for each search array index.

08db0e4f3a29.title: Hash table
08db0e4f3a29.sentence: The collided items are chained together through a single linked list, which can be traversed during lookup of a specific key.

a97e873b19cb.title: Hash table
a97e873b19cb.sentence: Open addressing is another collision resolution technique in which every entry record is stored in the bucket array itself, and the hash resolution is performed through probing.

fa6dcf418d60.title: Hash table
fa6dcf418d60.sentence: When a new entry has to be inserted, the buckets are examined, starting with the hashed-to slot and proceeding in some probe sequence, until an unoccupied slot is found.

5fd00baa3473.title: Hash table
5fd00baa3473.sentence: When searching for an entry, the buckets are scanned in the same sequence, until either the target record is found, or an unused array slot is found, which indicates an unsuccessful search.

769fb422575b.title: Hash table
769fb422575b.sentence: - Linear probing, in which the interval between probes is fixed (usually 1).

7d476eb043f6.title: Hash table
7d476eb043f6.sentence: - Quadratic probing, in which the interval between probes is increased by adding the successive outputs of a quadratic polynomial to the value given by the original hash computation.

8920b79a4db9.title: Hash table
8920b79a4db9.sentence: - Double hashing, in which the interval between probes is computed by a secondary hash function.

2485f3b71d48.title: Hash table
2485f3b71d48.section: Overview > Load factor > Load factor for open addressing
2485f3b71d48.sentence: Therefore an open-addressed hash table cannot have a load factor greater than 1.

fbce49471103.title: Hash table
fbce49471103.section: Overview > Load factor > Load factor for open addressing
fbce49471103.sentence: The performance of open addressing becomes very bad when the load factor approaches 1.

51e9cec49142.title: Hash table
51e9cec49142.section: Overview > Load factor > Load factor for open addressing
51e9cec49142.sentence: With open addressing, acceptable figures of max load factor αmax should range around 0.6 to 0.75.

6411e8889954.title: Hash table
6411e8889954.section: Overview > Load factor > Load factor for separate chaining
6411e8889954.sentence: Separate chaining hash tables suffer gradually declining performance as the load factor grows, unlike the sharply decreasing performance of open addressing hash tables around α=1.

5e15d026eed3.title: Hash table
5e15d026eed3.section: Overview > Load factor > Load factor for separate chaining
5e15d026eed3.sentence: With separate chaining, the value of αmax that gives best performance is typically between 1 and 3.

655f53c70b10.title: Hash table
655f53c70b10.section: Collision resolution > Open addressing > Other collision resolution techniques based on open addressing > Cuckoo hashing
655f53c70b10.sentence: Cuckoo hashing is a form of open addressing collision resolution which guarantees O(1) worst-case lookup complexity and constant amortized time for insertions.

19d564683ea4.title: Hash table
19d564683ea4.section: Collision resolution > Open addressing > Other collision resolution techniques based on open addressing > Cuckoo hashing
19d564683ea4.sentence: Collisions are resolved through maintaining two hash tables, each having its own hashing function, and collided slot gets replaced with the given item, and the preoccupied element of the slot gets displaced into the other hash table.

aa96974a278a.title: Hash table
aa96974a278a.section: Collision resolution > Separate chaining > Other data structures for separate chaining
aa96974a278a.sentence: In dynamic perfect hashing, two-level hash tables are used to reduce the look-up complexity to be a guaranteed O(1) in the worst case.

4619f5621695.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/b-tree-vs.md
4619f5621695.sentence: The biggest difference is probably this:

fa5d9f761d02.title: Database index
