875d6a2f04dd.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
875d6a2f04dd.sentence: PostgreSQL provides several index types: B-tree, Hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN, BRIN, and the extension bloom.

7a11405ba81b.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
7a11405ba81b.sentence: Each index type uses a different algorithm that is best suited to different types of indexable clauses.

c903032425bd.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
c903032425bd.sentence: By default, the CREATE INDEX command creates B-tree indexes, which fit the most common situations.

dc975dfc01cc.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
dc975dfc01cc.sentence: The other index types are selected by writing the keyword USING followed by the index type name.

29f52ab835ae.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
29f52ab835ae.sentence: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering.

af21a3806fd8.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
af21a3806fd8.sentence: B-tree indexes can also be used to retrieve data in sorted order.

d7b12c9bf446.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
d7b12c9bf446.sentence: The optimizer can also use a B-tree index for queries involving the pattern matching operators LIKE and ~ if the pattern is a constant and is anchored to the beginning of the string — for example, col LIKE 'foo%' or col ~ '^foo', but not col LIKE '%bar'.

f7b3dec490b8.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
f7b3dec490b8.sentence: Hash indexes store a 32-bit hash code derived from the value of the indexed column.

2fb64943a701.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
2fb64943a701.sentence: Hence, such indexes can only handle simple equality comparisons.

268492b272bf.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
268492b272bf.sentence: GiST indexes are not a single kind of index, but rather an infrastructure within which many different indexing strategies can be implemented.

a29ff779f3b1.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
a29ff779f3b1.sentence: As an example, the standard distribution of PostgreSQL includes GiST operator classes for several two-dimensional geometric data types, which support indexed queries using these operators:

97de6f36cad2.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
97de6f36cad2.sentence: GiST indexes are also capable of optimizing “nearest-neighbor” searches, such as

be0fd16f791a.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
be0fd16f791a.sentence: SP-GiST indexes, like GiST indexes, offer an infrastructure that supports various kinds of searches.

240684dff753.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
240684dff753.sentence: SP-GiST permits implementation of a wide range of different non-balanced disk-based data structures, such as quadtrees, k-d trees, and radix trees (tries).

17ff32da1695.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
17ff32da1695.sentence: BRIN indexes (a shorthand for Block Range INdexes) store summaries about the values stored in consecutive physical block ranges of a table.

ffc98c6e3d7e.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
ffc98c6e3d7e.sentence: Thus, they are most effective for columns whose values are well-correlated with the physical order of the table rows.

7801bd055090.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html
7801bd055090.sentence: For data types that have a linear sort order, the indexed data corresponds to the minimum and maximum values of the values in the column for each block range.

b8122defbecd.title: Skip list
b8122defbecd.sentence: In computer science, a skip list (or skiplist) is a probabilistic data structure that allows 𝒪(log⁡n) average complexity for search as well as 𝒪(log⁡n) average complexity for insertion within an ordered sequence of n elements.

51839f90c3fb.title: Skip list
51839f90c3fb.sentence: Fast search is made possible by maintaining a linked hierarchy of subsequences, with each successive subsequence skipping over fewer elements than the previous one (see the picture below).

09c06860f4e8.title: Skip list
09c06860f4e8.sentence: The bottom layer 1 is an ordinary ordered linked list.

bd5c8f044978.title: Skip list
bd5c8f044978.sentence: Each higher layer acts as an "express lane" for the lists below, where an element in layer i appears in layer i+1 with some fixed probability p (two commonly used values for p are 1/2 or 1/4).

224bf9380fe8.title: Skip list
224bf9380fe8.sentence: A search for a target element begins at the head element in the top list, and proceeds horizontally until the current element is greater than or equal to the target.

819990b6b9f0.title: Skip list
819990b6b9f0.sentence: If the current element is greater than the target, or the search reaches the end of the linked list, the procedure is repeated after returning to the previous element and dropping down vertically to the next lower list.

07f5ccee1152.title: Skip list
07f5ccee1152.sentence: Therefore, the total expected cost of a search is 1plog1/pn which is 𝒪(log⁡n), when p is a constant.

79d043bd485d.title: Skip list
79d043bd485d.sentence: By choosing different values of p, it is possible to trade search costs against storage costs.

09bd2bf849ef.title: Skip list
09bd2bf849ef.sentence: A skip list does not provide the same absolute worst-case performance guarantees as more traditional balanced tree data structures, because it is always possible (though with very low probability) that the coin-flips used to build the skip list will produce a badly balanced structure.

1e1f13b9de15.title: Skip list
1e1f13b9de15.sentence: However, they work well in practice, and the randomized balancing scheme has been argued to be easier to implement than the deterministic balancing schemes used in balanced binary search trees.

8643b5cda86b.title: Skip list
8643b5cda86b.sentence: Skip lists are also useful in parallel computing, where insertions can be done in different parts of the skip list in parallel without any global rebalancing of the data structure.

f31b2980ca04.title: Skip list
f31b2980ca04.sentence: - Redis, an ANSI-C open-source persistent key/value store for Posix systems, uses skip lists in its implementation of ordered sets.

89576415b83d.title: Skip list
89576415b83d.sentence: - RocksDB uses skip lists for its default Memtable implementation.

afbf226cce47.title: Skip list
afbf226cce47.sentence: - Java uses skip lists for its ConcurrentSkipListSet and ConcurrentSkipListMap.

9e27ad3a143b.title: Log-structured merge-tree
9e27ad3a143b.sentence: When a write operation is initiated, the data is first buffered in an in-memory component, often implemented using a sorted data structure such as a Skip list or B+ tree.

b67c65cae707.title: Log-structured merge-tree
b67c65cae707.sentence: Once the in-memory buffer becomes full, it is flushed to the disk as an immutable sorted component at the first level (C1).

bf064722ec6e.title: Log-structured merge-tree
bf064722ec6e.sentence: As data accumulates across levels on the disk, LSM trees employ a merge process similar to merge sort to consolidate entries and maintain a consistent sorted order across levels.

151c5d478fcc.title: Log-structured merge-tree
151c5d478fcc.sentence: In LSM-trees, write operations are designed to optimize performance by reducing random I/O and leveraging sequential disk writes.

5d1de14d65e3.title: Log-structured merge-tree
5d1de14d65e3.sentence: This flush is performed sequentially, ensuring high I/O efficiency by avoiding the costly random writes typical of traditional indexing methods.

5713d33bb0a0.title: Log-structured merge-tree
5713d33bb0a0.sentence: To maintain durability, the system may use a write-ahead log (WAL) that records all incoming writes before they are added to the memory buffer.

3a92a5945e68.title: Log-structured merge-tree
3a92a5945e68.sentence: This ensures that no data is lost in the event of a crash during a write.

7dc7460ebad7.title: Log-structured merge-tree
7dc7460ebad7.sentence: This process also handles updates and deletes, removing redundant or obsolete entries.

1f12bfa8c7b1.title: Log-structured merge-tree
1f12bfa8c7b1.sentence: Updates are treated as new writes, while deletes are marked with a tombstone entry, which is a placeholder indicating that the key has been deleted.

75dff0aed690.title: Log-structured merge-tree
75dff0aed690.sentence: These tombstones are later removed during the merging process.

bdb2ae8e9221.title: Log-structured merge-tree
bdb2ae8e9221.sentence: Two common merging policies govern how data flows through the levels: levelling and tiering.

c0f9d0096cbf.title: Log-structured merge-tree
c0f9d0096cbf.sentence: In levelling, only one component exists per level, and merging happens more frequently, reducing the total number of components but increasing write amplification.

7002619d6d0d.title: Log-structured merge-tree
7002619d6d0d.sentence: In tiering, multiple components can coexist within a level, and merging occurs less frequently, reducing write amplification but increasing read costs because more components need to be searched.

c213161e1233.title: B-tree
c213161e1233.sentence: All insertions start at a leaf node.

e47f4bac1949.title: B-tree
e47f4bac1949.sentence: There are two popular strategies for deletion from a B-tree.

26b561ea4198.title: B-tree
26b561ea4198.sentence: To insert a new element, search the tree to find the leaf node where the new element should be added.

1088c251778b.title: B-tree
1088c251778b.sentence: - If the node contains fewer than the maximum allowed number of elements, then there is room for the new element.

29c36748afb7.title: B-tree
29c36748afb7.sentence: Insert the new element in the node, keeping the node's elements ordered.

94d22386053c.title: B-tree
94d22386053c.sentence: - Otherwise, the node is full, evenly split it into two nodes, so:

d11ab7356f5b.title: B-tree
d11ab7356f5b.sentence: - A single median is chosen from among the leaf's elements and the new element that is being inserted.

9a47f7c95d6d.title: B-tree
9a47f7c95d6d.sentence: - The separation value is inserted in the node's parent, which may cause it to be split, and so on.

105f16fcd61f.title: B-tree
105f16fcd61f.sentence: If the node has no parent (i.e., the node was the root), create a new root above this node (increasing the height of the tree).

00a75f69bcc9.title: B-tree
00a75f69bcc9.sentence: If the splitting goes all the way up to the root, it creates a new root with a single separator value and two children, which is why the lower bound on the size of internal nodes does not apply to the root.

234ed4dee129.title: B-tree
234ed4dee129.sentence: - Locate and delete the item, then restructure the tree to retain its invariants, OR

a730f1c2b4b5.title: B-tree
a730f1c2b4b5.sentence: - Do a single pass down the tree, but before entering (visiting) a node, restructure the tree so that once the key to be deleted is encountered, it can be deleted without triggering the need for any further restructuring.

cb38536eac00.title: B-tree
cb38536eac00.sentence: If deleting an element from a node has brought it under the minimum size, then some elements must be redistributed to bring all nodes up to the minimum.

88caa4ec80b5.title: B-tree
88caa4ec80b5.sentence: Usually, the redistribution involves moving an element from a sibling node that has more than the minimum number of nodes.

c599479fe409.title: B-tree
c599479fe409.sentence: That redistribution operation is called a rotation.

b3c71c7b1edb.title: B-tree
b3c71c7b1edb.sentence: If no sibling can spare an element, then the deficient node must be merged with a sibling.

53e15644ea18.title: B-tree
53e15644ea18.sentence: The merge causes the parent to lose a separator element, so the parent may become deficient and need rebalancing.

1ef7ef5e27c8.title: B-tree
1ef7ef5e27c8.sentence: The merging and rebalancing may continue all the way to the root.

11eaee8211a8.title: Database index
11eaee8211a8.sentence: A bitmap index is a special kind of indexing that stores the bulk of its data as bit arrays (bitmaps) and answers most queries by performing bitwise logical operations on these bitmaps.

9dc0278a0afc.title: Database index
9dc0278a0afc.sentence: The most commonly used indexes, such as B+ trees, are most efficient if the values they index do not repeat or repeat a small number of times.

4477b864ba00.title: Database index
4477b864ba00.sentence: In contrast, the bitmap index is designed for cases where the values of a variable repeat very frequently.

8ba719b429c9.title: Database index
8ba719b429c9.sentence: For example, the sex field in a customer database usually contains at most three distinct values: male, female or unknown (not recorded).

67813ac81f24.title: Database index
67813ac81f24.sentence: For such variables, the bitmap index can have a significant performance advantage over the commonly used trees.

95b5234a9766.title: Database index
95b5234a9766.sentence: A covering index is a special case where the index itself contains the required data fields and can answer the required data.

86b05374ba8b.title: Database index
86b05374ba8b.sentence: In most cases, an index is used to quickly locate the data records from which the required data is read.

649774b1ee0d.title: Database index
649774b1ee0d.sentence: In other words, the index is only used to locate data records in the table and not to return data.

2f649f1504da.title: Database index
2f649f1504da.sentence: To find the Name for ID 13, an index on (ID) is useful, but the record must still be read to get the Name.

8b2a55e3e6fb.title: Database index
8b2a55e3e6fb.sentence: However, an index on (ID, Name) contains the required data field and eliminates the need to look up the record.

5be0feaddcdb.title: Database index
5be0feaddcdb.sentence: A covering index can dramatically speed up data retrieval but may itself be large due to the additional keys, which slow down data insertion and update.

912bc12b3aa7.title: Database index
912bc12b3aa7.sentence: To reduce such index size, some systems allow including non-key fields in the index.

7c73f374cadf.title: Database index
7c73f374cadf.sentence: Non-key fields are not themselves part of the index ordering but only included at the leaf level, allowing for a covering index with less overall index size.

15f9bdd78004.title: Database index
15f9bdd78004.sentence: This can be done in SQL with CREATE INDEX my_index ON my_table (id) INCLUDE (name);.

9f5fb75a5d83.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
9f5fb75a5d83.sentence: In a dense index, an index record is created for every row of the table.

b4fbf3ade73a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
b4fbf3ade73a.sentence: In a sparse index, index records are created only for some of the records.

b1b40114d87f.title: Database index
b1b40114d87f.sentence: A dense index in databases is a file with pairs of keys and pointers for every record in the data file.

5532a5a00616.title: Database index
5532a5a00616.sentence: A sparse index in databases is a file with pairs of keys and pointers for every block in the data file.

faf95c86d48b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
faf95c86d48b.sentence: Records can be located directly as each record of the index holds the search key value and the pointer to the actual record.

cdb1ff44ebad.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
cdb1ff44ebad.sentence: Dense indexes require more maintenance than sparse indexes at write-time.

12acf99e42b2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
12acf99e42b2.sentence: Since every row must have an entry, the database must maintain the index on inserts, updates, and deletes.

b730f8dd1aa2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
b730f8dd1aa2.sentence: Having an entry for every row also means that dense indexes will require more memory.

a73cb98c1472.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
a73cb98c1472.sentence: The benefit of a dense index is that values can be quickly found with just a binary search.

926a9fddf502.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
926a9fddf502.sentence: Dense indexes also do not impose any ordering requirements on the data.

55e5ee511b7f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
55e5ee511b7f.sentence: Sparse indexes require less maintenance than dense indexes at write-time since they only contain a subset of the values.

2589e06e267f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
2589e06e267f.sentence: This lighter maintenance burden means that inserts, updates, and deletes will be faster.

28abc099a2e7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
28abc099a2e7.sentence: Having fewer entries also means that the index will use less memory.

b12f1a1f270c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
b12f1a1f270c.sentence: Finding data is slower since a scan across the page typically follows the binary search.

4ad487d8e27c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::indexes
4ad487d8e27c.sentence: Sparse indexes are also optional when working with ordered data.

ab4c4c6bc12f.title: Database index
ab4c4c6bc12f.sentence: Indexes are used to police database constraints, such as UNIQUE, EXCLUSION, PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY.

239a297be5a1.title: Database index
239a297be5a1.sentence: An index may be declared as UNIQUE, which creates an implicit constraint on the underlying table.

b2ae80bf20ea.title: Database index
b2ae80bf20ea.sentence: Database systems usually implicitly create an index on a set of columns declared PRIMARY KEY, and some are capable of using an already-existing index to police this constraint.

47954f6dc441.title: Database index
47954f6dc441.sentence: Many database systems require that both referencing and referenced sets of columns in a FOREIGN KEY constraint are indexed, thus improving performance of inserts, updates and deletes to the tables participating in the constraint.

c750902fdbf7.title: Database index
c750902fdbf7.sentence: Some database systems support an EXCLUSION constraint that ensures that, for a newly inserted or updated record, a certain predicate holds for no other record.

bcd3548720e8.title: Database index
bcd3548720e8.sentence: This can be used to implement a UNIQUE constraint (with equality predicate) or more complex constraints, like ensuring that no overlapping time ranges or no intersecting geometry objects would be stored in the table.

781ce3a2bef0.title: Database index
781ce3a2bef0.sentence: Every key in this file is associated with a particular pointer to a record in the sorted data file.

42a315a1ea74.title: Database index
42a315a1ea74.sentence: Every key in this file is associated with a particular pointer to the block in the sorted data file.

8290a826a6c1.title: Database index
8290a826a6c1.sentence: A reverse-key index reverses the key value before entering it in the index.

48f6985e619f.title: Database index
48f6985e619f.sentence: E.g., the value 24538 becomes 83542 in the index.

902ab83416ae.title: Database index
902ab83416ae.sentence: Reversing the key value is particularly useful for indexing data such as sequence numbers, where new key values monotonically increase.

735a4f25e704.title: Database index
735a4f25e704.sentence: The primary index contains the key fields of the table and a pointer to the non-key fields of the table.

05dffdee4895.title: Database index
05dffdee4895.sentence: The primary index is created automatically when the table is created in the database.

1dd6d15582e2.title: Database index
1dd6d15582e2.sentence: It is used to index fields that are neither ordering fields nor key fields (there is no assurance that the file is organized on key field or primary key field).

c03830f395ae.title: Database index
c03830f395ae.sentence: An inverted index maps a content word to the document containing it, thereby allowing full-text searches.

4e3c9ca5b817.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
4e3c9ca5b817.sentence: Locks are essential to maintain data consistency and integrity in multi-user environments.

bdb71630207a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
bdb71630207a.sentence: They prevent simultaneous modifications that can lead to data inconsistencies.

e3ee49d5a350.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
e3ee49d5a350.sentence: Pessimistic locking assumes conflicts will occur and locks the data before any changes are made.

17365c5775c4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
17365c5775c4.sentence: It prevents other users from accessing and updating the data until the lock is released.

c17dda80c51f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
c17dda80c51f.sentence: Optimistic locking assumes conflicts are rare.

90fcba804d0d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
90fcba804d0d.sentence: It allows multiple users to access data simultaneously and checks for conflicts when changes are committed.

0ea87fde050b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
0ea87fde050b.sentence: If a conflict is detected, the operation is rolled back.

437bca27eba5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
437bca27eba5.sentence: - Pessimistic locking is better for data integrity but can impact performance.

fac7548c3aaf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
fac7548c3aaf.sentence: - Optimistic locking is better for efficiency and performance.

542fdf88286d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
542fdf88286d.sentence: - Hold locks for the minimum possible time to reduce contention.

7b3f16402f5d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
7b3f16402f5d.sentence: - Apply locks at the most granular level such as rows rather than tables.

30f0528c3a17.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/pessimistic-vs-optimistic-locking.md
30f0528c3a17.sentence: - Implement retry logic for transactions that fail due to conflicts.

1fff736929d6.title: Log-structured merge-tree
1fff736929d6.sentence: The process begins with a search in the in-memory component (C0), which holds the latest data.

8e71384fca05.title: Log-structured merge-tree
8e71384fca05.sentence: If the key isn't found in memory, the search moves to the disk components, starting with the first level (C1) and continuing through deeper levels (C2, C3, etc.).

8ba9fdfa302b.title: Log-structured merge-tree
8ba9fdfa302b.sentence: Newer levels are checked first because they contain the most recent updates and deletions for the key.

70a013296953.title: Log-structured merge-tree
70a013296953.sentence: In LSM trees, because of the multi-level structure and the immutability of disk components, point lookups involve checking several levels to ensure the most up-to-date value for the key is returned.

52fa68b530c7.title: Log-structured merge-tree
52fa68b530c7.sentence: The lookup operation stops as soon as the key is found, ensuring the most recent version is returned.

52bfdb706424.title: Log-structured merge-tree
52bfdb706424.sentence: These filters are probabilistic structures that help quickly determine whether a key is definitely absent from a component.

36ac7fa86e3a.title: Log-structured merge-tree
36ac7fa86e3a.sentence: Before accessing any disk component, the system checks the Bloom filter.

6438c38e2817.title: Log-structured merge-tree
6438c38e2817.sentence: If the filter indicates the key is not present, the component is skipped, saving time.

0b16f073420d.title: Log-structured merge-tree
0b16f073420d.sentence: Point lookup complexity is O(L) without Bloom filters, as each level must be searched.

9ed54009d28d.title: Log-structured merge-tree
9ed54009d28d.sentence: For existing key lookups, the cost is O(1) due to the presence of Bloom filters.

d8daa6bd18c2.title: Log-structured merge-tree
d8daa6bd18c2.sentence: To perform the range query, the system locates the starting point in each relevant component and scans sequentially until the end of the range is reached.

9ad0581bb5e1.title: Log-structured merge-tree
9ad0581bb5e1.sentence: The results from each component are then merged into a priority queue to reconcile duplicates, updates, and deletes, ensuring the final result only includes the latest version of each key.

76156e26e9da.title: Log-structured merge-tree
76156e26e9da.sentence: For short-range queries, which access fewer keys than twice the number of levels, the query must examine components across all levels, leading to a cost proportional to the number of levels.

daf3f6973136.title: Log-structured merge-tree
daf3f6973136.sentence: For long-range queries, which access many keys, the price is dominated by scanning the largest level, as it contains most of the data.

92498aec3f82.title: Log-structured merge-tree
92498aec3f82.sentence: For this reason, the runtime for short-range queries is O(L) and O(sB) for long-range queries, where s is the number of keys in the range.

99e05acfed22.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
99e05acfed22.sentence: Primary key: Column or group of columns that can be used to uniquely identify every row of the table.

609b19a436c5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
609b19a436c5.sentence: Candidate key: Attributes that identify rows uniquely in a table.

f81d1a6dac6e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
f81d1a6dac6e.sentence: Composite key: A primary key made up of multiple columns.

f8304b89348c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
f8304b89348c.sentence: Super key: Set of all keys that can uniquely identify all the rows present in a table.

4e37335e07c9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
4e37335e07c9.sentence: Alternate key: Keys that are not primary keys are known as alternate keys.

60fc949aac7c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
60fc949aac7c.sentence: Foreign key: It is a reference to a primary key of another table.

00525a26e854.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
00525a26e854.sentence: Surrogate key: A system-generated value that uniquely identifies each entry in a table when no other column was able to hold properties of a primary key.

cd379cb02243.title: Database index
cd379cb02243.sentence: The order that the index definition defines the columns in is important.

2cca4912a069.title: Database index
2cca4912a069.sentence: It is possible to retrieve a set of row identifiers using only the first indexed column.

8d3335a932dd.title: Database index
8d3335a932dd.sentence: However, it is not possible or efficient (on most databases) to retrieve the set of row identifiers using only the second or greater indexed column.

e92591274dfb.title: Database index
e92591274dfb.sentence: For example, in a phone book organized by city first, then by last name, and then by first name, in a particular city, one can easily extract the list of all phone numbers.

42c960838a39.title: Database index
42c960838a39.sentence: However, it would be very tedious to find all the phone numbers for a particular last name.

6a57355cdb14.title: Database index
6a57355cdb14.sentence: In the phone book example with a composite index created on the columns (city, last_name, first_name), if we search by giving exact values for all the three fields, search time is minimal—but if we provide the values for city and first_name only, the search uses only the city field to retrieve all matched records.

f4b2a3e09c11.title: Database index
f4b2a3e09c11.sentence: Then a sequential lookup checks the matching with first_name.

ca378031f521.title: Database index
ca378031f521.sentence: So, to improve the performance, one must ensure that the index is created on the order of search columns.

6bbafbcf94de.title: Database index
6bbafbcf94de.sentence: To process this statement without an index the database software must look at the last_name column on every row in the table (this is known as a full table scan).

a1933e329a4d.title: Database index
a1933e329a4d.sentence: With an index the database simply follows the index data structure (typically a B-tree) until the Smith entry has been found; this is much less computationally expensive than a full table scan.

150d67f7ce54.title: Database index
150d67f7ce54.sentence: This query would yield an email address for every customer whose email address ends with "@wikipedia.org", but even if the email_address column has been indexed the database must perform a full index scan.

58e0f790dd9c.title: Database index
58e0f790dd9c.sentence: This is because the index is built with the assumption that words go from left to right.

d5017c8849cb.title: Database index
d5017c8849cb.sentence: With a wildcard at the beginning of the search-term, the database software is unable to use the underlying index data structure (in other words, the WHERE-clause is not sargable).

c8b97979773b.title: Database index
c8b97979773b.sentence: This problem can be solved through the addition of another index created on reverse(email_address) and a SQL query like this: SELECT email_address FROM customers WHERE reverse(email_address) LIKE reverse('%@wikipedia.org');.

b6b75e883882.title: Database index
b6b75e883882.sentence: This puts the wild-card at the right-most part of the query (now gro.aidepikiw@%), which the index on reverse(email_address) can satisfy.

151483373556.title: Database index
151483373556.sentence: When the wildcard characters are used on both sides of the search word as %wikipedia.org%, the index available on this field is not used.

39f4feef031e.title: Database index
39f4feef031e.sentence: Rather only a sequential search is performed, which takes ⁠O(N)⁠ time.

f2a85454ffd1.title: Database index
f2a85454ffd1.sentence: To mitigate this, a full-text indexing approach can be used.

0698e13924c2.title: Database index
0698e13924c2.sentence: For example, text can be split into trigrams (3-character chunks) and stored in a GIN (Generalized inverted index) to reduce complexity of lookup to about O(logN) time

f65e288054bf.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
f65e288054bf.sentence: Functional dependency: It is a relationship that exists between two attributes, typically between the primary key and non-key attribute within a table.

036226fc67c1.title: Database normalization
036226fc67c1.sentence: To conform to 2NF and remove duplicates, every non-candidate-key attribute must depend on the whole candidate key, not just part of it.

06e431729492.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
06e431729492.sentence: - Should not have any partial dependency.

bfb3c28af0fb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
bfb3c28af0fb.sentence: Transitive functional dependency: Occurs when some non-key attribute determines some other attribute.

066cc1349801.title: Database normalization
066cc1349801.sentence: The Book table still has a transitive functional dependency ({Author Nationality} is dependent on {Author}, which is dependent on {Title}).

8e488320164e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
8e488320164e.sentence: - Transitive functional dependencies are not permitted.

7037daf1f528.title: Database normalization
7037daf1f528.sentence: The normal forms (from least normalized to most normalized) are:

9da3d787dbc7.title: Database normalization
9da3d787dbc7.sentence: Scalar columns (columns cannot contain relations or composite values)

ad133180b606.title: Database normalization
ad133180b606.sentence: Every non-prime attribute has a full functional dependency on each candidate key (attributes depend on the whole of every key)

80149b18b991.title: Database normalization
80149b18b991.sentence: Every non-trivial functional dependency either begins with a superkey or ends with a prime attribute (attributes depend only on candidate keys)

c2e88d209061.title: Database normalization
c2e88d209061.sentence: Every non-trivial functional dependency begins with a superkey (a stricter form of 3NF) | | — N/a

5574736cad7e.title: Database normalization
5574736cad7e.sentence: Informally, a relational database relation is often described as "normalized" if it meets third normal form.

6ff7af631411.title: Database normalization
6ff7af631411.sentence: However, normal forms beyond 4NF are mainly of academic interest, as the problems they exist to solve rarely appear in practice.

ae5cbb481752.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
ae5cbb481752.sentence: Boyce-Codd normal form (or BCNF) is a slightly stronger version of the third normal form (3NF) used to address certain types of anomalies not dealt with by 3NF as originally defined.

745a9bd2845f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
745a9bd2845f.sentence: Sometimes it is also known as the 3.5 normal form (3.5NF).

570d0a9b14ce.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
570d0a9b14ce.sentence: - For every functional dependency X → Y, X should be the super key.

e82869bae4da.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
e82869bae4da.sentence: As with many formal rules and specifications, real-world scenarios do not always allow for perfect compliance.

2a432d2b70a0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::normalization-and-denormalization
2a432d2b70a0.sentence: If you decide to violate one of the first three rules of normalization, make sure that your application anticipates any problems that could occur, such as redundant data and inconsistent dependencies.

f1b951a302dd.title: Database normalization
f1b951a302dd.sentence: Codd introduced the concept of normalization and what is now known as the first normal form (1NF) in 1970.

ee83b17391ef.title: Database normalization
ee83b17391ef.sentence: Codd went on to define the second normal form (2NF) and third normal form (3NF) in 1971, and Codd and Raymond F. Boyce defined the Boyce–Codd normal form (BCNF) in 1974.

ef4952a98e5f.title: Database normalization
ef4952a98e5f.sentence: Ronald Fagin introduced the fourth normal form (4NF) in 1977 and the fifth normal form (5NF) in 1979.

858ae2924fe4.title: Database normalization
858ae2924fe4.sentence: Normalization is a database design technique, which is used to design a relational database table up to higher normal form.

0ca79f1768ca.title: Database normalization
0ca79f1768ca.sentence: The process is progressive, and a higher level of database normalization cannot be achieved unless the previous levels have been satisfied.

06781cbd9e8c.title: Database normalization
06781cbd9e8c.sentence: In practice, it is often possible to skip some of the normalization steps because the data is already normalized to some extent.

076e000b07a6.title: Database normalization
076e000b07a6.sentence: In the first normal form each field contains a single value.

6b1e0367d8e1.title: Database normalization
6b1e0367d8e1.sentence: A field may not contain a set of values or a nested record.

3093cae0a803.title: Database normalization
3093cae0a803.sentence: Subject contains a set of subject values, meaning it does not comply.

db869ed80dd7.title: Database normalization
db869ed80dd7.sentence: To solve the problem, the subjects are extracted into a separate Subject table:

20c106b50f55.title: Database normalization
20c106b50f55.sentence: All of the attributes that are not part of the candidate key depend on Title, but only Price also depends on Format.

44b7c8befa3f.title: Database normalization
44b7c8befa3f.sentence: To normalize this table, make {Title} a (simple) candidate key (the primary key) so that every non-candidate-key attribute depends on the whole candidate key, and remove Price into a separate table so that its dependency on Format can be preserved:

5f926cecbe0a.title: Database normalization
5f926cecbe0a.sentence: Similar violations exist for publisher ({Publisher Country} is dependent on {Publisher}, which is dependent on {Title}) and for genre ({Genre Name} is dependent on {Genre ID}, which is dependent on {Title}).

e1654f27f11f.title: Database normalization
e1654f27f11f.sentence: To resolve this, we can place {Author Nationality}, {Publisher Country}, and {Genre Name} in their own respective tables, thereby eliminating the transitive functional dependencies:

a589047a6c9f.title: Database normalization
a589047a6c9f.sentence: However, assuming that all available books are offered in each area, the Title is not unambiguously bound to a certain Location and therefore the table does not satisfy 4NF.

48a23dc4a84d.title: Database normalization
48a23dc4a84d.sentence: That means that, to satisfy the fourth normal form, this table needs to be decomposed as well:

6d296dd86414.title: Database normalization
6d296dd86414.sentence: Now, every record is unambiguously identified by a superkey, therefore 4NF is satisfied.

3eae21585c8e.title: Database normalization
3eae21585c8e.sentence: Fixing a violation of one normal form also often fixes a violation of a higher normal form.

68aa68f49c43.title: Database normalization
68aa68f49c43.sentence: A simple and intuitive definition of the sixth normal form is that "a table is in 6NF when the row contains the Primary Key, and at most one other attribute".

b12795defebe.title: Database normalization
b12795defebe.sentence: The obvious drawback of 6NF is the proliferation of tables required to represent the information on a single entity.

0674ad9b39dd.title: Database normalization
0674ad9b39dd.sentence: If a table in 5NF has one primary key column and N attributes, representing the same information in 6NF will require N tables; multi-field updates to a single conceptual record will require updates to multiple tables; and inserts and deletes will similarly require operations across multiple tables.

ea122469a323.title: Database normalization
ea122469a323.sentence: For this reason, in databases intended to serve online transaction processing (OLTP) needs, 6NF should not be used.

6c408157bd3c.title: Database normalization
6c408157bd3c.sentence: However, in data warehouses, which do not permit interactive updates and which are specialized for fast query on large data volumes, certain DBMSs use an internal 6NF representation – known as a columnar data store.

c4214eea2d25.title: Database normalization
c4214eea2d25.sentence: In situations where the number of unique values of a column is far less than the number of rows in the table, column-oriented storage allow significant savings in space through data compression.

119aa9f562ce.title: Database normalization
119aa9f562ce.sentence: Columnar storage also allows fast execution of range queries (e.g., show all records where a particular column is between X and Y, or less than X.)

92c7be51a145.title: Computer data storage
92c7be51a145.sentence: Computer data storage or digital data storage is the retention of digital data via technology consisting of computer components and recording media.

a707215cea07.title: Computer data storage
a707215cea07.sentence: Generally, the faster and volatile storage components are referred to as "memory", while slower persistent components are referred to as "storage".

8cf737b6f313.title: Computer data storage
8cf737b6f313.sentence: In contemporary usage, the term "storage" typically refers to a subset of computer data storage that comprises storage devices and their media not directly accessible by the CPU, that is, secondary or tertiary storage.

59e6aa1db2fc.title: Computer data storage
59e6aa1db2fc.sentence: On the other hand, the term "memory" is used to refer to semiconductor read-write data storage, typically dynamic random-access memory (DRAM).

a7bd1d9d9170.title: Computer data storage
a7bd1d9d9170.sentence: Text, numbers, pictures, audio, and nearly any other form of information can be converted into a string of bits, or binary digits, each of which has a value of 0 or 1.

e7be2944f840.title: Computer data storage
e7be2944f840.sentence: The most common unit of storage is the byte, equal to 8 bits.

663654b1ff0d.title: Computer data storage
663654b1ff0d.sentence: Data compression methods allow in many cases (such as a database) to represent a string of bits by a shorter bit string ("compress") and reconstruct the original string ("decompress") when needed.

5f8d746b20f6.title: Computer data storage
5f8d746b20f6.sentence: This utilizes substantially less storage (tens of percent) for many types of data at the cost of more computation (compress and decompress when needed).

23d7c263b1cc.title: Computer data storage
23d7c263b1cc.sentence: Analysis of the trade-off between storage cost saving and costs of related computations and possible delays in data availability is done before deciding whether to keep certain data compressed or not.

b882817363f2.title: Computer data storage
b882817363f2.sentence: For security reasons, certain types of data may be encrypted in storage to prevent the possibility of unauthorized information reconstruction from chunks of storage snapshots.

061b3faff0cc.title: Computer data storage
061b3faff0cc.sentence: Encryption in transit protects data as it is being transmitted.

6ba5f8202ffd.title: Computer data storage
6ba5f8202ffd.sentence: Redundancy allows the computer to detect errors in coded data (for example, a random bit flip due to random radiation) and correct them based on mathematical algorithms.

50435eba6532.title: Computer data storage
50435eba6532.sentence: Redundancy solutions include storage replication, disk mirroring and redundant array of independent disks (RAID).

d3d85085752b.title: Computer data storage
d3d85085752b.sentence: Distinct types of data storage have different points of failure and various methods of predictive failure analysis.

d40019c12d05.title: Computer data storage
d40019c12d05.sentence: Vulnerabilities that can instantly lead to total loss are head crashing on mechanical hard drives and failure of electronic components on flash storage.

800f2df9840c.title: Hard disk drive
800f2df9840c.sentence: A hard disk drive (HDD), hard disk, hard drive, or fixed disk is an electro-mechanical computer data storage device that stores and retrieves digital data using magnetic storage with one or more rigid rapidly rotating platters coated with magnetic material.

db4f6cfc42af.title: Hard disk drive
db4f6cfc42af.sentence: The platters are paired with magnetic heads, usually arranged on a moving actuator arm, which read and write data to the platter surfaces.

f8193b694eb0.title: Hard disk drive
f8193b694eb0.sentence: Data is accessed in a random-access manner, meaning that individual blocks of data can be stored and retrieved in any order.

49a8b3a77f4a.title: Hard disk drive
49a8b3a77f4a.sentence: HDDs are a type of non-volatile storage, retaining stored data when powered off.

91ad928c6d73.title: Hard disk drive
91ad928c6d73.sentence: The factors that limit the time to access the data on an HDD are mostly related to the mechanical nature of the rotating disks and moving heads, including:

e0a124292a4f.title: Hard disk drive
e0a124292a4f.sentence: - Seek time is a measure of how long it takes the head assembly to travel to the track of the disk that contains data.

8786231e61dc.title: Hard disk drive
8786231e61dc.sentence: - Rotational latency is incurred because the desired disk sector may not be directly under the head when data transfer is requested.

913dec62e347.title: Hard disk drive
913dec62e347.sentence: - The bit rate or data transfer rate (once the head is in the right position) creates delay which is a function of the number of blocks transferred; typically relatively small, but can be quite long with the transfer of large contiguous files.

f2b089abf34c.title: Hard disk drive
f2b089abf34c.sentence: Average rotational latency is shown in the table, based on the statistical relation that the average latency is one-half the rotational period.

ef7d9ca3c370.title: Hard disk drive
ef7d9ca3c370.sentence: The time to access data has not kept up with throughput increases, which themselves have not kept up with growth in bit density and storage capacity.

85307a04c7d1.title: Hard disk drive
85307a04c7d1.sentence: Though SSDs have four to nine times higher cost per bit, they are replacing HDDs in applications where speed, power consumption, small size, high capacity and durability are important.

76b3f7662e9e.title: Hard disk drive
76b3f7662e9e.sentence: HDDs dominate the volume of storage produced (exabytes per year) for servers.

d8f5d8fc299c.title: Hard disk drive
d8f5d8fc299c.sentence: Modern drives make extensive use of error correction codes (ECCs), particularly Reed–Solomon error correction.

a6f91e1b0672.title: Hard disk drive
a6f91e1b0672.sentence: These techniques store extra bits, determined by mathematical formulas, for each block of data; the extra bits allow many errors to be corrected invisibly.

e8f48d346ce8.title: Hard disk drive
e8f48d346ce8.sentence: The extra bits themselves take up space on the HDD, but allow higher recording densities to be employed without causing uncorrectable errors, resulting in much larger storage capacity.

ce4b5b30a080.title: Hard disk drive
ce4b5b30a080.sentence: For example, a typical 1 TB hard disk with 512-byte sectors provides additional capacity of about 93 GB for the ECC data.

b15ca2b21e41.title: Hard disk drive
b15ca2b21e41.sentence: Data is stored on a hard drive in a series of logical blocks.

e63144457763.title: Hard disk drive
e63144457763.sentence: Each block is delimited by markers identifying its start and end, error detecting and correcting information, and space between blocks to allow for minor timing variations.

b7f3e16edb76.title: Hard disk drive
b7f3e16edb76.sentence: These blocks often contained 512 bytes of usable data, but other sizes have been used.

1f14b05e6670.title: Hard disk drive
1f14b05e6670.sentence: To minimize cost and overcome failures of individual HDDs, storage systems providers rely on redundant HDD arrays.

69559caa8b05.title: Hard disk drive
69559caa8b05.sentence: HDDs that fail are replaced on an ongoing basis.

cee40d9e5d2a.title: Volatile memory
cee40d9e5d2a.sentence: Volatile memory, in contrast to non-volatile memory, is computer memory that requires power to maintain the stored information; it retains its contents while powered on but when the power is interrupted, the stored data is quickly lost.

0a954ab6f4bc.title: Volatile memory
0a954ab6f4bc.sentence: Most general-purpose random-access memory (RAM) is volatile.

520d2c3bec76.title: Volatile memory
520d2c3bec76.sentence: Volatile memory has several uses, including as primary storage.

2815f4945adc.title: Volatile memory
2815f4945adc.sentence: In addition to usually being faster than forms of mass storage such as a hard disk drive, volatility can protect sensitive information, as it becomes unavailable on power-down.

c7a8677d5b66.title: Volatile memory
c7a8677d5b66.sentence: There are two kinds of volatile RAM: dynamic and static.

77e3cc6441b4.title: Volatile memory
77e3cc6441b4.sentence: Even though both types need continuous electrical current to retain data, there are some important differences between them.

d5cfcf4e6e55.title: Volatile memory
d5cfcf4e6e55.sentence: Dynamic RAM (DRAM) is very popular due to its cost-effectiveness.

3c66b36ee16a.title: Volatile memory
3c66b36ee16a.sentence: DRAM stores each bit of information in a different capacitor within the integrated circuit.

059ed3875368.title: Volatile memory
059ed3875368.sentence: DRAM chips need just one single capacitor and one transistor to store each bit of information.

d9bc2bbfc8c0.title: Volatile memory
d9bc2bbfc8c0.sentence: This makes it space-efficient and inexpensive.

333a38fadd89.title: Volatile memory
333a38fadd89.sentence: The main advantage of static RAM (SRAM) is that it is much faster than dynamic RAM.

8c00be2416dc.title: Volatile memory
8c00be2416dc.sentence: SRAM does not need continuous electrical refreshes, but it still requires constant current to sustain the difference in voltage.

5b0ebc35bb4e.title: Volatile memory
5b0ebc35bb4e.sentence: Every single bit in a static RAM chip needs a cell of six transistors, whereas dynamic RAM requires only one capacitor and one transistor.

0bffac11fc7f.title: Volatile memory
0bffac11fc7f.sentence: As a result, SRAM is unable to accomplish the storage capabilities of the DRAM family.

805ca45266c8.title: Volatile memory
805ca45266c8.sentence: SRAM is commonly used as CPU cache and for processor registers and in networking devices.

c06542d12fb4.title: Non-volatile memory
c06542d12fb4.sentence: Non-volatile memory (NVM) or non-volatile storage is a type of computer memory that can retain stored information even after power is removed.

adb6093ef4eb.title: Non-volatile memory
adb6093ef4eb.sentence: Non-volatile memory is typically used for the task of secondary storage or long-term persistent storage.

fbe5f925eb02.title: Non-volatile memory
fbe5f925eb02.sentence: However, most forms of non-volatile memory have limitations that make them unsuitable for use as primary storage.

4fc234e873ad.title: Non-volatile memory
4fc234e873ad.sentence: Typically, non-volatile memory costs more, provides lower performance, or has a limited lifetime compared to volatile random access memory.

d34a448525ab.title: Non-volatile memory
d34a448525ab.sentence: Non-volatile data storage can be categorized into electrically addressed systems, for example, flash memory, and read-only memory) and mechanically addressed systems (hard disks, optical discs, magnetic tape, holographic memory, and such).

88aeb6b8b057.title: Non-volatile memory
88aeb6b8b057.sentence: Generally speaking, electrically addressed systems are expensive, and have limited capacity, but are fast, whereas mechanically addressed systems cost less per bit, but are slower.

6a62f9cd4735.title: Non-volatile memory
6a62f9cd4735.sentence: Mechanically addressed systems use a recording head to read and write on a designated storage medium.

3c777fc7d612.title: Non-volatile memory
3c777fc7d612.sentence: Since the access time depends on the physical location of the data on the device, mechanically addressed systems may be sequential access.

9bb5d9197115.title: Non-volatile memory
9bb5d9197115.sentence: For example, magnetic tape stores data as a sequence of bits on a long tape; transporting the tape past the recording head is required to access any part of the storage.

bb13ce52785c.title: Non-volatile memory
bb13ce52785c.sentence: Hard disk drives use a rotating magnetic disk to store data; access time is longer than for semiconductor memory, but the cost per stored data bit is very low, and they provide random access to any location on the disk.

d9c5766f943f.title: Non-volatile memory
d9c5766f943f.sentence: Optical discs store data by altering a pigment layer on a plastic disk and are similarly random access.

b6f80229d724.title: Non-volatile memory
b6f80229d724.section: Electrically addressed > Read-only and read-mostly devices

eb3b9352b188.sentence: Ferroelectric RAM (FeRAM, F-RAM or FRAM) is a form of random-access memory similar in construction to DRAM; both use a capacitor and transistor but instead of using a simple dielectric layer in the capacitor, an F-RAM cell contains a thin ferroelectric film of lead zirconate titanate [Pb(Zr,Ti)O3], commonly referred to as PZT.

bcbb989b3ff1.title: Durability (database systems)
bcbb989b3ff1.sentence: In database systems, durability is the ACID property that guarantees that the effects of transactions that have been committed will survive permanently, even in cases of failures, including incidents and catastrophic events.

7a850f8e196f.title: Durability (database systems)
7a850f8e196f.sentence: Formally, a database system ensures the durability property if it tolerates three types of failures: transaction, system, and media failures.

11684966c1b1.title: Durability (database systems)
11684966c1b1.sentence: In particular, a transaction fails if its execution is interrupted before all its operations have been processed by the system.

ed48045b9c2b.title: Durability (database systems)
ed48045b9c2b.sentence: At the system level, a failure occurs if the contents of the volatile storage are lost, due, for instance, to system crashes, like out-of-memory events.

98841a87055a.title: Durability (database systems)
98841a87055a.sentence: At the media level, where media means a stable storage that withstands system failures, failures happen when the stable storage, or part of it, is lost.

e85933298134.title: Durability (database systems)
e85933298134.sentence: These cases are typically represented by disk failures.

682437f221d8.title: Durability (database systems)
682437f221d8.sentence: Thus, to be durable, the database system should implement strategies and operations that guarantee that the effects of transactions that have been committed before the failure will survive the event (even by reconstruction), while the changes of incomplete transactions, which have not been committed yet at the time of failure, will be reverted and will not affect the state of the database system.

ca3f5ee6a831.title: Durability (database systems)
ca3f5ee6a831.sentence: In systems that include non-volatile storage, durability can be achieved by keeping and flushing an immutable sequential log of the transactions to such non-volatile storage before acknowledging commitment.

46a021516721.title: Durability (database systems)
46a021516721.sentence: In particular, the logging mechanism is called write-ahead log (WAL) and allows durability by buffering changes to the disk before they are synchronized from the main memory.

c9ca47c11217.title: Durability (database systems)
c9ca47c11217.sentence: In this way, by reconstruction from the log file, all committed transactions are resilient to system-level failures, because they can be redone.

c3e133075b64.title: Durability (database systems)
c3e133075b64.sentence: Non-committed transactions, instead, are recoverable, since their operations are logged to non-volatile storage before they effectively modify the state of the database.

5d6842049b77.title: Durability (database systems)
5d6842049b77.sentence: In this way, the partially executed operations can be undone without affecting the state of the system.

28d837b2b2fb.title: Durability (database systems)
28d837b2b2fb.sentence: Therefore, the transaction log from non-volatile storage can be reprocessed to recreate the system state right before any later system-level failure.

43756fcfd878.title: Durability (database systems)
43756fcfd878.sentence: Existing database systems use volatile storage (i.e. the main memory of the system) for different purposes: some store their whole state and data in it, even without any durability guarantee; others keep the state and the data, or part of them, in memory, but also use the non-volatile storage for data; other systems only keep the state in main memory, while keeping all the data on disk.

4e07366101cf.title: Durability (database systems)
4e07366101cf.sentence: The reason behind the choice of having volatile storage, which is subject to this type of failure, and non-volatile storage, is found in the performance differences of the existing technologies that are used to implement these kinds of storage.

ab193ab5217c.title: Durability (database systems)
ab193ab5217c.sentence: To guarantee durability at this level, the database system shall rely on stable memory, which is a memory that is completely and ideally failure-resistant.

54c5544e1cd2.title: Durability (database systems)
54c5544e1cd2.sentence: This kind of memory can be achieved with mechanisms of replication and robust writing protocols.

7575243c5ddf.title: Durability (database systems)
7575243c5ddf.sentence: Many tools and technologies are available to provide a logical stable memory, such as the mirroring of disks, and their choice depends on the requirements of the specific applications.

e76c9ba9e66a.title: Durability (database systems)
e76c9ba9e66a.sentence: In this way, even in case of catastrophic events where the storage hardware is damaged, data loss can be prevented.

8173f50364ee.title: Durability (database systems)
8173f50364ee.sentence: These last techniques fall into the categories of backup, data loss prevention, and IT disaster recovery.

99ca4a810423.title: Durability (database systems)
99ca4a810423.sentence: There exist several mechanisms to store and reconstruct the state of a database system that improves the performance, both in terms of space and time, compared to managing all the log files created from the beginning of the database system.

f51fcfa2b866.title: Durability (database systems)
f51fcfa2b866.sentence: These mechanisms often include incremental dumping, differential files, and checkpoints.

e102669d8c33.title: Durability (database systems)
e102669d8c33.sentence: In distributed transactions, ensuring durability requires additional mechanisms to preserve a consistent state sequence across all database nodes.

b9655274b130.title: Durability (database systems)
b9655274b130.sentence: For this reason, all participating nodes must coordinate before a commit can be acknowledged.

059e20951be2.title: Durability (database systems)
059e20951be2.sentence: This is usually done by a two-phase commit protocol.

e698f86e681c.title: Durability (database systems)
e698f86e681c.sentence: In addition, in distributed databases, even the protocols for logging and recovery shall address the issues of distributed environments, such as deadlocks, that could prevent the resilience and recoverability of transactions and, thus, durability.

190c27d9affa.title: Durability (database systems)
190c27d9affa.sentence: A widely adopted family of algorithms that ensures these properties is Algorithms for Recovery and Isolation Exploiting Semantics (ARIES).

e84e222ebb8f.title: Computer data storage

6e03c85a5920.title: Computer data storage

89844db72bba.sentence: The CPU continuously reads instructions stored there and executes them as required.

3073f717c874.title: Computer data storage

a9e35c02b9cd.title: Computer data storage

29c6403586d9.title: Computer data storage

29edb8dcbb6f.title: Computer data storage

a3d92e859b0d.title: Solid-state drive
a3d92e859b0d.sentence: A solid-state drive (SSD) is a type of solid-state storage device that uses integrated circuits to store data persistently.

d4154bb241cc.sentence: SSDs rely on non-volatile memory, typically NAND flash, to store data in memory cells.

b51400d045c2.title: Solid-state drive
b51400d045c2.sentence: Unlike traditional hard disk drives (HDDs), SSDs have no moving parts, allowing them to deliver faster data access speeds, reduced latency, increased resistance to physical shock, lower power consumption, and silent operation.

b03d48999d6f.sentence: Random-access performance | SSD random access times typically range from 0.05-0.2 ms (50-200 microseconds) for consumer NAND SSDs, with NVMe drives achieving 0.05-0.1 ms and SATA SSDs around 0.5-0.6 ms. | HDD random access times range from 2.9 ms (high-end) to 12 ms (laptop HDDs).

3889efdabf1f.sentence: For example, incomplete or failed writes due to sudden power loss may be more problematic than with HDDs, and the failure of a single chip may result in the loss of all data stored on it.

706ea21a95e5.title: Solid-state drive

96b8dfda24ce.title: Solid-state drive

ca0e84f8fffe.sentence: The wear-leveling algorithms are complex and difficult to test exhaustively.

7a902f2d77de.sentence: Higher-performing SSDs may include capacitors, supercapacitors or batteries, which helps preserve data integrity in the event of an unexpected power loss.

6a84f3ab60fd.sentence: EFDs often have higher specifications than consumer SSDs (cSSDs), including enterprise-class flashes, supercapacators for robust power loss protection (PLP), larger DRAM buffers, and more flash channels, making them suitable for mission-critical applications.

0e5c3f39ac6b.title: Hard disk drive
0e5c3f39ac6b.sentence: Due to the extremely close spacing between the heads and the disk surface, HDDs are vulnerable to being damaged by a head crash – a failure of the disk in which the head scrapes across the platter surface, often grinding away the thin magnetic film and causing data loss.

db44df6be709.title: Hard disk drive
db44df6be709.sentence: Typical hard disk drives attempt to "remap" the data in a physical sector that is failing to a spare physical sector provided by the drive's "spare sector pool" (also called "reserve pool"), while relying on the ECC to recover stored data while the number of errors in a bad sector is still low enough.

4a1054100be1.title: Hard disk drive
4a1054100be1.sentence: Head crashes can be caused by electronic failure, a sudden power failure, physical shock, contamination of the drive's internal enclosure, wear and tear, corrosion, or poorly manufactured platters and heads.

2627e50cee2e.title: Hard disk drive

9bd61d96d6c7.title: Hard disk drive
