c91fa9c8fd6b.sentence: This is the most flexible and versatile form of storage.

72aac725a139.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
72aac725a139.sentence: Some applications like a database or a virtual machine engine manage these blocks directly in order to squeeze every drop of performance out of them.

700be23cf664.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
700be23cf664.sentence: Block storage also decouples data from user environments, allowing that data to be spread across multiple environments.

9114314897e6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
9114314897e6.sentence: This creates multiple paths to the data and allows the user to retrieve it quickly.

3251e1978ebd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
3251e1978ebd.sentence: When a user or application requests data from a block storage system, the underlying storage system reassembles the data blocks and presents the data to the user or application

40e68f7be3f0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
40e68f7be3f0.sentence: Common storage devices like hard disk drives (HDD) and solid-state drives (SSD) that are physically attached to servers are all considered as block storage.

60fb72fb7d91.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
60fb72fb7d91.sentence: Block storage could be connected to a server over a high-speed network or over industry-standard connectivity protocols like Fibre Channel (FC) and iSCSI.

196bf02742cf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
196bf02742cf.sentence: Conceptually, the network-attached block storage still presents raw blocks.

8013954e1f1d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
8013954e1f1d.sentence: To the servers, it works the same as physically attached block storage.

696620a2ed47.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
696620a2ed47.sentence: Whether to a network or physically attached, block storage is fully owned by a single server.

56b6c454884b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
56b6c454884b.sentence: It is not a shared resource.

10480337b7e4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
10480337b7e4.sentence: Volume is a fixed amount of storage on a disk or tape.

90a789aef168.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
90a789aef168.sentence: The term volume is often used as a synonym for the storage itself, but it is possible for a single disk to contain more than one volume or a volume to span more than one disk.

aeaeeff292fe.title: Computer data storage
aeaeeff292fe.sentence: - Block-level storage is a concept in cloud-hosted data persistence where cloud services emulate the behaviour of a traditional block device, such as a physical hard drive, where storage is organised as blocks.

47a58708ddc4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
47a58708ddc4.sentence: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks) is a way of storing the same data on multiple hard disks or solid-state drives (SSDs) to protect data in the case of a drive failure.

d2239c254ac6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
d2239c254ac6.sentence: There are different RAID levels, however, and not all have the goal of providing redundancy.

3608f7305613.title: RAID
3608f7305613.sentence: Instead of storing all data in a single hard disk drive or solid-state drive, RAID coordinates two or more such devices into a disk array.

5c1ccc87b0fe.title: RAID
5c1ccc87b0fe.sentence: When the computer writes data to secondary storage, the RAID system distributes the data across the array.

7d65189780d1.title: RAID
7d65189780d1.sentence: There are several possible ways of doing this, and those various configurations are called RAID levels.

d7406c095419.title: RAID
d7406c095419.sentence: RAID levels are distinguished by the amount of redundancy they afford and the minimum number of drives they require, as well as by their relative complexity, performance, energy efficiency, fault tolerance, and availability.

005b6b3cb7ad.title: RAID
005b6b3cb7ad.sentence: The definitive techniques used by RAID were conceived in the 1970s and 1980s: data striping to improve read/write efficiency, and disk mirroring or parity drives for data recovery.

4429da7252e2.title: RAID
4429da7252e2.sentence: Although incidence of hard disk drive failure rises in proportion to the number of drives in use, the reliability of an array could far exceed that of any single, high-capacity drive if one built redundancy into the computer storage system by configuring it to write data to more than one disk automatically.

5f9a2af65370.title: RAID
5f9a2af65370.sentence: Some RAID levels use parity data to increase fault tolerance.

c5f9e939093d.title: RAID
c5f9e939093d.sentence: Most parity data is calculated using XOR, but RAID 6 uses addition and multiplication in a particular Galois field or Reed–Solomon error correction.

5f759e9fd182.title: RAID
5f759e9fd182.sentence: With the exception of RAID 1, all of the standard RAID levels use storage virtualization to abstract multiple storage devices into one logical storage volume.

04b42673b046.title: RAID
04b42673b046.sentence: While RAID may protect against physical drive failure, the data is still exposed to operator, software, hardware, and virus destruction.

5f0a4582ac97.title: RAID
5f0a4582ac97.sentence: Many studies cite operator fault as a common source of malfunction, such as a server operator replacing the incorrect drive in a faulty RAID, and disabling the system (even temporarily) in the process.

83b7edd62711.title: RAID
83b7edd62711.sentence: An array can be overwhelmed by catastrophic failure that exceeds its recovery capacity and the entire array is at risk of physical damage by fire, natural disaster, and human forces, however backups can be stored off site.

c2c3ce8a37ad.title: ISCSI
c2c3ce8a37ad.sentence: Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI; /aɪˈskʌzi/ ⓘ eye-SKUZ-ee) is an Internet Protocol-based storage networking standard for linking data storage facilities. iSCSI provides block-level access to storage devices by carrying SCSI commands over a TCP/IP network. iSCSI facilitates data transfers over intranets and to manage storage over long distances.

57fa187bb8b7.title: ISCSI
57fa187bb8b7.sentence: The protocol allows clients (called initiators) to send SCSI commands (CDBs) to storage devices (targets) on remote servers.

a89d8addfe64.title: ISCSI
a89d8addfe64.sentence: It is a storage area network (SAN) protocol, allowing organizations to consolidate storage into storage arrays while providing clients (such as database and web servers) with the illusion of locally attached SCSI disks.

1f8fcab87421.title: ISCSI
1f8fcab87421.sentence: Unlike some SAN protocols, iSCSI requires no dedicated cabling; it can be run over existing IP infrastructure.

bffe38c554d2.title: ISCSI
bffe38c554d2.sentence: As a result, iSCSI is often seen as a low-cost alternative to Fibre Channel, which requires dedicated infrastructure except in its FCoE (Fibre Channel over Ethernet) form.

8b31fd0f363e.title: ISCSI
8b31fd0f363e.sentence: However, the performance of an iSCSI SAN deployment can be severely degraded if not operated on a dedicated network or subnet (LAN or VLAN), due to competition for a fixed amount of bandwidth.

53b565476edd.title: ISCSI
53b565476edd.sentence: In SCSI terminology, LU stands for logical unit, which is specified by a unique logical unit number.

81e5b6955a54.title: ISCSI
81e5b6955a54.sentence: A LUN represents an individually addressable (logical) SCSI device that is part of a physical SCSI device (target).

b44c0c17b0a8.title: ISCSI
b44c0c17b0a8.sentence: In an iSCSI environment, LUNs are essentially numbered disk drives.

07f1f8a29e39.title: ISCSI
07f1f8a29e39.sentence: In enterprise deployments, LUNs usually represent subsets of large RAID disk arrays, often allocated one per client. iSCSI imposes no rules or restrictions on multiple computers sharing individual LUNs; it leaves shared access to a single underlying filesystem as a task for the operating system.

8b014d5b7e44.title: ISCSI
8b014d5b7e44.sentence: Initiators treat iSCSI LUNs the same way as they would a raw SCSI or IDE hard drive; for instance, rather than mounting remote directories as would be done in NFS or CIFS environments, iSCSI systems format and directly manage filesystems on iSCSI LUNs.

0b98aead35cd.title: ISCSI
0b98aead35cd.sentence: Organizations move disparate storage resources from servers around their network to central locations, often in data centers; this allows for more efficiency in the allocation of storage, as the storage itself is no longer tied to a particular server.

1c6a58f0d65e.title: ISCSI
1c6a58f0d65e.sentence: In a SAN environment, a server can be allocated a new disk volume without any changes to hardware or cabling.

5e3135c0d789.title: ISCSI
5e3135c0d789.sentence: Organizations mirror storage resources from one data center to a remote data center, which can serve as a hot / standby in the event of a prolonged outage.

6fa12e29f23e.title: ISCSI
6fa12e29f23e.sentence: In particular, iSCSI SANs allow entire disk arrays to be migrated across a WAN with minimal configuration changes, in effect making storage "routable" in the same manner as network traffic.

9c159d0fc417.title: ISCSI
9c159d0fc417.sentence: Software initiators are available for most popular operating systems and are the most common method of deploying iSCSI.

dc16774cd5af.title: ISCSI
dc16774cd5af.sentence: Typically, this happens in a kernel-resident device driver that uses the existing network card (NIC) and network stack to emulate SCSI devices for a computer by speaking the iSCSI protocol.

5bb54b7b3d13.title: ISCSI
5bb54b7b3d13.sentence: A hardware initiator uses dedicated hardware, typically in combination with firmware running on that hardware, to implement iSCSI.

27029d79f4ce.title: ISCSI
27029d79f4ce.sentence: A hardware initiator mitigates the overhead of iSCSI and TCP processing and Ethernet interrupts, and therefore may improve the performance of servers that use iSCSI.

957b58fafe66.title: ISCSI
957b58fafe66.sentence: An iSOE "offloads" the iSCSI initiator operations for this particular network interface from the host processor, freeing up CPU cycles for the main host applications. iSCSI HBAs or iSOEs are used when the additional performance enhancement justifies the additional expense of using an HBA for iSCSI, rather than using a software-based iSCSI client (initiator). iSOE may be implemented with additional services such as TCP offload engine (TOE) to further reduce host server CPU usage.

503b2ce83fe9.title: ISCSI
503b2ce83fe9.sentence: iSCSI uses TCP (typically TCP ports 860 and 3260) for the protocols itself, with higher-level names used to address the objects within the protocol.

5a1edc0d8a8f.title: ISCSI
5a1edc0d8a8f.sentence: For the most part, iSCSI operates as a cleartext protocol that provides no cryptographic protection for data in motion during SCSI transactions.

a033f68ee5de.title: ISCSI
a033f68ee5de.sentence: To ensure that only valid initiators connect to storage arrays, administrators most commonly run iSCSI only over logically isolated backchannel networks.

b9547b4625dc.title: ISCSI
b9547b4625dc.sentence: iSCSI initiators and targets prove their identity to each other using CHAP, which includes a mechanism to prevent cleartext passwords from appearing on the wire.

13e06960592c.title: RAID
13e06960592c.sentence: Data scrubbing (referred to in some environments as patrol read) involves periodic reading and checking by the RAID controller of all the blocks in an array, including those not otherwise accessed.

29e2ea1c4d14.title: RAID
29e2ea1c4d14.sentence: This detects bad blocks before use.

45bbf70eb759.title: RAID
45bbf70eb759.sentence: Data scrubbing checks for bad blocks on each storage device in an array, but also uses the redundancy of the array to recover bad blocks on a single drive and to reassign the recovered data to spare blocks elsewhere on the drive.

b4adf8d1fc5f.title: RAID
b4adf8d1fc5f.section: Weaknesses > Unrecoverable read errors during rebuild
b4adf8d1fc5f.sentence: The recovery of UREs involves remapping of affected underlying disk sectors, utilizing the drive's sector remapping pool; in case of UREs detected during background scrubbing, data redundancy provided by a fully operational RAID set allows the missing data to be reconstructed and rewritten to a remapped sector.

404e192679c7.title: RAID
404e192679c7.section: Weaknesses > Unrecoverable read errors during rebuild
404e192679c7.sentence: Data scrubbing, as a background process, can be used to detect and recover from UREs, effectively reducing the risk of them happening during RAID rebuilds and causing double-drive failures.

f149b1487c03.title: RAID
f149b1487c03.sentence: The distribution of data across multiple drives can be managed either by dedicated computer hardware or by software.

5eb58949f00a.title: RAID
5eb58949f00a.sentence: A software solution may be part of the operating system, part of the firmware and drivers supplied with a standard drive controller (so-called "hardware-assisted software RAID"), or it may reside entirely within the hardware RAID controller.

8585535b3293.title: RAID
8585535b3293.sentence: However, hardware RAID controllers are expensive and proprietary.

dd16932e583f.title: RAID
dd16932e583f.sentence: Unlike the network interface controllers for Ethernet, which can usually be configured and serviced entirely through the common operating system paradigms like ifconfig in Unix, without a need for any third-party tools, each manufacturer of each RAID controller usually provides their own proprietary software tooling for each operating system that they deem to support, ensuring a vendor lock-in, and contributing to reliability issues.

195c551725bd.title: RAID
195c551725bd.sentence: Software RAID implementations are provided by many modern operating systems.

5ff75f02f8c9.title: RAID
5ff75f02f8c9.sentence: - A layer that abstracts multiple devices, thereby providing a single virtual device (such as Linux kernel's md and OpenBSD's softraid)

8401f933aa24.title: RAID
8401f933aa24.sentence: - A more generic logical volume manager (provided with most server-class operating systems such as Veritas or LVM)

54ce0b9399a3.title: RAID
54ce0b9399a3.sentence: - A component of the file system (such as ZFS, Spectrum Scale or Btrfs)

a2bc20b29203.title: RAID
a2bc20b29203.sentence: To fill this gap, inexpensive "RAID controllers" were introduced that do not contain a dedicated RAID controller chip, but simply a standard drive controller chip, or the chipset built-in RAID function, with proprietary firmware and drivers.

2170226633b7.title: RAID
2170226633b7.sentence: During early bootup, the RAID is implemented by the firmware and, once the operating system has been more completely loaded, the drivers take over control.

1d0256b92fe8.title: RAID
1d0256b92fe8.sentence: Consequently, such controllers may not work when driver support is not available for the host operating system.

03fc71ebc77e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
03fc71ebc77e.sentence: File storage is a solution to store data as files and present it to its final users as a hierarchical directories structure.

bb28f48d5a40.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
bb28f48d5a40.sentence: File storage is built on top of block storage.

5959ecb84793.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
5959ecb84793.sentence: It provides a higher-level abstraction to make it easier to handle files and directories.

6cf9705d9eef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
6cf9705d9eef.sentence: To locate a file in file storage, the complete path of the file is required.

6a476c91e507.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
6a476c91e507.sentence: File storage is the most common general-purpose storage solution.

a886a445190d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
a886a445190d.sentence: The main advantage is to provide a user-friendly solution to store and retrieve files.

e51297545492.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
e51297545492.sentence: It is economical and easily structured and is usually found on hard drives, which means that they appear exactly the same for the user and on the hard drive.

7aa34e497753.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
7aa34e497753.sentence: File storage could be made accessible by a large number of servers using common file-level network protocols like SMB/CIFS and NFS.

88d744600243.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
88d744600243.sentence: The servers accessing file storage do not need to deal with the complexity of managing the blocks, formatting volume, etc. The simplicity of file storage makes it a great solution for sharing a large number of files and folders within an organization.

ce6685c908ae.title: Computer data storage
ce6685c908ae.sentence: Secondary storage is often formatted according to a file system format, which provides the abstraction necessary to organize data into files and directories, while also providing metadata describing the owner of a certain file, the access time, the access permissions, and other information.

40328150b012.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
40328150b012.sentence: Example: Amazon EFS, Azure files, Google Cloud Filestore, etc.

e70b9ea30410.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
e70b9ea30410.sentence: Object storage, which is also known as object-based storage, breaks data files up into pieces called objects.

1886de092076.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
1886de092076.sentence: It then stores those objects in a single repository, which can be spread out across multiple networked systems.

d25100857506.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
d25100857506.sentence: Object storage stores all data as objects in a flat structure.

f1ad183c79bb.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
f1ad183c79bb.sentence: There is no hierarchical directory structure.

6b697b7364b7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explain-the-top-6-use-cases-of-object-stores.md
6b697b7364b7.sentence: Compared with file storage which uses a hierarchical structure to store files, or block storage which divides files into equal block sizes, object storage stores metadata together with the objects.

1bf06f9e911d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
1bf06f9e911d.sentence: It makes a very deliberate tradeoff to sacrifice performance for high durability, vast scale, and low cost.

6542d688a306.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
6542d688a306.sentence: It is relatively slow compared to other storage types.

b9b25652f2a1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
b9b25652f2a1.sentence: It targets relatively “cold” data and is mainly used for archival and backup.

df2e738d2f03.title: Object storage
df2e738d2f03.sentence: Each object is typically associated with a variable amount of metadata, and a globally unique identifier.

6ecf30cd4adc.title: Object storage
6ecf30cd4adc.section: Architecture > Inclusion of rich custom metadata within the object
6ecf30cd4adc.sentence: As opposed to fixed metadata in file systems (filename, creation date, type, etc.), object storage provides for full function, custom, object-level metadata in order to:

c79324e9f363.title: Object storage
c79324e9f363.section: Architecture > Inclusion of rich custom metadata within the object
c79324e9f363.sentence: - Capture application-specific or user-specific information for better indexing purposes

f667c307b177.title: Object storage
f667c307b177.section: Architecture > Inclusion of rich custom metadata within the object
f667c307b177.sentence: - Support data-management policies (e.g. a policy to drive object movement from one storage tier to another)

69a3a561e19a.title: Object storage
69a3a561e19a.section: Architecture > Inclusion of rich custom metadata within the object
69a3a561e19a.sentence: - Centralize management of storage across many individual nodes and clusters

b53c58ddd9ea.title: Object storage
b53c58ddd9ea.sentence: Object storage provides programmatic interfaces to allow applications to manipulate data.

a1bb30278d23.title: Object storage
a1bb30278d23.sentence: At the base level, this includes Create, read, update and delete (CRUD) functions for basic read, write and delete operations.

1ab41e21f6e7.title: Object storage
1ab41e21f6e7.sentence: Some object storage implementations go further, supporting additional functionality like object/file versioning, object replication, life-cycle management and movement of objects between different tiers and types of storage.

47f75c2c2f92.title: Object storage
47f75c2c2f92.sentence: Most API implementations are REST-based, allowing the use of many standard HTTP calls.

e83d04c1e4b2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/storage-systems-overview.md
e83d04c1e4b2.sentence: Data access is normally provided via a RESTful API.

c5094ad1bcad.title: Object storage
c5094ad1bcad.sentence: One of the design principles of object storage is to abstract some of the lower layers of storage away from the administrators and applications.

6f8220f78611.title: Object storage
6f8220f78611.sentence: Administrators do not have to perform lower-level storage functions like constructing and managing logical volumes to utilize disk capacity or setting RAID levels to deal with disk failure.

f80f4ec629e1.title: Object storage
f80f4ec629e1.sentence: Object storage adds a unique identifier within a bucket, or across the entire system, to support much larger namespaces and eliminate name collisions.

c8a0425e51a1.title: Object storage
c8a0425e51a1.sentence: Object storage systems allow retention of massive amounts of unstructured data in which data is written once and read once (or many times).

58e7f6295076.title: Object storage
58e7f6295076.sentence: One of the limitations with object storage is that it is not intended for transactional data, as object storage was not designed to replace NAS file access and sharing; it does not support the locking and sharing mechanisms needed to maintain a single, accurately updated version of a file.

ff3ccd9d0b69.title: Object storage
ff3ccd9d0b69.sentence: The vast majority of cloud storage available in the market leverages an object-storage architecture.

6ec43e5a626e.title: Object storage
6ec43e5a626e.sentence: Some notable examples are Amazon S3, which debuted in March 2006, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, IBM Cloud Object Storage, Rackspace Cloud Files (whose code was donated in 2010 to Openstack project and released as OpenStack Swift), and Google Cloud Storage released in May 2010.

0231afc4537e.title: Computer data storage
0231afc4537e.sentence: Cloud storage is based on highly virtualized infrastructure.

1c61c471fa33.title: Computer data storage
1c61c471fa33.sentence: A subset of cloud computing, it has particular cloud-native interfaces, near-instant elasticity and scalability, multi-tenancy, and metered resources.

09e511ab8d46.title: Computer data storage
09e511ab8d46.sentence: Cloud storage services can be used from an off-premises service or deployed on-premises.

e894c12d13c0.title: Computer data storage
e894c12d13c0.sentence: There are three types of cloud storage:

cf4e592c8ab6.title: Computer data storage
cf4e592c8ab6.sentence: - Instance stores are a form of cloud-hosted block-level storage, being provided as part of a cloud instance.

c928c174af1f.title: Computer data storage
c928c174af1f.sentence: Unlike other forms of block storage, instance store data will be lost the cloud instance is stopped.

9e84b2a58533.title: Amazon S3
9e84b2a58533.sentence: Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is a service offered by Amazon Web Services (AWS) that provides object storage through a web service interface.

f7d0ff9ddc8d.title: Amazon S3
f7d0ff9ddc8d.sentence: Amazon S3 manages data with an object storage architecture which aims to provide scalability, high availability, and low latency with high durability.

295b538bce1f.title: Amazon S3
295b538bce1f.sentence: Amazon S3 can store any type of object, which allows uses like storage for Internet applications, backups, disaster recovery, data archives, data lakes for analytics, and hybrid cloud storage.

d0d862b9d228.title: Amazon S3
d0d862b9d228.sentence: The basic storage units of Amazon S3 are objects which are organized into buckets.

893d1bdc6e54.title: Amazon S3
893d1bdc6e54.sentence: Each object is identified by a unique, user-assigned key.

1a0e57a1dcca.title: Amazon S3
1a0e57a1dcca.sentence: Buckets can be managed using the console provided by Amazon S3, programmatically with the AWS SDK, or the REST application programming interface.

dd3f48c58e33.title: Amazon S3
dd3f48c58e33.sentence: An object in S3 can be between 0 bytes and 5 TB.

9ab8c9b8f55c.title: Amazon S3
9ab8c9b8f55c.sentence: If an object is larger than 5 GB, it must be divided into chunks prior to uploading.

1a70facc3762.title: Amazon S3
1a70facc3762.sentence: When uploading, Amazon S3 allows a maximum of 5 GB in a single upload operation; hence, objects larger than 5 GB must be uploaded via the S3 multipart upload API.

1c8a521808b6.title: Amazon S3
1c8a521808b6.sentence: Requests are authorized using an access control list associated with each object bucket and support versioning which is disabled by default.

5b5c9f9286b3.title: Amazon S3
5b5c9f9286b3.sentence: The Amazon AWS authentication mechanism allows the creation of authenticated URLs, valid for a specified amount of time.

29aa4f546660.title: Amazon S3
29aa4f546660.section: Technical details > Amazon S3 storage classes
29aa4f546660.sentence: Amazon S3 offers nine different storage classes with different levels of durability, availability, and performance requirements.

39594d4b8bda.title: Amazon S3
39594d4b8bda.section: Technical details > Amazon S3 storage classes
39594d4b8bda.sentence: - Amazon S3 Standard is the default.

fecf435626f2.title: Amazon S3
fecf435626f2.section: Technical details > Amazon S3 storage classes
fecf435626f2.sentence: It is general purpose storage for frequently accessed data.

76bafb7eb7c8.title: Amazon S3
76bafb7eb7c8.section: Technical details > Amazon S3 storage classes
76bafb7eb7c8.sentence: - Amazon S3 Express One Zone is a single-digit millisecond latency storage for frequently accessed data and latency-sensitive applications.

cc8059f1f511.title: Amazon S3
cc8059f1f511.section: Technical details > Amazon S3 storage classes
cc8059f1f511.sentence: It stores data only in one availability zone.

ca193e7e2f74.title: Amazon S3
ca193e7e2f74.sentence: Various User Mode File System (FUSE)–based file systems for Linux or other Unix-like operating systems can be used to mount an S3 bucket as a file system.

8ef007dd856d.title: Amazon S3
8ef007dd856d.sentence: The semantics of the Amazon S3 file system are not that of a POSIX file system, so the file system may not behave entirely as expected.

5eef9601df06.title: Amazon S3
5eef9601df06.sentence: As of 2025, S3 stores 500 trillion objects, 100s of exabytes of data, serves 200 million requests per second, and peaks at about 1 petabyte per second in bandwidth.

41445b9b7af2.title: Amazon S3
41445b9b7af2.sentence: The broad adoption of Amazon S3 and related tooling has given rise to competing services based on the S3 API.

854c891b4f02.title: Amazon S3
854c891b4f02.sentence: Users are not required to go directly to Amazon as several storage providers such as Cloudian, Backblaze B2, Wasabi offer S3-compatible storage with options of on-premises and private cloud deployments.

7748435210bc.title: Amazon S3
7748435210bc.sentence: Several open-source implementations of S3-compatible object store servers can be self-hosted, such as Garage.

985a619ae9b9.title: Computer data storage
985a619ae9b9.sentence: - Direct-attached storage (DAS) is a traditional mass storage that does not use any network.

cbe40dc20851.title: Computer data storage
cbe40dc20851.sentence: - Network-attached storage (NAS) is mass storage attached to a computer that another computer can access at file level over a local area network, a private wide area network, or in the case of online file storage, over the Internet.

997f79b08690.title: Computer data storage
997f79b08690.sentence: - Storage area network (SAN) is a specialized network that provides other computers with storage capacity.

b6d02aaf8d33.title: Computer data storage
b6d02aaf8d33.sentence: Secondary or tertiary storage may connect to a computer utilizing computer networks.

29dcad62dcd7.title: Computer data storage
29dcad62dcd7.sentence: This concept does not pertain to the primary storage.

b8ed067d5512.title: Computer data storage
b8ed067d5512.sentence: NAS is commonly associated with the Network File System and Server Message Block protocol.

c494d13cf371.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
c494d13cf371.sentence: A NAS (Network Attached Storage) is a storage device connected to a network that allows storage and retrieval of data from a central location for authorized network users.

c3f554612377.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
c3f554612377.sentence: NAS devices are flexible, meaning that as we need additional storage, we can add to what we have.

43e024bc8448.title: Computer data storage
43e024bc8448.sentence: SAN is commonly associated with Fibre Channel networks.

32883d71109f.title: Computer data storage
32883d71109f.sentence: At one time, block-level storage was provided by SAN, and NAS provided file-level storage.

4d58508cc580.title: Computer data storage
4d58508cc580.sentence: With the shift from on-premises hosting to cloud services, this distinction has shifted.

684aa494f772.title: Fibre Channel
684aa494f772.sentence: Fibre Channel (FC) is a high-speed data transfer protocol providing in-order, lossless delivery of raw block data.

ae66e807864a.title: Fibre Channel
ae66e807864a.sentence: Fibre Channel is primarily used to connect computer data storage to servers in storage area networks (SAN) in commercial data centers.

22be5f77fed0.title: Fibre Channel
22be5f77fed0.sentence: Two major characteristics of Fibre Channel networks are in-order delivery and lossless delivery of raw block data.

4c827093f7a1.title: Fibre Channel
4c827093f7a1.sentence: Lossless delivery of raw data block is achieved based on a credit mechanism.

60698a381933.title: Fibre Channel
60698a381933.sentence: The SAN is a dedicated network that enables multiple servers to access data from one or more storage devices.

0f713029c289.title: Fibre Channel
0f713029c289.sentence: The goal of Fibre Channel is to create a storage area network (SAN) to connect servers to storage.

d942af7271c6.title: Fibre Channel
d942af7271c6.sentence: Fibre Channel Protocol (FCP) is a protocol that transports SCSI commands over Fibre Channel networks.

924b3f1dee76.title: Fibre Channel
924b3f1dee76.sentence: FICON is a protocol that transports ESCON commands, used by IBM mainframe computers, over Fibre Channel.

c70c92061ca3.title: Fibre Channel
c70c92061ca3.sentence: Fibre Channel can be used to transport data from storage systems that use solid-state flash memory storage medium by transporting NVMe protocol commands.

0cdb4cd85d69.title: Fibre Channel
0cdb4cd85d69.sentence: There are three major Fibre Channel topologies, describing how a number of ports are connected together.

b20c5b8511d3.title: Fibre Channel
b20c5b8511d3.sentence: Two devices are connected directly to each other using Node ports.

7f1d4d9dd544.title: Fibre Channel
7f1d4d9dd544.sentence: In this design, all devices are in a loop or ring, similar to Token Ring networking.

2e83bbf01c59.title: Fibre Channel
2e83bbf01c59.sentence: - Only one pair of ports can communicate concurrently on a loop.

a285450d7bfa.title: Fibre Channel
a285450d7bfa.sentence: The failure of one device causes a break in the ring.

25a0f34df22e.title: Fibre Channel
25a0f34df22e.sentence: - Arbitrated loop has been rarely used after 2010 and its support is being discontinued for new-generation switches.

491675ab515e.title: Fibre Channel
491675ab515e.sentence: In this design, all devices are connected to Fibre Channel switches, similar conceptually to modern Ethernet implementations.

dff389776f13.title: Fibre Channel
dff389776f13.sentence: - The Fabric can scale to tens of thousands of ports.

5a5955096b89.title: Fibre Channel
5a5955096b89.sentence: - The switches manage the state of the Fabric, providing optimized paths via Fabric Shortest Path First (FSPF) data routing protocol.

afd9e23945d0.title: Fibre Channel
afd9e23945d0.sentence: - Multiple pairs of ports may communicate simultaneously in a Fabric.

35b386b527ae.title: Fibre Channel
35b386b527ae.sentence: - Failure of a port is isolated to a link and should not affect operation of other ports.

7b5d554053f2.title: Fibre Channel
7b5d554053f2.sentence: SANs are often designed with dual fabrics to increase fault tolerance.

34187ae24f10.title: Fibre Channel
34187ae24f10.sentence: Two completely separate fabrics are operational and if the primary fabric fails, then the second fabric becomes the primary.

fbe40666a74f.title: Fibre Channel
fbe40666a74f.sentence: HBAs connect servers to the Fibre Channel network and are part of a class of devices known as translation devices.

c44d5305d77b.title: Fibre Channel
c44d5305d77b.sentence: Each HBA has a unique World Wide Name (WWN), which is similar to an Ethernet MAC address in that it uses an Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI) assigned by the IEEE.

28914b46d923.title: Fibre Channel
28914b46d923.sentence: There are two types of WWNs on an HBA; a World Wide Node Name (WWNN), which can be shared by some or all ports of a device, and a World Wide Port Name (WWPN), which is necessarily unique to each port.

1af8430d55fe.title: Fibre Channel
1af8430d55fe.sentence: Fibre Channel does not follow the OSI model layering, and is split into five layers:

5e738094bb64.title: Fibre Channel
5e738094bb64.sentence: - FC-4 – Protocol-mapping layer, in which upper-level protocols such as NVM Express (NVMe), SCSI, IP, and FICON are encapsulated into Information Units (IUs) for delivery to FC-2.

3b6a61aa0806.title: Fibre Channel
3b6a61aa0806.sentence: - FC-0 – physical layer, defined by Fibre Channel Physical Interfaces standard, includes cabling, connectors etc.;

75a8da0cdeb4.title: Fibre Channel
75a8da0cdeb4.sentence: Supported data rates include 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 gigabit per second resulting from improvements in successive technology generations.

abbd20649aa5.title: Network File System
abbd20649aa5.sentence: Network File System (NFS) is a distributed file system protocol originally developed by Sun Microsystems (Sun) in 1984, allowing a user on a client computer to access files over a computer network much like local storage is accessed.

295c4261b737.title: Network File System
295c4261b737.sentence: NFS, like many other protocols, builds on the Open Network Computing Remote Procedure Call (ONC RPC) system.

3243eaa0150f.title: Network File System
3243eaa0150f.sentence: After the first experimental version developed in house at Sun Microsystems, all subsequent versions of the protocol are defined in a series of Request for Comments i.e. RFCs, allowing anyone to implement the protocol.

6c4636040007.title: Network File System
6c4636040007.sentence: Version 2 of the protocol (defined in RFC 1094, March 1989) originally operated only over User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

ec4a77caa290.title: Network File System
ec4a77caa290.sentence: Its designers meant to keep the server side stateless, with locking (for example) implemented outside of the core protocol.

a5a0d55f3a68.title: Network File System
a5a0d55f3a68.sentence: NFSv2 only allows the first 2 GB of a file to be read due to 32-bit limitations.

87e6693087af.title: Network File System
87e6693087af.sentence: - support for 64-bit file sizes and offsets, to handle files larger than 2 gigabytes (GB);

f8a1c8347e56.title: Network File System
f8a1c8347e56.sentence: - support for asynchronous writes on the server, to improve write performance;

fac3fa0a08f1.title: Network File System
fac3fa0a08f1.sentence: The principal motivation was an attempt to mitigate the performance issue of the synchronous write operation in NFS Version 2.

64e4756152b9.title: Network File System
64e4756152b9.sentence: - a READDIRPLUS operation, to get file handles and attributes along with file names when scanning a directory;

e3b2b30b8c9b.title: Network File System
e3b2b30b8c9b.sentence: Using TCP as a transport made using NFS over a WAN more feasible, and allowed the use of larger read and write transfer sizes beyond the 8 KB limit imposed by User Datagram Protocol.

897b0e09940c.title: Network File System
897b0e09940c.sentence: Version 4 (RFC 3010, December 2000; revised in RFC 3530, April 2003 and again in RFC 7530, March 2015), influenced by Andrew File System (AFS) and Server Message Block (SMB), includes performance improvements, mandates strong security, and introduces a stateful protocol.

022f456def7e.title: Network File System
022f456def7e.sentence: One big advantage of NFSv4 over its predecessors is that only one UDP or TCP port, 2049, is used to run the service, which simplifies using the protocol across firewalls.

41fc1a73e9ba.title: Network File System
41fc1a73e9ba.sentence: NFS version 4.1 (RFC 5661, January 2010; revised in RFC 8881, August 2020) aims to provide protocol support to take advantage of clustered server deployments including the ability to provide scalable parallel access to files distributed among multiple servers (pNFS extension).

ad7d4aedbb96.title: Network File System
ad7d4aedbb96.sentence: NFS version 4.2 (RFC 7862) was published in November 2016 with new features including: server-side clone and copy, application I/O advise, sparse files, space reservation, application data block (ADB), labeled NFS with sec_label that accommodates any MAC security system, and two new operations for pNFS (LAYOUTERROR and LAYOUTSTATS).

9ea6efe843ac.title: Network File System
9ea6efe843ac.sentence: - Unix-like operating systems (Solaris, AIX, HP-UX, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, DragonFly BSD, Linux distributions, and macOS, although the default networking protocol in macOS is Server Message Block (SMB))

cb241597ac4b.title: Network File System
cb241597ac4b.sentence: - Microsoft Windows, although the default networking protocol is Server Message Block (SMB)

189b4b079a73.title: Server Message Block
189b4b079a73.sentence: Server Message Block (SMB) is a communication protocol used to share files, printers, serial ports, and miscellaneous communications between nodes on a network.

a03897e04ec7.title: Server Message Block
a03897e04ec7.sentence: Server Message Block (SMB) enables file sharing, printer sharing, network browsing, and inter-process communication (through named pipes) over a computer network.

57711977319b.title: Server Message Block
57711977319b.sentence: SMB relies on the TCP and IP protocols for transport.

d42e4f3f6a41.title: Server Message Block
d42e4f3f6a41.sentence: This combination allows file sharing over complex, interconnected networks, including the public Internet.

cd1c70226e8e.title: Server Message Block
cd1c70226e8e.sentence: The SMB server component uses TCP port 445.

4e013d12a2df.title: Server Message Block
4e013d12a2df.sentence: SMB uses the Kerberos protocol to authenticate users against Active Directory on Windows domain networks.

1bad82f638da.title: Server Message Block
1bad82f638da.sentence: On simpler, peer-to-peer networks, SMB uses the NTLM protocol.

840f7b050111.title: Server Message Block
840f7b050111.sentence: Windows NT 4.0 SP3 and later can digitally sign SMB messages to prevent some man-in-the-middle attacks.

5638a2c06d2b.title: Server Message Block
5638a2c06d2b.sentence: Network designers have found that latency has a significant impact on the performance of the SMB 1.0 protocol, that it performs more poorly than other protocols like FTP.

0d7accede287.title: Server Message Block
0d7accede287.sentence: Monitoring reveals a high degree of "chattiness" and a disregard of network latency between hosts.

5ad98372bc17.title: Server Message Block
5ad98372bc17.sentence: Microsoft has explained that performance issues come about primarily because SMB 1.0 is a block-level rather than a streaming protocol, that was originally designed for small LANs; it has a block size that is limited to 64K, SMB signing creates an additional overhead and the TCP window size is not optimized for WAN links.

a061715a5ad1.title: Server Message Block
a061715a5ad1.sentence: SMB2 reduces the 'chattiness' of the SMB 1.0 protocol by reducing the number of commands and subcommands from over a hundred to just nineteen.

c87686055b57.title: Server Message Block
c87686055b57.sentence: It has mechanisms for pipelining, that is, sending additional requests before the response to a previous request arrives, thereby improving performance over high-latency links.

ca32067cdfbb.title: Server Message Block
ca32067cdfbb.sentence: It adds the ability to compound multiple actions into a single request, which significantly reduces the number of round-trips the client needs to make to the server, improving performance as a result.

6ac82083ba0e.title: Server Message Block
6ac82083ba0e.sentence: It brought several significant changes that are intended to add functionality and improve SMB2 performance, notably in virtualized data centers:

3cdc89264a3b.title: Server Message Block
3cdc89264a3b.sentence: - the SMB Direct Protocol (SMB over remote direct memory access [RDMA])

064ee81f6bb1.title: Server Message Block
064ee81f6bb1.sentence: - SMB Multichannel (multiple connections per SMB session),

1578ca3fa1ba.title: Server Message Block
1578ca3fa1ba.sentence: It also introduces several security enhancements, such as end-to-end encryption and a new AES based signing algorithm.

57b67c788ce3.title: Server Message Block
57b67c788ce3.sentence: SMB over QUIC was introduced in Windows Server 2022 as part of the Azure Edition, providing a secure alternative to VPN for remote file access over untrusted networks such as the internet.

4e19fb4f8366.title: Server Message Block
4e19fb4f8366.sentence: It uses QUIC as a transport layer, creating a TLS 1.3-encrypted tunnel over UDP port 443 instead of the legacy TCP port 445, so that no SMB traffic — including authentication — is exposed to the underlying network.

9351708371ba.title: Server Message Block
9351708371ba.sentence: In 1996, Microsoft published a version of SMB 1.0 with minor modifications under the Common Internet File System (CIFS /sɪfs/) moniker.

4f92859f184f.title: Server Message Block
4f92859f184f.sentence: It supports symbolic links, hard links, and larger file size, but none of the features of SMB 2.0 and later.

8198f7848d93.title: Server Message Block
8198f7848d93.sentence: Microsoft has since discontinued the CIFS moniker but continues developing SMB and publishing subsequent specifications.

ff91d3b65eda.title: Server Message Block
ff91d3b65eda.sentence: Samba is a free software reimplementation of the SMB protocol and the Microsoft extensions to it.

3b908798fd30.title: Server Message Block
3b908798fd30.sentence: Because of the importance of the SMB protocol in interacting with the widespread Microsoft Windows platform, Samba became a popular free software implementation of a compatible SMB client and server to allow non-Windows operating systems, such as Unix-like operating systems, to interoperate with Windows.

e6badfb67682.title: Solid-state drive
e6badfb67682.sentence: In a distributed computing environment, SSDs can be used as a distributed cache layer that temporarily absorbs the large volume of user requests to slower HDD-based backend storage systems.

b58936d09e35.title: Solid-state drive
b58936d09e35.sentence: This layer provides much higher bandwidth and lower latency than the storage system would, and can be managed in a number of forms, such as a distributed key-value database and a distributed file system.

6a20aa1b086b.title: Solid-state drive
6a20aa1b086b.sentence: On supercomputers, this layer is typically referred to as burst buffer.

d74ad3efb71e.title: Solid-state drive
d74ad3efb71e.sentence: In 2011, Intel introduced a caching mechanism for their Z68 chipset (and mobile derivatives) called Smart Response Technology, which allows a SATA SSD to be used as a cache (configurable as write-through or write-back) for a conventional, magnetic hard disk drive.

d226fc2f8118.title: Solid-state drive
d226fc2f8118.sentence: Solid-state hybrid drives (SSHDs) are based on the same principle, but integrate some amount of flash memory on board of a conventional drive instead of using a separate SSD.

48dfac28a62e.title: Solid-state drive
48dfac28a62e.sentence: Dual-drive hybrid systems are combining the usage of separate SSD and HDD devices installed in the same computer, with overall performance optimization managed by the computer user, or by the computer's operating system software.

fc6528e4f5a8.title: Solid-state drive
fc6528e4f5a8.sentence: Examples of this type of system are bcache and dm-cache on Linux, and Apple's Fusion Drive.

5412a536626e.title: Solid-state drive
5412a536626e.sentence: A low-latency SSD can be used for the ZFS Intent Log (ZIL), where it is named the SLOG.

372f2196ac87.title: Solid-state drive
372f2196ac87.sentence: An SSD may also be used for the level 2 Adaptive Replacement Cache (L2ARC), which is used to cache data for reading.

18c308cf7385.title: Solid-state drive
18c308cf7385.sentence: The endurance of an SSD is typically listed on its datasheet in one of two forms:

575329663c55.title: Solid-state drive
575329663c55.sentence: - either n DW/D (n drive writes per day)

f04d6398cee0.title: Solid-state drive
f04d6398cee0.sentence: - or m TBW (maximum terabytes written), abbreviated TBW.

980b65c149f6.title: Solid-state drive
980b65c149f6.sentence: The JEDEC Solid State Technology Association (JEDEC) has established standards for SSD reliability metrics, which include:

aa8fdff25ebc.title: Solid-state drive
aa8fdff25ebc.sentence: - Terabytes Written (TBW) – the total number of terabytes that can be written to a drive within its warranty period

afb9cd44e8da.title: Solid-state drive
afb9cd44e8da.sentence: - Drive Writes Per Day (DWPD) – the number of times the full capacity of the drive can be written to per day within its warranty period

eeba1a7d9fc7.title: Solid-state drive
eeba1a7d9fc7.sentence: The basic parameter for determining the lifespan of Flash-NAND systems is the number of programming-erase (P/E) cycles.

f3879c87a8a1.title: Solid-state drive
f3879c87a8a1.sentence: The TBW parameter is the product of the P/E cycle resource and the SSD capacity.

3dc083092dab.title: Solid-state drive
3dc083092dab.sentence: For an SSD with a capacity of 1 TB and TBW = 600 TB, the number of P/E cycles is 600.

33a67a243a12.title: Solid-state drive
33a67a243a12.section: Attributes > Comparison with other technologies > Hard disk drives
33a67a243a12.sentence: Reliability – data retention | If the nominal written life of SSDs (the terabytes written) is reached, the SSDs may start losing data after three months (enterprise SSDs) or one year (consumer SSDs) without power, especially at high temperatures. Newer SSDs, depending on usage, may retain data longer. SSDs are generally not suited for long-term archival storage. | HDDs, when stored in a cool, dry environment, can retain data for longer periods without power. However, over time, mechanical parts may fail, such as the inability to spin up after prolonged storage.

608caeeb80cb.title: Solid-state drive
608caeeb80cb.sentence: SSDs have a limited lifetime number of writes, and also slow down as they reach their full storage capacity.

fd922b4130a4.title: Solid-state drive
fd922b4130a4.section: Architecture and function > Controller > Wear leveling
fd922b4130a4.sentence: Wear leveling is a technique used in SSDs to ensure that write and erase operations are distributed evenly across all blocks of the flash memory.

226e4b1a9ffc.title: Solid-state drive
226e4b1a9ffc.section: Architecture and function > Controller > Wear leveling
226e4b1a9ffc.sentence: Without this, specific blocks could wear out prematurely due to repeated use, reducing the overall lifespan of the SSD.

2c0a58e43db5.title: Solid-state drive
2c0a58e43db5.section: Architecture and function > Controller > Wear leveling
2c0a58e43db5.sentence: The process moves data that is infrequently changed (cold data) from heavily used blocks, so that data that changes more frequently (hot data) can be written to those blocks.

fd67b8c459f6.title: Solid-state drive
fd67b8c459f6.section: Architecture and function > Controller > Wear leveling
fd67b8c459f6.sentence: This helps distribute wear more evenly across the entire SSD.

479f3fcdcdce.title: Solid-state drive
479f3fcdcdce.section: Architecture and function > Controller > Wear leveling
479f3fcdcdce.sentence: However, this process introduces additional writes, known as write amplification, which must be managed to balance performance and durability.

ae4bb4394041.title: Solid-state drive
ae4bb4394041.section: Attributes > Comparison with other technologies > Hard disk drives
ae4bb4394041.sentence: In traditional HDDs, a rewritten file will generally occupy the same location on the disk surface as the original file, whereas in SSDs the new copy will often be written to different NAND cells for the purpose of wear leveling.

c60d3a7f634f.title: Solid-state drive
c60d3a7f634f.sentence: The file system does not need to manage wear leveling or other flash memory characteristics, as they are handled internally by the SSD.

21aec0daa6e4.title: Solid-state drive
21aec0daa6e4.sentence: File systems that support SSDs generally also support the TRIM command, which helps the SSD to recycle discarded data.

04b28a4ad16b.title: Solid-state drive
04b28a4ad16b.sentence: Windows 7 also includes support for the TRIM command to reduce garbage collection for data that the operating system has already determined is no longer valid.

f8a5b08d6a2c.title: Solid-state drive
f8a5b08d6a2c.sentence: Some log-structured file systems (e.g. F2FS, JFFS2) help to reduce write amplification on SSDs, especially in situations where only very small amounts of data are changed, such as when updating file-system metadata.

91a212f93bb8.title: Network File System
91a212f93bb8.sentence: The NFSv4.1 protocol defines a method of separating the filesystem meta-data from file data location; it goes beyond the simple name/data separation by striping the data amongst a set of data servers.

9b47d481a1dd.title: Network File System
9b47d481a1dd.sentence: The pNFS client still accesses one meta-data server for traversal or interaction with the namespace; when the client moves data to and from the server it may directly interact with the set of data servers belonging to the pNFS server collection.

8bf0961d0597.title: Network File System
8bf0961d0597.sentence: This differs from the traditional NFS server which holds the names of files and their data under the single umbrella of the server.

44c263d6f101.title: Network File System
44c263d6f101.sentence: The NFSv4.1 pNFS server is a set of server resources or components; these are assumed to be controlled by the meta-data server.

b92d9ab628c6.title: Network File System
b92d9ab628c6.sentence: The NFSv4.1 client can be enabled to be a direct participant in the exact location of file data and to avoid solitary interaction with one NFS server when moving data.

84492d49be5b.title: Network File System
84492d49be5b.sentence: Some products are multi-node NFS servers, but the participation of the client in separation of meta-data and data is limited.

9941e3f9c834.title: Server Message Block
9941e3f9c834.sentence: In the SMB protocol, opportunistic locking is a mechanism designed to improve performance by controlling caching of network files by the client.

2bacf05981cd.title: Server Message Block
2bacf05981cd.sentence: Unlike traditional locks, opportunistic lock (OpLocks) are not strictly file locking or used to provide mutual exclusion.

acf04cfb891e.title: Server Message Block
acf04cfb891e.sentence: When an application opens in "shared mode" a file hosted on an SMB server which is not opened by any other process (or other clients) the client receives an exclusive OpLock from the server.

648cc508bf4e.title: Server Message Block
648cc508bf4e.sentence: This means that the client may now assume that it is the only process with access to this particular file, and the client may now cache all changes to the file before committing it to the server.

3935bdb8cec4.title: Server Message Block
3935bdb8cec4.sentence: This is a performance improvement, since fewer round-trips are required in order to read and write to the file.

5e281e03bfc2.title: Server Message Block
5e281e03bfc2.sentence: If another client/process tries to open the same file, the server sends a message to the client (called a break or revocation) which invalidates the exclusive lock previously given to the client.

37df126461f5.title: Server Message Block
37df126461f5.sentence: The client then flushes all changes to the file.

25ce1a7ed4f5.title: Server Message Block
25ce1a7ed4f5.sentence: The first client is then sent an OpLock break and required to send all its local changes (in case of batch or exclusive OpLocks), if any, and acknowledge the OpLock break.

66ef80041a6e.title: Server Message Block
66ef80041a6e.sentence: Upon this acknowledgment the server can reply to the second client in a consistent manner.

cbc4fc16e2a6.title: Server Message Block
cbc4fc16e2a6.sentence: A client may then receive a "Level 2 OpLock" from the server.

e13bd259cb33.title: Server Message Block
e13bd259cb33.sentence: A Level 2 OpLock allows the caching of read requests but excludes write caching.

3006f4e91f58.title: Server Message Block
3006f4e91f58.sentence: Batch OpLocks were created originally to support a particular behavior of DOS batch file execution operation in which the file is opened and closed many times in a short period, which is a performance problem.

ed6c3f792c99.title: Server Message Block
ed6c3f792c99.sentence: In this case, the client delays sending the close request and if a subsequent open request is given, the two requests cancel each other.

46143c54fef3.title: Server Message Block
46143c54fef3.sentence: Clients holding an OpLock do not really hold a lock on the file, instead they are notified via a break when another client wants to access the file in a way inconsistent with their lock.

5bc7cce9e4f9.title: Server Message Block
5bc7cce9e4f9.sentence: The other client's request is held up while the break is being processed.

f27a77601be1.title: Object storage
f27a77601be1.section: Differences between key–value and object stores
f27a77601be1.sentence: The border between an object store and a key–value store is blurred, with key–value stores being sometimes loosely referred to as object stores.

6605e7701ff3.title: Object storage
6605e7701ff3.section: Differences between key–value and object stores
6605e7701ff3.sentence: There are, however, a few key differences between key–value stores and object stores.

572c6fa51fc0.title: Object storage
572c6fa51fc0.section: Differences between key–value and object stores
572c6fa51fc0.sentence: With a key–value store, data is identified by a key rather than a LBN.

2c003d0a7211.title: Object storage

4cb03e13d07b.title: Object storage

1d4996d28f32.title: Object storage

9c697e68a5d8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explain-the-top-6-use-cases-of-object-stores.md
9c697e68a5d8.sentence: We need to have layers of storage plan.

9618c07e87d0.sentence: We often need to deal with unstructured data or semi-structured data.

b35a7d78dada.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explain-the-top-6-use-cases-of-object-stores.md

46b4bc18b137.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explain-the-top-6-use-cases-of-object-stores.md

e772c27b7e2c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explain-the-top-6-use-cases-of-object-stores.md

4b8f9e17049e.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
4b8f9e17049e.sentence: In information theory and coding theory, Reed–Solomon codes are a group of error-correcting codes that were introduced by Irving S. Reed and Gustave Solomon in 1960.

43df1574887b.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
43df1574887b.sentence: Reed–Solomon codes operate on a block of data treated as a set of finite-field elements called symbols.

cf81cda04970.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
cf81cda04970.sentence: Reed–Solomon codes RS(n, k) are able to detect and correct multiple symbol errors.

c59aa48e9030.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
c59aa48e9030.sentence: By adding t = n − k check symbols to the data, a Reed–Solomon code can detect (but not correct) any combination of up to t erroneous symbols, or locate and correct up to ⌊t/2⌋ erroneous symbols at unknown locations.

f47f9a5ff404.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
f47f9a5ff404.sentence: As an erasure code, it can correct up to t erasures at locations that are known and provided to the algorithm, or it can detect and correct combinations of errors and erasures.

5773eda4323a.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
5773eda4323a.sentence: A Reed–Solomon code (like any MDS code) is able to correct twice as many erasures as errors, and any combination of errors and erasures can be corrected as long as the relation 2E + S ≤ n − k is satisfied, where E is the number of errors and S is the number of erasures in the block.

3abb22f279e4.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
3abb22f279e4.sentence: The Reed–Solomon code is a [n, k, n − k + 1] code; in other words, it is a linear block code of length n (over F) with dimension k and minimum Hamming distance dmin=n−k+1.

bda7fd1019d5.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
bda7fd1019d5.sentence: The Reed–Solomon code is optimal in the sense that the minimum distance has the maximum value possible for a linear code of size (n, k); this is known as the Singleton bound.

3fd847eab851.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
3fd847eab851.sentence: Such a code is also called a maximum distance separable (MDS) code.

1a32137af9a6.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
1a32137af9a6.section: Constructions (encoding) > Reed & Solomon's original view: The codeword as a sequence of values
1a32137af9a6.sentence: In the original view of Reed and Solomon, every codeword of the Reed–Solomon code is a sequence of function values of a polynomial of degree less than k.

9df47c5da5f8.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
9df47c5da5f8.section: Constructions (encoding) > Reed & Solomon's original view: The codeword as a sequence of values
9df47c5da5f8.sentence: In order to obtain a codeword of the Reed–Solomon code, the message symbols (each within the q-sized alphabet) are treated as the coefficients of a polynomial p of degree less than k, over the finite field F with q elements.

6fbc8dd996b8.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
6fbc8dd996b8.section: Constructions (encoding) > Reed & Solomon's original view: The codeword as a sequence of values
6fbc8dd996b8.sentence: In turn, the polynomial p is evaluated at a set of n≤q distinct points in any order a1,…,an of the field F, and the sequence of values is the corresponding codeword.

41d208f0d93f.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
41d208f0d93f.sentence: The Reed–Solomon code properties discussed above make them especially well-suited to applications where errors occur in bursts.

e3c66f603b2c.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
e3c66f603b2c.sentence: This is because it does not matter to the code how many bits in a symbol are in error — if multiple bits in a symbol are corrupted it only counts as a single error.

be2231c878a7.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
be2231c878a7.sentence: Conversely, if a data stream is not characterized by error bursts or drop-outs but by random single bit errors, a Reed–Solomon code is usually a poor choice compared to a binary code.

cb56242981e7.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
cb56242981e7.sentence: For practical uses of Reed–Solomon codes, it is common to use a finite field F with 2m elements.

6f62f3032970.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
6f62f3032970.sentence: Thus a Reed–Solomon code operating on 8-bit symbols has n=28−1=255 symbols per block.

7c38dcfa28a3.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
7c38dcfa28a3.sentence: A commonly used code encodes k=223 eight-bit data symbols plus 32 eight-bit parity symbols in an n=255-symbol block; this is denoted as a (n,k)=(255,223) code, and is capable of correcting up to 16 symbol errors per block.

26705fbd858d.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
26705fbd858d.sentence: Reed–Solomon coding is very widely used in mass storage systems to correct the burst errors associated with media defects.

b4b1f6c07ffe.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
b4b1f6c07ffe.sentence: They have many applications, including consumer technologies such as MiniDiscs, CDs, DVDs, Blu-ray discs, QR codes, Data Matrix, data transmission technologies such as DSL and WiMAX, broadcast systems such as satellite communications, DVB and ATSC, and storage systems such as RAID 6.

bd902f02545d.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
bd902f02545d.sentence: Specialized forms of Reed–Solomon codes, specifically Cauchy-RS and Vandermonde-RS, can be used to overcome the unreliable nature of data transmission over erasure channels.

ab201fe767ce.title: Reed–Solomon error correction
ab201fe767ce.sentence: Any combination of K codewords received at the other end is enough to reconstruct all of the N codewords.

492b0d443c7a.sentence: Fault Tolerance | None | Single-drive failure | Two-drive failure | Up to one disk failure in each sub-array

ba77688698fc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage
ba77688698fc.sentence: - RAID 1: Also known as mirroring, at least two drives contains the exact copy of a set of data.

3f6475554693.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage

f186fc768635.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage

c038553e4dbe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::storage

8a4ad3125902.title: RAID
8a4ad3125902.sentence: On the other hand, the benefit of RAID 0 is that the throughput of read and write operations to any file is multiplied by the number of drives because, unlike spanned volumes, reads and writes are performed concurrently.

f2ebb0e07b68.title: RAID
f2ebb0e07b68.sentence: However, because striping distributes the contents of each file across all drives, the failure of any drive renders the entire RAID 0 volume inaccessible.

4b653f897bb7.title: RAID
4b653f897bb7.sentence: The cost is increased vulnerability to drive failures—since any drive in a RAID 0 setup failing causes the entire volume to be lost, the average failure rate of the volume rises with the number of attached drives.

8a124a3f0c6c.title: RAID

5dd0a20df42b.title: RAID

4c78d372d837.title: Erasure code
4c78d372d837.sentence: In coding theory, an erasure code is a forward error correction (FEC) code under the assumption of bit erasures (rather than bit errors), which transforms a message of k symbols into a longer message (code word) with n symbols such that the original message can be recovered from a subset of the n symbols.

565fd3757df1.title: Erasure code
565fd3757df1.sentence: Optimal erasure codes have the property that any k out of the n code word symbols are sufficient to recover the original message (i.e., they have optimal reception efficiency).

0bed546a7ebe.title: Erasure code
0bed546a7ebe.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems
0bed546a7ebe.sentence: The classical way to recover from failures in storage systems was to use replication.

466a2a45700d.title: Erasure code
466a2a45700d.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems
466a2a45700d.sentence: However, replication incurs significant overhead in terms of wasted bytes.

8b5989e76b52.title: Erasure code
8b5989e76b52.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems
8b5989e76b52.sentence: Therefore, increasingly large storage systems, such as those used in data centers use erasure-coded storage.

5f79a9a2c2a6.title: Erasure code
5f79a9a2c2a6.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems
5f79a9a2c2a6.sentence: The most common form of erasure coding used in storage systems is Reed-Solomon (RS) code, an advanced mathematics formula used to enable regeneration of missing data from pieces of known data, called parity blocks.

d6a1a8979592.title: Erasure code
d6a1a8979592.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems > RS(10,4)
d6a1a8979592.sentence: Example: In RS(10, 4) code, which is used in Facebook for their HDFS (now part of Apache Hadoop), 10 MB of user data is divided into ten 1MB blocks.

2f9b8dcb1597.title: Erasure code
2f9b8dcb1597.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems > RS(10,4)
2f9b8dcb1597.sentence: Then, four additional 1 MB parity blocks are created to provide redundancy.

e3ac7cabc756.title: Erasure code
e3ac7cabc756.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems > RS(10,4)
e3ac7cabc756.sentence: This can tolerate up to 4 concurrent failures.

f3de809df80a.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems > RS(10,4)

bda3c82f569b.title: Erasure code
bda3c82f569b.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems > RS(10,4)
bda3c82f569b.sentence: In the case of a fully replicated system, the 10 MB of user data will have to be replicated 4 times to tolerate up to 4 concurrent failures.

7ba68f21e234.title: Erasure code
7ba68f21e234.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems > RS(10,4)
7ba68f21e234.sentence: The storage overhead in that case will be 50/10 = 5.0×.

41bd9e239300.title: Erasure code
41bd9e239300.sentence: While technically RAID can be seen as a kind of erasure code, RAID is generally applied to an array attached to a single host computer (which is a single point of failure), while "erasure coding" generally implies multiple hosts, sometimes called a redundant array of inexpensive servers (RAIS).

ffb41b6ec022.sentence: The erasure code allows operations to continue when any one of those hosts stops.

4b2e7975e4df.title: Erasure code
4b2e7975e4df.sentence: RAID 5 is a widely used application of the parity check erasure code using XOR.

488ff984fcfe.section: Applications of erasure coding in storage systems > Hot data
488ff984fcfe.sentence: The classic example of erasing coding improving performance is RAID 5, which provides the same single-drive failure protection while requiring fewer hard drives compared to RAID 1.

0e1982a9512b.title: RAID

0e1982a9512b.sentence: Therefore, larger-capacity drives may take hours if not days to rebuild, during which time other drives may fail or yet undetected read errors may surface.

6ddb8c2b15b2.title: RAID
6ddb8c2b15b2.section: Weaknesses > Increasing rebuild time and failure probability
6ddb8c2b15b2.sentence: Given an array with only one redundant drive (which applies to RAID levels 3, 4 and 5, and to "classic" two-drive RAID 1), a second drive failure would cause complete failure of the array.

d0f27fa9ba73.title: RAID
d0f27fa9ba73.sentence: A system crash or other interruption of a write operation can result in states where the parity is inconsistent with the data due to non-atomicity of the write process, such that the parity cannot be used for recovery in the case of a disk failure.

f5d9da680f3d.title: RAID
f5d9da680f3d.sentence: In practice, the drives are often the same age (with similar wear) and subject to the same environment.

28999a919a28.title: RAID
28999a919a28.sentence: Since many drive failures are due to mechanical issues (which are more likely on older drives), this violates the assumptions of independent, identical rate of failure amongst drives; failures are in fact statistically correlated.

98dcb46fddc4.title: RAID
98dcb46fddc4.sentence: In a study of about 100,000 drives from at least four different vendors, the probability of two drives in the same cluster failing within one hour was four times larger than predicted by the exponential statistical distribution—which characterizes processes in which events occur continuously and independently at a constant average rate.

8643f067da35.title: RAID

8643f067da35.sentence: Drive capacity has grown at a much faster rate than transfer speed, and error rates have only fallen a little in comparison.

e35bcca7c194.title: RAID

e35bcca7c194.sentence: Double-protection parity-based schemes, such as RAID 6, attempt to address this issue by providing redundancy that allows double-drive failures; as a downside, such schemes suffer from elevated write penalty—the number of times the storage medium must be accessed during a single write operation.

b008b2c0626d.sentence: Schemes that duplicate (mirror) data in a drive-to-drive manner, such as RAID 1 and RAID 10, have a lower risk from UREs than those using parity computation or mirroring between striped sets.

f4eb4c32745b.title: RAID
f4eb4c32745b.sentence: This is commonly termed the write hole which is a known data corruption issue in older and low-end RAIDs, caused by interrupted destaging of writes to disk.

4a97d8e4ce72.title: RAID
4a97d8e4ce72.sentence: - Hardware RAID systems use an onboard nonvolatile cache for this purpose.

cc8d25833011.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-on-architectural-scalability.md

53554332639f.sentence: High availability (HA) is a characteristic of a system that aims to ensure an agreed level of operational performance, usually uptime, for a higher than normal period.

a6ebd5b02875.title: High availability

b2cccfb29502.title: High availability

c46bc93206c7.title: High availability

bfea4182fc0c.title: High availability

c500ef93d07a.title: Stateless protocol
c500ef93d07a.sentence: A stateless protocol is a communication protocol in which the receiver does not retain session state from previous requests.

2cb46fab6d6b.title: Stateless protocol
2cb46fab6d6b.sentence: In contrast, a stateful protocol is a communication protocol in which the receiver may retain session state from previous requests.

cc45d09f9fa0.title: Stateless protocol
cc45d09f9fa0.sentence: The sender transfers relevant session state to the receiver in such a way that every request can be understood in isolation, without reference to session state from previous requests.

a04f17b1b756.title: Stateless protocol
a04f17b1b756.sentence: In computer networks, examples of stateless protocols include the Internet Protocol (IP), which is the foundation for the Internet, and the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), which is the foundation of the World Wide Web.

067cc24320ac.title: Stateless protocol
067cc24320ac.sentence: Examples of stateful protocols include the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and the File Transfer Protocol (FTP).

3335fb92e09c.title: Stateless protocol
3335fb92e09c.sentence: During the session, a user is provided a means to be authenticated and set various variables (working directory, transfer mode) all stored on the server as part of the session state.

e6c68661a767.title: Stateless protocol
e6c68661a767.sentence: An HTTP server can understand each request in isolation.

f05dd13d1278.title: Stateless protocol
f05dd13d1278.sentence: Stateless protocols have superior visibility, reliability, and scalability properties.

b7cfecabf301.title: Stateless protocol
b7cfecabf301.sentence: Visibility is improved because a monitoring system does not have to look beyond a single request in order to determine its full nature.

d838e33872d3.title: Stateless protocol
d838e33872d3.sentence: Reliability is improved because it eases the task of recovering from failures such as packet loss.

f389341a9f66.title: Stateless protocol
f389341a9f66.sentence: Scalability is improved because not having to store session state between requests allows the server to quickly free resources and further simplifies implementation.

b153144c6e1d.title: Stateless protocol
b153144c6e1d.sentence: The disadvantage of stateless protocols is that they may decrease network performance by increasing the repetitive data sent in a series of requests, since that data is not retained or reused at the receiver.

8140813a11ad.title: Stateless protocol
8140813a11ad.section: Stacking of stateless and stateful protocol layers
8140813a11ad.sentence: As a workaround for the lack of a retained session state, HTTP servers implement various session management methods, typically utilizing a session identifier in an HTTP cookie referencing a session state stored on the server, effectively creating a stateful protocol on top of HTTP.

ef419d246d76.title: Stateless protocol
ef419d246d76.section: Stacking of stateless and stateful protocol layers
ef419d246d76.sentence: There can be complex interactions between stateful and stateless protocols among different protocol layers.

c484e4bc731d.title: Stateless protocol

c484e4bc731d.sentence: For example, HTTP, a stateless protocol, is layered on top of TCP, a stateful protocol, which is layered on top of IP, another stateless protocol, which is routed on a network that employs BGP, another stateful protocol, to direct the IP packets riding on the network.
