651f4fbeb756.title: Amdahl's law
651f4fbeb756.sentence: In computer architecture, Amdahl's law (or Amdahl's argument) is a formula limiting the speedup of a task as resources are added to the system executing that task.

9f81ad4b6bd9.title: Amdahl's law
9f81ad4b6bd9.sentence: > the overall performance improvement gained by optimizing a single part of a system is limited by the fraction of time that the improved part is actually used.

3dc4589dca4c.title: Amdahl's law
3dc4589dca4c.sentence: Amdahl's law is often used in parallel computing to predict the theoretical speedup when using multiple processors.

ffda180423d4.title: Amdahl's law
ffda180423d4.sentence: The part that scans the directory and creates the file list cannot be sped up on a parallel computer, but the part that processes the files can.

f671caaf1570.title: Amdahl's law
f671caaf1570.sentence: - Speedupoverall represents the total speedup of a program

4b85463d554a.title: Amdahl's law
4b85463d554a.sentence: - Timeoptimized represents the proportion of time spent on the portion of the code where improvements are made

d9725a551232.title: Amdahl's law
d9725a551232.sentence: - Speedupoptimized represents the extent of the improvement

39e2665088f0.title: Amdahl's law
39e2665088f0.sentence: The Speedupoverall is frequently much lower than one might expect.

492c260beefd.title: Amdahl's law
492c260beefd.sentence: For instance, if a programmer enhances a part of the code that represents 10% of the total execution time (i.e. Timeoptimized of 0.10) and achieves a Speedupoptimized of 10,000, then Speedupoverall becomes 1.11 which means only 11% improvement in total speedup of the program.

59446a533ff7.title: Amdahl's law
59446a533ff7.sentence: So, despite a massive improvement in one section, the overall benefit is quite small.

646468da1a18.title: Amdahl's law
646468da1a18.sentence: In another example, if the programmer optimizes a section that accounts for 99% of the execution time (i.e. Timeoptimized of 0.99) with a speedup factor of 100 (i.e. Speedupoptimizedof 100), the Speedupoverall only reaches 50.

9883931b293a.title: Amdahl's law
9883931b293a.sentence: This indicates that half of the potential performance gain (Speedupoverall will reach 100 if 100% of the execution time is covered) is lost due to the remaining 1% of execution time that was not improved.

245f980b9a0b.title: Amdahl's law
245f980b9a0b.sentence: For example, with a serial program in two parts A and B for which TA = 3 s and TB = 1 s,

9ab138b491e2.title: Amdahl's law
9ab138b491e2.sentence: - if part B is made to run 5 times faster, that is s = 5 and p = TB/(TA + TB) = 0.25, then Slatency=11−0.25+0.255=1.25;

b128914ca95a.title: Amdahl's law
b128914ca95a.sentence: - if part A is made to run 2 times faster, that is s = 2 and p = TA/(TA + TB) = 0.75, then Slatency=11−0.75+0.752=1.60.

30caf9452637.title: Amdahl's law
30caf9452637.sentence: Therefore, making part A to run 2 times faster is better than making part B to run 5 times faster.

afa0fe0b634f.title: Amdahl's law
afa0fe0b634f.section: Relation to the law of diminishing returns
afa0fe0b634f.sentence: Amdahl's law does represent the law of diminishing returns if one is considering what sort of return one gets by adding more processors to a machine, if one is running a fixed-size computation that will use all available processors to their capacity.

f3f1307e84df.title: Amdahl's law
f3f1307e84df.section: Relation to the law of diminishing returns
f3f1307e84df.sentence: Each new processor added to the system will add less usable power than the previous one.

f43109e113a7.title: Amdahl's law
f43109e113a7.section: Relation to the law of diminishing returns
f43109e113a7.sentence: Each time one doubles the number of processors the speedup ratio will diminish, as the total throughput heads toward the limit of 11−p.

b3cef1075bc4.title: Amdahl's law
b3cef1075bc4.section: Relation to the law of diminishing returns
b3cef1075bc4.sentence: This analysis neglects other potential bottlenecks such as memory bandwidth and I/O bandwidth.

c155c9f07933.title: Amdahl's law
c155c9f07933.section: Relation to the law of diminishing returns
c155c9f07933.sentence: If these resources do not scale with the number of processors, then merely adding processors provides even lower returns.

4b426955e28a.title: Autoscaling
4b426955e28a.sentence: Autoscaling, (also written as auto scaling, auto-scaling, or known as automatic scaling), is a method used in cloud computing that dynamically adjusts the amount of computational resources in a server farm - typically measured by the number of active servers - automatically based on the load on the farm.

ea4a7a52e591.title: Autoscaling
ea4a7a52e591.sentence: Since such metrics may change dramatically throughout the course of the day, and servers are a limited resource that cost money to run even while idle, there is often an incentive to run "just enough" servers to support the current load while still being able to support sudden and large spikes in activity.

d16f493c16c6.title: Autoscaling
d16f493c16c6.sentence: Autoscaling is helpful for such needs, as it can reduce the number of active servers when activity is low, and launch new servers when activity is high.

b14da221a4eb.title: Autoscaling
b14da221a4eb.sentence: Autoscaling differs from having a fixed daily, weekly, or yearly cycle of server use in that it is responsive to actual usage patterns, and thus reduces the potential downside of having too few or too many servers for the traffic load.

7c19a1451245.title: Autoscaling
7c19a1451245.sentence: Autoscaling, on the other hand, can handle unexpected traffic spikes better.

8e376355277f.title: Autoscaling
8e376355277f.sentence: - For companies using infrastructure hosted in the cloud, autoscaling can mean lower bills, because most cloud providers charge based on total usage rather than maximum capacity.

267b470d9f70.title: Autoscaling
267b470d9f70.sentence: Health check | A way for the autoscaling group to determine if the instances attached to it are functioning properly. A health check may be based on whether the instance still exists and is reachable, or it could be based on whether the instance is still registered and in service with an associated load balancer

3f59afe09b33.title: Autoscaling
3f59afe09b33.sentence: - Autoscaling solutions, such as the one offered by Amazon Web Services, can also take care of replacing unhealthy instances and therefore protecting somewhat against hardware, network, and application failures.

475dbe0b2902.title: Autoscaling
475dbe0b2902.sentence: That is because autoscaling offers two other advantages: automatic replacement of any instances that become unhealthy for any reason (such as hardware failure, network failure, or application error), and automatic replacement of spot instances that get interrupted for price or capacity reasons, making it more feasible to use spot instances for production purposes.

67fd0aaa8397.title: Autoscaling
67fd0aaa8397.sentence: Autoscaling group | The collection of instances subject to autoscaling, along with all the associated policies and state information | Managed instance group (Google Cloud Platform)

e044b96c275b.title: Autoscaling
e044b96c275b.sentence: Desired capacity (or desired size) | The number of instances that the autoscaling group should have at any given point in time. If the size is less than the desired size, the autoscaling group will try to launch (provision and attach) new instances. If the size is more than the desired size, the autoscaling group will try to remove (detach and terminate) instances

8eb0ea3687f9.title: Autoscaling
8eb0ea3687f9.sentence: Minimum size | A number of instances below which the desired capacity is not allowed to fall

6ec34bcb1a39.title: Autoscaling
6ec34bcb1a39.sentence: Maximum size | A number of instances above which the desired capacity is not allowed to rise

4bd4e29fe057.title: Autoscaling
4bd4e29fe057.sentence: Metric | A measurement (such as CPU utilization, memory usage, network usage) associated with the autoscaling group, for which a time series of data points is generated regularly. Thresholds for metrics can be used to set autoscaling policies. Metrics can be based on aggregates of metrics for instances of the autoscaling group, or based on load balancers associated with the autoscaling group

b08981f54f34.title: Autoscaling
b08981f54f34.sentence: Scaling policy (or autoscaling policy) | A policy that specifies a change to the autoscaling group's desired capacity (or sometimes, its minimum and maximum size) in response to metrics crossing specific thresholds. Scaling policies can have associated cooldown periods, which prevent additional scaling actions from occurring immediately after a specific scaling action. Changes to desired capacity could be incremental (increase or decrease by a specific number) or could specify a new value of the desired capacity. Policies that increase the desired capacity are called "scaling out" or "scaling up" policies, and policies that decrease the desired capacity are called "scaling in" or "scaling down" policies

82cc89d92d8a.title: Autoscaling
82cc89d92d8a.sentence: Autoscaling by default uses reactive decision approach for dealing with traffic scaling: scaling only happens in response to real-time changes in metrics.

1d421ef9f2d8.title: Autoscaling
1d421ef9f2d8.sentence: In some cases, particularly when the changes occur very quickly, this reactive approach to scaling is insufficient.

de60d6833443.title: Autoscaling
de60d6833443.section: Alternative autoscaling decision approaches > Scheduled autoscaling approach
de60d6833443.sentence: This is an approach to autoscaling where changes are made to the minimum size, maximum size, or desired capacity of the autoscaling group at specific times of day.

4fb3dbffd8f8.title: Autoscaling
4fb3dbffd8f8.section: Alternative autoscaling decision approaches > Scheduled autoscaling approach
4fb3dbffd8f8.sentence: Scheduled scaling is useful, for instance, if there is a known traffic load increase or decrease at specific times of the day, but the change is too sudden for reactive approach based autoscaling to respond fast enough.

4826a54bbc72.title: Autoscaling
4826a54bbc72.section: Alternative autoscaling decision approaches > Predictive autoscaling
4826a54bbc72.sentence: This approach to autoscaling uses predictive analytics.

83cfbd04f52e.title: Autoscaling
83cfbd04f52e.section: Alternative autoscaling decision approaches > Predictive autoscaling
83cfbd04f52e.sentence: The idea is to combine recent usage trends with historical usage data as well as other kinds of data to predict usage in the future, and autoscale based on these predictions.

ea5fb1a77372.title: Autoscaling
ea5fb1a77372.section: Alternative autoscaling decision approaches > Predictive autoscaling
ea5fb1a77372.sentence: For parts of their infrastructure and specific workloads, Netflix found that Scryer, their predictive analytics engine, gave better results than Amazon's reactive autoscaling approach.

8a419dd41f0a.title: Autoscaling
8a419dd41f0a.sentence: On-demand video provider Netflix documented their use of autoscaling with Amazon Web Services to meet their highly variable consumer needs.

abfbb34492d5.title: Autoscaling
abfbb34492d5.sentence: They found that aggressive scaling up and delayed and cautious scaling down served their goals of uptime and responsiveness best.

95d7f6386720.title: Scalability
95d7f6386720.sentence: Scalability can be measured over multiple dimensions, such as:

21c9dc5d4ea1.title: Scalability
21c9dc5d4ea1.sentence: - Administrative scalability: The ability for an increasing number of organizations or users to access a system.

d2e655d92d98.title: Scalability
d2e655d92d98.sentence: - Geographic scalability: The ability to maintain effectiveness during expansion from a local area to a larger region.

a1acaad965f9.title: Scalability
a1acaad965f9.sentence: - Functional scalability: The ability to enhance the system by adding new functionality without disrupting existing activities.

d1c8464f6187.title: Scalability
d1c8464f6187.sentence: - Load scalability: The ability for a distributed system to expand and contract to accommodate heavier or lighter loads, including, the ease with which a system or component can be modified, added, or removed, to accommodate changing loads.

92316c922019.title: Scalability
92316c922019.sentence: - Generation scalability: The ability of a system to scale by adopting new generations of components.

5919e61748ee.title: Scalability
5919e61748ee.sentence: - Heterogeneous scalability is the ability to adopt components from different vendors.

691a94a39636.title: Scalability
691a94a39636.sentence: But this approach can have diminishing returns (as discussed in performance engineering).

27d1f73d89bd.title: Scalability
27d1f73d89bd.sentence: If α is the fraction of a calculation that is sequential, and 1−α is the fraction that can be parallelized, the maximum speedup that can be achieved by using P processors is given according to Amdahl's Law:

978d374afefe.title: Scalability
978d374afefe.sentence: It is often advised to focus system design on hardware scalability rather than on capacity.

684a7f401cdb.title: Scalability
684a7f401cdb.sentence: It is typically cheaper to add a new node to a system in order to achieve improved performance than to partake in performance tuning to improve the capacity that each node can handle.

4fafabce47a1.title: Scalability
4fafabce47a1.sentence: For example: suppose 70% of a program can be sped up if parallelized and run on multiple CPUs instead of one.

b35f64e11e80.title: Scalability
b35f64e11e80.sentence: Substituting the value for this example, using 4 processors gives

d64987f89d13.title: Scalability
d64987f89d13.sentence: Doubling the computing power to 8 processors gives

987e25118660.title: Scalability
987e25118660.sentence: Doubling the processing power has only sped up the process by roughly one-fifth.

4d1b209be3ab.title: Scalability
4d1b209be3ab.sentence: If the whole problem were parallelizable, the speed would also double.

433a23d18b59.title: Scalability
433a23d18b59.sentence: Therefore, throwing in more hardware is not necessarily the optimal approach.

8e20367aaa95.title: Scalability
8e20367aaa95.sentence: In distributed systems, you can use Universal Scalability Law (USL) to model and to optimize scalability of your system.

a36df17c3322.title: Scalability
a36df17c3322.sentence: USL is coined by Neil J. Gunther and quantifies scalability based on parameters such as contention and coherency.

d5bfb997a374.title: Scalability
d5bfb997a374.sentence: Contention refers to delay due to waiting or queueing for shared resources.

c7a824872352.title: Scalability
c7a824872352.sentence: Coherence refers to delay for data to become consistent.

a16b3bb39a61.title: Scalability
a16b3bb39a61.sentence: For example, having a high contention indicates sequential processing that could be parallelized, while having a high coherency suggests excessive dependencies among processes, prompting you to minimize interactions.

623633765a14.title: Scalability
623633765a14.sentence: Also, with help of USL, you can, in advance, calculate the maximum effective capacity of your system: scaling up your system beyond that point is a waste.

4266242a4372.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
4266242a4372.sentence: Here are 8 must-know strategies to scale your system.

cabb5d9b736c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
cabb5d9b736c.sentence: - Stateless Services Design stateless services because they don’t rely on server-specific data and are easier to scale.

04065c7c820e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
04065c7c820e.sentence: - Horizontal Scaling Add more servers so that the workload can be shared.

b5ccfedd9836.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
b5ccfedd9836.sentence: - Load Balancing Use a load balancer to distribute incoming requests evenly across multiple servers.

f1cdca7329e2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
f1cdca7329e2.sentence: - Auto Scaling Implement auto-scaling policies to adjust resources based on real-time traffic.

8850fd45c47d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
8850fd45c47d.sentence: - Caching Use caching to reduce the load on the database and handle repetitive requests at scale.

c5911e9c2794.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
c5911e9c2794.sentence: - Database Replication Replicate data across multiple nodes to scale the read operations while improving redundancy.

6c4b7e8232b2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
6c4b7e8232b2.sentence: - Database Sharding Distribute data across multiple instances to scale the writes as well as reads.

b3dbca0e3db0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-must-know-scalability-strategies.md
b3dbca0e3db0.sentence: - Async Processing Move time-consuming and resource-intensive tasks to background workers using async processing to scale out new requests.

98cf89ec36c1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-on-architectural-scalability.md
98cf89ec36c1.sentence: - Event-Driven Processing: Use an async processing approach to process long-running tasks.

41a2d3c34053.title: Scalability
41a2d3c34053.sentence: Scalability for databases requires that the database system be able to perform additional work given greater hardware resources, such as additional servers, processors, memory and storage.

0325562b96a1.title: Scalability
0325562b96a1.sentence: Algorithmic innovations include row-level locking and table and index partitioning.

b2dec349a969.title: Scalability
b2dec349a969.sentence: Architectural innovations include shared-nothing and shared-everything architectures for managing multi-server configurations.

666b0b477e82.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
666b0b477e82.sentence: Check the query patterns of your application and create the right indexes.

42c72e0b560b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
42c72e0b560b.sentence: Pre-compute complex query results and store them for faster access.

15d235e873c3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
15d235e873c3.sentence: Reduce complex joins to improve query performance.

56e2e2623378.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
56e2e2623378.sentence: Boost your database server by adding more CPU, RAM, or storage.

b8bb8db6c8e2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
b8bb8db6c8e2.sentence: Store frequently accessed data in a faster storage layer to reduce database load.

4b9f6ea21135.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
4b9f6ea21135.sentence: Create replicas of your primary database on different servers for scaling the reads.

091c2f8ceafe.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
091c2f8ceafe.sentence: Split your database tables into smaller pieces and spread them across servers.

b2eed29471bd.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/7-must-know-strategies-to-scale-your-database.md
b2eed29471bd.sentence: Used for scaling the writes as well as the reads.

59af568fd95e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
59af568fd95e.sentence: At a high level, a computer cluster is a group of two or more computers, or nodes, that run in parallel to achieve a common goal.

31643e636a69.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
31643e636a69.sentence: This allows workloads consisting of a high number of individual, parallelizable tasks to be distributed among the nodes in the cluster.

b1cdac831ea1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
b1cdac831ea1.sentence: As a result, these tasks can leverage the combined memory and processing power of each computer to increase overall performance.

7b0e57102bb0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
7b0e57102bb0.sentence: To build a computer cluster, the individual nodes should be connected to a network to enable internode communication.

43e100f2ae1c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
43e100f2ae1c.sentence: The software can then be used to join the nodes together and form a cluster.

f1f3c73610a4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
f1f3c73610a4.sentence: It may have a shared storage device and/or local storage on each node.

49f7a49afcb3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
49f7a49afcb3.sentence: Typically, at least one node is designated as the leader node and acts as the entry point to the cluster.

711b0d2a3ea9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
711b0d2a3ea9.sentence: The leader node may be responsible for delegating incoming work to the other nodes and, if necessary, aggregating the results and returning a response to the user.

b351f5d2b173.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
b351f5d2b173.sentence: Ideally, a cluster functions as if it were a single system.

009074c8f725.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
009074c8f725.sentence: A user accessing the cluster should not need to know whether the system is a cluster or an individual machine.

67658a171af6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
67658a171af6.sentence: Furthermore, a cluster should be designed to minimize latency and prevent bottlenecks in node-to-node communication.

6cf18a7d235b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
6cf18a7d235b.sentence: Computer clusters can generally be categorized into three types:

7e109d16fc4e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
7e109d16fc4e.sentence: Four key advantages of cluster computing are as follows:

b54d4838add2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
b54d4838add2.sentence: The most obvious challenge clustering presents is the increased complexity of installation and maintenance.

0aa320247be7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
0aa320247be7.sentence: An operating system, the application, and its dependencies must each be installed and updated on every node.

c528615fcf59.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
c528615fcf59.sentence: Resource utilization for each node must also be closely monitored, and logs should be aggregated to ensure that the software is behaving correctly.

02e7866f7f17.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
02e7866f7f17.sentence: Additionally, storage becomes more difficult to manage, a shared storage device must prevent nodes from overwriting one another and distributed data stores have to be kept in sync.

da32b851f73a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
da32b851f73a.sentence: Clustering is commonly used in the industry, and often many technologies offer some sort of clustering mode.

0c758d156ff4.title: Scalability
0c758d156ff4.sentence: In the context of scale-out data storage, scalability is defined as the maximum storage cluster size which guarantees full data consistency, meaning there is only ever one valid version of stored data in the whole cluster, independently from the number of redundant physical data copies.

157815ee6f76.title: Scalability
157815ee6f76.sentence: Clusters which provide "lazy" redundancy by updating copies in an asynchronous fashion are called 'eventually consistent'.

1a25901059c9.title: Scalability
1a25901059c9.sentence: This type of scale-out design is suitable when availability and responsiveness are rated higher than consistency, which is true for many web file-hosting services or web caches (if you want the latest version, wait some seconds for it to propagate).

49706b9b5de5.title: Scalability
49706b9b5de5.sentence: For all classical transaction-oriented applications, this design should be avoided.

ed3a9bc900c6.title: Scalability
ed3a9bc900c6.sentence: Write operations invalidate other copies, but often don't wait for their acknowledgements.

5202d4938c44.title: Scalability
5202d4938c44.sentence: Read operations typically don't check every redundant copy prior to answering, potentially missing the preceding write operation.

c2c15073a134.title: Scalability
c2c15073a134.sentence: Many open-source and even commercial scale-out storage clusters, especially those built on top of standard PC hardware and networks, provide eventual consistency only, such as some NoSQL databases like CouchDB and others mentioned above.

f5a67ae5ebac.title: High availability
f5a67ae5ebac.sentence: The term downtime is generally used to refer to describe periods when a system is unavailable.

e6b517430a2b.title: High availability
e6b517430a2b.sentence: A distinction can be made between scheduled and unscheduled downtime.

5fe7b006627f.title: High availability
5fe7b006627f.sentence: Typically, scheduled downtime is a result of maintenance that is disruptive to system operation and usually cannot be avoided with a currently installed system design.

1d533627aa1d.title: High availability
1d533627aa1d.sentence: Scheduled downtime events might include patches to system software that require a reboot or system configuration changes that only take effect upon a reboot.

bf1f823e2dba.title: High availability
bf1f823e2dba.sentence: In general, scheduled downtime is usually the result of some logical, management-initiated event.

590ca575b633.title: High availability
590ca575b633.sentence: Unscheduled downtime events typically arise from some physical event, such as a hardware or software failure or environmental anomaly.

e6826d9eaf49.title: High availability
e6826d9eaf49.sentence: Examples of unscheduled downtime events include power outages, failed CPU or RAM components (or possibly other failed hardware components), an over-temperature-related shutdown, logically or physically severed network connections, security breaches, or various application, middleware, and operating system failures.

4b65494369fa.title: High availability
4b65494369fa.sentence: Many computing sites exclude scheduled downtime from availability calculations, assuming that it has little or no impact upon the computing user community.

6cb5044f834e.title: High availability
6cb5044f834e.sentence: By doing this, they can claim to have phenomenally high availability, which might give the illusion of continuous availability.

341b77531440.title: High availability
341b77531440.sentence: But if the requirement is for true high availability, then downtime is downtime whether or not it is scheduled.

512763320592.title: High availability
512763320592.sentence: Systems that exhibit truly continuous availability are comparatively rare and higher priced, and most have carefully implemented specialty designs that eliminate any single point of failure and allow online hardware, network, operating system, middleware, and application upgrades, patches, and replacements.

f430c61221df.title: High availability
f430c61221df.sentence: Availability is usually expressed as a percentage of uptime in a given year.

fbe07eb077b0.title: High availability
fbe07eb077b0.sentence: Availability is often quoted in terms of "nines", with 90% availability being called "one nine", 99% "two nines", 99.9% "three nines" and so on.

72e18fc7cef4.title: High availability
72e18fc7cef4.sentence: As the number of nines gets larger, the availability targets get exponentially more stringent.

bf409eea7749.title: High availability
bf409eea7749.sentence: A simple mnemonic rule states that 5 nines allows approximately 5 minutes of downtime per year.

6000dcc3cdf1.title: High availability
6000dcc3cdf1.sentence: Variants can be derived by multiplying or dividing by 10: 4 nines is 50 minutes and 3 nines is 500 minutes.

2768aee442b0.title: High availability
2768aee442b0.sentence: In the opposite direction, 6 nines is 0.5 minutes (30 sec) and 7 nines is 3 seconds.

a1b6fb23d9e9.title: High availability
a1b6fb23d9e9.sentence: Service level agreements often refer to monthly downtime or availability in order to calculate service credits to match monthly billing cycles.

8e9ed93bf0fa.title: High availability
8e9ed93bf0fa.sentence: The terms uptime and availability are often used interchangeably but do not always refer to the same thing.

ef83dc78ad32.title: High availability
ef83dc78ad32.sentence: For example, a system can be "up" with its services not "available" in the case of a network outage.

628df4eeaf9c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
628df4eeaf9c.sentence: Availability is the time a system remains operational to perform its required function in a specific period.

5bcfbbc90181.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
5bcfbbc90181.sentence: Availability is often quantified by uptime (or downtime) as a percentage of time the service is available.

2fab5fabd8cc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
2fab5fabd8cc.sentence: It is generally measured in the number of 9s.

82efee771a87.title: Mean time to repair
82efee771a87.sentence: Mean time to repair (MTTR) is a basic measure of the maintainability of repairable items.

9848a1fae490.title: Mean time to repair
9848a1fae490.sentence: It represents the average time required to repair a failed component or device.

6ab0ee6032ae.title: Mean time to repair
6ab0ee6032ae.sentence: Expressed mathematically, it is the total corrective maintenance time for failures divided by the total number of corrective maintenance actions for failures during a given period of time.

fc502ffdaa12.title: Mean time to repair
fc502ffdaa12.sentence: It generally does not include lead time for parts not readily available or other Administrative or Logistic Downtime (ALDT).

5ed56ec6a93e.title: Mean time to repair
5ed56ec6a93e.sentence: In fault-tolerant design, MTTR is usually considered to also include the time the fault is latent (the time from when the failure occurs until it is detected).

7a9ff69b42d0.title: Mean time to repair
7a9ff69b42d0.sentence: If a latent fault goes undetected until an independent failure occurs, the system may not be able to recover.

40e48c0485c3.title: Mean time to repair
40e48c0485c3.sentence: However, in the context of a maintenance contract, it would be important to distinguish whether MTTR is meant to be a measure of the mean time between the point at which the failure is first discovered until the point at which the equipment returns to operation (usually termed "mean time to recovery"), or only a measure of the elapsed time between the point where repairs actually begin until the point at which the equipment returns to operation (usually termed "mean time to repair").

cafd9de5de36.title: Mean time to repair
cafd9de5de36.sentence: For example, a system with a service contract guaranteeing a mean time to "repair" of 24 hours, but with additional part lead times, administrative delays, and technician transportation delays adding up to a mean of 6 days, would not be any more attractive than another system with a service contract guaranteeing a mean time to "recovery" of 7 days.

222efc963565.title: Mean time to repair
222efc963565.sentence: MTTR is often part of a maintenance contract, where a system whose MTTR is 24 hours is generally more valuable than for one of 7 days if mean time between failures is equal, because its Operational Availability is higher.

259b37f2baf9.title: Fault tolerance
259b37f2baf9.sentence: In such systems the mean time between failures should be long enough for the operators to have sufficient time to fix the broken devices (mean time to repair) before the backup also fails.

2b0434d73a31.title: High availability
2b0434d73a31.sentence: Availability measurement is subject to some degree of interpretation.

9ee8e48329b3.title: High availability
9ee8e48329b3.sentence: A system that has been up for 365 days in a non-leap year might have been eclipsed by a network failure that lasted for 9 hours during a peak usage period; the user community will see the system as unavailable, whereas the system administrator will claim 100% uptime.

cf5c86d2c0e6.title: High availability
cf5c86d2c0e6.sentence: However, given the true definition of availability, the system will be approximately 99.9% available, or three nines (8751 hours of available time out of 8760 hours per non-leap year).

433ea3b49e29.title: High availability
433ea3b49e29.sentence: Also, systems experiencing performance problems are often deemed partially or entirely unavailable by users, even when the systems are continuing to function.

5f5ab78aaf9b.title: High availability
5f5ab78aaf9b.sentence: Similarly, unavailability of select application functions might go unnoticed by administrators yet be devastating to users – a true availability measure is holistic.

5580381ec98b.title: High availability
5580381ec98b.sentence: Availability must be measured to be determined, ideally with comprehensive monitoring tools ("instrumentation") that are themselves highly available.

78aeebee3d8d.title: High availability
78aeebee3d8d.sentence: Recovery time (or estimated time of repair (ETR), also known as recovery time objective (RTO), the total time required for a planned outage or the time required to fully recover from an unplanned outage, is closely related to availability.

379de0b5557a.title: High availability
379de0b5557a.sentence: Another metric is mean time to recovery (MTTR).

c5aae096c84d.title: High availability
c5aae096c84d.sentence: Recovery time could be infinite with certain system designs and failures, i.e., full recovery is impossible.

1b37a6600fbc.title: High availability
1b37a6600fbc.sentence: One such example is a fire or flood that destroys a data center and its systems when there is no secondary disaster recovery data center.

2a389223fc1e.title: High availability
2a389223fc1e.sentence: Another related concept is data availability, that is, the degree to which databases and other information storage systems faithfully record and report system transactions.

0593bdbf1a15.title: High availability
0593bdbf1a15.sentence: Information management often focuses separately on data availability, or Recovery Point Objective, in order to determine acceptable (or actual) data loss with various failure events.

e9bf5987421d.title: High availability
e9bf5987421d.sentence: Some users can tolerate application service interruptions but cannot tolerate data loss.

08ba4bdafed0.title: High availability
08ba4bdafed0.sentence: A service level agreement ("SLA") formalizes an organization's availability objectives and requirements.

8db1281f40d1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
8db1281f40d1.sentence: The two most commonly used high availability (HA) clustering configurations are active-active and active-passive.

8c82d6c07f59.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
8c82d6c07f59.sentence: An active-active cluster is typically made up of at least two nodes, both actively running the same kind of service simultaneously.

938a2bad2bd8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
938a2bad2bd8.sentence: The main purpose of an active-active cluster is to achieve load balancing.

9a68d53904ca.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
9a68d53904ca.sentence: A load balancer distributes workloads across all nodes to prevent any single node from getting overloaded.

a97488f7562f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
a97488f7562f.sentence: Because there are more nodes available to serve, there will also be an improvement in throughput and response times.

24bbb25ba65d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
24bbb25ba65d.sentence: Like the active-active cluster configuration, an active-passive cluster also consists of at least two nodes.

06006ffd537a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
06006ffd537a.sentence: However, as the name active-passive implies, not all nodes are going to be active.

230313a57097.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
230313a57097.sentence: For example, in the case of two nodes, if the first node is already active, then the second node must be passive or on standby.

fa3f7e18e407.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
fa3f7e18e407.section: Availability in Sequence vs Parallel > Sequence
fa3f7e18e407.sentence: Overall availability decreases when two components are in sequence.

d1cdc4541568.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
d1cdc4541568.section: Availability in Sequence vs Parallel > Parallel
d1cdc4541568.sentence: Overall availability increases when two components are in parallel.

7c9fea05d44d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
7c9fea05d44d.sentence: If a service consists of multiple components prone to failure, the service's overall availability depends on whether the components are in sequence or in parallel.

c502b6b0aca9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
c502b6b0aca9.section: Availability in Sequence vs Parallel > Sequence

ba69023fafb5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
ba69023fafb5.section: Availability in Sequence vs Parallel > Sequence
ba69023fafb5.sentence: For example, if both Foo and Bar each had 99.9% availability, their total availability in sequence would be 99.8%.

bd6d43782215.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
bd6d43782215.section: Availability in Sequence vs Parallel > Parallel

7f386140cda4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::availability
7f386140cda4.section: Availability in Sequence vs Parallel > Parallel
7f386140cda4.sentence: For example, if both Foo and Bar each had 99.9% availability, their total availability in parallel would be 99.9999%.

c0aba9692016.title: Redundancy (engineering)
c0aba9692016.sentence: In computer science, there are four major forms of redundancy:

d6568cbf21e8.title: Redundancy (engineering)
d6568cbf21e8.sentence: - Hardware redundancy, such as dual modular redundancy and triple modular redundancy

ce0aaa7a08b9.title: Redundancy (engineering)
ce0aaa7a08b9.sentence: - Information redundancy, such as error detection and correction methods

516107788951.title: Redundancy (engineering)
516107788951.sentence: - Time redundancy, performing the same operation multiple times such as multiple executions of a program or multiple copies of data transmitted

eb907e57fb95.title: Redundancy (engineering)
eb907e57fb95.sentence: - Software redundancy such as N-version programming

3649f381bef0.title: Redundancy (engineering)
3649f381bef0.sentence: Unlike traditional redundancy, which uses more than one of the same thing, dissimilar redundancy uses different things.

0f21dc59c4fd.title: Redundancy (engineering)
0f21dc59c4fd.sentence: The idea is that the different things are unlikely to contain identical flaws.

595c6376be18.title: Redundancy (engineering)
595c6376be18.sentence: Dissimilar redundancy is often used with software, because identical software contains identical flaws.

8b3c891dfc23.title: Redundancy (engineering)
8b3c891dfc23.sentence: Geographic redundancy corrects the vulnerabilities of redundant devices deployed by geographically separating backup devices.

1e09d9fa6a50.title: Redundancy (engineering)
1e09d9fa6a50.sentence: Geographic redundancy reduces the likelihood of events such as power outages, floods, HVAC failures, lightning strikes, tornadoes, building fires, wildfires, and mass shootings disabling most of the system if not the entirety of it.

dc208e3e75a6.title: Redundancy (engineering)
dc208e3e75a6.sentence: Geographic redundancy is used by Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure, Netflix, Dropbox, Salesforce, LinkedIn, PayPal, Twitter, Facebook, Apple iCloud, Cisco Meraki, and many others to provide geographic redundancy, high availability, fault tolerance and to ensure availability and reliability for their cloud services.

555c63dfef08.title: Redundancy (engineering)
555c63dfef08.sentence: - different buildings that are more than 300 feet (91 m) apart on the same campus.

39bfdd21828e.title: Capacity planning
39bfdd21828e.sentence: Capacity planning is the process of determining the production capacity needed by an organization to meet changing demands for its products.

a2b995404d4c.title: Capacity planning
a2b995404d4c.sentence: IT capacity planning involves estimating the storage, computer hardware, software and connection infrastructure resources required over some future period of time.

2cc4e2fdd7dc.title: Capacity planning
2cc4e2fdd7dc.sentence: A common concern of enterprises is whether the required resources are in place to handle an increase in users or number of interactions.

af7ec90a1f81.title: Capacity planning
af7ec90a1f81.sentence: A discrepancy between the capacity of an organization and the demands of its customers results in inefficiency, either in under-utilized resources or unfulfilled customer demand.

171396a0a761.title: Capacity planning
171396a0a761.sentence: The goal of capacity planning is to minimize this discrepancy.

3cb887e7876b.title: Capacity planning
3cb887e7876b.sentence: The broad classes of capacity planning are lead strategy, lag strategy, match strategy, and adjustment strategy.

074cbb8a4f76.title: Capacity planning
074cbb8a4f76.sentence: - Lead strategy is adding capacity according to the increasing demand.

ce3a75ed6882.title: Capacity planning
ce3a75ed6882.sentence: - Lag strategy refers to adding capacity only after the organization is running at full capacity or beyond due to increase in demand (North Carolina State University, 2006).

f53fab085572.title: Capacity planning
f53fab085572.sentence: - Match strategy is adding capacity in small amounts in response to changing demand in the market.

1966c59bc2b3.title: Capacity planning
1966c59bc2b3.sentence: Of course, a lead capacity strategy can be very risky, particularly if demand is unpredictable or technology is evolving rapidly.

e15ac77e09db.title: Capacity planning
e15ac77e09db.sentence: It decreases the risk of waste, but it may result in the loss of possible customers either by stockout or low service levels.

e54f9b1a9fdb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e54f9b1a9fdb.sentence: Capacity planning should be coupled with performance testing to determine the load at which the service will fail.

28b50bd1923c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
28b50bd1923c.sentence: Good capacity planning can reduce the probability that a cascading failure will occur.

b37aefbd635a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b37aefbd635a.sentence: Capacity planning reduces the probability of triggering a cascading failure, but it is not sufficient to protect the service from cascading failures.

0537cd47b4cb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0537cd47b4cb.sentence: When you lose major parts of your infrastructure during a planned or unplanned event, no amount of capacity planning may be sufficient to prevent cascading failures.

4ff53ba648ea.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-on-architectural-scalability.md
4ff53ba648ea.sentence: Three main bottlenecks to scalability are:

6750a7420069.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-on-architectural-scalability.md
6750a7420069.sentence: - Centralized components: This can become a single point of failure

7668cefcf575.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-on-architectural-scalability.md
7668cefcf575.sentence: - High Latency Components: These are components that perform time-consuming operations.

f775f3a0303a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-on-architectural-scalability.md
f775f3a0303a.sentence: - Tight Coupling: Makes the components difficult to scale

04b3d3f28c33.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-on-architectural-scalability.md
04b3d3f28c33.sentence: Therefore, to build a scalable system, we should follow the principles of statelessness, loose coupling, and asynchronous processing.

8ff862ce6710.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
8ff862ce6710.sentence: Servers in a cluster are aware of each other and work together toward a common purpose.

7ba9e9bbb105.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
7ba9e9bbb105.sentence: But with load balancing, servers are not aware of each other.

551e932a1926.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
551e932a1926.sentence: Load balancing shares some common traits with clustering, but they are different processes.

177fb758b6fd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
177fb758b6fd.sentence: Clustering provides redundancy and boosts capacity and availability.

a2eb6954f57b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
a2eb6954f57b.sentence: Instead, they react to the requests they receive from the load balancer.

ce0c39ac7a3a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::clustering
ce0c39ac7a3a.sentence: We can employ load balancing in conjunction with clustering, but it also is applicable in cases involving independent servers that share a common purpose such as to run a website, business application, web service, or some other IT resource.

ae643f9ae151.title: Replication (computing)
ae643f9ae151.sentence: Replication in computing refers to maintain multiple copies of data, processes, or resources to ensure consistency across redundant components.

b3f6156f18aa.title: Replication (computing)
b3f6156f18aa.sentence: This fundamental technique spans databases, file systems, and distributed systems, serving to improve availability, fault-tolerance, accessibility, and performance.

3bec1e0bd76a.title: Replication (computing)
3bec1e0bd76a.sentence: Through replication, systems can continue operating when components fail (failover), serve requests from geographically distributed locations, and balance load across multiple machines.

70f2b07f9acd.title: Replication (computing)
70f2b07f9acd.sentence: The challenge lies in maintaining consistency between replicas while managing the fundamental tradeoffs between data consistency, system availability, and network partition tolerance – constraints known as the CAP theorem.

173abc67ba2c.title: Replication (computing)
173abc67ba2c.sentence: - Data replication, where the same data is stored on multiple storage devices

2590414ba085.title: Replication (computing)
2590414ba085.sentence: - Computation replication, where the same computing task is executed many times.

8c64fa6fae1b.title: Replication (computing)
8c64fa6fae1b.sentence: - Replicated in space, where tasks are executed on separate devices

90c6cffb567b.title: Replication (computing)
90c6cffb567b.sentence: - Replicated in time, where tasks are executed repeatedly on a single device

cacfc020623b.title: Replication (computing)
cacfc020623b.sentence: Access to a replicated entity is typically uniform with access to a single non-replicated entity.

f21543a57d9e.title: Replication (computing)
f21543a57d9e.sentence: The replication itself should be transparent to an external user.

78820ad7291e.title: Replication (computing)
78820ad7291e.sentence: In a failure scenario, a failover of replicas should be hidden as much as possible with respect to quality of service.

b9ba07ef403d.title: Replication (computing)
b9ba07ef403d.sentence: Backup differs from replication in that the saved copy of data remains unchanged for a long period of time.

e56c2ece4eaf.title: Replication (computing)
e56c2ece4eaf.sentence: Replicas, on the other hand, undergo frequent updates and quickly lose any historical state.

d05cb2d492b2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
d05cb2d492b2.sentence: Replication is a process that involves sharing information to ensure consistency between redundant resources such as multiple databases, to improve reliability, fault-tolerance, or accessibility.

f52b7dd2685d.title: Single point of failure
f52b7dd2685d.sentence: A single point of failure (SPOF) is a part of a system that would stop the entire system from working if it were to fail.

5f3e78ee7a8a.title: Single point of failure
5f3e78ee7a8a.sentence: The term single point of failure implies that there is no backup or redundant option that would enable the system to continue to function without it.

52853c8f1044.title: Single point of failure
52853c8f1044.sentence: SPOFs are undesirable in any system with a goal of high availability or reliability, be it a business practice, software application, or other industrial system.

e83b796ba00d.title: Single point of failure
e83b796ba00d.sentence: If there is a SPOF present in a system, it produces a potential interruption to the system that is substantially more disruptive than an error would be elsewhere in the system.

7b549f6b6b9d.title: Single point of failure
7b549f6b6b9d.sentence: Systems can be made robust by adding redundancy in all potential SPOFs.

fd9750be3495.title: Single point of failure
fd9750be3495.sentence: The assessment of a potential SPOF involves identifying the critical components of a complex system that would provoke a total systems failure in case of malfunction.

201a89dddd63.title: Single point of failure
201a89dddd63.sentence: A fault-tolerant computer system can be achieved at the internal component level, at the system level (multiple machines), or site level (replication).

c1a6ea8c1537.title: Single point of failure
c1a6ea8c1537.sentence: One would normally deploy a load balancer to ensure high availability for a server cluster at the system level.

5d300cce8269.title: Single point of failure
5d300cce8269.sentence: System-level redundancy could be obtained by having spare servers waiting to take on the work of another server if it fails.

46f1214b8e99.title: Single point of failure
46f1214b8e99.sentence: Since a data center is often a support center for other operations, such as business logic, it represents a potential SPOF in itself.

e9492a6db549.title: Single point of failure
e9492a6db549.sentence: Thus, at the site level, the entire cluster may be replicated at another location, where it can be accessed in case the primary location becomes unavailable.

29f1d23da731.title: Single point of failure
29f1d23da731.sentence: This is typically addressed as part of an IT disaster recovery program.

18d1133e1e55.title: Single point of failure
18d1133e1e55.sentence: While previously the solution to this SPOF was physical duplication of clusters, the high demand for this duplication led multiple businesses to outsource duplication to 3rd parties using cloud computing.

e5e7ec279fe9.title: Single point of failure
e5e7ec279fe9.sentence: It has been argued by scholars, however, that doing so simply moves the SPOF and may even increase the likelihood of a failure or cyberattack.

deea2eb4c64b.title: Single point of failure
deea2eb4c64b.sentence: Such networks – including ARPANET and the Internet – are designed to have no single point of failure.

8d687a9ef67a.title: Single point of failure
8d687a9ef67a.sentence: Multiple paths between any two points on the network allow those points to continue communicating with each other, the packets "routing around" damage, even after any single failure of any one particular path or any one intermediate node.

ec7434886030.title: Replication (computing)
ec7434886030.sentence: For example, the primary might perform some computation, streaming a log of updates to a backup (standby) process, which can then take over if the primary fails.

39a16c2d366e.title: Multi-master replication
39a16c2d366e.sentence: Multi-master replication can also be contrasted with failover clustering where passive replica servers are replicating the master data in order to prepare for takeover in the event that the master stops functioning.

716a97a69838.title: Multi-master replication
716a97a69838.sentence: The master is the only server active for client interaction.

53573be7f094.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
53573be7f094.sentence: If the master goes offline, the system can continue to operate in read-only mode until a slave is promoted to a master or a new master is provisioned.

54477007ed47.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
54477007ed47.sentence: Both masters serve reads/writes and coordinate with each other.

de393c2c0603.title: Failover
de393c2c0603.sentence: Failover is switching to a redundant or standby computer server, system, hardware component or network upon the failure or abnormal termination of the previously active application, server, system, hardware component, or network in a computer network.

9cbd2ea3a8c6.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
9cbd2ea3a8c6.section: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers # > 26.2.2. Standby Server Operation #
9cbd2ea3a8c6.sentence: Standby mode is exited and the server switches to normal operation when pg_ctl promote is run, or pg_promote() is called.

f6a448c7bf6a.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
f6a448c7bf6a.sentence: Recovery performance is sufficiently good that the standby will typically be only moments away from full availability once it has been activated.

eb00ae50e092.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
eb00ae50e092.section: Case Study 2: Failover Requires Human Intervention
eb00ae50e092.sentence: If the primary canât determine the health of its secondary, it makes itself unavailable and escalates to a human in order to avoid the split-brain scenario seen in Case Study 1.

b0fc45966a13.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
b0fc45966a13.section: Case Study 2: Failover Requires Human Intervention
b0fc45966a13.sentence: This solution doesnât risk data loss, but it does negatively impact availability of data.

2d00e0c36def.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2d00e0c36def.section: Case Study 2: Failover Requires Human Intervention
2d00e0c36def.sentence: It also unnecessarily increases operational load on the engineers who run the system, and human intervention scales poorly.

2bd86f293386.title: Gossip protocol
2bd86f293386.sentence: A gossip protocol or epidemic protocol is a procedure or process of computer peer-to-peer communication that is based on the way epidemics spread.

8773ee54864a.title: Gossip protocol
8773ee54864a.sentence: Computer systems typically implement this type of protocol with a form of random "peer selection": with a given frequency, each machine picks another machine at random and shares any rumors.

89470182bc4e.title: Gossip protocol
89470182bc4e.sentence: After each water cooler rendezvous, the number of individuals who have heard the rumor roughly doubles (though this doesn't account for gossiping twice to the same person; perhaps Dave tries to tell the story to Frank, only to find that Frank already heard it from Alice).

737ebfd33fb5.title: Gossip protocol
737ebfd33fb5.sentence: In the next "round" of gossip A and B will pick additional random peers, maybe C and D. This round-by-round doubling phenomenon makes the protocol very robust, even if some messages get lost, or some of the selected peers are the same or already know about the search string.

d862a1d4acc3.title: Gossip protocol
d862a1d4acc3.sentence: - The core of the protocol involves periodic, pairwise, inter-process interactions.

0cc79ed20690.title: Gossip protocol
0cc79ed20690.sentence: - The information exchanged during these interactions is of bounded size.

1050b4ff1114.title: Gossip protocol
1050b4ff1114.sentence: - The frequency of the interactions is low compared to typical message latencies so that the protocol costs are negligible.

9aee0839486a.title: Gossip protocol
9aee0839486a.sentence: - There is some form of randomness in the peer selection.

554470b6cac5.title: Gossip protocol
554470b6cac5.sentence: - Due to the replication there is an implicit redundancy of the delivered information.

cfb15cf3a8ef.title: Gossip protocol
cfb15cf3a8ef.sentence: These use gossip to spread information; they basically work by flooding agents in the network, but in a manner that produces bounded worst-case loads:

f98aef293832.title: Gossip protocol
f98aef293832.sentence: These compute a network-wide aggregate by sampling information at the nodes in the network and combining the values to arrive at a system-wide value – the largest value for some measurement nodes are making, smallest, etc. The key requirement is that the aggregate must be computable by fixed-size pairwise information exchanges; these typically terminate after a number of rounds of information exchange logarithmic in the system size, by which time an all-to-all information flow pattern will have been established.

b7bad6c1ed0c.title: Gossip protocol
b7bad6c1ed0c.sentence: It follows that within logarithmic time in the size of the network (the number of agents), any new search string will have reached all agents.

ffc250541775.title: Gossip protocol
ffc250541775.sentence: For example, in a network with 25,000 machines, we can find the best match after about 30 rounds of gossip: 15 to spread the search string and 15 more to discover the best match.

240821fd3118.title: Gossip protocol
240821fd3118.sentence: For this purpose, a protocol must propagate any new information to all nodes that will be affected by the information within time logarithmic in the size of the system (the "mixing time" must be logarithmic in system size).

74872aaa5aca.title: Gossip protocol
74872aaa5aca.sentence: Gossip protocols have also been used for achieving and maintaining distributed database consistency or with other types of data in consistent states, counting the number of nodes in a network of unknown size, spreading news robustly, organizing nodes according to some structuring policy, building so-called overlay networks, computing aggregates, sorting the nodes in a network, electing leaders, etc.

76c862210349.title: Dynamo (storage system)
76c862210349.sentence: Membership and failure detection | Gossip-based membership protocol and failure detection | Avoids having a centralized registry for storing membership and node liveness information, preserving symmetry.

880cceb5cdbe.sentence: Ad hoc means of solving these sorts of problems (such as heartbeats and gossip protocols) will always have reliability problems in practice.
