6ba298148ee4.title: Replication (computing)
6ba298148ee4.sentence: In single-leader (also called primary/replica) replication, one database instance is designated as the leader (primary), which handles all write operations.

aae67c3f1ae5.title: Replication (computing)
aae67c3f1ae5.sentence: The leader logs these updates, which then propagate to replica nodes.

525a768a827e.title: Replication (computing)
525a768a827e.sentence: Each replica acknowledges receipt of updates, enabling subsequent write operations.

e1bb7b865aa7.title: Replication (computing)
e1bb7b865aa7.sentence: Replicas primarily serve read requests, though they may serve stale data due to replication lag – the delay in propagating changes from the leader.

00a238a3739d.title: Replication (computing)
00a238a3739d.sentence: This approach is common for replicating databases, despite the risk that if a portion of the log is lost during a failure, the backup might not be in a state identical to the primary, and transactions could then be lost.

293dcf72dd3e.title: Replication (computing)
293dcf72dd3e.sentence: A weakness of primary-backup schemes is that only one is actually performing operations.

c1291a977ff5.title: Replication (computing)
c1291a977ff5.sentence: Fault-tolerance is gained, but the identical backup system doubles the costs.

97fa5d5828dc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
97fa5d5828dc.sentence: The master serves reads and writes, replicating writes to one or more slaves, which serve only reads.

ca6a15e8d0e4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
ca6a15e8d0e4.sentence: Slaves can also replicate additional slaves in a tree-like fashion.

4ca56dedb580.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
4ca56dedb580.sentence: - Backups of the entire database have relatively no impact on the master.

afdfad84cdc7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
afdfad84cdc7.sentence: - Applications can read from the slave(s) without impacting the master.

5df53334a39b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
5df53334a39b.sentence: - Slaves can be taken offline and synced back to the master without any downtime.

366317f2127f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
366317f2127f.sentence: - Replication adds more hardware and additional complexity.

a5671c2379ed.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
a5671c2379ed.sentence: - Downtime and possibly loss of data when a master fails.

35c6fc8f73a4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
35c6fc8f73a4.sentence: - All writes also have to be made to the master in a master-slave architecture.

253c53060a22.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
253c53060a22.sentence: - The more read slaves, the more we have to replicate, which will increase replication lag.

094b070a3d34.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
094b070a3d34.sentence: Continuous archiving can be used to create a high availability (HA) cluster configuration with one or more standby servers ready to take over operations if the primary server fails.

5961ca8e51a2.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
5961ca8e51a2.sentence: This capability is widely referred to as warm standby or log shipping.

a9ea9bf64a33.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
a9ea9bf64a33.sentence: Directly moving WAL records from one database server to another is typically described as log shipping.

355a25a91359.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
355a25a91359.sentence: The primary server operates in continuous archiving mode, while each standby server operates in continuous recovery mode, reading the WAL files from the primary.

6aaaa8e08560.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
6aaaa8e08560.sentence: The primary and standby server work together to provide this capability, though the servers are only loosely coupled.

cea14c738cc5.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
cea14c738cc5.sentence: No changes to the database tables are required to enable this capability, so it offers low administration overhead compared to some other replication solutions.

4c6a4c543ad0.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
4c6a4c543ad0.sentence: This configuration also has relatively low performance impact on the primary server.

03e9c19bbe56.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
03e9c19bbe56.sentence: PostgreSQL implements file-based log shipping by transferring WAL records one file (WAL segment) at a time.

48a4e0190981.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
48a4e0190981.sentence: WAL files (16MB) can be shipped easily and cheaply over any distance, whether it be to an adjacent system, another system at the same site, or another system on the far side of the globe.

4ac3c7cd56e7.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
4ac3c7cd56e7.sentence: The bandwidth required for this technique varies according to the transaction rate of the primary server.

d0a2f4cd6b45.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
d0a2f4cd6b45.sentence: Record-based log shipping is more granular and streams WAL changes incrementally over a network connection (see Section 26.2.5).

6b12c6b5e657.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
6b12c6b5e657.sentence: It should be noted that log shipping is asynchronous, i.e., the WAL records are shipped after transaction commit.

a12c1aed656a.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
a12c1aed656a.sentence: As a result, there is a window for data loss should the primary server suffer a catastrophic failure; transactions not yet shipped will be lost.

7dc8fe7b5ec7.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
7dc8fe7b5ec7.sentence: The size of the data loss window in file-based log shipping can be limited by use of the archive_timeout parameter, which can be set as low as a few seconds.

a5ed96cfe8f1.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
a5ed96cfe8f1.sentence: However such a low setting will substantially increase the bandwidth required for file shipping.

bca3352b3de6.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
bca3352b3de6.sentence: Streaming replication (see Section 26.2.5) allows a much smaller window of data loss.

159e63d7bcae.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
159e63d7bcae.sentence: As a result, this is called a warm standby configuration which offers high availability.

49f58cb51669.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
49f58cb51669.sentence: Restoring a server from an archived base backup and rollforward will take considerably longer, so that technique only offers a solution for disaster recovery, not high availability.

44f17b8ae338.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
44f17b8ae338.sentence: A standby server can also be used for read-only queries, in which case it is called a hot standby server.

e583f90b3397.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
e583f90b3397.section: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers # > 26.2.2. Standby Server Operation #
e583f90b3397.sentence: In standby mode, the server continuously applies WAL received from the primary server.

21fd670ab3f3.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
21fd670ab3f3.section: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers # > 26.2.2. Standby Server Operation #
21fd670ab3f3.sentence: At startup, the standby begins by restoring all WAL available in the archive location, calling restore_command.

6cacdb4078fb.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
6cacdb4078fb.section: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers # > 26.2.2. Standby Server Operation #
6cacdb4078fb.sentence: If that fails, and streaming replication has been configured, the standby tries to connect to the primary server and start streaming WAL from the last valid record found in archive or pg_wal.

f48d74707e38.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
f48d74707e38.section: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers # > 26.2.2. Standby Server Operation #
f48d74707e38.sentence: This loop of retries from the archive, pg_wal, and via streaming replication goes on until the server is stopped or is promoted.

0d019dca20c7.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
0d019dca20c7.sentence: It is usually wise to create the primary and standby servers so that they are as similar as possible, at least from the perspective of the database server.

dd5e2399e424.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
dd5e2399e424.sentence: In any case the hardware architecture must be the same — shipping from, say, a 32-bit to a 64-bit system will not work.

4b82183eea01.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
4b82183eea01.sentence: In general, log shipping between servers running different major PostgreSQL release levels is not possible.

51ab7c03559e.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
51ab7c03559e.section: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers # > 26.2.3. Preparing the Primary for Standby Servers #
51ab7c03559e.sentence: The archive location should be accessible from the standby even when the primary is down, i.e., it should reside on the standby server itself or another trusted server, not on the primary server.

03814cdd7c95.title: Leader election
03814cdd7c95.sentence: In distributed computing, leader election is the process of designating a single process as the organizer of some task distributed among several computers (nodes).

42643d1f84e9.title: Leader election
42643d1f84e9.sentence: After a leader election algorithm has been run, however, each node throughout the network recognizes a particular, unique node as the task leader.

cca36ca517bd.title: Leader election
cca36ca517bd.sentence: - Termination: the algorithm should finish within a finite time once the leader is selected.

42f062200897.title: Leader election
42f062200897.sentence: - Uniqueness: there is exactly one processor that considers itself as leader.

0c7453446178.title: Leader election
0c7453446178.sentence: - Agreement: all other processors know who the leader is.

bb385231223d.title: Leader election
bb385231223d.sentence: For that, they need some method in order to break the symmetry among them.

328d54d2d174.title: Leader election
328d54d2d174.sentence: For example, if each node has unique and comparable identities, then the nodes can compare their identities, and decide that the node with the highest identity is the leader.

d736bc53982c.title: Leader election
d736bc53982c.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Anonymous rings
d736bc53982c.sentence: There is no deterministic algorithm to elect a leader in anonymous rings, even when the size of the network is known to the processes.

f10532ba91e2.title: Leader election
f10532ba91e2.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Anonymous rings
f10532ba91e2.sentence: This is due to the fact that there is no possibility of breaking symmetry in an anonymous ring if all processes run at the same speed.

486710f40fa8.title: Leader election
486710f40fa8.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Randomized (probabilistic) leader election
486710f40fa8.sentence: A common approach to solve the problem of leader election in anonymous rings is the use of probabilistic algorithms.

e4c2e78f290a.title: Leader election
e4c2e78f290a.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Randomized (probabilistic) leader election
e4c2e78f290a.sentence: At the end, through the application of an algorithm, a leader is selected (with high probability).

f24fa5b198a8.title: Leader election
f24fa5b198a8.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Rings with unique IDs
f24fa5b198a8.sentence: In one of the early works, Chang and Roberts proposed a uniform algorithm in which a processor with the highest ID is selected as the leader.

9a063cefbe1d.title: Leader election
9a063cefbe1d.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Rings with unique IDs
9a063cefbe1d.sentence: Each processor sends its ID in a clockwise direction.

53fe77032a54.title: Leader election
53fe77032a54.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Rings with unique IDs
53fe77032a54.sentence: A processor receives a message and compares the ID with its own.

493dd1f3f947.title: Leader election
493dd1f3f947.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Rings with unique IDs
493dd1f3f947.sentence: If the ID is bigger than the processor passes it through, otherwise it discards the message.

7d6fd50e92bb.title: Leader election
7d6fd50e92bb.section: Algorithms > Leader election in rings > Rings with unique IDs
7d6fd50e92bb.sentence: The authors show that this algorithm uses O(n2) messages in the worst case and O(nlog⁡n) in the average case.

f63f2f48b75d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
f63f2f48b75d.section: Highly Available Processing Using Leader Election
f63f2f48b75d.sentence: Leader election in distributed systems is an equivalent problem to distributed consensus.

523a21fab024.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
523a21fab024.section: Chapter 23 - Managing Critical State: Distributed Consensus for Reliability
523a21fab024.sentence: Whenever you see leader election, critical shared state, or distributed locking, we recommend using distributed consensus systems that have been formally proven and tested thoroughly.

2c25a76939ab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2c25a76939ab.section: Highly Available Processing Using Leader Election
2c25a76939ab.sentence: System designers can construct a highly available service by writing it as though it was a simple program, replicating that process and using leader election to ensure that only one leader is working at any point in time (as shown in Figure 23-3).

83d03a55b012.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
83d03a55b012.section: Highly Available Processing Using Leader Election
83d03a55b012.sentence: Replicated services that use a single leader to perform some specific type of work in the system are very common; the single leader mechanism is a way of ensuring mutual exclusion at a coarse level.

f8282cb51431.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
f8282cb51431.section: Highly Available Processing Using Leader Election
f8282cb51431.sentence: Often the work of the leader is that of coordinating some pool of workers in the system.

9999b22934f0.title: Raft (algorithm)
9999b22934f0.sentence: If no heartbeat is received the follower changes its status to candidate and starts a leader election.

3eba9097d464.title: Paxos (computer science)
3eba9097d464.section: Basic Paxos > Paxos can be used to select a leader
3eba9097d464.sentence: This satisfies the needs of leader election because there is a single node believing it is the leader and a single node known to be the leader at all times.

0c4db7021eac.title: Multi-master replication
0c4db7021eac.sentence: Multi-master replication is a method of database replication which allows data to be stored by a group of computers, and updated by any member of the group.

ff0c38020d0a.title: Multi-master replication
ff0c38020d0a.sentence: All members are responsive to client data queries.

d6ff2544f4e4.title: Multi-master replication
d6ff2544f4e4.sentence: The multi-master replication system is responsible for propagating the data modifications made by each member to the rest of the group and resolving any conflicts that might arise between concurrent changes made by different members.

7f7794f516e1.title: Multi-master replication
7f7794f516e1.sentence: Multi-master replication can be contrasted with master-slave replication, in which a single member of the group is designated as the "master" for a given piece of data and is the only node allowed to modify that data item.

c809105cf474.title: Multi-master replication
c809105cf474.sentence: Other members wishing to modify the data item must first contact the master node.

3b34d9518624.title: Multi-master replication
3b34d9518624.sentence: Allowing only a single master makes it easier to achieve consistency among the members of the group, but is less flexible than multi-master replication.

6a9cfe59c871.title: Multi-master replication
6a9cfe59c871.sentence: The primary purposes of multi-master replication are increased availability and faster server response time.

fbf31c1cd7db.title: Multi-master replication
fbf31c1cd7db.sentence: - Availability: If one master fails, other masters continue to update the database.

2e907c949cf3.title: Multi-master replication
2e907c949cf3.sentence: - Distributed access: Masters can be located in several physical sites, i.e. distributed across the network.

a506c131d3d8.title: Replication (computing)
a506c131d3d8.sentence: This approach is particularly beneficial in multi-data center deployments, where it enables local write processing while masking inter-data center network latency.

4b32cdc1efcd.title: Multi-master replication
4b32cdc1efcd.sentence: - Consistency: Most multi-master replication systems are only loosely consistent, i.e. lazy and asynchronous, violating ACID properties.

9ecdea188032.title: Multi-master replication
9ecdea188032.sentence: - Performance: Eager replication systems are complex and increase communication latency.

dc5d46ac6004.title: Multi-master replication
dc5d46ac6004.sentence: - Integrity: Issues such as conflict resolution can become intractable as the number of nodes involved rises and latency increases.

803322debb86.title: Replication (computing)
803322debb86.sentence: He argued that unless the data splits in some natural way so that the database can be treated as n disjoint sub-databases, concurrency control conflicts will result in seriously degraded performance and the group of replicas will probably slow as a function of n.

d66dcc904954.title: Replication (computing)
d66dcc904954.sentence: Gray suggested that the most common approaches are likely to result in degradation that scales as O(n³).

39687cf1ed48.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
39687cf1ed48.sentence: If either master goes down, the system can continue to operate with both reads and writes.

a9e6563783c7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
a9e6563783c7.sentence: - Applications can read from both masters.

d812914e39db.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
d812914e39db.sentence: - Distributes write load across both master nodes.

6ede4442c666.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
6ede4442c666.sentence: - Not as simple as master-slave to configure and deploy.

f4d10fdaf8d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
f4d10fdaf8d4.sentence: - Either loosely consistent or have increased write latency due to synchronization.

a9c85739cc44.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-replication
a9c85739cc44.sentence: - Conflict resolution comes into play as more write nodes are added and as latency increases.

76e29b8e9744.title: Replication (computing)
76e29b8e9744.sentence: The most common challenge that exists in multi-master replication is transactional conflict prevention or resolution when concurrent modifications occur on different leader nodes.

d3edd376e5eb.title: Replication (computing)
d3edd376e5eb.sentence: Most synchronous (or eager) replication solutions perform conflict prevention, while asynchronous (or lazy) solutions have to perform conflict resolution.

ddbecf213585.title: Replication (computing)
ddbecf213585.sentence: For instance, if the same record is changed on two nodes simultaneously, an eager replication system would detect the conflict before confirming the commit and abort one of the transactions.

f87a8098a6c4.title: Replication (computing)
f87a8098a6c4.sentence: A lazy replication system would allow both transactions to commit and run a conflict resolution during re-synchronization.

920ccc270f24.title: Replication (computing)
920ccc270f24.sentence: Conflict resolution methods can include techniques like last-write-wins, application-specific logic, or merging concurrent updates.

ee18e74db74b.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
ee18e74db74b.sentence: In distributed computing, a conflict-free replicated data type (CRDT) is a data structure that is replicated across multiple computers in a network, with the following features:

b14d5b5e8cba.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
b14d5b5e8cba.sentence: - The application can update any replica independently, concurrently and without coordinating with other replicas.

0958bab19b01.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
0958bab19b01.sentence: - An algorithm (itself part of the data type) automatically resolves any inconsistencies that might occur.

623e3312fc4b.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
623e3312fc4b.sentence: - Although replicas may have different state at any particular point in time, they are guaranteed to eventually converge.

c5a8b920fa12.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
c5a8b920fa12.sentence: Concurrent updates to multiple replicas of the same data, without coordination between the computers hosting the replicas, can result in inconsistencies between the replicas, which in the general case may not be resolvable.

8b122b55e60c.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
8b122b55e60c.sentence: But another possible approach is optimistic replication, where all concurrent updates are allowed to go through, with inconsistencies possibly created, and the results are merged or "resolved" later.

fe61d67d5bae.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
fe61d67d5bae.sentence: While optimistic replication might not work in the general case, there is a significant and practically useful class of data structures, CRDTs, where it does work — where it is always possible to merge or resolve concurrent updates on different replicas of the data structure without conflicts.

eeac0ef50e0a.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
eeac0ef50e0a.sentence: There are two approaches to CRDTs, both of which can provide strong eventual consistency: state-based CRDTs and operation-based CRDTs.

b57cbaa5b97e.title: Eventual consistency
b57cbaa5b97e.sentence: A common approach to ensure SEC is conflict-free replicated data types.

7ce7f7066ce4.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
7ce7f7066ce4.sentence: Development was initially motivated by collaborative text editing and mobile computing.

d5382d3c1870.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
d5382d3c1870.sentence: CRDTs have also been used in online chat systems, online gambling, and in the SoundCloud audio distribution platform.

27a84f6c6f72.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
27a84f6c6f72.sentence: The NoSQL distributed databases Redis, Riak and Cosmos DB have CRDT data types.

8b780940ddd1.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
8b780940ddd1.sentence: A sequence, list, or ordered set CRDT can be used to build a collaborative real-time editor, as an alternative to operational transformation (OT).

bfcd8c674d16.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
bfcd8c674d16.sentence: Some known Sequence CRDTs are Treedoc, RGA, Woot, Logoot, and LSEQ.

bc6fe2dbf440.title: Operational transformation
bc6fe2dbf440.sentence: Another alternative to OT is using sequence types of conflict-free replicated data type.

c6ca02f59ba6.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
c6ca02f59ba6.sentence: League of Legends uses the Riak CRDT implementation for its in-game chat system, which handles 7.5 million concurrent users and 11,000 messages per second.

5da62fd83767.title: Replication (computing)
5da62fd83767.sentence: Synchronous replication guarantees "zero data loss" by the means of atomic write operations, where the write operation is not considered complete until acknowledged by both the local and remote storage.

e132027a65ac.title: Replication (computing)
e132027a65ac.sentence: In asynchronous replication, the write operation is considered complete as soon as local storage acknowledges it.

0c7a7b64cc73.title: Replication (computing)
0c7a7b64cc73.sentence: Most applications wait for a write transaction to complete before proceeding with further work, hence overall performance decreases considerably.

0d17fee83367.title: Replication (computing)
0d17fee83367.sentence: Inherently, performance drops proportionally to distance, as minimum latency is dictated by the speed of light.

5fdecfdcdc42.title: Replication (computing)
5fdecfdcdc42.sentence: For 10 km distance, the fastest possible roundtrip takes 67 μs, whereas an entire local cached write completes in about 10–20 μs.

d381ce5e89d1.title: Replication (computing)
d381ce5e89d1.sentence: For replication, latency is the key factor because it determines either how far apart the sites can be or the type of replication that can be employed.

33d00ef3bf2f.title: Replication (computing)

fb5de3f4f462.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication.html

422d67b94c3d.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication.html

6275ec68855c.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication.html

95e3291769fb.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication.html

f1d2fad3abb1.title: doc>www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication.html

09eaf9ec0dba.title: Split-brain (computing)
09eaf9ec0dba.sentence: In computing, split-brain is a state indicating data or availability inconsistencies originating from the maintenance of two separate data sets with overlap in scope, either because of servers in a network design, or a failure condition based on servers not communicating and synchronizing their data to each other.

e973dda0c9ae.title: Split-brain (computing)
e973dda0c9ae.sentence: This last case is also commonly referred to as a network partition.

062ba30329fa.title: Split-brain (computing)
062ba30329fa.sentence: High-availability clusters (HA clusters) usually use a heartbeat private network connection which is used to monitor the health and status of each node in the cluster.

1350f768c538.title: Split-brain (computing)
1350f768c538.sentence: For example, the split-brain syndrome may occur when all of the private links go down simultaneously, but the cluster nodes are still running, each one believing they are the only one running.

bf7b96726269.title: Split-brain (computing)
bf7b96726269.sentence: The data sets of each cluster may then randomly serve clients by their own "idiosyncratic" data set updates, without any coordination with the other data sets.

1ed578e63a59.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state

c6901ff45775.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
c6901ff45775.sentence: File server pairs may now be in a state in which both nodes are expected to be active for the same resource, or where both are down because both issued and received STONITH commands.

80df1ee51f1f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state

c5dfea8361e5.title: Split-brain (computing)

4549beec9cea.title: Split-brain (computing)

7c29a2767c4f.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
7c29a2767c4f.sentence: State-based CRDTs simply send their full local state to other replicas on every update, where the received new state is then merged into the local state.

9417bf4f9c6e.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
9417bf4f9c6e.sentence: Instead of transmitting states, the update actions are transmitted directly to replicas and applied.

37987d4e60f4.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
37987d4e60f4.sentence: In particular, this means that the merge function must be commutative, associative, and idempotent.

8daa38014f99.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
8daa38014f99.sentence: The intuition behind commutativity, associativity and idempotence is that these properties are used to make the CRDT invariant under package re-ordering and duplication.

472acf2d09b3.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
472acf2d09b3.sentence: Operation-based CRDTs (also called commutative replicated data types, or CmRDTs) are defined without a merge function.

bd0a94d2748e.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
bd0a94d2748e.sentence: For example, an operation-based CRDT of a single integer might broadcast the operations “+10” or “−20”.

406b149974bd.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
406b149974bd.sentence: The application of operations should still be commutative and associative.

ddc2813945f4.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
ddc2813945f4.sentence: However, instead of requiring that application of operations is idempotent, stronger assumptions on the communications infrastructure are expected — all operations must be delivered to the other replicas without duplication.

53e193c6f8ea.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
53e193c6f8ea.sentence: State-based CRDTs are often simpler to design and to implement; their only requirement from the communication substrate is some kind of gossip protocol.

dea8cfca4c09.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
dea8cfca4c09.sentence: Their drawback is that the entire state of every CRDT must be transmitted eventually to every other replica, which may be costly.

67a424a26fbf.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
67a424a26fbf.sentence: Delta state CRDTs (or simply delta CRDTs) are optimized state-based CRDTs where only recently applied changes to a state are disseminated instead of the entire state.

2778e0c1e798.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
2778e0c1e798.sentence: Gossip protocols work well for propagating state-based CRDT state to other replicas while reducing network use and handling topology changes.

b4c0c8a2b9ee.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
b4c0c8a2b9ee.sentence: In contrast, operation-based CRDTs transmit only the update operations, which are typically small.

ac316d89986d.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
ac316d89986d.sentence: While operations-based CRDTs place more requirements on the protocol for transmitting operations between replicas, they use less bandwidth than state-based CRDTs when the number of transactions is small in comparison to the size of internal state.

bacdcedf7ff2.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
bacdcedf7ff2.sentence: However, operation-based CRDTs require guarantees from the communication middleware; that the operations are not dropped or duplicated when transmitted to the other replicas, and that they are delivered in causal order.

6c962c999372.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
6c962c999372.sentence: payload integer[n] P initial [0,0,...,0] update increment() let g = myId() P[g]:= P[g] + 1 query value(): integer v let v = Σi P[i] compare (X, Y): boolean b let b = (∀i ∈ [0, n - 1]: X.P[i] ≤ Y.P[i]) merge (X, Y): payload Z let ∀i ∈ [0, n - 1]: Z.P[i] = max(X.P[i], Y.P[i])

56a4ceeceb29.sentence: The merger of two G-Sets is their union.

c3aa517754ce.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
c3aa517754ce.sentence: Thus each node is assigned its own slot in the array P, which it increments locally.

5a00922bd793.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
5a00922bd793.sentence: In this case, two G-Counters are combined to create a data type supporting both increment and decrement operations.

f3d593883b8e.sentence: The "P" G-Counter counts increments; and the "N" G-Counter counts decrements.

adda9697134d.sentence: The value of the PN-Counter is the value of the P counter minus the value of the N counter.

cc72569d3970.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
cc72569d3970.sentence: A common strategy in CRDT development is to combine multiple CRDTs to make a more complex CRDT.

54a989637ef7.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
54a989637ef7.sentence: The G-Set (grow-only set) is a set which only allows adds.

02aedb6f066b.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
02aedb6f066b.sentence: With the addition of a remove set (called the "tombstone" set), elements can be added and also removed.

95a6c17c7908.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
95a6c17c7908.sentence: Once removed, an element cannot be re-added; that is, once an element e is in the tombstone set, query will never again return True for that element.

4e78eb86c962.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
4e78eb86c962.sentence: LWW-Element-Set is similar to 2P-Set in that it consists of an "add set" and a "remove set", with a timestamp for each element.

e932cdd423fa.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
e932cdd423fa.sentence: An element is a member of the LWW-Element-Set if it is in the add set, and either not in the remove set, or in the remove set but with an earlier timestamp than the latest timestamp in the add set.

afcfeca4c7bc.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
afcfeca4c7bc.sentence: OR-Set resembles LWW-Element-Set, but using unique tags instead of timestamps.

fb0bac6894ac.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
fb0bac6894ac.sentence: Elements are removed from the OR-Set by having all the tags in the element's add-tag list added to the element's remove-tag (tombstone) list.

cb972b817ae4.title: Conflict-free replicated data type
cb972b817ae4.sentence: An element is a member of the set if and only if the add-tag list less the remove-tag list is nonempty.

642c3130a40c.title: Partition (database)
642c3130a40c.sentence: A partition is a division of a logical database or its constituent elements into distinct independent parts.

ad1c58120cc7.title: Partition (database)
ad1c58120cc7.sentence: Database partitioning refers to intentionally breaking a large database into smaller ones for scalability purposes, distinct from network partitions which are a type of network fault between nodes.

d4ec6c83c7c8.title: Partition (database)
d4ec6c83c7c8.sentence: In a partitioned database, each piece of data belongs to exactly one partition, effectively making each partition a small database of its own.

ef9b8648dc0c.title: Partition (database)
ef9b8648dc0c.sentence: In any partitioning scheme, data is typically arranged so that each piece of data (record, row, or document) belongs to exactly one partition.

9f392b11f589.title: Partition (database)
9f392b11f589.sentence: Database partitioning is normally done for manageability, performance or availability reasons, or for load balancing.

b276517b1d35.title: Partition (database)
b276517b1d35.sentence: Partitioning enables distribution of datasets across multiple disks and query loads across multiple processors.

169d6f34dc53.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
169d6f34dc53.sentence: It is the process of splitting up a database or a table across multiple machines to improve the manageability, performance, and availability of a database.

1c3de0bc9fe4.title: Partition (database)
1c3de0bc9fe4.sentence: For queries that operate on a single partition, each node executes queries independently on its local partition, enabling linear scaling of query throughput with additional nodes.

94fa0104bf0e.title: Partition (database)
94fa0104bf0e.sentence: More complex queries can be parallelized across multiple nodes, though this presents additional challenges.

a24c973cbf04.title: Partition (database)

ed94f6cc4332.title: Partition (database)
ed94f6cc4332.sentence: Each record belongs to one partition but may exist on multiple nodes for fault tolerance.

5137486be406.title: Partition (database)
5137486be406.sentence: In leader-follower replication systems, nodes can simultaneously serve as leaders for some partitions and followers for others.

651014ca0fd9.title: Partition (database)
651014ca0fd9.sentence: Different DBMSs use varying terminology for partitioning:

4a1eac4ee1a7.title: Partition (database)

e4f1a865e80b.title: Partition (database)
e4f1a865e80b.sentence: They take a partitioning key and assign a partition based on certain criteria.

dcc96b5df336.title: Partition (database)
dcc96b5df336.sentence: - Range partitioning: assigns continuous key ranges to partitions, analogous to encyclopedia volumes.

ac41dd66986e.title: Partition (database)
ac41dd66986e.sentence: - List partitioning: a partition is assigned a list of values.

a6d009145e1c.title: Partition (database)
a6d009145e1c.sentence: - Composite partitioning: allows for certain combinations of the above partitioning schemes, by for example first applying a range partitioning and then a hash partitioning.

aca51c66e9d3.title: Partition (database)
aca51c66e9d3.sentence: - Round-robin partitioning: the simplest strategy, it ensures uniform data distribution.

1a628b7dc95b.title: Partition (database)
1a628b7dc95b.sentence: - Hash partitioning: applies a hash function to convert skewed data into uniform distributions for even load distribution across partitions.

9f5afc6aec09.title: Partition (database)
9f5afc6aec09.sentence: Current high-end relational database management systems provide for different criteria to split the database.

3c9cec68c9b8.title: Partition (database)
3c9cec68c9b8.sentence: If the partitioning key has one of these values, the partition is chosen.

f205d65f6d60.title: Partition (database)
f205d65f6d60.sentence: For example, all rows where the column Country is either Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Finland or Denmark could build a partition for the Nordic countries.

e94c373c65eb.sentence: In list-based partitioning, each partition is defined and selected based on the list of values on a column rather than a set of contiguous ranges of values.

162cb226a3a1.title: Shared-nothing architecture
162cb226a3a1.sentence: A shared-nothing architecture (SN) is a distributed computing architecture in which each update request is satisfied by a single node (processor/memory/storage unit) in a computer cluster.

b59814888346.title: Shared-nothing architecture
b59814888346.sentence: Nodes do not share (independently access) the same memory or storage.

f56bccfe7d77.title: Shared-nothing architecture
f56bccfe7d77.sentence: The intent is to eliminate contention among nodes.

003324ec25bc.title: Shared-nothing architecture
003324ec25bc.sentence: One alternative architecture is shared everything, in which requests are satisfied by arbitrary combinations of nodes.

8075f6c7fe70.title: Shared-nothing architecture
8075f6c7fe70.sentence: This may introduce contention, as multiple nodes may seek to update the same data at the same time.

6f025d885576.title: Shared-nothing architecture
6f025d885576.sentence: It also contrasts with shared-disk and shared-memory architectures.

d82d54f83635.title: Shared-nothing architecture
d82d54f83635.sentence: SN eliminates single points of failure, allowing the overall system to continue operating despite failures in individual nodes and allowing individual nodes to upgrade hardware or software without a system-wide shutdown.

e65d0f0516ad.title: Shared-nothing architecture
e65d0f0516ad.sentence: A SN system can scale simply by adding nodes, since no central resource bottlenecks the system.

0eb21b65f202.title: Shared-nothing architecture
0eb21b65f202.sentence: A SN system typically partitions its data among many nodes.

395bf6235c27.title: Shared-nothing architecture

4222f7ed7170.title: Shared-nothing architecture
4222f7ed7170.sentence: A refinement is to replicate commonly used but infrequently modified data across many nodes, allowing more requests to be resolved on a single node.

1ce53ade7038.sentence: Shared-nothing is popular for web development.

d829a73ec735.title: Shared-nothing architecture

c33eb50ed532.title: Shard (database architecture)

34cb2ddf2945.sentence: Consistent hashing solves this horizontal scalability problem by ensuring that every time we scale up or down, we do not have to re-arrange all the keys or touch all the servers.

ca9ea7036c98.title: Consistent hashing
ca9ea7036c98.sentence: In computer science, consistent hashing is a special kind of hashing technique such that when a hash table is resized, only n/m keys need to be remapped on average where n is the number of keys and m is the number of slots.

cca5dff5e29a.title: Consistent hashing
cca5dff5e29a.sentence: In contrast, in most traditional hash tables, a change in the number of array slots causes nearly all keys to be remapped because the mapping between the keys and the slots is defined by a modular operation.

29149e141f73.title: Consistent hashing
29149e141f73.sentence: However, when a server is added or removed during outage or scaling (when n changes), all the BLOBs in every server should be reassigned and moved due to rehashing, but this operation is expensive.

3d5e70d02c60.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/consistent-hashing.md
3d5e70d02c60.section: What’s the issue with simple hashing?
3d5e70d02c60.sentence: But when new servers get added to meet new demand, or when existing servers get removed, it triggers a storm of misses and a lot of objects to be moved.

c66d08c61bd1.title: Consistent hashing
c66d08c61bd1.sentence: The central idea is to use a hash function that maps both the BLOB and servers to a unit circle, usually 2π radians.

f016d7772e81.title: Consistent hashing
f016d7772e81.sentence: Each BLOB is then assigned to the next server that appears on the circle in clockwise order.

4860a09b62a6.title: Consistent hashing
4860a09b62a6.sentence: But, more importantly, if a server fails and is removed from the circle, only the BLOBs that were mapped to the failed server need to be reassigned to the next server in clockwise order.

bf9713e4fcb2.title: Consistent hashing
bf9713e4fcb2.sentence: Likewise, if a new server is added, it is added to the unit circle, and only the BLOBs that would now be assigned to the new server need to be reassigned.

5db4af5acccf.title: Consistent hashing
5db4af5acccf.sentence: Importantly, when a server is added or removed, the vast majority of the BLOBs maintain their prior server assignments, and the addition of nth server only causes 1/n fraction of the BLOBs to relocate.

2659e93c7a03.title: Consistent hashing
2659e93c7a03.sentence: Consistent hashing evenly distributes cache keys across shards, even if some of the shards crash or become unavailable.

503952a88325.sentence: Our protocols are particularly designed for use with very large networks such as the Internet, where delays caused by hot spots can be severe, and where it is not feasible for every server to have complete information about the current state of the entire network.
