d5f7d05e1927.sentence: The protocols work with local control, make efficient use of existing resources, and scale gracefully as the network grows.

0e6f45ea65e6.title: Consistent hashing
0e6f45ea65e6.sentence: This academic paper from 1997 in Symposium on Theory of Computing introduced the term "consistent hashing" as a way of distributing requests among a changing population of web servers.

0cc111c0c503.title: Distributed hash table
0cc111c0c503.sentence: A distributed hash table (DHT) is a distributed system that provides a lookup service similar to a hash table.

8a524c6c990a.title: Distributed hash table
8a524c6c990a.sentence: Key–value pairs are stored in a DHT, and any participating node can efficiently retrieve the value associated with a given key.

eea595b04487.title: Distributed hash table
eea595b04487.sentence: Keys are unique identifiers which map to particular values, which in turn can be anything from addresses, to documents, to arbitrary data.

dd1f84c4506f.title: Distributed hash table
dd1f84c4506f.sentence: The main advantage of a DHT is that nodes can be added or removed with minimum work around re-distributing keys.

779b386806b3.title: Distributed hash table
779b386806b3.sentence: Responsibility for maintaining the mapping from keys to values is distributed among the nodes, in such a way that a change in the set of participants causes a minimal amount of disruption.

7415bdc3689f.title: Distributed hash table
7415bdc3689f.sentence: This allows a DHT to scale to extremely large numbers of nodes and to handle continual node arrivals, departures, and failures.

afae47428023.title: Distributed hash table
afae47428023.sentence: The structure of a DHT can be decomposed into several main components.

6888727c8516.title: Distributed hash table
6888727c8516.sentence: The foundation is an abstract keyspace, such as the set of 160-bit strings.

68b46d97cfd8.title: Distributed hash table
68b46d97cfd8.sentence: A keyspace partitioning scheme splits ownership of this keyspace among the participating nodes.

d45f146c937d.title: Distributed hash table
d45f146c937d.sentence: An overlay network then connects the nodes, allowing them to find the owner of any given key in the keyspace.

160c9fd8ab6f.title: Distributed hash table
160c9fd8ab6f.sentence: Most DHTs use some variant of consistent hashing or rendezvous hashing to map keys to nodes.

88d587911617.title: Distributed hash table
88d587911617.sentence: Both consistent hashing and rendezvous hashing have the essential property that removal or addition of one node changes only the set of keys owned by the nodes with adjacent IDs, and leaves all other nodes unaffected.

81294f5684ad.title: Distributed hash table
81294f5684ad.sentence: Contrast this with a traditional hash table in which addition or removal of one bucket causes nearly the entire keyspace to be remapped.

602d641f0c43.title: Distributed hash table
602d641f0c43.sentence: Since any change in ownership typically corresponds to bandwidth-intensive movement of objects stored in the DHT from one node to another, minimizing such reorganization is required to efficiently support high rates of churn (node arrival and failure).

05826f82948e.title: Distributed hash table
05826f82948e.sentence: Each node maintains a set of links to other nodes (its neighbors or routing table).

31beb23dea1a.title: Distributed hash table
31beb23dea1a.sentence: All DHT topologies share some variant of the most essential property: for any key k, each node either has a node ID that owns k or has a link to a node whose node ID is closer to k, in terms of the keyspace distance defined above.

2de64ba1c053.title: Distributed hash table
2de64ba1c053.sentence: It is then easy to route a message to the owner of any key k using the following greedy algorithm (that is not necessarily globally optimal): at each step, forward the message to the neighbor whose ID is closest to k.

afb3b9495b21.title: Distributed hash table
afb3b9495b21.sentence: This style of routing is sometimes called key-based routing.

64468bbc45e8.title: Distributed hash table
64468bbc45e8.sentence: A key technique used to achieve these goals is that any one node needs to coordinate with only a few other nodes in the system‍— most commonly, O(log n) of the n participants (see below)‍— so that only a limited amount of work needs to be done for each change in membership.

651c47f3fa41.title: Distributed hash table
651c47f3fa41.sentence: The most common choice, O(log⁡n) degree/route length, is not optimal in terms of degree/route length tradeoff, but such topologies typically allow more flexibility in choice of neighbors.

03c01f62b574.title: Distributed hash table
03c01f62b574.sentence: O (log ⁡ n) | Chord Kademlia Pastry Tapestry | Most common, but not optimal (degree/route length). Chord is the most basic version, with Kademlia seeming the most popular optimized variant (should have improved average lookup)

8df6f60395ee.title: Distributed hash table
8df6f60395ee.sentence: Of course, having shorter routes requires higher maximum degree.

cc3c9ec337aa.title: Distributed hash table
cc3c9ec337aa.sentence: - Autonomy and decentralization: The nodes collectively form the system without any central coordination.

5ea97dcd4e1e.title: Distributed hash table
5ea97dcd4e1e.sentence: - Fault tolerance: The system should be reliable (in some sense) even with nodes continuously joining, leaving, and failing.

e3ce763a5da6.title: Distributed hash table
e3ce763a5da6.sentence: - Scalability: The system should function efficiently even with thousands or millions of nodes.

82d6d51a1064.title: Distributed hash table
82d6d51a1064.sentence: DHTs form an infrastructure that can be used to build more complex services, such as anycast, cooperative web caching, distributed file systems, domain name services, instant messaging, multicast, and also peer-to-peer file sharing and content distribution systems.

8fb55ee0ce30.title: Distributed hash table
8fb55ee0ce30.sentence: Notable distributed networks that use DHTs include BitTorrent's distributed tracker, the Kad network, the Storm botnet, the Tox instant messenger, Freenet, the YaCy search engine, and the InterPlanetary File System.

311cbdb287b1.title: Distributed hash table
311cbdb287b1.sentence: Locality-preserving hashing ensures that similar keys are assigned to similar objects.

ae24c8723315.title: Distributed hash table
ae24c8723315.sentence: This can enable a more efficient execution of range queries, however, in contrast to using consistent hashing, there is no more assurance that the keys (and thus the load) is uniformly randomly distributed over the key space and the participating peers.

7eda22f2f8b1.title: Rendezvous hashing
7eda22f2f8b1.sentence: Rendezvous or highest random weight (HRW) hashing is an algorithm that allows clients to achieve distributed agreement on a set of k options out of a possible set of n options.

c05fb955d124.title: Rendezvous hashing
c05fb955d124.sentence: A typical application is when clients need to agree on which sites (or proxies) objects are assigned to.

89fc5cd64811.title: Rendezvous hashing
89fc5cd64811.sentence: Each client is to make its selection independently, but all clients must end up picking the same subset of sites.

1f21a35d2708.title: Rendezvous hashing
1f21a35d2708.sentence: The standard version of the problem uses k = 1.

f4839b6ef821.title: Rendezvous hashing
f4839b6ef821.sentence: All clients first agree on a hash function h(⋅).

062b0bc8df59.title: Rendezvous hashing
062b0bc8df59.sentence: For object Oi, the site Sj is defined to have weight wi,j=h(Oi,Sj).

c4313923f083.title: Rendezvous hashing
c4313923f083.sentence: The basic idea is to give each site Sj a score (a weight) for each object Oi, and assign the object to the highest scoring site.

7784358de9b9.title: Rendezvous hashing
7784358de9b9.sentence: Each client independently computes these weights wi,1,wi,2…wi,n and picks the k sites that yield the k largest hash values.

a792723d364b.title: Rendezvous hashing
a792723d364b.sentence: Unfortunately, if any of the sites fails or is unreachable, the hash table size changes, forcing all objects to be remapped.

edd1608930cc.title: Rendezvous hashing
edd1608930cc.sentence: This massive disruption makes such direct hashing unworkable.

539010313f52.title: Rendezvous hashing
539010313f52.sentence: Under rendezvous hashing, however, clients handle site failures by picking the site that yields the next largest weight.

a149c579ccf3.title: Rendezvous hashing
a149c579ccf3.sentence: Remapping is required only for objects currently mapped to the failed site, and disruption is minimal.

ccff01c1001d.title: Rendezvous hashing
ccff01c1001d.sentence: - Low overhead: The hash function used is efficient, so overhead at the clients is very low.

e2b240c308b2.title: Rendezvous hashing
e2b240c308b2.sentence: - Load balancing: Since the hash function is randomizing, each of the n sites is equally likely to receive the object O. Loads are uniform across the sites.

c8eda41a0563.title: Rendezvous hashing
c8eda41a0563.sentence: - Minimal disruption: When a site fails, only the objects mapped to that site need to be remapped.

6643d95bae45.title: Rendezvous hashing
6643d95bae45.sentence: HRW easily accommodates different capacities among sites.

00b854b2cc80.title: Rendezvous hashing
00b854b2cc80.sentence: If site Sk has twice the capacity of the other sites, we simply represent Sk twice in the list, say, as Sk,1,Sk,2.

76e2d800ed52.title: Rendezvous hashing
76e2d800ed52.sentence: Clearly, twice as many objects will now map to Sk as to the other sites.

ea8a0bd80772.title: Rendezvous hashing
ea8a0bd80772.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Advantages of Rendezvous hashing over consistent hashing
ea8a0bd80772.sentence: Rendezvous hashing (HRW) is much simpler conceptually and in practice.

810adcea2e6b.title: Rendezvous hashing
810adcea2e6b.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Advantages of Rendezvous hashing over consistent hashing
810adcea2e6b.sentence: Unlike consistent hashing, HRW requires no precomputing or storage of tokens.

b9bfa84a6cfd.title: Rendezvous hashing
b9bfa84a6cfd.sentence: Because of its simplicity, lower overhead, and generality (it works for any k < n), rendezvous hashing is increasingly being preferred over consistent hashing.

dcb0d1d47b80.title: Rendezvous hashing
dcb0d1d47b80.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Advantages of Rendezvous hashing over consistent hashing
dcb0d1d47b80.sentence: If Sk is taken offline, its objects will be remapped uniformly to the remaining n−1 sites.

c58d128b1bec.title: Rendezvous hashing
c58d128b1bec.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Advantages of Rendezvous hashing over consistent hashing
c58d128b1bec.sentence: HRW completely avoids all the overhead and complexity associated with correctly handling multiple tokens for each site and associated metadata.

012f855b6c96.title: Consistent hashing
012f855b6c96.section: Comparison with rendezvous hashing and other alternatives
012f855b6c96.sentence: It can in fact be shown that consistent hashing is a special case of rendezvous hashing.

41388636c70d.title: Rendezvous hashing
41388636c70d.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Consistent hashing is a special case of Rendezvous hashing
41388636c70d.sentence: Consistent hashing can be shown to be a special case of HRW by an appropriate choice of a two-place hash function.

2e554536068c.title: Rendezvous hashing
2e554536068c.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Consistent hashing is a special case of Rendezvous hashing
2e554536068c.sentence: It is not possible, however, to reduce HRW to consistent hashing (assuming the number of tokens per site is bounded), since HRW potentially reassigns the objects from a removed site to an unbounded number of other sites.

06918ffa4296.title: Rendezvous hashing
06918ffa4296.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Advantages of Rendezvous hashing over consistent hashing
06918ffa4296.sentence: Variants of the HRW algorithm, such as the use of a skeleton (see below), can reduce the O(n) time for object location to O(log⁡n), at the cost of less global uniformity of placement.

4e807cb508ca.title: Rendezvous hashing
4e807cb508ca.section: Comparison with consistent hashing > Advantages of Rendezvous hashing over consistent hashing
4e807cb508ca.sentence: When n is not too large, however, the O(n) placement cost of basic HRW is not likely to be a problem.

fc4eb0f3029c.title: Rendezvous hashing
fc4eb0f3029c.section: O(log n) running time via skeleton-based hierarchical rendezvous hashing
fc4eb0f3029c.sentence: This approach creates a virtual hierarchical structure (called a "skeleton"), and achieves O(log⁡n) running time by applying HRW at each level while descending the hierarchy.

7130ae21e548.title: Rendezvous hashing
7130ae21e548.section: O(log n) running time via skeleton-based hierarchical rendezvous hashing
7130ae21e548.sentence: The standard version of Rendezvous Hashing described above works quite well for moderate n, but when n is extremely large, the hierarchical use of Rendezvous Hashing achieves O(log⁡n) running time.

9c05cc00dc99.title: Consistent hashing
9c05cc00dc99.section: Comparison with rendezvous hashing and other alternatives
9c05cc00dc99.sentence: Rendezvous hashing, designed in 1996, is a simpler and more general technique, and permits fully distributed agreement on a set of k options out of a possible set of n options.

934620c44302.title: Rendezvous hashing
934620c44302.sentence: Rendezvous hashing was invented by David Thaler and Chinya Ravishankar at the University of Michigan in 1996.

212e139d7e8b.title: Consistent hashing
212e139d7e8b.section: Comparison with rendezvous hashing and other alternatives
212e139d7e8b.sentence: Because of its simplicity and generality, rendezvous hashing is now being used in place of Consistent Hashing in many applications.

2f9b162269fd.title: Rendezvous hashing
2f9b162269fd.sentence: Other examples of real-world systems that use Rendezvous Hashing include the GitHub load balancer, the Apache Ignite distributed database, the Tahoe-LAFS file store, the CoBlitz large-file distribution service, Apache Druid, IBM's Cloud Object Store, the Arvados Data Management System, Apache Kafka, and the Twitter EventBus pub/sub platform.

c53ab5030935.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::consistent-hashing
c53ab5030935.sentence: Hence, virtual nodes are basically existing physical nodes mapped multiple times across the hash ring to minimize changes to a node's assigned range.

71019171f5f4.title: Consistent hashing
71019171f5f4.sentence: Those duplicate labels are called "virtual nodes" i.e. multiple labels which point to a single "real" label or server within the cluster.

066b668c36c8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::consistent-hashing
066b668c36c8.sentence: In order to ensure a more evenly distributed load, we can introduce the idea of a virtual node, sometimes also referred to as a VNode.

24b462393762.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::consistent-hashing
24b462393762.sentence: Instead of assigning a single position to a node, the hash range is divided into multiple smaller ranges, and each physical node is assigned several of these smaller ranges.

49e776f7f44a.title: Consistent hashing
49e776f7f44a.sentence: The amount of virtual nodes or duplicate labels used for a particular server within a cluster is called the "weight" of that particular server.

e931b3b5d3e0.title: Consistent hashing
e931b3b5d3e0.sentence: In the basic scheme above, if a server fails, all its BLOBs are reassigned to the next server in clockwise order, potentially doubling the load of that server.

f90de17f3c53.title: Consistent hashing
f90de17f3c53.sentence: To ensure a more even redistribution of BLOBs on server failure, each server can be hashed to multiple locations on the unit circle.

3e72c62523c5.title: Consistent hashing
3e72c62523c5.sentence: When a server fails, the BLOBs assigned to each of its replicas on the unit circle will get reassigned to a different server in clockwise order, thus redistributing the BLOBs more evenly.

799879d8c24c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::consistent-hashing
799879d8c24c.sentence: As VNodes help spread the load more evenly across the physical nodes on the cluster by dividing the hash ranges into smaller subranges, this speeds up the re-balancing process after adding or removing nodes.

2b1fcccac083.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::consistent-hashing
2b1fcccac083.sentence: This also helps us reduce the probability of hotspots.

809c9805f4da.title: Consistent hashing
809c9805f4da.sentence: To avoid skewness of multiple nodes within the radian, which happen due to lack of uniform distribution of the servers within the cluster, multiple labels are used.

fe0f5aa6245a.title: paper>10.1145/383059.383071
fe0f5aa6245a.sentence: A fundamental problem that confronts peer-to-peer applications is to efficiently locate the node that stores a particular data item.

745226c764d3.title: paper>10.1145/383059.383071
745226c764d3.sentence: This paper presents Chord, a distributed lookup protocol that addresses this problem.

07b65a637cbf.title: paper>10.1145/383059.383071
07b65a637cbf.sentence: Chord provides support for just one operation: given a key, it maps the key onto a node.

365434ab1171.title: paper>10.1145/383059.383071
365434ab1171.sentence: Data location can be easily implemented on top of Chord by associating a key with each data item, and storing the key/data item pair at the node to which the key maps.

dd8efa968cbb.title: Distributed hash table
dd8efa968cbb.sentence: For example, the Chord DHT uses consistent hashing, which treats nodes as points on a circle, and δ(k1,k2) is the distance traveling clockwise around the circle from k1 to k2.

32fffc8227a2.title: Distributed hash table
32fffc8227a2.sentence: Thus, the circular keyspace is split into contiguous segments whose endpoints are the node identifiers.

9508201482c6.title: paper>10.1145/383059.383071
9508201482c6.sentence: Chord adapts efficiently as nodes join and leave the system, and can answer queries even if the system is continuously changing.

89f805ad3759.title: paper>10.1145/383059.383071
89f805ad3759.sentence: Results from theoretical analysis, simulations, and experiments show that Chord is scalable, with communication cost and the state maintained by each node scaling logarithmically with the number of Chord nodes.

9bacca7fc337.title: Partition (database)
9bacca7fc337.sentence: Vertical partitioning involves creating tables with fewer columns and using additional tables to store the remaining columns.

df84db9c995b.title: Partition (database)
df84db9c995b.sentence: This type of partitioning is also called "row splitting", since rows get split by their columns, and might be performed explicitly or implicitly.

99bef5125225.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/vertical-partitioning-vs-horizontal-partitioning.md
99bef5125225.sentence: - Vertical partitioning: it means some columns are moved to new tables.

0599fcc9a902.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/vertical-partitioning-vs-horizontal-partitioning.md
0599fcc9a902.sentence: Each table contains the same number of rows but fewer columns (see diagram below).

a1e5a074b04d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
a1e5a074b04d.sentence: In vertical partitioning, we partition the data vertically based on columns.

eb043ad60f11.title: Partition (database)
eb043ad60f11.sentence: Generally, this practice is known as normalization.

00c7d4856ff1.title: Partition (database)
00c7d4856ff1.sentence: However, vertical partitioning extends further, and partitions columns even when already normalized.

f5113c66442b.title: Partition (database)
f5113c66442b.sentence: Distinct physical machines might be used to realize vertical partitioning: storing infrequently used or very wide columns, taking up a significant amount of memory, on a different machine, for example, is a method of vertical partitioning.

e23e8abd40d2.title: Partition (database)
e23e8abd40d2.sentence: A common form of vertical partitioning is to split static data from dynamic data, since the former is faster to access than the latter, particularly for a table where the dynamic data is not used as often as the static.

da707477a7ce.title: Partition (database)
da707477a7ce.sentence: Creating a view across the two newly created tables restores the original table with a performance penalty, but accessing the static data alone will show higher performance.

1ff4a6d26892.title: Partition (database)
1ff4a6d26892.sentence: A columnar database can be regarded as a database that has been vertically partitioned until each column is stored in its own table.

78ddc6e45d92.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
78ddc6e45d92.sentence: Federation (or functional partitioning) splits up databases by function.

f32dc9196806.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
f32dc9196806.sentence: The federation architecture makes several distinct physical databases appear as one logical database to end-users.

69b2ff02a060.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
69b2ff02a060.sentence: All of the components in a federation are tied together by one or more federal schemas that express the commonality of data throughout the federation.

90ac9a11ddce.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
90ac9a11ddce.sentence: These federated schemas are used to specify the information that can be shared by the federation components and to provide a common basis for communication among them.

ca31c1b7c622.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
ca31c1b7c622.sentence: Federation also provides a cohesive, unified view of data derived from multiple sources.

1dd805a7f6f0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
1dd805a7f6f0.sentence: The data sources for federated systems can include databases and various other forms of structured and unstructured data.

3993eb410bd6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
3993eb410bd6.sentence: - Transparency: Federated database masks user differences and implementations of underlying data sources.

12ca0b609492.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
12ca0b609492.sentence: Therefore, the users do not need to be aware of where the data is stored.

97a3ef16bb37.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
97a3ef16bb37.sentence: A federated database system can handle different hardware, network protocols, data models, etc.

1252cb25604d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
1252cb25604d.sentence: - Autonomy: A Federated database does not change existing data sources, interfaces should remain the same.

e17803be33ed.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
e17803be33ed.sentence: - Access heterogeneous data in a unified way.

68f8c7212376.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
68f8c7212376.sentence: - No tight coupling of applications with legacy databases.

b2c0725b6132.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
b2c0725b6132.sentence: - Adds more hardware and additional complexity.

0e09c1075c7d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::database-federation
0e09c1075c7d.sentence: - Joining data from two databases is complex.

57dabedd1b66.title: Shard (database architecture)
57dabedd1b66.sentence: Sharding a database table before it has been optimized locally can introduce unnecessary complexity.

0ebd6e33a405.title: Shard (database architecture)
0ebd6e33a405.sentence: Sharding is generally recommended when other optimization strategies have proven insufficient.

88ff52440dd2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
88ff52440dd2.sentence: The justification for data sharding is that, after a certain point, it is cheaper and more feasible to scale horizontally by adding more machines than to scale it vertically by adding powerful servers.

328182266add.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-in-database-sharding.md
328182266add.sentence: Sharding is implemented to solve these problems:

5f1a95b104e1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-in-database-sharding.md
5f1a95b104e1.sentence: - Too much data on one machine: A single database server can only handle so much data.

4f6520f1f668.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-in-database-sharding.md
4f6520f1f668.sentence: - Too many requests on one machine: A single database server can only handle so many requests.

1d052d66ae64.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-crash-course-in-database-sharding.md
1d052d66ae64.sentence: - High Latency: As data grows, query latency increases.

cd4b3a16a309.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
cd4b3a16a309.sentence: Here are some reasons why sharding might be the right choice:

703c29a0ad18.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
703c29a0ad18.sentence: - Leveraging existing hardware instead of high-end machines.

ca4ca5dc64f4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
ca4ca5dc64f4.sentence: - Maintain data in distinct geographic regions.

9b5a738c0296.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
9b5a738c0296.sentence: - Quickly scale by adding more shards.

6b44fe372092.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
6b44fe372092.sentence: - Better performance as each machine is under less load.

b0003a456637.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sharding
b0003a456637.sentence: - When more concurrent connections are required.

13c2973ffa5e.title: Consistency model
13c2973ffa5e.sentence: In computer science, a consistency model specifies a contract between the programmer and a system, wherein the system guarantees that if the programmer follows the rules for operations on memory, memory will be consistent and the results of reading, writing, or updating memory will be predictable.

79e60aa0948a.title: Consistency model
79e60aa0948a.sentence: Consistency models are used in distributed systems like distributed shared memory systems or distributed data stores (such as filesystems, databases, optimistic replication systems or web caching).

b7521514a9f3.title: Consistency model
b7521514a9f3.sentence: - The row X is replicated on nodes M and N

b080894a17a7.title: Consistency model
b080894a17a7.sentence: - The client A writes row X to node M

57ae67993618.title: Consistency model
57ae67993618.sentence: - After a period of time t, client B reads row X from node N

6e0cac6a67f6.title: Consistency model
6e0cac6a67f6.sentence: The consistency model determines whether client B will definitely see the write performed by client A, will definitely not, or cannot depend on seeing the write.

245903144870.title: Consistency model
245903144870.sentence: Consistency models define rules for the apparent order and visibility of updates, and are on a continuum with tradeoffs.

05a55cddac46.title: Consistency model
05a55cddac46.sentence: One consistency model can be considered stronger than another if it requires all conditions of that model and more.

a04f097c9bae.title: Consistency model
a04f097c9bae.sentence: In other words, a model with fewer constraints is considered a weaker consistency model.

e724a8389e38.title: Consistency model
e724a8389e38.sentence: Strict consistency is the strongest consistency model.

66fdde424adc.title: Consistency model
66fdde424adc.sentence: Under this model, a write to a variable by any processor needs to be seen instantaneously by all processors.

eee6a0b274ce.title: Consistency model
eee6a0b274ce.sentence: Its practical relevance is restricted to a thought experiment and formalism, because instantaneous message exchange is impossible.

fdf2d322f01a.title: Consistency model
fdf2d322f01a.sentence: While replication can improve performance and reliability, it can cause consistency problems between multiple copies of data.

3eab299a2def.title: Consistency model
3eab299a2def.sentence: Tanenbaum, Andrew, & Maarten Van Steen, 2007 refer to this type of consistency as tight consistency provided by synchronous replication.

90fe18026a13.title: Consistency model
90fe18026a13.sentence: However, applying global synchronizations to keep all copies consistent is costly.

b129bc4bcbcd.title: Consistency model
b129bc4bcbcd.sentence: One way to decrease the cost of global synchronization and improve the performance can be weakening the consistency restrictions.

478cf89f3837.title: Eventual consistency
478cf89f3837.sentence: Eventual consistency is a consistency model used in distributed computing to achieve high availability.

b145a2597e34.title: Eventual consistency
b145a2597e34.sentence: An eventually consistent system ensures that if no new updates are made to a given data item, eventually all read accesses to that item will return the last updated value.

5c9325daa958.title: Eventual consistency
5c9325daa958.sentence: Eventual consistency, also called optimistic replication, is widely deployed in distributed systems and has origins in early mobile computing projects.

fe403cac0f13.title: Eventual consistency
fe403cac0f13.sentence: A system that has achieved eventual consistency is said to have converged, or achieved replica convergence.

4d2b611727c2.title: Eventual consistency
4d2b611727c2.sentence: Eventual consistency is a weak guarantee – most stronger models, like linearizability, are trivially eventually consistent.

5d99b486b5ed.title: Eventual consistency
5d99b486b5ed.sentence: Thus, even without further external updates, until an update converges, it is possible that different queries for a record see different values.

b5025cf666cb.title: Eventual consistency
b5025cf666cb.sentence: This complexity arises because eventual consistency provides only a liveness guarantee (ensuring reads eventually return the same value) without safety guarantees—allowing any intermediate value before convergence.

415a8405bfa5.title: Eventual consistency
415a8405bfa5.sentence: Eventually-consistent services are often classified as providing BASE semantics (basically-available, soft-state, eventual consistency), in contrast to traditional ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability).

465e3e6649cc.title: ACID
465e3e6649cc.sentence: BASE stands for basically available, soft state, and eventually consistent: the acronym highlights that BASE is opposite of ACID, like their chemical equivalents, acid and base.

6600f82b8895.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-eventual-consistency-patterns-you-must-know.md
6600f82b8895.sentence: Techniques like async replication help achieve eventual consistency.

0c8aa8b176c7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-eventual-consistency-patterns-you-must-know.md
0c8aa8b176c7.sentence: However, eventual consistency can also result in data inconsistency.

4e517034384e.title: Eventual consistency
4e517034384e.sentence: Eventual consistency faces criticism for adding complexity to distributed software applications.

55744c620dd3.title: Eventual consistency
55744c620dd3.sentence: With weak consistency guarantees, developers must carefully consider these limitations, as incorrect assumptions about consistency levels can lead to subtle bugs that only surface during network failures or high concurrency.

8dd97abbcc7c.title: Network partition
8dd97abbcc7c.sentence: A network partition is a division of a computer network into relatively independent subnets, either by design, to optimize them separately, or due to the failure of network devices.

d1d907fe45d4.title: Network partition
d1d907fe45d4.sentence: For example, in a network with multiple subnets where nodes A and B are located in one subnet and nodes C and D are in another, a partition occurs if the network switch device between the two subnets fails.

a101fa3a0c0c.title: Network partition
a101fa3a0c0c.sentence: In that case nodes A and B can no longer communicate with nodes C and D, but all nodes A-D work the same as before.

6886f07273f4.title: Network partition
6886f07273f4.sentence: Distributed software must be designed to be partition-tolerant, that is, even after the network is partitioned, it still works correctly.

19560702ecc5.title: Network partition
19560702ecc5.sentence: Partition tolerance, in this context, means the ability of a data processing system to continue processing data even if a network partition causes communication errors between subsystems.

88e9fcbea9eb.title: Network partition
88e9fcbea9eb.sentence: The CAP theorem is based on three trade-offs: consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

ff95461bd963.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
ff95461bd963.section: Chapter 23 - Managing Critical State: Distributed Consensus for Reliability > CAP Theorem
ff95461bd963.sentence: Because network partitions are inevitable (cables get cut, packets get lost or delayed due to congestion, hardware breaks, networking components become misconfigured, etc.), understanding distributed consensus really amounts to understanding how consistency and availability work for your particular application.

14ede54df252.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
14ede54df252.section: Chapter 23 - Managing Critical State: Distributed Consensus for Reliability > CAP Theorem
14ede54df252.sentence: The logic is intuitive: if two nodes canât communicate (because the network is partitioned), then the system as a whole can either stop serving some or all requests at some or all nodes (thus reducing availability), or it can serve requests as usual, which results in inconsistent views of the data at each node.

0c89243382da.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
0c89243382da.section: Motivating the Use of Consensus: Distributed Systems Coordination Failure
0c89243382da.sentence: Network partitions are particularly challengingâa problem that appears to be caused by a full partition may instead be the result of:

c4e1d8fcdca4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
c4e1d8fcdca4.section: Motivating the Use of Consensus: Distributed Systems Coordination Failure

4345a10dd3e5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
4345a10dd3e5.section: Motivating the Use of Consensus: Distributed Systems Coordination Failure
4345a10dd3e5.sentence: - Some, but not all, messages being dropped

33971f3ca291.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
33971f3ca291.section: Motivating the Use of Consensus: Distributed Systems Coordination Failure
33971f3ca291.sentence: - Throttle occurring in one direction, but not the other direction

610b0a6f249d.title: CAP theorem
610b0a6f249d.sentence: In database theory, the CAP theorem, also named Brewer's theorem after computer scientist Eric Brewer, states that any distributed data store can provide at most two of the following three guarantees:

c806acb47986.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
c806acb47986.sentence: CAP theorem states that a distributed system can deliver only two of the three desired characteristics Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance (CAP).

572bf2fafca9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
572bf2fafca9.sentence: CAP theorem states that a distributed system can't provide more than two of these three guarantees simultaneously.

7f75abe42460.title: paper>10.1145/564585.564601
7f75abe42460.sentence: When designing distributed web services, there are three properties that are commonly desired: consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

e8002462d723.title: CAP theorem
e8002462d723.sentence: Every read receives the most recent write or an error.

81ff9f77e5a4.title: CAP theorem
81ff9f77e5a4.sentence: Consistency means that all clients see the same data at the same time, no matter which node they connect to.

4ea417244622.title: CAP theorem
4ea417244622.sentence: Every request received by a non-failing node in the system must result in a response, without the guarantee that it contains the most recent version of the data.

f9dec4c05138.title: CAP theorem
f9dec4c05138.sentence: This is the definition of availability in CAP theorem as defined by Gilbert and Lynch.

fa832f552a31.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
fa832f552a31.sentence: Availability means that any client making a request for data gets a response, even if one or more nodes are down.

a88de01cfb5a.title: CAP theorem
a88de01cfb5a.sentence: The system continues to operate despite an arbitrary number of messages being dropped (or delayed) by the network between nodes.

b6f1a5238236.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
b6f1a5238236.sentence: Partition tolerance means the system continues to work despite message loss or partial failure.

aa9b0861d913.title: CAP theorem
aa9b0861d913.sentence: No distributed system is safe from network failures, thus network partitioning generally has to be tolerated.

bc2d3021c9be.title: CAP theorem
bc2d3021c9be.sentence: In the presence of a partition, one is then left with two options: consistency or availability.

ef2721de04ee.title: CAP theorem
ef2721de04ee.sentence: Thus, if there is a network partition, one has to choose between consistency or availability.

b79f3d72b9c6.title: CAP theorem
b79f3d72b9c6.sentence: When choosing consistency over availability, the system will return an error or a time out if particular information cannot be guaranteed to be up to date due to network partitioning.

096052d2e74a.title: CAP theorem
096052d2e74a.sentence: When choosing availability over consistency, the system will always process the query and try to return the most recent available version of the information, even if it cannot guarantee it is up to date due to network partitioning.

7a99290384d5.title: CAP theorem
7a99290384d5.sentence: In the absence of a network partition, both availability and consistency can be satisfied.

cda4d3cdc287.title: CAP theorem
cda4d3cdc287.sentence: During times of normal operations, a data store covers all three.

6955f6bf626a.title: paper>10.1145/564585.564601
6955f6bf626a.sentence: In this note, we prove this conjecture in the asynchronous network model, and then discuss solutions to this dilemma in the partially synchronous model.

a6cb382b3edc.title: paper>10.1145/564585.564601
a6cb382b3edc.sentence: It is impossible to achieve all three.

2ddb5608aac7.title: CAP theorem
2ddb5608aac7.sentence: In 2002, Seth Gilbert and Nancy Lynch of MIT published a formal proof of Brewer's conjecture, elevating it to a theorem.

71db49d792f9.title: CAP theorem
71db49d792f9.sentence: A similar theorem stating the trade-off between consistency and availability in distributed systems had been published by Birman and Friedman in 1996.

f3d935e7a59a.title: CAP theorem
f3d935e7a59a.sentence: According to computer scientist Eric Brewer of the University of California, Berkeley, the theorem first appeared in autumn 1998.

3d8f635c6021.title: CAP theorem
3d8f635c6021.sentence: It was published as the CAP principle in 1999 and presented as a conjecture by Brewer at the 2000 Symposium on Principles of Distributed Computing (PODC).

45203b28a0e3.title: Eventual consistency
45203b28a0e3.sentence: In order to ensure replica convergence, a system must reconcile differences between multiple copies of distributed data.

85714e243e11.title: Eventual consistency
85714e243e11.sentence: - exchanging versions or updates of data between servers (often known as anti-entropy); and

46627abd01cd.title: Eventual consistency
46627abd01cd.sentence: - choosing an appropriate final state when concurrent updates have occurred, called reconciliation.

7acb943e455d.title: Eventual consistency
7acb943e455d.sentence: The most appropriate approach to reconciliation depends on the application.

079bfa6ae8e5.title: Eventual consistency
079bfa6ae8e5.sentence: A widespread approach is "last writer wins".

2c2d8a2908af.title: Eventual consistency
2c2d8a2908af.sentence: Some people use "first writer wins" in situations where "last writer wins" is unacceptable.

34e3702d36ff.title: Eventual consistency
34e3702d36ff.sentence: Another is to invoke a user-specified conflict handler.

784966570338.title: Eventual consistency
784966570338.sentence: Timestamps and vector clocks are often used to detect concurrency between updates.

633f667ebebf.title: Eventual consistency
633f667ebebf.sentence: Reconciliation of concurrent writes must occur sometime before the next read, and can be scheduled at different instants:

3d210c9f1434.title: Eventual consistency
3d210c9f1434.sentence: - Read repair: The correction is done when a read finds an inconsistency.

fb7c0f58e2aa.title: Eventual consistency
fb7c0f58e2aa.sentence: - Write repair: The correction takes place during a write operation, slowing down the write operation.

09183b2a74aa.title: Eventual consistency
09183b2a74aa.sentence: - Asynchronous repair: The correction is not part of a read or write operation.

1f2553eb7dd6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
1f2553eb7dd6.sentence: When the partition is resolved, the AP databases typically re-syncs the nodes to repair all inconsistencies in the system.

47c3f8443ab0.title: PACELC design principle
47c3f8443ab0.sentence: In database theory, the PACELC design principle is an extension to the CAP theorem.

d015b24751b0.title: PACELC design principle
d015b24751b0.sentence: It states that in case of network partitioning (P) in a distributed computer system, one has to choose between availability (A) and consistency (C) (as per the CAP theorem), but else (E), even when the system is running normally in the absence of partitions, one has to choose between latency (L) and loss of consistency (C).

f1de73a6d11d.title: PACELC design principle
f1de73a6d11d.sentence: In practice, most systems rely on explicit acknowledgments rather than timed delays to ensure delivery, requiring a full network round trip and therefore message delay on both reads and writes to ensure consistency.

0dc25c7e7d94.title: PACELC design principle
0dc25c7e7d94.sentence: In low latency systems, in contrast, consistency is relaxed in order to reduce latency.

a656eb7a91de.title: PACELC design principle
a656eb7a91de.sentence: The purpose of PACELC is to address his thesis that "Ignoring the consistency/latency trade-off of replicated systems is a major oversight [in CAP], as it is present at all times during system operation, whereas CAP is only relevant in the arguably rare case of a network partition." PACELC was proved formally in 2018 in a SIGACT News article.

97cd198c34e2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::pacelc-theorem
97cd198c34e2.sentence: PACELC theorem was developed to address a key limitation of the CAP theorem as it makes no provision for performance or latency.

23e24fd1c8f2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::pacelc-theorem
23e24fd1c8f2.sentence: For example, according to the CAP theorem, a database can be considered available if a query returns a response after 30 days.

71df3de13a41.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::pacelc-theorem
71df3de13a41.sentence: Obviously, such latency would be unacceptable for any real-world application.

57f67fd7a2b5.title: PACELC design principle
57f67fd7a2b5.sentence: There are four configurations or trade-offs in the PACELC space:

54c6efa6b420.title: PACELC design principle
54c6efa6b420.sentence: - PA/EL - prioritize availability and low latency over consistency

fd91e91c814c.title: PACELC design principle
fd91e91c814c.sentence: - PA/EC - when there is a partition, choose availability; else, choose consistency

46f58ef3cc61.title: PACELC design principle
46f58ef3cc61.sentence: - PC/EL - when there is a partition, choose consistency; else, choose lower latency

59ddcaa0a9ca.title: PACELC design principle
59ddcaa0a9ca.sentence: - PC/EC - choose consistency at all times

47607daf7f1f.title: PACELC design principle
47607daf7f1f.sentence: A PC/EC system provides a firm guarantee of atomic consistency, as in ACID, while PA/EL provides high availability and low latency with a more complex consistency model.

4391d81a06e1.title: PACELC design principle
4391d81a06e1.sentence: In contrast, PA/EC and PC/EL systems only make conditional guarantees of consistency.

429267f16e31.title: PACELC design principle
429267f16e31.sentence: The developer still has to write code to handle the cases where the guarantee is not upheld.

5bab57303209.title: PACELC design principle
5bab57303209.sentence: PC does not indicate that the system is fully consistent; rather it indicates that the system does not reduce consistency beyond the baseline consistency level when a network partition occurs—instead, it reduces availability.

de9dd17ff959.title: PACELC design principle
de9dd17ff959.sentence: Some experts like Marc Brooker argue that the CAP theorem is particularly relevant in intermittently connected environments, such as those related to the Internet of Things (IoT) and mobile applications.

0f1d20dc7757.title: PACELC design principle
0f1d20dc7757.sentence: In these contexts, devices may become partitioned due to challenging physical conditions, such as power outages or when entering confined spaces like elevators.

ce8e183bb3fc.title: PACELC design principle
ce8e183bb3fc.sentence: For distributed systems, such as cloud applications, it is more appropriate to use PACELC, which is more comprehensive and considers trade-offs such as latency and consistency even in the absence of network partitions.

e225d0ea19c1.title: PACELC design principle
e225d0ea19c1.sentence: The PACELC design principle was first described by Daniel Abadi from Yale University in 2010 in a blog post, which he later clarified in a paper in 2012.

869bc83f9fbf.title: Eventual consistency
869bc83f9fbf.sentence: Whereas eventual consistency is only a liveness guarantee (updates will be observed eventually), strong eventual consistency (SEC) adds the safety guarantee that any two nodes that have received the same (unordered) set of updates will be in the same state.

ac6d8f95c799.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
ac6d8f95c799.sentence: We live in a physical world and can't guarantee the stability of a network, so distributed databases must choose Partition Tolerance (P).

2e70e2b84371.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
2e70e2b84371.sentence: This implies a tradeoff between Consistency (C) and Availability (A).

18df27f026fc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
18df27f026fc.sentence: A CA database delivers consistency and availability across all nodes.

bb856b7d2a2b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
bb856b7d2a2b.sentence: It can't do this if there is a partition between any two nodes in the system, and therefore can't deliver fault tolerance.

d1ccf0cd3b78.title: CAP theorem
d1ccf0cd3b78.sentence: There are no NoSQL databases one would classify as CA.

db65cf659ebf.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
db65cf659ebf.sentence: A CP database delivers consistency and partition tolerance at the expense of availability.

67a33e85af92.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
67a33e85af92.sentence: When a partition occurs between any two nodes, the system has to shut down the non-consistent node until the partition is resolved.

dbf9c9b1b276.title: Kubernetes
dbf9c9b1b276.sentence: Etcd favors consistency over availability in the event of a network partition (see CAP theorem).

ee3c12006172.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
ee3c12006172.sentence: An AP database delivers availability and partition tolerance at the expense of consistency.

00491068e1a7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::cap-theorem
00491068e1a7.sentence: When a partition occurs, all nodes remain available but those at the wrong end of a partition might return an older version of data than others.

1fe5a07fb886.title: CAP theorem
1fe5a07fb886.sentence: CouchDB, Cassandra, and ScyllaDB are examples of AP databases.

db4203c2e466.title: CAP theorem
db4203c2e466.sentence: Most modern distributed databases offer configuration options for both consistency and availability.

f483f98953ad.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
f483f98953ad.sentence: The “2 of 3” formulation can be useful, but this simplification could be misleading.

391c37f109f3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
391c37f109f3.sentence: - “CAP prohibits only a tiny part of the design space: perfect availability and consistency in the presence of partitions, which are rare”.

8e5c9555a0d1.title: CAP theorem
8e5c9555a0d1.sentence: In 2012, Brewer clarified some of his positions, including why the often-used "two out of three" concept can be somewhat misleading because system designers only need to sacrifice consistency or availability in the presence of partitions; partition management and recovery techniques exist.

3daa3150fb46.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
3daa3150fb46.sentence: Quoted from the paper: CAP Twelve Years Later: How the “Rules” Have Changed.

6762ef55ff48.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
6762ef55ff48.sentence: - The theorem is about 100% availability and consistency.

94a5be8a3579.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
94a5be8a3579.sentence: A more realistic discussion would be the trade-offs between latency and consistency when there is no network partition.

2a4a31825538.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
2a4a31825538.sentence: See PACELC theorem for more details.

cabe39e71a6f.title: CAP theorem
cabe39e71a6f.sentence: Consistency as defined in the CAP theorem is quite different from the consistency guaranteed in ACID database transactions.

413f59cb5439.title: CAP theorem
413f59cb5439.sentence: Availability as defined in CAP theorem is different from high availability in software architecture.

f38dd90e003a.title: CAP theorem
f38dd90e003a.sentence: Brewer also noted the different definition of consistency used in the CAP theorem relative to the definition used in ACID.

b0d70850ffdf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
b0d70850ffdf.sentence: Justifying our choice purely based on the CAP theorem is not enough.

67448a8ee0c8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
67448a8ee0c8.sentence: For example, companies don't choose Cassandra for chat applications simply because it is an AP system.

9a5f20df9484.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
9a5f20df9484.sentence: There is a list of good characteristics that make Cassandra a desirable option for storing chat messages.

c46776d6a431.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/cap-theorem-one-of-the-most-misunderstood-terms.md
c46776d6a431.section: Is the CAP theorem really useful?
c46776d6a431.sentence: I think it is still useful as it opens our minds to a set of tradeoff discussions, but it is only part of the story.

be41111c688b.title: Consistency model
be41111c688b.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols
be41111c688b.sentence: In these protocols, there is an associated primary for each data item in a data store to coordinate write operations on that data item.

94a3e3786b7c.title: Consistency model
94a3e3786b7c.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
94a3e3786b7c.sentence: In the simplest primary-based protocol that supports replication, also known as primary-backup protocol, write operations are forwarded to a single server and read operations can be performed locally.

637fc8d4c90c.title: Consistency model
637fc8d4c90c.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
637fc8d4c90c.sentence: When a client requests a write, the write request is forwarded to a primary server.

6ef3b1363285.title: Consistency model
6ef3b1363285.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
6ef3b1363285.sentence: The primary server sends request to backups to perform the update.

b8f31ea66c4b.title: Consistency model
b8f31ea66c4b.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
b8f31ea66c4b.sentence: The server then receives the update acknowledgement from all backups and sends the acknowledgement of completion of writes to the client.

26a212a29dbd.title: Consistency model
26a212a29dbd.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
26a212a29dbd.sentence: The trade-off of this protocol is that a client who sends the update request might have to wait so long to get the acknowledgement in order to continue.

c9cba640a24f.title: Consistency model
c9cba640a24f.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
c9cba640a24f.sentence: This problem can be solved by performing the updates locally, and then asking other backups to perform their updates.

6193d3ba76b0.title: Consistency model
6193d3ba76b0.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
6193d3ba76b0.sentence: The non-blocking primary-backup protocol does not guarantee the consistency of update on all backup servers.

f802f983c0b5.title: Consistency model
f802f983c0b5.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols

ef0d0c982436.title: Consistency model
ef0d0c982436.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
ef0d0c982436.sentence: In the primary-backup protocol, all processes will see the same order of write operations since this protocol orders all incoming writes based on a globally unique time.

178d2fa4de25.title: Consistency model
178d2fa4de25.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Primary-based protocols > Remote-write protocols
178d2fa4de25.sentence: Blocking protocols guarantee that processes view the result of the last write operation.

6db843c91433.title: Consistency model
6db843c91433.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Replicated-write protocols > Active replication
6db843c91433.sentence: In active replication, there is a process associated with each replica to perform the write operation.

5372c2fbcd94.title: Consistency model
5372c2fbcd94.section: Consistency and replication > Consistency protocols > Replicated-write protocols > Active replication
5372c2fbcd94.sentence: In other words, updates are sent to each replica in the form of an operation in order to be executed.

d590b4050cc9.sentence: Read operation is completed if all received version numbers are the most recent version.

27fccd2d54a1.title: Consistency model
27fccd2d54a1.sentence: Sequential consistency is met if "the result of any execution is the same as if the (read and write) operations of all processes on the data store were executed in some sequential order, and the operations of each individual processor appear in this sequence in the order specified by its program." Adve and Gharachorloo, 1996 define two requirements to implement the sequential consistency; program order and write atomicity.

85c40aa6828e.title: Consistency model
85c40aa6828e.sentence: A write to a variable does not have to be seen instantaneously, however, writes to variables by different processors have to be seen in the same order by all processors.

ea4e20eae41d.title: Consistency model
ea4e20eae41d.sentence: In sequential consistency, there is no notion of time or most recent write operations.

3d07f68a4094.title: Consistency model

07a7cb23c67a.title: Consistency model
07a7cb23c67a.sentence: The sequential consistency model was proposed by Lamport (1979).

da117ee8b4ee.title: Consistency model
da117ee8b4ee.sentence: Sequential consistency can produce non-deterministic results.

f7b071550181.title: Consistency model
f7b071550181.sentence: This is because the sequence of sequential operations between processors can be different during different runs of the program.

9790acf6763d.title: Linearizability
9790acf6763d.sentence: In a linearizable system, although operations overlap on a shared object, each operation appears to take place instantaneously.

44919d6a7f18.title: Consistency model
44919d6a7f18.sentence: Linearizability (also known as atomic consistency or atomic memory) can be defined as sequential consistency with a real-time constraint, by considering a begin time and end time for each operation.

cc5ed2ce947e.title: Linearizability
cc5ed2ce947e.sentence: Linearizability is a strong correctness condition, which constrains what outputs are possible when an object is accessed by multiple processes concurrently.

7d0d85dfc34a.title: Linearizability
7d0d85dfc34a.sentence: If a system is linearizable it allows a programmer to reason about the system.

da8ef48c04ce.title: Consistency model
da8ef48c04ce.sentence: An execution is linearizable if each operation taking place in linearizable order by placing a point between its begin time and its end time and guarantees sequential consistency.

e204dd12124b.title: Linearizability
e204dd12124b.sentence: - All function calls have a linearization point at some instant between their invocation and their response.

9d1995de1118.title: Linearizability
9d1995de1118.sentence: - All functions appear to occur instantly at their linearization point, behaving as specified by the sequential definition.

0f0d2365ac21.title: Linearizability
0f0d2365ac21.sentence: This alternative is usually much easier to prove.

4758a38274f2.title: Linearizability
4758a38274f2.sentence: This property of occurring instantaneously, or indivisibly, leads to the use of the term atomic as an alternative to the longer "linearizable".

f73b4ee66c27.title: Linearizability
f73b4ee66c27.sentence: Note that the definition of linearizability only precludes responses that precede invocations from being reordered; since the original history had no responses before invocations, they can be reordered.

c2923f697723.title: Linearizability
c2923f697723.sentence: However, under serializability, B's unlock operation may be moved to before A's original lock, which is a valid history (assuming the object begins the history in a locked state):

8d9c8dbc9111.title: Linearizability
8d9c8dbc9111.sentence: This reordering is sensible provided there is no alternative means of communicating between A and B. Linearizability is better when considering individual objects separately, as the reordering restrictions ensure that multiple linearizable objects are, considered as a whole, still linearizable.

82816d84347c.title: Linearizability
82816d84347c.sentence: Specifically, linearizability guarantees that the invariants of a system are observed and preserved by all operations: if all operations individually preserve an invariant, the system as a whole will.

aa4116ae6b39.title: Linearizability
aa4116ae6b39.sentence: This simple implementation is not linearizable, as is demonstrated by the following example.

19ca385ad2dc.title: Linearizability
19ca385ad2dc.sentence: In the above example, two processes invoked an increment command, however the value of the object only increased from 0 to 1, instead of 2 as it should have.

9467e33d7c8b.title: Linearizability
9467e33d7c8b.sentence: One of the increment operations was lost as a result of the system not being linearizable.

7b7fdfe33c43.title: Linearizability
7b7fdfe33c43.sentence: Read the value in the memory location; add one to the value; use compare-and-swap to write the incremented value back; retry if the value read in by the compare-and-swap did not match the value we originally read.

9f3f9dcd6ea9.title: Linearizability
9f3f9dcd6ea9.sentence: Since the compare-and-swap occurs (or appears to occur) instantaneously, if another process updates the location while we are in-progress, the compare-and-swap is guaranteed to fail.

e5d179d8d948.title: Linearizability
e5d179d8d948.sentence: Many systems provide an atomic fetch-and-increment instruction that reads from a memory location, unconditionally writes a new value (the old value plus one), and returns the old value.

ae7799ff793e.title: Linearizability
ae7799ff793e.sentence: Acquire a lock, excluding other threads from running the critical section (steps 2–4) at the same time; read the value in the memory location; add one to the value; write the incremented value back to the memory location; release the lock.

0b9fa5dfa5ca.title: Linearizability

bc59e395f59e.title: PACELC design principle

7e39cc5dfc10.title: Consistency model
7e39cc5dfc10.sentence: Causal consistency defined by Hutto and Ahamad, 1990, is a weakening of the sequential consistency model by categorizing events into those causally related and those that are not.

8da4c236592f.title: Consistency model
8da4c236592f.sentence: It defines that only write operations that are causally related, need to be seen in the same order by all processes.

eb8759327b03.title: Consistency model
eb8759327b03.sentence: For example, if an event b takes effect from an earlier event a, the causal consistency guarantees that all processes see event b after event a.

b4a5a043d389.title: Consistency model
b4a5a043d389.sentence: - Writes that are potentially causally related must be seen by all processes in the same order.

b88b1e72aee9.title: Consistency model
b88b1e72aee9.sentence: - Concurrent writes may be seen in a different order on different machines.

afec8c76dcaa.title: Consistency model
afec8c76dcaa.sentence: Two writes can become causally related if one write to a variable is dependent on a previous write to any variable if the processor doing the second write has just read the first write.

1140a22a2499.title: Consistency model
1140a22a2499.sentence: The two writes could have been done by the same processor or by different processors.

bd79def407a1.title: Consistency model
bd79def407a1.sentence: These 4 consistency models were proposed in a 1994 paper.

279800b8754d.title: Consistency model
279800b8754d.sentence: They focus on guarantees in the situation where only a single user or application is making data modifications.

2bc21fa59750.title: Consistency model
2bc21fa59750.section: Consistency and replication > Client-centric consistency models
2bc21fa59750.sentence: In some special data stores without simultaneous updates, client-centric consistency models can deal with inconsistencies in a less costly way.

b41e58ac1a1b.title: Consistency model
b41e58ac1a1b.sentence: If a process reads the value of a data item x, any successive read operation on x by that process will always return that same value or a more recent value.

0d40c07091a4.title: Consistency model
0d40c07091a4.sentence: A write operation by a process on a data item X is completed before any successive write operation on X by the same process.

5cc0f4eb7f49.title: Consistency model
5cc0f4eb7f49.sentence: A value written by a process on a data item X will always be available to a successive read operation performed by the same process on data item X.

226d78737537.title: Consistency model
226d78737537.sentence: A write operation by a process on a data item x following a previous read operation on x by the same process is guaranteed to take place on the same or a more recent value of x that was read.

40e1f893eecb.title: PACELC design principle
40e1f893eecb.sentence: - The default versions of Amazon's early (internal) Dynamo, Cassandra, Riak, and Cosmos DB are PA/EL systems: if a partition occurs, they give up consistency for availability, and under normal operation they give up consistency for lower latency.

e0fe1a0504e3.title: PACELC design principle
e0fe1a0504e3.sentence: - Fully ACID systems such as VoltDB/H-Store, Megastore, MySQL Cluster, and PostgreSQL are PC/EC: they refuse to give up consistency, and will pay the availability and latency costs to achieve it.

8e7a3c927b08.title: PACELC design principle
8e7a3c927b08.sentence: Bigtable and related systems such as HBase are also PC/EC.

0fb468548a94.title: PACELC design principle

d347c0284f2b.title: PACELC design principle
d347c0284f2b.sentence: In the baseline case, the system guarantees reads and writes to be consistent.

4bf44342ce95.title: PACELC design principle
4bf44342ce95.sentence: DynamoDB follows a strong leader model, where every write is strictly serialized (and conditional writes carry no penalty) and supports read-after-write consistency.

876a222efe8a.title: PACELC design principle
876a222efe8a.sentence: The DynamoDB SDKs use eventually consistent reads by default (improved availability and throughput), but when a consistent read is requested the service will return either a current view to the item or an error.

d1b58881c5e8.title: Distributed transaction
d1b58881c5e8.sentence: A distributed transaction operates within a distributed environment, typically involving multiple nodes across a network depending on the location of the data.

4b523f83a790.title: Distributed transaction
4b523f83a790.sentence: A key aspect of distributed transactions is atomicity, which ensures that the transaction is completed in its entirety or not executed at all.

8f483604d8a7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
8f483604d8a7.section: Why do we need distributed transactions?
8f483604d8a7.sentence: In other words, all the nodes must commit, or all must abort and the entire transaction rolls back.

c39dd1687c72.title: Distributed transaction
c39dd1687c72.sentence: It's essential to note that distributed transactions are not limited to databases.

fb75d579a4b4.title: Distributed transaction
fb75d579a4b4.sentence: Databases are common transactional resources and, often, transactions span a couple of such databases.

19fc7552ed47.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
19fc7552ed47.section: Why do we need distributed transactions?
19fc7552ed47.sentence: Unlike an ACID transaction on a single database, a distributed transaction involves altering data on multiple databases.

5f5fc68f6c75.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
5f5fc68f6c75.section: Why do we need distributed transactions?
5f5fc68f6c75.sentence: Consequently, distributed transaction processing is more complicated, because the database must coordinate the committing or rollback of the changes in a transaction as a self-contained unit.

6c292bb51a15.title: Distributed transaction
6c292bb51a15.sentence: The isolation property (the I of ACID) poses a special challenge for multi database transactions, since the (global) serializability property could be violated, even if each database provides it (see also global serializability).

5e9e96099099.title: Distributed transaction
5e9e96099099.sentence: A common algorithm for ensuring correct completion of a distributed transaction is the two-phase commit (2PC).

0a7ccd0a8058.title: Distributed transaction
0a7ccd0a8058.sentence: This algorithm is usually applied for updates able to commit in a short period of time, ranging from couple of milliseconds to couple of minutes.

960e68e0bd4a.title: Distributed transaction
960e68e0bd4a.sentence: There are also long-lived distributed transactions, for example a transaction to book a trip, which consists of booking a flight, a rental car and a hotel.

1e0635ba4d0f.title: Distributed transaction
1e0635ba4d0f.sentence: Since booking the flight might take up to a day to get a confirmation, two-phase commit is not applicable here, it will lock the resources for this long.

0d719a83f536.title: Distributed transaction
0d719a83f536.sentence: In this case more sophisticated techniques that involve multiple undo levels are used.

3c2889c088ff.title: Distributed transaction
3c2889c088ff.sentence: Usually these transactions utilize principles of compensating transactions, Optimism and Isolation Without Locking.

a87ed97929ca.title: Distributed transaction
a87ed97929ca.sentence: The Open Group, a vendor consortium, proposed the X/Open Distributed Transaction Processing Model (X/Open XA), which became a de facto standard for the behavior of transaction model components.

7c5b5662737a.title: Two-phase commit protocol
7c5b5662737a.sentence: It is a distributed algorithm that coordinates all the processes that participate in a distributed atomic transaction on whether to commit or abort (roll back) the transaction.

46c1ae5500cb.title: Two-phase commit protocol
46c1ae5500cb.sentence: In transaction processing, databases, and computer networking, the two-phase commit protocol (2PC, tupac) is a type of atomic commitment protocol (ACP).

efb0c4172cc8.title: Two-phase commit protocol
efb0c4172cc8.sentence: The protocol works in the following manner: one node is a designated coordinator, which is the master site, and the rest of the nodes in the network are designated the participants.

9a457ea40053.title: Two-phase commit protocol
9a457ea40053.section: Basic algorithm > Commit request (or voting) phase
9a457ea40053.sentence: - The coordinator sends a query to commit message to all participants and waits until it has received a reply from all participants.

9910a7d2f311.title: Two-phase commit protocol
9910a7d2f311.section: Basic algorithm > Commit request (or voting) phase
9910a7d2f311.sentence: - The participants execute the transaction up to the point where they will be asked to commit.

289fe333a689.title: Two-phase commit protocol
289fe333a689.section: Basic algorithm > Commit request (or voting) phase
289fe333a689.sentence: They each write an entry to their undo log and an entry to their redo log.

2b936a172c17.title: Two-phase commit protocol
2b936a172c17.sentence: - The commit-request phase (or voting phase), in which a coordinator process attempts to prepare all the transaction's participating processes (named participants, cohorts, or workers) to take the necessary steps for either committing or aborting the transaction and to vote, either "Yes": commit (if the transaction participant's local portion execution has ended properly), or "No": abort (if a problem has been detected with the local portion), and

d0314f35c8d2.title: Two-phase commit protocol
d0314f35c8d2.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Success
d0314f35c8d2.sentence: If the coordinator received an agreement message from all participants during the commit-request phase:

7cb8dbda2fda.title: Two-phase commit protocol
7cb8dbda2fda.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Success
7cb8dbda2fda.sentence: - The coordinator sends a commit message to all the participants.

9879e5c2722e.title: Two-phase commit protocol
9879e5c2722e.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Success
9879e5c2722e.sentence: - Each participant completes the operation, and releases all the locks and resources held during the transaction.

d33c56910c98.title: Two-phase commit protocol
d33c56910c98.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Success
d33c56910c98.sentence: - Each participant sends an acknowledgement to the coordinator.

0f65cd780fbb.title: Two-phase commit protocol
0f65cd780fbb.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Success
0f65cd780fbb.sentence: - The coordinator completes the transaction when all acknowledgements have been received.

8f43447f38de.title: Two-phase commit protocol
8f43447f38de.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Failure
8f43447f38de.sentence: If any participant votes No during the commit-request phase (or the coordinator's timeout expires):

0a6ff4605bf3.title: Two-phase commit protocol
0a6ff4605bf3.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Failure
0a6ff4605bf3.sentence: - The coordinator sends a rollback message to all the participants.

f2e317e50b5b.title: Two-phase commit protocol
f2e317e50b5b.section: Basic algorithm > Commit (or completion) phase > Failure
f2e317e50b5b.sentence: - Each participant undoes the transaction using the undo log, and releases the resources and locks held during the transaction.

f69741e84441.title: Two-phase commit protocol
f69741e84441.sentence: - there is stable storage at each node with a write-ahead log,

755d3225b107.title: Two-phase commit protocol
755d3225b107.sentence: - the data in the write-ahead log is never lost or corrupted in a crash, and

51f8dceeaa13.title: Two-phase commit protocol
51f8dceeaa13.sentence: To accommodate recovery from failure (automatic in most cases) the protocol's participants use logging of the protocol's states.

01cf7ad13682.title: Two-phase commit protocol
01cf7ad13682.sentence: Log records, which are typically slow to generate but survive failures, are used by the protocol's recovery procedures.

02c8d910c4df.title: Two-phase commit protocol
02c8d910c4df.sentence: - The greatest disadvantage of the two-phase commit protocol is that it is a blocking protocol.

11cb8f98cd70.title: Two-phase commit protocol
11cb8f98cd70.sentence: - If the coordinator fails permanently, some participants will never resolve their transactions: After a participant has sent an agreement message as a response to the commit-request message from the coordinator, it will block until a commit or rollback is received.

f07fa9b4bf08.title: Two-phase commit protocol
f07fa9b4bf08.sentence: - A two-phase commit protocol cannot dependably recover from a failure of both the coordinator and a cohort member during the commit phase.

a1be46acfc97.title: Two-phase commit protocol
a1be46acfc97.sentence: If, however, both the coordinator and a cohort member failed, it is possible that the failed cohort member was the first to be notified, and had actually done the commit.

cff7a4e9fbf5.title: Two-phase commit protocol
cff7a4e9fbf5.sentence: Even if a new coordinator is selected, it cannot confidently proceed with the operation until it has received an agreement from all cohort members, and hence must block until all cohort members respond.

e0d7c9836f29.title: Two-phase commit protocol
e0d7c9836f29.sentence: This protocol (a specialised type of consensus protocol) achieves its goal even in many cases of temporary system failure (involving either process, network node, communication, etc. failures), and is thus widely used.

4e2d6f16166b.title: Two-phase commit protocol
4e2d6f16166b.sentence: However, it is not resilient to all possible failure configurations, and in rare cases, manual intervention is needed to remedy an outcome.

13adbf068dc0.title: Microservices
13adbf068dc0.sentence: - Two-phased commits are regarded as an anti-pattern in microservices-based architectures, resulting in a tighter coupling of all the participants within the transaction.

d7472071a40b.title: Lamport timestamp
d7472071a40b.sentence: The Lamport timestamp algorithm is a simple logical clock algorithm used to determine the order of events in a distributed computer system.

df747c566f4b.title: Lamport timestamp
df747c566f4b.section: Lamport's logical clock in distributed systems
df747c566f4b.sentence: In a distributed system, it is not possible in practice to synchronize time across entities (typically thought of as processes) within the system; hence, the entities can use the concept of a logical clock based on the events through which they communicate.

74510eb434e0.title: Lamport timestamp
74510eb434e0.sentence: A Lamport logical clock is a numerical software counter value maintained in each process.

1b704f1e6be9.title: Lamport timestamp
1b704f1e6be9.sentence: Conceptually, this logical clock can be thought of as a clock that only has meaning in relation to messages moving between processes.

ca0630031f16.title: Lamport timestamp
ca0630031f16.sentence: If there is a timing delay causing the disk to receive both messages at the same time, it can determine which message happened-before the other: A happens-before B if one can get from A to B by a sequence of moves of two types: moving forward while remaining in the same process, and following a message from its sending to its reception.

cc3270f34ef5.title: Lamport timestamp
cc3270f34ef5.sentence: Note that if two events happen in different processes that do not exchange messages directly or indirectly via third-party processes, then we say that the two processes are concurrent, that is, nothing can be said about the ordering of the two events.

00676da0ddce.title: Lamport timestamp
00676da0ddce.sentence: - A process increments its counter before each local event (e.g., message sending event);

97112df956f8.title: Lamport timestamp
97112df956f8.sentence: - When a process sends a message, it includes its counter value with the message after executing step 1;

f86b64aa3c68.title: Lamport timestamp
f86b64aa3c68.sentence: - On receiving a message, the counter of the recipient is updated, if necessary, to the greater of its current counter and the timestamp in the received message.

9e5464cd86c3.title: Lamport timestamp
9e5464cd86c3.sentence: The counter is then incremented by 1 before the message is considered received.
