5f829fb57321.title: Happened-before
5f829fb57321.sentence: In computer science, the happened-before relation (denoted: →) is a relation between the result of two events, such that if one event should happen before another event, the result must reflect that, even if those events are in reality executed out of order (usually to optimize program flow).

0c8007afdfd6.title: Happened-before
0c8007afdfd6.sentence: This involves ordering events based on the potential causal relationship of pairs of events in a concurrent system, especially asynchronous distributed systems.

5c82f59ffe49.title: Happened-before
5c82f59ffe49.sentence: The happened-before relation is formally defined as the least strict partial order on events such that:

efa46095ec06.title: Happened-before
efa46095ec06.sentence: - If events a and b occur on the same process, a→b if the occurrence of event a preceded the occurrence of event b.

0ba9fadb40b0.title: Happened-before
0ba9fadb40b0.sentence: - If event a is the sending of a message and event b is the reception of the message sent in event a, a→b.

0cda7561cb2e.title: Happened-before
0cda7561cb2e.sentence: Like all strict partial orders, the happened-before relation is transitive, irreflexive, (and, vacuously, asymmetric), i.e.:

2cd760a66d9b.title: Happened-before
2cd760a66d9b.sentence: If two events happen in different isolated processes (that do not exchange messages directly or indirectly via third-party processes), then the two processes are said to be concurrent, that is neither a→b nor b→a is true.

b6658d0e75d9.title: Happened-before
b6658d0e75d9.sentence: The processes that make up a distributed system have no knowledge of the happened-before relation unless they use a logical clock, like a Lamport clock or a vector clock.

dc5c58ec7cec.title: Happened-before

97617c72b89c.title: Vector clock
97617c72b89c.sentence: A vector clock is a data structure used for determining the partial ordering of events in a distributed system and detecting causality violations.

6ad28a6691ca.title: Vector clock
6ad28a6691ca.sentence: A vector clock of a system of n processes is a vector (equivalently, a 1-dimensional array) of n logical clocks, one clock per process.

6af3f31a4f4e.title: Vector clock
6af3f31a4f4e.sentence: Just as in Lamport timestamps, inter-process messages contain the state of the sending process's logical clock.

279db14d5b3e.title: Vector clock
279db14d5b3e.sentence: Besides maintaining its own clock, every process also keeps track of the largest value of each of the other processes' clocks that it has so far been informed of.

792183253779.title: Vector clock
792183253779.sentence: - Each time a process experiences an internal event, it increments its own logical clock in the vector by one.

917ce226a7dc.title: Vector clock
917ce226a7dc.sentence: - Each time a process sends a message, it increments its own logical clock in the vector by one (as in the bullet above, but not twice for the same event) then it pairs the message with a copy of its own vector and finally sends the pair.

a215f8a3dfb5.title: Vector clock
a215f8a3dfb5.sentence: - Each time a process receives a message-vector clock pair, it increments its own logical clock in the vector by one and updates each element in its vector by taking the maximum of the value in its own vector clock and the value in the vector in the received pair (for every element).

ee24a2a5e527.title: Vector clock
ee24a2a5e527.sentence: - In English: VC(x) is less than VC(y), if and only if VC(x)z is less than or equal to VC(y)z for all process indices z, and at least one of those relationships is strictly smaller (that is, VC(x)z′<VC(y)z′).

feb8d711704e.title: Consensus (computer science)
feb8d711704e.sentence: The consensus problem requires agreement among a number of processes (or agents) on a single data value.

aaa612ea79e6.title: Consensus (computer science)
aaa612ea79e6.sentence: Some of the processes (agents) may fail or be unreliable in other ways, so consensus protocols must be fault-tolerant or resilient.

ace9adcba892.title: Consensus (computer science)
ace9adcba892.sentence: This often requires coordinating processes to reach consensus, or agree on some data value that is needed during computation.

be514f3c8500.title: Consensus (computer science)
be514f3c8500.sentence: The processes must put forth their candidate values, communicate with one another, and agree on a single consensus value.

cc8e3ce86f4f.title: Consensus (computer science)

e1a2a6969ca9.title: Consensus (computer science)
e1a2a6969ca9.sentence: One approach to generating consensus is for all processes (agents) to agree on a majority value.

032811bfb61e.title: Consensus (computer science)
032811bfb61e.sentence: In this context, a majority requires at least one more than half of the available votes (where each process is given a vote).

5385b4133f41.title: Consensus (computer science)
5385b4133f41.sentence: However, one or more faulty processes may skew the resultant outcome such that consensus may not be reached or may be reached incorrectly.

e418f2a392ff.title: Consensus (computer science)
e418f2a392ff.sentence: For instance, a trivial protocol could have all processes output binary value 1.

36dec1ba2149.title: Consensus (computer science)
36dec1ba2149.sentence: That is, the output value of a consensus protocol must be the input value of some process.

e90dadf0df82.title: Consensus (computer science)
e90dadf0df82.sentence: Another requirement is that a process may decide upon an output value only once, and this decision is irrevocable.

cacdfb364a4e.title: Consensus (computer science)
cacdfb364a4e.sentence: Eventually, every correct process decides some value.

38a1cad19191.title: Consensus (computer science)
38a1cad19191.sentence: Every correct process must agree on the same value.

4c61c1007f55.title: Consensus (computer science)
4c61c1007f55.sentence: If all the correct processes proposed the same value v, then any correct process must decide v.

72ed9ae86bd6.title: Consensus (computer science)
72ed9ae86bd6.sentence: A protocol that can correctly guarantee consensus amongst n processes of which at most t fail is said to be t-resilient.

e68b57954d66.title: Consensus (computer science)
e68b57954d66.sentence: In evaluating the performance of consensus protocols two factors of interest are running time and message complexity.

733c814e074d.title: Consensus (computer science)

fbbc7ce464df.title: Consensus (computer science)

39e3e153a6ad.sentence: - Task Scheduling In a distributed task scheduler, distributed locks ensure that a scheduled task is executed by only one worker node, preventing duplicate execution.

43bfda757772.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-do-we-need-to-use-a-distributed-lock.md
43bfda757772.section: Top 6 Use Cases for Distributed Locks

e015086ff309.sentence: - Microservices Coordination When multiple microservices need to perform coordinated operations, such as updating related data in different databases, distributed locks ensure that these operations are performed in a controlled and orderly manner.

d8f0bfca2a2a.title: Distributed lock manager
d8f0bfca2a2a.sentence: This is the traditional exclusive lock which allows read and update access to the resource, and prevents others from having any access to it.

8d93f8c67f84.title: Distributed lock manager
8d93f8c67f84.sentence: When one or more processes have obtained locks on resources, it is possible to produce a situation where each is preventing another from obtaining a lock, and none of them can proceed.

e36687f1e622.title: Distributed lock manager
e36687f1e622.sentence: But if Process 2 then tries to lock Resource A, both processes will wait forever for each other.

1e74dfaecb07.title: Distributed lock manager
1e74dfaecb07.sentence: The OpenVMS DLM periodically checks for deadlock situations.

018c78b13e81.title: Distributed lock manager
018c78b13e81.sentence: In the example above, the second lock enqueue request of one of the processes would return with a deadlock status.

75154a9262b0.title: Distributed lock manager
75154a9262b0.sentence: It would then be up to this process to take action to resolve the deadlock—in this case by releasing the first lock it obtained.

f3124e84da6a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
f3124e84da6a.sentence: In practice, it is essential to use renewable leases with timeouts instead of indefinite locks, because doing so prevents locks from being held indefinitely by processes that crash.

a19aa6f545c0.title: Consensus (computer science)
a19aa6f545c0.sentence: Chubby maintains lock information in small files which are stored in a replicated database to achieve high availability in the face of failures.

bb3b25a6b1bb.title: Consensus (computer science)

d2b96dbd6a56.title: Distributed lock manager
d2b96dbd6a56.sentence: - HashiCorp's Consul, which was created by HashiCorp, is open-source software and can be used to perform distributed locks as well.
