4862bfda195b.title: Paxos (computer science)
4862bfda195b.sentence: State machine replication is a technique for converting an algorithm into a fault-tolerant, distributed implementation.

d300f94e203b.title: Paxos (computer science)
d300f94e203b.sentence: Consensus protocols are the basis for the state machine replication approach to distributed computing, as suggested by Leslie Lamport and surveyed by Fred Schneider.

730f90309272.title: Paxos (computer science)
730f90309272.sentence: Ad-hoc techniques may leave important cases of failures unresolved.

6cc1aedd4462.title: Paxos (computer science)
6cc1aedd4462.sentence: The principled approach proposed by Lamport et al. ensures all cases are handled safely.

f8b206493b81.title: Raft (algorithm)
f8b206493b81.sentence: Raft offers a generic way to distribute a state machine across a cluster of computing systems, ensuring that each node in the cluster agrees upon the same series of state transitions.

0ce26f9dd876.title: Raft (algorithm)
0ce26f9dd876.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
0ce26f9dd876.sentence: Each client request consists of a command to be executed by the replicated state machines in the cluster.

3fbee471873c.title: Raft (algorithm)
3fbee471873c.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
3fbee471873c.sentence: Once the leader receives confirmation from half or more of its followers that the entry has been replicated, the leader applies the entry to its local state machine, and the request is considered committed.

0d003df94f9a.title: Paxos (computer science)
0d003df94f9a.sentence: A typical deployment of Paxos requires a continuous stream of agreed values acting as commands to a distributed state machine.

629d469ca0af.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
629d469ca0af.sentence: The operations on an RSM are ordered globally through a consensus algorithm.

eff1bac532e2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
eff1bac532e2.sentence: The consensus algorithm deals with agreement on the sequence of operations, and the RSM executes the operations in that order.

4b4eaed6263b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
4b4eaed6263b.sentence: RSMs are the fundamental building block of useful distributed systems components and services such as data or configuration storage, locking, and leader election (described in more detail later).

fa393ddaea2d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
fa393ddaea2d.sentence: This is a powerful concept: several papers ([Agu10], [Kir08], [Sch90]) show that any deterministic program can be implemented as a highly available replicated service by being implemented as an RSM.

b15999a71dbe.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
b15999a71dbe.sentence: Because not every member of the consensus group is necessarily a member of each consensus quorum, RSMs may need to synchronize state from peers.

b54702dbe909.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
b54702dbe909.sentence: As described by Kirsch and Amir [Kir08], you can use a sliding-window protocol to reconcile state between peer processes in an RSM.

47d93e575fb1.title: Consensus (computer science)
47d93e575fb1.section: Models of computation > Inputs and outputs of consensus
47d93e575fb1.sentence: In the most traditional single-value consensus protocols such as Paxos, cooperating nodes agree on a single value such as an integer, which may be of variable size so as to encode useful metadata such as a transaction committed to a database.

3ad5fe206b85.title: Consensus (computer science)
3ad5fe206b85.section: Models of computation > Inputs and outputs of consensus
3ad5fe206b85.sentence: In multi-valued consensus protocols such as Multi-Paxos and Raft, the goal is to agree on not just a single value but a series of values over time, forming a progressively-growing history.

a9da9cea5508.title: Consensus (computer science)
a9da9cea5508.section: Models of computation > Inputs and outputs of consensus
a9da9cea5508.sentence: A special case of the single-value consensus problem, called binary consensus, restricts the input, and hence the output domain, to a single binary digit {0,1}.

f1d08d32f985.title: Consensus (computer science)
f1d08d32f985.section: Models of computation > Inputs and outputs of consensus
f1d08d32f985.sentence: While not highly useful by themselves, binary consensus protocols are often useful as building blocks in more general consensus protocols, especially for asynchronous consensus.

346c87f68be7.title: Consensus (computer science)
346c87f68be7.section: Models of computation > Inputs and outputs of consensus
346c87f68be7.sentence: While multi-valued consensus may be achieved naively by running multiple iterations of a single-valued consensus protocol in succession, many optimizations and other considerations such as reconfiguration support can make multi-valued consensus protocols more efficient in practice.

855e33b63abc.title: Consensus (computer science)
855e33b63abc.section: Models of computation > Asynchronous and synchronous systems
855e33b63abc.sentence: In synchronous systems, it is assumed that all communications proceed in rounds.

5f2debf4efe6.title: Consensus (computer science)
5f2debf4efe6.section: Models of computation > Asynchronous and synchronous systems
5f2debf4efe6.sentence: The consensus problem may be considered in the case of asynchronous or synchronous systems.

dc5e59e4907a.title: Consensus (computer science)
dc5e59e4907a.section: Models of computation > Asynchronous and synchronous systems
dc5e59e4907a.sentence: In one round, a process may send all the messages it requires, while receiving all messages from other processes.

0e827cbaabe1.title: Consensus (computer science)
0e827cbaabe1.section: Models of computation > Asynchronous and synchronous systems
0e827cbaabe1.sentence: In this manner, no message from one round may influence any messages sent within the same round.

3d7a0dfa3991.title: Consensus (computer science)
3d7a0dfa3991.section: Models of computation > Asynchronous and synchronous systems
3d7a0dfa3991.sentence: While real world communications are often inherently asynchronous, it is more practical and often easier to model synchronous systems, given that asynchronous systems naturally involve more issues than synchronous ones.

3def1d887950.title: Consensus (computer science)
3def1d887950.section: Models of computation > Asynchronous and synchronous systems > The FLP impossibility result for asynchronous deterministic consensus
3def1d887950.sentence: In a fully asynchronous message-passing distributed system, in which at least one process may have a crash failure, it has been proven in the famous 1985 FLP impossibility result by Fischer, Lynch and Paterson that a deterministic algorithm for achieving consensus is impossible.

a32c9385b7ae.title: Three-phase commit protocol
a32c9385b7ae.sentence: In computer networking and distributed databases, the three-phase commit protocol (3PC) is a distributed algorithm that ensures all nodes in a system agree to commit or abort a transaction.

603e8d8d2412.title: Three-phase commit protocol
603e8d8d2412.sentence: It improves upon the two-phase commit protocol (2PC) by eliminating the possibility of indefinite blocking caused by a specific type of failure during the commit phase.

43d1bcde1a16.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
43d1bcde1a16.sentence: Three-phase commit (3PC) is an extension of the two-phase commit where the commit phase is split into two phases.

94d98ad69567.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
94d98ad69567.sentence: Coordinator issues the pre-commit message and all the participating nodes must acknowledge it.

827201c73dd6.title: Three-phase commit protocol
827201c73dd6.sentence: The three-phase commit protocol eliminates this problem by introducing the Prepared to commit state.

1bdfc7b25c8b.title: Three-phase commit protocol
1bdfc7b25c8b.sentence: The coordinator will not send out a doCommit message until all cohort members have ACKed that they are prepared to commit.

af57c9de77f1.title: Three-phase commit protocol
af57c9de77f1.sentence: This eliminates the possibility that any cohort member actually completed the transaction before all cohort members were aware of the decision to do so (an ambiguity that necessitated indefinite blocking in the two-phase commit protocol).

d4415fc94b87.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
d4415fc94b87.section: Three-phase commit > Why is the Pre-commit phase helpful?
d4415fc94b87.sentence: - Every phase can now time out and avoid indefinite waits.

cdbca3e96ea1.title: Three-phase commit protocol
cdbca3e96ea1.sentence: If the coordinator fails before sending preCommit messages, the cohort will unanimously agree that the operation was aborted.

90f71d31b778.title: Three-phase commit protocol
90f71d31b778.sentence: When the recovery coordinator takes over after the coordinator failed during a commit phase of two-phase commit, the new pre-commit comes handy as follows: On querying participants, if it learns that some nodes are in commit phase then it assumes that the previous coordinator before crashing has made the decision to commit.

62b468d71b26.title: Three-phase commit protocol
62b468d71b26.sentence: Hence it can shepherd the protocol to commit.

054fd259f350.title: Three-phase commit protocol
054fd259f350.sentence: Similarly, if a participant says that it had not received a PrepareToCommit message, then the new coordinator can assume that the previous coordinator failed even before it completed the PrepareToCommit phase.

639e5891d582.title: Three-phase commit protocol
639e5891d582.sentence: Hence it can safely assume that no participant has committed the changes, and hence safely abort the transaction.

52e6547727cf.title: Three-phase commit protocol
52e6547727cf.sentence: Three-phase commit assumes a network with bounded delay and nodes with bounded response times; in most practical systems with unbounded network delay and process pauses, it cannot guarantee atomicity.

2301a26b13b5.title: Three-phase commit protocol
2301a26b13b5.sentence: The other drawback of the protocol is it requires at least three round trips to complete, needing a minimum of three round trip times (RTTs).

c2433112dfe1.title: Three-phase commit protocol
c2433112dfe1.sentence: This is potentially a long latency to complete each transaction.

af5a7c726e73.title: Three-phase commit protocol
af5a7c726e73.sentence: Using Skeen's original three-phase commit protocol, it is possible that a quorum becomes connected without being able to make progress (this is not a deadlock situation; the system will still progress if the network partitioning is resolved).

e4c86fd629c0.title: Three-phase commit protocol
e4c86fd629c0.sentence: Keidar and Dolev's E3PC refines Skeen's three-phase commit protocol and solves this problem in a way which always allows a quorum to make progress.

c847bdd042ad.title: Two Generals' Problem
c847bdd042ad.sentence: In computing, the Two Generals' Problem (or Chinese Generals Problem) is a thought experiment meant to illustrate the pitfalls and design challenges of attempting to coordinate an action by communicating over an unreliable link.

9f8c20d72197.title: Two Generals' Problem
9f8c20d72197.sentence: In the experiment, two generals are only able to communicate with one another by sending a messenger through enemy territory.

3ca67019941a.title: Two Generals' Problem
3ca67019941a.sentence: Unfortunately, the valley is occupied by the city's defenders and there is a chance that any given messenger sent through the valley will be captured.

cfacf3423155.title: Two Generals' Problem
cfacf3423155.sentence: It is required that the two generals have their armies attack the city simultaneously to succeed, lest the lone attacker army die trying.

96607d430bf9.title: Two Generals' Problem
96607d430bf9.sentence: Because acknowledgement of message receipt can be lost as easily as the original message, a potentially infinite series of messages is required to come to consensus.

474538bb0ff4.title: Two Generals' Problem
474538bb0ff4.sentence: Thus, it quickly becomes evident that no matter how many rounds of confirmation are made, there is no way to guarantee the second requirement that each general is sure the other has agreed to the attack plan.

a51e89158a6a.title: Two Generals' Problem
a51e89158a6a.sentence: Both generals will always be left wondering whether their last messenger got through.

5804c2235f0b.title: Two Generals' Problem
5804c2235f0b.sentence: The Two Generals' Problem was the first computer communication problem to be proven to be unsolvable.

ad9dc4d251c5.title: Two Generals' Problem
ad9dc4d251c5.sentence: Consider the last such message that was successfully delivered.

bc9a0a9b09d0.title: Two Generals' Problem
bc9a0a9b09d0.sentence: From the viewpoint of the sender of that last message, however, the sequence of messages sent and delivered is exactly the same as it would have been, had that message been delivered.

20cc8695f4a1.title: Two Generals' Problem
20cc8695f4a1.sentence: We've now created a situation where the suggested protocol leads one general to attack and the other not to attack—contradicting the assumption that the protocol was a solution to the problem.

e7ed3ccbc315.title: Two Generals' Problem
e7ed3ccbc315.sentence: An important consequence of this proof is that generalizations such as the Byzantine Generals problem are also unsolvable in the face of arbitrary communication failures, thus providing a base of realistic expectations for any distributed consistency protocols.

e8b45c3ea8aa.title: Two Generals' Problem
e8b45c3ea8aa.sentence: The Two Generals' Problem appears often as an introduction to the more general Byzantine Generals problem in introductory classes about computer networking (particularly with regard to the Transmission Control Protocol, where it shows that TCP cannot guarantee state consistency between endpoints and why this is the case), though it applies to any type of two-party communication where failures of communication are possible.

0e16686b64ff.title: Two Generals' Problem
0e16686b64ff.sentence: A pragmatic approach to dealing with the Two Generals' Problem is to use schemes that accept the uncertainty of the communications channel and not attempt to eliminate it, but rather mitigate it to an acceptable degree.

1a293472a50f.title: Two Generals' Problem
1a293472a50f.sentence: For example, the first general could send 100 messengers, anticipating that the probability of all being captured is low.

236f13e525df.title: Two Generals' Problem
236f13e525df.sentence: There is no algorithm that they can use (e.g. attack if more than four messages are received) that will be certain to prevent one from attacking without the other.

ce3dbf8c93d7.title: Consensus (computer science)
ce3dbf8c93d7.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
ce3dbf8c93d7.sentence: There are two types of failures a process may undergo, a crash failure or a Byzantine failure.

21e67af82c0f.title: Consensus (computer science)
21e67af82c0f.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
21e67af82c0f.sentence: A crash failure occurs when a process abruptly stops and does not resume.

f5bc0c7aa25d.title: Consensus (computer science)
f5bc0c7aa25d.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
f5bc0c7aa25d.sentence: Byzantine failures are failures in which absolutely no conditions are imposed.

98ff5fb99b61.title: Consensus (computer science)
98ff5fb99b61.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
98ff5fb99b61.sentence: For example, they may occur as a result of the malicious actions of an adversary.

335df9fc5cdf.title: Consensus (computer science)
335df9fc5cdf.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
335df9fc5cdf.sentence: A process that experiences a Byzantine failure may send contradictory or conflicting data to other processes, or it may sleep and then resume activity after a lengthy delay.

db7b304a221e.title: Consensus (computer science)
db7b304a221e.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
db7b304a221e.sentence: Of the two types of failures, Byzantine failures are far more disruptive.

3a0cba22b041.title: Consensus (computer science)
3a0cba22b041.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
3a0cba22b041.sentence: Thus, a consensus protocol tolerating Byzantine failures must be resilient to every possible error that can occur.

d909add7fd88.title: Consensus (computer science)
d909add7fd88.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
d909add7fd88.sentence: A stronger version of consensus tolerating Byzantine failures is given by strengthening the Integrity constraint:

6ff6fe6447d0.title: Consensus (computer science)
6ff6fe6447d0.section: Models of computation > Crash and Byzantine failures
6ff6fe6447d0.sentence: If a correct process decides v, then v must have been proposed by some correct process.

98664390ff28.title: Consensus (computer science)
98664390ff28.section: Solvability results for some agreement problems
98664390ff28.sentence: For systems with n processors, of which f are Byzantine, it has been shown that there exists no algorithm that solves the consensus problem for n ≤ 3f in the oral-messages model.

fbdea5ccba5e.title: Consensus (computer science)
fbdea5ccba5e.section: Solvability results for some agreement problems
fbdea5ccba5e.sentence: In the written-messages model there are protocols that can tolerate n = f + 1.

bd30c7d60fbd.title: Consensus (computer science)
bd30c7d60fbd.section: Models of computation > Communication channels with direct or transferable authentication
bd30c7d60fbd.sentence: Some models assume a stronger, transferable form of authentication, where each message is signed by the sender, so that a receiver knows not just the immediate source of every message, but the participant that initially created the message.

16fb62feb20f.title: Consensus (computer science)
16fb62feb20f.section: Models of computation > Communication channels with direct or transferable authentication
16fb62feb20f.sentence: This stronger type of authentication is achieved by digital signatures, and when this stronger form of authentication is available, protocols can tolerate a larger number of faults.

9890403dc077.title: Consensus (computer science)
9890403dc077.sentence: PBFT | Asynchronous (safety) Synchronous (liveness) | Oral | n > 3 f

b0a449b51420.title: Atomic broadcast
b0a449b51420.sentence: In fault-tolerant distributed computing, an atomic broadcast or total order broadcast is a broadcast where all correct processes in a system of multiple processes receive the same set of messages in the same order; that is, the same sequence of messages.

165c722133bd.title: Atomic broadcast
165c722133bd.sentence: The broadcast is termed "atomic" because it either eventually completes correctly at all participants, or all participants abort without side effects.

a159cdb9605e.title: Atomic broadcast
a159cdb9605e.sentence: Atomic broadcasts are an important distributed computing primitive.

081e72633a79.title: Atomic broadcast
081e72633a79.sentence: - Validity: if a correct participant broadcasts a message, then all correct participants will eventually receive it.

772bfd43abfa.title: Atomic broadcast
772bfd43abfa.sentence: - Uniform Agreement: if one correct participant receives a message, then all correct participants will eventually receive that message.

377d8ff2a595.title: Atomic broadcast
377d8ff2a595.sentence: - Uniform Integrity: a message is received by each participant at most once, and only if it was previously broadcast.

a64e90c22c6f.title: Atomic broadcast
a64e90c22c6f.sentence: - Uniform Total Order: the messages are totally ordered in the mathematical sense; that is, if any correct participant receives message 1 first and message 2 second, then every other correct participant must receive message 1 before message 2.

ac35156fe61b.title: Atomic broadcast
ac35156fe61b.sentence: Note that total order is not equivalent to FIFO order, which requires that if a process sent message 1 before it sent message 2, then all participants must receive message 1 before receiving message 2.

2a7abfabd5be.title: Atomic broadcast
2a7abfabd5be.sentence: It is also not equivalent to "causal order", where if message 2 "depends on" or "occurs after" message 1 then all participants must receive message 2 after receiving message 1.

ca95497b1f99.title: Atomic broadcast
ca95497b1f99.sentence: While a strong and useful condition, total order requires only that all participants receive the messages in the same order, but does not place other constraints on that order such as that in which the messages are sent.

69fda6f91c3f.title: Atomic broadcast
69fda6f91c3f.sentence: Designing an algorithm for atomic broadcasts is relatively easy if it can be assumed that computers will not fail.

23d6fdbfc711.title: Atomic broadcast
23d6fdbfc711.sentence: For example, if there are no failures, atomic broadcast can be achieved simply by having all participants communicate with one "leader" which determines the order of the messages, with the other participants following the leader.

55b6d3e92767.title: Atomic broadcast
55b6d3e92767.sentence: For example, in the follow-the-leader algorithm, what if the leader fails at the wrong time?

ed3ed0ea2866.title: Atomic broadcast
ed3ed0ea2866.sentence: In such an environment achieving atomic broadcasts is difficult.

e0f77dea7213.title: Atomic broadcast
e0f77dea7213.sentence: Such considerations indicate that in systems with crash failures, atomic broadcast and consensus are equivalent problems.

7fb9a20dec37.title: Atomic broadcast
7fb9a20dec37.sentence: A value can be proposed by a process for consensus by atomically broadcasting it, and a process can decide a value by selecting the value of the first message which it atomically receives.

887c198e9c6f.title: Atomic broadcast
887c198e9c6f.sentence: Thus, consensus can be reduced to atomic broadcast.

37ae07955735.title: Atomic broadcast
37ae07955735.sentence: Conversely, a group of participants can atomically broadcast messages by achieving consensus regarding the first message to be received, followed by achieving consensus on the next message, and so forth until all the messages have been received.

497d3a5de7ad.title: Atomic broadcast
497d3a5de7ad.sentence: Thus, atomic broadcast reduces to consensus.

0d9179d6e4e6.title: Atomic broadcast
0d9179d6e4e6.sentence: Since consensus and atomic broadcast are equivalent, FLP applies also to atomic broadcast.

32377a6af097.title: Atomic broadcast
32377a6af097.sentence: The FLP result does not prohibit the implementation of atomic broadcast in practice, but it does require making less stringent assumptions than FLP in some respect, such as about processor and communication timings.

7a2b1334ea45.title: Atomic broadcast
7a2b1334ea45.sentence: The Chandra-Toueg algorithm is a consensus-based solution to atomic broadcast.

436990b71c13.title: Atomic broadcast
436990b71c13.sentence: The Zookeeper Atomic Broadcast (ZAB) protocol is the basic building block for Apache ZooKeeper, a fault-tolerant distributed coordination service which underpins Hadoop and many other important distributed systems.

5f2a3f6de5d9.title: Head-of-line blocking
5f2a3f6de5d9.sentence: While atomic broadcast algorithms solve the single point of failure problem of centralized servers, those algorithms introduce a head-of-line blocking problem.

d6515dede00d.title: Apache ZooKeeper
d6515dede00d.sentence: Apache ZooKeeper is an open-source server for highly reliable distributed coordination of cloud applications.

dbb0686e5aa8.title: Apache ZooKeeper
dbb0686e5aa8.sentence: ZooKeeper is essentially a service for distributed systems offering a hierarchical key-value store, which is used to provide a distributed configuration service, synchronization service, and naming registry for large distributed systems (see Use cases).

6cb8e511b104.title: Apache ZooKeeper
6cb8e511b104.sentence: ZooKeeper nodes store their data in a hierarchical name space, like a file system or a tree data structure.

56b6c66375ef.title: Apache ZooKeeper
56b6c66375ef.sentence: Clients can read from and write to the nodes and in this way have a shared configuration service.

2ccdffe9ed9c.title: Apache ZooKeeper
2ccdffe9ed9c.sentence: The services in the cluster are replicated and stored on a set of servers (called an "ensemble"), each of which maintains an in-memory database containing the entire data tree of state as well as a transaction log and snapshots stored persistently.

fd8de8b13af4.title: Apache ZooKeeper
fd8de8b13af4.sentence: Multiple client applications can connect to a server, and each client maintains a TCP connection through which it sends requests and heartbeats and receives responses and watch events for monitoring.

e7cb1b571d17.title: Apache ZooKeeper
e7cb1b571d17.sentence: ZooKeeper can be viewed as an atomic broadcast system, through which updates are totally ordered.

4b5859be7e2a.title: Apache ZooKeeper
4b5859be7e2a.sentence: The ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast (ZAB) protocol is the core of the system.

21bd8c755818.title: Apache ZooKeeper
21bd8c755818.sentence: Typical use cases for ZooKeeper are:

cd65b1403c9c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
cd65b1403c9c.sentence: The Zookeeper consensus service can implement the barrier pattern: see [Hun10] and [Zoo14].

dcb92c0cb8d2.title: Apache ZooKeeper
dcb92c0cb8d2.sentence: - Fast Processing: especially fast in "read-dominant" workloads (i.e. workloads in which reads are much more common than writes).

784b9d0f5cab.title: Apache ZooKeeper
784b9d0f5cab.sentence: - Scalable: performance can be improved by adding nodes.

f651cc96d786.title: Apache ZooKeeper
f651cc96d786.sentence: ZooKeeper is modeled after Google's Chubby lock service and was originally developed at Yahoo! for streamlining the processes running on big-data clusters by storing the status in local log files on the ZooKeeper servers.

3ce0f37084ec.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
3ce0f37084ec.section: System Architecture Patterns for Distributed Consensus
3ce0f37084ec.sentence: Zookeeper [Hun10] was the first open source consensus system to gain traction in the industry because it was easy to use, even with applications that werenât designed to use distributed consensus.

a10062733f56.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
a10062733f56.section: System Architecture Patterns for Distributed Consensus
a10062733f56.sentence: Many systems that successfully use consensus algorithms actually do so as clients of some service that implements those algorithms, such as Zookeeper, Consul, and etcd.

193c7234301b.title: Consensus (computer science)
193c7234301b.section: Solvability results for some agreement problems
193c7234301b.sentence: In a fully asynchronous system there is no consensus solution that can tolerate one or more crash failures even when only requiring the non triviality property.

e0eca38b757c.title: Consensus (computer science)
e0eca38b757c.section: Solvability results for some agreement problems
e0eca38b757c.sentence: The FLP result has been mechanically verified to hold even under fairness assumptions.

0358302b15f3.title: Consensus (computer science)
0358302b15f3.section: Solvability results for some agreement problems
0358302b15f3.sentence: However, FLP does not state that consensus can never be reached: merely that under the model's assumptions, no algorithm can always reach consensus in bounded time.

882666f7990d.title: Consensus (computer science)
882666f7990d.section: Solvability results for some agreement problems
882666f7990d.sentence: In practice it is highly unlikely to occur.

6a1702764da4.title: Consensus (computer science)
6a1702764da4.section: Models of computation > Asynchronous and synchronous systems > The FLP impossibility result for asynchronous deterministic consensus
6a1702764da4.sentence: Randomized consensus algorithms can circumvent the FLP impossibility result by achieving both safety and liveness with overwhelming probability, even under worst-case scheduling scenarios such as an intelligent denial-of-service attacker in the network.

81588a5267a2.title: Paxos (computer science)
81588a5267a2.sentence: In computer science, Paxos is a family of protocols for solving consensus in a network of unreliable or fallible processors.

ce8491c57a07.title: Paxos (computer science)
ce8491c57a07.sentence: Paxos is usually used where durability is required (for example, to replicate a file or a database), in which the amount of durable state could be large.

42e61cc0ac1c.title: Paxos (computer science)
42e61cc0ac1c.sentence: In most deployments of Paxos, each participating process acts in three roles: Proposer, Acceptor and Learner.

826343e5b71d.title: Paxos (computer science)
826343e5b71d.sentence: By merging roles, the protocol "collapses" into an efficient client-master-replica style deployment, typical of the database community.

17e4918b95ad.title: Paxos (computer science)
17e4918b95ad.sentence: In order to guarantee safety (also called "consistency"), Paxos defines three properties and ensures the first two are always held, regardless of the pattern of failures:

4519c16cb670.title: Paxos (computer science)
4519c16cb670.sentence: Only proposed values can be chosen and learned.

4659332bde90.title: Paxos (computer science)
4659332bde90.sentence: No two distinct learners can learn different values (or there can't be more than one decided value).

66b8a30dbb3e.title: Paxos (computer science)
66b8a30dbb3e.sentence: Note that Paxos is not guaranteed to terminate, and thus does not have the liveness property.

01d10c7b58a0.title: Paxos (computer science)
01d10c7b58a0.sentence: This is supported by the Fischer Lynch Paterson impossibility result (FLP) which states that a consistency protocol can only have two of safety, liveness, and fault tolerance.

8d1c9780c8a3.title: Paxos (computer science)
8d1c9780c8a3.sentence: Although no deterministic fault-tolerant consensus protocol can guarantee progress in an asynchronous network (a result proved in a paper by Fischer, Lynch and Paterson), Paxos guarantees safety (consistency), and the conditions that could prevent it from making progress are difficult to provoke.

3b4479f63a02.title: Paxos (computer science)
3b4479f63a02.sentence: In general, a consensus algorithm can make progress using n=2F+1 processors, despite the simultaneous failure of any F processors: in other words, the number of non-faulty processes must be strictly greater than the number of faulty processes.

2ac6e5450612.title: Paxos (computer science)
2ac6e5450612.sentence: - Messages are sent asynchronously and may take arbitrarily long to deliver.

c807b8697f85.title: Paxos (computer science)
c807b8697f85.sentence: - Processors with stable storage may re-join the protocol after failures (following a crash-recovery failure model).

6f9d69c4d0e1.title: Paxos (computer science)
6f9d69c4d0e1.sentence: The Paxos family of protocols includes a spectrum of trade-offs between the number of processors, number of message delays before learning the agreed value, the activity level of individual participants, number of messages sent, and types of failures.

0de63afafeb7.title: Paxos (computer science)
0de63afafeb7.sentence: Paxos may also be extended to support arbitrary failures of the participants, including lying, fabrication of messages, collusion with other participants, selective non-participation, etc. These types of failures are called Byzantine failures, after the solution popularized by Lamport.

23e924e1e385.title: Paxos (computer science)
23e924e1e385.sentence: - Google uses the Paxos algorithm in their Chubby distributed lock service in order to keep replicas consistent in case of failure.

edce77b9f8d1.title: Paxos (computer science)
edce77b9f8d1.sentence: - Google Spanner and Megastore use the Paxos algorithm internally.

270760355f3e.title: Paxos (computer science)
270760355f3e.sentence: - Amazon DynamoDB uses the Paxos algorithm for leader election and consensus.

33bdaa16aa85.title: Paxos (computer science)
33bdaa16aa85.sentence: - Apache Cassandra NoSQL database uses Paxos for Light Weight Transaction feature only.

5a17d1951af8.title: Byzantine fault
5a17d1951af8.sentence: A Byzantine fault is a condition of a system, particularly a distributed computing system, where a fault occurs such that different symptoms are presented to different observers, including imperfect information on whether a system component has failed.

27b8a2ee1a42.title: Byzantine fault
27b8a2ee1a42.sentence: A Byzantine fault is any fault presenting different symptoms to different observers.

faf4ee24f632.title: Byzantine fault
faf4ee24f632.sentence: Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) is the resilience of a fault-tolerant computer system or similar system to such conditions.

419e39b75137.title: Byzantine fault
419e39b75137.sentence: The important thing is that all generals agree on a common decision, for a half-hearted attack by a few generals would become a rout, and would be worse than either a coordinated attack or a coordinated retreat.

788ec756d3d1.title: Byzantine fault
788ec756d3d1.sentence: The problem is complicated by the presence of treacherous generals who may not only cast a vote for a suboptimal strategy; they may do so selectively.

cfc7158cc4fd.title: Byzantine fault
cfc7158cc4fd.sentence: For instance, if nine generals are voting, four of whom support attacking while four others are in favor of retreat, the ninth general may send a vote of retreat to those generals in favor of retreat, and a vote of attack to the rest.

176e15af1fa4.title: Byzantine fault
176e15af1fa4.sentence: The problem is complicated further by the generals being physically separated and having to send their votes via messengers who may fail to deliver votes or may forge false votes.

a16c8d2a0d5c.title: Byzantine fault
a16c8d2a0d5c.sentence: Whereas the fail-stop failure mode simply means that the only way to fail is a node crash, detected by other nodes, Byzantine failures imply no restrictions on what errors can be created, which means that a failed node can generate arbitrary data, including data that makes it appear like a functioning node to a subset of other nodes.

36fe92f3dff9.title: Byzantine fault
36fe92f3dff9.sentence: Thus, Byzantine failures can confuse failure detection systems, which makes fault tolerance difficult.

4a09e8349285.title: Byzantine fault
4a09e8349285.sentence: When considering failure propagation only via errors, Byzantine failures are considered the most general and most difficult class of failures among the failure modes.

17a20ecce1c3.title: Byzantine fault
17a20ecce1c3.sentence: Despite the allegory, a Byzantine failure is not necessarily a security problem involving hostile human interference: it can arise purely from physical or software faults.

fe7499abf82c.title: Byzantine fault
fe7499abf82c.sentence: Without message signing, Byzantine fault tolerance can only be achieved if the total number of generals is greater than three times the number of disloyal (faulty) generals.

7fe88b0dad5c.title: Byzantine fault
7fe88b0dad5c.sentence: The full set of BFT requirements are: For F number of Byzantine failures, there needs to be at least 3F+1 players (fault containment zones), 2F+1 independent communication paths, and F+1 rounds of communication.

5b4429cd2371.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
5b4429cd2371.sentence: In general, consensus-based systems operate using majority quorums, i.e., a group of 2f + 1 replicas may tolerate f failures (if Byzantine fault tolerance, in which the system is resistant to replicas returning incorrect results, is required, then 3f + 1 replicas may tolerate f failures [Cas99]).

bc1c57d3d5f6.title: Byzantine fault
bc1c57d3d5f6.sentence: - A second solution requires unforgeable message signatures.

dee44ce0b0ec.title: Byzantine fault
dee44ce0b0ec.sentence: Digital signatures can provide Byzantine fault tolerance in the presence of an arbitrary number of traitorous generals provided that n > F+1 (the problem becomes vacuous otherwise).

4eada722dc3b.title: Byzantine fault
4eada722dc3b.sentence: In particular, one Commander and two Lieutenants can reach consensus in the presence of a single traitor since the traitor cannot impersonate others.

dc1bf9ed1d6a.title: Byzantine fault
dc1bf9ed1d6a.sentence: Byzantine fault tolerance is only concerned with broadcast consistency, that is, the property that when a component broadcasts a value to all the other components, they all receive exactly this same value, or in the case that the broadcaster is not consistent, the other components agree on a common value themselves.

4374a34e1f1b.title: Byzantine fault
4374a34e1f1b.sentence: This kind of fault tolerance does not encompass the correctness of the value itself; for example, an adversarial component that deliberately sends an incorrect value, but sends that same value consistently to all components, will not be caught in the Byzantine fault tolerance scheme.

e73ce4751008.title: Byzantine fault
e73ce4751008.section: Applications > Artificial Intelligence > Applications and examples
e73ce4751008.sentence: Different blockchains use various BFT-based consensus mechanisms like Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT), Tendermint, Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS), and Avalanche consensus to handle Byzantine faults.

62c7f7eea4d8.title: Byzantine fault
62c7f7eea4d8.section: Applications > Artificial Intelligence > Applications and examples
62c7f7eea4d8.sentence: While traditional blockchains like Bitcoin use proof of work (PoW), which is susceptible to a 51% attack, BFT-based systems are designed to tolerate up to one-third of faulty or malicious nodes without compromising the network's integrity.

911ca096eacf.title: Byzantine fault
911ca096eacf.sentence: The Bitcoin network works in parallel to generate a blockchain with proof of work allowing the system to overcome Byzantine failures and reach a coherent global view of the system's state.

f90d72f44e21.title: Byzantine fault
f90d72f44e21.sentence: Some aircraft systems, such as the Boeing 777 Aircraft Information Management System (via its ARINC 659 SAFEbus network), the Boeing 777 flight control system, and the Boeing 787 flight control systems, use Byzantine fault tolerance; because these are real-time systems, their Byzantine fault tolerance solutions must have very low latency.

98eb721f2b09.title: Byzantine fault
98eb721f2b09.sentence: For example, SAFEbus can achieve Byzantine fault tolerance within the order of a microsecond of added latency.

95df0c82de4b.title: Byzantine fault
95df0c82de4b.sentence: This formulation of the problem, together with some additional results, were presented by the same authors in their 1982 paper, "The Byzantine Generals Problem".

d14f0353ca42.title: Raft (algorithm)
d14f0353ca42.sentence: Raft is a consensus algorithm designed as an alternative to the Paxos family of algorithms.

1c615c997a74.title: Raft (algorithm)
1c615c997a74.sentence: It was meant to be more understandable than Paxos by means of separation of logic, but it is also formally proven safe and offers some additional features.

31c35d1d9112.title: Raft (algorithm)
31c35d1d9112.sentence: Raft achieves consensus via an elected leader.

7788224ac59c.title: Raft (algorithm)
7788224ac59c.sentence: A server in a raft cluster is either a leader or a follower, and can be a candidate in the precise case of an election (leader unavailable).

0e8a482ac37d.title: Raft (algorithm)
0e8a482ac37d.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft
0e8a482ac37d.sentence: The cluster has one and only one elected leader which is fully responsible for managing log replication on the other servers of the cluster.

e8bc22b8e1cd.title: Raft (algorithm)
e8bc22b8e1cd.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft
e8bc22b8e1cd.sentence: It means that the leader can decide on new entries' placement and establishment of data flow between it and the other servers without consulting other servers.

d7152bc19067.title: Raft (algorithm)
d7152bc19067.section: Basics > Safety > Safety rules in Raft
d7152bc19067.sentence: - Election safety: at most one leader can be elected in a given term.

19c644a71fc2.title: Raft (algorithm)
19c644a71fc2.section: Basics > Safety > Safety rules in Raft
19c644a71fc2.sentence: - Leader append-only: a leader can only append new entries to its logs (it can neither overwrite nor delete entries).

4d2d8aefceb8.title: Raft (algorithm)
4d2d8aefceb8.section: Basics > Safety > Safety rules in Raft
4d2d8aefceb8.sentence: - Log matching: if two logs contain an entry with the same index and term, then the logs are identical in all entries up through the given index.

bdfc5148765a.title: Raft (algorithm)
bdfc5148765a.section: Basics > Safety > Safety rules in Raft
bdfc5148765a.sentence: - Leader completeness: if a log entry is committed in a given term then it will be present in the logs of the leaders since this term.

7420078f6b7b.title: Raft (algorithm)
7420078f6b7b.section: Basics > Safety > Safety rules in Raft
7420078f6b7b.sentence: - State machine safety: if a server has applied a particular log entry to its state machine, then no other server may apply a different command for the same log.

d4a933a34f34.title: Raft (algorithm)
d4a933a34f34.sentence: Stability is ensured by respecting the timing requirement of the algorithm:

acb063279d5f.title: Raft (algorithm)
acb063279d5f.sentence: - broadcastTime is the average time it takes a server to send a request to every server in the cluster and receive responses.

f05525de1946.title: Raft (algorithm)
f05525de1946.sentence: - MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) is the average time between failures for a server.

288f257ea232.title: Raft (algorithm)
288f257ea232.sentence: To address cluster membership change issues that can arise in Raft, the algorithm introduces joint consensus, a transitional configuration phase.

9eff435f3a83.title: Raft (algorithm)
9eff435f3a83.sentence: An extension to Raft is log compaction, where each server takes snapshots of its committed entries and saves it to stable storage, along with the index of its last entry and the term in the snapshotted log.

55ac007be933.title: Raft (algorithm)
55ac007be933.sentence: The leader occasionally sends its snapshots to servers that are lagging behind in its log.

5c1ad2db5d60.title: Raft (algorithm)
5c1ad2db5d60.sentence: Raft is not Byzantine fault tolerant in the base form; the nodes trust the elected leader, and the algorithm assumes all participants are trustworthy, yielding only crash fault tolerance.

a4cd0e25cae6.title: Raft (algorithm)
a4cd0e25cae6.sentence: This means that Raft is not a Byzantine fault tolerant algorithm.

ad9002ebab2f.title: Raft (algorithm)
ad9002ebab2f.sentence: Raft uses a single leader model, where client requests, reads and writes, and log replications goes through a single leader.

015b9ecd2f92.title: Raft (algorithm)
015b9ecd2f92.sentence: This means that there is a single point of failure and a bottleneck in performance.

4f0bf71bbf41.title: Raft (algorithm)
4f0bf71bbf41.sentence: Furthermore, it does not scale with increasing server workload.

d4809773f550.title: Raft (algorithm)
d4809773f550.sentence: - Etcd uses Raft to manage a highly-available replicated log

40b10636c280.title: Raft (algorithm)
40b10636c280.sentence: - CockroachDB uses Raft in the Replication Layer.

49b25ccbe1f7.title: Raft (algorithm)
49b25ccbe1f7.sentence: - MongoDB uses a variant of Raft in the replication set.

17406611084d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
17406611084d.section: System Architecture Patterns for Distributed Consensus
17406611084d.sentence: Distributed consensus algorithms are low-level and primitive: they simply allow a set of nodes to agree on a value, once.

7fdcc6826bf3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
7fdcc6826bf3.section: System Architecture Patterns for Distributed Consensus
7fdcc6826bf3.sentence: What makes distributed consensus useful is the addition of higher-level system components such as datastores, configuration stores, queues, locking, and leader election services to provide the practical system functionality that distributed consensus algorithms donât address.

11426432705c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
11426432705c.section: System Architecture Patterns for Distributed Consensus
11426432705c.sentence: Using higher-level components reduces complexity for system designers.

78b24efec6a2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
78b24efec6a2.section: System Architecture Patterns for Distributed Consensus
78b24efec6a2.sentence: It also allows underlying distributed consensus algorithms to be changed if necessary in response to changes in the environment in which the system runs or changes in nonfunctional requirements.

6364260417c6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
6364260417c6.section: System Architecture Patterns for Distributed Consensus
6364260417c6.sentence: The Chubby service fills a similar niche at Google.

45ca4977a3f2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
45ca4977a3f2.section: Reliable Replicated Datastores and Configuration Stores
45ca4977a3f2.sentence: Reliable replicated datastores are an application of replicated state machines.

c32c7aaf2f3f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
c32c7aaf2f3f.section: Reliable Replicated Datastores and Configuration Stores
c32c7aaf2f3f.sentence: Replicated datastores use consensus algorithms in the critical path of their work.

010d116a33cb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
010d116a33cb.section: Reliable Replicated Datastores and Configuration Stores
010d116a33cb.sentence: Thus, performance, throughput, and the ability to scale are very important in this type of design.

8807ab91bcf3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
8807ab91bcf3.section: Reliable Replicated Datastores and Configuration Stores
8807ab91bcf3.sentence: As with datastores built with other underlying technologies, consensus-based datastores can provide a variety of consistency semantics for read operations, which make a huge difference to how the datastore scales.

7c63e8ee8133.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
7c63e8ee8133.section: Highly Available Processing Using Leader Election
7c63e8ee8133.sentence: In this type of component, unlike the replicated datastore, the consensus algorithm is not in the critical path of the main work the system is doing, so throughput is usually not a major concern.

7c4b4c65ec76.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
7c4b4c65ec76.sentence: A barrier in a distributed computation is a primitive that blocks a group of processes from proceeding until some condition is met (for example, until all parts of one phase of a computation are completed).

922590964927.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
922590964927.sentence: Use of a barrier effectively splits a distributed computation into logical phases.

ee654c2243f9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
ee654c2243f9.sentence: For instance, as shown in Figure 23-4, a barrier could be used in implementing the MapReduce [Dea04] model to ensure that the entire Map phase is completed before the Reduce part of the computation proceeds.

d95138255d7d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
d95138255d7d.sentence: The barrier could be implemented by a single coordinator process, but this implementation adds a single point of failure that is usually unacceptable.

488c793eea84.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
488c793eea84.sentence: The barrier can also be implemented as an RSM.

cbdfee25cb6a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
cbdfee25cb6a.sentence: For that purpose, a lease system (discussed earlier in regard to locks) is recommended instead of an outright removal from the queue.

07a241bf47e7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
07a241bf47e7.sentence: The downside of queuing-based systems is that loss of the queue prevents the entire system from operating.

2b9c00001d53.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2b9c00001d53.sentence: Implementing the queue as an RSM can minimize the risk, and make the entire system far more robust.

f828332e7a33.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
f828332e7a33.sentence: Queuing and messaging systems often need excellent throughput, but donât need extremely low latency (due to seldom being directly user-facing).

e9e23ba09b2f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e9e23ba09b2f.sentence: Atomic broadcast is a distributed systems primitive in which messages are received reliably and in the same order by all participants.

a1170c0c6e61.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
a1170c0c6e61.sentence: This is an incredibly powerful distributed systems concept and very useful in designing practical systems.

55c9bea0fbb1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
55c9bea0fbb1.sentence: A huge number of publish-subscribe messaging infrastructures exist for the use of system designers, although not all of them provide atomic guarantees.

e4efa70756e5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e4efa70756e5.sentence: The most critical decisions system designers must make when deploying a consensus-based system concern the number of replicas to be deployed and the location of those replicas.

5c2ead85a625.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
5c2ead85a625.sentence: For non-Byzantine failures, the minimum number of replicas that can be deployed is threeâif two are deployed, then there is no tolerance for failure of any process.

e7068cd0b971.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e7068cd0b971.sentence: Three replicas may tolerate one failure.

65286ccaf29a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
65286ccaf29a.sentence: Most system downtime is a result of planned maintenance [Ken12]: three replicas allow a system to operate normally when one replica is down for maintenance (assuming that the remaining two replicas can handle system load at an acceptable performance).

982a7e27a894.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
982a7e27a894.sentence: If an unplanned failure occurs during a maintenance window, then the consensus system becomes unavailable.

94c335cb153d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
94c335cb153d.sentence: Unavailability of the consensus system is usually unacceptable, and so five replicas should be run, allowing the system to operate with up to two failures.

26b00a9f7a28.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
26b00a9f7a28.sentence: A typical deployment for Zookeeper or Chubby uses five replicas, so a majority quorum requires three replicas.

4aed5a51fe00.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
4aed5a51fe00.sentence: The system will still make progress if two replicas, or 40%, are unavailable.

d81c640cb558.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
d81c640cb558.sentence: With six replicas, a quorum requires four replicas: only 33% of the replicas can be unavailable if the system is to remain live.

e239a9331190.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e239a9331190.sentence: It should be noted that adding a replica in a majority quorum system can potentially decrease system availability somewhat (as shown in Figure 23-10).

baddc25be03e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
baddc25be03e.sentence: If a consensus system loses so many of its replicas that it cannot form a quorum, then that system is, in theory, in an unrecoverable state because the durable logs of at least one of the missing replicas cannot be accessed.

8f5a6916ac1e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
8f5a6916ac1e.sentence: If no quorum remains, itâs possible that a decision that was seen only by the missing replicas was made.

d007fc56d920.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
d007fc56d920.sentence: Administrators may be able to force a change in the group membership and add new replicas that catch up from the existing one in order to proceed, but the possibility of data loss always remainsâa situation that should be avoided if at all possible.

be1b6f618b15.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
be1b6f618b15.sentence: In order to maintain robustness of the system, it is important that these replicas do catch up.

af1a096c9614.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
af1a096c9614.sentence: There is a relationship between performance and the number of replicas in a system that do not need to form part of a quorum: a minority of slower replicas may lag behind, allowing the quorum of better-performing replicas to run faster (as long as the leader performs well).

4eac44c670b7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
4eac44c670b7.sentence: If replica performance varies significantly, then every failure may reduce the performance of the system overall because slow outliers will be required to form a quorum.

e6812f3029a9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e6812f3029a9.sentence: The more failures or lagging replicas a system can tolerate, the better the systemâs performance overall is likely to be.

25e671a77fae.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
25e671a77fae.sentence: The issue of cost should also be considered in managing replicas: each replica uses costly computing resources.

bdd723b51a54.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
bdd723b51a54.sentence: As the number of shards grows, so does the cost of each additional replica, because a number of processes equal to the number of shards must be added to the system.

2f9ee21973c3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2f9ee21973c3.sentence: The decision about the number of replicas for any system is thus a trade-off between the following factors:

92cb9af16a61.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
92cb9af16a61.sentence: In the case of sharded deployments, you can adjust capacity by adjusting the number of shards.

d11cbb7a4d5a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
d11cbb7a4d5a.sentence: However, for systems that can read from consensus group members that are not the leader, you can increase read capacity by adding more replicas.

8b73380ae4bb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
8b73380ae4bb.sentence: Adding more replicas has a cost: in an algorithm that uses a strong leader, adding replicas imposes more load on the leader process, while in a peer-to-peer protocol, adding replicas imposes more load on all processes.

1f792b2ee8d7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
1f792b2ee8d7.sentence: However, if there is ample capacity for write operations, but a read-heavy workload is stressing the system, adding replicas may be the best approach.

c78a67826275.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
c78a67826275.sentence: Decisions about where to deploy the processes that comprise a consensus cluster are made based upon two factors: a trade-off between the failure domains that the system should handle, and the latency requirements for the system.

9963054c287c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
9963054c287c.sentence: A failure domain is the set of components of a system that can become unavailable as a result of a single failure.

7150c7747daf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
7150c7747daf.sentence: Example failure domains include the following:

a232e74bf259.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
a232e74bf259.sentence: In general, as the distance between replicas increases, so does the round-trip time between replicas, as well as the size of the failure the system will be able to tolerate.

ec2de491de74.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
ec2de491de74.sentence: For most consensus systems, increasing the round-trip time between replicas will also increase the latency of operations.

fd4f10267c73.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
fd4f10267c73.sentence: It doesnât always make sense to continually increase the size of the failure domain whose loss the system can withstand.

baeb49b201a0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
baeb49b201a0.sentence: Probably not, because the systemâs clients will be down as well so the system will see no traffic.

9ca4d2561d56.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
9ca4d2561d56.sentence: The extra cost in terms of latency, throughput, and computing resources would give no benefit.

b499b6e9e76c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
b499b6e9e76c.sentence: However, when critical data is at stake, itâs important to back up regular snapshots elsewhere, even in the case of solid consensusâbased systems that are deployed in several diverse failure domains.

74db92db12a6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
74db92db12a6.sentence: There are two failure domains that you can never escape: the software itself, and human error on the part of the systemâs administrators.

2e38afa6ee13.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2e38afa6ee13.sentence: When making decisions about location of replicas, remember that the most important measure of performance is client perception: ideally, the network round-trip time from the clients to the consensus systemâs replicas should be minimized.

cf1a16162065.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
cf1a16162065.sentence: If clients are dense in a particular geographic region, it is best to locate replicas close to clients.

962b0b683cb9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
962b0b683cb9.sentence: Over a wide area network, leaderless protocols like Mencius or Egalitarian Paxos may have a performance edge, particularly if the consistency constraints of the application mean that it is possible to execute read-only operations on any system replica without performing a consensus operation.

05de3c7ac773.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
05de3c7ac773.sentence: Considerations regarding failure domains therefore apply even more strongly when a sixth replica is added: if an organization has five datacenters, and generally runs consensus groups with five processes, one in each datacenter, then loss of one datacenter still leaves one spare replica in each group.

a36295719df3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
a36295719df3.sentence: If a sixth replica is deployed in one of the five datacenters, then an outage in that datacenter removes both of the spare replicas in the group, thereby reducing capacity by 33%.

ecf14f0930ab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
ecf14f0930ab.sentence: Colocating multiple replicas in a single datacenter may reduce system availability: here, there is a quorum without any redundancy remaining.

392b6cb77a0f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
392b6cb77a0f.section: Capacity and Load Balancing > Quorum composition
392b6cb77a0f.sentence: This scenario is a key weakness of the simple majority quorum when applied to groups composed of replicas with very different RTTs between members.

716a9ab9ff29.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
716a9ab9ff29.section: Capacity and Load Balancing > Quorum composition
716a9ab9ff29.sentence: The east coast replica acts as a linchpin of sorts, where two possible quorums overlap.

ccb083d101a7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
ccb083d101a7.section: Capacity and Load Balancing > Quorum composition
ccb083d101a7.sentence: As shown in Figure 23-14, loss of this replica means that system latency is likely to change drastically: instead of being largely influenced by either central US to east coast RTT or EU to east coast RTT, latency will be based on EU to central RTT, which is around 50% higher than EU to east coast RTT.

b06c1858853e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
b06c1858853e.section: Capacity and Load Balancing > Quorum composition
b06c1858853e.sentence: As diagrammed in Figure 23-15, nine replicas may be deployed in three groups of three.

1176d6d62c4e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
1176d6d62c4e.section: Capacity and Load Balancing > Quorum composition
1176d6d62c4e.sentence: A quorum may be formed by a majority of groups, and a group may be included in the quorum if a majority of the groupâs members are available.

e9df0f33ed9a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e9df0f33ed9a.sentence: However, itâs important to understand that the leader replicas will use more computational resources, particularly outgoing network capacity.

c9b35a75d7d7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
c9b35a75d7d7.sentence: This is because the leader sends proposal messages that include the proposed data, but replicas send smaller messages, usually just containing agreement with a particular consensus transaction ID.

e06d4693d7c6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e06d4693d7c6.sentence: Organizations that run highly sharded consensus systems with a very large number of processes may find it necessary to ensure that leader processes for the different shards are balanced relatively evenly across different datacenters.

6c456a9fada3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
6c456a9fada3.sentence: Another downside of deploying consensus groups in multiple datacenters (shown by Figure 23-11) is the very extreme change in the system that can occur if the datacenter hosting the leaders suffers a widespread failure (power, networking equipment failure, or fiber cut, for instance).

639aabd3840f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
639aabd3840f.sentence: As shown in Figure 23-11, if a system simply routes client read requests to the nearest replica, then a large spike in load concentrated in one region may overwhelm the nearest replica, and then the next-closest replica, and so onâthis is cascading failure (see Addressing Cascading Failures).

978e6aca9b7c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
978e6aca9b7c.sentence: This type of overload can often happen as a result of batch jobs beginning, especially if several begin at the same time.

03e5912154e2.title: Paxos (computer science)
03e5912154e2.sentence: This protocol is the most basic of the Paxos family.

dc3b03b3a770.title: Paxos (computer science)
dc3b03b3a770.sentence: Each "instance" (or "execution") of the basic Paxos protocol decides on a single output value.

43afe3c8656e.title: Paxos (computer science)
43afe3c8656e.sentence: The protocol proceeds over several rounds.

eee5b2c449b5.title: Paxos (computer science)
eee5b2c449b5.sentence: A successful round has 2 phases: phase 1 (which is divided into parts a and b) and phase 2 (also divided into parts a and b).

f4b332699acc.title: Paxos (computer science)
f4b332699acc.sentence: The message is identified with a unique number, n, which must be greater than any number previously used in a Prepare message by this Proposer.

21cf3999c405.title: Paxos (computer science)
21cf3999c405.sentence: The Proposer chooses at least a Quorum of Acceptors and sends the Prepare message containing n to them.

1a21ffa34fdf.title: Paxos (computer science)
1a21ffa34fdf.sentence: Note that n is not the value to be proposed; it is simply a unique identifier of this initial message by the Proposer.

c43cc8952dec.title: Paxos (computer science)
c43cc8952dec.sentence: - If n is higher than every previous proposal number received by the Acceptor (from any Proposer), then the Acceptor must return a message (called a Promise) to the Proposer, indicating that the Acceptor will ignore all future proposals numbered less than or equal to n.

6baba20474b1.title: Paxos (computer science)
6baba20474b1.sentence: The Promise must include the highest number among the Proposals that the Acceptor previously accepted, along with the corresponding accepted value.

69e5a77d54ba.title: Paxos (computer science)
69e5a77d54ba.sentence: If a Proposer receives Promises from a Quorum of Acceptors, it needs to set a value v to its proposal.

209390d5fc44.title: Paxos (computer science)
209390d5fc44.sentence: If any Acceptors had previously accepted any proposal, then they'll have sent their values to the Proposer, who now must set the value of its proposal, v, to the value associated with the highest proposal number reported by the Acceptors, let's call it z.

775d90dbac5a.title: Paxos (computer science)
775d90dbac5a.sentence: If none of the Acceptors had accepted a proposal up to this point, then the Proposer may choose the value it originally wanted to propose, say x.

a26b2f866ebc.title: Paxos (computer science)
a26b2f866ebc.sentence: The Proposer sends an Accept message, (n, v), to a Quorum of Acceptors with the chosen value for its proposal, v, and the proposal number n (which is the same as the number contained in the Prepare message previously sent to the Acceptors).

45b6099ce2d7.title: Paxos (computer science)
45b6099ce2d7.sentence: If an Acceptor receives an Accept message, (n, v), from a Proposer, it must accept it if and only if it has not already promised (in Phase 1b of the Paxos protocol) to only consider proposals having an identifier greater than n.

e0c1416c5602.title: Paxos (computer science)
e0c1416c5602.sentence: If the Acceptor has not already promised (in Phase 1b) to only consider proposals having an identifier greater than n, it should register the value v (of the just received Accept message) as the accepted value (of the Protocol), and send an Accepted message to the Proposer and every Learner (which can typically be the Proposers themselves).

46d146d10927.title: Paxos (computer science)
46d146d10927.sentence: Learners will learn the decided value only after receiving Accepted messages from a majority of acceptors, i.e. not after receiving just the first Accept message.

8f5275b77a3e.title: Paxos (computer science)
8f5275b77a3e.sentence: Note that consensus is achieved when a majority of Acceptors accept the same identifier number (rather than the same value).

897f2b36897d.title: Paxos (computer science)
897f2b36897d.sentence: Because each identifier is unique to a Proposer and only one value may be proposed per identifier, all Acceptors that accept the same identifier thereby accept the same value.

fc039662fa1a.title: Paxos (computer science)
fc039662fa1a.sentence: However, the Paxos protocol guarantees that consensus is permanent and the chosen value is immutable.

dbd087ae28f9.title: Paxos (computer science)
dbd087ae28f9.sentence: Rounds fail when multiple Proposers send conflicting Prepare messages, or when the Proposer does not receive a Quorum of responses (Promise or Accepted).

cdef123ff606.title: Paxos (computer science)
cdef123ff606.sentence: In these cases, another round must be started with a higher proposal number.

eae50158db3f.title: Paxos (computer science)
eae50158db3f.section: Basic Paxos > Graphic representation of the flow of messages in the basic Paxos > Error cases in basic Paxos
eae50158db3f.sentence: The simplest error cases are the failure of an Acceptor (when a Quorum of Acceptors remains alive) and failure of a redundant Learner.

ad3ffc3140a7.title: Paxos (computer science)
ad3ffc3140a7.section: Basic Paxos > Graphic representation of the flow of messages in the basic Paxos > Error cases in basic Paxos
ad3ffc3140a7.sentence: In these cases, the protocol requires no "recovery" (i.e. it still succeeds): no additional rounds or messages are required, as shown below (in the next two diagrams/cases).

3827c3e4182a.title: Paxos (computer science)
3827c3e4182a.section: Basic Paxos > Paxos can be used to select a leader
3827c3e4182a.sentence: Notice that a Proposer in Paxos could propose "I am the leader" (or, for example, "Proposer X is the leader").

a340e9601eb2.title: Paxos (computer science)
a340e9601eb2.section: Basic Paxos > Paxos can be used to select a leader
a340e9601eb2.sentence: Because of the agreement and validity guarantees of Paxos, if accepted by a Quorum, then the Proposer is now known to be the leader to all other nodes.

52abb67cce89.title: Paxos (computer science)
52abb67cce89.section: Multi-Paxos > Graphic representation of the flow of messages in the Multi-Paxos > Multi-Paxos without failures
52abb67cce89.sentence: Note that a Multi-Paxos consists of several instances of the basic Paxos protocol.

d2a47c7e88ed.title: Paxos (computer science)
d2a47c7e88ed.sentence: If the leader is relatively stable, phase 1 becomes unnecessary.

9fc11efbf3c3.title: Paxos (computer science)
9fc11efbf3c3.sentence: If each command is the result of a single instance of the Basic Paxos protocol, a significant amount of overhead would result.

278c86957258.title: Paxos (computer science)
278c86957258.sentence: > In Paxos, clients send commands to a leader.

4efb1cfb90f8.title: Paxos (computer science)
4efb1cfb90f8.sentence: During normal operation, the leader receives a client's command, assigns it a new command number i, and then begins the ith instance of the consensus algorithm by sending messages to a set of acceptor processes.

86328f2b15fc.title: Paxos (computer science)
86328f2b15fc.sentence: Thus, it is possible to skip phase 1 for future instances of the protocol with the same leader.

acc82c229250.title: Paxos (computer science)
acc82c229250.sentence: To achieve this, the round number I is included along with each value which is incremented in each round by the same Leader.

4ea3562c23ae.title: Paxos (computer science)
4ea3562c23ae.section: Multi-Paxos > Graphic representation of the flow of messages in the Multi-Paxos > Multi-Paxos when phase 1 can be skipped
4ea3562c23ae.sentence: Note that the Leader should be stable, i.e. it should not crash or change.

a9d37aae4cda.title: Paxos (computer science)
a9d37aae4cda.sentence: Multi-Paxos reduces the failure-free message delay (proposal to learning) from 4 delays to 2 delays.

da89eb34758d.title: Paxos (computer science)
da89eb34758d.section: Multi-Paxos > Graphic representation of the flow of messages in the Multi-Paxos > Multi-Paxos when roles are collapsed
da89eb34758d.sentence: A common deployment of the Multi-Paxos consists in collapsing the role of the Proposers, Acceptors and Learners to "Servers".

e2ece8c24a50.title: Paxos (computer science)
e2ece8c24a50.section: Multi-Paxos > Graphic representation of the flow of messages in the Multi-Paxos > Multi-Paxos when roles are collapsed
e2ece8c24a50.sentence: So, in the end, there are only "Clients" and "Servers".

a7abffca1d05.title: Consensus (computer science)
a7abffca1d05.section: Models of computation > Permissioned versus permissionless consensus
a7abffca1d05.sentence: Consensus algorithms traditionally assume that the set of participating nodes is fixed and given at the outset: that is, that some prior (manual or automatic) configuration process has permissioned a particular known group of participants who can authenticate each other as members of the group.

0a3e2e1b3e04.title: Consensus (computer science)
0a3e2e1b3e04.section: Models of computation > Permissioned versus permissionless consensus
0a3e2e1b3e04.sentence: A permissionless consensus protocol, in contrast, allows anyone in the network to join dynamically and participate without prior permission, but instead imposes a different form of artificial cost or barrier to entry to mitigate the Sybil attack threat.

8ce3e8cced31.title: Consensus (computer science)
8ce3e8cced31.section: Models of computation > Permissioned versus permissionless consensus
8ce3e8cced31.sentence: In the absence of such a well-defined, closed group with authenticated members, a Sybil attack against an open consensus group can defeat even a Byzantine consensus algorithm, simply by creating enough virtual participants to overwhelm the fault tolerance threshold.

fc676a8d7f6c.title: Consensus (computer science)
fc676a8d7f6c.section: Models of computation > Permissioned versus permissionless consensus
fc676a8d7f6c.sentence: Bitcoin introduced the first permissionless consensus protocol using proof of work and a difficulty adjustment function, in which participants compete to solve cryptographic hash puzzles, and probabilistically earn the right to commit blocks and earn associated rewards in proportion to their invested computational effort.

96fcbfcabea1.title: Consensus (computer science)
96fcbfcabea1.section: Models of computation > Permissioned versus permissionless consensus
96fcbfcabea1.sentence: Motivated in part by the high energy cost of this approach, subsequent permissionless consensus protocols have proposed or adopted other alternative participation rules for Sybil attack protection, such as proof of stake, proof of space, and proof of authority.

f31e929ff885.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
f31e929ff885.sentence: The number of members running in each consensus group, and the status of each process (healthy or not healthy)

b07f140e4a11.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
b07f140e4a11.sentence: A system based on an algorithm such as Multi-Paxos that uses a leader role must be monitored to ensure that a leader exists, because if the system has no leader, it is totally unavailable.

dcf29aa1e5fb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
dcf29aa1e5fb.sentence: Most consensus algorithms use an increasing consensus transaction number to indicate progress.

9f368a513a90.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
9f368a513a90.sentence: A process may be running but unable to make progress for some (e.g., hardware-related) reason.

0dfa601d3a97.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
0dfa601d3a97.sentence: A group member may be recovering state from peers after startup, or lagging behind the quorum in the group, or it may be up-to-date and participating fully, and it may be the leader.

7a1d95e58201.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
7a1d95e58201.sentence: Rapid changes of leadership impair performance of consensus systems that use a stable leader, so the number of leader changes should be monitored.

63c1bb6982bc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
63c1bb6982bc.sentence: Consensus algorithms usually mark a leadership change with a new term or view number, so this number provides a useful metric to monitor.

a9abe5170ea4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
a9abe5170ea4.sentence: Too rapid of an increase in leader changes signals that the leader is flapping, perhaps due to network connectivity issues.

954d34262adf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
954d34262adf.sentence: A decrease in the view number could signal a serious bug.

73202449b889.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
73202449b889.sentence: This number should be seen to be increasing over time if a system is healthy.
