efc1fd379015.sentence: Number of proposals seen; number of proposals agreed upon

2e561e5903f6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2e561e5903f6.sentence: - The amount of time acceptors spend on durable logging

268323a20cda.title: Paxos (computer science)
268323a20cda.sentence: Cheap Paxos extends Basic Paxos to tolerate F failures with F+1 main processors and F auxiliary processors by dynamically reconfiguring after each failure.

c8d693128342.title: Paxos (computer science)
c8d693128342.sentence: During stable periods, the auxiliary processors take no part in the protocol.

ed6310953110.title: Paxos (computer science)
ed6310953110.sentence: The third processor can therefore be a small/slow/cheap one, or a processor primarily devoted to other tasks."

a2a5f935581a.title: Paxos (computer science)
a2a5f935581a.sentence: This reduction in processor requirements comes at the expense of liveness; if too many main processors fail in a short time, the system must halt until the auxiliary processors can reconfigure the system.

274648664bd0.title: Paxos (computer science)
274648664bd0.sentence: > "With only two processors p and q, one processor cannot distinguish failure of the other processor from failure of the communication medium.

2a05dbf27c9c.title: Paxos (computer science)
2a05dbf27c9c.sentence: Fast Paxos generalizes Basic Paxos to reduce end-to-end message delays.

fcf452f70cca.title: Paxos (computer science)
fcf452f70cca.sentence: In Basic Paxos, the message delay from client request to learning is 3 message delays.

e298cf7faad6.title: Paxos (computer science)
e298cf7faad6.sentence: Fast Paxos allows 2 message delays, but requires that (1) the system be composed of 3f+ 1 acceptors to tolerate up to f faults (instead of the classic 2f+1), and (2) the Client to send its request to multiple destinations.

ff53ffc8758b.title: Paxos (computer science)
ff53ffc8758b.sentence: If the leader detects a collision, it resolves the collision by sending Accept! messages for a new round which are Accepted as usual.

c69966d1f57d.title: Paxos (computer science)
c69966d1f57d.sentence: This coordinated recovery technique requires four message delays from Client to Learner.

e1010e5299cb.title: Paxos (computer science)
e1010e5299cb.sentence: The final optimization occurs when the leader specifies a recovery technique in advance, allowing the Acceptors to perform the collision recovery themselves.

13b9d1dc71c5.title: Paxos (computer science)
13b9d1dc71c5.sentence: Thus, uncoordinated collision recovery can occur in three message delays (and only two message delays if all Learners are also Acceptors).

54fb3a62312e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
54fb3a62312e.sentence: Conventional wisdom has generally held that consensus algorithms are too slow and costly to use for many systems that require high throughput and low latency [Bol11].

771530405e6c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
771530405e6c.sentence: This conception is simply not trueâwhile implementations can be slow, there are a number of tricks that can improve performance.

88b7febbf674.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
88b7febbf674.sentence: There is no one "best" distributed consensus and state machine replication algorithm for performance, because performance is dependent on a number of factors relating to workload, the systemâs performance objectives, and how the system is to be deployed.113 While some of the following sections present research, with the aim of increasing understanding of what is possible to achieve with distributed consensus, many of the systems described are available and are in use now.

599ae8e9ac19.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
599ae8e9ac19.sentence: In the case of a consensus system, workload may vary in terms of:

fb580887534f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
fb580887534f.sentence: - Throughput: the number of proposals being made per unit of time at peak load

158d2f1eeeb6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
158d2f1eeeb6.sentence: - The type of requests: proportion of operations that change state

38d9d77f11fd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
38d9d77f11fd.sentence: - The consistency semantics required for read operations

6f8b7822e13f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
6f8b7822e13f.sentence: - Request sizes, if size of data payload can vary

ced4a2f7e099.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
ced4a2f7e099.sentence: - Does the system use sharding, pipelining, and batching?

acd3158bdbab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
acd3158bdbab.section: Distributed Consensus Performance and Network Latency
acd3158bdbab.sentence: Consensus systems face two major physical constraints on performance when committing state changes.

d77d5eda1f0e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
d77d5eda1f0e.section: Distributed Consensus Performance and Network Latency
d77d5eda1f0e.sentence: One is network round-trip time and the other is time it takes to write data to persistent storage, which will be examined later.

86d6c9d1fda2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
86d6c9d1fda2.section: Distributed Consensus Performance and Network Latency
86d6c9d1fda2.sentence: Within a single datacenter, round-trip times between machines should be on the order of a millisecond.

af10ba2dfe0d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
af10ba2dfe0d.section: Distributed Consensus Performance and Network Latency
af10ba2dfe0d.sentence: A typical round-trip-time (RTT) within the United States is 45 milliseconds, and from New York to London is 70 milliseconds.

fd208baaffbc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
fd208baaffbc.sentence: We have seen how Multi-Paxos elects a stable leader to improve performance.

29542fac2709.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
29542fac2709.sentence: Zab [Jun11] and Raft [Ong14] are also examples of protocols that elect a stable leader for performance reasons.

210926c06622.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
210926c06622.sentence: The Multi-Paxos protocol uses a strong leader process: unless a leader has not yet been elected or some failure occurs, it requires only one round trip from the proposer to a quorum of acceptors to reach consensus.

e65dff1a5744.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e65dff1a5744.sentence: - All operations that change state must be sent via the leader, a requirement that adds network latency for clients that are not located near the leader.

0171c1212f29.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
0171c1212f29.sentence: - The leader processâs outgoing network bandwidth is a system bottleneck [Mao08], because the leaderâs Accept message contains all of the data related to any proposal, whereas other messages contain only acknowledgments of a numbered transaction with no data payload.

aa93b3709318.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
aa93b3709318.sentence: - If the leader happens to be on a machine with performance problems, then the throughput of the entire system will be reduced.

8edfeeb65ff5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
8edfeeb65ff5.sentence: Fast Paxos [Lam06] is a version of the Paxos algorithm designed to improve its performance over wide area networks.

a01d24499b32.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
a01d24499b32.sentence: Using Fast Paxos, each client can send Propose messages directly to each member of a group of acceptors, instead of through a leader, as in Classic Paxos or Multi-Paxos.

04c793bd26be.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
04c793bd26be.sentence: However, thatâs not true: if the client in the Fast Paxos system has a high RTT (round-trip time) to the acceptors, and the acceptors have fast connections to each other, we have substituted N parallel messages across the slower network links (in Fast Paxos) for one message across the slower link plus N parallel messages across the faster links (Classic Paxos).

f373904d521e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
f373904d521e.sentence: Having clients act as proposers also makes it much more difficult to batch proposals.

8b4a57a98068.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
8b4a57a98068.sentence: Another possible optimization is batching multiple client operations together into one operation at the proposer ([Ana13], [Bol11], [Cha07], [Jun11], [Mao08], [Mor12a]).

0e096678d3c3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
0e096678d3c3.sentence: This amortizes the fixed costs of the disk logging and network latency over the larger number of operations, increasing throughput.

8f3b3d5bff8e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
8f3b3d5bff8e.sentence: The inefficiencies presented by idle replicas can be solved by pipelining, which allows multiple proposals to be in-flight at once.

30593d49ce13.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
30593d49ce13.sentence: Pipelining is normally used in combination with batching.

1d7195275690.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
1d7195275690.sentence: The batches of requests in the pipeline are still globally ordered with a view number and a transaction number, so this method does not violate the global ordering properties required to run a replicated state machine.

2d88add7aeee.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2d88add7aeee.sentence: Logging to persistent storage is required so that a node, having crashed and returned to the cluster, honors whatever previous commitments it made regarding ongoing consensus transactions.

5ddf96cde610.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
5ddf96cde610.sentence: In the Paxos protocol, for instance, acceptors cannot agree to a proposal when they have already agreed to a proposal with a higher sequence number.

e51d1ba80b64.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
e51d1ba80b64.sentence: The time required to write an entry to a log on disk varies greatly depending on what hardware or virtualized environment is used, but is likely to take between one and several milliseconds.

11dad5013c6f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
11dad5013c6f.sentence: If latency for performing a small random write to disk is on the order of 10 milliseconds, the rate of consensus operations will be limited to approximately 100 per second.

2376a88ac1d7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
2376a88ac1d7.sentence: Replicated datastores have the advantage that the data is available in multiple places, meaning that if strong consistency is not required for all reads, data could be read from any replica.

5f902bfe1ecb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
5f902bfe1ecb.sentence: Photon uses an atomic compare-and-set operation for state modification (inspired by atomic registers), which must be absolutely consistent; but read operations may be served from any replica, because stale data results in extra work being performed but not incorrect results [Gup15].

cb4f9b453bec.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
cb4f9b453bec.sentence: In order to guarantee that data being read is up-to-date and consistent with any changes made before the read is performed, it is necessary to do one of the following:

f8b68ce4cd20.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
f8b68ce4cd20.sentence: - Use quorum leases, in which some replicas are granted a lease on all or part of the data in the system, allowing strongly consistent local reads at the cost of some write performance.

eb55e7622892.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
eb55e7622892.sentence: The quorum leasing technique simply grants a read lease on some subset of the replicated datastoreâs state to a quorum of replicas.

abab9bd85b35.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
abab9bd85b35.sentence: Any operation that changes the state of that data must be acknowledged by all replicas in the read quorum.

5bd7768bdc2b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
5bd7768bdc2b.section: Distributed Consensus Performance and Network Latency
5bd7768bdc2b.sentence: However, for systems with a very high number of clients, it may not be practical for all clients to keep a persistent connection to the consensus clusters open, because open TCP/IP connections do consume some resources, e.g., file descriptors, in addition to generating keepalive traffic.

d074ccafd192.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
d074ccafd192.section: Distributed Consensus Performance and Network Latency
d074ccafd192.sentence: A solution is to use a pool of regional proxies, as shown in Figure 23-9, which hold persistent TCP/IP connections to the consensus group in order to avoid the setup overhead over long distances.

01e51d83da7c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/managing-critical-state
01e51d83da7c.section: Distributed Consensus Performance and Network Latency
01e51d83da7c.sentence: Proxies may also be a good way to encapsulate sharding and load balancing strategies, as well as discovery of cluster members and leaders.

252a0f020bbd.title: Raft (algorithm)
252a0f020bbd.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
252a0f020bbd.sentence: When the existing leader fails or when the algorithm initializes, a new leader needs to be elected.

34053bf37b43.title: Raft (algorithm)
34053bf37b43.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
34053bf37b43.sentence: In this case, a new term starts in the cluster.

d32bc1a78d12.title: Raft (algorithm)
d32bc1a78d12.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
d32bc1a78d12.sentence: If a candidate receives a majority of votes, then it becomes the new leader.

4ef9239bcdaa.title: Raft (algorithm)
4ef9239bcdaa.sentence: It regularly informs the followers of its existence by sending a heartbeat message.

9d7a42b3100d.title: Raft (algorithm)
9d7a42b3100d.sentence: Each follower has a timeout (typically between 150 and 300 ms) in which it expects the heartbeat from the leader.

045ff850312e.title: Raft (algorithm)
045ff850312e.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
045ff850312e.sentence: A server becomes a candidate if it receives no communication by the leader over a period called the election timeout, so it assumes there is no acting leader anymore.

8a76942ab8e9.title: Raft (algorithm)
8a76942ab8e9.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
8a76942ab8e9.sentence: It starts the election by increasing the term counter, voting for itself as new leader, and sending a message to all other servers requesting their vote.

b101421f5cee.title: Raft (algorithm)
b101421f5cee.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
b101421f5cee.sentence: A server will vote only once per term, on a first-come-first-served basis.

16795273b259.title: Raft (algorithm)
16795273b259.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
16795273b259.sentence: If a candidate receives a message from another server with a term number larger than the candidate's current term, then the candidate's election is defeated and the candidate changes into a follower and recognizes the leader as legitimate.

e7d2ea7a24f6.title: Raft (algorithm)
e7d2ea7a24f6.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
e7d2ea7a24f6.sentence: If neither happens, e.g., because of a split vote, then a new term starts, and a new election begins.

8f8486328193.title: Raft (algorithm)
8f8486328193.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
8f8486328193.sentence: Raft uses a randomized election timeout to ensure that split vote problems are resolved quickly.

f499ba8bff65.title: Raft (algorithm)
f499ba8bff65.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Leader election
f499ba8bff65.sentence: This should reduce the chance of a split vote because servers won't become candidates at the same time: a single server will time out, win the election, then become leader and send heartbeat messages to other servers before any of the followers can become candidates.

b77654243acc.title: Raft (algorithm)
b77654243acc.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
b77654243acc.sentence: The leader is responsible for the log replication.

dd316e5b28cb.title: Raft (algorithm)
dd316e5b28cb.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication

caa1802c2f21.title: Raft (algorithm)
caa1802c2f21.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
caa1802c2f21.sentence: After being appended to the leader's log as a new entry, each of the requests is forwarded to the followers as AppendEntries messages.

f5557c26101f.title: Raft (algorithm)
f5557c26101f.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
f5557c26101f.sentence: In case of unavailability of the followers, the leader retries AppendEntries messages indefinitely, until the log entry is eventually stored by all of the followers.

2ba8ec9ad343.title: Raft (algorithm)
2ba8ec9ad343.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
2ba8ec9ad343.sentence: This event also commits all previous entries in the leader's log.

fc6c688a1333.title: Raft (algorithm)
fc6c688a1333.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
fc6c688a1333.sentence: In the case of a leader crash, the logs can be left inconsistent, with some logs from the old leader not being fully replicated through the cluster.

11e27108d6ff.title: Raft (algorithm)
11e27108d6ff.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
11e27108d6ff.sentence: The new leader will then handle inconsistency by forcing the followers to duplicate its own log.

5470d5a17ccf.title: Raft (algorithm)
5470d5a17ccf.section: Basics > Approach of the consensus problem in Raft > Log replication
5470d5a17ccf.sentence: To do so, for each of its followers, the leader will compare its log with the log from the follower, find the last entry where they agree, then delete all the entries coming after this critical entry in the follower log and replace it with its own log entries.

a180cb6228e9.title: Raft (algorithm)
a180cb6228e9.sentence: This rule is ensured by a simple restriction: a candidate can't win an election unless its log contains all committed entries.

732e1cb07945.title: Raft (algorithm)
732e1cb07945.sentence: Raft determines which of two logs (carried by two distinct servers) is more up-to-date by comparing the index term of the last entries in the logs.

66b3634466f7.title: Raft (algorithm)
66b3634466f7.sentence: If the logs have a last entry with different terms, then the log with the later term is more up-to-date.

99d1cd635c90.title: Raft (algorithm)
99d1cd635c90.sentence: If the logs end with the same term, then whichever log is longer is more up-to-date.

903c237962c5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
903c237962c5.sentence: A saga is a sequence of local transactions.

7b9da9b45ccd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
7b9da9b45ccd.sentence: Each local transaction updates the database and publishes a message or event to trigger the next local transaction in the saga.

eb8364eea3bd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
eb8364eea3bd.sentence: If a local transaction fails because it violates a business rule then the saga executes a series of compensating transactions that undo the changes that were made by the preceding local transactions.

c08bf126b378.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
c08bf126b378.sentence: Saga is used to manage data consistency across multiple services in distributed systems, especially in microservices architectures where each service manages its own database.

12c2d883ce8e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
12c2d883ce8e.sentence: The saga pattern addresses the challenge of maintaining data consistency without relying on distributed transactions, which are difficult to scale and can negatively impact system performance.

0657c69c0e95.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
0657c69c0e95.sentence: There are two common implementation approaches:

5d734eb091fb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
5d734eb091fb.sentence: - Choreography: Each local transaction publishes domain events that trigger local transactions in other services.

8783e9ffef94.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
8783e9ffef94.sentence: - Orchestration: An orchestrator tells the participants what local transactions to execute.

b7a04110b71c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
b7a04110b71c.sentence: - The Saga pattern is particularly hard to debug.

a0b37b21c81f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
a0b37b21c81f.sentence: - There's a risk of cyclic dependency between saga participants.

31c5c3651b67.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
31c5c3651b67.sentence: - Lack of participant data isolation imposes durability challenges.

2e567dd08085.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::distributed-transactions
2e567dd08085.sentence: - Testing is difficult because all services must be running to simulate a transaction.

8ce5a41cd755.title: paper>10.1145/38713.38742
8ce5a41cd755.sentence: Long lived transactions (LLTs) hold on to database resources for relatively long periods of time, significantly delaying the termination of shorter and more common transactions.

aa3ba4ad8e31.title: paper>10.1145/38713.38742
aa3ba4ad8e31.sentence: To alleviate these problems we propose the notion of a saga.

4f10eabfd745.title: paper>10.1145/38713.38742
4f10eabfd745.sentence: The database management system guarantees that either all the transactions in a saga are successfully completed or compensating transactions are run to amend a partial execution.

60e1434d93e7.title: paper>10.1145/38713.38742
60e1434d93e7.sentence: Both the concept of saga and its implementation are relatively simple, but they have the potential to improve performance significantly.

ebb9f752ac16.title: paper>10.1145/38713.38742
ebb9f752ac16.sentence: We analyze the various implementation issues related to sagas, including how they can be run on an existing system that does not directly support them.

ed043ae0d3d4.title: Compensating transaction
ed043ae0d3d4.sentence: In transaction processing and distributed computing, a compensating transaction is a transaction that reverses the effects of a previously committed transaction.

6bb7c3f0c8b1.title: Compensating transaction
6bb7c3f0c8b1.sentence: A compensating transaction is necessary when a business process, which may consist of several individual transactions, fails after one or more of its steps have already been successfully completed (committed).

e69d17afffba.title: Compensating transaction
e69d17afffba.sentence: Unlike a database rollback, which discards uncommitted changes, a compensating transaction is a new transaction that applies business logic to semantically undo the work of a completed transaction, thereby restoring the system to a consistent state.

37f83dcce227.title: Compensating transaction
37f83dcce227.sentence: A compensating transaction works by executing an operation that is the logical inverse of the original operation.

668ee8ff6d0a.title: Compensating transaction
668ee8ff6d0a.sentence: For example, if the original transaction was "debit account by $100," its compensating transaction would be "credit account by $100." Each step in a long-running process must have a corresponding compensating transaction designed.

ff2fa387fcb9.title: Compensating transaction
ff2fa387fcb9.sentence: If the process fails at any point, the system executes the compensating transactions for all previously completed steps in reverse order to undo the process.

4ead4f1d6e9b.title: Compensating transaction
4ead4f1d6e9b.sentence: Compensating transactions are fundamental to the saga pattern.

3d560cd94ee5.title: Compensating transaction
3d560cd94ee5.sentence: Instead, each service commits its transaction and has a compensating transaction ready in case a subsequent step fails.

c0389c703a97.title: Compensating transaction
c0389c703a97.sentence: This differs from distributed transactions using the two-phase-commit protocol, as it avoids locking resources for extended durations.

262ac33cf5af.title: Compensating transaction
262ac33cf5af.sentence: Because these operations might span a long period and involve multiple independent web services, holding database locks is impractical.

50eb36b9d395.title: Compensating transaction
50eb36b9d395.sentence: - No true isolation: The results of the original transaction are visible to other processes before it is compensated.

48a7ce87c5f9.title: Compensating transaction
48a7ce87c5f9.sentence: - Compensation failure: A compensating transaction can itself fail.

05ccd6ae3e38.title: Compensating transaction
05ccd6ae3e38.sentence: This is a critical problem that requires a robust error-handling strategy, such as retrying the compensation, manual intervention by an administrator, or escalating the failure.

943d4858c720.title: Compensating transaction
943d4858c720.sentence: For instance, if a transaction resulted in an email being sent, the email cannot be "unsent." The compensating transaction can only perform actions like sending a follow-up apology email.

5a095fd57fb3.title: Compensating transaction
5a095fd57fb3.sentence: Because of these challenges, compensating transactions do not guarantee a return to the exact original state but rather to a state that is semantically consistent from a business perspective.

e0d27bb0f193.title: paper>10.1145/2491245
e0d27bb0f193.sentence: Spanner is Google’s scalable, multiversion, globally distributed, and synchronously replicated database.

ff051a017fce.title: Spanner (database)
ff051a017fce.sentence: Spanner is a distributed SQL database management and storage service developed by Google.

28296f7b386f.title: Spanner (database)
28296f7b386f.sentence: It provides features such as global transactions, strongly consistent reads, and automatic multi-site replication and failover.

593cc99b33fc.title: paper>10.1145/2491245
593cc99b33fc.sentence: It is the first system to distribute data at global scale and support externally-consistent distributed transactions.

e67ec98d8374.title: Spanner (database)
e67ec98d8374.sentence: Spanner allows users to perform arbitrary queries using SQL with relational data while maintaining strong consistency and high availability for that data with synchronous replication.

06bbebca3685.title: Spanner (database)
06bbebca3685.sentence: - Transactions can be applied across rows, columns, tables, and databases within a Spanner universe.

566f46c00fbe.title: Spanner (database)
566f46c00fbe.sentence: - Reads are strongly consistent and data is versioned to allow for stale reads: clients can read previous versions of data, subject to garbage collection windows.

35535ec05a78.title: Spanner (database)
35535ec05a78.sentence: Spanner uses the Paxos algorithm as part of its operation to shard (partition) data across up to hundreds of servers.

d64b42567134.title: Shard (database architecture)
d64b42567134.sentence: - Spanner, a distributed database developed by Google, shards across multiple Paxos state machines to scale to large numbers of machines, data centers, and rows.

6ec6db8a9073.title: Spanner (database)
6ec6db8a9073.sentence: It makes heavy use of hardware-assisted clock synchronization using GPS clocks and atomic clocks to ensure global consistency.

ef6c2777a9c9.title: Spanner (database)
ef6c2777a9c9.sentence: TrueTime is the brand name for Google's distributed cloud infrastructure, which provides Spanner with the ability to generate monotonically increasing timestamps in data centers around the world.

b5126af4a719.title: paper>10.1145/2491245
b5126af4a719.sentence: This article describes how Spanner is structured, its feature set, the rationale underlying various design decisions, and a novel time API that exposes clock uncertainty.

a7ddcac3bcc9.title: paper>10.1145/2491245
a7ddcac3bcc9.sentence: This API and its implementation are critical to supporting external consistency and a variety of powerful features: nonblocking reads in the past, lock-free snapshot transactions, and atomic schema changes, across all of Spanner.

5415196cbf17.title: Amazon DynamoDB
5415196cbf17.sentence: Content with compromising storage efficiency, Amazon's response was Dynamo: a highly available key–value store built for internal use.

c7b67afaec48.title: paper>10.1145/1294261.1294281
c7b67afaec48.sentence: At this scale, small and large components fail continuously and the way persistent state is managed in the face of these failures drives the reliability and scalability of the software systems.

d51bd6dd497e.title: paper>10.1145/1294261.1294281
d51bd6dd497e.sentence: Reliability at massive scale is one of the biggest challenges we face at Amazon.com, one of the largest e-commerce operations in the world; even the slightest outage has significant financial consequences and impacts customer trust.

661d8f9e7b18.title: paper>10.1145/1294261.1294281
661d8f9e7b18.sentence: The Amazon.com platform, which provides services for many web sites worldwide, is implemented on top of an infrastructure of tens of thousands of servers and network components located in many datacenters around the world.

a36c69851491.title: Amazon DynamoDB
a36c69851491.sentence: Traditional databases often split data into smaller pieces to save space, but combining those pieces during searches can make queries slower.

b65e65c06056.title: Amazon DynamoDB
b65e65c06056.sentence: Many of Amazon's services demanded mostly primary-key reads on their data, and with speed a top priority, putting these pieces together was extremely taxing.

501efdaeb449.title: Amazon DynamoDB
501efdaeb449.sentence: Dynamo, it seemed, was everything their engineers needed, but adoption lagged.

1e1690829243.title: Amazon DynamoDB
1e1690829243.sentence: Amazon engineers originally avoided Dynamo due to engineering overheads like provisioning and managing partitions and nodes.

1fe1104e4381.title: Amazon DynamoDB
1fe1104e4381.sentence: Amazon's next iteration of NoSQL technology, DynamoDB, automated these database management operations.

50bc7700479f.title: Apache Cassandra
50bc7700479f.sentence: It enables low-latency operations for all clients and incorporates Amazon's Dynamo distributed storage and replication techniques, combined with Google's Bigtable data storage engine model.

b0f1f86d4baa.title: Amazon DynamoDB
b0f1f86d4baa.sentence: Amazon DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database service provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS).

a105d01aaa8d.title: Amazon DynamoDB
a105d01aaa8d.sentence: It supports key-value and document data structures and is designed to handle a wide range of applications requiring scalability and performance.

93817e578cae.title: Amazon DynamoDB
93817e578cae.sentence: While these systems had noticeable design flaws, they did not demand the overhead of provisioning hardware and scaling and re-partitioning data.

9a79d1bb1302.title: Amazon DynamoDB
9a79d1bb1302.sentence: Each table contains items (rows), and each item is made up of attributes (columns).

2d09b2e59241.title: Amazon DynamoDB
2d09b2e59241.sentence: Given the NoSQL nature of DynamoDB, the Tables do not require that all items in a Table conform to some predefined schema.

6b5e8b6272a7.title: Amazon DynamoDB
6b5e8b6272a7.sentence: Upon entry, data is first distributed into different partitions by hashing on the partition key.

32a6bce1d3c3.title: Amazon DynamoDB
32a6bce1d3c3.sentence: Each partition can store up to 10 GB of data and handle by default 1,000 write capacity units (WCU) and 3,000 read capacity units (RCU).

3a4fd06d4077.title: Amazon DynamoDB
3a4fd06d4077.sentence: One RCU represents one strongly consistent read per second or two eventually consistent reads per second for items up to 4 KB in size.

4f7545dee922.title: Amazon DynamoDB
4f7545dee922.sentence: One WCU represents one write per second for an item up to 1 KB in size.

c6a87e1bd11b.title: Amazon DynamoDB
c6a87e1bd11b.sentence: Each partition features three nodes, each of which contains a copy of that partition's data.

e9116d29cb5a.title: Amazon DynamoDB
e9116d29cb5a.sentence: Within each partition, one of the three nodes is designated the "leader node".

acecb7692f85.title: Amazon DynamoDB
acecb7692f85.sentence: To maintain its status, the leader sends a "heartbeat" to each other node every 1.5 seconds.

a70583a54b7b.title: Amazon DynamoDB
a70583a54b7b.sentence: Should another node stop receiving heartbeats, it can initiate a new leader election.

0dcac5a10045.title: Amazon DynamoDB
0dcac5a10045.sentence: DynamoDB uses the Paxos algorithm to elect leaders.

fc463baf39cd.title: Amazon DynamoDB
fc463baf39cd.sentence: The system first writes to the leader node, then writes to a second node, then sends a "success" message, and finally continues propagating to the third node.

393dc4ba9fd4.title: Amazon DynamoDB
393dc4ba9fd4.sentence: Writes are consistent because they always travel first through the leader node.

1be9e98877aa.title: Amazon DynamoDB
1be9e98877aa.sentence: A consistent read visits the leader node.

3b584419ba40.title: Amazon DynamoDB
3b584419ba40.sentence: But the consistency-availability trade-off rears its head again here: in read-heavy systems, always reading from the leader can overwhelm a single node and reduce availability.

5ab07ce07b70.title: Amazon DynamoDB
5ab07ce07b70.sentence: The second option, an eventually consistent read, selects a random node.

9c4c9249aa89.title: Amazon DynamoDB
9c4c9249aa89.sentence: In practice, this is where DynamoDB trades consistency for availability.

611e5f79d87e.title: Amazon DynamoDB
611e5f79d87e.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
611e5f79d87e.sentence: A Primary Key is a set of attributes that uniquely identifies items in a DynamoDB Table.

2b937bac417b.title: Amazon DynamoDB
2b937bac417b.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
2b937bac417b.sentence: Primary Keys in Dynamo DB can consist of either one or two attributes.

b0b09ab4d896.title: Amazon DynamoDB
b0b09ab4d896.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
b0b09ab4d896.sentence: Creation of a DynamoDB Table requires definition of a Primary Key.

cb1153040e48.title: Amazon DynamoDB
cb1153040e48.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
cb1153040e48.sentence: Each item in a DynamoDB Table is required to have all of the attributes that constitute the Primary Key, and no two items in a Table can have the same Primary Key.

be81b792fffb.title: Amazon DynamoDB
be81b792fffb.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
be81b792fffb.sentence: When a Primary Key is made up of only one attribute, it is called a Partition Key.

af2c3dee25ad.title: Amazon DynamoDB
af2c3dee25ad.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
af2c3dee25ad.sentence: Partition Keys determine the physical location of the associated item.

00f3d5fa7f52.title: Amazon DynamoDB
00f3d5fa7f52.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
00f3d5fa7f52.sentence: In this case, no two items in a table can have the same Partition Key.

100dfd9d4a74.title: Amazon DynamoDB
100dfd9d4a74.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
100dfd9d4a74.sentence: When a Primary Key is made up of two attributes, the first one is called a "Partition Key" and the second is called a "Sort Key".

35576c771435.title: Amazon DynamoDB
35576c771435.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
35576c771435.sentence: As before, the Partition Key decides the physical Location of Data, but the Sort Key then decides the relative logical position of associated item's record inside that physical location.

47f8b8eb295b.title: Amazon DynamoDB
47f8b8eb295b.section: Overview > DynamoDB Items > Keys In DynamoDB
47f8b8eb295b.sentence: In this case, two items in a Table can have the same Partition Key, but no two items in a partition can have the same Sort Key.

33a8a0034aff.title: Amazon DynamoDB
33a8a0034aff.sentence: When a Secondary Index has same Partition Key as Primary Index but a different Sort Key, it is called as the Local Secondary Index.

521aeccd0ec1.title: Amazon DynamoDB
521aeccd0ec1.sentence: When Primary Index and Secondary Index have different Partition Key, the Secondary index is known as the Global Secondary Index.

c28cd1c5ded9.title: Amazon DynamoDB
c28cd1c5ded9.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
c28cd1c5ded9.sentence: DynamoDB data modeling patterns are architectural approaches used in Amazon DynamoDB, a NoSQL database service designed for distributed systems.

fe05e04b6558.title: Amazon DynamoDB
fe05e04b6558.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
fe05e04b6558.sentence: Each pattern addresses specific technical requirements.

4dd283244cec.title: Amazon DynamoDB
4dd283244cec.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
4dd283244cec.sentence: These patterns address various data organization challenges and include "Single Table Design", which consolidates related data while adhering to DynamoDB's 400KB item size limit; "Multiple Table Design", which separates data into distinct tables based on access patterns and data model differences; and Hybrid Design, which blends both approaches to balance flexibility and efficiency.

41ff810ea716.title: Amazon DynamoDB
41ff810ea716.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
41ff810ea716.sentence: "Single Table Design" can optimize query efficiency by co-locating related data under the same partition key to reduce access latency.

f4f194639349.title: Amazon DynamoDB
f4f194639349.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
f4f194639349.sentence: "Multiple Table Design" enables separation of concerns by isolating data into purpose-specific tables with distinct access patterns.

4f95fceb8acf.title: Amazon DynamoDB
4f95fceb8acf.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
4f95fceb8acf.sentence: Additional patterns described in AWS documentation include "Event Sourcing", where data changes are stored as immutable events, enabling historical state reconstruction; "Materialized Views", which simplify analytical queries through pre-computed aggregations, often implemented via DynamoDB Streams, application-level processing, or periodic batch updates using Lambda functions.

da1fdfa47633.title: Amazon DynamoDB
da1fdfa47633.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
da1fdfa47633.sentence: "Event Sourcing" preserves a historical log of state changes, often implemented with immutable data storage.

20b42fee00ce.title: Amazon DynamoDB
20b42fee00ce.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
20b42fee00ce.sentence: "Materialized Views" simplify complex analytical queries through pre-aggregation strategies tailored to access patterns.

46bbb7743919.title: Amazon DynamoDB
46bbb7743919.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
46bbb7743919.sentence: As well as "Time-Series Design", optimized for workloads like logging and metrics, typically using a partition key for entity identification and a sort key representing timestamps to efficiently query time-based datasets.

81568920edf9.title: Amazon DynamoDB
81568920edf9.section: Architectural patterns in DynamoDB data modeling
81568920edf9.sentence: "Time-Series Design" uses partitioning and sorting strategies to efficiently store and query large volumes of temporal data.

28804dbf5e30.title: Google File System
28804dbf5e30.sentence: Google File System (GFS or GoogleFS, not to be confused with the GFS Linux file system) is a proprietary distributed file system developed by Google to provide efficient, reliable access to data using large clusters of commodity hardware.

4f76a6928948.title: Google File System
4f76a6928948.sentence: GFS is enhanced for Google's core data storage and usage needs (primarily the search engine), which can generate enormous amounts of data that must be retained; Google File System grew out of an earlier Google effort, "BigFiles", developed by Larry Page and Sergey Brin in the early days of Google, while it was still located in Stanford.

775b319a5480.title: Google File System
775b319a5480.sentence: It is also designed and optimized to run on Google's computing clusters, dense nodes which consist of cheap "commodity" computers, which means precautions must be taken against the high failure rate of individual nodes and the subsequent data loss.

e8ee8c96bf08.title: Google File System
e8ee8c96bf08.sentence: Files are divided into fixed-size chunks of 64 megabytes, similar to clusters or sectors in regular file systems, which are only extremely rarely overwritten, or shrunk; files are usually appended to or read.

152a060e6a06.title: Google File System
152a060e6a06.sentence: Other design decisions select for high data throughputs, even when it comes at the cost of latency.

512fecd42d38.title: Google File System
512fecd42d38.sentence: These nodes are divided into two types: one Master node and multiple Chunkservers.

3dfcf28b4610.title: Google File System
3dfcf28b4610.sentence: Each chunk is assigned a globally unique 64-bit label by the master node at the time of creation, and logical mappings of files to constituent chunks are maintained.

94d15739843a.title: Google File System
94d15739843a.sentence: Each chunk is replicated several times throughout the network.

2d6ae02150e9.title: Google File System
2d6ae02150e9.sentence: At default, it is replicated three times, but this is configurable.

803714a818fd.title: Google File System
803714a818fd.sentence: Files which are in high demand may have a higher replication factor, while files for which the application client uses strict storage optimizations may be replicated less than three times - in order to cope with quick garbage cleaning policies.

24113e8ceee0.title: Google File System
24113e8ceee0.sentence: The Master server does not usually store the actual chunks, but rather all the metadata associated with the chunks, such as the tables mapping the 64-bit labels to chunk locations and the files they make up (mapping from files to chunks), the locations of the copies of the chunks, what processes are reading or writing to a particular chunk, or taking a "snapshot" of the chunk pursuant to replicate it (usually at the instigation of the Master server, when, due to node failures, the number of copies of a chunk has fallen beneath the set number).

6ae7614e2130.title: Google File System
6ae7614e2130.sentence: All this metadata is kept current by the Master server periodically receiving updates from each chunk server ("Heart-beat messages").

c737f69cdbe9.title: Google File System
c737f69cdbe9.sentence: Permissions for modifications are handled by a system of time-limited, expiring "leases", where the Master server grants permission to a process for a finite period of time during which no other process will be granted permission by the Master server to modify the chunk.

aad734077492.title: Google File System
aad734077492.sentence: The modifying chunkserver, which is always the primary chunk holder, then propagates the changes to the chunkservers with the backup copies.

b9962bf33b1c.title: Google File System
b9962bf33b1c.sentence: The changes are not saved until all chunkservers acknowledge, thus guaranteeing the completion and atomicity of the operation.

f0ed9ad6c2f4.title: Google File System
f0ed9ad6c2f4.sentence: Programs access the chunks by first querying the Master server for the locations of the desired chunks; if the chunks are not being operated on (i.e. no outstanding leases exist), the Master replies with the locations, and the program then contacts and receives the data from the chunkserver directly (similar to Kazaa and its supernodes).

9ce9a387472a.title: Google File System
9ce9a387472a.sentence: It supports Record Append which allows multiple clients to append data to the same file concurrently and atomicity is guaranteed.

ae412500eb6d.title: Google File System
ae412500eb6d.sentence: The Google File System does not provide a POSIX interface.

5b0da8edbab5.title: Google File System
5b0da8edbab5.sentence: As the master node is not directly involved in data reading (the data are passed from the chunk server directly to the reading client), the read rate increases significantly with the number of chunk servers, achieving 583 MB/s for 342 nodes.

afce6338ece4.title: paper>10.1145/1365815.1365816
afce6338ece4.sentence: Bigtable is a distributed storage system for managing structured data that is designed to scale to a very large size: petabytes of data across thousands of commodity servers.

23f65e1f5df5.title: paper>10.1145/1365815.1365816
23f65e1f5df5.sentence: Many projects at Google store data in Bigtable, including web indexing, Google Earth, and Google Finance.

cd2f8711425c.title: paper>10.1145/1365815.1365816
cd2f8711425c.sentence: These applications place very different demands on Bigtable, both in terms of data size (from URLs to web pages to satellite imagery) and latency requirements (from backend bulk processing to real-time data serving).

2cda97901807.title: paper>10.1145/1365815.1365816
2cda97901807.sentence: Despite these varied demands, Bigtable has successfully provided a flexible, high-performance solution for all of these Google products.

3821c418c5a8.title: Bigtable
3821c418c5a8.sentence: Google's reasons for developing its own database include scalability and better control of performance characteristics.

c0a947647d09.title: Bigtable
c0a947647d09.sentence: Bigtable is designed to scale into the petabyte range across "hundreds or thousands of machines, and to make it easy to add more machines [to] the system and automatically start taking advantage of those resources without any reconfiguration".

65b46e519be1.title: Bigtable
65b46e519be1.sentence: It is built on Colossus (Google File System), Chubby Lock Service, SSTable (log-structured storage like LevelDB) and a few other Google technologies.

d0e52b1b8d41.title: Bigtable
d0e52b1b8d41.sentence: Tables are split into multiple tablets – segments of the table are split at certain row keys so that each tablet is a few hundred megabytes or a few gigabytes in size.

c39fae0a0164.title: Bigtable
c39fae0a0164.sentence: A bigtable is somewhat like a mapreduce worker pool in that thousands to hundreds of thousands of tablet shards may be served by hundreds to thousands of BigTable servers.

9002b9024fce.title: Bigtable
9002b9024fce.sentence: The locations in the GFS of tablets are recorded as database entries in multiple special tablets, which are called "META1" tablets.

f8d54cd884ca.title: Bigtable
f8d54cd884ca.sentence: META1 tablets are found by querying the single "META0" tablet, which typically resides on a server of its own since it is often queried by clients as to the location of the "META1" tablet which itself has the answer to the question of where the actual data is located.

f7b8ee2ab555.title: Bigtable
f7b8ee2ab555.sentence: Like GFS's master server, the META0 server is not generally a bottleneck since the processor time and bandwidth necessary to discover and transmit META1 locations is minimal and clients aggressively cache locations to minimize queries.

04295c93e93e.title: Bigtable
04295c93e93e.sentence: Apache HBase and Cassandra are some of the best known open source projects that were modeled after Bigtable.

fb3f06ddeafa.title: Bigtable
fb3f06ddeafa.sentence: As of April 2024, Bigtable manages over 10 Exabytes of data and serves more than 7 billion requests per second.

185d18695245.title: Apache Cassandra
185d18695245.sentence: Apache Cassandra is a free and open-source database management system designed to handle large volumes of data across multiple commodity servers.

df35bb9790c1.title: paper>10.1145/1773912.1773922
df35bb9790c1.sentence: Cassandra is a distributed storage system for managing very large amounts of structured data spread out across many commodity servers, while providing highly available service with no single point of failure.

460844424366.title: paper>10.1145/1773912.1773922
460844424366.sentence: Cassandra system was designed to run on cheap commodity hardware and handle high write throughput while not sacrificing read efficiency.

e5074d843bbe.title: paper>10.1145/1773912.1773922
e5074d843bbe.sentence: Cassandra aims to run on top of an infrastructure of hundreds of nodes (possibly spread across different data centers).

4956da8dc9e0.title: paper>10.1145/1773912.1773922
4956da8dc9e0.sentence: At this scale, small and large components fail continuously.

46a12bd9ade7.title: paper>10.1145/1773912.1773922
46a12bd9ade7.sentence: The way Cassandra manages the persistent state in the face of these failures drives the reliability and scalability of the software systems relying on this service.

afa1a7d78818.title: Apache Cassandra
afa1a7d78818.sentence: Cassandra uses a distributed architecture where all nodes perform identical functions, eliminating single points of failure.

9e8aecdbe4d4.title: Apache Cassandra
9e8aecdbe4d4.sentence: Cassandra supports computer clusters which may span multiple data centers, featuring asynchronous and masterless replication.

403e3f03f282.title: Apache Cassandra
403e3f03f282.sentence: The system is capable of linear scaling, which increases read and write throughput with the addition of new nodes, while maintaining continuous service.

8e582dc0b08d.title: Apache Cassandra
8e582dc0b08d.sentence: Cassandra is categorized as an AP (Availability and Partition Tolerance) system, emphasizing availability and partition tolerance over consistency.

e3b10c3d778a.title: Apache Cassandra
e3b10c3d778a.sentence: While it offers tunable consistency levels for both read and write operations, its architecture makes it less suitable for use cases requiring strict consistency guarantees.

c929f3757bc6.title: paper>10.1145/1773912.1773922
c929f3757bc6.sentence: While in many ways Cassandra resembles a database and shares many design and implementation strategies therewith, Cassandra does not support a full relational data model; instead, it provides clients with a simple data model that supports dynamic control over data layout and format.

2ddbfb34039e.title: Apache Cassandra
2ddbfb34039e.sentence: As a wide-column store, Cassandra combines features of both key-value and tabular database systems.

e4eb151f35d1.title: Apache Cassandra
e4eb151f35d1.sentence: The system is optimized for applications with well-defined data access patterns that can be incorporated into the schema design.

58fb1ddf4b2d.title: Apache Cassandra
58fb1ddf4b2d.sentence: Cassandra does not support advanced query patterns such as multi-table JOINs, ad hoc aggregations, or complex queries.

6c112fff72e0.title: Apache Cassandra
6c112fff72e0.sentence: These limitations stem from its distributed architecture, which optimizes for scalability and availability rather than complex query operations.

afe36ad412c0.title: MapReduce
afe36ad412c0.sentence: MapReduce is a programming model and an associated implementation for processing and generating big data sets with a parallel and distributed algorithm on a cluster.

1b4a09b428c6.title: paper>10.1145/1327452.1327492
1b4a09b428c6.sentence: MapReduce is a programming model and an associated implementation for processing and generating large datasets that is amenable to a broad variety of real-world tasks.

27ad78d24601.title: paper>10.1145/1327452.1327492
27ad78d24601.sentence: Users specify the computation in terms of a map and a reduce function, and the underlying runtime system automatically parallelizes the computation across large-scale clusters of machines, handles machine failures, and schedules inter-machine communication to make efficient use of the network and disks.

4410247eae12.title: MapReduce
4410247eae12.sentence: A MapReduce program is composed of a map procedure, which performs filtering and sorting (such as sorting students by first name into queues, one queue for each name), and a reduce method, which performs a summary operation (such as counting the number of students in each queue, yielding name frequencies).

02ca3d53d95f.title: MapReduce
02ca3d53d95f.sentence: The key contributions of the MapReduce framework are not the actual map and reduce functions (which, for example, resemble the 1995 Message Passing Interface standard's reduce and scatter operations), but the scalability and fault-tolerance achieved for a variety of applications due to parallelization.

e95a09d14706.title: MapReduce
e95a09d14706.sentence: - Map: each worker node applies the map function to the local data, and writes the output to a temporary storage.

52183c5abac8.title: MapReduce
52183c5abac8.sentence: - Shuffle: worker nodes redistribute data based on the output keys (produced by the map function), such that all data belonging to one key is located on the same worker node.

81d2f1bf38d0.title: MapReduce
81d2f1bf38d0.sentence: - Reduce: worker nodes now process each group of output data, per key, in parallel.

f8d9dd18ebea.title: MapReduce
f8d9dd18ebea.sentence: MapReduce can take advantage of the locality of data, processing it near the place it is stored in order to minimize communication overhead.

e5e1c5c62b96.title: MapReduce
e5e1c5c62b96.sentence: While this process often appears inefficient compared to algorithms that are more sequential (because multiple instances of the reduction process must be run), MapReduce can be applied to significantly larger datasets than a single "commodity" server can handle – a large server farm can use MapReduce to sort a petabyte of data in only a few hours.

da317966cd4b.title: MapReduce
da317966cd4b.sentence: Each node is expected to report back periodically with completed work and status updates.

2b91537f202f.title: MapReduce
2b91537f202f.sentence: If a node falls silent for longer than that interval, the master node (similar to the master server in the Google File System) records the node as dead and sends out the node's assigned work to other nodes.

f6cbc917919f.title: MapReduce
f6cbc917919f.sentence: The parallelism also offers some possibility of recovering from partial failure of servers or storage during the operation: if one mapper or reducer fails, the work can be rescheduled – assuming the input data are still available.

ae6879f725be.title: paper>10.1145/1327452.1327492
ae6879f725be.sentence: Programmers find the system easy to use: more than ten thousand distinct MapReduce programs have been implemented internally at Google over the past four years, and an average of one hundred thousand MapReduce jobs are executed on Google's clusters every day, processing a total of more than twenty petabytes of data per day.

02e85b0cca09.title: MapReduce
02e85b0cca09.sentence: For processes that complete quickly, and where the data fits into main memory of a single machine or a small cluster, using a MapReduce framework usually is not effective.

bf12b4ef5801.title: MapReduce
bf12b4ef5801.sentence: Since these frameworks are designed to recover from the loss of whole nodes during the computation, they write interim results to distributed storage.

1dfdcb3f28e2.title: MapReduce
1dfdcb3f28e2.sentence: This crash recovery is expensive, and only pays off when the computation involves many computers and a long runtime of the computation.

dc74aae621a2.title: MapReduce
dc74aae621a2.sentence: MapReduce tasks must be written as acyclic dataflow programs, i.e. a stateless mapper followed by a stateless reducer, that are executed by a batch job scheduler.

ae0b1394f2bc.title: MapReduce
ae0b1394f2bc.sentence: This paradigm makes repeated querying of datasets difficult and imposes limitations that are felt in fields such as graph processing where iterative algorithms that revisit a single working set multiple times are the norm, as well as, in the presence of disk-based data with high latency, even the field of machine learning where multiple passes through the data are required even though algorithms can tolerate serial access to the data each pass.

d2a451174a4c.title: Apache Hadoop
d2a451174a4c.sentence: Apache Hadoop (/həˈduːp/) is a collection of open-source software utilities for reliable, scalable, distributed computing.

998de5d74f40.title: Apache Hadoop
998de5d74f40.sentence: The core of Apache Hadoop consists of a storage part, known as Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), and a processing part which is a MapReduce programming model.

9be747b94b11.title: Apache Hadoop
9be747b94b11.sentence: Hadoop splits files into large blocks and distributes them across nodes in a cluster.

1875529ac03f.title: Apache Hadoop
1875529ac03f.sentence: It then transfers packaged code into nodes to process the data in parallel.

5bdfdf18844f.title: Apache Hadoop
5bdfdf18844f.sentence: This approach takes advantage of data locality, where nodes manipulate the data they have access to.

b726aa6bb180.title: Apache Hadoop
b726aa6bb180.sentence: This allows the dataset to be processed faster and more efficiently than it would be in a more conventional supercomputer architecture that relies on a parallel file system where computation and data are distributed via high-speed networking.

45d4af8ff2aa.title: Apache Hadoop
45d4af8ff2aa.sentence: - Hadoop Common - contains libraries and utilities needed by other Hadoop modules;

c29c53c6c34b.title: Apache Hadoop
c29c53c6c34b.sentence: - Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) - a distributed file-system that stores data on commodity machines, providing very high aggregate bandwidth across the cluster;

0b1a0fc06c5d.title: Apache Hadoop
0b1a0fc06c5d.sentence: - Hadoop YARN - (introduced in 2012) is a platform responsible for managing computing resources in clusters and using them for scheduling users' applications;

c61316d30ee5.title: Apache Hadoop
c61316d30ee5.sentence: - Hadoop MapReduce - an implementation of the MapReduce programming model for large-scale data processing.

5d7c7f4e60c3.title: Apache Hadoop
5d7c7f4e60c3.sentence: - Hadoop Ozone - (introduced in 2020) An object store for Hadoop

2b3ffc5093ce.title: Apache Hadoop
2b3ffc5093ce.sentence: Apache Hadoop's MapReduce and HDFS components were inspired by Google papers on MapReduce and Google File System.

9b0cea920b65.title: Apache Hadoop
9b0cea920b65.sentence: Theoretically, Hadoop could be used for any workload that is batch-oriented rather than real-time, is very data-intensive, and benefits from parallel processing.

6e40dc50e16f.title: Apache Hadoop
6e40dc50e16f.sentence: It can also be used to complement a real-time system, such as lambda architecture, Apache Storm, Flink, and Spark Streaming.

bed965b9e70f.title: Apache Hadoop
bed965b9e70f.section: Architecture > Difference between Hadoop 2 and Hadoop 3
bed965b9e70f.sentence: For example, while there is one single namenode in Hadoop 2, Hadoop 3, enables having multiple name nodes, which solves the single point of failure problem.

0d334f47c7bd.title: Apache Hadoop
0d334f47c7bd.section: Architecture > Difference between Hadoop 2 and Hadoop 3
0d334f47c7bd.sentence: One of the biggest changes is that Hadoop 3 decreases storage overhead with erasure coding.

3dc112af52cc.title: Apache Hadoop
3dc112af52cc.sentence: Search Webmap is a Hadoop application that runs on a Linux cluster with more than 10,000 cores and produced data that was used in every Yahoo! web search query.

45db00160ff8.title: Apache Hadoop
45db00160ff8.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
45db00160ff8.sentence: The Hadoop distributed file system (HDFS) is a distributed, scalable, and portable file system written in Java for the Hadoop framework.

3ac79ec1d03b.title: Apache Hadoop
3ac79ec1d03b.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
3ac79ec1d03b.sentence: HDFS stores large files (typically in the range of gigabytes to terabytes) across multiple machines.

8e41dbb2a474.title: Apache Hadoop
8e41dbb2a474.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
8e41dbb2a474.sentence: Hadoop cluster has nominally a single namenode plus a cluster of datanodes, although redundancy options are available for the namenode due to its criticality.

42b00c5fd0c8.title: Apache Hadoop
42b00c5fd0c8.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
42b00c5fd0c8.sentence: The master node can track files, manage the file system and has the metadata of all of the stored data within it.

f58085f9d574.title: Apache Hadoop
f58085f9d574.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
f58085f9d574.sentence: In particular, the name node contains the details of the number of blocks, locations of the data node that the data is stored in, where the replications are stored, and other details.

fa2a69981479.title: Apache Hadoop
fa2a69981479.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
fa2a69981479.sentence: The name node has direct contact with the client.

bee445edaedc.title: Apache Hadoop
bee445edaedc.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
bee445edaedc.sentence: Data Node: A Data Node stores data in it as blocks.

36ed4e0945aa.title: Apache Hadoop
36ed4e0945aa.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
36ed4e0945aa.sentence: It achieves reliability by replicating the data across multiple hosts, and hence theoretically does not require redundant array of independent disks (RAID) storage on hosts (but to increase input-output (I/O) performance some RAID configurations are still useful).

83dc782d4e67.title: Apache Hadoop
83dc782d4e67.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
83dc782d4e67.sentence: With the default replication value, 3, data is stored on three nodes: two on the same rack, and one on a different rack.

d1f786bdaadc.title: Apache Hadoop
d1f786bdaadc.sentence: HDFS uses this method when replicating data for data redundancy across multiple racks.

6d00b71722c6.title: Apache Hadoop
6d00b71722c6.sentence: This approach reduces the impact of a rack power outage or switch failure; if any of these hardware failures occurs, the data will remain available.

2fc1a1d3d100.title: Apache Hadoop
2fc1a1d3d100.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system
2fc1a1d3d100.sentence: Every Data node sends a Heartbeat message to the Name node every 3 seconds and conveys that it is alive.

d89069d9cfe1.title: Apache Hadoop
d89069d9cfe1.section: Architecture > File systems > Hadoop distributed file system

d7cf59ddb497.title: Apache HBase

350e847cfeae.title: Message queue
