c6ebf3ebc9ea.sentence: Trading components talk to each other via a ring buffer.

2a38bf3a44e9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-the-4-most-commonly-used-types-of-queues-in-a-single-diagram.md
2a38bf3a44e9.sentence: This is implemented in memory and super fast.

be00564102e9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-the-4-most-commonly-used-types-of-queues-in-a-single-diagram.md
be00564102e9.sentence: The elements in a priority queue have predefined priorities.

79f60ca6ff92.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-the-4-most-commonly-used-types-of-queues-in-a-single-diagram.md
79f60ca6ff92.sentence: We take the element with the highest (or lowest) priority from the queue.

2821a2fb2a1f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-the-4-most-commonly-used-types-of-queues-in-a-single-diagram.md
2821a2fb2a1f.sentence: Under the hood, it is implemented using a max heap or a min heap where the element with the largest or lowest priority is at the root of the heap.

b774bfda2aad.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-the-4-most-commonly-used-types-of-queues-in-a-single-diagram.md
b774bfda2aad.sentence: Deque is also called double-ended queue.

20f1c082e791.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-the-4-most-commonly-used-types-of-queues-in-a-single-diagram.md
20f1c082e791.sentence: The insertion and deletion can happen at both the head and the tail.

e12979b02c2c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/explaining-the-4-most-commonly-used-types-of-queues-in-a-single-diagram.md
e12979b02c2c.sentence: Deque supports both FIFO and LIFO (Last In First Out), so we can use it to implement a stack data structure.

b0cbf4f8c5d0.title: Message queue
b0cbf4f8c5d0.sentence: In computer science, message queues and mailboxes are software-engineering components typically used for inter-process communication (IPC), or for inter-thread communication within the same process.

ed4a3d18eb99.title: Message queue
ed4a3d18eb99.sentence: They use a queue for messaging – the passing of control or of content.

36af7ca405e5.title: Message queue
36af7ca405e5.sentence: Messages placed onto the queue are stored until the recipient retrieves them.

9a8187809fe2.title: Message queue
9a8187809fe2.sentence: Message queues implement an asynchronous communication pattern between two or more processes/threads whereby the sending and receiving party do not need to interact with the message queue at the same time.

8232f336f9fb.title: Message queue
8232f336f9fb.sentence: The message queue paradigm is a sibling of the publisher/subscriber pattern, and is typically one part of a larger message-oriented middleware system.

57aa86e5414b.title: Message queue
57aa86e5414b.sentence: In a typical message-queueing implementation, a system administrator installs and configures message-queueing software (a queue manager or broker), and defines a named message queue.

94140e8c4e92.title: Message queue
94140e8c4e92.sentence: An application then registers a software routine that "listens" for messages placed onto the queue.

1855a88e9b53.title: Message queue
1855a88e9b53.sentence: Second and subsequent applications may connect to the queue and transfer a message onto it.

bf57a513f666.title: Message queue
bf57a513f666.sentence: The queue-manager software stores the messages until a receiving application connects and then calls the registered software routine.

fa4e7008c6a6.title: Message queue
fa4e7008c6a6.sentence: The receiving application then processes the message in an appropriate manner.

24440055fdcf.title: Message queue
24440055fdcf.sentence: Message queues have implicit or explicit limits on the size of data that may be transmitted in a single message and the number of messages that may remain outstanding on the queue.

6b9ef4247281.title: Message queue
6b9ef4247281.sentence: Other implementations allow the passing of messages between different computer systems, potentially connecting multiple applications and multiple operating systems.

f6f4bf79bd11.title: Message queue
f6f4bf79bd11.sentence: These message queuing systems typically provide resilience functionality to ensure that messages do not get "lost" in the event of a system failure.

29705e189c2e.title: Message queue
29705e189c2e.sentence: The message queue software can be either proprietary, open source or a mix of both.

27c1290c4e3e.title: Message queue
27c1290c4e3e.sentence: It is then run either on premise in private servers or on external cloud servers (message queuing service).

ae1e313728da.title: Message-oriented middleware
ae1e313728da.sentence: Message-oriented middleware (MOM) is software or hardware infrastructure supporting sending and receiving messages between distributed systems.

fd5af55a3b51.title: Message-oriented middleware
fd5af55a3b51.sentence: MOM allows application modules to be distributed over heterogeneous platforms and reduces the complexity of developing applications that span multiple operating systems and network protocols.

b7e9a46446a4.title: Message-oriented middleware
b7e9a46446a4.sentence: The middleware creates a distributed communications layer that insulates the application developer from the details of the various operating systems and network interfaces.

9c717e69e354.title: Message-oriented middleware
9c717e69e354.sentence: This middleware layer allows software components (applications, servlets, and other components) that have been developed independently and might run on different networked platforms to interact with one another.

58470273de53.title: Message-oriented middleware
58470273de53.sentence: They are different in that RPC- and ORB-based middleware create systems of tightly coupled components, whereas MOM-based systems allow for a loose coupling of components.

7d914ef64aa2.title: Message-oriented middleware
7d914ef64aa2.sentence: In an RPC- or ORB-based system, when one procedure calls another, it must wait for the called procedure to return before it can do anything else.

73dcf97ffb66.title: Message-oriented middleware
73dcf97ffb66.sentence: Using a MOM system, a client makes an API call to send a message to a destination managed by the provider.

c6409959a81a.title: Message-oriented middleware
c6409959a81a.sentence: Once it has sent the message, the client can continue to do other work, confident that the provider retains the message until a receiving client retrieves it.

6beb38c529d0.title: Message-oriented middleware
6beb38c529d0.sentence: In asynchronous systems, message queues provide temporary storage when the destination program is busy or not connected.

57780b5da4d9.title: Message-oriented middleware
57780b5da4d9.sentence: In addition, most asynchronous MOM systems provide persistent storage to back up the message queue.

d7761a01d763.title: Message-oriented middleware
d7761a01d763.sentence: This means that the sender and receiver do not need to connect to the network at the same time (asynchronous delivery), and problems with intermittent connectivity are solved.

e5998738f57a.title: Message-oriented middleware
e5998738f57a.sentence: It also means that should the receiver application fail for any reason, the senders can continue unaffected, as the messages they send will simply accumulate in the message queue for later processing when the receiver restarts.

7a507bbe11cf.title: Message-oriented middleware
7a507bbe11cf.sentence: Central reasons for using a message-based communications protocol include its ability to store (buffer), route, or transform messages while conveying them from senders to receivers.

0adb7427d7f4.title: Message-oriented middleware
0adb7427d7f4.sentence: A MOM system with built-in intelligence can transform messages and route to match the requirements of the sender or of the recipient.

ca3a00f52ab2.title: Message-oriented middleware
ca3a00f52ab2.sentence: In conjunction with the routing and broadcast/multicast facilities, one application can send a message in its own native format, and two or more other applications may each receive a copy of the message in their own native format.

d971e35fa43d.title: Message-oriented middleware
d971e35fa43d.sentence: The primary disadvantage of many message-oriented middleware systems is that they require an extra component in the architecture, the message transfer agent (message broker).

c6f56eac41ba.title: Message-oriented middleware
c6f56eac41ba.sentence: As with any system, adding another component can lead to reductions in performance and reliability, and can also make the system as a whole more difficult and expensive to maintain.

016e023f48d6.title: Message-oriented middleware
016e023f48d6.sentence: In addition, many inter-application communications have an intrinsically synchronous aspect, with the sender specifically wanting to wait for a reply to a message before continuing (see real-time computing and near-real-time for extreme cases).

436974e16f73.title: Message-oriented middleware
436974e16f73.sentence: Because message-based communication inherently functions asynchronously, it may not fit well in such situations.

8ef6c4f5e55b.title: Message-oriented middleware
8ef6c4f5e55b.sentence: That said, most MOM systems have facilities to group a request and a response as a single pseudo-synchronous transaction.

be50e975e4cc.title: Message-oriented middleware
be50e975e4cc.sentence: In a loosely coupled asynchronous system, the calling client can continue to load work upon the recipient until the resources needed to handle this work are depleted and the called component fails.

9e766de32439.title: Message-oriented middleware
9e766de32439.sentence: Of course, these conditions can be minimized or avoided by monitoring performance and adjusting message flow, but this is work that is not needed with a synchronous messaging system.

2fdad911fbff.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
2fdad911fbff.sentence: Today, let’s discuss different delivery semantics: at-most once, at-least once, and exactly once.

bf005baa53ad.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
bf005baa53ad.sentence: As the name suggests, at-most once means a message will be delivered not more than once.

ac3839dca2e4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
ac3839dca2e4.sentence: With this data delivery semantic, it’s acceptable to deliver a message more than once, but no message should be lost.

f72901a965ee.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
f72901a965ee.sentence: Messages may be lost but are not redelivered.

129d537dc6e3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
129d537dc6e3.sentence: - It is suitable for use cases like monitoring metrics, where a small amount of data loss is acceptable.

43f0b170927e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
43f0b170927e.sentence: - With at-least once, messages won’t be lost but the same message might be delivered multiple times.

a655eaaa7979.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
a655eaaa7979.sentence: While not ideal from a user perspective, at-least once delivery semantics are usually good enough for use cases where data duplication is not a big issue or deduplication is possible on the consumer side.

41c5f2057660.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
41c5f2057660.sentence: - For example, with a unique key in each message, a message can be rejected when writing duplicate data to the database.

1472b0e2cb08.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
1472b0e2cb08.sentence: - Most message brokers offer at-least-once delivery, so consumers will eventually see duplicates.

a9ee32009948.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
a9ee32009948.sentence: Exactly once is the most difficult delivery semantic to implement.

5dbede602b30.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
5dbede602b30.sentence: It is friendly to users, but it has a high cost for the system’s performance and complexity.

be5fb9ea5c2c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
be5fb9ea5c2c.sentence: - Financial-related use cases (payment, trading, accounting, etc.).

ebab98677163.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/delivery-semantics.md
ebab98677163.sentence: Exactly once is especially important when duplication is not acceptable and the downstream service or third party doesn’t support idempotency.

14b35f963d86.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
14b35f963d86.sentence: - Scalability: Message queues make it possible to scale precisely where we need to.

612413e547bc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
612413e547bc.sentence: - Decoupling: Message queues remove dependencies between components and significantly simplify the implementation of decoupled applications.

1f4e806b8d72.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
1f4e806b8d72.sentence: - Reliability: Queues make our data persistent, and reduce the errors that happen when different parts of our system go offline.

a043b1327726.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
a043b1327726.sentence: Queues are used to effectively manage requests in large-scale distributed systems.

6f9b3bee2537.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
6f9b3bee2537.sentence: In small systems with minimal processing loads and small databases, writes can be predictably fast.

404c44721d44.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
404c44721d44.sentence: However, in more complex and large systems writes can take an almost non-deterministic amount of time.

c3009fcfea2f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
c3009fcfea2f.sentence: When workloads peak, multiple instances of our application can add all requests to the queue without the risk of collision.

79c1e6f238b5.title: Message queue
79c1e6f238b5.sentence: Historically, message queuing has used proprietary, closed protocols, restricting the ability for different operating systems or programming languages to interact in a heterogeneous set of environments.

8cbb207a2dc6.title: Message queue
8cbb207a2dc6.sentence: Three standards have emerged which are used in open source message queue implementations:

4ff2a1a92e07.title: Message queue
4ff2a1a92e07.sentence: An early attempt to make message queuing more ubiquitous was Sun Microsystems' JMS specification, which provided a Java-only abstraction of a client API.

b7072dbdbdeb.title: Message queue
b7072dbdbdeb.sentence: - Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) – feature-rich message queue protocol, approved as ISO/IEC 19464 since April 2014

13c153fc3412.title: Message queue
13c153fc3412.sentence: - Streaming Text Oriented Messaging Protocol (STOMP) – simple, text-oriented message protocol

2a0c10e5fdc3.title: Message queue
2a0c10e5fdc3.sentence: - MQTT (formerly MQ Telemetry Transport) – lightweight message queue protocol especially for embedded devices

96200526826d.title: Message queue
96200526826d.sentence: The first two operate at the same level as HTTP, MQTT at the level of TCP/IP.

2c45a8503543.title: Message queue
2c45a8503543.sentence: Some proprietary implementations also use HTTP to provide message queuing by some implementations, such as Amazon's SQS.

14e221ec1056.title: Message broker
14e221ec1056.sentence: A message broker (also known as an integration broker or interface engine) is an intermediary computer program module that translates a message from the formal messaging protocol of the sender to the formal messaging protocol of the receiver.

20d6c0dedea7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
20d6c0dedea7.sentence: A message broker is a software that enables applications, systems, and services to communicate with each other and exchange information.

8efee6b0deca.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
8efee6b0deca.sentence: Message brokers can validate, store, route, and deliver messages to the appropriate destinations.

aa14a142d348.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
aa14a142d348.sentence: The message broker does this by translating messages between formal messaging protocols.

8e284f0bdd5c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
8e284f0bdd5c.sentence: This allows interdependent services to "talk" with one another directly, even if they were written in different languages or implemented on different platforms.

6c669e5633d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
6c669e5633d4.sentence: They serve as intermediaries between other applications, allowing senders to issue messages without knowing where the receivers are, whether or not they are active, or how many of them there are.

2c591da98f0e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
2c591da98f0e.sentence: This facilitates the decoupling of processes and services within systems.

22740e7209b9.title: Message broker
22740e7209b9.sentence: It mediates communication among applications, minimizing the mutual awareness that applications should have of each other in order to be able to exchange messages, effectively implementing decoupling.

780a0443d7ba.title: Message broker
780a0443d7ba.sentence: For example, a message broker may be used to manage a workload queue or message queue for multiple receivers, providing reliable storage, guaranteed message delivery and perhaps transaction management.

4ba7af699d85.title: Message broker
4ba7af699d85.sentence: - Route messages to one or more destinations

035ae10a832c.title: Message broker
035ae10a832c.sentence: - Transform messages to an alternative representation

d8441262295b.title: Message broker
d8441262295b.sentence: - Provide content and topic-based message routing using the publish–subscribe pattern

f9280770ef95.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
f9280770ef95.sentence: Message brokers offer two basic message distribution patterns or messaging styles:

baeafef63acd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
baeafef63acd.sentence: - Point-to-Point messaging: This is the distribution pattern utilized in message queues with a one-to-one relationship between the message's sender and receiver.

776778dc4e04.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
776778dc4e04.sentence: - Publish-Subscribe messaging: In this message distribution pattern, often referred to as "pub/sub", the producer of each message publishes it to a topic, and multiple message consumers subscribe to topics from which they want to receive messages.

24a18375300c.title: Message broker
24a18375300c.sentence: Message brokers are generally based on one of two fundamental architectures: hub-and-spoke and message bus.

e7be416a64b1.title: Message broker
e7be416a64b1.sentence: In the first, a central server acts as the mechanism that provides integration services, whereas with the latter, the message broker is a communication backbone or distributed service that acts on the bus.

48a53c24c7a6.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
48a53c24c7a6.sentence: The Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) is an open standard application layer protocol for message-oriented middleware.

c48d74c5ab3b.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
c48d74c5ab3b.sentence: Unlike JMS, which defines an API and a set of behaviors that a messaging implementation must provide, AMQP is a wire-level protocol.

c2908fe9983a.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
c2908fe9983a.sentence: A wire-level protocol is a description of the format of the data that is sent across the network as a stream of bytes.

6728398a3260.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
6728398a3260.sentence: Consequently, any tool that can create and interpret messages that conform to this data format can interoperate with any other compliant tool irrespective of implementation language.

875e0dc7afa1.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
875e0dc7afa1.sentence: Previous standardizations of middleware have happened at the API level (e.g. JMS) and were focused on standardizing programmer interaction with different middleware implementations, rather than on providing interoperability between multiple implementations.

aff579f3c699.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
aff579f3c699.sentence: The defining features of AMQP are message orientation, queuing, routing (including point-to-point and publish-and-subscribe), reliability and security.

b7063caf98c4.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
b7063caf98c4.sentence: AMQP is a binary application layer protocol, designed to efficiently support a wide variety of messaging applications and communication patterns.

e1ff1f057d1a.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
e1ff1f057d1a.sentence: It assumes an underlying reliable transport layer protocol such as Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).

3b380b9c5a73.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
3b380b9c5a73.sentence: It provides flow controlled, message-oriented communication with message-delivery guarantees such as at-most-once (where each message is delivered once or never), at-least-once (where each message is certain to be delivered, but may do so multiple times) and exactly-once (where the message will always certainly arrive and do so only once), and authentication and/or encryption based on SASL and/or TLS.

677333b28f99.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
677333b28f99.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
677333b28f99.sentence: The link protocol is at the heart of AMQP.

e2344f30da3e.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
e2344f30da3e.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
e2344f30da3e.sentence: Messages are sent over an established link using the transfer frame.

b175e88c8ec0.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
b175e88c8ec0.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
b175e88c8ec0.sentence: Messages on a link flow in only one direction.

778ad07fbd71.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
778ad07fbd71.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
778ad07fbd71.sentence: Transfers are subject to a credit-based flow control scheme, managed using flow frames.

bd54983a8cf4.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
bd54983a8cf4.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
bd54983a8cf4.sentence: This allows a process to protect itself from being overwhelmed by too large a volume of messages or more simply to allow a subscribing link to pull messages as and when desired.

69e1a263f41f.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
69e1a263f41f.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
69e1a263f41f.sentence: Each transferred message must eventually be settled.

81b6f7da3352.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
81b6f7da3352.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
81b6f7da3352.sentence: Settlement ensures that the sender and receiver agree on the state of the transfer, providing reliability guarantees.

5f0aaf0473ac.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
5f0aaf0473ac.section: Description of AMQP 1.0 > Performatives and the link protocol
5f0aaf0473ac.sentence: Various reliability guarantees can be enforced this way: at-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once.

a9246abfdc22.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
a9246abfdc22.sentence: AMQP defines as the bare message, that part of the message that is created by the sending application.

2a16a55c138f.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
2a16a55c138f.sentence: This is considered immutable as the message is transferred between one or more processes.

7bcedb82ed97.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
7bcedb82ed97.sentence: Ensuring the message as sent by the application is immutable allows for end-to-end message signing and/or encryption and ensures that any integrity checks (e.g. hashes or digests) remain valid.

8934c7c2838f.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
8934c7c2838f.sentence: The message can be annotated by intermediaries during transit, but any such annotations are kept distinct from the immutable bare message.

2b68db9b9c86.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
2b68db9b9c86.sentence: The header is a standard set of delivery-related annotations that can be requested or indicated for a message and includes time to live, durability, priority.

30fc6108b6c3.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
30fc6108b6c3.sentence: A key category is those nodes used as a rendezvous point between senders and receivers of messages (e.g. queues or topics).

db6109d50f73.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
db6109d50f73.sentence: The AMQP specification calls such nodes distribution nodes and codifies some common behaviors.

c651fc6b71e3.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
c651fc6b71e3.sentence: - some standard outcomes for transfers, through which receivers of messages can for example accept or reject messages

9c9604a4645f.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
9c9604a4645f.sentence: - a mechanism for indicating or requesting one of the two basic distribution patterns, competing- and non-competing- consumers, through the distribution modes move and copy respectively

5749de9f25d5.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
5749de9f25d5.sentence: - the ability to refine the set of message of interest to a receiver through filters

85217b2db519.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
85217b2db519.sentence: - the ability to create nodes on-demand, e.g. for temporary response queues

c3787a400aea.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
c3787a400aea.sentence: AMQP protocol version 1.0 is the current specification version.

fb73e1d369a7.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
fb73e1d369a7.sentence: It focuses on core features which are necessary for interoperability at Internet scale.

867a0c77957c.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
867a0c77957c.sentence: It contains less explicit routing than previous versions because core functionality is the first to be rigorously standardized.

1db4bd7f0128.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
1db4bd7f0128.sentence: Earlier versions of AMQP, published prior to the release of 1.0 (see History above) and significantly different from it, include:

dce22b61e1d8.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
dce22b61e1d8.sentence: - Apache Qpid, an open-source project at the Apache Foundation

c5783a594552.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
c5783a594552.sentence: - Apache ActiveMQ, an open-source project at the Apache Foundation

61eeff16ae61.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
61eeff16ae61.sentence: - Solace PubSub+, a multi-protocol broker in hardware, software, and cloud

90faae0a346f.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
90faae0a346f.sentence: - RabbitMQ, an open-source project sponsored by VMware, supports AMQP 1.0 with release 4.0

3373611bcff1.title: RabbitMQ
3373611bcff1.sentence: RabbitMQ is an open-source message-broker software (sometimes called message-oriented middleware) that originally implemented the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) and has since been extended with a plug-in architecture to support Streaming Text Oriented Messaging Protocol (STOMP), MQ Telemetry Transport (MQTT), and other protocols.

9d62cf3f26b1.title: RabbitMQ
9d62cf3f26b1.sentence: Written in Erlang, the RabbitMQ server is built on the Open Telecom Platform framework for clustering and failover.

5de698d6338c.title: RabbitMQ
5de698d6338c.sentence: Client libraries to interface with the broker are available for all major programming languages.

b76a13543cab.title: RabbitMQ
b76a13543cab.sentence: - A "Shovel" plug-in that takes care of moving or copying (replicating) messages from one broker to another.

2053568d1e33.title: RabbitMQ
2053568d1e33.sentence: - A "Federation" plug-in that enables efficient sharing of messages between brokers (at the exchange level).

232f69f2a56c.title: Message queue

3ae9a0fa9703.title: Message queue

c3eae2a7c047.title: Message queue

8ca662f27b43.title: Message queue

dc7645132e4c.title: Message queue

de8a2b6eb8f1.title: Message queue
de8a2b6eb8f1.sentence: One is part of the SYS V API, the other one is part of POSIX.

7f4a7fc077df.title: Message queue

42a72a62d728.title: Message queue
42a72a62d728.sentence: It is distinct from the SYS V API, but provides similar function.

f496ec6e369d.title: Message queue
f496ec6e369d.sentence: Blocking receive puts the child to sleep if it cannot find a requested message type.

1e790ab34cca.title: Message queue
1e790ab34cca.sentence: It sleeps until another message is posted in the queue, and then wakes up to check again.

0f56f213dbaa.title: Message queue

51aee0800574.title: Message queue

4064bd387583.title: Message queue

c479dec2a1e2.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
c479dec2a1e2.sentence: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) is a distributed message queuing service introduced by Amazon.com as a beta in late 2004, and generally available in mid 2006.

7d856ed3155f.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
7d856ed3155f.sentence: The service supports both unlimited queues and message traffic.

05a3e50d8d2e.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
05a3e50d8d2e.sentence: Messages can be of any type, and the data contained within is not restricted.

d2ad9118fce9.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
d2ad9118fce9.sentence: Amazon SQS FIFO sessions are queue-based messaging systems that provide ordering guarantees within a message group or session attempt but do not necessarily guarantee ordered delivery in cases of retries or failures.

2d9461708fd6.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
2d9461708fd6.sentence: In SQS FIFO, messages in the same message group are processed in order, with subsequent messages held until the preceding message is successfully processed or moved to the dead-letter queue (DLQ).

3c00e92a5be8.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
3c00e92a5be8.sentence: Message bodies were initially limited to 8KB in size but was later raised to 64KB on 2010-07-01 and then 256KB on 2013-06-18.

9ec32bd9fd7e.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
9ec32bd9fd7e.sentence: For larger messages, the user has a few options to get around this limitation.

5d02891531c3.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
5d02891531c3.sentence: A large message can be split into multiple segments that are sent separately, or the message data can be stored using Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) or Amazon DynamoDB with just a pointer to the data transmitted in the SQS message.

5a8e707eeabc.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
5a8e707eeabc.sentence: Amazon has made an Extended Client Library available for this purpose.

c4a8f61b494f.title: Dead letter queue
c4a8f61b494f.sentence: In message queueing a dead letter queue (DLQ), or dead letter topic (DLT) in some messaging systems, is a service implementation to store messages that the messaging system cannot or should not deliver.

211786b1e778.title: Dead letter queue
211786b1e778.sentence: Although implementation-specific, messages can be routed to the DLQ for the following reasons:

764c43fd7bac.title: Dead letter queue
764c43fd7bac.sentence: - The message is sent to a queue that does not exist.

b655d7785de2.title: Dead letter queue
b655d7785de2.sentence: - The message expires because it reached the TTL (time to live)

699010a994dc.title: Dead letter queue
699010a994dc.sentence: - The message is rejected by another queue exchange.

e6010f4a6ccf.title: Dead letter queue
e6010f4a6ccf.sentence: - The message has been read and rejected too many times.

dbd5b6c6772d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
dbd5b6c6772d.sentence: A dead-letter queue is a queue to which other queues can send messages that can't be processed successfully.

071ad4b8bc08.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
071ad4b8bc08.sentence: This makes it easy to set them aside for further inspection without blocking the queue processing or spending CPU cycles on a message that might never be consumed successfully.

64edd0950e4c.title: Dead letter queue
64edd0950e4c.sentence: Routing these messages to a dead letter queue enables analysis of common fault patterns and potential software problems.

f2f3310d0ed1.title: Dead letter queue
f2f3310d0ed1.sentence: If a message consumer receives a message that it considers invalid, it can instead forward it an Invalid Message Channel, allowing a separation between application-level faults and delivery failures.

b489be0a7bcf.title: Dead letter queue
b489be0a7bcf.sentence: Management of dead letter queues typically involves monitoring and alert systems.

6d92665b40e2.title: Dead letter queue
6d92665b40e2.sentence: Organizations may implement specialized handlers for automated remediation or manual processing of DLQ messages.

bb35e5884d30.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
bb35e5884d30.sentence: Once a message is placed in the DLQ, it is no longer retried, creating a gap in the sequence.

416dff658a02.title: Amazon Simple Queue Service
416dff658a02.sentence: However, the remaining messages continue to be delivered in order.

e9de16d23524.title: Dead letter queue
e9de16d23524.sentence: Queueing systems that incorporate dead letter queues include Amazon EventBridge, Amazon Simple Queue Service, Apache ActiveMQ, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, HornetQ, Microsoft Message Queuing, Microsoft Azure Event Grid and Azure Service Bus, WebSphere MQ, Solace Platform, Rabbit MQ, Confluent Cloud and Apache Pulsar.

bfa0b81a5db9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
bfa0b81a5db9.sentence: When duplicates can't be tolerated, FIFO (first-in-first-out) message queues will make sure that each message is delivered exactly once (and only once) by filtering out duplicates automatically.

1a2f5deb65ac.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
1a2f5deb65ac.sentence: Most message queues provide best-effort ordering which ensures that messages are generally delivered in the same order as they're sent and that a message is delivered at least once.

e20faa1eb560.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues
e20faa1eb560.sentence: In these queues, the oldest (or first) entry, sometimes called the "head" of the queue, is processed first.

b70c42a28501.sentence: Poison pills are special messages that can be received, but not processed.

528975291f37.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues

46dd0673dfd8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-queues

490b13a9e24d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers

66744d42a6b2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
66744d42a6b2.sentence: Designed for use with high volumes of messages, event streaming platforms are readily scalable.

70c97c1ea444.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
70c97c1ea444.sentence: Unlike message brokers, however, event streaming platforms cannot guarantee message delivery or track which consumers have received the messages.

fedd8a74816b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
fedd8a74816b.sentence: Event streaming platforms offer more scalability than message brokers but fewer features that ensure fault tolerance like message resending, as well as more limited message routing and queueing capabilities.

39048efed2c9.title: MQTT
39048efed2c9.sentence: These are classified in increasing order of overhead:

87538845035f.title: MQTT
87538845035f.sentence: The OASIS MQTT specification provides ordering guarantees only within a single client session on a single topic; events originating from separate clients or generated across independent connections may be delivered out of sequence.

8d55e05617f0.title: Message-oriented middleware
8d55e05617f0.sentence: The Java EE programming environment provides a standard API called Java Message Service (JMS), which is implemented by most MOM vendors and aims to hide the particular MOM API implementations; however, JMS does not define the format of the messages that are exchanged, so JMS systems are not interoperable.

51d2cab13acb.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
51d2cab13acb.sentence: On the other hand, AMQP is a wire-level protocol specification.

b2c8ded999df.title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
b2c8ded999df.sentence: In theory AMQP provides interoperability as different AMQP-compliant software can be deployed on the client and server sides.

87cf7a780ec4.title: MQTT
87cf7a780ec4.sentence: It is designed for connections with remote locations that have devices with resource constraints or limited network bandwidth, such as in the Internet of things (IoT).

91f71a1005c3.title: MQTT
91f71a1005c3.sentence: The MQTT specification defines communication between a client and a single broker and does not specify communication between brokers.

3c8935c1aaef.title: MQTT
3c8935c1aaef.sentence: Deployments that need more capacity or availability than a single broker provides rely on implementation-specific mechanisms.

80b21df8c895.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
80b21df8c895.sentence: An Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) is an architectural pattern whereby a centralized software component performs integrations between applications.

c7645de63e3f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
c7645de63e3f.sentence: It performs transformations of data models, handles connectivity, performs message routing, converts communication protocols, and potentially manages the composition of multiple requests.

262ff0b0c41c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
262ff0b0c41c.sentence: The ESB can make these integrations and transformations available as a service interface for reuse by new applications.

eafdc9e49784.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
eafdc9e49784.sentence: In theory, a centralized ESB offers the potential to standardize and dramatically simplify communication, messaging, and integration between services across the enterprise.

a01be81dacb6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
a01be81dacb6.sentence: - Simpler, more cost-effective scalability: Components can be scaled independently of others.

c540e4176f87.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
c540e4176f87.sentence: - Greater resilience: Failure of one component does not impact the others, and each microservice can adhere to its own availability requirements without risking the availability of other components in the system.

cef2c93f6f94.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
cef2c93f6f94.sentence: While ESBs were deployed successfully in many organizations, in many other organizations the ESB came to be seen as a bottleneck.

c8c8dc0e6045.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
c8c8dc0e6045.sentence: - A single point of failure can bring down all communications.

1fbcd742843f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::enterprise-service-bus-esb
1fbcd742843f.sentence: - Making changes or enhancements to one integration could destabilize others who use that same integration.

0977648711bc.sentence: Whereas message brokers are a "lightweight" alternative to ESBs that provide similar functionality, a mechanism for inter-service communication, at a lower cost.

1adfde090147.sentence: We can also use long-polling to allow pulls to wait a specified amount of time for new messages to arrive.

0a4c14494a8e.sentence: Pub/Sub messaging instantly pushes asynchronous event notifications when messages are published to the message topic.

d4f4f6de86aa.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
d4f4f6de86aa.sentence: - Eliminate Polling: Message topics allow instantaneous, push-based delivery, eliminating the need for message consumers to periodically check or "poll" for new information and updates.

c380dcabe618.title: Message queue
c380dcabe618.sentence: The Competing Consumers pattern enables multiple concurrent consumers to process messages on the same message queue.

ab46fc778913.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
ab46fc778913.sentence: This pattern enables multiple concurrent consumers to process messages received on the same messaging channel.

2cdeaee6b586.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
2cdeaee6b586.sentence: There is no need to configure complex coordination between the consumers.

02c18d889b15.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
02c18d889b15.sentence: However, this pattern cannot guarantee message ordering.

827af63b76be.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
827af63b76be.sentence: This pattern aims at providing determinism for long-running backend tasks.

71e97d69315d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
71e97d69315d.sentence: This pattern solves the transmision of large messages.

1df9da093d4a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
1df9da093d4a.sentence: It decouples backend processing from frontend clients.

4d0c4da7de7b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
4d0c4da7de7b.sentence: The API returns an HTTP 202 (Accepted) status code, acknowledging that the request has been received for processing.

7cea02ef826d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
7cea02ef826d.sentence: This pattern targets decoupling senders from consumers, and avoiding blocking the sender to wait for a response.

073d63cbb352.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
073d63cbb352.sentence: It stores the whole message payload into a database and transmits only the reference to the message, which will be used later to retrieve the payload from the database.

75a5fc703ec5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/top-6-cloud-messaging-patterns.md
75a5fc703ec5.sentence: This pattern prioritizes requests sent to services so that requests with a higher priority are received and processed more quickly than those with a lower priority.

8fabdb44f991.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
8fabdb44f991.sentence: In software architecture, the publish–subscribe pattern (pub/sub) is a messaging pattern in which message senders, called publishers, categorize messages into classes (or topics), and send them without needing to know which components will receive them.

891fca8f29ad.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
891fca8f29ad.sentence: Message recipients, called subscribers, express interest in one or more classes and only receive messages in those classes, without needing to know the identity of the publishers.

a322ff96b22c.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
a322ff96b22c.sentence: This pattern decouples the components that produce messages from those that consume them, and supports asynchronous, many-to-many communication.

2ce91fa76787.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
2ce91fa76787.sentence: In a pub/sub model, any message published to a topic is pushed immediately to all the subscribers of the topic.

3000b0160c5d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
3000b0160c5d.sentence: The subscribers to the message topic often perform different functions, and can each do something different with the message in parallel.

254a4c5c2ff4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
254a4c5c2ff4.sentence: Unlike message queues, which batch messages until they are retrieved, message topics transfer messages with little or no queuing and push them out immediately to all subscribers.

4784b4aeea7a.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
4784b4aeea7a.sentence: The publish–subscribe model is commonly contrasted with message queue-based and point-to-point messaging models, where producers send messages directly to consumers.

fef13afbc5bf.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
fef13afbc5bf.sentence: Many modern messaging frameworks and protocols, such as the Java Message Service (JMS), Apache Kafka, and MQTT, support both the pub/sub and queue-based models.

2c6f3bc5d74e.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
2c6f3bc5d74e.sentence: This pattern provides greater network scalability and supports more dynamic topologies, but can make it harder to modify the publisher’s logic or the structure of the published data.

078c0768c352.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
078c0768c352.sentence: Compared to synchronous patterns like RPC and point-to-point messaging, publish–subscribe provides the highest level of decoupling among architectural components.

be2595ab7748.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
be2595ab7748.sentence: However, it can also lead to semantic or format coupling between publishers and subscribers, which may cause systems to become entangled or brittle over time.

f766480d64d6.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
f766480d64d6.sentence: Although the publish–subscribe pattern is now typically distinguished from the observer pattern due to its emphasis on decoupling and distributed communication, early usage in literature and systems sometimes used the terms interchangeably, especially in the context of in-process event handling or GUI frameworks.

224aef93536b.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
224aef93536b.sentence: As distributed systems became more common, the publish–subscribe model evolved to emphasize asynchronous messaging and broker-mediated communication, setting it apart from the more tightly coupled observer pattern.

e22f19e4564a.title: MQTT
e22f19e4564a.sentence: MQTT is a lightweight, publish–subscribe, machine-to-machine network protocol for message queueing/message queueing services.

60e6e4034e6b.title: MQTT
60e6e4034e6b.sentence: It must run over a transport protocol that provides ordered, lossless, bi-directional connections—typically, TCP/IP.

cf952bc9d4bc.title: MQTT
cf952bc9d4bc.sentence: However, the protocol provides publish-and-subscribe messaging (no queues, in spite of the name).

1f585902efd9.title: MQTT
1f585902efd9.sentence: The MQTT protocol defines two types of network entities: a message broker and a number of clients.

c73f80b27540.title: MQTT
c73f80b27540.sentence: An MQTT broker is a server that receives messages from publishing clients and then routes the messages to the appropriate destination clients.

a20f532369a4.title: MQTT
a20f532369a4.sentence: Information is organized in a hierarchy of topics.

d0f9638290b5.title: MQTT
d0f9638290b5.sentence: The publisher does not need to have any data on the number or locations of subscribers; and subscribers, in turn, do not have to be configured with any data about the publishers.

918bf5d8fe0b.title: MQTT
918bf5d8fe0b.sentence: With the MQTT broker architecture, the client devices and server application become decoupled.

7368f152ee3a.title: MQTT
7368f152ee3a.sentence: If a broker receives a message on a topic for which there are no current subscribers, the broker discards the message unless the publisher of the message designated the message as a retained message.

0623bc47665a.title: MQTT
0623bc47665a.sentence: The broker stores the last retained message and the corresponding quality of service (QoS) for the selected topic.

0d1845035009.title: MQTT
0d1845035009.sentence: Each client that subscribes to a topic pattern that matches the topic of the retained message receives the retained message immediately after they subscribe.

5b6c45ddcdfe.title: MQTT
5b6c45ddcdfe.sentence: The broker stores only one retained message per topic.

6559281bcedb.title: MQTT
6559281bcedb.sentence: When a publishing client first connects to the broker, it can set up a default message to be sent to subscribers if the broker detects that the publishing client has unexpectedly disconnected from the broker.

3dd8fe3710b9.title: MQTT
3dd8fe3710b9.sentence: Each connection to the broker can specify a QoS measure.

e71766b8ca6f.title: MQTT
e71766b8ca6f.sentence: - At most once – the message is sent only once and the client and broker take no additional steps to acknowledge delivery (fire and forget).

94a40bf75132.title: MQTT
94a40bf75132.sentence: - At least once – the message is re-tried by the sender multiple times until acknowledgement is received (acknowledged delivery).

2f217e34754c.title: MQTT
2f217e34754c.sentence: - Exactly once – the sender and receiver engage in a two-level handshake to ensure only one copy of the message is received (assured delivery).

4470cb24e955.title: MQTT
4470cb24e955.sentence: This field does not affect handling of the underlying TCP data transmissions; it is only used between MQTT senders and receivers.

02f88fe85ada.title: MQTT
02f88fe85ada.sentence: The broker keeps track of all the session's information as the device goes on and off, in a function called "persistent sessions".

922e3d40939b.title: MQTT
922e3d40939b.sentence: In this state, a broker will store both connection info for each client, topics each client has subscribed to, and any messages for a topic with a QoS of 1 or 2.

e9162843ae56.title: MQTT
e9162843ae56.sentence: The two common approaches are bridging, in which one broker connects to another broker as a client and forwards messages for selected topics, and clustering, in which a group of broker nodes shares subscription and session state and appears to clients as a single logical broker.

ced180e6af55.title: MQTT
ced180e6af55.sentence: MQTT does not guarantee that messages published by independent clients arrive at subscribers in the order they were generated.

424d6c48d81d.title: MQTT
424d6c48d81d.sentence: Commonly applied mitigations include debounce windows (delaying action on disconnect events for a fixed interval to allow late-arriving messages to be processed), polling or re-query patterns, and application-layer sequence numbering.

6dac6e536673.title: MQTT
6dac6e536673.sentence: Each mitigation imposes trade-offs: debounce windows introduce detection latency for genuine disconnect events and may suppress legitimate notifications; polling adds network overhead and is unsuitable for passive sensors.

74d51cdaad42.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
74d51cdaad42.sentence: Publishers are loosely coupled to subscribers, and need not even know of their existence.

73f9582a3ecb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
73f9582a3ecb.sentence: Subscribers can change, upgrade, multiply or disappear and the system dynamically adjusts.

c82f2225b1b6.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
c82f2225b1b6.sentence: With the topic being the focus, publishers and subscribers are allowed to remain ignorant of system topology.

f09eb0b070f6.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
f09eb0b070f6.sentence: Each can continue to operate as per normal independently of the other.

a7f70717f37a.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
a7f70717f37a.sentence: Many pub/sub systems decouple not only the locations of the publishers and subscribers but also decouple them temporally.

126c193ea0f1.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
126c193ea0f1.sentence: In the traditional tightly coupled client–server paradigm, the client cannot post messages to the server while the server process is not running, nor can the server receive messages unless the client is running.

1b6e8f7a8ac9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
1b6e8f7a8ac9.sentence: This promotes faster response time and reduces the delivery latency which can be particularly problematic in systems where delays cannot be tolerated.

aa1a2c888afd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
aa1a2c888afd.sentence: Instead of maintaining a roster of peers where an application can send messages, a publisher will simply post messages to a topic.

349283c00917.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
349283c00917.sentence: Then, any interested party will subscribe its endpoint to the topic, and start receiving these messages.

4f55583b839e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
4f55583b839e.sentence: - Decoupled and Independent Scaling: Publishers and subscribers are decoupled and work independently from each other, which allows us to develop and scale them independently.

54c6bda2ecab.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
54c6bda2ecab.sentence: Pub/sub provides the opportunity for better scalability than traditional client-server, through parallel operation, message caching, tree-based or network-based routing, etc. However, in certain types of tightly coupled, high-volume enterprise environments, as systems scale up to become data centers with thousands of servers sharing the pub/sub infrastructure, current vendor systems often lose this benefit; scalability for pub/sub products under high load in these contexts is a research challenge.

fb5effe8a34f.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
fb5effe8a34f.sentence: Redundant subscribers in a pub/sub system can help assure message delivery with minimal additional complexity.

5b23da86b4a3.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
5b23da86b4a3.sentence: In a pub/sub system, redundant logging subscribers that are exact duplicates of the existing logger can be added to the system to increase logging reliability without any impact to any other equipment on the system.

00dd0bd17e45.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
00dd0bd17e45.sentence: Outside of the enterprise environment, on the other hand, the pub/sub paradigm has proven its scalability to volumes far beyond those of a single data center, providing Internet-wide distributed messaging through web syndication protocols such as RSS and Atom.

e2612f793451.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
e2612f793451.sentence: These syndication protocols accept higher latency and lack of delivery guarantees in exchange for the ability for even a low-end web server to syndicate messages to (potentially) millions of separate subscriber nodes.

d2aeb6e32547.title: Observer pattern
d2aeb6e32547.sentence: In software design and software engineering, the observer pattern is a software design pattern in which an object, called the subject (also known as event source or event stream), maintains a list of its dependents, called observers (also known as event sinks), and automatically notifies them of any state changes, typically by calling one of their methods.

32d784098b89.title: Observer pattern
32d784098b89.sentence: - A one-to-many dependency between objects should be defined without making the objects tightly coupled.

559bb0909017.title: Observer pattern
559bb0909017.sentence: - The responsibility of observers is to register and unregister themselves with a subject (in order to be notified of state changes) and to update their state (to synchronize it with the subject's state) when they are notified.

639cb044a06b.title: Observer pattern
639cb044a06b.sentence: The subject only needs to know that observers implement the update() method—it has no knowledge of observers' concrete types or internal implementation details.

92dc321109e5.title: Observer pattern
92dc321109e5.sentence: Observers can be added and removed independently at run time.

22a4a3a97756.title: Observer pattern
22a4a3a97756.sentence: Unlike the publish-subscribe pattern, there is no intermediary broker; the subject and observers have direct references to each other.

ed42195ba25c.title: Observer pattern
ed42195ba25c.sentence: This pattern creates a one-to-many dependency where multiple observers can listen to a single subject, but the coupling is typically synchronous and direct—the subject calls observer methods when changes occur, though asynchronous implementations using event queues are possible.

069611c1ffff.title: Observer pattern
069611c1ffff.sentence: It is commonly used to implement event handling systems in event-driven programming, particularly in-process systems like GUI toolkits or MVC frameworks.

83e1e72b992b.title: Observer pattern
83e1e72b992b.sentence: The observer pattern and the publish–subscribe pattern are closely related and often confused, as both support one-to-many communication between components.

e91d4a77f65f.title: Observer pattern
e91d4a77f65f.sentence: Coupling | Tightly coupled — the subject holds direct references to its observers via a standardized interface. | Loosely coupled — publishers and subscribers are unaware of each other.

18a853e01202.title: Observer pattern
18a853e01202.sentence: Scalability | Suitable for in-process systems like GUI toolkits. | More scalable; supports distributed systems and asynchronous messaging.

87dea0533e33.title: Observer pattern
87dea0533e33.sentence: Filtering | Limited — observers receive all events and filter internally. | Rich filtering — brokers may filter by topic, content, or rules.

3b16f832aff4.title: Observer pattern
3b16f832aff4.sentence: Fault Tolerance | Observer failures can affect the subject. | Failures are isolated; the broker decouples participants.

1454710b0e92.title: Observer pattern
1454710b0e92.sentence: To reduce this coupling, publish–subscribe systems introduce a message broker or event bus that intermediates between publishers and subscribers.

e491015028b6.title: Observer pattern
e491015028b6.sentence: The observer pattern, as formalized in Design Patterns, deliberately omits concerns such as unsubscription, notification filtering, delivery guarantees, and message logging.

4a5811400c91.title: Observer pattern
4a5811400c91.sentence: These advanced capabilities are typically implemented in robust message queuing systems, where the observer pattern may serve as a foundational mechanism but is not sufficient by itself.

64c14f9b5970.title: NATS Messaging
64c14f9b5970.sentence: NATS ("Neural Autonomic Transport System") is an open-source messaging system developed under the stewardship of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation.

de945826e086.title: NATS Messaging
de945826e086.sentence: The NATS server is written in the Go programming language.

b4e73d5618c7.title: NATS Messaging
b4e73d5618c7.sentence: Client libraries to interface with the server are available for dozens of major programming languages.

a25249c90bdc.title: NATS Messaging
a25249c90bdc.sentence: The core design principles of NATS are performance, scalability, and ease of use.

f3a9749761ac.title: NATS Messaging
f3a9749761ac.sentence: - The NATS Server - The core Publish-Subscribe Server for NATS.

f4b8fe70be21.title: NATS Messaging
f4b8fe70be21.sentence: The NATS server is often referred to as either 'Core NATS' or NATS with 'JetStream'. 'Core NATS' is the set of core NATS functionalities and qualities of service. 'JetStream' is the (optionally enabled) built-in persistence layer that adds streaming, queues, at-least-once and exactly-once delivery guarantees, historical data replay, decoupled flow-control and key/value store functionalities to Core NATS.

261960b96740.title: NATS Messaging
261960b96740.sentence: JetStream replaced the old STAN (NATS Streaming) approach.

8ac7d492cf16.title: Raft (algorithm)
8ac7d492cf16.sentence: - NATS Messaging uses the Raft consensus algorithm for Jetstream cluster management and data replication

1cfca3f7a5de.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
1cfca3f7a5de.sentence: The most serious problems with pub/sub systems are a side-effect of their main advantage: the decoupling of publisher from subscriber.

7dcfe100c0dd.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
7dcfe100c0dd.sentence: A pub/sub system must be designed carefully to be able to provide stronger system properties that a particular application might require, such as assured delivery.

2b81c0d74165.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
2b81c0d74165.sentence: - The broker in a pub/sub system may be designed to deliver messages for a specified time, but then stop attempting delivery, whether or not it has received confirmation of successful receipt of the message by all subscribers.

b23f0a97c8d8.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
b23f0a97c8d8.sentence: A pub/sub system designed in this way cannot guarantee delivery of messages to any applications that might require such assured delivery.

68f62ac3bdf7.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
68f62ac3bdf7.sentence: Tighter coupling of the designs of such a publisher and subscriber pair must be enforced outside of the pub/sub architecture to accomplish such assured delivery (e.g. by requiring the subscriber to publish receipt messages).

eceb0b1cd02e.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
eceb0b1cd02e.sentence: - A publisher in a pub/sub system may assume that a subscriber is listening, when in fact it is not.

083ed69408a1.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
083ed69408a1.sentence: If the logger fails (crashes), equipment problem publishers won't necessarily receive notice of the logger failure, and error messages will not be displayed or recorded by any equipment on the pub/sub system.

2fe2eb89358a.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
2fe2eb89358a.sentence: The pub/sub pattern scales well for small networks with a small number of publisher and subscriber nodes and low message volume.

52e73c9c0795.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
52e73c9c0795.sentence: However, as the number of nodes and messages grows, the likelihood of instabilities increases, limiting the maximum scalability of a pub/sub network.

83ef50fb9f36.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
83ef50fb9f36.sentence: - Load surges—periods when subscriber requests saturate network throughput followed by periods of low message volume (underutilized network bandwidth)

d2fb754197b6.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
d2fb754197b6.sentence: - Slowdowns—as more and more applications use the system (even if they are communicating on separate pub/sub channels) the message volume flow to an individual subscriber will slow

f414f6929637.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
f414f6929637.sentence: Brokers themselves could be overloaded as they allocate resources to track created subscriptions.

e890ccfe7396.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
e890ccfe7396.sentence: Brokers might be fooled into sending notifications to the wrong client, amplifying denial of service requests against the client.

13ded135001a.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
13ded135001a.sentence: Encryption (e.g. Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS)) can prevent unauthorized access, but cannot prevent damaging messages from being introduced by authorized publishers.

e8e6d9aa43eb.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
e8e6d9aa43eb.sentence: In publish–subscribe systems, subscribers typically receive only a subset of messages.

0b93bac82a03.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
0b93bac82a03.sentence: The process of selecting relevant messages is called filtering, and it can be implemented in several ways:

51fab9ca570d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
51fab9ca570d.sentence: This feature empowers the subscriber to create a message filtering policy so that it will only get the notifications it is interested in, as opposed to receiving every single message posted to the topic.

743e1986c7ff.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
743e1986c7ff.sentence: - Topic-based filtering: Messages are published to named topics or channels.

9c46fce033ab.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
9c46fce033ab.sentence: Subscribers register to receive messages on specific topics, and receive all messages published to them.

a1a37762548b.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
a1a37762548b.sentence: - Content-based filtering: Subscribers define constraints based on message attributes or content.

b19900644210.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
b19900644210.sentence: Messages are delivered only if they match the subscriber's criteria.

6f3f48c2e079.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
6f3f48c2e079.sentence: - Hybrid systems: Some implementations combine topic- and content-based filtering.

e4c5f40b49c9.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
e4c5f40b49c9.sentence: Messages are categorized by topic, and subscribers apply content-based filters to messages within those topics.

344f8ffadf4e.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
344f8ffadf4e.sentence: In most pub/sub systems, publishers and subscribers communicate through a central intermediary such as a message broker or event bus.

31d1cbc7c2d8.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
31d1cbc7c2d8.sentence: Some pub/sub systems use brokerless architectures, in which publishers and subscribers discover each other and exchange messages directly.

cad9084f3d54.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
cad9084f3d54.sentence: Subscriber registration can occur at different times:

8b79c4a2c24a.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
8b79c4a2c24a.sentence: - Build time: Subscribers are hardcoded to handle specific messages or events (e.g., GUI event handlers).

2ba13863801f.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
2ba13863801f.sentence: - Initialization time: Subscriptions are defined in XML configuration files or metadata.

3eeaf86b6f00.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
3eeaf86b6f00.sentence: - Runtime: Subscriptions can be added or removed dynamically (e.g., database triggers, RSS readers).

c8d85dc2fe56.title: Publish–subscribe pattern
c8d85dc2fe56.sentence: For example, the Data Distribution Service (DDS) middleware uses IP multicast and metadata sharing to establish communication paths.

8620e72c7a90.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::message-brokers
8620e72c7a90.sentence: They're capable of ordering streams of records into categories called topics and storing them for a predetermined amount of time.

19b27b92f11b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
19b27b92f11b.sentence: In the Publish-Subscribe model, topics can typically connect to multiple types of endpoints, such as message queues, serverless functions, HTTP servers, etc.

321ea3959e16.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
321ea3959e16.sentence: This scenario happens when a message is sent to a topic and then replicated and pushed to multiple endpoints.

13cf9eb2fbc2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
13cf9eb2fbc2.sentence: Pub/Sub messaging services often provide very high durability, and at least once delivery, by storing copies of the same message on multiple servers.

1ee03fb47cb7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
1ee03fb47cb7.sentence: Fanout provides asynchronous event notifications which in turn allows for parallel processing.

ea95d121956e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
ea95d121956e.sentence: Message topics authenticate applications that try to publish content, this allows us to use encrypted endpoints and encrypt messages in transit over the network.

6ac2fa3fe42f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
6ac2fa3fe42f.sentence: - All components that subscribe to the topic (known as subscribers) will receive every message that was broadcasted.

ceda84d477df.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
ceda84d477df.sentence: This style of messaging is a bit different than message queues, where the component that sends the message often knows the destination it is sending to.

c2f1a33fbe4d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::publish-subscribe
c2f1a33fbe4d.sentence: The publisher doesn't need to know who is using the information that it is broadcasting, and the subscribers don't need to know where the message comes from.

b95720fd1c7a.title: Message queue
b95720fd1c7a.sentence: Most messaging systems support both the publisher/subscriber and message queue models in their API, e.g. Java Message Service (JMS).

141fa02d92de.title: Apache Kafka
141fa02d92de.sentence: Apache Kafka is a distributed event store and stream-processing platform.

8f3a292b9920.title: Apache Kafka
8f3a292b9920.sentence: Unlike queue-based systems, Kafka retains messages in a durable, append-only log, allowing multiple consumers to read at different offsets.

3c5d769684bd.title: Apache Kafka
3c5d769684bd.sentence: It is an open-source system developed by the Apache Software Foundation written in Java and Scala.

22a754eb6b2c.title: Apache Kafka
22a754eb6b2c.sentence: The project aims to provide a unified, high-throughput, low-latency platform for handling real-time data feeds.

52f82ee56b18.title: Batch processing
52f82ee56b18.sentence: In computing, batch processing is the running of a software job in an automated and unattended way.

d2e2131235e8.title: Batch processing
d2e2131235e8.sentence: A user schedules a job to run and then waits for a processing system to run it.

2f5c9e402983.title: Batch processing
2f5c9e402983.sentence: Typically, a job is scheduled to run at a configured time of day or when an event occurs or when computer resources are available.

d21134804635.title: Batch processing
d21134804635.sentence: Batch applications are still critical in most organizations in large part because many common business processes are amenable to batch processing.

b1cd8de56067.title: Batch processing
b1cd8de56067.sentence: While online systems can also function when manual intervention is not desired, they are not typically optimized to perform high-volume, repetitive tasks.

e1cbd56caff4.title: Batch processing
e1cbd56caff4.sentence: Therefore, even new systems usually contain one or more batch applications for updating information at the end of the day, generating reports, printing documents, and other non-interactive tasks that must complete reliably within certain business deadlines.

0d402a171f5a.title: Batch processing
0d402a171f5a.sentence: Some applications are amenable to flow processing, namely those that only need data from a single input at once (not totals, for instance): start the next step for each input as it completes the previous step.

267ffcbe740f.title: Batch processing
267ffcbe740f.sentence: In this case flow processing lowers latency for individual inputs, allowing them to be completed without waiting for the entire batch to finish.

fd5f8786cb93.title: Batch processing
fd5f8786cb93.sentence: However, many applications require data from all records, notably computations such as totals.

bfcf9ae184be.title: Batch processing
bfcf9ae184be.sentence: In this case the entire batch must be completed before one has a usable result: partial results are not usable.

90c4a017389d.title: Batch processing
90c4a017389d.sentence: For example, an e-commerce website might want to process customer transactions in an hourly batch to update the model that produces related product recommendations, in order to save computational resources.

8c7192f2669d.title: Job queue
8c7192f2669d.sentence: In system software, a job queue (a.k.a. batch queue, input queue), is a data structure maintained by job scheduler software containing jobs to run.

67943da0507b.title: Job queue

a7ccc1e8f277.title: Job queue

d75575ccd1ab.title: Job queue

1bd105e089f1.title: Stream processing
1bd105e089f1.sentence: In computer science, stream processing (also known as event stream processing, data stream processing, or distributed stream processing) is a programming paradigm that views streams, or sequences of events in time, as the central input and output objects of computation.

c9fa598edd00.title: Stream processing
c9fa598edd00.sentence: Stream processing encompasses dataflow programming, reactive programming, and distributed data processing.

f2654e13968e.title: Stream processing
f2654e13968e.section: Comparison to prior parallel paradigms > Parallel stream paradigm (SIMD/MIMD)
f2654e13968e.sentence: In the stream processing paradigm, data is treated as an unbounded, continuous sequence of elements rather than a static dataset.

cee4f46789cd.title: Stream processing
cee4f46789cd.sentence: Given a sequence of data (a stream), a series of operations (kernel functions) is applied to each element in the stream.

76143735883a.title: Stream processing
76143735883a.sentence: Uniform streaming, in which a single kernel function is applied to all elements in the stream, is typical.

f6edb45adc93.title: Stream processing
f6edb45adc93.section: Comparison to prior parallel paradigms > Parallel stream paradigm (SIMD/MIMD)
f6edb45adc93.sentence: Instead of managing iteration explicitly, the program defines a dataflow sequence, allowing the execution environment to apply the compute kernel function automatically as new data elements arrive.

a81a08791de6.title: Stream processing
a81a08791de6.section: Comparison to prior parallel paradigms > Parallel stream paradigm (SIMD/MIMD)
a81a08791de6.sentence: Although a 1:1 mapping between input and output data is commonly used for simplicity, it is not an inherent architectural requirement; kernels can perform complex transformations, aggregation windows, or stateful modifications.

cdf03d079506.title: Stream processing
cdf03d079506.sentence: The stream processing paradigm simplifies parallel software and hardware by restricting the kinds of parallel computation that can be performed.

1885bbba9e63.title: Stream processing
1885bbba9e63.sentence: - Data parallelism, which exists in a kernel when the same function is applied to all records of an input stream, allowing multiple records to be processed simultaneously without waiting for results from previous records.

3f276b195236.title: Stream processing
3f276b195236.sentence: Stream processing can be viewed as a compromise, driven by a data-centric model that works well for traditional DSP- or GPU-type applications (such as image, video and digital signal processing), but less well for general purpose processing with more randomized data access (such as databases).

a4f8e023a137.title: Stream processing

73b431ee3e2a.title: Apache Spark
73b431ee3e2a.sentence: Spark provides an interface for programming clusters with implicit data parallelism and fault tolerance.

92327360c673.title: Apache Spark
92327360c673.sentence: Apache Spark requires a cluster manager and a distributed storage system.

6031157ad2f8.title: Apache Spark
6031157ad2f8.sentence: For cluster management, Spark supports standalone native Spark, Hadoop YARN, Apache Mesos or Kubernetes.

710c2e6d342d.title: Apache Spark
710c2e6d342d.sentence: For distributed storage Spark can interface with a wide variety of distributed systems, including Alluxio, Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), MapR File System (MapR-FS), Cassandra, OpenStack Swift, Amazon S3, Kudu, Lustre file system, or a custom solution can be implemented.

2a8b9366f839.title: Apache Spark
2a8b9366f839.sentence: Apache Spark has its architectural foundation in the resilient distributed dataset (RDD), a read-only multiset of data items distributed over a cluster of machines, that is maintained in a fault-tolerant way.

97bb9f31228a.title: Apache Spark
97bb9f31228a.sentence: RDDs are immutable and their operations are lazy; fault-tolerance is achieved by keeping track of the "lineage" of each RDD (the sequence of operations that produced it) so that it can be reconstructed in the case of data loss.

bedd28f7b69b.title: Apache Spark
bedd28f7b69b.sentence: Spark and its RDDs were developed in 2012 in response to limitations in the MapReduce cluster computing paradigm, which forces a particular linear dataflow structure on distributed programs: MapReduce programs read input data from disk, map a function across the data, reduce the results of the map, and store reduction results on disk.

ca6b521130eb.title: Apache Spark
ca6b521130eb.sentence: Spark facilitates the implementation of both iterative algorithms, which visit their data set multiple times in a loop, and interactive/exploratory data analysis, i.e., the repeated database-style querying of data.

a4aaae355bd4.title: Apache Spark
a4aaae355bd4.sentence: The latency of such applications may be reduced by several orders of magnitude compared to Apache Hadoop MapReduce implementation.

4488fc134ed5.title: Apache Spark
4488fc134ed5.sentence: Inside Apache Spark the workflow is managed as a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

b617a773f2b6.title: Apache Spark
b617a773f2b6.sentence: Nodes represent RDDs while edges represent the operations on the RDDs.

184baa169846.title: Apache Spark
184baa169846.sentence: Spark SQL is a component on top of Spark Core that introduced a data abstraction called DataFrames, which provides support for structured and semi-structured data.

99d4af0785c8.title: Apache Spark

8a18ad2fbdcc.title: Apache Spark
