56965346e1e3.sentence: It can configure an alternative if, for example, a status column is set up on a table row indicating that the row has changed (e.g., a boolean column that, when set to true, indicates that the row has changed).

bdccb8505bb4.title: Change data capture
bdccb8505bb4.sentence: In this approach, triggers log events that happen to the transactional table into another queue table that can later be "played back".

999a036401a0.title: Change data capture
999a036401a0.sentence: CDC solutions based on transaction log files have distinct advantages that include:

182eaf1768ad.title: Change data capture
182eaf1768ad.sentence: Any row in any table that has a timestamp in that column that is more recent than the last time data was captured is considered to have changed.

7882a0214737.title: Change data capture
7882a0214737.sentence: When a change capture occurs, all data with the latest version number is considered to have changed.

386a20006f68.title: Change data capture
386a20006f68.sentence: Once the change capture is complete, the reference table is updated with a new version number.

4d662faebe9e.title: Change data capture
4d662faebe9e.sentence: Otherwise, it can act as a complement to the previous methods, indicating that a row, despite having a new version number or a later date, still shouldn't be updated on the target (for example, the data may require human validation).

e4fd57bb6d00.title: Change data capture
e4fd57bb6d00.sentence: As noted, it is not uncommon to see multiple CDC solutions at work in a single system, however, the combination of time, version, and status provides a particularly powerful mechanism and programmers should utilize them as a trio where possible.

f0b7ea29ff1f.title: Change data capture
f0b7ea29ff1f.sentence: The three elements are not redundant or superfluous.

1bbf57b8f2a9.title: Change data capture
1bbf57b8f2a9.sentence: This queue table could then be "played back" to replicate the data from the source system to a target.

0fcb30acff1e.title: Change data capture
0fcb30acff1e.sentence: - minimal impact on the database (even more so if one uses log shipping to process the logs on a dedicated host).

31a4de893e49.title: Change data capture
31a4de893e49.sentence: - no need for programmatic changes to the applications that use the database.

17fbec30f1e0.title: Change data capture
17fbec30f1e0.sentence: - transactional integrity: log scanning can produce a change stream that replays the original transactions in the order they were committed.

9731d3fe81b7.title: Change data capture
9731d3fe81b7.sentence: Unlike data access, no standard exists for transaction logs.

bf9ba0fa06f3.title: Change data capture
bf9ba0fa06f3.sentence: Most database management systems do not document the internal format of their transaction logs, although some provide programmatic interfaces to their transaction logs (for example: Oracle, DB2, SQL/MP, SQL/MX and SQL Server 2008).

a586db35635a.title: Change data capture
a586db35635a.sentence: - Eliminating uncommitted changes that the database wrote to the transaction log and later rolled back.

9e9712126ccc.title: Stream processing
9e9712126ccc.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
9e9712126ccc.sentence: Modern cluster-scale data infrastructure categorizes stream architectures based on their execution models:

27de473847c8.title: Stream processing
27de473847c8.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
27de473847c8.sentence: - Native Continuous Stream Processing: Frameworks that process elements individually as they arrive, optimizing for sub-second, real-time latencies:

bf4462e8bae7.title: Stream processing
bf4462e8bae7.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
bf4462e8bae7.sentence: - Micro-Batch Stream Processing: Frameworks that achieve high-throughput stream semantics by automatically collecting incoming elements into tightly constrained time windows or miniature batches:

9a823fb997ec.title: Stream processing
9a823fb997ec.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
9a823fb997ec.sentence: - Distributed Logging Fabrics: Infrastructure that serves as the persistent, append-only transport layer for continuous stream architectures:

df39afb77251.title: Stream processing
df39afb77251.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
df39afb77251.sentence: - Apache Storm: A native, low-latency distributed real-time computation system.

4376edb8f138.title: Stream processing
4376edb8f138.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
4376edb8f138.sentence: - Apache Flink: A true streaming execution engine that treats batch computing strictly as a specialized subset of continuous streaming.

33f589d11786.title: Stream processing
33f589d11786.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
33f589d11786.sentence: - Apache Samza: A stateful distributed stream processing engine built over Apache Kafka.

982f1befe064.title: Stream processing
982f1befe064.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
982f1befe064.sentence: - Apache Spark Streaming: An extension of the core Apache Spark API that ingests live data streams and processes them in small discrete chunks (micro-batches).

827b875055e5.title: Stream processing
827b875055e5.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Distributed and cloud-scale execution ecosystems
827b875055e5.sentence: - Apache Kafka: A highly scalable, distributed event streaming platform used to ingest and store fault-tolerant streams of records.

a123c3b119e9.title: Stream processing
a123c3b119e9.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Managed cloud streaming services
a123c3b119e9.sentence: - Amazon Web Services (AWS) Kinesis: A managed cloud service for real-time processing of large-scale, distributed data streams.

331f8d481b29.title: Stream processing
331f8d481b29.section: Stream programming libraries and languages > Managed cloud streaming services
331f8d481b29.sentence: - Google Cloud Dataflow: A fully managed cloud service executing unified stream and batch processing pipelines based on the Apache Beam architecture.

670ba960ff5a.title: Apache Flink
670ba960ff5a.sentence: Apache Flink is an open-source, unified stream-processing and batch-processing framework developed by the Apache Software Foundation.

fb159100dae2.title: Apache Flink
fb159100dae2.sentence: The core of Apache Flink is a distributed streaming data-flow engine written in Java and Scala.

2338e30818c0.title: Apache Flink
2338e30818c0.sentence: Flink's pipelined runtime system enables the execution of bulk/batch and stream processing programs.

3902b0bc3dfe.title: Apache Flink
3902b0bc3dfe.sentence: Apache Flink's dataflow programming model provides event-at-a-time processing on both finite and infinite datasets.

27d696cd7fbc.title: Apache Flink
27d696cd7fbc.section: Overview > Programming Model and Distributed Runtime
27d696cd7fbc.sentence: Every Flink dataflow starts with one or more sources (a data input, e.g., a message queue or a file system) and ends with one or more sinks (a data output, e.g., a message queue, file system, or database).

ef53c2cd1736.title: Apache Flink
ef53c2cd1736.section: Overview > Programming Model and Distributed Runtime
ef53c2cd1736.sentence: An arbitrary number of transformations can be performed on the stream.

6ff504f3d6f7.title: Apache Flink
6ff504f3d6f7.section: Overview > Programming Model and Distributed Runtime
6ff504f3d6f7.sentence: These streams can be arranged as a directed, acyclic dataflow graph, allowing an application to branch and merge dataflows.

34faa3967d5d.title: Apache Flink
34faa3967d5d.sentence: Flink provides a high-throughput, low-latency streaming engine as well as support for event-time processing and state management.

e9f2c0d5e504.title: Apache Flink
e9f2c0d5e504.sentence: Flink executes arbitrary dataflow programs in a data-parallel and pipelined (hence task parallel) manner.

25a5156dbaef.title: Apache Flink
25a5156dbaef.section: Overview > Programming Model and Distributed Runtime
25a5156dbaef.sentence: Flink programs run as a distributed system within a cluster and can be deployed in a standalone mode as well as on YARN, Mesos, Docker-based setups along with other resource management frameworks.

f2c04578e6d7.title: Apache Flink
f2c04578e6d7.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
f2c04578e6d7.sentence: Apache Flink includes a lightweight fault tolerance mechanism based on distributed checkpoints.

4f55f31b8403.title: Apache Flink
4f55f31b8403.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
4f55f31b8403.sentence: A checkpoint is an automatic, asynchronous snapshot of the state of an application and the position in a source stream.

956970d31f6f.title: Apache Flink
956970d31f6f.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
956970d31f6f.sentence: In the case of a failure, a Flink program with checkpointing enabled will, upon recovery, resume processing from the last completed checkpoint, ensuring that Flink maintains exactly-once state semantics within an application.

4c40cb809a5a.title: Apache Flink
4c40cb809a5a.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
4c40cb809a5a.sentence: The checkpointing mechanism exposes hooks for application code to include external systems into the checkpointing mechanism as well (like opening and committing transactions with a database system).

4512ccefc97f.title: Apache Flink
4512ccefc97f.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
4512ccefc97f.sentence: Flink also includes a mechanism called savepoints, which are manually-triggered checkpoints.

343ec7574b29.title: Apache Flink
343ec7574b29.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
343ec7574b29.sentence: A user can generate a savepoint, stop a running Flink program, then resume the program from the same application state and position in the stream.

f4cc3a6f2163.title: Apache Flink
f4cc3a6f2163.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
f4cc3a6f2163.sentence: Savepoints enable updates to a Flink program or a Flink cluster without losing the application's state.

f10693c9866d.title: Apache Flink
f10693c9866d.section: Overview > State: Checkpoints, Savepoints, and Fault-tolerance
f10693c9866d.sentence: As of Flink 1.2, savepoints also allow to restart an application with a different parallelism—allowing users to adapt to changing workloads.

90680f48c5e0.title: Apache Flink
90680f48c5e0.sentence: Flink's DataStream API enables transformations (e.g. filters, aggregations, window functions) on bounded or unbounded streams of data.

71744902123c.title: Apache Flink
71744902123c.sentence: Apache Flink includes two core APIs: a DataStream API for bounded or unbounded streams of data and a DataSet API for bounded data sets.

94553c0052c6.title: Apache Flink
94553c0052c6.sentence: The highest-level language supported by Flink is SQL, which is semantically similar to the Table API and represents programs as SQL query expressions.

482489dcaf5f.title: Apache Flink
482489dcaf5f.sentence: This API is deprecated at Flink version 2.0

2da7f6fffe87.title: Apache Flink
2da7f6fffe87.sentence: Flink does not provide its own data-storage system, but provides data-source and sink connectors to systems such as Apache Doris, Amazon Kinesis, Apache Kafka, HDFS, Apache Cassandra, and ElasticSearch.

a3f5e750b876.title: Apache Flink
a3f5e750b876.section: Overview > Programming Model and Distributed Runtime
a3f5e750b876.sentence: Flink offers ready-built source and sink connectors with Apache Kafka, Amazon Kinesis, HDFS, Apache Cassandra, and more.

943f36f982c7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
943f36f982c7.sentence: The first one is Kafka’s reliance on Sequential I/O.

5e77599cb253.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
5e77599cb253.sentence: The second design choice that gives Kafka its performance advantage is its focus on efficiency: zero copy principle.

b504a8ff02c4.title: Apache Kafka
b504a8ff02c4.sentence: Kafka uses a binary TCP-based protocol that is optimized for efficiency and relies on a "message set" abstraction that naturally groups messages together to reduce the overhead of the network roundtrip.

20bc0d138114.title: Apache Kafka
20bc0d138114.sentence: This "leads to larger network packets, larger sequential disk operations, contiguous memory blocks [...] which allows Kafka to turn a bursty stream of random message writes into linear writes."

bb5a8acff300.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
bb5a8acff300.sentence: - 2.1: The data is loaded from disk to OS cache

b45fcebbc4bc.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
b45fcebbc4bc.sentence: - 2.2 The data is copied from OS cache to Kafka application

9c143fcb2ea2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
9c143fcb2ea2.sentence: - 2.3 Kafka application copies the data into the socket buffer

c6bb1f614f93.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
c6bb1f614f93.sentence: - 2.4 The data is copied from socket buffer to network card

f512f229e0a8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
f512f229e0a8.sentence: - 3.1: The data is loaded from disk to OS cache

974097b1e91d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
974097b1e91d.sentence: - 3.2 OS cache directly copies the data to the network card via sendfile() command

7e24863a675b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/why-is-kafka-fast.md
7e24863a675b.sentence: Zero copy is a shortcut to save multiple data copies between the application context and kernel context.

b9af9640e540.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
b9af9640e540.sentence: Event-Driven Architecture (EDA) is about using events as a way to communicate within a system.

449a804e6525.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
449a804e6525.sentence: Generally, leveraging a message broker to publish and consume events asynchronously.

a5e65b004e8a.title: Event-driven architecture
a5e65b004e8a.sentence: Event-driven architecture (EDA) is a software architecture paradigm concerning the production and detection of events.

9fc0942f83c1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
9fc0942f83c1.sentence: An event is a data point that represents state changes in a system.

06b51d894f8c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
06b51d894f8c.sentence: It doesn't specify what should happen and how the change should modify the system, it only notifies the system of a particular state change.

2f2b2ee7e097.title: Event-driven architecture
2f2b2ee7e097.sentence: An event can be defined as "a significant change in state".

2b09e6e89c14.title: Event-driven architecture
2b09e6e89c14.sentence: For example, when a consumer purchases a car, the car's state changes from "for sale" to "sold".

02865c30d1e2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
02865c30d1e2.sentence: The publisher is unaware of who is consuming an event and the consumers are unaware of each other.

85ca46a09145.title: Event-driven architecture
85ca46a09145.sentence: An Event Emitter does not know the consumers of the event, it does not even know if a consumer exists, and in case it exists, it does not know how the event is used or further processed.

3fccf968c5c9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
3fccf968c5c9.sentence: Event-driven architectures have three key components:

3fcc0bfbec8c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
3fcc0bfbec8c.sentence: - Event producers: Publishes an event to the router.

33399624a28b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
33399624a28b.sentence: - Event routers: Filters and pushes the events to consumers.

8e49a70559f6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
8e49a70559f6.sentence: - Event consumers: Uses events to reflect changes in the system.

725dd4b5e3e1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
725dd4b5e3e1.sentence: Event-Driven Architecture is simply a way of achieving loose coupling between services within a system.

60b7f8d25865.title: Event-driven architecture
60b7f8d25865.sentence: Building systems around an event-driven architecture simplifies horizontal scalability in distributed computing models and makes them more resilient to failure.

553336639e14.title: Event-driven architecture
553336639e14.sentence: Event-driven architectures are evolutionary in nature and provide a high degree of fault tolerance, performance, and scalability.

b37d7b243e29.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
b37d7b243e29.sentence: - Exactly once, in-order processing of events.

c9b11b3b13b7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
c9b11b3b13b7.sentence: - Event-driven systems are complex in general.

793951e428ce.title: Event-driven architecture
793951e428ce.sentence: However, they are complex and inherently challenging to test.

c3bc96ceea14.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::event-driven-architecture-eda
c3bc96ceea14.sentence: Here are some widely used technologies for implementing event-driven architectures:

d65dd0ddedc9.title: Domain-driven design
d65dd0ddedc9.sentence: Domain-driven design (DDD) is a software design approach that focuses on modeling software to match a domain according to input from that domain's experts.

3e4af24ab5bb.title: Domain-driven design
3e4af24ab5bb.sentence: Under domain-driven design, the structure and language of software code (class names, class methods, class variables) should match the business domain.

338c02086508.title: Domain-driven design
338c02086508.sentence: For example: if software processes loan applications, it might have classes like "loan application", "customers", and methods such as "accept offer" and "withdraw".

be6ae8868246.title: Domain-driven design
be6ae8868246.sentence: These aspects of domain-driven design aim to foster a common language shared by domain experts, users, and developers—the ubiquitous language.

5429704d93be.title: Domain-driven design
5429704d93be.sentence: The ubiquitous language is used in the domain model and for describing system requirements.

c5e16d7142ac.title: Domain-driven design
c5e16d7142ac.sentence: Ubiquitous language is one of the pillars of DDD together with strategic design and tactical design.

4363b0aba196.title: Domain-driven design
4363b0aba196.sentence: DDD is against the idea of having a single unified model; instead it divides a large system into bounded contexts, each of which have their own model.

bc73fb329616.title: Domain-driven design
bc73fb329616.sentence: Context Mapping identifies and defines the boundaries of different domains or subdomains within a larger system.

02dd3703a2ec.title: Domain-driven design
02dd3703a2ec.sentence: - Shared Kernel: "Designate with an explicit boundary some subset of the domain model that the teams agree to share.

878b8ff3d4ab.title: Domain-driven design
878b8ff3d4ab.sentence: - Customer/Supplier Development: "Establish a clear customer/supplier relationship between the two teams", when "two teams are in [a] upstream-downstream relationship"

231cecf94afb.title: Domain-driven design
231cecf94afb.sentence: - Anticorruption Layer: "create an isolating layer to provide your system with functionality of the upstream system in terms of your own domain model"

8c3de6ca4d3f.title: Domain-driven design
8c3de6ca4d3f.sentence: For example, an entity is an object defined not by its attributes, but its identity.

5c790cf268da.title: Domain-driven design
5c790cf268da.sentence: In contrast, a value object is an immutable object that contains attributes but has no conceptual identity.

7a36380a7d0d.title: Domain-driven design
7a36380a7d0d.sentence: A domain event is an event that domain experts care about.

be5fffda236c.title: Domain-driven design
be5fffda236c.sentence: Models can be bound together by a root entity to become an aggregate.

1219fb1c070b.title: Domain-driven design
1219fb1c070b.sentence: Objects outside the aggregate are allowed to hold references to the root but not to any other object of the aggregate.

4e030785da32.title: Domain-driven design
4e030785da32.sentence: The aggregate root checks the consistency of changes in the aggregate.

f428537b8da1.title: Domain-driven design
f428537b8da1.sentence: A repository, for instance, is an object with methods for retrieving domain objects from a data store (e.g. a database).

d4be1b664dd5.title: Domain-driven design
d4be1b664dd5.sentence: Similarly, a factory is an object with methods for directly creating domain objects.

733a1e0f0f95.title: Domain-driven design
733a1e0f0f95.section: Relationship to other ideas > Event sourcing
733a1e0f0f95.sentence: When event sourcing is combined with CQRS and domain-driven design, aggregate roots are responsible for validating and applying commands (often by having their instance methods invoked from a Command Handler), and then publishing events.

3e69beb6ae06.title: Domain-driven design
3e69beb6ae06.section: Relationship to other ideas > Event sourcing
3e69beb6ae06.sentence: Hence, the input is a command and the output is one or many events which are saved to an event store, and then often published on a message broker for those interested (such as an application's view).

7fa2223a52e8.title: Domain-driven design
7fa2223a52e8.section: Relationship to other ideas > Event storming
7fa2223a52e8.sentence: Event storming is a collaborative, workshop-based modeling technique which can be used as a precursor in the context of Domain-Driven Design (DDD) to identify and understand domain events.

8b790b8b5183.title: Domain-driven design
8b790b8b5183.section: Relationship to other ideas > Event storming
8b790b8b5183.sentence: This interactive discovery process involves stakeholders, domain experts, and developers working together to visualize the flow of domain events, their causes, and their effects, fostering a shared understanding of the domain.

d8d491ab0d42.title: Domain-driven design
d8d491ab0d42.section: Relationship to other ideas > Event storming
d8d491ab0d42.sentence: Event storming can aid in discovering subdomains, bounded contexts, and aggregate boundaries, which are key constructs in DDD.

0f35926e2707.title: Domain-driven design
0f35926e2707.sentence: In microservices architecture, a bounded context often maps to a microservice, but this relationship can vary depending on the design approach.

e6bb5d041446.title: Domain-driven design
e6bb5d041446.sentence: A one-to-one relationship, where each bounded context is implemented as a single microservice, is typically ideal as it maintains clear boundaries, reduces coupling, and enables independent deployment and scaling.

27d87edbb8ca.title: Domain-driven design
27d87edbb8ca.sentence: Critics of domain-driven design argue that developers must typically implement a great deal of isolation and encapsulation to maintain the model as a pure and helpful construct.

9d22172a066e.title: Domain-driven design
9d22172a066e.sentence: While domain-driven design provides benefits such as maintainability, Microsoft recommends it only for complex domains where the model provides clear benefits in formulating a common understanding of the domain.

22df783cfba2.title: Event store
22df783cfba2.sentence: An event store is a type of database optimized for storage of events.

571814d4c297.title: Event store
571814d4c297.sentence: Conceptually, an event store records only the events affecting an entity, dossier, or policy, and the state of the entity at any point in its history can be reconstructed by replaying its contributing events in sequential order.

e024300c150f.title: Event store
e024300c150f.sentence: Events (and their corresponding data) are the only "real" facts that should be stored in the database.

77ef74228c38.title: Event store
77ef74228c38.sentence: All other objects can be derived from these events, meaning they are instantiated in memory by runtime code as needed (e.g. for showing in a user interface).

7378b14d7b47.title: Event store
7378b14d7b47.sentence: In theory, any object that aggregates over recorded event data is not stored in the database.

91001f05990f.title: Event store
91001f05990f.sentence: Instead these objects are built 'on the fly', by traversing the event history.

16463bb795b9.title: Event store
16463bb795b9.sentence: When the aggregated object instance is no longer needed, it can simply be discarded (released from memory).

64bebe36a50b.title: Event store
64bebe36a50b.sentence: Another crucial part of an event store database is that events that are stored are not allowed to be changed.

7714e61d3b81.title: Event store
7714e61d3b81.sentence: Once stored, also erroneous events are not changed anymore.

7a3a1262615b.title: Event store
7a3a1262615b.sentence: The only way to change (or better: correct) these events is to instantiate a new event with the new values and using the double timeline.

8c595cae627a.title: Event store
8c595cae627a.sentence: One advantage of the event store concept is that handling the effects of back dated events (events that take effect before previous events and that may even invalidate them) is much easier.

182aa8853411.title: Event store
182aa8853411.sentence: An event store will simplify the code in that rolling back erroneous situations and rolling up the new, correct situations is not needed anymore.

6f0283ae0a9d.title: Event store
6f0283ae0a9d.sentence: In regular databases, handling backdated events to correct previous, erroneous events can be painful as it often results in rolling back all previous, erroneous transactions and objects and rolling up the new, correct transactions and objects.

780bc21b61cd.title: Event store
780bc21b61cd.sentence: In an event store, only the new event (and its corresponding facts) are stored.

5a64d3f1b824.title: Event store
5a64d3f1b824.sentence: The code will then redetermine the transactions and objects based on the new facts in memory.

11dfbe1405c0.title: Event store
11dfbe1405c0.sentence: Disadvantage may be that the code needs to re-instantiate all objects in memory based on the events each time a service call is received for a specific dossier or policy.

0be5c4162057.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-incorporate-event-sourcing-into-the-systems.md
0be5c4162057.sentence: The newspaper website stores every article, image, and byline since 1851 in an event store.

5dc57061c0c4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-incorporate-event-sourcing-into-the-systems.md
5dc57061c0c4.sentence: The raw data is then denormalized into different views and fed into different ElasticSearch nodes for website searches.

d6b73daa0997.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/the-ultimate-kafka-101-you-cannot-miss.md

fee28c90b4dd.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
fee28c90b4dd.sentence: The fallacies of distributed computing are a set of assertions made by L. Peter Deutsch and others at Sun Microsystems describing false assumptions that programmers new to distributed applications invariably make.

828b8eff5075.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
828b8eff5075.sentence: - Software applications are written with little error-handling on networking errors.

d602f5dbb52f.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
d602f5dbb52f.sentence: During a network outage, such applications may stall or infinitely wait for an answer packet, permanently consuming memory or other resources.

ea8404a473ea.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
ea8404a473ea.sentence: When the failed network becomes available, those applications may also fail to retry any stalled operations or require a (manual) restart.

811c7d7c145a.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
811c7d7c145a.sentence: - Ignorance of network latency, and of the packet loss it can cause, induces application- and transport-layer developers to allow unbounded traffic, greatly increasing dropped packets and wasting bandwidth.

5b4145cbd72c.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
5b4145cbd72c.sentence: - Ignorance of bandwidth limits on the part of traffic senders can result in bottlenecks.

897ae5214105.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
897ae5214105.sentence: - Complacency regarding network security results in being blindsided by malicious users and programs that continually adapt to security measures.

ea370fe864c6.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
ea370fe864c6.sentence: - Changes in network topology can have effects on both bandwidth and latency issues, and therefore can have similar problems.

e0fcfb215089.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
e0fcfb215089.sentence: - Multiple administrators, as with subnets for rival companies, may institute conflicting policies of which senders of network traffic must be aware in order to complete their desired paths.

a55e49922dc8.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
a55e49922dc8.sentence: - The "hidden" costs of building and maintaining a network or subnet are non-negligible and must consequently be noted in budgets to avoid vast shortfalls.

d1f26b7e85b3.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
d1f26b7e85b3.sentence: - If a system assumes a homogeneous network, then it can lead to the same problems that result from the first three fallacies.

dfb444992962.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
dfb444992962.sentence: In an episode of "Software Engineering Radio" Peter Deutsch added a ninth fallacy: "It's really an expansion of number 4.

98faff658338.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
98faff658338.sentence: The party you are communicating with is trustworthy."

f31336def644.title: Fallacies of distributed computing
f31336def644.sentence: Later in 2020, Mark Richards and Neal Ford expanded upon the original "Fallacies of Distributed Computing" by introducing three additional fallacies to address contemporary challenges in distributed systems:

c6b8316dd2b4.title: Event-driven architecture
c6b8316dd2b4.sentence: Event driven architecture has two primary topologies.

fdf04aa36810.title: Event-driven architecture
fdf04aa36810.sentence: With “broker topology”, components broadcast events to the entire system without any orchestrator.

8216a0c0425c.title: Event-driven architecture
8216a0c0425c.sentence: With “mediator topology”, there is a central orchestrator which controls workflow of events.

50ad2fb8e08f.title: Event-driven architecture
50ad2fb8e08f.sentence: You can also use a hybrid model and combine these two topologies.

db55ff72f733.title: Event-driven architecture
db55ff72f733.sentence: This topology provides higher performance and scalability.

bd764d6afa81.title: Event-driven architecture
bd764d6afa81.sentence: This topology provides better control and error handling capabilities.

2094838c9f61.title: Event-driven architecture
2094838c9f61.sentence: One of the challenges of using event driven architecture is error handling.

560530fe137d.title: Event-driven architecture
560530fe137d.sentence: Another challenge of using event driven architecture is data loss.

33cb56d69f36.title: Event-driven architecture
33cb56d69f36.sentence: One way to address this issue is to use a separate error-handler processor.

8c2b66b46cd0.title: Event-driven architecture
8c2b66b46cd0.sentence: So, when the event consumer experiences an error, it immediately and asynchronously sends the erroneous event to the error-handler processor and moves on.

85862dd49b2c.title: Event-driven architecture
85862dd49b2c.sentence: Error-handler processor tries to fix the error and sends the event back to the original channel.

5c36339764fc.title: Event-driven architecture
5c36339764fc.sentence: But if the error-handler processor fails, then it can send the erroneous event to an administrator for further inspection.

092e9fdb0a64.title: Event-driven architecture
092e9fdb0a64.sentence: Note that if you use an error-handler processor, erroneous events will be processed out of sequence when they are resubmitted.

0d8a95fd42dc.title: Event-driven architecture
0d8a95fd42dc.sentence: If any of the components crashes before successfully processing and handing over the event to its next component, then the event is dropped and never makes it into the final destination.

ca9152067590.title: Event-driven architecture
ca9152067590.sentence: To minimize the chance of data loss, you can persist in-transit events and remove / dequeue the events only when the next component has acknowledged the receipt of the event.

405d4043ffd6.title: Event-driven architecture
405d4043ffd6.sentence: These features are usually known as "client acknowledge mode" and "last participant support".

5262464465d1.title: Event-driven architecture
5262464465d1.sentence: Event driven architecture is susceptible to the fallacies of distributed computing, a series of misconceptions that can lead to significant issues in software development and deployment.

79a32c1f55f8.title: Event-driven architecture
79a32c1f55f8.sentence: There are three general styles of event processing: simple, stream, and complex.

0c32b9023dd7.title: Event-driven architecture
0c32b9023dd7.sentence: The three styles are often used together in a mature event-driven architecture.

619bb49ce394.title: Event-driven architecture
619bb49ce394.section: Event processing styles > Online event processing
619bb49ce394.sentence: Online event processing (OLEP) uses asynchronous distributed event logs to process complex events and manage persistent data.

a2ed26fb8560.title: Event-driven architecture

a2ed26fb8560.sentence: Simple event processing concerns events that are directly related to specific, measurable changes of condition.

0ce923662c79.title: Event-driven architecture
0ce923662c79.section: Event processing styles > Simple event processing
0ce923662c79.sentence: In simple event processing, a notable event happens which initiates downstream action(s).

9263a3ed7010.title: Event-driven architecture
9263a3ed7010.section: Event processing styles > Simple event processing
9263a3ed7010.sentence: Simple event processing is commonly used to drive the real-time flow of work, thereby reducing lag time and cost.

2cca0b92473c.title: Event-driven architecture
2cca0b92473c.section: Event processing styles > Event stream processing
2cca0b92473c.sentence: In event stream processing (ESP), both ordinary and notable events happen.

4c46d76d0217.title: Event-driven architecture
4c46d76d0217.section: Event processing styles > Event stream processing
4c46d76d0217.sentence: Ordinary events (orders, RFID transmissions) are screened for notability and streamed to information subscribers.

7998d99fdabb.title: Event-driven architecture
7998d99fdabb.section: Event processing styles > Event stream processing
7998d99fdabb.sentence: Event stream processing is commonly used to drive the real-time flow of information in and around the enterprise, which enables in-time decision making.

db179872544a.title: Event-driven architecture
db179872544a.section: Event processing styles > Complex event processing
db179872544a.sentence: Complex event processing (CEP) allows patterns of simple and ordinary events to be considered to infer that a complex event has occurred.

1a8cf61e1d2d.title: Event-driven architecture
1a8cf61e1d2d.section: Event processing styles > Complex event processing
1a8cf61e1d2d.sentence: Complex event processing evaluates a confluence of events and then takes action.

36d0f0ec31be.title: Event-driven architecture

36d0f0ec31be.sentence: The events (notable or ordinary) may cross event types and occur over a long period of time.

1d19ff946e8b.title: Event-driven architecture
1d19ff946e8b.section: Event processing styles > Complex event processing
1d19ff946e8b.sentence: The event correlation may be causal, temporal, or spatial.

c9c334465a28.sentence: CEP requires the employment of sophisticated event interpreters, event pattern definition and matching, and correlation techniques.

647f43137d16.sentence: CEP is commonly used to detect and respond to business anomalies, threats, and opportunities.

7a54a172d40f.title: Event-driven architecture
7a54a172d40f.section: Event processing styles > Online event processing
7a54a172d40f.sentence: OLEP allows reliably composing related events of a complex scenario across heterogeneous systems.

54e1b0f3bd2b.title: Event-driven architecture

54e1b0f3bd2b.sentence: It thereby enables very flexible distribution patterns with high scalability and offers strong consistency.

e91374e4ef66.title: Event-driven architecture
e91374e4ef66.section: Event processing styles > Online event processing
e91374e4ef66.sentence: However, it cannot guarantee upper bounds on processing time.

2d67c08ceddd.title: Event-driven architecture
2d67c08ceddd.sentence: An event can be made of two parts, the event header and the event body also known as event payload.

abc9ab46f909.title: Event-driven architecture
abc9ab46f909.sentence: The event header might include information such as event name, time stamp for the event, and type of event.

8248965cdd0e.title: Event-driven architecture
8248965cdd0e.sentence: The event payload provides the details of the state change detected.

f68638f79bcb.title: Event-driven architecture

8afe2c0cca71.title: Event-driven architecture
8afe2c0cca71.sentence: There are two primary methods for structuring event payloads in event-driven architectures:

8e6d7f62f9df.title: Event-driven architecture

ce2ac75fe5e6.title: Event-driven architecture

8ec30fbc33a1.title: Event-driven architecture

025087adeabc.title: Command–query separation
025087adeabc.sentence: It states that every method should either be a command that performs an action, or a query that returns data to the caller, but not both.

698c8c773887.title: Command–query separation
698c8c773887.sentence: It was devised by Bertrand Meyer as part of his pioneering work on the Eiffel programming language.

e43be13445c9.title: Command–query separation
e43be13445c9.sentence: In other words, asking a question should not change the answer.

5a54fbf34454.title: Command–query separation
5a54fbf34454.sentence: More formally, methods should return a value only if they are referentially transparent and hence possess no side effects.

7ad7850a6d66.title: Command–query separation
7ad7850a6d66.sentence: CQS is beneficial to DbC because any value-returning method (any query) can be called by any assertion without fear of modifying program state.

1177b9fb346a.title: Command–query separation
1177b9fb346a.sentence: In theoretical terms, this establishes a measure of sanity, whereby one can reason about a program's state without simultaneously modifying that state.

4758c1116e38.title: Command–query separation
4758c1116e38.sentence: Even beyond the connection with design by contract, CQS is considered by its adherents to have a simplifying effect on a program, making its states (via queries) and state changes (via commands) more comprehensible.

814e967741ed.title: Command–query separation
814e967741ed.sentence: Command query responsibility segregation (CQRS) generalises CQS to services, at the architectures level: it applies the CQS principle by using separate Query and Command interfaces and usually data models to retrieve and modify data, respectively.

e5a3ebad62fc.title: Command–query separation

a82ff8875807.title: Command–query separation
a82ff8875807.sentence: Even in single-threaded programs, it is sometimes arguably significantly more convenient to have a method that is a combined query and command.

e18087ce4695.title: Command–query separation

737239db3b43.title: Command–query separation

b76c205fd46e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
b76c205fd46e.sentence: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) is an architectural pattern that divides a system's actions into commands and queries.

c5391286811d.title: Command Query Responsibility Segregation
c5391286811d.sentence: In information technology, Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) is a software architecture that extends the idea behind command–query separation (CQS) to the level of services.

e1472ea8926e.title: Command Query Responsibility Segregation
e1472ea8926e.sentence: Such a system will have separate interfaces to send queries and to send commands.

deb46cae62d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
deb46cae62d4.sentence: In CQRS, a command is an instruction, a directive to perform a specific task.

8a1741577819.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
8a1741577819.sentence: It is an intention to change something and doesn't return a value, only an indication of success or failure.

c92e7e17c6af.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
c92e7e17c6af.sentence: And, a query is a request for information that doesn't change the system's state or cause any side effects.

e9c55b17feb2.title: Command Query Responsibility Segregation
e9c55b17feb2.sentence: As in CQS, fulfilling a query request will only retrieve data and will not modify the state of the system (with some exceptions like logging access), while fulfilling a command request will modify the state of the system.

0c287c6957d6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
0c287c6957d6.sentence: The core principle of CQRS is the separation of commands and queries.

030e937da31b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
030e937da31b.sentence: They perform fundamentally different roles within a system, and separating them means that each can be optimized as needed, which distributed systems can really benefit from.

5fb1e2acc29d.title: Command Query Responsibility Segregation
5fb1e2acc29d.sentence: Many systems push the segregation to the data models used by the system.

8bafe4f9b9c9.title: Command Query Responsibility Segregation
8bafe4f9b9c9.sentence: The models used to process queries are usually called read models and the models used to process commands are write models.

b33df3612db0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
b33df3612db0.sentence: CQRS-based systems use separate read and write data models, each tailored to relevant tasks and often located in physically separate stores.

b2ac4261649f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
b2ac4261649f.sentence: The CQRS pattern is often used along with the Event Sourcing pattern.

e3081b68a8ca.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
e3081b68a8ca.sentence: When used with the Event Sourcing pattern, the store of events is the write model and is the official source of information.

5e48629b339c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
5e48629b339c.sentence: The read model of a CQRS-based system provides materialized views of the data, typically as highly denormalized views.

de99821037ef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
de99821037ef.sentence: - Allows independent scaling of read and write workloads.

c777d9a78f50.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
c777d9a78f50.sentence: - Easier scaling, optimizations, and architectural changes.

70b7960acf1e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
70b7960acf1e.sentence: - Clear boundaries between the system behavior.

6f1795150f90.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs

104399e84f51.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
104399e84f51.sentence: - Message failures or duplicate messages can occur.

f03ddbcac135.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
f03ddbcac135.sentence: - Dealing with eventual consistency is a challenge.

e9ccad8bfd2e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
e9ccad8bfd2e.sentence: - The performance of data reads must be fine-tuned separately from the performance of data writes.

57ebafbee8c0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
57ebafbee8c0.sentence: - The system is expected to evolve over time and might contain multiple versions of the model, or where business rules change regularly.

44429bce8b5e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::command-and-query-responsibility-segregation-cqrs
44429bce8b5e.sentence: - Integration with other systems, especially in combination with event sourcing, where the temporal failure of one subsystem shouldn't affect the availability of the others.

836f4b16e31b.title: Event-driven architecture

36398b635997.title: Event-driven architecture
36398b635997.sentence: The first logical layer is the event producer, which senses a fact and represents that fact as an event message.

ebea5b8627bd.title: Event-driven architecture

7d0b79de18be.sentence: The event processing engine is the logical layer responsible for identifying an event, and then selecting and executing the appropriate reaction.

586f80771e66.title: Event-driven architecture

586f80771e66.sentence: This is the logical layer where the consequences of the event are shown.

6e7d1651892b.title: Event-driven architecture

9ce80a7c065c.title: Event-driven architecture

3760b97fb97e.title: Event-driven architecture

b90b6d0305d0.title: Apache Avro
b90b6d0305d0.sentence: Avro is a row-oriented remote procedure call and data serialization framework developed within Apache's Hadoop project.

440c57371c9e.title: Apache Avro
440c57371c9e.sentence: Its primary use is in Apache Hadoop, where it can provide both a serialization format for persistent data, and a wire format for communication between Hadoop nodes, and from client programs to the Hadoop services.

060d45c69f80.title: Apache Avro
060d45c69f80.sentence: It uses JSON for defining data types and protocols, and serializes data in a compact binary format.

f52752a1e81c.title: Apache Avro
f52752a1e81c.sentence: It has two different types of schema languages: one for human editing (Avro IDL) and another which is more machine-readable based on JSON.

327b9ae07a5c.title: Apache Avro
327b9ae07a5c.sentence: Schemas are composed of primitive types (null, boolean, int, long, float, double, bytes, and string) and complex types (record, enum, array, map, union, and fixed).

e3acc67519f7.title: Apache Avro
e3acc67519f7.sentence: Data in Avro might be stored with its corresponding schema, meaning a serialized item can be read without knowing the schema ahead of time.

3ac59a22805b.title: Apache Avro
3ac59a22805b.sentence: An Avro Object Container File consists of:

b0a1707a8b3b.title: Apache Avro
b0a1707a8b3b.sentence: - File metadata, including the schema definition.

041677d57ad2.title: Apache Avro
041677d57ad2.sentence: It is similar to Thrift and Protocol Buffers, but does not require running a code-generation program when a schema changes (unless desired for statically-typed languages).

82b6245fe7db.title: Apache Avro
82b6245fe7db.sentence: Most applications will use the binary encoding, as it is smaller and faster.

3365a24c987c.title: Apache Avro
3365a24c987c.sentence: For debugging and web-based applications, the JSON encoding may sometimes be appropriate.

fd393973cc89.title: Event-driven architecture
fd393973cc89.sentence: Event evolution strategies in event-driven architectures (EDA) can ensure that systems can handle changes to events without disruption.

5f81a76a2e40.title: Event-driven architecture
5f81a76a2e40.sentence: These strategies can include versioning events, such as semantic versioning or schema evolution, to maintain backward and forward compatibility.

2fd4476bef34.title: Event-driven architecture
2fd4476bef34.sentence: In event driven architectures, event evolution poses challenges, such as managing inconsistent event schemas across services and ensuring compatibility during gradual system updates.

1b51087d0a5d.title: Event-driven architecture
1b51087d0a5d.sentence: Adapters can translate events between old and new formats, ensuring consistent processing across components.

e4a6714e274b.title: Event-driven architecture
e4a6714e274b.sentence: These techniques can enable systems to evolve while remaining compatible and reliable in complex, distributed environments.

0fb5068557d1.title: Event-driven architecture
0fb5068557d1.section: Extreme loose coupling and well distributed > Semantic coupling and further research
0fb5068557d1.sentence: Event-driven architectures have loose coupling within space, time and synchronization, providing a scalable infrastructure for information exchange and distributed workflows.

d44470e13d5d.title: Event-driven architecture
d44470e13d5d.section: Extreme loose coupling and well distributed > Semantic coupling and further research
d44470e13d5d.sentence: However, event-architectures are tightly coupled, via event subscriptions and patterns, to the semantics of the underlying event schema and values.

94b2b1293fa3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
