28209fabc7c5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
28209fabc7c5.sentence: - Event Registry: An event registry to define a standardized schema.

1739b8d1cee2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
1739b8d1cee2.sentence: - Custom SDKs: Custom software development kits (SDKs) to process events and handle errors.

2014cb6b1000.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
2014cb6b1000.sentence: - Event Gateway: An event gateway that performs identity authentication and authorization.

92ff124c866d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
92ff124c866d.sentence: - Utilities and Tools: Utilities and tools to fix events, keep the cluster healthy, and perform administrative tasks.

c937eb93d1a5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
c937eb93d1a5.sentence: To scale event processing, McDonald uses a regional architecture that provides global availability based on AWS.

417da8d6093d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
417da8d6093d.sentence: Within a region, producers shard events by domains, and each domain is processed by an MSK cluster.

c6f8544ea2ff.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/mcdonald's-event-driven-architecture.md
c6f8544ea2ff.sentence: The cluster auto-scales based on MSK metrics (e.g., CPU usage), and the auto-scale workflow is based on step-functions and re-assignment tasks.

d7423f9364e3.title: Loose coupling
d7423f9364e3.sentence: - in which components are weakly associated (have breakable relationships) with each other, and thus changes in one component least affect existence or performance of another component.

ad4e066c6b60.title: Loose coupling
ad4e066c6b60.sentence: - in which each of its components has, or makes use of, little or no knowledge of the definitions of other separate components.

18c4bc35d727.title: Loose coupling
18c4bc35d727.sentence: Loose coupling is the opposite of tight coupling.

df1744c98f5e.title: Loose coupling
df1744c98f5e.sentence: Subareas include the coupling of classes, interfaces, data, and services.

e6d28ff940a2.title: Loose coupling
e6d28ff940a2.sentence: Components in a loosely coupled system can be replaced with alternative implementations that provide the same services.

03445a9680a6.title: Loose coupling
03445a9680a6.sentence: Components in a loosely coupled system are less constrained to the same platform, language, operating system, or build environment.

6c0149f9251a.title: Loose coupling
6c0149f9251a.sentence: Loose coupling occurs when the dependent class contains a pointer only to an interface, which can then be implemented by one or many concrete classes.

383e8a95666f.title: Loose coupling
383e8a95666f.sentence: Any class that implements the interface can thus satisfy the dependency of a dependent class without having to change the class.

eaa157253533.title: Loose coupling
eaa157253533.sentence: A new class implementing an interface can be written to replace a current dependency in some or all situations, without requiring a change to the dependent class; the new and old classes can be interchanged freely.

101c3bf62da6.title: Loose coupling
101c3bf62da6.sentence: An example of tight coupling is when a dependent class contains a pointer directly to a concrete class which provides the required behavior.

43355c885425.title: Loose coupling
43355c885425.sentence: The dependency cannot be substituted, or its "signature" changed, without requiring a change to the dependent class.

799457ae01b3.title: Loose coupling
799457ae01b3.sentence: Loose coupling in broader distributed system design is achieved by the use of transactions, queues provided by message-oriented middleware, and interoperability standards.

c02c710ebf0b.title: Loose coupling
c02c710ebf0b.sentence: Event-driven architecture also aims at promoting loose coupling.

40ee4a8e41cf.title: Loose coupling
40ee4a8e41cf.section: In integration > Methods for decreasing coupling
40ee4a8e41cf.sentence: Loose coupling of interfaces can be enhanced by publishing data in a standard format (such as XML or JSON).

ed96668f13f5.title: Loose coupling
ed96668f13f5.section: In integration > Methods for decreasing coupling
ed96668f13f5.sentence: Loose coupling of services can be enhanced by reducing the information passed into a service to the key data.

f191677c2392.title: Loose coupling
f191677c2392.section: In integration > Methods for decreasing coupling
f191677c2392.sentence: For example, a service that sends a letter is most reusable when just the customer identifier is passed and the customer address is obtained within the service.

80e2bbfd0f94.title: Loose coupling
80e2bbfd0f94.sentence: Four types of autonomy which promote loose coupling, are: reference autonomy, time autonomy, format autonomy, and platform autonomy.

0a9228e6207b.title: Loose coupling
0a9228e6207b.sentence: If systems are decoupled in time, it is difficult to also provide transactional integrity; additional coordination protocols are required.

c662edb21e98.title: Loose coupling
c662edb21e98.sentence: Data replication across different systems provides loose coupling (in availability), but creates issues in maintaining consistency (data synchronization).

17ca87c79862.title: Monolithic application
17ca87c79862.sentence: In software engineering, a monolithic application is a single unified software application that is self-contained and independent from other applications, but typically lacks flexibility.

12d7d6e1e4a8.title: Monolithic application
12d7d6e1e4a8.sentence: In software engineering, a monolithic application describes a software application that is designed as a single service.

84373c712275.title: Monolithic application
84373c712275.sentence: The design philosophy is that the application is responsible not just for a particular task, but can perform every step needed to complete a particular function.

eb632157d79e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
eb632157d79e.sentence: A monolith is a self-contained and independent application.

85556745a659.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
85556745a659.sentence: It is built as a single unit and is responsible for not just a particular task, but can perform every step needed to satisfy a business need.

50baad2614b3.title: Monolithic application
50baad2614b3.sentence: Monolith applications are relatively simple and have a low cost but their shortcomings are lack of elasticity, fault tolerance and scalability.

e6c1f2e486f3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
e6c1f2e486f3.sentence: - Maintenance becomes hard as the codebase grows.

f95effeeac96.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
f95effeeac96.sentence: - Tightly coupled application, hard to extend.

710bbf5c150a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
710bbf5c150a.sentence: - Requires commitment to a particular technology stack.

d0fae4565db0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
d0fae4565db0.sentence: - On each update, the entire application is redeployed.

ec1edfe90c59.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
ec1edfe90c59.sentence: - Reduced reliability as a single bug can bring down the entire system.

aac3daffb21d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
aac3daffb21d.sentence: - Difficult to scale or adopt new technologies.

dc6aa78a25da.title: Monolithic application
dc6aa78a25da.sentence: Despite their popularity in recent years, monolithic applications are still a good choice for applications with small team and little complexity.

695e0b68c874.title: Monolithic application
695e0b68c874.sentence: However, once it becomes too complex, you can consider refactoring it into microservices or a distributed application.

e6dabb2cf85f.title: Monolithic application
e6dabb2cf85f.sentence: Note that a monolithic application deployed on a single machine, may be performant enough for your current workload but it's less available, less durable, less changeable, less fine-tuned and less scalable than a well designed distributed system.

26b478e00881.title: Monolithic application
26b478e00881.sentence: The following are common architectural patterns used for monolithic applications, with each having their own trade-offs:

d820b0395017.title: Microservices
d820b0395017.sentence: In software engineering, a microservice architecture is an architectural pattern that organizes an application into a collection of loosely coupled, fine-grained services that communicate through lightweight protocols.

bfb77ff79acb.title: Microservices
bfb77ff79acb.sentence: This pattern allows teams to develop, deploy, and scale services independently, improving modularity, scalability, and adaptability.

a8b06ce0d6b9.title: Microservices
a8b06ce0d6b9.sentence: There is no single, universally agreed-upon definition of microservices.

f600d94880e5.title: Microservices
f600d94880e5.sentence: However, they are generally characterized by a focus on modularity, with each service designed around a specific business capability.

9b41483a6921.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
9b41483a6921.sentence: A microservices architecture consists of a collection of small, autonomous services where each service is self-contained and should implement a single business capability within a bounded context.

6e7df9aa9677.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
6e7df9aa9677.sentence: Each service has a separate codebase, which can be managed by a small development team.

b3922ab770a0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
b3922ab770a0.sentence: Services are responsible for persisting their own data or external state (database per service).

f4b52f4ed867.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
f4b52f4ed867.sentence: This differs from the traditional model, where a separate data layer handles data persistence.

fa073404399c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
fa073404399c.sentence: - Loosely coupled: Services should be loosely coupled so that they can be independently deployed and scaled.

ee518e9f67f0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
ee518e9f67f0.sentence: - Small but focused: It's about scope and responsibilities and not size, a service should be focused on a specific problem.

c6f62cb8644e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
c6f62cb8644e.sentence: - Built for businesses: The microservices architecture is usually organized around business capabilities and priorities.

8981dd22ae91.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
8981dd22ae91.sentence: - Resilience & Fault tolerance: Services should be designed in such a way that they still function in case of failure or errors.

95431eff6ec4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
95431eff6ec4.sentence: - Highly maintainable: Service should be easy to maintain and test because services that cannot be maintained will be rewritten.

16031ae53a53.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
16031ae53a53.sentence: - Highly agile for multiple development teams.

7f99c4a1d88c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
7f99c4a1d88c.sentence: - Improves fault tolerance and data isolation.

9d9cd77495ad.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
9d9cd77495ad.sentence: - Eliminates any long-term commitment to a particular technology stack.

87fcdb2c95d1.title: Microservices
87fcdb2c95d1.sentence: - Distributed development: it parallelizes development by enabling small autonomous teams to develop, deploy and scale their respective services independently.

32747b44f35a.title: Microservices
32747b44f35a.sentence: In the monolithic approach, an application supporting three functions would have to be scaled in its entirety even if only one of these functions had a resource constraint.

432a3ce7e9dc.title: Microservices
432a3ce7e9dc.sentence: With microservices, only the microservice supporting the function with resource constraints needs to be scaled out, thus providing resource and cost optimization benefits.

5016fe55a789.title: Microservices
5016fe55a789.sentence: - Scalability: Since microservices are implemented and deployed independently of each other, i.e. they run within independent processes, they can be monitored and scaled independently.

6509161eb35f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
6509161eb35f.sentence: - Expensive to maintain (individual servers, databases, etc.).

0e3bc8bcca4c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
0e3bc8bcca4c.sentence: - Inter-service communication has its own challenges.

9e2cc67f00e3.title: Microservices
9e2cc67f00e3.sentence: - Inter-service calls over a network have a higher cost in terms of network latency and message processing time than in-process calls within a monolithic service process.

fe9ec3693f3e.title: Microservices
fe9ec3693f3e.sentence: The complexity of a monolithic application does not disappear if it is re-implemented as a set of microservices.

f564959f956f.title: Microservices
f564959f956f.sentence: Some of the complexity gets translated into operational complexity.

ffb5d69811f8.title: Microservices
ffb5d69811f8.sentence: According to Fowler, because of the large number (when compared to monolithic application implementations) of services, decentralized continuous delivery and DevOps with holistic service monitoring are necessary to effectively develop, maintain, and operate such applications.

d1b3ac80a176.title: Microservices
d1b3ac80a176.sentence: However, it introduces additional complexity, particularly in managing distributed systems and inter-service communication, making the initial implementation more challenging compared to a monolithic architecture.

4f0dd79143da.title: Service-oriented architecture
4f0dd79143da.sentence: In software engineering, service-oriented architecture (SOA) is an architectural style that focuses on discrete services instead of a monolithic design.

2f2ca139b03c.title: Service-oriented architecture
2f2ca139b03c.sentence: A service is a discrete unit of functionality that can be accessed remotely and acted upon and updated independently, such as retrieving a credit card statement online.

78474dfdb499.title: Service-oriented architecture
78474dfdb499.sentence: SOA is also intended to be independent of vendors, products and technologies.

f65dd51ee7bd.title: Service-oriented architecture
f65dd51ee7bd.sentence: SOA is a good choice for system integration.

e57c55161ac9.title: Service-oriented architecture
e57c55161ac9.sentence: A service has four properties according to one of many definitions of SOA:

8cd53b95fbd4.title: Service-oriented architecture
8cd53b95fbd4.sentence: - It logically represents a repeatable business activity with a specified outcome.

6428b1b769d1.title: Service-oriented architecture
6428b1b769d1.sentence: - It is a black box for its consumers, meaning the consumer does not have to be aware of the service's inner workings.

6ebbb9b5caaa.title: Service-oriented architecture
6ebbb9b5caaa.sentence: - It may be composed of other services.

960c5e0abee5.title: Service-oriented architecture
960c5e0abee5.sentence: These services and their corresponding consumers communicate with each other by passing data in a well-defined, shared format, or by coordinating an activity between two or more services.

e7d1f588f252.title: Service-oriented architecture
e7d1f588f252.sentence: Service-oriented architecture aims to allow users to combine large chunks of functionality to form applications which are built purely from existing services and combining them in an ad hoc manner.

91085334f071.title: Service-oriented architecture
91085334f071.sentence: This style of architecture promotes reuse at the macro (service) level rather than micro (classes) level.

30ec9bd70715.title: Service-oriented architecture
30ec9bd70715.sentence: It can also simplify interconnection to—and usage of—existing IT (legacy) assets.

9af89c26719f.title: Service-oriented architecture
9af89c26719f.sentence: - Separation promotes the concept to the business that services can be delivered quickly and independently from the larger and slower-moving projects common in the organization.

d26c6a157e00.title: Service-oriented architecture
d26c6a157e00.sentence: - Separation promotes the decoupling of services from consuming projects.

dfe15661d0bb.title: Service-oriented architecture
dfe15661d0bb.sentence: This encourages good design insofar as the service is designed without knowing who its consumers are.

830140dcd42d.title: Service-oriented architecture
830140dcd42d.sentence: Service-oriented architecture can be implemented with web services or microservices.

5607b425dfa0.title: Service-oriented architecture
5607b425dfa0.sentence: Implementers commonly build SOAs using web services standards.

e2d107bd60f3.title: Service-oriented architecture
e2d107bd60f3.sentence: One example is SOAP, which has gained broad industry acceptance after the recommendation of Version 1.2 from the W3C (World Wide Web Consortium) in 2003.

9a9d71e3aecd.title: Service-oriented architecture
9a9d71e3aecd.sentence: One can, however, also implement SOA using any other service-based technology, such as Jini, CORBA, Internet Communications Engine, REST, or gRPC.

111217ca29b7.title: Service-oriented architecture
111217ca29b7.sentence: In the absence of native or binary forms of remote procedure call (RPC), applications could run more slowly and require more processing power, increasing costs.

f66e760ebed8.title: Service-oriented architecture
f66e760ebed8.sentence: Most implementations do incur these overheads, but SOA can be implemented using technologies (for example, Java Business Integration (JBI), Windows Communication Foundation (WCF) and data distribution service (DDS)) that do not depend on remote procedure calls or translation through XML or JSON.

4b5d5e597d19.title: Service-oriented architecture
4b5d5e597d19.sentence: Stateful services require both the consumer and the provider to share the same consumer-specific context, which is either included in or referenced by messages exchanged between the provider and the consumer.

aeb3baa02a87.title: Service-oriented architecture
aeb3baa02a87.sentence: This constraint has the drawback that it could reduce the overall scalability of the service provider if the service-provider needs to retain the shared context for each consumer.

84e048d1b871.title: Service-oriented architecture
84e048d1b871.sentence: It also increases the coupling between a service provider and a consumer and makes switching service providers more difficult.

9efd4332ab5e.title: Service-oriented architecture
9efd4332ab5e.sentence: Another major problem faced by SOA is the lack of a uniform testing framework.

ef1bb59eff95.title: Service discovery
ef1bb59eff95.sentence: Service discovery is the process of automatically detecting devices and services on a computer network.

53a7b62de66f.title: Service discovery
53a7b62de66f.sentence: It aims to reduce the manual configuration effort required from users and administrators.

a3ba12c22bb7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
a3ba12c22bb7.sentence: Service discovery is the detection of services within a computer network.

af28c0890e81.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
af28c0890e81.section: Why do we need Service Discovery?
af28c0890e81.sentence: In a monolithic application, services invoke one another through language-level methods or procedure calls.

f67e2595106b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
f67e2595106b.section: Why do we need Service Discovery?
f67e2595106b.sentence: However, modern microservices-based applications typically run in virtualized or containerized environments where the number of instances of a service and their locations change dynamically.

04501f9ad8d2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
04501f9ad8d2.section: Why do we need Service Discovery?
04501f9ad8d2.sentence: Consequently, we need a mechanism that enables the clients of service to make requests to a dynamically changing set of ephemeral service instances.

2292fc9d6a2c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/9-best-practices-for-building-microservices.md
2292fc9d6a2c.sentence: To communicate with each other, microservices need to discover each other over the network.

12687af98f0f.title: Service discovery
12687af98f0f.sentence: A service discovery protocol (SDP) is a network protocol that helps accomplish service discovery.

17c9e9384cd2.title: Service discovery
17c9e9384cd2.sentence: Service discovery requires a common language to allow software agents to make use of one another's services without the need for continuous user intervention.

39c912bc5c95.title: Service discovery
39c912bc5c95.sentence: There are many service discovery protocols, including:

0345dd33ee63.title: Service discovery
0345dd33ee63.sentence: - DNS Service Discovery (DNS-SD), a component of zero-configuration networking

e0b966b550a1.title: Service discovery
e0b966b550a1.sentence: - Simple Service Discovery Protocol (SSDP), a component of Universal Plug and Play (UPnP)

33f3a83b45b8.title: Service discovery
33f3a83b45b8.sentence: - DNS, as used for example in Kubernetes

fcd3ee7a5a1c.title: Kubernetes
fcd3ee7a5a1c.sentence: Kubernetes provides two modes of service discovery, using environment variables or using Kubernetes DNS.

af2fa7ab652f.title: Service mesh
af2fa7ab652f.sentence: In software architecture, a service mesh is a dedicated infrastructure layer for facilitating service-to-service communications between services or microservices using a proxy.

bde0aad9c621.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
bde0aad9c621.sentence: Service mesh enables managed, observable, and secure communication between individual services.

ee5eeecc4a44.title: Service mesh
ee5eeecc4a44.sentence: A dedicated communication layer can provide numerous benefits, such as providing observability into communications, providing secure connections, and automating retries and backoff for failed requests.

4fb0d592ea1c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
4fb0d592ea1c.sentence: Service-to-service communication is essential in a distributed application but routing this communication, both within and across application clusters, becomes increasingly complex as the number of services grows.

92667945c5ca.title: Service mesh
92667945c5ca.sentence: A service mesh consists of network proxies paired with each service in an application and a set of task-management processes.

2a1c2268f0ea.title: Service mesh
2a1c2268f0ea.sentence: The proxies are called the data plane and the management processes are called the control plane.

aed6e91953ab.title: Service mesh
aed6e91953ab.sentence: The data plane intercepts calls between different services and processes them; the control plane is the brain of the mesh that coordinates the behavior of proxies and provides APIs for operations and maintenance personnel to manipulate and observe the entire network.

64bc4f11659d.title: Microservices
64bc4f11659d.sentence: In a service mesh, each service instance is paired with an instance of a reverse proxy server, called a service proxy, sidecar proxy, or sidecar.

6e8b7fbf8295.title: Microservices
6e8b7fbf8295.sentence: The service instance and sidecar proxy share a container, and the containers are managed by a container orchestration tool such as Kubernetes, Docker Swarm, or DC/OS.

6d8bf41b0ce9.title: Microservices
6d8bf41b0ce9.sentence: The service proxies are responsible for communication with other service instances and can support capabilities such as service (instance) discovery, load balancing, authentication and authorization, secure communications, and others.

bf29cb178f5a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
bf29cb178f5a.sentence: It works with a service discovery protocol to detect services.

5adfc0937767.title: Service mesh
5adfc0937767.sentence: The service mesh architecture is implemented by software products such as Istio, Cilium, Linkerd, Consul, AWS App Mesh, Kuma, Traefik Mesh, and Greymatter.io.

8f4550b06b10.title: Service mesh
8f4550b06b10.sentence: Many service meshes use the Envoy proxy on the data plane.

d5a72d63eca2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
d5a72d63eca2.sentence: Istio and envoy are some of the most commonly used service mesh technologies.

dcd9fdef9ab7.title: Observability (software)
dcd9fdef9ab7.sentence: A cloud native application is typically made up of distributed services which together fulfill a single request.

da42bbd8d9f4.title: Observability (software)
da42bbd8d9f4.sentence: A distributed trace is an interrelated series of discrete events (also called spans) that track the progression of a single user request.

6d050a57c619.title: Observability (software)
6d050a57c619.sentence: A trace shows the causal and temporal relationships between the services that interoperate to fulfill a request.

56f36311b242.title: Observability (software)
56f36311b242.sentence: To be able to follow a request as it traverses multiple services, spans are labeled with unique identifiers that enable constructing a parent-child relationship between spans.

c3ee70911aff.title: Observability (software)
c3ee70911aff.sentence: Span information is typically shared in the HTTP headers of outbound requests.

6fceab4aa803.title: Observability (software)
6fceab4aa803.sentence: Instrumenting an application with traces means sending span information to a tracing backend.

853eb1a2f9e2.title: Observability (software)
853eb1a2f9e2.sentence: The tracing backend correlates the received spans to generate presentable traces.

2fde1b68341f.title: Tracing (software)
2fde1b68341f.sentence: Tracing is primarily used for anomaly detection, fault analysis, debugging or diagnostic purposes in distributed software systems, such as microservices or serverless functions.

00e7b97cda5f.title: Tracing (software)
00e7b97cda5f.sentence: The primary visualization method is the swimlane view, which is exemplified by tools like Jaeger and often includes annotations and key-value attributes.

e7dcb438f0de.title: Tracing (software)
e7dcb438f0de.sentence: Aggregate visualizations are also used for analyzing large volumes of traces, with systems like Canopy offering queryable metrics and Jaeger providing trace comparison features.

e2d568086130.title: Tracing (software)
e2d568086130.sentence: The overhead of tracing depends on the used framework and the activated features; in production servers, there is a trade-off between how fine-grained the tracing is and the incurred overhead.

a9653583286e.title: Tracing (software)
a9653583286e.sentence: Given its low-level nature, tracing can generate a large volume of messages.

abab783ccda6.title: Tracing (software)
abab783ccda6.sentence: To mitigate performance issues, it's often necessary to have the option to deactivate software tracing, either at the time of compilation or during run-time.

df4f418daf5c.title: Tracing (software)
df4f418daf5c.sentence: OpenTelemetry is a CNCF open source project that provides comprehensive support for distributed tracing.

e25c9a72dc07.title: Cloud Native Computing Foundation
e25c9a72dc07.sentence: - Jaeger, Created by Uber Engineering, Jaeger is an open source distributed tracing system inspired by Google Dapper paper and OpenZipkin community.

13cfa53571cc.title: Tracing (software)
13cfa53571cc.sentence: Google and Meta have developed their own tracing frameworks, named Dapper and Canopy respectively.

2f1dbbba5ea9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
2f1dbbba5ea9.sentence: N-tier architecture divides an application into logical layers and physical tiers.

0e7f52df81a9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
0e7f52df81a9.sentence: Layers are a way to separate responsibilities and manage dependencies.

4662fad83d9a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
4662fad83d9a.sentence: Each layer has a specific responsibility.

0dc5d7f1780e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
0dc5d7f1780e.sentence: A higher layer can use services in a lower layer, but not the other way around.

72ec1cd38d62.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
72ec1cd38d62.sentence: Tiers are physically separated, running on separate machines.

9ce6fa6ab25f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
9ce6fa6ab25f.sentence: A tier can call to another tier directly, or use asynchronous messaging.

a27332c57819.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
a27332c57819.sentence: Although each layer might be hosted in its own tier, that's not required.

4e15d34a9a60.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
4e15d34a9a60.sentence: Several layers might be hosted on the same tier.

a4ab837655be.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
a4ab837655be.sentence: Physically separating the tiers improves scalability and resiliency and adds latency from the additional network communication.

1b1ceb253c20.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
1b1ceb253c20.sentence: - In a closed layer architecture, a layer can only call the next layer immediately down.

76ed818e1d3d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
76ed818e1d3d.sentence: - In an open layer architecture, a layer can call any of the layers below it.

24c5c81fbbfc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
24c5c81fbbfc.sentence: A closed-layer architecture limits the dependencies between layers.

786aa4d0923a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
786aa4d0923a.sentence: However, it might create unnecessary network traffic, if one layer simply passes requests along to the next layer.

c914c63bca6f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
c914c63bca6f.sentence: 3-Tier is widely used and consists of the following different layers:

ade2930372df.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
ade2930372df.sentence: - Presentation layer: Handles user interactions with the application.

ea1acd84939e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
ea1acd84939e.sentence: - Business Logic layer: Accepts the data from the application layer, validates it as per business logic and passes it to the data layer.

9d607d17ec28.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
9d607d17ec28.sentence: - Data Access layer: Receives the data from the business layer and performs the necessary operation on the database.

69100af854d1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
69100af854d1.sentence: In this architecture, the presentation layer runs on the client and communicates with a data store.

321df1c4d234.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
321df1c4d234.sentence: There is no business logic layer or immediate layer between client and server.

b18e36b7fd5d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
b18e36b7fd5d.section: Types of N-Tier architectures > Single Tier or 1-Tier architecture
b18e36b7fd5d.sentence: It is the simplest one as it is equivalent to running the application on a personal computer.

4b65d5cc434b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
4b65d5cc434b.section: Types of N-Tier architectures > Single Tier or 1-Tier architecture
4b65d5cc434b.sentence: All of the required components for an application to run are on a single application or server.

17b2f4685ca4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
17b2f4685ca4.sentence: - Better security as layers can behave like a firewall.

35f6b4b6348b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
35f6b4b6348b.sentence: - Separate tiers allow us to scale them as needed.

476798270ede.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
476798270ede.sentence: - Improve maintenance as different people can manage different tiers.

eae4d832599e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
eae4d832599e.sentence: - Increased complexity of the system as a whole.

4e4b29c450ca.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
4e4b29c450ca.sentence: - Increased network latency as the number of tiers increases.

849afe3d0cb2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::n-tier-architecture
849afe3d0cb2.sentence: - Expensive as every tier will have its own hardware cost.

343a614cb3cc.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
343a614cb3cc.sentence: How do microservices collaborate and interact with each other?

1ba44ed1b68c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
1ba44ed1b68c.sentence: Service choreography describes this exchange of messages and the rules by which the microservices interact.

617ae7e2e4d3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
617ae7e2e4d3.sentence: The orchestrator acts as a center of authority.

a1978140186a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
a1978140186a.sentence: It is responsible for invoking and combining the services.

765d391b4083.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
765d391b4083.sentence: - Reliability - orchestration has built-in transaction management and error handling, while choreography is point-to-point communications and the fault tolerance scenarios are much more complicated.

8c9dbe7d35ea.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
8c9dbe7d35ea.sentence: It describes the interactions between all the participating services.

15a03ad72bfe.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
15a03ad72bfe.sentence: The orchestration pattern also includes the transaction management among different services.

069fc9627171.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
069fc9627171.sentence: - Scalability - when adding a new service into orchestration, only the orchestrator needs to modify the interaction rules, while in choreography all the interacting services need to be modified.

39c7a27eae9d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
39c7a27eae9d.sentence: - Performance - all the services talk via a centralized orchestrator, so latency is higher than it is with choreography.

735f88ac7dc5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
735f88ac7dc5.sentence: Also, the throughput is bound to the capacity of the orchestrator.

254673428c6c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
254673428c6c.sentence: - Single point of failure - if the orchestrator goes down, no services can talk to each other.

3b6efeb34af3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
3b6efeb34af3.sentence: To mitigate this, the orchestrator must be highly available.

7f368016e150.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/orchestration-vs-choreography-microservices.md
7f368016e150.sentence: Real-world use case: Netflix Conductor is a microservice orchestrator and you can read more details on the orchestrator design.

da7dc9beb333.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
da7dc9beb333.sentence: You might have seen Service-oriented architecture (SOA) mentioned around the internet, sometimes even interchangeably with microservices, but they are different from each other and the main distinction between the two approaches comes down to scope.

1e1f40857409.title: Service-oriented architecture
1e1f40857409.sentence: Microservices are a modern interpretation of service-oriented architectures used to build distributed software systems.

b2445df12182.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
b2445df12182.sentence: Service-oriented architecture (SOA) defines a way to make software components reusable via service interfaces.

a88244e01724.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices
a88244e01724.sentence: These interfaces utilize common communication standards and focus on maximizing application service reusability whereas microservices are built as a collection of various smallest independent service units focused on team autonomy and decoupling.

b0d431bd7f69.title: Service-oriented architecture
b0d431bd7f69.sentence: Microservices are a new realisation and implementation approach to SOA, which have become popular since 2014 (and after the introduction of DevOps), and which also emphasize continuous deployment and other agile practices.

11445f804b96.title: Service-oriented architecture
11445f804b96.sentence: The following characteristics and principles can be found in the literature:

e78434b44fd6.title: Service-oriented architecture
e78434b44fd6.sentence: Each SOA building block can play any of the three roles:

33ae2ebd4f98.title: Service-oriented architecture
33ae2ebd4f98.sentence: It creates a web service and provides its information to the service registry.

4cb0bb3242e1.title: Service-oriented architecture
4cb0bb3242e1.sentence: Its main functionality is to make information regarding the web service available to any potential requester.

7df30a89406c.title: Service-oriented architecture
7df30a89406c.sentence: It locates entries in the broker registry using various find operations and then binds to the service provider in order to invoke one of its web services.

982e00b784a2.title: Service-oriented architecture
982e00b784a2.sentence: Service broker, service registry or service repository

7d783629af1a.title: Service-oriented architecture
7d783629af1a.sentence: Public brokers are available anywhere and everywhere but private brokers are only available to a limited amount of public.

963d75564c82.title: Service-oriented architecture
963d75564c82.sentence: The service consumer–provider relationship is governed by a standardized service contract, which has a business part, a functional part and a technical part.

034cf745cb4b.title: Service-oriented architecture
034cf745cb4b.sentence: There are no industry standards relating to the exact composition of a service-oriented architecture, although many industry sources have published their own principles.

80aa170d087a.title: Service-oriented architecture
80aa170d087a.sentence: Some of these include the following:

59c0717c5666.title: Service-oriented architecture
59c0717c5666.sentence: Services adhere to a standard communications agreement, as defined collectively by one or more service description documents within a given set of services.

aab00c22f841.title: Service-oriented architecture
aab00c22f841.sentence: The relationship between services is minimized to the level that they are only aware of their existence.

58b3387e07c9.title: Service-oriented architecture
58b3387e07c9.sentence: Services can be called from anywhere within the network that it is located no matter where it is present.

b9f81bcd0641.title: Service-oriented architecture
b9f81bcd0641.sentence: The services act as black boxes, that is their inner logic is hidden from the consumers.

ea3279dbbc77.title: Service-oriented architecture
ea3279dbbc77.sentence: Services are independent and control the functionality they encapsulate, from a Design-time and a run-time perspective.

44542cc0f86e.title: Service-oriented architecture
44542cc0f86e.sentence: Services are stateless, that is either return the requested value or give an exception hence minimizing resource use.

30780e343e4c.title: Service-oriented architecture
30780e343e4c.sentence: Services should be designed to be long lived.

d3be3dce27a3.title: Service-oriented architecture
d3be3dce27a3.sentence: Where possible, services should avoid forcing consumers to change if they do not require new features; if you call a service today, you should be able to call the same service tomorrow.

165650db5c1f.title: Service-oriented architecture
165650db5c1f.sentence: Services can be used to compose other services.

9c9fdb632ae4.title: Service-oriented architecture
9c9fdb632ae4.sentence: Services are supplemented with communicative meta data by which they can be effectively discovered and interpreted.

600402a855b8.title: Service-oriented architecture
600402a855b8.sentence: Logic is divided into various services, to promote reuse of code.

1cfc52885bcb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
1cfc52885bcb.sentence: A service registry is basically a database containing the network locations of service instances to which the clients can reach out.

9a09ea168be6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
9a09ea168be6.sentence: A Service Registry must be highly available and up-to-date.

6b63d81fa362.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
6b63d81fa362.sentence: We also need a way to obtain service information, often known as service registration.

1beec6556e41.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
1beec6556e41.sentence: When using the self-registration model, a service instance is responsible for registering and de-registering itself in the Service Registry.

12e5b4b53f87.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
12e5b4b53f87.sentence: In addition, if necessary, a service instance sends heartbeat requests to keep its registration alive.

6a62003475fe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
6a62003475fe.sentence: The registry keeps track of changes to running instances by polling the deployment environment or subscribing to events.

e04e353c4aa0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
e04e353c4aa0.sentence: When it detects a newly available service instance, it records it in its database.

300889931311.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
300889931311.sentence: The Service Registry also de-registers terminated service instances.

7de6e2370d56.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
7de6e2370d56.sentence: - Load Balancer: This distributes incoming traffic across multiple backend services.

37be123b3db0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
37be123b3db0.sentence: - CDN (Content Delivery Network): CDN is a group of geographically distributed servers that hold static content for faster delivery.

9bf205ed6d4d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
9bf205ed6d4d.sentence: - API Gateway: This handles incoming requests and routes them to the relevant services.

1287bf8a1b59.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
1287bf8a1b59.sentence: - Identity Provider: This handles authentication and authorization for users.

8fa996e6ef88.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
8fa996e6ef88.sentence: - Service Registry & Discovery: Microservice registration and discovery happen in this component, and the API gateway looks for relevant services in this component to talk to.

2edfec600d1c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
2edfec600d1c.sentence: - Management: This component is responsible for monitoring the services.

999bd91108e7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
999bd91108e7.sentence: - Microservices: Microservices are designed and deployed in different domains.

c82b635f4eee.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
c82b635f4eee.sentence: The clients look for content in CDN first, then progress to backend services.

04739d4b0e56.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-does-a-typical-microservice-architecture-look-like.md
04739d4b0e56.sentence: It talks to the identity provider and service discovery.

e38402b32b4d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery
e38402b32b4d.sentence: There are two main service discovery patterns:

01c5b169b794.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::service-discovery

17b3856bf8b9.title: Microservices

fa3749706bf2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::monoliths-and-microservices

0dec8863ca90.title: Microservices
0dec8863ca90.sentence: In microservices architecture, a bounded context often maps to a microservice, but this relationship can vary depending on the design approach.

d1e0fb6ff606.title: Microservices
d1e0fb6ff606.sentence: A one-to-one relationship, where each bounded context is implemented as a single microservice, is typically ideal as it maintains clear boundaries, reduces coupling, and enables independent deployment and scaling.

5d9c2ca1df07.title: Microservices
5d9c2ca1df07.sentence: However, other mappings may also be appropriate: a one-to-many relationship can arise when a bounded context is divided into multiple microservices to address varying scalability or other operational needs, while a many-to-one relationship may consolidate multiple bounded contexts into a single microservice for simplicity or to minimize operational overhead.

fcf249a22e06.title: Microservices
fcf249a22e06.sentence: The choice of relationship should balance the principles of DDD with the system's business goals, technical constraints, and operational requirements.

915f06ea3faa.title: Microservices

9a9621a19c02.title: Microservices

b8ce47527291.title: Microservices
b8ce47527291.sentence: A cell typically consists of multiple microservices and functions as an autonomous unit.

109872191e65.title: Microservices
109872191e65.sentence: In some implementations, entire sets of microservices are replicated across multiple cells, enabling requests to be rerouted to another operational cell if one experiences a failure.

1d414417f4ba.title: Microservices
1d414417f4ba.sentence: This approach is intended to improve system-wide resilience by limiting the impact of localized failures.

7324dafd183f.title: Microservices
7324dafd183f.sentence: Some implementations incorporate circuit breakers within and between cells.

f2e87d76c068.title: Microservices
f2e87d76c068.sentence: Within a cell, circuit breakers may be used to mitigate cascading failures among microservices, while inter-cell circuit breakers can isolate failing cells and redirect traffic to those that remain operational.

5a7c0c4b5da8.title: Microservices

546f1efea1e2.title: Microservices

fbffbb1d6c60.title: Microservices

8c62774e58b5.title: Microservices

25f378e1b51a.title: Microservices

2aa42662a5f7.title: Microservices

98eba171a118.title: Microservices

f079f72bac47.title: Strangler fig pattern
f079f72bac47.sentence: In programming, the strangler fig pattern or strangler pattern is an architectural pattern that involves wrapping old code, with the intent of redirecting it to newer code or to log uses of the old code.

c24b6609ee53.title: Strangler fig pattern
c24b6609ee53.sentence: One use of this pattern is during software rewrites.

9f5ce1321054.title: Strangler fig pattern

dab60cecde5a.title: Strangler fig pattern

945cba5214ac.title: Strangler fig pattern

3527e1a9ab7f.title: Strangler fig pattern

1f40228a4ee9.title: API
