0c026ba5a2e2.title: API
0c026ba5a2e2.sentence: One of the main purpose of APIs is to hide the internal details of how a system works, exposing only those parts a programmer will find useful and keeping them consistent even if the internal details later change.

3b792fa25789.title: API
3b792fa25789.sentence: A well-designed API exposes only objects or actions needed by software or software developers.

469054ae2079.title: API
469054ae2079.sentence: It hides details that have no use.

7df650f3833d.title: REST
7df650f3833d.sentence: REST (Representational State Transfer) is a software architectural style that was created to describe the design and guide the development of the architecture for the World Wide Web.

0c4b4004a304.title: REST
0c4b4004a304.sentence: REST defines a set of constraints for how the architecture of a distributed, Internet-scale hypermedia system, such as the Web, should behave.

950232b7f26a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
950232b7f26a.sentence: A REST API (also known as RESTful API) is an application programming interface that conforms to the constraints of REST architectural style and allows for interaction with RESTful web services.

68d9ca4354fc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
68d9ca4354fc.sentence: REST stands for Representational State Transfer and it was first introduced by Roy Fielding in the year 2000.

09023a9b687c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
09023a9b687c.sentence: In REST API, the fundamental unit is a resource.

24f1031be542.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
24f1031be542.sentence: HTTP defines a set of request methods to indicate the desired action to be performed for a given resource.

4df2ee31d510.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
4df2ee31d510.sentence: - GET: Request a representation of the specified resource.

a408ddc41b39.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
a408ddc41b39.sentence: - POST: Submits an entity to the specified resource, often causing a change in state or side effects on the server.

fe1ab767e282.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
fe1ab767e282.sentence: - PUT: Replaces all current representations of the target resource with the request payload.

052c35c24a90.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
052c35c24a90.sentence: - PATCH: Applies partial modifications to a resource.

adaac0d92af0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
adaac0d92af0.sentence: /users/{id} | GET | Get a user by id

1d54fce17850.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
1d54fce17850.sentence: /users/{id} | PATCH | Update a user by id

99111af5a5de.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
99111af5a5de.sentence: /users/{id} | DELETE | Delete a user by id

ead70b13a7cb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
ead70b13a7cb.sentence: - Sometimes multiple round trips to the server are required.

03b2b51e9f7a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
03b2b51e9f7a.sentence: REST APIs are pretty much used universally and are the default standard for designing APIs.

e5fe56ea5422.title: REST
e5fe56ea5422.sentence: An application that adheres to the REST architectural constraints may be informally described as RESTful, although this term is more commonly associated with the design of HTTP-based APIs and what are widely considered best practices regarding the "verbs" (HTTP methods) a resource responds to, while having little to do with REST as originally formulated—and is often even at odds with the concept.

98e11273f36d.title: REST
98e11273f36d.sentence: The REST architectural style emphasizes uniform interfaces, independent deployment of components, the scalability of interactions between them, and creating a layered architecture to promote caching to reduce user-perceived latency, enforce security, and encapsulate legacy systems.

58b9fff2bb14.title: Remote procedure call
58b9fff2bb14.sentence: In distributed computing, a remote procedure call (RPC) is an action in which a computer program causes a procedure (subroutine) to execute in a different address space of the current process (commonly on another computer on a shared computer network), which is written as if it were a normal (local) procedure call, without the programmer explicitly writing the details for the remote interaction.

9dc319312bdf.title: Remote procedure call
9dc319312bdf.sentence: That is, the programmer writes essentially the same code whether the subroutine is local to the executing program, or remote.

d69880822e4b.title: Remote procedure call
d69880822e4b.sentence: This is a form of server interaction (caller is client, executor is server), typically implemented via a request–response message passing system.

406e30555bd5.title: Remote procedure call
406e30555bd5.sentence: An RPC is initiated by the client, which sends a request message to a known remote server to execute a specified procedure with supplied parameters.

76cc5231244c.title: Remote procedure call
76cc5231244c.sentence: The remote server sends a response to the client, and the application continues its process.

23bcd1b40697.title: Remote procedure call
23bcd1b40697.sentence: While the server is processing the call, the client is blocked (it waits until the server has finished processing before resuming execution), unless the client sends an asynchronous request to the server, such as an XMLHttpRequest.

a30e069e1cb0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
a30e069e1cb0.sentence: RPC (Remote Procedure Call) is called “remote” because it enables communications between remote services when services are deployed to different servers under microservice architecture.

f5207a797947.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
f5207a797947.sentence: From the user’s point of view, it acts like a local function call.

1b7a8edea17d.title: Remote procedure call
1b7a8edea17d.sentence: The RPC model implies a level of location transparency, namely that calling procedures are largely the same whether they are local or remote, but usually, they are not identical, so local calls can be distinguished from remote calls.

a77ec0ddf03d.title: Remote procedure call
a77ec0ddf03d.sentence: Remote calls are usually orders of magnitude slower and less reliable than local calls, so distinguishing them is important.

c5102002edf5.title: Remote procedure call
c5102002edf5.sentence: An important difference between remote procedure calls and local calls is that remote calls can fail because of unpredictable network problems.

868ed83b3b40.title: Remote procedure call
868ed83b3b40.sentence: Also, callers generally must deal with such failures without knowing whether the remote procedure was actually invoked.

fe67fb9fe6a3.title: Remote procedure call
fe67fb9fe6a3.sentence: Idempotent procedures (those that have no additional effects if called more than once) are easily handled, but enough difficulties remain that code to call remote procedures is often confined to carefully written low-level subsystems.

cf90a0a261fc.title: Remote procedure call
cf90a0a261fc.sentence: To let different clients access servers, a number of standardized RPC systems have been created.

0fb68e7b8890.title: Remote procedure call
0fb68e7b8890.sentence: Most of these use an interface description language (IDL) to let various platforms call the RPC.

8ef742ff6fc9.title: Remote procedure call
8ef742ff6fc9.sentence: The IDL files can then be used to generate code to interface between the client and servers.

225c28e9731d.title: Remote procedure call
225c28e9731d.sentence: Many different (often incompatible) technologies have been used to implement the concept.

5da87affc262.title: Remote procedure call
5da87affc262.sentence: - XML-RPC is an RPC protocol that uses XML to encode its calls and HTTP as a transport mechanism.

5bfab7d7f7db.title: Remote procedure call
5bfab7d7f7db.sentence: - JSON-RPC is an RPC protocol that uses JSON-encoded messages.

3739eecfa56b.title: Remote procedure call
3739eecfa56b.sentence: - SOAP is a successor of XML-RPC and also uses XML to encode its HTTP-based calls.

1153ae4ce5d3.title: Remote procedure call
1153ae4ce5d3.sentence: In the object-oriented programming paradigm, RPCs are represented by remote method invocation (RMI).

0e61f1a4190f.title: Remote procedure call
0e61f1a4190f.sentence: Modern RPC frameworks, such as gRPC and Apache Thrift, enhance the basic RPC model by using efficient binary serialization (e.g., Protocol Buffers), HTTP/2 multiplexing, and built-in support for features such as authentication, load balancing, streaming, and error handling, making them well-suited for building scalable microservices and enabling language interoperability.

d4061b42f053.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
d4061b42f053.sentence: GraphQL is a query language and server-side runtime for APIs that prioritizes giving clients exactly the data they request and no more.

cef92993f005.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/rest-api-vs-graphql.md
cef92993f005.sentence: - Provides a single endpoint for clients to query for precisely the data they need.

7a27bc0ea3b3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/rest-api-vs-graphql.md
7a27bc0ea3b3.sentence: - Clients specify the exact fields required in nested queries, and the server returns optimized payloads containing just those fields.

e1f86fc0c81b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
e1f86fc0c81b.sentence: A GraphQL schema describes the functionality clients can utilize once they connect to the GraphQL server.

b7fed55061fc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
b7fed55061fc.sentence: A query is a request made by the client.

234a753b85ee.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
234a753b85ee.sentence: It can consist of fields and arguments for the query.

7854ea8b4331.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
7854ea8b4331.sentence: The operation type of a query can also be a mutation which provides a way to modify server-side data.

740e47d63edf.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
740e47d63edf.sentence: Resolver is a collection of functions that generate responses for a GraphQL query.

95c164624676.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
95c164624676.sentence: In simple terms, a resolver acts as a GraphQL query handler.

7845b498181e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/rest-api-vs-graphql.md
7845b498181e.sentence: - Supports Mutations for modifying data and Subscriptions for real-time notifications.

81cf335170a8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
81cf335170a8.sentence: Additionally, GraphQL gives API maintainers the flexibility to add or deprecate fields without impacting existing queries.

a6e478cdefb8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
a6e478cdefb8.sentence: - Reducing app bandwidth usage as we can query multiple resources in a single query.

69b9abce5f96.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
69b9abce5f96.sentence: - When we are working with a graph-like data model.

ef5f0a600e15.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/rest-api-vs-graphql.md
ef5f0a600e15.sentence: - Great for aggregating data from multiple sources and works well with rapidly evolving frontend requirements.

bfe6c48b947b.title: GraphQL
bfe6c48b947b.sentence: A GraphQL server can process a client query using data from separate sources and present the results in a unified graph.

d3ca1b7978f2.title: GraphQL
d3ca1b7978f2.sentence: The language is not tied to any specific database or storage engine.

3a007d366023.title: GraphQL
3a007d366023.section: Design > Comparison to other query languages
3a007d366023.sentence: GraphQL does not provide a full-fledged graph query language such as SPARQL, or even in dialects of SQL that support transitive closure.

1f999975b37f.title: GraphQL
1f999975b37f.section: Design > Comparison to other query languages
1f999975b37f.sentence: For example, a GraphQL interface that reports the parents of an individual cannot return, in a single query, the set of all their ancestors.

79a78ba218bf.title: Serialization
79a78ba218bf.sentence: In computing, serialization (or serialisation, also referred to as pickling in Python) is the process of translating a data structure or object state into a format that can be stored (e.g. files in secondary storage devices, data buffers in primary storage devices) or transmitted (e.g. data streams over computer networks) and reconstructed later (possibly in a different computer environment).

05d4b00782af.title: Serialization
05d4b00782af.sentence: When the resulting series of bits is reread according to the serialization format, it can be used to create a semantically identical clone of the original object.

3da9df5473d6.title: Serialization
3da9df5473d6.sentence: This process of serializing an object is also called marshalling in some situations.

381178f559f2.title: Serialization
381178f559f2.sentence: The opposite operation, extracting a data structure from a series of bytes, is deserialization (also called unserialization or unmarshalling).

0db7d238350c.title: Serialization
0db7d238350c.sentence: - storing data (in databases, on hard disk drives).

825864afe588.title: Serialization
825864afe588.sentence: - remote procedure calls, e.g., as in SOAP.

56715210b24b.title: Serialization
56715210b24b.sentence: - distributing objects, especially in component-based software engineering such as COM, CORBA, etc.

431aff1ed523.title: Serialization
431aff1ed523.sentence: For example, for maximal use of distribution, a computer running on a different hardware architecture should be able to reliably reconstruct a serialized data stream, regardless of endianness.

72231cdce01f.title: Serialization
72231cdce01f.sentence: This means that the simpler and faster procedure of directly copying the memory layout of the data structure cannot work reliably for all architectures.

c76bef7464f5.title: Serialization
c76bef7464f5.sentence: Serializing the data structure in an architecture-independent format means preventing the problems of byte ordering, memory layout, or simply different ways of representing data structures in different programming languages.

1b94043c6c74.title: Serialization
1b94043c6c74.sentence: Inherent to any serialization scheme is that, because the encoding of the data is by definition serial, extracting one part of the serialized data structure requires that the entire object be read from start to end, and reconstructed.

cf4aca72b242.title: Serialization
cf4aca72b242.sentence: In many applications, this linearity is an asset, because it enables simple, common I/O interfaces to be utilized to hold and pass on the state of an object.

20f0472a3f6b.title: Serialization
20f0472a3f6b.sentence: In applications where higher performance is an issue, it can make sense to expend more effort to deal with a more complex, non-linear storage organization.

ecf8dee18a87.title: Serialization
ecf8dee18a87.sentence: Serialization breaks the opacity of an abstract data type by potentially exposing private implementation details.

5d5bc8da9b11.title: Serialization
5d5bc8da9b11.sentence: Trivial implementations which serialize all data members may violate encapsulation.

cf652fb60dc1.title: Serialization
cf652fb60dc1.sentence: Yet, interoperability requires that applications be able to understand each other's serialization formats.

72d27d247bc5.title: Serialization
72d27d247bc5.sentence: Therefore, remote method call architectures such as CORBA define their serialization formats in detail.

a5dfa7c68802.title: Serialization
a5dfa7c68802.sentence: It is a cross-version customizable but unsafe (not secure against erroneous or malicious data) serialization format.

0bea9cf605b4.title: Serialization
0bea9cf605b4.sentence: The built-in unserialize() function is often dangerous when used on completely untrusted data.

30ec10503452.title: REST
30ec10503452.sentence: The REST architectural style defines six guiding constraints.

5b7109b1744b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
5b7109b1744b.sentence: In order for an API to be considered RESTful, it has to conform to these architectural constraints:

3e847d14bfbc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
3e847d14bfbc.sentence: - Uniform Interface: There should be a uniform way of interacting with a given server.

7e7c3248104a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
7e7c3248104a.sentence: - Client-Server: A client-server architecture managed through HTTP.

c77e8dfb849f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
c77e8dfb849f.sentence: - Stateless: No client context shall be stored on the server between requests.

8ba114ef21db.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
8ba114ef21db.sentence: - Cacheable: Every response should include whether the response is cacheable or not and for how much duration responses can be cached at the client-side.

411404963229.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
411404963229.sentence: - Layered system: An application architecture needs to be composed of multiple layers.

a7d4cd06ec12.title: REST
a7d4cd06ec12.sentence: - Code on demand (optional) – Servers are able to temporarily extend or customize the functionality of a client by transferring logic to the client that can be executed within a standard virtual machine

433668f64c53.title: REST
433668f64c53.sentence: - Client/Server – Clients are separated from servers by a well-defined interface

383324c2cd55.title: REST
383324c2cd55.sentence: - Stateless – A specific client does not consume server storage when the client is "at rest"

da2cbfdb104a.title: REST
da2cbfdb104a.sentence: - Cache – Responses indicate their own cacheability

fa4ebe206148.title: REST
fa4ebe206148.sentence: - Layered system – A client cannot ordinarily tell whether it is connected directly to the end server, or to an intermediary along the way

791d134f5abb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
791d134f5abb.sentence: - Code on demand: Return executable code to support a part of your application.

cf7ec2aeb92b.title: REST
cf7ec2aeb92b.sentence: When these constraints are applied to the system architecture, it gains desirable non-functional properties, such as performance, scalability, simplicity, modifiability, visibility, portability, and reliability.

143657279e75.title: REST
143657279e75.sentence: For example, Fielding identified the embedding of session information in URIs as a violation of the constraints of REST which can negatively affect shared caching and server scalability.

22e2f73b203b.title: REST
22e2f73b203b.sentence: HTTP cookies also violate REST constraints because they can become out of sync with the browser's application state, making them unreliable; they also contain opaque data that can be a concern for privacy and security.

52b4ee0db754.title: REST
52b4ee0db754.sentence: The uniform interface constraint is fundamental to the design of any RESTful system.

3b166d263209.title: REST
3b166d263209.sentence: It simplifies and decouples the architecture, which enables each part to evolve independently.

7b868243aac3.title: REST
7b868243aac3.sentence: - Resource identification in requests: Individual resources are identified in requests using URIs.

a741dce69d0a.title: REST
a741dce69d0a.sentence: The resources themselves are conceptually separate from the representations that are returned to the client.

f34dccf122ab.title: REST
f34dccf122ab.sentence: For example, the server could send data from its database as HTML, XML or as JSON—none of which are the server's internal representation.

2db82849a31f.title: REST
2db82849a31f.sentence: - Resource manipulation through representations: When a client holds a representation of a resource, including any metadata attached, it has enough information to modify or delete the resource's state.

96c5adbf9f8c.title: REST
96c5adbf9f8c.sentence: - Self-descriptive messages: Each message includes enough information to describe how to process the message.

1b90e03bae5f.title: REST
1b90e03bae5f.sentence: For example, which parser to invoke can be specified by a media type.

5f4c3e61169f.title: REST
5f4c3e61169f.sentence: - Hypermedia as the engine of application state (HATEOAS) – Having accessed an initial URI for the REST application—analogous to a human Web user accessing the home page of a website—a REST client should then be able to use server-provided links dynamically to discover all the available resources it needs.

155b3f148f04.title: REST
155b3f148f04.sentence: As access proceeds, the server responds with text that includes hyperlinks to other resources that are available at the time of the response.

1b41dccb1676.title: REST
1b41dccb1676.sentence: There is no need for the client to be hard-coded with information regarding the structure of the server.

9ca1a012bc37.title: REST
9ca1a012bc37.sentence: An important consequence is that the only identifier that needs to be known is the identifier of the first resource requested, and all other identifiers will be discovered.

ca59ac44cdee.title: REST
ca59ac44cdee.sentence: This means that those identifiers can change without the need to inform the client beforehand and that client and server must be inherently loosely coupled.

df53792fa4b8.title: HATEOAS
df53792fa4b8.sentence: Hypermedia as the engine of application state (HATEOAS) is a constraint of the REST software architectural style that distinguishes it from other network architectural styles.

0fdded3a7c2a.title: HATEOAS
0fdded3a7c2a.sentence: With HATEOAS, a client interacts with a network application whose application servers provide information dynamically through hypermedia.

28a103fa4137.title: HATEOAS
28a103fa4137.sentence: A REST client needs little to no prior knowledge about how to interact with an application or server beyond a generic understanding of hypermedia.

841f5b04a014.title: HATEOAS
841f5b04a014.sentence: By contrast, clients and servers in Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA) interact through a fixed interface shared through documentation or an interface description language (IDL).

c66473475364.title: HATEOAS
c66473475364.sentence: The HATEOAS constraint is an essential part of the "uniform interface" feature of REST, as defined in Roy Fielding's doctoral dissertation.

57b979301251.title: HATEOAS
57b979301251.sentence: The restrictions imposed by HATEOAS decouple client and server.

670c502de727.title: HATEOAS
670c502de727.sentence: This enables server functionality to evolve independently.

2f509d2d7536.title: HATEOAS
2f509d2d7536.sentence: A user-agent makes an HTTP request to a REST API through an entry point URL.

af93e518a83b.title: HATEOAS
af93e518a83b.sentence: All subsequent requests the user-agent may make are discovered inside the response to each request.

83ead8147829.title: HATEOAS
83ead8147829.sentence: The client transitions through application states by selecting from the links within a representation or by manipulating the representation in other ways afforded by its media type.

94ba3ffb257a.title: HATEOAS
94ba3ffb257a.sentence: In this way, RESTful interaction is driven by hypermedia, rather than out-of-band information.

5cce40a02b83.title: HATEOAS
5cce40a02b83.sentence: The response contains these possible follow-up links: POST a deposit, withdrawal, transfer, or close request (to close the account).

5e018512e3a8.title: HATEOAS
5e018512e3a8.sentence: Now only one link is available: to deposit more money (by POSTing to deposits).

604bb54d3808.title: HATEOAS
604bb54d3808.sentence: What actions are possible varies as the state of the resource varies.

cd5c643f2e7b.title: HATEOAS
cd5c643f2e7b.sentence: - HTML itself is hypermedia, with the <form>...</form> element in control of HTTP requests to links.

bb97da7f6dd4.title: HATEOAS
bb97da7f6dd4.sentence: - HAL, hypermedia built on top of JSON or XML.

5711a56dae6c.title: HATEOAS
5711a56dae6c.sentence: Defines links, but not actions (HTTP requests).

beab71d0c99e.title: HATEOAS
beab71d0c99e.sentence: - Siren, hypermedia built on top of JSON.

714d572b263e.title: HATEOAS
714d572b263e.sentence: - Collection+JSON, hypermedia built on top of JSON.

7e8ef17a6e57.title: HATEOAS
7e8ef17a6e57.sentence: The purpose of some of the strictness of this and other REST constraints, Fielding explains, is "software design on the scale of decades: every detail is intended to promote software longevity and independent evolution.

bf95521db96a.title: HATEOAS
bf95521db96a.sentence: Many of the constraints are directly opposed to short-term efficiency.

eec2c37a6c73.title: Serialization
eec2c37a6c73.sentence: Sun Microsystems published the External Data Representation (XDR) in 1987.

2fc5cf200dcf.title: Serialization
2fc5cf200dcf.sentence: In the late 1990s, a push to provide an alternative to the standard serialization protocols started: XML, an SGML subset, was used to produce a human-readable text-based encoding.

48ad79ce1d6e.title: Serialization
48ad79ce1d6e.sentence: JSON is a lightweight plain-text alternative to XML and is also commonly used for client-server communication in web applications.

be4c432fc3a1.title: Serialization
be4c432fc3a1.sentence: XDR is an open format, and standardized as STD 67 (RFC 4506) by IETF.

5a9956659fa9.title: Serialization
5a9956659fa9.sentence: Such an encoding can be useful for persistent objects that may be read and understood by humans or communicated to other systems regardless of programming language.

30859274cb6a.title: Serialization
30859274cb6a.sentence: It has the disadvantage of losing the more compact, byte-stream-based encoding, but by this point larger storage and transmission capacities made file size less of a concern than in the early days of computing.

baee843dac1b.title: Serialization
baee843dac1b.sentence: JSON is based on JavaScript syntax but is independent of JavaScript and supported in many other programming languages.

4f8c7f2628ef.title: Serialization
4f8c7f2628ef.sentence: JSON is standardized as STD 90 (RFC 8259), ECMA-404, and ISO/IEC 21778:2017.

b97abbb0a0ba.title: Serialization
b97abbb0a0ba.sentence: YAML is a strict superset of JSON and includes additional features such as a data type tags, support for cyclic data structures, indentation-sensitive syntax, and multiple forms of scalar data quoting.

4e69b0a206aa.title: Serialization
4e69b0a206aa.sentence: For large volume scientific datasets, such as satellite data and output of numerical climate, weather, or ocean models, specific binary serialization standards have been developed, e.g. HDF, netCDF and the older GRIB.

8a9f09a43659.title: Apache Avro
8a9f09a43659.sentence: For data blocks Avro specifies two serialization encodings: binary and JSON.

f8712210ddfb.title: Protocol Buffers
f8712210ddfb.sentence: Protocol Buffers (Protobuf) is a free and open-source cross-platform data format used to serialize structured data.

0b6d9056052d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
0b6d9056052d.sentence: Protocol buffers provide a language and platform-neutral extensible mechanism for serializing structured data in a forward and backward-compatible way.

2e877817f995.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
2e877817f995.sentence: It's like JSON, except it's smaller and faster, and it generates native language bindings.

d392f82e6c8a.title: Protocol Buffers
d392f82e6c8a.sentence: In particular, it was designed to be smaller and faster than XML.

faab9130d521.title: Protocol Buffers
faab9130d521.sentence: Data structure schemas (called messages) and services are described in a proto definition file (.proto) and compiled with protoc.

634adb39e88e.title: Protocol Buffers
634adb39e88e.sentence: This compilation generates code that can be invoked by a sender or recipient of these data structures.

5caf32e50ce3.title: Protocol Buffers
5caf32e50ce3.sentence: A schema for a particular use of protocol buffers associates data types with field names, using integers to identify each field.

28e13235351d.title: Protocol Buffers
28e13235351d.sentence: (The protocol buffer data contains only the numbers, not the field names, providing some bandwidth/storage savings compared with systems that include the field names in the data.)

4e9bcd5a9a9d.title: Protocol Buffers
4e9bcd5a9a9d.sentence: Canonically, messages are serialized into a binary wire format which is compact, forward- and backward-compatible, but not self-describing (that is, there is no way to tell the names, meaning, or full datatypes of fields without an external specification).

599a1f5f676a.title: Protocol Buffers
599a1f5f676a.sentence: The officially supported implementation includes an ASCII serialization format, but this format—though self-describing—loses the forward- and backward-compatibility behavior, and is thus not a good choice for applications other than human editing and debugging.

7ed23976b31c.title: GRPC
7ed23976b31c.sentence: Protocol buffers provide a serialization format and an interface definition language.

391216434d7d.title: GRPC
391216434d7d.sentence: gRPC uses Protocol Buffers to encode data.

a5ae8c189648.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
a5ae8c189648.sentence: Like many RPC systems, gRPC is based on the idea of defining a service and specifying the methods that can be called remotely with their parameters and return types. gRPC uses protocol buffers as the Interface Definition Language (IDL) for describing both the service interface and the structure of the payload messages.

16e95b3b317f.title: Protocol Buffers
16e95b3b317f.sentence: The format is best suited for small data chunks that don't exceed a few megabytes and can be loaded/sent into memory right away and therefore is not a streamable format.

c5a2be81151c.title: Protocol Buffers
c5a2be81151c.sentence: The library doesn't provide compression out of the box.

d3aa3603024d.title: Protocol Buffers
d3aa3603024d.sentence: The format also isn't well supported in non–object-oriented languages (e.g. Fortran).

fd8ab666b0ee.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
fd8ab666b0ee.sentence: gRPC is a modern open-source high-performance Remote Procedure Call (RPC) framework that can run in any environment.

f86fa3eccade.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
f86fa3eccade.sentence: It can efficiently connect services in and across data centers with pluggable support for load balancing, tracing, health checking, authentication and much more.

4380cc37a2b3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
4380cc37a2b3.sentence: - Steps 2 - 4: The order service (gRPC client) receives the REST call, transforms it, and makes an RPC call to the payment service. gPRC encodes the client stub into a binary format and sends it to the low-level transport layer.

9e9cb92e32ad.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
9e9cb92e32ad.sentence: - Step 5: gRPC sends the packets over the network via HTTP2.

5109a7811f5b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
5109a7811f5b.sentence: - Steps 6 - 8: The payment service (gRPC server) receives the packets from the network, decodes them, and invokes the server application.

f886ad0d075e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
f886ad0d075e.sentence: - Steps 9 - 11: The result is returned from the server application, and gets encoded and sent to the transport layer.

0b8ca20cd561.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
0b8ca20cd561.sentence: - Steps 12 - 14: The order service receives the packets, decodes them, and sends the result to the client application.

f8c55bf91815.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-grpc-work.md
f8c55bf91815.sentence: Because of binary encoding and network optimizations, gRPC is said to be 5X faster than JSON.

dc3238321ce4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
dc3238321ce4.sentence: - Relatively new compared to REST and GraphQL.

fd3273129a57.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
fd3273129a57.sentence: - Low latency and high throughput communication.

be4b2dc381ac.title: GRPC
be4b2dc381ac.sentence: gRPC uses HTTP/2 for transport, Protocol Buffers as the interface description language, and provides features such as authentication, bidirectional streaming and flow control, blocking or nonblocking bindings, and cancellation and timeouts.

c3a1950645ea.title: GRPC
c3a1950645ea.sentence: It generates cross-platform client and server bindings for many languages.

3da5be62aea6.title: GRPC
3da5be62aea6.sentence: gRPC's use of HTTP trailers makes it impossible to implement a gRPC client in a browser, instead requiring a proxy.

0df050926eba.title: SOAP
0df050926eba.sentence: SOAP (originally an acronym for Simple Object Access Protocol) is a messaging protocol specification for exchanging structured information in the implementation of web services in computer networks.

6b869dc4df06.title: SOAP
6b869dc4df06.sentence: It uses XML Information Set for its message format, and relies on application layer protocols, most often Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), although some legacy systems communicate over Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), for message negotiation and transmission.

0f7b3a4b4e65.title: SOAP
0f7b3a4b4e65.sentence: It is an XML-based protocol consisting of three parts:

0e36bef601b0.title: SOAP
0e36bef601b0.sentence: - an envelope, which defines the message structure and how to process it

778570ee706c.title: SOAP
778570ee706c.sentence: - a set of encoding rules for expressing instances of application-defined datatypes

22c8233d444b.title: SOAP
22c8233d444b.sentence: - a convention for representing procedure calls and responses

5ca0121b550c.title: SOAP
5ca0121b550c.sentence: A SOAP message is an ordinary XML document containing the following elements:

78238a512b69.title: SOAP
78238a512b69.sentence: Envelope | Identifies the XML document as a SOAP message. | Yes

8b70756203c9.title: SOAP
8b70756203c9.sentence: Body | Contains call and response information. | Yes

fcdb02a97aed.title: SOAP
fcdb02a97aed.sentence: Fault | Provides information about errors that occurred while processing the message. | No

cd55b8bed97d.title: SOAP
cd55b8bed97d.sentence: - extensibility (security and WS-Addressing are among the extensions under development)

9b97f7a87245.title: SOAP
9b97f7a87245.sentence: - neutrality (SOAP can operate over any protocol such as HTTP, SMTP, TCP, UDP)

1dcf9a25db1c.title: SOAP
1dcf9a25db1c.sentence: - independence (SOAP allows for any programming model)

30bde9e8dec8.title: SOAP
30bde9e8dec8.section: SOAP terminology > Message sender and receiver concepts
30bde9e8dec8.sentence: This is the node which originated the SOAP message to be transmitted.

10bd4b7fb555.title: SOAP
10bd4b7fb555.section: SOAP terminology > Message sender and receiver concepts
10bd4b7fb555.sentence: It processes the SOAP header blocks targeted at it and acts to forward a SOAP message towards an ultimate SOAP receiver.

36e281406bec.title: SOAP
36e281406bec.section: SOAP terminology > Message sender and receiver concepts
36e281406bec.sentence: The destination receiver of the SOAP message.

6c8f0c224bba.title: SOAP
6c8f0c224bba.section: SOAP terminology > Message sender and receiver concepts
6c8f0c224bba.sentence: The path consisting of all the nodes that the SOAP message traversed to reach the destination node.

4c3d2a877004.title: SOAP
4c3d2a877004.sentence: Both SMTP and HTTP are valid application layer protocols used as transport for SOAP, but HTTP has gained wider acceptance as it works well with today's internet infrastructure; specifically, HTTP works well with network firewalls.

6505b365b2c9.title: SOAP
6505b365b2c9.sentence: This is a major advantage over other distributed protocols like GIOP/IIOP or DCOM, which are normally filtered by firewalls.

f189f8117aeb.title: SOAP
f189f8117aeb.sentence: The somewhat lengthy syntax of XML can be both a benefit and a drawback.

0b2a8d7a85b0.title: SOAP
0b2a8d7a85b0.sentence: While it facilitates error detection and avoids interoperability problems such as byte-order (endianness), it can slow processing speed and can be cumbersome.

92e855b02557.title: SOAP
92e855b02557.sentence: In financial messaging SOAP was found to result in a 2–4 times larger message than previous protocols FIX (Financial Information Exchange) and CDR (Common Data Representation).

223a929cf5a4.title: SOAP
223a929cf5a4.sentence: - Being protocol-agnostic, SOAP is unable to take advantage of protocol-specific features and optimizations such as REST's Uniform Interface or caching – instead having to reimplement them (as with WS-Addressing).

c2b7cb0afb12.title: SOAP
c2b7cb0afb12.sentence: The verbosity of the protocol, low parsing speed of XML, and lack of a standardized interaction model led to the dominance of services using the HTTP protocol more directly.

2a2b3e25862f.title: API
2a2b3e25862f.sentence: API documentation describes what services an API offers and how to use those services, aiming to cover everything a client would need to know for practical purposes.

5e0da3763ec5.title: API
5e0da3763ec5.sentence: Documentation is crucial for the development and maintenance of applications using the API.

e41de3420c45.title: API
e41de3420c45.sentence: In the interest of clarity, API documentation may include a description of classes and methods in the API as well as typical usage scenarios, code snippets, design rationales, performance discussions, and contracts, but implementation details of the API services themselves are usually omitted.

16ea3e4fc0c9.title: API
16ea3e4fc0c9.sentence: Restrictions and limitations on how the API can be used are also covered by the documentation.

aee02101f862.title: API
aee02101f862.sentence: For instance, documentation for an API function could note that its parameters cannot be null, that the function itself is not thread safe.

7a5f3671b9a3.title: API
7a5f3671b9a3.sentence: Because API documentation tends to be comprehensive, it is a challenge for writers to keep the documentation updated and for users to read it carefully, potentially yielding bugs.

c1d62fbae1e2.title: API
c1d62fbae1e2.sentence: The main policies for releasing an API are:

f8ca43ff3675.title: API
f8ca43ff3675.sentence: - Private: The API is for internal company use only.

f694a605aca9.title: API
f694a605aca9.sentence: - Partner: Only specific business partners can use the API.

675a682fad35.title: API
675a682fad35.sentence: - Public: The API is available for use by the public.

aa75d96cde73.title: API
aa75d96cde73.sentence: This allows the companies to exercise quality control by curating which apps have access to the API, and provides them with an additional revenue stream.

5673be3e2400.title: API
5673be3e2400.sentence: Not all public APIs are generally accessible by everybody.

012a8981e334.title: API
012a8981e334.sentence: Access to such APIs is granted either by "API tokens", or customer status validations.

8f7f4497862d.title: API
8f7f4497862d.sentence: When used in the context of web development, an API is typically defined as a set of specifications, such as Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) request messages, along with a definition of the structure of response messages, usually in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) or JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) format.

bc634a1617a7.title: API
bc634a1617a7.sentence: The term API is often used to refer to web APIs, which allow communication between computers that are joined by the internet.

0ddac6daeae7.title: API
0ddac6daeae7.sentence: While "web API" historically has been virtually synonymous with web service, the recent trend (so-called Web 2.0) has been moving away from Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) based web services and service-oriented architecture (SOA) towards more direct representational state transfer (REST) style web resources and resource-oriented architecture (ROA).

b8472e87b2fd.title: API
b8472e87b2fd.sentence: An example might be a shipping company API that can be added to an eCommerce-focused website to facilitate ordering shipping services and automatically include current shipping rates, without the site developer having to enter the shipper's rate table into a web database.

5a45f1d982f6.title: API
5a45f1d982f6.sentence: An important factor when an API becomes public is its "interface stability".

f837a6c95a8f.title: API
f837a6c95a8f.sentence: Changes to the API—for example adding new parameters to a function call—could break compatibility with the clients that depend on that API.

fbf03e67dc2a.title: API
fbf03e67dc2a.sentence: When parts of a publicly presented API are subject to change and thus not stable, such parts of a particular API should be documented explicitly as "unstable".

e97db7c7fde9.title: API
e97db7c7fde9.sentence: A public API can sometimes declare parts of itself as deprecated or rescinded.

1f297643d0bb.title: API
1f297643d0bb.sentence: This usually means that part of the API should be considered a candidate for being removed, or modified in a backward incompatible way.

295d9f2c8817.title: API
295d9f2c8817.sentence: Therefore, these changes allow developers to transition away from parts of the API that will be removed or not supported in the future.

47efe7c8aa43.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
47efe7c8aa43.sentence: - Versioning Designing the version number for the API in advance can simplify upgrade work.

939772769234.title: GraphQL
939772769234.sentence: While there's nothing that prevents a GraphQL service from being versioned just like any other API, GraphQL takes a strong opinion on avoiding versioning by providing the tools for the continuous evolution of a GraphQL schema.

4f574d3ad0a6.title: GraphQL
4f574d3ad0a6.sentence: GraphQL only returns the data that's explicitly requested, so new capabilities can be added via new types or new fields on existing types without creating a breaking change.

10821a0d807d.title: GraphQL
10821a0d807d.sentence: The @deprecated built-in directive is used within the type system definition language to indicate deprecated portions of a GraphQL service's schema, such as deprecated fields on a type or deprecated enum values.

883b956bbbb2.title: GraphQL
883b956bbbb2.sentence: This has led to a common practice of always avoiding breaking changes and serving a versionless API.

ba18e12eae55.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
ba18e12eae55.sentence: Pagination is crucial in API design to handle large datasets efficiently and improve performance.

9c29dcb1aac1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
9c29dcb1aac1.sentence: - Offset-based Pagination: This technique uses an offset and a limit parameter to define the starting point and the number of records to return.

a44bc18fe454.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
a44bc18fe454.sentence: - Pros: Simple to implement and understand.

b0b41daeeb7f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
b0b41daeeb7f.sentence: - Cons: Can become inefficient for large offsets, as it requires scanning and skipping rows.

d508ce5accdb.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
d508ce5accdb.sentence: - Cursor-based Pagination: This technique uses a cursor (a unique identifier) to mark the position in the dataset.

87c757e8e13a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
87c757e8e13a.sentence: Typically, the cursor is an encoded string that points to a specific record.

c04cd15385f5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
c04cd15385f5.sentence: - Pros: More efficient for large datasets, as it doesn't require scanning skipped records.

db64b58b6108.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
db64b58b6108.sentence: - Cons: Slightly more complex to implement and understand.

bf5591ec7971.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
bf5591ec7971.sentence: - Page-based Pagination: This technique specifies the page number and the size of each page.

228bb4a7fd8a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
228bb4a7fd8a.sentence: - Pros: Easy to implement and use.

afc871513ece.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
afc871513ece.sentence: - Cons: Similar performance issues as offset-based pagination for large page numbers.

2b196c7d1456.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
2b196c7d1456.sentence: - Keyset-based Pagination: This technique uses a key to filter the dataset, often the primary key or another indexed column.

ea104d0c4b0b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
ea104d0c4b0b.sentence: - Pros: Efficient for large datasets and avoids performance issues with large offsets.

a118f8340e11.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
a118f8340e11.sentence: - Cons: Requires a unique and indexed key, and can be complex to implement.

5a9c33bfaaf7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
5a9c33bfaaf7.sentence: - Time-based Pagination: This technique uses a timestamp or date to paginate through records.

ff831f4a25fa.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
ff831f4a25fa.sentence: - Pros: Useful for datasets ordered by time, ensures no records are missed if new ones are added.

a35b1d422fc1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
a35b1d422fc1.sentence: - Cons: Requires a reliable and consistent timestamp.

6674c3061335.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
6674c3061335.sentence: - Hybrid Pagination: This technique combines multiple pagination techniques to leverage their strengths.

cf9b051ecc58.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
cf9b051ecc58.sentence: - Example: Combining cursor and time-based pagination for efficient scrolling through time-ordered records.

cfeaa088f12a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
cfeaa088f12a.sentence: - Pros: Can offer the best performance and flexibility for complex datasets.

c5ae650c5671.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-perform-pagination-in-api-design.md
c5ae650c5671.sentence: - Cons: More complex to implement and requires careful design.

fb6258b9a8f1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-effective-and-safe-apis.md
fb6258b9a8f1.sentence: Note that API design is not just URL path design.

dfac9e5b9433.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-effective-and-safe-apis.md
dfac9e5b9433.sentence: Most of the time, we need to choose the proper resource names, identifiers, and path patterns.

4b6c2190be85.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-effective-and-safe-apis.md
4b6c2190be85.sentence: It is equally important to design proper HTTP header fields or to design effective rate-limiting rules within the API gateway.

e80f80e49467.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
e80f80e49467.sentence: - Domain Model Driven When designing the path structure of a RESTful API, we can refer to the domain model.

6d6595fa4eb5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
6d6595fa4eb5.sentence: - Semantic Paths Using semantic paths makes APIs easier to understand, so that users can find the correct APIs in the documentation.

598b2990f94d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
598b2990f94d.sentence: - Choose Proper HTTP Methods Defining a few basic HTTP Methods can simplify the API design.

cf3e2a5cc2c5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
cf3e2a5cc2c5.sentence: For example, PATCH can often be a problem for teams.

713fd4a81efc.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
713fd4a81efc.sentence: - Implement Idempotence Properly Designing for idempotence in advance can improve the robustness of an API.

b279be0ab665.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
b279be0ab665.sentence: GET method is idempotent, but POST needs to be designed properly to be idempotent.

8c1054c89f63.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
8c1054c89f63.sentence: - Choose Proper HTTP Status Codes Define a limited number of HTTP status codes to use to simplify application development.

8b63856fd249.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
8b63856fd249.sentence: - Batch Processing Use batch/bulk as a keyword and place it at the end of the path.

035b76c2e422.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
035b76c2e422.sentence: - Query Language Designing a set of query rules makes the API more flexible.

53895dda3058.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/8-tips-for-efficient-api-design.md
53895dda3058.sentence: For example, pagination, sorting, filtering etc.

3ea3d841d64d.title: Remote procedure call
3ea3d841d64d.sentence: The call is a local procedure call, with parameters pushed on to the stack in the normal way.

336b66533fca.title: Remote procedure call
336b66533fca.sentence: The reply traces the same steps in the reverse direction.

a0f92ef3cc9e.title: Remote procedure call
a0f92ef3cc9e.sentence: - The client stub packs the parameters into a message and makes a system call to send the message.

e0bbb93d7f61.title: Remote procedure call
e0bbb93d7f61.sentence: Packing the parameters is called marshalling.

3874df217e76.title: Remote procedure call
3874df217e76.sentence: - The client's local operating system sends the message from the client machine to the server machine.

1de317c521fb.title: Remote procedure call
1de317c521fb.sentence: - The local operating system on the server machine passes the incoming packets to the server stub.

1fb0fae54d93.title: Remote procedure call
1fb0fae54d93.sentence: - The server stub unpacks the parameters from the message.

a6bf714d2c4e.title: Remote procedure call
a6bf714d2c4e.sentence: Unpacking the parameters is called unmarshalling.

d440645ff8ac.title: Remote procedure call
d440645ff8ac.sentence: - Finally, the server stub calls the server procedure.

d2000e1e574e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
d2000e1e574e.sentence: Now that we know how these API designing techniques work, let's compare them based on the following parameters:

cddeded57bdf.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
cddeded57bdf.section: REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC > Which API technology is better?
cddeded57bdf.sentence: Well, the answer is none of them.

6e83aee8224e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
6e83aee8224e.sentence: - How chatty (distinct API calls to get needed information) are the APIs?

889f8aea9d50.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
889f8aea9d50.sentence: - How complex is it to integrate?

3b94492e2552.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rest-graphql-grpc
3b94492e2552.sentence: - How well does the caching work?

94e71be348a0.title: GraphQL
94e71be348a0.sentence: The GraphQL type system describes what data can be queried from the API.

9c3a312aacae.title: GraphQL
9c3a312aacae.sentence: The types and fields make up what is known as the schema definition.

0d40ce4cb49e.title: GraphQL
0d40ce4cb49e.sentence: A GraphQL service is created by defining types with fields, then providing functions to resolve the data for each field.

4da1b46a03bc.title: GraphQL
4da1b46a03bc.sentence: The functions that retrieve and map the data are called resolvers.

0343a5d76e27.title: GraphQL
0343a5d76e27.sentence: The collection of those capabilities is referred to as the service's schema and clients can use that schema to send queries to the API that return predictable results.

4f3e19a158f6.title: GraphQL
4f3e19a158f6.sentence: The root type of a GraphQL schema, Query by default, contains all of the fields that can be queried.

eae497390427.title: GraphQL
eae497390427.sentence: There are several base types, called scalars, to represent things like strings, numbers, and IDs.

00f27819862e.title: GraphQL
00f27819862e.sentence: Fields are defined as nullable by default, and a trailing exclamation mark can be used to make a field non-nullable (required).

73b87e614a9e.title: GraphQL
73b87e614a9e.sentence: A field can be defined as a list by wrapping the field's type in square brackets (for example, authors: [String]).

007563be3bfd.title: GraphQL
007563be3bfd.sentence: After being validated against the schema, a GraphQL query is executed by the server.

76b7cf2df63a.title: GraphQL
76b7cf2df63a.sentence: The server returns a result that mirrors the shape of the original query, typically as JSON.

d25c81ed0df7.title: GraphQL
d25c81ed0df7.sentence: GraphQL supports reading, writing (mutating), and subscribing to changes to data (realtime updates – commonly implemented using WebSockets).

cc08e696ede3.title: GraphQL
cc08e696ede3.sentence: A GraphQL query defines the exact shape of the data needed by the client.

30e95d8fd31d.title: GraphQL
30e95d8fd31d.sentence: Once validated and executed by the GraphQL server, the data is returned in the same shape.

f5cb34613e08.title: GraphQL
f5cb34613e08.sentence: A GraphQL mutation allows for data to be created, updated, or deleted.

c36e4ae19f51.title: GraphQL
c36e4ae19f51.sentence: Mutations generally contain variables, which allow data to be passed into the server from the client.

097383d08443.title: GraphQL
097383d08443.sentence: The mutation also defines the shape of the data that will be returned to the client after the operation is complete.

8d847fc19bf8.title: GraphQL
8d847fc19bf8.sentence: GraphQL also supports live updates sent from the server to client in an operation called a subscription.

bdae75ef8c8c.title: GraphQL
bdae75ef8c8c.sentence: Again, the client defines the shape of the data that it needs whenever an update is made.

5c8184e157ec.title: GraphQL
5c8184e157ec.sentence: When a mutation is made through the GraphQL server that updates the associated field, data is sent to all subscribed clients in the format setup through the subscription.

bd3edc043f0d.title: OpenAPI Specification
bd3edc043f0d.sentence: The OpenAPI Specification (OAS), previously known as the Swagger Specification, is a specification for a machine-readable interface definition language for describing, producing, consuming and visualizing web services.

5868e1c40cc5.title: OpenAPI Specification
5868e1c40cc5.sentence: An OpenAPI Description (OAD) represents a formal description of an API that tools can use to generate code, documentation, test cases, and more.

1f76c7d7df2a.title: OpenAPI Specification
1f76c7d7df2a.sentence: Applications can use OADs to automatically generate documentation of methods, parameters and data models.

4e8f00b5b0fd.title: OpenAPI Specification
4e8f00b5b0fd.sentence: This helps keep the documentation, client libraries and source code in sync.

7c48302029a5.title: OpenAPI Specification
7c48302029a5.sentence: When an OAD is used to generate source code stubs for servers, the process is called scaffolding.

001482f76c9b.title: OpenAPI Specification
001482f76c9b.section: Usage > Relationships to software engineering practices
001482f76c9b.sentence: The paradigm of agreeing on an API contract first and then programming business logic afterwards, in contrast to coding the program first and then writing a retrospective description of its behavior as the contract, is called contract-first development.

c4df41183178.title: OpenAPI Specification
c4df41183178.section: Usage > Relationships to software engineering practices
c4df41183178.sentence: Since the interface is determined before any code is written, downstream developers can mock the server behavior and start testing right away.

6e6582d5ce10.title: OpenAPI Specification
6e6582d5ce10.section: Usage > Relationships to software engineering practices
6e6582d5ce10.sentence: In this sense, contract-first development is also a practice of shift-left testing.

42ebbc935a41.title: OpenAPI Specification
42ebbc935a41.sentence: With OpenAPI's declarative resource specification, clients can understand and consume services without knowledge of server implementation or access to the server code.

bee51d4ba50e.sentence: To reduce data transmission time, requests and responses can be compressed (e.g., using gzip), making the upload and download processes quicker.

2b3d2517c934.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
2b3d2517c934.sentence: Polling involves repeatedly checking the external service or endpoint at fixed intervals to retrieve updated information.

a7bec21da82b.title: Polling (computer science)
a7bec21da82b.sentence: Polling, or interrogation, refers to actively sampling the status of an external device by a client program as a synchronous activity.

358b7b5ac662.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
358b7b5ac662.sentence: It’s like constantly asking, “Do you have something new for me?” even where there might not be any update.

a0001bf08ac6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
a0001bf08ac6.sentence: This approach is resource-intensive and inefficient.

e0841386124f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
e0841386124f.sentence: Also, you get updates only when you ask for it, thereby missing any real-time information.

6907bea3dfe5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
6907bea3dfe5.sentence: However, developers have more control over when and how the data is fetched.

0db78e034aa1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
0db78e034aa1.sentence: With short polling, the browser will retry until it gets the latest data.

4ea0671e4fff.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
4ea0671e4fff.sentence: Polling is a solid option when there is some infrastructural limitation that prevents the use of webhooks.

ace92991cdf8.title: Polling (computer science)
ace92991cdf8.sentence: In this situation, when an I/O operation is required, the computer does nothing other than check the status of the I/O device until it is ready, at which point the device is accessed.

ed48bfa63c7d.title: Polling (computer science)
ed48bfa63c7d.sentence: Polling also refers to the situation where a device is repeatedly checked for readiness, and if it is not, the computer returns to a different task.

f1c5e999ee3e.title: Polling (computer science)
f1c5e999ee3e.sentence: Although not as wasteful of CPU cycles as busy waiting, this is generally not as efficient as the alternative to polling, interrupt-driven I/O.

bab0e0bbf7e5.title: Polling (computer science)
bab0e0bbf7e5.sentence: A polling cycle is the time in which each element is monitored once.

5dfa5d4d4c30.title: Polling (computer science)
5dfa5d4d4c30.sentence: The optimal polling cycle will vary according to several factors, including the desired speed of response and the overhead (e.g., processor time and bandwidth) of the polling.

c336319bbfbd.title: Polling (computer science)
c336319bbfbd.sentence: Polling has the disadvantage that if there are too many devices to check, the time required to poll them can exceed the time available to service the I/O device.

31db04be7101.title: Polling (computer science)
31db04be7101.sentence: In roll call polling, the polling device or process queries each element on a list in a fixed sequence.

f5598bb6b032.title: Polling (computer science)
f5598bb6b032.sentence: Because it waits for a response from each element, a timing mechanism is necessary to prevent lock-ups caused by non-responding elements.

3b2d4cad546e.title: Polling (computer science)
3b2d4cad546e.sentence: Roll call polling can be inefficient if the overhead for the polling messages is high, there are numerous elements to be polled in each polling cycle and only a few elements are active.

32e417af4b94.title: Polling (computer science)
32e417af4b94.sentence: An alternative to polling is the use of interrupts, which are signals generated by devices or processes to indicate that they need attention, want to communicate, etc. Although polling can be very simple, in many situations (e.g., multitasking operating systems) it is more efficient to use interrupts because it can reduce processor spinnning and/or bandwidth consumption.

7c9e556e04dc.title: Push technology
7c9e556e04dc.sentence: Push technology, also known as server push, is a communication method where the communication is initiated by a server rather than a client.

142b71a3d4f9.title: Push technology
142b71a3d4f9.sentence: This approach is different from the "pull" method where the communication is initiated by a client.

9949af8a542b.title: Push technology
9949af8a542b.sentence: In push technology, clients can express their preferences for certain types of information or data, typically through a process known as the publish–subscribe model.

8d2d4f507261.title: Push technology
8d2d4f507261.sentence: In this model, a client "subscribes" to specific information channels hosted by a server.

90f45515d27e.title: Push technology
90f45515d27e.sentence: When new content becomes available on these channels, the server automatically sends, or "pushes," this information to the subscribed client.

ce069f528d65.title: Push technology
ce069f528d65.sentence: Under certain conditions, such as restrictive security policies that block incoming HTTP requests, push technology is sometimes simulated using a technique called polling.

fe3952d77a56.title: Push technology
fe3952d77a56.sentence: In these cases, the client periodically checks with the server to see if new information is available, rather than receiving automatic updates.

5a8060de7921.title: Push technology
5a8060de7921.sentence: Synchronous conferencing and instant messaging are examples of push services.

2c3b169aaba6.title: Push technology
2c3b169aaba6.sentence: Chat messages and sometimes files are pushed to the user as soon as they are received by the messaging service.

eadaea46a3f8.title: Push technology
eadaea46a3f8.sentence: Email may also be a push system: SMTP is a push protocol (see Push e-mail).

0ffd3bf82cad.title: Push technology
0ffd3bf82cad.sentence: However, the last step—from mail server to desktop computer—typically uses a pull protocol like POP3 or IMAP.

4386f40cd90f.title: Push technology
4386f40cd90f.sentence: Modern e-mail clients make this step seem instantaneous by repeatedly polling the mail server, frequently checking it for new mail.

da0d4f1f806e.title: Push technology
da0d4f1f806e.sentence: The IMAP protocol includes the IDLE command, which allows the server to tell the client when new messages arrive.

81439c676363.title: Push technology
81439c676363.sentence: Other uses of push-enabled web applications include software updates distribution ("push updates"), market data distribution (stock tickers), online chat/messaging systems (webchat), auctions, online betting and gaming, sport results, monitoring consoles, and sensor network monitoring.

ec5bfa81aadd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
ec5bfa81aadd.sentence: HTTP Long polling is a technique used to push information to a client as soon as possible from the server.

18a18d4cb058.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
18a18d4cb058.sentence: Instead, the server responds only if any new message is available or a timeout threshold is reached.

dc43c8605c25.sentence: If the server has no new information for the client when the poll is received, then instead of sending an empty response, the server holds the request open and waits for response information to become available.

a2921102ed74.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
a2921102ed74.sentence: In Long polling, the server does not close the connection once it receives a request from the client.

c5b25333aa1d.title: Push technology
c5b25333aa1d.sentence: Once it does have new information, the server immediately sends an HTTP response to the client, completing the open HTTP request.

253e232732c7.title: Push technology
253e232732c7.sentence: Upon receipt of the server response, the client often immediately issues another server request.

5e75411446e3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
5e75411446e3.sentence: Once the client receives a response, it immediately sends a new request to the server to have a new pending connection to send data to the client, and the operation is repeated.

a1e58fb1b8c6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
a1e58fb1b8c6.sentence: - The client receives the response and makes a new request immediately or after some defined interval to establish a connection again.

973a20ae8e01.title: Push technology
973a20ae8e01.sentence: Long polling is itself not a true push; long polling is a variation of the traditional polling technique, but it allows emulating a push mechanism under circumstances where a real push is not possible, such as sites with security policies that require rejection of incoming HTTP requests.

2f8a970b6736.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
2f8a970b6736.sentence: With this approach, the server emulates a real-time server push feature.

ff1b2d20aa72.title: Push technology
ff1b2d20aa72.sentence: In this way the usual response latency (the time between when the information first becomes available and the next client request) otherwise associated with polling clients is eliminated.

4e8c98c6bc0d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
4e8c98c6bc0d.sentence: - Easy to implement, good for small-scale projects.

65b0772ac99f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
65b0772ac99f.sentence: A major downside of long polling is that it is usually not scalable.

2d043f38d3f7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
2d043f38d3f7.sentence: - Creates a new connection each time, which can be intensive on the server.

6f5d85fcbec2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
6f5d85fcbec2.sentence: - Reliable message ordering can be an issue for multiple requests.

9d250f70d80a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
9d250f70d80a.sentence: - Increased latency as the server needs to wait for a new request.

fcce1e1fcf13.title: Push technology
fcce1e1fcf13.sentence: A push notification is a message that is "pushed" from a back-end server or application to a user interface, e.g. mobile applications or desktop applications.

b6f4a2cefb67.title: Push technology
b6f4a2cefb67.sentence: Push notifications are mainly divided into two approaches, local notifications and remote notifications.

eb1e8cb3f365.title: Push technology
eb1e8cb3f365.sentence: For local notifications, the application schedules the notification with the local device's OS.

51f3b0bdf84d.title: Push technology
51f3b0bdf84d.sentence: Remote notifications are handled by a remote server.

94ca55a11575.title: Push technology
94ca55a11575.sentence: Under this scenario, the client application needs to be registered on the server with a unique key (e.g., a UUID or Apple Device Token).

9bc470a07bab.title: Push technology
9bc470a07bab.sentence: The server then transmits the message against the unique key to deliver it to the client via an agreed client/server protocol such as HTTP or XMPP.

0c2e9a4b727d.title: Push technology
0c2e9a4b727d.sentence: When the push notification arrives at the client, it can cause the display of short notifications or messages, set badges on application icons, blink or continuously light up the notification LED, or play alert sounds to attract user's attention.

e293ca14fd38.title: Push technology
e293ca14fd38.sentence: - Chat messages from a messaging application such as Facebook Messenger sent by other users.

5a755455fa67.title: Push technology
5a755455fa67.sentence: - Vendor special offers: A vendor may want to advertise their offers to customers.

c5833fb5246c.title: Push technology
c5833fb5246c.sentence: - Event reminders: Some applications may allow the customer to create a reminder or alert for a specific time.

4fe4f65a88b0.title: Push technology
4fe4f65a88b0.sentence: - Subscribed topic changes: Users may want to get updates regarding the weather in their location, or monitor a web page to track changes, for instance.

7c0d9091631e.title: Push technology
7c0d9091631e.sentence: Real-time push notifications may raise privacy issues since they can be used to bind virtual identities of social network pseudonyms to the real identities of the smartphone owners.

387f3e8e9a5b.sentence: This document describes a simple protocol for the delivery of real-time events to user agents.

8c02e07f75dd.title: rfc>8030
8c02e07f75dd.sentence: Radio communications consume a significant portion of the energy budget on a wireless device.

7064ca66e36d.title: rfc>8030
7064ca66e36d.sentence: Uncoordinated use of persistent connections or sessions from multiple applications can contribute to unnecessary use of the device radio, since each independent session can incur its own overhead.

637811b93640.title: rfc>8030
637811b93640.sentence: In particular, keep-alive traffic used to ensure that middleboxes do not prematurely time out sessions can result in significant waste.

190493024f9c.title: rfc>8030
190493024f9c.sentence: Consolidating all real-time events into a single session ensures more efficient use of network and radio resources.

dec288e2a6e1.title: rfc>8030
dec288e2a6e1.sentence: A single service consolidates all events, distributing those events to applications as they arrive.

d737c400d7ab.title: rfc>8030
d737c400d7ab.sentence: This requires just one session, avoiding duplicated overhead costs.

9c1bf04da726.sentence: The protocol consolidates all real-time events into a single session which ensures more efficient use of network and radio resources.
