844cb5fb1550.title: rfc>8030
844cb5fb1550.sentence: A general model for push services includes three basic actors: a user agent, a push service, and an application (server).

c8178fd933d3.title: rfc>8030
c8178fd933d3.sentence: At the very beginning of the process, a new message subscription is created by the user agent and then distributed to its application server.

e8f68d49156c.title: rfc>8030
e8f68d49156c.sentence: This subscription is the basis of all future interactions between the actors.

30e32959a5f6.title: rfc>8030
30e32959a5f6.sentence: A subscription is used by the application server to send messages to the push service for delivery to the user agent.

0f19cf7b1075.title: rfc>8030
0f19cf7b1075.sentence: The user agent uses the subscription to monitor the push service for any incoming message.

637b88168562.title: rfc>8030
637b88168562.sentence: To offer more control for authorization, a message subscription is modeled as two resources with different capabilities:

b5204cc57841.title: rfc>8030
b5204cc57841.sentence: - A subscription resource is used to receive messages from a subscription and to delete a subscription.

be4f25ca5e45.title: rfc>8030
be4f25ca5e45.sentence: It is private to the user agent.

a47aa0d74f01.title: rfc>8030
a47aa0d74f01.sentence: - A push resource is used to send messages to a subscription.

1a0dd864e148.title: rfc>8030
1a0dd864e148.sentence: It is public and shared by the user agent with its application server.

09916d76f4c8.title: rfc>8030
09916d76f4c8.sentence: A user agent sends a POST request to its configured push service resource to create a new subscription.

3a4b564587f0.title: rfc>8030
3a4b564587f0.sentence: A 201 (Created) response indicates that the push subscription was created.

0a5fda568daf.title: rfc>8030
0a5fda568daf.sentence: An application server requests the delivery of a push message by sending an HTTP POST request to a push resource distributed to the application server by a user agent.

16b7dd8b1ec1.title: rfc>8030
16b7dd8b1ec1.sentence: The content of the push message is included in the body of the request.

67bdc9c501ef.title: rfc>8030
67bdc9c501ef.section: 6. Receiving Push Messages for a Subscription
67bdc9c501ef.sentence: A user agent requests the delivery of new push messages by making a GET request to a push message subscription resource.

275b0427547c.title: rfc>8030
275b0427547c.section: 6. Receiving Push Messages for a Subscription
275b0427547c.sentence: The push service does not respond to this request; instead, it uses HTTP/2 server push to send the contents of push messages as they are sent by application servers.

3c82ca7cba3c.title: rfc>8030
3c82ca7cba3c.section: 6. Receiving Push Messages for a Subscription > 6.2. Acknowledging Push Messages
3c82ca7cba3c.sentence: To ensure that a push message is properly delivered to the user agent at least once, the user agent MUST acknowledge receipt of the message by performing an HTTP DELETE on the push message resource.

853b90e888f1.title: rfc>8030
853b90e888f1.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.1. Requesting Push Message Receipts
853b90e888f1.sentence: An application server can include the Prefer header field with the "respond-async" preference to request confirmation from the push service when a push message is delivered and then acknowledged by the user agent.

9f3950d9b2a2.title: rfc>8030
9f3950d9b2a2.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.1. Requesting Push Message Receipts
9f3950d9b2a2.sentence: The push service MUST support delivery confirmations.

582c86b8d7de.title: Push technology
582c86b8d7de.sentence: Web Notifications are part of the W3C standard and define an API for end-user notifications.

fbac5d1890c0.title: Push technology
fbac5d1890c0.sentence: A notification allows alerting the user of an event, such as the delivery of an email, outside the context of a web page.

661a562135ae.title: rfc>8030
661a562135ae.sentence: The W3C Push API describes an API that enables the use of a consolidated push service from web applications.

35ddfd9e959b.title: Push technology
35ddfd9e959b.sentence: As part of this standard, Push API is fully implemented in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, and partially implemented in Safari as of February 2023.

872aa8411987.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
872aa8411987.sentence: An HTTP server cannot automatically initiate a connection to a browser.

0a0ad1d8491a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
0a0ad1d8491a.sentence: - Web browsers do the heavy lifting: short polling or long polling.

c71cba374187.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
c71cba374187.sentence: - HTTP server and web browser cooperate: WebSocket or SSE (server-sent event).

98f6ff10623f.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
98f6ff10623f.sentence: As a result, the web browser is the initiator.

8e00c3eb73c6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
8e00c3eb73c6.sentence: Web applications were initially developed around a client-server model, where the web client is always the initiator of transactions like requesting data from the server.

c12ea1073386.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
c12ea1073386.sentence: Thus, there was no mechanism for the server to independently send, or push, data to the client without the client first making a request.

7c4d4f68b5f8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
7c4d4f68b5f8.sentence: With long polling, the HTTP server doesn’t return results until new data has arrived.

90768b1970f0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
90768b1970f0.sentence: In both cases, the HTTP server could directly send the latest data to the browser after the connection is established.

d2c6e0cb29b2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/shortlong-polling-sse-websocket.md
d2c6e0cb29b2.sentence: The difference is that SSE is uni-directional, so the browser cannot send a new request to the server, while WebSocket is fully-duplex, so the browser can keep sending new requests.

39060fe844f4.title: WebSocket
39060fe844f4.sentence: WebSocket is a computer communications protocol, providing a bidirectional communication channel over a single Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connection.

7e53a82f7026.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
7e53a82f7026.sentence: It is a persistent connection between a client and a server that both parties can use to start sending data at any time.

a7352493fc11.title: rfc>6455
a7352493fc11.sentence: This is a two-way communication channel where each side can, independently from the other, send data at will.

9f6a0c2fc9cf.title: WebSocket
9f6a0c2fc9cf.sentence: The WebSocket protocol enables full-duplex interaction between a web browser (or other client application) and a web server with lower overhead than half-duplex alternatives such as HTTP polling, facilitating real-time data transfer from and to the server.

f808fef044ba.title: WebSocket
f808fef044ba.sentence: This is achieved by providing a standardized way for the server to send content to the client without being first requested by the client, and allowing messages to be exchanged while keeping the connection open.

df1d6f2b07e8.title: rfc>6455
df1d6f2b07e8.sentence: The goal of this technology is to provide a mechanism for browser-based applications that need two-way communication with servers that does not rely on opening multiple HTTP connections (e.g., using XMLHttpRequest or <iframe>s and long polling).

4564ed6e5a48.title: rfc>6455
4564ed6e5a48.sentence: Historically, creating web applications that need bidirectional communication between a client and a server (e.g., instant messaging and gaming applications) has required an abuse of HTTP to poll the server for updates while sending upstream notifications as distinct HTTP calls.

3d402585f6fd.title: rfc>6455
3d402585f6fd.sentence: - The server is forced to use a number of different underlying TCP connections for each client: one for sending information to the client and a new one for each incoming message.

e17e658dba87.title: rfc>6455
e17e658dba87.sentence: - The wire protocol has a high overhead, with each client-to-server message having an HTTP header.

f16767281fab.title: rfc>6455
f16767281fab.sentence: - The client-side script is forced to maintain a mapping from the outgoing connections to the incoming connection to track replies.

8058e7e31939.title: rfc>6455
8058e7e31939.section: 1. Introduction > 1.7. Relationship to TCP and HTTP
8058e7e31939.sentence: The WebSocket Protocol is an independent TCP-based protocol.

64e0228203e1.title: rfc>6455
64e0228203e1.section: 1. Introduction > 1.7. Relationship to TCP and HTTP
64e0228203e1.sentence: Its only relationship to HTTP is that its handshake is interpreted by HTTP servers as an Upgrade request.

d9017f549cf2.title: rfc>6455
d9017f549cf2.sentence: Conceptually, WebSocket is really just a layer on top of TCP that does the following:

758c53af5501.title: rfc>6455
758c53af5501.sentence: - adds a web origin-based security model for browsers

a7e679a45735.title: rfc>6455
a7e679a45735.sentence: - adds an addressing and protocol naming mechanism to support multiple services on one port and multiple host names on one IP address

74fb721627d6.title: rfc>6455
74fb721627d6.sentence: - layers a framing mechanism on top of TCP to get back to the IP packet mechanism that TCP is built on, but without length limits

7f9ee10ae91f.title: rfc>6455
7f9ee10ae91f.sentence: - includes an additional closing handshake in-band that is designed to work in the presence of proxies and other intermediaries

b00509a3fee1.title: WebSocket
b00509a3fee1.sentence: TCP alone deals with streams of bytes with no inherent concept of a message.

81bba66c3995.title: WebSocket
81bba66c3995.sentence: Additionally, WebSocket enables streams of messages on top of TCP.

2db3e7474af0.title: rfc>6455
2db3e7474af0.sentence: The same technique can be used for a variety of web applications: games, stock tickers, multiuser applications with simultaneous editing, user interfaces exposing server-side services in real time, etc.

b0ac1eadd7fe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
b0ac1eadd7fe.sentence: - Lightweight for both client and server.

2dbb45b0e987.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
2dbb45b0e987.sentence: - Older browsers don't support WebSockets (becoming less relevant).

5e41cdc43105.title: WebSocket
5e41cdc43105.sentence: WebSocket is supported by modern major web browsers using the standardized protocol defined by RFC 6455.

4415f7220fcc.title: rfc>6455
4415f7220fcc.sentence: The opening handshake is intended to be compatible with HTTP-based server-side software and intermediaries, so that a single port can be used by both HTTP clients talking to that server and WebSocket clients talking to that server.

bd5fec4436eb.title: WebSocket
bd5fec4436eb.sentence: After the Switching Protocols HTTP response, the opening handshake is complete, the HTTP protocol stops being used, and communication switches to a binary frame-based protocol.

fc970e0225a9.title: rfc>6455
fc970e0225a9.sentence: To this end, the WebSocket client's handshake is an HTTP Upgrade request:

eb7e41682db8.title: WebSocket
eb7e41682db8.sentence: HTTP and WebSocket clients can connect to a server using the same port because the opening handshake uses HTTP.

858df8340a9a.title: WebSocket
858df8340a9a.sentence: Request | Sec-WebSocket-Key | base64 -encode(16 random bytes) | Yes

33bd1b4cb8b6.title: WebSocket
33bd1b4cb8b6.sentence: Request | Origin | Varies | Yes (for browser clients)

79477c80b8d2.title: rfc>6455
79477c80b8d2.sentence: This header field is sent by browser clients; for non-browser clients, this header field may be sent if it makes sense in the context of those clients.

326c1d57fd76.title: rfc>6455
326c1d57fd76.sentence: Finally, the server has to prove to the client that it received the client's WebSocket handshake, so that the server doesn't accept connections that are not WebSocket connections.

8a1ba8cec616.title: rfc>6455
8a1ba8cec616.sentence: This prevents an attacker from tricking a WebSocket server by sending it carefully crafted packets using XMLHttpRequest [XMLHttpRequest] or a form submission.

ca8dd52833ce.title: rfc>6455
ca8dd52833ce.sentence: For this header field, the server has to take the value (as present in the header field, e.g., the base64-encoded version minus any leading and trailing whitespace) and concatenate this with the Globally Unique Identifier (GUID, ) "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11" in string form, which is unlikely to be used by network endpoints that do not understand the WebSocket Protocol.

45f19ea297d7.title: rfc>6455
45f19ea297d7.sentence: A SHA-1 hash (160 bits) [FIPS.180-3], base64-encoded (see Section 4 of ), of this concatenation is then returned in the server's handshake.

f97528fa1a3b.title: rfc>6455
f97528fa1a3b.sentence: The first line is an HTTP Status-Line, with the status code 101:

5a647b584dab.title: rfc>6455
5a647b584dab.sentence: Any status code other than 101 indicates that the WebSocket handshake has not completed and that the semantics of HTTP still apply.

42dad0f02cda.title: rfc>6455
42dad0f02cda.sentence: If the |Sec-WebSocket-Accept| value does not match the expected value, if the header field is missing, or if the HTTP status code is not 101, the connection will not be established, and WebSocket frames will not be sent.

7e65f1a31ebe.title: rfc>6455
7e65f1a31ebe.section: 4. Opening Handshake > 4.2. Server-Side Requirements > 4.2.2. Sending the Server's Opening Handshake
7e65f1a31ebe.sentence: If the server does not wish to accept this connection, it MUST return an appropriate HTTP error code (e.g., 403 Forbidden) and abort the WebSocket handshake described in this section.

3f2fc858cd58.title: rfc>6455
3f2fc858cd58.section: 4. Opening Handshake > 4.2. Server-Side Requirements > 4.2.2. Sending the Server's Opening Handshake
3f2fc858cd58.sentence: If this version does not match a version understood by the server, the server MUST abort the WebSocket handshake described in this section and instead send an appropriate HTTP error code (such as 426 Upgrade Required) and a |Sec-WebSocket-Version| header field indicating the version(s) the server is capable of understanding.

accfd24d50f4.title: rfc>6455
accfd24d50f4.section: 4. Opening Handshake > 4.2. Server-Side Requirements > 4.2.2. Sending the Server's Opening Handshake
accfd24d50f4.sentence: If the requested service is not available, the server MUST send an appropriate HTTP error code (such as 404 Not Found) and abort the WebSocket handshake.

e04ce4c18682.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
e04ce4c18682.sentence: - A WebSocket connection will be opened once the client receives a successful handshake response.

9550554f857c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
9550554f857c.sentence: - Now the client and server can start sending data in both directions allowing real-time communication.

a0da1d57a005.title: WebSocket
a0da1d57a005.sentence: WebSockets can also be established over HTTP/2 using the extended CONNECT method defined by RFC 8441.

8ecaa1e1dcd6.title: WebSocket
8ecaa1e1dcd6.sentence: Unlike the HTTP/1.1 Upgrade handshake, this method carries a WebSocket connection within a single HTTP/2 stream, allowing other streams to carry regular HTTP traffic.

a27be28f0557.title: WebSocket
a27be28f0557.sentence: RFC 9220 adapts the same mechanism for HTTP/3.

334ef89ab504.title: WebSocket
334ef89ab504.sentence: After the opening handshake, the client and server can, at any time, send data messages (text or binary) and control messages (Close, Ping, Pong) to each other.

5509909374dc.title: WebSocket
5509909374dc.sentence: A message is composed of one frame if unfragmented or at least two frames if fragmented.

8673a3648891.title: rfc>6455
8673a3648891.sentence: Broadly speaking, there are types for textual data (which is interpreted as UTF-8 text), binary data (whose interpretation is left up to the application), and control frames (which are not intended to carry data for the application but instead for protocol-level signaling, such as to signal that the connection should be closed).

591aa85e6d43.title: rfc>6455
591aa85e6d43.sentence: A data frame MAY be transmitted by either the client or the server at any time after opening handshake completion and before that endpoint has sent a Close frame (Section 5.5.1).

4884564b3c98.title: rfc>6455
4884564b3c98.sentence: The WebSocket Protocol is designed on the principle that there should be minimal framing (the only framing that exists is to make the protocol frame-based instead of stream-based and to support a distinction between Unicode text and binary frames).

241bf19a5bd5.title: rfc>6455
241bf19a5bd5.sentence: An intermediary might coalesce and/or split frames, if no extensions were negotiated by the client and the server or if some extensions were negotiated, but the intermediary understood all the extensions negotiated and knows how to coalesce and/or split frames in the presence of these extensions.

c65e5c198e88.title: rfc>6455
c65e5c198e88.sentence: One implication of this is that in absence of extensions, senders and receivers must not depend on the presence of specific frame boundaries.

95385bcc42fc.title: rfc>6455
95385bcc42fc.sentence: The primary purpose of fragmentation is to allow sending a message that is of unknown size when the message is started without having to buffer that message.

e5935c4aea96.title: rfc>6455
e5935c4aea96.sentence: If messages couldn't be fragmented, then an endpoint would have to buffer the entire message so its length could be counted before the first byte is sent.

76bbe0e5b610.title: WebSocket
76bbe0e5b610.sentence: It enables sending messages with initial data available but complete length unknown.

6215d90e254b.title: WebSocket
6215d90e254b.sentence: Without fragmentation, the whole message must be sent in one frame, so the complete length is needed before the first byte can be sent, which requires a buffer.

985c4282bf46.title: rfc>6455
985c4282bf46.sentence: - An unfragmented message consists of a single frame with the FIN bit set (Section 5.2) and an opcode other than 0.

1944dab86a44.title: rfc>6455
1944dab86a44.sentence: - A fragmented message consists of a single frame with the FIN bit clear and an opcode other than 0, followed by zero or more frames with the FIN bit clear and the opcode set to 0, and terminated by a single frame with the FIN bit set and an opcode of 0.

a6fc6673a368.title: rfc>6455
a6fc6673a368.sentence: - Message fragments MUST be delivered to the recipient in the order sent by the sender.

d1030ae7e4e5.title: rfc>6455
d1030ae7e4e5.sentence: - The fragments of one message MUST NOT be interleaved between the fragments of another message unless an extension has been negotiated that can interpret the interleaving.

77513c6388c6.title: rfc>6455
77513c6388c6.sentence: - Control frames (see Section 5.5) MAY be injected in the middle of a fragmented message.

7c03d1ffc093.title: rfc>6455
7c03d1ffc093.sentence: Control frames themselves MUST NOT be fragmented.

ec253f6fd233.title: rfc>6455
ec253f6fd233.sentence: NOTE: If control frames could not be interjected, the latency of a ping, for example, would be very long if behind a large message.

852ae12a2d12.title: WebSocket
852ae12a2d12.sentence: 0 | FIN | 1 | 1 = final frame of a message. 0 = message is fragmented and this is not the final frame.

5ea0057062a5.title: rfc>6455
5ea0057062a5.sentence: This version of the protocol defines six frame types and leaves ten reserved for future use.

299f3afcd777.title: WebSocket
299f3afcd777.sentence: While the WebSocket protocol itself is unaware of proxy servers and firewalls, it features an HTTP-compatible handshake, thus allowing HTTP servers to share their default HTTP and HTTPS ports (80 and 443 respectively) with a WebSocket gateway or server.

18f1d81f8348.title: WebSocket
18f1d81f8348.sentence: Some proxy servers are transparent and work fine with WebSocket; others will prevent WebSocket from working correctly, causing the connection to fail.

7ac0bbcf2c05.title: WebSocket
7ac0bbcf2c05.sentence: WebSocket protocol client implementations try to detect whether the user agent is configured to use a proxy when connecting to destination host and port, and if it is, uses HTTP CONNECT method to set up a persistent tunnel.

7d3ed1e1402b.title: WebSocket
7d3ed1e1402b.sentence: If unencrypted WebSocket traffic flows through an explicit or a transparent proxy server without WebSockets support, the connection will likely fail.

538ec398727b.title: WebSocket
538ec398727b.sentence: In some cases, additional proxy-server configuration may be required, and certain proxy servers may need to be upgraded to support WebSocket.

c0ca3ded4678.title: WebSocket
c0ca3ded4678.sentence: If an encrypted WebSocket connection is used, then the use of Transport Layer Security (TLS) in the WebSocket Secure connection ensures that an HTTP CONNECT command is issued when the browser is configured to use an explicit proxy server.

d6147f8f6705.title: WebSocket
d6147f8f6705.sentence: However, since the wire traffic is encrypted, intermediate transparent proxy servers may simply allow the encrypted traffic through, so there is a much better chance that the WebSocket connection will succeed if WebSocket Secure is used.

6cd9d1a8b3a0.title: rfc>6455
6cd9d1a8b3a0.sentence: At the time of writing of this specification, it should be noted that connections on ports 80 and 443 have significantly different success rates, with connections on port 443 being significantly more likely to succeed, though this may change with time.

ded420883618.title: rfc>6455
ded420883618.sentence: Servers MAY offload the management of the connection to other agents on the network, for example, load balancers and reverse proxies.

fb2f2eba0271.title: rfc>6455
fb2f2eba0271.sentence: In such a situation, the server for the purposes of this specification is considered to include all parts of the server-side infrastructure from the first device to terminate the TCP connection all the way to the server that processes requests and sends responses.

7b541d411117.title: rfc>6455
7b541d411117.sentence: In more elaborate setups (e.g., with load balancers and multiple servers), a dedicated set of hosts for WebSocket connections separate from the HTTP servers is probably easier to manage.

b8709a13221f.title: rfc>6455
b8709a13221f.sentence: This last point is important because the traffic patterns of interactive messaging do not closely match standard HTTP traffic and can induce unusual loads on some components.

c203fdf57e30.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::load-balancing
c203fdf57e30.sentence: - Persistence connections: Allowing a server to open a persistent connection with a client such as a WebSocket.

bbd297da5a91.title: WebSocket
bbd297da5a91.sentence: - Nginx has supported WebSockets since 2013, implemented in version 1.3.13 including acting as a reverse proxy and load balancer of WebSocket applications.

05f75d3ffa3b.title: rfc>6455
05f75d3ffa3b.sentence: Either peer can send a control frame with data containing a specified control sequence to begin the closing handshake (detailed in Section 5.5.1).

88d7827ed7d7.title: rfc>6455
88d7827ed7d7.sentence: Upon receiving such a frame, the other peer sends a Close frame in response, if it hasn't already sent one.

5d9825d95334.title: rfc>6455
5d9825d95334.sentence: Upon receiving _that_ control frame, the first peer then closes the connection, safe in the knowledge that no further data is forthcoming.

8b1a9807b206.title: rfc>6455
8b1a9807b206.sentence: It is safe for both peers to initiate this handshake simultaneously.

aeea45ad89a4.title: rfc>6455
aeea45ad89a4.sentence: The Close frame contains an opcode of 0x8.

82b9c4ce579d.title: rfc>6455
82b9c4ce579d.sentence: After sending a control frame indicating the connection should be closed, a peer does not send any further data; after receiving a control frame indicating the connection should be closed, a peer discards any further data received.

c08cb2745a8e.title: rfc>6455
c08cb2745a8e.sentence: The application MUST NOT send any more data frames after sending a Close frame.

0b60a8159983.title: rfc>6455
0b60a8159983.sentence: After both sending and receiving a Close message, an endpoint considers the WebSocket connection closed and MUST close the underlying TCP connection.

a2cb7d04cb10.title: rfc>6455
a2cb7d04cb10.sentence: The server MUST close the underlying TCP connection immediately; the client SHOULD wait for the server to close the connection but MAY close the connection at any time after sending and receiving a Close message, e.g., if it has not received a TCP Close from the server in a reasonable time period.

86f624cece5e.title: rfc>6455
86f624cece5e.sentence: The closing handshake is intended to complement the TCP closing handshake (FIN/ACK), on the basis that the TCP closing handshake is not always reliable end-to-end, especially in the presence of intercepting proxies and other intermediaries.

1f8e3bad741e.title: rfc>6455
1f8e3bad741e.sentence: By sending a Close frame and waiting for a Close frame in response, certain cases are avoided where data may be unnecessarily lost.

b77a768995ca.title: rfc>6455
b77a768995ca.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.3. Normal Closure of Connections
b77a768995ca.sentence: Servers MAY close the WebSocket connection whenever desired.

0473e480e68c.title: rfc>6455
0473e480e68c.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.3. Normal Closure of Connections
0473e480e68c.sentence: Clients SHOULD NOT close the WebSocket connection arbitrarily.

6cbc4e3b4ced.title: rfc>6455
6cbc4e3b4ced.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.3. Normal Closure of Connections
6cbc4e3b4ced.sentence: In either case, an endpoint initiates a closure by following the procedures to _Start the WebSocket Closing Handshake_ (Section 7.1.2).

6b162327193f.title: rfc>6455
6b162327193f.sentence: If there is a body, the first two bytes of the body MUST be a 2-byte unsigned integer (in network byte order) representing a status code with value /code/ defined in Section 7.4.

bd7739d2cf85.title: rfc>6455
bd7739d2cf85.sentence: Following the 2-byte integer, the body MAY contain UTF-8-encoded data with value /reason/, the interpretation of which is not defined by this specification.

049ce85b5a26.title: rfc>6455
049ce85b5a26.sentence: As the data is not guaranteed to be human readable, clients MUST NOT show it to end users.

0f0826c05601.title: rfc>6455
0f0826c05601.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
0f0826c05601.sentence: 1000 indicates a normal closure, meaning that the purpose for which the connection was established has been fulfilled.

fdd6fa1d5405.title: rfc>6455
fdd6fa1d5405.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
fdd6fa1d5405.sentence: 1001 indicates that an endpoint is "going away", such as a server going down or a browser having navigated away from a page.

e041be09ab1d.title: rfc>6455
e041be09ab1d.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
e041be09ab1d.sentence: 1002 indicates that an endpoint is terminating the connection due to a protocol error.

7ec9516628c6.title: rfc>6455
7ec9516628c6.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
7ec9516628c6.sentence: 1003 indicates that an endpoint is terminating the connection because it has received a type of data it cannot accept (e.g., an endpoint that understands only text data MAY send this if it receives a binary message).

1a21de427b72.title: rfc>6455
1a21de427b72.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
1a21de427b72.sentence: 1007 indicates that an endpoint is terminating the connection because it has received data within a message that was not consistent with the type of the message (e.g., non-UTF-8 data within a text message).

40419e8a7a4b.title: rfc>6455
40419e8a7a4b.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
40419e8a7a4b.sentence: 1008 indicates that an endpoint is terminating the connection because it has received a message that violates its policy.

a2e686c9784a.title: rfc>6455
a2e686c9784a.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
a2e686c9784a.sentence: 1009 indicates that an endpoint is terminating the connection because it has received a message that is too big for it to process.

e33533ae7ffb.title: rfc>6455
e33533ae7ffb.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
e33533ae7ffb.sentence: 1011 indicates that a server is terminating the connection because it encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.

b41d0f72b618.title: rfc>6455
b41d0f72b618.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
b41d0f72b618.sentence: 1005 is a reserved value and MUST NOT be set as a status code in a Close control frame by an endpoint.

2e93a2a3b636.title: rfc>6455
2e93a2a3b636.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
2e93a2a3b636.sentence: 1006 is a reserved value and MUST NOT be set as a status code in a Close control frame by an endpoint.

1e04c89ec2ab.title: rfc>6455
1e04c89ec2ab.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.1. Defined Status Codes
1e04c89ec2ab.sentence: 1015 is a reserved value and MUST NOT be set as a status code in a Close control frame by an endpoint.

20a673e46975.title: rfc>6455
20a673e46975.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.2. Reserved Status Code Ranges
20a673e46975.sentence: Status codes in the range 1000-2999 are reserved for definition by this protocol, its future revisions, and extensions specified in a permanent and readily available public specification.

3833f1029e29.title: rfc>6455
3833f1029e29.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.2. Reserved Status Code Ranges
3833f1029e29.sentence: Status codes in the range 3000-3999 are reserved for use by libraries, frameworks, and applications.

b43d027ecce7.title: rfc>6455
b43d027ecce7.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.2. Reserved Status Code Ranges
b43d027ecce7.sentence: These status codes are registered directly with IANA.

dee0c3dbcddc.title: rfc>6455
dee0c3dbcddc.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.4. Status Codes > 7.4.2. Reserved Status Code Ranges
dee0c3dbcddc.sentence: Status codes in the range 4000-4999 are reserved for private use and thus can't be registered.

2c89577e98a5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
2c89577e98a5.sentence: Instead you create an endpoint in your application server and provide it as a callback to the external service (such as a payment processor or a shipping vendor)

08e4cccc5033.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
08e4cccc5033.sentence: Every time something interesting happens, the external service calls the endpoint and provides the information.

1fdf8b878c64.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
1fdf8b878c64.sentence: You don’t continuously ask for information.

a1682cdf28c2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
a1682cdf28c2.sentence: This makes webhooks ideal for dealing with real-time updates because data is pushed to your application as soon as it’s available.

c821969b1d26.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
c821969b1d26.sentence: Webhooks are recommended for applications that need instant data delivery.

e8cb8cd336ac.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
e8cb8cd336ac.sentence: Also, webhooks are efficient in terms of resource utilization especially in high throughput environments.

83924f628503.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/polling-vs-webhooks.md
83924f628503.sentence: Also, with webhooks there is a risk of missed notifications due to network issues, hence proper retry mechanisms are needed.

c6be0ae7b38c.title: Webhook
c6be0ae7b38c.sentence: They are usually triggered by some event, such as pushing code to a repository, a purchase, a comment being posted to a blog and many more use cases.

3769879c88a7.title: Webhook
3769879c88a7.sentence: When that event occurs, the source site makes an HTTP request to the URL configured for the webhook.

6d5d309183da.title: Webhook
6d5d309183da.sentence: Because webhooks use HTTP, they can be integrated into web services without adding new infrastructure.

d30e327e9a6e.title: Webhook
d30e327e9a6e.sentence: When the client (the originating website or application) makes a webhook call to the third-party user's server, the incoming POST request should be authenticated to avoid a spoofing attack and its timestamp verified to avoid a replay attack.

6e370a37e8c4.title: Webhook
6e370a37e8c4.sentence: - HTTP basic authentication can be used to authenticate the client.

4675da0ca125.title: Webhook
4675da0ca125.sentence: - The webhook can include information about what type of event it is, and a shared secret or digital signature to verify the webhook.

a9c7b56f5c48.title: Webhook
a9c7b56f5c48.sentence: - An HMAC signature can be included as an HTTP header.

b50e49f906e8.title: Webhook
b50e49f906e8.sentence: - Mutual TLS authentication can be used when the connection is established.

03f296fc801a.title: Webhook
03f296fc801a.sentence: The sender may choose to keep a constant list of IP addresses from which requests will be sent.

c3d08bf78eaf.title: Webhook
c3d08bf78eaf.sentence: This is not a sufficient security measure on its own, but it is useful for when the receiving endpoint is behind a firewall or NAT.

59382557106a.title: Webhook
59382557106a.section: Authenticating the webhook notification > Server-side request forgery risk
59382557106a.sentence: Because a webhook's sender typically lets a user configure an arbitrary destination URL, the OWASP Foundation identifies this as a common vector for server-side request forgery, where the sender's own server can be made to request internal network resources.

7fdfeb02559e.title: Webhook
7fdfeb02559e.section: Authenticating the webhook notification > Server-side request forgery risk
7fdfeb02559e.sentence: Recommended mitigation is to re-check the resolved IP before each delivery, not only at registration.

0ffd7247b7da.title: WebSocket
0ffd7247b7da.sentence: A web application (e.g. web browser) may use the WebSocket interface to maintain bidirectional communications with a WebSocket server.

a58abd5f6248.title: WebSocket
a58abd5f6248.sentence: Constructor | ws = new WebSocket (url [, protocols]) | Start opening handshake. url: A string containing: Scheme: must be ws, wss, http or https. Host. Optional port: If not specified, 80 is used for ws and http, and 443 for wss and https. Optional path. Optional query. No fragment. Optional protocols: A string or an array of strings used as the value of the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header in the opening handshake. Exceptions: SyntaxError: url parsing failed. url has an invalid scheme. url has a fragment. protocols has duplicate strings.

bdcc1b0e97cc.title: WebSocket
bdcc1b0e97cc.sentence: Method | ws. send (data) | Send data message. data: must be string, Blob, ArrayBuffer or ArrayBufferView. Return: undefined. Exceptions: InvalidStateError: ws.readyState is CONNECTING. Note: If the data cannot be sent (e.g. because it would need to be buffered but the buffer is full), the connection is closed and the error event is fired.

281d52754ce1.title: WebSocket
281d52754ce1.sentence: Event | ws. onopen = (event) => {} ws.addEventListener("open", (event) => {}) | Opening handshake succeeded. event type is Event.

43dc9b393f21.title: WebSocket
43dc9b393f21.sentence: Event | ws. onmessage = (event) => {} ws.addEventListener("message", (event) => {}) | Data message received. event type is MessageEvent. This event is only fired if ws.readyState is OPEN. event.data is the data received, of type: string for text. Blob or ArrayBuffer for binary (see ws.binaryType). event.origin is ws.url but only with the scheme, host, and port (if any).

4d70339cee35.title: WebSocket
4d70339cee35.sentence: Event | ws. onclose = (event) => {} ws.addEventListener("close", (event) => {}) | The underlying TCP connection closed. event type is CloseEvent. event.code: status code (integer). event.reason: reason for closing (string). event.wasClean: true if the TCP connection was closed after the closing handshake was completed, else false. Note: If the received Close frame contains a payload, event.code and event.reason get their value from the payload. If the received Close frame contains no payload, event.code is 1005 (No code received) and event.reason is an empty string. If no Close frame was received, event.code is 1006 (Connection closed abnormally) and event.reason is an empty string.

a4eda743bf6e.title: WebSocket
a4eda743bf6e.sentence: Event | ws. onerror = (event) => {} ws.addEventListener("error", (event) => {}) | Connection closed due to error. event type is Event.

3bd25a9a5118.title: WebSocket
3bd25a9a5118.sentence: Constant | WebSocket. CONNECTING = 0 | Opening handshake is currently in progress. The initial state of the connection.

8087fc635d4b.title: WebSocket
8087fc635d4b.sentence: Constant | WebSocket. OPEN = 1 | Opening handshake succeeded. The client and server may send messages to each other.

ee62e2e5f992.title: WebSocket
ee62e2e5f992.sentence: Constant | WebSocket. CLOSING = 2 | Closing handshake is currently in progress. Either ws.close() was called or a Close message was received.

0c66d7a5876d.title: WebSocket
0c66d7a5876d.sentence: Constant | WebSocket. CLOSED = 3 | The underlying TCP connection is closed.

64dd889142f2.title: WebSocket
64dd889142f2.sentence: Method | ws. close ([code] [, reason]) | Start closing handshake. Optional code: If specified, must be 1000 (Normal closure) or in the range 3000 to 4999 (application-defined). Defaults to 1000. Optional reason: If specified, must be a string whose UTF-8 encoding is up to 123 bytes. Defaults to an empty string. Return: undefined. Exceptions: InvalidAccessError: code is not 1000 nor is in the range 3000 to 4999. SyntaxError: UTF-8-encoded reason is longer than 123 bytes. Note: If ws.readyState is OPEN or CONNECTING, ws.readyState is set to CLOSING and the closing handshake starts. If ws.readyState is CLOSING or CLOSED, nothing happens (because the closing handshake has already started).

2ade90a1b5a9.title: Push technology
2ade90a1b5a9.sentence: HTTP server push (also known as HTTP streaming) is a mechanism for sending unsolicited (asynchronous) data from a web server to a web browser.

bf56d6c996fa.title: Push technology
bf56d6c996fa.sentence: Generally, the web server does not terminate a connection after response data has been served to a client.

596ad060c872.title: Push technology
596ad060c872.sentence: The web server leaves the connection open so that if an event occurs (for example, a change in internal data which needs to be reported to one or multiple clients), it can be sent out immediately; otherwise, the event would have to be queued until the client's next request is received.

7a37207b4e02.title: Push technology
7a37207b4e02.sentence: The underlying mechanism for this approach is chunked transfer encoding.

910cc6b2f077.title: Push technology
910cc6b2f077.sentence: Another mechanism is related to a special MIME type called multipart/x-mixed-replace, which was introduced by Netscape in 1995.

3f5ff01e2194.title: Push technology
3f5ff01e2194.sentence: Web browsers interpret this as a document that changes whenever the server pushes a new version to the client.

d4a912905e78.title: Push technology
d4a912905e78.sentence: In this technique, the server takes advantage of persistent HTTP connections, leaving the response perpetually "open" (i.e., the server never terminates the response), effectively fooling the browser to remain in "loading" mode after the initial page load could be considered complete.

4809c7174a88.title: Push technology
4809c7174a88.sentence: The server then periodically sends snippets of JavaScript to update the content of the page, thereby achieving push capability.

fab70d4b6e16.title: Push technology
fab70d4b6e16.sentence: By using this technique, the client doesn't need Java applets or other plug-ins in order to keep an open connection to the server; the client is automatically notified about new events, pushed by the server.

ced997c1200c.title: Push technology
ced997c1200c.sentence: One serious drawback to this method, however, is the lack of control the server has over the browser timing out; a page refresh is always necessary if a timeout occurs on the browser end.

42215024f7af.title: Server-sent events
42215024f7af.sentence: Server-Sent Events (SSE) is a server push technology enabling a client to receive automatic updates from a server via an HTTP connection, and describes how servers can initiate data transmission towards clients once an initial client connection has been established.

9465f7393bd0.title: Server-sent events
9465f7393bd0.sentence: They are commonly used to send message updates or continuous data streams to a browser client and designed to enhance native, cross-browser streaming through a JavaScript API called EventSource, through which a client requests a particular URL in order to receive an event stream.

0e4c418a8cdd.title: Server-sent events
0e4c418a8cdd.sentence: The media type for SSE is text/event-stream.

00639ba1693a.title: Server-sent events
00639ba1693a.sentence: The EventSource API is standardized as part of HTML Living Standard by the WHATWG.

3c13388079e3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
3c13388079e3.sentence: - The client makes a request to the server.

262296922b3f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
262296922b3f.sentence: - The connection between client and server is established and it remains open.

3853f7a7a72c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
3853f7a7a72c.sentence: - The server sends responses or events to the client when new data is available.

67b12c514bbc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
67b12c514bbc.sentence: It is unidirectional, meaning once the client sends the request it can only receive the responses without the ability to send new requests over the same connection.

23b9ebc2eac3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
23b9ebc2eac3.sentence: Server-Sent Events (SSE) is a way of establishing long-term communication between client and server that enables the server to proactively push data to the client.

b2d42a3810f3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
b2d42a3810f3.sentence: - Simple to implement and use for both client and server.

1ca327ead524.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::long-polling-websockets-server-sent-events-sse
1ca327ead524.sentence: - Limitation for the maximum number of open connections.

f0607a3a139f.title: Server-sent events
f0607a3a139f.sentence: When sending high-frequency data, the server must manage backpressure to prevent saturating clients.

1269cf30d8ad.title: Server-sent events
1269cf30d8ad.sentence: - Client-side buffering: Browsers have limited buffer space for incoming server-sent events

ffc258973fcd.title: Server-sent events
ffc258973fcd.sentence: - Adaptive rate limiting: Servers can adjust event frequency and monitor connection health

10928976dc3f.title: Server-sent events
10928976dc3f.sentence: - Event batching: Combining multiple events into larger and less frequent transmissions

c5ce972d4995.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::whatsapp
c5ce972d4995.sentence: We can use WebSockets or Server-Sent Events (SSE) for this.

7f17d6616937.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
7f17d6616937.sentence: We can use WebSockets or Server-Sent Events (SSE) for this.

b97883ebb2dc.title: Server-sent events
b97883ebb2dc.sentence: The SSE mechanism was first specified by Ian Hickson as part of the "WHATWG Web Applications 1.0" proposal starting in 2004.

bdca5737b1eb.title: Server-sent events
bdca5737b1eb.sentence: The W3C published Server-Sent Events as a Recommendation on February 3, 2015, after years of development through Working Drafts and Candidate Recommendations.

ebec3a1cf69c.title: Presence information
ebec3a1cf69c.sentence: In computer and telecommunications networks, presence information is a status indicator that conveys ability and willingness of a potential communication partner—for example a user—to communicate.

259f44accbb6.title: Presence information
259f44accbb6.sentence: A user's client provides presence information (presence state) via a network connection to a presence service, which is stored in what constitutes their personal availability record (called a presentity) and can be made available for distribution to other users (called watchers) to convey their availability for communication.

a5b876b58111.title: Presence information
a5b876b58111.sentence: A user client may publish a presence state to indicate its current communication status.

0222caae19fe.title: Presence information
0222caae19fe.sentence: The most common use of presence today is to display an indicator icon on instant messaging clients, typically from a choice of graphic symbols with easy-to-convey meanings, and a list of corresponding text descriptions of each of the states.

48192c88eadf.title: Presence information
48192c88eadf.sentence: Common states on the user's availability are "free for chat", "busy", "away", "do not disturb", "out to lunch".

421fa174d422.title: Presence information
421fa174d422.sentence: Current standards support a rich choice of additional presence attributes that can be used for presence information, such as user mood, location, or free text status.

137acb20cbcb.title: Presence information
137acb20cbcb.sentence: The idea that multiple communication devices can combine state, to provide an aggregated view of a user's presence has been termed Multiple Points of Presence (MPOP).

ca2be97ac67a.title: Presence information
ca2be97ac67a.sentence: MPOP becomes even more powerful when it is automatically inferred from passive observation of a user's actions.

9b666fd548f4.title: Presence information
9b666fd548f4.sentence: This idea is already familiar to instant messaging users who have their status set to "Away" (or equivalent) if their computer keyboard is inactive for some time.

fd33e0dd6f1e.title: Presence information
fd33e0dd6f1e.sentence: XMPP, discussed below, allows for MPOP by assigning each client a "resource" (a specific identifier) and a priority number for each resource.

82c4f5e681f5.title: Presence information
82c4f5e681f5.sentence: A message directed to the user's ID would go to the resource with highest priority, although messaging a specific resource is possible by using the form user@domain/resource.

b3b73fb098d2.title: Presence information
b3b73fb098d2.sentence: Presence is highly sensitive information and in non-trivial systems a presentity may define limits to which its presence information may be revealed to different watchers.

c7eb735d8ce1.title: Presence information
c7eb735d8ce1.sentence: Basic versions of this idea are already common in instant messaging clients as a "Blocking" facility, where users can appear as unavailable to selected watchers.

0a23894d03bd.title: XMPP
0a23894d03bd.sentence: Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (abbreviation XMPP, originally named Jabber) is an open communication protocol designed for instant messaging (IM), presence information, and contact list maintenance.

ebedbf06c781.title: XMPP
ebedbf06c781.sentence: Based on XML (Extensible Markup Language), it enables the near-real-time exchange of structured data between two or more network entities.

16d4ebe602bc.title: XMPP
16d4ebe602bc.sentence: Designed to be extensible, the protocol offers a multitude of applications beyond traditional IM in the broader realm of message-oriented middleware, including signalling for VoIP, video, file transfer, gaming and other uses.

cbcc336eda69.title: XMPP
cbcc336eda69.sentence: Unlike most commercial instant messaging protocols, XMPP is defined in an open standard in the application layer.

aa7f8e0ca25a.title: XMPP
aa7f8e0ca25a.sentence: The architecture of the XMPP network is similar to email; anyone can run their own XMPP server and there is no central master server.

103633aef7dc.title: XMPP
103633aef7dc.sentence: This federated open system approach allows users to interoperate with others on any server using a Jabber identifier (JID) user account, similar to an email address.

6df25f2c8707.title: XMPP
6df25f2c8707.sentence: By design, there is no central authoritative server as there is with messaging services such as AIM, WLM, WhatsApp or Telegram.

996247a152b0.title: XMPP
996247a152b0.sentence: The XMPP network architecture is reminiscent of the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), a client–server model; clients do not talk directly to one another as it is decentralized – anyone can run a server.

7615fe223c37.title: XMPP
7615fe223c37.sentence: A client Alice ("alice@example.com") has a message for some other user, Beth ("beth@example.com"), and uses XMPP to convey this to the example.com server.

40291c73d529.title: XMPP
40291c73d529.sentence: If Beth is online, the server delivers the message instantly, otherwise it will be held for delivery later.

8d68553c2725.title: XMPP
8d68553c2725.sentence: If the message is for a user on another server, Charles ("charles@example.net"), then the example.com server connects using XMPP to pass the message to the example.net server.

d875f7486782.title: XMPP
d875f7486782.section: Federated Instant Messaging > Client-to-Server XMPP and Server-to-Server XMPP
d875f7486782.sentence: The XMPP client communicates with the server over a TLS-encrypted TCP stream on port 5222.

54be4ef7789c.title: XMPP
54be4ef7789c.section: Federated Instant Messaging > Client-to-Server XMPP and Server-to-Server XMPP
54be4ef7789c.sentence: XMPP servers communicate with each other over a TLS-encrypted TCP stream on port 5269.

6a2493d21ed5.title: XMPP
6a2493d21ed5.sentence: - RFC 6120, Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP): Core, which describes client–server messaging using two open-ended XML streams.

5fa62f97e7ff.title: XMPP
5fa62f97e7ff.sentence: Every user on the network has a unique XMPP address, called a Jabber ID (JID).

c9cc24806518.title: XMPP
c9cc24806518.sentence: The JID is structured like an email address with a username and a domain name (or IP address) for the server where that user resides, separated by an at sign (@) – for example, alice@example.com Here alice is the username and example.com the server with which the user is registered.

c6abaab66b62.title: XMPP
c6abaab66b62.sentence: Since a user may wish to log in from multiple locations, they may specify a resource.

ce78932bd7e6.title: XMPP
ce78932bd7e6.sentence: A resource identifies a particular client belonging to the user (for example home, work, or mobile).

345f2c6468ad.title: XMPP
345f2c6468ad.sentence: This may be included in the JID by appending a slash followed by the name of the resource.

f8754773ee10.title: XMPP
f8754773ee10.sentence: The original and "native" transport protocol for XMPP is Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), using open-ended XML streams over long-lived TCP connections.

a11fd6686ee5.title: XMPP
a11fd6686ee5.sentence: As an alternative to the TCP transport, the XMPP community has also developed an HTTP transport for web clients as well as users behind restricted firewalls.

f11d837b81a1.title: XMPP
f11d837b81a1.sentence: The binding method, implemented using Bidirectional-streams Over Synchronous HTTP (BOSH), allows servers to push messages to clients as soon as they are sent.

513b5d223e30.title: XMPP
513b5d223e30.sentence: XMPP also supports using WebSockets to communicate to a server.

a29f3f27961b.title: XMPP
a29f3f27961b.sentence: The XMPP Standards Foundation or XSF (formerly the Jabber Software Foundation) is active in developing open XMPP extensions, so called XEPs.

e924f52b12d3.title: XMPP
e924f52b12d3.sentence: XMPP supports conferences with multiple users, using the specification Multi-User Chat (MUC) (XEP-0045).

83b742747f14.title: XMPP
83b742747f14.sentence: Using the extension called Jingle, XMPP can provide an open means to support machine-to-machine or peer-to-peer communications across a diverse set of networks.

b9593e9f84e1.title: XMPP
b9593e9f84e1.sentence: It has since been replaced by a better extension, multi-end-to-multi-end encryption (OMEMO, XEP-0384) end-to-end encryption between users.

d62520b8a937.title: XMPP
d62520b8a937.sentence: This gives a higher level of security, by encrypting all data from the source client and decrypting again at the target client; the server operator cannot decrypt the data they are forwarding.

00c29d2cf8ad.title: XMPP
00c29d2cf8ad.sentence: Since XML is text based, normal XMPP has a higher network overhead compared to purely binary solutions.

e1eef763209b.title: XMPP
e1eef763209b.sentence: In-band binary data transfer is limited.

1f83ddf666df.title: XMPP
1f83ddf666df.sentence: Binary data must be first base64 encoded before it can be transmitted in-band.

819f41382a12.title: XMPP
819f41382a12.sentence: Therefore, any significant amount of binary data (e.g., file transfers) is best transmitted out-of-band, using in-band messages to coordinate.

8c81a8d65346.title: rfc>8030
8c81a8d65346.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
8c81a8d65346.sentence: An application server MUST include the TTL (Time-To-Live) header field in its request for push message delivery.

010e8f914518.title: rfc>8030
010e8f914518.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.3. Push Message Urgency
010e8f914518.sentence: An application server MAY include an Urgency header field in its request for push message delivery.

504a7905a3de.title: rfc>8030
504a7905a3de.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.4. Replacing Push Messages
504a7905a3de.sentence: A push message topic is a string carried in a Topic header field.

57632c22b158.title: rfc>8030
57632c22b158.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
57632c22b158.sentence: A push service can improve the reliability of push message delivery considerably by storing push messages for a period.

652b8b2e01c7.title: rfc>8030
652b8b2e01c7.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
652b8b2e01c7.sentence: User agents are often only intermittently connected, and so benefit from having short-term message storage at the push service.

74b69efb32ba.title: rfc>8030
74b69efb32ba.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
74b69efb32ba.sentence: The TTL header field contains a value in seconds that suggests how long a push message is retained by the push service.

a4a1390a0895.title: rfc>8030
a4a1390a0895.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
a4a1390a0895.sentence: A push service MAY retain a push message for a shorter duration than requested.

9a1306cc5636.title: rfc>8030
9a1306cc5636.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
9a1306cc5636.sentence: Once the TTL period elapses, the push service MUST NOT attempt to deliver the push message to the user agent.

7935435b67e6.title: rfc>8030
7935435b67e6.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
7935435b67e6.sentence: A Push message with a zero TTL is immediately delivered if the user agent is available to receive the message.

b3e115d53205.title: rfc>8030
b3e115d53205.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
b3e115d53205.sentence: If the user agent is unavailable, a push message with a zero TTL expires and is never delivered.

fb97f230a3b4.title: rfc>8030
fb97f230a3b4.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.2. Push Message Time-To-Live
fb97f230a3b4.sentence: Consequently, an application server cannot rely on receiving acknowledgement receipts for zero TTL push messages.

a1dcd32d92b7.title: rfc>8030
a1dcd32d92b7.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.3. Push Message Urgency
a1dcd32d92b7.sentence: For a device that is battery-powered, it is often critical that it remains dormant for extended periods.

dbdb66bc0fd7.title: rfc>8030
dbdb66bc0fd7.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.3. Push Message Urgency
dbdb66bc0fd7.sentence: To avoid consuming resources to receive trivial messages, it is helpful if an application server can communicate the urgency of a message and if the user agent can request that the push server only forwards messages of a specific urgency.

77b05107712d.title: rfc>8030
77b05107712d.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.3. Push Message Urgency

49d89c7c689d.title: rfc>8030
49d89c7c689d.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.3. Push Message Urgency
49d89c7c689d.sentence: A push message without the Urgency header field defaults to a value of "normal".

da7b6974535e.title: rfc>8030
da7b6974535e.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.3. Push Message Urgency
da7b6974535e.sentence: A user agent MAY include the Urgency header field when monitoring for push messages to indicate the lowest urgency of push messages that it is willing to receive.

7baba11a9772.title: rfc>8030
7baba11a9772.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.3. Push Message Urgency
7baba11a9772.sentence: A push service MUST NOT deliver push messages with lower urgency than the value indicated by the user agent in its monitoring request.

7e3273b5009d.title: rfc>8030
7e3273b5009d.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.4. Replacing Push Messages
7e3273b5009d.sentence: If the user agent is offline during the time that the push messages are sent, updating a push message avoids the situation where outdated or redundant messages are sent to the user agent.

65252d701993.title: rfc>8030
65252d701993.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.4. Replacing Push Messages
65252d701993.sentence: Only push messages that have been assigned a topic can be replaced.

8a9a7a4981e5.title: rfc>8030
8a9a7a4981e5.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.4. Replacing Push Messages
8a9a7a4981e5.sentence: A push message with a topic replaces any outstanding push message with an identical topic.

63c574b41ef0.title: rfc>8030
63c574b41ef0.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.4. Replacing Push Messages
63c574b41ef0.sentence: For use with this protocol, the Topic header field MUST be restricted to no more than 32 characters from the URL and a filename-safe Base 64 alphabet.

0c2486787895.title: rfc>6455
0c2486787895.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.2. Abnormal Closures > 7.2.3. Recovering from Abnormal Closure
0c2486787895.sentence: To prevent this, clients SHOULD use some form of backoff when trying to reconnect after abnormal closures as described in this section.

770906e02236.title: rfc>6455
770906e02236.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.2. Abnormal Closures > 7.2.3. Recovering from Abnormal Closure
770906e02236.sentence: The first reconnect attempt SHOULD be delayed by a random amount of time.

c7942b52e2c0.title: rfc>6455
c7942b52e2c0.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.2. Abnormal Closures > 7.2.3. Recovering from Abnormal Closure
c7942b52e2c0.sentence: Should the first reconnect attempt fail, subsequent reconnect attempts SHOULD be delayed by increasingly longer amounts of time, using a method such as truncated binary exponential backoff.

98d49b086939.title: rfc>6455
98d49b086939.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.2. Abnormal Closures > 7.2.3. Recovering from Abnormal Closure
98d49b086939.sentence: Such closures could be the result of a transient error, in which case reconnecting may lead to a good connection and a resumption of normal operations.

d20e560797c9.title: rfc>6455
d20e560797c9.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.2. Abnormal Closures > 7.2.3. Recovering from Abnormal Closure
d20e560797c9.sentence: Such closures may also be the result of a nontransient problem, in which case if each deployed client experiences an abnormal closure and immediately and persistently tries to reconnect, the server may experience what amounts to a denial-of-service attack by a large number of clients trying to reconnect.

f16842ee5cd7.title: rfc>6455
f16842ee5cd7.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.2. Abnormal Closures > 7.2.3. Recovering from Abnormal Closure
f16842ee5cd7.sentence: The end result of such a scenario could be that the service is unable to recover in a timely manner or recovery is made much more difficult.

549bc309ad13.title: rfc>6455
549bc309ad13.section: 7. Closing the Connection > 7.2. Abnormal Closures > 7.2.3. Recovering from Abnormal Closure
549bc309ad13.sentence: The parameters by which this random delay is chosen are left to the client to decide; a value chosen randomly between 0 and 5 seconds is a reasonable initial delay though clients MAY choose a different interval from which to select a delay length based on implementation experience and particular application.

62adc9a717cc.title: rfc>6455
62adc9a717cc.sentence: This specification defines two URI schemes, using the ABNF syntax defined in RFC 5234, and terminology and ABNF productions defined by the URI specification RFC 3986.

12fe9acffdba.title: rfc>6455
12fe9acffdba.section: 11. IANA Considerations > 11.1. Registration of New URI Schemes > 11.1.2. Registration of "wss" Scheme
12fe9acffdba.sentence: A |wss| URI identifies a WebSocket server and resource name and indicates that traffic over that connection is to be protected via TLS (including standard benefits of TLS such as data confidentiality and integrity and endpoint authentication).

b427abd1fe4c.title: rfc>6455
b427abd1fe4c.sentence: The port component is OPTIONAL; the default for "ws" is port 80, while the default for "wss" is port 443.

7e9e2a02d0b7.title: rfc>6455
7e9e2a02d0b7.sentence: The URI is called "secure" (and it is said that "the secure flag is set") if the scheme component matches "wss" case-insensitively.

8e5b7ce8681a.title: rfc>6455
8e5b7ce8681a.sentence: The "resource-name" (also known as /resource name/ in Section 4.1) can be constructed by concatenating the following:

60aeefe39cea.title: rfc>6455
60aeefe39cea.sentence: - "/" if the path component is empty

5b8e99d4e7f9.title: rfc>6455
5b8e99d4e7f9.section: 12. Using the WebSocket Protocol from Other Specifications
5b8e99d4e7f9.sentence: - A /resource name/, which allows for multiple services to be identified at one host and port.

3128cda8071a.title: rfc>6455
3128cda8071a.sentence: Fragment identifiers are meaningless in the context of WebSocket URIs and MUST NOT be used on these URIs.

50d9110281c2.title: WebSocket
50d9110281c2.sentence: Unlike regular cross-domain HTTP requests, WebSocket requests are not restricted by the same-origin policy.

d4e5c0904041.title: rfc>6455
d4e5c0904041.sentence: The |Origin| header field is used to protect against unauthorized cross-origin use of a WebSocket server by scripts using the WebSocket API in a web browser.

86f656d44c8d.title: rfc>6455
86f656d44c8d.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.6. Connection Confidentiality and Integrity
86f656d44c8d.sentence: Connection confidentiality and integrity is provided by running the WebSocket Protocol over TLS (wss URIs).

a89b1df2e12a.title: rfc>6455
a89b1df2e12a.sentence: The server is informed of the script origin generating the WebSocket connection request.

d2f6cdc17770.title: rfc>6455
d2f6cdc17770.sentence: Servers that are not intended to process input from any web page but only for certain sites SHOULD verify the |Origin| field is an origin they expect.

7a1b18d589de.title: rfc>6455
7a1b18d589de.sentence: If the origin indicated is unacceptable to the server, then it SHOULD respond to the WebSocket handshake with a reply containing HTTP 403 Forbidden status code.

066d2772c978.title: WebSocket
066d2772c978.sentence: Therefore, WebSocket servers must validate the "Origin" header against the expected origins during connection establishment, to avoid cross-site WebSocket hijacking attacks (similar to cross-site request forgery), which might be possible when the connection is authenticated with cookies or HTTP authentication.

32fea30b501f.title: rfc>6455
32fea30b501f.sentence: The intent is not to prevent non-browsers from establishing connections but rather to ensure that trusted browsers under the control of potentially malicious JavaScript cannot fake a WebSocket handshake.

6519d9871edc.title: rfc>6455
6519d9871edc.sentence: Such hosts are acting on their own behalf and can therefore send fake |Origin| header fields, misleading the server.

3a00aee60619.title: rfc>6455
3a00aee60619.sentence: Servers should therefore be careful about assuming that they are talking directly to scripts from known origins and must consider that they might be accessed in unexpected ways.

49c6630f19a6.title: rfc>6455
49c6630f19a6.sentence: In particular, a server should not trust that any input is valid.

faba1d47ccf6.title: rfc>6455
faba1d47ccf6.sentence: This protocol doesn't prescribe any particular way that servers can authenticate clients during the WebSocket handshake.

71fa80dd928a.title: rfc>6455
71fa80dd928a.sentence: The WebSocket server can use any client authentication mechanism available to a generic HTTP server, such as cookies, HTTP authentication, or TLS authentication.

e13a51caf7f9.title: WebSocket
e13a51caf7f9.sentence: It is better to use tokens or similar protection mechanisms to authenticate the WebSocket connection when sensitive (private) data is being transferred over the WebSocket.

207930ac38bc.title: rfc>6455
207930ac38bc.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.6. Connection Confidentiality and Integrity
207930ac38bc.sentence: WebSocket implementations MUST support TLS and SHOULD employ it when communicating with their peers.

1bb9d8bfab76.title: rfc>6455
1bb9d8bfab76.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.7. Handling of Invalid Data
1bb9d8bfab76.sentence: Incoming data MUST always be validated by both clients and servers.

acc0ad02358e.title: rfc>6455
acc0ad02358e.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.7. Handling of Invalid Data
acc0ad02358e.sentence: This protocol specifies that messages with a Text data type (as opposed to Binary or other types) contain UTF-8-encoded data.

2073dafca250.title: rfc>6455
2073dafca250.section: 8. Error Handling > 8.1. Handling Errors in UTF-8-Encoded Data
2073dafca250.sentence: When an endpoint is to interpret a byte stream as UTF-8 but finds that the byte stream is not, in fact, a valid UTF-8 stream, that endpoint MUST _Fail the WebSocket Connection_.

f3b9c4e99d9f.title: rfc>6455
f3b9c4e99d9f.sentence: Implementations that have implementation- and/or platform-specific limitations regarding the frame size or total message size after reassembly from multiple frames MUST protect themselves against exceeding those limits.

d93a238e8851.title: rfc>6455
d93a238e8851.sentence: (For example, a malicious endpoint can try to exhaust its peer's memory or mount a denial-of-service attack by sending either a single big frame (e.g., of size 2**60) or by sending a long stream of small frames that are a part of a fragmented message.) Such an implementation SHOULD impose a limit on frame sizes and the total message size after reassembly from multiple frames.

9f6c9f6ee39f.title: rfc>6455
9f6c9f6ee39f.sentence: Extensions provide a mechanism for implementations to opt-in to additional protocol features.

153375a142c2.title: rfc>6455
153375a142c2.sentence: The endpoints of a connection MUST negotiate the use of any extensions during the opening handshake.

c1e47dd12329.title: rfc>6455
c1e47dd12329.sentence: This document doesn't define any extension, but implementations MAY use extensions defined separately.

3c243e081c11.title: rfc>6455
3c243e081c11.sentence: WebSocket clients MAY request extensions to this specification, and WebSocket servers MAY accept some or all extensions requested by the client.

199e1bba460b.title: rfc>6455
199e1bba460b.sentence: A server MUST NOT respond with any extension not requested by the client.

45cd9098596b.title: rfc>6455
45cd9098596b.sentence: A server accepts one or more extensions by including a |Sec-WebSocket-Extensions| header field containing one or more extensions that were requested by the client.

702d5ee142ee.title: rfc>6455
702d5ee142ee.sentence: Note that the client is only offering to use any advertised extensions and MUST NOT use them unless the server indicates that it wishes to use the extension.

d2fc7b1d47d4.title: rfc>6455
d2fc7b1d47d4.sentence: The extensions listed by the server in response represent the extensions actually in use for the connection.

94f2259df767.title: rfc>6455
94f2259df767.sentence: Note that the order of extensions is significant.

0dc0cfe1b78d.title: rfc>6455
0dc0cfe1b78d.sentence: In the absence of such definitions, the interpretation is that the header fields listed by the client in its request represent a preference of the header fields it wishes to use, with the first options listed being most preferable.

f0ef0b4a8e3c.title: rfc>6455
f0ef0b4a8e3c.sentence: Should the extensions modify the data and/or framing, the order of operations on the data should be assumed to be the same as the order in which the extensions are listed in the server's response in the opening handshake.

bde902cb1ee4.title: rfc>6455
bde902cb1ee4.sentence: For example, if there are two extensions "foo" and "bar" and if the header field |Sec-WebSocket-Extensions| sent by the server has the value "foo, bar", then operations on the data will be made as bar(foo(data)), be those changes to the data itself (such as compression) or changes to the framing that may "stack".

a798dd1a968f.title: rfc>6455
a798dd1a968f.sentence: This specification provides opcodes 0x3 through 0x7 and 0xB through 0xF, the "Extension data" field, and the frame-rsv1, frame-rsv2, and frame-rsv3 bits of the frame header for use by extensions.

3cd3333fe565.title: WebSocket
3cd3333fe565.sentence: The permessage-deflate extension allows data messages to be compressed using the DEFLATE algorithm.

d359d3f58fac.title: WebSocket
d359d3f58fac.sentence: The RSV1 field of the first frame of a data message must be set to indicate the payload data is compressed.

c160d31f093c.title: rfc>6455
c160d31f093c.sentence: The masking key is a 32-bit value chosen at random by the client.

0ff134b95602.title: rfc>6455
0ff134b95602.sentence: Thus, the defense adopted is to mask all data from the client to the server, so that the remote script (attacker) does not have control over how the data being sent appears on the wire and thus cannot construct a message that could be misinterpreted by an intermediary as an HTTP request.

34c4b075ebf4.title: rfc>6455
34c4b075ebf4.sentence: To avoid confusing network intermediaries (such as intercepting proxies) and for security reasons that are further discussed in Section 10.3, a client MUST mask all frames that it sends to the server (see Section 5.3 for further details).

87dddba11102.title: rfc>6455
87dddba11102.sentence: (Note that masking is done whether or not the WebSocket Protocol is running over TLS.) The server MUST close the connection upon receiving a frame that is not masked.

42496c0b3f88.title: rfc>6455
42496c0b3f88.sentence: A server MUST NOT mask any frames that it sends to the client.

673a116bf391.title: rfc>6455
673a116bf391.sentence: Octet i of the transformed data ("transformed-octet-i") is the XOR of octet i of the original data ("original-octet-i") with octet at index i modulo 4 of the masking key ("masking-key-octet-j"):

f1fb7f34d204.title: rfc>6455
f1fb7f34d204.sentence: The same algorithm applies regardless of the direction of the translation, e.g., the same steps are applied to mask the data as to unmask the data.

fe15e4e246b3.title: WebSocket
fe15e4e246b3.sentence: Frame masking applies XOR between the payload and the masking key.

64b7506c216c.title: rfc>6455
64b7506c216c.sentence: When preparing a masked frame, the client MUST pick a fresh masking key from the set of allowed 32-bit values.

5e2a29adef83.title: rfc>6455
5e2a29adef83.sentence: The masking key needs to be unpredictable; thus, the masking key MUST be derived from a strong source of entropy, and the masking key for a given frame MUST NOT make it simple for a server/proxy to predict the masking key for a subsequent frame.

b40cacb781a9.title: rfc>6455
b40cacb781a9.sentence: The unpredictability of the masking key is essential to prevent authors of malicious applications from selecting the bytes that appear on the wire.

a76dc9cf3d34.title: rfc>6455
a76dc9cf3d34.sentence: As this protocol was being developed, an experiment was conducted to demonstrate a class of attacks on proxies that led to the poisoning of caching proxies deployed in the wild.

39fef8a0863e.title: rfc>6455
39fef8a0863e.sentence: The general form of the attack was to establish a connection to a server under the "attacker's" control, perform an UPGRADE on the HTTP connection similar to what the WebSocket Protocol does to establish a connection, and subsequently send data over that UPGRADEd connection that looked like a GET request for a specific known resource (which in an attack would likely be something like a widely deployed script for tracking hits or a resource on an ad-serving network).

2cbea97cbeb0.title: rfc>6455
2cbea97cbeb0.sentence: NOTE: A Ping frame may serve either as a keepalive or as a means to verify that the remote endpoint is still responsive.

8cd006709759.title: rfc>6455
8cd006709759.sentence: An endpoint MAY send a Ping frame any time after the connection is established and before the connection is closed.

038c993707a8.title: rfc>6455
038c993707a8.sentence: Upon receipt of a Ping frame, an endpoint MUST send a Pong frame in response, unless it already received a Close frame.

fac09e348809.title: rfc>6455
fac09e348809.sentence: It SHOULD respond with Pong frame as soon as is practical.

55f312a73952.title: rfc>6455
55f312a73952.sentence: A Pong frame sent in response to a Ping frame must have identical "Application data" as found in the message body of the Ping frame being replied to.

1f1e3c6a0572.title: rfc>6455
1f1e3c6a0572.sentence: A Pong frame MAY be sent unsolicited.

77d41c95777a.title: rfc>6455
77d41c95777a.sentence: This serves as a unidirectional heartbeat.

5e3cbf176c4a.title: rfc>6455
5e3cbf176c4a.sentence: A response to an unsolicited Pong frame is not expected.

0754cdab10de.title: rfc>6455
0754cdab10de.sentence: Typical options available in this version are the subprotocol selector (|Sec-WebSocket-Protocol|), list of extensions support by the client (|Sec-WebSocket-Extensions|), |Origin| header field, etc. The |Sec-WebSocket-Protocol| request-header field can be used to indicate what subprotocols (application-level protocols layered over the WebSocket Protocol) are acceptable to the client.

d8845ec635fd.title: rfc>6455
d8845ec635fd.section: 1. Introduction > 1.9. Subprotocols Using the WebSocket Protocol
d8845ec635fd.sentence: The client can request that the server use a specific subprotocol by including the |Sec-WebSocket-Protocol| field in its handshake.

b7f88855afef.title: rfc>6455
b7f88855afef.section: 4. Opening Handshake > 4.2. Server-Side Requirements > 4.2.1. Reading the Client's Opening Handshake
b7f88855afef.sentence: - Optionally, a |Sec-WebSocket-Protocol| header field, with a list of values indicating which protocols the client would like to speak, ordered by preference.

970187bd9e76.title: rfc>6455
970187bd9e76.section: 4. Opening Handshake > 4.2. Server-Side Requirements > 4.2.2. Sending the Server's Opening Handshake
970187bd9e76.sentence: The value chosen MUST be derived from the client's handshake, specifically by selecting one of the values from the |Sec-WebSocket-Protocol| field that the server is willing to use for this connection (if any).

a122080be7b7.title: rfc>6455
a122080be7b7.section: 1. Introduction > 1.9. Subprotocols Using the WebSocket Protocol
