6ec420f867d7.title: Comet (programming)
6ec420f867d7.sentence: Comet is a web application model in which a long-held HTTPS request allows a web server to push data to a browser, without the browser explicitly requesting it.

e22ec6a65b76.title: Comet (programming)
e22ec6a65b76.sentence: Comet is an umbrella term, encompassing multiple techniques for achieving this interaction.

0ee936fc307c.title: Comet (programming)
0ee936fc307c.sentence: All these methods rely on features included by default in browsers, such as JavaScript, rather than on non-default plugins.

93e49920480c.title: Comet (programming)
93e49920480c.sentence: Comet applications attempt to eliminate the limitations of the page-by-page web model and traditional polling by offering two-way sustained interaction, using a persistent or long-lasting HTTP connection between the server and the client.

756c16f74f3c.title: Comet (programming)
756c16f74f3c.sentence: Specific methods of implementing Comet fall into two major categories: streaming and long polling.

e0bd0fcada4b.title: Comet (programming)
e0bd0fcada4b.sentence: An application using streaming Comet opens a single persistent connection from the client browser to the server for all Comet events.

5c30b97db2e1.title: Comet (programming)
5c30b97db2e1.sentence: These events are incrementally handled and interpreted on the client side every time the server sends a new event, with neither side closing the connection.

f52ff0dbe22d.title: Comet (programming)
f52ff0dbe22d.sentence: This invisible iframe is sent as a chunked block, which implicitly declares it as infinitely long (sometimes called "forever frame").

25c020a00f83.title: Comet (programming)
25c020a00f83.sentence: As events occur, the iframe is gradually filled with script tags, containing JavaScript to be executed in the browser.

97aae9d7eba3.title: Comet (programming)
97aae9d7eba3.sentence: The XMLHttpRequest (XHR) object, a tool used by Ajax applications for browser–server communication, can also be pressed into service for server–browser Comet messaging by generating a custom data format for an XHR response, and parsing out each event using browser-side JavaScript; relying only on the browser firing the onreadystatechange callback each time it receives new data.

bffc4fb68c8f.title: Comet (programming)
bffc4fb68c8f.sentence: The browser makes an Ajax-style request to the server, which is kept open until the server has new data to send to the browser, which is sent to the browser in a complete response.

c3a2f071ef2f.title: Comet (programming)
c3a2f071ef2f.sentence: The browser initiates a new long polling request in order to obtain subsequent events.

872e47715225.title: Comet (programming)
872e47715225.sentence: None of the above streaming transports work across all modern browsers without negative side-effects.

1f031ed6d321.title: Comet (programming)
1f031ed6d321.sentence: Consequently, many Comet applications use long polling, which is easier to implement on the browser side, and works, at minimum, in every browser that supports XHR.

fd8d7c04653f.title: Comet (programming)
fd8d7c04653f.sentence: The biggest hurdle is the HTTP 1.1 specification, which states "this specification... encourages clients to be conservative when opening multiple connections".

99c70025acb2.title: Comet (programming)
99c70025acb2.sentence: Therefore, holding one connection open for real-time events has a negative impact on browser usability: the browser may be blocked from sending a new request while waiting for the results of a previous request, e.g., a series of images.

6656afc76755.title: Comet (programming)
6656afc76755.sentence: This can be worked around by creating a distinct hostname for real-time information, which is an alias for the same physical server.

d44a32c5985b.title: Comet (programming)
d44a32c5985b.sentence: This strategy is an application of domain sharding.

4a0697bb0aac.title: Comet (programming)
4a0697bb0aac.sentence: The standardisation around 2011 and widespread support since 2020 of WebSocket and Server-sent events has rendered the Comet model obsolete.

e54cd0b943ba.title: Comet (programming)
e54cd0b943ba.sentence: - The HTML 5 specification produced by the Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group (WHATWG) specifies so called server-sent events, which defines a new JavaScript interface EventSource and a new MIME type text/event-stream.

f8398a631590.title: Comet (programming)
f8398a631590.sentence: - The HTML 5 WebSocket API specifies a method for creating a persistent connection with a server and receiving messages via an onmessage callback.

17871b513740.title: C10k problem
17871b513740.sentence: The C10k problem was the problem of optimizing computer networking stacks to handle a large number of clients at the same time.

4bc61f220b72.title: C10k problem
4bc61f220b72.sentence: The name C10k is a numeronym for concurrently handling ten thousand connections.

dadbec3f4e56.title: C10k problem
dadbec3f4e56.sentence: Handling many concurrent connections is a different problem from handling many requests per second: the latter requires high throughput (processing them quickly), while the former does not have to be fast, but requires efficient scheduling of connections to network sockets or other stateful endpoints.

61f05d9b12bd.title: C10k problem
61f05d9b12bd.sentence: The problem of socket server optimisation has been studied because a number of factors must be considered to allow a web server to support many clients.

f98126a0fe26.title: C10k problem
f98126a0fe26.sentence: This can involve a combination of operating system constraints and web server software limitations.

1c3220ba1ee9.title: C10k problem
1c3220ba1ee9.sentence: According to the scope of services to be made available and the capabilities of the operating system as well as hardware considerations such as multi-processing capabilities, a multi-threading model or a single threading model can be preferred.

4b8a6dc05c4b.title: C10k problem
4b8a6dc05c4b.sentence: Concurrently with this aspect, which involves considerations regarding memory management (usually operating system related), strategies implied relate to the very diverse aspects of I/O management.

bf5593e602e9.title: C10k problem
bf5593e602e9.sentence: By the early 2010s millions of connections on a single commodity 1U rackmount server became possible.

17944d866183.title: C10k problem
17944d866183.sentence: Examples include WhatsApp serving over 2 million connections (with 24 cores using Erlang on FreeBSD), and MigratoryData serving 10–12 million connections (with 12 cores, using Java on Linux).

24d573e57ca8.title: C10k problem

3d07d38382a0.title: Nginx
3d07d38382a0.sentence: Originally, nginx was developed to solve the C10k problem, and to fill the needs of multiple websites including the Rambler search engine and portal, for which it was serving 500 million requests per day by September 2008.

caa052c800f5.title: C10k problem
caa052c800f5.sentence: Common applications of very high numbers of connections include general public servers that have to serve thousands or even millions of users at a time, such as file servers, FTP servers, proxy servers, web servers, and load balancers.

567ed40d8fb7.sentence: Fault tolerance is the ability of a system to contain the propagation of faults (e.g. failed transistor, shorted connector, intermittent data bus).

1e1283a70769.title: Fault tolerance
1e1283a70769.sentence: Faults may manifest as errors (e.g. bad data value, missing message) causing incorrect system state.

7545182525bc.title: Fault tolerance
7545182525bc.sentence: This capability is essential for high-availability, mission-critical, or even life-critical systems.

4181b29e3bf0.title: Fault tolerance
4181b29e3bf0.sentence: Fault tolerance specifically refers to a system's capability to handle faults without any degradation or downtime.

1572f13e70fe.title: Fault tolerance
1572f13e70fe.sentence: In the event of an error, end-users remain unaware of any issues.

b2484eca3244.title: Fault tolerance
b2484eca3244.sentence: Conversely, a system that experiences errors with some interruption in service or graceful degradation of performance is termed 'resilient'.

7bd89b7d53df.title: Fault tolerance

50b590d82a43.title: Fault tolerance

5a9616c0cdde.title: Fault tolerance
5a9616c0cdde.sentence: - Fault containment to prevent propagation of the failure – Some failure mechanisms can cause a system to fail by propagating the failure to the rest of the system.

98be097ef16a.title: Fault tolerance
98be097ef16a.sentence: - Availability of reversion modes, which is the abandonment of recent changes, usually to software, that bring a system back to reasonably proper behavior and function.

69cf202f3a4b.title: Fault tolerance

59eefdf546e7.title: Fault tolerance

c12ef9bd4d04.title: Fault tolerance

a9d4576eee57.title: Fault tolerance
a9d4576eee57.sentence: - Replication: Providing multiple identical instances of the same system or subsystem, directing tasks or requests to all of them in parallel, and choosing the correct result on the basis of a quorum;

ce23e4008c41.title: Fault tolerance

fed3f9784bab.sentence: In either case, traffic is routed to or through another (alternative) path.

cdcd5d4f1d21.title: Cascading failure
cdcd5d4f1d21.sentence: This alternative path, as a result, becomes overloaded, causing it to go down, and so on.

cbc0e1fe65f0.title: Cascading failure
cbc0e1fe65f0.sentence: The symptoms of a cascade failure include: packet loss and high network latency, not just to single systems, but to whole sections of a network or the internet.

36eb19a52a0e.title: Cascading failure
36eb19a52a0e.sentence: The high latency and packet loss is caused by the nodes that fail to operate due to congestion collapse, which causes them to still be present in the network but without much or any useful communication going through them.

80e1b148bf55.title: Cascading failure
80e1b148bf55.sentence: As a result, routes can still be considered valid, without them actually providing communication.

76b32ff2cf23.title: Cascading failure
76b32ff2cf23.sentence: A common occurrence during a cascade failure is a walking failure, where sections go down, causing the next section to fail, after which the first section comes back up.

b8caded5ba47.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b8caded5ba47.sentence: The most common cause of cascading failures is overload.

2b03b91acf10.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
2b03b91acf10.sentence: Suppose the frontend in cluster A is handling 1,000 requests per second (QPS), as in Figure 22-2.

abaa582f43c8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
abaa582f43c8.sentence: If cluster B fails (Figure 22-3), requests to cluster A increase to 1,200 QPS.

106ee09c64e4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
106ee09c64e4.sentence: The frontends in A are not able to handle requests at 1,200 QPS, and therefore start running out of resources, which causes them to crash, miss deadlines, or otherwise misbehave.

c11ff01bd46a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c11ff01bd46a.sentence: As a result, the rate of successfully handled requests in A dips well below 1,000 QPS.

d5ca98170b75.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d5ca98170b75.sentence: This reduction in the rate of useful work being done can spread into other failure domains, potentially spreading globally.

e8a0e90d9170.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e8a0e90d9170.sentence: For example, local overload in one cluster may lead to its servers crashing; in response, the load balancing controller sends requests to other clusters, overloading their servers, leading to a service-wide overload failure.

b70989634c21.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b70989634c21.sentence: It may not take long for these events to transpire (e.g., on the order of a couple minutes), because the load balancer and task scheduling systems involved may act very quickly.

e100af96a110.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e100af96a110.sentence: Once a couple of servers crash on overload, the load on the remaining servers can increase, causing them to crash as well.

d11452a0a26c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d11452a0a26c.sentence: The problem tends to snowball and soon all servers begin to crash-loop.

fb8414a4ae81.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
fb8414a4ae81.sentence: Itâs often difficult to escape this scenario because as soon as servers come back online theyâre bombarded with an extremely high rate of requests and fail almost immediately.

c4b6eb8db382.title: Cascading failure
c4b6eb8db382.sentence: Monitoring the operation of a system, in real-time, and judicious disconnection of parts can help stop a cascade.

1048166a0bac.title: Cascading failure
1048166a0bac.sentence: Another common technique is to calculate a safety margin for the system by computer simulation of possible failures, to establish safe operating levels below which none of the calculated scenarios is predicted to cause cascading failure, and to identify the parts of the network which are most likely to cause cascading failures.

61a9cee2c601.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
61a9cee2c601.sentence: RPC deadlines define how long a request can wait before the frontend gives up, limiting the time that the backend may consume the frontendâs resources.

84331aec0722.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
84331aec0722.sentence: Rather than inventing a deadline when sending RPCs to backends, servers should employ deadline propagation.

0c8f909f7a1e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0c8f909f7a1e.sentence: The tree of RPCs emanating from an initial request will all have the same absolute deadline.

14e185138e9e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
14e185138e9e.sentence: When a frontend sends an RPC to a backend server, the frontend consumes resources waiting for a reply.

1676b893c881.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1676b893c881.section: Latency and Deadlines > Picking a deadline
1676b893c881.sentence: Setting either no deadline or an extremely high deadline may cause short-term problems that have long since passed to continue to consume server resources until the server restarts.

4a9985fd6b3a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
4a9985fd6b3a.section: Latency and Deadlines > Picking a deadline
4a9985fd6b3a.sentence: Short deadlines can cause some more expensive requests to fail consistently.

d959303f041a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d959303f041a.sentence: - Having deadlines several orders of magnitude longer than the mean request latency is usually bad.

0474344f718f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0474344f718f.sentence: With a 100-second deadline, 5% of requests would consume 5,000 threads (50 QPS * 100 seconds), but the frontend doesnât have that many threads available.

785ec56ff60c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
785ec56ff60c.sentence: This means that the frontend has a total of 1,000 threads of capacity.

d27eac9e7e4c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d27eac9e7e4c.sentence: A common theme in many cascading outages is that servers spend resources handling requests that will exceed their deadlines on the client.

5baf2a1e217e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
5baf2a1e217e.sentence: As a result, resources are spent while no progress is made: you donât get credit for late assignments with RPCs.

19e7695c0a0d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
19e7695c0a0d.sentence: Under most circumstances, it would be unwise for the server to attempt to handle this request, because it would be doing work for which no credit will be grantedâthe client doesnât care what work the server does after the deadline has passed, because itâs given up on the request already.

829d5fd2d9c2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
829d5fd2d9c2.sentence: If handling a request is performed over multiple stages (e.g., there are a few callbacks and RPC calls), the server should check the deadline left at each stage before attempting to perform any more work on the request.

a7a11621eafd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
a7a11621eafd.sentence: With deadline propagation, a deadline is set high in the stack (e.g., in the frontend).

17a03a98b179.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
17a03a98b179.sentence: For example, if server A selects a 30-second deadline, and processes the request for 7 seconds before sending an RPC to server B, the RPC from A to B will have a 23-second deadline.

1ba026acf205.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1ba026acf205.sentence: If server B takes 4 seconds to handle the request and sends an RPC to server C, the RPC from B to C will have a 19-second deadline, and so on.

c34e43cf42af.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c34e43cf42af.sentence: - If server B uses deadline propagation, it should set a 2-second deadline, but suppose it instead uses a hardcoded 20-second deadline for the RPC to server C.

0301f547a9cd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0301f547a9cd.sentence: - Server C pulls the request off its queue after 5 seconds.

c36c88ab4e60.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c36c88ab4e60.sentence: However, in this scenario, server C processes the request thinking it has 15 seconds to spare, but is not doing useful work, since the request from server A to server B has already exceeded its deadline.

2d8495ba1b77.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
2d8495ba1b77.sentence: Had server B used deadline propagation, server C could immediately give up on the request because the 2-second deadline was exceeded.

c3fc8911f3c4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c3fc8911f3c4.sentence: You may want to reduce the outgoing deadline a bit (e.g., a few hundred milliseconds) to account for network transit times and post-processing in the client.

4ea4edcc9a29.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
4ea4edcc9a29.sentence: Also consider setting an upper bound for outgoing deadlines.

e1a3e12d83ad.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e1a3e12d83ad.sentence: You may want to limit how long the server waits for outgoing RPCs to noncritical backends, or for RPCs to backends that typically complete in a short duration.

1c4de6c37b27.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1c4de6c37b27.sentence: However, be sure to understand your traffic mix, because you might otherwise inadvertently make particular types of requests fail all the time (e.g., requests with large payloads, or requests that require responding to a lot of computation).

0566e254014d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0566e254014d.sentence: Propagating cancellations reduces unneeded or doomed work by advising servers in an RPC call stack that their efforts are no longer necessary.

dd22fe590000.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
dd22fe590000.sentence: To reduce latency, some systems use "hedged requests" [Dea13] to send RPCs to a primary server, then some time later, send the same request to other instances of the same service in case the primary is slow in responding; once the client has received a response from any server, it sends messages to the other servers to cancel the now-superfluous requests.

7ad88d4bafe8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
7ad88d4bafe8.sentence: Those requests may themselves transitively fan out to many other servers, so cancellations should be propagated throughout the entire stack.

18907b07b876.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
18907b07b876.sentence: Sending fatal errors or timeouts up the stack and cancelling other RPCs in the call tree prevents unneeded work if the request as a whole can't be fulfilled.

536e50bd9b36.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
536e50bd9b36.sentence: - This problem can be avoided if the requests that donât complete return with an error early, rather than waiting the full deadline.

e90243ad86a1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e90243ad86a1.sentence: For example, if a backend is unavailable, itâs usually best to immediately return an error for that backend, rather than consuming resources until the backend is available.

bdf1e48a9be8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
bdf1e48a9be8.sentence: If your RPC layer supports a fail-fast option, use it.

922efccb1816.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
922efccb1816.sentence: In particular, it may not be clear that bimodal latency is the cause of an outage when you are looking at mean latency.

724bdf2966bf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
724bdf2966bf.sentence: When you see a latency increase, try to look at the distribution of latencies in addition to the averages.

b3ba05baec6d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b3ba05baec6d.sentence: Running out of a resource can result in higher latency, elevated error rates, or the substitution of lower-quality results.

1552ca2966e7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1552ca2966e7.sentence: Depending on what resource becomes exhausted in a server and how the server is built, resource exhaustion can render the server less efficient or cause the server to crash, prompting the load balancer to distribute the resource problems to other servers.

def77b8ab516.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
def77b8ab516.sentence: When this happens, the rate of successfully handled requests can drop and possibly send the cluster or an entire service into a cascade failure.

738e6a7bac9b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
738e6a7bac9b.sentence: These are in fact desired effects of running out of resources: something eventually needs to give as the load increases beyond what a server can handle.

cfc367c7ea06.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
cfc367c7ea06.sentence: If there is insufficient CPU to handle the request load, typically all requests become slower.

022024cbf7cd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
022024cbf7cd.sentence: Because requests take longer to handle, more requests are handled concurrently (up to a possible maximum capacity at which queuing may occur).

84fcb263f830.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
84fcb263f830.sentence: This affects almost all resources, including memory, number of active threads (in a thread-per-request server model), number of file descriptors, and backend resources (which in turn can have other effects).

823212c9ac45.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
823212c9ac45.sentence: If there is insufficient capacity to handle all the requests at steady state, the server will saturate its queues.

4d28ca25fc7c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
4d28ca25fc7c.sentence: This means that latency increases (the requests are queued for longer amounts of time) and the queue uses more memory.

2bef15688bce.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
2bef15688bce.sentence: As a server becomes overloaded, its responses to RPCs from its clients arrive later, which may exceed any deadlines those clients set.

b20222add33d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b20222add33d.sentence: The work the server did to respond is then wasted, and clients may retry the RPCs, leading to even more overload.

5ac5d3676076.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
5ac5d3676076.sentence: When a thread canât make progress because itâs waiting for a lock, health checks may fail if the health check endpoint canât be served in time.

4fc19624efc3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
4fc19624efc3.sentence: Internal watchdogs108 in the server detect that the server isnât making progress, causing the servers to crash due to CPU starvation, or due to request starvation if watchdog events are triggered remotely and processed as part of the request queue.

4d5c914ab00f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
4d5c914ab00f.sentence: If nothing else, more in-flight requests consume more RAM from allocating the request, response, and RPC objects.

5bb5ca6352fe.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
5bb5ca6352fe.sentence: For example, a task might be evicted by the container manager (VM or otherwise) for exceeding available resource limits, or application-specific crashes may cause tasks to die.

f0896ab14d67.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f0896ab14d67.sentence: Increased rate of garbage collection (GC) in Java, resulting in increased CPU usage

b778a11dd7ff.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b778a11dd7ff.sentence: A vicious cycle can occur in this scenario: less CPU is available, resulting in slower requests, resulting in increased RAM usage, resulting in more GC, resulting in even lower availability of CPU.

5558f055dfa0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
5558f055dfa0.sentence: This is known colloquially as the âGC death spiral.â

458e47fdaf4d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
458e47fdaf4d.sentence: Reduction in available RAM can reduce application-level cache hit rates, resulting in more RPCs to the backends, which can possibly cause the backends to become overloaded.

869494a2a821.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
869494a2a821.sentence: Thread starvation can directly cause errors or lead to health check failures.

e2d2d4b4a1e4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e2d2d4b4a1e4.sentence: If the server adds threads as needed, thread overhead can use too much RAM.

ed8afa0606e5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
ed8afa0606e5.sentence: Running out of file descriptors can lead to the inability to initialize network connections, which in turn can cause health checks to fail.

a07d6a7d74b5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
a07d6a7d74b5.sentence: Note that many of these resource exhaustion scenarios feed from one anotherâa service experiencing overload often has a host of secondary symptoms that can look like the root cause, making debugging difficult.

6bfd8e4d501b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6bfd8e4d501b.sentence: - Under high (but expected) load, the frontend runs out of CPU due to GC.

b2ac0bb52958.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b2ac0bb52958.sentence: - Memory pressure due to requests, in combination with a fixed memory allocation for the frontend process as a whole, leaves less RAM available for caching.

998656cbf64c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
998656cbf64c.sentence: - The increase in cache misses means that more requests fall through to the backend for servicing.

d442adc8b1a5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d442adc8b1a5.sentence: - The backend, in turn, runs out of CPU or threads.

f36d327e7d95.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f36d327e7d95.sentence: - Finally, the lack of CPU causes basic health checks to fail, starting a cascading failure.

2a1ed9be9fec.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
2a1ed9be9fec.sentence: Load shedding drops some proportion of load by dropping traffic as the server approaches overload conditions.

b81d974e2169.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b81d974e2169.sentence: The goal is to keep the server from running out of RAM, failing health checks, serving with extremely high latency, or any of the other symptoms associated with overload, while still doing as much useful work as it can.

715ae721633f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
715ae721633f.sentence: One straightforward way to shed load is to do per-task throttling based on CPU, memory, or queue length; limiting queue length as discussed in Queue Management is a form of this strategy.

e0dc2db1d968.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e0dc2db1d968.sentence: For example, one effective approach is to return an HTTP 503 (service unavailable) to any incoming request when there are more than a given number of client requests in flight.

f782640f37a5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f782640f37a5.sentence: Once a service passes its breaking point, it is better to allow some user-visible errors or lower-quality results to slip through than try to fully serve every request.

2afaf11b82c9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
2afaf11b82c9.sentence: Servers should protect themselves from becoming overloaded and crashing.

c5ef634f037d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c5ef634f037d.sentence: When overloaded at either the frontend or backend layers, fail early and cheaply.

682d75200a8b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
682d75200a8b.sentence: Changing the queuing method from the standard first-in, first-out (FIFO) to last-in, first-out (LIFO) or using the controlled delay (CoDel) algorithm [Nic12] or similar approaches can reduce load by removing requests that are unlikely to be worth processing [Mau15].

f6f1479fe0aa.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f6f1479fe0aa.sentence: If a userâs web search is slow because an RPC has been queued for 10 seconds, thereâs a good chance the user has given up and refreshed their browser, issuing another request: thereâs no point in responding to the first one, since it will be ignored!

4b4e19d501cf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
4b4e19d501cf.sentence: This strategy works well when combined with propagating RPC deadlines throughout the stack, described in Latency and Deadlines.

1b115a9106dc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1b115a9106dc.sentence: More sophisticated approaches include identifying clients to be more selective about what work is dropped, or picking requests that are more important and prioritizing.

e6f16c908783.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e6f16c908783.sentence: Such strategies are more likely to be needed for shared services.

c201df1dcda7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c201df1dcda7.sentence: Depending on the nature and complexity of the service, this rate limiting can be indiscriminate (âdrop all traffic above X requests per secondâ) or more selective (âdrop requests that arenât from users who have recently interacted with the serviceâ or âdrop requests for low-priority operations like background synchronization, but keep serving interactive user sessionsâ).

312f1baceeab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
312f1baceeab.sentence: - Which metrics should you use to determine when load shedding or graceful degradation should kick in (e.g,.

213f3010c888.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
213f3010c888.sentence: CPU usage, latency, queue length, number of threads used, whether your service enters degraded mode automatically or if manual intervention is necessary)?

2d1487d43f7f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
2d1487d43f7f.sentence: - At what layer should load shedding and graceful degradation be implemented?

746f0dddaee8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
746f0dddaee8.sentence: Does it make sense to implement these strategies at every layer in the stack, or is it sufficient to have a high-level choke-point?

b24f28941060.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b24f28941060.sentence: - Remember that the code path you never use is the code path that (often) doesnât work.

f25280268b8a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f25280268b8a.sentence: You can make sure that graceful degradation stays working by regularly running a small subset of servers near overload in order to exercise this code path.

0c973f31d955.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0c973f31d955.sentence: - Monitor and alert when too many servers enter these modes.

00ead2dee117.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
00ead2dee117.sentence: - Complex load shedding and graceful degradation can cause problems themselvesâexcessive complexity may cause the server to trip into a degraded mode when it is not desired, or enter feedback cycles at undesired times.

dd1b2f2c46ed.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
dd1b2f2c46ed.sentence: Design a way to quickly turn off complex graceful degradation or tune parameters if needed.

e24ee547363d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
e24ee547363d.sentence: Client-side throttling addresses this problem.106 When a client detects that a significant portion of its recent requests have been rejected due to "out of quota" errors, it starts self-regulating and caps the amount of outgoing traffic it generates.

dc4f9099d967.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
dc4f9099d967.sentence: Requests above the cap fail locally without even reaching the network.

7058d7fd0c4f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
7058d7fd0c4f.sentence: For example, it's almost equally expensive to reject a request that requires a simple RAM lookup (where the overhead of the request/response protocol handling is significantly larger than the overhead of producing the response) as it is to accept and run that request.

7dd561dd83b8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
7dd561dd83b8.sentence: And even in the case where rejecting requests saves significant resources, those requests still consume some resources.

c09f284d2d34.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
c09f284d2d34.sentence: If the amount of rejected requests is significant, these numbers add up quickly.

69a5a048f57c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
69a5a048f57c.sentence: In such cases, the backend can become overloaded even though the vast majority of its CPU is spent just rejecting requests!

d994de9bb8a3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
d994de9bb8a3.sentence: We implemented client-side throttling through a technique we call adaptive throttling.

c41f7b8a36f2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
c41f7b8a36f2.sentence: Specifically, each client task keeps the following information for the last two minutes of its history:

5f9b3100f2f4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload

ec097e6440f6.title: Bandwidth throttling
ec097e6440f6.sentence: Bandwidth throttling is the limitation of the rate of data transfer to or from a network node or network device such as a computer or mobile phone.

244ab831e486.title: Bandwidth throttling
244ab831e486.sentence: A bandwidth intensive device, such as a server, might limit (throttle) the speed at which it receives or sends data, in order to avoid overloading its processing capacity or to saturate network bandwidth.

3734596a4b29.title: Bandwidth throttling
3734596a4b29.sentence: Bandwidth throttling works by limiting (throttling) the speed at which a bandwidth intensive device (a server) receives data or the speed (i.e. bytes or kilobytes per second) of each data response.

29e7c68875ac.title: Bandwidth throttling
29e7c68875ac.sentence: If these limits are not in place, the device can overload its processing capacity.

46ee3e3fd62d.title: Bandwidth throttling
46ee3e3fd62d.sentence: The traffic on such a network will vary over time, and there will be periods when client requests will peak or sent responses will be huge, sometimes exceeding the capacity of parts of network and causing congestion, especially in parts of the network that form bottlenecks.

39e321c7a76a.title: Bandwidth throttling
39e321c7a76a.sentence: This can cause data request failures, or in worst cases, server crashes.

0a5a76a91bd3.title: Bandwidth throttling
0a5a76a91bd3.sentence: - at application software level (a client program or a server program, i.e. ftp server, web server, etc.) which can be run and configured to throttle data sent through network or even to throttle data received from network (by reading data at most at a throttled amount per second);

c34487d4f487.title: Bandwidth throttling
c34487d4f487.sentence: - at network management level (typically done by an ISP).

8c7763068339.title: Bandwidth throttling
8c7763068339.sentence: Limiting the speed of data sent by a data originator (a client computer or a server computer) is much more efficient than limiting the speed in an intermediate network device between client and server because while in the first case usually no network packets are lost, in the second case network packets can be lost / discarded whenever ingoing data speed overcomes the bandwidth limit or the capacity of device and data packets cannot be temporarily stored in a buffer queue (because it is full or it does not exist); the usage of such a buffer queue is to absorb the peaks of incoming data for very short time lapse.

01202ed751af.title: Bandwidth throttling
01202ed751af.sentence: The difference is that bandwidth throttling regulates a bandwidth intensive device (such as a server) by limiting how much data that device can receive from each node / client or can output or can send for each response.

27ba59ae1b96.title: Bandwidth throttling
27ba59ae1b96.sentence: Bandwidth capping on the other hand limits the total transfer capacity, upstream or downstream, of data over a medium.

d7e769e85d7d.title: Bandwidth throttling
d7e769e85d7d.sentence: NOTE: Bandwidth throttling should not be confused with rate limiting which operates on client requests at application server level and/or at network management level (i.e. by inspecting protocol data packets).

b9844f28aeb8.title: Bandwidth throttling
b9844f28aeb8.sentence: Bandwidth throttling should be done along with rate limiting pattern to minimize the number of throttling errors.

c25b06442ecc.title: Token bucket
c25b06442ecc.sentence: The token bucket is an algorithm used in packet-switched and telecommunications networks.

617c382f4a2f.title: Token bucket
617c382f4a2f.sentence: It can be used to check that data transmissions, in the form of packets, conform to defined limits on bandwidth and burstiness (a measure of the unevenness or variations in the traffic flow).

87ae14c8a45d.title: Token bucket
87ae14c8a45d.sentence: The token bucket algorithm is based on an analogy of a fixed-capacity bucket into which tokens, normally representing a unit of bytes or a single packet of predetermined size, are added at a fixed rate.

54ad7c50d68e.title: Token bucket
54ad7c50d68e.sentence: - A token is added to the bucket every 1/r seconds.

c071070dcab4.title: Token bucket
c071070dcab4.sentence: - The bucket can hold at the most b tokens.

f954afcd9dd3.title: Token bucket
f954afcd9dd3.sentence: If a token arrives when the bucket is full, it is discarded.

402244d05710.title: Token bucket
402244d05710.sentence: - if at least n tokens are in the bucket, n tokens are removed from the bucket, and the packet is sent to the network.

b4773adfdcf8.title: Token bucket
b4773adfdcf8.sentence: - if fewer than n tokens are available, no tokens are removed from the bucket, and the packet is considered to be non-conformant.

a06bce909f84.title: Token bucket
a06bce909f84.sentence: The packet does not conform if there are insufficient tokens in the bucket, and the contents of the bucket are not changed.

b7cfefc75dd1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
b7cfefc75dd1.sentence: When a request comes in, a token from the bucket must be taken and processed.

b0a869bbd781.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
b0a869bbd781.sentence: The request will be refused if no token is available in the bucket, and the requester will have to try again later.

486753a2a197.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
486753a2a197.sentence: As a result, the token bucket gets refreshed after a certain time period.

40c96779dd52.title: Token bucket
40c96779dd52.sentence: - They may be enqueued for subsequent transmission when sufficient tokens have accumulated in the bucket.

c0dad505e37f.title: Token bucket
c0dad505e37f.sentence: - They may be transmitted, but marked as being non-conformant, possibly to be dropped subsequently if the network is overloaded.

819f10e15256.title: Token bucket
819f10e15256.sentence: A conforming flow can thus contain traffic with an average rate up to the rate at which tokens are added to the bucket, and have a burstiness determined by the depth of the bucket.

d5c9ff4c2519.title: Token bucket
d5c9ff4c2519.sentence: Over the long run the output of conformant packets is limited by the token rate, r.

22d79bd8acd4.title: Token bucket
22d79bd8acd4.sentence: The token bucket can be used in either traffic shaping or traffic policing.

cb7d4e28a35c.title: Token bucket
cb7d4e28a35c.sentence: In traffic policing, nonconforming packets may be discarded (dropped) or may be reduced in priority (for downstream traffic management functions to drop if there is congestion).

d9e2f178b93e.title: Token bucket
d9e2f178b93e.sentence: In traffic shaping, packets are delayed until they conform.

65b316e83ffd.title: Token bucket
65b316e83ffd.sentence: The token bucket algorithm is also used in controlling database IO flow.

8427da8f12cc.title: Token bucket
8427da8f12cc.sentence: In it, limitation applies to neither IOPS nor the bandwidth but rather to a linear combination of both.

4f556d4ea4d9.title: Leaky bucket
4f556d4ea4d9.sentence: The leaky bucket is an algorithm based on an analogy of how a bucket with a constant leak will overflow if either the average rate at which water is poured in exceeds the rate at which the bucket leaks or if more water than the capacity of the bucket is poured in all at once.

372024c35d39.title: Leaky bucket
372024c35d39.sentence: It can be used to determine whether some sequence of discrete events conforms to defined limits on their average and peak rates or frequencies, e.g. to limit the actions associated with these events to these rates or delay them until they do conform to the rates.

b4d9801bdec5.title: Leaky bucket
b4d9801bdec5.sentence: This counter is used only to check that the traffic or events conform to the limits: The counter is incremented as each packet arrives at the point where the check is being made or an event occurs, which is equivalent to the way water is added intermittently to the bucket.

0e1248aa3499.title: Leaky bucket
0e1248aa3499.sentence: The counter is also decremented at a fixed rate, equivalent to the way the water leaks out of the bucket.

c786349f74bd.title: Leaky bucket
c786349f74bd.sentence: If the counter remains below a specified limit value when a packet arrives or an event occurs, i.e., the bucket does not overflow, that indicates its conformance to the bandwidth and burstiness limits or the average and peak rate event limits.

a092bfd811c8.title: Leaky bucket
a092bfd811c8.sentence: Jonathan S. Turner is credited with the original description of the leaky bucket algorithm and describes it as follows: "A counter associated with each user transmitting on a connection is incremented whenever the user sends a packet and is decremented periodically.

a49379cdb9b6.title: Leaky bucket
a49379cdb9b6.sentence: If the counter exceeds a threshold upon being incremented, the network discards the packet.

82a33619a822.title: Leaky bucket
82a33619a822.sentence: The user specifies the rate at which the counter is decremented (this determines the average bandwidth) and the value of the threshold (a measure of burstiness)".

0b9bc40fce08.title: Leaky bucket
0b9bc40fce08.sentence: The leaky bucket as a queue is essentially a way of describing a simple FIFO buffer or queue that is serviced at a fixed rate to remove burstiness or jitter.

4a1fbb46b7d2.title: Leaky bucket
4a1fbb46b7d2.sentence: When a packet arrives, if there is room in the queue, it is appended to the queue; otherwise, it is discarded.

f1f5b3af4913.title: Leaky bucket
f1f5b3af4913.sentence: At every clock tick, one packet is transmitted (unless the queue is empty)".

bd27ca4403a9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
bd27ca4403a9.sentence: Leaky Bucket is an algorithm that provides a simple, intuitive approach to rate limiting via a queue.

8ac3c9c04888.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
8ac3c9c04888.sentence: When registering a request, the system appends it to the end of the queue.

3fef6007b07b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
3fef6007b07b.sentence: Processing for the first item on the queue occurs at a regular interval or first-in, first-out (FIFO).

c5485ec99a6f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
c5485ec99a6f.sentence: If the queue is full, then additional requests are discarded (or leaked).

05d42fce43c5.title: Leaky bucket
05d42fce43c5.sentence: An implementation of the leaky bucket as a queue is therefore always a form of traffic shaping function.

ac326e105c18.title: Leaky bucket
ac326e105c18.sentence: As can be seen, this implementation is restricted in that the packets are only ever transmitted at a fixed rate.

5f89cba1b1d6.title: Leaky bucket
5f89cba1b1d6.sentence: To underline this, Tanenbaum also states that "The leaky bucket algorithm enforces a rigid output pattern at the average rate, no matter how bursty the [input] traffic is." However, this assertion is only strictly true as long as the queue does not become empty: if the average arrival rate is less than the rate of clock ticks, or if the input is sufficiently bursty that the losses bring the rate of the remainder below the clock tick rate (i.e. gaps in the input stream are long enough and the queue is small enough that it can become empty), there will be gaps in the output stream.

78e2d3b817fa.title: Leaky bucket
78e2d3b817fa.sentence: Analysis of the two versions of the leaky bucket algorithm shows that the version as a queue is a special case of the version as a meter.

edcca9bad66d.title: Leaky bucket
edcca9bad66d.sentence: It is used in packet-switched computer networks and telecommunications networks in both the traffic policing, traffic shaping and scheduling of data transmissions, in the form of packets, to defined limits on bandwidth and burstiness (a measure of the variations in the traffic flow).

8b99bfe605b4.sentence: Note that because rate limiting often doesnât take overall service health into account, it may not be able to stop a failure that has already begun.

f218befa04a8.sentence: Simple rate-limiting implementations are also likely to leave capacity unused.

36941f91da58.sentence: Graceful degradation takes the concept of load shedding one step further by reducing the amount of work that needs to be performed.

a1ed5c008098.title: Fault tolerance
a1ed5c008098.sentence: Likewise, a fail-fast component is designed to report at the first point of failure, rather than generating reports when downstream components fail.

d51aaa553ee4.title: Fault tolerance
d51aaa553ee4.sentence: A system that is designed to fail safe, or fail-secure, or fail gracefully, whether it functions at a reduced level or fails completely, does so in a way that protects people, property, or data from injury, damage, intrusion, or disclosure.

34d9b836f7d5.title: Fault tolerance
34d9b836f7d5.sentence: This allows easier diagnosis of the underlying problem, and may prevent improper operation in a broken state.

6b45723d955b.title: Fault tolerance
6b45723d955b.sentence: In computers, a program might fail-safe by executing a graceful exit (as opposed to an uncontrolled crash) to prevent data corruption after an error occurs.

fffb61961c1f.title: Fault tolerance
fffb61961c1f.sentence: A system designed to experience graceful degradation, or to fail soft (used in computing, similar to "fail safe") operates at a reduced level of performance after some component fails.

a38312e396c9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/a-cheat-sheet-for-designing-fault-tolerant-systems.md
a38312e396c9.sentence: Graceful degradation ensures that a system continues to operate at reduced functionality rather than completely failing when some components fail.

d93e196c51b0.title: Fault tolerance
d93e196c51b0.sentence: For example, if grid power fails, a building may operate lighting at reduced levels or elevators at reduced speeds.

3415b429a767.title: Fault tolerance
3415b429a767.sentence: In computing, if insufficient network bandwidth is available to stream an online video, a lower-resolution version might be streamed in place of the high-resolution version.

4e292a919b0d.title: Fault tolerance
4e292a919b0d.sentence: Progressive enhancement is another example, where web pages are available in a basic functional format for older, small-screen, or limited-capability web browsers, but in an enhanced version for browsers capable of handling additional technologies or that have a larger display.

754f3b68e558.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
754f3b68e558.section: Immediate Steps to Address Cascading Failures
754f3b68e558.sentence: Once you have identified that your service is experiencing a cascading failure, you can use a few different strategies to remedy the situationâand of course, a cascading failure is a good opportunity to use your incident management protocol (Managing Incidents).

786a3133398f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
786a3133398f.sentence: If your system is running at degraded capacity and you have idle resources, adding tasks can be the most expedient way to recover from the outage.

3d5a4f5ab474.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
3d5a4f5ab474.sentence: Dropping load is a big hammer, usually reserved for situations in which you have a true cascading failure on your hands and you cannot fix it by other means.

978b85eaed7f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
978b85eaed7f.sentence: However, if the service has entered a death spiral of some sort, adding more resources may not be sufficient to recover.

0d66a3a8f943.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0d66a3a8f943.sentence: This practice may create a failure mode in which health-checking itself makes the service unhealthy.

855e472d74c6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
855e472d74c6.sentence: For example, if half the tasks arenât able to accomplish any work because theyâre starting up and the other half will soon be killed because theyâre overloaded and failing health checks, temporarily disabling health checks may permit the system to stabilize until all the tasks are running.

be2e6b774e99.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
be2e6b774e99.sentence: Process health checking (âis this binary responding at all?â) and service health checking (âis this binary able to respond to this class of requests right now?â) are two conceptually distinct operations.

27348bffd852.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
27348bffd852.sentence: Process health checking is relevant to the cluster scheduler, whereas service health checking is relevant to the load balancer.

ab3d8abe92f4.sentence: If servers are somehow wedged and not making progress, restarting them may help.

eb8266ae9c5f.sentence: - Java servers are in a GC death spiral

fcd6846e05d8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
fcd6846e05d8.sentence: Make sure that you identify the source of the cascading failure before you restart your servers.

f84d1615da77.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f84d1615da77.sentence: Canary this change, and make it slowly.

ca47401f2e33.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
ca47401f2e33.sentence: Your actions may amplify an existing cascading failure if the outage is actually due to an issue like a cold cache.

d4b72494f10d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d4b72494f10d.sentence: For example, if a service was healthy at 10,000 QPS, but started a cascading failure due to crashes at 11,000 QPS, dropping the load to 9,000 QPS will almost certainly not stop the crashes.

6c6872fb5377.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6c6872fb5377.sentence: This is because the service will be handling increased demand with reduced capacity; only a small fraction of servers will usually be healthy enough to handle requests.

7290dc5ca6c4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
7290dc5ca6c4.sentence: In this example, if 10% of the servers are healthy enough to handle requests, the request rate would need to drop to about 1,000 QPS in order for the system to stabilize and recover.

e38f6792216c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e38f6792216c.sentence: Consider being aggressive hereâif the entire service is crash-looping, only allow, say, 1% of the traffic through.

4a2e42440ddd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures

8537626801b0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
8537626801b0.sentence: If the issue that started the cascading failure is not fixed (e.g., insufficient global capacity), then the cascading failure may trigger shortly after all traffic returns.

90d1b3473162.sentence: Therefore, before using this strategy, consider fixing (or at least papering over) the root cause or triggering condition.
