f8db57c22f3c.sentence: For example, if index updates, data copies, or statistics gathering consume resources of the serving path, consider turning off those sources of load during an outage.

1badd300479f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1badd300479f.sentence: If some queries are creating heavy load or crashes (e.g., queries of death), consider blocking them or eliminating them via other means.

4057fa618028.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
4057fa618028.sentence: There are various algorithms for API rate limiting, each with its advantages and disadvantages.

d8e6595101d3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
d8e6595101d3.sentence: Here we use a concept of a bucket.

2040e6926fe2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
2040e6926fe2.sentence: The system uses a window size of n seconds to track the fixed window algorithm rate.

97b1935afdf9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
97b1935afdf9.sentence: Each incoming request increments the counter for the window.

807806f30710.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
807806f30710.sentence: It discards the request if the counter exceeds a threshold.

b1ea37422cf2.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
b1ea37422cf2.sentence: Sliding Log rate-limiting involves tracking a time-stamped log for each request.

949b13e971fd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
949b13e971fd.sentence: The system stores these logs in a time-sorted hash set or table.

934d97c0a78c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
934d97c0a78c.sentence: It also discards logs with timestamps beyond a threshold.

c1037e4ddaa6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
c1037e4ddaa6.sentence: When a new request comes in, we calculate the sum of logs to determine the request rate.

19b9cf070c3b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
19b9cf070c3b.sentence: If the request would exceed the threshold rate, then it is held.

9eef85dea081.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
9eef85dea081.sentence: Sliding Window is a hybrid approach that combines the fixed window algorithm's low processing cost and the sliding log's improved boundary conditions.

b9ba13223a3a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
b9ba13223a3a.sentence: Like the fixed window algorithm, we track a counter for each fixed window.

51d115d8bc3a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
51d115d8bc3a.sentence: Next, we account for a weighted value of the previous window's request rate based on the current timestamp to smooth out bursts of traffic.

1affd6819982.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
1affd6819982.sentence: Rate Limiting becomes complicated when distributed systems are involved.

7b2faf37948e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
7b2faf37948e.sentence: The two broad problems that come with rate limiting in distributed systems are:

823d86354d6a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
823d86354d6a.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Inconsistencies
823d86354d6a.sentence: When using a cluster of multiple nodes, we might need to enforce a global rate limit policy.

002b57fa6efe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
002b57fa6efe.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Inconsistencies
002b57fa6efe.sentence: Because if each node were to track its rate limit, a consumer could exceed a global rate limit when sending requests to different nodes.

af3dff4eb141.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
af3dff4eb141.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Inconsistencies
af3dff4eb141.sentence: The greater the number of nodes, the more likely the user will exceed the global limit.

840935711425.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
840935711425.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Inconsistencies
840935711425.sentence: The simplest way to solve this problem is to use sticky sessions in our load balancers so that each consumer gets sent to exactly one node but this causes a lack of fault tolerance and scaling problems.

b80a0fbb195d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
b80a0fbb195d.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Inconsistencies
b80a0fbb195d.sentence: Another approach might be to use a centralized data store like Redis but this will increase latency and cause race conditions.

56aedae369dd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
56aedae369dd.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Race Conditions
56aedae369dd.sentence: This issue happens when we use a naive "get-then-set" approach, in which we retrieve the current rate limit counter, increment it, and then push it back to the datastore.

3a0db933990e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
3a0db933990e.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Race Conditions
3a0db933990e.sentence: This model's problem is that additional requests can come through in the time it takes to perform a full cycle of read-increment-store, each attempting to store the increment counter with an invalid (lower) counter value.

30dc80d9b15c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
30dc80d9b15c.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Race Conditions
30dc80d9b15c.sentence: This allows a consumer to send a very large number of requests to bypass the rate limiting controls.

cb915234b372.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
cb915234b372.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Race Conditions
cb915234b372.sentence: One way to avoid this problem is to use some sort of distributed locking mechanism around the key, preventing any other processes from accessing or writing to the counter.

2cb6bd41fcd8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
2cb6bd41fcd8.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Race Conditions
2cb6bd41fcd8.sentence: Though the lock will become a significant bottleneck and will not scale well.

4e43edcbe249.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::rate-limiting
4e43edcbe249.section: Rate Limiting in Distributed Systems > Race Conditions
4e43edcbe249.sentence: A better approach might be to use a "set-then-get" approach, allowing us to quickly increment and check counter values without letting the atomic operations get in the way.

9e8b650f0904.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
9e8b650f0904.sentence: We learned this lesson the hard way: modeling capacity as "queries per second" or using static features of the requests that are believed to be a proxy for the resources they consume (e.g., "how many keys are the requests reading") often makes for a poor metric.

2783133c16b9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
2783133c16b9.sentence: A better solution is to measure capacity directly in available resources.

0cf275cd7912.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
0cf275cd7912.sentence: Different queries can have vastly different resource requirements.

ceba1393713d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
ceba1393713d.sentence: A query's cost can vary based on arbitrary factors such as the code in the client that issues them (for services that have many different clients) or even the time of the day (e.g., home users versus work users; or interactive end-user traffic versus batch traffic).

d1dd04d04a2f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
d1dd04d04a2f.sentence: Even if these metrics perform adequately at one point in time, the ratios can change.

25998b1c3388.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
25998b1c3388.sentence: Sometimes the change is gradual, but sometimes the change is drastic (e.g., a new version of the software suddenly made some features of some requests require significantly fewer resources).

8f565f1800de.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
8f565f1800de.sentence: A moving target makes a poor metric for designing and implementing load balancing.

b0647d75c76a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
b0647d75c76a.sentence: For example, you may have a total of 500 CPU cores and 1 TB of memory reserved for a given service in a given datacenter.

bd854ee00287.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
bd854ee00287.sentence: Naturally, it works much better to use those numbers directly to model a datacenter's capacity.

696bfacc50fa.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
696bfacc50fa.sentence: We often speak about the cost of a request to refer to a normalized measure of how much CPU time it has consumed (over different CPU architectures, with consideration of performance differences).

18d3bfd3fa99.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
18d3bfd3fa99.sentence: In a majority of cases (although certainly not in all), we've found that simply using CPU consumption as the signal for provisioning works well, for the following reasons:

0b52571100c2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
0b52571100c2.sentence: - In platforms with garbage collection, memory pressure naturally translates into increased CPU consumption.

cb3ad0c504c7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
cb3ad0c504c7.sentence: In cases where over-provisioning the non-CPU resources is prohibitively expensive, we take each system resource into account separately when considering resource consumption.

0e09f037849b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
0e09f037849b.sentence: When global overload does occur, it's vital that the service only delivers error responses to misbehaving customers, while other customers remain unaffected.

a73dd0e8930a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
a73dd0e8930a.sentence: To achieve this outcome, service owners provision their capacity based on the negotiated usage with their customers and define per-customer quotas according to these agreements.

f786cd2c17aa.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
f786cd2c17aa.sentence: Here in reality, global overload occurs quite frequently (especially for internal services that tend to have many clients run by many teams).

88e8712aa126.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
88e8712aa126.sentence: For example, if a backend service has 10,000 CPUs allocated worldwide (over various datacenters), their per-customer limits might look something like the following:

b0ae0026a1d4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
b0ae0026a1d4.sentence: - Gmail is allowed to consume up to 4,000 CPU seconds per second.

75ef946cdc96.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
75ef946cdc96.sentence: Note that these numbers may add up to more than the 10,000 CPUs allocated to the backend service.

2bcee1df658f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
2bcee1df658f.sentence: The service owner is relying on the fact that it's unlikely for all of their customers to hit their resource limits simultaneously.

f6a96e127e0b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
f6a96e127e0b.sentence: We aggregate global usage information in real time from all backend tasks, and use that data to push effective limits to individual backend tasks.

398a2881e201.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
398a2881e201.sentence: An interesting part of the puzzle is computing in real time the amount of resourcesâspecifically CPUâconsumed by each individual request.

e1032b0f1f54.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
e1032b0f1f54.sentence: This computation is particularly tricky for servers that don't implement a thread-per-request model, where a pool of threads just executes different parts of all requests as they come in, using nonblocking APIs.

eb19198b0ede.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
eb19198b0ede.sentence: Criticality is another notion that we've found very useful in the context of global quotas and throttling.

4d748a49edba.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
4d748a49edba.sentence: A request made to a backend is associated with one of four possible criticality values, depending on how critical we consider that request:

9bcabe939dc0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
9bcabe939dc0.sentence: - When a task is itself overloaded, it will reject requests of lower criticalities sooner.

5ee363b101f1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
5ee363b101f1.sentence: Reserved for the most critical requests, those that will result in serious user-visible impact if they fail.

b1deb5c14d44.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
b1deb5c14d44.sentence: The default value for requests sent from production jobs.

a81f7d1c6428.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
a81f7d1c6428.sentence: Traffic for which partial unavailability is expected.

a3bf25761b51.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
a3bf25761b51.sentence: This is the default for batch jobs, which can retry requests minutes or even hours later.

eedae31d12bd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
eedae31d12bd.sentence: Traffic for which frequent partial unavailability and occasional full unavailability is expected.

1ad3254d6970.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
1ad3254d6970.sentence: - When a customer runs out of global quota, a backend task will only reject requests of a given criticality if it's already rejecting all requests of all lower criticalities (in fact, the per-customer limits that our system supports, described earlier, can be set per criticality).

13794e36ff08.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
13794e36ff08.sentence: As utilization approaches configured thresholds, we start rejecting requests based on their criticality (higher thresholds for higher criticalities).

0b03ab1b95a8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
0b03ab1b95a8.sentence: - The adaptive throttling system also keeps separate stats for each criticality.

0906c4d1d35e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
0906c4d1d35e.sentence: The criticality of a request is orthogonal to its latency requirements and thus to the underlying network quality of service (QoS) used.

b613a76c237e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
b613a76c237e.sentence: For example, when a system displays search results or suggestions while the user is typing a search query, the underlying requests are highly sheddable (if the system is overloaded, it's acceptable to not display these results), but tend to have stringent latency requirements.

99eddd23ef9b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
99eddd23ef9b.sentence: We've also significantly extended our RPC system to propagate criticality automatically.

246d5a5a6496.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
246d5a5a6496.sentence: If a backend receives request A and, as part of executing that request, issues outgoing request B and request C to other backends, request B and request C will use the same criticality as request A by default.

8c27a3d6c55c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
8c27a3d6c55c.sentence: Our practice is thus to set the criticality as close as possible to the browsers or mobile clientsâtypically in the HTTP frontends that produce the HTML to be returnedâand only override the criticality in specific cases where it makes sense at specific points in the stack.

e3ab42a75edb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
e3ab42a75edb.sentence: By standardizing and propagating criticality as a part of our RPC system, we are now able to consistently set the criticality at specific points.

813665e62565.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
813665e62565.sentence: When a service is susceptible to cascading failures, there are several possible disturbances that can initiate the domino effect.

0f1db07da3e0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0f1db07da3e0.sentence: This section identifies some of the factors that trigger cascading failures.

491ff48e1750.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
491ff48e1750.sentence: Some server tasks may die, reducing the amount of available capacity.

ae7d4fc19f17.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
ae7d4fc19f17.sentence: Tasks might die because of a Query of Death (an RPC whose contents trigger a failure in the process), cluster issues, assertion failures, or a number of other reasons.

5614ecd5462f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
5614ecd5462f.sentence: Pushing a new version of the binary or updating its configuration may initiate a cascading failure if a large number of tasks are affected simultaneously.

48e798b8983f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
48e798b8983f.sentence: To prevent this scenario, either account for necessary capacity overhead when setting up the serviceâs update infrastructure, or push off-peak.

e3deb4eac1de.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e3deb4eac1de.sentence: A new binary, configuration changes, or a change to the underlying infrastructure stack can result in changes to request profiles, resource usage and limits, backends, or a number of other system components that can trigger a cascading failure.

914dc9bc5fb5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
914dc9bc5fb5.sentence: During a cascading failure, itâs usually wise to check for recent changes and consider reverting them, particularly if those changes affected capacity or altered the request profile.

fe335b11421d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
fe335b11421d.sentence: In many cases, a cascading failure isnât triggered by a specific service change, but because a growth in usage wasnât accompanied by an adjustment to capacity.

cfefdf9db9c5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
cfefdf9db9c5.sentence: If your service is multihomed, some of your capacity may be unavailable because of maintenance or outages in a cluster.

37c92e1b2f1d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
37c92e1b2f1d.sentence: Similarly, one of the serviceâs critical dependencies may be drained, resulting in a reduction in capacity for the upstream service due to drain dependencies, or an increase in latency due to having to send the requests to a more distant cluster.

3ce9b064eb59.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
3ce9b064eb59.section: Planned Changes, Drains, or Turndowns > Request profile changes
3ce9b064eb59.sentence: A backend service may receive requests from different clusters because a frontend service shifted its traffic due to load balancing configuration changes, changes in the traffic mix, or cluster fullness.

d0cff7fb991e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d0cff7fb991e.section: Planned Changes, Drains, or Turndowns > Request profile changes
d0cff7fb991e.sentence: Also, the average cost to handle an individual payload may have changed due to frontend code or configuration changes.

97c2901a2dcc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
97c2901a2dcc.sentence: Processes are often slower at responding to requests immediately after starting than they will be in steady state.

48e6fa527c38.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
48e6fa527c38.sentence: If the service is not provisioned to handle requests under a cold cache, itâs at greater risk of outages and should take steps to avoid them.

db30786aa010.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
db30786aa010.sentence: Setting up connections upon receiving the first request that needs a given backend

bbb4263c745d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
bbb4263c745d.sentence: Just-In-Time compilation, hotspot optimization, and deferred class loading

c67cf09f68bc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c67cf09f68bc.sentence: For example, in the case of some of Googleâs services, most requests are served out of caches, so requests that miss the cache are significantly more expensive.

c663705308e8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c663705308e8.sentence: In steady-state operation with a warm cache, only a few cache misses occur, but when the cache is completely empty, 100% of requests are costly.

e093fc451f03.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e093fc451f03.sentence: Itâs important to note the distinction between a latency cache versus a capacity cache: when a latency cache is employed, the service can sustain its expected load with an empty cache, but a service using a capacity cache cannot sustain its expected load under an empty cache.

ef9036af9f94.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
ef9036af9f94.sentence: Sometimes caches are added to a service to improve performance, but actually wind up being hard dependencies.

1fe32fdb9def.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1fe32fdb9def.sentence: The following scenarios can lead to a cold cache:

b90c0419540c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b90c0419540c.sentence: A recently added cluster will have an empty cache.

89b8cdc714cc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
89b8cdc714cc.sentence: If a task with a cache has recently restarted, filling its cache will take some time.

3449ceb09b69.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
3449ceb09b69.sentence: In particular, servers should reject requests when theyâre overloaded or enter degraded modes, and testing should be performed to see how the service behaves after events such as a large restart.

6207a6e8526a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6207a6e8526a.sentence: - When adding load to a cluster, slowly increase the load.

cf7cc539d098.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
cf7cc539d098.sentence: The initially small request rate warms up the cache; once the cache is warm, more traffic can be added.

c6eb1128b3ec.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c6eb1128b3ec.sentence: Itâs a good idea to ensure that all clusters carry nominal load and that the caches are kept warm.

6108851552c8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6108851552c8.sentence: Understanding the behavior of the service under heavy load is perhaps the most important first step in avoiding cascading failures.

0762d520c6ab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0762d520c6ab.sentence: Load test components until they break.

f3509af57670.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f3509af57670.sentence: As load increases, a component typically handles requests successfully until it reaches a point at which it canât handle more requests.

e681741d2e49.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e681741d2e49.sentence: At this point, the component should ideally start serving errors or degraded results in response to additional load, but not significantly reduce the rate at which it successfully handles requests.

f0df18fa0305.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f0df18fa0305.sentence: A component that is highly susceptible to a cascading failure will start crashing or serving a very high rate of errors when it becomes overloaded; a better designed component will instead be able to reject a few requests and survive.

7eeb8984503a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
7eeb8984503a.sentence: Because of caching effects, gradually ramping up load may yield different results than immediately increasing to expected load levels.

b5cd2150d19a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b5cd2150d19a.sentence: Therefore, consider testing both gradual and impulse load patterns.

854f23511cee.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
854f23511cee.sentence: You should also test and understand how the component behaves as it returns to nominal load after having been pushed well beyond that load.

6f4121ebe28c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6f4121ebe28c.sentence: - If a component enters a degraded mode on heavy load, is it capable of exiting the degraded mode without human intervention?

0a7b2a67c67f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
0a7b2a67c67f.sentence: - If a couple of servers crash under heavy load, how much does the load need to drop in order for the system to stabilize?

7332e939a8ec.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
7332e939a8ec.sentence: Keep in mind that individual components may have different breaking points, so load test each component separately.

a9bbe074adab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
a9bbe074adab.sentence: If you believe your system has proper protections against being overloaded, consider performing failure tests in a small slice of production to find the point at which the components in your system fail under real traffic.

58e1c2b31907.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
58e1c2b31907.sentence: These limits may not be adequately reflected by synthetic load test traffic, so real traffic tests may provide more realistic results than load tests, at the risk of causing user-visible pain.

56ade4fd9ba1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
56ade4fd9ba1.sentence: Be careful when testing on real traffic: make sure that you have extra capacity available in case your automatic protections donât work and you need to manually fail over.

e73d9764c513.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e73d9764c513.sentence: Understand how large clients use your service.

742d5ca0722a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
742d5ca0722a.sentence: - Use randomized exponential backoff on errors

9d394265de9a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
9d394265de9a.sentence: Test your noncritical backends, and make sure their unavailability does not interfere with the critical components of your service.

1855e9cb4eec.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
1855e9cb4eec.sentence: In addition to testing behavior when the noncritical backend is unavailable, test how the frontend behaves if the noncritical backend never responds (for example, if it is blackholing requests).

763ec8321fed.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
763ec8321fed.sentence: The frontend should not start rejecting lots of requests, running out of resources, or serving with very high latency when a noncritical backend blackholes.

8bf0699666ed.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
8bf0699666ed.sentence: Most thread-per-request servers use a queue in front of a thread pool to handle requests.

24da83ea6120.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
24da83ea6120.sentence: For a system with fairly steady traffic over time, it is usually better to have small queue lengths relative to the thread pool size (e.g., 50% or less), which results in the server rejecting requests early when it canât sustain the rate of incoming requests.

b76763924172.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b76763924172.sentence: Requests come in, they sit on a queue, and then threads pick requests off the queue and perform the actual work (whatever actions are required by the server).

ccf64851cee6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
ccf64851cee6.sentence: Usually, if the queue is full, the server will reject new requests.

9b02451324c4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
9b02451324c4.sentence: Queued requests consume memory and increase latency.

21930a799f1a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
21930a799f1a.sentence: For example, if the queue size is 10x the number of threads, the time to handle the request on a thread is 100 milliseconds.

d75a29774a5e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
d75a29774a5e.sentence: If the queue is full, then a request will take 1.1 seconds to handle, most of which time is spent on the queue.

eebb6a5500c2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
eebb6a5500c2.sentence: For example, Gmail often uses queueless servers, relying instead on failover to other server tasks when the threads are full.

38616386b056.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
38616386b056.sentence: On the other end of the spectrum, systems with âburstyâ load for which traffic patterns fluctuate drastically may do better with a queue size based on the current number of threads in use, processing time for each request, and the size and frequency of bursts.

97ac30ab54eb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
97ac30ab54eb.sentence: The following list presents strategies for avoiding server overload in rough priority order:

59e9e956c230.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
59e9e956c230.sentence: Load test the serverâs capacity limits, and test the failure mode for overload

cb3883c5c0de.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
cb3883c5c0de.sentence: This is the most important exercise you should conduct in order to prevent server overload.

a465f0d2e0fd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
a465f0d2e0fd.sentence: Unless you test in a realistic environment, itâs very hard to predict exactly which resource will be exhausted and how that resource exhaustion will manifest.

e3c3932d3906.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
e3c3932d3906.sentence: Serve lower-quality, cheaper-to-compute results to the user.

3d82c1def999.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
3d82c1def999.sentence: Your strategy here will be service-specific.

102a4344dddf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
102a4344dddf.sentence: Rate limiting can be implemented in a number of places:

8f946a85990a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
8f946a85990a.sentence: At the reverse proxies, by limiting the volume of requests by criteria such as IP address to mitigate attempted denial-of-service attacks and abusive clients.

f75334d6b95b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f75334d6b95b.sentence: At the load balancers, by dropping requests when the service enters global overload.

5db64cf3dc57.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
5db64cf3dc57.sentence: At individual tasks, to prevent random fluctuations in load balancing from overwhelming the server.

6bdf5912dfee.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6bdf5912dfee.sentence: For instance, if every clusterâs breaking point is 5,000 QPS, the load is evenly spread across clusters,109 and the serviceâs peak load is 19,000 QPS, then approximately six clusters are needed to run the service at N + 2.

b78d6cca9b6d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
b78d6cca9b6d.sentence: Load balancing problems, network partitions, or unexpected traffic increases can create pockets of high load beyond what was planned.

aca7f967151b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
aca7f967151b.sentence: Some systems can grow the number of tasks for your service on demand, which may prevent overload; however, proper capacity planning is still needed.

4e6d2d31a14d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
4e6d2d31a14d.sentence: In distributed systems and networked applications, retry strategies are crucial for handling transient errors and network instability effectively.

4787f09e9a3d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
4787f09e9a3d.sentence: Linear backoff involves waiting for a progressively increasing fixed interval between retry attempts.

30292308422a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
30292308422a.sentence: - Advantages: Simple to implement and understand.

6daf09e93a89.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
6daf09e93a89.sentence: - Disadvantages: May not be ideal under high load or in high-concurrency environments as it could lead to resource contention or "retry storms".

81dc9d9e30a1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
81dc9d9e30a1.sentence: Linear jitter backoff modifies the linear backoff strategy by introducing randomness to the retry intervals.

8aa5073fbf04.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
8aa5073fbf04.sentence: This strategy still increases the delay linearly but adds a random "jitter" to each interval.

77697ea91abc.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
77697ea91abc.sentence: - Advantages: The randomness helps spread out the retry attempts over time, reducing the chance of synchronized retries across instances.

c6f8c689d7b6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
c6f8c689d7b6.sentence: - Disadvantages: Although better than simple linear backoff, this strategy might still lead to potential issues with synchronized retries as the base interval increases only linearly.

bb480e872895.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
bb480e872895.sentence: Exponential backoff involves increasing the delay between retries exponentially.

bfd1efeff78c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
bfd1efeff78c.sentence: The interval might start at 1 second, then increase to 2 seconds, 4 seconds, 8 seconds, and so on, typically up to a maximum delay.

a268832cdf5c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
a268832cdf5c.sentence: - Advantages: Significantly reduces the load on the system and the likelihood of collision or overlap in retry attempts, making it suitable for high-load environments.

d7dba4f6cc14.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
d7dba4f6cc14.sentence: - Disadvantages: In situations where a quick retry might resolve the issue, this approach can unnecessarily delay the resolution.

b2b1ffb4c6a2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
b2b1ffb4c6a2.sentence: Exponential jitter backoff combines exponential backoff with randomness.

6cc684c7cbae.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
6cc684c7cbae.sentence: After each retry, the backoff interval is exponentially increased, and then a random jitter is applied.

8ad4422717d0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
8ad4422717d0.sentence: The jitter can be either additive (adding a random amount to the exponential delay) or multiplicative (multiplying the exponential delay by a random factor).

ad4daf863038.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
ad4daf863038.sentence: - Advantages: Offers all the benefits of exponential backoff, with the added advantage of reducing retry collisions even further due to the introduction of jitter.

d202bdfef6db.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-retry-on-failures.md
d202bdfef6db.sentence: - Disadvantages: The randomness can sometimes result in longer than necessary delays, especially if the jitter is significant.

782ace914d25.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
782ace914d25.sentence: The Circuit Breaker is a design pattern commonly used in software development to improve system resilience and fault tolerance.

b7727e613ef9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::circuit-breaker
b7727e613ef9.sentence: The circuit breaker is a design pattern used to detect failures and encapsulates the logic of preventing a failure from constantly recurring during maintenance, temporary external system failure, or unexpected system difficulties.

d4fa31fc5846.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::circuit-breaker
d4fa31fc5846.section: Why do we need circuit breaking?
d4fa31fc5846.sentence: One of the big differences between in-memory calls and remote calls is that remote calls can fail, or hang without a response until some timeout limit is reached.

96faf5da87e6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::circuit-breaker
96faf5da87e6.section: Why do we need circuit breaking?
96faf5da87e6.sentence: What's worse is if we have many callers on an unresponsive supplier, then we can run out of critical resources leading to cascading failures across multiple systems.

46992574035b.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
46992574035b.sentence: Unlike timeout-based methods, which can lead to delayed error responses or the premature failure of healthy requests, the Circuit Breaker pattern can proactively identify unresponsive services and can prevent repeated attempts.

ae5b3b8d6d02.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
ae5b3b8d6d02.sentence: In distributed systems, the Circuit Breaker pattern can be used to monitor service health and can detect failures dynamically.

a2b95d023b59.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
a2b95d023b59.sentence: The circuit breaker pattern can be used in conjunction with other patterns, such as retry, fallback, and timeout, to enhance fault tolerance in systems.

cbf332c38ef5.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
cbf332c38ef5.sentence: According to Marc Brooker, circuit breakers can misinterpret a partial failure as total system failure and inadvertently bring down the entire system.

4dbc04ef957d.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
4dbc04ef957d.sentence: In particular, sharded systems and cell-based architectures are vulnerable to this issue.

c09d15cfdae4.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
c09d15cfdae4.sentence: A workaround is that the server indicates to the client which specific part is overloaded and the client uses a corresponding mini circuit breaker.

a776e5a4fbbf.title: Circuit breaker design pattern
a776e5a4fbbf.sentence: However, this workaround can be complex and expensive.

da5317ffa120.title: Idempotence
da5317ffa120.sentence: Idempotence (UK: /ˌɪdɛmˈpoʊtəns/, US: /ˈaɪdəm-/) is the property of certain operations in mathematics and computer science whereby they can be applied multiple times without changing the result beyond the initial application.

d32c839f7548.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
d32c839f7548.sentence: An operation is idempotent if performing it multiple times has the same effect as performing it once.

6792580c8bb1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
6792580c8bb1.sentence: Setting a user's email to a@example.com is idempotent, while "add $10 to the balance" is not, because every repeat changes the result.

720227ce3888.title: Idempotence
720227ce3888.sentence: - in imperative programming, a subroutine with side effects is idempotent if multiple calls to the subroutine have the same effect on the system state as a single call, in other words if the function from the system state space to itself associated with the subroutine is idempotent in the mathematical sense given in the definition;

c845d599717e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
c845d599717e.sentence: In distributed systems, networks drop responses, clients time out, and load balancers retry.

900f3a05fbfc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
900f3a05fbfc.sentence: As a result, the same request often reaches a server more than once.

aeefac622ea1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
aeefac622ea1.sentence: Consider a client that sends a payment request and the connection times out.

222f28f884a5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
222f28f884a5.sentence: The client cannot know whether the server never received the request, processed it but the response was lost, or is still processing it.

762b89ff61fe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
762b89ff61fe.sentence: The only safe way to recover is to retry, but without idempotency a retry can charge the customer twice.

b2f8d4558088.title: Idempotence
b2f8d4558088.sentence: This is a very useful property in many situations, as it means that an operation can be repeated or retried as often as necessary without causing unintended effects.

5d9345b9ded3.title: Idempotence
5d9345b9ded3.sentence: With non-idempotent operations, the algorithm may have to keep track of whether the operation was already performed or not.

50b420307c7c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
50b420307c7c.sentence: - It makes retries safe, which is what allows us to build reliable systems on top of unreliable networks.

937267d03109.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
937267d03109.sentence: - It simplifies client logic, as clients can retry aggressively without reasoning about the server's state.

bb56e2dfb72c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
bb56e2dfb72c.sentence: - It protects against duplicate submissions caused by users double-clicking or refreshing a page.

2d767ca14ee5.title: Idempotence
2d767ca14ee5.section: Computer science meaning > Computer science examples
2d767ca14ee5.sentence: A function looking up a customer's name and address in a database is typically idempotent, since this will not cause the database to change.

fe5a46135dd7.title: Idempotence
fe5a46135dd7.section: Computer science meaning > Computer science examples
fe5a46135dd7.sentence: Similarly, a request for changing a customer's address to XYZ is typically idempotent, because the final address will be the same no matter how many times the request is submitted.

c0f745a3d1e3.title: Idempotence
c0f745a3d1e3.section: Computer science meaning > Computer science examples
c0f745a3d1e3.sentence: A request for canceling a particular order is idempotent because no matter how many requests are made the order remains canceled.

04c9855c5857.title: Idempotence
04c9855c5857.section: Computer science meaning > Computer science examples
04c9855c5857.sentence: However, a customer request for placing an order is typically not idempotent since multiple requests will lead to multiple orders being placed.

8072aed5c20f.title: Idempotence
8072aed5c20f.section: Computer science meaning > Computer science examples
8072aed5c20f.sentence: Of the major HTTP methods, GET, PUT, and DELETE should be implemented in an idempotent manner according to the standard, but POST doesn't need to be.

c9d471945ec4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
c9d471945ec4.sentence: Note that idempotent means the server state is the same after one or many calls, not that the response is identical.

3c76a18ee491.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
3c76a18ee491.sentence: For example, a repeated DELETE may return 404 instead of 200.

f7d8e58cd8c3.title: Idempotence
f7d8e58cd8c3.section: Computer science meaning > Computer science examples
f7d8e58cd8c3.sentence: PUT and DELETE with unique identifiers reduce to the simple case of assignment to a variable of either a value or the null-value, respectively, and are idempotent for the same reason; the end result is always the same as the result of the initial execution, even if the response differs.

168d4095a834.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::idempotency
168d4095a834.sentence: We need extra storage and lookups for keys, and additional logic to handle concurrent and in-flight requests.

9706d89b7bbf.title: Exponential backoff
9706d89b7bbf.sentence: Exponential backoff is an algorithm that uses feedback to multiplicatively decrease the rate of some process, in order to gradually find an acceptable rate.

d0dcffe0ecb0.title: Exponential backoff
d0dcffe0ecb0.sentence: An exponential backoff algorithm is a form of closed-loop control system that reduces the rate of a controlled process in response to adverse events.

e7f0bb2effea.title: Exponential backoff
e7f0bb2effea.sentence: Other examples of adverse events include collisions of network traffic, packet loss, an error response from a service, or an explicit request to reduce the rate (i.e., back off).

ce0700599dc2.title: Exponential backoff
ce0700599dc2.sentence: For example, if a mobile app fails to connect to its server, the mobile app might try again 1 second later, then if it fails again, 2 seconds later, then 4, etc. Each time, the pause is multiplied by a fixed amount (in this case, 2).

0378c8c07866.title: Exponential backoff
0378c8c07866.sentence: In this case, the adverse event is failing to connect to the server.

7871cadc8d50.title: Exponential backoff
7871cadc8d50.sentence: The rate reduction can be modelled as an exponential function:

454c6e2c69c1.title: Exponential backoff
454c6e2c69c1.sentence: Here, t is the time delay applied between actions, b is the multiplicative factor or base, and c is the number of adverse events observed.

084525eca6ce.title: Exponential backoff
084525eca6ce.sentence: The value of c is incremented each time an adverse event is observed, leading to an exponential rise in delay and, therefore, an inversely proportionate rate.

9dd2f3720c7f.title: Exponential backoff
9dd2f3720c7f.sentence: An exponential backoff algorithm where b = 2 is referred to as a binary exponential backoff algorithm.

d4fd2d3bf443.title: Exponential backoff
d4fd2d3bf443.sentence: Exponential backoff is commonly utilised as part of rate limiting mechanisms in computer systems such as web services, to help enforce fair distribution of access to resources and prevent network congestion.

d9e15466e7a6.title: Exponential backoff
d9e15466e7a6.sentence: Each time a service informs a client that it is sending requests too frequently, the client reduces its rate by some predetermined factor until the client's request rate reaches an acceptable equilibrium.

e8d02ab023b6.title: Exponential backoff
e8d02ab023b6.sentence: The service may enforce rate limiting by refusing to respond to requests when the client is sending them too frequently, so that misbehaving clients are not allowed to exceed their allotted resources.

6730e28fe943.title: Exponential backoff
6730e28fe943.sentence: A benefit of utilising an exponential backoff algorithm over a fixed rate limit is that rate limits through exponential backoff can be achieved dynamically without providing any prior information to the client.

44a503bcff0a.title: Exponential backoff
44a503bcff0a.sentence: In the event that resources are unexpectedly constrained, e.g., due to heavy load or a service disruption, backoff requests and error responses from the service can automatically decrease the request rate from clients.

1ce28d75a4ba.title: Exponential backoff
1ce28d75a4ba.sentence: This can help maintain some level of availability rather than overloading the service.

07cdd79610c4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
07cdd79610c4.sentence: First, we implement a per-request retry budget of up to three attempts.

47697a26ea27.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
47697a26ea27.sentence: Secondly, we implement a per-client retry budget.

6c72be839d24.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6c72be839d24.sentence: - Assume our backend has a known limit of 10,000 QPS per task, after which point all further requests are rejected in an attempt at graceful degradation.

8541a688cc64.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
8541a688cc64.sentence: - The frontend calls MakeRequest at a constant rate of 10,100 QPS and overloads the backend by 100 QPS, which the backend rejects.

f441e9fe36ab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
f441e9fe36ab.sentence: But the retries are themselves adding to the requests sent to the backend, which now receives 10,200 QPSâ200 QPS of which are failing due to overload.

4d462b23cdcc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
4d462b23cdcc.sentence: - The volume of retries grows: 100 QPS of retries in the first second leads to 200 QPS, then to 300 QPS, and so on.

6cac6e62c997.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
6cac6e62c997.sentence: - If the backend task is unable to handle the increase in loadâwhich is consuming file descriptors, memory, and CPU time on the backendâit can melt down and crash under the sheer load of requests and retries.

021da1794b94.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
021da1794b94.sentence: Some simplifying assumptions were made here to illustrate this scenario,110 but the point remains that retries can destabilize a system.

314a6451a298.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
314a6451a298.sentence: If a large subset of backend tasks in the datacenter are overloaded, requests should not be retried and errors should bubble up all the way to the caller (e.g., returning an error to the end user).

f9f4acaf1442.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
f9f4acaf1442.sentence: It's much more typical that only a small portion of tasks become overloaded, in which case the preferred response is to retry the request immediately.

e096fc11f9b2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
e096fc11f9b2.sentence: These requests can then be retried immediately on a different backend task that may have spare resources.

f17a93bd7e8f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
f17a93bd7e8f.sentence: If a request has already failed three times, we let the failure bubble up to the caller.

247da647ce34.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
247da647ce34.sentence: The rationale is that if a request has already landed on overloaded tasks three times, it's relatively unlikely that attempting it again will help because the whole datacenter is likely overloaded.

01d59317b844.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
01d59317b844.sentence: Each client keeps track of the ratio of requests that correspond to retries.

ba9ee6b240e4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
ba9ee6b240e4.sentence: A request will only be retried as long as this ratio is below 10%.

510873f6047c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
510873f6047c.sentence: Due to the number of retries that will occur, the number of requests will grow significantly, to somewhere just below 3X.

778a08f4e851.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
778a08f4e851.sentence: However, layering on the per-client retry budget (a 10% retry ratio) reduces the growth to just 1.1x in the general caseâa significant improvement.

8c58cc1d3e23.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
8c58cc1d3e23.sentence: For example, only allow 60 retries per minute in a process, and if the retry budget is exceeded, donât retry; just fail the request.

ad99119d4430.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
ad99119d4430.sentence: This strategy can contain the retry effect and be the difference between a capacity planning failure that leads to some dropped queries and a global cascading failure.

c8157fc6b729.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
c8157fc6b729.sentence: In particular, avoid amplifying retries by issuing retries at multiple levels: a single request at the highest layer may produce a number of attempts as large as the product of the number of attempts at each layer to the lowest layer.

afe6ae705fdc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
afe6ae705fdc.sentence: If the database canât service requests because itâs overloaded, and the backend, frontend, and JavaScript layers all issue 3 retries (4 attempts), then a single user action may create 64 attempts (4^3) on the database.

e01b26156616.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
e01b26156616.sentence: In this architecture, requests should only be retried at the layer immediately above the layer that is rejecting them.

ea9d69bcfff1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload
ea9d69bcfff1.sentence: If multiple layers retried, we'd have a combinatorial explosion.

dfbc551c09d8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures
dfbc551c09d8.sentence: - Use clear response codes and consider how different failure modes should be handled.

d41576c1ee54.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures

011a5b4e2d4a.title: Exponential backoff
011a5b4e2d4a.sentence: A deterministic exponential backoff algorithm is unsuitable for this use case since each sender would back off for the same time period, leading them to retransmit simultaneously and cause another collision.

c405b811fd37.title: Exponential backoff
c405b811fd37.sentence: Instead, for purposes of collision avoidance, the time between retransmissions is randomized and the exponential backoff algorithm sets the range of delay values that are possible.

b15444e18893.title: Exponential backoff
b15444e18893.sentence: After the first collision, each sender will wait 0 or 1 slot times.

49f1d62a4b2e.title: Exponential backoff
49f1d62a4b2e.sentence: After the second collision, the senders will wait anywhere from 0 to 3 slot times (inclusive).

20dd1d07dc4f.title: Exponential backoff
20dd1d07dc4f.sentence: After the third collision, the senders will wait anywhere from 0 to 7 slot times (inclusive), and so forth.

5e27548d3409.title: Exponential backoff
5e27548d3409.sentence: As the number of retransmission attempts increases, the number of possibilities for delay increases exponentially.

b09ef260f6df.title: Exponential backoff
b09ef260f6df.sentence: This decreases the probability of a collision but increases the average latency.

6cec73eddae3.title: Exponential backoff
6cec73eddae3.sentence: The 'truncated' variant of the algorithm introduces a limit on c. This simply means that after a certain number of increases, the exponentiation stops.

ee25ff3057f6.title: Exponential backoff
ee25ff3057f6.sentence: Without a limit on c, the delay between transmissions may become undesirably long if a sender repeatedly observes adverse events, e.g., due to a degradation in network performance.

44953102de06.title: Exponential backoff
44953102de06.sentence: Limiting c helps to reduce the possibility of unexpectedly long transmission latencies and improve recovery times after a transient outage.

38eaa872f93a.title: Exponential backoff

0f1e49b5bf02.title: Exponential backoff

f9336d2b631c.title: Exponential backoff

c88d7cab98e3.title: Exponential backoff
