70ca6c5182d5.sentence: Making a more recent recovery point achievable requires increasing the frequency of synchronization between the source data and the backup repository.

c7d85dad3f79.title: Backup
c7d85dad3f79.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Objectives
c7d85dad3f79.sentence: - Recovery time objective (RTO): The amount of time elapsed between disaster and restoration of business functions.

9e524b48ff49.title: Backup
9e524b48ff49.sentence: Online backup storage is typically the most accessible type of data storage, and can begin a restore in milliseconds.

89f43a2279f2.title: Backup
89f43a2279f2.sentence: Nearline storage is typically less accessible and less expensive than online storage, but still useful for backup data storage.

303c0702fac8.title: Backup
303c0702fac8.sentence: Because the data is not accessible via any computer except during limited periods in which they are written or read back, they are largely immune to on-line backup failure modes.

1901ae56dd11.title: Backup
1901ae56dd11.sentence: Backup media may be sent to an off-site vault to protect against a disaster or other site-specific problem.

cfc313a7652d.title: Backup
cfc313a7652d.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Deduplication
cfc313a7652d.sentence: Redundancy due to backing up similarly configured workstations can be reduced, thus storing just one copy.

54d1bf522e6d.title: Backup
54d1bf522e6d.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Deduplication
54d1bf522e6d.sentence: This technique can be applied at the file or raw block level.

0a36c9ffaa34.title: Backup
0a36c9ffaa34.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Deduplication
0a36c9ffaa34.sentence: It can occur on a server before any data moves to backup media, sometimes referred to as source/client side deduplication.

f36dd0f6c91e.title: Backup
f36dd0f6c91e.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Deduplication
f36dd0f6c91e.sentence: This approach also reduces bandwidth required to send backup data to its target media.

7942ceef8eef.title: Backup
7942ceef8eef.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Deduplication
7942ceef8eef.sentence: The process can also occur at the target storage device, sometimes referred to as inline or back-end deduplication.

2a4758889141.title: Backup
2a4758889141.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Compression
2a4758889141.sentence: Various schemes can be employed to shrink the size of the source data to be stored so that it uses less storage space.

2d52dfcd214a.title: Backup
2d52dfcd214a.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Encryption
2d52dfcd214a.sentence: High-capacity removable storage media such as backup tapes present a data security risk if they are lost or stolen.

1af8d62fd5f1.title: Backup
1af8d62fd5f1.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Encryption
1af8d62fd5f1.sentence: Encrypting the data on these media can mitigate this problem, however encryption is a CPU intensive process that can slow down backup speeds, and the security of the encrypted backups is only as effective as the security of the key management policy.

d3d54d303032.title: Backup
d3d54d303032.section: Manipulation of data and dataset optimization > Objectives
d3d54d303032.sentence: - Checksum or hash function validation: Applications that back up to tape archive files need this option to verify that the data was accurately copied.

ef68fe68a86a.title: Backup
ef68fe68a86a.sentence: Backup schemes may include dry runs that validate the reliability of the data being backed up.

d474f9beb6e4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
d474f9beb6e4.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
d474f9beb6e4.sentence: To revise our earlier definition of data integrity, we might say that data integrity means that services in the cloud remain accessible to users.

fdd9111f4626.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
fdd9111f4626.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
fdd9111f4626.sentence: Data loss, data corruption, and extended unavailability are typically indistinguishable to users.

ea5cc79f05a6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
ea5cc79f05a6.section: Data Integrity Is the Means; Data Availability Is the Goal
ea5cc79f05a6.sentence: Data integrity refers to the accuracy and consistency of data throughout its lifetime.

6cedc16e34ca.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
6cedc16e34ca.section: Data Integrity Is the Means; Data Availability Is the Goal
6cedc16e34ca.sentence: The moral of this example: From the userâs point of view, data integrity without expected and regular data availability is effectively the same as having no data at all.

f78e99662626.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
f78e99662626.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
f78e99662626.sentence: Therefore, data integrity applies to all types of data across all services.

9f5ffa2cf9ad.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
9f5ffa2cf9ad.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
9f5ffa2cf9ad.sentence: As demonstrated by an actual Gmail incident in 2011 [Hic11], four days is a long timeâperhaps "too long." Subsequently, we believe 24 hours is a good starting point for establishing the threshold of "too long" for Google Apps.

47eb2b56f8d2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
47eb2b56f8d2.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
47eb2b56f8d2.sentence: From the user perspective, then, every service has independent uptime and data integrity requirements, even if these requirements are implicit.

16a46eef9980.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
16a46eef9980.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
16a46eef9980.sentence: An SLO of 99.99% uptime leaves room for only an hour of downtime in a whole year.

dfda0f15c8ad.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
dfda0f15c8ad.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
dfda0f15c8ad.sentence: In contrast, an SLO of 99.99% good bytes in a 2 GB artifact would render documents, executables, and databases corrupt (up to 200 KB garbled).

84f60cd9cc6d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
84f60cd9cc6d.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
84f60cd9cc6d.sentence: This amount of corruption is catastrophic in the majority of casesâresulting in executables with random opcodes and completely unloadable databases.

16c6bd4e4867.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
16c6bd4e4867.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
16c6bd4e4867.sentence: As demonstrated by this example, the secret to superior data integrity is proactive detection and rapid repair and recovery.

4542e33c56ea.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
4542e33c56ea.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
4542e33c56ea.sentence: In an alternate universe, suppose the corruption were immediately detected before users were affected and that the artifact was removed, fixed, and returned to service within half an hour.

18e3f608abbc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
18e3f608abbc.section: Data Integrity: What You Read Is What You Wrote
18e3f608abbc.sentence: Ignoring any other downtime during that 30 minutes, such an object would be 99.99% available that year.

41ff069f3d58.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
41ff069f3d58.section: Google SRE Objectives in Maintaining Data Integrity and Availability
41ff069f3d58.sentence: While SREâs goal of âmaintaining integrity of persistent dataâ is a good vision, we thrive on concrete objectives with measurable indicators.

ab0f7de28eab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
ab0f7de28eab.sentence: Rather than focusing on the means to the end, Google SRE finds it useful to borrow a page from test-driven development by proving that our systems can maintain data availability with a predicted maximum down time.

b9dd99ae23d6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
b9dd99ae23d6.section: Choosing a Strategy for Superior Data Integrity
b9dd99ae23d6.sentence: All of these strategies trade uptime against data integrity with respect to affected users.

8f5c4fb2def8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
8f5c4fb2def8.section: Choosing a Strategy for Superior Data Integrity
8f5c4fb2def8.sentence: Most cloud computing applications seek to optimize for some combination of uptime, latency, scale, velocity, and privacy.

3f4d934c15c7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
3f4d934c15c7.section: Choosing a Strategy for Superior Data Integrity
3f4d934c15c7.sentence: The answer depends on your computing paradigm.

630aeed1fa25.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
630aeed1fa25.sentence: Collecting, processing, aggregating, and displaying real-time quantitative data about a system, such as query counts and types, error counts and types, processing times, and server lifetimes.

133aa3928b2f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
133aa3928b2f.sentence: Comparing over time or experiment groups

a861533ddf33.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
a861533ddf33.sentence: Something is broken, and somebody needs to fix it right now!

4f7233f9c274.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
4f7233f9c274.sentence: Or, something might break soon, so somebody should look soon.

9eaef8bb4b74.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
9eaef8bb4b74.sentence: Conducting ad hoc retrospective analysis (i.e., debugging)

fa14de22c6ac.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
fa14de22c6ac.sentence: An application (usually web-based) that provides a summary view of a serviceâs core metrics.

b7b5526a0db1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
b7b5526a0db1.sentence: A dashboard may have filters, selectors, and so on, but is prebuilt to expose the metrics most important to its users.

f435815c2554.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
f435815c2554.sentence: Dashboards should answer basic questions about your service, and normally include some form of the four golden signals (discussed in The Four Golden Signals).

1a55d52a645b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
1a55d52a645b.sentence: A notification intended to be read by a human and that is pushed to a system such as a bug or ticket queue, an email alias, or a pager.

f8898e8e1ca4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
f8898e8e1ca4.sentence: Respectively, these alerts are classified as tickets, email alerts,22 and pages.

2062894e629f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
2062894e629f.sentence: Monitoring and alerting enables a system to tell us when itâs broken, or perhaps to tell us whatâs about to break.

7d3007a21dda.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
7d3007a21dda.sentence: When the system isnât able to automatically fix itself, we want a human to investigate the alert, determine if thereâs a real problem at hand, mitigate the problem, and determine the root cause of the problem.

37eb96c6f0b3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
37eb96c6f0b3.sentence: Monitoring a complex application is a significant engineering endeavor in and of itself.

b31002e8bf73.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
b31002e8bf73.sentence: This number has decreased over time as we generalize and centralize common monitoring infrastructure, but every SRE team typically has at least one âmonitoring person.â (That being said, while it can be fun to have access to traffic graph dashboards and the like, SRE teams carefully avoid any situation that requires someone to âstare at a screen to watch for problems.â)

4c75b13b4464.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
4c75b13b4464.sentence: In general, Google has trended toward simpler and faster monitoring systems, with better tools for post hoc analysis.

316d355863d0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
316d355863d0.sentence: We avoid "magic" systems that try to learn thresholds or automatically detect causality.

8d8b68b8b5ed.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
8d8b68b8b5ed.section: As Simple as Possible, No Simpler
8d8b68b8b5ed.sentence: Like all software systems, monitoring can become so complex that itâs fragile, complicated to change, and a maintenance burden.

081e84e3a4a6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
081e84e3a4a6.section: As Simple as Possible, No Simpler
081e84e3a4a6.sentence: - The rules that catch real incidents most often should be as simple, predictable, and reliable as possible.

e5254f4e9701.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
e5254f4e9701.section: As Simple as Possible, No Simpler
e5254f4e9701.sentence: - Data collection, aggregation, and alerting configuration that is rarely exercised (e.g., less than once a quarter for some SRE teams) should be up for removal.

f2380fd87043.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
f2380fd87043.section: As Simple as Possible, No Simpler
f2380fd87043.sentence: - Signals that are collected, but not exposed in any prebaked dashboard nor used by any alert, are candidates for removal.

ba24ee405ae1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
ba24ee405ae1.section: Choosing an Appropriate Resolution for Measurements
ba24ee405ae1.sentence: Different aspects of a system should be measured with different levels of granularity.

2fea7124c059.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
2fea7124c059.section: Choosing an Appropriate Resolution for Measurements
2fea7124c059.sentence: - On the other hand, for a web service targeting no more than 9 hours aggregate downtime per year (99.9% annual uptime), probing for a 200 (success) status more than once or twice a minute is probably unnecessarily frequent.

f30c8ef1917d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
f30c8ef1917d.section: Choosing an Appropriate Resolution for Measurements
f30c8ef1917d.sentence: Collecting per-second measurements of CPU load might yield interesting data, but such frequent measurements may be very expensive to collect, store, and analyze.

066dfd954e4a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
066dfd954e4a.section: Choosing an Appropriate Resolution for Measurements
066dfd954e4a.sentence: If your monitoring goal calls for high resolution but doesnât require extremely low latency, you can reduce these costs by performing internal sampling on the server, then configuring an external system to collect and aggregate that distribution over time or across servers.

717e1e9c2a40.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
717e1e9c2a40.section: Choosing an Appropriate Resolution for Measurements
717e1e9c2a40.sentence: - Using buckets of 5% granularity, increment the appropriate CPU utilization bucket each second.

befff11abc94.title: Service level indicator
befff11abc94.sentence: In information technology, a service level indicator (SLI) is a measure of the service level provided by a service provider to a customer.

56e1d214be1f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
56e1d214be1f.sentence: An SLI, or Service Level Indicator, is a key metric used to determine whether or not the SLO is being met.

7094abb9049b.title: Service level indicator
7094abb9049b.sentence: SLIs form the basis of service level objectives (SLOs), which in turn form the basis of service level agreements (SLAs); an SLI can also be called an SLA metric (also customer service metric, or simply service metric).

b44d15195b0b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
b44d15195b0b.sentence: It is the measured value of the metric described within the SLO.

ea379e683e90.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
ea379e683e90.sentence: In order to remain in compliance with the SLA, the SLI's value must always meet or exceed the value determined by the SLO.

529646cd6ada.title: Service level indicator
529646cd6ada.sentence: Though every system is different in the services provided, often common SLIs are used.

9e3690f343ac.title: Service level indicator
9e3690f343ac.sentence: Common SLIs include latency, throughput, availability, and error rate; others include durability (in storage systems), end-to-end latency (for complex data processing systems, especially pipelines), and correctness.

f981dd3a2182.title: Service-level objective
f981dd3a2182.sentence: The availability SLI used will vary based on the nature and architecture of the service.

b073ef57d0eb.title: Service-level objective
b073ef57d0eb.sentence: For example, a simple web service might use the ratio of successful responses served vs the total number of valid requests received.

589fa674e6c8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
589fa674e6c8.sentence: An SLI is a service level indicatorâa carefully defined quantitative measure of some aspect of the level of service that is provided.

721c9538c31a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
721c9538c31a.sentence: Most services consider request latencyâhow long it takes to return a response to a requestâas a key SLI.

d402c3e17baf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
d402c3e17baf.sentence: Other common SLIs include the error rate, often expressed as a fraction of all requests received, and system throughput, typically measured in requests per second.

fb53649ac509.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
fb53649ac509.sentence: Ideally, the SLI directly measures a service level of interest, but sometimes only a proxy is available because the desired measure may be hard to obtain or interpret.

1129b8480bf6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
1129b8480bf6.sentence: For example, client-side latency is often the more user-relevant metric, but it might only be possible to measure latency at the server.

07bb76d5a86e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
07bb76d5a86e.sentence: Many indicator metrics are most naturally gathered on the server side, using a monitoring system such as Borgmon (see Practical Alerting from Time-Series Data) or Prometheus, or with periodic log analysisâfor instance, HTTP 500 responses as a fraction of all requests.

b0f3a44213d5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
b0f3a44213d5.sentence: However, some systems should be instrumented with client-side collection, because not measuring behavior at the client can miss a range of problems that affect users but donât affect server-side metrics.

daf243d64259.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
daf243d64259.sentence: For example, concentrating on the response latency of the Shakespeare search backend might miss poor user latency due to problems with the pageâs JavaScript: in this case, measuring how long it takes for a page to become usable in the browser is a better proxy for what the user actually experiences.

3ea8bb76dbf0.title: Service-level objective
3ea8bb76dbf0.sentence: A service-level objective (SLO) is a target value or range of values for a service level that is measured by a service level indicator (SLI).

0ae1990797ad.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
0ae1990797ad.sentence: An SLO, or Service Level Objective, is the promise that a company makes to users regarding a specific metric such as incident response or uptime.

c6d18038c300.title: Service-level objective
c6d18038c300.sentence: An SLO is a key element of a service-level agreement (SLA) between a service provider and a customer.

49a6410566dc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
49a6410566dc.sentence: SLOs exist within an SLA as individual promises contained within the full user agreement.

15cac8c6eac6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
15cac8c6eac6.sentence: The SLO is the specific goal that the service must meet in order to comply with the SLA.

e72dcc99bb9a.title: Service-level objective
e72dcc99bb9a.sentence: SLOs are specific measurable characteristics of the SLA, such as availability, throughput, frequency, response time, or quality.

a6004b38742a.title: Service-level objective
a6004b38742a.sentence: SLOs provide a quantitative means to define the level of service a customer can expect from a provider.

bb052f7c7847.title: Service-level objective
bb052f7c7847.sentence: SLOs are agreed upon as a means of measuring the performance of the service provider and are outlined as a way of avoiding disputes between the two parties based on misunderstanding.

84e6b5fa1024.title: Service-level objective
84e6b5fa1024.sentence: In simple terms, SLOs are "targets for how often you can fail or otherwise not operate properly and still ensure that your users aren't meaningfully upset."

acd8a53b9a89.title: Service-level objective
acd8a53b9a89.sentence: The SLO are formed by setting goals for metrics (commonly called service level indicators, SLIs).

e952c13aae9e.title: Service-level objective
e952c13aae9e.sentence: As an example, an availability SLO may be defined as the expected measured value of an availability SLI over a prescribed duration (e.g. four weeks).

d3e144b72769.title: Service-level objective
d3e144b72769.sentence: SLOs should generally be specified in terms of an achievement value or service level, a target measurement, a measurement period, and where and how they are measured.

cdd3e7471f90.title: Service-level objective
cdd3e7471f90.sentence: As an example, "90% of calls to the helpdesk should be answered in less than 20 seconds measured over a one-month period as reported by the ACD system".

31791239ef44.title: Service-level objective
31791239ef44.sentence: Availability | The application will be available 99.95% of the time | Over a year

e5d07dcd9ecc.title: Service-level objective
e5d07dcd9ecc.sentence: Response time | 85% of TCP replies within 1.5 seconds of receiving a request 99.5% of TCP replies within 4 seconds of receiving a request | Over a month

483ecef01739.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
483ecef01739.sentence: SLOs should always be simple, clearly defined, and easily measured to determine whether or not the objective is being fulfilled.

186c6c6408b4.title: Service-level objective
186c6c6408b4.sentence: Companies may also define internal SLOs for internal services that depend on each other, especially companies that apply the practice of site reliability engineering.

9598a1da512a.title: Service-level agreement
9598a1da512a.sentence: A service-level agreement (SLA) is an agreement, typically a binding contract, between a service provider and a customer that define particular aspects of the service – such as quality of service, availability, responsibilities – as terms of contract.

1fca3e93efab.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
1fca3e93efab.sentence: An SLA, or Service Level Agreement, is an agreement made between a company and its users of a given service.

c061626923f6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
c061626923f6.sentence: The SLA defines the different promises that the company makes to users regarding specific metrics, such as service availability.

6b404be80e3f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
6b404be80e3f.sentence: SLAs are often written by a company's business or legal team.

987df144003c.title: Service-level agreement
987df144003c.sentence: SLAs are commonly used in the technology industry, and often contain specific service-level objectives for defined service level indicators, such as mean time between failures, mean time to repair, mean time to recovery, network throughput, jitter, uptime, first-call resolution, and turnaround time.

8ae25b6a6e9e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
8ae25b6a6e9e.sentence: SLAs, SLOs, and SLIs allow companies to define, track and monitor the promises made for a service to its users.

4a76a666e7d0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::sla-slo-sli
4a76a666e7d0.sentence: Together, SLAs, SLOs, and SLIs should help teams generate more user trust in their services with an added emphasis on continuous improvement to incident management and response processes.

4d21204c5c97.title: Service-level agreement
4d21204c5c97.sentence: Unlike traditional contracts, SLAs often require parties involved to meet regularly to create an open forum for communication, apply rewards and penalties for performance, and leave room for periodic revisitation to make changes.

578ebc129795.title: Service-level agreement
578ebc129795.sentence: Larger organizations often maintain many SLAs internally, such that two different units in an organization script an SLA with one unit being the customer and another being the service provider.

19a9c5086d0d.title: Service-level agreement
19a9c5086d0d.sentence: This practice helps to maintain the same quality of service amongst different units in the organization and also across multiple locations of the organization.

3e84ff2a00a3.title: Service-level agreement
3e84ff2a00a3.sentence: This internal scripting of SLA also helps to compare the quality of service between an in-house department and an external service provider.

28c76608236b.title: Service-level agreement
28c76608236b.sentence: Service level agreements are also defined at different levels:

ea9a8c33b629.title: Service-level agreement
ea9a8c33b629.sentence: - Customer-based SLA: An agreement with an individual customer group, covering all the services they use.

1e1353db740b.title: Service-level agreement
1e1353db740b.sentence: - Service-based SLA: An agreement for all customers using the services being delivered by the service provider.

adc7b3e32553.title: Service-level agreement
adc7b3e32553.sentence: - Multilevel SLA: The SLA is split into the different levels, each addressing different set of customers for the same services, in the same SLA.

450c6339cb2d.title: Service-level agreement
450c6339cb2d.sentence: This new arrangement is managed through a contract that may include one or more SLAs.

67e557700bfd.title: Service-level agreement
67e557700bfd.sentence: The contract may involve financial penalties and the right to terminate if any of the SLA metrics are consistently missed.

1247344c927f.title: Service-level agreement
1247344c927f.sentence: Specific SLAs are typically negotiated upfront as part of the outsourcing contract and used as one of the primary tools of outsourcing governance.

f40bb459d487.title: Service-level agreement
f40bb459d487.sentence: SLAs may be supported by operational-level agreements, or OLAs.

You can think of lazy deletion as behind the scenes purging, controlled by the storage system (whereas soft deletion is controlled by and expressed to the client application or service).

fe1f78a6541e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
fe1f78a6541e.sentence: In a lazy deletion scenario, data that is deleted by a cloud application becomes immediately inaccessible to the application, but is preserved by the cloud service provider for up to a few weeks before destruction.

33bc3fc560bf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
33bc3fc560bf.sentence: Lazy deletion isnât advisable in all defense in depth strategies: a long lazy deletion period is costly in systems with much short-lived data, and impractical in systems that must guarantee destruction of deleted data within a reasonable time frame (i.e., those that offer privacy guarantees).

5c6369a4cecb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
5c6369a4cecb.sentence: - A trash folder that allows users to undelete data is the primary defense against user error.

b4dfcd802450.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
b4dfcd802450.sentence: - Soft deletion is the primary defense against developer error and the secondary defense against user error.

1ef778419b56.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
1ef778419b56.sentence: - In developer offerings, lazy deletion is the primary defense against internal developer error and the secondary defense against external developer error.

502bc3f57b95.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
502bc3f57b95.sentence: Google has also found that the most devastating acute data deletion cases are caused by application developers unfamiliar with existing code but working on deletion-related code, especially batch processing pipelines (e.g., an offline MapReduce or Hadoop pipeline).

a644a08f8b8a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
a644a08f8b8a.sentence: Itâs advantageous to design your interfaces to hinder developers unfamiliar with your code from circumventing soft deletion features with new code.

be20d7e535bf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
be20d7e535bf.sentence: One effective way of achieving this is to implement cloud computing offerings that include built-in soft deletion and undeletion APIs, making sure to enable said feature.128 Even the best armor is useless if you donât put it on.

ba51ef66d908.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
ba51ef66d908.sentence: At Google, revision history has proven useful in recovering from certain data corruption scenarios, but not in recovering from most data loss scenarios involving accidental deletion, programmatic or otherwise.

420c236c961d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
420c236c961d.sentence: This is because some revision history implementations treat deletion as a special case in which previous states must be removed, as opposed to mutating an item whose history may be retained for a certain time period.

5411692a4941.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
5411692a4941.sentence: To provide adequate protection against unwanted deletion, apply the lazy and/or soft deletion principles to revision history also.

ab9542b03ac8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
ab9542b03ac8.section: Limiting the Connections Pool with Subsetting
ab9542b03ac8.sentence: In addition to health management, another consideration for load balancing is subsetting: limiting the pool of potential backend tasks with which a client task interacts.

682342a65b41.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
682342a65b41.section: Limiting the Connections Pool with Subsetting
682342a65b41.sentence: Every connection requires some memory and CPU (due to periodic health checking) at both ends.

18b015337470.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
18b015337470.section: Limiting the Connections Pool with Subsetting
18b015337470.sentence: Subsetting avoids the situation in which a single client connects to a very large number of backend tasks or a single backend task receives connections from a very large number of client tasks.

4a10fc069669.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
4a10fc069669.section: Limiting the Connections Pool with Subsetting
4a10fc069669.sentence: In both cases, you potentially waste a very large amount of resources for very little gain.

1856a3dab6be.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
1856a3dab6be.sentence: We typically use a subset size of 20 to 100 backend tasks, but the "right" subset size for a system depends heavily on the typical behavior of your service.

113e0fc4823c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
113e0fc4823c.sentence: - The number of clients is significantly smaller than the number of backends.

f4280a8b6e79.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
f4280a8b6e79.sentence: In this case, you want the number of backends per client to be large enough that you donât end up with backend tasks that will never receive any traffic.

5c37946537f1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
5c37946537f1.sentence: - There are frequent load imbalances within the client jobs (i.e., one client task sends more requests than others).

65f11755825b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
65f11755825b.sentence: Because a burst of requests will be concentrated in the clientâs assigned subset, you need a larger subset size to ensure the load is spread evenly across the larger set of available backend tasks.

b97479e71af7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
b97479e71af7.sentence: The selection algorithm for clients should assign backends uniformly to optimize resource provisioning.

38a9e22cc1dc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
38a9e22cc1dc.sentence: For example, if subsetting overloads one backend by 10%, the whole set of backends needs to be overprovisioned by 10%.

5a29230203f9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
5a29230203f9.sentence: The algorithm should also handle restarts and failures gracefully and robustly by continuing to load backends as uniformly as possible while minimizing churn.

e99aa1eb2d30.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
e99aa1eb2d30.sentence: The algorithm should also handle resizes in the number of clients and/or number of backends, with minimal connection churn and without knowing these numbers in advance.

d4a53af315c2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
d4a53af315c2.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Random Subsetting
d4a53af315c2.sentence: A naive implementation of a subset selection algorithm might have each client randomly shuffle the list of backends once and fill its subset by selecting resolvable/healthy backends from the list.

278e06921b5a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
278e06921b5a.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Random Subsetting
278e06921b5a.sentence: However, weâve found that this strategy actually works very poorly in most practical scenarios because it spreads load very unevenly.

e5241170f7df.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
e5241170f7df.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Random Subsetting
e5241170f7df.sentence: For example, Figure 20-4 depicts the results if the subset size is reduced to 10% (30 backends per client).

debf64cebbde.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
debf64cebbde.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Random Subsetting
debf64cebbde.sentence: In this case, the least loaded backend receives 50% of the average load (15 connections) and the most loaded receives 150% (45 connections).

09d9c7c6e0fc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
09d9c7c6e0fc.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Random Subsetting
09d9c7c6e0fc.sentence: We concluded that for random subsetting to spread the load relatively evenly across all available tasks, we would need subset sizes as large as 75%.

2baefc82d65d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
2baefc82d65d.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
2baefc82d65d.sentence: We divide client tasks into "rounds," where round i consists of subset_count consecutive client tasks, starting at task subset_count Ã i, and subset_count is the number of subsets (i.e., the number of backend tasks divided by the desired subset size).

52c047ea5038.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
52c047ea5038.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
52c047ea5038.sentence: Within each round, each backend is assigned to exactly one client (except possibly the last round, which may not contain enough clients, so some backends may not be assigned).

dc91995a7ae7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
dc91995a7ae7.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
dc91995a7ae7.sentence: To assign a subset to a client task, we just take the subset that corresponds to its position within its round (e.g., (i % 4) for client[i] with four subsets):

1dee77c3a276.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
1dee77c3a276.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
1dee77c3a276.sentence: The list should be shuffled; otherwise, clients are assigned a group of consecutive backend tasks that may all become temporarily unavailable (for example, because the backend job is being updated gradually in order, from the first task to the last).

0b3142da45e5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
0b3142da45e5.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
0b3142da45e5.sentence: Different rounds use a different seed for shuffling.

475b65b3f7c8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
475b65b3f7c8.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
475b65b3f7c8.sentence: If they donât, when a backend fails, the load it was receiving is only spread among the remaining backends in its subset.

931615b0391b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
931615b0391b.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
931615b0391b.sentence: A much better approach is to spread this load over all remaining backends by using a different shuffle for each round.

b32450c4ddae.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
b32450c4ddae.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
b32450c4ddae.sentence: As Figure 20-5 shows, the distribution for the former example of 300 clients each connecting to 10 of 300 backends yields very good results: each backend receives exactly the same number of connections.

2a37900a79f8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
2a37900a79f8.section: A Subset Selection Algorithm: Deterministic Subsetting
2a37900a79f8.sentence: In cases where the total number of backends is not divisible by the desired subset size, we allow a few subsets to be slightly larger than others, but in most cases the number of clients assigned to a backend will differ by at most 1.

94e33cb69958.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
94e33cb69958.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
94e33cb69958.sentence: The backend task is listening on its port and can serve, but is explicitly asking clients to stop sending requests.

18bff7217daa.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
18bff7217daa.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
18bff7217daa.sentence: When a task enters lame duck state, it broadcasts that fact to all its active clients.

6a532a9501f7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
6a532a9501f7.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
6a532a9501f7.sentence: From a client perspective, a given backend task can be in any of the following states:

e1767a8f21c6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
e1767a8f21c6.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
e1767a8f21c6.sentence: The backend task has initialized correctly and is processing requests.

19f59edc6cd1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
19f59edc6cd1.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State

5d5e676c6e6f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
5d5e676c6e6f.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State

8677ac8dcd59.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
8677ac8dcd59.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
8677ac8dcd59.sentence: This can happen because the task is starting up or shutting down, or because the backend is in an abnormal state (though it would be rare for a backend to stop listening on its port if it is not shutting down).

11f4339f0ba3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
11f4339f0ba3.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
11f4339f0ba3.sentence: With Googleâs RPC implementation, inactive clients (i.e., clients with no active TCP connections) still send periodic UDP health checks.

5817702913a7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
5817702913a7.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
5817702913a7.sentence: The result is that lame duck information is propagated quickly to all clientsâtypically in 1 or 2 RTTâregardless of their current state.

763cff091251.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
763cff091251.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
763cff091251.sentence: The main advantage of allowing a task to exist in a quasi-operational lame duck state is that it simplifies clean shutdown, which avoids serving errors to all the unlucky requests that happened to be active on backend tasks that are shutting down.

63d492d739da.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
63d492d739da.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
63d492d739da.sentence: Bringing down a backend task that has active requests without serving any errors facilitates code pushes, maintenance activities, or machine failures that may require restarting all related tasks.

8a783df081f2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
8a783df081f2.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
8a783df081f2.sentence: - The job scheduler sends a SIGTERM signal to the backend task.

081103439441.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
081103439441.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
081103439441.sentence: - The backend task enters lame duck state and asks its clients to send new requests to other backend tasks.

ebb126e3b5c8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
ebb126e3b5c8.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
ebb126e3b5c8.sentence: - Any ongoing request started before the backend task entered lame duck state (or after it entered lame duck state but before a client detected it) executes normally.

afc98b8ad405.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
afc98b8ad405.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
afc98b8ad405.sentence: - As responses flow back to the clients, the number of active requests against the backend gradually decreases to zero.

7e705eed4934.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
7e705eed4934.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
7e705eed4934.sentence: - After a configured interval, the backend task either exits cleanly or the job scheduler kills it.

f004cb42cb1f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
f004cb42cb1f.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
f004cb42cb1f.sentence: The interval should be set to a large enough value that all typical requests have sufficient time to finish.

8a3562f41be9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
8a3562f41be9.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
8a3562f41be9.sentence: This value is service dependent, but a good rule of thumb is between 10s and 150s depending on client complexity.

97dfad5848a7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
97dfad5848a7.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
97dfad5848a7.sentence: This strategy also allows a client to establish connections to backend tasks while performing potentially long-lived initialization procedures (and thus are not yet ready to start serving).

e460c8d9add3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
e460c8d9add3.section: A Robust Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Lame Duck State
e460c8d9add3.sentence: As soon as the backend task is ready to start serving, it signals this explicitly to the clients.

00021af43738.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
00021af43738.sentence: In response, weâve actually added to the logic of some server codeâwe keep servers in lame duck state and prewarm them (triggering these optimizations) for a period of time after they start, until their performance is nominal.

89386512bc37.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
89386512bc37.section: A Simple Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Flow Control
89386512bc37.sentence: Assume our client tasks track the number of active requests they have sent on each connection to a backend task.

53b75598db63.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
53b75598db63.section: A Simple Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Flow Control
53b75598db63.sentence: When this active-request count reaches a configured limit, the client treats the backend as unhealthy and no longer sends it requests.

95f7dd7aa5eb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
95f7dd7aa5eb.section: A Simple Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Flow Control
95f7dd7aa5eb.sentence: For most backends, 100 is a reasonable limit; in the average case, requests tend to finish fast enough that it is very rare for the number of active requests from a given client to reach this limit under normal operating conditions.

c1ab1928d2d8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
c1ab1928d2d8.section: A Simple Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Flow Control
c1ab1928d2d8.sentence: Unfortunately, this very simplistic approach only protects backend tasks against very extreme forms of overload and itâs very easy for backends to become overloaded well before this limit is ever reached.

49f8a16020f3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
49f8a16020f3.section: A Simple Approach to Unhealthy Tasks: Flow Control
49f8a16020f3.sentence: Weâve seen cases in which this default limit has backfired, causing all backend tasks to become unreachable, with requests blocked in the clients until they time out and fail.

d3b9e63155d9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
d3b9e63155d9.sentence: One very simple approach to load balancing has each client send requests in round-robin fashion to each backend task in its subset to which it can successfully connect and which isnât in lame duck state.

ecd074308a3b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
ecd074308a3b.sentence: Unfortunately, while Round Robin has the advantage of being very simple and performing significantly better than just selecting backend tasks randomly, the results of this policy can be very poor.

dcafba140942.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
dcafba140942.sentence: While actual numbers depend on many factors, such as varying query cost and machine diversity, weâve found that Round Robin can result in a spread of up to 2x in CPU consumption from the least to the most loaded task.

143906fa7ba9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
143906fa7ba9.sentence: One of the simplest reasons Round Robin distributes load poorly is that all of its clients may not issue requests at the same rate.

d4d14628428a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
d4d14628428a.sentence: Different rates of requests among clients are especially likely when vastly different processes share the same backends.

c4bc56588df5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
c4bc56588df5.sentence: In this case, and especially if youâre using relatively small subset sizes, backends in the subsets of the clients generating the most traffic will naturally tend to be more loaded.

00d6902ac4a6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
00d6902ac4a6.sentence: In practice, weâve found that the semantics of many services in Google are such that the most expensive requests consume 1000x (or more) CPU than the cheapest requests.

0d36f6f1221b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
0d36f6f1221b.sentence: Load balancing using Round Robin is even more difficult when query cost canât be predicted in advance.

aaa234541e4d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
aaa234541e4d.sentence: For example, for one of our Java backends, queries consume around 15 ms of CPU on average but some queries can easily require up to 10 seconds.

91d1d9347f49.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
91d1d9347f49.sentence: A given datacenter may have machines with CPUs of varying performance, and therefore, the same request may represent a significantly different amount of work for different machines.

d2b82205c27b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
d2b82205c27b.sentence: In theory, the solution to working with heterogeneous resource capacity in a fleet is simple: scale the CPU reservations depending on the processor/machine type.

ec7dd9c0ed9a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
ec7dd9c0ed9a.sentence: In an attempt to mitigate this complexity, we created a virtual unit for CPU rate called "GCU" (Google Compute Units).

ea500be4767a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
ea500be4767a.sentence: GCUs became the standard for modeling CPU rates, and were used to maintain a mapping from each CPU architecture in our datacenters to its corresponding GCU based upon its performance.

12640fb94002.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
12640fb94002.sentence: Weâve seen differences in performance of this nature of up to 20%.

366f94b1c35c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
366f94b1c35c.sentence: Other processes (often completely unrelated and run by different teams) can have a significant impact on the performance of your processes.

f6d303a83a98.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
f6d303a83a98.sentence: When a task gets restarted, it often requires significantly more resources for a few minutes.

fbafac85ad7c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
fbafac85ad7c.sentence: This example illustrates how poor in-datacenter load balancing practices artificially limit resource availability: you may be reserving 1,000 CPUs for your service in a given datacenter, but be unable to actually use more than, say, 700 CPUs.

d401960ee4ca.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
d401960ee4ca.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
d401960ee4ca.sentence: Virtual IP addresses (VIPs) are not assigned to any particular network interface.

51063c17b59a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
51063c17b59a.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
51063c17b59a.sentence: Instead, they are usually shared across many devices.

c7d54e8492e5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
c7d54e8492e5.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
c7d54e8492e5.sentence: However, from the userâs perspective, the VIP remains a single, regular IP address.

028fa9059a05.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
028fa9059a05.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
028fa9059a05.sentence: In practice, the most important part of VIP implementation is a device called the network load balancer.

27f77265533e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
27f77265533e.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
27f77265533e.sentence: The balancer receives packets and forwards them to one of the machines behind the VIP.

ad7c20f00e43.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
ad7c20f00e43.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
ad7c20f00e43.sentence: In theory, this practice allows us to hide implementation details (such as the number of machines behind a particular VIP) and facilitates maintenance, because we can schedule upgrades or add more machines to the pool without the user knowing.

8506b132d23f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
8506b132d23f.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
8506b132d23f.sentence: The first (and perhaps most intuitive) approach is to always prefer the least loaded backend.

c98005794df2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
c98005794df2.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
c98005794df2.sentence: Unfortunately, this logic breaks down quickly in the case of stateful protocols, which must use the same backend for the duration of a request.

20cdb49b286b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
20cdb49b286b.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
20cdb49b286b.sentence: This requirement means that the balancer must keep track of all connections sent through it in order to make sure that all subsequent packets are sent to the correct backend.

0e9f76b812a2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
0e9f76b812a2.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
0e9f76b812a2.sentence: The alternative is to use some parts of a packet to create a connection ID (possibly using a hash function and some information from the packet), and to use the connection ID to select a backend.

1b5644012a6b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
1b5644012a6b.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
1b5644012a6b.sentence: This avoids storing state, and all packets belonging to a single connection are always forwarded to the same backend.

d9fcd0d26b58.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
d9fcd0d26b58.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
d9fcd0d26b58.sentence: What happens if one backend fails and needs to be removed from the backend list?

1769d771f87f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
1769d771f87f.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
1769d771f87f.sentence: Suddenly N becomes N-1 and then, id(packet) mod N becomes id(packet) mod N-1.

4ad36e5a6fbe.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
4ad36e5a6fbe.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
4ad36e5a6fbe.sentence: Almost every packet suddenly maps to a different backend!

5564e48cbf78.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
5564e48cbf78.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
5564e48cbf78.sentence: If backends donât share any state between themselves, this remapping forces a reset of almost all of the existing connections.

42dcfacba022.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
42dcfacba022.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
42dcfacba022.sentence: Fortunately, there is an alternate solution that doesnât require keeping the state of every connection in memory, but wonât force all connections to reset when a single machine goes down: consistent hashing.

8a2e3871e6d6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
8a2e3871e6d6.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
8a2e3871e6d6.sentence: Proposed in 1997, consistent hashing [Kar97] describes a way to provide a mapping algorithm that remains relatively stable even when new backends are added to or removed from the list.

569a47e4036d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
569a47e4036d.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
569a47e4036d.sentence: This approach minimizes the disruption to existing connections when the pool of backends changes.

2a0cdb7497a8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
2a0cdb7497a8.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
2a0cdb7497a8.sentence: As a result, we can usually use simple connection tracking, but fall back to consistent hashing when the system is under pressure (e.g., during an ongoing denial of service attack).

02dc08e3327a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
02dc08e3327a.sentence: Instead, it is better to allow an error budgetâa rate at which the SLOs can be missedâand track that on a daily or weekly basis.

c15e1772fbd6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
c15e1772fbd6.sentence: The error budget provides a clear, objective metric that determines how unreliable the service is allowed to be within a single quarter.

345ae5c8668f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
345ae5c8668f.sentence: Itâs both unrealistic and undesirable to insist that SLOs will be met 100% of the time: doing so can reduce the rate of innovation and deployment, require expensive, overly conservative solutions, or both.

98192a993173.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
98192a993173.sentence: (An error budget is just an SLO for meeting other SLOs!)

72769855766d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
72769855766d.sentence: In order to base these decisions on objective data, the two teams jointly define a quarterly error budget based on the serviceâs service level objective, or SLO (see Service Level Objectives).

8b9189d5e466.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
8b9189d5e466.sentence: - Product Management defines an SLO, which sets an expectation of how much uptime the service should have per quarter.

493e60727f9c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
493e60727f9c.sentence: - The actual uptime is measured by a neutral third party: our monitoring system.

86c9907467be.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
86c9907467be.sentence: - The difference between these two numbers is the "budget" of how much "unreliability" is remaining for the quarter.

36d0e5cc8d55.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
36d0e5cc8d55.sentence: - As long as the uptime measured is above the SLOâin other words, as long as there is error budget remainingânew releases can be pushed.

2b93d6c87d07.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
2b93d6c87d07.sentence: For example, imagine that a serviceâs SLO is to successfully serve 99.999% of all queries per quarter.

e32ba3e1e43e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
e32ba3e1e43e.sentence: This means that the serviceâs error budget is a failure rate of 0.001% for a given quarter.

2413e952f123.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
2413e952f123.sentence: If a problem causes us to fail 0.0002% of the expected queries for the quarter, the problem spends 20% of the serviceâs quarterly error budget.

f4414756f2fd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
f4414756f2fd.sentence: Product development performance is largely evaluated on product velocity, which creates an incentive to push new code as quickly as possible.

8afb7feea987.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
8afb7feea987.sentence: Meanwhile, SRE performance is (unsurprisingly) evaluated based upon reliability of a service, which implies an incentive to push back against a high rate of change.

f23a186ba24f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
f23a186ba24f.sentence: This metric removes the politics from negotiations between the SREs and the product developers when deciding how much risk to allow.

4c3063b49c57.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
4c3063b49c57.sentence: The main benefit of an error budget is that it provides a common incentive that allows both product development and SRE to focus on finding the right balance between innovation and reliability.

e8343b24cf3e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
e8343b24cf3e.sentence: Many products use this control loop to manage release velocity: as long as the systemâs SLOs are met, releases can continue.

8e4d56d2d786.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
8e4d56d2d786.sentence: If SLO violations occur frequently enough to expend the error budget, releases are temporarily halted while additional resources are invested in system testing and development to make the system more resilient, improve its performance, and so on.

794dff805f68.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
794dff805f68.sentence: More subtle and effective approaches are available than this simple on/off technique:15 for instance, slowing down releases or rolling them back when the SLO-violation error budget is close to being used up.

a2a93f9e530c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
a2a93f9e530c.sentence: When the budget is large, the product developers can take more risks.

a31ec41144ef.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
a31ec41144ef.sentence: When the budget is nearly drained, the product developers themselves will push for more testing or slower push velocity, as they donât want to risk using up the budget and stall their launch.

b8c13e6b3a1a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
b8c13e6b3a1a.sentence: In effect, the product development team becomes self-policing.

2a732a7a9dba.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
2a732a7a9dba.sentence: (Of course, this outcome relies on an SRE team having the authority to actually stop launches if the SLO is broken.)

12e0b203b143.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
12e0b203b143.sentence: What happens if a network outage or datacenter failure reduces the measured SLO?

932765dcf3aa.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
932765dcf3aa.sentence: Such events also eat into the error budget.

35c974865423.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
35c974865423.sentence: As a result, the number of new pushes may be reduced for the remainder of the quarter.

bdc1af1c6d7f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
bdc1af1c6d7f.sentence: If the team is having trouble launching new features, they may elect to loosen the SLO (thus increasing the error budget) in order to increase innovation.

55b36e34e23b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
55b36e34e23b.sentence: It turns out that past a certain point, however, increasing reliability is worse for a service (and its users) rather than better!

71a86999db19.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
71a86999db19.sentence: Extreme reliability comes at a cost: maximizing stability limits how fast new features can be developed and how quickly products can be delivered to users, and dramatically increases their cost, which in turn reduces the numbers of features a team can afford to offer.

c7ec69166599.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
c7ec69166599.sentence: Further, users typically donât notice the difference between high reliability and extreme reliability in a service, because the user experience is dominated by less reliable components like the cellular network or the device they are working with.

b39fe2f11d97.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
b39fe2f11d97.sentence: Put simply, a user on a 99% reliable smartphone cannot tell the difference between 99.99% and 99.999% service reliability!

eb4985162868.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
eb4985162868.sentence: However, experience shows that as we build systems, cost does not increase linearly as reliability incrementsâan incremental improvement in reliability may cost 100x more than the previous increment.

973cbacc2be0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
973cbacc2be0.sentence: The cost of redundant machine/compute resources

b19b7655df1d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
b19b7655df1d.sentence: The cost associated with redundant equipment that, for example, allows us to take systems offline for routine or unforeseen maintenance, or provides space for us to store parity code blocks that provide a minimum data durability guarantee.

9a62f984b288.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
9a62f984b288.sentence: The cost borne by an organization when it allocates engineering resources to build systems or features that diminish risk instead of features that are directly visible to or usable by end users.

edd3b4cba627.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
edd3b4cba627.sentence: In SRE, we manage service reliability largely by managing risk.

6eb98287d6d5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
6eb98287d6d5.sentence: We conceptualize risk as a continuum.

44b777856dde.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
44b777856dde.sentence: Doing so allows us to perform a cost/benefit analysis to determine, for example, where on the (nonlinear) risk continuum we should place Search, Ads, Gmail, or Photos.

5e08385c21fc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
5e08385c21fc.sentence: Our goal is to explicitly align the risk taken by a given service with the risk the business is willing to bear.

a126b32ea0a0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
a126b32ea0a0.sentence: We strive to make a service reliable enough, but no more reliable than it needs to be.

16d65fc53230.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
16d65fc53230.sentence: That is, when we set an availability target of 99.99%,we want to exceed it, but not by much: that would waste opportunities to add features to the system, clean up technical debt, or reduce its operational costs.

b6400eb1ce3a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
b6400eb1ce3a.sentence: In a sense, we view the availability target as both a minimum and a maximum.

4c1ab62554b2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
4c1ab62554b2.sentence: The four golden signals of monitoring are latency, traffic, errors, and saturation.

b9c039e225c5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
b9c039e225c5.sentence: If you can only measure four metrics of your user-facing system, focus on these four.

69730d31b740.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
69730d31b740.sentence: The time it takes to service a request.

3f863680780a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
3f863680780a.sentence: Itâs important to distinguish between the latency of successful requests and the latency of failed requests.

cfde8c74e9b2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
cfde8c74e9b2.sentence: For example, an HTTP 500 error triggered due to loss of connection to a database or other critical backend might be served very quickly; however, as an HTTP 500 error indicates a failed request, factoring 500s into your overall latency might result in misleading calculations.

4c9bf8ae0c74.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
4c9bf8ae0c74.sentence: On the other hand, a slow error is even worse than a fast error!

bf310d168932.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
bf310d168932.sentence: Therefore, itâs important to track error latency, as opposed to just filtering out errors.

484924ac7be1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
484924ac7be1.sentence: A measure of how much demand is being placed on your system, measured in a high-level system-specific metric.

71783527fdee.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
71783527fdee.sentence: For a web service, this measurement is usually HTTP requests per second, perhaps broken out by the nature of the requests (e.g., static versus dynamic content).

4203be967a38.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
4203be967a38.sentence: For an audio streaming system, this measurement might focus on network I/O rate or concurrent sessions.

355a1b217ec9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
355a1b217ec9.sentence: For a key-value storage system, this measurement might be transactions and retrievals per second.

ebec6c5fea06.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
ebec6c5fea06.sentence: The rate of requests that fail, either explicitly (e.g., HTTP 500s), implicitly (for example, an HTTP 200 success response, but coupled with the wrong content), or by policy (for example, "If you committed to one-second response times, any request over one second is an error").

3e04c17c58d5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
3e04c17c58d5.sentence: Monitoring these cases can be drastically different: catching HTTP 500s at your load balancer can do a decent job of catching all completely failed requests, while only end-to-end system tests can detect that youâre serving the wrong content.

8ebd6b10786e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
8ebd6b10786e.sentence: A measure of your system fraction, emphasizing the resources that are most constrained (e.g., in a memory-constrained system, show memory; in an I/O-constrained system, show I/O).

6163c06209dc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
6163c06209dc.sentence: Note that many systems degrade in performance before they achieve 100% utilization, so having a utilization target is essential.

3da8123a2731.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
3da8123a2731.sentence: Latency increases are often a leading indicator of saturation.

7c6075ab6d9b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
7c6075ab6d9b.sentence: Finally, saturation is also concerned with predictions of impending saturation, such as "It looks like your database will fill its hard drive in 4 hours."

337dde805742.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
337dde805742.sentence: If you measure all four golden signals and page a human when one signal is problematic (or, in the case of saturation, nearly problematic), your service will be at least decently covered by monitoring.

47cef41dbd67.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
47cef41dbd67.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
47cef41dbd67.sentence: You shouldnât use every metric you can track in your monitoring system as an SLI; an understanding of what your users want from the system will inform the judicious selection of a few indicators.

e9b8a8476654.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
e9b8a8476654.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
e9b8a8476654.sentence: We typically find that a handful of representative indicators are enough to evaluate and reason about a systemâs health.

13f26c3880ca.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
13f26c3880ca.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
13f26c3880ca.sentence: Choosing too many indicators makes it hard to pay the right level of attention to the indicators that matter, while choosing too few may leave significant behaviors of your system unexamined.

d5809f4408db.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
d5809f4408db.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
d5809f4408db.sentence: - User-facing serving systems, such as the Shakespeare search frontends, generally care about availability, latency, and throughput.

ad830774f295.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
ad830774f295.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
ad830774f295.sentence: - Storage systems often emphasize latency, availability, and durability.

c9181c5a7a71.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
c9181c5a7a71.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
c9181c5a7a71.sentence: - Big data systems, such as data processing pipelines, tend to care about throughput and end-to-end latency.

f7949b1c4872.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
f7949b1c4872.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
f7949b1c4872.sentence: - All systems should care about correctness: was the right answer returned, the right data retrieved, the right analysis done?

ab3672582ed9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
ab3672582ed9.section: What Do You and Your Users Care About?
ab3672582ed9.sentence: Correctness is important to track as an indicator of system health, even though itâs often a property of the data in the system rather than the infrastructure per se, and so usually not an SRE responsibility to meet.

613ce8ba1756.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
613ce8ba1756.sentence: Is the measurement obtained once a second, or by averaging requests over a minute?

24679e975bcc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
24679e975bcc.sentence: The latter may hide much higher instantaneous request rates in bursts that last for only a few seconds.

cad05beef9eb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
cad05beef9eb.sentence: We recommend that you standardize on common definitions for SLIs so that you donât have to reason about them from first principles each time.

cc7cff095e2c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
cc7cff095e2c.sentence: Any feature that conforms to the standard definition templates can be omitted from the specification of an individual SLI, e.g.:

3f2d6b9ef5a3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
3f2d6b9ef5a3.sentence: - Aggregation regions: âAll the tasks in a clusterâ

26061955950b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
26061955950b.sentence: - How frequently measurements are made: âEvery 10 secondsâ

c65efd073717.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
c65efd073717.sentence: - Which requests are included: âHTTP GETs from black-box monitoring jobsâ

468f194ffa8b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
468f194ffa8b.sentence: Choosing targets (SLOs) is not a purely technical activity because of the product and business implications, which should be reflected in both the SLIs and SLOs (and maybe SLAs) that are selected.

ce3645b2ef7d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
ce3645b2ef7d.sentence: Similarly, it may be necessary to trade off certain product attributes against others within the constraints posed by staffing, time to market, hardware availability, and funding.

2099287277d5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
2099287277d5.sentence: While SRE should be part of this conversation, and advise on the risks and viability of different options, weâve learned a few lessons that can help make this a more productive discussion:

2cf6744c55ad.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
2cf6744c55ad.sentence: Start by thinking about (or finding out!) what your users care about, not what you can measure.

f0ed62d4d60a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
f0ed62d4d60a.sentence: Often, what your users care about is difficult or impossible to measure, so youâll end up approximating usersâ needs in some way.

c4879ca94326.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
c4879ca94326.sentence: However, if you simply start with whatâs easy to measure, youâll end up with less useful SLOs.

8706f790c63d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
8706f790c63d.sentence: As a result, weâve sometimes found that working from desired objectives backward to specific indicators works better than choosing indicators and then coming up with targets.

5d2a70108480.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
5d2a70108480.sentence: Donât pick a target based on current performance

478dafa50caa.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
478dafa50caa.sentence: While understanding the merits and limits of a system is essential, adopting values without reflection may lock you into supporting a system that requires heroic efforts to meet its targets, and that cannot be improved without significant redesign.

3cbabe2c3aea.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
3cbabe2c3aea.sentence: Have as few SLOs as possible

5cdba7f5cc8e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
5cdba7f5cc8e.sentence: Choose just enough SLOs to provide good coverage of your systemâs attributes.

d01a61a3aaa2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
d01a61a3aaa2.sentence: Defend the SLOs you pick: if you canât ever win a conversation about priorities by quoting a particular SLO, itâs probably not worth having that SLO.17 However, not all product attributes are amenable to SLOs: itâs hard to specify "user delight" with an SLO.

cfba551e8b97.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
cfba551e8b97.sentence: While itâs tempting to ask for a system that can scale its load "infinitely" without any latency increase and that is "always" available, this requirement is unrealistic.

2ab8fae95f73.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
2ab8fae95f73.sentence: Even a system that approaches such ideals will probably take a long time to design and build, and will be expensive to operateâand probably turn out to be unnecessarily better than what users would be happy (or even delighted) to have.

18ea7674178a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
18ea7674178a.sentence: You can always refine SLO definitions and targets over time as you learn about a systemâs behavior.

c836c01800b5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
c836c01800b5.sentence: Itâs better to start with a loose target that you tighten than to choose an overly strict target that has to be relaxed when you discover itâs unattainable.

ce8b5c5e124d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
ce8b5c5e124d.sentence: SLOs canâand shouldâbe a major driver in prioritizing work for SREs and product developers, because they reflect what users care about.

9b0509dd9037.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
9b0509dd9037.sentence: A good SLO is a helpful, legitimate forcing function for a development team.

b46dcba159d9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
b46dcba159d9.sentence: But a poorly thought-out SLO can result in wasted work if a team uses heroic efforts to meet an overly aggressive SLO, or a bad product if the SLO is too lax.

15c1e49c1fb9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
15c1e49c1fb9.sentence: SLOs are a massive lever: use them wisely.

3713df141305.title: Chaos engineering
3713df141305.sentence: Chaos engineering is the discipline of experimenting on a system in order to build confidence in the system's capability to withstand turbulent conditions in production.

3a41699fa3ef.title: Chaos engineering
3a41699fa3ef.sentence: In software development, the ability of a given software to tolerate failures while still ensuring adequate quality of service—often termed resilience—is typically specified as a requirement.

1c0d712dc918.title: Chaos engineering
1c0d712dc918.sentence: However, development teams may fail to meet this requirement due to factors such as short deadlines or lack of domain knowledge.

dfafbb70d65d.title: Chaos engineering
dfafbb70d65d.sentence: Chaos engineering encompasses techniques aimed at meeting resilience requirements.

9f9f7b3948ec.title: Chaos engineering
9f9f7b3948ec.sentence: Chaos engineering can be used to achieve resilience against infrastructure failures, network failures, and application failures; The latter includes resilience to unhandled exceptions.

9a6fac502676.title: Chaos engineering
9a6fac502676.sentence: We have created Chaos Monkey, a program that randomly chooses a server and disables it during its usual hours of activity.

57e474c3c593.title: Chaos engineering
57e474c3c593.sentence: It works by intentionally disabling computers in Netflix's production network to test how the remaining systems respond to the outage.

9de316b9f0f2.title: Chaos engineering
9de316b9f0f2.sentence: Knowing that this would happen frequently has created a strong alignment among engineers to build redundancy and process automation to survive such incidents, without impacting the millions of Netflix users.

c105ab10e2ec.title: Chaos engineering
c105ab10e2ec.sentence: By regularly "killing" random instances of a software service, it is possible to test a redundant architecture to verify that a server failure did not noticeably impact customers.

92d360be765a.title: Chaos engineering
92d360be765a.sentence: The intent was to move from a development model that assumed no breakdowns to a model where breakdowns were considered to be inevitable, driving developers to consider built-in resilience to be an obligation rather than an option:

a78b8b39267b.title: Chaos engineering
