a78b8b39267b.sentence: The Simian Army is a suite of tools developed by Netflix to test the reliability, security, or resilience of its Amazon Web Services infrastructure and includes the following tools:

24001cd66b41.title: Chaos engineering
24001cd66b41.sentence: - At the very top of the Simian Army hierarchy, Chaos Kong drops a full AWS "Region".

b3bf8433599b.title: Chaos engineering
b3bf8433599b.sentence: Though rare, loss of an entire region does happen and Chaos Kong simulates a systems response and recovery to this type of event.

a234e565c84b.title: Chaos engineering
a234e565c84b.sentence: - Chaos Gorilla drops a full Amazon "Availability Zone" (one or more entire data centers serving a geographical region).

c6f8794112f0.title: Chaos engineering
c6f8794112f0.sentence: While working to improve website reliability at Amazon, Jesse Robbins created "Game day", an initiative that increases reliability by purposefully creating major failures on a regular basis.

f0f56a1c85e6.title: Chaos engineering
f0f56a1c85e6.sentence: Robbins has said it was inspired by firefighter training and research in other fields lessons in complex systems, reliability engineering.

1c973b500562.title: Chaos engineering
1c973b500562.sentence: While at Google, Kripa Krishnan created a similar program to Amazon's Game day (see above) called "DiRT" (Disaster Recovery Testing).

204699d6fc0f.title: Chaos engineering
204699d6fc0f.sentence: Operational readiness can be evaluated using chaos engineering simulations.

50bb4803120d.title: Chaos engineering
50bb4803120d.sentence: An evaluation to induce chaos in a Kubernetes environment terminated random pods receiving data from edge devices in data centers while processing analytics on a big data network.

82ce6021d2cc.title: Chaos engineering
82ce6021d2cc.sentence: The pods' recovery time was a resiliency metric that estimated the response time.

72a5fc464ba4.title: Business continuity planning
72a5fc464ba4.sentence: Business continuity may be defined as "the capability of an organization to continue the delivery of products or services at pre-defined acceptable levels following a disruptive incident", and business continuity planning (or business continuity and resiliency planning) is the process of creating systems of prevention and recovery to deal with potential threats to a company.

9c7102ed9f5e.title: Business continuity planning
9c7102ed9f5e.sentence: Business continuity is the intended outcome of proper execution of both business continuity planning and disaster recovery.

878a4d0290ac.title: Business continuity planning
878a4d0290ac.sentence: In addition to prevention, the goal is to enable ongoing operations before and during execution of disaster recovery.

ea0f43063524.title: Business continuity planning
ea0f43063524.sentence: As such, BCP is a subset of risk management.

ae4e0916312a.title: Business continuity planning
ae4e0916312a.sentence: Any event that could negatively impact operations should be included in the plan, such as supply chain interruption, loss of or damage to critical infrastructure (major machinery or computing/network resource).

ab4a495c5b04.title: Business continuity planning
ab4a495c5b04.sentence: A business continuity plan outlines a range of disaster scenarios and the steps the business will take in any particular scenario to return to regular trade.

4fbf4e443e0e.title: Business continuity planning
4fbf4e443e0e.sentence: BCP's are written ahead of time and can also include precautions to be put in place.

489738eae4aa.title: Business continuity planning
489738eae4aa.sentence: Continuity does not need to apply to every activity which the organization undertakes.

6e3195363d1e.title: Business continuity planning
6e3195363d1e.sentence: For example, under ISO 22301:2019, organizations are required to define their business continuity objectives, the minimum levels of product and service operations which will be considered acceptable and the maximum tolerable period of disruption (MTPD) which can be allowed.

db24bf2a8b9e.title: Business continuity planning
db24bf2a8b9e.section: Implementation and testing > Testing and organizational acceptance
db24bf2a8b9e.sentence: The 2008 book Exercising for Excellence, published by The British Standards Institution identified three types of exercises that can be employed when testing business continuity plans.

8a3f0961fb9c.title: Business continuity planning
8a3f0961fb9c.section: Implementation and testing > Testing and organizational acceptance
8a3f0961fb9c.sentence: - Tabletop exercises - a small number of people concentrate on a specific aspect of a BCP.

883c47377be0.title: Business continuity planning
883c47377be0.section: Implementation and testing > Testing and organizational acceptance
883c47377be0.sentence: - Medium exercises - Several departments, teams or disciplines concentrate on multiple BCP aspects; the scope can range from a few teams from one building to multiple teams operating across dispersed locations.

39c0e8a33521.title: Business continuity planning
39c0e8a33521.section: Implementation and testing > Testing and organizational acceptance

55e75bdd420a.title: Business continuity planning
55e75bdd420a.section: Implementation and testing > Testing and organizational acceptance
55e75bdd420a.sentence: - Complex exercises - All aspects of a medium exercise remain, but for maximum realism no-notice activation, actual evacuation and actual invocation of a disaster recovery site is added.

400f802e117d.title: Business continuity planning
400f802e117d.sentence: Biannual or annual maintenance cycle maintenance of a BCP manual is broken down into three periodic activities.

cb000ef8359e.title: Business continuity planning
cb000ef8359e.sentence: - Confirmation of information in the manual, roll out to staff for awareness and specific training for critical individuals.

d5ad72577bf4.title: Business continuity planning
d5ad72577bf4.sentence: - Testing and verification of technical solutions established for recovery operations.

fb331c5e0688.title: Business continuity planning
fb331c5e0688.sentence: - Testing and verification of organization recovery procedures.

5c753a4dcf92.title: Business continuity planning
5c753a4dcf92.section: Maintenance > Testing and verification of recovery procedures
5c753a4dcf92.sentence: Software and work process changes must be documented and validated, including verification that documented work process recovery tasks and supporting disaster recovery infrastructure allow staff to recover within the predetermined recovery time objective.

9123f71088b4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
9123f71088b4.sentence: - Primary-Backup: the backup node is just a stand-by, and the data is replicated from primary to backup.

77bc2d2d38d8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
77bc2d2d38d8.sentence: - Primary-Secondary: this architecture looks similar to primary-backup architecture, but the secondary node can take read requests to balance the reading load.

a470aa7a29e5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
a470aa7a29e5.sentence: - Primary-Primary: both nodes act as primary nodes, both nodes can handle read/write operations, and the data is replicated between the two nodes.

a1ba9c7f8075.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
a1ba9c7f8075.sentence: In the famous CAP theorem by computer scientist Eric Brewer, Availability means ​​all (non-failing) nodes are available for queries in a distributed system.

28fc38dc6142.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
28fc38dc6142.sentence: When you send out requests to the nodes, a non-failing node will return a reasonable response within a reasonable amount of time (with no error or timeout).

00173f16d5a0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
00173f16d5a0.sentence: For example, when we say the design target is 4-9’s, it means the services should be up 99.99% of the time.

8c86ca6c815b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
8c86ca6c815b.sentence: This also means the services can only be down for 52.5 minutes per year.

b4dd1f82f1f6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
b4dd1f82f1f6.sentence: Note that availability only guarantees that we will receive a response; it doesn’t guarantee the data is the most up-to-date.

ce32937b8fc1.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
ce32937b8fc1.sentence: When the primary fails, we need to manually switch to the backup node.

6182987362ba.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
6182987362ba.sentence: The backup node might be a waste of hardware resources.

f869595f58ce.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
f869595f58ce.sentence: Due to latency when replicating data from primary to secondary, the data read from the secondary may be inconsistent with the primary.

79a734510924.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
79a734510924.sentence: This type of architecture increases the throughput, but it has limited use cases.

13b046f2a7c9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
13b046f2a7c9.sentence: For example, if both nodes need to update the same product, the final state might be unpredictable.

e3fd449de534.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-for-high-availability.md
e3fd449de534.sentence: If we deploy the node on Amazon EC2, which has 90% availability, the double-node architecture will increase availability from 90% to 99%.

e208cabc00b3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
e208cabc00b3.sentence: Logging, tracing, and metrics are 3 pillars of system observability.

07fe0b08a260.title: Site reliability engineering
07fe0b08a260.sentence: - Observability, the ability to ask arbitrary questions about a system without having to know ahead of time what to ask.

e2393d50149c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
e2393d50149c.sentence: Logging records discrete events in the system.

aba154068b29.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
aba154068b29.sentence: For example, we can record an incoming request or a visit to databases as events.

6940cadb5c35.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
6940cadb5c35.sentence: We often define a standardized logging format for different teams to implement, so that we can leverage keywords when searching among massive amounts of logs.

c43b8bc9d465.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
c43b8bc9d465.sentence: ELK (Elastic-Logstash-Kibana) stack is often used to build a log analysis platform.

90ff4b9b650a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
90ff4b9b650a.sentence: For example, a user request goes through the API gateway, load balancer, service A, service B, and database, which can be visualized in the tracing systems.

f77331bd3d79.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
f77331bd3d79.sentence: This is useful when we are trying to identify the bottlenecks in the system.

8d68292fe034.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
8d68292fe034.sentence: Metrics are usually aggregatable information from the system.

590ffce595c7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
590ffce595c7.sentence: For example, service QPS, API responsiveness, service latency, etc. The raw data is recorded in time-series databases like InfluxDB.

839d1b7260f8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
839d1b7260f8.sentence: Prometheus pulls the data and transforms the data based on pre-defined alerting rules.

3654985b5502.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
3654985b5502.sentence: Then the data is sent to Grafana for display or to the alert manager which then sends out email, SMS, or Slack notifications or alerts.

4e68c7b36eea.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/logging-tracing-metrics.md
4e68c7b36eea.sentence: We use OpenTelemetry to showcase the typical architecture, which unifies the 3 pillars in a single framework.

c8ab11236f93.title: Observability (software)
c8ab11236f93.section: Etymology, terminology and definition > Observability vs. monitoring
c8ab11236f93.sentence: The terms are commonly contrasted in that systems are monitored using predefined sets of telemetry, and monitored systems may be observable.

db5549266251.title: Observability (software)
db5549266251.sentence: Observability is based on exploring properties and patterns not defined in advance.

f49f65c34826.title: Observability (software)
f49f65c34826.sentence: Metrics are typically tagged to facilitate grouping and searchability.

ee7829f14c2a.title: Observability (software)
ee7829f14c2a.sentence: Since metrics are cardinality-limited, they are often used to represent aggregate values (for example: average page load time, or 5-second average of the request rate).

26eac7e3a296.title: Observability (software)
26eac7e3a296.sentence: As a result, when a previously unknown issue is encountered, it is impossible to add new metrics without shipping new code.

6e4b8883863e.title: Observability (software)
6e4b8883863e.sentence: As with metrics, an application developer must instrument the application upfront and ship new code if different logging information is required.

392007a58e53.title: Site reliability engineering
392007a58e53.sentence: Site reliability engineering (SRE) is a discipline in the field of software engineering and IT infrastructure support that monitors and improves the availability and performance of deployed software systems and large software services (which are expected to deliver reliable response times across events such as new software deployments, hardware failures, and cybersecurity attacks).

656a8682f560.title: Site reliability engineering
656a8682f560.sentence: SRE uses elements of software engineering, IT infrastructure, web development, and operations to assist with reliability.

abf2c654ce36.title: Site reliability engineering
abf2c654ce36.sentence: Site reliability engineers (SREs) are responsible for a combination of system availability, latency, performance, efficiency, change management, monitoring, emergency response, and capacity planning.

16b647288b39.title: Site reliability engineering
16b647288b39.sentence: The focuses of SRE include automation, system design, and improvements to system resilience.

ad2167397523.title: Site reliability engineering
ad2167397523.sentence: There is typically a focus on automation and an infrastructure as code methodology.

93c65526ab62.title: Site reliability engineering
93c65526ab62.sentence: SRE is considered a specific implementation of DevOps; focusing specifically on building reliable systems, whereas DevOps covers a broader scope of operations.

dec2b6c7c1c5.title: Site reliability engineering
dec2b6c7c1c5.sentence: It is similar to DevOps as they both aim to improve the reliability and availability of deployed software systems.

285194f62d9a.title: Site reliability engineering
285194f62d9a.sentence: - Automation of repetitive tasks for cost-effectiveness.

03f3bc76df6f.title: Site reliability engineering
03f3bc76df6f.sentence: - Defining reliability goals to prevent endless effort.

c983cffc6085.title: Site reliability engineering
c983cffc6085.sentence: - Design of systems with a goal to reduce risks to availability, latency, and efficiency.

fe0cf0c3c295.title: Site reliability engineering
fe0cf0c3c295.sentence: - Toil management, toil refers to manual, repetitive, automatable operational work.

9f0f683bbe28.title: Site reliability engineering
9f0f683bbe28.sentence: - Defining and measuring reliability goals—SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets.

3e2a4d520b3b.title: Site reliability engineering
3e2a4d520b3b.sentence: - Defining, testing, and running an incident management process.

7132cff4f59b.title: Site reliability engineering
7132cff4f59b.sentence: - Change and release management, including CI/CD.

1ad72d7b4298.title: Backup
1ad72d7b4298.sentence: It states that there should be at least 3 copies of the data, stored on 2 different types of storage media, and one copy should be kept offsite, in a remote location (this can include cloud storage).

eaeb9eb933fe.title: Backup
eaeb9eb933fe.sentence: 2 or more different media should be used to eliminate data loss due to similar reasons (for example, optical discs may tolerate being underwater while LTO tapes may not, and SSDs cannot fail due to head crashes or damaged spindle motors since they do not have any moving parts, unlike hard drives).

8256a848ff2c.title: Backup
8256a848ff2c.sentence: An offsite copy protects against fire, theft of physical media (such as tapes or discs) and natural disasters like floods and earthquakes.

e8c1355ba585.title: Backup
e8c1355ba585.sentence: Because there is no perfect storage, many backup experts recommend maintaining a second copy on a local physical device, even if the data is also backed up offsite.

7963648ddd19.title: Backup
7963648ddd19.sentence: Physically protected hard drives are an alternative to an offsite copy, but they have limitations like only being able to resist fire for a limited period of time, so an offsite copy still remains as the ideal choice.

1f4feb5a7c43.title: Backup
1f4feb5a7c43.sentence: Ransomware can still overwrite data on a backup drive if it is plugged and accessible to a computer.

755744b06ad1.title: Backup
755744b06ad1.sentence: Because of this, it is recommended to disconnect at least one of the backup media if not in use.

ee8101fb7456.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
ee8101fb7456.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
ee8101fb7456.sentence: To sum up our advice for guarding against the 24 combinations of data integrity failure modes: addressing a broad range of scenarios at reasonable cost demands a tiered backup strategy.

cbc094d2f1dc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
cbc094d2f1dc.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
cbc094d2f1dc.sentence: The first tier comprises many frequent and quickly restored backups stored closest to the live datastores, perhaps using the same or similar storage technologies as the data sources.

e0172c8c4963.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
e0172c8c4963.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
e0172c8c4963.sentence: Subsequent tiers take advantage of nearline storage such as dedicated tape libraries and offsite storage of the backup media (e.g., tapes or disk drives).

564eacc54f2d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
564eacc54f2d.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
564eacc54f2d.sentence: The most important principle in this layer is that backups donât matter; what matters is recovery.

de9fcab8b210.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
de9fcab8b210.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
de9fcab8b210.sentence: The factors supporting successful recovery should drive your backup decisions, not the other way around.

6dea67d8cd80.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
6dea67d8cd80.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
6dea67d8cd80.sentence: In other words, the scenarios in which you want your backups to help you recover should dictate the following:

857a3700689c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
857a3700689c.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
857a3700689c.sentence: - Which backup and recovery methods to use

0c13b5648cde.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
0c13b5648cde.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
0c13b5648cde.sentence: - How frequently you establish restore points by taking full or incremental backups of your data

4a7617a7a29f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
4a7617a7a29f.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods

3a62a45a6c31.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
3a62a45a6c31.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods

ba14e9d9f0df.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
ba14e9d9f0df.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
ba14e9d9f0df.sentence: How much recent data can you afford to lose during a recovery effort?

5c3bdb9c21cf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
5c3bdb9c21cf.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
5c3bdb9c21cf.sentence: The less data you can afford to lose, the more serious you should be about an incremental backup strategy.

f021feb41e7e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
f021feb41e7e.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
f021feb41e7e.sentence: Even if money isnât a limitation, frequent full backups are expensive in other ways.

017d44dafe54.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
017d44dafe54.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
017d44dafe54.sentence: Most notably, they impose a compute burden on the live datastores of your service while itâs serving users, driving your service closer to its scalability and performance limits.

2db39f3911c8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
2db39f3911c8.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
2db39f3911c8.sentence: To ease this burden, you can take full backups during off-peak hours, and then a series of incremental backups when your service is busier.

a00a8a860e33.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
a00a8a860e33.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
a00a8a860e33.sentence: The faster your users need to be rescued, the more local your backups should be.

aaa27cf7a258.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
aaa27cf7a258.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
aaa27cf7a258.sentence: Often Google retains costly but quick-to-restore snapshots129 for very short periods of time within the storage instance, and stores less recent backups on random access distributed storage within the same (or nearby) datacenter for a slightly longer time.

1b4abff5f4ba.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
1b4abff5f4ba.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
1b4abff5f4ba.sentence: Such a strategy alone would not protect from site-level failures, so those backups are often transferred to nearline or offline locations for a longer time period before theyâre expired in favor of newer backups.

3d2681c582cf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
3d2681c582cf.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
3d2681c582cf.sentence: In Googleâs experience, low-grade data mutation or deletion bugs within application code demand the furthest reaches back in time, as some of those bugs were noticed months after the first data loss began.

1509b7d94611.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
1509b7d94611.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
1509b7d94611.sentence: Your backup strategy becomes more costly the further back you reach, while the scenarios from which you can hope to recover increase (although this increase is subject to diminishing returns).

280a66ae7b40.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
280a66ae7b40.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
280a66ae7b40.sentence: On the flip side, in a high-velocity development environment, changes to code and schema may render older backups expensive or impossible to use.

2bad493f38cb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
2bad493f38cb.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
2bad493f38cb.sentence: Google chose to draw the line between 30 and 90 days of backups for many services.

7b0a006579b9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
7b0a006579b9.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
7b0a006579b9.sentence: Doing so confers protection from the majority of scenarios involving software bugs and developer error.

31f8861e1694.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
31f8861e1694.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
31f8861e1694.sentence: Due to relative expense, backups are retained in this tier for anywhere from hours to single-digit days, and may take minutes to restore.

95865368339c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
95865368339c.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
95865368339c.sentence: The second tier comprises fewer backups retained for single-digit or low double-digit days on random access distributed filesystems local to the site.

862bd5f868b0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
862bd5f868b0.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
862bd5f868b0.sentence: These backups may take hours to restore and confer additional protection from mishaps affecting particular storage technologies in your serving stack, but not the technologies used to contain the backups.

124b687df7fc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
124b687df7fc.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
124b687df7fc.sentence: This tier also protects against bugs in your application that are detected too late to rely upon the first tier of your backup strategy.

c771fe461b6b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
c771fe461b6b.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
c771fe461b6b.sentence: Backups in these tiers confer protection against site-level issues, such as a datacenter power outage or distributed filesystem corruption due to a bug.

d5522c38c3bb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
d5522c38c3bb.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
d5522c38c3bb.sentence: It is expensive to move large amounts of data to and from tiers.

bae21737a1ad.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
bae21737a1ad.section: Second Layer: Backups and Their Related Recovery Methods
bae21737a1ad.sentence: As a result, backups in these tiers tend to be taken less frequently but retained longer.

7bb9d4a5719c.title: Backup
7bb9d4a5719c.section: Selection and extraction of data > Live data
7bb9d4a5719c.sentence: Files that are actively being updated present a challenge to back up.

085805333ce5.title: Backup
085805333ce5.section: Selection and extraction of data > Live data
085805333ce5.sentence: One way to back up live data is to temporarily quiesce them (e.g., close all files), take a "snapshot", and then resume live operations.

a71607191c8b.title: Backup
a71607191c8b.section: Selection and extraction of data > Live data
a71607191c8b.sentence: At this point the snapshot can be backed up through normal methods.

16c606a5023d.title: Backup
16c606a5023d.section: Selection and extraction of data > Live data
16c606a5023d.sentence: A snapshot is an instantaneous function of some filesystems that presents a copy of the filesystem as if it were frozen at a specific point in time, often by a copy-on-write mechanism.

3206266493b8.title: Backup
3206266493b8.section: Selection and extraction of data > Live data
3206266493b8.sentence: Snapshotting a file while it is being changed results in a corrupted file that is unusable.

95a0bc6bc792.title: Backup

c4fcbf94f458.title: Backup

c4fcbf94f458.sentence: The term fuzzy backup can be used to describe a backup of live data that looks like it ran correctly, but does not represent the state of the data at a single point in time.

f2e4f87b381b.sentence: - Interrelated database files backup: Some interrelated database file systems offer a means to generate a "hot backup" of the database while it is online and usable.

b55e3ba5211b.sentence: This may include a snapshot of the data files plus a snapshotted log of changes made while the backup is running.

098d9d183c66.title: Backup
098d9d183c66.section: Selection and extraction of data > Live data
098d9d183c66.sentence: Upon a restore, the changes in the log files are applied to bring the copy of the database up to the point in time at which the initial backup ended.

04f533c7f040.title: Backup

cb9ec46444cd.title: IT disaster recovery
cb9ec46444cd.sentence: The disaster recovery strategy derives from the business continuity plan.

6b562f67a256.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::disaster-recovery
6b562f67a256.sentence: A variety of disaster recovery (DR) strategies can be part of a disaster recovery plan.

91fbaf286834.title: IT disaster recovery
91fbaf286834.sentence: A cost-benefit analysis highlights which disaster recovery measures are appropriate.

af0cf92314f3.title: IT disaster recovery
af0cf92314f3.sentence: Different strategies make sense based on the cost of downtime compared to the cost of implementing a particular strategy.

622aa3fbbf52.title: IT disaster recovery
622aa3fbbf52.sentence: - backups to tape and sent off-site

733a7498fa09.title: IT disaster recovery
733a7498fa09.sentence: - backups to disk on-site (copied to off-site disk) or off-site

983761b50e0a.title: IT disaster recovery
983761b50e0a.sentence: - replication off-site, such that once the systems are restored or synchronized, possibly via storage area network technology

727874dcef3e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::disaster-recovery
727874dcef3e.sentence: This is the simplest type of disaster recovery and involves storing data off-site or on a removable drive.

1186f6109759.title: IT disaster recovery
1186f6109759.sentence: - private cloud solutions that replicate metadata (VMs, templates and disks) into the private cloud.

6171b6610855.title: IT disaster recovery
6171b6610855.sentence: - hybrid cloud solutions that replicate both on-site and to off-site data centers.

537d3c6c03cd.title: IT disaster recovery
537d3c6c03cd.sentence: This provides instant fail-over to on-site hardware or to cloud data centers.

87052f0059df.title: IT disaster recovery
87052f0059df.sentence: - high availability systems which keep both the data and system replicated off-site, enabling continuous access to systems and data, even after a disaster (often associated with cloud storage).

2549207e86bb.title: IT disaster recovery
2549207e86bb.sentence: Disaster recovery as a service (DRaaS) is an arrangement with a third party vendor to perform some or all DR functions for scenarios such as power outages, equipment failures, cyber attacks, and natural disasters.

431a1352ba50.title: IT disaster recovery
431a1352ba50.sentence: - local mirrors of systems and/or data and use of disk protection technology such as RAID

3962e745952b.title: IT disaster recovery
3962e745952b.sentence: - surge protectors — to minimize the effect of power surges on delicate electronic equipment

44bb0e6f7195.title: IT disaster recovery
44bb0e6f7195.sentence: - use of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) and/or backup generator to keep systems going in the event of a power failure

cca412c14d20.title: IT disaster recovery
cca412c14d20.sentence: - fire prevention/mitigation systems such as alarms and fire extinguishers

0bda94c12a63.title: IT disaster recovery
0bda94c12a63.sentence: - anti-virus software and other security measures.

4b63792339e7.title: IT disaster recovery
4b63792339e7.sentence: Control measures are steps or mechanisms that can reduce or eliminate threats.

d676887650a8.title: IT disaster recovery
d676887650a8.sentence: The choice of mechanisms is reflected in a disaster recovery plan (DRP).

15debabe3459.title: IT disaster recovery
15debabe3459.sentence: Control measures can be classified as controls aimed at preventing an event from occurring, controls aimed at detecting or discovering unwanted events, and controls aimed at correcting or restoring the system after a disaster or an event.

fe6932acd9d9.title: IT disaster recovery
fe6932acd9d9.sentence: These controls are documented and exercised regularly using so-called "DR tests".

66091a908336.title: IT disaster recovery
66091a908336.sentence: - Regular testing: Regular testing of the disaster recovery plan can verify its effectiveness and identify any weaknesses or gaps.

2ec846b5d349.title: IT disaster recovery
2ec846b5d349.sentence: - Flexibility: The disaster recovery strategy should be adaptable to support both partial failures (such as recovering specific files) and full environment failures.

0d8de4c9f52a.title: IT disaster recovery
0d8de4c9f52a.sentence: - Clear roles and permissions: It should be clearly defined who is authorized to execute the disaster recovery plan, with separate access and permissions for these individuals.

e51ccc99345f.title: IT disaster recovery
e51ccc99345f.sentence: Implementing a clear separation of permissions between those who can execute the recovery and those who have access to backup data helps minimize the risk of unauthorized actions.

9fbcec6afb7b.title: IT disaster recovery
9fbcec6afb7b.sentence: - Documentation: The plan should be well-documented and easy-to-follow to ensure that operators can effectively follow it during stressful situations.

9add6e2fe598.title: IT disaster recovery
9add6e2fe598.sentence: Research supports the idea that implementing a more holistic pre-disaster planning approach is more cost-effective.

d30a7112a3ae.title: IT disaster recovery
d30a7112a3ae.sentence: Every $1 spent on hazard mitigation (such as a disaster recovery plan) saves society $4 in response and recovery costs.

44aca16e29e0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity

b02c0254efee.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
b02c0254efee.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
b02c0254efee.sentence: Anything and everythingâwhich is why the only test that should let you sleep at night is a full end-to-end test.

899962878d85.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
899962878d85.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
899962878d85.sentence: If you take away just one lesson from this chapter, remember that you only know that you can recover your recent state if you actually do so.

993181e67dab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
993181e67dab.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
993181e67dab.sentence: If recovery tests are a manual, staged event, testing becomes an unwelcome bit of drudgery that isnât performed either deeply or frequently enough to deserve your confidence.

5e2207d2a774.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
5e2207d2a774.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
5e2207d2a774.sentence: Therefore, automate these tests whenever possible and then run them continuously.

286fce9a4bf3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
286fce9a4bf3.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
286fce9a4bf3.sentence: - Are your backups valid and complete, or are they empty?

b3c5e490f21c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
b3c5e490f21c.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
b3c5e490f21c.sentence: - Do you have sufficient machine resources to run all of the setup, restore, and post-processing tasks that comprise your recovery?

cee6fa1d8d1a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
cee6fa1d8d1a.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
cee6fa1d8d1a.sentence: - Does the recovery process complete in reasonable wall time?

ce319ddb51ea.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
ce319ddb51ea.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
ce319ddb51ea.sentence: - Are you able to monitor the state of your recovery process as it progresses?

f81739340166.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
f81739340166.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
f81739340166.sentence: - Are you free of critical dependencies on resources outside of your control, such as access to an offsite media storage vault that isnât available 24/7?

9a7dd551249a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
9a7dd551249a.sentence: System components that arenât continually exercised fail when you need them most.

3ffdb71ea936.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
3ffdb71ea936.sentence: Prove that data recovery works with regular exercise, or data recovery wonât work.

1a52ba55c70b.section: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
1a52ba55c70b.sentence: If testing forces the failures to happen before actual catastrophe strikes, you can fix problems before any harm comes to fruition.

35463b0396fc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
35463b0396fc.sentence: The most important difference between backups and archives is that backups can be loaded back into an application, while archives cannot.

47a01e7139b2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
47a01e7139b2.sentence: However, the real focus of such backup efforts should be data recovery, which distinguishes real backups from archives.

63e7e1a05c68.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
63e7e1a05c68.sentence: Archives safekeep data for long periods of time to meet auditing, discovery, and compliance needs.

93ca410d4594.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
93ca410d4594.sentence: Data recovery for such purposes generally doesnât need to complete within uptime requirements of a service.

4ccecc24e0b1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
4ccecc24e0b1.sentence: Retrieving and recovering the logs during a month-long financial audit may take a week, and this weeklong time window for recovery may be acceptable for an archive.

da1ec3404a1f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
da1ec3404a1f.sentence: On the other hand, when disaster strikes, data must be recovered from real backups quickly, preferably well within the uptime needs of a service.

32f2e6c38642.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
32f2e6c38642.sentence: Otherwise, affected users are left without useful access to the application from the onset of the data integrity issue until the completion of the recovery effort.

96e43e7904fd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
96e43e7904fd.sentence: Itâs also important to consider that because the most recent data is at risk until safely backed up, it may be optimal to schedule real backups (as opposed to archives) to occur daily, hourly, or more frequently, using full and incremental or continuous (streaming) approaches.

72665f85559d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
72665f85559d.sentence: Therefore, when formulating a backup strategy, consider how quickly you need to be able to recover from a problem, and how much recent data you can afford to lose.

e55fd0da9ff9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
e55fd0da9ff9.sentence: As is sometimes observed: No one really wants to make backups; what people really want are restores.

d04b68579540.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
d04b68579540.section: Delivering a Recovery System, Rather Than a Backup System
d04b68579540.sentence: - Teams define service level objectives (SLOs) for data availability in a variety of failure modes.

03d726ca2e33.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
03d726ca2e33.section: Delivering a Recovery System, Rather Than a Backup System
03d726ca2e33.sentence: - A team practices and demonstrates their ability to meet those SLOs.

9794e79a9028.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity

9794e79a9028.sentence: As illustrated by Figure 26-3, at a very high level, there are 24 distinct types of failures when the 3 factors can occur in any combination.

94455d881e93.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
94455d881e93.sentence: The factors of data integrity failure modes are as follows:

6382d3f96b4a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
6382d3f96b4a.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
6382d3f96b4a.sentence: An effective restore plan must account for any of these failure modes occurring in any conceivable combination.

f3f9ca86e235.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
f3f9ca86e235.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
f3f9ca86e235.sentence: An unrecoverable loss of data may be caused by a number of factors: user action, operator error, application bugs, defects in infrastructure, faulty hardware, or site catastrophes.

013ffee48d4f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
013ffee48d4f.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
013ffee48d4f.sentence: Some losses are widespread, affecting many entities.

fee5d25e7b8f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
fee5d25e7b8f.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
fee5d25e7b8f.sentence: Some losses are narrow and directed, deleting or corrupting data specific to a small subset of users.

454c9daddeee.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
454c9daddeee.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
454c9daddeee.sentence: Some data losses are a big bang event (for example, 1 million rows are replaced by only 10 rows in a single minute), whereas some data losses are creeping (for example, 10 rows of data are deleted every minute over the course of weeks).

2e836e7c7596.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
2e836e7c7596.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
2e836e7c7596.sentence: What may be a perfectly effective strategy for guarding against a data loss caused by a creeping application bug may be of no help whatsoever when your colocation datacenter catches fire.

a0d23c5bd054.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
a0d23c5bd054.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
a0d23c5bd054.sentence: A study of 19 data recovery efforts at Google found that the most common user-visible data loss scenarios involved data deletion or loss of referential integrity caused by software bugs.

d5bd22fdd20f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
d5bd22fdd20f.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
d5bd22fdd20f.sentence: The most challenging variants involved low-grade corruption or deletion that was discovered weeks to months after the bugs were first released into the production environment.

75fcc4d203bc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
75fcc4d203bc.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
75fcc4d203bc.sentence: To prevent data quality from degrading before usersâ eyes, and to detect low-grade data corruption or data loss scenarios before they become unrecoverable, a system of out-of-band checks and balances is needed both within and between an applicationâs datastores.

a0a6038c51d0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
a0a6038c51d0.sentence: âBadâ data doesnât sit idly by, it propagates.

944485c48b27.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
944485c48b27.sentence: References to missing or corrupt data are copied, links fan out, and with every update the overall quality of your datastore goes down.

073bcba3710d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
073bcba3710d.sentence: The sooner you know about a data loss, the easier and more complete your recovery can be.

9afb4f0ef017.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
9afb4f0ef017.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Challenges faced by cloud developers
9afb4f0ef017.sentence: While such algorithms are infallible in theory, their implementations are often riddled with hacks, optimizations, bugs, and educated guesses.

3e600e65958f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity

3e600e65958f.sentence: Affected applications have no way to know that 100% of their data is good until they check: trust storage systems, but verify!

2b1954f000e9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity

2b1954f000e9.sentence: Most often, these data validation pipelines are implemented as collections of map-reductions or Hadoop jobs.

c0bd19773522.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
c0bd19773522.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
c0bd19773522.sentence: Shunting some developers to work on a data validation pipeline can slow engineering velocity in the short term.

7159befd57d9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
7159befd57d9.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
7159befd57d9.sentence: However, devoting engineering resources to data validation endows other developers with the courage to move faster in the long run, because the engineers know that data corruption bugs are less likely to sneak into production unnoticed.

6a6b633753e9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
6a6b633753e9.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
6a6b633753e9.sentence: Similar to the effects enjoyed when units test are introduced early in the project lifecycle, a data validation pipeline results in an overall acceleration of software development projects.

e80a6ea6d4a0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
e80a6ea6d4a0.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
e80a6ea6d4a0.sentence: Out-of-band data validation is tricky to implement correctly.

dabaa2abc9d1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
dabaa2abc9d1.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
dabaa2abc9d1.sentence: When too strict, even simple, appropriate changes cause validation to fail.

b9f3cf8ca5e1.sentence: If the data validation isnât strict enough, user experienceâaffecting data corruption can slip through undetected.

6e080fc48193.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity

6e080fc48193.sentence: This safeguard turned a potential emergency "all-hands-on-deck-omigosh-files-are-disappearing!" data loss situation in 2013 into a business as usual, "letâs go home and fix the root cause on Monday," situation.

b12a5b98b9c2.sentence: By transforming emergencies into business as usual, validators improve engineering morale, quality of life, and predictability.

35519c90f9e5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
35519c90f9e5.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
35519c90f9e5.sentence: Out-of-band validators can be expensive at scale.

af1c751dbc67.sentence: Similar to its application in data recovery, a tiered strategy can also be useful in out-of-band data validation.

3348decae10a.sentence: Make sure that daily validators continue to catch the most disastrous scenarios within 24 hours, but continue with more rigorous validation at reduced frequency to contain costs and latency.

6c679cb85d14.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation

fccc4672c086.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation

beb7cd43d674.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation

9c31063d0b28.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation

ba57d6915e37.section: Third Layer: Early Detection > Out-of-band data validation
ba57d6915e37.sentence: - Data validation APIs that make validators easy to add and refactor
