9ac22f84863c.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
9ac22f84863c.sentence: To recover from such scenarios, a large and successful application needs to retrieve data for perhaps millions of users spread across days, weeks, or months.

d6fb26d2c342.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
d6fb26d2c342.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
d6fb26d2c342.sentence: The application may also need to recover each affected artifact to a unique point in time.

9d8871a217c5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
9d8871a217c5.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
9d8871a217c5.sentence: This data recovery scenario is called "point-in-time recovery" outside Google, and "time-travel" inside Google.

d341a68dee5c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
d341a68dee5c.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
d341a68dee5c.sentence: A backup and recovery solution that provides point-in-time recovery for an application across its ACID and BASE datastores while meeting strict uptime, latency, scalability, velocity, and cost goals is a chimera today!

51e5f7e166c5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
51e5f7e166c5.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
51e5f7e166c5.sentence: Solving this problem with your own engineers entails sacrificing velocity.

fdcc8bbe3e25.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
fdcc8bbe3e25.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
fdcc8bbe3e25.sentence: Many projects compromise by adopting a tiered backup strategy without point-in-time recovery.

1f98f5dbb876.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
1f98f5dbb876.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
1f98f5dbb876.sentence: Expensive local "snapshots" may provide limited protection from application bugs and offer quick restoration functionality, so you might retain a few days of such local "snapshots," taken several hours apart.

ac79f8b78618.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
ac79f8b78618.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
ac79f8b78618.sentence: Cost-effective full and incremental copies every two days may be retained longer.

2486146e05b6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
2486146e05b6.section: Types of Failures That Lead to Data Loss
2486146e05b6.sentence: If you can have both features, use both features.

3f08b5e80b33.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
3f08b5e80b33.section: Challenges of Maintaining Data Integrity Deep and Wide > Retention
3f08b5e80b33.sentence: While itâs likely that you or your customers will quickly notice the sudden emptying of an entire database, it might take days for a more gradual loss of data to attract the right personâs attention.

e52f85ae7923.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
e52f85ae7923.section: Challenges of Maintaining Data Integrity Deep and Wide > Retention
e52f85ae7923.sentence: Restoring the lost data in the latter scenario requires snapshots taken further back in time.

70fde68a2cc1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
70fde68a2cc1.section: Challenges of Maintaining Data Integrity Deep and Wide > Retention
70fde68a2cc1.sentence: When reaching back this far, youâll likely want to merge the restored data with the current state.

a8099ffd0b07.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
a8099ffd0b07.section: Challenges of Maintaining Data Integrity Deep and Wide > Retention
a8099ffd0b07.sentence: Doing so significantly complicates the restore process.

603e4c3cee1f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
603e4c3cee1f.sentence: An alternative approach to Simple Round Robin is to have each client task keep track of the number of active requests it has to each backend task in its subset and use Round Robin among the set of tasks with a minimal number of active requests.

cdb4e488975f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
cdb4e488975f.sentence: The idea behind the least-loaded policy is that loaded tasks will tend to have higher latency than those with spare capacity, and this strategy will naturally take load away from these loaded tasks.

083cef0fe474.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
083cef0fe474.sentence: This implementation actually uses Round Robin, but itâs applied across the set of tasks with minimal active requests.

303101b6131b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
303101b6131b.sentence: Without such filtering, the policy might not be able to spread the requests well enough to avoid a situation in which some portion of the available backend tasks goes unused.

07b474249b93.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
07b474249b93.sentence: All that said, weâve learned (the hard way!) about one very dangerous pitfall of the Least-Loaded Round Robin approach: if a task is seriously unhealthy, it might start serving 100% errors.

48cbf8accf51.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
48cbf8accf51.sentence: Depending on the nature of those errors, they may have very low latency; itâs frequently significantly faster to just return an "Iâm unhealthy!" error than to actually process a request.

3d6580c57c32.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
3d6580c57c32.sentence: As a result, clients might start sending a very large amount of traffic to the unhealthy task, erroneously thinking that the task is available, as opposed to fast-failing them!

088879b97485.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
088879b97485.sentence: We say that the unhealthy task is now sinkholing traffic.

2a3158e82a85.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
2a3158e82a85.sentence: Fortunately, this pitfall can be solved relatively easily by modifying the policy to count recent errors as if they were active requests.

403fbac10712.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
403fbac10712.sentence: This way, if a backend task becomes unhealthy, the load balancing policy begins to divert load from it the same way it would divert load from an overburdened task.

096572de9166.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
096572de9166.sentence: The count of active requests may not be a very good proxy for the capability of a given backend

50ace7d883a8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
50ace7d883a8.sentence: Many requests spend a significant portion of their life just waiting for a response from the network (i.e., waiting for responses to requests they initiate to other backends) and very little time on actual processing.

74951962053b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
74951962053b.sentence: For example, one backend task may be able to process twice as many requests as another (e.g., because itâs running in a machine with a CPU thatâs twice as fast as the rest), but the latency of its requests may still be roughly the same as the latency of requests in the other task (because requests spend most of their life just waiting for the network to respond).

c6a849c25ee1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
c6a849c25ee1.sentence: However, Least-Loaded Round Robin will consider both backend tasks equally loaded.

8331e0e91ba4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
8331e0e91ba4.sentence: The count of active requests in each client doesnât include requests from other clients to the same backends

3f0e333d113c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
3f0e333d113c.sentence: That is, each client task has only a very limited view into the state of its backend tasks: the view of its own requests.

3874b6634e40.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
3874b6634e40.sentence: In practice, weâve found that large services using Least-Loaded Round Robin will see their most loaded backend task using twice as much CPU as the least loaded, performing about as poorly as Round Robin.

105243d4d6f1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
105243d4d6f1.sentence: Weighted Round Robin is an important load balancing policy that improves on Simple and Least-Loaded Round Robin by incorporating backend-provided information into the decision process.

9468e595aff7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
9468e595aff7.sentence: Weighted Round Robin is fairly simple in principle: each client task keeps a "capability" score for each backend in its subset.

d7fcc3bff5cc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
d7fcc3bff5cc.sentence: Requests are distributed in Round-Robin fashion, but clients weigh the distributions of requests to backends proportionally.

6c9be689a954.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
6c9be689a954.sentence: In each response (including responses to health checks), backends include the current observed rates of queries and errors per second, in addition to the utilization (typically, CPU usage).

b27f2e41b250.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
b27f2e41b250.sentence: Clients adjust the capability scores periodically to pick backend tasks based upon their current number of successful requests handled and at what utilization cost; failed requests result in a penalty that affects future decisions.

e67a043ef4de.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
e67a043ef4de.sentence: In practice, Weighted Round Robin has worked very well and significantly reduced the difference between the most and the least utilized tasks.

fbd38369146a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
fbd38369146a.sentence: Figure 20-6 shows the CPU rates for a random subset of backend tasks around the time its clients switched from Least-Loaded to Weighted Round Robin.

7fbca225bf93.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
7fbca225bf93.sentence: The spread from the least to the most loaded tasks decreased drastically.

0cadf25ff38d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
0cadf25ff38d.sentence: Many of the complexities in load balancing policies stem from the distributed nature of the decision-making process in which clients need to decide, in real time (and with only partial and/or stale backend state information), which backend should be used for each request.

b893f479c2d6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
b893f479c2d6.sentence: Load balancing policies can be very simple and not take into account any information about the state of the backends (e.g., Round Robin) or can act with more information about the backends (e.g., Least-Loaded Round Robin or Weighted Round Robin).

24f95460a83a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
24f95460a83a.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
24f95460a83a.sentence: Returning to the larger question: how exactly should a network load balancer forward packets to a selected VIP backend?

af099cc35881.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
af099cc35881.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
af099cc35881.sentence: One solution is to perform a Network Address Translation.

c0f02a380757.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
c0f02a380757.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
c0f02a380757.sentence: Another solution is to modify information on the data link layer (layer 2 of the OSI networking model).

a841092ebc41.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
a841092ebc41.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
a841092ebc41.sentence: Our current VIP load balancing solution [Eis16] uses packet encapsulation.

e186303b0ee8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
e186303b0ee8.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
e186303b0ee8.sentence: However, this requires keeping an entry of every single connection in the tracking table, which precludes having a completely stateless fallback mechanism.

36f5eb138271.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
36f5eb138271.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
36f5eb138271.sentence: By changing the destination MAC address of a forwarded packet, the balancer can leave all the information in upper layers intact, so the backend receives the original source and destination IP addresses.

a0775eda4448.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
a0775eda4448.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
a0775eda4448.sentence: The backend can then send a reply directly to the original senderâa technique known as Direct Server Response (DSR).

59fbaf231905.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
59fbaf231905.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
59fbaf231905.sentence: If user requests are small and replies are large (e.g., most HTTP requests), DSR provides tremendous savings, because only a small fraction of traffic need traverse the load balancer.

79e4cf5ca58a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
79e4cf5ca58a.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
79e4cf5ca58a.sentence: Even better, DSR does not require us to keep state on the load balancer device.

a5d1d2188592.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
a5d1d2188592.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
a5d1d2188592.sentence: Unfortunately, using layer 2 for internal load balancing does incur serious disadvantages when deployed at scale: all machines (i.e., all load balancers and all their backends) must be able to reach each other at the data link layer.

be0644e21f90.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
be0644e21f90.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
be0644e21f90.sentence: This isnât an issue if this connectivity can be supported by the network and the number of machines doesnât grow excessively, because all the machines need to reside in a single broadcast domain.

1fb7f4ba8c63.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
1fb7f4ba8c63.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
1fb7f4ba8c63.sentence: As you may imagine, Google outgrew this solution quite some time ago, and had to find an alternate approach.

b9125f0afca9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
b9125f0afca9.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
b9125f0afca9.sentence: A network load balancer puts the forwarded packet into another IP packet with Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) [Han94], and uses a backendâs address as the destination.

ad0885d4f535.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
ad0885d4f535.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
ad0885d4f535.sentence: The network load balancer and the backend no longer need to exist in the same broadcast domain; they can even be on separate continents as long as a route between the two exists.

408cc87a46ab.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-frontend
408cc87a46ab.section: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address
408cc87a46ab.sentence: Encapsulation introduces overhead (24 bytes in the case of IPv4+GRE, to be precise), which can cause the packet to exceed the available Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) size and require fragmentation.

7eabd5de8e32.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
7eabd5de8e32.sentence: Publishing SLOs sets expectations for system behavior.

c86efb5a484f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
c86efb5a484f.sentence: Users (and potential users) often want to know what they can expect from a service in order to understand whether itâs appropriate for their use case.

5a49f90bd8f4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
5a49f90bd8f4.sentence: For instance, a team wanting to build a photo-sharing website might want to avoid using a service that promises very strong durability and low cost in exchange for slightly lower availability, though the same service might be a perfect fit for an archival records management system.

7d4a4ce6a41c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
7d4a4ce6a41c.sentence: Using a tighter internal SLO than the SLO advertised to users gives you room to respond to chronic problems before they become visible externally.

98e11ed22b00.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
98e11ed22b00.sentence: An SLO buffer also makes it possible to accommodate reimplementations that trade performance for other attributes, such as cost or ease of maintenance, without having to disappoint users.

fb612faa90d8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
fb612faa90d8.sentence: If your serviceâs actual performance is much better than its stated SLO, users will come to rely on its current performance.

132cde4b4032.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
132cde4b4032.sentence: Users build on the reality of what you offer, rather than what you say youâll supply, particularly for infrastructure services.

2452f602ece7.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
2452f602ece7.sentence: You can avoid over-dependence by deliberately taking the system offline occasionally (Googleâs Chubby service introduced planned outages in response to being overly available),18 throttling some requests, or designing the system so that it isnât faster under light loads.

be292f34bd86.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
be292f34bd86.sentence: Understanding how well a system is meeting its expectations helps decide whether to invest in making the system faster, more available, and more resilient.

eccee120a62b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives
eccee120a62b.sentence: Alternatively, if the service is doing fine, perhaps staff time should be spent on other priorities, such as paying off technical debt, adding new features, or introducing other products.

3724de4a225d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
3724de4a225d.sentence: Therefore, instead of using metrics around uptime, we define availability in terms of the request success rate.

01fc5024f7c6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
01fc5024f7c6.sentence: Aggregate availability shows how this yield-based metric is calculated over a rolling window (i.e., proportion of successful requests over a one-day window).

6808db51e2a8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
6808db51e2a8.sentence: For example, a system with an availability target of 99.99% can be down for up to 52.56 minutes in a year and stay within its availability target; see Availability Table for a table.

a02cb5a12d0c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
a02cb5a12d0c.sentence: At Google, however, a time-based metric for availability is usually not meaningful because we are looking across globally distributed services.

a271b9730b8b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
a271b9730b8b.sentence: Our approach to fault isolation makes it very likely that we are serving at least a subset of traffic for a given service somewhere in the world at any given time (i.e., we are at least partially "up" at all times).

923b863eeadb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
923b863eeadb.sentence: For example, a system that serves 2.5M requests in a day with a daily availability target of 99.99% can serve up to 250 errors and still hit its target for that given day.

cded5820be9f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
cded5820be9f.sentence: In a typical application, not all requests are equal: failing a new user sign-up request is different from failing a request polling for new email in the background.

33114751ee97.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
33114751ee97.sentence: In many cases, however, availability calculated as the request success rate over all requests is a reasonable approximation of unplanned downtime, as viewed from the end-user perspective.

16cc0aed333c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
16cc0aed333c.sentence: Quantifying unplanned downtime as a request success rate also makes this availability metric more amenable for use in systems that do not typically serve end users directly.

ef984fd28971.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
ef984fd28971.sentence: Using a request success rate defined in terms of records successfully and unsuccessfully processed, we can calculate a useful availability metric despite the fact that the batch system does not run constantly.

927d5af1167a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
927d5af1167a.sentence: Most often, we set quarterly availability targets for a service and track our performance against those targets on a weekly, or even daily, basis.

b72168255a6a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
b72168255a6a.sentence: This strategy lets us manage the service to a high-level availability objective by looking for, tracking down, and fixing meaningful deviations as they inevitably arise.

8c1cf37cec8d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
8c1cf37cec8d.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
8c1cf37cec8d.sentence: The target level of availability for a given Google service usually depends on the function it provides and how the service is positioned in the marketplace.

8e12400d075e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
8e12400d075e.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
8e12400d075e.sentence: - What level of service will the users expect?

b2dd93c70bdf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
b2dd93c70bdf.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
b2dd93c70bdf.sentence: - Does this service tie directly to revenue (either our revenue, or our customersâ revenue)?

6f19ffef9e63.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
6f19ffef9e63.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
6f19ffef9e63.sentence: - Is this a paid service, or is it free?

0419ed4d3adb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
0419ed4d3adb.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
0419ed4d3adb.sentence: - If there are competitors in the marketplace, what level of service do those competitors provide?

7cb52592bc83.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
7cb52592bc83.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
7cb52592bc83.sentence: - Is this service targeted at consumers, or at enterprises?

96332dbc2e33.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
96332dbc2e33.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
96332dbc2e33.sentence: For a typical Google Apps for Work service, we might set an external quarterly availability target of 99.9%, and back this target with a stronger internal availability target and a contract that stipulates penalties if we fail to deliver to the external target.

6c4970b83479.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
6c4970b83479.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Target level of availability
6c4970b83479.sentence: We set a lower availability target for YouTube than for our enterprise products because rapid feature development was correspondingly more important.

a055a0aa8821.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
a055a0aa8821.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost
a055a0aa8821.sentence: - If we were to build and operate these systems at one more nine of availability, what would our incremental increase in revenue be?

5a54431be5a9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
5a54431be5a9.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost
5a54431be5a9.sentence: - Does this additional revenue offset the cost of reaching that level of reliability?

19c3768576e3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
19c3768576e3.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost

96384652c140.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
96384652c140.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost

7317922bb1fb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
7317922bb1fb.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost
7317922bb1fb.sentence: In this case, if the cost of improving availability by one nine is less than $900, it is worth the investment.

a5195921217b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
a5195921217b.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost
a5195921217b.sentence: One useful strategy may be to consider the background error rate of ISPs on the Internet.

6eb6d11c54b4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
6eb6d11c54b4.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost
6eb6d11c54b4.sentence: If failures are being measured from the end-user perspective and it is possible to drive the error rate for the service below the background error rate, those errors will fall within the noise for a given userâs Internet connection.

da8eb5b89c00.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
da8eb5b89c00.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Cost
da8eb5b89c00.sentence: While there are significant differences between ISPs and protocols (e.g., TCP versus UDP, IPv4 versus IPv6), weâve measured the typical background error rate for ISPs as falling between 0.01% and 1%.

e45e9a5597ba.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
e45e9a5597ba.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Types of failures
e45e9a5597ba.sentence: Which is worse for the service: a constant low rate of failures, or an occasional full-site outage?

4084860d4784.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
4084860d4784.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Types of failures
4084860d4784.sentence: Both types of failure may result in the same absolute number of errors, but may have vastly different impacts on the business.

f877566e8da4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
f877566e8da4.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Consumer Services > Types of failures
f877566e8da4.sentence: Because most of this work takes place during normal business hours, we determined that occasional, regular, scheduled outages in the form of maintenance windows would be acceptable, and we counted these scheduled outages as planned downtime, not unplanned downtime.

e5169b475c7e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
e5169b475c7e.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services
e5169b475c7e.sentence: A fundamental difference is that, by definition, infrastructure components have multiple clients, often with varying needs.

0a1d09e9c3bf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
0a1d09e9c3bf.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
0a1d09e9c3bf.sentence: One way to satisfy these competing constraints in a cost-effective manner is to partition the infrastructure and offer it at multiple independent levels of service.

58bfef6f4e9a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
58bfef6f4e9a.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Types of failures
58bfef6f4e9a.sentence: The low-latency user wants Bigtableâs request queues to be (almost always) empty so that the system can process each outstanding request immediately upon arrival.

4eb12ee788b8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
4eb12ee788b8.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Types of failures
4eb12ee788b8.sentence: (Indeed, inefficient queuing is often a cause of high tail latency.) The user concerned with offline analysis is more interested in system throughput, so that user wants request queues to never be empty.

055bd976d0b3.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
055bd976d0b3.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Types of failures
055bd976d0b3.sentence: To optimize for throughput, the Bigtable system should never need to idle while waiting for its next request.

0a728331a48f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
0a728331a48f.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Types of failures
0a728331a48f.sentence: As you can see, success and failure are antithetical for these sets of users.

982696af8759.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
982696af8759.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
982696af8759.sentence: In the Bigtable example, we can build two types of clusters: low-latency clusters and throughput clusters.

211781727856.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
211781727856.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
211781727856.sentence: To ensure short queue lengths and satisfy more stringent client isolation requirements, the Bigtable system can be provisioned with a substantial amount of slack capacity for reduced contention and increased redundancy.

90845c0911d5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
90845c0911d5.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
90845c0911d5.sentence: The throughput clusters, on the other hand, can be provisioned to run very hot and with less redundancy, optimizing throughput over latency.

ab6920667e56.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
ab6920667e56.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
ab6920667e56.sentence: In practice, we are able to satisfy these relaxed needs at a much lower cost, perhaps as little as 10â50% of the cost of a low-latency cluster.

b47992b670c8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
b47992b670c8.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
b47992b670c8.sentence: The key strategy with regards to infrastructure is to deliver services with explicitly delineated levels of service, thus enabling the clients to make the right risk and cost trade-offs when building their systems.

3608d75a1676.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
3608d75a1676.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
3608d75a1676.sentence: With explicitly delineated levels of service, the infrastructure providers can effectively externalize the difference in the cost it takes to provide service at a given level to clients.

e5b9c8fb047e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
e5b9c8fb047e.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
e5b9c8fb047e.sentence: Exposing cost in this way motivates the clients to choose the level of service with the lowest cost that still meets their needs.

594988214f3b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
594988214f3b.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
594988214f3b.sentence: For example, Google+ can decide to put data critical to enforcing user privacy in a high-availability, globally consistent datastore (e.g., a globally replicated SQL-like system like Spanner [Cor12]), while putting optional data (data that isnât critical, but that enhances the user experience) in a cheaper, less reliable, less fresh, and eventually consistent datastore (e.g., a NoSQL store with best-effort replication like Bigtable).

27b26034b358.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
27b26034b358.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
27b26034b358.sentence: Note that we can run multiple classes of services using identical hardware and software.

1734cc5e005b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk
1734cc5e005b.section: Identifying the Risk Tolerance of Infrastructure Services > Cost
1734cc5e005b.sentence: We can provide vastly different service guarantees by adjusting a variety of service characteristics, such as the quantities of resources, the degree of redundancy, the geographical provisioning constraints, and, critically, the infrastructure software configuration.

e9bc9d8c9e9f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
e9bc9d8c9e9f.sentence: Borg, illustrated in Figure 2-2, is a distributed cluster operating system [Ver15], similar to Apache Mesos.10 Borg manages its jobs at the cluster level.

b3a676a37c27.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
b3a676a37c27.sentence: Borg is responsible for running usersâ jobs, which can either be indefinitely running servers or batch processes like a MapReduce [Dea04].

9daf8ae1498f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
9daf8ae1498f.sentence: Jobs can consist of more than one (and sometimes thousands) of identical tasks, both for reasons of reliability and because a single process canât usually handle all cluster traffic.

61a23665fc25.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
61a23665fc25.sentence: In a single cluster in a typical year, thousands of machines fail and thousands of hard disks break; when multiplied by the number of clusters we operate globally, these numbers become somewhat breathtaking.

e66a7c59c338.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
e66a7c59c338.sentence: Therefore, we want to abstract such problems away from users, and the teams running our services similarly donât want to be bothered by hardware failures.

7f8cd65c89b5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
7f8cd65c89b5.sentence: Machines can run any server, so we donât dedicate specific machines to specific server programs.

987fffb008c5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
987fffb008c5.sentence: When Borg starts a job, it finds machines for the tasks and tells the machines to start the server program.

ed07f931329a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
ed07f931329a.sentence: Borg then continually monitors these tasks.

0d69c48cfe8d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
0d69c48cfe8d.sentence: If a task malfunctions, it is killed and restarted, possibly on a different machine.

fb44dee3d51f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
fb44dee3d51f.sentence: Because tasks are fluidly allocated over machines, we canât simply rely on IP addresses and port numbers to refer to the tasks.

f0d113dbe2bb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
f0d113dbe2bb.sentence: We solve this problem with an extra level of indirection: when starting a job, Borg allocates a name and index number to each task using the Borg Naming Service (BNS).

9a5ac44eeb5e.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
9a5ac44eeb5e.sentence: Rather than using the IP address and port number, other processes connect to Borg tasks via the BNS name, which is translated to an IP address and port number by BNS.

9528d4ffa10c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
9528d4ffa10c.sentence: Every job needs to specify its required resources (e.g., 3 CPU cores, 2 GiB of RAM).

b7d4e80f9e8f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
b7d4e80f9e8f.sentence: Using the list of requirements for all jobs, Borg can binpack the tasks over the machines in an optimal way that also accounts for failure domains (for example: Borg wonât run all of a jobâs tasks on the same rack, as doing so means that the top of rack switch is a single point of failure for that job).

b41200b51663.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
b41200b51663.sentence: If a task tries to use more resources than it requested, Borg kills the task and restarts it (as a slowly crashlooping task is usually preferable to a task that hasnât been restarted at all).

c8f479379a3b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
c8f479379a3b.sentence: To obtain the corresponding IP address, the userâs device resolves the address with its DNS server (1).

1f7843d0d70c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
1f7843d0d70c.sentence: This request ultimately ends up at Googleâs DNS server, which talks to GSLB.

ac1efd1dba0d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
ac1efd1dba0d.sentence: This server (named the Google Frontend, or GFE) is a reverse proxy that terminates the TCP connection (2).

b81d6a0a98f2.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
b81d6a0a98f2.sentence: Again using GSLB, the server finds an available Shakespeare frontend server, and sends that server an RPC containing the HTTP request (3).

bd08fc46c7f5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
bd08fc46c7f5.sentence: The Shakespeare frontend server now needs to contact the Shakespeare backend server: the frontend server contacts GSLB to obtain the BNS address of a suitable and unloaded backend server (4).

8830e8d2f359.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
8830e8d2f359.sentence: That Shakespeare backend server now contacts a Bigtable server to obtain the requested data (5).

cd4305761726.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
cd4305761726.sentence: The backend hands a protobuf containing the results to the Shakespeare frontend server, which assembles the HTML and returns the answer to the user.

a87cd3f4a8af.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
a87cd3f4a8af.sentence: As GSLB keeps track of traffic load among frontend servers across regions, it picks which server IP address to send to this user.

1f21e08cc923.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
1f21e08cc923.sentence: The browser connects to the HTTP server on this IP.

b661bb9a8e65.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
b661bb9a8e65.sentence: The GFE looks up which service is required (web search, maps, orâin this caseâShakespeare).

958b2f7d58c5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
958b2f7d58c5.sentence: The Shakespeare server analyzes the HTTP request and constructs a protobuf containing the word to look up.

7226aa0a6571.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
7226aa0a6571.sentence: The answer is written to the reply protobuf and returned to the Shakespeare backend server.

fc996e47179b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
fc996e47179b.sentence: This entire chain of events is executed in the blink of an eyeâjust a few hundred milliseconds!

c8b26b7d6da0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
c8b26b7d6da0.sentence: Because many moving parts are involved, there are many potential points of failure; in particular, a failing GSLB would wreak havoc.

42a69901b4d4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
42a69901b4d4.sentence: However, Googleâs policies of rigorous testing and careful rollout, in addition to our proactive error recovery methods such as graceful degradation, allow us to deliver the reliable service that our users have come to expect.

4c8380909bc8.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
4c8380909bc8.sentence: Load testing determined that our backend server can handle about 100 queries per second (QPS).

38b2983c4a6f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
38b2983c4a6f.sentence: Trials performed with a limited set of users lead us to expect a peak load of about 3,470 QPS, so we need at least 35 tasks.

53838d4ac941.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
53838d4ac941.sentence: However, the following considerations mean that we need at least 37 tasks in the job, or N+2:

d816d7817726.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
d816d7817726.sentence: - During updates, one task at a time will be unavailable, leaving 36 tasks.

69fa6eaa1d53.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
69fa6eaa1d53.sentence: - A machine failure might occur during a task update, leaving only 35 tasks, just enough to serve peak load.13

5e57b3c49125.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
5e57b3c49125.sentence: 13We assume the probability of two simultaneous task failures in our environment is low enough to be negligible.

4fc5efe3d5c0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
4fc5efe3d5c0.sentence: Single points of failure, such as top-of-rack switches or power distribution, may make this assumption invalid in other environments.

9657d66a5943.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
9657d66a5943.sentence: Instead of locating all backends at one site, we distribute them across the USA, South America, Europe, and Asia.

03e16d4bd9cd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
03e16d4bd9cd.sentence: Allowing for N+2 redundancy per region means that we end up with 17 tasks in the USA, 16 in Europe, and 6 in Asia.

0780f728fc76.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
0780f728fc76.sentence: However, we decide to use 4 tasks (instead of 5) in South America, to lower the overhead of N+2 to N+1.

f758d8856bef.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
f758d8856bef.sentence: In this case, weâre willing to tolerate a small risk of higher latency in exchange for lower hardware costs: if GSLB redirects traffic from one continent to another when our South American datacenter is over capacity, we can save 20% of the resources weâd spend on hardware.

545518b1008a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
545518b1008a.sentence: A backend in Asia contacting a Bigtable in the USA adds a significant amount of latency, so we replicate the Bigtable in each region.

1f3018bb4d2b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
1f3018bb4d2b.sentence: Bigtable replication helps us in two ways: it provides resilience should a Bigtable server fail, and it lowers data-access latency.

f3e637dcae24.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/production-environment
f3e637dcae24.sentence: While Bigtable only offers eventual consistency, it isnât a major problem because we donât need to update the contents often.

46786e819c2b.title: Service-level agreement
46786e819c2b.sentence: According to Dinesh Verma, a well-defined and typical SLA will contain the following components:

6193503a90cc.title: Service-level agreement
6193503a90cc.sentence: - It specifies the type of service and any additional details of the type of service to be provided.

8a8e17c0f649.title: Service-level agreement
8a8e17c0f649.sentence: - The service's desired performance level, especially its reliability and responsiveness

1541a24cac9c.title: Service-level agreement
1541a24cac9c.sentence: - Monitoring process and service level reporting

44ca8896f2e2.title: Service-level agreement
44ca8896f2e2.sentence: - The steps for reporting issues with the service

d7c3826dd48d.title: Service-level agreement
d7c3826dd48d.sentence: - Response and issue resolution time frame

166c74cc8146.title: Service-level agreement
166c74cc8146.sentence: - Repercussions for the service provider not meeting its commitment

bcd72bb08e5e.title: Service-level agreement
bcd72bb08e5e.sentence: - A reliable service will be the one that suffers minimum disruption in a specific amount of time and is available at almost all times.

d4face4bfe79.title: Service-level agreement
d4face4bfe79.sentence: Service with good responsiveness will perform the desired action promptly after the customer requests it.

700cecb50109.title: Service-level agreement
700cecb50109.sentence: - This component describes how the performance levels are supervised and monitored.

cef4556bcddb.title: Service-level agreement
cef4556bcddb.sentence: This process involves gathering different types of statistics, how frequently these statistics will be collected and how they will be accessed by the customers.

bdc7135cc850.title: Service-level agreement
bdc7135cc850.sentence: - This component will specify the contact details to report the problem and the order in which details about the issue have to be reported.

92809f04c5e2.title: Service-level agreement
92809f04c5e2.sentence: - The response time frame is the period by which the service provider will start the investigation of the issue.

319e2c25a087.title: Service-level agreement
319e2c25a087.sentence: Issue resolution time frame is the period by which the current service issue will be resolved and fixed.

3118d2da54cc.title: Service-level agreement
3118d2da54cc.sentence: - If the provider is not able to meet the requirements as stated in SLA then the service provider will have to face consequences.

df4782cf3a9b.title: Service-level agreement
df4782cf3a9b.sentence: These consequences may include the customer's right to terminate the contract or ask for a refund for losses incurred by the customer due to failure of service.

71da515d3abb.title: Service-level agreement
71da515d3abb.sentence: The underlying benefit of cloud computing is shared resources, which are supported by the underlying nature of a shared infrastructure environment.

c4b95f7d72b9.title: Service-level agreement
c4b95f7d72b9.sentence: Thus, SLAs span across the cloud and are offered by service providers as a service-based agreements rather than a customer-based agreements.

ff40e7c8a324.title: Service-level agreement
ff40e7c8a324.sentence: Measuring, monitoring and reporting on cloud performance is based on the end UX or their ability to consume resources.

06cc8aea4cf2.title: Service-level agreement
06cc8aea4cf2.sentence: SLAs for cloud services focus on characteristics of the data center and more recently include characteristics of the network (see carrier cloud) to support end-to-end SLAs.

99533b9a1a7c.title: Service-level agreement
99533b9a1a7c.sentence: The downside of cloud computing relative to SLAs is the difficulty in determining the root cause of service interruptions due to the complex nature of the environment.

18f5d5418295.title: Service-level agreement
18f5d5418295.sentence: As applications are moved from dedicated hardware into the cloud, they need to achieve the same even more demanding levels of service than classical installations.

73c1a88b7cd5.title: Service-level agreement
73c1a88b7cd5.sentence: Any SLA management strategy considers two well-differentiated phases: negotiating the contract and monitoring its fulfillment in real-time.

99762ee7b049.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
99762ee7b049.sentence: Testing externally visible behavior as a user would see it.

cc85aa7545c5.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
cc85aa7545c5.sentence: Monitoring based on metrics exposed by the internals of the system, including logs, interfaces like the Java Virtual Machine Profiling Interface, or an HTTP handler that emits internal statistics.

525447995356.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
525447995356.sentence: The simplest way to think about black-box monitoring versus white-box monitoring is that black-box monitoring is symptom-oriented and represents activeânot predictedâproblems: "The system isnât working correctly, right now." White-box monitoring depends on the ability to inspect the innards of the system, such as logs or HTTP endpoints, with instrumentation.

a288f7643e4d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
a288f7643e4d.sentence: White-box monitoring therefore allows detection of imminent problems, failures masked by retries, and so forth.

97806fe0dcbc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
97806fe0dcbc.sentence: For paging, black-box monitoring has the key benefit of forcing discipline to only nag a human when a problem is both already ongoing and contributing to real symptoms.

84b2475f0a99.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
84b2475f0a99.sentence: On the other hand, for not-yet-occurring but imminent problems, black-box monitoring is fairly useless.

705485cda796.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
705485cda796.sentence: When collecting telemetry for debugging, white-box monitoring is essential.

391a1a58c849.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
391a1a58c849.sentence: If web servers seem slow on database-heavy requests, you need to know both how fast the web server perceives the database to be, and how fast the database believes itself to be.

313559ce853c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
313559ce853c.sentence: Otherwise, you canât distinguish an actually slow database server from a network problem between your web server and your database.

9e0df6e2a6c6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
9e0df6e2a6c6.sentence: Note that in a multilayered system, one personâs symptom is another personâs cause.

008b4ea392b1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
008b4ea392b1.sentence: Slow database reads are a symptom for the database SRE who detects them.

5f2a66aa7cf6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
5f2a66aa7cf6.sentence: However, for the frontend SRE observing a slow website, the same slow database reads are a cause.

9586432a9a52.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
9586432a9a52.sentence: - Does this rule detect an otherwise undetected condition that is urgent, actionable, and actively or imminently user-visible?25

cf0a32df8189.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
cf0a32df8189.sentence: Effective alerting systems have good signal and very low noise.

8cb02968d570.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
8cb02968d570.sentence: Your monitoring system should address two questions: whatâs broken, and why?

af1b54225075.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
af1b54225075.sentence: The "whatâs broken" indicates the symptom; the "why" indicates a (possibly intermediate) cause.

d4c56755a1a0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
d4c56755a1a0.sentence: "What" versus "why" is one of the most important distinctions in writing good monitoring with maximum signal and minimum noise.

7d0de6eb6d2a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
7d0de6eb6d2a.sentence: Paging a human is a quite expensive use of an employeeâs time.

8c2ad65da12c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
8c2ad65da12c.sentence: If an employee is at work, a page interrupts their workflow.

1b0f58cc139a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
1b0f58cc139a.sentence: If the employee is at home, a page interrupts their personal time, and perhaps even their sleep.

70bf3059f803.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
70bf3059f803.sentence: When pages occur too frequently, employees second-guess, skim, or even ignore incoming alerts, sometimes even ignoring a "real" page thatâs masked by the noise.

6cac190f9f7c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
6cac190f9f7c.sentence: Outages can be prolonged because other noise interferes with a rapid diagnosis and fix.

12dec59c14af.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
12dec59c14af.sentence: - Every page response should require intelligence.

b442379900bc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
b442379900bc.sentence: If a page merely merits a robotic response, it shouldnât be a page.

6468cb1e1ccd.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
6468cb1e1ccd.sentence: - Pages should be about a novel problem or an event that hasnât been seen before.

4c4e7acdc445.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
4c4e7acdc445.sentence: - Every time the pager goes off, I should be able to react with a sense of urgency.

086c83159b8c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
086c83159b8c.sentence: I can only react with a sense of urgency a few times a day before I become fatigued.

56cac80b1820.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
56cac80b1820.sentence: - Will I ever be able to ignore this alert, knowing itâs benign?

2a3bb56f2e9f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
2a3bb56f2e9f.sentence: - Does this alert definitely indicate that users are being negatively affected?

f7c7645fde0a.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
f7c7645fde0a.sentence: - Can I take action in response to this alert?

3d8049d54794.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
3d8049d54794.sentence: Is that action urgent, or could it wait until morning?

6733bd9c430f.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
6733bd9c430f.sentence: Could the action be safely automated?

7895349e8e78.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
7895349e8e78.sentence: - Are other people getting paged for this issue, therefore rendering at least one of the pages unnecessary?

454531e917b4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
454531e917b4.sentence: This perspective also amplifies certain distinctions: itâs better to spend much more effort on catching symptoms than causes; when it comes to causes, only worry about very definite, very imminent causes.

61cc0e878b95.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
61cc0e878b95.sentence: Unless youâre performing security auditing on very narrowly scoped components of a system, you should never trigger an alert simply because "something seems a bit weird."

859b2628cb3c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
859b2628cb3c.sentence: Email alerts are of very limited value and tend to easily become overrun with noise; instead, you should favor a dashboard that monitors all ongoing subcritical problems for the sort of information that typically ends up in email alerts.

ca08fbe654bf.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
ca08fbe654bf.sentence: A dashboard might also be paired with a log, in order to analyze historical correlations.

5c463d39e40b.sentence: Because of problems in Bigtable and lower layers of the storage stack, the mean performance was driven by a "large" tail: the worst 5% of requests were often significantly slower than the rest.

5c71bc8ee84d.sentence: To remedy the situation, the team used a three-pronged approach: while making great efforts to improve the performance of Bigtable, we also temporarily dialed back our SLO target, using the 75th percentile request latency.

819783bff3fc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems

819783bff3fc.sentence: We also disabled email alerts, as there were so many that spending time diagnosing them was infeasible.

ed0acc76a946.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems
ed0acc76a946.section: Bigtable SRE: A Tale of Over-Alerting
ed0acc76a946.sentence: This strategy gave us enough breathing room to actually fix the longer-term problems in Bigtable and the lower layers of the storage stack, rather than constantly fixing tactical problems.

eef86a744ac6.title: Incident management
eef86a744ac6.sentence: Incident management is therefore the process of limiting the potential disruption caused by such an event, followed by a return to business as usual.

768f03b86561.title: Incident management
768f03b86561.sentence: An incident is an event that could lead to loss of, or disruption to, an organization's operations, services, or functions.

b282ebbf65b3.title: Incident management
b282ebbf65b3.sentence: Incident management (IcM) refers to the activities an organization undertakes to identify, analyze, and correct hazards to prevent future recurrence.

20aa288c1c29.title: Incident management
20aa288c1c29.sentence: If not managed, an incident can escalate into an emergency, crisis or disaster.

3537a100e0a5.title: Incident management
3537a100e0a5.sentence: Incidents within a structured organization are normally dealt with by either an incident response team (IRT), or an incident management team (IMT).

f614f0ab8751.title: Incident management
f614f0ab8751.sentence: These are often designated beforehand or during the event and are placed in control of the organization while the incident is being addressed, to restore normal functions.

30c2796a79c1.title: Incident management
30c2796a79c1.sentence: The incident commander manages the response to a security incident and leads the members of the incident response team(s) through the process, as defined by the Incident Command System (ICS).

7623539a9dd5.title: Incident management
7623539a9dd5.sentence: Incident management frameworks for critical infrastructure commonly follow a lifecycle-based approach that includes incident detection, classification, response coordination, containment, recovery, and post-incident review.

7021931ca2f5.title: Incident management
7021931ca2f5.sentence: The first goal of the incident management process is to restore a normal service operation as quickly as possible and to minimize the impact on business operations, thus ensuring that the best possible levels of service quality and availability are maintained. 'Normal service operation' is defined here as service operation within service-level agreement (SLA).

9d2b40a670b6.title: Incident management
9d2b40a670b6.sentence: The ITIL incident management process ensures that normal service operation is restored as quickly as possible and the business impact is minimized.

498a146e162c.title: Incident management
498a146e162c.sentence: Usually, as part of the wider management process in private organizations, incident management is followed by post-incident analysis where it is determined why the incident happened despite precautions and controls.

ef5b3b961dd9.title: Incident management
ef5b3b961dd9.sentence: This information is then used as feedback to further develop the security policy and/or its practical implementation.

9edb53f05851.title: Incident management
9edb53f05851.sentence: During the root cause analysis, human factors should be assessed.

020209e0f20a.title: Incident management
020209e0f20a.sentence: There are two types of events: active failure—an action that has immediate effects and has the likelihood to cause an accident—and latent or delayed action—events can take years to have an effect and are usually combined with triggering events that then cause the accident.

1faa62f4b5de.title: Incident management
1faa62f4b5de.sentence: Latent failures are created as the result of decisions taken at the higher echelons of an organisation.

fa6966840b19.title: Incident management
fa6966840b19.sentence: Their damaging consequences may lie dormant for a long time, only becoming evident when they combine with local triggering factors (e.g., the spring tide, the loading difficulties at Zeebrugge harbour, etc.) to breach the system's defences.

50e62a770828.title: Incident management
50e62a770828.sentence: The main challenges and cause for problems in the Incident management are:

69b76c54ac94.title: Incident management
69b76c54ac94.sentence: - Constantly increasing Alert and Event Noise

565b56907f38.title: Incident management
565b56907f38.sentence: - Complex and Lengthy IT Problem Resolution Process

9ad6c5d66b48.title: Incident management
9ad6c5d66b48.sentence: - Inability to effectively predict and prevent IT service degradations or outages

d513623c7ce6.title: Incident management
d513623c7ce6.section: Incident management in critical infrastructure > Computer security incident management
d513623c7ce6.sentence: Today, an important role is played by a Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT), due to the rise of internet crime, and is a common example of an incident faced by companies in developed nations all across the world.

d6c72fd20d7a.title: Incident management
d6c72fd20d7a.section: Incident management in critical infrastructure > Computer security incident management
d6c72fd20d7a.sentence: For example, if an organization discovers that an intruder has gained unauthorized access to a computer system, the CSIRT would analyze the situation, determine the breadth of the compromise, and take corrective action.

b42a004992f5.title: Site reliability engineering
b42a004992f5.sentence: Kitchen Sink refers to the expansive and often unbounded scope of services and workflows that SRE teams oversee.

b245d6e0cb8d.title: Site reliability engineering
b245d6e0cb8d.sentence: Infrastructure SRE teams focus on maintaining and improving the reliability of systems that support other teams' workflows.

6ef2f8b99650.title: Site reliability engineering
6ef2f8b99650.sentence: SRE teams dedicated to specific products or applications are common in large organizations.

c6e13e401759.title: Site reliability engineering
c6e13e401759.sentence: In an embedded model, individual SREs or small SRE pairs are integrated within software engineering teams.

797eab8fcb1d.title: Site reliability engineering
797eab8fcb1d.sentence: Consulting SRE teams specialize in advising organizations on the implementation of SRE principles and practices.

cd91f632a4b2.title: Site reliability engineering
cd91f632a4b2.sentence: Unlike traditional roles with clearly defined boundaries, SREs are tasked with various responsibilities, including system performance optimization, incident management, and automation.

cb8105531ae8.title: Site reliability engineering
cb8105531ae8.sentence: While they sometimes collaborate with platform engineering teams, their primary responsibility is ensuring up-time, performance, and efficiency.

4f29057d01da.title: Site reliability engineering
4f29057d01da.sentence: Platform teams, on the other hand, primarily develop the software and systems used across the organization.

8b7854aa97b6.title: Site reliability engineering
8b7854aa97b6.sentence: In larger companies, it's typical to have multiple SRE teams, each focusing on different products or applications, ensuring that each area receives specialized attention to meet performance and availability targets.

62d29bf1acfd.title: Site reliability engineering
62d29bf1acfd.sentence: These SREs collaborate with developers, applying core SRE principles—such as automation, monitoring, and incident response—directly to the software development lifecycle.

a671dd82d28b.title: Business continuity planning
a671dd82d28b.sentence: A Business Impact Analysis (BIA) is a process used to identify and evaluate the effects of disruptions on an organization's operations, and to determine recovery priorities and strategies appropriate to the organizational needs.

46a24a88a62d.title: Business continuity planning
46a24a88a62d.sentence: Identify critical activities and dependencies (people, processes, vendors, technology & facilities).

5ea7639216c3.title: Business continuity planning
5ea7639216c3.sentence: Assess the impact of disruptions on these activities (financial, operational, reputational, legal).

e6c5c1729dd2.title: Business continuity planning
e6c5c1729dd2.sentence: For each function, two values are assigned:

472bab461870.title: Business continuity planning
472bab461870.sentence: - Recovery point objective (RPO) – the acceptable latency of data that will not be recovered.

20503681b425.title: Business continuity planning
20503681b425.sentence: For example, is it acceptable for the company to lose 2 days of data?

5b1de3f827bd.title: Business continuity planning
5b1de3f827bd.sentence: - Recovery time objective (RTO) – the acceptable amount of time to restore the function

e41a0196a6a2.title: Business continuity planning
e41a0196a6a2.section: Analysis > Business impact analysis (BIA) > Maximum RTO
e41a0196a6a2.sentence: Maximum time constraints for how long an enterprise's key products or services can be unavailable or undeliverable before stakeholders perceive unacceptable consequences have been named as:

57eced26d282.title: Business continuity planning
57eced26d282.section: Analysis > Business impact analysis (BIA) > Maximum RTO

bdee94f5b432.title: Business continuity planning
bdee94f5b432.section: Analysis > Business impact analysis (BIA) > Maximum RTO

4f4b41287a11.title: Business continuity planning
4f4b41287a11.section: Analysis > Business impact analysis (BIA) > Maximum RTO
4f4b41287a11.sentence: According to ISO 22301 the terms maximum acceptable outage and maximum tolerable period of disruption mean the same thing and are defined using exactly the same words.

cffd00d796e8.title: Business continuity planning
cffd00d796e8.sentence: When more than one system crashes, recovery plans must balance the need for data consistency with other objectives, such as RTO and RPO.

e56ba8bf0ef3.title: Business continuity planning
e56ba8bf0ef3.sentence: Recovery Consistency Objective (RCO) is the name of this goal.

3b350811f55a.title: Business continuity planning
3b350811f55a.sentence: While RTO and RPO are absolute per-system values, RCO is expressed as a percentage that measures the deviation between actual and targeted state of business data across systems for process groups or individual business processes.

64772db078b9.title: Business continuity planning
64772db078b9.sentence: 100% RCO means that post recovery, no business data deviation occurs.

c4a10ba4b281.title: Business continuity planning
c4a10ba4b281.sentence: SHARE's seven tiers of disaster recovery released in 1992, were updated in 2012 by IBM as an eight tier model:

bdb3df21bb10.title: Business continuity planning
bdb3df21bb10.sentence: - Tier 0 – No off-site data • Businesses with a Tier 0 Disaster Recovery solution have no Disaster Recovery Plan.

c37b0deb98ab.title: Business continuity planning
c37b0deb98ab.sentence: There is no saved information, no documentation, no backup hardware, and no contingency plan.

50c2847d0cd4.title: Business continuity planning
50c2847d0cd4.sentence: In fact, it may not be possible to recover at all.

c2cab2c0f8e1.title: Business continuity planning
c2cab2c0f8e1.sentence: - Tier 1 – Data backup with no Hot Site • Businesses that use Tier 1 Disaster Recovery solutions back up their data at an off-site facility.

46f6bf0f8408.title: Business continuity planning
46f6bf0f8408.sentence: Depending on how often backups are made, they are prepared to accept several days to weeks of data loss, but their backups are secure off-site.

3e89f111ee56.title: Business continuity planning
3e89f111ee56.sentence: However, this Tier lacks the systems on which to restore data.

90cc9e0fcef2.title: Business continuity planning
90cc9e0fcef2.sentence: - Tier 2 – Data backup with Hot Site • Tier 2 Disaster Recovery solutions make regular backups on tape.

dd44c26a8f24.title: Business continuity planning
dd44c26a8f24.sentence: This is combined with an off-site facility and infrastructure (known as a hot site) in which to restore systems from those tapes in the event of a disaster.

20866c9e2890.title: Business continuity planning
20866c9e2890.sentence: This tier solution will still result in the need to recreate several hours to days worth of data, but it is less unpredictable in recovery time.

d80cc4d6d9a8.title: Business continuity planning
d80cc4d6d9a8.sentence: - Tier 3 – Electronic vaulting • Tier 3 solutions utilize components of Tier 2.

48d4eeda2547.title: Business continuity planning
48d4eeda2547.sentence: Additionally, some mission-critical data is electronically vaulted.

bba35ddee615.title: Business continuity planning
bba35ddee615.sentence: This electronically vaulted data is typically more current than that which is shipped via PTAM.

2d3f19177d6e.title: Business continuity planning
2d3f19177d6e.sentence: - Tier 4 – Point-in-time copies • Tier 4 solutions are used by businesses that require both greater data currency and faster recovery than users of lower tiers.

bc3d2bc809f0.title: Business continuity planning
bc3d2bc809f0.sentence: Rather than relying largely on shipping tape, as is common in the lower tiers, Tier 4 solutions begin to incorporate more disk-based solutions.

e612f30b54d7.title: Business continuity planning
e612f30b54d7.sentence: - Tier 5 – Transaction integrity • Tier 5 solutions are used by businesses with a requirement for consistency of data between production and recovery data centers.

f9f1970690ef.title: Business continuity planning
f9f1970690ef.sentence: There is little to no data loss in such solutions; however, the presence of this functionality is entirely dependent on the application in use.

5f94b1791575.title: Business continuity planning
5f94b1791575.sentence: - Tier 6 – Zero or little data loss • Tier 6 Disaster Recovery solutions maintain the highest levels of data currency.

100c4aa4de95.title: Business continuity planning
100c4aa4de95.sentence: They are used by businesses with little or no tolerance for data loss and who need to restore data to applications rapidly.

a33edee055e5.title: Business continuity planning
a33edee055e5.sentence: These solutions have no dependence on the applications to provide data consistency.

429d7b589a35.title: Business continuity planning
429d7b589a35.sentence: - Tier 7 – Highly automated, business-integrated solution • Tier 7 solutions include all the major components being used for a Tier 6 solution with the additional integration of automation.

e4e670a4fdee.title: Business continuity planning
e4e670a4fdee.sentence: Additionally, recovery of the applications is automated, allowing for restoration of systems and applications much faster and more reliably than would be possible through manual Disaster Recovery procedures.

2faae76acc72.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity

2faae76acc72.sentence: In just short of 7 days, 1.5 petabytes of audio data had been reinstated to users with the help of offsite tape backups; 5 of the 7 days comprised the actual data recovery effort.

1239f53e65a9.sentence: The majority of these files were store-bought and promotional tracks, and the original store copies were unaffected by the bug.

2f6eb5d91b21.section: Google MusicâMarch 2012: Runaway Deletion Detection > Addressing the root cause
2f6eb5d91b21.sentence: But the stages may take longer to complete as the volume of data grows.

040ec9690a54.sentence: Eventually, the original design assumptions may no longer hold for certain pieces of data needed by the second stage.

cd004da5eed9.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity
cd004da5eed9.section: Google MusicâMarch 2012: Runaway Deletion Detection > Addressing the root cause
cd004da5eed9.sentence: But as the volume of data increases, a larger and larger fraction of the data is at risk for triggering a race condition.

c1dfeff42151.section: Google MusicâMarch 2012: Runaway Deletion Detection > Addressing the root cause
c1dfeff42151.sentence: When such race conditions occur in a data deletion pipeline, the wrong data can be deleted nondeterministically.

4742d04031d7.sentence: In the wake of the recovery effort, Google Music redesigned its data deletion pipeline to eliminate this type of race condition.

258dff68d391.sentence: In addition, we enhanced production monitoring and alerting systems to detect similar large-scale runaway deletion bugs with the aim of detecting and fixing such issues before users notice any problems.133
