100bc5aee2af.title: Chroot
100bc5aee2af.sentence: chroot is a shell command and a system call on Unix and Unix-like operating systems that changes the apparent root directory for the current running process and its children.

dc4f8983ccbb.title: Chroot
dc4f8983ccbb.sentence: A program that is run in such a modified environment cannot name (and therefore normally cannot access) files outside the designated directory tree.

68ad7937c6a3.title: Chroot
68ad7937c6a3.sentence: The modified environment is called a chroot jail.

74479a0d956d.title: Chroot
74479a0d956d.sentence: Software can be developed, built and tested in a chroot populated only with its expected dependencies.

0d2c3c4859f8.title: Chroot
0d2c3c4859f8.sentence: This can prevent some kinds of linkage skew that can result from developers building projects with different sets of program libraries installed.

9e1ef204ca33.title: Chroot
9e1ef204ca33.sentence: Legacy software or software using a different ABI must sometimes be run in a chroot because their supporting libraries or data files may otherwise clash in name or linkage with those of the host system.

c61ef1e9ebe2.title: Chroot
c61ef1e9ebe2.sentence: The chroot mechanism is not intended to defend against intentional tampering by privileged (root) users.

449c04e786a0.title: Chroot
449c04e786a0.sentence: On most systems, chroot contexts do not stack properly and chrooted programs with sufficient privileges may perform a second chroot to break out.

d3f17b556d3d.title: Chroot
d3f17b556d3d.sentence: It is not intended to restrict the use of resources like I/O, bandwidth, disk space or CPU time.

a1e62e6a7b65.title: OS-level virtualization
a1e62e6a7b65.sentence: On Unix-like operating systems, this feature can be seen as an advanced implementation of the standard chroot mechanism, which changes the apparent root folder for the current running process and its children.

94748a0f4ed7.title: Chroot
94748a0f4ed7.sentence: To make it useful for virtualization, FreeBSD expanded the concept and in its 4.0 release in 2000 introduced the jail command.

440658687457.title: Kubernetes
440658687457.sentence: Kubernetes (/ˌk(j)uːbərˈnɛtɪs, -ˈneɪtɪs, -ˈneɪtiːz, -ˈnɛtiːz/), also known as K8s, is an open-source container orchestration system for automating software deployment, scaling, and management.

af1da472ad79.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-k8s-kubernetes.md
af1da472ad79.sentence: k8s is a container orchestration system.

232b3df1a3f9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-k8s-kubernetes.md
232b3df1a3f9.sentence: It is used for container deployment and management.

d8a93e3540df.title: Kubernetes
d8a93e3540df.sentence: Kubernetes assembles one or more computers, either virtual machines or bare metal, into a cluster which can run workloads in containers.

632a8293309b.title: Kubernetes
632a8293309b.sentence: The software consists of a control plane and nodes on which the actual applications run.

cb9ff475e691.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-k8s-kubernetes.md
cb9ff475e691.sentence: A k8s cluster consists of a set of worker machines, called nodes, that run containerized applications.

50008849f940.title: Kubernetes
50008849f940.sentence: Kubernetes defines a set of building blocks ("primitives") that collectively provide mechanisms that deploy, maintain, and scale applications based on CPU, memory or custom metrics.

95956263aff5.title: Kubernetes
95956263aff5.sentence: Kubernetes is loosely coupled and extensible to meet the needs of different workloads.

ae88a40a7d4a.title: Kubernetes
ae88a40a7d4a.sentence: The internal components as well as extensions and containers that run on Kubernetes rely on the Kubernetes API.

027ebd60ae90.title: Kubernetes
027ebd60ae90.sentence: The platform exerts its control over compute and storage resources by defining resources as objects, which can then be managed as such.

957a315fa61c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-k8s-kubernetes.md
957a315fa61c.sentence: In production environments, the control plane usually runs across multiple computers and a cluster usually runs multiple nodes, providing fault tolerance and high availability.

21ca4c7e46b5.title: Kubernetes
21ca4c7e46b5.sentence: Kubernetes is commonly used as a way to host a microservice-based implementation, because it and its associated ecosystem of tools provide all the capabilities needed to address key concerns of any microservice architecture.

4b44547e5254.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-k8s-kubernetes.md
4b44547e5254.sentence: Its design is greatly impacted by Google’s internal system Borg.

9fba9d0c38b4.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
9fba9d0c38b4.sentence: - Additionally, Kubernetes is not a mere orchestration system.

af04909662e3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
af04909662e3.sentence: The technical definition of orchestration is execution of a defined workflow: first do A, then B, then C. In contrast, Kubernetes comprises a set of independent, composable control processes that continuously drive the current state towards the provided desired state.

43ead9998862.title: OS-level virtualization
43ead9998862.sentence: OS-level virtualization is an operating system (OS) virtualization paradigm in which the kernel allows the existence of multiple isolated user space instances, including containers (LXC, Solaris Containers, AIX WPARs, HP-UX SRP Containers, Docker, Podman, Guix), zones (Solaris Containers), virtual private servers (OpenVZ), partitions, virtual environments (VEs), virtual kernels (DragonFly BSD), and jails (FreeBSD jail and chroot).

ff76e8c94dc0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
ff76e8c94dc0.sentence: A container is a standard unit of software that packages up code and all its dependencies such as specific versions of runtimes and libraries so that the application runs quickly and reliably from one computing environment to another.

466a3c24a6f6.title: OS-level virtualization
466a3c24a6f6.sentence: Programs running inside a container can only see the container's contents and devices assigned to the container.

db2fdc45703f.title: OS-level virtualization
db2fdc45703f.sentence: Several containers can be created on each operating system, to each of which a subset of the computer's resources is allocated.

53488c2d343a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
53488c2d343a.sentence: Containers offer a logical packaging mechanism in which applications can be abstracted from the environment in which they actually run.

1a1c4bb6e60c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
1a1c4bb6e60c.sentence: This decoupling allows container-based applications to be deployed easily and consistently, regardless of the target environment.

9e193dcbb148.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
9e193dcbb148.section: Containers > Why do we need containers?
9e193dcbb148.sentence: Containerization provides a clear separation of responsibility, as developers focus on application logic and dependencies, while operations teams can focus on deployment and management.

dde089a1e198.title: OS-level virtualization
dde089a1e198.sentence: In addition to isolation mechanisms, the kernel often provides resource-management features to limit the impact of one container's activities on other containers.

2df25c16c249.title: OS-level virtualization
2df25c16c249.sentence: Linux containers are all based on the virtualization, isolation, and resource management mechanisms provided by the Linux kernel, notably Linux namespaces and cgroups.

514cd318515d.title: OS-level virtualization
514cd318515d.sentence: Operating-system level virtualization usually imposes less overhead than full virtualization because programs in OS-level virtual partitions use the operating system's normal system call interface and do not need to be subjected to emulation or be run in an intermediate virtual machine, as is the case with full virtualization (such as VMware ESXi, QEMU, or Hyper-V) and paravirtualization (such as Xen or User-mode Linux).

c3d477a45dc1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
c3d477a45dc1.section: Containers > Why do we need containers?
c3d477a45dc1.sentence: Containers are lightweight and allow us to use just the computing resources we need.

7f830e9d0af7.title: OS-level virtualization
7f830e9d0af7.sentence: Operating-system level virtualization is not as flexible as other virtualization approaches since it cannot host a guest operating system different from the host one, or a different guest kernel.

879c9cc4fe8c.title: OS-level virtualization
879c9cc4fe8c.sentence: For example, with Linux, different distributions are fine, but other operating systems such as Windows cannot be hosted.

5c558e14af78.title: OS-level virtualization
5c558e14af78.sentence: Operating-system level virtualization is commonly used in virtual hosting environments, where it is useful for securely allocating finite hardware resources among a large number of mutually-distrusting users.

a0b9ca87a799.title: OS-level virtualization
a0b9ca87a799.sentence: System administrators may also use it for consolidating server hardware by moving services on separate hosts into containers on the one server.

224306351283.title: Cgroups
224306351283.sentence: cgroups (abbreviated from control groups) is a Linux kernel feature that limits, accounts for, and isolates the resource usage (CPU, memory, disk I/O, etc.) of a collection of processes.

df63743251e2.title: Cgroups
df63743251e2.sentence: A control group (abbreviated as cgroup) is a collection of processes that are bound by the same criteria and associated with a set of parameters or limits.

e617b02bc4c3.title: Cgroups
e617b02bc4c3.sentence: These groups can be hierarchical, meaning that each group inherits limits from its parent group.

91605ebc105b.title: Cgroups
91605ebc105b.sentence: The kernel provides access to multiple controllers (also called subsystems) through the cgroup interface; for example, the "memory" controller limits memory use, "cpuacct" accounts CPU usage, etc.

e1d516c8035d.title: Cgroups
e1d516c8035d.sentence: groups can be set not to exceed a configured memory limit, which also includes the file system cache, I/O bandwidth limit, CPU quota limit, CPU set limit, or maximum open files.

2ce839ecd0ea.title: Cgroups
2ce839ecd0ea.sentence: some groups may get a larger share of CPU utilization or disk I/O throughput

4ccddc2969d4.title: Cgroups
4ccddc2969d4.sentence: measures a group's resource usage, which may be used, for example, for billing purposes

bad4a5b71f9f.title: Cgroups
bad4a5b71f9f.sentence: freezing groups of processes, their checkpointing and restarting

f30a8843d73a.title: Cgroups
f30a8843d73a.sentence: Both versions of cgroup act through a pseudo-filesystem (cgroup for v1 and cgroup2 for v2).

dd9e93caaba3.title: Cgroups
dd9e93caaba3.sentence: Like all filesystems they can be mounted on any path, but the general convention is to mount one of the versions (generally v2) on /sys/fs/cgroup under the sysfs default location of /sys.

6d7c6a4daaa8.title: Cgroups
6d7c6a4daaa8.sentence: To create a subgroup, one simply creates a new directory under an existing group (including the top-level one).

acaa999a094d.title: Cgroups
acaa999a094d.sentence: The files corresponding to available controls for this group are automatically created.

27a9baa967ea.title: Cgroups
27a9baa967ea.sentence: Unlike v1, cgroup v2 has only a single process hierarchy (because a controller can only be assigned to one hierarchy, processes in separate hierarchies cannot be managed by the same controller; this change sidesteps the issue).

bd60cd795c40.title: Cgroups
bd60cd795c40.sentence: It also removes the ability to discriminate between threads, choosing to work on a granularity of processes instead (disabling an "abuse" of the system which led to convoluted APIs).

1ffbc4f661bd.title: Cgroups
1ffbc4f661bd.sentence: Linux kernel 4.5 released on 14 March 2016 is the first version that supports cgroup v2.

0f714e970644.title: Cgroups
0f714e970644.sentence: - Indirectly through other software that uses cgroups, such as Docker, Firejail, LXC, libvirt, systemd, Open Grid Scheduler/Grid Engine, and Google's developmentally defunct lmctfy.

cc411c487686.title: Cgroups
cc411c487686.sentence: Various projects use cgroups as their basis, including CoreOS, Docker (in 2013), Hadoop, Jelastic, Kubernetes, lmctfy (Let Me Contain That For You), LXC (Linux Containers), systemd, Mesos and Mesosphere, HTCondor, and Flatpak.

460281e32e27.title: Cgroups
460281e32e27.section: Major evolutions > Changes after v2 > cgroup awareness of OOM killer
460281e32e27.sentence: Linux Kernel 4.19 (October 2018) introduced cgroup awareness of OOM killer implementation which adds an ability to kill a cgroup as a single unit and so guarantee the integrity of the workload.

d9db25084461.title: Linux namespaces
d9db25084461.sentence: While cgroups dictate how much of a system's resources a process can use (such as CPU, memory, and disk I/O limits), namespaces dictate what a process is allowed to see and interact with.

6797f303ba72.title: Docker (software)
6797f303ba72.sentence: The Linux kernel's support for namespaces mostly isolates an application's view of the operating environment, including process trees, network, user IDs and mounted file systems, while the kernel's cgroups provide resource limiting for memory and CPU.

ad3dc47d6244.title: Linux namespaces
ad3dc47d6244.sentence: Namespaces are a feature of the Linux kernel that partition kernel resources such that one set of processes sees one set of resources, while another set of processes sees a different set of resources.

615da8d99be7.title: Linux namespaces
615da8d99be7.sentence: This provides the illusion that a process or a process group is the sole user of the system's hardware and software resources.

beff41c4d66c.title: Linux namespaces
beff41c4d66c.sentence: Linux namespaces, alongside cgroups (control groups), are the foundational technologies underpinning modern OS-level virtualization and Linux containerization platforms such as Docker, Kubernetes, LXC, and Podman.

4696bb53f0f4.title: Linux namespaces
4696bb53f0f4.sentence: A Linux system begins with a single initial namespace of each type, which is shared by all processes.

eb9e9176aab0.title: Linux namespaces
eb9e9176aab0.sentence: Processes can subsequently create additional namespaces or join existing ones, allowing complex, nested isolation boundaries.

98cccf13f1f3.title: Linux namespaces
98cccf13f1f3.sentence: Examples of such resources include process IDs, hostnames, user IDs, file names, network interfaces, and inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms.

3538e9422b57.title: Linux namespaces
3538e9422b57.sentence: As of Linux kernel version 5.6, there are exactly eight kinds of namespaces.

d97351995a92.title: Linux namespaces
d97351995a92.sentence: Mount namespaces, the first namespace to be added to Linux, control mount points.

3e3c18c7d749.title: Linux namespaces
3e3c18c7d749.sentence: The PID namespace provides processes with an independent set of process IDs (PIDs).

88871deddc77.title: Linux namespaces
88871deddc77.sentence: Network namespaces virtualize the network stack.

f5272bc15c85.title: Linux namespaces
f5272bc15c85.sentence: IPC namespaces isolate processes from SysV style inter-process communication mechanisms, as well as POSIX message queues.

bba62446b4ae.title: Linux namespaces
bba62446b4ae.sentence: UTS namespaces isolate two system identifiers: the hostname and the NIS domain name.

96ada10fdd36.title: Linux namespaces
96ada10fdd36.sentence: User namespaces are a critical security feature designed to provide both privilege isolation and user identification segregation across multiple sets of processes.

e03b8011709b.title: Linux namespaces
e03b8011709b.sentence: The cgroup namespace hides the identity of the control group hierarchy to which a process belongs.

f70529243421.title: Linux namespaces
f70529243421.sentence: The time namespace allows processes to observe different system times.

459b63fef400.title: Linux namespaces
459b63fef400.sentence: Hence, processes in the initial PID namespace (like the host operating system) are able to see all processes across all containers, albeit with different PIDs than those seen inside the containers.

f69f422a33e6.title: Linux namespaces
f69f422a33e6.sentence: The first process created in a PID namespace is assigned process ID number 1.

14f10c4d7fd6.title: Linux namespaces
14f10c4d7fd6.sentence: If this PID 1 process terminates, the kernel will immediately terminate all other processes within that PID namespace and any of its descendants by sending them a SIGKILL signal.

d7491b49e1e6.title: Linux namespaces
d7491b49e1e6.sentence: Each network namespace maintains a private set of IP addresses, its own routing table, socket listing, connection tracking table, firewall rules (such as iptables or nftables), and other network-related resources.

24bb6e618399.title: Linux namespaces
24bb6e618399.sentence: To grant a container network connectivity, administrators typically create a Virtual Ethernet (veth) pair, placing one end in the host namespace and the other inside the container's network namespace, and then bridge the host end to a physical network.

7ed40c43b853.title: Linux namespaces
7ed40c43b853.sentence: A user namespace maintains a mapping table that converts user IDs (UIDs) and group IDs (GIDs) from the container's internal perspective to the host system's global perspective.

e0937d70b812.title: Linux namespaces
e0937d70b812.sentence: This allows a process to possess root privileges (UID 0) inside the container, but mathematically map to an unprivileged, restricted user ID (e.g., UID 100000) on the underlying host machine.

dbb967353e54.title: Linux namespaces
dbb967353e54.sentence: Introduced completely in kernel 3.8, they are the backbone of unprivileged containers.

ec45972ad908.title: Linux namespaces
ec45972ad908.sentence: By passing specific flags (such as CLONE_NEWPID or CLONE_NEWNET), the kernel will create the specified new namespaces and place the child process inside them.

d5ba40603e4b.title: Linux namespaces
d5ba40603e4b.sentence: - unshare: Allows a process to disassociate parts of its execution context from its parent, effectively moving the calling process into a brand new namespace.

96a3c22fe383.title: Linux namespaces
96a3c22fe383.sentence: - setns: Allows a running process to enter an already existing namespace.

ae23431984e0.title: Linux namespaces
ae23431984e0.sentence: If a namespace is no longer referenced by any part of the system, the kernel will automatically destroy it.

769a7bdd2911.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
769a7bdd2911.sentence: Pods follow a defined lifecycle, starting in the Pending phase, moving through Running if at least one of its primary containers starts OK, and then through either the Succeeded or Failed phases depending on whether any container in the Pod terminated in failure.

60a9e8549298.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
60a9e8549298.sentence: Like individual application containers, Pods are considered to be relatively ephemeral (rather than durable) entities.

86ff7489309f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
86ff7489309f.sentence: Pods are created, assigned a unique ID (UID), and scheduled to run on nodes where they remain until termination (according to restart policy) or deletion.

482981b11a8c.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
482981b11a8c.sentence: Pods are only scheduled once in their lifetime; assigning a Pod to a specific node is called binding, and the process of selecting which node to use is called scheduling.

dd607429384a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
dd607429384a.sentence: The phase of a Pod is a simple, high-level summary of where the Pod is in its lifecycle.

c9154903eb2b.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
c9154903eb2b.sentence: The phase is not intended to be a comprehensive rollup of observations of container or Pod state, nor is it intended to be a comprehensive state machine.

8c3c98b6b35f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
8c3c98b6b35f.sentence: Pending | The Pod has been accepted by the Kubernetes cluster, but one or more of the containers has not been set up and made ready to run. This includes time a Pod spends waiting to be scheduled as well as the time spent downloading container images over the network.

2bee4cb2fe07.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
2bee4cb2fe07.sentence: Running | The Pod has been bound to a node, and all of the containers have been created. At least one container is still running, or is in the process of starting or restarting.

6d252c8c0b80.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
6d252c8c0b80.sentence: Succeeded | All containers in the Pod have terminated in success, and will not be restarted.

56efde003f69.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
56efde003f69.sentence: Failed | All containers in the Pod have terminated, and at least one container has terminated in failure. That is, the container either exited with non-zero status or was terminated by the system, and is not set for automatic restarting.

ecade6597de6.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
ecade6597de6.sentence: Unknown | For some reason the state of the Pod could not be obtained. This phase typically occurs due to an error in communicating with the node where the Pod should be running.

d8b17b7ffce7.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
d8b17b7ffce7.sentence: There are three possible container states: Waiting, Running, and Terminated.

9f9c9ea5fdf9.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
9f9c9ea5fdf9.sentence: A container in the Waiting state is still running the operations it requires in order to complete start up: for example, pulling the container image from a container image registry, or applying Secret data.

5ce0278cf616.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
5ce0278cf616.sentence: The Running status indicates that a container is executing without issues.

33d926fbc83a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
33d926fbc83a.sentence: If there was a postStart hook configured, it has already executed and finished.

5ee7813c0f85.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle

975f0d9f2c73.sentence: If one of the containers in the Pod fails, then Kubernetes may try to restart that specific container.

704d6675c8b3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
704d6675c8b3.section: Pod lifetime > Pods and fault recovery
704d6675c8b3.sentence: Pods can however fail in a way that the cluster cannot recover from, and in that case Kubernetes does not attempt to heal the Pod further; instead, Kubernetes deletes the Pod and relies on other components to provide automatic healing.

9b4952bef9cc.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
9b4952bef9cc.section: Pod lifetime > Pods and fault recovery
9b4952bef9cc.sentence: If a Pod is scheduled to a node and that node then fails, the Pod is treated as unhealthy and Kubernetes eventually deletes the Pod.

7a5d018c805a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
7a5d018c805a.section: Pod lifetime > Pods and fault recovery
7a5d018c805a.sentence: A Pod won't survive an eviction due to a lack of resources or Node maintenance.

d4e691ffe6c2.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
d4e691ffe6c2.section: Pod lifetime > Pods and fault recovery
d4e691ffe6c2.sentence: Kubernetes uses a higher-level abstraction, called a controller, that handles the work of managing the relatively disposable Pod instances.

b693669a3a2b.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
b693669a3a2b.sentence: If a Node dies, the Pods running on (or scheduled to run on) that node are marked for deletion.

f0d2e83c1bfd.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
f0d2e83c1bfd.sentence: The control plane marks the Pods for removal after a timeout period.

779eef1ee9e2.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
779eef1ee9e2.section: Pod lifetime > Pods and fault recovery
779eef1ee9e2.sentence: A given Pod (as defined by a UID) is never "rescheduled" to a different node; instead, that Pod can be replaced by a new, near-identical Pod.

0742dbcafbbe.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
0742dbcafbbe.section: Pod lifetime > Pods and fault recovery
0742dbcafbbe.sentence: If you make a replacement Pod, it can even have same name (as in.metadata.name) that the old Pod had, but the replacement would have a different.metadata.uid from the old Pod.

e334800fc299.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
e334800fc299.section: Pod lifetime > Pods and fault recovery
e334800fc299.sentence: Kubernetes does not guarantee that a replacement for an existing Pod would be scheduled to the same node as the old Pod that was being replaced.

e14baf5437ba.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
e14baf5437ba.sentence: When something is said to have the same lifetime as a Pod, such as a volume, that means that the thing exists as long as that specific Pod (with that exact UID) exists.

4e49ff39a8c3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
4e49ff39a8c3.sentence: If that Pod is deleted for any reason, and even if an identical replacement is created, the related thing (a volume, in this example) is also destroyed and created anew.

111b3a373e97.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
111b3a373e97.sentence: A probe is a diagnostic performed periodically by the kubelet on a container.

88f2b9546b70.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
88f2b9546b70.sentence: Based on the probe results, Kubernetes can restart unhealthy containers or stop sending traffic to containers that are not ready.

b8cfddf900f0.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle

988f8e48bad9.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods

a4480da6287d.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
a4480da6287d.sentence: To perform a probe, the kubelet executes the command cat /tmp/healthy in the target container.

26c1e4476679.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
26c1e4476679.sentence: If the command succeeds, it returns 0, and the kubelet considers the container to be alive and healthy.

172cae4f8ce4.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes

1d0682b487bf.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
1d0682b487bf.sentence: If it can establish a connection, the container is considered healthy, if it can't it is considered a failure.

184b9382a1a5.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes

db6cb0447680.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
db6cb0447680.sentence: Any code greater than or equal to 200 and less than 400 indicates success.

49c53f7a4228.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
49c53f7a4228.sentence: If your application implements the gRPC Health Checking Protocol, this example shows how to configure Kubernetes to use it for application liveness checks.

36f68ca10c91.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
36f68ca10c91.sentence: All errors are considered as probe failures.

1aa99ff514c5.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
1aa99ff514c5.sentence: Liveness probes determine when to restart a container.

42df6122a3b1.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
42df6122a3b1.sentence: For example, liveness probes could catch a deadlock, where an application is running, but unable to make progress.

b001db75c663.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
b001db75c663.sentence: If a container fails its liveness probe more times than the configured tolerance, the kubelet restarts that container.

ce7f2ef3e36e.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
ce7f2ef3e36e.sentence: If you want to wait before executing a liveness probe, you can either define initialDelaySeconds or use a startup probe.

8cee5fe94e81.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
8cee5fe94e81.sentence: The periodSeconds field specifies that the kubelet should perform a liveness probe every 5 seconds.

80c38f2999de.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes

163fd83083b7.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
163fd83083b7.sentence: Readiness probes determine when a container is ready to accept traffic.

e5e2462e3ba3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
e5e2462e3ba3.sentence: This is useful when waiting for an application to perform time-consuming initial tasks, such as establishing network connections, loading files, and warming caches.

969c39104e21.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
969c39104e21.sentence: Readiness probes can also be useful later in the container's lifecycle, for example, when recovering from temporary faults or overloads.

0906265b7800.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle

438e42bf521c.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
438e42bf521c.sentence: Startup probes verify whether the application within a container is started.

545074fcca2f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
545074fcca2f.sentence: If a startup probe is configured, Kubernetes does not execute liveness or readiness probes until the startup probe succeeds, allowing the application time to finish its initialization.

32d665c6d853.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
32d665c6d853.sentence: This type of probe is only executed at startup, unlike liveness and readiness probes, which are run periodically.

a7ae30eebc11.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle
a7ae30eebc11.sentence: If the startup probe fails, the kubelet kills the container, and the container is subjected to its restart policy.

a68a5ee31a91.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
a68a5ee31a91.section: Protect slow starting containers with startup probes
a68a5ee31a91.sentence: In such cases, it can be tricky to set up liveness probe parameters without compromising the fast response to deadlocks that motivated such a probe.

c4f83208073c.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes

c4f83208073c.sentence: The solution is to set up a startup probe with the same command, HTTP or TCP check, with a failureThreshold * periodSeconds long enough to cover the worst case startup time.

7cd61340aa28.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes
7cd61340aa28.section: Protect slow starting containers with startup probes

a596212f9808.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes

a596212f9808.sentence: Once the startup probe has succeeded once, the liveness probe takes over to provide a fast response to container deadlocks.

0bbeb385d1db.title: Docker (software)
0bbeb385d1db.sentence: Docker is a set of products that uses operating system-level virtualization to deliver software in packages called containers.

50a74e6ab5dd.title: Docker (software)
50a74e6ab5dd.sentence: Docker automates the deployment of applications within lightweight containers, enabling them to run consistently across different computing environments.

2f7fe2a2cd81.title: Docker (software)
2f7fe2a2cd81.sentence: The core software that runs and manages these containers is called Docker Engine.

a885023b6beb.title: Docker (software)
a885023b6beb.sentence: Containers are isolated from one another and bundle their own software, libraries and configuration files; they can communicate with each other through well-defined channels.

47033e3fc097.title: Docker (software)
47033e3fc097.sentence: Because all of the containers share the services of a single operating system kernel, they use fewer resources than virtual machines.

9a215d6224f0.title: Docker (software)
9a215d6224f0.sentence: Because Docker containers are lightweight, a single server or virtual machine can run several containers simultaneously.

75e120bcc47e.title: Docker (software)
75e120bcc47e.sentence: When running on Linux, Docker uses the resource isolation features of the Linux kernel (such as cgroups and kernel namespaces) and a union-capable file system (such as OverlayFS) to allow containers to run within a single Linux instance, avoiding the overhead of starting and maintaining virtual machines.

f86338c523e5.title: Docker (software)
f86338c523e5.sentence: Docker on macOS uses a Linux virtual machine to run the containers.

ac753cf4c288.title: Docker (software)
ac753cf4c288.sentence: The Docker daemon, called dockerd, is a persistent process that manages Docker containers and handles container objects.

adf139943717.title: Docker (software)
adf139943717.sentence: The daemon listens for requests that are sent via the Docker Engine API.

46ea60e021b9.title: Docker (software)
46ea60e021b9.sentence: The Docker client program, called docker, provides a command-line interface (CLI) that allows users to interact with Docker daemons.

a158f0e92742.title: Docker (software)
a158f0e92742.sentence: The main classes of Docker objects are images, containers, and services.

58adfe687902.title: Docker (software)
58adfe687902.sentence: A Docker container is a standardized, encapsulated environment that runs applications.

229a86ac2c03.title: Docker (software)
229a86ac2c03.sentence: A Docker image is a read-only template used to build containers.

06d34915d948.title: Docker (software)
06d34915d948.sentence: A Docker registry is a repository for Docker images.

dd99927f112a.title: Docker (software)
dd99927f112a.sentence: Images are used to store and ship applications.

0c4a48e1a7e2.title: Docker (software)
0c4a48e1a7e2.sentence: A Dockerfile is a text file that commonly specifies several aspects of a Docker image: the Linux distribution, installation commands for the programming language runtime environment and application source code.

00135ba37fde.title: Docker (software)
00135ba37fde.sentence: Docker clients connect to registries to download ("pull") images for use or upload ("push") images that they have built.

18506e0b4629.title: Docker (software)
18506e0b4629.sentence: Docker Hub is the default registry where Docker looks for images.

1b0c99729bd9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
1b0c99729bd9.sentence: Docker Hub is a public registry that anyone can use.

dc14f2951ec8.title: Docker (software)
dc14f2951ec8.sentence: Docker registries also allow the creation of notifications based on events.

eb593e242a05.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
eb593e242a05.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
eb593e242a05.sentence: In a production environment, you need to manage the containers that run the applications and ensure that there is no downtime.

6058650f9cfc.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
6058650f9cfc.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
6058650f9cfc.sentence: For example, if a container goes down, another container needs to start.

a4c96e1803c6.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
a4c96e1803c6.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
a4c96e1803c6.sentence: Kubernetes provides you with a framework to run distributed systems resiliently.

c6e0e45e9940.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
c6e0e45e9940.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
c6e0e45e9940.sentence: It takes care of scaling and failover for your application, provides deployment patterns, and more.

7a58eb7f497d.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
7a58eb7f497d.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
7a58eb7f497d.sentence: - Service discovery and load balancing Kubernetes can expose a container using a DNS name or its own IP address.

10c8f37ee8e1.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
10c8f37ee8e1.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
10c8f37ee8e1.sentence: If traffic to a container is high, Kubernetes is able to load balance and distribute the network traffic so that the deployment is stable.

c71ae2209c5a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
c71ae2209c5a.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
c71ae2209c5a.sentence: - Automated rollouts and rollbacks You can describe the desired state for your deployed containers using Kubernetes, and it can change the actual state to the desired state at a controlled rate.

129fd3e4465c.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
129fd3e4465c.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
129fd3e4465c.sentence: For example, you can automate Kubernetes to create new containers for your deployment, remove existing containers and adopt all their resources to the new container.

11fb454ffe2c.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
11fb454ffe2c.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
11fb454ffe2c.sentence: - Automatic bin packing You provide Kubernetes with a cluster of nodes that it can use to run containerized tasks.

e8ec94655ef8.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
e8ec94655ef8.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
e8ec94655ef8.sentence: You tell Kubernetes how much CPU and memory (RAM) each container needs.

1201ceb73cfd.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
1201ceb73cfd.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
1201ceb73cfd.sentence: Kubernetes can fit containers onto your nodes to make the best use of your resources.

ef1080bc1009.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
ef1080bc1009.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
ef1080bc1009.sentence: - Self-healing Kubernetes restarts containers that fail, replaces containers, kills containers that don't respond to your user-defined health check, and doesn't advertise them to clients until they are ready to serve.

69562d3a3dbe.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
69562d3a3dbe.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
69562d3a3dbe.sentence: - Horizontal scaling Scale your application up and down with a simple command, with a UI, or automatically based on CPU usage.

49e8e96e93c4.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
49e8e96e93c4.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
49e8e96e93c4.sentence: - Storage orchestration Kubernetes allows you to automatically mount a storage system of your choice, such as local storage, public cloud providers, and more.

d069f46907b4.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
d069f46907b4.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
d069f46907b4.sentence: - Secret and configuration management Kubernetes lets you store and manage sensitive information, such as passwords, OAuth tokens, and SSH keys.

6574c92cf9bf.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
6574c92cf9bf.section: Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do
6574c92cf9bf.sentence: You can deploy and update secrets and application configuration without rebuilding your container images, and without exposing secrets in your stack configuration.

65d26d027ffe.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
65d26d027ffe.sentence: Kubernetes is not a traditional, all-inclusive PaaS (Platform as a Service) system.

6296257f6f1d.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
6296257f6f1d.sentence: Since Kubernetes operates at the container level rather than at the hardware level, it provides some generally applicable features common to PaaS offerings, such as deployment, scaling, load balancing, and lets users integrate their logging, monitoring, and alerting solutions.

e0605c64742f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
e0605c64742f.sentence: However, Kubernetes is not monolithic, and these default solutions are optional and pluggable.

1df0d134f69b.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
1df0d134f69b.sentence: - Does not deploy source code and does not build your application.

3d6d5fac7ed9.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
3d6d5fac7ed9.sentence: - Does not provide application-level services, such as middleware (for example, message buses), data-processing frameworks (for example, Spark), databases (for example, MySQL), caches, nor cluster storage systems (for example, Ceph) as built-in services.

696b3a4a481a.sentence: A container runtime is responsible for the lifecycle of containers, including launching, reconciling and killing of containers. kubelet interacts with container runtimes via the Container Runtime Interface (CRI), which decouples the maintenance of core Kubernetes from the actual CRI implementation.

eb49b7abc1b4.title: Kubernetes
eb49b7abc1b4.sentence: Every node in the cluster must run a container runtime, as well as the below-mentioned components, for communication with the primary network configuration of these containers.

19bcc64fc4b6.title: Kubernetes
19bcc64fc4b6.sentence: As of 2026, widely used CRI-compliant container runtimes include containerd and CRI-O.

3cfdb81a19bd.title: Kubernetes
3cfdb81a19bd.sentence: Originally, kubelet was tightly coupled to Docker as a container runtime.

38e54ddb0acc.title: Kubernetes
38e54ddb0acc.sentence: With the release of v1.24 in May 2022, the "dockershim" has been removed entirely, dropping official support for Docker as a container runtime.

6609faafd18e.title: Docker (software)
6609faafd18e.sentence: Since version 1.11, released in April 2016, Docker Engine has been built on containerd and runc, the reference implementation of the Open Container Initiative runtime specification, which Docker donated to the OCI in 2015. containerd uses runc by default, but Docker can be configured to use other runtimes, including the sandboxed runtimes gVisor and Kata Containers.

c600c0a5acf4.title: Kubernetes
c600c0a5acf4.sentence: A node, also known as a worker or a minion, is a machine where containers (workloads) are deployed.
