29888e0f171e.sentence: This means that a restart of the container will wipe out its filesystem.

96eeacead95a.title: Kubernetes
96eeacead95a.sentence: A Kubernetes volume provides persistent storage.

9e806933c018.title: Kubernetes
9e806933c018.sentence: Therefore, this form of storage is quite limiting in anything but trivial applications.

63fabd4d88c8.title: Kubernetes
63fabd4d88c8.sentence: This storage can also be used as shared disk space for containers within the pod.

7a26b7f3167f.title: Kubernetes
7a26b7f3167f.sentence: The same volume can be mounted at different points in the file system tree by different containers.

f70050f1bf01.title: Docker (software)
f70050f1bf01.sentence: Docker Volume facilitates the independent persistence of data, allowing data to remain even after the container is deleted or re-created.

714be124d440.title: Kubernetes
714be124d440.sentence: Historically Kubernetes was suitable only for stateless services.

cc42648b7fe5.title: Kubernetes
cc42648b7fe5.sentence: However, many applications have a database, which requires persistence, leading to the creation of persistent storage for Kubernetes.

ad08bfd92ce1.title: Kubernetes
ad08bfd92ce1.sentence: By creating a standardized CSI, the code required to interface with external storage systems was separated from the core Kubernetes code base.

5d38dad24ce1.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
5d38dad24ce1.sentence: Pods are designed to support multiple cooperating processes (as containers) that form a cohesive unit of service.

d03e1d8b34ad.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
d03e1d8b34ad.sentence: You can also have sidecar containers that provide auxiliary services to the main application Pod (for example: a service mesh).

a97c78742904.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
a97c78742904.sentence: The containers in a Pod are automatically co-located and co-scheduled on the same physical or virtual machine in the cluster.

b81b6a07fc62.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
b81b6a07fc62.sentence: The containers can share resources and dependencies, communicate with one another, and coordinate when and how they are terminated.

fc3bd5a0fe4a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
fc3bd5a0fe4a.sentence: The "one-container-per-Pod" model is the most common Kubernetes use case; in this case, you can think of a Pod as a wrapper around a single container; Kubernetes manages Pods rather than managing the containers directly.

95a4f0bda132.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
95a4f0bda132.sentence: These co-located containers form a single cohesive unit of service—for example, one container serving data stored in a shared volume to the public, while a separate sidecar container refreshes or updates those files.

9acefab4afb3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
9acefab4afb3.sentence: For example, you might have a container that acts as a web server for files in a shared volume, and a separate sidecar container that updates those files from a remote source, as in the following diagram:

faf45a8d28ce.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
faf45a8d28ce.sentence: Enabled by default, the SidecarContainers feature gate allows you to specify restartPolicy: Always for init containers.

e9d6c5520032.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
e9d6c5520032.sentence: Setting the Always restart policy ensures that the containers where you set it are treated as sidecars that are kept running during the entire lifetime of the Pod.

9c073ce491b4.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
9c073ce491b4.sentence: Containers that you explicitly define as sidecar containers start up before the main application Pod and remain running until the Pod is shut down.

49e196ef67a6.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
49e196ef67a6.sentence: Some Pods have init containers as well as app containers.

5cd865fa8913.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods
5cd865fa8913.sentence: By default, init containers run and complete before the app containers are started.

54478ad70210.title: Kubernetes
54478ad70210.sentence: Kubernetes enables clients (users or internal components) to attach keys called labels to any API object in the system, such as pods and nodes.

cb595c1d9a00.title: Kubernetes
cb595c1d9a00.sentence: Correspondingly, label selectors are queries against labels that resolve to matching objects.

c7230a5c50fa.title: Kubernetes
c7230a5c50fa.sentence: When a service is defined, one can define the label selectors that will be used by the service router/load balancer to select the pod instances that the traffic will be routed to.

6b0bdf85ce4c.title: Kubernetes
6b0bdf85ce4c.sentence: Thus, simply changing the labels of the pods or changing the label selectors on the service can be used to control which pods get traffic and which don't, which can be used to support various deployment patterns like blue–green deployments or A/B testing.

594d7a92bcda.title: Kubernetes
594d7a92bcda.sentence: This capability to dynamically control how services utilize implementing resources provides a loose coupling within the infrastructure.

142f59d43b43.title: Kubernetes
142f59d43b43.sentence: A Kubernetes service is a set of pods that work together, such as one tier of a multi-tier application.

a0e7a6d66082.title: Kubernetes
a0e7a6d66082.sentence: Service discovery assigns a stable IP address and DNS name to the service, and load balances traffic in a round-robin manner to network connections of that IP address among the pods matching the selector (even as failures cause the pods to move from machine to machine).

e3fded717814.title: Kubernetes
e3fded717814.sentence: The set of pods that constitute a service are defined by a label selector.

d664f16e4fde.title: Kubernetes
d664f16e4fde.sentence: By default a service is exposed inside a cluster (e.g., back end pods might be grouped into a service, with requests from the front-end pods load-balanced among them), but a service can also be exposed outside a cluster (e.g., for clients to reach front-end pods).

b57cf08d0bc5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-k8s-kubernetes.md
b57cf08d0bc5.sentence: It routes traffic coming into a node from the service.

b10c1a9d83bf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/what-is-k8s-kubernetes.md
b10c1a9d83bf.sentence: It forwards requests for work to the correct containers.

d2209054b579.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
d2209054b579.sentence: Pods are ephemeral resources (you should not expect that an individual Pod is reliable and durable).

b4dec46b39a9.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
b4dec46b39a9.sentence: From one moment to the next, you don't know how many of those Pods are working and healthy; you might not even know what those healthy Pods are named.

935a348f3af3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
935a348f3af3.sentence: While the actual Pods that compose the backend set may change, the frontend clients should not need to be aware of that, nor should they need to keep track of the set of backends themselves.

ac51f7395b3f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
ac51f7395b3f.sentence: The Service abstraction enables this decoupling.

b3d1fbcfe302.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
b3d1fbcfe302.sentence: EndpointSlices are objects that represent a subset (a slice) of the backing network endpoints for a Service.

849a221ebe60.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
849a221ebe60.sentence: By default, Kubernetes makes a new EndpointSlice once the existing EndpointSlices all contain at least 100 endpoints.

54cd871a1c92.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
54cd871a1c92.section: Defining a Service > Endpoints (deprecated) > Over-capacity endpoints
54cd871a1c92.sentence: When there are over 1000 backing endpoints for a Service, Kubernetes truncates the data in the Endpoints object.

3a99c149035e.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
3a99c149035e.section: Defining a Service > Services without selectors
3a99c149035e.sentence: Services most commonly abstract access to Kubernetes Pods thanks to the selector, but when used with a corresponding set of EndpointSlices objects and without a selector, the Service can abstract other kinds of backends, including ones that run outside the cluster.

bea2faec6951.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
bea2faec6951.section: Defining a Service > Services without selectors
bea2faec6951.sentence: - You want to have an external database cluster in production, but in your test environment you use your own databases.

d61155daa3cb.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
d61155daa3cb.section: Defining a Service > Services without selectors
d61155daa3cb.sentence: - You want to point your Service to a Service in a different Namespace or on another cluster.

bf95bc7c41c2.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
bf95bc7c41c2.sentence: Kubernetes Service types allow you to specify what kind of Service you want.

92d5c513897a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
92d5c513897a.sentence: The available type values and their behaviors are:

b0853424736a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
b0853424736a.sentence: Exposes the Service on a cluster-internal IP.

acc254b2d339.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
acc254b2d339.sentence: Choosing this value makes the Service only reachable from within the cluster.

1249e696b379.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
1249e696b379.sentence: This is the default that is used if you don't explicitly specify a type for a Service.

9d1972bc7e3e.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
9d1972bc7e3e.sentence: You can expose the Service to the public internet using an Ingress or a Gateway.

43cfca2d895c.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
43cfca2d895c.sentence: Exposes the Service on each Node's IP at a static port (the NodePort).

0f73b3dc1afe.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
0f73b3dc1afe.sentence: If you set the type field to NodePort, the Kubernetes control plane allocates a port from a range specified by --service-node-port-range flag (default: 30000-32767).

c22dff38fdfe.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
c22dff38fdfe.sentence: Each node proxies that port (the same port number on every Node) into your Service.

ee4109d4c9eb.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
ee4109d4c9eb.sentence: Exposes the Service externally using an external load balancer.

556b1a11d50e.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
556b1a11d50e.sentence: Kubernetes does not directly offer a load balancing component; you must provide one, or you can integrate your Kubernetes cluster with a cloud provider.

bc9d042faa8d.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
bc9d042faa8d.sentence: On cloud providers which support external load balancers, setting the type field to LoadBalancer provisions a load balancer for your Service.

5dd1a61f7c74.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
5dd1a61f7c74.sentence: To implement a Service of type: LoadBalancer, Kubernetes typically starts off by making the changes that are equivalent to you requesting a Service of type: NodePort.

0de1dd1811d2.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
0de1dd1811d2.sentence: The cloud-controller-manager component then configures the external load balancer to forward traffic to that assigned node port.

f0909dbfa4f1.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
f0909dbfa4f1.sentence: The actual creation of the load balancer happens asynchronously, and information about the provisioned balancer is published in the Service's.status.loadBalancer field.

798ce0200f20.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
798ce0200f20.sentence: Services of type ExternalName map a Service to a DNS name, not to a typical selector such as my-service or cassandra.

1dd1737c2297.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
1dd1737c2297.sentence: Maps the Service to the contents of the externalName field (for example, to the hostname api.foo.bar.example).

5be41b52646a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
5be41b52646a.sentence: The mapping configures your cluster's DNS server to return a CNAME record with that external hostname value.

41aebe528038.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
41aebe528038.sentence: No proxying of any kind is set up.

fdb718139bb0.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
fdb718139bb0.sentence: The type field in the Service API is designed as nested functionality - each level adds to the previous.

1cf86a6dd4b0.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
1cf86a6dd4b0.sentence: Several of the other types for Service build on the ClusterIP type as a foundation.

b8becea9d4ae.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
b8becea9d4ae.sentence: In this case, you can create what are termed headless Services, by explicitly specifying "None" for the cluster IP address (.spec.clusterIP).

56fe9072aaca.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
56fe9072aaca.sentence: For headless Services, a cluster IP is not allocated, kube-proxy does not handle these Services, and there is no load balancing or proxying done by the platform for them.

a46818ff34a2.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
a46818ff34a2.sentence: Services that are headless don't configure routes and packet forwarding using virtual IP addresses and proxies; instead, headless Services report the endpoint IP addresses of the individual pods via internal DNS records, served through the cluster's DNS service.

a29be08ca667.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
a29be08ca667.sentence: A headless Service allows a client to connect to whichever Pod it prefers, directly.

89fa6cd2927a.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
89fa6cd2927a.sentence: If your workload speaks HTTP, you might choose to use an Ingress to control how web traffic reaches that workload.

e85711f8cc20.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
e85711f8cc20.sentence: Ingress is not a Service type, but it acts as the entry point for your cluster.

e1edb1b70ff6.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service
e1edb1b70ff6.sentence: An Ingress lets you consolidate your routing rules into a single resource, so that you can expose multiple components of your workload, running separately in your cluster, behind a single listener.

b6d2d7f7eb79.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
b6d2d7f7eb79.sentence: Ingress exposes HTTP and HTTPS routes from outside the cluster to services within the cluster.

a16020b939b6.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
a16020b939b6.sentence: Feature state: Stable since Kubernetes v1.19An API object that manages external access to the services in a cluster, typically HTTP.Ingress may provide load balancing, SSL termination and name-based virtual hosting.

4bf819963fc8.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
4bf819963fc8.sentence: Traffic routing is controlled by rules defined on the Ingress resource.

23227692c871.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
23227692c871.sentence: An Ingress may be configured to give Services externally-reachable URLs, load balance traffic, terminate SSL / TLS, and offer name-based virtual hosting.

182493b9da2c.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
182493b9da2c.sentence: An Ingress controller is responsible for fulfilling the Ingress, usually with a load balancer, though it may also configure your edge router or additional frontends to help handle the traffic.

fd1a31eb930d.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
fd1a31eb930d.sentence: You must have an Ingress controller to satisfy an Ingress.

1ebab6ff1e7f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
1ebab6ff1e7f.sentence: Only creating an Ingress resource has no effect.

8f82626f0e48.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
8f82626f0e48.sentence: - A list of paths (for example, /testpath), each of which has an associated backend defined with a service.name and a service.port.name or service.port.number.

8dfd6f818089.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
8dfd6f818089.sentence: Both the host and path must match the content of an incoming request before the load balancer directs traffic to the referenced Service.

6a9c3f9661af.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
6a9c3f9661af.sentence: A fanout configuration routes traffic from a single IP address to more than one Service, based on the HTTP URI being requested.

4dc5ed97a969.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
4dc5ed97a969.sentence: An Ingress allows you to keep the number of load balancers down to a minimum.

c22b4090a587.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
c22b4090a587.sentence: You can secure an Ingress by specifying a Secret that contains a TLS private key and certificate.

fb70bc1fc94d.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
fb70bc1fc94d.sentence: The Ingress resource only supports a single TLS port, 443, and assumes TLS termination at the ingress point (traffic to the Service and its Pods is in plaintext).

2d4049b340fa.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
2d4049b340fa.sentence: More advanced load balancing concepts (e.g. persistent sessions, dynamic weights) are not yet exposed through the Ingress.

91807e095f95.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
91807e095f95.sentence: You can instead get these features through the load balancer used for a Service.

ca384d117e08.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
ca384d117e08.sentence: An Ingress does not expose arbitrary ports or protocols.

9f1d60dc5d8d.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
9f1d60dc5d8d.sentence: Exposing services other than HTTP and HTTPS to the internet typically uses a service of type Service.Type=NodePort or Service.Type=LoadBalancer.

af3815207b83.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
af3815207b83.sentence: Each path in an Ingress is required to have a corresponding path type.

851f638c5cd3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
851f638c5cd3.sentence: There are three supported path types:

628e64445a1f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
628e64445a1f.sentence: Paths that do not include an explicit pathType will fail validation.

56b0230b4f0b.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
56b0230b4f0b.sentence: - Exact: Matches the URL path exactly and with case sensitivity.

62652a7dc18b.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
62652a7dc18b.sentence: - Prefix: Matches based on a URL path prefix split by /.

7fa0f600b226.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
7fa0f600b226.sentence: Matching is case sensitive and done on a path element by element basis.

22c93096f58b.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
22c93096f58b.sentence: A request is a match for path p if every p is an element-wise prefix of p of the request path.Note:If the last element of the path is a substring of the last element in request path, it is not a match (for example: /foo/bar matches /foo/bar/baz, but does not match /foo/barbaz).

c52dc36887f8.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
c52dc36887f8.section: The Ingress resource > Examples > Multiple matches
c52dc36887f8.sentence: In those cases precedence will be given first to the longest matching path.

da1db3bdf14b.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
da1db3bdf14b.section: The Ingress resource > Examples > Multiple matches
da1db3bdf14b.sentence: If two paths are still equally matched, precedence will be given to paths with an exact path type over prefix path type.

5755228ef757.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
5755228ef757.sentence: Hosts can be precise matches (for example “foo.bar.com”) or a wildcard (for example “*.foo.com”).

c9d72f8d69cb.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
c9d72f8d69cb.sentence: *.foo.com | baz.bar.foo.com | No match, wildcard only covers a single DNS label

5b1c9317a0c2.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
5b1c9317a0c2.section: Types of Ingress > Name based virtual hosting
5b1c9317a0c2.sentence: Name-based virtual hosts support routing HTTP traffic to multiple host names at the same IP address.

90006aa146c3.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
90006aa146c3.section: Types of Ingress > Name based virtual hosting
90006aa146c3.sentence: The following Ingress tells the backing load balancer to route requests based on the Host header.

3d2623f3e2d1.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
3d2623f3e2d1.sentence: If none of the hosts or paths match the HTTP request in the Ingress objects, the traffic is routed to your default backend.

d973da80b5a6.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
d973da80b5a6.sentence: An Ingress with no rules sends all traffic to a single default backend and.spec.defaultBackend is the backend that should handle requests in that case.

ff2c32b66b5f.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
ff2c32b66b5f.sentence: If no.spec.rules are specified,.spec.defaultBackend must be specified.

4c87514d49cb.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress
4c87514d49cb.sentence: If defaultBackend is not set, the handling of requests that do not match any of the rules will be up to the ingress controller (consult the documentation for your ingress controller to find out how it handles this case).

50806b3d3882.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
50806b3d3882.sentence: Let’s take the “docker run” command as an example.

37df60b545a7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
37df60b545a7.sentence: - Docker pulls the image from the registry.

7ddb8e612d79.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
7ddb8e612d79.sentence: There are 3 components in Docker architecture:

33349f77ac65.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
33349f77ac65.sentence: - Docker client The docker client talks to the Docker daemon.

baa2f6d3fbd0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
baa2f6d3fbd0.sentence: - Docker host The Docker daemon listens for Docker API requests and manages Docker objects such as images, containers, networks, and volumes.

e99917a6a5d2.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
e99917a6a5d2.sentence: - Docker registry A Docker registry stores Docker images.

4ff69b9307c4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
4ff69b9307c4.sentence: - Docker allocates a read-write filesystem to the container.

2edc422bbcd7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-docker-work.md
2edc422bbcd7.sentence: - Docker creates a network interface to connect the container to the default network.

f4d525730f7c.title: Docker (software)
f4d525730f7c.sentence: Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications.

afca45695a1c.title: Docker (software)
afca45695a1c.sentence: It uses YAML files to configure the application's services and performs the creation and start-up process of all the containers with a single command.

1120f8bf7fa2.title: Docker (software)
1120f8bf7fa2.sentence: The docker-compose.yml file is used to define an application's services and includes various configuration options.

a9d09d70ddc1.title: Docker (software)
a9d09d70ddc1.sentence: For example, the build option defines configuration options such as the Dockerfile path, the command option allows one to override default Docker commands, and more.

98c79f951af1.title: Docker (software)
98c79f951af1.sentence: The docker compose CLI utility allows users to run commands on multiple containers at once; for example, building images, scaling containers, running containers that were stopped, and more.

6540c14d61fe.title: Docker (software)
6540c14d61fe.sentence: Docker Swarm provides native clustering functionality for Docker containers, which turns a group of Docker engines into a single virtual Docker engine.

92cd1b46bea1.title: Docker (software)
92cd1b46bea1.sentence: A Docker service allows containers to be scaled across multiple Docker daemons.

10b90dcb8004.title: Docker (software)
10b90dcb8004.sentence: The result is known as a swarm, a set of cooperating daemons that communicate through the Docker API.

cff6504e595a.title: Docker (software)
cff6504e595a.sentence: In Docker 1.12 and higher, Swarm mode is integrated with Docker Engine.

4a1076bfbe83.title: Docker (software)
4a1076bfbe83.sentence: Docker manages swarms using the Raft consensus algorithm.

9bdfaa89c675.title: Docker (software)
9bdfaa89c675.sentence: According to Raft, for an update to be performed, the majority of Swarm nodes need to agree on the update.

2b0c1dba0bc1.title: Docker (software)
2b0c1dba0bc1.sentence: In addition to the docker swarm CLI, docker stack is a tool designed to manage Swarm services with greater flexibility.

970453c7f9a5.title: Docker (software)
970453c7f9a5.sentence: It can use a configuration file very similar to a docker-compose.yml, with a few nuances.

1734a59da0a2.title: Docker (software)
1734a59da0a2.sentence: Using docker stack instead of docker compose offers several advantages, such as the ability to manage a Swarm cluster across multiple machines or the capability to work with docker secret combined with docker context, a feature that allows executing Docker commands on a remote host, enabling remote container management.

c4778ae4ab99.title: Virtual machine
c4778ae4ab99.sentence: In computing, a virtual machine (VM) is the virtualization or emulation of a computer system.

633a6f2d9dfc.title: Virtual machine
633a6f2d9dfc.sentence: Virtual machines are based on computer architectures and provide the functionality of a physical computer.

dbb3106f77d1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
dbb3106f77d1.sentence: A Virtual Machine (VM) is a virtual environment that functions as a virtual computer system with its own CPU, memory, network interface, and storage, created on a physical hardware system.

a1d969a96a9e.title: Virtual machine
a1d969a96a9e.sentence: Their implementations may involve specialized hardware, software, or a combination of the two.

f6523c12b2fe.title: Virtual machine
f6523c12b2fe.sentence: The physical, "real-world" hardware running the VM is generally referred to as the 'host', and the virtual machine emulated on that machine is generally referred to as the 'guest'.

c6e6c5c72f2a.title: Virtual machine
c6e6c5c72f2a.sentence: A host can emulate several guests, each of which can emulate different operating systems and hardware platforms.

1132e0d9fe8d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
1132e0d9fe8d.sentence: VMs are isolated from the rest of the system, and multiple VMs can exist on a single piece of hardware, like a server.

933029a2abf1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
933029a2abf1.sentence: They can be moved between host servers depending on the demand or to use resources more efficiently.

bf73424f58d1.title: Virtual machine
bf73424f58d1.sentence: - System virtual machines (also called full virtualization VMs, or SysVMs) provide a substitute for a real machine.

1c6c3358c816.title: Virtual machine
1c6c3358c816.sentence: They provide the functionality needed to execute entire operating systems.

0953429b2cbc.title: Virtual machine
0953429b2cbc.sentence: - Process virtual machines are designed to execute computer programs in a platform-independent environment.

3d3ce74ff0e3.title: Virtual machine
3d3ce74ff0e3.sentence: A process virtual machine, sometimes called an application virtual machine, or Managed Runtime Environment (MRE), runs as a normal application inside a host OS and supports a single process.

007186f2a183.title: Virtual machine
007186f2a183.sentence: It is created when that process is started and deleted when it is closed.

dde8058fdd65.title: Virtual machine
dde8058fdd65.sentence: Its purpose is to provide a platform-independent programming environment that abstracts away details of the underlying hardware or operating system and allows a program to execute in the same way on any platform.

b4443330ad03.title: Virtual machine
b4443330ad03.sentence: This type of VM has become popular with the Java programming language, which is implemented using the Java virtual machine.

9acd93040d11.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
9acd93040d11.section: Virtual Machines (VM) > Why use a Virtual Machine?
9acd93040d11.sentence: Server consolidation is a top reason to use VMs.

1f5b02c00a49.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
1f5b02c00a49.section: Virtual Machines (VM) > Why use a Virtual Machine?
1f5b02c00a49.sentence: Most operating system and application deployments only use a small amount of the physical resources available.

8855b5186c3c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
8855b5186c3c.section: Virtual Machines (VM) > Why use a Virtual Machine?
8855b5186c3c.sentence: By virtualizing our servers, we can place many virtual servers onto each physical server to improve hardware utilization.

9ab938454e45.title: Virtual machine
9ab938454e45.sentence: Multiple VMs running their own guest operating system are frequently engaged for server consolidation.

c44fda064850.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
c44fda064850.section: Virtual Machines (VM) > Why use a Virtual Machine?
c44fda064850.sentence: A VM provides an environment that is isolated from the rest of a system, so whatever is running inside a VM won't interfere with anything else running on the host hardware.

a0baf142af92.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
a0baf142af92.section: Virtual Machines (VM) > Why use a Virtual Machine?
a0baf142af92.sentence: Because VMs are isolated, they are a good option for testing new applications or setting up a production environment.

b9f7e1fdabaf.title: Virtual machine
b9f7e1fdabaf.sentence: Virtual machines are frequently used to isolate applications from one another for security.

77f2070795c0.title: Hypervisor
77f2070795c0.sentence: A hypervisor, also known as a virtual machine monitor (VMM), is a type of computer software, firmware, or hardware that creates and runs virtual machines.

683c18fd60c0.title: Hypervisor
683c18fd60c0.sentence: A computer on which a hypervisor runs one or more virtual machines is called a host machine or virtualization server, and each virtual machine is called a guest machine.

d84ccd86a918.title: Hypervisor
d84ccd86a918.sentence: The hypervisor presents the guest operating systems with a virtual operating platform and manages the execution of the guest operating systems.

18a1a5af315f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
18a1a5af315f.section: Virtual Machines (VM) > What is a Hypervisor?
18a1a5af315f.sentence: The hypervisor treats resources like CPU, memory, and storage as a pool of resources that can be easily reallocated between existing guests or new virtual machines.

8f6f6f083b6f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
8f6f6f083b6f.sentence: A software called a hypervisor separates the machine's resources from the hardware and provisions them appropriately so they can be used by the VM.

0a0ffc34b299.title: Hypervisor
0a0ffc34b299.sentence: Unlike an emulator, the guest executes most instructions on the native hardware.

698dfbcc95d1.title: Hypervisor
698dfbcc95d1.sentence: This contrasts with operating system-level virtualization, where all instances (usually called containers) must share a single kernel, though the guest operating systems can differ in user space, such as different Linux distributions with the same kernel.

5bdc2e2c1266.title: Virtual machine
5bdc2e2c1266.sentence: A hypervisor uses native execution to share and manage hardware, allowing for multiple environments that are isolated from one another yet exist on the same physical machine.

949b0bf739ae.title: Hypervisor
949b0bf739ae.sentence: These hypervisors run directly on the host's hardware to control the hardware and to manage guest operating systems.

64a3448caa2a.title: Hypervisor
64a3448caa2a.sentence: For this reason, they are sometimes called bare-metal hypervisors.

f0f24b7d15ee.title: Hypervisor
f0f24b7d15ee.sentence: Examples of Type-1 hypervisor include Hyper-V, Xen and VMware ESXi.

5d12c60f5f83.title: Hypervisor
5d12c60f5f83.sentence: These hypervisors run on a conventional operating system (OS) just as other computer programs do.

e9b1cce2143f.title: Hypervisor
e9b1cce2143f.sentence: A virtual machine monitor runs as a process on the host, such as VirtualBox.

5bc486db2b93.title: Hypervisor
5bc486db2b93.sentence: Examples of Type-2 hypervisor include VirtualBox and VMware Workstation.

57e496b8235b.title: Hypervisor
57e496b8235b.sentence: By running multiple operating systems concurrently, the hypervisor increased system robustness and stability: Even if one operating system crashed, the others would continue working without interruption.

8dc7bc00800f.title: Hypervisor
8dc7bc00800f.sentence: Indeed, this even allowed beta or experimental versions of operating systems‍—‌or even of new hardware‍—‌to be deployed and debugged, without jeopardizing the stable main production system or requiring costly additional development systems.

9247b2eeb9bd.title: Virtual machine
9247b2eeb9bd.sentence: Modern hypervisors use hardware-assisted virtualization, with virtualization-specific hardware features on the host CPUs providing assistance to hypervisors.

a80985b74a6f.title: Hypervisor
a80985b74a6f.sentence: Intel and AMD released their first x86 processors with hardware virtualisation in 2005 with Intel VT-x (code-named Vanderpool) and AMD-V (code-named Pacifica).

36b68af9f3d6.title: Hypervisor
36b68af9f3d6.sentence: An alternative approach requires modifying the guest operating system to make a system call to the underlying hypervisor, rather than executing machine I/O instructions that the hypervisor simulates.

6cbfb1896b10.title: Hypervisor
6cbfb1896b10.sentence: This is called paravirtualization in Xen, a "hypercall" in Parallels Workstation, and a "DIAGNOSE code" in IBM VM.

9d3deabca993.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
9d3deabca993.sentence: In traditional virtualization, a hypervisor virtualizes physical hardware.

8da09d4a45ad.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
8da09d4a45ad.sentence: The result is that each virtual machine contains a guest OS, a virtual copy of the hardware that the OS requires to run, and an application and its associated libraries and dependencies.

2cc55f1bdb72.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
2cc55f1bdb72.sentence: Instead of virtualizing the underlying hardware, containers virtualize the operating system so each container contains only the application and its dependencies making them much more lightweight than VMs.

468a2b0272c0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::virtual-machines-vms-and-containers
468a2b0272c0.sentence: Containers also share the OS kernel and use a fraction of the memory VMs require.

2ee184bb6c59.title: Virtual machine
2ee184bb6c59.sentence: A snapshot is a state of a virtual machine, and generally its storage devices, at an exact point in time.

651182b441ab.title: Virtual machine
651182b441ab.sentence: A snapshot enables the virtual machine's state at the time of the snapshot to be restored later, effectively undoing any changes that occurred afterwards.

244e158f9e43.title: Virtual machine
244e158f9e43.sentence: This capability is useful as a backup technique, for example, prior to performing a risky operation.

460efd69f9c2.title: Virtual machine
460efd69f9c2.sentence: Every time a snapshot is taken, a new file is created, and used as an overlay for its predecessors.

af271a7f7f92.title: Virtual machine
af271a7f7f92.sentence: New data is written to the topmost overlay; reading existing data, however, needs the overlay hierarchy to be scanned, resulting in accessing the most recent version.

80b378dfdb81.title: Virtual machine
80b378dfdb81.sentence: The snapshots described above can be moved to another host machine with its own hypervisor; when the VM is temporarily stopped, snapshotted, moved, and then resumed on the new host, this is known as migration.

f2e13e19b295.title: Virtual machine
f2e13e19b295.sentence: Similar to the migration mechanism described above, failover allows the VM to continue operations if the host fails.

6de3838902bd.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
6de3838902bd.sentence: There was no way to define resource boundaries for applications in a physical server, and this caused resource allocation issues.

89adb930e5f5.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
89adb930e5f5.sentence: It allows you to run multiple Virtual Machines (VMs) on a single physical server's CPU.

b88b662d74c6.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
b88b662d74c6.sentence: Containers are similar to VMs, but they have relaxed isolation properties to share the Operating System (OS) among the applications.

92ab1ab68380.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
92ab1ab68380.sentence: For example, if multiple applications run on a physical server, there can be instances where one application would take up most of the resources, and as a result, the other applications would underperform.

66fc4c248f83.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
66fc4c248f83.sentence: But this did not scale as resources were underutilized, and it was expensive for organizations to maintain many physical servers.

9f11f5ac4c17.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
9f11f5ac4c17.sentence: Virtualization allows applications to be isolated between VMs and provides a level of security as the information of one application cannot be freely accessed by another application.

80b1c9872126.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
80b1c9872126.sentence: Virtualization allows better utilization of resources in a physical server and allows better scalability because an application can be added or updated easily, reduces hardware costs, and much more.

f962d10e8519.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
f962d10e8519.sentence: Each VM is a full machine running all the components, including its own operating system, on top of the virtualized hardware.

a2f7ba60ff58.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
a2f7ba60ff58.sentence: Similar to a VM, a container has its own filesystem, share of CPU, memory, process space, and more.

3bff3b5a0ae9.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
3bff3b5a0ae9.sentence: As they are decoupled from the underlying infrastructure, they are portable across clouds and OS distributions.

adebd0a2f8b0.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
adebd0a2f8b0.sentence: - Agile application creation and deployment: increased ease and efficiency of container image creation compared to VM image use.

59e695628f33.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
59e695628f33.sentence: - Continuous development, integration, and deployment: provides reliable and frequent container image build and deployment with quick and efficient rollbacks (due to image immutability).

179fc0f5c509.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
179fc0f5c509.sentence: - Environmental consistency across development, testing, and production: runs the same on a laptop as it does in the cloud.

7c37b576f234.title: doc>kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview
7c37b576f234.sentence: - Resource utilization: high efficiency and density.

449d6ee003c2.title: Continuous delivery
449d6ee003c2.sentence: Continuous delivery (CD) is a software engineering approach in which teams produce software in short cycles, ensuring that the software can be reliably released at any time.

75aadb5d51a3.title: Continuous delivery
75aadb5d51a3.sentence: It aims at building, testing, and releasing software with greater speed and frequency.

3b9ffaf00987.title: Continuous delivery
3b9ffaf00987.sentence: The approach helps reduce the cost, time, and risk of delivering changes by allowing for more incremental updates to applications in production.

cccf480fe0ed.title: Continuous delivery
cccf480fe0ed.sentence: Code is compiled if necessary and then packaged by a build server every time a change is committed to a source control repository, then tested by a number of different techniques (possibly including manual testing) before it can be marked as releasable.

24fd4f2978f8.title: Continuous delivery
24fd4f2978f8.sentence: Any code commit may be released to customers at any point.

642ee24722a6.title: Continuous delivery
642ee24722a6.sentence: Continuous delivery treats the commonplace notion of a deployment pipeline as a lean Poka-Yoke: a set of validations through which a piece of software must pass on its way to release.

6779ac91a5cd.title: Continuous delivery
6779ac91a5cd.sentence: Continuous delivery is enabled through the deployment pipeline.

31e59a5a8827.title: Continuous delivery
31e59a5a8827.sentence: The purpose of the deployment pipeline has three components: visibility, feedback, and continually deploy.

d9e7ce73e615.title: Continuous delivery
d9e7ce73e615.sentence: - Continually deploy – Through a fully automated process, you can deploy and release any version of the software to any environment.

ff7397418ee2.title: Continuous delivery
ff7397418ee2.sentence: According to Neal Ford, continuous delivery adopts "Bring the pain forward," tackling tough tasks early, fostering automation and swift issue detection.

4ed0fbc18c59.title: Continuous delivery
4ed0fbc18c59.sentence: A straightforward and repeatable deployment process is important for continuous delivery.

11525c5be48a.title: Continuous delivery
11525c5be48a.sentence: Patterns such as feature toggles can be very useful for committing code early which is not yet ready for use by end users.

5d8841a5fc64.title: Continuous delivery
5d8841a5fc64.sentence: Other useful techniques for developing code in isolation such as code branching are not obsolete in a CD world, but must be adapted to fit the principles of CD - for example, running multiple long-lived code branches can prove impractical, as a releasable artifact must be built early in the CD process from a single code branch if it is to pass through all phases of the pipeline.

4b341546b809.title: Continuous delivery
4b341546b809.sentence: To practice continuous delivery effectively, software applications have to meet a set of architecturally significant requirements (ASRs) such as deployability, modifiability, and testability.

0706beddfa25.title: Continuous delivery
0706beddfa25.sentence: Microservices are often used when architecting for continuous delivery.

612b7e704a31.title: Continuous delivery
612b7e704a31.sentence: The observed deployability improvements include: deployment independence, shorter deployment time, simpler deployment procedures, and zero downtime deployment.

cba0fe943e49.title: Continuous delivery
cba0fe943e49.sentence: With continuous delivery, the deployment process and scripts are tested repeatedly before deployment to production.

3537626502b1.title: Continuous delivery
3537626502b1.sentence: With more frequent releases, the number of code changes in each release decreases.

7568d870567c.title: Continuous delivery
7568d870567c.sentence: This makes finding and fixing any problems that do occur easier, reducing the time in which they have an impact.

ed3bfb03e490.title: Continuous delivery
ed3bfb03e490.sentence: - Lack of test automation: Lack of test automation leads to a lack of developer confidence and can prevent using continuous delivery.

0fcaa8c9075c.title: Continuous delivery
0fcaa8c9075c.sentence: - Differences in environments: Different environments used in the development, testing and production can result in undetected issues slipping to the production environment.

0db9e13267a8.title: Continuous delivery
0db9e13267a8.sentence: - Tests needing a human oracle: Not all quality attributes can be verified with automation.

106eb029eea1.title: Continuous delivery
106eb029eea1.sentence: - Domain restrictions: In some domains, such as telecom, medical, avionics, railway and heavy industries, regulations require customer-side or even on-site testing of new versions.

91291bb1c448.title: CI/CD
91291bb1c448.sentence: In software engineering, CI/CD or CICD is the combined practices of continuous integration (CI) and continuous delivery (CD) or, less often, continuous deployment.

6c535cc312f5.title: CI/CD
6c535cc312f5.sentence: Frequent merging of several small changes into a main branch.

d9caddfaa918.title: CI/CD
d9caddfaa918.sentence: Producing software in short cycles with high speed and frequency so that reliable software can be released at any time, with a simple and repeatable deployment process when deciding to deploy.

690a1d0e0f22.title: CI/CD
690a1d0e0f22.sentence: Automatic rollout of new software functionality.

619cae0c39ca.title: CI/CD
619cae0c39ca.sentence: When these three processes occur in order, they may be described as a "CI/CD pipeline".

2555e89f5af1.title: CI/CD
2555e89f5af1.sentence: CI/CD services compile the incremental code changes made by developers, then link and package them into software deliverables.

fa01f43817d9.title: CI/CD
fa01f43817d9.sentence: Automated tests verify the software functionality, and automated deployment services deliver them to end users.

fca9982f26f7.title: CI/CD
fca9982f26f7.sentence: The aim is to increase early defect discovery, increase productivity, and provide faster release cycles.

1646e4c8e8f4.title: CI/CD
1646e4c8e8f4.sentence: The process contrasts with traditional methods where a collection of software updates were integrated into one large batch before deploying the newer version.

e9519d280ec9.title: CI/CD
e9519d280ec9.sentence: CI/CD bridges the gaps between teams, development, and operation activities by enforcing automation in building, testing, and deployment of applications.

054870387330.title: CI/CD
054870387330.sentence: The CI/CD practice, or CI/CD pipeline, forms the backbone of modern day DevOps operations.

eac55ce08bb2.title: CI/CD
eac55ce08bb2.sentence: - Number of pipelines: Small teams can be more productive by having one repository and one pipeline.

00bff96ed87e.title: CI/CD
00bff96ed87e.sentence: In contrast, larger organizations may have separate repositories and pipelines for each team or even separate repositories and pipelines for each service within a team.

5bb4c44f8502.title: CI/CD
5bb4c44f8502.sentence: - Permissions: In the context of pipeline-related permissions, adhering to the principle of least privilege can be challenging due to the dynamic nature of architecture.

0660541fbdb5.title: CI/CD
0660541fbdb5.sentence: Administrators may opt for more permissive permissions while implementing compensating security controls to minimize the blast radius.

dd145246cd6b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
dd145246cd6b.sentence: Release engineering is a relatively new and fast-growing discipline of software engineering that can be concisely described as building and delivering software [McN14a].

ce964736533b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
ce964736533b.sentence: Release engineers work with software engineers (SWEs) in product development and SREs to define all the steps required to release softwareâfrom how the software is stored in the source code repository, to build rules for compilation, to how testing, packaging, and deployment are conducted.

fef5a2170cfb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
fef5a2170cfb.sentence: Running reliable services requires reliable release processes.

7e13814ba038.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
7e13814ba038.sentence: Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) need to know that the binaries and configurations they use are built in a reproducible, automated way so that releases are repeatable and arenât âunique snowflakes.â Changes to any aspect of the release process should be intentional, rather than accidental.

b519c1dcaddc.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
b519c1dcaddc.sentence: Release engineering has developed best practices and tools that allow our product development teams to control and run their own release processes.

d20e55ad2006.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
d20e55ad2006.sentence: Although we have thousands of engineers and products, we can achieve a high release velocity because individual teams can decide how often and when to release new versions of their products.

2bb2bee8720d.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
2bb2bee8720d.sentence: Release processes can be automated to the point that they require minimal involvement by the engineers, and many projects are automatically built and released using a combination of our automated build system and our deployment tools.

9ffee0f9144b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
9ffee0f9144b.sentence: Releases are truly automatic, and only require engineer involvement if and when problems arise.

0223a4ef2ee4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
0223a4ef2ee4.sentence: We have embraced the philosophy that frequent releases result in fewer changes between versions.

9e832d6fd704.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
9e832d6fd704.sentence: This approach makes testing and troubleshooting easier.

b723c9d914d4.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
b723c9d914d4.sentence: Some teams perform hourly builds and then select the version to actually deploy to production from the resulting pool of builds.

cb86382fe558.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
cb86382fe558.sentence: Selection is based upon the test results and the features contained in a given build.

253425541534.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
253425541534.sentence: Several layers of security and access control determine who can perform specific operations when releasing a project.

d2efea9160b6.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
d2efea9160b6.sentence: - Approving source code changesâthis operation is managed through configuration files scattered throughout the codebase

9785c03efcc0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
9785c03efcc0.sentence: - Approving the initial integration proposal (which is a request to perform a build at a specific revision number in the source code repository) and subsequent cherry picks

732abb450df1.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
732abb450df1.sentence: Almost all changes to the codebase require a code review, which is a streamlined action integrated into our normal developer workflow.

76bab4da0456.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
76bab4da0456.sentence: Our automated release system produces a report of all changes contained in a release, which is archived with other build artifacts.

061d51962b4c.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
061d51962b4c.sentence: By allowing SREs to understand what changes are included in a new release of a project, this report can expedite troubleshooting when there are problems with a release.

939697883cc0.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
939697883cc0.section: The Role of a Release Engineer
939697883cc0.sentence: In order to make sure our release processes meet business requirements, release engineers and SREs work together to develop strategies for canarying changes, pushing out new releases without interrupting services, and rolling back features that demonstrate problems.

8bbeced89519.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
8bbeced89519.section: Start Release Engineering at the Beginning
8bbeced89519.sentence: Teams should budget for release engineering resources at the beginning of the product development cycle.

d04c03a9ce42.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
d04c03a9ce42.section: Start Release Engineering at the Beginning
d04c03a9ce42.sentence: Itâs cheaper to put good practices and process in place early, rather than have to retrofit your system later.

1543c58bcadb.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering
1543c58bcadb.section: Start Release Engineering at the Beginning
1543c58bcadb.sentence: It is essential that the developers, SREs, and release engineers work together.

040c949d19bb.title: Infrastructure as code
040c949d19bb.sentence: Infrastructure as code (IaC) is the process of managing and provisioning computer data center resources through machine-readable definition files, rather than via physical hardware configuration or interactive configuration tools.

14c4d43e1c33.title: Infrastructure as code
14c4d43e1c33.sentence: The IT infrastructure managed by this process includes physical equipment, such as bare-metal servers, and virtual machines and associated configuration resources.

bb943aee084a.title: Infrastructure as code
bb943aee084a.sentence: That is, instead of having to build a configuration manually, there is a pre-set configuration that can be applied to a machine.

778280b929c2.title: Infrastructure as code
778280b929c2.sentence: The definitions may exist in a version control system rather than manual processes.

12bca1167c1c.title: Infrastructure as code
12bca1167c1c.sentence: Treating infrastructure configuration like software - storing it in version control, reviewing it, and deploying it automatically allowed teams to reduce manual errors and reproduce environments reliably.

947c53654572.title: Infrastructure as code
947c53654572.sentence: The value of IaC can be broken down into three measurable categories: cost, speed, and risk.

3a97b0faf41a.title: Infrastructure as code
3a97b0faf41a.sentence: Automation removes the risk associated with human error, like manual misconfiguration; removing this can decrease downtime and increase reliability.

4d0e087b105b.title: Infrastructure as code
4d0e087b105b.sentence: The declarative approach defines the desired state and the system executes what needs to happen to achieve that desired state.

e435eddc7b50.title: Infrastructure as code
e435eddc7b50.sentence: Imperative defines specific commands that need to be executed in the appropriate order to end with the desired conclusion.

a51f89cd57cb.title: Infrastructure as code
a51f89cd57cb.sentence: Definition files may use either scripts or declarative definitions, but IaC more often employs declarative approaches.

c8f6197448a3.title: Infrastructure as code
c8f6197448a3.sentence: In the 'push' method, the system controlling the configuration directly sends instructions to the server.

2dcd414bf944.title: Infrastructure as code
2dcd414bf944.sentence: In the 'pull' method, the server retrieves its own instructions from the controlling system.
