9a7be375eb90.title: rfc>6749
9a7be375eb90.sentence: Access tokens are credentials used to access protected resources.

a793687bf001.title: rfc>6749
a793687bf001.sentence: An access token is a string representing an authorization issued to the client.

5c3c3b1fd528.title: rfc>6749
5c3c3b1fd528.sentence: The string is usually opaque to the client.

e9aebf41ce8b.title: rfc>6749
e9aebf41ce8b.sentence: Tokens represent specific scopes and durations of access, granted by the resource owner, and enforced by the resource server and authorization server.

c1d367b0d0eb.title: rfc>6749
c1d367b0d0eb.sentence: The token may denote an identifier used to retrieve the authorization information or may self-contain the authorization information in a verifiable manner (i.e., a token string consisting of some data and a signature).

fa46b9d49f07.title: rfc>6749
fa46b9d49f07.sentence: The access token provides an abstraction layer, replacing different authorization constructs (e.g., username and password) with a single token understood by the resource server.

79fd78928433.title: rfc>6749
79fd78928433.sentence: This abstraction enables issuing access tokens more restrictive than the authorization grant used to obtain them, as well as removing the resource server's need to understand a wide range of authentication methods.

f214e2f3c4a0.title: rfc>6749
f214e2f3c4a0.sentence: The client SHOULD request access tokens with the minimal scope necessary.

15b8d2c8f68b.title: rfc>6749
15b8d2c8f68b.sentence: The authorization server SHOULD take the client identity into account when choosing how to honor the requested scope and MAY issue an access token with less rights than requested.

0a6b93360343.title: rfc>6749
0a6b93360343.sentence: If the issued access token scope is different from the one requested by the client, the authorization server MUST include the "scope" response parameter to inform the client of the actual scope granted.

32734ec4e3b7.title: rfc>6749
32734ec4e3b7.sentence: The client accesses protected resources by presenting the access token to the resource server.

6af23dd8e5e1.title: rfc>6749
6af23dd8e5e1.sentence: The authorization server MUST ensure that access tokens cannot be generated, modified, or guessed to produce valid access tokens by unauthorized parties.

be63d449dcd7.title: rfc>6749
be63d449dcd7.sentence: The probability of an attacker guessing generated tokens (and other credentials not intended for handling by end-users) MUST be less than or equal to 2^(-128) and SHOULD be less than or equal to 2^(-160).

c1838baa10cd.title: rfc>6749
c1838baa10cd.sentence: Access token credentials (as well as any confidential access token attributes) MUST be kept confidential in transit and storage, and only shared among the authorization server, the resource servers the access token is valid for, and the client to whom the access token is issued.

7018227946e1.title: rfc>6749
7018227946e1.sentence: Access token credentials MUST only be transmitted using TLS as described in Section 1.6 with server authentication as defined by.

ded11653ee22.title: rfc>6749
ded11653ee22.sentence: Refresh tokens are credentials used to obtain access tokens.

c5a362cc6ccb.title: rfc>6749
c5a362cc6ccb.sentence: Refresh tokens are issued to the client by the authorization server and are used to obtain a new access token when the current access token becomes invalid or expires, or to obtain additional access tokens with identical or narrower scope (access tokens may have a shorter lifetime and fewer permissions than authorized by the resource owner).

1a7a34bd2e64.title: rfc>6749
1a7a34bd2e64.sentence: Issuing a refresh token is optional at the discretion of the authorization server.

ccff0b5fe6f5.title: rfc>6749
ccff0b5fe6f5.sentence: If the authorization server issues a refresh token, it is included when issuing an access token (i.e., step (D) in Figure 1).

cae9d1cdc76b.title: rfc>6749
cae9d1cdc76b.sentence: Unlike access tokens, refresh tokens are intended for use only with authorization servers and are never sent to resource servers.

93edd92bfe42.title: rfc>6749
93edd92bfe42.sentence: (G) The client requests a new access token by authenticating with the authorization server and presenting the refresh token.

c0a105678ae9.title: rfc>6749
c0a105678ae9.sentence: (H) The authorization server authenticates the client and validates the refresh token, and if valid, issues a new access token (and, optionally, a new refresh token).

86d013160d7c.title: rfc>6749
86d013160d7c.sentence: If valid and authorized, the authorization server issues an access token as described in Section 5.1.

87d133927f99.title: rfc>6749
87d133927f99.sentence: The requested scope MUST NOT include any scope not originally granted by the resource owner, and if omitted is treated as equal to the scope originally granted by the resource owner.

28dd6191304b.title: rfc>6749
28dd6191304b.sentence: Because refresh tokens are typically long-lasting credentials used to request additional access tokens, the refresh token is bound to the client to which it was issued.

fd1db7b9745c.title: rfc>6749
fd1db7b9745c.sentence: The authorization server MAY issue a new refresh token, in which case the client MUST discard the old refresh token and replace it with the new refresh token.

89e4a2ec7d5b.title: rfc>6749
89e4a2ec7d5b.sentence: Refresh tokens MUST be kept confidential in transit and storage, and shared only among the authorization server and the client to whom the refresh tokens were issued.

2c241fedea61.title: rfc>6749
2c241fedea61.sentence: Refresh tokens MUST only be transmitted using TLS as described in Section 1.6 with server authentication as defined by.

95b679832c53.title: rfc>6749
95b679832c53.sentence: For example, the authorization server could employ refresh token rotation in which a new refresh token is issued with every access token refresh response.

736eb5027087.title: rfc>6749
736eb5027087.sentence: The previous refresh token is invalidated

072c0d22861f.sentence: If a refresh token is compromised and subsequently used by both the attacker and the legitimate client, one of them will present an invalidated refresh token, which will inform the authorization server of the breach.

00b2925253d1.title: JSON Web Token
00b2925253d1.sentence: JSON Web Token (JWT, suggested pronunciation /dʒɒt/, same as the word "jot") is a proposed Internet standard for creating data with optional signature and/or optional encryption whose payload holds JSON that asserts some number of claims.

b9014deb6dce.sentence: JWT relies on other JSON-based standards: JSON Web Signature and JSON Web Encryption.

9edb706e3d97.title: JSON Web Token
9edb706e3d97.sentence: The tokens are signed either using a private secret or a public/private key.

14d9656d50a7.title: JSON Web Token
14d9656d50a7.sentence: The tokens can be signed by one party's private key (usually the server's) so that any party can subsequently verify whether the token is legitimate.

4d54b506629c.title: JSON Web Token
4d54b506629c.sentence: If the other party, by some suitable and trustworthy means, is in possession of the corresponding public key, they too are able to verify the token's legitimacy.

5d1186279cf8.title: JSON Web Token
5d1186279cf8.sentence: The tokens are designed to be compact, URL-safe, and usable, especially in a web-browser single-sign-on (SSO) context.

af69d7001b3b.title: JSON Web Token
af69d7001b3b.sentence: JWT claims can typically be used to pass identity of authenticated users between an identity provider and a service provider, or any other type of claims as required by business processes.

70627b01a988.title: JSON Web Token
70627b01a988.sentence: Identifies which algorithm is used to generate the signature.

270895e0075a.title: JSON Web Token
270895e0075a.sentence: The three are encoded separately using Base64url Encoding RFC 4648, and concatenated using periods to produce the JWT:

18849a1b7780.title: JSON Web Token
18849a1b7780.sentence: The signature is calculated by encoding the header and payload using Base64url Encoding RFC 4648 and concatenating the two together with a period separator.

699acab6bcba.title: JSON Web Token
699acab6bcba.sentence: That string is then run through the cryptographic algorithm specified in the header.

e9f72daf57b2.title: JSON Web Token
e9f72daf57b2.sentence: Typical cryptographic algorithms used are HMAC with SHA-256 (HS256) and RSA signature with SHA-256 (RS256).

ae7a2df096f9.title: JSON Web Token
ae7a2df096f9.sentence: The JWT specification defines seven Registered Claim Names, which are the standard fields commonly included in tokens.

d86ea566c2e5.title: JSON Web Token
d86ea566c2e5.sentence: Custom claims are usually also included, depending on the purpose of the token.

1d2a809afa3e.title: JSON Web Token
1d2a809afa3e.sentence: iss | Issuer | Identifies principal that issued the JWT, e.g. the name of an organization or a URL of a website.

ec0bab52665d.title: JSON Web Token
ec0bab52665d.sentence: sub | Subject | Identifies the subject of the JWT, e.g. a username or account number.

61601bda3bcb.title: JSON Web Token
61601bda3bcb.sentence: aud | Audience | Identifies the recipients that the JWT is intended for. Each principal intended to process the JWT must identify itself with a value in the audience claim. c80384cd4065.title: Rainbow table
c80384cd4065.sentence: A rainbow table is a precomputed table for caching the outputs of a cryptographic hash function, usually for cracking password hashes.

30791f34fbd6.title: Rainbow table
30791f34fbd6.sentence: If such a database of hashed passwords falls into the hands of attackers, they can use a precomputed rainbow table to recover the plaintext passwords.

38d947e6b440.title: Rainbow table
38d947e6b440.sentence: Rainbow tables are a practical example of a space–time tradeoff: they use less computer processing time and more storage than a brute-force attack which calculates a hash on every attempt, but more processing time and less storage than a simple table that stores the hash of every possible password.

a3603e5c7d3b.title: Rainbow table
a3603e5c7d3b.sentence: To generate the table, we choose a random set of initial passwords from P, compute chains of some fixed length k for each one, and store only the first and last password in each chain.

8531610896f2.title: Rainbow table
8531610896f2.sentence: The idea is to define a reduction function R that maps hash values back into values in P. The reduction function is, however, not an inverse of the hash function, but rather a different function with a swapped domain and codomain of the hash function.

f92993e5de0f.title: Rainbow table
f92993e5de0f.sentence: By alternating the hash function with the reduction function, chains of alternating passwords and hash values are formed.

a6cd354d5b15.title: Rainbow table
a6cd354d5b15.sentence: Rainbow tables effectively solve the problem of collisions with ordinary hash chains by replacing the single reduction function R with a sequence of related reduction functions R1 through Rk.

14afca225e36.title: Rainbow table
14afca225e36.sentence: Rainbow tables are specific to the hash function they were created for e.g., MD5 tables can crack only MD5 hashes.

9f410bb36b68.title: Rainbow table
9f410bb36b68.sentence: A rainbow table is ineffective against one-way hashes that include large salts.

42c9d769fc21.title: Rainbow table
42c9d769fc21.sentence: In order to succeed, an attacker needs to precompute tables for each possible salt value.

f9f9e5311829.title: Rainbow table
f9f9e5311829.sentence: Another technique that helps prevent precomputation attacks is key stretching.

474e16bb8c00.title: Rainbow table
474e16bb8c00.sentence: When stretching is used, the salt, password, and some intermediate hash values are run through the underlying hash function multiple times to increase the computation time required to hash each password.

ac3e816ef177.title: Rainbow table
ac3e816ef177.sentence: Rainbow tables have seen reduced usage as of 2020 as salting is more common and GPU-based brute force attacks have become more practical.

c704666f5cc6.sentence: - Storing password hashes directly is not sufficient because it is prone to precomputation attacks, such as rainbow tables.

d0db2dffadac.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
d0db2dffadac.sentence: - To mitigate precomputation attacks, we salt the passwords.

d51b6ebd153d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
d51b6ebd153d.section: How to store a password and salt?
d51b6ebd153d.sentence: - A salt is not meant to be secret and it can be stored in plain text in the database.

6af535923f78.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
6af535923f78.section: How to store a password and salt?
6af535923f78.sentence: It is used to ensure the hash result is unique to each password.

8c07e01c2d3d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
8c07e01c2d3d.sentence: To validate a password, it can go through the following process:

f7ac8023c278.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
f7ac8023c278.sentence: - The system fetches the corresponding salt from the database.

cf4845ba8671.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
cf4845ba8671.sentence: - The system appends the salt to the password and hashes it.

29a6451c290e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
29a6451c290e.sentence: - The system compares H1 and H2, where H2 is the hash stored in the database.

02149990d0f0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md
02149990d0f0.sentence: If they are the same, the password is valid.

0818d0e755ac.title: rfc>6749
0818d0e755ac.sentence: Before initiating the protocol, the client registers with the authorization server.

76340727fdf8.title: rfc>6749
76340727fdf8.sentence: When registering a client, the client developer SHALL:

82d18ce90127.title: rfc>6749
82d18ce90127.sentence: - specify the client type as described in Section 2.1,

0d3734cdb350.title: rfc>6749
0d3734cdb350.sentence: - provide its client redirection URIs as described in Section 3.1.2, and

33d82b7f48ec.title: rfc>6749
33d82b7f48ec.sentence: The authorization server issues the registered client a client identifier -- a unique string representing the registration information provided by the client.

96ae4b679e88.title: rfc>6749
96ae4b679e88.sentence: The client identifier is not a secret; it is exposed to the resource owner and MUST NOT be used alone for client authentication.

2a0953b3981a.title: rfc>6749
2a0953b3981a.sentence: OAuth defines two client types, based on their ability to authenticate securely with the authorization server (i.e., ability to maintain the confidentiality of their client credentials):

2397f4d0b5c8.title: rfc>6749
2397f4d0b5c8.sentence: confidential Clients capable of maintaining the confidentiality of their credentials (e.g., client implemented on a secure server with restricted access to the client credentials), or capable of secure client authentication using other means.

960d2ed52763.title: rfc>6749
960d2ed52763.sentence: public Clients incapable of maintaining the confidentiality of their credentials (e.g., clients executing on the device used by the resource owner, such as an installed native application or a web browser-based application), and incapable of secure client authentication via any other means.

0df436538ed6.title: rfc>6749
0df436538ed6.sentence: web application A web application is a confidential client running on a web server.

b418d346b9f5.title: rfc>6749
b418d346b9f5.sentence: The client credentials as well as any access token issued to the client are stored on the web server and are not exposed to or accessible by the resource owner.

db74fdef6510.title: rfc>6749
db74fdef6510.sentence: user-agent-based application A user-agent-based application is a public client in which the client code is downloaded from a web server and executes within a user-agent (e.g., web browser) on the device used by the resource owner.

672e28d974a5.title: rfc>6749
672e28d974a5.sentence: native application A native application is a public client installed and executed on the device used by the resource owner.

c68ee80796e7.title: rfc>6749
c68ee80796e7.sentence: It is assumed that any client authentication credentials included in the application can be extracted.

c70f038d0b33.title: rfc>6749
c70f038d0b33.sentence: The authorization process utilizes two authorization server endpoints (HTTP resources):

d583e5169260.title: rfc>6749
d583e5169260.sentence: - Authorization endpoint - used by the client to obtain authorization from the resource owner via user-agent redirection.

e969ee52f155.title: rfc>6749
e969ee52f155.sentence: - Token endpoint - used by the client to exchange an authorization grant for an access token, typically with client authentication.

b19cb684ef09.title: rfc>6749
b19cb684ef09.sentence: - Redirection endpoint - used by the authorization server to return responses containing authorization credentials to the client via the resource owner user-agent.

204dda308bd0.title: rfc>6749
204dda308bd0.section: 3. Protocol Endpoints > 3.2. Token Endpoint > 3.2.1. Client Authentication
204dda308bd0.sentence: Confidential clients or other clients issued client credentials MUST authenticate with the authorization server as described in Section 2.3 when making requests to the token endpoint.

8100921daaa9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::oauth-20-and-openid-connect-oidc
8100921daaa9.sentence: - The Authorization Server redirects back to the client with either an Authorization Code or Access Token, depending on the grant type.

11552116343d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::oauth-20-and-openid-connect-oidc
11552116343d.sentence: - With the Access Token, the client can request access to the resource from the Resource Server.

9b6ae88e241d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::oauth-20-and-openid-connect-oidc
9b6ae88e241d.sentence: - The client requests authorization from the Authorization Server, supplying the client id and secret as identification.

8d19fcb48cb9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::oauth-20-and-openid-connect-oidc
8d19fcb48cb9.sentence: It also provides the scopes and an endpoint URI to send the Access Token or the Authorization Code.

becc6e5090ca.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::oauth-20-and-openid-connect-oidc
becc6e5090ca.sentence: - The Authorization Server authenticates the client and verifies that the requested scopes are permitted.

58c9601684c4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::oauth-20-and-openid-connect-oidc
58c9601684c4.sentence: - The resource owner interacts with the authorization server to grant access.

165bc7609783.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::oauth-20-and-openid-connect-oidc
165bc7609783.sentence: A Refresh Token may also be returned.

eeed2803c517.title: OAuth
eeed2803c517.sentence: An access token is provided through the granting of "authorization grant" or "authorization flow".

8a7b71c78b5f.title: OAuth
8a7b71c78b5f.sentence: The OAuth framework specifies several grant types for different use cases.

cf43c8f7681a.title: OAuth
cf43c8f7681a.sentence: Some of the most common OAuth grant types are:

1bf0dd6e772f.title: rfc>6749
1bf0dd6e772f.sentence: An authorization grant is a credential representing the resource owner's authorization (to access its protected resources) used by the client to obtain an access token.

827027206bab.title: rfc>6749
827027206bab.sentence: This specification defines four grant types -- authorization code, implicit, resource owner password credentials, and client credentials -- as well as an extensibility mechanism for defining additional types.

49625d6254ca.title: rfc>6749
49625d6254ca.sentence: Instead of requesting authorization directly from the resource owner, the client directs the resource owner to an authorization server (via its user-agent as defined in ), which in turn directs the resource owner back to the client with the authorization code.

5b90305f514f.title: rfc>6749
5b90305f514f.sentence: Before directing the resource owner back to the client with the authorization code, the authorization server authenticates the resource owner and obtains authorization.

2343e0919c91.title: rfc>6749
2343e0919c91.sentence: Because the resource owner only authenticates with the authorization server, the resource owner's credentials are never shared with the client.

9fde1e056925.title: rfc>6749
9fde1e056925.sentence: The authorization code provides a few important security benefits, such as the ability to authenticate the client, as well as the transmission of the access token directly to the client without passing it through the resource owner's user-agent and potentially exposing it to others, including the resource owner.

00737db4917b.title: rfc>6749
00737db4917b.sentence: The authorization code grant type is used to obtain both access tokens and refresh tokens and is optimized for confidential clients.

875b38e2b744.title: rfc>6749
875b38e2b744.sentence: The implicit grant is a simplified authorization code flow optimized for clients implemented in a browser using a scripting language such as JavaScript.

7b6abd266f9f.title: rfc>6749
7b6abd266f9f.sentence: In the implicit flow, instead of issuing the client an authorization code, the client is issued an access token directly

cfbd60a8d9a1.title: rfc>6749
cfbd60a8d9a1.sentence: When issuing an access token during the implicit grant flow, the authorization server does not authenticate the client.

7295bcd09fea.title: rfc>6749
7295bcd09fea.sentence: The access token may be exposed to the resource owner or other applications with access to the resource owner's user-agent.

616b0b33e403.title: rfc>6749
616b0b33e403.sentence: Implicit grants improve the responsiveness and efficiency of some clients (such as a client implemented as an in-browser application), since it reduces the number of round trips required to obtain an access token.

6666edebb660.title: rfc>6749
6666edebb660.sentence: The implicit grant type is used to obtain access tokens (it does not support the issuance of refresh tokens) and is optimized for public clients known to operate a particular redirection URI.

c2982ae02be3.title: rfc>6749
c2982ae02be3.section: 1. Introduction > 1.3. Authorization Grant > 1.3.3. Resource Owner Password Credentials
c2982ae02be3.sentence: The resource owner password credentials (i.e., username and password) can be used directly as an authorization grant to obtain an access token.

74aae49bacb2.title: rfc>6749
74aae49bacb2.section: 1. Introduction > 1.3. Authorization Grant > 1.3.3. Resource Owner Password Credentials
74aae49bacb2.sentence: The credentials should only be used when there is a high degree of trust between the resource owner and the client (e.g., the client is part of the device operating system or a highly privileged application), and when other authorization grant types are not available (such as an authorization code).

ed27d1b19683.title: rfc>6749
ed27d1b19683.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.7. Resource Owner Password Credentials
ed27d1b19683.sentence: This grant type carries a higher risk than other grant types because it maintains the password anti-pattern this protocol seeks to avoid.

cd1291328722.title: rfc>6749
cd1291328722.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.7. Resource Owner Password Credentials
cd1291328722.sentence: The client could abuse the password, or the password could unintentionally be disclosed to an attacker (e.g., via log files or other records kept by the client).

e6b26083f719.title: rfc>6749
e6b26083f719.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.7. Resource Owner Password Credentials
e6b26083f719.sentence: The authorization server and client SHOULD minimize use of this grant type and utilize other grant types whenever possible.

e15aa9e20e56.title: rfc>6749
e15aa9e20e56.sentence: The client credentials (or other forms of client authentication) can be used as an authorization grant when the authorization scope is limited to the protected resources under the control of the client, or to protected resources previously arranged with the authorization server.

dfeee6a6b855.title: rfc>6749
dfeee6a6b855.sentence: Client credentials are used as an authorization grant typically when the client is acting on its own behalf (the client is also the resource owner) or is requesting access to protected resources based on an authorization previously arranged with the authorization server.

f0c9e283e4ed.title: rfc>6749
f0c9e283e4ed.sentence: The client credentials grant type MUST only be used by confidential clients.

e0a4b9927df2.title: rfc>6749
e0a4b9927df2.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.4. Client Credentials Grant > 4.4.3. Access Token Response
e0a4b9927df2.sentence: A refresh token SHOULD NOT be included.

7dc1ced17e00.title: rfc>6749
7dc1ced17e00.sentence: The client uses an extension grant type by specifying the grant type using an absolute URI (defined by the authorization server) as the value of the "grant_type" parameter of the token endpoint, and by adding any additional parameters necessary.

6d207c4daa0b.title: rfc>6749
6d207c4daa0b.section: 8. Extensibility > 8.3. Defining New Authorization Grant Types
6d207c4daa0b.sentence: New authorization grant types can be defined by assigning them a unique absolute URI for use with the "grant_type" parameter.

b929931620e2.title: rfc>6749
b929931620e2.sentence: Since this is a redirection-based flow, the client must be capable of interacting with the resource owner's user-agent (typically a web browser) and capable of receiving incoming requests (via redirection) from the authorization server.

ac0884a10e42.title: rfc>6749
ac0884a10e42.sentence: (A) The client initiates the flow by directing the resource owner's user-agent to the authorization endpoint.

151afc851cae.title: rfc>6749
151afc851cae.sentence: The client includes its client identifier, requested scope, local state, and a redirection URI to which the authorization server will send the user-agent back once access is granted (or denied).

13ea9998cfac.title: rfc>6749
13ea9998cfac.sentence: (B) The authorization server authenticates the resource owner (via the user-agent) and establishes whether the resource owner grants or denies the client's access request.

8b1f76836292.title: rfc>6749
8b1f76836292.sentence: (C) Assuming the resource owner grants access, the authorization server redirects the user-agent back to the client using the redirection URI provided earlier (in the request or during client registration).

3cbf5f7a96ea.title: rfc>6749
3cbf5f7a96ea.sentence: The redirection URI includes an authorization code and any local state provided by the client earlier.

08c6e1e55ef3.title: rfc>6749
08c6e1e55ef3.sentence: (D) The client requests an access token from the authorization server's token endpoint by including the authorization code received in the previous step.

ddab37529baa.title: rfc>6749
ddab37529baa.sentence: When making the request, the client authenticates with the authorization server.

bada6fc538b0.title: rfc>6749
bada6fc538b0.sentence: The client includes the redirection URI used to obtain the authorization code for verification.

6132d6449137.title: rfc>6749
6132d6449137.sentence: (E) The authorization server authenticates the client, validates the authorization code, and ensures that the redirection URI received matches the URI used to redirect the client in step (C).

964683263e66.title: rfc>6749
964683263e66.sentence: If valid, the authorization server responds back with an access token and, optionally, a refresh token.

11889e27c59c.title: rfc>6749
11889e27c59c.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.1. Authorization Request

61b27802a65b.title: rfc>6749
61b27802a65b.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.1. Authorization Request
61b27802a65b.sentence: The parameter SHOULD be used for preventing cross-site request forgery as described in Section 10.12.

3db369bd1aa1.title: rfc>6749
3db369bd1aa1.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response
3db369bd1aa1.sentence: The exact value received from the client.

62307b38ccc2.title: rfc>6749
62307b38ccc2.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response
62307b38ccc2.sentence: The authorization code MUST expire shortly after it is issued to mitigate the risk of leaks.

74fc1d61a6a6.title: rfc>6749
74fc1d61a6a6.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response
74fc1d61a6a6.sentence: A maximum authorization code lifetime of 10 minutes is RECOMMENDED.

bb4e77c8a5f1.title: rfc>6749
bb4e77c8a5f1.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response
bb4e77c8a5f1.sentence: The client MUST NOT use the authorization code

1ac8a0d73d66.title: rfc>6749
1ac8a0d73d66.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response

84ae5797890f.title: rfc>6749
84ae5797890f.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response
84ae5797890f.sentence: If an authorization code is used more than once, the authorization server MUST deny the request and SHOULD revoke (when possible) all tokens previously issued based on that authorization code.

c75dd9b3cf4b.title: rfc>6749
c75dd9b3cf4b.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response
c75dd9b3cf4b.sentence: The authorization code is bound to the client identifier and redirection URI.

1fd0c3d2cc9e.title: rfc>6749
1fd0c3d2cc9e.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.3. Access Token Request

03ce8e42929b.title: rfc>6749
03ce8e42929b.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.3. Access Token Request

047043980ea1.title: rfc>6749
047043980ea1.sentence: The client MUST use the HTTP "POST" method when making access token requests.

39b95f7dfcf1.title: rfc>6749
39b95f7dfcf1.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.3. Access Token Request
39b95f7dfcf1.sentence: If the client type is confidential or the client was issued client credentials (or assigned other authentication requirements), the client MUST authenticate with the authorization server as described in Section 3.2.1.

fe968bde9a56.title: rfc>6749
fe968bde9a56.section: 4. Obtaining Authorization > 4.1. Authorization Code Grant > 4.1.2. Authorization Response > 4.1.2.1. Error Response
fe968bde9a56.sentence: If the request fails due to a missing, invalid, or mismatching redirection URI, or if the client identifier is missing or invalid, the authorization server SHOULD inform the resource owner of the error and MUST NOT automatically redirect the user-agent to the invalid redirection URI.

59b6e49ba196.title: rfc>6749
59b6e49ba196.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.6. Authorization Code Redirection URI Manipulation
59b6e49ba196.sentence: If an attacker can manipulate the value of the redirection URI, it can cause the authorization server to redirect the resource owner user-agent to a URI under the control of the attacker with the authorization code.

6d1bb2e3f05d.title: rfc>6749
6d1bb2e3f05d.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.6. Authorization Code Redirection URI Manipulation
6d1bb2e3f05d.sentence: In order to prevent such an attack, the authorization server MUST ensure that the redirection URI used to obtain the authorization code is identical to the redirection URI provided when exchanging the authorization code for an access token.

2e5e13040c63.title: rfc>6749
2e5e13040c63.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.6. Authorization Code Redirection URI Manipulation
2e5e13040c63.sentence: The authorization server MUST require public clients and SHOULD require confidential clients to register their redirection URIs.

dcc727ee5ea9.title: rfc>6749
dcc727ee5ea9.sentence: An open redirector is an endpoint using a parameter to automatically redirect a user-agent to the location specified by the parameter value without any validation.

f2cfb212a219.title: rfc>6749
f2cfb212a219.sentence: In addition, if the authorization server allows the client to register only part of the redirection URI, an attacker can use an open redirector operated by

1ae0ba5f89de.title: rfc>6749
1ae0ba5f89de.sentence: the client to construct a redirection URI that will pass the authorization server validation but will send the authorization code or access token to an endpoint under the control of the attacker.

6220bfa3e216.title: OAuth
6220bfa3e216.sentence: In January 2013, the Internet Engineering Task Force published a threat model for OAuth 2.0 in RFC 6819.

779aebd020ec.title: OAuth
779aebd020ec.sentence: Among the threats outlined is one called "Open Redirector"; in early 2014, a variant of this was described under the name "Covert Redirect" by Wang Jing.

a8978e30234e.title: Single sign-on
a8978e30234e.sentence: Covert Redirect takes advantage of third-party clients susceptible to cross-site scripting (XSS) or open redirect.

f076115d17e0.title: rfc>6749
f076115d17e0.sentence: A CSRF attack against the client's redirection URI allows an attacker to inject its own authorization code or access token, which can result in the client using an access token associated with the attacker's protected resources rather than the victim's (e.g., save the victim's bank account information to a protected resource controlled by the attacker).

267280c1fe8c.title: rfc>6749
267280c1fe8c.sentence: The client MUST implement CSRF protection for its redirection URI.

784a63d48fb9.title: rfc>6749
784a63d48fb9.sentence: The client SHOULD utilize the "state" request parameter to deliver this value to the authorization server when making an authorization request.

731140cf4df2.title: rfc>6749
731140cf4df2.sentence: The binding value used for CSRF protection MUST contain a non-guessable value (as described in Section 10.10), and the user-agent's authenticated state (e.g., session cookie, HTML5 local storage) MUST be kept in a location accessible only to the client and the user-agent (i.e., protected by same-origin policy).

b1cc8f102474.title: rfc>6749
b1cc8f102474.sentence: The authorization server MUST implement CSRF protection for its authorization endpoint and ensure that a malicious client cannot obtain authorization without the awareness and explicit consent of the resource owner.

c41090988b50.title: rfc>6749
c41090988b50.sentence: In a clickjacking attack, an attacker registers a legitimate client and then constructs a malicious site in which it loads the authorization server's authorization endpoint web page in a transparent iframe overlaid on top of a set of dummy buttons, which are carefully constructed to be placed directly under important buttons on the authorization page.

45aa40226338.title: rfc>6749
45aa40226338.sentence: To prevent this form of attack, native applications SHOULD use external browsers instead of embedding browsers within the application when requesting end-user authorization.

b1f1caff3a4e.title: rfc>6749
b1f1caff3a4e.sentence: This header can have two values, "deny" and "sameorigin", which will block any framing, or framing by sites with a different origin, respectively.

2a84b923d2bf.title: rfc>6749
2a84b923d2bf.sentence: When using the implicit grant type, the access token is transmitted in the URI fragment, which can expose it to unauthorized parties.

4d3880d88241.title: rfc>6749
4d3880d88241.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.16. Misuse of Access Token to Impersonate Resource Owner in Implicit
4d3880d88241.sentence: In the implicit flow (response_type=token), the attacker can easily switch the token in the response from the authorization server, replacing the real access token with the one previously issued to the attacker.

e53a719d9af5.title: rfc>6749
e53a719d9af5.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.16. Misuse of Access Token to Impersonate Resource Owner in Implicit
e53a719d9af5.sentence: Any specification that uses the authorization process as a form of delegated end-user authentication to the client (e.g., third-party sign-in service) MUST NOT use the implicit flow without additional security mechanisms that would enable the client to determine if the access token was issued for its use (e.g., audience-restricting the access token).

7bf38684063e.title: rfc>6749
7bf38684063e.sentence: The client MUST validate the authorization server's TLS certificate as defined by and in accordance with its requirements for server identity authentication.

6c35550920cd.title: OAuth
6c35550920cd.sentence: This analysis revealed that in setups with multiple authorization servers, one of which is behaving maliciously, clients can become confused about the authorization server to use and may forward secrets to the malicious authorization server (AS Mix-Up Attack).

cb552ac8c10f.title: OAuth
cb552ac8c10f.sentence: This prompted the creation of a new best current practice internet draft that sets out to define a new security standard for OAuth 2.0.

ac3a975cc575.title: OAuth
ac3a975cc575.sentence: Assuming a fix against the AS Mix-Up Attack in place, the security of OAuth 2.0 has been proven under strong attacker models using formal analysis.

089cb7ecf7bd.title: OAuth
089cb7ecf7bd.sentence: The PKCE (RFC 7636) extension for native apps has been recommended for all types of OAuth clients, including web applications and other confidential clients, in the draft of OAuth 2.1.

7117ee9e0509.title: OpenID
7117ee9e0509.sentence: The OpenID Connect protocol mandates strict measures that preclude open redirectors to prevent this vulnerability."

824be1f6d762.title: rfc>7636
824be1f6d762.sentence: This specification describes the attack as well as a technique to mitigate against the threat through the use of Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE, pronounced "pixy").

629b0d1e4448.title: rfc>7636
629b0d1e4448.sentence: To mitigate this attack, this extension utilizes a dynamically created cryptographically random key called "code verifier".

33196d179fc3.title: rfc>7636
33196d179fc3.sentence: OAuth 2.0 public clients are susceptible to the authorization code interception attack.

66a0ba1303f2.title: rfc>7636
66a0ba1303f2.sentence: In this attack, the attacker intercepts the authorization code returned from the authorization endpoint within a communication path not protected by Transport Layer Security (TLS), such as inter-application communication within the client's operating system.

bf0402a5e00a.title: rfc>7636
bf0402a5e00a.sentence: Once the attacker has gained access to the authorization code, it can use it to obtain the access token.

ef287e64b35f.title: rfc>7636
ef287e64b35f.sentence: Note that it is possible for a malicious app to register itself as a handler for the custom scheme in addition to the legitimate OAuth 2.0 app.

9cb2649f04fd.title: rfc>7636
9cb2649f04fd.sentence: Once it does so, the malicious app is now able to intercept the authorization code in step (4).

61fd6a8f084a.title: rfc>7636
61fd6a8f084a.sentence: Secrets provisioned in client binary applications cannot be considered confidential.

d06df496f21a.title: rfc>7636
d06df496f21a.sentence: A unique code verifier is created for every authorization request, and its transformed value, called "code challenge", is sent to the authorization server to obtain the authorization code.

c662e9449a8f.title: rfc>7636
c662e9449a8f.sentence: A. The client creates and records a secret named the "code_verifier" and derives a transformed version "t(code_verifier)" (referred to as the "code_challenge"), which is sent in the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Request along with the transformation method "t_m".

2e25ff54719c.title: rfc>7636
2e25ff54719c.sentence: B. The Authorization Endpoint responds as usual but records "t(code_verifier)" and the transformation method.

e247e988cf4e.title: rfc>7636
e247e988cf4e.sentence: C. The client then sends the authorization code in the Access Token Request as usual but includes the "code_verifier" secret generated at (A).

90b21eaf3206.title: rfc>7636
90b21eaf3206.sentence: D. The authorization server transforms "code_verifier" and compares it to "t(code_verifier)" from (B).

3742d347e4fe.title: rfc>7636
3742d347e4fe.sentence: Access is denied if they are not equal.

bfb0318a14a4.title: rfc>7636
bfb0318a14a4.section: 4. Protocol > 4.6. Server Verifies code_verifier before Returning the Tokens
bfb0318a14a4.sentence: If the values are not equal, an error response indicating "invalid_grant" as described in Section 5.2 of MUST be returned.

16057dc5fbac.title: rfc>7636
16057dc5fbac.sentence: An attacker who intercepts the authorization code at (B) is unable to redeem it for an access token, as they are not in possession of the "code_verifier" secret.

b322b76e1511.title: rfc>7636
b322b76e1511.sentence: This works as the mitigation since the attacker would not know this one-time key, since it is sent over TLS and cannot be intercepted.

83ffccc08435.title: rfc>7636
83ffccc08435.section: 4. Protocol > 4.1. Client Creates a Code Verifier
83ffccc08435.sentence: code_verifier = high-entropy cryptographic random STRING using the unreserved characters [A-Z] / [a-z] / [0-9] / "-" / "." / "_" / "~" from Section 2.3 of, with a minimum length of 43 characters and a maximum length of 128 characters.

9cf3bb284322.title: rfc>7636
9cf3bb284322.section: 7. Security Considerations > 7.1. Entropy of the code_verifier
9cf3bb284322.sentence: The client SHOULD create a "code_verifier" with a minimum of 256 bits of entropy.

4cab18d7527c.title: rfc>7636
4cab18d7527c.section: 7. Security Considerations > 7.1. Entropy of the code_verifier
4cab18d7527c.sentence: This can be done by having a suitable random number generator create a 32-octet sequence.

25fdb3cac70a.title: rfc>7636
25fdb3cac70a.section: 7. Security Considerations > 7.1. Entropy of the code_verifier
25fdb3cac70a.sentence: The octet sequence can then be base64url-encoded to produce a 43-octet URL safe string to use as a "code_challenge" that has the required entropy.

b33d90679548.title: rfc>7636
b33d90679548.section: 4. Protocol > 4.2. Client Creates the Code Challenge

80f5a7338306.title: rfc>7636
80f5a7338306.section: 4. Protocol > 4.2. Client Creates the Code Challenge

f91d7dbd6a37.title: rfc>7636
f91d7dbd6a37.section: 4. Protocol > 4.2. Client Creates the Code Challenge
f91d7dbd6a37.sentence: If the client is capable of using "S256", it MUST use "S256", as "S256" is Mandatory To Implement (MTI) on the server.

f326a53cec42.title: rfc>7636
f326a53cec42.sentence: Since the code challenge is the same as the code verifier in this case, the "plain" method does not protect against the eavesdropping of the initial request.

fa62a1c8d482.title: rfc>7636
fa62a1c8d482.sentence: The "plain" method SHOULD NOT be used in new implementations, unless they cannot support "S256" for some technical reason.

58598f00d2dc.title: rfc>7636
58598f00d2dc.sentence: Clients MUST NOT downgrade to "plain" after trying the "S256" method.

fe58c6d9b9f8.title: rfc>7636
fe58c6d9b9f8.sentence: To reduce implementation complexity, salting is not used in the production of the code challenge, as the code verifier contains sufficient entropy to prevent brute-force attacks.

21ea7a8dd53b.title: Cross-site scripting
21ea7a8dd53b.section: Preventive measures > Contextual output encoding/escaping of string input
21ea7a8dd53b.sentence: Most web applications that do not need to accept rich data can use escaping to largely eliminate the risk of XSS attacks in a fairly straightforward manner.

3fb3ca3ad82a.title: Cross-site scripting
3fb3ca3ad82a.section: Preventive measures > Contextual output encoding/escaping of string input
3fb3ca3ad82a.sentence: Some web template systems understand the structure of the HTML they produce and automatically pick an appropriate encoder.

f38336ff3f2f.title: Cross-site scripting
f38336ff3f2f.section: Preventive measures > Safely validating untrusted HTML input
f38336ff3f2f.sentence: When accepting HTML input from users (say, very large), output encoding (such as <b>very</b> large) will not suffice since the user input needs to be rendered as HTML by the browser (so it shows as very large, instead of very large).

4870fc485a23.title: Cross-site scripting
4870fc485a23.section: Preventive measures > Safely validating untrusted HTML input
4870fc485a23.sentence: Stopping an XSS attack when accepting HTML input from users is much more complex in this situation.

18549afd5d69.title: Cross-site scripting
18549afd5d69.section: Preventive measures > Safely validating untrusted HTML input
18549afd5d69.sentence: Often, untrusted HTML input must be run through an HTML sanitization engine to ensure that it does not contain potentially malicious JavaScript code.

bb279a402fd8.title: Cross-site scripting

bb279a402fd8.sentence: then the application processing the markup may allow the <span> but escape the script when the input is displayed:

8b8d830b25f0.title: Cross-site scripting
8b8d830b25f0.sentence: Many web applications rely on session cookies for authentication between individual HTTP requests, and because client-side scripts generally have access to these cookies, simple XSS exploits can steal these cookies.

b28138f7aa7b.title: Cross-site scripting
b28138f7aa7b.section: Preventive measures > Cookie security > Http-only cookie
b28138f7aa7b.sentence: Another mitigation present in Internet Explorer (since version 6), Firefox (since version 2.0.0.5), Safari (since version 4), Opera (since version 9.5) and Google Chrome, is an HttpOnly flag which allows a web server to set a cookie that is unavailable to client-side scripts.

7396bf2ea5ef.title: Cross-site scripting
7396bf2ea5ef.section: Preventive measures > Cookie security > Http-only cookie
7396bf2ea5ef.sentence: While beneficial, the feature can neither fully prevent cookie theft nor prevent attacks within the browser.

5f7869854895.title: Cross-site scripting
5f7869854895.sentence: When a cookie is set with the SameSite=Strict parameter, it is stripped from all cross-origin requests.

7759568fb7de.title: Cross-site scripting
7759568fb7de.sentence: Trusted types changes Web APIs to check that values have been trademarked as trusted.

38ab59ac4d4f.title: Cross-site scripting
38ab59ac4d4f.sentence: As long as programs only trademark trustworthy values, an attacker who controls a JavaScript string value cannot cause XSS.

420614e908fe.title: Cross-site scripting
420614e908fe.sentence: Prevention strategies for DOM-based XSS attacks include very similar measures to traditional XSS prevention strategies but implemented in JavaScript code and contained in web pages (i.e. input validation and escaping).

93eb3f11078b.title: WebAuthn
93eb3f11078b.sentence: Web Authentication (WebAuthn) is a web standard published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C).

ee9ba3964c65.title: WebAuthn
ee9ba3964c65.sentence: It defines an API that websites use to authenticate with WebAuthn credentials (commonly known as passkeys) and outlines what WebAuthn authenticators should do.

653acf3258f0.title: WebAuthn
653acf3258f0.sentence: Users routinely reuse passwords across services (which exposes them to credential stuffing), choose weak passwords that can be brute-forced and predicted in a short amount of time, and store them in insecure ways that allows for their disclosure (for example writing them down on a piece of paper or a document), with each of those contributing to the likelihood of credentials and account compromise.

2addcd46d440.title: WebAuthn
2addcd46d440.sentence: Flaws include plain-text storage, lack of salted hashing (or more advanced schemes for at-rest credentials), arbitrary restrictions on password length and charset, mandatory ineffective password changes, and deliberate incompatibility with password managers (for instance, by preventing passwords to be pasted).

045e9e9ed4ce.title: WebAuthn
045e9e9ed4ce.sentence: The WebAuthn standard provides a mechanism for a device or a program, known as the "authenticator") to verify a user's identity to a website through their web browser by confirming that the user possesses the device.

933310658d7f.title: WebAuthn
933310658d7f.sentence: To do this in a secure manner, the standard defines two events, the registration ceremony and the authentication ceremony.

03d0623bb500.title: WebAuthn
03d0623bb500.sentence: During these events the authenticator communicates with the website through the web browser to register itself as a device the user possesses and proves to the website that the user still possesses the device respectively.

6f8413a90049.title: WebAuthn
6f8413a90049.sentence: Authenticator is a multi-factor cryptographic authenticator that uses public-key cryptography to sign an authentication assertion targeted at the website.

cbf84cbe060a.title: WebAuthn
cbf84cbe060a.sentence: To obtain a public key for the user, the website initiates a WebAuthn registration flow that is similar to the authentication flow illustrated above.

b6c72008e6f3.title: WebAuthn
b6c72008e6f3.sentence: The signed attestation statement contains a copy of the public key that the website ultimately uses to verify a signed authentication assertion.

e3e70309f2ea.title: WebAuthn
e3e70309f2ea.sentence: The most common authenticator type is a platform authenticator, which is built into the operating system of the device.

c316c28963a8.title: WebAuthn
c316c28963a8.sentence: Common platform authenticators include Android, Apple Keychain and Windows Hello.

df5ef1650de2.title: WebAuthn
df5ef1650de2.sentence: Another common authenticator type is a roaming authenticator, where a separate hardware device authenticates the user by connecting over USB, Bluetooth Low Energy, or near-field communications (NFC).

517a142031ad.title: WebAuthn
517a142031ad.sentence: A hardware authenticator in the user's possession conforms to the FIDO Client to Authenticator Protocol (CTAP), and connects over USB, Bluetooth Low Energy, or near-field communications (NFC).

83b3c9b7b05e.title: WebAuthn
83b3c9b7b05e.sentence: Password managers can also be used as an authenticator, often with cloud sync.

127d419bc251.title: WebAuthn
127d419bc251.sentence: The Web Authentication API extends the Credential Management navigator.credentials.create() and navigator.credentials.get() JavaScript methods so they accept a publicKey parameter.

20bc84a07012.title: WebAuthn
20bc84a07012.sentence: The create() method is used for registering public key authenticators as part of associating them with user accounts (possibly at initial account creation time but more likely when adding a new security device to an existing account) while the get() method is used for authenticating (such as when logging in).

394f68503506.title: WebAuthn
394f68503506.sentence: Like legacy U2F, WebAuthn is resistant to some phishing attacks as the authenticator only offers credentials that were registered on the same website.

0f328321f557.title: WebAuthn
0f328321f557.sentence: However, unlike U2F, WebAuthn can be implemented in a passwordless manner.

87b426fafcdb.title: WebAuthn
87b426fafcdb.sentence: Moreover, a roaming hardware authenticator resists malware, since the keys are stored on a separate device, which prevents the malware from accessing them directly.

dd4540a91e46.title: WebAuthn
dd4540a91e46.sentence: As a result, in 2012, Google alongside Yubico started working on a standard called Universal 2 Factor (U2F) that would allow websites to programmatically verify a second-factor about the user by verifying the presence of hardware-based tokens (like smart cards) on the user.

90b14ef3d4ef.title: WebAuthn
90b14ef3d4ef.sentence: This standard was considered an improvement over existing solutions like time-based one-time password (TOTP) or SMS-based authentication that still left the user vulnerable to sophisticated phishing campaigns.

b8bd2f096481.title: WebAuthn
b8bd2f096481.sentence: Although WebAuthn is often touted as a complete replacement for passwords, most websites that implement it continue to use passwords in some capacity.

e0ff94dfe19d.title: rfc>6749
e0ff94dfe19d.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.14. Code Injection and Input Validation
e0ff94dfe19d.sentence: A code injection attack occurs when an input or otherwise external variable is used by an application unsanitized and causes modification to the application logic.

94b214fb5a52.title: rfc>6749
94b214fb5a52.section: 10. Security Considerations > 10.14. Code Injection and Input Validation
94b214fb5a52.sentence: The authorization server and client MUST sanitize (and validate when possible) any value received -- in particular, the value of the "state" and "redirect_uri" parameters.

b46e947554bc.title: Multi-factor authentication
b46e947554bc.sentence: MFA requires rate limiting to be secure.

a04938adf881.title: Multi-factor authentication
a04938adf881.sentence: Without rate limiting, an attacker can preform an arbitrary number of auth requests attempting different codes until they eventually get access.

0e416fe2ba06.title: Multi-factor authentication
0e416fe2ba06.sentence: If the rate limit is tied to a session ID or request token, the attacker may generate new sessions or request tokens to reset the limit.

2db8fd091925.title: Zero trust architecture
2db8fd091925.sentence: Zero trust architecture (ZTA) is a design and implementation strategy of IT systems.

c2e6a4405cb5.title: Zero trust architecture
c2e6a4405cb5.sentence: The traditional approach by trusting users and devices within a notional "corporate perimeter" or via a VPN connection is commonly not sufficient in the complex environment of a corporate network.

c80930a20360.title: Zero trust architecture
c80930a20360.sentence: Most modern corporate networks consist of many interconnected zones, cloud services and infrastructure, connections to remote and mobile environments, and connections to non-conventional IT, such as IoT devices.

b1ed6e58323a.title: Zero trust architecture
b1ed6e58323a.sentence: The zero trust approach advocates mutual authentication, including checking the identity and integrity of users and devices without respect to location, and providing access to applications and services based on the confidence of user and device identity and device status in combination with user authentication.

3d3116f538e7.title: Zero trust architecture
3d3116f538e7.sentence: In 2018, the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (NCCoE) published NIST SP 800-207 – zero trust architecture.

4472e40d2b50.title: Zero trust architecture
4472e40d2b50.sentence: The publication defines zero trust as a collection of concepts and ideas designed to reduce the uncertainty in enforcing accurate, per-request access decisions in information systems and services in the face of a network viewed as compromised.

2735016b84ff.title: Zero trust architecture
2735016b84ff.sentence: There are several ways to implement all the tenets of ZT; a full ZTA solution will include elements of all three:

2433e63dcea9.title: Zero trust architecture
2433e63dcea9.sentence: - Using enhanced identity governance and policy-based access controls.

4752713210e6.title: Zero trust architecture
4752713210e6.sentence: - Using overlay networks or software-defined perimeters

9caab6f24966.title: Zero trust architecture
9caab6f24966.sentence: This brings about zero trust data security where every request to access the data needs to be authenticated dynamically and ensure least privileged access to resources.

a91e6849cf5a.title: Zero trust architecture
a91e6849cf5a.sentence: In order to determine if access can be granted, policies can be applied based on the attributes of the data, who the user is, and the type of environment using attribute-based access control (ABAC).

a32a6c61cf6f.title: rfc>7519
a32a6c61cf6f.sentence: If the JOSE Header is for a JWS, the JWT is represented as a JWS and the claims are digitally signed or MACed, with the JWT Claims Set being the JWS Payload.

188d0823b4ec.title: rfc>7519
188d0823b4ec.sentence: If the JOSE Header is for a JWE, the JWT is represented as a JWE and the claims are encrypted, with the JWT Claims Set being the plaintext encrypted by the JWE.

dccd248fe9d1.title: rfc>7519
dccd248fe9d1.sentence: A JWT may be enclosed in another JWE or JWS structure to create a Nested JWT, enabling nested signing and encryption to be performed.

1c0b120d182d.title: rfc>7519
1c0b120d182d.sentence: The contents of the JOSE Header describe the cryptographic operations applied to the JWT Claims Set.

d86cfa8a6faf.title: rfc>7519
d86cfa8a6faf.section: 11. Security Considerations > 11.2. Signing and Encryption Order
d86cfa8a6faf.sentence: While syntactically the signing and encryption operations for Nested JWTs may be applied in any order, if both signing and encryption are necessary, normally producers should sign the message and then

b3a08dd5430d.title: rfc>7519
b3a08dd5430d.section: 11. Security Considerations > 11.2. Signing and Encryption Order
b3a08dd5430d.sentence: encrypt the result (thus encrypting the signature).

a46db8aed8b2.title: rfc>7519
a46db8aed8b2.section: 11. Security Considerations > 11.2. Signing and Encryption Order
a46db8aed8b2.sentence: This prevents attacks in which the signature is stripped, leaving just an encrypted message, as well as providing privacy for the signer.

3854ce780716.title: rfc>7519
3854ce780716.sentence: To support use cases in which the JWT content is secured by a means other than a signature and/or encryption contained within the JWT (such as a signature on a data structure containing the JWT), JWTs MAY also be created without a signature or encryption.

3e36f3fae7da.title: rfc>7519
3e36f3fae7da.sentence: An Unsecured JWT is a JWS using the "alg" Header Parameter value "none" and with the empty string for its JWS Signature value, as defined in the JWA specification; it is an Unsecured JWS with the JWT Claims Set as its JWS Payload.

835bd8fab2f5.title: rfc>7519
835bd8fab2f5.sentence: Of the signature and MAC algorithms specified in JSON Web Algorithms, only HMAC SHA-256 ("HS256") and "none" MUST be implemented by conforming JWT implementations.

85783c5e4de1.title: rfc>7519
85783c5e4de1.sentence: It is RECOMMENDED that implementations also support RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with the SHA-256 hash algorithm ("RS256") and ECDSA using the P-256 curve and the SHA-256 hash algorithm ("ES256").

9c588ad98da3.title: rfc>7519
9c588ad98da3.sentence: Support for other algorithms and key sizes is OPTIONAL.

8e65fed2d335.title: rfc>7519
8e65fed2d335.sentence: Support for encrypted JWTs is OPTIONAL.

ecaa7a17b153.title: rfc>7519
ecaa7a17b153.sentence: Support for Nested JWTs is OPTIONAL.

2bcb356fcf2e.title: rfc>7519
2bcb356fcf2e.sentence: The contents of a JWT cannot be relied upon in a trust decision unless its contents have been cryptographically secured and bound to the context necessary for the trust decision.

441d030b5520.title: rfc>7519
441d030b5520.sentence: In particular, the key(s) used to sign and/or encrypt the JWT will typically need to verifiably be under the control of the party identified as the issuer of the JWT.

19c534727066.title: JSON Web Token
19c534727066.sentence: Security consultant Tim McLean reported vulnerabilities in some JWT libraries that used the alg field to incorrectly validate tokens, most commonly by accepting a alg=none token.

b56ba2e59b89.title: JSON Web Token
b56ba2e59b89.sentence: - Never let the JWT header alone drive verification

071a3cbfb0ea.title: JSON Web Token
071a3cbfb0ea.sentence: - Know the algorithms (avoid depending on the alg field alone)

ee2300706514.title: JSON Web Token
ee2300706514.sentence: This token should be sent to the client using a secure mechanism like an HTTP-only cookie.

c6b3dbbb69a8.title: JSON Web Token
c6b3dbbb69a8.sentence: Storing the JWT locally in browser storage mechanisms like local or session storage is discouraged.

ba3aa9591da9.title: JSON Web Token
ba3aa9591da9.sentence: This is because JavaScript running on the client-side (including browser extensions) can access these storage mechanisms, exposing the JWT and compromising security.

3453de33d585.title: JSON Web Token
3453de33d585.sentence: But if project requirements allow session invalidation before JWT expiration, services can no longer trust token assertions by the token alone.

ea90bb96ac4a.title: JSON Web Token
ea90bb96ac4a.sentence: To validate that the session stored in the token is not revoked, token assertions must be checked against a data store.

63fdff3414c8.title: JSON Web Token
63fdff3414c8.sentence: This renders the tokens no longer stateless, undermining the primary advantage of JWTs.

a494287f87db.title: rfc>7519
a494287f87db.sentence: A JWT may contain privacy-sensitive information.

8421456b9bc5.title: rfc>7519
8421456b9bc5.sentence: One way to achieve this is to use an encrypted JWT and authenticate the recipient.

d691454a9b6d.title: rfc>7519
d691454a9b6d.sentence: Another way is to ensure that JWTs containing unencrypted privacy-sensitive information are only transmitted using protocols utilizing encryption that support endpoint authentication, such as Transport Layer Security (TLS).

de231f7dd609.title: rfc>7519
de231f7dd609.sentence: Omitting privacy-sensitive information from a JWT is the simplest way of minimizing privacy issues.

8c6f54672b56.title: JSON Web Token
8c6f54672b56.sentence: Some have argued that JSON web tokens are difficult to use securely due to the many different encryption algorithms and options available in the standard, and that alternate standards should be used instead for both web frontends and backends.

448b4efaae6c.title: Argon2
448b4efaae6c.sentence: Argon2 is a key derivation function that was selected as the winner of the 2015 Password Hashing Competition.

cd5b08621f53.title: Argon2
cd5b08621f53.sentence: The Argon2 function uses a large, fixed-size memory region (often called the 'memory array' in documentation) to make brute-force attacks computationally expensive.

51691c1962f8.title: Argon2
51691c1962f8.sentence: All three modes allow specification by three parameters that control:

0865e71a99bd.title: Argon2
0865e71a99bd.sentence: - Argon2d maximizes resistance to GPU cracking attacks.

6ea8d724ef98.title: Argon2
6ea8d724ef98.sentence: It accesses the memory array in a password-dependent order, which reduces the possibility of time–memory trade-off (TMTO) attacks, but introduces possible side-channel attacks.

35b3b0559049.title: Argon2
35b3b0559049.sentence: - Argon2i is optimized to resist side-channel attacks.

e8514f76f7ae.title: Argon2
e8514f76f7ae.sentence: It accesses the memory array in a password-independent order.

28d6b873c354.title: Argon2
28d6b873c354.sentence: RFC 9106 recommends using Argon2id if one does not know the difference between the types or if side-channel attacks are considered to be a viable threat.

2b3ce960bc0b.title: Argon2
2b3ce960bc0b.sentence: To address these concerns, RFC9106 recommends using Argon2id to largely mitigate such attacks.

fd4249c4ed50.title: Argon2
fd4249c4ed50.sentence: The Request for Comments document standardizing Argon2, which was published in September 2021, recommends:

9fac8e8311ac.title: Argon2
9fac8e8311ac.sentence: - Memory: 2 GiB, Iterations: 1, Parallelism: 4; for "a default setting for all environments"

96febc64de54.title: Argon2
96febc64de54.sentence: - Memory: 64 MiB, Iterations: 3, Parallelism: 4; for "memory-constrained environments"

703b0698866f.title: Bcrypt
703b0698866f.sentence: bcrypt is a password-hashing function designed by Niels Provos and David Mazières.

5d5d24e01917.title: Bcrypt
5d5d24e01917.sentence: It is based on the Blowfish cipher and presented at USENIX in 1999.

6a3ad4d66aa6.title: Bcrypt
6a3ad4d66aa6.sentence: Besides incorporating a salt to protect against rainbow table attacks, bcrypt is an adaptive function: over time, the iteration count can be increased to make it slower, so it remains resistant to brute-force search attacks even with increasing computation power.

b0762e58f2de.title: Bcrypt
b0762e58f2de.sentence: The key setup begins with a modified form of the standard Blowfish key setup, in which both the salt and password are used to set all subkeys.

08f735d89314.title: Bcrypt
08f735d89314.sentence: There are then a number of rounds in which the standard Blowfish keying algorithm is applied, using alternatively the salt and the password as the key, each round starting with the subkey state from the previous round.

d70782876448.title: Bcrypt
d70782876448.sentence: In theory, this is no stronger than the standard Blowfish key schedule, but the number of rekeying rounds is configurable; this process can therefore be made arbitrarily slow, which helps deter brute-force attacks upon the hash or salt.

e192a8390f7d.title: Bcrypt
e192a8390f7d.sentence: The input to the bcrypt function is the password string (up to 72 bytes), a numeric cost, and a 16-byte (128-bit) salt value.

d9d8063fbe65.title: Bcrypt
d9d8063fbe65.sentence: The bcrypt function uses these inputs to compute a 24-byte (192-bit) hash.

101f1c4a6542.title: Bcrypt
101f1c4a6542.sentence: Function bcrypt Input: cost: Number (4..31) log2(Iterations). e.g. 12 ==> 212 = 4,096 iterations salt: array of Bytes (16 bytes) random salt password: array of Bytes (1..72 bytes) UTF-8 encoded password Output: hash: array of Bytes (24 bytes) //Initialize Blowfish state with expensive key setup algorithm //P: array of 18 subkeys (UInt32[18]) //S: Four substitution boxes (S-boxes), S0...S3.

6c5b8c92aa36.title: Bcrypt
6c5b8c92aa36.sentence: bcrypt has a maximum password length of 72 bytes.

44c19984b2b0.title: Bcrypt
44c19984b2b0.sentence: In the worst case a password is limited to 18 characters, when every character requires 4 bytes of UTF-8 encoding.

aee08ac4270a.title: Bcrypt
aee08ac4270a.sentence: Many implementations of bcrypt truncate the password to the first 72 bytes, following the OpenBSD implementation.

75929f5b732e.title: Bcrypt
75929f5b732e.section: Comparison to other password hashing algorithms
75929f5b732e.sentence: Bcrypt is not a key derivation function (KDF).

8313cf9bb87c.title: Bcrypt
8313cf9bb87c.section: Comparison to other password hashing algorithms
8313cf9bb87c.sentence: For example, bcrypt cannot be used to derive a 512-bit key from a password.

ce5ed7ad64c4.title: Multi-factor authentication
ce5ed7ad64c4.sentence: Security issues which can cause the bypass of MFA are fatigue attacks, phishing and SIM swapping.

e479f0a6577a.title: Multi-factor authentication
e479f0a6577a.sentence: However, many multi-factor authentication approaches remain vulnerable to phishing, man-in-the-browser, and man-in-the-middle attacks.

20469a71985c.title: Multi-factor authentication
20469a71985c.sentence: To counter phishing attacks, users should not share their verification codes with anyone, and many web application providers will place an advisory in an e-mail or SMS containing a code.

6271218913ef.title: Multi-factor authentication
6271218913ef.sentence: Phones can be cloned, apps can run on several phones and cell-phone maintenance personnel can read SMS texts.

324e1c11936a.title: Multi-factor authentication
324e1c11936a.sentence: - The SS7 system underlying mobile phone roaming has vulnerabilities, and SMS messages may be redirected to attackers.

bce5ace5b330.title: Multi-factor authentication
bce5ace5b330.sentence: SIM swap attacks and Social-engineering attacks against mobile-operator companies have resulted in the handing over of duplicate SIM cards to criminals.

c3c14ac66a18.title: Multi-factor authentication
c3c14ac66a18.sentence: When MFA applications are configured to send push notifications to end users, an attacker can send a flood of login attempts in the hope that a user will click on accept at least once.

2e00ee4c546c.title: Multi-factor authentication
2e00ee4c546c.sentence: An increasingly common approach to defeating MFA is to bombard the user with many requests to accept a log-in, until the user eventually succumbs to the volume of requests and by mistake accepts one.

4e4aeaa76ab8.title: Multi-factor authentication
4e4aeaa76ab8.sentence: Where they could not yet do so, it recommended turning on number matching as an interim mitigation against fatigue attacks.

1a7f48cddf2a.title: Multi-factor authentication
1a7f48cddf2a.sentence: In October 2022 the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) advised organizations using push-notification MFA to move to phishing-resistant MFA.

48d6b896d6c5.title: Multi-factor authentication
48d6b896d6c5.sentence: Any auth token given prior to MFA should not have permission to access sensitive resources.

e1fd7152e9bd.title: Multi-factor authentication

c56ff865c3f3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso

6b3f272fb271.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
