87895c91802d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
87895c91802d.sentence: The identity provider can directly authenticate the user by validating a username and password or by validating an assertion about the user's identity as presented by a separate identity provider.

d2adbb1a05be.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
d2adbb1a05be.sentence: The identity provider handles the management of user identities in order to free the service provider from this responsibility.

84295889d3d7.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
84295889d3d7.sentence: They rely on identity providers to assert the identity of a user, and typically certain attributes about the user are managed by the identity provider.

f89923849f36.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
f89923849f36.sentence: A service provider provides services to the end-user.

16df5a28cd68.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
16df5a28cd68.sentence: Service providers may also maintain a local account for the user along with attributes that are unique to their service.

128170553bdc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
128170553bdc.sentence: An identity broker acts as an intermediary that connects multiple service providers with various different identity providers.

d961e9bd1619.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
d961e9bd1619.sentence: Using Identity Broker, we can perform single sign-on over any application without the hassle of the protocol it follows.

e01ef4a1d281.title: Single sign-on
e01ef4a1d281.sentence: Single sign-on (SSO) is an authentication scheme that allows a user to log in with a single ID to any of several related, yet independent, software systems.

288d8b4a268f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
288d8b4a268f.sentence: Single Sign-On (SSO) is an authentication process in which a user is provided access to multiple applications or websites by using only a single set of login credentials.

a33913ca5137.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
a33913ca5137.sentence: This prevents the need for the user to log separately into the different applications.

8b80446b1018.title: Single sign-on
8b80446b1018.sentence: True single sign-on allows the user to log in once and access services without re-entering authentication factors.

5758c0c2f614.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
5758c0c2f614.sentence: The user credentials and other identifying information are stored and managed by a centralized system called Identity Provider (IdP).

f4827a7e3e13.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
f4827a7e3e13.sentence: The Identity Provider is a trusted system that provides access to other websites and applications.

70f36fadfdc5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
70f36fadfdc5.sentence: - The user requests a resource from their desired application.

b47b0ed324d0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
b47b0ed324d0.sentence: - The application redirects the user to the Identity Provider (IdP) for authentication.

e9d92f34f51b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
e9d92f34f51b.sentence: - The user signs in with their credentials (usually, username and password).

7977cf4bc795.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
7977cf4bc795.sentence: - Identity Provider (IdP) sends a Single Sign-On response back to the client application.

97919d147dfa.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
97919d147dfa.sentence: - The application grants access to the user.

b7b36114ba68.title: Single sign-on
b7b36114ba68.sentence: For clarity, a distinction is made between Directory Server Authentication (same-sign on) and single sign-on: Directory Server Authentication refers to systems requiring authentication for each application but using the same credentials from a directory server, whereas single sign-on refers to systems where a single authentication provides access to multiple applications by passing the authentication token seamlessly to configured applications.

e8de0bc0385b.title: Single sign-on
e8de0bc0385b.sentence: It should not be confused with same sign-on (Directory Server Authentication), often accomplished by using the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) and stored LDAP databases on (directory) servers.

1ce089762edc.title: Single sign-on
1ce089762edc.sentence: As different applications and resources support different authentication mechanisms, single sign-on must internally store the credentials used for initial authentication and translate them to the credentials required for the different mechanisms.

1479bad30f49.title: Single sign-on
1479bad30f49.sentence: Conversely, single sign-off or single log-out (SLO) is the property whereby a single action of signing out terminates access to multiple software systems.

7e502ea3be69.title: Single sign-on
7e502ea3be69.sentence: Other shared authentication schemes, such as OpenID and OpenID Connect, offer other services that may require users to make choices during a sign-on to a resource, but can be configured for single sign-on if those other services (such as user consent) are disabled.

fdba8b6c5d16.title: Single sign-on
fdba8b6c5d16.sentence: An increasing number of federated social logons, like Facebook Connect, do require the user to enter consent choices upon first registration with a new resource, and so are not always single sign-on in the strictest sense.

2ea551623047.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
2ea551623047.sentence: - Ease of use as users only need to remember one set of credentials.

2ca7f8da54d4.title: Single sign-on
2ca7f8da54d4.sentence: - Reduce password fatigue from different username and password combinations

bdd9e88ca538.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
bdd9e88ca538.sentence: - Enforced security and compliance to protect sensitive data.

43f497a1f4bb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
43f497a1f4bb.sentence: - Simplifying the management with reduced IT support cost and admin time.

218000babb37.title: Single sign-on
218000babb37.sentence: - Reduce IT costs due to lower number of IT help desk calls about passwords

ed48b4673633.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
ed48b4673633.sentence: Single Sign-On (SSO) based authentication systems are commonly used in enterprise environments where employees require access to multiple applications of their organizations.

87bdd693cc7f.title: Single sign-on
87bdd693cc7f.sentence: SSO shares centralized authentication servers that all other applications and systems use for authentication purposes and combines this with techniques to ensure that users do not have to actively enter their credentials more than once.

b6cc663f476b.title: Single sign-on
b6cc663f476b.sentence: A simple version of single sign-on can be achieved over IP networks using cookies but only if the sites share a common DNS parent domain.

2d1b417a061a.title: Kerberos (protocol)
2d1b417a061a.sentence: Kerberos (/ˈkɜːr.bər.ɒs/) is a computer-network authentication protocol that works on the basis of tickets to allow nodes communicating over a non-secure network to prove their identity to one another in a secure manner.

d93b705efb42.title: Kerberos (protocol)
d93b705efb42.sentence: Its designers aimed it primarily at a client–server model, and it provides mutual authentication—both the user and the server verify each other's identity.

36a1dd4748c9.title: Kerberos (protocol)
36a1dd4748c9.sentence: Kerberos protocol messages are protected against eavesdropping and replay attacks.

672281a68643.title: Kerberos (protocol)
672281a68643.sentence: Kerberos builds on symmetric-key cryptography and requires a trusted third party, and optionally may use public-key cryptography during certain phases of authentication.

c481746929ff.title: Kerberos (protocol)
c481746929ff.sentence: The client authenticates itself to the Authentication Server (AS) which is part of the key distribution center (KDC).

12a5fe9b2c09.title: Kerberos (protocol)
12a5fe9b2c09.sentence: When the client needs to communicate with a service on another node (a "principal", in Kerberos parlance), the client sends the TGT to the TGS, which is another component of the KDC and usually shares the same host as the authentication server.

41fd17802150.title: Kerberos (protocol)
41fd17802150.sentence: The KDC issues a ticket-granting ticket (TGT), which is time stamped and encrypts it using the ticket-granting service's (TGS) secret key and returns the encrypted result to the user's workstation.

b7f70278685b.title: Kerberos (protocol)
b7f70278685b.sentence: (Note: Neither the secret key nor the password is sent to the AS.)

41729137da35.title: Kerberos (protocol)
41729137da35.section: Protocol > Description > User Login and Pre-authentication
41729137da35.sentence: This encrypted timestamp is sent to the AS along with the username as "pre-authentication" to prove the user knows the password before the AS issues any tickets, preventing offline brute-force attacks.

302900c58a9a.title: Kerberos (protocol)
302900c58a9a.sentence: After verifying that the TGT is valid and that the user is permitted to access the requested service, the TGS issues a service ticket (ST) and session keys to the client.

998295f812ab.title: Kerberos (protocol)
998295f812ab.sentence: The client then sends the ticket to the service server (SS) along with its service request.

b7dc672b98f3.title: Kerberos (protocol)
b7dc672b98f3.sentence: - The SS decrypts the ticket (message E) using its own secret key to retrieve the Client/Server Session Key.

32da03199dd5.title: Kerberos (protocol)
32da03199dd5.sentence: Using the sessions key, SS decrypts the Authenticator and compares client ID from messages E and G, if they match server sends the following message to the client to confirm its true identity and willingness to serve the client:

bad27fa065c6.title: Kerberos (protocol)
bad27fa065c6.sentence: - The client decrypts the confirmation (message H) using the Client/Server Session Key and checks whether the timestamp is correct.

4de03db720e5.title: Kerberos (protocol)
4de03db720e5.sentence: If so, then the client can trust the server and can start issuing service requests to the server.

d13dc859206b.title: Kerberos (protocol)
d13dc859206b.sentence: - Kerberos has strict time requirements, which means that the clocks of the involved hosts must be synchronized within configured limits.

0c61ffe68ae7.title: Kerberos (protocol)
0c61ffe68ae7.sentence: The tickets have a time availability period, and if the host clock is not synchronized with the Kerberos server clock, the authentication will fail.

64d13a1e108b.title: Kerberos (protocol)
64d13a1e108b.sentence: The default configuration per MIT requires that clock times be no more than five minutes apart.

2a3989e0c284.title: Kerberos (protocol)
2a3989e0c284.sentence: In practice, Network Time Protocol daemons are usually used to keep the host clocks synchronized.

4ec317c33d16.title: Kerberos (protocol)
4ec317c33d16.sentence: - In case of symmetric cryptography adoption (Kerberos can work using symmetric or asymmetric (public-key) cryptography), since all authentications are controlled by a centralized key distribution center (KDC), compromise of this authentication infrastructure will allow an attacker to impersonate any user.

8c502c36f58e.title: Kerberos (protocol)
8c502c36f58e.sentence: - Each network service that requires a different host name will need its own set of Kerberos keys.

a026429cc535.title: Kerberos (protocol)
a026429cc535.section: Support by operating systems > Microsoft Windows
a026429cc535.sentence: Windows 2000 and later versions use Kerberos as their default authentication method.

95aed4f03eef.title: Kerberos (protocol)
95aed4f03eef.section: Support by operating systems > Microsoft Windows
95aed4f03eef.sentence: Kerberos is used as the preferred authentication method: in general, joining a client to a Windows domain means enabling Kerberos as the default protocol for authentications from that client to services in the Windows domain and all domains with trust relationships to that domain.

14c3d7f7ddd6.title: Kerberos (protocol)
14c3d7f7ddd6.section: Support by operating systems > Microsoft Windows
14c3d7f7ddd6.sentence: In contrast, when either client or server or both are not joined to a domain (or not part of the same trusted domain environment), Windows will instead use NTLM for authentication between client and server.

cdf71aeadd4f.title: OpenID
cdf71aeadd4f.sentence: OpenID is an open standard and decentralized authentication protocol promoted by the non-profit OpenID Foundation.

acd934112e07.title: OpenID
acd934112e07.sentence: OpenID is a decentralized authentication protocol that allows users to authenticate with multiple websites using a single set of credentials, eliminating the need for separate usernames and passwords for each website.

44d44296f290.title: OpenID
44d44296f290.sentence: It allows users to be authenticated by co-operating sites (known as relying parties, or RP) using a third-party identity provider (IdP) service, eliminating the need for webmasters to provide their own ad hoc login systems, and allowing users to log in to multiple unrelated websites without having to have a separate identity and password for each.

d6cd8bca6b95.title: OpenID
d6cd8bca6b95.sentence: Users create accounts by selecting an OpenID identity provider, and then use those accounts to sign on to any website that accepts OpenID authentication.

dfbd010611e3.title: OpenID
dfbd010611e3.sentence: OpenID authenticates a user with an identity provider (IdP), who then provides the user with a unique identifier (called an OpenID).

ac676bfcda89.title: OpenID
ac676bfcda89.sentence: This identifier can then be used to authenticate the user with any website that supports OpenID.

b05a6c996e0d.title: OpenID
b05a6c996e0d.sentence: When a user visits a website that supports OpenID authentication, the website will redirect the user to their chosen IdP.

a451d0a636c7.title: OpenID
a451d0a636c7.sentence: The IdP will then prompt the user to authenticate themselves (e.g., by entering a username and password).

648d4a7a4734.title: OpenID
648d4a7a4734.sentence: Once they have registered an OpenID, a user can also use an existing URL under their own control (such as a blog or home page) as an alias or "delegated identity".

f41e99a70c8b.title: OpenID
f41e99a70c8b.sentence: An extension to the standard (the OpenID Attribute Exchange) facilitates the transfer of user attributes, such as name and gender, from the OpenID identity provider to the relying party (each relying party may request a different set of attributes, depending on its requirements).

6280e83ec649.title: OpenID
6280e83ec649.sentence: For example, a malicious relaying party may forward the end user to a bogus identity provider authentication page asking that end user to input their credentials.

12fdc4b791c6.title: OpenID
12fdc4b791c6.sentence: On completion of this, the malicious party (who in this case also controls the bogus authentication page) could then have access to the end user's account with the identity provider, and then use that end user's OpenID to log into other services.

8b5207c5fb5f.title: OpenID
8b5207c5fb5f.sentence: The Identity Provider does, however, get a log of your OpenID logins; they know when you logged into what website, making cross-site tracking much easier.

4ef957cef911.title: Single sign-on
4ef957cef911.sentence: As single sign-on provides access to many resources once the user is initially authenticated ("keys to the castle"), it increases the negative impact in case the credentials are available to other people and misused.

ce5e6a33159a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
ce5e6a33159a.sentence: - Single Password Vulnerability, if the main SSO password gets compromised, all the supported applications get compromised.

42118a0d9243.title: Single sign-on
42118a0d9243.sentence: Therefore, single sign-on requires an increased focus on the protection of the user credentials, and should ideally be combined with strong authentication methods like smart cards and one-time password tokens.

f3f28cc021b0.title: Single sign-on
f3f28cc021b0.sentence: Single sign-on also increases dependence on highly-available authentication systems; a loss of their availability can result in denial of access to all systems unified under the SSO.

3cc1ab743ab4.title: Single sign-on
3cc1ab743ab4.sentence: SSO can be configured with session failover capabilities in order to maintain the system operation.

628006a88c63.title: Single sign-on
628006a88c63.sentence: Nonetheless, the risk of system failure may make single sign-on undesirable for systems to which access must be guaranteed at all times, such as security or plant-floor systems.

bedd39286b3b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
bedd39286b3b.sentence: - The authentication process using Single Sign-On is slower than traditional authentication as every application has to request the SSO provider for verification.

dffe0c4eea6b.title: Single sign-on
dffe0c4eea6b.sentence: The term reduced sign-on (RSO) has been used by some to reflect the fact that single sign-on is impractical in addressing the need for different levels of secure access in the enterprise, and as such more than one authentication server may be necessary.

727ea9f2f071.title: Single sign-on
727ea9f2f071.sentence: Due to how single sign-on works, by sending a request to the logged-in website to get a SSO token and sending a request with the token to the logged-out website, the token cannot be protected with the HttpOnly cookie flag and thus can be stolen by an attacker if there is an XSS vulnerability on the logged-out website, in order to do session hijacking.

08ca845cc61a.title: Single sign-on
08ca845cc61a.sentence: Another security issue is that if the session used for SSO is stolen (which can be protected with the HttpOnly cookie flag unlike the SSO token), the attacker can access all the websites that are using the SSO system.

4074beab023a.title: Single sign-on
4074beab023a.sentence: As originally implemented in Kerberos and SAML, single sign-on did not give users any choices about releasing their personal information to each new resource that the user visited.

6c8ca2811349.title: Single sign-on
6c8ca2811349.sentence: However, as federated services like Active Directory Federation Services proliferated, the user's private information was sent out to affiliated sites not under control of the enterprise that collected the data from the user.

c232f5bb1cfe.title: Single sign-on
c232f5bb1cfe.sentence: Since privacy regulations are now tightening with legislation like the GDPR, the newer methods like OpenID Connect have started to become more attractive; for example MIT, the originator of Kerberos, now supports OpenID Connect.

0af5e01d7838.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
0af5e01d7838.sentence: Security Assertion Markup Language is an open standard that allows clients to share security information about identity, authentication, and permission across different systems.

06893453531e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
06893453531e.sentence: SAML is implemented with the Extensible Markup Language (XML) standard for sharing data.

916ac1c455bb.title: Single sign-on

916ac1c455bb.sentence: Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) is an XML-based method for exchanging user security information between an SAML identity provider and a SAML service provider.

33207450f434.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso
33207450f434.sentence: SAML specifically enables identity federation, making it possible for identity providers (IdPs) to seamlessly and securely pass authenticated identities and their attributes to service providers.

db8119119d82.title: Single sign-on

db8119119d82.sentence: The user requests a web resource protected by a SAML service provider.

57f9ab42c139.sentence: The service provider, wishing to know the identity of the user, issues an authentication request to a SAML identity provider through the user agent.

35fdf59d2572.title: Single sign-on
35fdf59d2572.section: Common configurations > Security Assertion Markup Language
35fdf59d2572.sentence: The service provider trusts the user information from the identity provider to provide access to its services or resources.

7384820c767f.sentence: SAML uses XML to pass messages, while OAuth and OIDC use JSON.

d60147361214.sentence: OAuth provides a simpler experience, while SAML is geared towards enterprise security.

bc3a5c9bfdaf.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso

bc3a5c9bfdaf.sentence: SAML can be complex to install and maintain, which only enterprise-size companies can handle well.

35ae37268a2e.sentence: OAuth and OIDC use RESTful communication extensively, which is why mobile, and modern web applications find OAuth and OIDC a better experience for the user.

b81b5cd13361.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso

b81b5cd13361.sentence: SAML, on the other hand, drops a session cookie in a browser that allows a user to access certain web pages.

5a2d29036003.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::single-sign-on-sso

5a2d29036003.sentence: This is great for short-lived workloads.

b107db8b151f.title: Single sign-on

ba909aec01d4.title: Single sign-on

e176d6758199.title: Single sign-on

149be67e0a76.title: Single sign-on

6153f6ec7d3f.title: Single sign-on

446db34841c6.section: Emerging configurations > Mobile devices as access credentials
446db34841c6.sentence: A newer variation of single-sign-on authentication has been developed using mobile devices as access credentials.

6d3b6576dc54.title: Single sign-on
6d3b6576dc54.section: Emerging configurations > Mobile devices as access credentials
6d3b6576dc54.sentence: Users' mobile devices can be used to automatically log them onto multiple systems, such as building-access-control systems and computer systems, through the use of authentication methods which include OpenID Connect and SAML, in conjunction with an X.509 ITU-T cryptography certificate used to identify the mobile device to an access server.

38b102f742bb.title: Single sign-on
38b102f742bb.section: Emerging configurations > Mobile devices as access credentials

4f4b59d7fb27.title: URL shortening

87d519a1c4ce.title: URL shortening
87d519a1c4ce.sentence: Every access requires more requests (at least one more DNS lookup, though it may be cached, and one more HTTP/HTTPS request), thereby increasing latency, the time taken to access the page, and also the risk of failure, since the shortening service may become unavailable.

702251541def.title: URL shortening

0df9a0b85be9.title: URL shortening

ab892c8877c5.title: URL shortening
ab892c8877c5.sentence: There are security implications, and obsolete short URLs remain in existence and may be circulated long after they cease to point to a relevant or even extant destination.

3d668878c2bb.title: URL shortening
3d668878c2bb.sentence: Sometimes a short URL is useful simply to give someone over a telephone conversation for a one-off access or file download, and no longer needed within a couple of minutes.

0d0ea0ead6e4.title: URL shortening

879a3988c4d2.title: URL shortening

e530d6573126.sentence: This will be a read-heavy system, so let's assume a 100:1 read/write ratio with 100 million links generated per month.

8142b76d985e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener

c72e0388e99e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener
c72e0388e99e.sentence: For caching, we will follow the classic Pareto principle also known as the 80/20 rule.

9349b4635173.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener
9349b4635173.sentence: This means that 80% of the requests are for 20% of the data, so we can cache around 20% of our requests.

0f595dc41d28.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener
0f595dc41d28.sentence: Since we get around 4K read or redirection requests each second, this translates into 350M requests per day.

3856d58519f3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener
3856d58519f3.sentence: Hence, we will need around 35GB of memory per day.

ba8f8fd7b009.sentence: Since the data is not strongly relational, NoSQL databases such as Amazon DynamoDB, Apache Cassandra, or MongoDB will be a better choice here, if we do decide to use an SQL database then we can use something like Azure SQL Database or Amazon RDS.

a831d13338aa.sentence: The MD5 message-digest algorithm is a widely used hash function producing a 128-bit hash value (or 32 hexadecimal digits).

50658e333f1c.sentence: We can try to re-compute the hash until we find a unique one but that will increase the overhead of our systems.

5529c526c2c9.sentence: In this approach, we will start with a single server which will maintain the count of the keys generated.

7ce817e1a377.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener
7ce817e1a377.sentence: The problem with this approach is that it can quickly become a single point for failure.

790c4c0f4b4f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener
790c4c0f4b4f.sentence: And if we run multiple instances of the counter we can have collision as it's essentially a distributed system.

c54292526a34.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener

77663ee66f5e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener

0da54b3874a5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener
0da54b3874a5.sentence: This approach can guarantee non-duplicate and collision-resistant URLs.

27029c21be8b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener

4d9867eff8d4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener

74ee82389b9f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::url-shortener

026ce17e3f9c.title: Pastebin

e8145c047e2d.title: Pastebin

1a39e1e26f41.title: Instant messaging
1a39e1e26f41.sentence: Instant messaging (IM) technology is a type of synchronous computer-mediated communication involving the immediate (real-time) transmission of messages between two or more parties over the Internet or another computer network.

ad53655f2276.title: Instant messaging
ad53655f2276.sentence: Instant messaging (IM), sometimes also called "messaging" or "texting", consists of computer-based human communication between two users (private messaging) or more (chat room or "group") in real-time, allowing immediate receipt of acknowledgment or reply.

18b8d6dcf655.title: Instant messaging
18b8d6dcf655.sentence: This is in direct contrast to email, where conversations are not in real-time, and the perceived quasi-synchrony of the communications by the users (although many systems allow users to send offline messages that the other user receives when logging in).

12f84ccb653a.title: Instant messaging
12f84ccb653a.sentence: Originally involving simple text message exchanges, modern instant messaging applications and services (also variously known as instant messenger, messaging app, chat app, chat client, or simply a messenger) tend to also feature the exchange of multimedia, emojis, file transfer, VoIP (voice calling), and video chat capabilities.

5611001653e1.title: Instant messaging
5611001653e1.sentence: Instant messaging systems facilitate connections between specified known users (often using a contact list also known as a "buddy list" or "friend list") or in chat rooms, and can be standalone apps or integrated into a wider social media platform, or in a website where it can, for instance, be used for conversational commerce.

a1f80e77f84d.title: Instant messaging
a1f80e77f84d.sentence: Modern IM services generally provide their own client, either a separately installed application or a browser-based client.

323e82d6e280.title: Instant messaging
323e82d6e280.sentence: They are normally centralised networks run by the servers of the platform's operators, unlike peer-to-peer protocols like XMPP.

8335921a62d8.title: Instant messaging
8335921a62d8.sentence: Most IM protocols are proprietary and are not designed to be interoperable with others, meaning that many IM networks have been incompatible and users have been unable to reach users on other networks.

3a835e276c78.title: Instant messaging
3a835e276c78.sentence: IM networks may store messages with either local-based device storage (e.g. WhatsApp, Viber, Line, WeChat, Signal etc. software) or cloud-based server storage provided by the service (e.g. Telegram, Skype, Facebook Messenger, Google Meet/Chat, Discord, Slack etc.).

4ea9a16a4ce8.title: Instant messaging
4ea9a16a4ce8.sentence: Although cloud-based storage is advertised to offer encrypted messages, it poses an increased risk that the IM provider may have access to the decryption keys and view the user's saved messages.

d85553ab14b3.title: Instant messaging
d85553ab14b3.sentence: Encryption is the primary method that instant messaging apps use to protect user's data privacy and security.

c7850c46c5e2.title: Instant messaging
c7850c46c5e2.section: Overview > Features > Private and group messaging
c7850c46c5e2.sentence: Privacy can also be enhanced in several ways, such as end-to-end encryption by default.

641317199be8.title: End-to-end encryption
641317199be8.sentence: End-to-end encryption (E2EE) is a method of implementing a secure communication system where only the sender and intended recipients can read the messages.

97a0bb4bd6ab.title: End-to-end encryption
97a0bb4bd6ab.sentence: In an E2EE-enabled service, messages are encrypted on the sender's device such that no third party, including the service provider, has the means to decrypt them.

19494d951077.title: End-to-end encryption
19494d951077.sentence: The recipients retrieve encrypted messages and decrypt them independently on their own devices.

3c115aa85acb.title: End-to-end encryption
3c115aa85acb.sentence: Under E2EE, messages are encrypted on the sender's device such that they can be decoded only by the final recipient's device.

e95d96d3957f.title: End-to-end encryption
e95d96d3957f.sentence: No one else, including the system provider, telecom providers, Internet providers or malicious actors, can access the cryptographic keys needed to read or send messages.

2109e482d177.title: End-to-end encryption
2109e482d177.sentence: End-to-end encryption prevents data from being read or secretly modified, except by the sender and intended recipients.

2adc506d749e.title: End-to-end encryption
2adc506d749e.sentence: In many non-E2EE messaging systems, including email and many chat platforms, messages pass through intermediaries and are stored by a third-party service provider, from which they are retrieved by the recipient.

98d079e1462f.title: End-to-end encryption
98d079e1462f.sentence: Even if messages are encrypted, they are only encrypted 'in transit', and are thus accessible by the service provider.

5cac09a737ba.title: End-to-end encryption
5cac09a737ba.sentence: Server-side disk encryption is also distinct from E2EE because it does not prevent the service provider from viewing the information, as they have the encryption keys and can simply decrypt it.

da62a88bb72d.title: End-to-end encryption
da62a88bb72d.sentence: Later, around 2014, the meaning of "end-to-end encryption" started to evolve when WhatsApp encrypted a portion of its network, requiring that not only the communication stays encrypted during transport, but also that the provider of the communication service is not able to decrypt the communications—maliciously or when requested by law enforcement agencies.

2d4b9ef09259.title: End-to-end encryption
2d4b9ef09259.sentence: Similarly, messages must be undecryptable in transit by attackers through man-in-the-middle attacks.

888bb2e2019a.title: End-to-end encryption
888bb2e2019a.sentence: This new meaning is now the widely accepted one.

fdcb010138a0.title: End-to-end encryption
fdcb010138a0.sentence: Since third parties cannot decrypt the data being communicated or stored, services with E2EE are better at protecting user data from data breaches and espionage.

d0fe6858fea0.title: End-to-end encryption
d0fe6858fea0.sentence: E2EE alone does not guarantee privacy or security.

b983ec4158f6.title: End-to-end encryption
b983ec4158f6.sentence: For example, the data may be held unencrypted on the user's own device or accessed through their own app if their credentials are compromised.

15166360c7ef.title: End-to-end encryption
15166360c7ef.sentence: Each user's computer can still be hacked to steal their cryptographic key (to create a MITM attack) or simply read the recipients' decrypted messages both in real time and from log files.

03deca433037.title: End-to-end encryption
03deca433037.sentence: A backdoor is usually a secret method of bypassing normal authentication or encryption in a computer system, a product, an embedded device, etc.

ec8ad1d715e8.title: End-to-end encryption
ec8ad1d715e8.sentence: Companies may also willingly or unwillingly introduce backdoors to their software that help subvert key negotiation or bypass encryption altogether.

6a7907c27693.title: Store and forward
6a7907c27693.sentence: Store and forward is a telecommunications technique in which a digital data stream is sent to an intermediate station where it is kept in digital storage and sent at a later time to the final destination or to another intermediate station.

c085000bd44e.title: Store and forward
c085000bd44e.sentence: The intermediate station, or node in a networking context, verifies the integrity of the message before forwarding it.

9c5dd7ec6932.title: Store and forward
9c5dd7ec6932.sentence: In general, this technique is used in networks with intermittent connectivity, especially in the wilderness or environments requiring high mobility.

424eee8862c9.title: Store and forward
424eee8862c9.sentence: It may also be preferable in situations when there are long delays in transmission and error rates are variable and high, or if a direct, end-to-end connection is not available.

b01e2942a70f.title: Store and forward
b01e2942a70f.sentence: A store-and-forward switching center is a message switching center in which a message is accepted from the originating user, i.e., sender, when it is offered, held in a physical storage, and forwarded to the destination user, i.e., receiver, in accordance with the priority placed upon the message by the originating user and the availability of an outgoing channel.

6856ef21f343.title: Store and forward
6856ef21f343.sentence: If the destination address isn't available, then the center stores this message and tries sending it later.

f0cf6ed59857.title: Store and forward
f0cf6ed59857.sentence: This improves the probability of the message being delivered.

f488ba0f337c.title: Store and forward

1b50fbf27868.title: Store and forward

b834fca560b9.title: Store and forward
b834fca560b9.sentence: SMS messages are first sent to a Short Message service center where they are stored temporarily before being forwarded to the intended recipient's phone, even if they are not currently reachable, allowing for delivery later when they come back online.

d26dacf1dcd6.title: Store and forward

5f1f8bca9fa6.title: Signal Protocol
5f1f8bca9fa6.sentence: The Signal Protocol (formerly known as the TextSecure Protocol) is a non-federated cryptographic protocol that provides end-to-end encryption for voice and instant messaging conversations.

e9cd5eca670d.title: Signal Protocol
e9cd5eca670d.sentence: The protocol combines the Double Ratchet Algorithm, prekeys (i.e., one-time ephemeral public keys that have been uploaded in advance to a central server), and key agreement protocols including the original triple elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman (3-DH) handshake and the post-quantum PQXDH protocol.

4d248fae13f5.title: Signal Protocol
4d248fae13f5.sentence: The design of the Axolotl Ratchet is based on the ephemeral key exchange that was introduced by OTR and combines it with a symmetric-key ratchet modeled after the Silent Circle Instant Message Protocol (SCIMP).

11d686e63f0b.title: Signal Protocol
11d686e63f0b.sentence: It brought about support for asynchronous communication ("offline messages") as its major new feature, as well as better resilience with distorted order of messages and simpler support for conversations with multiple participants.

55457a52161e.title: Signal Protocol
55457a52161e.sentence: The developers refer to the algorithm as self-healing because it automatically disables an attacker from accessing the cleartext of later messages after having compromised a session key.

3c1099962b1d.title: Signal Protocol
3c1099962b1d.sentence: The protocol provides confidentiality, integrity, authentication, participant consistency, destination validation, forward secrecy, post-compromise security (aka future secrecy), causality preservation, message unlinkability, message repudiation, participation repudiation, and asynchronicity.

7da9c10bbe23.title: Signal Protocol
7da9c10bbe23.sentence: It does not provide anonymity preservation and requires servers for the relaying of messages and storing of public key material.

928ce27def7c.title: Signal Protocol
928ce27def7c.sentence: The Signal Protocol also supports end-to-end encrypted group chats.

f5e10847bc5d.title: Signal Protocol
f5e10847bc5d.sentence: The group chat protocol is a combination of a pairwise double ratchet and multicast encryption.

f0f20997bbe3.title: Signal Protocol
f0f20997bbe3.sentence: In addition to the properties provided by the one-to-one protocol, the group chat protocol provides speaker consistency, out-of-order resilience, dropped message resilience, computational equality, trust equality, subgroup messaging, as well as contractible and expandable membership.

7f72b918ad6a.title: Signal Protocol
7f72b918ad6a.sentence: For authentication, users can manually compare public key fingerprints through an outside channel.

59855e3febbe.title: Signal Protocol
59855e3febbe.sentence: This makes it possible for users to verify each other's identities and avoid a man-in-the-middle attack.

99d6ea631a57.title: Signal Protocol

07a96f4cf63b.title: Signal Protocol

cbf1ed7b2aef.title: Signal Protocol

66c530972a09.sentence: Matrix is an open communications protocol that includes Olm, a library that provides optional end-to-end encryption on a room-by-room basis via a Double Ratchet Algorithm implementation.

3c5f8e0cd182.title: Signal Protocol
3c5f8e0cd182.sentence: Messaging Layer Security, an IETF proposal, uses Asynchronous ratcheting trees to efficiently improve upon security guarantees over Signal's Double Ratchet.

d3a80e959c55.title: End-to-end encryption
d3a80e959c55.sentence: Since end-to-end encrypted services cannot offer decrypted messages in response to government requests, the proliferation of E2EE has been met with controversy.

c153e04dfe78.title: End-to-end encryption
c153e04dfe78.sentence: Around the world, governments, law enforcement agencies and child protection groups have expressed concerns over its impact on criminal investigations.

75669291ba08.title: End-to-end encryption
75669291ba08.sentence: The lack of end-to-end encryption can allow service providers to easily provide search and other features, or to scan for illegal and unacceptable content.

d69755d4f78a.title: End-to-end encryption
d69755d4f78a.sentence: However, it also means that content can be read by anyone who has access to the data stored by the service provider, by design or via a backdoor.

f775d199b13d.title: End-to-end encryption
f775d199b13d.sentence: As of 2025, some governments have successfully passed legislation targeting E2EE, such as Australia's Telecommunications and Other Legislation Amendment Act (2018) and the Online Safety Act (2023) in the UK.

1830d1fa32d7.title: End-to-end encryption
1830d1fa32d7.sentence: Other attempts at restricting E2EE include the EARN IT Act in the US and the Child Sexual Abuse Regulation in the EU.[1] Nevertheless, some government bodies such as the UK's Information Commissioner's Office and the US's Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) have argued for the use of E2EE, with Jeff Greene of the CISA advising that "encryption is your friend" following the discovery of the Salt Typhoon espionage campaign in 2024.

fb911422a08d.title: End-to-end encryption
fb911422a08d.sentence: For example, many organizations are subject to mandates that require them to be able to decrypt any communication between their employees or between their employees and third parties.

d4799e9df3e6.title: End-to-end encryption
d4799e9df3e6.sentence: This might be needed for archival purposes, for inspection by Data Loss Prevention (DLP) systems, for litigation-related eDiscovery or for detection of malware and other threats in the data streams.

556e12c4e4b9.title: End-to-end encryption

b44c3d158f84.title: WhatsApp
b44c3d158f84.sentence: WhatsApp uses a "store and forward" mechanism for exchanging messages between two users.

52077a51e904.title: WhatsApp
52077a51e904.sentence: When a user sends a message, it is stored on a WhatsApp server, which tries to forward it to the addressee, and repeatedly requests acknowledgement of receipt.

aa5ee80689fa.title: WhatsApp
aa5ee80689fa.sentence: When the message is acknowledged, the server deletes it; if undelivered after 30 days, it is also deleted.

17153dadebbf.title: WhatsApp
17153dadebbf.sentence: Multimedia messages are sent by uploading the image, audio or video to be sent to an HTTP server and then sending a link to the content along with its Base64 encoded thumbnail, if applicable.

ff17e68e0e59.title: WhatsApp
ff17e68e0e59.sentence: WhatsApp uses a customized version of the open standard Extensible messaging and presence protocol (XMPP).

90725577ae5b.title: WhatsApp
90725577ae5b.sentence: A 2019 document released by the DOJ confirms this by naming "FunXMPP" as the protocol used by WhatsApp.

70ca21e7dc8b.title: WhatsApp
70ca21e7dc8b.sentence: Upon installation, it creates a user account using the user's phone number as the username (Jabber ID: [phone number]@s.whatsapp.net).

d992eccb517d.title: WhatsApp
d992eccb517d.sentence: WhatsApp automatically compares all the phone numbers from the device's address book with its central database of WhatsApp users to automatically add contacts to the user's WhatsApp contact list.

05f1162ae4c8.title: WhatsApp

36ee6cdb1bcd.title: WhatsApp
36ee6cdb1bcd.sentence: On April 5, 2016, WhatsApp and Open Whisper Systems announced that they had finished adding end-to-end encryption to "every form of communication" on WhatsApp, and that users could now verify each other's keys.

53258b9dcb73.title: WhatsApp
53258b9dcb73.sentence: WhatsApp calls are encrypted with SRTP, and all client-server communications are "layered within a separate encrypted channel".

c0bafb618972.title: WhatsApp

ff42897545de.title: WhatsApp

5cb36352f3a3.title: WhatsApp

ddd925ffd5cc.sentence: Apache Lucene is a free and open-source search engine software library, originally written in Java by Doug Cutting.

8263b3465007.title: Apache Lucene
8263b3465007.sentence: While suitable for any application that requires full text indexing and searching capability, Lucene is recognized for its utility in the implementation of Internet search engines and local, single-site searching.

8c8a1f61ac7d.title: Apache Lucene
8c8a1f61ac7d.sentence: Lucene is widely used as a standard foundation for production search applications.

8b78aa5ea6fa.title: Apache Lucene
8b78aa5ea6fa.sentence: Lucene itself is just an indexing and search library and does not contain crawling and HTML parsing functionality.

405ab7e774ad.title: Apache Lucene
405ab7e774ad.sentence: However, several projects extend Lucene's capability:

de4314c4d267.title: Apache Lucene
de4314c4d267.sentence: - Apache Nutch – provides web crawling and HTML parsing

4d6cf195c1d7.title: Apache Lucene
4d6cf195c1d7.sentence: Lucene includes a feature to perform a fuzzy search based on edit distance.

5a050ba82a79.title: Apache Lucene
5a050ba82a79.sentence: Lucene has also been used to implement recommendation systems.

2e3e9f6dc744.title: Apache Lucene
2e3e9f6dc744.sentence: For example, Lucene's 'MoreLikeThis' Class can generate recommendations for similar documents.

ffb43fdbe6c4.title: Apache Lucene
ffb43fdbe6c4.sentence: - Apache Solr – an enterprise search server

281878868f43.title: Apache Lucene
281878868f43.sentence: - Elasticsearch – an enterprise search server released in 2010

48f0ac058648.title: Apache Lucene
48f0ac058648.sentence: - OpenSearch – an open source enterprise search server based on a fork of Elasticsearch 7

9139460b586a.title: Apache Lucene
9139460b586a.sentence: - CrateDB – open source, distributed SQL database built on Lucene

ca9838b78a34.title: Apache Lucene

d9c004acf12d.title: Fan-out (software)
d9c004acf12d.sentence: In message-oriented middleware solutions, fan-out is a messaging pattern used to model an information exchange that implies the delivery (or spreading) of a message to one or multiple destinations possibly in parallel, and not halting the process that executes the messaging to wait for any response to that message.

564ab03a6b54.title: Message-oriented middleware
564ab03a6b54.sentence: AMQP may be used with flexible routing schemes, including common messaging paradigms like point-to-point, fan-out, publish/subscribe, and request-response (these are intentionally omitted from v1.0 of the protocol standard itself, but rely on the particular implementation and/or underlying network protocol for routing).

3b88f995cd4b.title: doc>sre.google/sre-book/load-balancing-datacenter
3b88f995cd4b.sentence: Sometimes the stack of dependencies can get relatively deep, where a single incoming HTTP request can trigger a long transitive chain of dependent requests to several systems, potentially with high fan-out at various points.

28980f828361.sentence: This prevents the system from having to go through a user's entire followers list to check for updates.

947846c1b9db.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
947846c1b9db.sentence: However, the downside of this approach is that it would increase the number of write operations on the database.

18903ee4b38c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
18903ee4b38c.sentence: The most recent feed is only loaded when the user requests it.

af737985d967.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
af737985d967.sentence: This approach reduces the number of write operations on our database.

b8e959c8c622.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
b8e959c8c622.sentence: The downside of this approach is that the users will not be able to view recent feeds unless they "pull" the data from the server, which will increase the number of read operations on the server.

577349c9f0ad.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
577349c9f0ad.sentence: As we discussed, we will need a ranking algorithm to rank each tweet according to its relevance to each specific user.

aa1eba396c58.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
aa1eba396c58.sentence: - Use a ranking algorithm to rank the tweets based on parameters such as relevance, time, engagement, etc.

0f5ae117a738.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
0f5ae117a738.sentence: For example, Facebook used to utilize an EdgeRank algorithm.

bc03ef20352c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
bc03ef20352c.sentence: Here, the rank of each feed item is described by:

1e48ee591c52.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
1e48ee591c52.sentence: Affinity: is the "closeness" of the user to the creator of the edge.

9a4885f67994.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
9a4885f67994.sentence: If a user frequently likes, comments, or messages the edge creator, then the value of affinity will be higher, resulting in a higher rank for the post.

37a4785bb02d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
37a4785bb02d.sentence: Weight: is the value assigned according to each edge.

e05d743d735e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
e05d743d735e.sentence: A comment can have a higher weightage than likes, and thus a post with more comments is more likely to get a higher rank.

c9920bf23861.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
c9920bf23861.sentence: Decay: is the measure of the creation of the edge.

4670a3fe32ce.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
4670a3fe32ce.sentence: The older the edge, the lesser will be the value of decay and eventually the rank.

2055265aff30.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::twitter
2055265aff30.sentence: Nowadays, algorithms are much more complex and ranking is done using machine learning models which can take thousands of factors into consideration.

020f5f8a0dc6.title: EdgeRank
020f5f8a0dc6.sentence: EdgeRank is the name commonly given to the algorithm that Facebook uses to determine what articles should be displayed in a user's News Feed.

96c748d439ce.title: EdgeRank
96c748d439ce.sentence: In 2010, a simplified version of the EdgeRank algorithm was presented as:

a462bc0c7ac4.title: EdgeRank
a462bc0c7ac4.sentence: - User Affinity: The User Affinity part of the algorithm in Facebook's EdgeRank looks at the relationship and proximity of the user and the content (post/status update).

84c5b9c12c12.title: EdgeRank
84c5b9c12c12.sentence: - Content Weight: What action was taken by the user on the content.

fe9bd1d0668c.title: EdgeRank
fe9bd1d0668c.sentence: - Time-Based Decay Parameter: New or old.

ec589ae067dd.title: EdgeRank
ec589ae067dd.sentence: Newer posts tend to hold a higher place than older posts.

2197f65a5ac2.title: EdgeRank
2197f65a5ac2.sentence: Some of the methods that Facebook uses to adjust the parameters are proprietary and not available to the public.

654409924ccf.title: EdgeRank
654409924ccf.sentence: As of 2011, Facebook has stopped using the EdgeRank system and uses a machine learning algorithm that, as of 2013, takes more than 100,000 factors into account.

02a53df75358.title: EdgeRank
02a53df75358.sentence: EdgeRank and its successors have a broad impact on what users actually see out of what they ostensibly follow: for instance, the selection can produce a filter bubble (if users are exposed to updates which confirm their opinions etc.) or alter people's mood (if users are shown a disproportionate amount of positive or negative updates).

23566f81bd24.title: Streaming media
23566f81bd24.sentence: Streaming media is the method by which multimedia data is delivered through a network for playback using a digital media player or media player software.

cb8fc151fa55.title: Streaming media
cb8fc151fa55.sentence: Media is transferred in a stream of packets from a server to a client and is rendered in real-time or near real-time; this contrasts with file downloading, a process in which the end-user obtains an entire media file before consuming the content.

b15f2e5e83cb.title: Streaming media
b15f2e5e83cb.sentence: Live streaming is the real-time delivery of content during production, much as live television broadcasts content via linear and cable channels.

9d384f70deb7.title: Streaming media
9d384f70deb7.sentence: Video and audio streams are compressed to make the file size smaller.

976dd3022d73.title: Streaming media
976dd3022d73.sentence: Video coding formats include H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9 and AV1.

c4f9c47fb6d4.title: Streaming media
c4f9c47fb6d4.sentence: Encoded audio and video streams are assembled in a container bitstream such as MP4, FLV, WebM, ASF or ISMA.

ffb472add4bb.title: Streaming media
ffb472add4bb.sentence: The bitstream is delivered from a streaming server to a streaming client (e.g., the computer user with their Internet-connected laptop) using a transport protocol, such as Adobe's RTMP or RTP.

ed4210401cdf.title: Streaming media
ed4210401cdf.sentence: In the 2010s, technologies such as Apple's HLS, Microsoft's Smooth Streaming, Adobe's HDS and non-proprietary formats such as MPEG-DASH emerged to enable adaptive bitrate streaming over HTTP as an alternative to using proprietary transport protocols.

94df22dea230.title: Streaming media
94df22dea230.sentence: A broadband speed of 2 Mbit/s or more is recommended for streaming standard-definition video, for example to a Roku, Apple TV, Google TV or a Sony TV Blu-ray Disc Player.

2d9a93690d5d.title: Streaming media
2d9a93690d5d.sentence: 5 Mbit/s is recommended for high-definition content and 25 Mbit/s for ultra-high-definition content.

8de63495c000.title: Streaming media
8de63495c000.sentence: Streaming media storage size is calculated from the streaming bandwidth and length of the media using the following formula (for a single user and file): storage size in megabytes is equal to length (in seconds) × bit rate (in bit/s) / (8 × 1024 × 1024).

611a0fa6a49c.title: Streaming media
611a0fa6a49c.sentence: For example, one hour of digital video encoded at 300 kbit/s (this was a typical broadband video in 2005 and it was usually encoded in 320 × 240 resolution) will be: (3,600 s × 300,000 bit/s) / (8 × 1024 × 1024) requires around 128 MB of storage.

df63c6a9100f.title: Streaming media
df63c6a9100f.sentence: Datagram protocols, such as the User Datagram Protocol (UDP), send the media stream as a series of small packets.

5fe6108cb259.title: Streaming media
5fe6108cb259.sentence: This is simple and efficient; however, there is no mechanism within the protocol to guarantee delivery.

14d040480609.title: Streaming media
14d040480609.sentence: It is up to the receiving application to detect loss or corruption and recover data using error correction techniques.

685e7c7a05fb.title: Streaming media
685e7c7a05fb.sentence: Reliable protocols, such as the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), guarantee correct delivery of each bit in the media stream.

b9c456fca0db.title: Streaming media
b9c456fca0db.sentence: It means, however, that when there is data loss on the network, the media stream stalls while the protocol handlers detect the loss and retransmit the missing data.

ccf6199220c2.title: Streaming media
ccf6199220c2.sentence: Clients can minimize this effect by buffering data for display.

3fb67daea6fe.title: Streaming media
3fb67daea6fe.sentence: While delay due to buffering is acceptable in video-on-demand scenarios, users of interactive applications such as video conferencing will experience a loss of fidelity if the delay caused by buffering exceeds 200 ms.

42c11d4b44ee.title: Recommender system
42c11d4b44ee.sentence: A recommender system, also called a recommendation engine or content discovery platform is a type of information filtering system that aims to suggest items most relevant for some input or to a particular user.

ba42e23cfb56.title: Streaming media
ba42e23cfb56.sentence: Most streaming services feature a recommender system for viewing based on each user's view history in conjunction with all viewers' aggregated view histories.

78f17e171754.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
78f17e171754.sentence: Netflix uses a machine learning model which uses the user's viewing history to predict what the user might like to watch next, an algorithm like Collaborative Filtering can be used.

5a16b6aef1b2.title: Recommender system
5a16b6aef1b2.sentence: The use of recommender systems is pervasive, with commonly recognised examples including the generation of playlists for video and music streaming services, product recommendations for e-commerce platforms, and topics and individual items posted on social media platforms and the open web.

b9fcd0029cdf.title: Recommender system
b9fcd0029cdf.sentence: The value of these systems becomes particularly evident in scenarios where users must select from a large number of options, such as products, media, or content.

94c3a7026ced.title: Recommender system
94c3a7026ced.sentence: Recommender systems are a useful alternative to search algorithms since they help users discover items they might not have found otherwise.

a0b649c04d82.title: Recommender system
a0b649c04d82.sentence: Collaborative filtering approaches build a model from a user's past behavior (e.g., items previously purchased or selected and/or numerical ratings given to those items) as well as similar decisions made by other users.

f675234e8b5d.title: Recommender system
f675234e8b5d.sentence: Content-based filtering approaches utilize a series of discrete, pre-tagged characteristics of an item in order to recommend additional items with similar properties.

029689f15e06.title: Recommender system
029689f15e06.sentence: Content-based filtering methods are based on a description of the item and a profile of the user's preferences.

c0031a610473.title: Recommender system
c0031a610473.sentence: In the above example, Last.fm requires a large amount of information about a user to make accurate recommendations.

1c45b5fb5161.title: Recommender system
1c45b5fb5161.sentence: This is an example of the cold start problem, and is common in collaborative filtering systems.

23d187b0886c.title: Recommender system
23d187b0886c.sentence: Whereas Pandora needs very little information to start, it is far more limited in scope (for example, it can only make recommendations that are similar to the original seed).

34270776c159.title: Recommender system
34270776c159.sentence: Collaborative filtering approaches often suffer from three problems: cold start, scalability, and sparsity.

e3ab549dc47d.title: Recommender system
e3ab549dc47d.sentence: - Cold start: For a new user or item, there is not enough data to make accurate recommendations.

1032a26d3e49.title: Recommender system
1032a26d3e49.sentence: Note: one commonly implemented solution to this problem is the multi-armed bandit algorithm.

e1895870545f.title: Recommender system
e1895870545f.sentence: Most recommender systems now use a hybrid approach, combining collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and other approaches.

e74e772cd6c3.title: Recommender system
e74e772cd6c3.sentence: - Weighted: Combining the score of different recommendation components numerically.

7b0bb3ce0912.title: Recommender system
7b0bb3ce0912.sentence: - Switching: Choosing among recommendation components and applying the selected one.

c23b83afeb3b.title: Recommender system
c23b83afeb3b.sentence: - Mixed: Recommendations from different recommenders are presented together to give the recommendation.

082a82368cc1.title: Recommender system
082a82368cc1.sentence: - Cascade: Recommenders are given strict priority, with the lower priority ones breaking ties in the scoring of the higher ones.

f2aaac09ef27.title: Recommender system
f2aaac09ef27.sentence: - Meta-level: One recommendation technique is applied and produces some sort of model, which is then the input used by the next technique.

1042f6363a9b.title: Recommender system
1042f6363a9b.sentence: Several studies that empirically compared the performance of the hybrid with the pure collaborative and content-based methods and demonstrated that the hybrid methods can provide more accurate recommendations than pure approaches.

6b808f73bc56.title: Recommender system
6b808f73bc56.sentence: These methods can also be used to overcome some of the common problems in recommender systems such as cold start and the sparsity problem, as well as the knowledge engineering bottleneck in knowledge-based approaches.

e78c88d99796.title: Streaming media
e78c88d99796.sentence: Rather than focusing on subjective categorization of content by content curators, there is an assumption that, with the immensity of data collected on viewing habits, the choices of those who are first to view content can be algorithmically extrapolated to the totality of the user base, with increasing probabilistic accuracy as to the likelihood of their choosing and enjoying the recommended content as more data is collected.

2074cd4dcde7.title: Recommender system
2074cd4dcde7.sentence: Netflix uses a hybrid recommender systems to make recommendations by comparing the watching and searching habits of similar users (i.e., collaborative filtering) as well as by offering movies that share characteristics with films that a user has rated highly (content-based filtering).
