5b4c39970747.title: Collaborative filtering
5b4c39970747.sentence: In the newer, narrower sense, collaborative filtering is a method of making automatic predictions (filtering) about a user's interests by utilizing preferences or taste information collected from many users (collaborating).

05d6e8edd708.title: Collaborative filtering
05d6e8edd708.sentence: This approach assumes that if persons A and B share similar opinions on one issue, they are more likely to agree on other issues compared to a random pairing of A with another person.

c35f49349610.title: Collaborative filtering
c35f49349610.sentence: Collaborative filtering (CF) is, besides content-based filtering, one of two major techniques used by recommender systems.

256280abcf56.title: Collaborative filtering
256280abcf56.sentence: These predictions are specific to the user, but use information gleaned from many users.

cf6da4fafa51.title: Collaborative filtering
cf6da4fafa51.sentence: This differs from the simpler approach of giving an average (non-specific) score for each item of interest, for example based on its number of votes.

c96824c33a98.title: Collaborative filtering
c96824c33a98.sentence: - Look for users who share the same rating patterns with the active user (the user whom the prediction is for).

4ac11820c607.title: Collaborative filtering
4ac11820c607.sentence: - Use the ratings from those like-minded users found in step 1 to calculate a prediction for the active user

ae504c4039aa.title: Collaborative filtering
ae504c4039aa.sentence: Alternatively, item-based collaborative filtering (users who bought x also bought y), proceeds in an item-centric manner:

1e1a571177b6.title: Collaborative filtering
1e1a571177b6.sentence: - Build an item-item matrix determining relationships between pairs of items

b18882cb20ba.title: Collaborative filtering
b18882cb20ba.sentence: - Infer the tastes of the current user by examining the matrix and matching that user's data

bab2b29ae74e.title: Collaborative filtering
bab2b29ae74e.sentence: Another form of collaborative filtering can be based on implicit observations of normal user behavior (as opposed to the artificial behavior imposed by a rating task).

a836aa839121.title: Collaborative filtering
a836aa839121.sentence: These systems observe what a user has done together with what all users have done (what music they have listened to, what items they have bought) and use that data to predict the user's behavior in the future, or to predict how a user might like to behave given the chance.

d63634410537.title: Collaborative filtering
d63634410537.sentence: The memory-based approach uses user rating data to compute the similarity between users or items.

3f5ef61e182e.title: Collaborative filtering
3f5ef61e182e.sentence: Multiple measures, such as Pearson correlation and vector cosine based similarity are used for this.

c8651ac213f7.title: Collaborative filtering
c8651ac213f7.sentence: The neighborhood-based algorithm calculates the similarity between two users or items, and produces a prediction for the user by taking the weighted average of all the ratings.

b58b70ec7d38.title: Collaborative filtering
b58b70ec7d38.sentence: An alternative to memory-based methods is to learn models to predict users' rating of unrated items.

c3b429159b10.title: Collaborative filtering
c3b429159b10.sentence: Specifically, methods like singular value decomposition, principal component analysis, known as latent factor models, compress a user-item matrix into a low-dimensional representation in terms of latent factors.

7292b1fff057.title: Collaborative filtering
7292b1fff057.sentence: This transforms the large matrix that contains many missing values, into a much smaller matrix.

bba69c3fa378.title: Collaborative filtering
bba69c3fa378.sentence: The advantages with this approach include: the explainability of the results, which is an important aspect of recommendation systems; easy creation and use; easy facilitation of new data; content-independence of the items being recommended; good scaling with co-rated items.

a4fba43c1ab0.title: Collaborative filtering
a4fba43c1ab0.sentence: Its performance decreases when data is sparse, which is common for web-related items.

5a0aae32ac16.title: Collaborative filtering
5a0aae32ac16.sentence: Adding new items requires inclusion of the new item and the re-insertion of all the elements in the structure.

6b91c19c6299.title: Collaborative filtering
6b91c19c6299.sentence: Usually most commercial recommender systems are hybrid, for example, the Google news recommender system.

60965a8bace6.title: Collaborative filtering
60965a8bace6.sentence: As in the personalized recommendation scenario, the introduction of new users or new items can cause the cold start problem, as there will be insufficient data on these new entries for the collaborative filtering to work accurately.

075d38c687a4.title: Collaborative filtering
075d38c687a4.sentence: As a result, the user-item matrix used for collaborative filtering could be extremely large and sparse, which brings about challenges in the performance of the recommendation.

a72937c67228.title: Collaborative filtering
a72937c67228.sentence: As the numbers of users and items grow, traditional CF algorithms will suffer serious scalability problems.

0d3cff162bf7.title: Collaborative filtering
0d3cff162bf7.sentence: For example, with tens of millions of customers O(M) and millions of items O(N), a CF algorithm with the complexity of n is already too large.

a65d2ce91384.title: Collaborative filtering
a65d2ce91384.sentence: In a recommendation system where everyone can give the ratings, people may give many positive ratings for their own items and negative ratings for their competitors'.

9584d19f02c6.title: Collaborative filtering
9584d19f02c6.sentence: It is often necessary for the collaborative filtering systems to introduce precautions to discourage such manipulations.

31f4b13a4e36.title: Collaborative filtering
31f4b13a4e36.section: Challenges > Diversity and the long tail
31f4b13a4e36.sentence: Because collaborative filters recommend products based on past sales or ratings, they cannot usually recommend products with limited historical data.

ad7aa88fb3a9.title: Collaborative filtering
ad7aa88fb3a9.section: Challenges > Diversity and the long tail
ad7aa88fb3a9.sentence: This can create a rich-get-richer effect for popular products, akin to positive feedback.

f61a717ef16a.title: Video codec
f61a717ef16a.sentence: A video codec is software or hardware that compresses and decompresses digital video.

ad0ab8568b74.title: Video codec
ad0ab8568b74.sentence: The compressed data format usually conforms to a standard video coding format.

182051714695.title: Video codec
182051714695.sentence: In the context of video compression, codec is a portmanteau of encoder and decoder, while a device that only compresses is typically called an encoder, and one that only decompresses is a decoder.

946e8fb097ee.title: Video codec
946e8fb097ee.sentence: In particular, they are widely used in applications that record or transmit video, which may not be feasible with the high data volumes and bandwidths of uncompressed video.

9c21b9eefb90.title: Video codec
9c21b9eefb90.sentence: Because of the large amount of storage and bandwidth needed to record and convey raw video, a method was needed to reduce the amount of data used to represent the raw video.

3be811ef1e1d.title: Video codec
3be811ef1e1d.sentence: The compression is typically lossy, meaning that the compressed video lacks some information present in the original video.

f46df322a224.title: Video codec
f46df322a224.sentence: A consequence of this is that decompressed video has lower quality than the original, uncompressed video because there is insufficient information to accurately reconstruct the original video.

0157dd3bd5e0.title: Video codec
0157dd3bd5e0.sentence: There are complex relationships between the video quality, the amount of data used to represent the video (determined by the bit rate), the complexity of the encoding and decoding algorithms, sensitivity to data losses and errors, ease of editing, random access, and end-to-end delay (latency).

031059587b62.title: Video codec
031059587b62.sentence: The conversion to YCbCr provides two benefits: first, it improves compressibility by providing decorrelation of the color signals; and second, it separates the luma signal, which is perceptually much more important, from the chroma signal, which is less perceptually important and which can be represented at lower resolution using chroma subsampling to achieve more efficient data compression.

2c9b0cdd9f84.title: Video codec
2c9b0cdd9f84.sentence: The most popular encoding transform is the 8x8 DCT.

b9729c7fe0a1.title: Video codec
b9729c7fe0a1.sentence: The output of the transform is first quantized, then entropy encoding is applied to the quantized values.

c54acc13169e.title: Video codec
c54acc13169e.sentence: The decoding process consists of performing, to the extent possible, an inversion of each stage of the encoding process.

b6cc6ffe31cf.title: Video codec
b6cc6ffe31cf.sentence: This part of the process is often called inverse quantization or dequantization, although quantization is an inherently non-invertible process.

116f655af7d2.title: Video codec
116f655af7d2.sentence: However, only the decoding process need be standardized to enable interoperability.

15a77c31bbd0.title: Video codec
15a77c31bbd0.sentence: The encoding process is typically not specified at all in a standard, and implementers are free to design their encoder however they want, as long as the video can be decoded in the specified manner.

b0b7bb483892.title: Video codec
b0b7bb483892.sentence: For this reason, the quality of the video produced by decoding the results of different encoders that use the same video codec standard can vary dramatically from one encoder implementation to another.

5735d68ae867.title: Video codec
5735d68ae867.sentence: The trade-off between compression power, speed, and fidelity (including artifacts) is usually considered the most important figure of technical merit.

0d3e9bdabde2.title: Video codec
0d3e9bdabde2.sentence: Since H.261, DCT compression has been adopted by all the major video coding standards that followed.

34094c805c16.title: Video codec
34094c805c16.sentence: The most widely used video coding format, as of 2016, is H.264/MPEG-4 AVC.

89708d7893f9.title: Video codec
89708d7893f9.sentence: AVC has been succeeded by HEVC (H.265), developed in 2013.

a641347dfe06.title: Video codec
a641347dfe06.sentence: There are also the open and free VP8, VP9 and AV1 video coding formats, used by YouTube, all of which were developed with involvement from Google.

d77003199cfb.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
d77003199cfb.sentence: More specifically, adaptive bitrate streaming is a method of video streaming over HTTP where the source content is encoded at multiple bit rates.

49fea5c972db.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
49fea5c972db.sentence: Adaptive bitrate streaming works by detecting a user's bandwidth, CPU capability, as well as device type (such as smartphone, desktop computer, or smart TV) in real time, adjusting the quality of the media stream accordingly.

d46166039c16.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
d46166039c16.sentence: The player client switches between streaming the different encodings depending on available resources.

34c370b04391.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
34c370b04391.sentence: This results in providing very little buffering, faster start times and a good experience for both high-end and low-end connections.

8178cdae85f8.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
8178cdae85f8.sentence: It requires the use of an encoder which encodes a single source media (video or audio) at multiple bit rates.

c2a91ebe7f09.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
c2a91ebe7f09.sentence: Each of the different bit rate streams are segmented into small multi-second parts.

14153142e1e2.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
14153142e1e2.sentence: First, the client downloads a manifest file that describes the available stream segments and their respective bit rates.

4072d18e810f.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
4072d18e810f.sentence: During stream start-up, the client usually requests the segments from the lowest bit rate stream.

2b6a9ee0cf72.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
2b6a9ee0cf72.sentence: If the client finds that the network throughput is greater than the bit rate of the downloaded segment, then it will request a higher bit rate segment.

f9794a2d0254.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
f9794a2d0254.sentence: Later, if the client finds that the network throughput has deteriorated, it will request a lower bit rate segment.

ebf57c199f61.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
ebf57c199f61.sentence: An adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithm in the client performs the key function of deciding which bit rate segments to download, based on the current state of the network.

861b0f4fdb9b.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
861b0f4fdb9b.sentence: Several types of ABR algorithms are in commercial use: throughput-based algorithms use the throughput achieved in recent prior downloads for decision-making (e.g., throughput rule in dash.js), buffer-based algorithms use only the client's current buffer level (e.g., BOLA in dash.js), and hybrid algorithms combine both types of information (e.g., DYNAMIC in dash.js).

5c92f126a40b.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
5c92f126a40b.sentence: While in the past most video or audio streaming technologies utilized packetized, stateful, single-bitrate streaming protocols such as RTP with RTSP, today's adaptive streaming technologies are based almost exclusively on HTTP, and are designed to work efficiently over large distributed HTTP networks.

7a34483b5c92.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
7a34483b5c92.sentence: First, since the streaming technology is built on top of HTTP, contrary to RTP-based adaptive streaming, the packets have no difficulties traversing firewalls and NAT devices.

06996dde0b30.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
06996dde0b30.sentence: Second, since HTTP streaming is purely client-driven, all adaptation logic resides at the client.

59b483c07962.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
59b483c07962.sentence: Furthermore, the server is not required to maintain session state information on each client, increasing scalability.

b0fef793bba8.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
b0fef793bba8.sentence: Finally, existing HTTP delivery infrastructure, such as HTTP caches and servers, can be seamlessly adopted.

9d4cbdc09df7.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
9d4cbdc09df7.sentence: When distributed over HTTP using content delivery networks adaptive bitrate streaming can easily be scaled to support streaming video content to millions of viewers concurrently.

3f43e459b631.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
3f43e459b631.sentence: The use of HTTP-based adaptive streaming allows the Edge server to run a simple HTTP server software, whose license cost is cheap or free, reducing software licensing cost, compared to costly media server licences (e.g., Adobe Flash Media Streaming Server).

8d27f2b9fcb1.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
8d27f2b9fcb1.sentence: Adaptive bitrate technology requires additional encoding, but simplifies the overall workflow and creates better results.

504ae1a9c3c0.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
504ae1a9c3c0.sentence: HTTP-based adaptive bit rate technologies are significantly more operationally complex than traditional streaming technologies.

f651e19f1a48.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
f651e19f1a48.sentence: Some of the documented considerations are things such as additional storage and encoding costs, and challenges with maintaining quality globally.

4fa4f1cfc825.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
4fa4f1cfc825.sentence: With no single clearly defined or open standard for the digital rights management used in the above methods, there is no 100% compatible way of delivering restricted or time-sensitive content to any device or player.

8f29ec5e0fad.title: rfc>8216
8f29ec5e0fad.sentence: This document describes a protocol for transferring unbounded streams of multimedia data.

f245c7891ad3.title: rfc>8216
f245c7891ad3.sentence: HTTP Live Streaming provides a reliable, cost-effective means of delivering continuous and long-form video over the Internet.

caead19e698c.title: rfc>8216
caead19e698c.sentence: It allows a receiver to adapt the bit rate of the media to the current network conditions in order to maintain uninterrupted playback at the best possible quality.

883fded3cd45.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
883fded3cd45.sentence: HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) is an HTTP-based media streaming communications protocol implemented by Apple Inc. as part of QuickTime X and iOS.

0633181958d0.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
0633181958d0.sentence: HLS supports both live and video on demand content.

c7210e3ba510.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
c7210e3ba510.sentence: This was officially accepted as RFC 8216.

34f68852de69.title: rfc>8216
34f68852de69.sentence: This document describes version 7 of the protocol.

56ae6a9ccfb1.title: rfc>8216
56ae6a9ccfb1.sentence: A multimedia presentation is specified by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) to a Playlist.

ffec36cc583f.title: rfc>8216
ffec36cc583f.sentence: A Playlist is either a Media Playlist or a Master Playlist.

24bc4bf17428.title: rfc>8216
24bc4bf17428.sentence: Both are UTF-8 text files containing URIs and descriptive tags.

b721ac265ada.title: rfc>8216
b721ac265ada.sentence: A Media Playlist contains a list of Media Segments, which, when played sequentially, will play the multimedia presentation.

42376654fc91.title: rfc>8216
42376654fc91.sentence: A Master Playlist provides a set of Variant Streams, each of which describes a different version of the same content.

afb59ea4cf0c.title: rfc>8216
afb59ea4cf0c.sentence: A Variant Stream includes a Media Playlist that specifies media encoded at a particular bit rate, in a particular format, and at a particular resolution for media containing video.

5e1b6131e58c.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
5e1b6131e58c.sentence: This is typically done at multiple bitrates using a stream or file segmenter application, also known as a packager.

442475daf859.title: rfc>8216
442475daf859.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.1. General Server Responsibilities
442475daf859.sentence: The server MUST divide the source media into individual Media Segments whose duration is less than or equal to a constant target duration.

f76d1bc413d7.title: rfc>8216
f76d1bc413d7.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.1. General Server Responsibilities
f76d1bc413d7.sentence: The server MUST create a URI for every Media Segment that enables its clients to obtain the segment data.

ece66c6f22dc.title: rfc>8216
ece66c6f22dc.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.1. General Server Responsibilities
ece66c6f22dc.sentence: A typical target duration is 10 seconds.

a93391290ac6.title: rfc>8216
a93391290ac6.sentence: MPEG-2 Transport Streams are specified by [ISO_13818].

8d386306fad3.title: rfc>8216
8d386306fad3.sentence: MPEG-4 Fragments are specified by the ISO Base Media File Format.

3862bb7cb4b6.title: rfc>8216
3862bb7cb4b6.sentence: A Packed Audio Segment contains encoded audio samples and ID3 tags that are simply packed together with minimal framing and no per-sample timestamps.

97805d6afdd2.title: rfc>8216
97805d6afdd2.sentence: Each segment in a Media Playlist has a unique integer Media Sequence Number.

1b2670db343e.title: rfc>8216
1b2670db343e.sentence: The Media Sequence Number of every other segment is equal to the Media Sequence Number of the segment that precedes it plus one.

df90ea81041c.title: rfc>8216
df90ea81041c.sentence: The duration of each Media Segment is indicated in the Media Playlist by its EXTINF tag (Section 4.3.2.1).

1acce8fcf64c.title: rfc>8216
1acce8fcf64c.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.4. Providing Variant Streams
1acce8fcf64c.sentence: - Each Variant Stream MUST present the same content.

7b4debb20504.title: rfc>8216
7b4debb20504.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.4. Providing Variant Streams
7b4debb20504.sentence: - Matching content in Variant Streams MUST have matching timestamps.

c18461c2edca.title: rfc>8216
c18461c2edca.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.4. Providing Variant Streams
c18461c2edca.sentence: - Each Media Playlist in each Variant Stream MUST have the same target duration.

77fd1b77da6d.title: rfc>8216
77fd1b77da6d.sentence: Clients should switch between different Variant Streams to adapt to network conditions.

89c46d359183.title: rfc>8216
89c46d359183.sentence: Clients should choose Renditions based on user preferences.

573ed4209aeb.title: rfc>8216
573ed4209aeb.sentence: Renditions are alternate versions of the content, such as audio produced in different languages or video recorded from different camera angles.

f7af5313d929.title: rfc>8216
f7af5313d929.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.1. General Server Responsibilities
f7af5313d929.sentence: The server MUST NOT change the Media Playlist file, except to:

13f8ced2c68f.title: rfc>8216
13f8ced2c68f.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.2. Live Playlists
13f8ced2c68f.sentence: If Media Segments are to be removed, the Playlist file MUST contain an EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE tag.

2750e0ee4481.title: rfc>8216
2750e0ee4481.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.2. Live Playlists
2750e0ee4481.sentence: Its value MUST be incremented by 1 for every Media Segment that is removed from the Playlist file; it MUST NOT decrease or wrap.

87de060a1591.title: rfc>8216
87de060a1591.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.2. Live Playlists
87de060a1591.sentence: The server MUST NOT remove a Media Segment from a Playlist file without an EXT-X-ENDLIST tag if that would produce a Playlist whose duration is less than three times the target duration.

299a4026b7a9.title: rfc>8216
299a4026b7a9.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.1. General Server Responsibilities
299a4026b7a9.sentence: If the Media Playlist contains the final Media Segment of the presentation, then the Playlist file MUST contain the EXT-X-ENDLIST tag; this allows clients to minimize unproductive Playlist reloads.

08eda19f7ffd.title: rfc>8216
08eda19f7ffd.sentence: To play this Playlist, the client first downloads it and then downloads and plays each Media Segment declared within it.

76328a8ad7e5.title: rfc>8216
76328a8ad7e5.sentence: The client reloads the Playlist as described in this document to discover any added segments.

550e71a099c6.title: rfc>8216
550e71a099c6.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.3. Client Responsibilities > 6.3.4. Reloading the Media Playlist File
550e71a099c6.sentence: When a client loads a Playlist file for the first time or reloads a Playlist file and finds that it has changed since the last time it was loaded, the client MUST wait for at least the target duration before attempting to reload the Playlist file again, measured from the last time the client began loading the Playlist file.

7e5fecddefd5.title: rfc>8216
7e5fecddefd5.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.3. Client Responsibilities > 6.3.4. Reloading the Media Playlist File
7e5fecddefd5.sentence: If the client reloads a Playlist file and finds that it has not changed, then it MUST wait for a period of one-half the target duration before retrying.

ba255ac90cf6.title: rfc>8216
ba255ac90cf6.sentence: It offers compatibility with large-scale HTTP caching infrastructure to support delivery to large audiences.

82fcb2c69737.title: rfc>8216
82fcb2c69737.sentence: Data SHOULD be carried over HTTP, but, in general, a URI can specify any protocol that can reliably transfer the specified resource on demand.

b09d2f2e4620.title: rfc>8216
b09d2f2e4620.section: 6. Client/Server Responsibilities > 6.2. Server Responsibilities > 6.2.3. Encrypting Media Segments
b09d2f2e4620.sentence: Every encrypted Media Segment MUST have an EXT-X-KEY tag (Section 4.3.2.4) applied to it with a URI that the client can use to obtain a Key file (Section 5) containing the decryption key.

586e55977e06.title: rfc>8216
586e55977e06.section: 4. Playlists > 4.3. Playlist Tags > 4.3.2. Media Segment Tags > 4.3.2.4. EXT-X-KEY

1fca3de8bf1c.title: rfc>8216
1fca3de8bf1c.sentence: Encryption keys are specified by URI.

b200d1068475.title: rfc>8216
b200d1068475.sentence: The delivery of these keys SHOULD be secured by a mechanism such as HTTP Over TLS (formerly SSL) in conjunction with a secure realm or a session token.

ec93a38054ae.title: Video on demand
ec93a38054ae.sentence: Video on demand (VOD) is a media distribution system that allows users to access television shows, films, and videos digitally on request.

c3145d0b6737.title: Video on demand
c3145d0b6737.sentence: The majority of cable and telephone company–based television providers offer VOD streaming, whereby a user selects a video programme that begins to play immediately (i.e., streaming), or downloading to a DVR rented or purchased from the provider, or to a PC or to a portable device for deferred viewing.

8b382765f395.title: Video on demand
8b382765f395.sentence: VOD users may also permanently download content to a device such as a computer, digital video recorder (DVR) or a portable media player for continued viewing.

fa5be5d75808.title: Video on demand
fa5be5d75808.sentence: Streaming media has emerged as an increasingly popular medium of VOD provision over downloading, including BitTorrent.

4cc0fc8e3f79.title: Video on demand
4cc0fc8e3f79.sentence: Some VOD systems store and stream programs from hard disk drives and use a memory buffer to allow the user to fast-forward and rewind videos.

4d5b9e84ec72.title: Video on demand
4d5b9e84ec72.sentence: It is possible to put video servers on local area networks; these can provide rapid responses to users.

e5b388c7c26a.title: Video on demand
e5b388c7c26a.sentence: Subscription video on demand (SVOD) services use a subscription business model in which subscribers are charged a regular fee to access unlimited programs.

4aafa989a2d9.title: Video on demand
4aafa989a2d9.sentence: Transactional video on demand (TVOD) is a distribution method by which customers pay for each piece of video-on-demand content.

37ff94be3418.title: Video on demand
37ff94be3418.sentence: Advertising video on demand (AVOD) uses an advertising-based revenue model.

57529bbb29c0.title: Video on demand
57529bbb29c0.sentence: This model also allows people to watch content without paying subscription fees.

07f97de962da.title: Video on demand
07f97de962da.sentence: Multiple copies of a programme are broadcast at short time intervals (typically staggered on a schedule of every 10–20 minutes) on linear channels providing convenience for viewers, who can watch the programme without needing to tune in at the only scheduled point in time.

0440ccc8ccaa.title: Video on demand
0440ccc8ccaa.sentence: This form is bandwidth-intensive, reduces the number of channels a provider can offer, and is generally provided by large operators with a great deal of redundant capacity.

fb6b7daa8d8f.title: Video on demand
fb6b7daa8d8f.sentence: Push VOD is also used by broadcasters that want to optimize their video streaming infrastructures by pre-loading the most popular contents to the consumers' set-top device.

7e5106e5721e.title: Video on demand
7e5106e5721e.sentence: Push video on demand (Push VOD) is so-named because the provider "pushes" the content out to the viewer's set-top box without the viewer having requested the content.

019ea357c503.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
019ea357c503.sentence: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH), also known as MPEG-DASH, is an adaptive bitrate streaming technique that enables high quality streaming of media content over the Internet delivered from conventional HTTP web servers.

37bb376fb976.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
37bb376fb976.sentence: MPEG-DASH is the first adaptive bit-rate HTTP-based streaming solution that is an international standard.

afea159854a7.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
afea159854a7.sentence: Similar to Apple's HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) solution, MPEG-DASH works by breaking the content into a sequence of small segments, which are served over HTTP.

c173415f3282.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
c173415f3282.sentence: Each segment contains a short interval of playback time of content that is potentially many hours in duration, such as a movie or the live broadcast of a sport event.

0f8ddb2de8ef.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
0f8ddb2de8ef.sentence: The content is made available at a variety of different bit rates, i.e., alternative segments encoded at different bit rates covering aligned short intervals of playback time.

95d4e5bd1abd.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
95d4e5bd1abd.sentence: While the content is being played back by an MPEG-DASH client, the client uses a bit rate adaptation (ABR) algorithm to automatically select the segment with the highest bit rate possible that can be downloaded in time for playback without causing stalls or re-buffering events in the playback.

860a4cad2916.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
860a4cad2916.sentence: Thus, an MPEG-DASH client can seamlessly adapt to changing network conditions and provide high quality playback with few stalls or re-buffering events.

65a307553592.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
65a307553592.sentence: DASH standard does not specify the adaptive bitrate streaming (ABR) logic.

bcd583fc7740.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
bcd583fc7740.sentence: The current MPEG-DASH reference client dash.js offers both buffer-based (BOLA) and hybrid (DYNAMIC) bit rate adaptation algorithms.

c7db0e330a10.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
c7db0e330a10.sentence: A media presentation description (MPD) describes segment information (timing, URL, media characteristics like video resolution and bit rates), and can be organized in different ways such as SegmentList, SegmentTemplate, SegmentBase and SegmentTimeline, depending on the use case.

7d018beaf274.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
7d018beaf274.sentence: Segments can contain any media data, however the specification provides specific guidance and formats for use with two types of containers: ISO base media file format (e.g. MP4 file format) or MPEG-2 Transport Stream.

80ba0e3c3f15.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
80ba0e3c3f15.sentence: MPEG-DASH uses existing HTTP web server infrastructure that is used for delivery of essentially all World Wide Web content.

7762ef4738fd.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
7762ef4738fd.sentence: Note that no specific support is required from the server for DASH content, with the exception of Live Streaming.

6f155e18b6bc.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
6f155e18b6bc.sentence: MPEG-DASH should not be confused with a transport protocol — the transport protocol that MPEG-DASH uses depends on which version of HTTP is used: TCP is the transport over which HTTP and HTTP/2 run, while HTTP/3 runs over QUIC (which in turn runs over UDP).

8778ae08b702.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
8778ae08b702.section: Implementations > Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH)
8778ae08b702.sentence: The MPEG-DASH standard was published as ISO/IEC 23009-1:2012 in April 2012.

fc637bf827d0.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
fc637bf827d0.section: Implementations > Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH)
fc637bf827d0.sentence: The goal of standardizing an adaptive streaming solution is to assure the market that the solution can work universally, unlike other solutions that are more specific to certain vendors, such as Apple's HLS, Microsoft's Smooth Streaming, or Adobe's HDS.

e5d28abcbbec.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
e5d28abcbbec.sentence: Unlike HDS, or Smooth Streaming, DASH is codec-agnostic, which means it can use content encoded with any coding format, such as H.265, H.264, VP9, etc.

e645a4e761b7.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
e645a4e761b7.sentence: YouTube as well as Netflix already support MPEG-DASH, and different MPEG-DASH players are available.

62be5a83f997.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
62be5a83f997.sentence: While MPEG-DASH isn't directly supported in HTML5, there are JavaScript implementations of MPEG-DASH which allow using MPEG-DASH in web browsers using the HTML5 Media Source Extensions (MSE).

91267a1ea69b.title: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP
91267a1ea69b.sentence: There are also JavaScript implementations such as the bitdash player which support DRM for MPEG-DASH using the HTML5 Encrypted Media Extensions.

63f7f5c02411.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
63f7f5c02411.section: Related technologies > Common Media Application Format (CMAF)
63f7f5c02411.sentence: CMAF is a presentation container format used for the delivery of both HLS and MPEG-DASH.

aaf9ed13c267.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
aaf9ed13c267.section: Related technologies > Common Media Application Format (CMAF)
aaf9ed13c267.sentence: Hence, it is intended to simplify delivery of HTTP-based streaming media.

e2cad403fc15.title: Adaptive bitrate streaming
e2cad403fc15.sentence: Of the ABR streaming implementations described here the only ones still actively developed and used in 2026 are Apple HLS and MPEG DASH.

9434888de1f9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
9434888de1f9.sentence: Transcoding is a process in which the original data is decoded to an intermediate uncompressed format, which is then encoded into the target format.

f5b058e8746d.title: Transcoding
f5b058e8746d.sentence: Transcoding is the direct digital-to-digital conversion of one encoding to another, such as for video files, audio files, or character encoding.

00445b32685d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-does-youtube-handle-massive-video-content-upload.md
00445b32685d.sentence: YouTube’s mission is to transcode raw video into different compression rates to adapt to different viewing devices - mobile(720p), laptop(1080p), or high-resolution TV(4k).

64967b88d435.title: Transcoding
64967b88d435.sentence: Transcoding is a two-step process in which the original data is decoded to an intermediate uncompressed format (e.g., PCM for audio; YUV for video), which is then encoded into the target format.

331e79c8509e.title: Transcoding
331e79c8509e.sentence: This is usually done in cases where a target device (or workflow) does not support the format or has limited storage capacity that mandates a reduced file size, or to convert incompatible or obsolete data to a better-supported or modern format.

4f86ccd0646c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
4f86ccd0646c.sentence: This process uses different codecs to perform bitrate adjustment, image downsampling, or re-encoding the media.

a5e88d164ab5.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
a5e88d164ab5.sentence: This results in a smaller size file and a much more optimized format for the target devices.

4469a1d4c76c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
4469a1d4c76c.sentence: This is the last step of the processing pipeline and as the name suggests, this step handles the conversion of the transcoded media from the previous step into different resolutions such as 4K, 1440p, 1080p, 720p, etc.

1eb58d62ae20.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
1eb58d62ae20.sentence: It allows us to fetch the desired quality of the video as per the user's request, and once the media file finishes processing, it gets uploaded to a distributed file storage such as HDFS, GlusterFS, or an object storage such as Amazon S3 for later retrieval during streaming.

0a04e85f3eb5.title: Transcoding
0a04e85f3eb5.sentence: Transrating is a process similar to transcoding in which files are coded to a lower bitrate without changing video formats; this can include sample rate conversion, but may use an identical sampling rate with higher compression.

4bca76f4c482.title: Transcoding
4bca76f4c482.sentence: Changing the picture size of video is known as transsizing, and is used if the output resolution differs from the resolution of the media.

b9883265febe.title: Transcoding
b9883265febe.sentence: Although transcoding can be found in many areas of content adaptation, it is commonly used in the area of mobile phone content adaptation.

ec7cb6310c71.title: Transcoding
ec7cb6310c71.sentence: In this case, transcoding is a must, due to the diversity of mobile devices and their capabilities.

32ec6cdca8c6.title: Transcoding
32ec6cdca8c6.sentence: The key drawback of transcoding in lossy formats is decreased quality.

e31569aee7d4.title: Transcoding
e31569aee7d4.sentence: Compression artifacts are cumulative, so transcoding causes a progressive loss of quality with each successive generation, known as digital generation loss.

6206c652ed79.title: Transcoding
6206c652ed79.sentence: Transcoding is commonly a lossy process, introducing generation loss; however, transcoding can be lossless if the output is either losslessly compressed or uncompressed.

aa1a857ef9e9.title: Transcoding
aa1a857ef9e9.sentence: Effectively this means that any transcoding will involve some cumulative image loss, and hence the most practical solution insofar as minimizing loss of quality is for the original recording to be deemed the master copy, and for desired subsequent transcoded versions, which will often be in a different format and smaller file size, to be transcoded only from that master copy.

e98f96d311b9.title: Transcoding
e98f96d311b9.sentence: For this reason, transcoding (in lossy formats) is generally discouraged unless unavoidable.

6a117fb432ee.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
6a117fb432ee.sentence: Standalone solutions such as FFmpeg or cloud-based solutions like AWS Elemental MediaConvert can be used to implement this step of the pipeline.

ac719d63441e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
ac719d63441e.sentence: Livestreaming differs from regular streaming because the video content is sent via the internet in real-time, usually with a latency of just a few seconds.

01b1511c1fb5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
01b1511c1fb5.sentence: Step 1: The raw video data is captured by a microphone and camera.

ba60d0565bc0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
ba60d0565bc0.sentence: The data is sent to the server side.

cdad6f0db87e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
cdad6f0db87e.sentence: Step 2: The video data is compressed and encoded.

3dd87507e256.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
3dd87507e256.sentence: After compression, the video is encoded to standards such as H.264.

b16401d65a99.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
b16401d65a99.sentence: The size of the video data is much smaller after this step.

97b7d08a90fc.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
97b7d08a90fc.sentence: Step 3: The encoded data is divided into smaller segments, usually seconds in length, so it takes much less time to download or stream.

0fd54a65c1b8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
0fd54a65c1b8.sentence: The streaming server needs to support different devices and network conditions.

590e52edf285.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
590e52edf285.sentence: This is called ‘Adaptive Bitrate Streaming.’ This means we need to produce multiple files at different bitrates in steps 2 and 3.

4af900bdd9fe.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
4af900bdd9fe.sentence: Step 5: The live streaming data is pushed to edge servers supported by CDN (Content Delivery Network.) Millions of viewers can watch the video from an edge server nearby.

a848d83bbc63.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
a848d83bbc63.sentence: CDN significantly lowers data transmission latency.

26c23ae6b65b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
26c23ae6b65b.sentence: Step 6: The viewers’ devices decode and decompress the video data and play the video in a video player.

198b253602a6.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
198b253602a6.sentence: Steps 7 and 8: If the video needs to be stored for replay, the encoded data is sent to a storage server, and viewers can request a replay from it later.

543385978533.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
543385978533.sentence: - RTMP (Real-Time Messaging Protocol): This was originally developed by Macromedia to transmit data between a Flash player and a server.

23e3fbe8cd11.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
23e3fbe8cd11.sentence: Now it is used for streaming video data over the internet.

4ac1d0eefb1d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
4ac1d0eefb1d.sentence: - HLS (HTTP Live Streaming): It requires the H.264 or H.265 encoding.

575b5cfbc0e9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
575b5cfbc0e9.sentence: Both HLS and DASH support adaptive bitrate streaming.

3184a280b812.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/live-streaming-explained.md
3184a280b812.sentence: Note that video conferencing applications like Skype use RTC (Real-Time Communication) protocol for lower latency.

5a55d9da2fb9.title: Streaming media
5a55d9da2fb9.sentence: Unicast protocols send a separate copy of the media stream from the server to each recipient.

a7d600b60f70.title: Streaming media
a7d600b60f70.sentence: These protocols send a single stream from the source to a group of recipients.

284dfa41cc8e.title: Streaming media
284dfa41cc8e.sentence: Peer-to-peer (P2P) protocols arrange for prerecorded streams to be sent between computers.

16c8661f1879.title: Streaming media
16c8661f1879.sentence: Content delivery networks (CDNs) use intermediate servers to distribute the load.

196fcd4e68d5.title: Streaming media
196fcd4e68d5.sentence: Unicast is the norm for most Internet connections but does not scale well when many users want to view the same television program concurrently.

ba258a247862.title: Streaming media
ba258a247862.sentence: If the file is stored on a server for on-demand streaming and this stream is viewed by 1,000 people at the same time using a Unicast protocol, the requirement is 300 kbit/s × 1,000 =300,000 kbit/s =300 Mbit/s of bandwidth.

36fabd65ac8b.title: Streaming media
36fabd65ac8b.sentence: Using a multicast protocol, the server sends out only a single stream that is common to all users.

ff0178183216.title: Streaming media
ff0178183216.sentence: Therefore, such a stream would only use 300 kbit/s of server bandwidth.

292f948f3d2f.title: Streaming media
292f948f3d2f.sentence: Multicast protocols were developed to reduce server and network loads resulting from duplicate data streams that occur when many recipients receive unicast content streams independently.

93323f4db111.title: Streaming media
93323f4db111.sentence: Depending on the network infrastructure and type, multicast transmission may or may not be feasible.

17c9455d9b54.title: Streaming media
17c9455d9b54.sentence: One potential disadvantage of multicasting is the loss of video on demand functionality.

62c7eff82dd3.title: Streaming media
62c7eff82dd3.sentence: This prevents the server and its network connections from becoming a bottleneck.

a7724f205c3a.title: Streaming media
a7724f205c3a.sentence: However, it raises technical, performance, security, quality, and business issues.

358614f06e3e.title: Streaming media
358614f06e3e.sentence: Internet-compatible unicast delivery is used between CDN nodes and streaming destinations.

939c56221329.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
939c56221329.sentence: Real-Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP) is a communication protocol for streaming audio, video, and data over the Internet.

71735a0f23b3.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
71735a0f23b3.sentence: Originally developed as a proprietary protocol by Macromedia for streaming between Flash Player and the Flash Communication Server, Adobe (which acquired Macromedia) has released an incomplete version of the specification of the protocol for public use.

12e95437d992.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
12e95437d992.sentence: - RTMP proper, the "plain" protocol which works on top of Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and uses port number 1935 by default.

b6e6f3e55769.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
b6e6f3e55769.sentence: RTMP is a TCP-based protocol which maintains persistent connections and allows low-latency communication.

3878fcb4f81e.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
3878fcb4f81e.sentence: After establishing a TCP connection, an RTMP connection is established first, performing a handshake through the exchange of three packets from each side (also referred to as Chunks in the official documentation).

ea1ac7428b5c.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
ea1ac7428b5c.sentence: To deliver streams smoothly and transmit as much information as possible, it splits streams into fragments, and their size is negotiated dynamically between the client and server.

a470669895f8.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
a470669895f8.sentence: Sometimes, it is kept unchanged; the default fragment sizes are 64 bytes for audio data, and 128 bytes for video data and most other data types.

29b396f86c6a.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
29b396f86c6a.sentence: The RTMP defines several virtual channels on which packets may be sent and received, and which operate independently of each other.

c72f0d0ccfc9.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
c72f0d0ccfc9.sentence: For example, there is a channel for handling RPC requests and responses, a channel for video stream data, a channel for audio stream data, a channel for out-of-band control messages (fragment size negotiation, etc.), and so on.

9708c2a5aeaf.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
9708c2a5aeaf.sentence: Fragments from different streams may then be interleaved, and multiplexed over a single connection.

fc9a46b5bcac.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
fc9a46b5bcac.sentence: Instead, the interleaving and multiplexing is done at the packet level, with RTMP packets across several different active channels being interleaved in such a way as to ensure that each channel meets its bandwidth, latency, and other quality-of-service requirements.

2124e2b418d2.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
2124e2b418d2.sentence: - RTMPS, which is RTMP over a Transport Layer Security (TLS/SSL) connection.

28e166c6af64.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
28e166c6af64.sentence: - RTMPE, which is RTMP encrypted using Adobe's own security mechanism.

3d857e6ea4f8.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
3d857e6ea4f8.sentence: - RTMPT, which is encapsulated within HTTP requests to traverse firewalls.

1e065e6d4ff8.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
1e065e6d4ff8.sentence: RTMPT is frequently found utilizing cleartext requests on TCP ports 80 and 443 to bypass most corporate traffic filtering.

42ba6e8c733c.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
42ba6e8c733c.sentence: - RTMFP, which is RTMP over User Datagram Protocol (UDP) instead of TCP, replacing RTMP Chunk Stream.

4deb18daa8ce.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
4deb18daa8ce.sentence: However, the limited codec selections of FLV and RTMP has necessitated the industry to add things to the format and the protocol directly.

35a2f9606bea.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
35a2f9606bea.sentence: Enhanced RTMP (E-RTMP) is an enhancement to the Real-Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP) and FLV specifications, modernizing streaming workflows while maintaining compatibility with existing RTMP infrastructure.

17bd94488ca1.title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
17bd94488ca1.sentence: E-RTMP enhances RTMP by adding features such as advanced timestamp precision, multitrack capabilities, expanded codec support, FourCC signaling, and a reconnect request feature.

e9b953e6b01f.title: Advanced Video Coding
e9b953e6b01f.sentence: Advanced Video Coding (AVC), also referred to as H.264 or MPEG-4 Part 10, is a video compression standard based on block-oriented, motion-compensated coding.

9b593fe44fa2.title: Advanced Video Coding
9b593fe44fa2.sentence: The ITU-T H.264 standard and the ISO/IEC MPEG-4 AVC standard (formally, ISO/IEC 14496-10 – MPEG-4 Part 10, Advanced Video Coding) are jointly maintained so that they have identical technical content.

72e59406170a.title: Advanced Video Coding
72e59406170a.sentence: It is by far the most commonly used format for the recording, compression, and distribution of video content, used by 79% of video industry developers as of December 2024.

4041fdfadb77.title: Advanced Video Coding
4041fdfadb77.sentence: It has also been widely used by streaming Internet sources, such as videos from Netflix, Hulu, Amazon Prime Video, Vimeo, YouTube (more recently transitioning to VP9 and AV1) and the iTunes Store, Web software such as the Adobe Flash Player and Microsoft Silverlight, and also various HDTV broadcasts over terrestrial (ATSC, ISDB-T, DVB-T or DVB-T2), cable (DVB-C), and satellite (DVB-S and DVB-S2) systems.

f91b9c45a003.title: Advanced Video Coding
f91b9c45a003.sentence: With the use of H.264, bit rate savings of 50% or more compared to MPEG-2 Part 2 are reported.

28157ebaaf16.title: Advanced Video Coding
28157ebaaf16.sentence: For example, H.264 has been reported to give the same Digital Satellite TV quality as current MPEG-2 implementations with less than half the bitrate, with current MPEG-2 implementations working at around 3.5 Mbit/s and H.264 at only 1.5 Mbit/s.

3d4ea38e2f92.title: Advanced Video Coding
3d4ea38e2f92.sentence: The standard defines several sets of capabilities, which are referred to as profiles, targeting specific classes of applications.

e3e99add5f35.title: Advanced Video Coding
e3e99add5f35.sentence: (And in many system environments, only one or two profiles are allowed to be used, so decoders in those environments do not need to be concerned with recognizing the less commonly used profiles.) By far the most commonly used profile is the High Profile.

e7a6d25c5f40.title: Advanced Video Coding
e7a6d25c5f40.sentence: As the term is used in the standard, a "level" is a specified set of constraints that indicate a degree of required decoder performance for a profile.

92c4f545a88d.title: Advanced Video Coding
92c4f545a88d.sentence: For example, a level of support within a profile specifies the maximum picture resolution, frame rate, and bit rate that a decoder may use.

1f6db250b754.title: Advanced Video Coding
1f6db250b754.sentence: A decoder that conforms to a given level must be able to decode all bitstreams encoded for that level and all lower levels.

c502e6def6b5.title: Advanced Video Coding
c502e6def6b5.sentence: H.264 is restricted by patents owned by various parties.

92b0df7fff00.title: Advanced Video Coding
92b0df7fff00.sentence: The commercial use of patented H.264 technologies requires the payment of royalties to Via and other patent owners.

9cea94d30990.title: Advanced Video Coding
9cea94d30990.sentence: Because H.264 encoding and decoding require significant computational power for specific arithmetic operations, software implementations running on general-purpose CPUs are typically less power-efficient.

2e803a5f9bd4.title: Advanced Video Coding
2e803a5f9bd4.sentence: Therefore, the difference between hardware- and software-based implementations is more on power efficiency, flexibility and cost.

5b162c462a8d.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
5b162c462a8d.sentence: High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC), also known as H.265 and MPEG-H Part 2, is a patent-encumbered video compression standard designed as part of the MPEG-H project as a successor to the widely used Advanced Video Coding (AVC, H.264, or MPEG-4 Part 10).

d14e7620dafa.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
d14e7620dafa.sentence: In comparison to AVC, HEVC can be used to achieve from 25% to 50% better data compression at the same level of video quality, or substantially improved video quality at the same bit rate.

108ee3c74265.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
108ee3c74265.sentence: For example, standard 4K video capture at 30 frames per second typically requires a target bitrate of approximately 50 Mbps using HEVC, requiring roughly 22.5 GB of storage volume per hour, compared to the 100 Mbps and 45 GB per hour required by older H.264 profiles.

034fe4841aa2.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
034fe4841aa2.sentence: In most ways, HEVC is an extension of the concepts in H.264/MPEG-4 AVC.

5ea801c5eaad.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
5ea801c5eaad.sentence: Both work by comparing different parts of a frame of video to find areas that are redundant, both within a single frame and between consecutive frames.

12e938f89f00.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
12e938f89f00.section: Features > Coding tools > Coding tree unit
12e938f89f00.sentence: HEVC replaces 16×16 pixel macroblocks, which were used with previous standards, with coding tree units (CTUs) which can use larger block structures of up to 64×64 samples and can better sub-partition the picture into variable sized structures.

c974f7285eea.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
c974f7285eea.sentence: Effective use of these improvements requires much more signal processing capability for compressing the video but has less impact on the amount of computation needed for decompression.

7164ecfb07b3.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
7164ecfb07b3.sentence: It supports resolutions up to 8192×4320, including 8K UHD, and unlike the primarily eight-bit AVC, HEVC's higher-fidelity Main 10 profile has been incorporated into nearly all supporting hardware.

fead06339cfe.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
fead06339cfe.sentence: Two of the key features where HEVC was improved compared with H.264/MPEG-4 AVC was support for higher resolution video and improved parallel processing methods.

c0853d4d2734.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
c0853d4d2734.section: Features > Coding tools > Parallel processing tools
c0853d4d2734.sentence: - Tiles allow for the picture to be divided into a grid of rectangular regions that can independently be decoded/encoded.

b5da8ccf2297.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
b5da8ccf2297.section: Features > Coding tools > Parallel processing tools
b5da8ccf2297.sentence: - Wavefront parallel processing (WPP) is when a slice is divided into rows of CTUs in which the first row is decoded normally but each additional row requires that decisions be made in the previous row.

a5fdacba0e6f.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
a5fdacba0e6f.sentence: The combined licensing fees currently offered by all of the patent licensing bodies are higher than for AVC.

ee8d0688350e.title: High Efficiency Video Coding
ee8d0688350e.sentence: The licensing fees are one of the main reasons HEVC adoption has been low on the web and is why some of the largest tech companies (Amazon, AMD, Apple, ARM, Cisco, Google, Intel, Microsoft, Mozilla, Netflix, Nvidia, and more) have joined the Alliance for Open Media, which finalized royalty-free alternative video coding format AV1 on March 28, 2018.

75be674d0ba8.title: AV1
75be674d0ba8.sentence: AOMedia Video 1 (AV1) is an open, royalty-free video coding format initially designed for video transmissions over the Internet.

3b4a20c5ff12.title: AV1
3b4a20c5ff12.sentence: It was developed as a successor to VP9 by the Alliance for Open Media (AOMedia), a consortium founded in 2015 that includes semiconductor firms, video on demand providers, video content producers, software development companies and web browser vendors.

31acab0ec506.title: AV1
31acab0ec506.sentence: Like VP9, but unlike H.264 (AVC) and H.265 (HEVC), AV1 has a royalty-free licensing model that does not hinder adoption in open-source projects.

7841d9f84fd8.title: AV1
7841d9f84fd8.sentence: The Alliance's motivations for creating AV1 included the high cost and uncertainty involved with the patent licensing of HEVC (also known as H.265), the MPEG-designed codec expected to succeed AVC.

0056135358f9.title: AV1
0056135358f9.sentence: AV1 is a traditional block-based frequency transform format featuring new techniques.

d6f585e7e3ad.title: AV1
d6f585e7e3ad.sentence: Based on Google's VP9, AV1 incorporates additional techniques that mainly give encoders more coding options to enable better adaptation to different types of input.

afe85d6a5cf7.title: AV1
afe85d6a5cf7.sentence: Similar to the concept of a macroblock, superblocks are square-shaped and can either be of size 128×128 or 64×64 pixels.

baf6e3919a10.title: AV1
baf6e3919a10.sentence: AV1 is primarily intended for lossy encoding, although lossless compression is supported as well.

905f6a6731de.title: AV1
905f6a6731de.sentence: Tests from Netflix in 2017, based on measurements with PSNR and VMAF at 720p, showed that AV1 was about 25% more efficient than VP9 (libvpx).

7bda88f4897b.title: AV1
7bda88f4897b.sentence: On 5 February 2020, Netflix began using AV1 to stream select titles on Android, providing 20% improved compression efficiency over their VP9 streams.

4b86558f4494.title: AV1
4b86558f4494.sentence: They also concluded that at the time of the study at 2160p the AV1 video encodes on average took 590× longer compared to encoding with AVC; while HEVC took on average 4.2× longer and VP9 took on average 5.2× longer than AVC respectively.

fad76d5c36cd.title: AV1
fad76d5c36cd.sentence: Decoding performance was at about half the speed of VP9 according to internal measurements from 2017.

df32cd6f61a7.title: Geo-blocking
df32cd6f61a7.sentence: Geo-blocking, geoblocking or geolocking is technology that restricts access to Internet content based upon the user's geographical location.

d2abacd1af32.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::netflix
d2abacd1af32.sentence: Platforms like Netflix and YouTube use Geo-blocking to restrict content in certain geographical areas or countries.

52884a572233.title: Geo-blocking
52884a572233.sentence: Geo-blocking is commonly implemented by identifying a user's geographic location primarily through their IP address, which is mapped to a country or region using GeoIP databases.

e92a6bc6f003.title: Geo-blocking
e92a6bc6f003.sentence: In a geo-blocking scheme, the user's location is determined using Internet geolocation techniques, such as checking the user's IP address against a blacklist or whitelist, GPS queries in the case of a mobile device, accounts, and measuring the end-to-end delay of a network connection to estimate the physical location of the user.

640ee1d373a0.title: Geo-blocking
640ee1d373a0.sentence: The result of this check is used to determine whether the system will approve or deny access to the website or to particular content.

3686784ca5c8.title: Nearest neighbor search
3686784ca5c8.sentence: Nearest neighbor search (NNS), as a form of proximity search, is the optimization problem of finding the point in a given set that is closest (or most similar) to a given point.

d572daa6e0c6.title: Nearest neighbor search
d572daa6e0c6.sentence: Closeness is typically expressed in terms of a dissimilarity function: the less similar the objects, the larger the function values.

17e8f9b30c19.title: Nearest neighbor search
17e8f9b30c19.sentence: Even more common, M is taken to be the d-dimensional vector space where dissimilarity is measured using the Euclidean distance, Manhattan distance or other distance metric.

f1c17880e491.title: Nearest neighbor search
f1c17880e491.sentence: A direct generalization of this problem is a k-NN search, where we need to find the k closest points.

a651436bc7b7.title: Nearest neighbor search
a651436bc7b7.sentence: - Recommendation systems, e.g. see Collaborative filtering

43587ddedf83.title: Nearest neighbor search
43587ddedf83.sentence: - Vector databases, where nearest-neighbor lookup over embeddings is used to retrieve semantically similar records

746ee90c816f.title: Nearest neighbor search
746ee90c816f.sentence: The simplest solution to the NNS problem is to compute the distance from the query point to every other point in the database, keeping track of the "best so far".

3660e802dddc.title: Nearest neighbor search
3660e802dddc.sentence: This algorithm, sometimes referred to as the naive approach, has a running time of O(dN), where N is the cardinality of S and d is the dimensionality of S. There are no search data structures to maintain, so the linear search has no space complexity beyond the storage of the database.

57bd7e9162be.title: Nearest neighbor search
57bd7e9162be.sentence: The absolute distance is not required for distance comparison, only the relative distance.

b1482fd0b7b9.title: Nearest neighbor search
b1482fd0b7b9.sentence: In geometric coordinate systems the distance calculation can be sped up considerably by omitting the square root calculation from the distance calculation between two coordinates.

ccf936157567.title: Nearest neighbor search
ccf936157567.sentence: Perhaps the simplest is the k-d tree, which iteratively bisects the search space into two regions containing half of the points of the parent region.

a153333e773d.title: Nearest neighbor search
a153333e773d.sentence: Queries are performed via traversal of the tree from the root to a leaf by evaluating the query point at each split.

f16eb7ab4b5f.title: Nearest neighbor search
f16eb7ab4b5f.sentence: For constant dimension query time, average complexity is O(log N) in the case of randomly distributed points, worst case complexity is O(kN^(1-1/k)) Alternatively the R-tree data structure was designed to support nearest neighbor search in dynamic context, as it has efficient algorithms for insertions and deletions such as the R* tree.

c8907804e946.title: Nearest neighbor search
c8907804e946.sentence: The informal observation usually referred to as the curse of dimensionality states that there is no general-purpose exact solution for NNS in high-dimensional Euclidean space using polynomial preprocessing and polylogarithmic search time.

66a5b564cbdf.title: Nearest neighbor search
66a5b564cbdf.section: Methods > Approximation methods > Vector approximation files
66a5b564cbdf.sentence: In high-dimensional spaces, tree indexing structures become useless because an increasing percentage of the nodes need to be examined anyway.

869b96464db4.title: Nearest neighbor search
869b96464db4.sentence: Naive search can, on average, outperform space partitioning approaches on higher dimensional spaces.

cad3e3e8ada0.title: Nearest neighbor search
cad3e3e8ada0.sentence: An approximate nearest neighbor search algorithm is allowed to return points whose distance from the query is at most c times the distance from the query to its nearest points.

9b989ed1b880.title: Nearest neighbor search
9b989ed1b880.sentence: The appeal of this approach is that, in many cases, an approximate nearest neighbor is almost as good as the exact one.

143f88b2f46d.title: Nearest neighbor search
143f88b2f46d.sentence: In those cases, we can use an algorithm which doesn't guarantee to return the actual nearest neighbor in every case, in return for improved speed or memory savings.

6240cec3c910.title: Nearest neighbor search
6240cec3c910.section: Methods > Approximation methods > Greedy search in proximity neighborhood graphs
6240cec3c910.sentence: Proximity graph methods (such as navigable small world graphs and HNSW) are considered the current state-of-the-art for the approximate nearest neighbors search.

da9cb7683baf.title: Nearest neighbor search
da9cb7683baf.section: Methods > Approximation methods > Greedy search in proximity neighborhood graphs
da9cb7683baf.sentence: The basic algorithm – greedy search – works as follows: search starts from an enter-point vertex vi∈V by computing the distances from the query q to each vertex of its neighborhood {vj:(vi,vj)∈E}, and then finds a vertex with the minimal distance value.

931e36118f40.title: Nearest neighbor search
931e36118f40.section: Methods > Approximation methods > Greedy search in proximity neighborhood graphs
931e36118f40.sentence: The algorithm stops when it reaches a local minimum: a vertex whose neighborhood does not contain a vertex that is closer to the query than the vertex itself.

eb434ea55c47.title: Nearest neighbor search
eb434ea55c47.sentence: Locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) is a technique for grouping points in space into 'buckets' based on some distance metric operating on the points.

43844888b452.title: Nearest neighbor search
43844888b452.sentence: Points that are close to each other under the chosen metric are mapped to the same bucket with high probability.

476627fa2167.title: Nearest neighbor search
476627fa2167.section: Methods > Approximation methods > Vector approximation files

5e52654682ff.sentence: The final candidates are determined in a second stage using the uncompressed data from the disk for distance calculation.

50dd961009b7.sentence: How do we find nearby restaurants on Yelp or Google Maps?

1a5c4339e9cb.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md
1a5c4339e9cb.sentence: - Given a radius and location, return a list of nearby restaurants

a90e720a20fa.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md
a90e720a20fa.sentence: There are two key services (see the diagram below):

5fd230c08570.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md
5fd230c08570.sentence: Store the latitude and longitude of restaurants in the database?

f7aa5beb2d16.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md
f7aa5beb2d16.sentence: The query will be very inefficient when you need to calculate the distance between you and every restaurant.

7dd1082fcee9.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md
7dd1082fcee9.sentence: One way to speed up the search is using the geohash algorithm.

35a6e0eaeecf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md
35a6e0eaeecf.sentence: First, divide the planet into four quadrants along with the prime meridian and equator：

8308c0a0a739.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md

a696c197d30d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md

f4bd928262d7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md

a54b8e68dce0.sentence: SELECT * FROM geohash_index WHERE geohash LIKE `01%`

0a05fc9e2a04.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/proximity-service.md
0a05fc9e2a04.sentence: There can be a lot of restaurants in one grid (downtown New York), but none in another grid (ocean).

ba05181edcf1.title: Dynamic pricing
ba05181edcf1.sentence: Dynamic pricing, also referred to as surge pricing, demand pricing, time-based pricing and variable pricing, is a revenue management pricing strategy in which businesses set flexible prices for products or services based on current market demands.

35255d6a7e16.title: Dynamic pricing
35255d6a7e16.sentence: It usually entails raising prices during periods of peak demand and lowering prices during periods of low demand.

b739627c5197.title: Dynamic pricing
b739627c5197.sentence: As a pricing strategy, it encourages consumers to make purchases during periods of low demand (such as buying tickets well in advance of an event or buying meals outside of lunch and dinner rushes) and disincentivizes them during periods of high demand (such as using less electricity during peak electricity hours).

ae573f596110.title: Dynamic pricing
ae573f596110.sentence: In some sectors, economists have characterized dynamic pricing as improving welfare relative to uniform pricing and contributing to the more efficient allocation of limited resources.

9cf3c0736b31.title: Dynamic pricing
9cf3c0736b31.sentence: Algorithmic pricing is the practice of automatically setting the requested price for items for sale, in order to maximize the seller's profits.

8330ed4ae602.title: Dynamic pricing
8330ed4ae602.sentence: Dynamic pricing algorithms usually rely on one or more of the following data.

08bbe812bc1b.title: Dynamic pricing
08bbe812bc1b.sentence: - Probabilistic and statistical information on potential buyers; see Bayesian-optimal pricing.

aa70775d5c12.title: Dynamic pricing
aa70775d5c12.sentence: - Personal information of the currently active buyer, such as her or his demographics and her or his interest in the product.

49f41afbb066.title: Dynamic pricing
49f41afbb066.sentence: - Business information of the seller, such as the expected date in which he or she is going to receive new stocks, or her or his target selling velocity in units per day.

4507ac5f2dd1.title: Dynamic pricing
4507ac5f2dd1.sentence: Many industries, especially online retailers, change prices depending on the time of day.

31e87eadcaa8.title: Dynamic pricing
31e87eadcaa8.sentence: A store will simply charge consumers the cost required to produce a product plus a predetermined amount of profit.

321d6b9ab78c.title: Dynamic pricing
321d6b9ab78c.sentence: Businesses that want to price competitively will monitor their competitors' prices and adjust accordingly.

9f33252f1957.title: Dynamic pricing
9f33252f1957.section: Methods > Pricing based on value or elasticity
9f33252f1957.sentence: However, consumers' willingness to pay can be used as a proxy for the perceived value.

ae20f0c21d67.title: Dynamic pricing
ae20f0c21d67.section: Methods > Pricing based on value or elasticity
ae20f0c21d67.sentence: Products with high elasticities are highly sensitive to changes in price, while products with low elasticities are less sensitive to price changes (ceteris paribus).

a9056d91f2fe.title: Dynamic pricing
a9056d91f2fe.sentence: Dynamic pricing is often criticized as price gouging.

66206cb2fed2.title: Dynamic pricing
66206cb2fed2.sentence: After this incident, the company started placing caps on how high surge pricing can go during times of emergency, starting in 2015.

2d262e0af51e.title: Dynamic pricing
2d262e0af51e.sentence: Drivers have been known to hold off on accepting rides in an area until surge pricing forces fares up to a level satisfactory to them.

031c41df0260.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
031c41df0260.sentence: We will design our system for two types of users: Customers and Drivers.

51d42519a73d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
51d42519a73d.sentence: - Customers should be able to see all the cabs in the vicinity with an ETA and pricing information.

cc5b4a87da57.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
cc5b4a87da57.sentence: - Customers should be able to book a cab to a destination.

a7fa08bd723a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
a7fa08bd723a.sentence: - Customers should be able to see the location of the driver.

630dc78d84f6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
630dc78d84f6.sentence: - Drivers should be able to accept or deny the customer-requested ride.

7d64dc382d2e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
7d64dc382d2e.sentence: - Once a driver accepts the ride, they should see the pickup location of the customer.

2cd351ade2f3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
2cd351ade2f3.sentence: - Drivers should be able to mark the trip as complete on reaching the destination.

d76ecabb64df.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
d76ecabb64df.sentence: - The system should be scalable and efficient.

159b5cb27d1e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
159b5cb27d1e.sentence: - Customers can rate the trip after it's completed.

ee684c551071.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
ee684c551071.sentence: Let us assume we have 100 million daily active users (DAU) with 1 million drivers and on average our platform enables 10 million rides daily.

44e926e6c70b.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
44e926e6c70b.sentence: If on average each user performs 10 actions (such as request a check available rides, fares, book rides, etc.) we will have to handle 1 billion requests daily.

5637fdbe2ac1.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
5637fdbe2ac1.sentence: 1 billion requests per day translate into 12K requests per second.

fc8ff3850a59.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
fc8ff3850a59.sentence: If we assume each message on average is 400 bytes, we will require about 400 GB of database storage every day.

b75979af4340.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
b75979af4340.sentence: And for 10 years, we will require about 1.4 PB of storage.

7dd973820d87.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
7dd973820d87.sentence: As our system is handling 400 GB of ingress every day, we will require a minimum bandwidth of around 5 MB per second.

0e553ab8c6b0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
0e553ab8c6b0.sentence: This table will contain a customer's information such as name, email, and other details.

4d3a896accee.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
4d3a896accee.sentence: This table will contain a driver's information such as name, email, dob and other details.

81ab589a81ed.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
81ab589a81ed.sentence: This table represents the trip taken by the customer and stores data such as source, destination, and status of the trip.

4873d099cc9e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
4873d099cc9e.sentence: This table stores data such as the registration number, and type (like Uber Go, Uber XL, etc.) of the cab that the driver will be driving.

78f96336b832.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
78f96336b832.sentence: As the name suggests, this table stores the rating and feedback for the trip.

de01e7bc7ce3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
de01e7bc7ce3.sentence: The payments table contains the payment-related data with the corresponding tripID.

7115104c01ab.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
7115104c01ab.section: Data model design > What kind of database should we use?
7115104c01ab.sentence: While our data model seems quite relational, we don't necessarily need to store everything in a single database, as this can limit our scalability and quickly become a bottleneck.

525ceb28095c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
525ceb28095c.section: Data model design > What kind of database should we use?
525ceb28095c.sentence: We will split the data between different services each having ownership over a particular table.

bf5744cbe084.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
bf5744cbe084.section: Data model design > What kind of database should we use?
bf5744cbe084.sentence: Then we can use a relational database such as PostgreSQL or a distributed NoSQL database such as Apache Cassandra for our use case.

6fc0e59583e4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
6fc0e59583e4.sentence: Through this API, customers will be able to request a ride.

851c9296b1ad.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber

a843e1c6fa4d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber

e85cace31b3b.section: API design > Accept or Deny the Ride
e85cace31b3b.sentence: This API will allow the driver to accept or deny the trip.

85b401de3272.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
85b401de3272.section: API design > Accept or Deny the Ride
