2153ae2fb1e2.sentence: Using this API, a driver will be able to start and end the trip.

c6c4781ecc3c.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
c6c4781ecc3c.section: API design > Start or End the Trip
c6c4781ecc3c.sentence: Trip ID (UUID): ID of the requested trip.

627985a3a863.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
627985a3a863.sentence: This API will enable customers to rate the trip.

bc2df8f258c4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
bc2df8f258c4.sentence: We will be using microservices architecture since it will make it easier to horizontally scale and decouple our services.

eba3b789ca05.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
eba3b789ca05.sentence: Each service will have ownership of its own data model.

b0a3351e08f3.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
b0a3351e08f3.sentence: This service will be responsible for ride matching and quadtree aggregation.

b320c3751616.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
b320c3751616.sentence: Generally, REST or HTTP performs well but we can further improve the performance using gRPC which is more lightweight and efficient.

7c39b6d630b6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
7c39b6d630b6.sentence: Service discovery is another thing we will have to take into account.

f5849010517e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
f5849010517e.section: High-level design > How is the service expected to work?
f5849010517e.sentence: - Customer requests a ride by specifying the source, destination, cab type, payment method, etc.

b5c354353d97.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
b5c354353d97.section: High-level design > How is the service expected to work?
b5c354353d97.sentence: - Ride service registers this request, finds nearby drivers, and calculates the estimated time of arrival (ETA).

089ff88cebef.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
089ff88cebef.section: High-level design > How is the service expected to work?
089ff88cebef.sentence: - The request is then broadcasted to the nearby drivers for them to accept or deny.

0f4460fe7a0e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
0f4460fe7a0e.section: High-level design > How is the service expected to work?
0f4460fe7a0e.sentence: - If the driver accepts, the customer is notified about the live location of the driver with the estimated time of arrival (ETA) while they wait for pickup.

4a728d967730.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
4a728d967730.sentence: The client can periodically send an HTTP request to servers to report its current location and receive ETA and pricing information.

fa80e06e8c3e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
fa80e06e8c3e.sentence: This can be achieved via something like Long polling.

89ff1bdb5107.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
89ff1bdb5107.sentence: The pull model approach is not scalable as it will create unnecessary request overhead on our servers and most of the time the response will be empty, thus wasting our resources.

6f3d107a23cc.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
6f3d107a23cc.sentence: To minimize latency, using the push model with WebSockets is a better choice because then we can push data to the client once it's available without any delay, given that the connection is open with the client.

23bf61803aab.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
23bf61803aab.sentence: Also, WebSockets provide full-duplex communication, unlike Server-Sent Events (SSE) which are only unidirectional.

a216f0a23f19.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
a216f0a23f19.sentence: We already have access to the latitude and longitude of our customers, and with databases like PostgreSQL and MySQL we can perform a query to find nearby driver locations given a latitude and longitude (X, Y) within a radius (R).

7490d876c58d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
7490d876c58d.sentence: However, this is not scalable, and performing this query on large datasets will be quite slow.

2b65d64fc027.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
2b65d64fc027.sentence: Geohashing is a geocoding method used to encode geographic coordinates such as latitude and longitude into short alphanumeric strings.

32a4fa53e3a6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
32a4fa53e3a6.sentence: Geohash is a hierarchical spatial index that uses Base-32 alphabet encoding, the first character in a geohash identifies the initial location as one of the 32 cells.

fee15bce3fc6.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
fee15bce3fc6.sentence: Now, using the customer's geohash we can determine the nearest available driver by simply comparing it with the driver's geohash.

466e1453d95d.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
466e1453d95d.sentence: For better performance, we will index and store the geohash of the driver in memory for faster retrieval.

bff0b165d55a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
bff0b165d55a.sentence: A Quadtree is a tree data structure in which each internal node has exactly four children.

4537fdab3bb8.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
4537fdab3bb8.sentence: They are often used to partition a two-dimensional space by recursively subdividing it into four quadrants or regions.

b7bbb6a19c1e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
b7bbb6a19c1e.sentence: Quadtrees enable us to search points within a two-dimensional range efficiently, where those points are defined as latitude/longitude coordinates or as cartesian (x, y) coordinates.

df2f9efaeebe.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
df2f9efaeebe.sentence: We can save further computation by only subdividing a node after a certain threshold.

eb5dfda13433.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
eb5dfda13433.sentence: Quadtree seems perfect for our use case, we can update the Quadtree every time we receive a new location update from the driver.

89d65d9dbb26.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
89d65d9dbb26.sentence: To reduce the load on the quadtree servers we can use an in-memory datastore such as Redis to cache the latest updates.

7f8b67e464a4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
7f8b67e464a4.sentence: Race conditions can easily occur when a large number of customers will be requesting rides simultaneously.

6679d7cbb7bd.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
6679d7cbb7bd.sentence: To avoid this, we can wrap our ride matching logic in a Mutex to avoid any race conditions.

200804fe4724.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
200804fe4724.sentence: Furthermore, every action should be transactional in nature.

790198923838.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
790198923838.sentence: Once we have a list of nearby drivers from the Quadtree servers, we can perform some sort of ranking based on parameters like average ratings, relevance, past customer feedback, etc. This will allow us to broadcast notifications to the best available drivers first.

21f403aa0539.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
21f403aa0539.sentence: In cases of high demand, we can use the concept of Surge Pricing.

23bdf920fd36.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
23bdf920fd36.sentence: Surge pricing is a dynamic pricing method where prices are temporarily increased as a reaction to increased demand and mostly limited supply.

2fb8bf1f8ed0.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
2fb8bf1f8ed0.sentence: Handling payments at scale is challenging, to simplify our system we can use a third-party payment processor like Stripe or PayPal.

8f16c16886bb.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
8f16c16886bb.sentence: Once the payment is complete, the payment processor will redirect the user back to our application and we can set up a webhook to capture all the payment-related data.

088654072972.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
088654072972.sentence: We can use a message queue or a message broker such as Apache Kafka with the notification service to dispatch requests to Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) or Apple Push Notification Service (APNS) which will handle the delivery of the push notifications to user devices.

095dbcfe0e4f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
095dbcfe0e4f.sentence: We can shard our database either based on existing partition schemes or regions.

b0c49cf8f37e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
b0c49cf8f37e.sentence: If we divide the locations into regions using let's say zip codes, we can effectively store all the data in a given region on a fixed node.

e6ce4d508d76.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
e6ce4d508d76.sentence: But this can still cause uneven data and load distribution, we can solve this using Consistent hashing.

96e460ed0591.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
96e460ed0591.sentence: We have to be able to cache the recent locations of the customers and drivers for fast retrieval.

d89f17381c74.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
d89f17381c74.sentence: We can use solutions like Redis or Memcached but what kind of cache eviction policy would best fit our needs?

8803779782e4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
8803779782e4.sentence: Whenever there is a cache miss, our servers can hit the database directly and update the cache with the new entries.

c1a0dcbbf091.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
c1a0dcbbf091.sentence: Let us identify and resolve bottlenecks such as single points of failure in our design:

b57961a3208e.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
b57961a3208e.sentence: - Running multiple instances of each of our services.

c348bdf8d47a.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
c348bdf8d47a.sentence: - Introducing load balancers between clients, servers, databases, and cache servers.

4806241d05a4.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
4806241d05a4.sentence: - Using multiple read replicas for our databases.

5c36cd90787f.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
5c36cd90787f.sentence: - Multiple instances and replicas for our distributed cache.

e2258845c8b9.title: gh>karanpratapsingh/system-design/README.md::uber
e2258845c8b9.sentence: - Exactly once delivery and message ordering is challenging in a distributed system, we can use a dedicated message broker such as Apache Kafka or NATS to make our notification system more robust.

f7777cd50d4b.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/uber-tech-stack.md
f7777cd50d4b.sentence: Web frontend: Uber builds Fusion.js as a modern React framework to create robust web applications.

a37f7b8f8c4e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/uber-tech-stack.md
a37f7b8f8c4e.sentence: The service uses gRPC and QUIC for client-server communication, and Apache Thrift for API definition.

8a520acd9aed.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/uber-tech-stack.md
8a520acd9aed.sentence: Database end: the OLTP mainly uses the strongly-consistent DocStore, which employs MySQL and PostgreSQL, along with the RocksDB database engine.

3cf0029d3a9c.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/uber-tech-stack.md
3cf0029d3a9c.sentence: They also develop visualization.js for geospatial visualization scenarios.

2264b0967220.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/uber-tech-stack.md
2264b0967220.sentence: Mobile side: Uber builds the RIB cross-platform with the VIPER architecture instead of MVC.

35070d98902a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/uber-tech-stack.md
35070d98902a.sentence: This architecture can work with different languages: Swift for iOS, and Java for Android.

5da8a37fcbf7.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/uber-tech-stack.md

a8c4fd8033fa.title: Web crawler
a8c4fd8033fa.sentence: A web crawler, sometimes called a spider or spiderbot and often shortened to crawler, is an Internet bot that systematically browses the World Wide Web and that is typically operated by search engines for the purpose of Web indexing (web spidering).

0410203bfb0f.title: Web crawler
0410203bfb0f.sentence: A web crawler starts with a list of URLs to visit.

71aa74279902.title: Web crawler
71aa74279902.sentence: Those first URLs are called the seeds.

14a14d378ae6.title: Web crawler
14a14d378ae6.sentence: As the crawler visits these URLs, by communicating with web servers that respond to those URLs, it identifies all the hyperlinks in the retrieved web pages and adds them to the list of URLs to visit, called the crawl frontier.

10cf4d9b4ac6.title: Web crawler
10cf4d9b4ac6.sentence: URLs from the frontier are recursively visited according to a set of policies.

f64d938a44d3.title: Web crawler
f64d938a44d3.sentence: The behavior of a web crawler is the outcome of a combination of policies:

d6df7105a960.title: Web crawler
d6df7105a960.sentence: - a selection policy which states the pages to download

90ca1f954053.title: Web crawler
90ca1f954053.sentence: - a re-visit policy which states when to check for changes to the pages

4ae14babcfae.title: Web crawler
4ae14babcfae.sentence: - a politeness policy that states how to avoid overloading websites

72147251fd8d.title: Web crawler
72147251fd8d.sentence: - a parallelization policy that states how to coordinate distributed web crawlers

146f155a1cc0.title: Web crawler
146f155a1cc0.sentence: The large volume implies the crawler can only download a limited number of the Web pages within a given time, so it needs to prioritize its downloads.

9aac34b76b1c.title: Web crawler
9aac34b76b1c.sentence: The high rate of change can imply the pages might have already been updated or even deleted.

e95f73d9da57.title: Web crawler
e95f73d9da57.sentence: The number of possible URLs crawled being generated by server-side software has also made it difficult for web crawlers to avoid retrieving duplicate content.

6964eb2bcb8e.title: Web crawler
6964eb2bcb8e.sentence: Endless combinations of HTTP GET (URL-based) parameters exist, of which only a small selection will actually return unique content.

66fe485aad54.title: Web crawler
66fe485aad54.sentence: If there exist four ways to sort images, three choices of thumbnail size, two file formats, and an option to disable user-provided content, then the same set of content can be accessed with 48 different URLs, all of which may be linked on the site.

c2ad99bc8983.title: Web crawler
c2ad99bc8983.sentence: A parallel crawler is a crawler that runs multiple processes in parallel.

a430c4876a5c.title: Web crawler
a430c4876a5c.sentence: The goal is to maximize the download rate while minimizing the overhead from parallelization and to avoid repeated downloads of the same page.

cf882b37051b.title: Web crawler
cf882b37051b.sentence: To avoid downloading the same page more than once, the crawling system requires a policy for assigning the new URLs discovered during the crawling process, as the same URL can be found by two different crawling processes.

eef41c21c8ef.title: Web crawler
eef41c21c8ef.sentence: Web crawlers typically identify themselves to a Web server by using the User-agent field of an HTTP request.

b0c8f3b71c83.title: Web crawler
b0c8f3b71c83.sentence: Web site administrators typically examine their Web servers' log and use the user agent field to determine which crawlers have visited the web server and how often.

ec0e9462aced.title: Robots.txt
ec0e9462aced.sentence: The Robots Exclusion Protocol (often referred to by the filename used to implement it, robots.txt) is a standard used by websites to indicate to visiting web crawlers and other web robots which portions of the website they are allowed to visit.

8ca7cf2388ea.title: Web crawler
8ca7cf2388ea.sentence: A partial solution to these problems is the robots exclusion protocol, also known as the robots.txt protocol that is a standard for administrators to indicate which parts of their Web servers should not be accessed by crawlers.

a261cffb0f2b.title: Robots.txt
a261cffb0f2b.sentence: A site owner wishing to give instructions to web robots places a text file called robots.txt in the root of the web site hierarchy (e.g. https://www.example.com/robots.txt).

f8c912376e06.title: Robots.txt
f8c912376e06.sentence: Robots that choose to follow the instructions try to fetch this file and read the instructions before fetching any other file from the website.

ee6ff6c17d78.title: Web crawler
ee6ff6c17d78.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
ee6ff6c17d78.sentence: Website owners may instruct crawlers on what resources they are allowed and forbidden to request with the robots.txt file.

f31556b5d161.title: Web crawler
f31556b5d161.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
f31556b5d161.sentence: A crawler can then use that information to choose what links to follow and which to avoid.

0cb9b9ccda9e.title: Robots.txt
0cb9b9ccda9e.sentence: If this file does not exist, web robots assume that the website owner does not wish to place any limitations on crawling the entire site.

b5ec2e3ea0d8.title: Robots.txt
b5ec2e3ea0d8.sentence: Despite the use of the terms allow and disallow, the protocol is purely advisory and relies on the compliance of the web robot; it cannot enforce any of what is stated in the file.

becb4bb0216c.title: Robots.txt
becb4bb0216c.sentence: The standard, developed in 1994, relies on voluntary compliance.

2587ac9a02df.title: Robots.txt
2587ac9a02df.sentence: Malicious web robots are unlikely to honor robots.txt; some may even use the robots.txt as a guide to find disallowed links and go straight to them.

49729b60aec9.title: Robots.txt
49729b60aec9.sentence: While this is sometimes claimed to be a security risk, this sort of security through obscurity is discouraged by standards bodies.

8dd35607751e.title: Robots.txt
8dd35607751e.sentence: A proposed standard was published in September 2022 as RFC 9309.

2ec29a89d5d7.title: Robots.txt
2ec29a89d5d7.section: Meta tags and headers > Maximum size of a robots.txt file
2ec29a89d5d7.sentence: The Robots Exclusion Protocol requires crawlers to parse at least 500 kibibytes (512000 bytes) of robots.txt files, which Google maintains as a 500 kibibyte file size restriction for robots.txt files.

6ce3bf733137.title: Robots.txt
6ce3bf733137.section: The use of the wildcard * in rules
6ce3bf733137.sentence: The directive Disallow: /something/ blocks all files and subdirectories starting with /something/.

1d76e837d682.title: Robots.txt
1d76e837d682.section: The use of the wildcard * in rules
1d76e837d682.sentence: In contrast, using a wildcard (if supported by the crawler) allows for more complex patterns in specifying paths and files to allow or disallow from crawling, for example Disallow: /something/*/other blocks URLs such as:

cbed2aeb7e7a.title: Robots.txt
cbed2aeb7e7a.section: The use of the wildcard * in rules
cbed2aeb7e7a.sentence: The wildcard * allows greater flexibility but, although it is part of the Robots Exclusion Protocol (RFC), may not be recognized by all crawlers.

1c484782e971.title: Robots.txt
1c484782e971.sentence: Some crawlers support a Sitemap directive, allowing multiple Sitemaps in the same robots.txt in the form Sitemap: full-url:

d820066717de.title: Web crawler
d820066717de.sentence: This standard does not include a suggestion for the interval of visits to the same server, even though this interval is the most effective way of avoiding server overload.

a9ed2d11ba50.title: Web crawler
a9ed2d11ba50.sentence: Search are able to use an extra "Crawl-delay:" parameter in the robots.txt file to indicate the number of seconds to delay between requests.

ff9333d77098.title: Robots.txt
ff9333d77098.sentence: Since this value is not part of the standard, its interpretation is dependent on the crawler reading it.

c2d75a77b912.title: Robots.txt
c2d75a77b912.sentence: Yandex interprets the value as the number of seconds to wait between subsequent visits.

66c4e8aad024.title: Robots.txt
66c4e8aad024.sentence: Bing defines crawl-delay as the size of a time window (from 1 to 30 seconds) during which BingBot will access a web site only once.

0ef7a672342b.title: Robots.txt
0ef7a672342b.sentence: Google ignores this directive, but provides an interface in its search console for webmasters, to control the Googlebot's subsequent visits.

e3ea55aa348f.title: Robots.txt
e3ea55aa348f.sentence: In addition to root-level robots.txt files, robots exclusion directives can be applied at a more granular level through the use of Robots meta tags and X-Robots-Tag HTTP headers.

02c1b35390aa.title: Robots.txt
02c1b35390aa.section: Meta tags and headers > A "noindex" HTTP response header
02c1b35390aa.sentence: The X-Robots-Tag is only effective after the page has been requested and the server responds, and the robots meta tag is only effective after the page has loaded, whereas robots.txt is effective before the page is requested.

977670088ca9.title: Robots.txt
977670088ca9.section: Meta tags and headers > A "noindex" HTTP response header
977670088ca9.sentence: Thus if a page is excluded by a robots.txt file, any robots meta tags or X-Robots-Tag headers are effectively ignored because the robot will not see them in the first place.

02f257d0f596.title: gh>donnemartin/system-design-primer/solutions/system_design/web_crawler/README.md
02f257d0f596.section: Step 3: Design core components > Determining when to update the crawl results
02f257d0f596.sentence: We might also choose to support a Robots.txt file that gives webmasters control of crawl frequency.

6dff642e64b0.title: Web crawler
6dff642e64b0.sentence: Crawlers can retrieve data much quicker and in greater depth than human searchers, so they can have a crippling impact on the performance of a site.

7300363acecc.title: Web crawler
7300363acecc.sentence: If a single crawler is performing multiple requests per second and/or downloading large files, a server can have a hard time keeping up with requests from multiple crawlers.

6440cac41130.title: Web crawler
6440cac41130.sentence: - network resources, as crawlers require considerable bandwidth and operate with a high degree of parallelism during a long period of time;

742f36129069.title: Web crawler
742f36129069.sentence: - server overload, especially if the frequency of accesses to a given server is too high;

dcc96d089d6b.title: Web crawler
dcc96d089d6b.sentence: - poorly written crawlers, which can crash servers or routers, or which download pages they cannot handle; and

4218e6064161.title: Web crawler
4218e6064161.sentence: Recently commercial search engines like Google, Ask Jeeves, MSN and Yahoo!

962e5474948a.title: Web crawler
962e5474948a.sentence: The first proposed interval between successive page loads was 60 seconds.

a1d64ca4915b.title: Web crawler
a1d64ca4915b.sentence: However, if pages were downloaded at this rate from a website with more than 100,000 pages over a perfect connection with zero latency and infinite bandwidth, it would take more than 2 months to download only that entire Web site; also, only a fraction of the resources from that Web server would be used.

b96a42bd04b3.title: Web crawler
b96a42bd04b3.sentence: Cho uses 10 seconds as an interval for accesses, and the WIRE crawler uses 15 seconds as the default.

d113d329a1bc.title: Web crawler
d113d329a1bc.sentence: The MercatorWeb crawler follows an adaptive politeness policy: if it took t seconds to download a document from a given server, the crawler waits for 10t seconds before downloading the next page.

3970b598c138.title: Web crawler
3970b598c138.sentence: From the search engine's point of view, there is a cost associated with not detecting an event, and thus having an outdated copy of a resource.

b444b93832bc.title: Web crawler
b444b93832bc.sentence: The Web has a very dynamic nature, and crawling a fraction of the Web can take weeks or months.

02a628297d96.title: Web crawler
02a628297d96.sentence: By the time a web crawler has finished its crawl, many events could have happened, including creations, updates, and deletions.

631b9dce5f3a.title: Web crawler
631b9dce5f3a.sentence: The most-used cost functions are freshness and age.

2b195271310e.title: Web crawler
2b195271310e.sentence: Freshness: This is a binary measure that indicates whether the local copy is accurate or not.

683b6bdf30e3.title: Web crawler
683b6bdf30e3.sentence: Age: This is a measure that indicates how outdated the local copy is.

22cbb74da3d8.title: Web crawler
22cbb74da3d8.sentence: - Uniform policy: This involves re-visiting all pages in the collection with the same frequency, regardless of their rates of change.

50ee28458a9a.title: Web crawler
50ee28458a9a.sentence: - Proportional policy: This involves re-visiting more often the pages that change more frequently.

5d7bb339b0cd.title: Web crawler
5d7bb339b0cd.sentence: The visiting frequency is directly proportional to the (estimated) change frequency.

7b0840e8de03.title: Web crawler
7b0840e8de03.sentence: Cho and Garcia-Molina proved the surprising result that, in terms of average freshness, the uniform policy outperforms the proportional policy in both a simulated Web and a real web crawl.

d076374a22fe.title: Web crawler
d076374a22fe.sentence: Intuitively, the reasoning is that, as web crawlers have a limit to how many pages they can crawl in a given time frame, (1) they will allocate too many new crawls to rapidly changing pages at the expense of less frequently updating pages, and (2) the freshness of rapidly changing pages lasts for shorter period than that of less frequently changing pages.

99d2a45eef0e.title: Web crawler
99d2a45eef0e.sentence: In other words, a proportional policy allocates more resources to crawling frequently updating pages, but experiences less overall freshness time from them.

34a876097485.title: Web crawler
34a876097485.sentence: The optimal re-visiting policy is neither the uniform policy nor the proportional policy.

f89ca289a8ae.title: Web crawler
f89ca289a8ae.sentence: The optimal method for keeping average freshness high includes ignoring the pages that change too often, and the optimal for keeping average age low is to use access frequencies that monotonically (and sub-linearly) increase with the rate of change of each page.

4a68bab3d5ec.title: Web crawler
4a68bab3d5ec.sentence: In both cases, the optimal is closer to the uniform policy than to the proportional policy: as Coffman et al. note, "in order to minimize the expected obsolescence time, the accesses to any particular page should be kept as evenly spaced as possible".

8c35f046ef47.title: Web crawler
8c35f046ef47.sentence: Given the current size of the Web, even large search engines cover only a portion of the publicly available part.

702150cdcb90.title: Web crawler
702150cdcb90.sentence: As a crawler always downloads just a fraction of the Web pages, it is highly desirable for the downloaded fraction to contain the most relevant pages and not just a random sample of the Web.

4f4d446f9854.title: Web crawler
4f4d446f9854.sentence: This requires a metric of importance for prioritizing Web pages.

819e4f5bfddc.title: Web crawler
819e4f5bfddc.sentence: A 2009 study showed even large-scale search engines index no more than 40–70% of the indexable Web; a previous study by Steve Lawrence and Lee Giles showed that no search engine indexed more than 16% of the Web in 1999.

3e1392aa54a6.title: Web crawler
3e1392aa54a6.sentence: The importance of a page is a function of its intrinsic quality, its popularity in terms of links or visits, and even of its URL (the latter is the case of vertical search engines restricted to a single top-level domain, or search engines restricted to a fixed Web site).

a8480e5303c1.title: Web crawler
a8480e5303c1.sentence: Designing a good selection policy has an added difficulty: it must work with partial information, as the complete set of Web pages is not known during crawling.

17356f3c9064.title: Web crawler
17356f3c9064.sentence: They found that a breadth-first crawl captures pages with high Pagerank early in the crawl (but they did not compare this strategy against other strategies).

717fb5ca302c.title: Web crawler
717fb5ca302c.sentence: The explanation given by the authors for this result is that "the most important pages have many links to them from numerous hosts, and those links will be found early, regardless of on which host or page the crawl originates."

dd06159cfde9.title: Web crawler
dd06159cfde9.sentence: In OPIC, each page is given an initial sum of "cash" that is distributed equally among the pages it points to.

6030073abcf0.title: Web crawler
6030073abcf0.sentence: It is similar to a PageRank computation, but it is faster and is only done in one step.

c435fdbbab1b.title: Web crawler
c435fdbbab1b.sentence: An OPIC-driven crawler downloads first the pages in the crawling frontier with higher amounts of "cash".

95dca3135d52.title: Web crawler
95dca3135d52.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
95dca3135d52.sentence: A crawler may only want to seek out HTML pages and avoid all other MIME types.

27fce9ba9029.title: Web crawler
27fce9ba9029.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
27fce9ba9029.sentence: In order to request only HTML resources, a crawler may make an HTTP HEAD request to determine a Web resource's MIME type before requesting the entire resource with a GET request.

175812a88c13.title: Web crawler
175812a88c13.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
175812a88c13.sentence: To avoid making numerous HEAD requests, a crawler may examine the URL and only request a resource if the URL ends with certain characters such as.html,.htm,.asp,.aspx,.php,.jsp,.jspx or a slash.

3d5ef1aaeb18.title: Web crawler
3d5ef1aaeb18.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
3d5ef1aaeb18.sentence: This strategy may cause numerous HTML Web resources to be unintentionally skipped.

5dd039554fa4.title: Web crawler
5dd039554fa4.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
5dd039554fa4.sentence: Some crawlers may also avoid requesting any resources that have a "?" in them (are dynamically produced) in order to avoid spider traps that may cause the crawler to download an infinite number of URLs from a Web site.

970987bd858e.title: Web crawler
970987bd858e.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Restricting followed links
970987bd858e.sentence: This strategy is unreliable if the site uses URL rewriting to simplify its URLs.

afe843b63eb0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
afe843b63eb0.sentence: Search engines work through a combination of three core processes:

bf08d3210867.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
bf08d3210867.sentence: Search engines use automated programs called "crawlers" to discover and download web pages from the internet.

7d5dc56a95a0.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
7d5dc56a95a0.sentence: The information collected by the crawlers is then analyzed and organized into a massive database called an index.

ca1240cd6593.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
ca1240cd6593.sentence: When a user enters a query, the search engine's algorithm sifts through the index to identify the most relevant and helpful pages.

a8fac9b1fa0e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
a8fac9b1fa0e.sentence: These crawlers start with a list of known web pages (seeds) and follow links on those pages to find new ones, creating a vast network of interconnected content.

d7996cffda0a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
d7996cffda0a.sentence: This process involves extracting key elements such as keywords, content type, freshness, language, and other classification signals to understand what each page is about and how relevant it might be to different search queries.

e1dcaa6b2880.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
e1dcaa6b2880.sentence: - Query Analysis: The search engine analyzes the user's query to understand its meaning and intent.

2048d56b8f1a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
2048d56b8f1a.sentence: This includes identifying keywords, recognizing synonyms, and interpreting context.

0ca5aa253b34.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
0ca5aa253b34.sentence: - Retrieval: The search engine retrieves relevant pages from its vast index based on the query analysis.

cdabd7457d90.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
cdabd7457d90.sentence: This involves matching the query's keywords with the indexed content of web pages.

f585cc62d96d.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-search-engines-work.md
f585cc62d96d.sentence: - Ranking: The retrieved pages are then ranked based on their relevance and other factors.

9aa6b7c01996.title: Search engine indexing
9aa6b7c01996.sentence: Search engine indexing is the collecting, parsing, and storing of data to facilitate fast and accurate information retrieval.

de429c57e64e.title: Search engine indexing
de429c57e64e.sentence: Without an index, the search engine would scan every document in the corpus, which would require considerable time and computing power.

9a070a6527c0.title: Search engine indexing
9a070a6527c0.sentence: For example, while an index of 10,000 documents can be queried within milliseconds, a sequential scan of every word in 10,000 large documents could take hours.

523177509289.title: Search engine indexing
523177509289.sentence: The additional computer storage required to store the index, as well as the considerable increase in the time required for an update to take place, are traded off for the time saved during information retrieval.

507cff527a29.title: Search engine indexing
507cff527a29.sentence: Larger services typically perform indexing at a predetermined time interval due to the required time and processing costs, while agent-based search engines index in real time.

4e7189d2532f.title: Search engine indexing
4e7189d2532f.sentence: Major factors in designing a search engine's architecture include:

3aa21cae98af.title: Search engine indexing
3aa21cae98af.sentence: How data enters the index, or how words or subject features are added to the index during text corpus traversal, and whether multiple indexers can work asynchronously.

c59a1be25158.title: Search engine indexing
c59a1be25158.sentence: How to store the index data, that is, whether information should be data compressed or filtered.

b941e783629f.title: Search engine indexing
b941e783629f.sentence: How quickly a word can be found in the inverted index.

3df945329437.title: Search engine indexing
3df945329437.sentence: How the index is maintained over time.

8aefa2fbb4cf.title: Search engine indexing
8aefa2fbb4cf.sentence: Document parsing breaks apart the components (words) of a document or other form of media for insertion into the forward and inverted indices.

6751bb861662.title: Search engine indexing
6751bb861662.sentence: The words found are called tokens, and so, in the context of search engine indexing and natural language processing, parsing is more commonly referred to as tokenization.

6120509dbf7f.title: Search engine indexing
6120509dbf7f.sentence: If the search engine supports multiple languages, a common initial step during tokenization is to identify each document's language; many of the subsequent steps are language dependent (such as stemming and part of speech tagging).

cd18a1af7522.title: Search engine indexing
cd18a1af7522.sentence: If the search engine were to ignore the difference between content and 'markup', extraneous information would be included in the index, leading to poor search results.

66de8668c422.title: Search engine indexing
66de8668c422.section: Document parsing > Challenges in natural language processing
66de8668c422.sentence: Native English speakers may at first consider tokenization to be a straightforward task, but this is not the case with designing a multilingual indexer.

83690ec51695.title: Search engine indexing
83690ec51695.section: Document parsing > Challenges in natural language processing
83690ec51695.sentence: In digital form, the texts of other languages such as Chinese or Japanese represent a greater challenge, as words are not clearly delineated by whitespace.

38c677f63558.title: Search engine indexing
38c677f63558.section: Document parsing > Challenges in natural language processing
38c677f63558.sentence: Language-specific logic is employed to properly identify the boundaries of words, which is often the rationale for designing a parser for each language supported (or for groups of languages with similar boundary markers and syntax).

d9cf295330d4.title: Search engine indexing
d9cf295330d4.sentence: Consider that authors are producers of information, and a web crawler is the consumer of this information, grabbing the text and storing it in a cache (or corpus).

8fea881e9d3e.title: Search engine indexing
8fea881e9d3e.sentence: The forward index is the consumer of the information produced by the corpus, and the inverted index is the consumer of information produced by the forward index.

bf74e9ce613d.title: Search engine indexing
bf74e9ce613d.sentence: This is commonly referred to as a producer-consumer model.

b7cfb0261674.title: Search engine indexing
b7cfb0261674.sentence: The delineation enables asynchronous system processing, which partially circumvents the inverted index update bottleneck.

a14d33da8c84.title: Search engine indexing
a14d33da8c84.sentence: For example, a new document is added to the corpus and the index must be updated, but the index simultaneously needs to continue responding to search queries.

83fe6bfb38f5.title: Search engine indexing
83fe6bfb38f5.sentence: This is a collision between two competing tasks.

d968e0660d9c.title: Search engine indexing
d968e0660d9c.sentence: There are many opportunities for race conditions and coherent faults.

965aadb2a769.title: Search engine indexing
965aadb2a769.sentence: The challenge is magnified when working with distributed storage and distributed processing.

74f4586a02b6.title: Search engine indexing
74f4586a02b6.sentence: This increases the possibilities for incoherency and makes it more difficult to maintain a fully synchronized, distributed, parallel architecture.

fea884156353.title: Search engine indexing
fea884156353.sentence: Given this scenario, an uncompressed index (assuming a non-conflated, simple, index) for 2 billion web pages would need to store 500 billion word entries.

cb8abc785653.title: Search engine indexing
cb8abc785653.sentence: At 1 byte per character, or 5 bytes per word, this would require 2500 gigabytes of storage space alone.

c670f35de7ca.title: Search engine indexing
c670f35de7ca.sentence: Depending on the compression technique chosen, the index can be reduced to a fraction of this size.

b5633f348a4e.title: Search engine indexing
b5633f348a4e.sentence: The tradeoff is the time and processing power required to perform compression and decompression.

fb1d825dd8a6.title: PageRank
fb1d825dd8a6.sentence: PageRank (PR) is an algorithm used by Google Search to rank web pages in their search engine results.

57990466be52.title: PageRank
57990466be52.sentence: PageRank is a link analysis algorithm and it assigns a numerical weighting to each element of a hyperlinked set of documents, such as the World Wide Web, with the purpose of "measuring" its relative importance within the set.

b49866ab1890.title: PageRank
b49866ab1890.sentence: > PageRank works by counting the number and quality of links to a page to determine a rough estimate of how important the website is.

9d62643f1cdd.title: PageRank
9d62643f1cdd.sentence: The underlying assumption is that more important websites are likely to receive more links from other websites.

f0540ab984ce.title: PageRank
f0540ab984ce.sentence: A hyperlink to a page counts as a vote of support.

e03207eaa47d.title: PageRank
e03207eaa47d.sentence: The PageRank of a page is defined recursively and depends on the number and PageRank metric of all pages that link to it ("incoming links").

fce22dd37d21.title: PageRank
fce22dd37d21.sentence: A page that is linked to by many pages with high PageRank receives a high rank itself.

c0e2667c588a.title: PageRank
c0e2667c588a.sentence: A PageRank results from a mathematical algorithm based on the Webgraph, created by all World Wide Web pages as nodes and hyperlinks as edges, taking into consideration authority hubs such as cnn.com or mayoclinic.org.

ed149fd5610e.title: PageRank
ed149fd5610e.sentence: The PageRank algorithm outputs a probability distribution used to represent the likelihood that a person randomly clicking on links will arrive at any particular page.

d08c625a6582.title: PageRank
d08c625a6582.sentence: The PageRank value of a page reflects the chance that the random surfer will land on that page by clicking on a link.

c9704fe22695.title: PageRank
c9704fe22695.sentence: The PageRank transferred from a given page to the targets of its outbound links upon the next iteration is divided equally among all outbound links.

1a617f7655f1.title: PageRank
1a617f7655f1.sentence: In other words, the PageRank conferred by an outbound link is equal to the document's own PageRank score divided by the number of outbound links L().

d5f1d731da37.title: PageRank
d5f1d731da37.sentence: i.e. the PageRank value for a page u is dependent on the PageRank values for each page v contained in the set Bu (the set containing all pages linking to page u), divided by the number L(v) of links from page v.

b079b13fd055.title: PageRank
b079b13fd055.sentence: The probability, at any step, that the person will continue following links is a damping factor d.

f8055d224cec.title: PageRank
f8055d224cec.sentence: The probability that they instead jump to any random page is 1 - d.

3d25da3e7836.title: PageRank
3d25da3e7836.sentence: Various studies have tested different damping factors, but it is generally assumed that the damping factor will be set around 0.85.

19e1b43c2505.title: PageRank
19e1b43c2505.sentence: When calculating PageRank, pages with no outbound links are assumed to link out to all other pages in the collection.

15a3b635f81b.title: PageRank
15a3b635f81b.sentence: The PageRank computations require several passes, called "iterations", through the collection to adjust approximate PageRank values to more closely reflect the theoretical true value.

5e7f76394234.title: PageRank
5e7f76394234.sentence: The iterative method can be viewed as the power iteration method or the power method.

20e07636bcd8.title: PageRank
20e07636bcd8.sentence: Google's founders, in their original paper, reported that the PageRank algorithm for a network consisting of 322 million links (in-edges and out-edges) converges to within a tolerable limit in 52 iterations.

edfd46bc1ba2.title: PageRank
edfd46bc1ba2.sentence: Through this data, they concluded the algorithm can be scaled very well and that the scaling factor for extremely large networks would be roughly linear in log⁡n, where n is the size of the network.

379b376dd3d1.title: PageRank
379b376dd3d1.sentence: One main disadvantage of PageRank is that it favors older pages.

2234edf1d4b4.title: PageRank
2234edf1d4b4.sentence: A new page, even a very good one, will not have many links unless it is part of an existing site (a site being a densely connected set of pages, such as Wikipedia).

6b0f854d82c8.title: PageRank
6b0f854d82c8.sentence: Various strategies to manipulate PageRank have been employed in concerted efforts to improve search results rankings and monetize advertising links.

77b96a910548.title: PageRank
77b96a910548.sentence: Since December 2007, when it started actively penalizing sites selling paid text links, Google has combatted link farms and other schemes designed to artificially inflate PageRank.

f997e5dcb959.title: PageRank
f997e5dcb959.sentence: A Web crawler may use PageRank as one of a number of importance metrics it uses to determine which URL to visit during a crawl of the web.

3860733210bc.title: PageRank
3860733210bc.sentence: Google recalculates PageRank scores each time it crawls the Web and rebuilds its index.

d11ca37ae42e.title: PageRank
d11ca37ae42e.sentence: The SERP rank of a web page is a function not only of its PageRank, but of a relatively large and continuously adjusted set of factors (over 200).

86d92b66dcba.title: Cosine similarity
86d92b66dcba.sentence: In data analysis, cosine similarity is a measure of similarity between two non-zero vectors defined in an inner product space.

336e39bc32db.title: Cosine similarity
336e39bc32db.sentence: Cosine similarity is the cosine of the angle between the vectors; that is, it is the dot product of the vectors divided by the product of their lengths.

836d3343e95d.title: Cosine similarity
836d3343e95d.sentence: It follows that the cosine similarity does not depend on the magnitudes of the vectors, but only on their angle.

66a587479cb2.title: Cosine similarity
66a587479cb2.sentence: The cosine similarity always belongs to the interval [−1,+1].

2a56011b789c.title: Cosine similarity
2a56011b789c.sentence: For example, two proportional vectors have a cosine similarity of +1, two orthogonal vectors have a similarity of 0, and two opposite vectors have a similarity of −1.

29e7398aae95.title: Cosine similarity
29e7398aae95.sentence: For example, in information retrieval and text mining, each word is assigned a different coordinate and a document is represented by the vector of the numbers of occurrences of each word in the document.

71490d763cb5.title: Cosine similarity
71490d763cb5.sentence: Cosine similarity then gives a useful measure of how similar two documents are likely to be, in terms of their subject matter, and independently of the length of the documents.

89e140cd84f3.title: Cosine similarity
89e140cd84f3.sentence: In the case of information retrieval, the cosine similarity of two documents will range from 0→1, since the term frequencies cannot be negative.

3f4b98ff2038.title: Cosine similarity
3f4b98ff2038.sentence: One advantage of cosine similarity is its low complexity, especially for sparse vectors: only the non-zero coordinates need to be considered.

43b3d0ef2bf0.title: Cosine similarity
43b3d0ef2bf0.sentence: By virtue of being proportional to squared Euclidean distance, the cosine distance is not a true distance metric; it does not exhibit the triangle inequality property — or, more formally, the Schwarz inequality — and it violates the coincidence axiom.

b12e65a76ac9.title: Cosine similarity
b12e65a76ac9.sentence: Then the Euclidean distance over the end-points of any two vectors is a proper metric which gives the same ordering as the cosine distance (a monotonic transformation of Euclidean distance; see below) for any comparison of vectors, and furthermore avoids the potentially expensive trigonometric operations required to yield a proper metric.

035e2eadecb4.title: Sitemaps
035e2eadecb4.sentence: Sitemaps is a protocol in XML format meant for a webmaster to inform search engines about URLs on a website that are available for web crawling.

734c00e55932.title: Sitemaps
734c00e55932.sentence: It allows webmasters to include additional information about each URL: when it was last updated, how often it changes, and how important it is in relation to other URLs of the site.

284310cda294.title: Sitemaps
284310cda294.sentence: The Sitemaps protocol is a URL inclusion protocol and complements robots.txt, a URL exclusion protocol.

542e61dc95b7.title: Sitemaps
542e61dc95b7.sentence: This allows search engines to crawl the site more efficiently and to find URLs that may be isolated from the rest of the site's content.

e6f4ea6315b3.title: Sitemaps
e6f4ea6315b3.sentence: - The site is very large and there is a chance for the web crawlers to overlook some of the new or recently updated content

dfe8f4d56c8d.title: Sitemaps
dfe8f4d56c8d.sentence: - When websites have a huge number of pages that are isolated or not well linked together, or

b078d297f34b.title: Sitemaps
b078d297f34b.section: Search engine submission > Limitations for search engine indexing
b078d297f34b.sentence: Sitemaps supplement and do not replace the existing crawl-based mechanisms that search engines already use to discover URLs.

422747ad5e3e.title: Sitemaps
422747ad5e3e.section: Search engine submission > Limitations for search engine indexing
422747ad5e3e.sentence: Using this protocol does not guarantee that web pages will be included in search indexes, nor does it influence the way that pages are ranked in search results.

53369414ee38.title: Sitemaps
53369414ee38.sentence: The Sitemap Protocol format consists of XML tags.

02a4a7f9478f.title: Sitemaps
02a4a7f9478f.sentence: <loc> | Yes | Provides the full URL of the page or sitemap, including the protocol (e.g. http, https) and a trailing slash, if required by the site's hosting server. This value must be shorter than 2,048 characters. Note that ampersands in the URL need to be escaped as &.

dc4548bc0934.title: Sitemaps
dc4548bc0934.sentence: <lastmod> | No | The date that the file was last modified, in ISO 8601 format. This can display the full date and time or, if desired, may simply be the date in the format YYYY-MM-DD.

f6bcd0690511.title: Sitemaps
f6bcd0690511.sentence: <priority> | No | The priority of that URL relative to other URLs on the site. This allows webmasters to suggest to crawlers which pages are considered more important. The valid range is from 0.0 to 1.0, with 1.0 being the most important. The default value is 0.5. Rating all pages on a site with a high priority does not affect search listings, as it is only used to suggest to the crawlers how important pages of the site are to one another. Does not apply to <sitemap> elements.

44faf3b25bea.title: Sitemaps
44faf3b25bea.sentence: Support for the elements that are not required can vary from one search engine to another.

b3707acafb68.title: Sitemaps
b3707acafb68.sentence: Sitemaps can also be just a plain text list of URLs.

093236317fdc.title: Sitemaps
093236317fdc.sentence: They can also be compressed in.gz format.

1a6c61cdcdff.title: Sitemaps
1a6c61cdcdff.sentence: The file specifications of XML Sitemaps apply to text Sitemaps as well; the file must be UTF-8 encoded, and cannot be more than 50MiB (uncompressed) or contain more than 50,000 URLs.

9e0c2a305336.title: Sitemaps
9e0c2a305336.sentence: The maximum sitemap size of 50 MiB (uncompressed) or 50,000 URLs means this is necessary for large sites.

762f77cef3cf.title: Sitemaps
762f77cef3cf.sentence: The Sitemap XML protocol is also extended to provide a way of listing multiple Sitemaps in a sitemap index file.

88d96deca9fa.title: Sitemaps
88d96deca9fa.sentence: Sitemap index files may not list more than 50,000 Sitemaps and must be no larger than 50MiB and can be compressed.

527b17812200.title: Web crawler
527b17812200.sentence: A vast amount of web pages lie in the deep or invisible web.

aeee01359e2d.title: Web crawler
aeee01359e2d.sentence: These pages are typically only accessible by submitting queries to a database, and regular crawlers are unable to find these pages if there are no links that point to them.

fa5f06472a0f.title: Web crawler
fa5f06472a0f.sentence: Google's Sitemaps protocol and mod oai are intended to allow discovery of these deep-Web resources.

3adfeb05474f.title: Web crawler
3adfeb05474f.sentence: Deep web crawling also multiplies the number of web links to be crawled.

cc356e6a4e33.title: Web crawler
cc356e6a4e33.sentence: With a technique called screen scraping, specialized software may be customized to automatically and repeatedly query a given Web form with the intention of aggregating the resulting data.

e41ebcc55f41.title: Web crawler
e41ebcc55f41.sentence: Such software can be used to span multiple Web forms across multiple Websites.

952487bbada2.title: Web crawler
952487bbada2.sentence: Data extracted from the results of one Web form submission can be taken and applied as input to another Web form thus establishing continuity across the Deep Web in a way not possible with traditional web crawlers.

3151cc7018c5.title: Web crawler
3151cc7018c5.sentence: Pages built on AJAX are among those causing problems to web crawlers.

b6a484859779.title: Web crawler
b6a484859779.sentence: Google has proposed a format of AJAX calls that their bot can recognize and index.

e657078a9c5b.title: Web crawler
e657078a9c5b.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Focused crawling
e657078a9c5b.sentence: The importance of a page for a crawler can also be expressed as a function of the similarity of a page to a given query. web crawlers that attempt to download pages that are similar to each other are called focused crawler or topical crawlers.

4471d2422061.title: Web crawler
4471d2422061.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Focused crawling
4471d2422061.sentence: The main problem in focused crawling is that in the context of a web crawler, we would like to be able to predict the similarity of the text of a given page to the query before actually downloading the page.

6822dfd19ce2.title: Web crawler
6822dfd19ce2.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Focused crawling
6822dfd19ce2.sentence: A possible predictor is the anchor text of links; this was the approach taken by Pinkerton in the first web crawler of the early days of the Web.

7e1552588c35.title: Web crawler

7e1552588c35.sentence: Diligenti et al. propose using the complete content of the pages already visited to infer the similarity between the driving query and the pages that have not been visited yet.

63b63e5600fc.title: Web crawler
63b63e5600fc.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > Focused crawling
63b63e5600fc.sentence: The performance of a focused crawling depends mostly on the richness of links in the specific topic being searched, and a focused crawling usually relies on a general Web search engine for providing starting points.

3d7a556f13b8.title: Web crawler
3d7a556f13b8.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > URL normalization
3d7a556f13b8.sentence: The term URL normalization, also called URL canonicalization, refers to the process of modifying and standardizing a URL in a consistent manner.

a152934db589.title: Web crawler
a152934db589.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > URL normalization
a152934db589.sentence: Crawlers usually perform some type of URL normalization in order to avoid crawling the same resource more than once.

b67e90129372.title: Web crawler
b67e90129372.section: Crawling policy > Selection policy > URL normalization
b67e90129372.sentence: There are several types of normalization that may be performed including conversion of URLs to lowercase, removal of "." and ".." segments, and adding trailing slashes to the non-empty path component.

97bf5e8d868e.title: Spider trap
97bf5e8d868e.sentence: A spider trap (or crawler trap) is a set of web pages that may intentionally or unintentionally be used to cause a web crawler or search bot to make an infinite number of requests or cause a poorly constructed crawler to crash.

9c1d2af40574.title: Spider trap
9c1d2af40574.sentence: Spider traps may be created to "catch" spambots or other crawlers that waste a website's bandwidth.

5dd66ff5e699.title: Spider trap
5dd66ff5e699.sentence: They may also be created unintentionally by calendars that use dynamic pages with links that continually point to the next day or year.

c9b5760a893f.title: Spider trap
c9b5760a893f.sentence: - Creation of indefinitely deep directory structures such as http://example.com/abc/def/abc/def/abc/def/abc/...

0601aa9d774a.title: Spider trap
0601aa9d774a.sentence: - Dynamic pages that produce an unbounded number of documents for a web crawler to follow.

537d6f3dadfc.title: Spider trap
537d6f3dadfc.sentence: - Documents filled with many characters, crashing the lexical analyzer parsing the document.

a7b27644ca67.title: Spider trap
a7b27644ca67.sentence: - Documents with session-id's based on required cookies.

8858b59de87d.title: Spider trap
8858b59de87d.sentence: A spider trap causes a web crawler to enter something like an infinite loop, which wastes the spider's resources, lowers its productivity, and, in the case of a poorly written crawler, can crash the program.

4f9f7520e04b.title: Spider trap
4f9f7520e04b.sentence: There exists no universal algorithm capable of detecting all spider traps.

4b2249e0185e.title: Spider trap
4b2249e0185e.sentence: While certain categories of traps can be identified through automated methods, novel and previously unrecognized traps continue to emerge rapidly.

3d9e970f3d95.title: Spider trap
3d9e970f3d95.sentence: In addition, sites with spider traps usually have a robots.txt telling bots not to go to the trap, so a legitimate "polite" bot would not fall into the trap, whereas an "impolite" bot which disregards the robots.txt settings would be affected by the trap.

da1fd80ca498.title: Jaccard index
da1fd80ca498.sentence: The Jaccard index is a statistic used for gauging the similarity and diversity of sample sets.

102ce8051dc0.title: Jaccard index
102ce8051dc0.sentence: The Jaccard index measures similarity between finite non-empty sample sets and is defined as the size of the intersection divided by the size of the union of the sample sets:

760300fa60e4.title: Jaccard index

4b0b56b175d1.title: Heap (data structure)
4b0b56b175d1.sentence: In computer science, a heap is a tree-based data structure that satisfies the heap property: In a max heap, for any given node C, if P is the parent node of C, then the key (the value) of P is greater than or equal to the key of C. In a min heap, the key of P is less than or equal to the key of C.

f744ed6f1ca1.title: Heap (data structure)
f744ed6f1ca1.sentence: In a heap, the highest (or lowest) priority element is always stored at the root.

210b8e5f1c5c.title: Heap (data structure)
210b8e5f1c5c.sentence: However, a heap is not a sorted structure; it can be regarded as being partially ordered.

1f67d8fb6ea6.title: Heap (data structure)
1f67d8fb6ea6.sentence: Note that, as shown in the graphic, there is no implied ordering between siblings or cousins and no implied sequence for an in-order traversal (as there would be in, e.g., a binary search tree).

815fd328ff9b.title: Heap (data structure)
815fd328ff9b.sentence: The heap is one maximally efficient implementation of an abstract data type called a priority queue, and in fact, priority queues are often referred to as "heaps", regardless of how they may be implemented.

7aea59a41720.title: Heap (data structure)
7aea59a41720.sentence: - Priority queue: A priority queue is an abstract concept like "a list" or "a map"; just as a list can be implemented with a linked list or an array, a priority queue can be implemented with a heap or a variety of other methods.

e51c10786207.title: Heap (data structure)
e51c10786207.sentence: A heap is a useful data structure when it is necessary to repeatedly remove the object with the highest (or lowest) priority, or when insertions need to be interspersed with removals of the root node.

7b9a3c076a9d.title: Heap (data structure)

44594bd478a9.title: Heap (data structure)

d135c0c08674.title: Open banking
d135c0c08674.sentence: In financial services, open banking allows for financial data to be shared between banks and third-party service providers through the use of application programming interfaces (APIs).

84275df037d4.title: Open banking
84275df037d4.sentence: Traditionally, banks have kept customer financial data within their own closed systems.

01735646b051.title: Open banking
01735646b051.sentence: Open banking allows customers to share their financial information securely and electronically with other banks or other authorized financial organizations such as payment providers, lenders and insurance companies.

88dd47126ae0.title: Open banking
88dd47126ae0.sentence: In practice, open banking is implemented through standardised application programming interfaces (APIs) that enable authorised third-party providers to access account information or initiate payments on behalf of users, subject to explicit customer consent.

b0c566a31d77.title: Open banking
b0c566a31d77.sentence: Banks are typically required to expose dedicated interfaces for third-party access that are separate from consumer-facing online banking systems, ensuring consistent availability and performance.

9fd3ec587b84.title: Open banking
9fd3ec587b84.sentence: Implementation involves managing consent lifecycles, enforcing access scopes, and applying strong customer authentication to protect customer data and prevent unauthorised access.

7fc4cc6d4a0a.title: Open banking
7fc4cc6d4a0a.sentence: Between 2015 and 2021, a number of countries enacted laws and regulations forcing traditional banks to provide API access to customer data.

b6482e28c625.title: Open banking
b6482e28c625.sentence: In October 2015, the European Parliament adopted a revised Payment Services Directive known as PSD2.

12a8d23264c8.title: Open banking
12a8d23264c8.sentence: In August 2016, the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) issued a ruling that required the nine biggest UK banks – HSBC, Barclays, RBS, Santander, Bank of Ireland, Allied Irish Bank, Danske Bank, Lloyds, and Nationwide – to allow licensed startups direct access to their data, down to the transaction level.

f85625cd6f32.title: Open banking
f85625cd6f32.sentence: With open banking, banks open their APIs to third-party fintech companies, which comes with security risks.

625528af0f44.title: Open banking
625528af0f44.sentence: Hackers can target third-party apps and excessive access privileges could be given to employees.

f0762ed04a6e.title: Open banking
f0762ed04a6e.sentence: Malicious actors may be able to trick banking customers and third-party companies with phishing scams.

5b783d80a71a.title: Open banking
5b783d80a71a.sentence: There are also privacy concerns about open banking.

a1416350a5ee.title: Doubly linked list
a1416350a5ee.sentence: In computer science, a doubly linked list is a linked data structure that consists of a set of sequentially linked records called nodes.

b83782766793.title: Doubly linked list
b83782766793.sentence: Each node contains three fields: two link fields (references to the previous and to the next node in the sequence of nodes) and one data field.

5da29d083406.title: Doubly linked list
5da29d083406.sentence: The two node links allow traversal of the list in either direction.

b881190e74cd.title: Doubly linked list
b881190e74cd.sentence: The first and last nodes of a doubly linked list for all practical applications are immediately accessible (i.e., accessible without traversal, and usually called head and tail) and therefore allow traversal of the list from the beginning or end of the list, respectively: e.g., traversing the list from beginning to end, or from end to beginning, in a search of the list for a node with specific data value.

00fcd01e83d5.title: Doubly linked list
00fcd01e83d5.sentence: Any node of a doubly linked list, once obtained, can be used to begin a new traversal of the list, in either direction (towards beginning or end), from the given node.

e2df37376a55.title: Doubly linked list
e2df37376a55.section: Basic algorithms > Open doubly linked lists > Traversing the list
e2df37376a55.sentence: In fact, the direction of traversal can change many times, if desired.

e94b66c5c9d6.title: Doubly linked list
e94b66c5c9d6.sentence: The beginning and ending nodes' previous and next links, respectively, point to some kind of terminator, typically a sentinel node or null, to facilitate traversal of the list.

fcf9d44f802b.title: Doubly linked list
fcf9d44f802b.sentence: If there is only one sentinel node, then the list is circularly linked via the sentinel node.

e6c1dae71c52.title: Doubly linked list
e6c1dae71c52.sentence: While adding or removing a node in a doubly linked list requires changing more links than the same operations on a singly linked list, the operations are simpler and potentially more efficient (for nodes other than first nodes) because there is no need to keep track of the previous node during traversal or no need to traverse the list to find the previous node, so that its link can be modified.

44624e0c267e.title: Doubly linked list
44624e0c267e.section: Basic algorithms > Open doubly linked lists > Removing a node
44624e0c267e.sentence: Removal of a node is easier than insertion, but requires special handling if the node to be removed is the firstNode or lastNode:

ef2d820c2648.title: Doubly linked list
ef2d820c2648.section: Basic algorithms > Open doubly linked lists > Removing a node
ef2d820c2648.sentence: One subtle consequence of the above procedure is that deleting the last node of a list sets both firstNode and lastNode to null, and so it handles removing the last node from a one-element list correctly.

b2e726a925df.sentence: In graph theory and computer science, an adjacency matrix is a square matrix used to represent a finite graph.

959604b8e9b1.title: Adjacency matrix

5acd97a3ad23.title: Adjacency matrix

d6b92ed1664d.title: Adjacency matrix
d6b92ed1664d.sentence: The diagonal elements of the matrix are all 0, since edges from a vertex to itself (loops) are not allowed in simple graphs.

8f39129915a4.title: Adjacency matrix

3e7f182e07e8.title: Adjacency matrix
3e7f182e07e8.sentence: If the graph is undirected (i.e. all of its edges are bidirectional), the adjacency matrix is symmetric.

4ba584143958.title: Adjacency matrix

d56e80e812b1.title: Adjacency matrix

f65fbd284339.title: Adjacency matrix

95c8075fb5af.title: Adjacency matrix

f5eb2c4a8301.title: Adjacency list

20e95fc97451.title: Adjacency list

a53b2f18ef18.title: Adjacency list

c75876fe2953.title: Adjacency list

bfbf89ee87e8.title: Adjacency list

9a33e72e96be.title: Adjacency list

5f5104732d3e.sentence: Bidirectional search is a graph search algorithm that finds a shortest path from an initial vertex to a goal vertex in a directed graph.

4154ea64f5b8.title: Bidirectional search
4154ea64f5b8.sentence: It runs two simultaneous searches: one forward from the initial state, and one backward from the goal, stopping when the two meet.

e6aa6ca8931b.title: Bidirectional search

136e0d94880b.title: Virtual private cloud
136e0d94880b.sentence: A virtual private cloud (VPC) is an on-demand configurable pool of shared resources allocated within a public cloud environment, providing a certain level of isolation between the different organizations (denoted as users hereafter) using the resources.

b2f1331ec87e.title: Virtual private cloud
b2f1331ec87e.sentence: The isolation between one VPC user and all other users of the same cloud (other VPC users as well as other public cloud users) is achieved normally through allocation of a private IP subnet and a virtual communication construct (such as a VLAN or a set of encrypted communication channels) per user.

6156649014df.title: Virtual private cloud
6156649014df.sentence: With the introduction of the described isolation levels, an organization using this service is in effect working on a "virtually private" cloud (that is, as if the cloud infrastructure is not shared with other users), and hence the name VPC.

46c284ac9f4e.title: Virtual private cloud
46c284ac9f4e.sentence: In a VPC, the previously described mechanism, providing isolation within the cloud, is accompanied with a virtual private network (VPN) function (again, allocated per VPC user) that secures, by means of authentication and encryption, the remote access of the organization to its VPC resources.

4c347d772988.title: Virtual private cloud
4c347d772988.sentence: Amazon Web Services launched Amazon Virtual Private Cloud on 26 August 2009, which allows the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud service to be connected to legacy infrastructure over an IPsec VPN.

566f7d4dc745.title: Virtual private cloud
566f7d4dc745.sentence: With Google Cloud, VPCs are global resources and subnets within that VPC are regional resources.

a616e1bcc1ae.title: Virtual private cloud
a616e1bcc1ae.sentence: This allows users to connect zones and regions without the use of additional networking complexity as all data travels, encrypted in transit and at rest, on Google's own global, private network.

79c6e91e22a7.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
79c6e91e22a7.sentence: The Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is an Internet standard communication protocol for electronic mail transmission.

53e79c40c3f0.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
53e79c40c3f0.sentence: Mail servers and other message transfer agents use SMTP to send and receive mail messages.

dfbeb2ced77d.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
dfbeb2ced77d.sentence: SMTP is a connection-oriented, text-based protocol in which a mail sender communicates with a mail receiver by issuing command strings and supplying necessary data over a reliable ordered data stream channel, typically a Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connection.

a50e9c480afc.title: rfc>5321
a50e9c480afc.sentence: SMTP is independent of the particular transmission subsystem and requires only a reliable ordered data stream channel.

3be218ca5492.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
3be218ca5492.section: Protocol overview > SMTP vs mail retrieval
3be218ca5492.sentence: SMTP is a delivery protocol only.

2f0b3655631e.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
2f0b3655631e.section: Protocol overview > SMTP vs mail retrieval
2f0b3655631e.sentence: In normal use, mail is "pushed" to a destination mail server (or next-hop mail server) as it arrives.

51981cf681f5.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
51981cf681f5.section: Protocol overview > SMTP vs mail retrieval
51981cf681f5.sentence: Mail is routed based on the destination server, not the individual user(s) to which it is addressed.

d9ce9d07dad7.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
d9ce9d07dad7.section: Protocol overview > SMTP vs mail retrieval
d9ce9d07dad7.sentence: Other protocols, such as the Post Office Protocol (POP) and the Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) are specifically designed for use by individual users retrieving messages and managing mailboxes.

562c0a72d01d.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
562c0a72d01d.sentence: An SMTP transaction consists of three command/reply sequences:

09d6c870f2ec.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
09d6c870f2ec.sentence: - MAIL command, to establish the return address, also called return-path, reverse-path, bounce address, mfrom, or envelope sender.

fbeae5533e0b.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
fbeae5533e0b.sentence: - RCPT command, to establish a recipient of the message.

cf679a411565.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
cf679a411565.sentence: This command can be issued multiple times, one for each recipient.

45b71a77b3a6.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
45b71a77b3a6.sentence: - DATA to signal the beginning of the message text; the content of the message, as opposed to its envelope.

028501118e66.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
028501118e66.sentence: DATA is actually a group of commands, and the server replies twice: once to the DATA command itself, to acknowledge that it is ready to receive the text, and the second time after the end-of-data sequence, to either accept or reject the entire message.

db7813ed3a1a.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
db7813ed3a1a.sentence: Besides the intermediate reply for DATA, each server's reply can be either positive (2xx reply codes) or negative.

47061134fa4f.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
47061134fa4f.sentence: Negative replies can be permanent (5xx codes) or transient (4xx codes).

d4798e81f186.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
d4798e81f186.sentence: Communication between mail servers generally uses the standard TCP port 25 designated for SMTP.

acb93f376161.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
acb93f376161.sentence: Email is submitted by a mail client (mail user agent, MUA) to a mail server (mail submission agent, MSA) using SMTP on TCP port 465 or 587.

fbec635e8721.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
fbec635e8721.sentence: The main difference between an MTA and an MSA is that connecting to an MSA requires SMTP Authentication.

3cd30172b968.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
3cd30172b968.sentence: Fully capable SMTP servers maintain queues of messages for retrying message transmissions that resulted in transient failures.

5ecdbc12d8a4.title: rfc>5321
5ecdbc12d8a4.sentence: In either case, once the server has issued a success response at the end of the mail data, a formal handoff of responsibility for the message occurs: the protocol requires that a server MUST accept responsibility for either delivering the message or properly reporting the failure to do so (see Sections 6.1, 6.2, and 7.8, below).

48bcdfc78104.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
48bcdfc78104.sentence: Per RFC 5321 section 2.1, each hop is a formal handoff of responsibility for the message, whereby the receiving server must either deliver the message or properly report the failure to do so.

411608116121.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
411608116121.sentence: SMTP defines message transport, not the message content.

74d37b1a486b.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
74d37b1a486b.sentence: Thus, it defines the mail envelope and its parameters, such as the envelope sender, but not the header (except trace information) nor the body of the message itself.

bad829d07b09.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
bad829d07b09.sentence: STD 10 and RFC 5321 define SMTP (the envelope), while STD 11 and RFC 5322 define the message (header and body), formally referred to as the Internet Message Format.

ddd73dc25741.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
ddd73dc25741.sentence: The original design of SMTP had no facility to authenticate senders, or check that servers were authorized to send on their behalf, with the result that email spoofing is possible, and commonly used in email spam and phishing.

77b19d79ec40.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
77b19d79ec40.section: Outgoing mail SMTP server > Outgoing mail server access restrictions > Client authentication
77b19d79ec40.sentence: Modern SMTP servers typically require authentication of clients by credentials before allowing access, rather than restricting access by location as described earlier.

e70deb58ccf4.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
e70deb58ccf4.sentence: Instead, mail servers now use a range of techniques, such as stricter enforcement of standards such as RFC 5322, DomainKeys Identified Mail, Sender Policy Framework and DMARC, DNSBLs and greylisting to reject or quarantine suspicious emails.

a3df932fc5e0.title: rfc>5322
a3df932fc5e0.sentence: This document specifies the Internet Message Format (IMF), a syntax for text messages that are sent between computer users, within the framework of "electronic mail" messages.

7a4a9ab410ca.title: rfc>5322
7a4a9ab410ca.sentence: A message consists of header fields, optionally followed by a message body.

cc412744f827.title: Email
cc412744f827.sentence: Internet email messages consist of two sections, "header" and "body".

5a040947ace9.title: Email
5a040947ace9.sentence: The header is separated from the body by a blank line.

b74c9717461a.title: Email
b74c9717461a.sentence: The basic Internet message format used for email is defined by RFC 5322, with encoding of non-ASCII data and multimedia content attachments defined in RFC 2045 through RFC 2049, collectively called Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions or MIME.

425a35190bad.title: rfc>5322
425a35190bad.section: 2. Lexical Analysis of Messages > 2.2. Header Fields
425a35190bad.sentence: Header fields are lines beginning with a field name, followed by a colon (":"), followed by a field body, and terminated by CRLF.

3c52fd5475e7.title: rfc>5322
3c52fd5475e7.section: 2. Lexical Analysis of Messages > 2.2. Header Fields > 2.2.3. Long Header Fields
3c52fd5475e7.sentence: For convenience however, and to deal with the 998/78 character limitations per line, the field body portion of a header field can be split into a multiple-line representation; this is called "folding".

8995b10cffda.title: rfc>5322
8995b10cffda.section: 2. Lexical Analysis of Messages > 2.2. Header Fields > 2.2.3. Long Header Fields
8995b10cffda.sentence: Unfolding is accomplished by simply removing any CRLF that is immediately followed by WSP.

e68ddcaada48.title: rfc>5322
e68ddcaada48.section: 2. Lexical Analysis of Messages > 2.1. General Description
e68ddcaada48.sentence: A message that is conformant with this specification is composed of characters with values in the range of 1 through 127 and interpreted as US-ASCII characters.

c313850c49eb.title: rfc>5322
c313850c49eb.section: 2. Lexical Analysis of Messages > 2.1. General Description > 2.1.1. Line Length Limits
c313850c49eb.sentence: Each line of characters MUST be no more than 998 characters, and SHOULD be no more than 78 characters, excluding the CRLF.

bb290ec23f53.title: rfc>5322
bb290ec23f53.sentence: The header fields carry most of the semantic information and are defined in section 3.6.

ddd8c944568a.title: rfc>5322
ddd8c944568a.sentence: The body is simply a series of lines of text that are uninterpreted for the purposes of this specification.

3949ccaa6277.title: rfc>5322
3949ccaa6277.sentence: Note: As was stated earlier, there are other documents, specifically the MIME documents (,,,, ), that extend (and limit) this specification to allow for different sorts of message bodies.

e42b614ea893.title: Email
e42b614ea893.section: Message format > Message header > Header fields
e42b614ea893.sentence: Header fields defined by RFC 5322 contain only US-ASCII characters; for encoding characters in other sets, a syntax specified in RFC 2047 may be used.

50f07dc65d9d.title: Email
50f07dc65d9d.section: Message format > Message body > Content encoding
50f07dc65d9d.sentence: The MIME standard introduced character set specifiers and two content transfer encodings to enable transmission of non-ASCII data: quoted printable for mostly 7-bit content with a few characters outside that range and base64 for arbitrary binary data.

dbcc5a7e08d7.title: Email
dbcc5a7e08d7.section: Message format > Message header > Header fields
dbcc5a7e08d7.sentence: In some examples, the IETF EAI working group defines some standards track extensions, replacing previous experimental extensions so UTF-8 encoded Unicode characters may be used within the header.

6ba94f682aea.title: Email
6ba94f682aea.section: Message format > Message header > Header fields
6ba94f682aea.sentence: The message header must include at least the following fields:

0ed10c7d85c9.title: Email
