934b3499ef9b.section: 2. Protocol Overview > 2.3. Message Attributes > 2.3.1. Message Numbers > 2.3.1.1. Unique Identifier (UID) Message Attribute
934b3499ef9b.sentence: When a message is expunged, its UID MUST NOT be reused under the same UIDVALIDITY value.

e7ad9c7a764e.title: Email
e7ad9c7a764e.sentence: Email spoofing occurs when the email message header is designed to make the message appear to come from a known or trusted source.

decdf8a54e93.title: Email
decdf8a54e93.sentence: Email spam and phishing methods typically use spoofing to mislead the recipient about the true message origin.

6a3627834a61.title: rfc>5321
6a3627834a61.section: 7. Security Considerations > 7.1. Mail Security and Spoofing
6a3627834a61.sentence: SMTP mail is inherently insecure in that it is feasible for even fairly casual users to negotiate directly with receiving and relaying SMTP servers and create messages that will trick a naive recipient into believing that they came from somewhere else.

182f9d6a95a9.title: Email
182f9d6a95a9.sentence: Many email clients allow specifying the From field, and if the sender uses their own software, there is no way of preventing it.

48f65f8e655f.title: Email
48f65f8e655f.sentence: However, the domain owner can specify what servers are allowed to send email with their domain in the From or Sender fields, and email servers can sign email sent through them.

1cb37dcc39df.title: Email
1cb37dcc39df.sentence: These techniques, if implemented, can allow raising flags for spoofed addresses.

3abc008dabcc.title: rfc>5321
3abc008dabcc.section: 3. The SMTP Procedures: An Overview > 3.6. Relaying and Mail Routing > 3.6.2. Mail eXchange Records and Relaying
3abc008dabcc.sentence: Recent work, such as that on SPF and DKIM, has been done to provide ways to ascertain that an address is valid or belongs to the person who actually sent the message.

a07c5115b896.title: Email
a07c5115b896.sentence: This does not, however, in itself protect against misspelled domain names and the like.

37e1c7bff8be.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
37e1c7bff8be.sentence: Mail delivery can occur both over plain text and encrypted connections, however the communicating parties might not know in advance of other party's ability to use secure channel.

3498438f9527.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
3498438f9527.sentence: The SMTP-AUTH extension provides an access control mechanism.

2b1a15823c20.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
2b1a15823c20.sentence: It consists of an authentication step through which the client effectively logs into the mail server during the process of sending mail.

5c6cf66b838c.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
5c6cf66b838c.sentence: SMTP-AUTH can be used to allow legitimate users to relay mail while denying relay service to unauthorized users, such as spammers.

3ae00dc116b6.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
3ae00dc116b6.sentence: It does not necessarily guarantee the authenticity of either the SMTP envelope sender or the RFC 2822 "From:" header.

66278201a701.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
66278201a701.sentence: For example, spoofing, in which one sender masquerades as someone else, is still possible with SMTP-AUTH unless the server is configured to limit message from-addresses to addresses this AUTHed user is authorized for.

92c9c1e228d4.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
92c9c1e228d4.section: SMTP Extensions > Security extensions > STARTTLS or "Opportunistic TLS"
92c9c1e228d4.sentence: The STARTTLS extensions enables supporting SMTP servers to notify connecting clients that it supports TLS encrypted communication and offers the opportunity for clients to upgrade their connection by sending the STARTTLS command.

f30b29cb69b5.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
f30b29cb69b5.section: SMTP Extensions > Security extensions > STARTTLS or "Opportunistic TLS"
f30b29cb69b5.sentence: Servers supporting the extension do not inherently gain any security benefits from its implementation on its own, as upgrading to a TLS encrypted session is dependent on the connecting client deciding to exercise this option, hence the term opportunistic TLS.

d7302740700c.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
d7302740700c.section: SMTP Extensions > Security extensions > STARTTLS or "Opportunistic TLS"
d7302740700c.sentence: STARTTLS is effective only against passive observation attacks, since the STARTTLS negotiation happens in plain text and an active attacker can trivially remove STARTTLS commands.

b81c96ac9450.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
b81c96ac9450.section: SMTP Extensions > Security extensions > STARTTLS or "Opportunistic TLS"
b81c96ac9450.sentence: This type of man-in-the-middle attack is sometimes referred to as STRIPTLS, where the encryption negotiation information sent from one end never reaches the other.

04eb7e838d00.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
04eb7e838d00.sentence: Dijkstra's algorithm (/ˈdaɪk.strəz/, DYKE-strəz) is an algorithm for finding the shortest paths between nodes in a weighted graph, which may represent, for example, a road network.

cf87508ca764.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
cf87508ca764.sentence: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from a given source node to every other node.

24cd5df67ad4.title: Dijkstra's algorithm

018319a4ad4a.title: Dijkstra's algorithm

5f58ffcdc1a2.title: Dijkstra's algorithm

163d7ecb9b2d.title: A* search algorithm
163d7ecb9b2d.sentence: It does so based on the cost of the path and an estimate of the cost required to extend the path all the way to the goal.

7e3df3d4e905.title: A* search algorithm
7e3df3d4e905.sentence: A* is an informed search algorithm, or a best-first search, meaning that it is formulated in terms of weighted graphs: starting from a specific starting node of a graph, it aims to find a path to the given goal node having the smallest cost (least distance travelled, shortest time, etc.).

d941ab5808e2.title: A* search algorithm

5e4eab83d5d9.title: Address geocoding
5e4eab83d5d9.sentence: Address geocoding, or simply geocoding, is the process of taking a text-based description of a location, such as an address or the name of a place, and returning geographic coordinates (typically the latitude/longitude pair) to identify a location on the Earth's surface.

4bf4977cef39.title: Address geocoding
4bf4977cef39.sentence: Reverse geocoding on the other hand converts geographic coordinates to the description of a location, usually the name of a place or an addressable location.

500d2ba37fee.title: Address geocoding
500d2ba37fee.sentence: Geocoding relies on a computer representation of address points, the street / road network, together with postal and administrative boundaries.

e917120dd5ed.title: Address geocoding
e917120dd5ed.sentence: Input data are the descriptive, textual information (address or building name) which the user wants to turn into numerical, spatial data (latitude and longitude) through the process of geocoding.

688c482f56f1.title: Address geocoding
688c482f56f1.sentence: The second necessary dataset specifies the locations of geographic features in a common spatial reference system, usually stored in a GIS file format or spatial database.

ed0229ceedc2.title: Address geocoding
ed0229ceedc2.sentence: The third component is software that matches each geocode in the input dataset to the attributes of a corresponding feature in the reference dataset.

4c6c924417b7.title: Address geocoding
4c6c924417b7.sentence: Once a match is made, the location of the reference feature can be attached to the input row.

b929e195255b.title: Address geocoding
b929e195255b.sentence: The geocoder expects each input item to directly correspond to a single entire feature in the reference dataset.

ae29b47e68b8.title: Address geocoding
ae29b47e68b8.sentence: For example, a country or zip code, or matching street addresses to building point reference data.

e75a9250456e.title: Address geocoding
e75a9250456e.sentence: This kind of match is similar to a relational table join, except that geocoder algorithms usually incorporate some kind of uncertainty handling to recognize approximate matches (e.g., different capitalization or slight misspellings).

661105aad215.title: Address geocoding
661105aad215.sentence: This method makes use of data from a street geographic information system where the street network is already mapped within the geographic coordinate space.

b3235ee9360f.title: Address geocoding
b3235ee9360f.sentence: Each street segment is attributed with address ranges (e.g. house numbers from one segment to the next).

f33323692489.title: Address geocoding
f33323692489.sentence: First the geocoder parses the street address into its component parts (street name, number, directional prefix/suffix).

0964868986be.title: Address geocoding
0964868986be.sentence: The geocoder matches these components to a corresponding street segment with a number range that includes the input value.

f9b912ca7c71.title: Address geocoding
f9b912ca7c71.sentence: Then it calculates where the given number falls within the segment's range to estimate a location along the segment.

e971ec11a662.title: Address geocoding
e971ec11a662.sentence: The geographic coordinates representing locations often vary greatly in positional accuracy.

9819e935865f.title: Address geocoding
9819e935865f.sentence: Examples include building centroids, land parcel centroids, interpolated locations based on thoroughfare ranges, street segments centroids, postal code centroids (e.g. ZIP codes, CEDEX), and administrative division Centroids.

73f3600d498f.title: Address geocoding
73f3600d498f.sentence: The algorithm is rarely able to perfectly locate all of the input data; mismatches can occur due to misspelled or incomplete input data, imperfect (usually outdated) reference data, or unique regional geocoding systems that the algorithm does not recognize.

d03aa5877ff6.title: Address geocoding
d03aa5877ff6.sentence: As with the direct match, these algorithms usually have uncertainty handling to handle approximate matches (especially abbreviations such as "E" for "East" and "Dr" for "Drive").

d29e77f822af.title: Address geocoding
d29e77f822af.sentence: To achieve the greatest accuracy, the geocodes in the input dataset need to be as correct as possible, and formatted in standard ways.

bc264f393fa1.title: Contraction hierarchies
bc264f393fa1.sentence: In computer science, the method of contraction hierarchies is a speed-up technique for finding the shortest path in a graph.

e90e9bae8323.title: Contraction hierarchies
e90e9bae8323.sentence: The speed-up is achieved by creating shortcuts in a preprocessing phase which are then used during a shortest-path query to skip over "unimportant" vertices.

5cec5f66cf91.title: Contraction hierarchies
5cec5f66cf91.sentence: Intersections are represented by vertices, the road sections connecting them by edges.

a0128283500b.title: Contraction hierarchies
a0128283500b.sentence: The edge weights represent the time it takes to drive along this segment of the road.

71b030b69a36.title: Contraction hierarchies
71b030b69a36.sentence: The metric optimized here is the travel time.

e3b95bf53935.title: Contraction hierarchies
e3b95bf53935.sentence: The shortest path in a graph can be computed using Dijkstra's algorithm but, given that road networks consist of tens of millions of vertices, this is impractical.

c98233ba2694.title: Contraction hierarchies
c98233ba2694.sentence: The contraction hierarchies (CH) algorithm is a two-phase approach to the shortest path problem consisting of a preprocessing phase and a query phase.

156a23c3d22b.title: Contraction hierarchies
156a23c3d22b.sentence: As road networks change rather infrequently, more time (seconds to hours) can be used to once precompute some calculations before queries are to be answered.

70541a02e2c2.title: Contraction hierarchies
70541a02e2c2.sentence: Using this precomputed data, many queries can be answered taking very little time (microseconds) each.

9a7381355a5a.title: Contraction hierarchies
9a7381355a5a.sentence: This is based on the observation that road networks are highly hierarchical.

cd80e97ca0f6.title: Contraction hierarchies
cd80e97ca0f6.sentence: Some intersections, for example highway junctions, are "more important" and higher up in the hierarchy than for example a junction leading into a dead end.

3a6515dfabe2.title: Contraction hierarchies
3a6515dfabe2.sentence: A shortcut connects two vertices u and v not adjacent in the original graph.

0e2045535c28.title: Contraction hierarchies
0e2045535c28.sentence: Its edge weight is the sum of the edge weights on the shortest u-v path.

048544ef69dc.title: Contraction hierarchies
048544ef69dc.sentence: Shortcuts can be used to save the precomputed distance between two important junctions such that the algorithm doesn't have to consider the full path between these junctions at query time.

b5335a309454.title: Contraction hierarchies
b5335a309454.sentence: To achieve this, iterative vertex contractions are performed.

9defbb605eac.title: Contraction hierarchies
9defbb605eac.sentence: When contracting a vertex v it is temporarily removed from the graph G, and a shortcut is created between each pair {u,w} of neighboring vertices if the shortest path from u to w contains v.

ab986e442bae.title: Contraction hierarchies
ab986e442bae.sentence: The process of determining if the shortest path between u and w contains v is called witness search.

f22e1d7cd816.title: Contraction hierarchies
f22e1d7cd816.sentence: As the number of shortcuts is the primary factor that determines preprocessing and query runtime, we want to keep it as small as possible.

67e20d526ccc.title: Contraction hierarchies
67e20d526ccc.sentence: As optimal node ordering is NP-complete, heuristics are used.

a53574ff8d8f.title: Contraction hierarchies
a53574ff8d8f.sentence: On one hand, the computationally cheaper bottom-up heuristics decide the order in which to contract the vertices in a greedy fashion; this means the order is not known in advance but rather the next node is selected for contraction after the previous contraction has been completed.

d8966387c735.title: Contraction hierarchies
d8966387c735.sentence: This yields better results but needs more preprocessing time.

c5791cc667b7.title: Contraction hierarchies
c5791cc667b7.sentence: This, in combination with how shortcuts are created, means that both forward and backward search only need to relax edges leading to more important nodes (upwards) in the hierarchy which keeps the search space small.

8109e487c5c0.title: Contraction hierarchies
8109e487c5c0.sentence: A CH query, as described above, yields the time or distance from s to t but not the actual path.

a72944d0f300.title: Contraction hierarchies
a72944d0f300.sentence: To obtain the list of edges (roads) on the shortest path, the shortcuts taken have to be unpacked.

2895c60532a2.title: Contraction hierarchies
2895c60532a2.sentence: Storing the middle vertex of each shortcut during contraction enables linear-time recursive unpacking of the shortest route.

9cbab6c4063d.title: Contraction hierarchies
9cbab6c4063d.sentence: If the edge weights are changed more often than the network topology, CH can be extended to a three-phase approach by including a customization phase between the preprocessing and query phase.

5a2ef8db286e.title: Contraction hierarchies
5a2ef8db286e.sentence: This can be used for example to switch between shortest distance and shortest time or include current traffic information as well as user preferences like avoiding certain types of roads (ferries, highways,...).

72fbe2ec86b9.title: Tiled web map
72fbe2ec86b9.sentence: A tiled web map or tile map (also known as slippy map in OpenStreetMap), is a web map displayed by seamlessly joining dozens of individually requested data files, called "tiles".

ac52f6aea906.title: Tiled web map
ac52f6aea906.sentence: Each time the user pans, most of the tiles are still relevant, and can be kept displayed, while new tiles are fetched.

3697b7c7f203.title: Tiled web map
3697b7c7f203.sentence: This greatly improves the user experience, compared to fetching a single map image for the whole viewport.

b9f04354489d.title: Tiled web map
b9f04354489d.sentence: It also allows individual tiles to be pre-computed, a task easy to parallelize.

5f88e627e96f.title: Tiled web map
5f88e627e96f.sentence: Also, displaying rendered images served from a web server is less computationally demanding than rendering images in the browser, a benefit over technologies such as Web Feature Service (WFS).

0559d750ca62.title: Tiled web map
0559d750ca62.sentence: - At the outer most zoom level, 0, the entire world can be rendered in a single map tile.

3e9a7992e3c0.title: Tiled web map
3e9a7992e3c0.sentence: - Each zoom level doubles in both dimensions, so a single tile is replaced by 4 tiles when zooming in.

b568677a4e4b.title: Tiled web map
b568677a4e4b.sentence: This means that about 22 zoom levels are sufficient for most practical purposes.

85ec2ae1d7dd.title: Tiled web map
85ec2ae1d7dd.sentence: - The Web Mercator projection is used, with latitude limits of around 85 degrees.

932519d2af05.title: Tiled web map
932519d2af05.sentence: - Images are served through a Web server, with a URL like http://.../Z/X/Y.png, where Z is the zoom level, and X and Y identify the tile.

e0f0f754eb8c.title: Tiled web map
e0f0f754eb8c.sentence: One difference is the y axis is positive northwards in TMS, and southwards in OpenStreetMap.

4dcc4bae3611.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/design-google-maps.md

322b61d612f5.title: Web Mercator projection
322b61d612f5.sentence: Web Mercator, Pseudo-Mercator, or Google Web Mercator is a variant of the Mercator map projection used for coordinates in WGS 84 Web Mercator or WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator and visualisation.

b5bf9b999612.title: Web Mercator projection
b5bf9b999612.sentence: However, the Web Mercator uses the spherical formulas at all scales whereas large-scale Mercator maps normally use the ellipsoidal form of the projection.

54230da53c8b.title: Web Mercator projection
54230da53c8b.sentence: It is used by virtually all major online map providers, including Google Maps, CARTO, Mapbox, Bing Maps, OpenStreetMap, MapQuest, Esri, and many others.

d48daf3c5971.title: Web Mercator projection
d48daf3c5971.sentence: The EPSG identifier for the CRS is EPSG:3857, although others have been used historically.

7a5447a63cb5.title: Web Mercator projection
7a5447a63cb5.sentence: While the Web Mercator's formulas are for the spherical form of the Mercator, geographical coordinates are required to be in the WGS 84 ellipsoidal datum.

d0feed9f5bd1.title: Web Mercator projection
d0feed9f5bd1.sentence: This discrepancy causes the projection to be slightly non-conformal.

87bcd2a87f6d.title: Web Mercator projection
87bcd2a87f6d.sentence: The benefit the Web Mercator gains is that the spherical form is much simpler to calculate than the ellipsoidal form, and so requires only a fraction of the computing resources.

839b6c5eba51.title: Web Mercator projection
839b6c5eba51.sentence: Formulas for the Web Mercator are fundamentally the same as for the standard spherical Mercator, but before applying zoom, the "world coordinates" are adjusted such that the upper left corner is (0, 0) and the lower right corner is (2zoom level−1, 2zoom level−1): x=⌊12π⋅2zoom level(π+λ)⌋ pixelsy=⌊12π⋅2zoom level(π−ln⁡[tan⁡(π4+φ2)])⌋ pixels where λ is the longitude in radians and φ is geodetic latitude in radians.

4d609ff88cb5.title: Web Mercator projection
4d609ff88cb5.sentence: Because the Mercator projects the poles at infinity, a map using the Web Mercator projection cannot show the poles.

3970c306009f.title: Web Mercator projection
3970c306009f.sentence: Services such as Google Maps cut off coverage at 85.051129° north and south.

212e96721d74.title: Web Mercator projection
212e96721d74.sentence: The value 85.051129° is the latitude at which the full projected map becomes a square, and is computed as φ given y = 0: φmax=[2arctan⁡(eπ)−π2]

091f46400897.title: Non-blocking algorithm
091f46400897.sentence: In computer science, an algorithm is called non-blocking if failure or suspension of any thread cannot cause failure or suspension of another thread; for some operations, these algorithms provide a useful alternative to traditional blocking implementations.

ade3d03d9708.title: Non-blocking algorithm
ade3d03d9708.sentence: A non-blocking algorithm is lock-free if there is guaranteed system-wide progress, and wait-free if there is also guaranteed per-thread progress.

97fc67f934c1.title: Non-blocking algorithm
97fc67f934c1.sentence: Obstruction-freedom is the weakest natural non-blocking progress guarantee.

968ac1d4c8b1.title: Non-blocking algorithm
968ac1d4c8b1.sentence: An obvious reason is that while the thread is blocked, it cannot accomplish anything: if the blocked thread had been performing a high-priority or real-time task, it would be highly undesirable to halt its progress.

e79120a8f83e.title: Non-blocking algorithm
e79120a8f83e.sentence: For example, certain interactions between locks can lead to error conditions such as deadlock, livelock, and priority inversion.

6dad787d3fcb.title: Non-blocking algorithm
6dad787d3fcb.sentence: Using locks also involves a trade-off between coarse-grained locking, which can significantly reduce opportunities for parallelism, and fine-grained locking, which requires more careful design, increases locking overhead and is more prone to bugs.

e0152159f207.title: Non-blocking algorithm
e0152159f207.sentence: A lock-free data structure increases the amount of time spent in parallel execution rather than serial execution, improving performance on a multi-core processor, because access to the shared data structure does not need to be serialized to stay coherent.

8e0d37352d5b.title: Non-blocking algorithm
8e0d37352d5b.sentence: Unlike blocking algorithms, non-blocking algorithms do not suffer from these downsides, and in addition are safe for use in interrupt handlers: even though the preempted thread cannot be resumed, progress is still possible without it.

801c9c491417.title: Non-blocking algorithm
801c9c491417.sentence: With few exceptions, non-blocking algorithms use atomic read–modify–write primitives that the hardware must provide, the most notable of which is compare and swap (CAS).

0e0cec7cbcb1.title: Non-blocking algorithm
0e0cec7cbcb1.sentence: Non-blocking algorithms generally involve a series of read, read–modify–write, and write instructions in a carefully designed order.

25edb50be660.title: Non-blocking algorithm
25edb50be660.sentence: Optimizing compilers can aggressively re-arrange operations.

134afb43e759.title: Non-blocking algorithm
134afb43e759.sentence: Even when they don't, many modern CPUs often re-arrange such operations (they have a "weak consistency model"), unless a memory barrier is used to tell the CPU not to reorder.

d78d9e0adb7b.title: Non-blocking algorithm
d78d9e0adb7b.sentence: C++11 programmers can use std::atomic in <atomic>, and C11 programmers can use <stdatomic.h>, both of which supply types and functions that tell the compiler not to re-arrange such instructions, and to insert the appropriate memory barriers.

8436a55d87d3.title: Non-blocking algorithm
8436a55d87d3.sentence: - a single-reader single-writer ring buffer FIFO, with a size which evenly divides the overflow of one of the available unsigned integer types, can unconditionally be implemented safely using only a memory barrier

286e533c2171.title: Non-blocking algorithm
286e533c2171.sentence: Additionally, some non-blocking data structures are weak enough to be implemented without special atomic primitives.

5f5bd31b93a8.title: Non-blocking algorithm
5f5bd31b93a8.sentence: Several libraries internally use lock-free techniques, but it is difficult to write lock-free code that is correct.

68d919403ba8.title: Non-blocking algorithm
68d919403ba8.sentence: It was shown in the 1980s that all algorithms can be implemented wait-free, and many transformations from serial code, called universal constructions, have been demonstrated.

70e0b257707a.title: Non-blocking algorithm
70e0b257707a.sentence: However, the resulting performance does not in general match even naïve blocking designs.

503dc3060ab2.title: Non-blocking algorithm
503dc3060ab2.sentence: Thus, in the absence of hard deadlines, wait-free algorithms may not be worth the additional complexity that they introduce.

9dd57e917afd.title: Order (exchange)
9dd57e917afd.sentence: An order is an instruction to buy or sell on a trading venue such as a stock market, bond market, commodity market, financial derivative market or cryptocurrency exchange.

f4b2a0e00c2d.title: Order (exchange)
f4b2a0e00c2d.sentence: There are some standard instructions for such orders.

4629e285e6f0.title: Order (exchange)
4629e285e6f0.sentence: A market order is a buy or sell order to be executed immediately at the current market prices.

375aca21a3fe.title: Order (exchange)
375aca21a3fe.sentence: As long as there are willing sellers and buyers, market orders are filled.

2f108ec0760d.title: Order (exchange)
2f108ec0760d.sentence: Market orders are used when certainty of execution is a priority over the price of execution.

9adee2c6fb12.title: Order (exchange)
9adee2c6fb12.sentence: This order type does not allow any control over the price received.

8e6a97ea6a77.title: Order (exchange)
8e6a97ea6a77.sentence: The order is filled at the best price available at the relevant time.

d19bc5a65946.title: Order (exchange)
d19bc5a65946.sentence: In fast-moving markets, the price paid or received may be quite different from the last price quoted before the order was entered.

7829d66d8c0d.title: Order (exchange)
7829d66d8c0d.sentence: A market order may be split across multiple participants on the other side of the transaction, resulting in different prices for some of the shares.

199ef53eb220.title: Order (exchange)
199ef53eb220.sentence: A limit order is an order to buy a security at no more than a specific price, or to sell a security at no less than a specific price (called "or better" for either direction).

36f19791b4f2.title: Order (exchange)
36f19791b4f2.sentence: A buy limit order can only be executed at the limit price or lower.

d1f31a754f8b.title: Order (exchange)
d1f31a754f8b.sentence: A sell limit order is analogous; it can only be executed at the limit price or higher.

e969903de47d.title: Order (exchange)
e969903de47d.sentence: This gives the trader (customer) control over the price at which the trade is executed; however, the order may never be executed ("filled").

a685e91fe90c.title: Order (exchange)
a685e91fe90c.sentence: Limit orders are used when the trader wishes to control the price, rather than the certainty, of execution.

189ebd74f930.title: Order (exchange)
189ebd74f930.sentence: A limit order that can be satisfied by orders in the limit book when it is received is marketable.

59fb4b3ed993.title: Order (exchange)
59fb4b3ed993.sentence: A limit order may be partially filled from the book and the rest added to the book.

fbfeb5c77b14.title: Order (exchange)
fbfeb5c77b14.sentence: FOK orders are either filled completely on the first attempt or canceled outright, while AON orders stipulate that the order must be filled with the entire number of shares specified, or not filled at all.

5184176a2ac0.title: Order (exchange)
5184176a2ac0.sentence: Immediate or cancel (IOC) orders are immediately executed or cancelled by the exchange.

a8c5b8ef9ce9.title: Order (exchange)
a8c5b8ef9ce9.sentence: Unlike FOK orders, IOC orders allow for partial fills.

fb03e9d1a947.title: Order (exchange)
fb03e9d1a947.sentence: A day order or good for day order (GFD) (the most common) is a market or limit order that is in force from the time the order is submitted to the end of the day's trading session.

4754c2e6866c.title: Order (exchange)
4754c2e6866c.sentence: Good-til-cancelled (GTC) orders require a specific cancelling order, which can persist indefinitely (although brokers may set some limits, for example, 90 days).

0a851b7cbb05.title: Order (exchange)
0a851b7cbb05.sentence: A conditional order is any order other than a limit order which is executed only when a specific condition is satisfied.

b0466c846065.title: Order (exchange)
b0466c846065.sentence: A stop order or stop-loss order is an order to buy or sell a stock once the price of the stock reaches a specified price, known as the stop price.

42db3b2a6c3e.title: Order (exchange)
42db3b2a6c3e.section: Conditional orders > Stop orders > Stop-limit order
42db3b2a6c3e.sentence: A stop-limit order is an order to buy or sell a stock that combines the features of a stop order and a limit order.

aea7be04d8d9.title: Order (exchange)
aea7be04d8d9.section: Conditional orders > Stop orders > Stop-limit order
aea7be04d8d9.sentence: Once the stop price is reached, a stop-limit order becomes a limit order that will be executed at a specified price (or better).

728e45abc0fe.title: Financial Information eXchange
728e45abc0fe.sentence: The Financial Information eXchange (FIX) protocol is an electronic communications protocol initiated in 1992 for international real-time exchange of information related to securities transactions and markets.

dacc209fcf35.title: Financial Information eXchange
dacc209fcf35.sentence: FIX has become the standard electronic protocol for pre-trade communications and trade execution.

21c81c635ca7.title: Financial Information eXchange
21c81c635ca7.sentence: FIX is widely used by both the buy side (institutions) as well as the sell side (brokers/dealers) of the financial markets.

a7100600c095.title: Financial Information eXchange
a7100600c095.sentence: Among its users are mutual funds, investment banks, brokers, stock exchanges and ECNs.

ac7e21089434.title: Financial Information eXchange
ac7e21089434.section: Technical specifications > Message encodings > Tagvalue encoding (classic FIX)
ac7e21089434.sentence: Each field consists of a unique numeric tag and a value.

2e31baa81a72.title: Financial Information eXchange
2e31baa81a72.section: Technical specifications > Message encodings > Tagvalue encoding (classic FIX)

8fb545d52b13.title: Processor affinity
8fb545d52b13.sentence: In computer science, processor affinity, also called CPU pinning or cache affinity, enables the binding and unbinding of a process or a thread to a central processing unit (CPU) or a range of CPUs, so that the process or thread will execute only on the designated CPU or CPUs rather than any CPU.

b8d51959abfb.sentence: The execution of a thread may be interrupted by the OS scheduler to make space for other programs or threads during an interrupt.

a5692668d41a.title: Collaborative real-time editor
a5692668d41a.sentence: A collaborative real-time editor is a type of collaborative software or web application which enables real-time collaborative editing, simultaneous editing, or live editing of the same digital document, computer file or cloud-stored data – such as an online spreadsheet, word processing document, database or presentation – at the same time by different users on different computers or mobile devices, with automatic and nearly instantaneous merging of their edits.

9cd88b32562f.title: Collaborative real-time editor
9cd88b32562f.sentence: Real-time editing performs automatic, periodic, often nearly instantaneous synchronization of edits of all online users as they edit the document on their own device.

502f5a8f392c.title: Collaborative real-time editor
502f5a8f392c.sentence: This is designed to avoid or minimize edit conflicts.

b496aec5b9c1.title: Collaborative real-time editor
b496aec5b9c1.sentence: With asynchronous collaborative editing (i.e. non-real-time, delayed or offline), each user must typically manually submit (publish, push or commit), update (refresh, pull, download or sync) and (if any edit conflicts occur) merge their edits.

a5755ee98d31.title: Collaborative real-time editor
a5755ee98d31.sentence: Due to the delayed nature of asynchronous collaborative editing, multiple users can end up editing the same line, word, element, data, row or field resulting in edit conflicts which require manual edit merging or overwriting, requiring the user to choose which edits to use or (depending on the system and setup) automatically overwriting their edits or other people's edits, with or without a warning.

e45a9eceb187.title: Collaborative real-time editor
e45a9eceb187.sentence: The complexity of real-time collaborative editing solutions stems from communication latency.

de202483ad8b.title: Collaborative real-time editor
de202483ad8b.sentence: However, the speed of communication is limited by network latency.

49cc2bc96f47.title: Collaborative real-time editor
49cc2bc96f47.sentence: This creates a fundamental dilemma: users need their own edits incorporated into the document instantly, but if they are incorporated instantly, then because of communication latency, their edits must necessarily be inserted into different versions of the document.

fcd75e6670d8.title: Collaborative real-time editor
fcd75e6670d8.sentence: Suppose Bob and Alice start with a document containing the word Mary.

0414b90cff66.title: Collaborative real-time editor
0414b90cff66.sentence: Bob deletes 'M', then inserts 'H', to change the word into Hary.

963c3dd32cb3.title: Collaborative real-time editor
963c3dd32cb3.sentence: Alice, before she receives either edit from Bob, deletes 'r', then deletes 'a', to change it into My.

9edb485a5cdc.title: Collaborative real-time editor
9edb485a5cdc.sentence: Both Bob and Alice will then receive edits that were applied to versions of the document that never existed on their own machines.

e0d908026e4f.title: Collaborative real-time editor
e0d908026e4f.sentence: Thus, the challenge of real-time collaborative editing is to figure out exactly how to apply edits from remote users, which were originally created in versions of the document that never existed locally, and which may conflict with the user's own local edits.

5eb4e4096e3e.title: Collaborative real-time editor
5eb4e4096e3e.sentence: The most sophisticated solutions solve this problem in a way that does not require a server, does not use locking (all users can freely edit all parts of a document at the same time), and supports any number of users (limited only by the resources of the computers).

4dc9b0cf2958.title: Collaborative real-time editor
4dc9b0cf2958.sentence: In a client–server scenario, one of the editor instances is assigned the role of collaboration server when the document is opened.

3b79e1216d6d.title: Collaborative real-time editor
3b79e1216d6d.sentence: The server receives timestamped notifications of changes made to the document by other users.

c005ff92d396.title: Collaborative real-time editor
c005ff92d396.sentence: It determines how those changes should affect its local copy, and broadcasts its changes to the collaboration pool.

12b3b1ead53c.title: Collaborative real-time editor
12b3b1ead53c.sentence: This approach, while significantly less powerful, allows for basic collaboration at a relatively low cost.

1d4d4537d5e7.title: Collaborative real-time editor
1d4d4537d5e7.sentence: This makes it preferable in situations where processing resources are limited.

81c100dec6f2.title: Collaborative real-time editor
81c100dec6f2.sentence: Although marketed as real-time collaboration, these 'workspace' approaches require either document locking (so only one person can edit it at a time), or 'reconciliation' of conflicting changes, which is generally found by users to be unsatisfactory.

e48350f09551.title: Operational transformation
e48350f09551.sentence: Operational transformation (OT) is a technology for supporting a range of collaboration functionalities in advanced collaborative software systems.

540c013b4dec.title: Operational transformation
540c013b4dec.sentence: The basic idea of OT is to transform (or adjust) the parameters of an editing operation according to the effects of previously executed concurrent operations so that the transformed operation can achieve the correct effect and maintain document consistency.

6d8c73e64ee5.title: Operational transformation
6d8c73e64ee5.sentence: OT was originally invented for consistency maintenance and concurrency control in collaborative editing of plain text documents.

ff27647bf66a.title: Operational transformation
ff27647bf66a.sentence: Operational Transformation was pioneered by C. Ellis and S. Gibbs in the GROVE (GRoup Outline Viewing Edit) system in 1989.

f8553d023885.title: Operational transformation
f8553d023885.sentence: In 2009, OT was adopted as a core technique behind the collaboration features in then-Google Wave and Google Docs.

cdfc734f36c7.title: Operational transformation
cdfc734f36c7.sentence: Collaboration systems utilizing Operational Transformations typically use replicated document storage, where each client has their own copy of the document; clients operate on their local copies in a lock-free, non-blocking manner, and the changes are then propagated to the rest of the clients; this ensures the client high responsiveness in an otherwise high-latency environment such as the Internet.

56fc9e796520.title: Operational transformation
56fc9e796520.sentence: When a client receives the changes propagated from another client, it typically transforms the changes before executing them; the transformation ensures that application-dependent consistency criteria (invariants) are maintained by all sites.

ecbce53ec9a9.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
ecbce53ec9a9.sentence: Double-entry bookkeeping, also known as double-entry accounting, is a method of bookkeeping in which every financial transaction is recorded with equal and opposite entries (debits and credits) - thus "balancing the books".

ca2021bf37ba.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
ca2021bf37ba.sentence: The purpose of double-entry bookkeeping is to maintain accuracy in financial records and allow detection of errors or fraud.

2ca2cd232702.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
2ca2cd232702.sentence: The basis of double-entry bookkeeping is the accounting equation:

8975b9701cdd.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
8975b9701cdd.sentence: Every transaction recorded will keep this equation in balance.

244ca523089a.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
244ca523089a.sentence: In double-entry bookkeeping, every financial transaction is entered into at least two nominal ledger accounts to ensure that total debits equal total credits, maintaining balance in the general ledger.

74ed87bd812f.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
74ed87bd812f.sentence: This is a partial check that each and every transaction has been correctly recorded.

d65ba4e7cf77.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
d65ba4e7cf77.sentence: A debit entry in an account represents a transfer of value to that account, and a credit entry represents a transfer from the account.

131e68b9376c.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
131e68b9376c.sentence: Each transaction is recorded as a "debit entry" (Dr) in one account, and a "credit entry" (Cr) in a second account.

5ec2c923d948.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
5ec2c923d948.sentence: Based upon where an account sits within the accounting equation determines its normal balance - in this example, a debit to assets increases assets, whereas a credit to liabilities increases liabilities.

f999587913b3.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
f999587913b3.sentence: Since both sides of a double-entry bookkeeping entry must remain in balance, accounts then have a normal balance, which is based upon whether a debit or a credit increases the account.

571055f5f62f.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
571055f5f62f.sentence: Double entry is applied within nominal ledgers, while daybooks (journals) typically serve as preliminary records and are not part of the nominal ledger itself.

18e75beaf0c0.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
18e75beaf0c0.sentence: The reason for this is to limit the number of entries in the nominal ledger: entries in the daybooks can be totalled before they are entered in the nominal ledger.

8f30165bbf31.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
8f30165bbf31.sentence: The information from the daybooks will be used in the nominal ledger and it is the nominal ledgers that will ensure the integrity of the resulting financial information created from the daybooks (provided that the information recorded in the daybooks is correct).

9f98ce0ea5be.sentence: The service allows users to send and receive text messages of up to 160 characters, originally to and from GSM phones and later also CDMA and Digital AMPS; it has since been defined and supported on newer networks, including present-day 5G ones.

28f62c9de501.title: SMS
28f62c9de501.sentence: Messages are sent with the MAP MO- and MT-ForwardSM operations, whose payload length is limited by the constraints of the signaling protocol to precisely 140 bytes (140 bytes × 8 bits / byte = 1120 bits).

d932a203caf4.title: SMS
d932a203caf4.sentence: Short messages can be encoded using a variety of alphabets: the default GSM 7-bit alphabet, the 8-bit data alphabet, and the 16-bit UCS-2 or UTF-16 alphabets.

ba1239cadef9.title: SMS
ba1239cadef9.sentence: Using SMS gateways, messages can be transmitted over the Internet through an SMSC, allowing communication to computers, fixed landlines, and satellite.

6537f87c22e8.title: SMS
6537f87c22e8.sentence: A2P is a type of SMS sent from a subscriber to an application or sent from an application to a subscriber.

d3eecab16ccf.title: SMS
d3eecab16ccf.sentence: It is commonly used by businesses, such as banks, e-gaming, logistic companies, e-commerce, to send SMS messages from their systems to their customers.

0e206721b410.title: SMS
0e206721b410.sentence: Unlike dedicated texting systems like the Simple Network Paging Protocol and Motorola's ReFLEX protocol, SMS message delivery is not guaranteed, and many implementations provide no mechanism through which a sender can determine whether an SMS message has been delivered in a timely manner.

cb2f2f5ce308.title: SMS
cb2f2f5ce308.sentence: SMS messages are generally treated as lower-priority traffic than voice, and various studies have shown that around 1% to 5% of messages are lost entirely, even during normal operation conditions, and others may not be delivered until long after their relevance has passed.

d976a8b1f7f7.title: Instant messaging
d976a8b1f7f7.sentence: SMS messages are not encrypted, making them insecure, as the content of each SMS message is visible to mobile carriers and governments and can be intercepted by a third party, may leak metadata (such as phone numbers), or be spoofed and the sender of the message can be edited to impersonate another person.

4dd26201c3dd.title: SMS
4dd26201c3dd.sentence: One threat is SMS spoofing, which occurs when a fraudster manipulates address information in order to impersonate a user that has roamed onto a foreign network and is submitting messages to the home network.

3a420cc92254.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md

20829437ceb0.title: Firebase
20829437ceb0.sentence: Google Cloud Messaging, the Google service to send push notifications to Android devices, was superseded by a Firebase product, Firebase Cloud Messaging, which added the functionality to deliver push notifications to Android, iOS and web devices.

9ebea1ec34d3.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md

14cf9fb424ae.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md

218d7422e779.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md
218d7422e779.sentence: This token must be included in the notifications.

d02085ee61c8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md

5ec7c0799e01.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md
5ec7c0799e01.sentence: The app server caches the token for subsequent communications.

209061825f36.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md
209061825f36.sentence: Over time, the app server has too many tokens to maintain, so the recommended practice is to store the token with timestamps and to remove stale tokens from time to time.

98fb030da626.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md

dd18637859b5.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md
dd18637859b5.sentence: One is to compose messages directly in the console GUI (Step 4.1,) and the other is to send the messages from the app server (Step 4.2.) We can use the Firebase Admin SDK or HTTP for the latter.

851986ccac62.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md

827acf87ab14.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md
827acf87ab14.sentence: This transport layer handles platform-specific configurations.

76ac28d38741.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md

f9583ef9c3a5.title: Apple Push Notification service
f9583ef9c3a5.sentence: Apple Push Notification service (APNs), previously known as Apple Push Service (APS), is a platform notification service created by Apple that enables third-party application developers to send notification data to applications installed on Apple devices.

706ca3102d52.title: Apple Push Notification service
706ca3102d52.sentence: The notification information sent can include badges, sounds, newsstand updates, or custom text alerts.

fe71382a0970.title: Apple Push Notification service
fe71382a0970.sentence: At both events, Forstall stated that push notifications better conserve battery than background processes (which are used in pull technology) for receiving notifications.

5a26bd5c645f.title: Apple Push Notification service
5a26bd5c645f.sentence: In December 2015, a new HTTP/2 provider API was released by Apple, effectively replacing the now-legacy binary interface.

63a25f5f3bfa.title: Apple Push Notification service
63a25f5f3bfa.sentence: The maximum notification payload size allowed using the HTTP/2 API is 4 kilobytes.

20e7588f6f41.title: Apple Push Notification service
20e7588f6f41.sentence: In 2014, the maximum size allowed for a notification payload sent through the binary interface was increased from 256 bytes to 2 kilobytes.

9634ddc43aaf.title: Apple Push Notification service
9634ddc43aaf.sentence: Apple shut down the legacy binary API at the end of March 2021.

65151ad2e212.title: Apple Push Notification service
65151ad2e212.sentence: The HTTP/2 provider for APNs uses TCP port 443 as the main port of communication, but developers are also allowed to use TCP port 2197 if outbound access to port 443 is blocked by firewalls.

681bab06327a.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-are-notifications-pushed-to-our-phones-or-pcs.md
681bab06327a.sentence: A messaging solution (Firebase) can be used to support the notification push.

c1eff62da0ae.title: rfc>8030
c1eff62da0ae.sentence: The push service MUST provide a URI for the push resource corresponding to the push message subscription in a link relation of type "urn:ietf:params:push".

b1fd790f9782.title: rfc>8030
b1fd790f9782.sentence: An application-specific method is used to distribute the push URI to the application server.

261d5d5bc96e.title: rfc>8030
261d5d5bc96e.sentence: Confidentiality protection and application server authentication MUST be used to ensure that this URI is not disclosed to unauthorized recipients (Section 8.3).

5c9564afa8d8.title: rfc>8030
5c9564afa8d8.sentence: A 201 (Created) response indicates that the push message was accepted.

f255ff059f70.title: rfc>8030
f255ff059f70.sentence: This does not indicate that the message was delivered to the user agent.

3ac867a36502.title: rfc>8030
3ac867a36502.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.4. Replacing Push Messages
3ac867a36502.sentence: A push message that has been stored by the push service can be replaced with new content.

a55941d47afd.title: rfc>8030
a55941d47afd.section: 6. Receiving Push Messages for a Subscription > 6.2. Acknowledging Push Messages
a55941d47afd.sentence: If the push service does not receive the acknowledgement within a reasonable amount of time, then the message is considered to be not yet delivered.

b5de9fd77bae.title: rfc>8030
b5de9fd77bae.section: 6. Receiving Push Messages for a Subscription > 6.2. Acknowledging Push Messages
b5de9fd77bae.sentence: The push service SHOULD continue to retry delivery of the message until its advertised expiration.

e49048506f21.title: rfc>8030
e49048506f21.section: 5. Requesting Push Message Delivery > 5.1. Requesting Push Message Receipts
e49048506f21.sentence: When the push service accepts the message for delivery with confirmation, it MUST return a 202 (Accepted) response.

8358f1676258.title: rfc>8030
8358f1676258.section: 6. Receiving Push Messages for a Subscription > 6.3. Receiving Push Message Receipts
8358f1676258.sentence: A 204 (No Content) status code confirms that the message was delivered and acknowledged.

2c8eff87cf71.title: rfc>8030
2c8eff87cf71.section: 6. Receiving Push Messages for a Subscription > 6.3. Receiving Push Message Receipts
2c8eff87cf71.sentence: If the user agent fails to acknowledge the receipt of the push message and the push service ceases to retry delivery of the message prior to its advertised expiration, then the push service MUST push a failure response with a status code of 410 (Gone).

cf292c8c69dd.title: rfc>8030
cf292c8c69dd.section: 7. Operational Considerations > 7.4. Implications for Application Reliability
cf292c8c69dd.sentence: The availability of push message delivery receipts ensures that the application developer is not tempted to create alternative mechanisms for message delivery in case the push service fails to deliver a critical message.

7881c17d1d31.title: rfc>8030
7881c17d1d31.sentence: A push service MAY expire a subscription at any time.

3967b7eac83d.title: rfc>8030
3967b7eac83d.sentence: A push service MUST return a 404 (Not Found) status code if an application server attempts to send a push message to an expired push message subscription.

348771f44ca9.title: rfc>8030
348771f44ca9.sentence: User agents and application servers must be prepared to manage changes in the subscription state.

7ac64df9cb2b.title: rfc>8030
7ac64df9cb2b.sentence: To limit the size of messages, the push service MAY return a 413 (Payload Too Large) status code in response to requests that include an entity body that is too large.

c3e3e1e6c2d6.title: rfc>8030
c3e3e1e6c2d6.sentence: Push services MUST NOT return a 413 status code in responses to an entity body that is 4096 bytes or less in size.

6d0bfa86c424.title: Access-control list
6d0bfa86c424.sentence: In computer security, an access-control list (ACL) is a list of permissions associated with a system resource (object or facility).

5506031416e0.title: Access-control list
5506031416e0.sentence: An ACL specifies which users or system processes are granted access to resources, as well as what operations are allowed on given resources.

e37197ac497e.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-a-permission-system.md
e37197ac497e.sentence: ACL is a list of rules that specifies which users are granted or denied access to a particular resource.

faa588c0e1a1.title: Access-control list
faa588c0e1a1.sentence: Each entry in a typical ACL specifies a subject and an operation.

86ea191b179c.title: Access-control list
86ea191b179c.sentence: - If a file object has an ACL that contains(Alice: read,write; Bob: read), this would give Alice permission to read and write the file and give Bob permission only to read it.

2101ed0c752a.title: Access-control list
2101ed0c752a.sentence: A filesystem ACL is a data structure (usually a table) containing entries that specify individual user or group rights to specific system objects such as programs, processes, or files.

8db0f9bc98d3.title: Access-control list
8db0f9bc98d3.sentence: These entries are known as access-control entries (ACEs) in the Microsoft Windows NT, OpenVMS, and Unix-like operating systems such as Linux, macOS, and Solaris.

22c452cef9a5.title: Access-control list
22c452cef9a5.sentence: Each accessible object contains an identifier to its ACL.

c5bde42b69e2.title: Access-control list
c5bde42b69e2.sentence: ACLs are usually stored in the extended attributes of a file on these systems.

c59909c176cd.title: Access-control list
c59909c176cd.sentence: As with POSIX ACLs, NFSv4 ACLs are usually stored as extended attributes on Unix-like systems.

48b7f731db72.title: Access-control list
48b7f731db72.sentence: On some types of proprietary computer hardware (in particular, routers and switches), an access-control list provides rules that are applied to port numbers or IP addresses that are available on a host or other layer 3, each with a list of hosts and/or networks permitted to use the service.

9622b086f8e9.title: Access-control list
9622b086f8e9.sentence: Both individual servers and routers can have network ACLs.

2b7f42361a3b.title: Access-control list
2b7f42361a3b.sentence: Access-control lists can generally be configured to control both inbound and outbound traffic, and in this context they are similar to firewalls.

ba67ea850272.title: Access-control list
ba67ea850272.sentence: Although it is additionally possible to configure access-control lists based on network domain names, this is a questionable idea because individual TCP, UDP, and ICMP headers do not contain domain names.

884af1e0ea7f.title: Access-control list
884af1e0ea7f.sentence: Consequently, the device enforcing the access-control list must separately resolve names to numeric addresses.

af0e2e900474.title: Access-control list
af0e2e900474.sentence: This presents an additional attack surface for an attacker who is seeking to compromise security of the system which the access-control list is protecting.

ce6ce76575cf.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-a-permission-system.md
ce6ce76575cf.sentence: - Cons - error-prone, maintenance cost is high

5ba0dde796e8.title: Access-control list
5ba0dde796e8.sentence: A "minimal RBAC model", RBACm, can be compared with an ACL mechanism, ACLg, where only groups are permitted as entries in the ACL.

687da65972dc.title: Access-control list
687da65972dc.sentence: Barkley (1997) showed that RBACm and ACLg are equivalent.

e28e64d7292a.title: Access-control list
e28e64d7292a.sentence: In modern SQL implementations, ACLs also manage groups and inheritance in a hierarchy of groups.

7ab391d07c27.title: Access-control list
7ab391d07c27.sentence: So "modern ACLs" can express all that RBAC express and are notably powerful (compared to "old ACLs") in their ability to express access-control policy in terms of the way in which administrators view organizations.

2ff2c5b109bf.title: Role-based access control
2ff2c5b109bf.sentence: In information security, role-based access control (RBAC) or role-based security is an approach to restricting system access to authorized users.

ee931f679142.title: Role-based access control
ee931f679142.sentence: It is a policy-neutral computer access control mechanism defined around roles and privileges.

fa1e9aef791f.title: Role-based access control
fa1e9aef791f.sentence: Within an organization, roles are created for various job functions.

4c42df437a48.title: Role-based access control
4c42df437a48.sentence: The permissions to perform certain operations are assigned to specific roles.

85c412f0a842.title: Role-based access control
85c412f0a842.sentence: Since users are not assigned permissions directly, but only acquire them through their role (or roles), management of individual user rights becomes a matter of simply assigning appropriate roles to the user's account; this simplifies common operations, such as adding a user, or changing a user's department.

ba17c587eb48.title: Role-based access control
ba17c587eb48.sentence: - Role assignment: A subject can exercise a permission only if the subject has selected or been assigned a role.

a44a228d2b3a.title: Role-based access control
a44a228d2b3a.sentence: - Role authorization: A subject's active role must be authorized for the subject.

061addf0bda7.title: Role-based access control
061addf0bda7.sentence: - Permission authorization: A subject can exercise a permission only if the permission is authorized for the subject's active role.

322571c37980.title: Role-based access control
322571c37980.sentence: - S = Subject = A person or automated agent

318338198fc0.title: Role-based access control
318338198fc0.sentence: - R = Role = Job function or title which defines an authority level

8b4c48d786b7.title: Role-based access control
8b4c48d786b7.sentence: - P = Permissions = An approval of a mode of access to a resource

09eeb2a52885.title: Role-based access control
09eeb2a52885.sentence: - SE = Session = A mapping involving S, R and/or P

c57803474795.title: Role-based access control
c57803474795.sentence: - PA⊆P×R and is a many to many permission to role assignment relation.

0ed79e43e237.title: Role-based access control
0ed79e43e237.sentence: - SA⊆S×R and is a many to many subject to role assignment relation.

b4a0c2e00f29.title: Role-based access control
b4a0c2e00f29.sentence: A subject may have multiple simultaneous sessions with/in different roles.

9502ecfdffda.title: Role-based access control
9502ecfdffda.sentence: Additional constraints may be applied as well, and roles can be combined in a hierarchy where higher-level roles subsume permissions owned by sub-roles.

d62e9d0510f7.title: Role-based access control
d62e9d0510f7.sentence: A constraint places a restrictive rule on the potential inheritance of permissions from opposing roles.

5d7dbf3518c1.title: Role-based access control
5d7dbf3518c1.sentence: Thus it can be used to achieve appropriate separation of duties.

9890957c38fa.title: Role-based access control
9890957c38fa.sentence: The NIST/ANSI/INCITS RBAC standard (2004) recognizes three levels of RBAC:

074ef8933859.title: Role-based access control
074ef8933859.sentence: - Hierarchical RBAC, which adds support for inheritance between roles

876f48b57a9d.title: Role-based access control
876f48b57a9d.sentence: - Constrained RBAC, which adds separation of duties

0b71a5e43b27.title: Role-based access control
0b71a5e43b27.sentence: RBAC can be used to facilitate administration of security in large organizations with hundreds of users and thousands of permissions.

d8d6d7ca5d5e.title: Role-based access control
d8d6d7ca5d5e.sentence: The use of RBAC to manage user privileges (computer permissions) within a single system or application is widely accepted as a best practice.

741ed86827d2.title: Kubernetes
741ed86827d2.sentence: - Role-based access control (RBAC) mode: Grants access rights to users based on roles that are granted to the user, where each role defines a list of actions that are allowed.

b4f1a3dd84f0.title: Role-based access control
b4f1a3dd84f0.sentence: RBAC is a flexible access control technology whose flexibility allows it to implement discretionary access control (DAC) or mandatory access control (MAC).

5807c08c083d.title: Role-based access control
5807c08c083d.sentence: Although RBAC is different from mandatory access control and discretionary access control (DAC) frameworks, it can enforce these policies.

d7adc8a6187c.title: Role-based access control
d7adc8a6187c.sentence: Attribute-based access control and relationship-based access control are models that build on the concept of RBAC.

793084aa404b.title: Role-based access control
793084aa404b.sentence: RBAC has also been criticized for leading to role explosion, a problem in large enterprise systems which require access control of finer granularity than what RBAC can provide as roles are inherently assigned to operations and data types.

a981e38b1282.title: Role-based access control
a981e38b1282.sentence: In an organization with a heterogeneous IT infrastructure and requirements that span dozens or hundreds of systems and applications, using RBAC to manage sufficient roles and assign adequate role memberships becomes extremely complex without hierarchical creation of roles and privilege assignments.

09b4eff46f06.title: Role-based access control
09b4eff46f06.sentence: Unlike context-based access control (CBAC), RBAC does not look at the message context (such as a connection's source).

52f96b78a7e4.title: Role-based access control
52f96b78a7e4.section: Relation to other models > Comparing to ACL
52f96b78a7e4.sentence: Access control lists (ACLs) are used in traditional discretionary access-control (DAC) systems to affect low-level data-objects.

ab5a1e16b8ea.title: Role-based access control
ab5a1e16b8ea.section: Relation to other models > Comparing to ACL
ab5a1e16b8ea.sentence: For example, an ACL could be used for granting or denying write access to a particular system file, but it wouldn't dictate how that file could be changed.

1ee22e90d891.title: Role-based access control
1ee22e90d891.section: Relation to other models > Comparing to ACL
1ee22e90d891.sentence: In an RBAC-based system, an operation might be to 'create a credit account' transaction in a financial application or to 'populate a blood sugar level test' record in a medical application.

0a9871d1b601.title: Discretionary access control
0a9871d1b601.sentence: In computer security, discretionary access control (DAC) is a type of access control defined by the Trusted Computer System Evaluation Criteria (TCSEC) as a means of restricting access to objects based on the identity of subjects and/or groups to which they belong.

2fe002f38a73.title: Discretionary access control
2fe002f38a73.sentence: The controls are discretionary in the sense that a subject with a certain access permission is capable of passing that permission (perhaps indirectly) on to any other subject (unless restrained by mandatory access control).

e12a361a17ef.title: Discretionary access control
e12a361a17ef.sentence: The term DAC is commonly used in contexts that assume that every object has an owner that controls the permissions to access the object, likely because many systems do indeed implement DAC using the concept of an owner.

01365f2f8eb7.title: Discretionary access control
01365f2f8eb7.sentence: Under this DAC implementation, users (owners) have the ability to make policy decisions and/or assign security attributes.

be8fda8590f4.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-a-permission-system.md
be8fda8590f4.sentence: It grants or restricts object access via an access policy determined by an object's owner group.

46f79ca640f5.title: Discretionary access control
46f79ca640f5.sentence: A straightforward example is the Unix file mode, which represents write, read, and execute in each of the 3 bits for each of User, Group and Others.

17d9fc7ad841.title: Discretionary access control
17d9fc7ad841.sentence: There are at least two implementations: with owner (as a widespread example) and with capabilities.

38ca2f6e512b.title: Discretionary access control
38ca2f6e512b.sentence: As another example, capability systems are sometimes described as providing discretionary controls because they permit subjects to transfer their access to other subjects, even though capability-based security is fundamentally not about restricting access "based on the identity of subjects".

243148145788.title: Discretionary access control
243148145788.sentence: In general, capability systems do not allow permissions to be passed "to any other subject"; the subject wanting to pass its permissions must first have access to the receiving subject, and subjects generally only have access to a strictly limited set of subjects consistent with the principle of least privilege.

bbc8a27a4a1b.title: Discretionary access control
bbc8a27a4a1b.sentence: On the other hand, systems can implement both MAC and DAC simultaneously, where DAC refers to one category of access controls that subjects can transfer among each other, and MAC refers to a second category of access controls that imposes constraints upon the first.

73aea0fd5ca8.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-a-permission-system.md
73aea0fd5ca8.sentence: - Cons - Scattered permission control, too much power for the object’s owner group.

f1f55958e9bf.title: Attribute-based access control
f1f55958e9bf.sentence: Attribute-based access control (ABAC), also known as policy-based access control for IAM, defines an access control paradigm whereby a subject's authorization to perform a set of operations is determined by evaluating attributes associated with the subject, object, requested operations, and, in some cases, environment attributes.

dfc7310c1620.title: Attribute-based access control
dfc7310c1620.sentence: ABAC policy rules are generated as Boolean functions of the subject's attributes, the object's attributes, and the environment attributes.

bf187ca0d3aa.title: Attribute-based access control
bf187ca0d3aa.sentence: The only limitations on the policies that can be implemented with ABAC are the capabilities of the computational language and the availability of relevant attributes.

8310f1b68851.title: gh>ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/data/guides/how-do-we-design-a-permission-system.md
8310f1b68851.sentence: Evaluate permissions based on attributes of the Resource owner, Action, Resource, and Environment.

79dbe75a2675.title: Attribute-based access control
79dbe75a2675.sentence: They tend to fall into 4 different categories:

fa1e50da9855.title: Attribute-based access control
fa1e50da9855.sentence: - Subject attributes: attributes that describe the user attempting the access e.g. age, clearance, department, role, job title

8a4c9a104d1a.title: Attribute-based access control
8a4c9a104d1a.sentence: - Action attributes: attributes that describe the action being attempted e.g. read, delete, view, approve

b1a9ea2f2f48.title: Attribute-based access control
b1a9ea2f2f48.sentence: - Object attributes: attributes that describe the object (or resource) being accessed e.g. the object type (medical record, bank account), the department, the classification or sensitivity, the location

f72d114491ef.title: Attribute-based access control
f72d114491ef.sentence: - Contextual (environment) attributes: attributes that deal with time, location or dynamic aspects of the access control scenario

2a77779a4378.title: Attribute-based access control
2a77779a4378.sentence: Unlike role-based access control (RBAC), which defines roles that carry a specific set of privileges associated with them and to which subjects are assigned, ABAC can express complex rule sets that can evaluate many different attributes.

a404bcb8d7a6.title: Attribute-based access control
a404bcb8d7a6.sentence: Through defining consistent subject and object attributes into security policies, ABAC eliminates the need for explicit authorizations to individuals’ subjects needed in a non-ABAC access method, reducing the complexity of managing access lists and groups.

cbc9e8a26ee3.title: Attribute-based access control
cbc9e8a26ee3.sentence: These access control models are user-centric and do not take into account additional parameters such as resource information, the relationship between the user (the requesting entity) and the resource, and dynamic information, e.g. time of the day or user IP.

09df1272b864.title: Attribute-based access control
09df1272b864.sentence: Policies are statements that bring together attributes to express what can happen and is not allowed.

5aece2eca939.title: Attribute-based access control
5aece2eca939.sentence: Policies in ABAC can be granting or denying policies.

348449e84931.title: Attribute-based access control
348449e84931.sentence: Policies can also be local or global and can be written in a way that they override other policies.

9141108a1846.title: Attribute-based access control
9141108a1846.sentence: - A user can edit a document if they are the owner and if the document is in draft mode

7881fb865750.title: Attribute-based access control
7881fb865750.sentence: - The PEP or Policy Enforcement Point: it is responsible for protecting the apps & data you want to apply ABAC to.

e6860ee287f0.title: Attribute-based access control

c43e46854f84.title: Attribute-based access control
c43e46854f84.sentence: - The PDP or Policy Decision Point is the brain of the architecture.

cd8e6a554c51.title: Attribute-based access control
cd8e6a554c51.sentence: This is the piece which evaluates incoming requests against policies it has been configured with.

02b29803bdc2.title: Attribute-based access control
02b29803bdc2.sentence: - The PIP or Policy Information Point bridges the PDP to external sources of attributes e.g. LDAP or databases.

daa61de2d48d.title: Attribute-based access control
daa61de2d48d.sentence: There are three main implementations of ABAC:

8612ec26159e.sentence: XACML, the eXtensible Access Control Markup Language, defines an architecture (shared with ALFA and NGAC), a policy language, and a request/response scheme.

24ed94fb7ea9.title: Attribute-based access control
24ed94fb7ea9.sentence: It does not handle attribute management (user attribute assignment, object attribute assignment, environment attribute assignment) which is left to traditional IAM tools, databases, and directories.

97e1ca66e6c5.title: Attribute-based access control
97e1ca66e6c5.sentence: ABAC can be used to apply attribute-based, fine-grained authorization to the API methods or functions.

9def21da28c6.title: Attribute-based access control
9def21da28c6.sentence: - Policy: managers can approve transactions up to their approval limit

e9c7199fdc9e.title: Attribute-based access control
e9c7199fdc9e.sentence: - Reworked policy in a data-centric way: users with role = manager can do the action SELECT on table = TRANSACTIONS if user.region = transaction.region

2ea14eea94ea.sentence: - Cons - the rules can be complicated, and the implementation is hard.

06310de70802.title: Attribute-based access control
06310de70802.sentence: An important consideration when evaluating ABAC solutions is to understand its potential overhead on performance and its impact on the user experience.

fd524fcae110.title: Attribute-based access control
fd524fcae110.sentence: It is expected that the more granular the controls, the higher the overhead.

9a76115fdc88.sentence: A policy is retrieved by a Policy Retrieval Point (PRP) from a Policy Repository, evaluated at a Policy Decision Point (PDP) or Policy Consumer, and enforced at a Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) or Policy Target.

95e5c28eadb9.sentence: Each independent policy must be 1) retrieved, 2) evaluated, and 3) enforced.

36bbb7b2b108.title: XACML

3f0907c80bd0.title: rfc>2904

3f0907c80bd0.sentence: Policy Enforcement is typically done by the Service Provider on the Service Equipment.

4b8d70e0a330.title: rfc>2904

4b8d70e0a330.sentence: Thus a NAS may enforce destination IP address limits via "filters" and a Router may enforce QoS restrictions on incoming packets.

66d3aba259b4.title: XACML
66d3aba259b4.sentence: Policy Decision Point (PDP) | Point that evaluates access requests against authorization policies before issuing access decisions

e364fc1e4f42.title: XACML
e364fc1e4f42.sentence: These refer to an environment-independent and central Policy Decision Point (PDP), which is responsible for making the final access decision.

7a40f6a531a6.title: XACML
7a40f6a531a6.sentence: - The PDP reaches a decision (Permit, Deny, NotApplicable, or Indeterminate) and returns it to the PEP.

ae129dd727ae.title: rfc>2904

ae129dd727ae.sentence: Information against which policy conditions are evaluated (such as resource status, session state, or time of day) are accessible at Policy Information Points (PIPs) and might be accessed using Policy Information Blocks (PIBs).

49d8aca4de5b.title: XACML

7aa4510626a1.title: XACML
7aa4510626a1.sentence: If needed, the PDP also retrieves attribute values from underlying Policy Information Points (PIP).

e2d3d47ca67b.sentence: Evaluation of policy requires access to information referenced by the policy.

c9338c04bcda.sentence: Often the information required is not available in the administration where the policy is retrieved.

55e09df7486b.sentence: But authorizing a user requiring a 2Mb/s path with less than 4 hops requires information available at a Service Provider and not directly available to the UHO, so the UHO must either 1) have a way to query a remote administration for the needed information or 2) forward the policy to the remote administration and have the remote administration do the actual evaluation or 3) attempt somehow to "shadow" the authoritative source of the information (e.g by having the Service Provider send updates to the UHO).

f63053a71919.title: rfc>2904

8ec09b901359.title: XACML
8ec09b901359.sentence: The eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) is an XML-based standard markup language for specifying access control policies.

fbc6d352f908.title: XACML
fbc6d352f908.sentence: The standard, published by OASIS, defines a declarative, fine-grained, attribute-based access control policy language, an architecture, and a processing model describing how to evaluate access requests according to the rules defined in policies.

d3a188dbc7ab.title: XACML
d3a188dbc7ab.sentence: XACML is primarily an attribute-based access control policy language, but it also defines syntaxes for the requests sent by the Policy Enforcement Point to the Policy Decision Point, also called authorization decision requests.

36ec157cf712.title: XACML
36ec157cf712.sentence: XACML can also be used to implement role-based access control.

15218431d051.title: XACML
15218431d051.sentence: - A user sends a request to access a resource; this request is intercepted by the Policy Enforcement Point (PEP).

6ab883e29307.title: XACML
6ab883e29307.sentence: - The PEP converts the request into a XACML authorization request.

660f7b47c150.title: XACML
660f7b47c150.sentence: - The PEP forwards the authorization request to the Policy Decision Point (PDP).

d0fb5b4f23b0.title: XACML
d0fb5b4f23b0.sentence: - The PDP evaluates the authorization request against its configured policies.

bbcd7e099a2a.title: XACML
bbcd7e099a2a.sentence: The policies are acquired via a Policy Retrieval Point (PRP) and managed by a Policy Administration Point (PAP).

3a613b4d6126.title: XACML
3a613b4d6126.sentence: - The PEP enforces the access decision against the user's request.

6cc5093ae9ef.title: XACML
6cc5093ae9ef.sentence: In XACML, Rules specify the conditions under which an access request is approved (Permit) or rejected (Deny).

ca6bdd8dab41.title: XACML
ca6bdd8dab41.sentence: If a Rule is applicable to a request but the conditions within the Rule fail to evaluate, the result is Indeterminate.

999aaae5e9cb.title: XACML
999aaae5e9cb.sentence: Rules are grouped together in Policies and combined according to a combining algorithm defined by the parent Policy (e.g., deny-unless-permit, permit-unless-deny).

056b5ad969c2.title: XACML
056b5ad969c2.sentence: Then, Policies may be grouped together in a larger Policy (or PolicySet in XACML 3.0) and combined according to its combining algorithm similarly.

62c25ecb0996.title: XACML
62c25ecb0996.sentence: Policies include a Target, which is a condition that determines whether that Policy should be evaluated for a given request.

4b8702bf997e.title: XACML
4b8702bf997e.sentence: What happens in XACML if there are two rules (or policies) that contradict each other?

7c115a0a72d0.title: XACML
7c115a0a72d0.sentence: The combining algorithm of a policy P defines a procedure for combining the individual decision results of the rules and/or policies in P into one final access decision for P.

6060d403e70f.title: XACML
6060d403e70f.sentence: An obligation is a directive from the policy decision point (PDP) to the policy enforcement point (PEP) on what must be carried out before or after an access is approved.

d1f7b907f3eb.title: XACML
d1f7b907f3eb.sentence: If the PEP is unable to comply with the directive, the approved access may or must not be realized.

7374dfe54cd8.title: XACML
7374dfe54cd8.sentence: In addition to obligations, XACML supports advice which are identical to obligations with the difference that a PEP is not obligated to enforce the advice (hence its name).

069e66c51451.title: XACML
069e66c51451.sentence: Obligations specify actions that must be executed during the processing of a request (e.g., for logging).

dc9e4093389b.title: XACML

dc9e4093389b.sentence: The XACML specification does not cover the design or implementation of Policy Decision Point (PDP), only the policy language they consume.

4eda795b22ea.sentence: Many proprietary and open-source PDPs use XACML as their policy definition language.

d5de7bf61f56.sentence: Open Policy Agent (OPA) is an open-source Policy Decision Point (PDP) implementation, capable of interpreting policy language to render policy decisions.

20aaa4757101.title: XACML
20aaa4757101.section: XACML and other standards > XACML and Open Policy Agent
20aaa4757101.sentence: OPA is a general-purpose PDP implementation which can be used for any scenario where a policy decision is required, much like PDP implementations that support the XACML specification.

e3a0928b7923.title: XACML

e3a0928b7923.sentence: It allows an authority (delegator) to delegate all or parts of its own authority or someone else's authority to another user (delegate) without any need to involve modification of the root policy.

b7c5353e302a.sentence: This memo serves as the base requirements for Authorization of Internet Resources and Services (AIRS).

4c909cb974d2.sentence: It presents an architectural framework for understanding the authorization of Internet resources and services and derives requirements for authorization protocols.

ad6ee566a71f.title: rfc>2904

36f423d7ff29.sentence: The User sends a request to the Service Equipment (1), which forwards it to the Service Provider's AAA Server (2), which evaluates the request and returns an appropriate response to the Service Equipment (3), which sets up the service and tells the User it is ready (4).

dbde666e954f.sentence: The push sequence (figure 5) requires that the User get from the Service Provider's AAA Server a ticket or certificate verifying that it is o.k. for the User to have access to the service (1,2).

672d9e0a7e06.title: rfc>2904

672d9e0a7e06.sentence: The Service Equipment uses the ticket to verify that the request is approved by the Service Provider's AAA Server.

aaeac6dcfbef.sentence: In many interesting situations, the organization that authorizes and authenticates the User is different from the organization providing the service.

ff90412b3b09.sentence: For purposes of this discussion, any situation in which the User Home Organization is different from the Service Provider is considered to be roaming.
